Summary: In 5280 (1520), Gershom Soncino founded a Hebrew printing house in Rimini.

Summary: In 5309 (1549), the responsa of Rabbi Yaakov Weil (Mahari Weil) were printed in Venice.

Title: Bragadin and Justinian Rambam controversy in Venice

Title: Cremona printing of the Zohar
Summary: A parallel edition of the Zohar was printed at Vincenzo Conti's press in Cremona in 1558.
Story: Concurrent with the Mantua edition, the Zohar was printed at the Cremona house of Vincenzo Conti in a larger format with textual variants from the Mantua text, known as the Zohar Gadol. This Cremona text was reprinted twice more, in Lublin (1623-4) and Sulzbach (1684).
Tags: cremona, zohar, kabbalah, vincenzo conti, zohar gadol

Title: First printing of the Zohar in Mantua
Summary: The first edition of the Zohar was printed in Mantua between 1558 and 1560.
Story: The Zohar of Rashbi was first printed in 5318-5320 (1558-1560). The Mantua edition was produced at the press of R. Meir b. Efraim of Padua and R. Yaakov b. Naftali of Gazzuolo, and it became the textual basis for most subsequent printings of the Zohar.
Tags: mantua, zohar, kabbalah, rashbi, meir of padua

Title: Maarechet HaElokut printed in Ferrara
Summary: Maarechet HaElokut with R. Yehuda Chayyat's Minchat Yehuda commentary was printed in Ferrara in 1558.
Story: R. Peretz HaKohen of Spain (1305-1370), a Talmudic commentator and kabbalist, authored Maarechet HaElokut. R. Yehuda Chayyat, an exile of the Spanish expulsion who helped disseminate Kabbalah in Italy, wrote the commentary Minchat Yehuda upon it. The combined work was printed in Ferrara in 5318 (1558).
Tags: ferrara, italy, kabbalah, yehuda chayyat, spain exile

Title: Maarechet HaElokut printed in Mantua
Summary: Maarechet HaElokut was also printed in Mantua the same year, 1558.
Story: Parallel to the Ferrara edition, Maarechet HaElokut with Minchat Yehuda was issued in Mantua in 5318 (1558).
Tags: mantua, kabbalah, yehuda chayyat, minchat yehuda

Title: Riva di Trento Hebrew press founded
Summary: In 5318 (1558), Rabbi Yosef Ottolenghi and Rabbi Yaakov Marcaria founded the Hebrew printing house in Riva di Trento; its first book was the Rif.
Story: In 5318 (1558), Rabbi Yosef Ottolenghi and Rabbi Yaakov Marcaria founded the Hebrew printing house in Riva di Trento, Italy. It operated for four years; its first imprint was an edition of the Rif in a smaller format than the preceding Sabbioneta edition.
Tags: italy, riva di trento, ottolenghi, marcaria, rif

Title: Mantua machzor printing completed
Summary: The Mantua Roman-rite machzor was completed in 5320 (1560).
Story: Begun in 1557, the Mantua edition of the Roman-rite machzor was completed in 5320 (1560).
Tags: mantua, machzor, roman rite

Title: Machzor printed in Venice
Summary: A machzor was printed in Venice in 5328 (1568).
Story: The Venice edition of 5328 (1568) is one of the early machzorim preserved in the library's collection.
Tags: venice, italy, machzor

Title: Rabbi Yosef Karo brings new Rambam edition to press in Venice
Summary: In 5334 (1574), after a twenty-year hiatus following the 1550 controversy, Rabbi Yosef Karo issued a new edition of Rambam in Venice with his Kessef Mishneh commentary.
Story: In 5334 (1574), after more than twenty years in which no Rambam was printed in the wake of the Bragadin–Justinian controversy, Rabbi Yosef Karo (author of the Shulchan Aruch) brought a corrected edition of Rambam's Mishneh Torah to press in Venice. The edition included his commentary Kessef Mishneh, and several copies are preserved in the Chabad Library.
Tags: italy, venice, yosef karo, rambam, kessef mishneh

Title: Shulchan Aruch printed in Venice
Summary: Rabbi Yosef Karo's Shulchan Aruch was printed in Venice in 5334 (1574).
Story: Among the early Venetian printings of the Shulchan Aruch, this 1574 edition helped fix Karo's halachic code as the central reference work of Jewish law.
Tags: shulchan aruch, venice, yosef karo

Title: Small-format Shulchan Aruch printed in Venice
Summary: In 5334 (1574), a small octavo-format edition of the Shulchan Aruch was printed in Venice.
Story: In 5334 (1574), a small octavo (8°) format edition of Rabbi Yosef Karo's Shulchan Aruch was issued in Venice, alongside the larger Rambam edition published that year. The small format was intended for portable personal use.
Tags: italy, venice, shulchan aruch, yosef karo

Title: Venice edition of Rambam printed
Summary: A Venice edition of the Rambam was printed in 5334.
Story: In 5334 (1574), a Venice edition of the Rambam was printed. A surviving copy bearing the stamp of R' Avraham Klatzkin, the Chabad rabbi of Lozna, turned up in the Polyakov collection (originally the Schneersohn collection) at the Lenin Library in Moscow when Chabad emissaries searched it in 1991, helping confirm the collection's true origin.
Tags: rambam, venice, klatzkin, lozna, early print

Title: Tosafot Chagigah copied by hand in Egypt
Summary: In 5349 (1589), a portion of Tosafot to Tractate Chagigah was copied by hand in Egypt onto a blank page of the Wadi al-Hijara Talmud.
Story: In 5349 (1589), a rabbi in Egypt who owned a Spanish-edition Talmud — which had been printed with Rashi but without Tosafot — copied a portion of the Tosafot on Tractate Chagigah by hand into a blank leaf at the start of his copy. The page is preserved in the Chabad Library archive.
Tags: egypt, manuscript, tosafot, chagigah

Title: Lublin reprint of the Cremona Zohar
Summary: The Cremona-text Zohar Gadol was reprinted in Lublin in 5383-5384 (1623-1624).
Story: The large-format Cremona edition of the Zohar was reissued in Lublin in 5383-5384 (1623-1624), continuing the textual tradition distinct from the Mantua line.
Tags: lublin, poland, zohar gadol, kabbalah

Title: Manuscript of Darkei Moshe and Maharshal's glosses copied in Szydłów
Summary: In 5401 (1641), a manuscript volume containing the long Darkei Moshe of the Rema and the Maharshal's glosses on the Tur was completed in Szydłów.
Story: In 5401 (1641), a scribe in Szydłów, near Krakow, completed copying a manuscript volume containing two works of glosses on the Tur and Beit Yosef: the long recension of Rema's Darkei Moshe, and Maharshal's glosses on the Tur (which were never independently printed but were later incorporated into the Derisha, Perisha, and Bach).
Tags: poland, szydlow, manuscript, rema, maharshal, tur

Title: R' Shmuel Vital begins writing Shemoneh Shearim in Damascus
Summary: In 5409, R' Shmuel Vital began writing in Damascus the eight-volume Shemoneh Shearim manuscript of his father R' Chaim Vital's teachings of the Arizal.
Story: R' Shmuel Vital completed the eight-volume autograph of the Shaarim between 5409 and 5413 (1649-1653), noting his location and date in each volume. The set was acquired for the Lubavitch library and catalogued as numbers 1942-1949. It was one of the manuscript treasures that drew Soviet interest during the 1927 search.
Tags: shmuel vital, damascus, kabbalah, arizal, manuscript

Title: Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar born in Fez
Summary: Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar, future head of the rabbis of Fez, was born in Fez (5415).
Story: Yehuda ibn Attar was born in Fez (פאס) in the Hebrew year 5415 (1655). He would become the leading halachic authority of Moroccan Jewry, known by Moroccan Jews as 'Arbi Alkabir' (Our Great Rabbi). His family pedigree traced through generations of Fez scholars: his father R. Yaakov, grandfather R. Avraham, and great-grandfather R. Yaakov.
Tags: morocco, fez, yehuda ibn attar, sephardi

Title: Ancient Moroccan ketubah
Summary: A decorated parchment ketubah dated 8 Cheshvan 5420, apparently from Morocco, records the marriage of Avraham to Esther bat Massoud ibn Attiyah.
Story: A second ancient ketubah in the Lubavitcher archive, discovered inside the binding of an old library book, is written on parchment in square and Sephardic Rashi script with decorative ornamentation. Dated 8 Cheshvan 5420 (with the place name partially damaged but appearing to be in Morocco), it records the wedding of a groom named Avraham to the maiden Esther bat Massoud ibn Attiyah.
Tags: morocco, ketubah, manuscript, sephardi

Title: Ancient ketuba dated 5420
Summary: A ketuba dated to 5420 (1660) is preserved in the Chabad library's manuscript collection.
Story: Among the library's ancient ketubot is this 1660 marriage contract, witnessing Jewish family life of the mid-seventeenth century.
Tags: ketuba, manuscript

Title: Highly accurate Amsterdam Tanach printed
Summary: An exceptionally accurate Tanach was printed in Amsterdam in 5426–5427 (1666–1667), later used by the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: This Amsterdam edition of the Tanach was edited by Jewish and Christian scholars and regarded as essentially error-free, with Latin glosses on certain words. Printing began in 5426 and concluded with approbations dated 5427. The Tzemach Tzedek later owned a copy, used it to recite the haftarah, and added marginal notes on textual readings, on minhag differences for which haftarah to read, and on triennial division points.
Tags: amsterdam, tanach, tzemach tzedek bible, printing

Title: Birth of Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur (the Yaavetz) in Meknes
Summary: Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur, known as the Yaavetz, was born on Shabbat 27 Iyar 5433 in Meknes, Morocco.
Story: Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur, later known as the Yaavetz and one of Morocco's preeminent halachic authorities, was born on Shabbat, 27 Iyar 5433 (May 1673), in Meknes. He was the son of Rabbi Reuven ibn Tzur. Strikingly, on the day of his circumcision (5 Sivan 5433) the renowned Land of Israel emissary Rabbi Elisha Ashkenazi passed away in Meknes, evoking the Talmudic image of one sun rising as another sets.
Tags: morocco, meknes, yaavetz, yaakov-ibn-tzur, sephardic, ibn-tzur-family

Title: Ancient ketubah from Crimea
Summary: A ketubah dated 21 Av 5440 from Krasov in Crimea records the marriage of Menachem ben Yosef to Sara bat Gershon Ashkenazi, with a dowry of 49,148 lakhans.
Story: Among the more than fifty ancient ketubot in the Lubavitcher library archive is one from Krasov (Karasubazar) in Crimea, dated 21 Av 5440. The document records the union of Menachem ben Yosef Walid with Sara bat Gershon Ashkenazi; her dowry — including gold jewelry, silverware, garments listed in Tatar, copper vessels, and bedding — totaled 44,680 lakhans, to which the groom added 4,468 for a total of 49,148 lakhans in the coin of Murat Giray. The ketubah reached the Rebbe Rayatz in 5685 through the bibliographer R' Shmuel Wiener.
Tags: crimea, krasov, ketubah, manuscript, tatar

Title: Ibn Tzur family relocates from Meknes to Fez
Summary: A 5443 book-purchase notation suggests the Yaavetz's father moved the family from Meknes to Fez when Yaakov was about ten.
Story: Rabbi Reuven ibn Tzur, father of the Yaavetz, relocated his family from Meknes to Fez during the Yaavetz's youth. A note in a 1559 Riva di Trento Mishnayot volume — now preserved in the Library of Agudat Chasidei Chabad — records his father purchasing it in Fez in 5443 (1683), suggesting the move took place when Yaakov was roughly ten years old. The Yaavetz would spend most of his life in Fez.
Tags: morocco, meknes, fez, yaavetz, ibn-tzur-family

Title: Sulzbach reprint of the Cremona Zohar
Summary: The Cremona-text Zohar Gadol was reprinted in Sulzbach in 5444 (1684).
Story: The Sulzbach edition of 5444 (1684) was the second reprint of the Cremona Zohar Gadol, preserving the variant text of Vincenzo Conti's 1558 edition.
Tags: sulzbach, germany, zohar gadol, kabbalah

Title: Yaavetz begins serving in a Fez synagogue as shaliach
Summary: From 5448, the Yaavetz served as shaliach for sacred matters in a Fez synagogue, reading Torah and delivering sermons.
Story: From 5448 (1688), the young Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur served as 'shaliach for every matter of holiness' in a Fez synagogue, including Torah reading and weekly sermons on halacha, aggadah, and ethics. His later rabbinic appointment letter (1697), preserved in the Ibn Tzur archive at the Agudat Chasidei Chabad library, lavishly praises his cantillation and preaching during these years.
Tags: morocco, fez, yaavetz, synagogue, chazan

Title: Yosef Schneur founds Hebrew press in Furth
Summary: The Furth Hebrew printing house was established by Yosef Schneur in 5451 (1691).
Story: The printer Yosef Schneur founded the Furth press in 5451 (1691). He died shortly afterwards, but the house continued to operate under his name.
Tags: furth, germany, yosef schneur, printing

Title: Furth press notice of printed books
Summary: In 5452 (1692) the Furth press printed an announcement of the books issued in its house.
Story: The Furth press of the late Yosef Schneur printed a broadside in 5452 (1692) advertising 'the books printed in the holy community of Furth in the excellent press of the eminent Yosef Schneur z"l.' Such notices are exceptionally rare survivals from this period.
Tags: furth, germany, broadside, yosef schneur

Title: Yaavetz appointed scribe of the Fez beit din at age 20
Summary: In 5453, at age 20, the Yaavetz was appointed scribe of the Fez beit din under Rabbis Vidal Tzarfati and Menachem Serero.
Story: In 5453 (1693), at age twenty, Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur was appointed scribe (sofer beit din) of the Fez rabbinical court led by Rabbis Vidal Tzarfati and Menachem Serero. He later recorded that during this period he visited the court rabbis two or three times daily, presenting his halachic questions and observing their adjudication. An archive document from 5459 still bears his signature with the title 'sofer.'
Tags: morocco, fez, yaavetz, beit-din, rabbinical-court, vidal-tzarfati, menachem-serero

Title: Amsterdam Haggadah desert-journey map printed
Summary: A fold-out map of the Israelites' desert journeys was printed in Amsterdam in 5455 (1695) for inclusion in a Passover Haggadah.
Story: Early printers sometimes issued large broadsheets meant to be folded and bound into a book. The Amsterdam map of the journeys of the Children of Israel through the wilderness was produced in 5455 (1695) for binding into the Amsterdam Haggadah of that year.
Tags: amsterdam, netherlands, haggadah, passover, map

Title: Amsterdam Haggadah printed with map of the Land of Israel
Summary: A Pesach Haggadah was printed in Amsterdam in 5455 (1695) accompanied by a map of the Land of Israel.
Story: The 1695 Amsterdam Haggadah included one of the early printed maps of the Holy Land bound with a Pesach service, a notable example of early modern Jewish cartography.
Tags: haggadah, amsterdam, map, land of israel

Title: Fez synagogue formally installs Yaavetz as permanent rabbi
Summary: In 5457 the members of his Fez synagogue signed a binding rabbinic appointment for the Yaavetz and his descendants in perpetuity.
Story: In 5457 (1697) the congregation of the Yaavetz's Fez synagogue ratified a sweeping rabbinic appointment installing him as their permanent leader, with the position to pass to his descendants 'until the coming of Messiah.' The signed contract — which also turned over three Torah scrolls and the entire synagogue endowment to his discretion — is preserved in the Ibn Tzur archive at the Library of Agudat Chasidei Chabad.
Tags: morocco, fez, yaavetz, synagogue, rabbinical-appointment

Title: R. Shmuel ibn Danan sells future inheritance share to brother in Fez
Summary: R. Shmuel ibn Danan formally sold his anticipated inheritance from his still-living father, R. Saadia, to his brother Yitzchak for 500 ouguiyas.
Story: On 29 Shevat 5457 (1697) in Fez, R. Shmuel ibn Danan, son of the elder R. Saadia, sold to his brother Yitzchak whatever he would inherit from their still-living father, both the firstborn share and the regular share, in exchange for 500 ouquiyot. Because the inheritance was 'a thing not yet in the world,' a standard kinyan was legally insufficient, so the sale was reinforced by a severe oath that Shmuel would repay the sum in full if the sale ever lapsed. The shtar was signed by R. Yehuda ibn Atar and R. Avraham ibn Masud ibn Atia.
Tags: morocco, fez, beit din, ibn danan, inheritance, yehuda ibn atar

Title: Heirs of R. Binyamin Navarro grant mechilah to Avraham Tzarfati
Summary: The widow and heirs of R. Binyamin Navarro waived all claims against Avraham Tzarfati while preserving joint ownership of a parcel of land inherited from Navarro.
Story: On 13 Elul 5457 (1697) in Fez, Yosef Piso ben R. Moshe, Yitzchak Navarro, and Avraham ibn Lachsin (acting under power of attorney for Chana, widow of R. Binyamin Navarro) executed a sweeping mechilah to Avraham Tzarfati ben R. Meir, waiving every claim and grievance from the dawn of creation, even up to 1,000 ouquiyot. Only their shared ownership in a known parcel of land inherited from R. Binyamin remained between them. R. Yehuda ibn Atar and R. Avraham ibn Masud ben Atia signed the deed.
Tags: morocco, fez, beit din, navarro, tzarfati, inheritance, partnership

Title: Birth of the Baal Shem Tov
Summary: Rabbi Israel Baal Shem Tov was born on 18 Elul 5458 in Okup.
Story: The founder of the chassidic movement, Rabbi Israel ben Eliezer, known as the Baal Shem Tov, was born on 18 Elul 5458 (1698) in the town of Okup. He passed away in Medzhibuzh in 5520 (1760).
Tags: baal shem tov, okup, 18 elul

Title: Latin translation of the Haggadah printed in Frankfurt
Summary: A Haggadah with a Latin translation and musical notation for liturgical poems was printed in Frankfurt.
Story: In 5458 (1698), a Haggadah was published in Frankfurt featuring the Hebrew text alongside a parallel Latin translation. The Hebrew was printed without vowel points, and the edition included musical notation for the songs 'Ki Lo Naeh' and 'Adir Hu'. The 70-page work made the Seder text accessible to Latin-reading scholars of the era.
Tags: haggadah, latin, frankfurt, germany, musical notation

Title: Fez beit din pesharah on the shop of Yitzchak's heirs
Summary: A Fez beit din ratified a corrected compromise allowing R. Maimon to collect a supplement at redemption time, safeguarding the heirs' interest in a disputed shop.
Story: In the last third of Kislev 5459 (late 1698) in Fez, the beit din finalized a ruling concerning a shop linked to one Yitzchak, ruling that his relatives who inherited would pay in full to rescue the shop from claimants and that R. Maimon would also be empowered to collect an additional sum at the time of redemption. After a clerical error in the amount, '30' was corrected to '20' between the lines before the remaining dayanim signed. The document was signed by R. Menachem Sirero, R. Vidal Hatzarfati, R. Yehuda ibn Atar, R. Shmuel Hatzarfati, and endorsed by R. Moshe ibn Hamu.
Tags: morocco, fez, beit din, yehuda ibn atar, menachem sirero, shop, inheritance

Title: Birth of Rabbi Yisrael Baal Shem Tov
Summary: The Baal Shem Tov, founder of the chasidic movement, was born in 1700.
Story: The Baal Shem Tov launched a religious revival emphasizing the divine spark in every Jew, joyful worship, and spiritual access for all. His teachings reshaped Eastern European Jewry and laid the foundation for Chabad and other chasidic dynasties.
Tags: baal shem tov, besht, chasidism founder

Title: Chevrat Mishmeret HaBoker veHaErev founded in Mantua
Summary: On 1 Nisan 5462 (March 1702) the Mantua society for early-morning and late-Shabbat Torah study was founded.
Story: On Rosh Chodesh Nisan 5462 (March 1702) the 'Chevrat Mishmeret HaBoker veHaErev' was established in Mantua for those who would rise early and remain late on Shabbat for Torah study. Thirteen years later the society celebrated its founding.
Tags: mantua, italy, torah study, early-rising, chevrah

Title: Widow Alaz acknowledges Yaakov ibn Atar's debt of 400 ouquiyot
Summary: Alaz, widow of R. Yitzchak ben Mordechai Adhan, and her son Mordechai formally recognized that Yaakov ben Avraham ibn Atar still owed 400 ouquiyot from orphan funds entrusted to him to lend out.
Story: On 18 Shevat 5463 (1703) in Fez, Alaz and her son Mordechai issued a mechilah to Yaakov ben Avraham ibn Atar, formally acknowledging that of orphan funds entrusted to him to be lent out on pledges in the customary manner, 400 ouquiyot remained outstanding. A debt note for that exact sum was executed the same day. Over the following years Yaakov repaid in installments noted on the back of the shtar, until only about 104 ouquiyot remained when he became impoverished.
Tags: morocco, fez, ibn atar, adhan, orphan funds, loan

Title: Yaavetz elevated to dayan of Fez after Rabbi Vidal Tzarfati's death
Summary: Following Rabbi Vidal Tzarfati's death in 5464, the Yaavetz was promoted to dayan of the Fez beit din.
Story: After Rabbi Vidal Tzarfati's passing in 5464 (1704), Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur was appointed to fill his seat as dayan on the Fez rabbinical court. He served alongside his teacher Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar (the Maharibav) and Rabbi Shmuel Tzarfati, marking his ascension to the senior tier of Moroccan poskim. He would later author the influential responsa work Mishpat u'Tzedakah B'Yaakov.
Tags: morocco, fez, yaavetz, beit-din, dayan, vidal-tzarfati, yehuda-ibn-attar

Title: Death of R' Yehuda Leib, great-grandson of the Maharal of Prague
Summary: R' Yehuda Leib, son of R' Shmuel and great-grandson of the Maharal of Prague, died in Tishrei 5466.
Story: According to the Prague tombstone records compiled by R' Sinai Hock, R' Yehuda Leib ben R' Shmuel (grandson of R' Bezalel, the Maharal's only son) died in Tishrei 5466. This discovery overturned the long-held claim by R' Meir Pereles and others that R' Shmuel left only daughters, and helped establish the Alter Rebbe's descent from the Maharal through his great-great-grandfather R' Yehuda Leib of Posen.
Tags: maharal, prague, genealogy, ancestry

Title: Birth of Rabbi Refael Oved ibn Tzur, son and future successor
Summary: Rabbi Refael Oved ibn Tzur, the Yaavetz's son and eventual successor, was born on 3 Shevat 5466.
Story: Rabbi Refael Oved ibn Tzur was born on Monday, 3 Shevat 5466 (January 1706) in Fez. He was one of seventeen children born to the Yaavetz, of whom only he and his brother Reuven survived their father. He would eventually inherit his father's rabbinic mantle and continue the family's marriage-registration pinkas, now preserved as MS 1605 in the Library of Agudat Chasidei Chabad.
Tags: morocco, fez, yaavetz, ibn-tzur-family, refael-oved

Title: Fez beit din awards 1.5 shops to heirs of R. Refael Moshe ibn Tzur
Summary: Fez beit din settled a dispute between R. Yitzchak ibn Tzur and the kahal's treasurers over three shops his late father had owned, granting 1.5 to the heirs and 1.5 to the poor.
Story: On 29 Iyar 5466 (1706) in Fez, R. Yitzchak ben R. Refael Moshe ibn Tzur sued the community treasurers, R. Yitzchak Hatzarfati and R. Saadia Aflalo, over three shops in the New Vegetable Market that had belonged to his father. The shops had been sealed when R. Refael Moshe departed for Tetouan years earlier, after which the kahal opened them and used them in his prolonged absence. Witness testimony, a former attempt to claim them by R. Moshe HaKohen on behalf of the heirs, and the surviving doorpost markings led the beit din — R. Yehuda ibn Atar, R. Shmuel Hatzarfati, and R. Yaakov ben R. Reuven ibn Tzur — to award one and a half shops to the heirs and one and a half to the poor of the kahal. The treasurers and parnasim of the community signed their agreement.
Tags: morocco, fez, tetouan, beit din, ibn tzur, community property, yaakov ibn tzur

Title: Esther bat Yitzchak Adhan renounces inheritance for her dowry
Summary: The orphan Esther formally renounced all claims to her late father's estate in exchange for the dowry her mother and brothers were providing for her marriage.
Story: On 25 Iyar 5468 (1708) in Fez, Esther bat the late R. Yitzchak ben Mordechai Adhan, confirmed to be of full age, formally relinquished every claim and right she had against her mother Alaz and her brothers in exchange for the dowry they were providing for her marriage. She additionally granted them by way of an open, public, healthy-person's gift all the documents, notes, and remaining property from her father's estate, on land and movables alike. The deed was signed in Fez by R. Shlomo Amiel and R. Moshe ben Makhluf ben Maman, written up on 19 Sivan 5468 at the request of Yaakov ben Atar, who had a stake in the underlying mechilah.
Tags: morocco, fez, beit din, adhan, dowry, inheritance

Title: R. Yehuda ibn Atar orders Yaakov ben Atar to borrow at interest for Adhan orphans
Summary: R. Yehuda ibn Atar compelled impoverished Yaakov ben Atar to borrow from gentiles at interest to repay the Adhan orphans, enabling the orphan Esther to marry.
Story: On 13 Sivan 5468 (1708) in Fez, with Yaakov ben Avraham ibn Atar having sworn poverty and unable to repay the widow Alaz and her sons Mordechai and Yosef on the debts to their late father R. Yitzchak ben Mordechai Adhan, R. Yehuda ibn Atar intervened. Moved by Yaakov's pursuit by many creditors and by the plight of Esther, a daughter who had reached marriageable age without dowry, R. Yehuda ordered Yaakov to borrow 50 ouquiyot from gentiles on credit and pay an additional 25 to the heirs within eighteen months. In return, the widow and orphans waived every claim against Yaakov, freed him from oaths and bans, and committed to indemnify him against any future claim.
Tags: morocco, fez, yehuda ibn atar, ibn atar, adhan, interest, dowry, orphans

Title: Sale of R' Yehuda Uziel's synagogue in Fes to R' Emanuel Mansano
Summary: R' Yosef ben Menachem Uziel sold two-thirds of the synagogue inherited from R' Yehuda Uziel to R' Emanuel Mansano on 19 Marcheshvan 5470 in Fes.
Story: Following an existing mortgage, R' Yosef sold two-thirds of the synagogue (including Torah scrolls, ark, benches, and ritual items) to R' Emanuel Mansano for 680 ounces. R' Yaakov ibn Tzur, holding a one-sixth share, asserted neighbor's right and the parties compromised so that Mansano and Ibn Tzur each took one-third. The document was confirmed by the dayanim of Fes, including R' Yehuda ibn Attar.
Tags: morocco, fes, synagogue, emanuel mansano, yaakov ibn tzur, yehuda ibn attar, property

Title: R. Moshe Yisrael sent on Safed mission to North Africa
Summary: R. Moshe Yisrael departed Jerusalem on a fundraising mission for the holy city of Safed to the lands of North Africa.
Story: Born in Jerusalem around 1680 and son-in-law of R. Moshe ibn Habib, R. Moshe Yisrael was dispatched as an emissary (shadar) of Safed to North Africa in 1710. He remained on this mission until 1713, traveling through Moroccan communities including Meknes and Fez. During this period he corresponded with fellow emissary R. Nissim Avraham Hakohen regarding the collection of pledged donations.
Tags: safed, north africa, morocco, shadar, moshe yisrael, fundraising

Title: Testimony of investment in mortgaged building in Fes
Summary: In mid-Tevet 5470, R' Yitzchak ben David ve-Chayun added 52 ounces of building repairs to his mortgage on R' Chaim Yaakov's upper-story property in Fes.
Story: R' Yitzchak rebuilt half of a shared wall in the mortgaged upper story, spending on lime, sand, bricks, debris removal, and workers' wages and meals. The owner R' Chaim Yaakov consented before the court to add this sum to the mortgage, so that on redemption the principal and addition would be paid together. The ruling was signed by R' Yehuda ibn Attar and other Fes dayanim.
Tags: morocco, fes, beit din, mortgage, property, yehuda ibn attar

Title: Marriage of Shi'acha bat Yehuda ibn Attar to Shem Tov ben Avraham
Summary: Shi'acha, daughter of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar, married her cousin Shem Tov ben Avraham in Fez on 17 Cheshvan 5472.
Story: On Friday, 17 Cheshvan 5472 (Nov 7, 1711), Shi'acha bat Yehuda ibn Attar married Shem Tov, son of her uncle Avraham ibn Attar, in Fez. The wedding was recorded in the marriage register of Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur (the Ya'abetz). The match kept the ibn Attar family lineage close, with Shi'acha marrying her first cousin.
Tags: morocco, fez, yehuda ibn attar, marriage register, yaabetz

Title: Illustrated Abarbanel Haggadah printed in Amsterdam by Shlomo Proops
Summary: Shlomo Proops printed an illustrated Haggadah in Amsterdam featuring the Abarbanel and other commentaries.
Story: In 5472 (1712), Shlomo Proops issued a richly illustrated Haggadah in Amsterdam with commentaries by Don Isaac Abarbanel, Ma'aseh Hashem, Mateh Aharon, and Chevel Bnei Yehudah, alongside abridgments of other commentators. The work included an engraved map showing all the Israelite wanderings in the desert, etched on copper plates. The 31-leaf folio became an iconic illustrated edition of the era.
Tags: haggadah, abarbanel, amsterdam, shlomo proops, illustrated, copper engraving

Title: R. Eliezer Behlul composes Mareh Einayim in Meknes
Summary: R. Eliezer Behlul, one of the sages of Meknes, composed a manuscript book of sermons titled Mareh Einayim.
Story: R. Eliezer Behlul of Meknes wrote his homiletical work Mareh Einayim in 1712, which remained in manuscript form. The book incorporated novel teachings he heard from the visiting emissaries R. Moshe Yisrael and R. Nissim Avraham Hakohen, who were then traveling through Morocco on Land of Israel missions.
Tags: morocco, meknes, manuscript, homiletics, eliezer behlul

Title: Marriage of R. Shmuel ben Yosef ibn Attar
Summary: R. Shmuel, son of Yosef ibn Attar (brother of Rabbi Yehuda), was married on 26 Cheshvan 5473 in Fez.
Story: On Friday, 26 Cheshvan 5473 (Nov 5, 1712), Shmuel ben Yosef ibn Attar — a nephew of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar — was married. The event was registered in Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur's marriage records. This entry reveals that Rabbi Yehuda had a previously unrecorded brother named Yosef who had three sons: Shmuel, Yaakov, and Yitzchak.
Tags: morocco, fez, ibn attar, marriage register

Title: Marriage of Rivka bat Oved ibn Attar to Shmuel ben Nachmosh
Summary: Rivka, granddaughter of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar, married Shmuel ben Nachmosh ben Mayara on 17 Kislev 5473.
Story: On Friday, 17 Kislev 5473 (Dec 6, 1712), Rivka bat Oved — a granddaughter of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar through his son Oved — was married to Shmuel ben Nachmosh of the Mayara family in Fez. The marriage was registered in the records of Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur (the Ya'abetz).
Tags: morocco, fez, ibn attar, mayara family, marriage register

Title: Haggadah with commentary of Eliyahu ben Todros Broda printed in Prague
Summary: A Haggadah with a Yiddish translation by Eliyahu ben Todros Broda was printed in Prague by Shlomo Proops.
Story: In 5473 (1713), Shlomo Proops printed a Haggadah in Prague featuring a Yiddish translation by Eliyahu ben Todros Broda. The 16-leaf folio edition served the Yiddish-speaking Jewish community of Bohemia. The surviving copy in the library is missing its title page and possibly its opening section.
Tags: haggadah, prague, shlomo proops, yiddish

Title: R. Moshe Yisrael becomes rabbi of Rhodes
Summary: R. Moshe Yisrael was accepted as the rabbi of the Jewish community of Rhodes in eastern Greece.
Story: After completing his North African emissary mission in 1713, R. Moshe Yisrael was appointed rabbi of Rhodes in 1714. He served the community there until 1736, with an interruption between 1727 and 1731 when he undertook a Jerusalem emissary mission to Italy and Holland.
Tags: rhodes, greece, rabbinate, moshe yisrael

Title: Mantua society marks 13th anniversary
Summary: On 1 Nisan 5475 (April 1715) Mantua's Chevrat Mishmeret marked its 13th anniversary with a printed Shir LaMaalot.
Story: Thirteen years after its founding, the Mantua Chevrat Mishmeret HaBoker veHaErev celebrated 'the birthday of the chevrah' on 1 Nisan 5475 (April 1715), and printed a Shir LaMaalot poem in honor of the occasion.
Tags: mantua, italy, chevrah, anniversary, shir lamaalot

Title: Heirs of R' Yitzchak ben David ve-Chayun add further building repairs to mortgage
Summary: In Tishrei 5476, the orphans of R' Yitzchak ben David ve-Chayun added expenses for repairs to a mortgaged property in Fes.
Story: Witnesses Yaakov ben Mordechai Azulai (mason) and Yaakov Punitz (carpenter) testified before the Fes beit din that the orphans had paid for essential repairs to the bathroom wall, the roof, the courtyard floor, doors, and beams of the mortgaged property. These sums of roughly 5.25 and 12 ounces were added to the existing mortgage, to be repaid in full at redemption.
Tags: morocco, fes, beit din, mortgage, property

Title: Pawn-sale deed of courtyard property from Saadia to Yeshua in Fez
Summary: Saadia Cabalero pledged a house in the courtyard of Yissachar ibn Zazon to R' Yeshua ben Yissachar for 150 ounces, with formal cancellation of secret protests.
Story: Saadia obligated himself to repay 150 ounces by the end of Nisan, failing which the mortgaged house would pass to Yeshua. The deed extensively voided any prior moda'a (secret protest) by Saadia and provided that scribes and any future court could repeatedly write cancellations of such protests. Witnessed in Fez by Avraham Serero and Shaul.
Tags: morocco, fez, sephardic, real-estate, moda'a-cancellation, ibn-zazon

Title: Rivkah bat Shem Tov Cohen waives inheritance upon marriage to R' Shmuel Elbaz
Summary: On 27 Tevet 5477, Rivkah, daughter of the late R' Shem Tov Cohen, formally relinquished her claims on her father's estate after receiving an oversized dowry from her mother Reina ahead of her marriage to R' Shmuel Elbaz.
Story: Rivkah's mother provided her with cash and goods worth approximately 1,000 ounces, far more than her legal portion of the estate. Rivkah and, on 1 Shevat, her betrothed R' Shmuel Elbaz (later author of Vayomer Shmuel) renounced all further claims against the estate. The dayanim R' Yehuda ibn Attar, R' Yaakov ibn Attar, R' Yaakov ibn Tzur and R' Avraham Tzarfati ratified the waiver.
Tags: morocco, fes, marriage, inheritance, shmuel elbaz, vayomer shmuel, yehuda ibn attar

Title: Transfer of Fez mortgage deed from Yeshua ibn Zazon to R' Yaakov Halevi
Summary: Yeshua ibn Zazon sold the Cabalero mortgage deed to R' Yaakov Halevi ben Shmuel via the four-cubits-of-land method.
Story: On 25 Kislev 5478, Yeshua transferred all his rights in the pawn deed to R' Yaakov Halevi, swearing he had not collected on it and accepting responsibility for any future challengers including R' Shlomo Cabalero. Witnessed by Yaakov ibn Attar and Yaakov HaTzarfati in Fez.
Tags: morocco, fez, sephardic, real-estate, mortgage-transfer, yaakov-halevi

Title: Crispo writes from Fez to ibn Tzur on new Meknes post
Summary: Crispo wrote ibn Tzur on 13 Av 1718 about overseeing the collection of pledges in Fez and surrounding towns after the latter's move to Meknes.
Story: On 13 Av 1718, R. Yom Tov Crispo wrote from Fez to R. Yaakov ibn Tzur, who had just been appointed rabbi of Meknes. The letter expressed joy at the appointment and asked ibn Tzur to oversee the collection from a distance of the various pledges promised in Fez, Taza, Debdou, and other communities for the Jerusalem mission.
Tags: morocco, fez, meknes, shadar, fundraising, 13 av

Title: R. Yaakov ibn Tzur becomes rabbi of Meknes
Summary: R. Yaakov ibn Tzur was appointed rabbi of Meknes in the middle of summer 1718.
Story: After serving as a judge in Fez, R. Yaakov ibn Tzur (the Ya'avetz), author of Mishpat U'Tzedaka B'Yaakov, was accepted as rabbi of Meknes in the summer of 1718. He served there until 1729, when he returned to Fez. Following the death of his teacher R. Yehuda ibn Atar, he served as head of the Fez rabbinical court until his death in 1753.
Tags: morocco, meknes, fez, rabbinate, yaakov ibn tzur

Title: R. Yom Tov Crispo begins Jerusalem mission to North Africa
Summary: R. Yom Tov Crispo departed Jerusalem as an emissary to the communities of North Africa.
Story: R. Yom Tov Crispo was sent in 1718 on a Jerusalem emissary mission to North Africa, beginning with the towns of Morocco. The mission continued for four years until 1722, during which he traveled through Algeria, Tunisia, and Egypt. In Fez he was assisted by R. Yaakov ibn Tzur in raising support both locally and in surrounding towns.
Tags: north africa, morocco, algeria, tunisia, egypt, shadar, yom tov crispo

Title: Rabbi Menachem Sirero, son-in-law of the Yaavetz, dies young
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Sirero, husband of the Yaavetz's daughter Azi Bueno, died in Cheshvan 5479 at about 26 years old.
Story: Rabbi Menachem Sirero, son-in-law of the Yaavetz, passed away in Cheshvan 5479 (autumn 1718). Born in 5453, he was only about twenty-six. The Yaavetz had inscribed Sirero's marriage to his daughter Azi Bueno in his own hand on 8 Adar in the family marriage-records register.
Tags: morocco, fez, sirero, yaavetz, ibn-tzur-family

Title: Yaavetz moves from Fez to Meknes to head the community
Summary: Between Iyar and Menachem Av 5478, the Yaavetz relocated from Fez to Meknes, where he was received as 'head and dignitary' of the community.
Story: Between Iyar and Menachem Av of 5478 (spring–summer 1718), Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur left Fez and settled in Meknes, where the community received him as 'head and dignitary.' A 13 Menachem Av letter from Jerusalem emissary Rabbi Yom Tov Crispo expresses joy at the news of his installation. He would remain in Meknes for roughly eleven years.
Tags: morocco, fez, meknes, yaavetz, yom-tov-crispo

Title: Marriage of Miriam bat Yaakov ibn Attar
Summary: Miriam, daughter of R. Yaakov (Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar's nephew), was married on 20 Tevet 5478.
Story: On 20 Tevet 5478 (Jan 12, 1718), Miriam bat Yaakov ben Yosef ibn Attar was married. The match was recorded in the Ya'abetz's marriage register. Yaakov was a son of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar's brother Yosef, making Miriam a grandniece of the head rabbi of Fez.
Tags: morocco, fez, ibn attar, marriage register

Title: R' Yehoshua Serero appointed cantor of Ibn Ravuach synagogue in Fes
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Adar 5482, the rabbis of Fes confirmed R' Yehoshua Serero as permanent cantor at the synagogue named for R' Saadia ibn Ravuach, overruling a competing appointment.
Story: After the death of cantor R' Yaakov ibn Danan, the congregation had endorsed Serero's appointment, but a later writ claimed Ibn Danan had instructed that R' Yosef ibn Shikrun succeed him. The Fes beit din ruled the earlier congregational decision authoritative and barred any other cantor. The dispute was significant enough that the rabbis of Meknes - including R' Moshe Toledano, R' Yaakov ibn Tzur, and R' Moshe Berdugo - co-signed in support.
Tags: morocco, fes, meknes, cantor, synagogue, yehoshua serero, yaakov ibn danan, yosef ibn shikrun, yehuda ibn attar

Title: Crispo dedicates 'Shiyarei Knesset HaGedolah' to the Yaavetz
Summary: On 25 Tammuz 5482 in Alexandria, Jerusalem emissary Yom Tov Crispo purchased and dedicated 'Shiyarei Knesset HaGedolah' to the Yaavetz.
Story: On 25 Tammuz 5482 (July 1722), Rabbi Yom Tov Crispo — a Jerusalem emissary returning from Morocco — purchased the volume 'Shiyarei Knesset HaGedolah' in Alexandria and inscribed it as a gift to the Yaavetz. Earlier letters from Crispo (7 and 12 Marcheshvan 5482) record that he had also sent two other rare volumes, 'She'elot u'Teshuvot Bach' and 'Ginat Veradim,' at the Yaavetz's request. Several of these volumes are today held in the Library of Agudat Chasidei Chabad.
Tags: morocco, egypt, yaavetz, yom-tov-crispo, shadar, library, books

Title: Beit Din ruling on Ibn Saadon vs. Ibn Danan debt in Fez
Summary: Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar issued a ruling in Fez requiring the heir of R' Shlomo ibn Danan to pay the Ibn Saadon brothers from his courtyard property.
Story: The Ibn Saadon brothers had sold ostrich feathers to R' Shlomo ibn Danan on credit and were never fully paid before his death. His son R' Shmuel claimed his father had paid more than recorded and that non-Jewish creditors had seized all the inherited land. R' Yehuda ibn Attar ruled that the creditors could collect from the 'almasriya' still in the heir's courtyard, subject to mutual oaths.
Tags: morocco, fez, bet-din, sephardic, yehuda-ibn-attar, ostrich-feathers, debt-dispute

Title: Mantua Pragmatica sumptuary regulations renewed
Summary: On 29 Cheshvan 5483 (November 1722) the Mantua community renewed its Pragmatica sumptuary regulations for six years.
Story: Mantua's community ordinances, known as the Pragmatica, restricted royal dress, jewelry, and dancing so that Jews would not stand out before the gentile population. On 29 Cheshvan 5483 (November 1722) the regulations were renewed for six years, from Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni 5483 through Erev Rosh Chodesh Adar 5489, signed by Rabbi David Pinzi and the scribe R. Shimshon Moron.
Tags: mantua, italy, pragmatica, sumptuary, community ordinances

Title: Fez Beit Din confirms transfer of mortgage to R' Avraham Toledano
Summary: On 7 Adar Sheni 5483, the Fez Beit Din formalized the orphans' half-share in the mortgage in favor of R' Avraham Toledano.
Story: Acting on behalf of the heirs of R' Yaakov Halevi, R' Yehuda ibn Attar and fellow dayanim conveyed the orphans' half of the rights in the mortgage to R' Avraham Toledano. The ruling cleared and emptied the orphans' lien on the pawn document.
Tags: morocco, fez, sephardic, bet-din, real-estate, orphans, yehuda-ibn-attar

Title: Widow of R' Yaakov Halevi sells Fez mortgage to R' Avraham Toledano
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni 5483, the widow of R' Yaakov Halevi formally conveyed the long-traveled pawn deed in Fez to R' Avraham ben Baruch Toledano.
Story: Acting with her late husband's interest, the widow used the kinyan-and-four-cubits-of-land form to convey the mortgage deed and all rights it carried. She swore she had not collected on it and would not transfer it again. Witnessed by Shmuel ibn Saadon and Mordechai Tzaba.
Tags: morocco, fez, sephardic, real-estate, widow, toledano

Title: Settlement between Moshe Vechiyon and Moshe ibn Assoulin in Fez
Summary: On 14 Iyar 5483, the Fez Beit Din ratified a compromise between Moshe ben Yitzchak Vechiyon and Moshe ben Ayyush ibn Assoulin closing all mutual claims.
Story: Vechiyon was owed about 170 ounces; mediators settled the dispute and Shlomo ben Masoud ibn Botbol assumed a written obligation for the agreed sum. The parties mutually released all past money, oath, and gilgul-shevua claims, retaining only an outstanding loan with extended repayment until Sukkot eve. Witnessed by R' Yehuda ibn Attar and Yitzchak Maimran.
Tags: morocco, fez, sephardic, bet-din, debt-settlement, yehuda-ibn-attar

Title: R' Avraham Toledano conveys Fez mortgage to Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur (Yaavetz)
Summary: On 18 Sivan 5483, R' Avraham Toledano transferred the chain-of-title mortgage deed to R' Yaakov ibn Tzur (the Yaavetz), then rabbi of Meknes.
Story: R' Yaakov ibn Tzur served as rabbi of Meknes from circa 5478-5488 (1717/8-1727/8). Despite his seat in Meknes, in 5483 he acquired this Fez pawn deed, which had passed through many hands since 5476. Witnessed by Yehuda Halevi and David Shacrun in Fez.
Tags: morocco, fez, meknes, sephardic, real-estate, yaakov-ibn-tzur, yaavetz

Title: Letter on drought and tax oppression in Fez community
Summary: Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar wrote to Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur in 5485 lamenting severe drought and oppressive tax extraction from the Fez community.
Story: In the year 5485 (1725), Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar wrote anguished letters to Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur, then serving as rabbi in Meknes. He described the dire situation in Fez: severe drought, Torah scholars imprisoned by the local governor for three days over debts, and a punishing communal tax of 500 ounces per seventy households in the Mellah. He wrote in tears, fearing violence between debtors and oppressors.
Tags: morocco, fez, meknes, taxes, drought, yehuda ibn attar, yaakov ibn tzur

Title: Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar adjudicates dilapidated property dispute
Summary: On 25 Tammuz 5486, Rabbi Yehuda of Fez wrote to the Meknes beit din about an endangered building requiring urgent demolition and rebuilding.
Story: On 25 Tammuz 5486 (July 25, 1726), Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar wrote from Fez to the rabbis and leaders of Meknes regarding the case of Shlomo Ag'iani and Yosef Abuzaglu over the property known as 'Dar Mawlana' purchased from the royal court. A previous letter from him in the same period addressed an upper-story building in the 'Dar Bunfad' courtyard that had become structurally dangerous and required immediate sale or repair authorization.
Tags: morocco, fez, meknes, yehuda ibn attar, responsa, property

Title: Fez community begins effort to bring the Yaavetz back from Meknes
Summary: During Hanukkah 5487, thirty to forty Fez community members met in Meknes and swore a commitment to bring the Yaavetz back as their rabbi.
Story: During Hanukkah 5487 (December 1726), some thirty to forty leading members of the Fez community traveled to Meknes and committed under oath to support Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur if he would return to Fez. The agreement, which detailed financial terms and pledged unconditional obedience to his rulings, was eventually ratified in Adar Sheni 5489 once the move actually took place. The signed parchment survives in the Ibn Tzur archive at the Agudat Chasidei Chabad library.
Tags: morocco, fez, meknes, yaavetz, rabbinical-appointment

Title: R' Meir Pereles completes Megillat Yuchasin in Prague
Summary: R' Meir Pereles of Prague finished his genealogical work Megillat Yuchasin in 5487.
Story: Megillat Yuchasin, a key source on the descendants of the Maharal of Prague, was written by R' Meir Pereles in 5487 (he states 'until today, which is the year 5487'). The work omitted the male line through R' Yehuda Leib ben R' Shmuel, an omission that later researchers had to correct using Prague gravestone evidence.
Tags: prague, genealogy, maharal

Title: R. Moshe Yisrael's Jerusalem mission to Italy and Holland
Summary: R. Moshe Yisrael departed on a Jerusalem emissary mission to Italy and Holland.
Story: In 1727, while serving as rabbi of Rhodes, R. Moshe Yisrael was dispatched as a Jerusalem emissary to the communities of Italy and Holland. He remained on this mission for four years until 1731, when he returned to Rhodes. During this period his rabbinical post in Rhodes was temporarily vacated.
Tags: italy, holland, jerusalem, shadar, moshe yisrael

Title: R. Yom Tov Crispo's second mission from Hebron to Europe
Summary: R. Yom Tov Crispo departed on a Hebron emissary mission to the lands of Europe.
Story: In 1727, R. Yom Tov Crispo was sent on a second emissary mission, this time on behalf of Hebron to the European Jewish communities. The mission lasted four years until 1731. Some years earlier he had returned from his first Jerusalem mission to North Africa.
Tags: hebron, europe, shadar, yom tov crispo

Title: Fez Beit Din settlement over R' Yitzchak ibn Assoulin's estate
Summary: On 25-27 Kislev 5488, the Fez Beit Din finalized a compromise between Chaim Levi and R' Moshe ibn Assoulin regarding the estate of his deceased brother R' Yitzchak.
Story: Chaim, who had married R' Yitzchak's widow, demanded an accounting of the estate that R' Moshe had managed during years of famine, while R' Moshe claimed nothing remained. Mediators settled the case for sixteen ounces, all other claims were mutually waived, and a dwelling was preserved for the orphan Ayyush. R' Yehuda ibn Attar and Shmuel Gabbai presided and witnessed.
Tags: morocco, fez, sephardic, bet-din, inheritance, widow, yibum, famine, yehuda-ibn-attar

Title: Mantua prayer for excessive rain printed
Summary: A 'prayer for excessive rains that damage crops' was printed in Mantua in 5489 (1729).
Story: Following the halachic ruling in Shulchan Aruch (OC 576:11) that one prays when excessive rains cause distress, Mantua's community printed a sheet of prayers for excessive rains that were damaging the grain harvest in 5489 (1729).
Tags: mantua, italy, broadside, tefillah, rain

Title: Yaavetz returns from Meknes to Fez after eleven years
Summary: In Adar Sheni 5489, after roughly eleven years serving in Meknes, the Yaavetz returned to Fez.
Story: In Adar Sheni 5489 (spring 1729), after some eleven years leading the Meknes community, Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur returned to Fez. The Fez community formally re-ratified its earlier oath of support just before his arrival. His marriage-records pinkas, which had recorded 'Meknesa' as the place of entry since 5480, switches back to 'Fez' from 5489 onward.
Tags: morocco, fez, meknes, yaavetz

Title: Marriage of R. Yom Tov ben Yitzchak ibn Attar
Summary: R. Yom Tov, son of Yitzchak ibn Attar, was married on 13 Adar 5491 in Fez.
Story: On 13 Adar 5491 (~March 2, 1731), Yom Tov ben Yitzchak ibn Attar was married. The wedding was recorded in the Ya'abetz's marriage register in Fez. Yitzchak was a son of R. Yosef ibn Attar, brother of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar.
Tags: morocco, fez, ibn attar, marriage register

Title: Marriage of Dona bat Oved ibn Attar to Avraham
Summary: Dona, granddaughter of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar, married Avraham ben Chaim Shem Tov on 20 Elul 5491.
Story: On 20 Elul 5491 (~September 22, 1731), Dona bat Oved ibn Attar — a granddaughter of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar — was married to Avraham, son of Chaim Shem Tov ben Avraham ibn Attar. Like her aunt Shi'acha a generation earlier, Dona married within the extended ibn Attar family. The marriage was inscribed in the Ya'abetz's register.
Tags: morocco, fez, ibn attar, marriage register

Title: Wedding poem printed for R. Yitzchak Marini in Mantua
Summary: In 5492 (1732) R. Yeshayahu Bassan printed a praise-poem for the Mantua wedding of R. Yitzchak Marini and Yudita.
Story: The 5492 (1732) wedding of R. Yitzchak Marini and his bride Yudita in Mantua was honored with a printed poem of praise by R. Yeshayahu Bassan, author of Lechmei Todah. A companion sheet preserved in the library archive bears a poem by his son R. Yisrael Binyamin Bassan for the wedding of Ben-Tzion Ashkenazi and his bride Brachah.
Tags: mantua, italy, wedding, yeshayahu bassan, lechmei todah

Title: Death of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar of Fez
Summary: Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar, the head of Fez's rabbis known as 'Arbi Alkabir,' died in 5493 (1733).
Story: Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar passed away in the Hebrew year 5493 (1733), having served as the leading rabbinical authority of Fez and one of the most revered figures of Moroccan Jewry. Honored by Moroccan Jews as 'Arbi Alkabir' (Our Great Rabbi), he left behind a rich corpus of responsa and a network of correspondence with Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur of Meknes.
Tags: morocco, fez, yehuda ibn attar, sephardi

Title: Wandsbeck Haggadah printed by Yisrael ben Avraham
Summary: A small-format Haggadah was printed in Wandsbeck by Yisrael ben Avraham.
Story: In 5493 (1733), Yisrael ben Avraham produced a small-format Haggadah in Wandsbeck (Germany), bearing the Yiddish title noting this 'great mitzvah of telling'. The 24-leaf miniature edition included the Akdamut at its conclusion. It served the Yiddish-speaking Ashkenazic communities of Northern Germany.
Tags: haggadah, wandsbeck, germany, yiddish

Title: R. Moshe Yisrael prints Mishat Moshe in Constantinople
Summary: R. Moshe Yisrael printed the first two volumes of his responsa work Mishat Moshe in Constantinople.
Story: Between 1734 and 1735, R. Moshe Yisrael printed the first two parts of his responsa collection She'elot U'Teshuvot Mishat Moshe in Constantinople. The third volume was later printed posthumously by his son R. Avraham in 1742, and his sermons were collected and published as Apei Moshe in Livorno in 1828.
Tags: constantinople, responsa, moshe yisrael, mishat moshe

Title: Second marriage of R. Oved ibn Attar, son of Rabbi Yehuda
Summary: R. Oved ibn Attar, son of Rabbi Yehuda, took a second wife on 18 Av 5494 in Fez.
Story: On the night of Tuesday, 18 Av 5494 (~July 19, 1734), Rabbi Oved ibn Attar — son of the late Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar — was married for the second time. The wedding entry refers to Rabbi Yehuda with the honorific 'savah de-mishpatim' (elder of judgments) and as a 'hasid,' 'light of Israel,' indicating Rabbi Yehuda had already passed away (he died in 5493).
Tags: morocco, fez, ibn attar, marriage register

Title: Marriage of R. Yosef ben Yitzchak ibn Attar
Summary: R. Yosef, son of Yitzchak ibn Attar, was married on 8 Tishri 5495 in Fez.
Story: On 8 Tishri 5495 (~October 5, 1734), Yosef ben Yitzchak ibn Attar was married. The Ya'abetz's marriage register in Fez recorded the event. Like his brother Yom Tov who married three years earlier, Yosef was a grandnephew of the late Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar through Yehuda's brother Yosef.
Tags: morocco, fez, ibn attar, marriage register

Title: Florence prayer printed for Reggio plague
Summary: In 5495 (1735) a 'prayer for many illnesses' was printed at Shmuel Falasos's Florence press during a plague in Reggio.
Story: When a plague struck Reggio in northern Italy in 5495 (1735), a 'tefillah leribbui chalaim' was composed and printed at the Florence press of Shmuel Falasos to be recited during the outbreak.
Tags: florence, italy, reggio, plague, broadside, shmuel falasos

Title: Ketuba from Finale dated 5496
Summary: A ketuba from Finale, Italy, dated 5496 (1736) is among the library's manuscript holdings.
Story: The 1736 Finale ketuba represents the rich Italian-Jewish tradition of decorated marriage contracts displayed in the library's exhibition.
Tags: ketuba, finale, italy, manuscript

Title: R. Moshe Yisrael dies in Alexandria
Summary: R. Moshe Yisrael, former rabbi of Rhodes and Jerusalem emissary, died in Alexandria, Egypt.
Story: Around 1737 R. Moshe Yisrael moved from Rhodes to Alexandria, Egypt, and died there in 1740. His third responsa volume was printed posthumously by his son R. Avraham in Constantinople in 1742, while his collected sermons appeared as Apei Moshe in Livorno in 1828.
Tags: alexandria, egypt, moshe yisrael, death

Title: Kalligrapher Chaim ben Asher Anshil begins illuminated Haggadah work in Kitzee
Summary: The famed calligrapher Chaim ben Asher Anshil began producing illuminated Haggadot and prayer books in Kitzee near Pressburg in 5501.
Story: Between 5501 and 5542 (1741–1782), Chaim ben Asher Anshil worked as a calligrapher and illustrator in Kitzee, near Pressburg. During this period he wrote and decorated Haggadot, Birkat HaMazon booklets, and prayer texts that became prized manuscripts.
Tags: manuscript, kitzee, pressburg, calligraphy

Title: Death of Rabbi Reuven ibn Tzur, son of the Yaavetz, in Salé
Summary: Rabbi Reuven ibn Tzur, son of the Yaavetz, died around age 25 on 3 Av 5502 during Chol HaMoed in Salé.
Story: On 3 Av 5502 (summer 1742), Rabbi Reuven ibn Tzur — son of the Yaavetz and a young scholar of about twenty-five — passed away in Salé during Chol HaMoed. Rabbi Eliyahu Tzarfati delivered a eulogy for him on 21 Av, preserved in the work 'Na'ar Bocheh.' He was buried in Alcazar (Ksar), and his death left Rabbi Refael Oved as the Yaavetz's only surviving son.

Title: Birth of Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, the Alter Rebbe
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, founder of Chabad chasidut, was born.
Story: The Alter Rebbe established the Chabad school of chasidic thought, emphasizing intellectual engagement with mystical concepts. His magnum opus, the Tanya, became the foundational text of the movement.

Title: Schneur Zalman of Liadi born
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, founder of Chabad Chasidism, is born.
Story: He went on to author the Tanya and institute the maamad tradition of Chasidim supporting the Rebbe's court — a tradition stretched thin during the Rayatz's Riga years when Soviet Chasidim could no longer contribute.

Title: Baal Shem Tov ascends to heaven on Rosh HaShanah and meets Messiah
Summary: On Rosh HaShanah 1746 the Baal Shem Tov's soul ascends and the Messiah tells him to disseminate his teachings publicly.
Story: According to the historic letter the Baal Shem Tov sent to his brother, using kabbalistic secrets his soul rose to heaven. He asked the Messiah, 'When will you come?' The answer: 'In the time when your teachings will become public and revealed in the world.' This principle later anchored the Chabad mission of spreading chasidic teachings to the world.

Title: Baal Shem Tov's soul ascends to Mashiach
Summary: Per his famous letter, the founder of Chasidism's soul ascended on high and encountered the Messiah.
Story: Rabbi Yisrael Baal Shem Tov wrote to his brother-in-law about a mystical ascent in which he asked the Messiah when he would come. The Messiah replied, 'When your wellsprings will spread to the outside' — a phrase that would later guide the Rebbe Rayatz's vision for spreading chasidic teachings to America.

Title: Baal Shem Tov's soul ascent on Rosh Hashanah
Summary: Rabbi Yisrael Baal Shem Tov experiences a mystical ascent and receives the Messiah's instruction to spread chasidic teachings.
Story: Asked when he would come, the Messiah replied, 'In the time when your teachings will become public and revealed in the world.' This vision became the foundational principle of Chabad's mission of disseminating Chasidut, which the Rayatz expanded in Riga.

Title: R' Baruch, father of the Alter Rebbe, joins Liozna Chevra Kadisha
Summary: R' Baruch ben R' Avraham was accepted into the Liozna burial society on 15 Kislev 5507.
Story: The Liozna communal register records that on 15 Kislev 5507 (December 8, 1746), 'the Torah scholar Moreinu Baruch ben Moreinu Avraham was accepted into the Chevra Kadisha.' This entry is one of the earliest documentary anchors for the Alter Rebbe's father and identifies his own father's name as Avraham, contradicting other traditions that named him Shneur Zalman.

Title: Birth of MaharI"L of Yanovich, brother of the Alter Rebbe
Summary: R' Yehuda Leib of Yanovich, younger brother of the Alter Rebbe, was born approximately in 5509.
Story: MaharI"L of Yanovich, author of Shearit Yehuda and constant collaborator of his brother the Alter Rebbe, was born around 5509 (~1749). He would become the household manager of the Alter Rebbe's affairs, the chief transcriber of his discourses (later printed in Torah Or), and editor of his Shulchan Aruch.
Tags: mahari"l, yanovich, alter rebbe, family

Title: Young Shneur Zalman accepted into Liozna Chevra Kadisha
Summary: The child Shneur Zalman ben R' Baruch was inducted into the Liozna burial society on 15 Kislev 5510.
Story: The Liozna ledger records that on 15 Kislev 5510 (December 5, 1749), 'the boy Shneur Zalman ben Moreinu Baruch was accepted into the Chevra Kadisha,' with his grandfather obligated to make annual donations on his behalf. This entry is a key biographical anchor for the future Alter Rebbe's earliest years in Liozna.

Title: First Haggadah printed in Zhovkva
Summary: The first Haggadah was printed in Zhovkva (Galicia) in 5510, bound with the commentary Shimon v'Levi.
Story: In 5510 (1750), the first Haggadah of Zhovkva was printed together with the commentary Sefer Shimon v'Levi by Shimon ben Kadish HaLevi. It marked the beginning of Haggadah printing in this important Galician printing center.
Tags: haggadah, zhovkva, galicia

Title: Florence printing of Orchot Chaim
Summary: The first edition of Orchot Chaim by Rabbi Aharon HaKohen of Lunel was printed in Florence in 5510.
Story: About two hundred years after the second edition of Orchot Chaim was completed in Majorca, the first printed edition of part one appeared in Florence in 5510 (1750), using the earlier mahadura kama text. Efforts by Maharam Padua to print the later edition had not succeeded.
Tags: florence, orchot chaim, aharon hakohen of lunel

Title: Illustrated Abarbanel Haggadah with Yiddish translation printed in Fürth
Summary: An illustrated Abarbanel Haggadah with Yiddish liturgical translations was printed in Fürth.
Story: Around 5510 (1750), an ornate folio Haggadah was printed in Fürth (Furth, Bavaria) containing the commentary of Don Isaac Abarbanel together with a Kabbalistic commentary. Yiddish translations of the liturgical poems appeared in Tzene-Rene script, and illustrations were placed below the Hebrew text and commentaries. The 16-leaf folio also exists in a variant dated 1757.

Title: Passing of Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur (the Yaavetz) in Fez
Summary: The Yaavetz passed away on the eve of Shabbat, 2 Tevet 5513, five months shy of his eightieth birthday, and was buried 3 Tevet.
Story: Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur — the Yaavetz, author of Mishpat u'Tzedakah B'Yaakov and one of Morocco's foremost halachic authorities — passed away on the night of Shabbat, 2 Tevet 5513 (December 1752) in Fez, just under five months before what would have been his eightieth birthday. He was buried on Sunday, 3 Tevet. His marriage-records pinkas, in continuous use since 5466, passed to his descendants who maintained it until 5617.
Tags: morocco, fez, yaavetz, yaakov-ibn-tzur

Title: Marriage of R. Yehuda ben Oved ibn Attar, grandson of Rabbi Yehuda
Summary: R. Yehuda ben Oved, grandson and namesake of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar, was married on 24 Cheshvan 5516.
Story: On Wednesday, 24 Cheshvan 5516 (~November 8, 1755), Yehuda ben Oved ibn Attar was married. He was a grandson and namesake of the renowned Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar of Fez, who had died over two decades earlier. The marriage was recorded in the Ya'abetz's register, which referred to his late grandfather as 'the great rabbi, the wondrous of the Sanhedrin, elder of judgments.'
Tags: morocco, fez, ibn attar, marriage register

Title: Alter Rebbe urges refugees to farm
Summary: At age eleven, Rabbi Schneur Zalman urged Prague refugees in Russia to become farmers for stable livelihood.
Story: In 1756, at the age of eleven, the future Alter Rebbe, Rabbi Schneur Zalman, urged refugees arriving in Russia from Prague to become farmers as a means of earning a stable livelihood. This early act of communal service initiated the 140-year tradition of communal work by the Lubavitcher Rebbes that the Rashab would later recount to his son at the Ohel. The episode established a lifelong pattern of practical leadership concerned with Jewish material welfare.
Tags: russia, alter rebbe, schneur zalman, prague, refugees, farming, communal work

Title: Kitzee illuminated Haggadah manuscript completed
Summary: Chaim ben Asher Anshil completed the famous illuminated Kitzee Haggadah manuscript on parchment in 5520.
Story: In 5520 (1760), the calligrapher Chaim ben Asher Anshil of Kitzee, near Pressburg, completed his ornate manuscript Haggadah on parchment. Twenty-two leaves of square Hebrew text and Yiddish ritual instructions in tzena u'rena script were enhanced with elaborate illustrations.

Title: Passing of the Baal Shem Tov
Summary: The Baal Shem Tov passed away in 1760.
Story: His passing left the leadership of the chasidic movement to his closest disciple, the Maggid of Mezeritch. The Baal Shem Tov's brief revolution had set in motion a generations-long spiritual transformation of Eastern European Jewry.
Tags: baal shem tov, besht

Title: Passing of the Baal Shem Tov in Medzhibuzh
Summary: The Baal Shem Tov passed away in Medzhibuzh in 5520.
Story: Rabbi Israel Baal Shem Tov, founder of chassidut, passed away in Medzhibuzh in 5520 (1760). His yahrzeit falls on Shavuot. Throughout his lifetime (5494–5520), not a single chassidic book was printed.
Tags: baal shem tov, medzhibuzh, shavuot

Title: Baal Shem Tov passes away on Shavuot
Summary: The Baal Shem Tov, founder of Chassidism, passed away on Shavuot 5520.
Story: Rabbi Israel Baal Shem Tov founded the Chassidic movement and gathered a circle of disciples who carried his teachings forward. He passed away on Shavuot 5520 (1760). Over the next two generations his students collected the stories about him, eventually published as Shivchei HaBaal Shem Tov.
Tags: baal shem tov, yahrzeit, shavuot, ukraine

Title: Birth of Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler
Summary: Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler was born in Posval in 5524.
Story: Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler, future av beit din of Vilna, was born in Posval in 5524 (1764). He came from a family that had served in the Posval rabbinate for generations, including his grandfather, father, and brother.
Tags: posval, posveler, vilna

Title: Alter Rebbe arrives at the Maggid of Mezeritch around age 20
Summary: Around the age of 20, R. Schneur Zalman traveled from Vitebsk to study Kabbalah and chassidut under the Maggid of Mezeritch.
Story: After exhausting available sources of knowledge in revealed Torah, the future Alter Rebbe sought a teacher of inner Torah. Around age twenty he left his father-in-law's home in Vitebsk to study under the Maggid, where he found 'rest for his soul' and was eventually entrusted with composing a new Shulchan Aruch.
Tags: alter rebbe, maggid of mezeritch, vitebsk, mezeritch, first journey

Title: Maggid of Mezeritch grants approbation to 'Halakhah Pesukah' (Turka)
Summary: The Maggid of Mezeritch issued his only known approbation, for the halachic work 'Halakhah Pesukah' printed in Turka.
Story: The Maggid, who normally declined to give approbations, made an exception for 'Halakhah Pesukah' because of its value in clarifying practical halachic rulings. The approbation testifies to his deep concern for clear and accessible psak halacha among his circle and is the only such endorsement of his preserved to us.
Tags: maggid of mezeritch, halakhah pesukah, turka, approbation, halacha

Title: Maggid of Mezeritch issues approbation for Halacha Pesuka
Summary: Rabbi Dov Ber of Mezeritch granted his only known approbation, for the work Halacha Pesuka printed in Turka.
Story: The 1765 Turka edition of Halacha Pesuka carries what is regarded as the sole approbation ever issued by the Maggid of Mezeritch. It survives as a rare textual witness to the Maggid's personal endorsements during the early diffusion of Chassidism.
Tags: maggid of mezeritch, approbation, turka, halacha pesuka

Title: Tzli Esh Haggadah by Yehuda Aryeh of Modena printed in Amsterdam
Summary: The illustrated 'Tzli Esh' Haggadah by Yehuda Aryeh of Modena, with full Yiddish translation, was printed in Amsterdam.
Story: In 5525 (1765), an illustrated Haggadah was printed in Amsterdam featuring the 'Tzli Esh' commentary by Yehuda Aryeh of Modena, an abridgment of his earlier work 'Zevach Pesach'. The 32-leaf quarto edition included a complete Yiddish translation of the Haggadah in Tzene-Rene script. The work became a popular Amsterdam edition of the Italian-influenced Haggadah tradition.
Tags: haggadah, amsterdam, yehuda aryeh modena, tzli esh

Title: Bet Chorin Haggadah with commentaries printed in Metz
Summary: The 'Bet Chorin' Haggadah, with Alshich, Gevurot Hashem, and Olelot Efraim commentaries, was printed in Metz.
Story: In 5527 (1767), the 'Bet Chorin' Haggadah was issued in Metz, France, with commentaries by Moshe ben Chaim Alshich, the Maharal's 'Gevurot Hashem', and 'Olelot Efraim'. The 30-leaf quarto edition included beautiful illustrations and concluded with a map of the Land of Israel in vernacular language. It exemplified the French-printed Haggadah tradition of the late 18th century.
Tags: haggadah, metz, france, alshich, maharal, illustrated

Title: Earliest reported Alter Rebbe maamarim
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz transmitted that the Alter Rebbe delivered certain maamarim as early as 5528 (1768).
Story: These earliest discourses may have been brief teachings or repetitions of the Maggid's Torah. No fixed practice of writing down discourses existed yet, which is why none of them reached us in dated manuscript form. A regular practice of delivering discourses appears to have begun around 1783 with his settling in Liozna.
Tags: alter rebbe, maggid of mezeritch, early teachings

Title: Death of Rabbi Refael Oved ibn Tzur, son of the Yaavetz
Summary: Rabbi Refael Oved ibn Tzur, the Yaavetz's son and successor, died on Friday, 19 Iyar 5529.
Story: On Friday afternoon, 19 Iyar 5529 (May 1769), Rabbi Refael Oved ibn Tzur passed away in Fez. He had inherited his father's rabbinic mantle, served as a senior dayan, and continued the family's marriage-registration practice. His own son Rabbi Shlomo Shmuel ibn Tzur recorded the entry in the family pinkas, citing his grandfather the Yaavetz's note that Refael Oved had been born on 3 Shevat 5466.

Title: Alter Rebbe begins composing the Shulchan Aruch HaRav
Summary: After being pressed repeatedly by the Maggid of Mezeritch, the young Alter Rebbe began work on his Shulchan Aruch after the year 1770.
Story: The Maggid searched among his disciples for one who could compose a clear, reasoned compendium of halachic rulings and chose the young Schneur Zalman, refusing to relent until he agreed. Composition of the Shulchan Aruch HaRav began after 5530, becoming the authoritative halachic work of Chabad.
Tags: alter rebbe, shulchan aruch harav, maggid of mezeritch, halacha

Title: Alter Rebbe begins composing the Shulchan Aruch under the Maggid
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi began drafting his Shulchan Aruch while studying under the Maggid of Mezeritch around 1770.
Story: According to the preface written by his sons, the Alter Rebbe began the Shulchan Aruch while "sitting under the wing of Tachkemoni" with the Maggid in Mezeritch, around 5530 (1770). He started with Orach Chaim, completing that section within about two years, and continued reworking the code for over forty years.
Tags: alter rebbe, maggid of mezeritch, shulchan aruch, mezeritch

Title: Brothers R. Shmelke and R. Pinchas Horowitz praise Alter Rebbe's halachic writings
Summary: While studying together at the Maggid's court, R. Shmelke and R. Pinchas Horowitz reviewed and praised the Alter Rebbe's nascent halachic writings.
Story: The 'two golden pipes' — the brothers Horowitz — joined the Maggid's circle and examined two halachic works the young Alter Rebbe had composed. They praised him highly and urged him to 'be strong and complete the work,' showing that halachic study was part of the curriculum at Mezeritch alongside chassidic teaching.
Tags: maggid of mezeritch, shmelke of nikolsburg, pinchas of frankfurt, alter rebbe, halacha

Title: Alter Rebbe begins editing Hilchos Tzitzis and Pesach at the Maggid's court
Summary: In summer 5531 (1771) the Alter Rebbe completed the first drafts of Hilchos Tzitzis and Hilchos Pesach for his Shulchan Aruch while residing at the Maggid of Mezritch's court.
Story: Selected by the Maggid of Mezritch from among his disciples to compose a new Shulchan Aruch with clear halachic rulings and their reasoning, the young Alter Rebbe began the project with Hilchos Tzitzis and Hilchos Pesach. According to the introduction by his sons, both sections were begun and finished while he sat at the Maggid's court. This marked the start of what would become a multi-decade halachic project.
Tags: alter rebbe, shulchan aruch, halacha, tzitzis, pesach, maggid of mezritch, mezritch

Title: R. Shmelka and R. Pinchas Horowitz visit the Maggid in Rovno and praise Alter Rebbe's work
Summary: Before traveling to take up their rabbinates in Germany, the brothers R. Shmelka and R. Pinchas Horowitz visited the Maggid in Rovno, where they reviewed and lavishly praised the Alter Rebbe's draft of Hilchos Tzitzis and Pesach.
Story: After being chosen as rabbis of Nikolsburg and Frankfurt-am-Main respectively, the two brothers came to take counsel from the Maggid before assuming their posts. At his court they saw the Alter Rebbe's draft of the Shulchan Aruch and praised it greatly, telling him to be strong and complete the work. The Alter Rebbe later recalled this meeting in his correspondence with R. Pinchas, the Baal Haflaah.
Tags: pinchas horowitz, shmelka horowitz, maggid of mezritch, rovno, shulchan aruch, alter rebbe

Title: Alter Rebbe meets R. Pinchas of the Hafla'ah at Rovno
Summary: By Tishrei 1771 the Maggid had relocated to Rovno, where the Alter Rebbe encountered R. Pinchas Horowitz, author of the Hafla'ah.
Story: The Alter Rebbe's later letter recalls a 'beloved acquaintance from days past in Mezeritch and Rovno' with R. Pinchas Horowitz. Since R. Pinchas left for the Frankfurt rabbinate by Tishrei 1771, the meeting at Rovno must have occurred no later than that date — establishing that the Maggid had already moved from Mezeritch to Rovno by then.
Tags: alter rebbe, baal hafla'ah, rovno, mezeritch

Title: R. Pinchas Horowitz stays in Brod en route to the Frankfurt rabbinate
Summary: On 15 Cheshvan 5532 R. Pinchas Horowitz, the Baal Haflaah, was in Brod en route to assume the rabbinate of Frankfurt-am-Main, where he wrote a haskamah for Sefer Totza'os Chaim.
Story: Traveling from Volhynia to Germany after taking leave of the Maggid, R. Pinchas Horowitz stopped in Brod for Shabbos. His approbation for the Zolkva 5532 edition of Totza'os Chaim was dated there on Wednesday 15 Cheshvan 5532, fixing the timing of his journey precisely. From Brod he continued westward toward Frankfurt.
Tags: pinchas horowitz, brod, frankfurt, haflaah

Title: Alter Rebbe and R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk fail to meet the Vilna Gaon
Summary: During the winter of 5532 the Alter Rebbe and R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk traveled to Vilna to meet the Vilna Gaon, but the Gaon refused to receive them and left the city.
Story: Hoping to defuse the opposition to chassidus by direct dialogue, the two leaders came to the Gaon's home but the door was closed against them twice. When they pressed further the Gaon departed Vilna entirely, staying away until they left. The Alter Rebbe recounted the failed attempt in his Iggeres 34.
Tags: alter rebbe, menachem mendel of vitebsk, vilna gaon, vilna, mitnagdim, lithuania

Title: Alter Rebbe and Rabbi Levi Yitzchak study with the Maggid in Ravna
Summary: In summer 5532, Rabbi Schneur Zalman and Rabbi Levi Yitzchak study halacha together at the Maggid of Mezeritch's court in Ravna, where the Maggid rules leniently on a kashrut question.
Story: In the summer of 5532, the Alter Rebbe and Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev studied together at the Maggid of Mezeritch's home in Ravna. A halachic question about sirchot in the lung was brought before the Maggid, who ruled leniently and proved it from the Talmud. Nearly four decades later, when rabbis challenged Rabbi Levi Yitzchak's late ruling on the same question, the Alter Rebbe defended it by citing this very session with their teacher.

Title: Alter Rebbe disputes with mitnagdim in Shklov
Summary: Following the failed Vilna visit in winter 5532, the Alter Rebbe and R. Avraham of Kalisk went to Shklov to debate the mitnagdim there, but the local opponents reneged on their promise of safe debate and resorted to force.
Story: After leaving Vilna the two chassidic leaders attempted a public disputation in Shklov. The local mitnagdim initially agreed to a peaceful debate but, unable to refute the chassidic arguments, broke their word and acted aggressively. The Alter Rebbe described the events in Iggeres 34 and Iggeres 51.
Tags: alter rebbe, avraham of kalisk, shklov, mitnagdim, belarus

Title: Alter Rebbe studies halacha with the Maggid in Rovno
Summary: In the summer of 5532, Rabbi Shneur Zalman discussed a halachic pilpul with the Maggid in Rovno.
Story: In his own writing the Alter Rebbe records that during summer 5532 (1772) he was in the home of the Maggid of Mezeritch in Rovno. They discussed a halachic question concerning shechita, and the Maggid concurred with his ruling. The episode reflects the close halachic training he received.
Tags: alter rebbe, maggid of mezeritch, rovno, halacha

Title: Alter Rebbe travels to Mezeritch to study Kabbalah
Summary: At about age 20, Rabbi Shneur Zalman left Vitebsk for Mezeritch to study Kabbalah under the Maggid.
Story: The young Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi, then about twenty years old, traveled from Vitebsk to Mezeritch to learn the foundations of Chassidic teachings and conduct. As he later wrote in his own hand, he began studying Kabbalah there under Rabbi Dov Ber. He also studied halacha with the Maggid during this period.
Tags: alter rebbe, maggid of mezeritch, vitebsk, mezeritch

Title: Alter Rebbe travels to the Maggid in Rovno in summer 5532
Summary: In summer 5532 (1772) the Alter Rebbe traveled with R. Avraham of Kalisk to the Maggid of Mezritch in Rovno, where he continued editing his Shulchan Aruch and discussed halachic questions with the Maggid.
Story: After the Vilna and Shklov debates, the two leaders went up to their teacher in Rovno. The Alter Rebbe remained with the Maggid in Rovno, and later in Anipoli, until the Maggid's passing. He continued working on Hilchos Orach Chaim during this period and presented halachic novellae to the Maggid for approval.
Tags: alter rebbe, maggid of mezritch, rovno, avraham of kalisk

Title: Lubavitch area joins the Russian Empire with the First Partition of Poland
Summary: In the summer of 5532 (1772), with the First Partition of Poland, the Lubavitch region was annexed to the Russian Empire.
Story: The First Partition of Poland in 1772 absorbed huge swaths of formerly Polish-Lithuanian territory into Russia. Lubavitch, sitting on the border, became Russian. The town would remain near the Russia-Belarus border under tsarist rule for the next century and a half.
Tags: poland, russia, partition, empire, lubavitch

Title: Passing of Rabbi Dovber, the Maggid of Mezeritch
Summary: The Maggid of Mezeritch, successor to the Baal Shem Tov, passed away in 1772.
Story: Under the Maggid's leadership, chasidism spread across Eastern Europe through a circle of brilliant disciples. Among them was Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, who would go on to found the Chabad branch of chasidism.
Tags: maggid of mezeritch, dovber, chasidism

Title: Passing of the Maggid of Mezritch
Summary: Rabbi Dov Ber, the Maggid of Mezritch, passed away in Anipoli in 5533.
Story: Rabbi Dov Ber, the Maggid of Mezritch, successor to the Baal Shem Tov and teacher of the leading chassidic figures of the next generation, passed away in Anipoli in 5533 (1772–73).
Tags: maggid of mezritch, anipoli

Title: R' Shlomo of Karlin becomes rabbi of Karlin
Summary: R' Shlomo of Karlin took up the rabbinate of Karlin around 5532.
Story: The historical record establishes that R' Shlomo HaKohen of Karlin served as rabbi of Karlin starting in 5532 (1772) and continued there until shortly before 5544. He was a leading disciple of the Maggid of Mezritch and later a major chassidic leader in Lithuania.
Tags: r' shlomo of karlin, karlin, rabbinate

Title: Summer 1772: 'Zemir Aritzim v'Charvot Tzurim' published in Brody
Summary: Mitnagdim in Vilna sent material to Brody where the polemical 'Zemir Aritzim v'Charvot Tzurim' against the chassidim was printed in late summer 1772.
Story: Following the Shklov debate, the sages of Shklov wrote to the Vilna Gaon, who in turn coordinated with Brody. The resulting pamphlet attacked chassidic practices — including the upside-down acrobatics ('koliyen zich') of R. Avraham of Kalisk's circle — and triggered widespread persecution of the tzaddikim of Volyn.
Tags: zemir aritzim, brody, mitnagdim, polemic, vilna

Title: Summer 1772: Alter Rebbe's halachic deliberation with the Maggid in Rovno
Summary: In summer 1772 at Rovno the Alter Rebbe debated with the Maggid the laws of sirkhot, with the Maggid ruling it sufficed to remove the protruding adhesion.
Story: The Alter Rebbe's responsum on the leniency of R. Levi Yitzchok of Berditchev in checking lungs records this earlier discussion at Rovno. The Maggid demonstrated from the Talmud that residual filaments on the lung are not themselves a sirkha, illustrating how halacha was taught alongside chassidut in Mezeritch/Rovno.
Tags: alter rebbe, maggid of mezeritch, rovno, sirkhot, halacha, shechita

Title: Summer 1772: Volyn tzaddikim convene at Rovno around the Maggid
