Summary: Driven from their homes by the campaign against chassidim, the tzaddikim of Volyn gathered in Rovno around the Maggid of Mezeritch to take counsel.
Story: The Alter Rebbe and R. Avraham of Kalisk arrived together; R. Avraham, fearful of the Maggid's reproach, waited at the outskirts while R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk interceded on his behalf. Only then did the Alter Rebbe bring him into the Maggid's chamber. The gathering attempted to coordinate the chassidic response to the herem.
Tags: maggid of mezeritch, rovno, volyn, alter rebbe, menachem mendel of vitebsk, avraham of kalisk

Title: Winter 1772: Alter Rebbe and R. Menachem Mendel attempt debate with Vilna Gaon
Summary: During the winter of 1772 the Alter Rebbe and R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk traveled to Vilna seeking a debate with the Vilna Gaon, who refused to meet them.
Story: Hoping to refute the slanders being told to the Vilna Gaon and forestall a herem against chassidim, the two emissaries went to his home twice and were turned away each time. When city leaders pressed the Gaon to debate, he left the city and only returned after they had departed.
Tags: vilna gaon, alter rebbe, menachem mendel of vitebsk, vilna, mitnagdim

Title: Winter 1772: Shklov debate between Alter Rebbe and R. Avraham of Kalisk
Summary: After the failed Vilna mission, the Alter Rebbe and R. Avraham of Kalisk traveled to Shklov for a public debate with mitnagdim, which ended badly for the chassidim.
Story: The mitnagdim of Shklov broke prior assurances and confronted the chassidic leaders with force. Unable to answer the chassidic arguments, they appealed back to the Vilna Gaon, who then leaned toward declaring chassidim as 'moridin' — kindling the wider campaign against the movement.
Tags: alter rebbe, avraham of kalisk, shklov, mitnagdim, belarus

Title: R. Pinchas Horowitz arrives in Frankfurt-am-Main to take his rabbinical seat
Summary: According to the Frankfurt community register, R. Pinchas Horowitz arrived in Frankfurt-am-Main on 26 Tevet 5532 to begin his tenure as rabbi.
Story: After being elected by the Frankfurt community in spring 1771 and traveling via Brod, the Baal Haflaah's journey from Volhynia stretched from Cheshvan to Tevet of 5532. Frankfurt's communal records date his arrival to 26 Tevet 5532. He would serve as Frankfurt's rabbi for more than thirty-three years until his passing in 5565.
Tags: pinchas horowitz, frankfurt, haflaah, germany

Title: Maggid of Mezeritch delivers final Sukkot teaching
Summary: The Maggid of Mezeritch gave his last recorded Sukkot teaching in Tishrei 5533 (autumn 1772), preserved through the Alter Rebbe.
Story: A maamar of the Alter Rebbe from 1812 cites a teaching he heard from the Maggid 'on the last Sukkot, 5533.' It is one of the latest surviving teachings of the Maggid before his passing two months later.
Tags: maggid of mezeritch, sukkot, torah, alter rebbe

Title: Maggid of Mezeritch passes away on 19 Kislev
Summary: Rabbi Dov Ber, the Maggid of Mezeritch, passed away on 19 Kislev 5533.
Story: The Maggid of Mezeritch led the Chassidic movement after the Baal Shem Tov's passing. He died on 19 Kislev 5533 (1772). Over the next eight years his students compiled his teachings into Maggid Devarav L'Yaakov, first printed in Koretz in 1781.
Tags: maggid of mezeritch, yahrzeit, 19 kislev

Title: Passing of the Maggid of Mezeritch
Summary: Rabbi Dovber, the Maggid of Mezeritch, passes away on 19 Kislev 5533, after which his disciples return to Russia to spread Chassidism.
Story: On 19 Kislev 5533, the Maggid of Mezeritch—chief disciple of the Baal Shem Tov—passed away. His three Russian-Lithuanian disciples, Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk, and Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, returned to Russia to spread Chassidic teaching. Decades later, this date acquired additional weight when the Alter Rebbe was released from Tsarist imprisonment on the same day in 1798.
Tags: dov ber of mezeritch, yahrzeit, yud-tes kislev, mezeritch

Title: Passing of the Maggid of Mezeritch in Anipoli
Summary: Rabbi Dov Ber, the Maggid of Mezeritch, passed away on 19 Kislev 5533 in Anipoli, with the Alter Rebbe present at his passing.
Story: After moving from Rovno to Anipoli, the Maggid passed on 19 Kislev. The Alter Rebbe is recorded as having been present, and the lot fell on him to perform the taharah and burial. The date later took on iconic significance in Chabad after the Alter Rebbe's release from imprisonment on the same date in 1798.
Tags: maggid of mezeritch, anipoli, 19 kislev, yahrtzeit, alter rebbe

Title: Passing of the Maggid of Mezritch
Summary: The Maggid of Mezritch, R. Dov Ber, passed away on 19 Kislev 5533 in Anipoli.
Story: R. Dov Ber, successor to the Baal Shem Tov and teacher of the founders of the major chassidic dynasties including the Alter Rebbe, passed away on 19 Kislev 5533. His passing marked the close of the period during which the Alter Rebbe consulted him on the editing of the Shulchan Aruch. Decades later 19 Kislev would also become the date of the Alter Rebbe's own redemption from imprisonment.
Tags: maggid of mezritch, dov ber, anipoli, yahrzeit

Title: Alter Rebbe begins composing Shulchan Aruch with the Maggid
Summary: By 5533 (1773), the Alter Rebbe had completed Hilchos Tzitzis and Hilchos Pesach of his Shulchan Aruch under the Maggid's encouragement.
Story: The Maggid of Mezeritch repeatedly urged the young Shneur Zalman to compile a Shulchan Aruch. The project began during Shabbos Tachkemoni at the Maggid's court, where he completed the laws of Tzitzis and Pesach. The complete work would not be printed until decades after his passing.
Tags: shulchan aruch harav, alter rebbe, maggid of mezeritch, mezeritch

Title: Birth of Rabbi Dov Ber, the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: Rabbi Dov Ber, second Lubavitcher Rebbe, was born.
Story: The Mitteler Rebbe succeeded his father as the second Lubavitcher Rebbe and was known for prolific chasidic discourses. He moved the movement's center to Lubavitch, the town that gave Chabad its alternate name.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, dov ber

Title: Initial editing of Shulchan Aruch Orach Chaim concludes
Summary: Around the time of the Maggid's passing in late 5533, the Alter Rebbe completed the first round of editing of his Shulchan Aruch on Orach Chaim.
Story: According to his sons' introduction, the foundational editing of Orach Chaim took roughly two years. Beginning in summer 5531 with Tzitzis and Pesach, the Alter Rebbe continued through Vilna, Shklov, Rovno and Anipoli, completing the section in proximity to the Maggid's histalkus on 19 Kislev 5533. He continued to revise and add to the work in the following years until about 5537.
Tags: alter rebbe, shulchan aruch, orach chaim, halacha

Title: Aliyah of R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: In 1777 R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk led a group of chassidim in aliyah to the Land of Israel, settling first in the north.
Story: Following years of persecution and the mounting conflict with the mitnagdim, R. Menachem Mendel emigrated with a chassidic group to Eretz Yisrael, eventually settling in Tzfat. He would continue to guide the Russian chassidic community by letter from there.
Tags: menachem mendel of vitebsk, eretz yisrael, aliyah, tzfat, chassidim

Title: Aliyah of Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk; Alter Rebbe turns back at Mohilev
Summary: In summer 5537, Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk lead a group of Chassidim on aliyah; the Alter Rebbe accompanies them as far as Mohilev on the Dniester before being persuaded to return.
Story: In summer 5537, Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk led an aliyah of Chassidic disciples to Eretz Yisrael. The Alter Rebbe joined them as far as Mohilev in Podolia, where Chassidim and his fellow rebbes pleaded with him to remain in Russia to oversee their spiritual and material welfare. He stayed in Mohilev about a year and a half before returning to Vitebsk in 5539.
Tags: menachem mendel of vitebsk, avraham of kalisk, schneur zalman, aliyah, eretz yisrael, mohilev, podolia

Title: Alter Rebbe accompanies aliyah group as far as Mohilov on the Dniester
Summary: In 5537 the Alter Rebbe joined R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk's group setting out to settle in the Land of Israel, traveling with them as far as Mohilov on the Dniester.
Story: Reaching Mohilov in Podolia near the Turkish border, the leaders agreed that the Alter Rebbe should not continue but remain in Russia to care for the spiritual and material needs of the chassidim. R. Mendel and his colleagues parted from him with great weeping. The Alter Rebbe remained in Mohilov for about a year and a half, where he completed his sixteenth review of the entire Talmud, standing day and night.
Tags: alter rebbe, menachem mendel of vitebsk, mohilov, dniester, podolia, aliyah, eretz yisrael

Title: Beginning of Chabad settlement in the Holy Land
Summary: Chabad aliyah to Eretz Yisrael begins in 5537.
Story: The Chabad presence in the Land of Israel traces to 5537 (1777), when the first Chassidic settlers arrived. This year became the starting point used in the companion volume 'Toldot Chabad B'Eretz HaKodesh,' which covers the history of the movement in the Holy Land through 5710.
Tags: eretz yisrael, aliyah, settlement

Title: Chassidic aliyah to Eretz Yisrael led by R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk
Summary: R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and his group ascended to Eretz Yisrael in the summer, joined initially by the Alter Rebbe who turned back at Mohilov.
Story: In the summer of 5537 (1777), R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk led a major group of Chassidim to settle in Eretz Yisrael. The Alter Rebbe accompanied them as far as Mohilov in Podolia, where the Chassidim pressed him to remain in Russia to lead their community. The parting was marked by great weeping, and the Alter Rebbe returned to Russia while the group continued on.
Tags: aliyah, eretz yisrael, tzfat, menachem mendel of vitebsk, alter rebbe, chassidim

Title: Chassidic caravan ship sinks in Black Sea; some 30 of 80 survive
Summary: One of the chassidic caravan's ships sank in the Black Sea; about 30 of 80 Jewish passengers survived.
Story: On the journey from Mohilov to Constantinople in 1777, a severe storm sank one of the caravan's ships near Crimea. About 80 Jews were aboard; only some 30 survived, landing destitute in Gozlov (Eupatoria). With help from Jews of Krasov and Keilah and the Karaite community of Kafa, some survivors made their way back to Russia while others continued on to Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: aliyah, shipwreck, black sea, crimea, kafa, karaite

Title: First chasidic aliyah led by Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk led the first chasidic immigration to Eretz Yisrael, founding settlements in Tiberias and Safed.
Story: His protege Rabbi Schneur Zalman, the future founder of Chabad, escorted him until Mogilev-Podolski in southern Ukraine and considered continuing on himself, but his mentor instructed him to remain in Europe to spread chasidic teachings. This aliyah established a chasidic presence in the Holy Land that endured for generations.
Tags: aliyah, tiberias, safed, menachem-mendel-vitebsk

Title: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk's aliyah to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and his group ascended to Eretz Yisrael, with primary financial support coming from the Hasidim of White Russia and Lithuania.
Story: In 5537 (1777), R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and R' Avraham of Kalisk led a group of Hasidim from White Russia and Lithuania to settle in Eretz Yisrael. The main flow of financial support came from those regions, though some assistance also arrived from Volhynia and Poland. This aliyah marked the foundation of the Hasidic Yishuv whose support eventually became the responsibility of the Alter Rebbe.
Tags: aliyah, tiberias, menachem mendel of vitebsk, avraham of kalisk, white russia, lithuania

Title: R. Israel of Polotzk sent as shadar to raise funds in the Diaspora
Summary: Soon after arriving in Eretz Yisrael, R. Israel of Polotzk was dispatched as an emissary to organize fundraising for the impoverished new community.
Story: Within weeks of the group's arrival in Tzfat, the dire poverty of the settlers and the many poor who had attached themselves to the aliyah forced R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk to send R. Israel of Polotzk back to the Diaspora as a shadar. In a letter, R. Menachem Mendel wrote that if they received 10,000 monthly it still would not suffice. R. Israel left Eretz Yisrael in Marcheshvan 5538 and traveled through Constantinople to raise funds for the new chassidic settlement.
Tags: shadar, fundraising, israel of polotzk, constantinople, maamadot, eretz yisrael fund

Title: Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk leads chassidim to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: In 5537, Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk led a group of chassidim on aliyah to Eretz Yisrael.
Story: Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, a disciple of the Maggid of Mezritch, led a major group of chassidim on aliyah to Eretz Yisrael in 5537 (1777). They settled primarily in Tiberias, founding one of the earliest chassidic communities in the Holy Land.
Tags: aliyah, tiberias, menachem mendel of vitebsk, eretz yisrael

Title: Vilna Gaon issues first cherem against chasidim
Summary: Rabbi Eliyahu of Vilna issued a ban of excommunication against the chasidic movement.
Story: The Vilna Gaon, one of the most influential Jewish scholars of the eighteenth century, formally opposed the nascent chasidic movement with a cherem. He issued the ban again in 1781, and after his passing his students orchestrated accusations against Rabbi Schneur Zalman that led to the Chabad founder's imprisonment by the czar.
Tags: vilna-gaon, mitnagdim, chasidism, excommunication

Title: RMM of Vitebsk leads chassidic caravan from Russia to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk led a chassidic caravan of over 300 souls from Russia toward Eretz Yisrael.
Story: In Adar 5537 (March 1777), R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk set out from Russia with two of the Maggid's disciples, R. Avraham of Kalisk and R. Yisrael of Polotsk, intending to lead a select group to Eretz Yisrael. Along the way more than 400 people joined them, gathering at Mohilov Podolsk on the Dniester to sail in several ships via Constantinople.
Tags: aliyah, russia, rmm of vitebsk, avraham of kalisk, yisrael of polotsk, eretz yisrael

Title: Two R' Aharons emigrate to Eretz Yisrael; ship sinks near Crimea
Summary: Two Chassidim named R' Aharon emigrated to Eretz Yisrael with R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk's caravan, surviving a shipwreck near Crimea.
Story: In summer 1777 (תקל"ז), R' Aharon b"R Yitzchak Aizik (Aharon the Great) and R' Aharon b"R Meir of Smilyan (Aharon the Small) joined R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk's caravan to Eretz Yisrael. Their ship sank near Crimea, but both survived. They settled first in Tzfat and later moved to Tiberias.
Tags: aliyah, tzfat, tiberias, crimea, shipwreck, menachem mendel of vitebsk, aharon the great, aharon the small

Title: Chasidim arrive in Eretz Yisrael, settle in Tzfat
Summary: The first major group of Chasidim arrived in Eretz Yisrael in Elul 5537 and settled in Tzfat rather than Tiberias.
Story: When the early Chasidic aliyah reached the Holy Land in Elul 5537, the group settled initially in Tzfat, not Tiberias. This is corrected by the author against a folk tradition that placed the arrival in Tiberias. The Tiberias community was only established several years later.
Tags: aliyah, tzfat, chasidim, eretz yisrael

Title: R. Israel of Polotzk's group arrives in Eretz Yisrael
Summary: On 5 Elul 5537, the Chassidic group including R. Israel of Polotzk arrived in Eretz Yisrael and settled in Tzfat.
Story: After a long and difficult journey, the group of Chassidim led by R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and including R. Israel of Polotzk reached Eretz Yisrael on 5 Elul 5537. Hundreds of Constantinople Jews joined them on the way to visit ancestral graves. The new settlers established themselves in Tzfat, where they began building a synagogue and faced immediate financial hardship from the many poor who attached themselves to the group.
Tags: aliyah, tzfat, israel of polotzk, eretz yisrael, chassidim

Title: RMM of Vitebsk and chassidic caravan arrive in Tzfat
Summary: R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and roughly 300 chassidim arrived in Tzfat after a six-month journey.
Story: On 5 Elul 5537 (September 1777), the chassidic caravan led by R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk arrived safely in Tzfat. The six-month journey from Russia had cost many lives in a Black Sea shipwreck, but the remaining group of about 300 souls reached the Holy Land, an event documented in letters by R. Yisrael of Polotsk and R. Avraham of Kalisk.
Tags: aliyah, tzfat, rmm of vitebsk, eretz yisrael

Title: Alter Rebbe begins revising Hilchos Netilas Yadayim for the Siddur
Summary: While residing in Mohilov in 5538-5539 (1778-1779), the Alter Rebbe began producing a second, revised edition of the laws of his Shulchan Aruch starting with Hilchos Netilas Yadayim.
Story: His sons relate that after his sixteenth review of the Talmud the Alter Rebbe began emending and renewing his Shulchan Aruch, starting with Hilchos Netilas Yadayim. The revised version was later printed as the kuntres 'Luach Birchas Hanehenin' and 'Seder Netilas Yadayim Lese'udah' in his Siddur. This opened a roughly twenty-year middle period of writing thirty kuntreisei halachos, lasting through 5557.
Tags: alter rebbe, netilas yadayim, shulchan aruch, siddur, halacha, mohilov

Title: R. Avraham of Kalisk writes to Smilian about the aliyah journey
Summary: R. Avraham of Kalisk wrote to the community of Smilian recounting the aliyah journey from Russia.
Story: In the winter of 5538 (1777-1778), R. Avraham of Kalisk wrote a letter (Likkutei Amarim 29) to the community of Smilian recounting the chassidic caravan's journey from Russia in Adar 5537 and its eventual arrival in Eretz Yisrael. This is one of the earliest documentary sources for that aliyah.
Tags: avraham of kalisk, smilian, aliyah, rmm of vitebsk

Title: R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk writes from Tzfat to chassidim of Vilna
Summary: From Tzfat in 1778, R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk wrote to the chassidim of Vilna recalling his unsuccessful efforts to be cleared in the eyes of the mitnagdim.
Story: The letter calls on the Vilna chassidim as witnesses to his earlier attempts to reconcile and explain the chassidic position. It is among the foundational documents of the chassidic side of the early conflict, paralleling the Alter Rebbe's later epistles on the same theme.
Tags: menachem mendel of vitebsk, tzfat, vilna, letter, mitnagdim

Title: RMM of Vitebsk writes first letter from Eretz Yisrael
Summary: R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk wrote his first letter from Eretz Yisrael describing the arrival and shipwreck.
Story: In the winter of 5538 (1777-1778), R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk composed his first letter from the Holy Land. He described the safe arrival of the caravan in Tzfat despite the tragic shipwreck, marveled at the survival of about 30 souls who later joined him in Eretz Yisrael, and asked his disciples in Russia to pray for the new community.
Tags: rmm of vitebsk, tzfat, eretz yisrael, aliyah

Title: Alter Rebbe returns to Liozna after parting from R. Menachem Mendel
Summary: According to the Rebbe Rayatz's writings, the Alter Rebbe arrived back in Liozna in mid-Shvat 5538 after his stay in Mohilov.
Story: After parting from R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk at Mohilov, the Alter Rebbe remained there for some time, where he reviewed the entire Talmud for the sixteenth time, standing day and night. Per the Rebbe Rayatz's notes in 'Avot HaChassidut,' he reached Liozna in mid-Shvat 5538. Other sources (Beis Rebbi) state he stayed in Mohilov a year and a half, returning home no earlier than 5539.
Tags: alter rebbe, liozna, russia, mohilov

Title: R. Avraham HaKohen of Kaliska writes from Tzfat about the new settlement
Summary: At the end of Shvat 5538, R. Avraham HaKohen of Kaliska wrote to the Chassidim of Smilian from Tzfat describing the new settlement's status.
Story: R. Avraham HaKohen of Kaliska, one of the leaders of the new chassidic settlement, sent a letter from Tzfat at the end of Shvat 5538 to his followers in Smilian. He reported on their safe arrival, the establishment of their community in Tzfat, and sent the letter via R. Shlomo Segal as a trusted messenger.
Tags: avraham of kaliska, tzfat, smilian, letter

Title: R. Yisrael of Polotsk writes from Jassy to Vitebsk-Polotsk leaders
Summary: R. Yisrael of Polotsk, returning as an emissary, wrote from Jassy reporting on the aliyah and shipwreck.
Story: On 9 Iyar 5538 (May 1778), R. Yisrael of Polotsk wrote from Jassy, while traveling as a shadar (emissary), to the leaders of the Vitebsk and Polotsk communities. He reported the arrival of the caravan in Tzfat on 5 Elul tarki''z, described the Black Sea shipwreck and the miraculous survival of about 30 souls, and detailed the spiritual aims of the new community.
Tags: yisrael of polotsk, vitebsk, polotsk, jassy, eretz yisrael, shadar

Title: R. Israel of Polotzk writes shadar letter from Iași
Summary: On 9 Iyar 5538, R. Israel of Polotzk wrote a fundraising letter from Iași describing the hardships and the journey of the aliyah group.
Story: While on his shadar mission back from Eretz Yisrael, R. Israel of Polotzk wrote a detailed letter from Iași on 9 Iyar 5538. He described the financial catastrophe caused by the many poor who joined the aliyah, the burden of supporting them through Constantinople, and pleaded for support of the new chassidic yishuv. The letter explicitly denied that he or R. Menachem Mendel had encouraged the poor to make aliyah, noting they had pressed themselves onto the group.
Tags: shadar, israel of polotzk, iasi, romania, letter, fundraising

Title: Famine strikes Eretz Yisrael
Summary: A severe famine struck Eretz Yisrael in 5539, described in letters as unprecedented in living memory.
Story: In 5539 a devastating famine struck Eretz Yisrael, described in chassidic letters as 'a famine in the land such as never was before.' A summer 5540 letter referred back to 'two years of famine in the land,' confirming the hardship spanned multiple years. This famine deepened the financial crisis of the new chassidic settlement and intensified the need for shadar fundraising.
Tags: famine, eretz yisrael, tzfat, tiberias, hardship

Title: R. Shlomo Segal sent as shadar from Eretz Yisrael
Summary: R. Shlomo Segal was dispatched as a shadar in winter 5539 and returned to Eretz Yisrael at the end of summer the same year.
Story: Following R. Israel of Polotzk's earlier mission, R. Shlomo Segal was sent as a shadar from the chassidic settlement to the Diaspora in winter 5539. According to the analysis correcting A. Yaari's chronology, R. Shlomo Segal carried letters from R. Avraham of Kaliska to the Chassidim and returned to Eretz Yisrael by late summer 5539.
Tags: shadar, shlomo segal, fundraising, tzfat

Title: R. Avraham of Kaliska visits Tiberias for Rosh Chodesh Shvat
Summary: R. Avraham of Kaliska traveled to Tiberias for Rosh Chodesh Shvat 5539 in response to repeated requests from the community there.
Story: After receiving repeated appeals from both Jerusalem and Tiberias, R. Avraham HaKohen of Kaliska traveled to Tiberias for Rosh Chodesh Shvat 5539. The trip was part of ongoing efforts to consolidate the chassidic presence in the holy cities and respond to community needs. This visit is documented in a letter that researcher Yaari originally misdated to 5538.
Tags: avraham of kaliska, tiberias, tzfat, jerusalem

Title: R. Shlomo arrives in Tiberias from the Diaspora
Summary: In Menachem Av 5539, a man named R. Shlomo arrived in Tiberias from the Diaspora bearing a letter for R. Yitzchak of Ciecierzec.
Story: A letter from summer 5540 records that in Menachem Av 5539 an individual named R. Shlomo arrived in Tiberias from abroad, carrying a letter addressed to R. Yitzchak of Ciecierzec. This mention is significant for the chronology of early chassidic shadarim, as it may relate to the identity and movements of R. Shlomo Segal.
Tags: shlomo, tiberias, yitzchak of ciecierzec, letter

Title: Toldot Yaakov Yosef printed in Koretz
Summary: Rabbi Yaakov Yosef HaKohen of Polonne's Toldot Yaakov Yosef was printed in Koretz in 5540.
Story: Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polonne, one of the Baal Shem Tov's foremost students, published Toldot Yaakov Yosef in Koretz in 1780. The book quotes hundreds of teachings he heard directly from the Baal Shem Tov. It was the very first Chassidic book to appear in print.
Tags: yaakov yosef of polonne, baal shem tov, koretz, first chassidic book

Title: Toldot Yaakov Yosef — first printed chassidic book
Summary: Toldot Yaakov Yosef, the first chassidic book ever printed, was published in Koretz in 5540.
Story: Toldot Yaakov Yosef by Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polonne, a disciple of the Baal Shem Tov, was printed in Koretz in 5540 (1780). It was the very first printed chassidic work — no chassidic book had been published during the lifetimes of either the Baal Shem Tov or the Maggid of Mezritch.
Tags: toldot yaakov yosef, koretz, yaakov yosef of polonne

Title: Baal Shem Tov's letter to his brother published
Summary: A disciple publishes the Baal Shem Tov's letter describing his 1746 mystical ascent for the first time.
Story: The letter, addressed to his brother and describing his encounter with the Messiah, became foundational text for the Chabad mission of spreading chasidic teachings outward.
Tags: baal-shem-tov, letter, publication, mashiach

Title: Ben Porat Yosef printed in Koretz
Summary: Ben Porat Yosef, by Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polonne, was printed in Koretz in 5541.
Story: Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polonne's second work, Ben Porat Yosef, was printed in Koretz in 5541 (1781). It contains chassidic teachings, responsa, and novellae.
Tags: yaakov yosef of polonne, koretz

Title: Maggid Devarav L'Yaakov first printed in Koretz
Summary: The teachings of the Maggid of Mezeritch first appeared in print as Maggid Devarav L'Yaakov in Koretz, 5541.
Story: Eight years after the Maggid's passing, his disciples compiled his teachings and published them as Maggid Devarav L'Yaakov in Koretz, 1781. The book went through several editions in quick succession over the next decade.
Tags: maggid of mezeritch, koretz, first edition

Title: Maggid Devarav LeYaakov first edition published in Koretz
Summary: The first edition of Maggid Devarav LeYaakov by the Maggid of Mezeritch was published in Koretz in 5541.
Story: In 5541 (1781), the first edition of Maggid Devarav LeYaakov by Rabbi Dovber, the Maggid of Mezeritch, was published in Koretz. The work transmits Chassidic teachings of the Maggid, successor to the Baal Shem Tov. A copy is preserved in the Lubavitch Library.
Tags: maggid of mezeritch, koretz, chassidus

Title: Maggid Devarav LeYaakov first printed in Koretz
Summary: Maggid Devarav LeYaakov, teachings of the Maggid of Mezritch, was first printed in Koretz in 5541.
Story: Following the first chassidic book by Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polonne, the teachings of the Maggid of Mezritch were printed under the title Maggid Devarav LeYaakov in Koretz in 5541 (1781). It was the first publication of the Maggid's own teachings.
Tags: maggid of mezritch, koretz, likutei amarim

Title: Maggid of Mezeritch's Maggid Devarav L'Yaakov printed in Korec
Summary: The first edition of the Maggid of Mezeritch's classic Maggid Devarav L'Yaakov was published in Korec in 1781.
Story: This Korec printing was one of the earliest Chassidic books to be published, presenting the Maggid's teachings to a wider readership. It would become foundational reading for Chassidic disciples for generations.
Tags: maggid of mezeritch, korec, first edition, chassidic literature

Title: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk migrates from Safed to Tiberias
Summary: In 5541 R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk left Safed for Tiberias after sustained harassment by the Sephardic pakid over communal tax payments.
Story: Unable in 5540 to pay the annual fee demanded by the Sephardic pakid for Safed's communal needs, R' Menachem Mendel suffered repeated threats including imprisonment in iron chains. Though relief funds arrived through the emissary R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen, the persistent torment caused him to fall ill for months and ultimately drove him to relocate to Tiberias. He found refuge in the house formerly occupied by R' Shlomo of Lvov, who had recently fled abroad.
Tags: menachem mendel of vitebsk, tiberias, safed, sephardic pakid, aliyah

Title: R' Yaakov of Smilyan becomes chief gabbai in chu"l
Summary: R' Yaakov of Smilyan began his role as chief gabbai in the diaspora for Eretz Yisrael Chassidim in 1781.
Story: R' Yaakov of Smilyan started his work as the chief gabbai abroad collecting funds for the Chassidic settlement in Eretz Yisrael in 1781 (תקמ"א). This role was foundational for the organized fundraising system that supported Chabad and other Chassidic groups in the Holy Land.
Tags: gabbai, fundraising, yaakov of smilyan, shadar

Title: Some Chasidim move from Tzfat to Tiberias
Summary: About three and a half years after settling in Tzfat, part of the Chasidic community relocated to Tiberias in 5541.
Story: The branching of the Chasidic yishuv from Tzfat to Tiberias took place in 5541. This created the Tiberias-based Chasidic community that would be led for decades by R' Avraham of Kalisk and R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk. Both Galilean cities would remain centers of Chasidic settlement.
Tags: tzfat, tiberias, chasidim

Title: Three tzaddikim issue decree forbidding loans from Eretz Yisrael fund
Summary: R. Yisrael of Polotsk, R. Yissachar Ber of Lubavitch and the Alter Rebbe banned loans from the Eretz Yisrael fund.
Story: Around 5541 (1781), the three tzaddikim entrusted with managing the Eretz Yisrael fund in Russia issued a binding decree (with nidui and shamta) forbidding anyone, including themselves, from borrowing even a single peruta from the money collected. The decree was prompted by losses sustained when administrators had used the money for other mitzvah purposes.
Tags: alter rebbe, avraham of kalisk, yisrael of polotsk, kollel funds, russia

Title: Vilna Gaon issues second cherem against chasidim
Summary: The Vilna Gaon renewed his ban of excommunication against the chasidic movement.
Story: Four years after the first cherem, the Vilna Gaon again formalized opposition to chasidism. The animosity between chasidim and their opponents shaped Jewish communal politics in Europe and the Holy Land for decades.
Tags: vilna-gaon, mitnagdim, chasidism, excommunication

Title: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk announces emissary's safe return
Summary: In a Nisan 5541 letter from Tiberias, R' Menachem Mendel announces the safe return of emissary R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen.
Story: Writing from Tiberias in Nisan 5541, R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk reports that 'our beloved, wondrous rabbi R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen, our emissary,' has returned safely with his person and finances intact. The letter does not specify when he had departed for the diaspora. Scholars conjecture, based on R' Shlomo Segal's 5539 journey, that R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen left on his first shadar mission in 5540.
Tags: menachem mendel of vitebsk, shlomo zalman hakohen, tiberias, shadar, eretz yisrael

Title: R' Shlomo of Lvov, author of Mercavat HaMishneh, dies in Salonika
Summary: On 21 Tammuz 5541 R' Shlomo of Lvov, author of Mercavat HaMishneh, died in Salonika after being driven from Tiberias and Acre.
Story: R' Shlomo had settled in 5539 in Tiberias's finest house on the strength of a letter from Istanbul recommending him for honor and a worthy dwelling. He was eventually expelled, wandering through Sha'farem, Acre, and other locations, suffering bodily and financial harm at each stop. He finally fled abroad to Salonika where he died, his vacated Tiberias house becoming the residence of R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk.
Tags: shlomo of lvov, mercavat hamishneh, salonika, tiberias, acre

Title: Alter Rebbe becomes sole leader of Russian-Lithuanian Chassidim
Summary: Around 5543, Rabbi Yisrael of Polotsk passes away and Rabbi Yissachar Ber of Lubavitch defers, leaving the Alter Rebbe—now settled in Liozna—as the sole leader appointed by Rabbis Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and Avraham of Kalisk.
Story: About a year after the three-leader appointment letter, Rabbi Yisrael of Polotsk passed away around 5543, and Rabbi Yissachar Ber of Lubavitch deferred to the Alter Rebbe. Rabbis Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and Avraham of Kalisk, writing from Eretz Yisrael, then designated him sole leader of Russian and Lithuanian Chassidim. In the same year he settled in his hometown Liozna as maggid-meisharim, where he would lead Chabad until 5561.
Tags: yisrael of polotsk, yissachar ber of lubavitch, schneur zalman, liozna, succession

Title: First Haggadah printed in Livorno
Summary: The Chida's Simchat HaRegel — the first Haggadah printed in Livorno — was issued in 5542.
Story: In 5542 (1782), the Chida's commentary Simchat HaRegel was printed in Livorno by Avraham Yitzchak Estilo and Eliezer Sadoun. It was the first Haggadah ever printed in Livorno, which would become a major center of Sephardi printing.
Tags: haggadah, livorno, italy, chida

Title: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk's letter on declining Volhynia support
Summary: R' Menachem Mendel wrote that Volhynia's support had dropped to only fifty gold coins for the year.
Story: In 5542 (1782), R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk wrote a letter noting that financial support from Volhynia had dropped sharply, sending only fifty gold pieces. He explained that since beginning his service as a leader, he had moved his residence from Volhynia to Russia, which may have weakened the relationship. The letter is preserved in Likutei Amarim, letter 5.
Tags: fundraising, volhynia, menachem mendel of vitebsk, eretz yisrael fund, letter

Title: Tzofnat Pa'aneach printed in Koretz
Summary: Tzofnat Pa'aneach by Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polonne was printed in Koretz in 5542.
Story: The third printed work of Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polonne, Tzofnat Pa'aneach, appeared in Koretz in 5542 (1782) as part of the earliest wave of chassidic publishing.
Tags: yaakov yosef of polonne, koretz

Title: Tzofnat Paneach printed in Koretz
Summary: Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polonne's Tzofnat Paneach appeared in Koretz in 5542.
Story: The third of Rabbi Yaakov Yosef's Chassidic works, Tzofnat Paneach, was printed in Koretz in 1782. Together with Toldot Yaakov Yosef and Ben Porat Yosef, it formed the trio of the earliest published Chassidic books quoting the Baal Shem Tov.
Tags: yaakov yosef of polonne, baal shem tov, koretz

Title: RMM of Vitebsk endorses three tzaddikim's leadership of Russian chassidim
Summary: RMM of Vitebsk wrote endorsing R. Yisrael of Polotsk, R. Yissachar Ber of Lubavitch and the Alter Rebbe.
Story: On 4 Adar 5542 (Feb 1782), R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk wrote that Russian chassidim should not travel long distances to other leaders in Volhynia but should consult the three great tzaddikim already among them. He named R. Yisrael of Polotsk, R. Yissachar Ber of Lubavitch and the Alter Rebbe (R. Shneur Zalman), affirming their authority over the Eretz Yisrael fund.
Tags: rmm of vitebsk, alter rebbe, yisrael of polotsk, yissachar ber of lubavitch, kollel funds

Title: Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk names three Russian Chassidic leaders
Summary: From Eretz Yisrael, Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk writes on 4 Adar 5542 directing Russian Chassidim to attach themselves exclusively to three named leaders.
Story: On 4 Adar 5542, Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk wrote from Eretz Yisrael instructing his Russian Chassidim not to travel to Volhynia for Chassidic guidance but to bind themselves only to three named leaders in Russia: Rabbi Yisrael of Polotsk, Rabbi Yissachar Ber of Lubavitch, and Rabbi Schneur Zalman. The letter notably omitted other Maggid disciples then in Russia—Rabbi Levi Yitzchak (then in Pinsk), Rabbi Shlomo of Karlin, and Rabbi Chaim Chaikel of Amdur—marking the beginning of what would become the proto-Chabad line of leadership.
Tags: menachem mendel of vitebsk, israel of polotsk, yissachar ber of lubavitch, schneur zalman, eretz yisrael, appointment

Title: Alter Rebbe describes R. Yaakov of Smilian's two years as ma'amados gabbai
Summary: The Alter Rebbe wrote that R. Yaakov of Smilian had served for two years as a faithful collector of Eretz Yisrael funds.
Story: In early summer 5543 (1783), the Alter Rebbe wrote in a letter (Yagdil Torah NY 51) that R. Yaakov of Smilian had served with great effort for two years as a trusted emissary collecting Eretz Yisrael funds. This implies that R. Yaakov was appointed in 5541, around the time the three tzaddikim formalized their joint leadership.
Tags: alter rebbe, yaakov of smilian, kollel funds, ma'amados

Title: Alter Rebbe settles in Liozna
Summary: R' Schneur Zalman of Liadi moved from Horodok to Liozna around summer 5543.
Story: After roughly two years in Horodok, the Alter Rebbe relocated to Liozna in the summer of 5543 (1783). In his later 1798 interrogation he himself testified that he had lived in Liozna 'about 15 years and more.' Liozna became the seat of his leadership of Belorussian and Lithuanian chassidim until 1801.
Tags: alter rebbe, liozna, white russia, schneur zalman of liadi

Title: Alter Rebbe settles in Liozna and begins leading White Russian Chassidim
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi settled in Liozna and began guiding the Chassidic community in White Russia.
Story: From 5543 (1783) onward, the Alter Rebbe based himself in Liozna and assumed leadership of the Chabad Chassidim across White Russia. From there, Chabad communities began to organize in Lithuania as well, especially in Vilna and Vidz. This marked the start of a structured Chabad presence in the region.
Tags: liozna, white russia, alter rebbe, chabad founding

Title: Chabad center established in Liozna under the Alter Rebbe
Summary: In 5543 (1783) Liozna became the seat of the Alter Rebbe's leadership and the center of the emerging Chabad movement.
Story: The Alter Rebbe, R' Shneur Zalman, founded the Chabad branch of Chassidus and led the movement from Liozna for the first phase of his nesius. Liozna sat near Lubavitch in White Russia. It would serve as the Chabad center for nearly two decades.
Tags: liozna, alter-rebbe, chabad-center

Title: R' Aharon of Tiveria recommends Alter Rebbe to Russian chassidim
Summary: R' Aharon HaGadol wrote from Tiveria in 5543 urging Russian chassidim to draw close to R' Schneur Zalman.
Story: In 5543 (1783) R' Aharon HaGadol of Tiveria sent a letter to the chassidim of White Russia, advising them to attach themselves to R' Schneur Zalman of Horodok as 'unique in his generation among you in wisdom and chassidut.' This is the earliest documented signal of the Alter Rebbe's emerging role as exclusive leader of Russian chassidim.
Tags: r' aharon of tiveria, white russia, leadership, letter

Title: R' Avraham of Kalisk and remaining Chassidim move from Safed to Tiberias
Summary: In 5543 R' Avraham of Kalisk and remaining Chassidim of Safed were forced to leave the city after the Sephardic pakid's escalating hostility.
Story: The pakid of Safed, hating that R' Avraham refused to eat from his shochet, expelled him forcefully, dragging many devoted Chassidim out with him. Some settled in the village of Pekiin, while R' Avraham himself moved to Tiberias where R' Menachem Mendel arranged a fine residence for him. The migration completed the relocation of the Chassidic community from Safed to Tiberias.
Tags: avraham of kalisk, safed, tiberias, pekiin, sephardic pakid, chassidim

Title: R' Shneur Zalman of Liadi reconciles with R' Aharon
Summary: R' Shneur Zalman wrote an undated letter to his Chassidim reporting reconciliation with R' Aharon and others after a dispute.
Story: In an undated letter (likely from 1783), R' Shneur Zalman of Liadi described investigating a dispute and finding that his beloved companions, including R' Tzvi b"R Mendel Segal and R' Aharon the Great, remained loyal to him. After two weeks together, the misunderstanding was resolved and their mutual love was renewed.
Tags: shneur zalman of liadi, aharon the great, reconciliation, tzvi hirsch of liadi

Title: Approximately fifty Jewish families recorded living in Lubavitch
Summary: A list of about fifty Jewish families living in Lubavitch was recorded in 5544 (1784), later published in the Hendel Deutsch booklet.
Story: Lubavitch was a small town, roughly 1.5 by 1.5 kilometers, but it served as a regional commercial hub. The 1784 list of about fifty Jewish families documents the local community well before Chabad's leadership moved there. The list was later reprinted in Deutsch's 1994 documentary booklet.
Tags: lubavitch, census, families, jewish-community

Title: List of approximately fifty Jewish families in Lubavitch recorded
Summary: A roster of roughly fifty Jewish families then residing in Lubavitch was recorded in 1784.
Story: This list, later published by Hendel Deutsch in his 1994 Russian booklet on Lubavitch, gives a snapshot of the town's Jewish community in the era of the Alter Rebbe's youth. It documents the modest scale of the settlement before Lubavitch became a movement headquarters. Around this period the future Alter Rebbe studied Torah in Lubavitch with Rabbi Yissachar Ber.
Tags: russia, census, demographics

Title: Maggid Devarav L'Yaakov reprinted in Koretz
Summary: A second edition of the Maggid's teachings appeared in Koretz in 5544.
Story: Three years after its first appearance, Maggid Devarav L'Yaakov was reprinted in Koretz in 1784, attesting to the demand for the Maggid's teachings.
Tags: maggid of mezeritch, koretz

Title: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk endorses Alter Rebbe and R' Yissachar Ber
Summary: In winter 5544 R' Menachem Mendel wrote from Tiveria directing Russian chassidim to the Alter Rebbe and R' Yissachar Ber.
Story: From Tiveria in the winter of 5544 (1784), R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk responded to complaints about livelihood and leadership reaching him from Russia. He instructed the chassidim to be content with the guidance of R' Yissachar Ber of Lubavitch and R' Schneur Zalman of Liozna rather than seeking new leadership from abroad.
Tags: menachem mendel of vitebsk, yissachar ber of lubavitch, white russia, leadership

Title: R' Shlomo of Karlin relocates to Ludmir
Summary: After being expelled by mitnagdim from Karlin, R' Shlomo was already in Ludmir by 5544.
Story: R' Shlomo of Karlin was driven from Karlin by the mitnagdim and resettled in Ludmir in Volhynia. The precise date of relocation is undocumented, but by 5544 (1784) he was already established in Ludmir, having earlier been denied the Alter Rebbe's full agreement to settle in Beshenkovich because of a doctrinal disagreement about the role of the tzaddik.
Tags: r' shlomo of karlin, ludmir, mitnagdim, volhynia, expulsion

Title: R' Aharon the Great departs as shadar to chu"l
Summary: R' Aharon b"R Yitzchak Aizik (Aharon the Great) left Eretz Yisrael as a shadar to the diaspora in 1785.
Story: According to Sheluchei Eretz Yisrael, R' Aharon the Great departed for the diaspora as an emissary in 1785 (תקמ"ה), carrying a letter of mission from R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and R' Avraham of Kalisk. He remained abroad for three years collecting funds and strengthening ties with the Chassidic communities.
Tags: shadar, fundraising, aharon the great, tiberias, menachem mendel of vitebsk

Title: R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev expelled from Pinsk
Summary: In summer 5545 R' Levi Yitzchak was driven from Pinsk by mitnagdim and moved to Berditchev.
Story: R' Levi Yitzchak had served as av beit din of Pinsk from 5535 to 5545. In the summer of 5545 (1785) the mitnagdim succeeded in expelling him from the city, and he relocated to Berditchev in Volhynia. His departure further consolidated the Alter Rebbe's position as sole chassidic leader in White Russia and Lithuania.
Tags: levi yitzchak of berditchev, pinsk, berditchev, mitnagdim, volhynia, expulsion

Title: R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen departs Tiberias on second shadar mission
Summary: R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen leaves Tiberias as emissary toward the end of winter 5545.
Story: His signature on a Mi Sheberach written by the chassidim of Tiberias during winter 5545 places him in the city at that time. He left Tiberias at the end of that winter as shadar on his second mission to the diaspora, returning to the Land of Israel in the autumn of the following year.
Tags: shlomo zalman hakohen, tiberias, shadar, chassidim

Title: R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen returns to Tiberias with companions
Summary: In mid-Cheshvan 5546 R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen reaches Tiberias with two companions and all collected donations.
Story: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk writes that in mid-Cheshvan 5546 the emissary R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen arrived safely back in Tiberias, accompanied by R' Tzvi Hirsch Besht of Vitebsk and R' Gershon Shochet. All three were in good health and brought the entirety of the trumah funds raised abroad.
Tags: shlomo zalman hakohen, tiberias, shadar, tzvi hirsch besht, gershon shochet, donations

Title: Plague strikes Safed, Tiberias and surrounding regions
Summary: In 5546 a severe plague struck Safed and nearby cities, eventually reaching Tiberias where R' Menachem Mendel and his community sequestered themselves to survive.
Story: The plague first ravaged Safed and surrounding areas, sending many Chassidim fleeing to Tiberias where R' Menachem Mendel arranged their needs. When the outbreak finally reached Tiberias from Purim through several days into Iyar, R' Menachem Mendel locked himself with over a minyan of followers inside his new courtyard rather than fleeing the city. Other Tiberias residents followed his example, sealing themselves into their homes; the surrounding villages including Pekiin were spared entirely.
Tags: plague, safed, tiberias, menachem mendel of vitebsk, pekiin

Title: R' Meir of Bychov's earliest known signature, from Tiberias
Summary: R' Meir of Bychov's signature first appears on a letter written in Tiberias in winter 5546.
Story: The earliest documentary trace of R' Meir of Bychov is his signature on a Tiberias letter from winter 5546, signed 'Meir son of R' Yaakov of Bychov.' This places him in the Chasidic yishuv of Tiberias by that date. He would later become one of the leading shadarim of the community.
Tags: meir of bychov, tiberias, shadar

Title: R' Menachem Mendel formally appoints Alter Rebbe as leader of Russia
Summary: In 5546 R' Menachem Mendel wrote insisting that the Alter Rebbe accept exclusive leadership of Russian chassidim.
Story: In 5546 (1786), responding to the Alter Rebbe's hesitation, R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk wrote from Tiveria urging him to 'be strong and courageous… for Hashem has given you as a shepherd' and to lead all the chassidim of Russia. R' Avraham of Kalisk wrote in parallel echoing the appointment.
Tags: menachem mendel of vitebsk, alter rebbe, leadership, letter, appointment

Title: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk completes his house and synagogue in Tiberias
Summary: By winter 5546 R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk completed a three-story house in Tiberias containing a beautiful synagogue.
Story: After years of struggle with the Sephardic pakid who initially refused permission for a separate Ashkenazi prayer space, R' Menachem Mendel built a permanent three-story house with an integrated synagogue. The Sephardic pakid who had tormented him died suddenly after attempting to extort funds, and the new pakid was peaceful. The synagogue served as a center of prayer and Torah study for the Chassidic community in Tiberias.
Tags: menachem mendel of vitebsk, tiberias, synagogue, construction

Title: Rabbi Avraham Avli leaves Posval
Summary: Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler left the town of Posval in 5546.
Story: In 5546 (1786), at about age 24, Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler left the town of Posval. By that point he had already served in the rabbinate there and was known as a major Torah scholar, as attested to in the responsa of Tiferet Tzvi.
Tags: posval, posveler, rabbinate

Title: Alter Rebbe replies to summons from Mohilov rabbinate
Summary: In 5547 the Alter Rebbe wrote refusing to appear before the Mohilov rabbinate and defending chassidim against shklov decrees.
Story: Between 5546–47 the heads of the Mohilov community summoned the Alter Rebbe to stand judgment before them and even appealed to the civil courts. In 5547 (1787) he responded with a lengthy letter rejecting the summons, refuting the charges, and protesting the harsh distancing decrees issued by some Shklov scholars against chassidim.
Tags: mohilov, white russia, mitnagdim, shklov, herem, letter

Title: Passing of Rabbi Elimelech of Lizhensk
Summary: Rabbi Elimelech of Lizhensk, author of Noam Elimelech, passed away in 5547.
Story: Rabbi Elimelech of Lizhensk, a leading disciple of the Maggid of Mezritch and author of Noam Elimelech, passed away in 5547 (1787). He shaped the development of chassidut in Poland and Galicia.
Tags: elimelech of lizhensk, lizhensk

Title: R' Aharon's confessional letter to R' Shneur Zalman
Summary: R' Aharon the Great wrote a remorseful letter to R' Shneur Zalman in 1787 begging forgiveness for slighting him.
Story: After returning to Eretz Yisrael, R' Aharon the Great was rebuked by R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk for having spoken against R' Shneur Zalman during his shadar mission. From Tiberias he wrote a tearful confession asking R' Shneur Zalman to forgive him so that he could be readmitted to R' Menachem Mendel's presence.
Tags: aharon the great, shneur zalman of liadi, menachem mendel of vitebsk, tiberias, confession

Title: R' Chaim Chaikel of Amdura passes away
Summary: R' Chaim Chaikel of Amdura died in winter 5547.
Story: In the winter of 5547 (1786/87) R' Chaim Chaikel of Amdura, one of the disciples of the Maggid of Mezritch active in Lithuania, passed away. His son and successor R' Shmuel, then twenty years old, began traveling to the Alter Rebbe to receive Torah from him.
Tags: r' chaim chaikel of amdura, amdura, succession, r' shmuel of amdura

Title: Alter Rebbe writes Igeret HaTanchumin urging continued EY support
Summary: Following the passing of R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, the Alter Rebbe wrote a letter of consolation urging chassidim not to reduce their support of the Eretz Yisrael community by even a single coin.
Story: After hearing that some chassidim wished to reduce their support of the Tiberias community because the original support had been directed at honoring the deceased tzaddik, the Alter Rebbe wrote his Igeret HaTanchumin (letter 11). He pleaded that not a single coin be withheld, emphasizing the supreme importance of supporting Jewish settlement in Eretz Yisrael, and praised R' Avraham HaKohen as the worthy successor.
Tags: alter rebbe, shneur zalman of liadi, eretz yisrael fund, tiberias, consolation letter

Title: Colel Chabad founded by Rabbi Schneur Zalman
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi established Colel Chabad in 1788 to support early chasidic immigration from Europe to the Land of Israel.
Story: Colel Chabad is the oldest continuously operating charitable organization in the Land of Israel. Its founding to assist Chabad immigrants from Europe predated by more than 150 years the Rebbe's postwar effort to refocus Chabad in Israel outward toward all Israeli Jews.
Tags: colel chabad, schneur zalman, eretz yisrael, charity, alter rebbe

Title: Marriage of the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: Dovber Schneuri, later the Mitteler Rebbe, was married in 5548.
Story: The future Mitteler Rebbe's wedding took place in 5548, a date deduced from the fact that his son R' Menachem Nochum was born after that year. The marriage is one of several family events that anchor the chronology of the Alter Rebbe's grandchildren born in 5549-5551.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, family, wedding

Title: Passing of Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk in Tiberias
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, who led chassidim to Eretz Yisrael, passed away in Tiberias in 5548.
Story: Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, a disciple of the Maggid of Mezritch, led a group of chassidim to settle in Eretz Yisrael in 5537 (1777). He passed away in Tiberias in 5548 (1788).
Tags: menachem mendel of vitebsk, tiberias, aliyah

Title: R' Chaim Halevi begins 42-year tenure as gabbai of Hebron
Summary: R' Chaim Halevi ibn Yakar began his 42-year tenure as gabbai and pakid of the Hebron community.
Story: In 5548 (1788), R' Chaim Yaakov Halevi ibn Yakar began serving as gabbai and pakid (treasurer and officer) of the Hebron Sephardic community. He held the post for 42 years, handling all communal affairs until 5590 (1830). As a sign of trust and recognition, in 5590 his son R' Yosef Halevi was appointed as his deputy and eventual successor.
Tags: chaim halevi ibn yakar, hebron, sephardic kollel, gabbai

Title: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk's final letter on Alter Rebbe's leadership
Summary: R' Menachem Mendel's last extant letter in 5548 again confirmed the Alter Rebbe as moreh tzedek for Russia.
Story: In his final letter from Tiveria, dated 5548 (1788), R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk wrote: 'We have anointed him to be moreh tzedek in their land, so that the congregation of Hashem should not be like sheep without a shepherd… who like him is teacher and rav in their country.' This sealed the Alter Rebbe's standing as exclusive leader.
Tags: menachem mendel of vitebsk, letter, leadership, alter rebbe

Title: Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk passes away
Summary: The leader of the first chasidic aliyah passed away in the Holy Land.
Story: His successor, Rabbi Avraham Karlisker, also a student of the Maggid of Mezeritch, differed with Rabbi Schneur Zalman on a variety of issues, leading to disagreements within the Holy Land chasidic community.
Tags: menachem-mendel-vitebsk, tiberias

Title: Rabbi Schneur Zalman establishes Colel Chabad
Summary: The Chabad founder created an international fund to support chasidic families settled in the Holy Land.
Story: After Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk's passing, Rabbi Schneur Zalman established the fund to ensure the continuity of the chasidic community in Eretz Yisrael. Today, Colel Chabad remains the oldest continuously operating charity in Israel and is the country's largest provider of food security.
Tags: colel-chabad, schneur-zalman, charity, eretz-yisrael

Title: R' Aharon the Great returns to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: R' Aharon the Great returned to Eretz Yisrael in mid-Adar I 1788 after three years abroad as a shadar.
Story: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk's last letter, written in Nisan 1788, reports that 'the ship arrived, thank G-d, with the aforementioned shadar and his companions... they came in peace in the middle of Adar I.' This confirmed R' Aharon the Great's return to Eretz Yisrael after his shadar mission.
Tags: shadar, aharon the great, tiberias, menachem mendel of vitebsk

Title: Passing of R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk
Summary: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, leader of the chassidic community in Tiberias, passed away on Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5548.
Story: On Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5548, the chassidic leader R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk passed away in Tiberias. His passing prompted some Russian chassidim to consider reducing or stopping their financial support of the chassidic settlement in Eretz Yisrael. Leadership of the Chabad chassidim in Tiberias transferred to R' Avraham of Kalisk.
Tags: tiberias, eretz yisrael, menachem mendel of vitebsk, chassidic leadership

Title: Passing of R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk
Summary: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk passed away on Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5548.
Story: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, leader of the chassidic aliyah to Eretz Yisrael and mentor to the Alter Rebbe, passed away on Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5548 (May 7, 1788) in Tiveria. After his passing, R' Avraham of Kalisk continued to write to the Russian chassidim affirming that R' Schneur Zalman alone was their leader.
Tags: menachem mendel of vitebsk, tiveria, tiberias, yahrtzeit, land of israel

Title: Final letter of R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk to chassidim in Russia
Summary: In early summer 1788 R. Menachem Mendel sent his last letter to the chassidim of Russia, designating the Alter Rebbe as their teacher and guide.
Story: The letter describes how the Alter Rebbe wore down his feet traveling 'to seek God' and was 'anointed' to be moreh tzedek for the Russian community. Printed as the 22nd letter of Likutei Amarim/Tanya, it formally transferred leadership of the Russian chassidim to the Alter Rebbe.
Tags: menachem mendel of vitebsk, alter rebbe, letter, leadership, tzfat

Title: Passing of R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk
Summary: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, leader of the chassidic settlement in the Holy Land, passes away in summer 5548.
Story: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, the foremost disciple of the Maggid of Mezritch who led the 1777 chassidic aliyah, passed away in summer 5548. After his passing, R' Avraham of Kalisk continued to guide the Holy Land community, while the Alter Rebbe assumed responsibility for the chassidim in Russia and their fundraising for Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: menachem mendel of vitebsk, tiberias, death, maggid of mezritch, chassidut

Title: R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen letter mentions passing of R' Menachem Mendel
Summary: R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen of Vilna wrote a summer 1788 letter mentioning the passing of R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk.
Story: In summer 1788, R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen of Vilna addressed a letter to the diaspora referencing the passing of R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk. The letter was also addressed to 'R' Aharon the Small,' confirming the latter's role 'attending the Rebbe' at that time.
Tags: menachem mendel of vitebsk, shlomo zalman hakohen, vilna, aharon the small, petira

Title: Birth of Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneersohn, the Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek, third Lubavitcher Rebbe, was born in 1789.
Story: Named for his classic work on Jewish law, the Tzemach Tzedek became a towering figure in 19th-century Russian Jewry. He led Chabad through major challenges to traditional Jewish life from the Russian government.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, menachem mendel schneersohn

Title: First long maamarim of the Alter Rebbe
Summary: On Rosh Hashana 5550 (1789) the Alter Rebbe delivered 'Mashbi'in Oso Tehi Tzadik', followed on Erev Shabbos Shuvah by 'Shuvah Yisrael' — among his first lengthy maamarim said publicly.
Story: According to Sefer HaSichos 5703, these were the earliest of the long-format Chasidic discourses delivered by the Alter Rebbe in public. They preceded the major shift toward extended discourses with multiple layered explanations that came after his return from Petersburg in 1801.
Tags: alter rebbe, maamarim, rosh hashana, shabbos shuvah

Title: Haggadah with Yiddish Kabbalistic commentary printed in Frankfurt an der Oder
Summary: A Passover Haggadah with Yiddish translation and Kabbalistic commentary was printed in Frankfurt an der Oder.
Story: In 5549 (1789), Itzik son of Aharon Zelig, typesetter and printer, produced a Haggadah in Frankfurt an der Oder that featured the original Hebrew alongside a Yiddish translation in parallel columns. Beneath these, a Kabbalistic commentary was printed in square Hebrew letters. The final page additionally contained a Yiddish commentary on Chad Gadya in Tzene-Rene script.
Tags: haggadah, yiddish, kabbalah, frankfurt an der oder, germany

Title: R' Meir of Bychov departs on his first shlichut
Summary: R' Meir of Bychov set out on his first emissary mission abroad in the summer of 5549.
Story: The author corrects the standard reference work 'Shluchei Eretz Yisrael,' showing that R' Meir of Bychov's first shlichut began in summer 5549 (not 5551 as commonly cited). Evidence includes a letter of Erev Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5549 from R' Shmuel Gronem introducing R' Meir as the bearer. R' Meir returned to Eretz Yisrael in Menachem Av 5551.
Tags: meir of bychov, shadar, tiberias, summer 5549

Title: R' Meir Refael's of Vilna draws close to Chassidus
Summary: R' Meir ben Refael Yaffe of Vilna and his two sons became disciples of the Alter Rebbe.
Story: Around 5549, the wealthy Vilna chassid R' Meir Refael's together with his sons Shlomo and Yaakov traveled to the Alter Rebbe in Liozna to study Chassidic conduct. He later became the head of the Chabad kehilla in Vilna and a close disciple of the Rebbe. He testified to this date during his interrogation in 5559.
Tags: vilna, meir refaels, alter rebbe, early disciples

Title: R' Tzvi Hirsch Harker continues to Tiberias on Alter Rebbe's instruction
Summary: In summer 5549 the emissary R' Tzvi Hirsch Harker wanted to return to Russia to revive flagging support but the Alter Rebbe instructed him to continue to Tiberias.
Story: By summer 5549 R' Tzvi Hirsch Harker was already on his way back to Tiberias when he saw that Russian chassidic support was dwindling. He wanted to return to Russia to rally support, but the Alter Rebbe instructed him to continue his journey, promising to personally take responsibility for increasing Russian chassidic support. From Zaslov mid-journey he wrote to anash describing the Alter Rebbe's great love and dedication.
Tags: tzvi hirsch harker, alter rebbe, shadar, tiberias, zaslov, eretz yisrael fund

Title: R' Yoel Smolyaner sent on shlichut to Russia
Summary: R' Yoel Smolyaner was dispatched from Eretz Yisrael to Russia in the winter of 5549 as the shadar for 5550.
Story: In winter 5549 R' Yoel Smolyaner left the Holy Land as the official emissary to the Chasidic communities of Russia for the year 5550. A Tiberias letter from Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5549 already noted that his correspondence had reached Constantinople and that he was diverting via Trieste. His mission was unusually long and he did not return until Nissan 5551.
Tags: yoel smolyaner, shadar, russia, tiberias

Title: R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen begins third shadar mission
Summary: In late summer 5549 R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen departs as emissary for a third time, carrying a letter signed by 21 chassidim.
Story: At the end of summer 5549 R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen left the Land of Israel as shadar for the third time. His authorization letter was signed by 21 chassidim from Tiberias, Tzfat, and Pekiin. This mission lasted three full years before he returned home.
Tags: shlomo zalman hakohen, shadar, tiberias, tzfat, pekiin, chassidim

Title: Birth of Rabbi Menachem Mendel (Tzemach Tzedek) in Liadi
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneersohn, later the third Chabad Rebbe known as the Tzemach Tzedek, was born on Erev Rosh Hashanah 5550 in Liadi.
Story: Born on the eve of Rosh Hashanah 5550, the future Tzemach Tzedek would later become both nephew and son-in-law of the Mittler Rebbe. He would assume Chabad leadership in 1827 and guide the movement from Lubavitch for nearly four decades. His birth in Liadi predates the relocation of the Chabad center to Lubavitch.
Tags: tzemach-tzedek, liadi, schneersohn

Title: Tzemach Tzedek born in Liozna
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneersohn (the Tzemach Tzedek) was born on the eve of Rosh Hashanah 5550.
Story: The third Chabad Rebbe, known as the Tzemach Tzedek after his magnum opus of responsa, was born on Erev Rosh Hashanah 5550. He was the grandson of the Alter Rebbe and would later become son-in-law of the Mitteler Rebbe. This birth date is used as the baseline for dating his earliest halachic activity.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, menachem mendel schneersohn, birth, russia

Title: Tzemach Tzedek born on Erev Rosh Hashanah
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek (R. Menachem Mendel of Lubavitch) was born on Erev Rosh Hashanah 5550 (September 1789).
Story: R. Menachem Mendel Schneersohn, later known as the Tzemach Tzedek, was born on Erev Rosh Hashanah 5550. On that very day his grandfather the Alter Rebbe began delivering the lengthy discourse 'Mashbiim Oto,' whose content forms the first three chapters of Tanya.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, chabad, birth, erev rosh hashanah, alter rebbe

Title: Birth of the Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: R' Menachem Mendel Schneersohn, the future Tzemach Tzedek, was born on Erev Rosh Hashanah 5550.
Story: The Tzemach Tzedek, third Chabad Rebbe and author of monumental halachic and Chassidic works, was born on Erev Rosh Hashanah 5550 (September 19, 1789) to R' Shalom Shachna and Devorah Leah (daughter of the Alter Rebbe). He was raised by his grandfather the Alter Rebbe after his mother's early death.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, birth, family

Title: R' Meir Refael's elected to the Vilna kahal
Summary: R' Meir ben Refael Yaffe was elected a member of the kahal of Vilna in 5550.
Story: Despite his Chassidic affiliation, R' Meir Refael's was elected to the Vilna kahal in 5550. In this early period there was no strong opposition in Vilna to the Chassidic kehilla, and the Chassidic minyan operated with the approval of the kahal head R' Moshe ben Asher.
Tags: vilna, meir refaels, kahal

Title: R' Shmuel of Amdura first travels to the Alter Rebbe
Summary: R' Shmuel of Amdura first traveled to learn from the Alter Rebbe in 5550.
Story: According to his own 1799 interrogation testimony, R' Shmuel of Amdura traveled to the Alter Rebbe to study from him three times: in 5550, 5554, and 5558. His extant letters also cite teachings received from the Alter Rebbe, evidencing the latter's growing role as teacher across Lithuanian chassidic communities.
Tags: r' shmuel of amdura, alter rebbe, interrogation, 1799 arrests

Title: R. Avraham David Wahrman begins rabbinate in Yazlovich
Summary: Rabbi Avraham David Wahrman began serving as rabbi of Yazlovich in 5550 (1790).
Story: Rabbi Avraham David of Buchach, a leading Galician halachist, started his rabbinic career in Yazlovich in 1790. He served there for twenty-four years, during which time he recorded daily every new Torah insight that came to him. Across his full fifty-year rabbinate this discipline produced tens of thousands of pages of chiddushim on the four parts of Shulchan Aruch, Tanach, and Talmud.
Tags: galicia, yazlovich, rabbinate, avraham david of buchach

Title: R' Avraham of Kalisk letter endorsing Alter Rebbe's leadership
Summary: On 11 Menachem Av 5550 R' Avraham of Kalisk wrote to chassidim abroad endorsing the Alter Rebbe's leadership over the chassidic community.
Story: Continuing the practice begun by R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk before his passing, R' Avraham of Kalisk wrote regularly to Russian chassidim urging them to attach themselves to the Alter Rebbe. In this 5550 letter he described the Alter Rebbe as the great rabbi 'this Sinai' through whose light they would see eternal light and the treasury of life and peace.
Tags: avraham of kalisk, alter rebbe, chassidic leadership, russia, endorsement letters

Title: Alter Rebbe's writings begin spreading widely
Summary: According to HaYom Yom, in 5551 (1791) the Alter Rebbe's writings in revealed and hidden Torah began spreading broadly.
Story: This pre-dated the first printing of Tanya by several years. By summer 5552 (1792), the work had already become publicly known under the name 'Tanya', and by 5553 (1793) the Alter Rebbe was citing and discussing it in his Tishrei–Kislev maamarim.
Tags: alter rebbe, hayom yom, tanya, nigleh, nistar

Title: First Haggadah printed in Hrodna
Summary: An early Russian-imprint Haggadah with Yiddish translation in tzena u'rena script appeared in Hrodna in 5551.
Story: In 5551 (1791), one of the first Haggadot ever printed in the Russian Empire was issued in Hrodna by the HaMelech press. It presented Hebrew text alongside a Yiddish translation in tzena u'rena script, side by side, marking an early Russian milestone in Haggadah printing.
Tags: haggadah, hrodna, russia, yiddish-translation

Title: Passing of R. Baruch, father of the Alter Rebbe
Summary: R. Baruch, the father of the Alter Rebbe, passed away in Tishrei 5552 (autumn 1791).
Story: Dating internal evidence in the Alter Rebbe's responsum on matza-baking practices relies on this yahrtzeit: since he still signs himself as 'son of my master and teacher R. Baruch,' the responsum predates Tishrei 5552, placing the change in matza-baking custom around 1772.
Tags: r. baruch, alter rebbe, father, yahrtzeit

Title: R' Avraham of Kalisk letter (5551) praising Alter Rebbe
Summary: In 5551 R' Avraham of Kalisk wrote praising the Alter Rebbe as a wondrous counselor and urging chassidim to seek his guidance in all matters.
Story: R' Avraham of Kalisk continued his yearly campaign of letters endorsing the Alter Rebbe's leadership. In 5551 he wrote that the Alter Rebbe was beloved and treasured, a holy man of God, a wondrous counselor who would show chassidim the way of God, and that they should listen to him.
Tags: avraham of kalisk, alter rebbe, chassidic leadership, endorsement letters

Title: Plague and quarantine begin in Tiberias
Summary: An epidemic struck Tiberias in Adar 5551, prompting the closure of the city gates for several months.
Story: The Chasidic letters from Tiberias describe a plague and quarantine that began in Adar 5551 and continued until the city gates were reopened in Tammuz. The community wrote of severe financial distress during the lockdown, when 'silver had no outlet.' The arrival of the shadar R' Meir of Bychov shortly after the gates reopened brought desperately needed relief.
Tags: plague, tiberias, quarantine

Title: R' Yoel Smolyaner returns to Eretz Yisrael after delayed shlichut
Summary: R' Yoel Smolyaner arrived back in Eretz Yisrael on 10 Nissan 5551 after his long delayed emissary mission.
Story: Sent abroad as the shadar for 5550, R' Yoel Smolyaner only returned to Eretz Yisrael on 10 Nissan 5551, well behind schedule. R' Avraham of Kalisk explicitly addressed 'the reason for the delay' in correspondence with the overseas overseers. His late arrival amid the Tiberias plague was contrasted with the more timely return of his successor R' Meir of Bychov.
Tags: yoel smolyaner, shadar, tiberias

Title: Tiberias plague quarantine ends as city gates reopen
Summary: The city gates of Tiberias were reopened in Tammuz 5551 after months of plague quarantine.
Story: After the Adar–Tammuz 5551 plague quarantine, Tiberias's gates were reopened in Tammuz. The Chasidic community wrote letters of thanksgiving to its overseas supporters describing the lifting of the closure. The timely arrival of the shadar R' Meir of Bychov soon after was seen as a divine deliverance.
Tags: plague, tiberias, quarantine

Title: R' Meir of Bychov returns from his first shlichut in Av 5551
Summary: R' Meir of Bychov returned to Eretz Yisrael as the shadar of 5551 in Menachem Av of that year.
Story: Having departed in summer 5549, R' Meir returned to Eretz Yisrael in Menachem Av 5551 as the shadar 'of this year.' His on-time return, immediately following the lifting of the Tiberias plague quarantine in Tammuz, was greeted as a salvation by the Chasidic community. A general letter from the Tiberias Chasidim and a separate letter from R' Avraham of Kalisk both announced his arrival.
Tags: meir of bychov, shadar, tiberias, av 5551

Title: Death of R' Baruch, father of the Alter Rebbe
Summary: R' Yisrael Baruch ben Avraham, father of the Alter Rebbe, died on 8 Tishrei 5552 in Sulish, Hungary.
Story: After self-exile in his later years, R' Baruch settled in the town of Sulish (Sulish/Sulez) in Hungary, where he died on 8 Tishrei 5552 (September 16, 1791). His tombstone inscription records his name as 'Yisrael Baruch ben Avraham' — supporting the tradition reported in Eden Tzion that he originally bore the name Yisrael but dropped it after joining the Baal Shem Tov's circle out of deference to his teacher.
Tags: alter rebbe, family, hungary, sulish

Title: Alter Rebbe releases Tanya for copying and distribution
Summary: In 5552 the Alter Rebbe handed over the Tanya manuscript for copying and circulation.
Story: In 5552 (1792) R' Schneur Zalman released the Likutei Amarim (Tanya) for copying and dissemination. In its 'Introduction of the Compiler' he explained that the work collected his answers to the questions chassidim brought him in private audience, since 'time no longer permits' him to address each one individually — directly linking the Tanya's publication to the Liozna takanos limiting yechidus.
Tags: tanya, manuscript, yechidut, liozna

Title: Chabad community established in Vidz, Lithuania
Summary: A Chabad community existed in Vidz no later than 5552, with R' Moshe ben Yitzchak as its head and Eretz Yisrael fund gabbai.
Story: Records of donations to the Chassidim settled in Tiberias, collected by R' Moshe ben Yitzchak of Vidz, prove that a Chabad kehilla functioned in Vidz from 5552 onward. Dozens of donors from Vidz are listed in the receipts covering the years 5552–5557 (1792–1797). The community grew under his leadership during this period.
Tags: vidz, lithuania, eretz yisrael fund, moshe ben yitzchak

Title: Likutim Yekarim — early Baal Shem Tov teachings printed in Lvov
Summary: Likutim Yekarim, gathering Baal Shem Tov's teachings, was printed in Lvov in 5552.
Story: Likutim Yekarim, an early compilation of the Baal Shem Tov's teachings together with those of his disciples, was printed in Lvov in 5552 (1792). It appeared roughly twelve years after the first printed works of his disciple Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polonne.
Tags: baal shem tov, likutim, lvov

Title: Maggid Devarav L'Yaakov printed in Lvov
Summary: A third edition of Maggid Devarav L'Yaakov was issued in Lvov in 5552.
Story: The Maggid's collected teachings appeared again in 1792, this time in Lvov. The book had now spread well beyond its original Volhynian center.
Tags: maggid of mezeritch, lvov, poland

Title: Passing of R' Baruch, father of the Alter Rebbe
Summary: R' Baruch, father of the Alter Rebbe of Chabad, passed away in 5552.
Story: Rabbi Baruch, father of Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi (the Alter Rebbe), died in 5552 (1791/92). His name was carried by his great-grandson Baruch Shalom, eldest son of the Tzemach Tzedek, in line with the Ashkenazi practice of naming a child after a deceased relative.
Tags: baruch, alter-rebbe, schneersohn, ancestry

Title: R' Shlomo of Karlin killed in Ludmir
Summary: R' Shlomo of Karlin was killed in Ludmir in 5552.
Story: In 5552 (1792) R' Shlomo of Karlin was killed in Ludmir. In subsequent years two of his leading disciples — R' Mordechai of Lechovich and R' Asher son of R' Aharon HaGadol of Stolin — would return to settle in White Russia and Lithuania, laying foundations for the spread of general chassidut into the region after 19 Kislev 5559.
Tags: r' shlomo of karlin, ludmir, death

Title: Tanya circulates widely in handwritten copies among chassidim
Summary: Around 5552 the Alter Rebbe's kuntreisim that became the Tanya were already in widespread manuscript circulation among chassidim.
Story: Around the year 5552 (1792), the kuntreisim that would later be printed as the Tanya were disseminated widely among Rabbi Schneur Zalman's chassidim. The work spread through many handwritten copies made by different scribes, leading to an accumulation of textual errors. This proliferation of corrupted copies eventually persuaded the Alter Rebbe to authorize a definitive printed edition of the work.
Tags: tanya, alter rebbe, chassidut, manuscript, kuntreisim

Title: Tanya first publicly circulated in manuscript
Summary: The Tanya was first circulated publicly in manuscript copies around the year 5552.
Story: Around 5552 (1792), Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi's Tanya began circulating publicly in handwritten manuscript copies. The Alter Rebbe initially did not wish to print it, but the proliferation of copyists' errors eventually persuaded him to release it to the printers.
Tags: tanya, alter rebbe, chabad, manuscript

Title: Rebbetzin Devorah Leah passes on Tzom Gedaliah
Summary: Rebbetzin Devorah Leah, daughter of the Alter Rebbe, passed away on Tzom Gedaliah 5553 (September 1792).
Story: When the Tzemach Tzedek was three years old, on Tzom Gedaliah 5553, his mother Rebbetzin Devorah Leah, daughter of the Alter Rebbe, passed away. From that point he was raised in the household of his grandfather the Alter Rebbe.
Tags: devorah leah, alter rebbe, tzom gedaliah, tzemach tzedek mother

Title: R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen returns to Tiberias from three-year mission
Summary: R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen returns to Tiberias for the Shabbat between Yom Kippur and Sukkot of 5553.
Story: After three years abroad, R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen reached Tiberias for the Shabbat between Yom Kippur and Sukkot 5553. In a letter to the chassidim in Russia he announced his return, writing that 'we have arrived in the holy city safely, all is peace.'
Tags: shlomo zalman hakohen, tiberias, shadar, russia, chassidim

Title: Earliest dated Alter Rebbe maamar manuscripts
Summary: Starting in 5553 (1793), dated manuscripts of the Alter Rebbe's maamarim are extant for every successive year through 5572 (1812).
Story: The earliest dated discourse in the surviving manuscripts is from the beginning of 5553. From this year onward, dated discourses exist continuously, marking the year in which Chabad teaching began to spread broadly in writing alongside the public release of Tanya.
Tags: alter rebbe, maamarim, manuscripts, tanya

Title: R' Avraham of Kalisk letter (9 Adar 5553)
Summary: On 9 Adar 5553 R' Avraham of Kalisk wrote praising the Alter Rebbe as one whose mouth produces pearls.
Story: In his 9 Adar 5553 letter, R' Avraham of Kalisk shortened his own writing because the chassidim had with them the holy Alter Rebbe, who waters mountains from his lofts, and from the fruit of whose deeds the land is satisfied.
Tags: avraham of kalisk, alter rebbe, endorsement letters, chassidic leadership

Title: Alter Rebbe publishes Hilchos Talmud Torah in Shklov
Summary: The Alter Rebbe released Hilchos Talmud Torah in Shklov in 1794, his first published work, with approbations but without naming the author.
Story: This 35-folio Shklov edition was the first book the Alter Rebbe sent to press—more than two years before his Tanya appeared. He had it published anonymously, with approbations from other authorities, foreshadowing the pattern of his later halachic publications.
Tags: alter rebbe, shklov, first publication, talmud torah

Title: First Chassidic Haggadah 'Chelkat Binyamin' by Binyamin of Zalozitz printed in Lvov
Summary: Binyamin of Zalozitz, a disciple of the Maggid of Zlotchov, published the first Chassidic Haggadah commentary 'Chelkat Binyamin' in Lvov.
Story: In 5554 (1794), 'Chelkat Binyamin', the first published Chassidic Haggadah commentary, was issued in Lvov by Rabbi Binyamin, maggid of Zalozitz, a leading disciple of Rabbi Yechiel Michel of Zlotchov. The 25-leaf quarto included a transcription of the Haggadah with the Kavanot of the Arizal. It marked a milestone in the printed dissemination of Chassidic teachings on the Passover liturgy.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, binyamin of zalozitz, lvov, galicia, ari

Title: Hilchos Talmud Torah first printed
Summary: The Alter Rebbe's Hilchos Talmud Torah, part of his kuntreisim of essential laws, was first printed in 5554 (1794).
Story: Unlike most of the other kuntreisim, which mainly summarize earlier poskim, Hilchos Talmud Torah contains many original rulings the Alter Rebbe derived from Talmudic sugyos in his Kuntres Acharon. Its first printing in 5554 provides one of the few firm dating anchors for the middle period of his halachic writing.
