The work was composed in the same era as the other Hilchos Hatzrichos compilations of 5545-5550.
Tags: alter rebbe, talmud torah, halacha, shulchan aruch

Title: Hilchot Talmud Torah printed in Shklov
Summary: The Alter Rebbe's Hilchot Talmud Torah was printed in Shklov in 5554.
Story: Before publishing the Tanya, the Alter Rebbe issued several of his halachic works. Hilchot Talmud Torah, his treatise on the laws of Torah study, was printed in Shklov in 1794.
Tags: alter rebbe, shklov, halacha

Title: Keser Shem Tov first edition published in Zolkiew
Summary: The first edition of Keser Shem Tov, teachings of the Baal Shem Tov, was published in Zolkiew in 5554.
Story: In 5554 (1794), the first edition of Keser Shem Tov, a collection of teachings of Rabbi Yisrael Baal Shem Tov, was published in Zolkiew. The Lubavitch Library preserves a copy of this first edition. The book is among the earliest printed sources for the Baal Shem Tov's teachings.
Tags: baal shem tov, zolkiew, chassidus

Title: Keter Shem Tov first edition printed in Zolkva
Summary: The first edition of Keter Shem Tov, an anthology of teachings of the Baal Shem Tov, was published in Zolkva in 1794.
Story: The 1794 Zolkva edition gathered teachings attributed to the Baal Shem Tov into one of the early printed Chassidic anthologies. It remains a foundational source for Baal Shem Tov's Torah and a benchmark text in the early Chassidic library.
Tags: baal shem tov, zolkva, first edition, keter shem tov

Title: Keter Shem Tov part 1 printed in Zhovkva
Summary: Keter Shem Tov part 1, anthology of Baal Shem Tov teachings, was printed in Zhovkva in 5554.
Story: Keter Shem Tov, an anthology of the Baal Shem Tov's teachings, was first printed in Zhovkva (Zalkva). Part 1 appeared in 5554 (1794) and Part 2 the following year, becoming one of the most widely studied collections of Baal Shem Tov teachings.
Tags: baal shem tov, keter shem tov, zhovkva

Title: Keter Shem Tov volume 1 printed in Zolkiew
Summary: The first volume of Keter Shem Tov, the main anthology of Baal Shem Tov teachings, appeared in Zolkiew in 5554.
Story: Keter Shem Tov, the principal anthology of teachings attributed to the Baal Shem Tov, was first published in Zolkiew in two parts. Volume one appeared in 1794, drawing on earlier printed Chassidic works.
Tags: baal shem tov, keter shem tov, zolkiew

Title: Ladino Haggadah 'Hamon Chogeg' by Elisha Chabilyo printed in Livorno
Summary: Elisha Chabilyo published 'Sefer Hamon Chogeg', a Haggadah with Ladino translation and two Hebrew commentaries, in Livorno.
Story: In 5554 (1794), Elisha Chabilyo authored 'Sefer Hamon Chogeg' which was printed in Livorno, Italy. The work presented the text of the Haggadah alongside a Ladino translation, with two Hebrew commentaries — one based on the plain meaning and the other on ethical instruction. The Hebrew original and Ladino translation were printed in vocalized square letters, passage by passage.
Tags: haggadah, ladino, livorno, italy, sephardic

Title: Noam Elimelech printed in Slavuta
Summary: Noam Elimelech by Rabbi Elimelech of Lizhensk was printed in Slavuta in 5554.
Story: Noam Elimelech, one of the foundational works of Polish chassidut by Rabbi Elimelech of Lizhensk, was printed in Slavuta in 5554 (1794), edited and published by his disciple Rabbi Zecharia Mendel of Yaroslav.
Tags: noam elimelech, elimelech of lizhensk, slavuta

Title: Polish Hasidim led by R' Yaakov Shimshon settle in Tiberias
Summary: A group of Polish Hasidim led by R' Yaakov Shimshon of Shepetivka made aliyah and settled in Tiberias.
Story: In 5554 (1794), several Hasidim from Poland led by R' Yaakov Shimshon of Shepetivka ascended to the Holy Land and settled in Tiberias. R' Avraham of Kalisk then turned to them and to the Hasidic communities in Volhynia and Poland, asking them to contribute proportionately to the Hasidic Yishuv. This aliyah eventually triggered demands for a separate Polish-Volhynian kollel in Tiberias.
Tags: aliyah, tiberias, yaakov shimshon of shepetivka, poland, volhynia

Title: R' Avraham of Kalisk letter (5554) on Alter Rebbe's burdens
Summary: In a 5554 letter R' Avraham of Kalisk described how the Alter Rebbe was constantly besieged by people seeking guidance from morning to evening.
Story: In this letter (interpreted as 5554 because it elaborates on the Takanot Laznia of 5553), R' Avraham of Kalisk described the Alter Rebbe as the divine leader upon whom bundles of troubles from people hovered all day, who was approached by every troubled person and creditor seeking guidance in matters great and small.
Tags: avraham of kalisk, alter rebbe, takanot laznia, chassidic leadership

Title: R. Yaakov Mordechai Twer born in Mogilev
Summary: R. Yaakov Mordechai Twer, a descendant of MaHaRIL (brother of the Alter Rebbe), was born in Mogilev in 5554 (c. 1794).
Story: The 1839 Montefiore census lists him as age 45 having been born in Mogilev, allowing reconstruction of his birth year. He would later make aliyah and become the patriarch of the Brimat, Saulson, Singer and Grossman families in Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: yaakov mordechai twer, mogilev, birth, chabad family

Title: Alter Rebbe delivers the 'Frumer Vaera' discourse
Summary: The Alter Rebbe delivered the famous 'Frumer Vaera' discourse on Shabbat Parshat Vaera 5554.
Story: The discourse known as 'Der Frumer Vaera,' given on Shabbat Parshat Vaera 5554 (January 1794), survived in MaharI"L's transcript with handwritten glosses by the Alter Rebbe himself — one of the very few such doubly-authenticated manuscripts to reach later generations. It became a touchstone for understanding how the Alter Rebbe edited the discourses his brother recorded for him.
Tags: alter rebbe, chassidus, discourse, manuscript

Title: Birth of Rabbi Hillel of Paritch
Summary: Rabbi Hillel ben Meir HaLevi Malisov, later known as 'Rabbi Hillel Paritcher,' is born in 5555.
Story: The great chossid, mekubal and author of Pelach HaRimon was born in 5555 (1795) to Rabbi Meir HaLevi of Alisov. He would become one of the most prominent figures of early Chabad chassidus and a senior mashpia, later serving as mara d'asra of Babruysk after Rabbi Baruch Mordechai departed for Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: hillel of paritch, chabad chassidim, birth, kabbalah

Title: Chassidic minyan in Vilna moves to R' Meir Refael's home
Summary: The Chabad minyan in Vilna relocated from R' Eliezer ben Chaim's house to R' Meir Refael's home, with kahal approval.
Story: Around 5555, the Vilna Chassidic minyan moved from the home of R' Eliezer ben Chaim to the home of R' Meir Refael's. The transfer was approved by Vilna kahal head R' Moshe ben Asher. This arrangement continued until persecutions intensified in 5557.
Tags: vilna, minyan, meir refaels, eliezer ben chaim

Title: Keter Shem Tov volume 2 printed in Zolkiew
Summary: The second volume of Keter Shem Tov was printed in Zolkiew in 5555.
Story: The companion volume to Keter Shem Tov part one appeared in Zolkiew in 1795. Together the two volumes became the standard collection of the Baal Shem Tov's recorded teachings.
Tags: baal shem tov, keter shem tov, zolkiew

Title: Luach Birchas Hanehenin first printed
Summary: The Alter Rebbe's 'Luach Birchas Hanehenin', a kuntres on the laws of berachos over food, was first printed around 5555 (1795).
Story: This work was printed several times together with Seder Netilas Yadayim Lese'udah and likely edited in the same period. It would later be supplanted by a revised version, 'Seder Birchas Hanehenin', integrated into the Alter Rebbe's Siddur of 5563. The revised edition departed from the Magen Avraham in several places based on study of the rishonim.
Tags: alter rebbe, berachos, birchas hanehenin, halacha

Title: R' Avraham of Kalisk winter letter (5555)
Summary: In winter 5555 R' Avraham of Kalisk again wrote endorsing the Alter Rebbe as the practical halachic authority and divinely beloved.
Story: R' Avraham of Kalisk continued in winter 5555 with another letter to the Russian chassidim. He emphasized that for practical halachic guidance the chassidim had with them the great rabbi, beloved of God, the renowned holy one - the Alter Rebbe - whose honor was the honor of the Omnipresent.
Tags: avraham of kalisk, alter rebbe, endorsement letters

Title: Tzava'at HaRivash printed in Zhovkva
Summary: Tzava'at HaRivash, attributed to the Baal Shem Tov, was printed in Zhovkva in 5555.
Story: Tzava'at HaRivash, a collection of practices and teachings attributed to the Baal Shem Tov, was printed in Zhovkva in 5555 (1795). This work would later become a flashpoint of controversy when Avigdor of Pinsk cited it in his denunciations against the Alter Rebbe.
Tags: baal shem tov, tzavaat harivash, zhovkva

Title: Alter Rebbe revises Tanya and sends to press
Summary: In 5556, the Alter Rebbe revised the Tanya anew and sent it to the printer.
Story: In 5556 (1796), Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi revised and completed the Tanya, then sent it to the press in Slavuta. The printing was completed on 20 Kislev 5557 (1796).
Tags: tanya, alter rebbe, slavuta

Title: Alter Rebbe sends 800 rubles via R' Aryeh Leib to fund Vilna Chassidim
Summary: R' Aryeh Leib ben Yehoshua Zelig brought 800 ruble assignats from the Alter Rebbe to support the Vilna Chassidic kehilla.
Story: Around 5556, R' Aryeh Leib ben Yehoshua Zelig of Vilna drew close to Chassidus and traveled three times to the Alter Rebbe in Liozna. The Rebbe entrusted him with a letter and 800 ruble assignats to be delivered to R' Nachum ben Yitzchak, treasurer of the Vilna Chassidic kehilla. Around the same time R' Meir Refael's received two letters from the Rebbe.
Tags: vilna, aryeh leib, alter rebbe, funding

Title: Alter Rebbe sends two shadarim to Volhynia to mediate kollel dispute
Summary: The Alter Rebbe dispatched two shadarim to Volhynia in winter to mediate the dispute over the separate Volhynia-Poland kollel in Tiberias.
Story: In winter 5556 (1796), the Alter Rebbe wrote about the 'great noise' that had erupted over the Eretz Yisrael funds from Volhynia and Ukraine, where new voices were challenging the long-standing arrangement of channeling all monies through R' Avraham of Kalisk. He dispatched two shadarim, R' Dovber of Dubrovna and R' Refael, to Volhynia to negotiate a compromise. The talks eventually produced an agreement that Volhynia's funds would be transported separately by a Polish shadar from Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: alter rebbe, shadarim, volhynia, kollel volhyn, avraham of kalisk, tiberias

Title: First edition of Tanya printed in Slavita
Summary: The Tanya of the Alter Rebbe was first printed in Slavita in 5556–5557 (1796–1797).
Story: Tradition suggests that the partners R' Shalom Shachna (the Alter Rebbe's son-in-law) and R' Mordechai HaLevi Horowitz jointly printed the first edition of Tanya in Slavita. They remained occupied with that print shop throughout their lives. This edition is the foundational text of Chabad Chasidic teaching.
Tags: tanya, slavita, alter rebbe, russia, ukraine, mordechai halevi horowitz, shalom shachna

Title: Manuscript of Tanya copied with colophon Tammuz 1796
Summary: A manuscript volume containing an early version of the Tanya was completed in Tammuz 5556 (1796).
Story: This manuscript, held as collection no. 268 in the library, contains an early recension of the Tanya alongside discourses of the Alter Rebbe and the Mitteler Rebbe. Its colophon dates the copying to Tammuz 5556, predating the printed first edition by roughly a year.
Tags: alter rebbe, tanya, manuscript, early version

Title: R' Mordechai of Neskhiz issues general appeal for Eretz Yisrael fund
Summary: R' Mordechai of Neskhiz issued a general appeal for the Eretz Yisrael fund, joined by the Chozeh of Lublin.
Story: In 5556 (1796), R' Mordechai of Neskhiz published a general appeal regarding the dire poverty of the Hasidic Yishuv in Eretz Yisrael, noting that he had previously stayed clear of fundraising. The Chozeh of Lublin joined the appeal, writing that Polish Jewry had until now lacked someone to organize collections as White Russia had. This launched a parallel Polish-Volhynian fundraising effort outside the Alter Rebbe's network.
Tags: fundraising, mordechai of neskhiz, yaakov yitzchak chozeh of lublin, poland, tiberias

Title: Tanya first printed
Summary: The Alter Rebbe's Tanya appears in print for the first time in 5557, formalizing the Chabad approach to Chassidic thought.
Story: In 5557, Rabbi Schneur Zalman's Tanya appeared in print for the first time, presenting his systematic Chabad approach to Chassidism. The same year, Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk launched a public critique of the Tanya's method, drawing in other Maggid disciples in Volhynia and Poland. The dispute lasted years and ultimately crystallized the separation between general Chassidism and the distinct Chabad movement.
Tags: tanya, schneur zalman, chabad chassidut, slavita

Title: MaharI"L co-signs psher ruling for Horodishtch community
Summary: MaharI"L signed a community settlement document at the Alter Rebbe's direction on 25 Tevet 5556.
Story: On 25 Tevet 5556 (January 5, 1796), MaharI"L of Yanovich signed a written compromise ruling for the community of Horodishtch, noting that 'all the above was done by law and by settlement, as my brother and master the Rabbi instructed me, with the consent of the entire community.' The document, preserved in the genizah, shows the Alter Rebbe routing communal halachic work through his trusted younger brother.
Tags: mahari"l, alter rebbe, horodishtch, halacha

Title: Alter Rebbe reaffirms Liozna takanos at handover of Tanya for print
Summary: On 27 Adar I 5556 the Alter Rebbe and chassidic leaders re-signed the Liozna takanos.
Story: On 27 Adar I 5556 (March 7, 1796), at the same time the Tanya was given to the printers, the Alter Rebbe re-confirmed his signature on the Liozna takanos and added new provisions, co-signed by leading chassidim including R' Yisrael ben Yitzchak of Kapust. The takanos restricted how often chassidim could come to him and limited entry to yechidut.
Tags: liozna takanos, tanya, yechidut, r' yisrael yaffe, kapust

Title: First printing of Tanya completed in Slavuta
Summary: The first printing of the Tanya was completed on 20 Kislev 5557.
Story: The first printing of the Tanya — comprising Likutei Amarim and Sha'ar HaYichud VeHa'emunah — was completed on 20 Kislev 5557 (December 1796) in Slavuta. The book was eagerly received by chassidim and reprinted at least six times in its first decade.
Tags: tanya, alter rebbe, slavuta, kislev

Title: Tanya first edition printed in Slavita
Summary: The first edition of the Tanya was completed in Slavita on 20 Kislev 5557.
Story: Printing of the foundational Chabad text, the Tanya, began in Elul 5556 (Aug 1796) in Slavita and concluded on 20 Kislev 5557 (Dec 19, 1796), at which point a short list of corrections was appended. Two surviving copies bear witness to this first printing.
Tags: alter rebbe, tanya, slavita, chabad foundation

Title: Printing of the Tanya completed
Summary: The first printing of the Tanya was completed on 20 Kislev 5557.
Story: After the manuscript was handed to the printer in late 5556, the first edition of the Tanya was completed on 20 Kislev 5557 (December 20, 1796). The publication marked the formal release of the Alter Rebbe's foundational Chabad text and signaled a new stage in chassidic instruction by the written word.
Tags: tanya, print, kapust, r' yisrael yaffe, likutei amarim

Title: Alter Rebbe writes letter to chassidim of Vilna defending the movement
Summary: In 1797 the Alter Rebbe wrote to the chassidim of Vilna recounting the rebuffed attempts to debate the Vilna Gaon a quarter-century earlier.
Story: The letter (Iggeret 34) is a key source for the early conflict, describing how the Vilna Gaon twice closed his door on R. Menachem Mendel and the Alter Rebbe and left town to avoid public debate. It frames the chassidic response to renewed persecution near the end of the century.
Tags: alter rebbe, vilna, vilna gaon, mitnagdim, letter

Title: Alter Rebbe writes Seder Hachnasas Shabbos and Hilchasa Rabsa LeShabsa
Summary: In 5557 the Alter Rebbe wrote his Seder Hachnasas Shabbos and Hilchasa Rabsa LeShabsa, as recorded in a contemporary manuscript index.
Story: Manuscript 1064, written close to the Alter Rebbe's lifetime, lists 'Hilchasa Rabsa LeShabsa' under the year 5557. These laws did not appear in the first three editions of his Siddur (printed in Shklov and Kapust during his lifetime) but were later printed on separate folios. They form one of the latest precisely dated kuntreisim of the Alter Rebbe's middle period.
Tags: alter rebbe, shabbos, halacha, shulchan aruch

Title: First printed edition of Tanya issued in Slavita
Summary: The Tanya was first printed in Slavita in 5557 (1797), marking the foundational publication of Chabad chassidic thought.
Story: The 86-folio Slavita edition is the first printed Tanya and the first to publicly transmit the Alter Rebbe's systematic work on chassidic psychology and avodah. Within the next decade the book would be reprinted at least six more times in Zhalkva, Shklov, and elsewhere.
Tags: alter rebbe, tanya, slavita, first edition, chassidic literature

Title: First printing of the Tanya
Summary: The Alter Rebbe's foundational chassidic work, the Tanya, is printed in winter 5557.
Story: During the winter of 5557 the Alter Rebbe published the Tanya, formalizing the Chabad approach to chassidic teachings in print. Until this point no doctrinal disputes had surfaced between him and R' Avraham of Kalisk, but the printing immediately drew a sharp critical response from R' Avraham, who argued that disseminating intellectual chassidic doctrine broadly contradicted the path of the Maggid of Mezritch.
Tags: tanya, alter rebbe, schneur zalman of liadi, chabad, chassidut, sefer shel beinonim

Title: R' Asher of Stolin's letter on R' Mordechai of Neskhiz's new role
Summary: R' Asher of Stolin wrote to R' Baruch of Mezhibuzh that R' Mordechai of Neskhiz was now involved in Eretz Yisrael fundraising.
Story: In winter 5557 (1797), R' Asher of Stolin wrote a letter to R' Baruch of Mezhibuzh describing how R' Mordechai of Neskhiz had received a letter from R' Avraham of Kalisk and the rav of Shepetivka about a new fundraising effort, and had begun involving himself for the first time. The letter also shows that the dispute over the proposed separate Volhynia-Poland kollel in Tiberias was still active a year after the Alter Rebbe's mediation attempt.
Tags: asher of stolin, mordechai of neskhiz, fundraising, letter, kollel volhyn

Title: R' Avraham of Kalisk critiques the Tanya in writing
Summary: After the Tanya's printing, R' Avraham of Kalisk writes a long letter critiquing the work and the Chabad doctrinal approach.
Story: Following the appearance of the Tanya in 5557, R' Avraham of Kalisk wrote to the Alter Rebbe that he found no value in 'the Book of the Beinonim' for saving souls, since common chassidim need only faith in their teachers, not intellectual analysis. He simultaneously addressed the Russian chassidic community, urging that chassidic texts be gathered and kept hidden among the spiritually refined rather than studied broadly. He grounded his position on the rabbinic teaching 'the righteous shall live by his faith.'
Tags: avraham of kalisk, alter rebbe, tanya, chassidut, dispute, maggid of mezritch, russia

Title: Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk opposes the Tanya's approach
Summary: In 5557, Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk publicly opposes the Alter Rebbe's Chabad approach, drawing other Maggid disciples into a multi-year dispute.
Story: Soon after the Tanya was printed in 5557, Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk—then leading Chassidim in Eretz Yisrael—came out publicly against its method. Disciples of the Maggid in Volhynia and Poland were drawn into the dispute, which continued for years and eventually produced a permanent split between general Chassidism and Chabad. Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev took the Alter Rebbe's side, writing that the Tanya approach reflected 'the entire essence of the Maggid's own conduct.'
Tags: avraham of kalisk, schneur zalman, tanya, levi yitzchak of berditchev, chabad chassidut, eretz yisrael

Title: Tanya first edition printed in Slavita
Summary: The first edition of the Tanya by the Alter Rebbe was printed in Slavita in 5557.
Story: In 5557 (1797), the first edition of the Tanya, the foundational work of Chabad Chassidic thought by Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, was printed in Slavita. The Lubavitch Library preserves a copy of this first edition. The book is one of Chabad's central canonical texts.
Tags: tanya, alter rebbe, slavita

Title: Gabbaim of old Vilna beis midrash decide to oppress Chassidim
Summary: On 18 Tishrei 5558 the gabbaim of the old beis midrash in Vilna resolved to pressure the Chassidim to abandon their nusach and not raise voices in prayer.
Story: On the second day of Chol HaMoed Sukkos 5558, one day before the Vilna Gaon's passing, the gabbaim of the Old Kloiz met to address what they viewed as the Chassidic deviation in prayer. They resolved to harass the 'Karliner' faction, deny them honors and aliyos, and force them to use the standard nusach without raising their voices. This formalized the institutional opposition in Vilna.
Tags: vilna, mitnagdim, cherem, sukkos, beis midrash

Title: Passing of the Vilna Gaon (Gra)
Summary: Rabbi Eliyahu of Vilna, the Vilna Gaon, passed away on 19 Tishrei 5558 (3rd day of Chol HaMoed Sukkos).
Story: The Vilna Gaon, leader of the Mitnagdim, died on the third day of Chol HaMoed Sukkos 5558. His death emboldened R' Moshe ben Asher and other opponents in Vilna to intensify their campaign against the Chassidim. The day after his passing they declared a cherem against the Chabad kehilla.
Tags: vilna, vilna gaon, gra, mitnagdim

Title: Vilna kahal declares cherem against the Chassidim on Hoshana Rabba
Summary: On Hoshana Rabba 5558 Vilna kahal proclaimed a cherem on the Chassidim, treating any follower as a non-Jew and authorizing a special committee against them.
Story: One day after the Vilna Gaon's burial, the Vilna kahal proclaimed a sweeping cherem on the Chassidim of the city. The decree, read in every shul amid shofar blasts and extinguished candles, declared Chassidim excommunicated, denied them communal standing, and barred their bread and wine. A committee of five empowered as 'rodef' was authorized to act against them, marking the legal start of the Vilna persecution.
Tags: vilna, cherem, mitnagdim, hoshana rabba, moshe ben asher

Title: Alter Rebbe arrested and taken to St. Petersburg
Summary: At the start of 5559 the Alter Rebbe was arrested and sent to St. Petersburg for interrogation.
Story: At the beginning of 5559 (autumn 1798) the Alter Rebbe was arrested following the mitnagdim's denunciation and immediately sent to the capital for questioning, while interrogations of the Vilna chassidim arrested with him began in Vilna itself. Some were later sent toward St. Petersburg but recalled to Vilna en route.
Tags: arrest, st petersburg, first imprisonment, vilna, interrogation

Title: Alter Rebbe freed from czarist imprisonment
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman is freed from czarist prison, beginning a new era of deeper public chasidic teaching.
Story: The seventh Rebbe identified this as a major turning point in the dissemination of chasidic teachings — the moment when Chasidut began to reach 'chutzah,' outside. The arc continued through the 1897 yeshivah and the Riga-era translations.
Tags: alter-rebbe, schneur-zalman, russia, yud-tes-kislev

Title: Alter Rebbe freed from czarist prison; chasidic teaching expands
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi is freed from czarist prison and begins teaching maamarim with deeper explanations.
Story: The seventh Rebbe identified the 1798 release as the second transformational point in disseminating chasidic teachings. 'This began a new stage, when the teachings went chutzah, outside.' The 1897 founding of Tomchei Temimim and the later translation of maamarim into other languages built on the same trajectory.
Tags: alter rebbe, schneur zalman, prison, russia, maamarim

Title: Alter Rebbe testifies under interrogation during his Petersburg imprisonment
Summary: During his 1798 imprisonment, the Alter Rebbe testified that at about age twenty he had left Vitebsk for Mezeritch to study Kabbalah under the Maggid.
Story: Among the autobiographical testimony recorded by the Russian authorities, the Alter Rebbe describes his discipleship of the Maggid as the formative period of his life. The recorded testimony is preserved in his collected letters and is a primary biographical source for his early years.
Tags: alter rebbe, petersburg, imprisonment, interrogation, kabbalah, mezeritch

Title: Alter Rebbe writes again to Vilna chassidim describing flight to Rovno
Summary: In summer 1798 the Alter Rebbe sent a second letter to the chassidim of Vilna recalling the 1772 gathering at Rovno around the Maggid.
Story: The letter narrates how the Volyn tzaddikim, unable to remain in their homes amid persecution, fled to the Maggid in Rovno to plan a response. It supplements the earlier 1797 letter and reinforces the chassidic memory of the foundational conflict.
Tags: alter rebbe, vilna, rovno, letter, mitnagdim

Title: Alter Rebbe's first arrest – Tzok HaItim
Summary: The Alter Rebbe is arrested in 5559, leaving him unable to respond to correspondence until 5560.
Story: In 5559 the Alter Rebbe was arrested during what he later called 'tzok haitim' – the pressing times. As a result, although R' Avraham of Kalisk's letter had reached him in 5558, he was unable to compose a proper reply until 5560. This first imprisonment in Petersburg is the famous episode that Chabad commemorates each Yud-Tes Kislev as the day of his miraculous liberation.
Tags: alter rebbe, schneur zalman of liadi, arrest, russia, petersburg, tzok haitim, imprisonment

Title: Arrest of Alter Rebbe at end of Sukkot 5559
Summary: At the end of Sukkot 5559, officers arrived to arrest the Alter Rebbe and transport him to Petersburg.
Story: In the last days of Sukkot 5559 (autumn 1798), Russian officers came to arrest Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi and transport him to Petersburg for interrogation, in execution of the Tsar's order. He was sent under guard of an officer and two soldiers.
Tags: alter rebbe, arrest, sukkot, liozna

Title: Arrest of Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi
Summary: Chabad's founder Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi was arrested by czarist authorities, the first of repeated imprisonments of Chabad Rebbes.
Story: In 1798, Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, the founder of Chabad, was arrested in czarist Russia for standing up for Judaism. This was the first in a series of imprisonments that Chabad Rebbes would endure under Russian oppression. The arrest became a foundational moment in Chabad history and a touchstone Yosef Yitzchak recalled while himself in prison.
Tags: russia, arrest, schneur zalman, alter rebbe, czarist russia

Title: Denouncement of Alter Rebbe to Russian government
Summary: In summer 5558 mitnagdim denounced the Alter Rebbe and some thirty chassidim to the Russian authorities.
Story: In the summer of 5558 (1798) the mitnagdim lodged a formal denunciation against the Alter Rebbe together with a group of about thirty chassidim. The charges led to the arrests at the beginning of 5559 and the Alter Rebbe's transfer to St. Petersburg for interrogation.
Tags: mitnagdim, denouncement, mesirah, st petersburg, alter rebbe

Title: Disputes over Alter Rebbe's chassidic approach begin; his system called 'Chabad'
Summary: In 5558 internal disputes broke out within the chassidic community over the Alter Rebbe's approach, and during the years 5558-5562 his system came to be known as 'Chabad'.
Story: Until 5558 the Alter Rebbe served as the sole acknowledged leader of the general chassidic community in Russia and Lithuania. That year, disputes emerged regarding his particular path in chassidus. Over the course of the controversy between 5558 and 5562, his approach became identified by the name 'Chabad'.
Tags: alter rebbe, chabad, chassidus, russia, lithuania

Title: Lithuanian chassidim leaders released on 5th night of Chanukah
Summary: Twenty-two leading Lithuanian chassidim arrested with the Alter Rebbe were released by lighting time of the fifth Chanukah candle 5559.
Story: Parallel to the arrest of the Alter Rebbe, twenty-two leading chassidim of Lithuania had been detained in early Cheshvan 5559 for interrogation. On 19 Kislev the Tsar ordered all of them released; the order reached Lithuania on 28 Kislev, and they were freed to their homes by the time of lighting the fifth Chanukah candle.
Tags: chanukah, vilna, lithuania, chassidim, arrest

Title: Or HaMeir printed in Koretz
Summary: Or HaMeir by Rabbi Zev Wolf of Zhitomir was printed in Koretz in 5558.
Story: Or HaMeir, the work of Rabbi Zev Wolf of Zhitomir on the weekly Torah portion and festivals, was printed in Koretz in 5558 (1798), the year following his passing.
Tags: zev wolf of zhitomir, koretz, or hameir

Title: Period of arrests and redemption of the Alter Rebbe begins
Summary: Starting in 5559 the Alter Rebbe entered the final fifteen-year period of his life, marked by the arrests and redemptions of 5559-5561 and the editing of the final 'mahadura basra' of his Shulchan Aruch.
Story: The years 5559-5561 saw the Alter Rebbe's two imprisonments and miraculous releases at the hands of the Czarist government. From this period onward he undertook the third and final phase of editing his Shulchan Aruch, the mahadura basra in three layers. This work continued through the last fifteen years of his life.
Tags: alter rebbe, arrest, redemption, yud tes kislev, russia

Title: Printing of Responsa Maharik in Lvov
Summary: The Lvov edition of Responsa Maharik was printed in 5558.
Story: The Lvov edition of Responsa Maharik was printed in 5558 (1798). A copy of this edition bearing handwritten marginal glosses of the Alter Rebbe of Chabad survived for nearly two centuries before being returned to the Chabad library in 1986.
Tags: maharik, lvov, alter rebbe

Title: Beis din ruling forbids R' Meir Refael's from hosting a Chassidic minyan
Summary: On 21 Adar 5558 the Vilna beis din ruled that R' Meir Refael's could never again host a minyan in his home and must dissociate from the Chassidic 'chevra'.
Story: After R' Meir Refael's defended himself before the beis din, replying that he had found the truth among the Chassidim rather than within the kahal, the court issued its ruling on 21 Adar 5558. He was barred from hosting any minyan for the rest of his life, ordered to stop supporting the Chassidic rebbes, and required to pray only in the main shul or kloiz. He was also told to make public confession before the appointed officials.
Tags: vilna, meir refaels, minyan, beis din

Title: Imperial provincial decision permits Chassidim of Vilna to pray as they wish
Summary: On 26 April 1798 the provincial government of Vilna ruled that Chassidim could pray according to their custom and that no fines or corporal punishments could be imposed on them.
Story: Following the complaint submitted by R' Yehuda ben Eliyahu against the elected committee of five, the cherem, and the looting of his home, the provincial authorities ruled in the Chassidim's favor. On 26 April 1798 the government publicly announced that the Chassidim of Vilna were free to pray as they pleased and that no fines or physical punishments were to be levied against them. The ruling briefly checked the wave of persecution.
Tags: vilna, russian empire, chassidim, religious freedom

Title: Informer denounces Alter Rebbe to Russian authorities
Summary: On 4 Sivan 5558 (8 May 1798), a Vilna informer submitted a denunciation accusing the Alter Rebbe of supporting the French Revolution.
Story: On 4 Sivan 5558 (8 May 1798), an informer from Vilna submitted a denunciation to the Russian authorities accusing Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi of organizing a conspiracy, gathering rebellious youth, supporting the French Revolution, and recommending exile to Siberia. This denunciation initiated the legal case against the Alter Rebbe.
Tags: alter rebbe, arrest, vilna, mitnagdim, russia

Title: Second denunciation against Vilna authorities filed on Shavuot
Summary: On 6 Sivan 5558 (10 May 1798), Shavuot, a follow-up denunciation was filed against Vilna's officials.
Story: On 6 Sivan 5558 (10 May 1798) — the first day of Shavuot — a second denunciation was filed, this one against the Vilna municipal authorities. The fact that it was composed on Shavuot and bore a distorted Hebrew signature suggests the actual author was not Jewish.
Tags: alter rebbe, shavuot, vilna, mitnagdim

Title: Mitnagdic denunciation submitted to Russian authorities against the Alter Rebbe
Summary: On 4 Sivan 5558 the Mitnagdim filed a formal denunciation against the Alter Rebbe and the Chassidim of Lithuania with the Russian authorities.
Story: On 4 Sivan 5558 the Mitnagdim submitted their formal denunciation against the Alter Rebbe and the Chassidim of Lithuania. The text of this denunciation was preserved and published in Kerem Chabad vol. 4. It led directly to the Alter Rebbe's arrest along with thirty Chassidim from Vilna, Vidz, Hamadora, Pandel and Vysokoye-Litovsk at the start of 5559.
Tags: vilna, mitnagdim, denunciation, alter rebbe, russian empire

Title: Vidz kahal disavows R' Hirsh ben Yosef's complaint against Vilna
Summary: On 19 Av 5558 the kahal of Vidz issued a written denial that they had authorized R' Hirsh ben Yosef's complaint against Vilna on behalf of the Chassidim.
Story: After Chassidim in Vidz submitted a complaint against the Vilna kahal's authority over them, the Vidz kahal moved to distance itself. On 19 Av 5558 they wrote a formal disavowal, asserting the action was taken without their knowledge by 'people belonging to the Karliner sect.' The episode is referenced by the Alter Rebbe in a 5571 letter as an example of denunciation he opposed.
Tags: vidz, vilna, hirsh ben yosef, karliner, kahal

Title: Case against Alter Rebbe formally opened
Summary: On 10 Elul 5558 (11 August 1798), the General Procurator presented the denunciation to the Tsar, opening the case.
Story: On 10 Elul 5558 (11 August 1798), the General Procurator of Russia formally presented the denunciation to Tsar Paul I, opening an official file against the Alter Rebbe and the chassidic movement.
Tags: alter rebbe, russia, procurator, arrest

Title: Tsar orders investigation of denunciation against Alter Rebbe
Summary: On 13 Elul 5558 (14 August 1798), the Tsar ordered investigation of the denunciation's content.
Story: On 13 Elul 5558 (14 August 1798), Tsar Paul I issued an order to investigate the contents of the denunciation against Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi. The General Procurator passed the order to the civil governor of Lithuania two days later.
Tags: alter rebbe, tsar, investigation, russia

Title: Lithuanian governor recommends arrest of Alter Rebbe
Summary: On 29 Elul 5558 (30 August 1798), Lithuania's civil governor recommended arresting the Alter Rebbe and chassidic leaders for interrogation.
Story: On 29 Elul 5558 (30 August 1798), the civil governor of Lithuania recommended that the Alter Rebbe and the heads of chassidic communities in Lithuania be taken into custody for interrogation.
Tags: alter rebbe, lithuania, arrest

Title: Tsar orders arrest of Alter Rebbe
Summary: On 13 Tishrei 5559 (12 September 1798), the Tsar ordered the arrest of the Alter Rebbe and chassidic leaders.
Story: On 13 Tishrei 5559 (12 September 1798), Tsar Paul I ordered that Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi and the leading chassidim be arrested and brought to Petersburg for interrogation. The order arrived during the holiday season of Sukkot 5559.
Tags: alter rebbe, arrest, petersburg, tishrei

Title: Alter Rebbe and thirty Chassidim arrested
Summary: At the start of 5559 the Alter Rebbe was arrested together with thirty Chassidim from Vilna, Vidz, Hamadora, Pandel and Vysokoye-Litovsk.
Story: Following the Mitnagdic denunciation of summer 5558, the Alter Rebbe was arrested at the start of 5559 along with thirty Chassidim from Vilna, Vidz, Hamadora, Pandel and Vysokoye-Litovsk. Heads of the Vilna Chassidic kehilla, including R' Meir Refael's, R' Aryeh Leib, R' Shlomo Zalman, R' Nachum ben Yitzchak, R' Yehuda Leib of Kraz and Rabbi Baruch Mordechai Ettinger, were interrogated. A separate arrest warrant was also issued against R' Moshe Meizlish, who managed to evade capture.
Tags: alter rebbe, arrest, petersburg, vilna, vidz, hamadora, pandel, vysokoye-litovsk

Title: Alter Rebbe arrives at Peter-Paul Fortress in Petersburg
Summary: On 8 MarCheshvan 5559 (7 October 1798), the Alter Rebbe arrived in Petersburg and was imprisoned in the Peter-Paul Fortress.
Story: On 8 MarCheshvan 5559 (7 October 1798), the General Procurator notified the governor of Belorussia that Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi had arrived in Petersburg and was incarcerated in the Peter-Paul Fortress, where he remained during the investigation.
Tags: alter rebbe, petersburg, peter-paul fortress, cheshvan

Title: First arrest of the Alter Rebbe
Summary: On 30 Tishrei 5559 (10 October 1798), Belorussian governor Zhgulin reported to Governor-General Lopukhin that the Alter Rebbe's papers and books had been seized.
Story: During the Alter Rebbe's first arrest, his books and writings were sealed in a box and a trunk with the governor's seal and sent on for investigation. The authorities suspected the writings might contain material against the government. This was the first of two such confiscations during his lifetime.
Tags: alter rebbe, arrest, petersburg, kgb forerunner, russia, belorussia, zhgulin, lopukhin

Title: Liberation of the Alter Rebbe — Yud-Tes Kislev
Summary: On 19 Kislev 5559 (16 November 1798), the Tsar ordered the release of the Alter Rebbe from prison.
Story: On 19 Kislev 5559 (16 November 1798), Tsar Paul I ordered the release of Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi from imprisonment in Petersburg. The day became known as Yud-Tes Kislev, celebrated annually as the 'Rosh Hashanah of Chassidut' marking the vindication of chassidic teachings.
Tags: alter rebbe, yud tes kislev, liberation, chassidut new year, redemption

Title: Alter Rebbe receives release certificate
Summary: On 20 Kislev 5559 (17 November 1798), the Alter Rebbe was issued a release certificate.
Story: On 20 Kislev 5559 (17 November 1798), the General Procurator issued an official release certificate to Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi and notified the governor of Belorussia of his liberation.
Tags: alter rebbe, release, kislev

Title: Tsar Paul I orders release of Alter Rebbe
Summary: On 19 Kislev 5559 Tsar Paul ordered the Alter Rebbe and the Karliner chassidim freed.
Story: After interrogation and the Alter Rebbe's written replies in Hebrew were translated for Tsar Paul, the Tsar issued a decree on 19 Kislev 5559 finding nothing harmful to the state in the conduct of 'the Karliner sect' and ordering all of them released. The day became the festival of 19 Kislev, Chag HaGeulah, the founding holiday of Chabad.
Tags: tsar paul, st petersburg, 19 kislev, redemption, alter rebbe

Title: Alter Rebbe receives release certificate
Summary: On 20 Kislev 5559 the Alter Rebbe was issued his official release document.
Story: On 20 Kislev 5559 (Nov 17, 1798 OS / Nov 28 NS) the Alter Rebbe received his written release certificate identifying him as 'Zalman ben Baruch' and authorizing his return to White Russia via Vitebsk. The same day, Prokuror General Pyotr Lopukhin formally notified the Belorussian governor Semyon Zhegulin of the imperial decision.
Tags: release certificate, st petersburg, zhegulin, vitebsk, prokuror lopukhin

Title: Alter Rebbe receives his official release document
Summary: On 20 Kislev 5559 the Alter Rebbe received the formal release certificate; Procurator General Pyotr Lopukhin wrote that day to Governor-General Zhegulin confirming the freedom of 'Zalman ben Baruch'.
Story: The day after the Tsar's order, the Alter Rebbe was handed the document making his freedom official. Lopukhin's letter to Semyon Zhegulin, governor-general of White Russia, formally notified the regional administration that Zalman ben Baruch had been released without restriction.
Tags: alter rebbe, russia, release, 20 kislev, 5559, lopukhin

Title: Tsar Paul I orders release of Alter Rebbe and Chabad chassidim
Summary: On 19 Kislev 5559, Tsar Paul I issued a written order freeing the Alter Rebbe and his chassidim after finding no harm to the state in their conduct.
Story: Following interrogations and the translation of his answers into Russian, the Tsar concluded that the Karliner sect (as the chassidim were called in the official record) had done nothing to disturb public order. On 19 Kislev 5559 he signed the order of release. This date later became the Chassidic festival of 19 Kislev.
Tags: alter rebbe, russia, tsar paul i, imperial pardon, 19 kislev, 5559, petersburg

Title: Vilna chassidim freed on fifth night of Chanukah
Summary: On 28 Kislev 5559, the fifth night of Chanukah, the chassidim arrested in Vilna were released home.
Story: Although the Alter Rebbe had been freed on 20 Kislev, his chassidim from Vilna only reached their homes a week later. Because Chanukah candle-lighting in that region precedes 3 pm, the release after lighting was attributed to the fifth night, and that date entered chassidic memory as the day of the Vilna chassidim's geulah.
Tags: vilna, lithuania, russia, chanukah, 28 kislev, 5559, release

Title: Vilna chassidim freed on fifth night of Chanukah
Summary: On 28 Kislev 5559, the eve of the fifth Chanukah light, the Vilna chassidim were freed.
Story: On 28 Kislev 5559 the chassidim arrested in Vilna together with the Alter Rebbe were also released. Tradition holds that the release occurred at night after candle-lighting, which is why the fifth light of Chanukah became associated with the redemption of the Vilna chassidim.
Tags: vilna, chanukah, 1798 arrests, release

Title: Belorussia notifies Vitebsk to allow chassidim to continue
Summary: On 18 Tevet 5559 (15 December 1798), the governor of Belorussia informed Vitebsk officials of the Alter Rebbe's release and order to leave the chassidic community in peace.
Story: On 18 Tevet 5559 (15 December 1798), the governor of Belorussia notified the Vitebsk authorities of the Alter Rebbe's release and conveyed the Tsar's order that the chassidic community be allowed to continue its existence undisturbed.
Tags: alter rebbe, vitebsk, belorussia, chassidim

Title: Alter Rebbe freed from Petersburg imprisonment on 19 Kislev
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman is released from imprisonment in Petersburg on 19 Kislev 5559—the yahrzeit of the Maggid—after being denounced by opponents of Chassidism.
Story: Following denunciations by opponents of Chassidism, the Alter Rebbe was arrested and interrogated in Petersburg. On 19 Kislev 5559, while reading from Psalms the verse 'He redeemed my soul in peace,' he was released. He immediately wrote a letter announcing the redemption to Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, noting that the date doubled in meaning as the yahrzeit of their teacher, the Maggid of Mezeritch.
Tags: schneur zalman, petersburg, tsarist russia, yud-tes kislev, denunciation, redemption

Title: Alter Rebbe's Hilchos Talmud Torah reissued in Lvov
Summary: An edition of the Alter Rebbe's Hilchos Talmud Torah was issued in Lvov in 1799 with fresh approbations and now attributed to the author of the Tanya.
Story: Unlike the anonymous 1794 Shklov first edition, the Lvov 5559 (1799) printing identifies the work as having been authored by "the author of the Tanya." The 34-folio duodecimo carried new approbations and helped circulate the Alter Rebbe's Torah-study halachot in Galicia.
Tags: alter rebbe, lvov, talmud torah

Title: Ketuba from Fez dated 5559
Summary: A ketuba from Fez, Morocco, dated 5559 (1799) is preserved in the library's collection.
Story: The 1799 Fez ketuba documents Sephardic-Moroccan marriage practice at the close of the eighteenth century and complements the library's other antique ketubot.
Tags: ketuba, fez, morocco, manuscript

Title: R' Yaakov Shimshon distributes funds independently, sparking conflict
Summary: R' Yaakov Shimshon of Shepetivka brought and distributed Polish funds alone in Tiberias, sparking conflict that R' Nachman of Breslov tried to mediate.
Story: In 5559 (1799), R' Yaakov Shimshon of Shepetivka brought the Polish-Volhynian funds to Tiberias and distributed them solely among his people, breaking from the previous arrangement under R' Avraham of Kalisk. The conflict between the two leaders intensified sharply. R' Nachman of Breslov attempted to mediate between them, as documented in Kovetz Beit Aharon V'Yisrael.
Tags: yaakov shimshon of shepetivka, avraham of kalisk, nachman of breslov, tiberias, kollel volhyn

Title: Second edition of Tanya printed in Zhalkva
Summary: The Tanya was reprinted in Zhalkva in 5559 (1799), one of several early reprints within a decade of its first edition.
Story: This 74-folio Zhalkva octavo edition is among the very earliest reprints of the Tanya. Such Galician printings helped spread Chabad chassidic thought beyond White Russia in the years following the first 1797 Slavita edition.
Tags: alter rebbe, tanya, zhalkva

Title: New Vilna kahal elected with chassid R. Meir Refaels at head
Summary: On 12 Adar I 5559 eight new kahal members were elected in Vilna, headed by the chassid R. Meir Refaels.
Story: Two days after the imperial dissolution of the old kahal, fresh elections produced a kehillah board of eight men with the chassid R. Meir Refaels at its head. This was a dramatic reversal for the chassidim of Vilna, who had been the target of formal communal bans for over a decade.
Tags: vilna, kahal, meir refaels, 5559, 12 adar i, elections

Title: R. Moshe ben Asher petitions to overturn new Vilna kahal
Summary: On 15 Adar I 5559 R. Moshe ben Asher filed a petition with the Russian authorities seeking annulment of the new Vilna kahal elections and reinstatement of the deposed leadership.
Story: Three days after the new chassidic-led kahal was sworn in, R. Moshe ben Asher, a leader of the mitnagdim, lodged a formal complaint demanding the old board be restored. He soon followed with a second petition urging the authorities to suppress the chassidic movement in Vilna entirely.
Tags: vilna, moshe ben asher, mitnagdim, 5559, 15 adar i, petition

Title: Russian officials dissolve Vilna kahal at the Great Synagogue
Summary: On 10 Adar I 5559, government officials entered the Vilna Great Synagogue and announced the dissolution of the existing kahal and new elections.
Story: After the flood of complaints against the chassidim, the imperial authorities concluded the Vilna kahal had abused its powers in persecuting the chassidic community. The administration ordered new elections, breaking the leadership of the anti-chassidic establishment.
Tags: vilna, kahal, mitnagdim, russia, 10 adar i, 5559

Title: Passing of R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen in Tiberias
Summary: R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen, three-time shadar of the Tiberias chassidim, passes away on 10 Adar II.
Story: On 10 Adar II 5559 R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen passed away in Tiberias. He had served the chassidic communities of the Holy Land on three lengthy shadar missions over more than two decades. His son R' Yitzchak later took up emissary duty in 5571.
Tags: shlomo zalman hakohen, tiberias, death, shadar, chassidim

Title: Tsar reaffirms right of chassidim to exist
Summary: On 20 Kislev 5560 (7 December 1799), the General Procurator confirmed the Tsar's order that the chassidic movement be allowed to exist.
Story: On 20 Kislev 5560 (7 December 1799), the General Procurator replied to the governor of Lithuania that, in accordance with the Tsar's order, the chassidic movement must be allowed to continue. This reaffirmation came in response to renewed denunciations by opponents of the chassidim.
Tags: chassidim, russia, kislev, lithuania

Title: Alter Rebbe moves from Liozna to Liadi
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman relocates from Liozna to Liadi in 5561, the move that gives the dynasty its standard appellation 'the Liadier Rav.'
Story: After roughly eighteen years in Liozna, the Alter Rebbe moved to Liadi in 5561. The move came shortly after his first Petersburg imprisonment and just before a second arrest the following year. He would lead Chabad from Liadi until his passing in 5573.
Tags: schneur zalman, liadi, liozna, russia

Title: Alter Rebbe sends full doctrinal reply to R' Avraham of Kalisk
Summary: After the delay caused by his imprisonment, the Alter Rebbe sends a substantive reply to R' Avraham of Kalisk in 5560.
Story: Only in 5560, after his release from imprisonment, did the Alter Rebbe finally answer R' Avraham of Kalisk's doctrinal challenges with what he called 'a proper response.' That foundational explanation of his approach has not survived. R' Avraham accepted the answer fully in his letters of 5561.
Tags: alter rebbe, avraham of kalisk, chabad, chassidut, correspondence

Title: Alter Rebbe's second arrest and transfer to St. Petersburg
Summary: A renewed denunciation at the start of 5561 brought the Alter Rebbe to St. Petersburg again for interrogation.
Story: At the beginning of 5561 (autumn 1800) a fresh denunciation against the Alter Rebbe was filed and he was once more brought to St. Petersburg for questioning. In his testimony there he cited Tsar Paul's earlier release decree and Beklashov's order tolerating the chassidim as proof of the lawfulness of the movement.
Tags: second arrest, st petersburg, mitnagdim, alter rebbe

Title: Chabad chassidim relocate from Tiberias to Tzfat
Summary: Between 5560 and 5565 the early Chabad chassidim of the Holy Land moved their main settlement from Tiberias to Tzfat.
Story: Chabad chassidim relocated from Tiberias to Tzfat in the years 5560-5565, establishing Tzfat as their principal center until the Mitteler Rebbe later redirected them to Hebron. The move set the stage for two decades of Chabad presence in Tzfat before the 1837 earthquake.
Tags: tiberias, tzfat, settlement, early chabad

Title: Lithuanian court rules against deposed Vilna kahal
Summary: In late summer of 5560 a Lithuanian court ruled that the deposed Vilna kahal had exceeded its authority in persecuting the chassidim, confirming the dissolution as just.
Story: The mitnagdim's appeal of the spring 1799 elections dragged on for over a year. The court ultimately upheld the government's winter 5558 decision to curtail the kahal's powers against the chassidim, ruling the old board had crossed legitimate bounds.
Tags: vilna, kahal, court, 5560, mitnagdim

Title: Luach Birkat HaNehenin published in Shklov
Summary: The Alter Rebbe's Luach Birkat HaNehenin was first printed in Shklov in 1800.
Story: This first printing of the Luach Birkat HaNehenin appeared in 5560 (1800) in Shklov, well before the full Shulchan Aruch reached press. It transmitted an early recension of the Alter Rebbe's halachot of blessings on food and remained a separate booklet alongside later expanded versions.
Tags: alter rebbe, shklov, birkat hanehenin, halacha

Title: Passing of R' Zusha of Anipoli
Summary: R' Zusha of Anipoli passed away on 2 Shevat 5560 (28 January 1800).
Story: R' Zusha, a leading disciple of the Maggid of Mezeritch, had earlier given a haskamah for the first edition of Tanya. His passing came roughly half a year before R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev issued his haskamah for the Slavita Talmud and Tur.
Tags: rebbe zusha, anipoli, chassidic masters, haskamos

Title: Procurator Beklashov rules Chabad chassidim must be tolerated
Summary: On 8 Shvat 5560 Chief Procurator Alexander Beklashov instructed Vilna police to notify the mitnagdic leadership that, by the Tsar's will, the Chabad sect must be tolerated.
Story: Responding to the mitnagdim's renewed petition to eliminate the chassidim of Vilna, Beklashov informed the city police that the imperial decision stood: the so-called Karliner sect was protected. The Alter Rebbe later referenced this ruling in answers given during his second arrest.
Tags: vilna, russia, beklashov, 8 shvat, 5560, tolerance

Title: Prokuror Beklashov orders chassidim be tolerated
Summary: On 8 Shevat 5560 Prokuror Beklashov instructed Vilna police to inform the kahal that the Karliner sect must be tolerated.
Story: After a second mitnagdic denunciation at the start of 5560, Prokuror General Alexander Beklashov issued an order on 8 Shevat 5560 (Feb 4, 1800) to the Vilna municipal police instructing them to summon the kahal heads and inform them that 'by the will of His Imperial Majesty the Karliner sect must be tolerated.' The order would later be cited in the Alter Rebbe's second interrogation.
Tags: vilna, beklashov, tsar paul, karliner, toleration

Title: Avigdor of Pinsk denounces Alter Rebbe to Tsar
Summary: On 10 Iyar 5560 (23 April 1800), Avigdor of Pinsk submitted a lengthy denunciation against the Alter Rebbe to the Tsar.
Story: On 10 Iyar 5560 (23 April 1800), Avigdor, formerly rabbi of Pinsk and then residing in Vilna, submitted to the Tsar a lengthy denunciation against Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi and the chassidic movement. He attacked Tzava'at HaRivash, argued the movement was a continuation of Sabbatianism, and complained that chassidim had caused his dismissal from the Pinsk rabbinate.
Tags: avigdor of pinsk, alter rebbe, denunciation, mitnagdim, tzavaat harivash

Title: R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev gives haskamah for Slavita Shas and Tur
Summary: On 13 Tammuz 5560 (5 July 1800), R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev gave his haskamah for printing Shas and Tur in Slavita.
Story: R' Shalom Shachna (son-in-law of the Alter Rebbe) and R' Mordechai of Orsha (the Alter Rebbe's brother) traveled to obtain this approbation. R' Levi Yitzchak praised them as 'two men of Ephraim' bringing the Shas and Turim to press. This signaled the formal start of the large Slavita printing project.
Tags: levi yitzchak of berditchev, slavita, shas, tur, haskamos, shalom shachna, mordechai of orsha

Title: Second arrest of the Alter Rebbe
Summary: On 4 Kislev 5561 (9 November 1800), the Alter Rebbe was arrested again and sent to Petersburg.
Story: On 4 Kislev 5561 (9 November 1800), Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi was arrested for a second time and sent under police escort to Petersburg, despite the Belorussian governor's findings that there was no basis for the accusations against him.
Tags: alter rebbe, arrest, petersburg, kislev

Title: Order issued to search Alter Rebbe's home
Summary: On 11 Kislev 5561 (16 November 1800), an order was issued to search the Alter Rebbe's home and seize his documents.
Story: On 11 Kislev 5561 (16 November 1800), the General Procurator ordered the governor of Belorussia to conduct a search of the Alter Rebbe's home, seize manuscripts and documents, and forward them to Petersburg for examination.
Tags: alter rebbe, liozna, search, manuscripts

Title: Alter Rebbe arrested and sent from Lozna to Petersburg
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi was sent from Lozna to Saint Petersburg on 4 Kislev for his second arrest.
Story: At the beginning of winter 5561, the Alter Rebbe was arrested for the second time on charges connected to his leadership of the Chassidic movement. On 4 Kislev 5561 (November 21, 1800) he was transferred from Lozna to the imperial capital of Saint Petersburg. His arrival there was confirmed roughly a week later in correspondence between the Russian general procurator and the governor of Belarus.
Tags: russia, arrest, alter rebbe, lozna, petersburg, tsarist

Title: Tsar orders Senate to investigate Alter Rebbe's case
Summary: On 21 Kislev 5561 (26 November 1800), the Tsar ordered the case transferred to the Senate for further investigation.
Story: On 21 Kislev 5561 (26 November 1800), after reviewing the Alter Rebbe's written replies, Tsar Paul I ordered the case transferred to the Senate, which then assigned the investigation to the Senate's Third Department (the secret police).
Tags: alter rebbe, senate, investigation, petersburg

Title: General Procurator confirms Alter Rebbe's arrival in Petersburg
Summary: General Procurator Obolininov wrote to the governor of Belarus confirming the Alter Rebbe's arrival and demanding any further papers be sent.
Story: On 11 Kislev 5561 (approximately November 28, 1800), General Procurator Obolininov sent a letter to Severin, governor of Belarus, confirming that Rabbi Schneur Zalman had been delivered to Petersburg. The procurator complained that no account books, documents, or correspondence had accompanied the prisoner, and ordered the governor to conduct a search and forward anything that could be found, including writings hidden with associates.
Tags: russia, petersburg, obolininov, alter rebbe, tsarist

Title: Tsar orders Alter Rebbe released on bail
Summary: On 23 Kislev 5561 (28 November 1800), the Tsar ordered the Alter Rebbe released from prison on condition he remain in Petersburg.
Story: On 23 Kislev 5561 (28 November 1800), Tsar Paul I ordered Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi released from his second imprisonment on bail, with the condition that he remain in Petersburg until permitted to leave. This date is observed by Chabad as a secondary day of redemption.
Tags: alter rebbe, release, petersburg, second liberation

Title: Search of Alter Rebbe's home in Liozna
Summary: On 24 Kislev 5561 (29 November 1800), Russian officials searched the Alter Rebbe's home and confiscated his books and manuscripts.
Story: On 24 Kislev 5561 (29 November 1800), Russian officials carried out the search of the Alter Rebbe's home in Liozna. Books and manuscripts were taken, and the lay leaders of the community signed a document acknowledging the confiscation and the sealing of the house.
Tags: alter rebbe, liozna, manuscripts, search

Title: Alter Rebbe placed under house arrest in St. Petersburg
Summary: On 23 Kislev 5561 Tsar Paul ordered the Alter Rebbe held under house arrest until investigation concluded.
Story: Following his second interrogation, an imperial order issued on 23 Kislev 5561 (Nov 30, 1800) directed that the Alter Rebbe be released to house arrest within St. Petersburg until the inquiry was completed, rather than being held in prison.
Tags: house arrest, st petersburg, tsar paul, second imprisonment

Title: Tsar orders Alter Rebbe's case transferred to the Senate
Summary: An imperial order assigned the Alter Rebbe's case to the Senate's third department, the political secret police.
Story: On 22 Kislev 5561 (November 27, 1800 Old Style), an order was issued in the Tsar's name directing that the proceedings against Rabbi Schneur Zalman be handed to the Senate. The Senate in turn assigned the investigation to its third department, the political secret police of Tsarist Russia, where the broader inquiry into the Chassidic movement and the future legal status of the kahal communities was being examined.
Tags: russia, tsar, senate, alter rebbe, secret police

Title: Russian police search Alter Rebbe's home and seize 103 books
Summary: Police searched the Alter Rebbe's home in Lozna and confiscated 103 books and 14 manuscript collections.
Story: On 24 Kislev 5561 (November 29, 1800 Old Style), Russian police searched Rabbi Schneur Zalman's home in Lozna in search of writings against the monarchy. They removed 103 books and 14 manuscript collections to Petersburg as evidence. The remaining volumes were sealed in the house under a special seal, with the leaders of the Lozna community signing a written undertaking to keep them locked and untouched.
Tags: russia, lozna, books, manuscripts, search, alter rebbe

Title: Alter Rebbe's seized writings handed to Senate's third department
Summary: Obolininov forwarded the Alter Rebbe's seized books and manuscripts, with a Russian summary, to Olenin of the Senate's third department.
Story: On 18 Tevet 5561 (December 22, 1800 Old Style), General Procurator Obolininov transferred the confiscated books and manuscripts of the Alter Rebbe to Olenin, prosecutor of the Senate's third department. The materials were accompanied by a Russian-language report prepared by the Jewish translators Leib ben Noach and Yehuda ben Feivish, who certified that they had found nothing in the writings opposed to Jewish law, the monarchy, or the welfare of the country.
Tags: russia, petersburg, translators, senate, books, alter rebbe

Title: Confiscated books and manuscripts delivered to Senate
Summary: On 18 Tevet 5561 (22 December 1800), the seized books and manuscripts from the Alter Rebbe's home were delivered to the Senate.
Story: On 18 Tevet 5561 (22 December 1800), the books and manuscripts taken from Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi's home were delivered to the Senate, accompanied by a list of 14 manuscripts and 103 books.
Tags: alter rebbe, manuscripts, senate, petersburg

Title: Avigdor files additional denunciation citing Tanya
Summary: On 24 Tevet 5561 (28 December 1800), Avigdor filed an additional denunciation citing passages from the Tanya about the souls of the nations.
Story: On 24 Tevet 5561 (28 December 1800), Avigdor of Pinsk submitted yet another denunciation, copying out passages from the Tanya concerning the souls of the nations and arguing that the chassidic movement was harmful to the state. He proposed that the leaders of the chassidim be arrested and interrogated.
Tags: avigdor of pinsk, tanya, denunciation, nefesh

Title: Alter Rebbe moves from Liozna to Liadi
Summary: Following his release, the Alter Rebbe left Petersburg and settled in Liadi rather than returning to Liozna.
Story: Around Elul 5561 (1801), Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi left Petersburg following his second release. Rather than return to his former home in Liozna, he settled in the town of Liadi, which would lend his name and that of his dynasty its lasting designation.
Tags: alter rebbe, liozna, liadi, relocation

Title: Alter Rebbe relocates from Liozna to Liadi
Summary: After his St. Petersburg release the Alter Rebbe did not return to Liozna but settled in Liadi in summer 5561.
Story: Following the conclusion of his summer 5561 stay in St. Petersburg, the Alter Rebbe did not return to Liozna but established his court in Liadi. From this point onward he was the rebbe of an identifiable Chabad community rather than the universal leader of Russian chassidim, and the special Liozna takanos limiting yechidut were not reinstated.
Tags: liadi, liozna, relocation, alter rebbe

Title: Alter Rebbe's second arrest as collection catalyst
Summary: Beginning in 5561 — the year of the Alter Rebbe's second arrest and journey to Petersburg — the future Tzemach Tzedek began systematically collecting and transcribing the Alter Rebbe's discourses.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz recorded that when the Alter Rebbe was taken to Petersburg in 5561, the future Tzemach Tzedek began assembling transcripts of his grandfather's teachings. By the time the Alter Rebbe returned in the summer of that year, the Tzemach Tzedek had over 1,100 bogen of transcripts. By the Alter Rebbe's passing in 5573, the collection exceeded 10,000 bogen — over a hundred large volumes — forming the foundation of the Chabad manuscript library.
Tags: alter rebbe, second arrest, tzemach tzedek, manuscripts, petersburg

Title: Chabad center moves from Liozna to Liadi
Summary: In 5561 (1801) the Alter Rebbe moved the Chabad center from Liozna to the neighboring town of Liadi.
Story: After about eighteen years in Liozna, the Alter Rebbe relocated to Liadi in 1801. Liadi would remain the Chabad center until his passing in 1812. The towns of Liozna, Liadi, and Lubavitch all sat near one another on the Russian-Belarusian frontier.
Tags: liadi, liozna, alter-rebbe, chabad-center

Title: Luach Birkat HaNehenin reprinted in Zhalkva
Summary: The Alter Rebbe's Luach Birkat HaNehenin was reprinted in Zhalkva in 1801.
Story: The 27-folio Zhalkva 5561 (1801) duodecimo carried the first recension of the Alter Rebbe's halachot of blessings. Multiple parallel printings in Russia-Poland and Korec followed in the early 1800s before the second recension superseded it in the 1803 siddur.
Tags: alter rebbe, zhalkva, birkat hanehenin

Title: Passing of R' Yaakov Shimshon of Shepetivka ends separate Volhynia kollel
Summary: With the passing of R' Yaakov Shimshon of Shepetivka, the separate Volhynia kollel in Eretz Yisrael appears to have dissolved.
Story: R' Yaakov Shimshon of Shepetivka passed away in 5561 (1801). From that point on, no separate Volhynia kollel existed in the Holy Land; funds again flowed through R' Avraham of Kalisk. Volhynian collections continued to be raised separately abroad, but distribution in Eretz Yisrael was reunified under a single Hasidic kollel.
Tags: yaakov shimshon of shepetivka, tiberias, kollel volhyn, passing

Title: R' Avraham of Kalisk reconciles with the Alter Rebbe
Summary: In 5561 R' Avraham of Kalisk writes accepting the Alter Rebbe's reply, calling for unity and asking that past disputes be forgotten.
Story: Two letters from R' Avraham of Kalisk in 5561 survive. One, addressed to the Alter Rebbe, asks that 'former matters not be remembered, what has passed is past.' The other, to the entire Chabad community in Russia, declares that no real difference exists between him and the Alter Rebbe — 'not a hairsbreadth' — especially regarding the practice of hitbonenut (contemplative meditation).
Tags: avraham of kalisk, alter rebbe, chabad, chassidut, hitbonenut, reconciliation, russia

Title: R' Meir of Bychov's second shlichut
Summary: R' Meir of Bychov undertook a second emissary mission for the Tiberias Chasidim in 5561.
Story: Years after his first shlichut, R' Meir of Bychov was dispatched again from Tiberias to the diaspora Chasidic communities in 5561. The details are documented in 'Shluchei Eretz Yisrael' pages 624–626. He would go out a third time only two years later.
Tags: meir of bychov, shadar, tiberias

Title: R. Avraham of Kalisk writes about the early 'talk' period
Summary: An 1801 letter of R. Avraham of Kalisk references 'the whole matter of the talk' from his Kalisk period before emigrating.
Story: The letter alludes to the boisterous, head-down behavior of the early Kalisk chassidim that had drawn fierce criticism from the mitnagdim. R. Avraham's remark contextualizes the practice as part of a passing early stage in chassidic development.
Tags: avraham of kalisk, letter, kalisk, tzfat

Title: R. Yosef Hatzaddik of Posen passes away
Summary: R. Yosef 'Hatzaddik' ben Pinchas, son-in-law of the Nodah BiYhudah and Av Beit Din of Posen, died on 5 Adar 5561.
Story: Born in Zolkov in 5486 (1726), R. Yosef Hatzaddik served as rabbi in Witkow, Skole, Yavorov and finally Posen, and was deeply praised by his father-in-law the Nodah BiYhudah. He died on 5 Adar 5561 (18 February 1801) and is buried in Posen; his book Zikhron She'erit Yosef was printed in Kolomea in 5642.
Tags: posen, poland, nodah biyhudah, rabbinate

Title: Assassination of Tsar Paul I
Summary: On 9 Nissan 5561 (11 March 1801), Tsar Paul I was assassinated and his son Alexander succeeded him.
Story: On 9 Nissan 5561 (11 March 1801), Tsar Paul I of Russia was assassinated, and his son Alexander I ascended to the throne. The change of regime would directly affect the Alter Rebbe's case still pending before the Senate.
Tags: tsar paul i, tsar alexander, russia, nissan

Title: Tsar Alexander orders Alter Rebbe's full release
Summary: On 19 Nissan 5561 (21 March 1801), Tsar Alexander I ordered the Alter Rebbe released to return home.
Story: On 19 Nissan 5561 (21 March 1801), the newly enthroned Tsar Alexander I ordered Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi released from his bail conditions in Petersburg and permitted to return home. A formal notice was sent to the White Russian authorities on 27 Nissan.
Tags: alter rebbe, tsar alexander, release, nissan

Title: Assassination of Tsar Paul I
Summary: Tsar Paul was assassinated on the night before 10 Nissan 5561 and succeeded by his son Alexander.
Story: On the eve of 10 Nissan 5561 (March 23/24, 1801) Tsar Paul I was murdered in his palace and his son Alexander I ascended the throne. Within two weeks the new Tsar issued a full release for the Alter Rebbe, ending his second imprisonment.
Tags: tsar paul, tsar alexander, russia, st petersburg

Title: Notice of release and freedom to spread chassidut
Summary: On 27 Nissan 5561 (29 March 1801), Petersburg notified White Russia of the Alter Rebbe's release and full license to spread chassidut.
Story: On 27 Nissan 5561 (29 March 1801), Petersburg sent notification to the governor of White Russia confirming the Alter Rebbe's release and granting him full permission to continue spreading chassidut throughout the White Russian district without any interference.
Tags: alter rebbe, white russia, chassidut, nissan

Title: Alter Rebbe released from Petersburg by tsarist decree
Summary: Civil governor Treviov issued a document permitting Rabbi Schneur Zalman to return from Petersburg to his home and continue his activities throughout White Russia without interference.
Story: Following his second arrest and interrogation in Petersburg in 1801, Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi (called Zalman Bruchavitch in Russian documents) was freed by imperial order. The civil governor of White Russia, Treviov, issued him a formal document on July 13, 1801, granting him full freedom to resume his religious leadership of the Chasidim throughout the region as he had done before.
Tags: alter rebbe, shneur zalman of liadi, russia, petersburg, treviov, white russia, release

Title: Alter Rebbe returns from Petersburg and settles in Liadi
Summary: On 11 Menachem Av 5561 (21 July 1801), the Alter Rebbe traveled from Petersburg directly to Liadi after his second arrest.
Story: Following his second arrest and release, the Alter Rebbe moved his residence from Liozna to Liadi. This marked the start of a new era — longer maamarim with multiple layered explanations — that became the hallmark of Chabad teaching.
Tags: alter rebbe, liadi, petersburg, second arrest, russia

Title: Tsar Alexander issues full release certificate for Alter Rebbe
Summary: A copy of the imperial release certificate reached the Alter Rebbe in Vitebsk on 15 Av 5561.
Story: By order of Tsar Alexander I, 'the Jew Zalman ben Baruch' was declared free to return home and enjoy full liberty in his former place of residence. A copy of the release was delivered to the Alter Rebbe through the Vitebsk governor's office on 15 Av 5561 (July 25, 1801), accompanied by a certificate from Pyotr Tarabeev confirming the Alter Rebbe's right to exercise his liberties throughout White Russia.
Tags: tsar alexander, release, vitebsk, tarabeev, second redemption

Title: Death of R. Moshe ben Asher, leader of Vilna mitnagdim
Summary: In Cheshvan 5562 (October 1801) R. Moshe ben Asher, the foremost campaigner against the chassidim of Vilna, passed away.
Story: With his death, the bitter public agitation in the streets of Vilna died down. Subsequent kahal elections in 5562 and 5565 included both chassidim and mitnagdim, and chassidic minyanim continued openly, eventually gaining a permanent space near the Old Kloyz.
Tags: vilna, moshe ben asher, mitnagdim, cheshvan, 5562

Title: Alter Rebbe sends his Siddur Nusach Ari to press in Shklov
Summary: The Alter Rebbe published his Siddur arranged according to the Arizal's nusach in Shklov in 5563 (1803), with appended laws and customs.
Story: Tradition records that the Alter Rebbe examined some sixty existing siddurim before fixing his own nusach, and that on his deathbed he counted the formulation of this nusach as one of his three lifetime achievements. The siddur also incorporated his collected halachot and customs—the second recension of Birkat HaNehenin—and shaped Chabad davening to this day.
Tags: alter rebbe, siddur, shklov, nusach ari, arizal

Title: Alter Rebbe's Siddur first printed in Shklov
Summary: The Alter Rebbe's Siddur was first printed in Shklov in 5563, incorporating his Psakei Hasiddur including Seder Mechiras Chametz and revised Hilchos Tzitzis and Tefillin.
Story: The Siddur was the vehicle by which many of the Alter Rebbe's later halachic rulings reached print, often differing from his earlier Shulchan Aruch. The Tzemach Tzedek noted that 'the Siddur was written a long time after the Shulchan Aruch.' Two more editions appeared during the Alter Rebbe's lifetime in Kapust.
Tags: alter rebbe, siddur, shklov, psakei hasiddur, mechiras chametz

Title: Beginning of opposition against the Alter Rebbe
Summary: A formal dispute against the Alter Rebbe by R. Avraham of Kalisk began in 5563.
Story: In 5563 (1802/1803), the dispute against the Alter Rebbe – originating from R. Avraham of Kalisk in Eretz Yisrael – formally erupted. The Alter Rebbe later noted that twenty-two years of supportive correspondence (beginning in 5542) had ended with this conflict, marking a significant rupture in the chassidic leadership of the time.
Tags: alter rebbe, avraham of kalisk, machloket

Title: Emissaries demand Alter Rebbe cancel old EY fund channels
Summary: In winter 5563 emissaries of R' Avraham of Kalisk demanded the Alter Rebbe cancel all existing Eretz Yisrael fundraising arrangements and let them create new ones.
Story: In winter 5563 emissaries arrived asking the Alter Rebbe to cancel all existing fundraising arrangements in Russia so they could circulate and create new arrangements through 'true friends' not called by the name Chabad. They claimed to act with R' Avraham of Kalisk's knowledge. The Alter Rebbe refused to avoid increasing strife but the dispute escalated.
Tags: avraham of kalisk, alter rebbe, eretz yisrael fund, shaliach, russia

Title: First documented use of the name 'Chabad' for the Alter Rebbe's chassidim
Summary: The name 'Chabad' first appears as a designation for the Alter Rebbe's chassidim in winter 5563.
Story: The earliest known use of 'Chabad' as the name of the Alter Rebbe's chassidim is in the demand brought by R' Avraham of Kalisk's emissaries in winter 5563 (1803) that maamadot emissaries 'not called by the name Chabad' replace the existing ones. This implies that by that point the designation had already become familiar in the chassidic world.
Tags: chabad, name, r' avraham of kalisk, identity

Title: R' Avraham of Kalisk's emissaries seek to displace Alter Rebbe's emissaries
Summary: In winter 5563 Kalisk emissaries demanded replacing all the Alter Rebbe's collectors with new ones not called Chabad.
Story: In the winter of 5563 (1802/03) emissaries from R' Avraham of Kalisk in Eretz Yisrael came to the Alter Rebbe asking that the existing chassidic emissaries handling the Land of Israel maamadot be removed and replaced with new ones from among 'true lovers who are not called by the name Chabad.' The dispute marked the open split between Chabad and the general chassidic movement led by Kalisk.
Tags: r' avraham of kalisk, maamadot, eretz yisrael, kollel, emissaries

Title: R' Meir of Bychov's third shlichut
Summary: R' Meir of Bychov went out on his third emissary mission in 5563.
Story: R' Meir of Bychov was sent abroad as a Tiberias shadar for a third time in 5563. This was his last documented shlichut before his appointment as a leader of the Tiberias kollel. Records of the mission are summarized in 'Shluchei Eretz Yisrael.'
Tags: meir of bychov, shadar, tiberias

Title: R' Moshe Meizlish flees Vilna amid Mitnagdic persecution
Summary: R' Moshe Meizlish, former neeman of the Vilna kahal turned Chabad chassid, fled Vilna because of the machlokes and wandered abroad.
Story: Once the Mitnagdim realized the Alter Rebbe had been freed, they turned their wrath on R' Moshe Meizlish, the former neeman of the Vilna kahal who had become a devoted disciple. He was stripped of his communal position and his livelihood, eventually being forced into wandering. The Alter Rebbe wrote a letter of introduction for him to the Baal HaHafla'ah in Germany. A pamphlet Meizlish printed in Kapust in 5572 dates his flight to the month of Ziv 5563.
Tags: vilna, moshe meizlish, alter rebbe, haflaa

Title: R. Chaim of Volozhin visits Belarus and discusses polished shechitah knives
Summary: In 1803 R. Chaim of Volozhin, visiting Belarus, reported in the name of the Vilna Gaon that there was no halachic prohibition on polished shechitah knives.
Story: Notables who were not chassidim heard from R. Chaim that the Vilna Gaon's ban on the chassidic-style polished shechitah knives had been issued as a 'distancing' measure against the chassidim, not as inherent halachic law. The Alter Rebbe cites this account in his 1811 epistle defending the practice.
Tags: chaim of volozhin, belarus, shechita, polished knives, vilna gaon, alter rebbe

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's wedding in Parshat Toldot
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek married Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka around Parshat Toldot 5564.
Story: The wedding of the future Tzemach Tzedek to Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka took place during Parshat Toldot 5564 (Cheshvan, late 1803). This dating is used in the family chronicle to argue against an earlier proposed birth year of 5564 for their son Baruch Shalom, since a child born to them could only have arrived after the wedding.
Tags: tzemach-tzedek, wedding, chaya-mushka, schneersohn

Title: Volozhin yeshivah established
Summary: The modern yeshivah movement began with the founding of the yeshivah in Volozhin.
Story: In 1803, the yeshivah in Volozhin was established, launching the modern Eastern European yeshivah movement. Over time, other major Lithuanian-style yeshivas would follow in Slabodka, Mir, Telz, and Novardok.
Tags: volozhin, lithuania, yeshivah, modern yeshivah

Title: Alexander I issues 'Regulations Concerning the Jews'
Summary: Tsar Alexander I issued the 'Regulations Concerning the Jews,' which included a decree expelling Jews from rural villages.
Story: These regulations launched a century-long process in which the Pale of Settlement steadily narrowed through ever new restrictions and prohibitions. The expulsion-from-villages decree set the template for later residency limits and gradually concentrated Russian Jewry into overcrowded urban areas of the Pale.
Tags: russia, pale of settlement, alexander i, village expulsion, tsarist regulations

Title: Mittler Rebbe urges Mordechai and Yehuda to help build a chassidic shul in their town
Summary: The Mittler Rebbe wrote two chassidim to join R' Yehuda Leib in handling synagogue construction and other community needs so that the latter could resume Torah study and avodah.
Story: Anash in one town had loaded the entire burden of building their new chassidic synagogue and managing communal affairs onto R' Yehuda Leib, leaving him no time for learning. The Mittler Rebbe asked R' Mordechai and R' Yehuda to take a share of the work, promising that the merit of the public would stand them in good stead. The undated letter belongs to the years after the 1804 statute opened the way for separate chassidic shuls.
Tags: mittler rebbe, synagogue building, anash, yehuda leib, mordechai, yehuda

Title: R. Avraham Avli of Pasvalys becomes rav of Vilna
Summary: From 5564 onward R. Avraham Avli of Pasvalys served as rav of Vilna; he maintained warm relations with the Chabad rebbes.
Story: His tenure marked a major shift from the era of the Vilna Gaon's followers. The Alter Rebbe and later the Tzemach Tzedek corresponded and met with him, and his cooperation helped contain disputes between chassidim and mitnagdim across Lithuania.
Tags: vilna, avraham avli, pasvalys, 5564, rabbinate

Title: Russian Jewish statute of 1804 permits chassidim to build separate synagogues
