Summary: The 1804 Russian Jewish statute, in §53, allowed a faction within a community that could not coexist with the other in one synagogue to build its own and appoint its own rabbis.
Story: Following years of informing against the chassidim that culminated in the Alter Rebbe's arrest, the imperial Jewish statute of 5564 (1804) codified the right of a divided community to split. Chassidim used §53 to found their own minyanim across many towns; the same paragraph was later cited in denunciations against the Alter Rebbe. In Pleshchenitz, for example, chassidim long blocked from a separate shul finally invoked this right to build a chassidisher shtibl.
Tags: russia, 1804 statute, chassidim, misnagdim, synagogue rights, alter rebbe

Title: Russian Jewish Statute restricting rabbinic fund collection
Summary: Czar Alexander I's Jewish Statute prohibited rabbis from collecting funds from the community beyond their fixed salary.
Story: The Russian Jewish Statute of 5565 (1804) regulated Jewish communal life and explicitly forbade rabbis from gathering money from their congregations beyond a fixed salary. This statute would later be invoked by opponents of Chabad and by Russian investigators questioning whether the Mitteler Rebbe's collection of ma'amad funds violated the law. The Senate ultimately ruled that the voluntary nature of the donations, combined with the Rebbe's non-official rabbinic status, placed him outside its prohibitions.
Tags: russia, law, jewish statute, alexander i

Title: Alexander I signs first comprehensive Jewish charter of Russia
Summary: On 9 December 1804 (20 Kislev 5565) Tsar Alexander I signed the first detailed 'Jewish charter' regulating the status of Jews in Russia.
Story: Following the partitions of Poland in 1772 that brought large Jewish populations under Russian rule, no comprehensive legal status had been established for them. The first detailed charter was prepared during 5564 (1804) and signed by Alexander I on 9 December that year. It would later be replaced by Nicholas I's expanded charter of 1835.
Tags: russia, alexander i, jewish charter, legislation

Title: Jewish Constitution of 1804 signed by the Tsar
Summary: Tsar Alexander I signed the Statute Concerning the Jews, regulating rabbinic appointments, taxes, and communal life across the Russian Empire.
Story: On December 9, 1804, the Tsar signed the comprehensive Jewish Constitution that governed Jewish life in the Empire for decades. Its provisions—including section 50 mandating triennial rabbinic elections, section 52 forbidding rabbis to collect funds beyond fixed salaries, and section 53 permitting separate congregations only under strict conditions—later became the legal basis for repeated investigations of the Chabad Rebbes.
Tags: russia, jewish constitution, law, tsar, rabbinic authority

Title: Tsar Alexander I issues Jewish Statute regulating rabbinate
Summary: Tsar Alexander I issued a statute on the Jews whose Sections 52-53 governed rabbinic fees and synagogue splits, later cited against the Mitteler Rebbe.
Story: The 1804 statute declared the rabbinate an office of honor rather than a paying position, forbidding rabbis from collecting funds beyond their fixed communal salary (Section 52). Section 53 allowed a faction to build its own synagogue when communal unity broke down, but limited each town to one official communal leader. Two decades later, the informer Shimcha Kissin invoked Section 52 to accuse Rabbi DovBer Schneuri of illegal fundraising.
Tags: russia, tsar alexander i, jewish statute, rabbinate, legislation

Title: Tsar Alexander signs Jewish Statute including section 53
Summary: On 18 Tevet 5565 (9 December 1804), Tsar Alexander signed the Jewish Statute granting chassidim the right to build their own synagogues.
Story: On 18 Tevet 5565 (9 December 1804), Tsar Alexander I signed the Russian Jewish Statute. Section 53 granted that wherever a community split such that one party did not want to share a synagogue with the other, either party could build its own synagogue and appoint its own rabbis — formally protecting the chassidim from interference by mitnagdim.
Tags: tsar alexander, jewish statute, chassidim, russia, legal recognition

Title: Alter Rebbe writes summer 1805 letter recounting Maggid's regard for him
Summary: In summer 1805 the Alter Rebbe wrote a letter recounting how he and R. Avraham of Kalisk arrived in Rovno in 1772 and the latter feared meeting the Maggid.
Story: The letter provides the most detailed first-person account of the 1772 Rovno gathering: R. Avraham waiting at the outskirts, R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk interceding, and the Alter Rebbe escorting him into the Maggid's chamber. It also defends the Alter Rebbe's status as a beloved disciple of the Maggid.
Tags: alter rebbe, maggid of mezeritch, letter, rovno, avraham of kalisk

Title: Alter Rebbe's letter (51) defending fund management
Summary: In late summer 5565 the Alter Rebbe wrote letter 51 explaining the breakdown of EY fund transfers and defending his actions.
Story: In late summer 5565 the Alter Rebbe wrote a detailed letter explaining the events: the winter 5563 demands by emissaries, the gabbai R' Yaakov Smilyaner's intervention, the letter he sent to R' Avraham of Kalisk offering to transfer all collected funds, and how 5563-5564 funds remained undelivered because Kalisker's own emissaries had said he would refuse them.
Tags: alter rebbe, avraham of kalisk, eretz yisrael fund, yaakov smilyaner

Title: Chabad Chassidim in Eretz Yisrael form a separate kollel
Summary: In 5565, Alter Rebbe-aligned Chassidim in Eretz Yisrael break from Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk's leadership to organize what would later be called Kollel Chabad.
Story: Following years of disagreement between Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk and the Alter Rebbe over the Chabad approach to Chassidism, the rift carried into Eretz Yisrael. In 5565, Chassidim in Tzfat who followed the Alter Rebbe organized their own kollel, separate from the general Chassidic community led from Tiberias. The same year, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev sent dedicated funds for his own Chassidim in the land through Rabbi Aryeh Leib of Volochisk.
Tags: eretz yisrael, tzfat, tiberias, kollel chabad, avraham of kalisk, schneur zalman

Title: Founding of Kollel Chabad in the Land of Israel
Summary: Kollel Chabad was founded in the Holy Land in 5565.
Story: The shadarut document of 5618 recounts that Kollel Chabad was founded over fifty years earlier when 'the great luminaries, the righteous foundations of the world,' established the seat of Chabad in the Holy Land. Settlement followed first in Hebron (5581–83) and later in Jerusalem (5607).
Tags: kollel chabad, eretz yisrael, alter rebbe

Title: Printing of Amudei Gola in Ladi with the Alter Rebbe's approbation
Summary: The book Amudei Gola was printed in Ladi in 5565 with the Alter Rebbe's approbation.
Story: The Ladi printing house, operated in part by R' Baruch ben Eliyahu, produced Amudei Gola in 5565 (1805) carrying the Alter Rebbe's haskama. The same printer would issue Tanya the following year in Shklov, and his role has often been confused in the literature with that of a grandson of the Alter Rebbe.
Tags: ladi, alter rebbe, approbation, printing

Title: R' Aryeh Leib of Volochisk emigrates to the Holy Land
Summary: R' Aryeh Leib of Volochisk ascends to Eretz Yisrael in summer 5565, carrying funds from R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev.
Story: In summer 5565 the elderly R' Aryeh Leib of Volochisk made aliyah, carrying with him funds entrusted by R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev for distribution to the poor in the Land of Israel. The Chozeh of Lublin's letter to R' Levi Yitzchak references this transmission. From this point a distinct Volhynian channel of support, separate from the Russian-Chabad collection, began operating openly.
Tags: aryeh leib of volochisk, levi yitzchak of berditchev, tzfat, tiberias, aliyah, chozeh of lublin

Title: R' Avraham of Kalisk appoints R' Mordechai of Lechovitch over Russian EY funds
Summary: In winter 5565 R' Avraham of Kalisk formally appointed R' Mordechai of Lechovitch to handle EY fund collection in Russia, separating from the Alter Rebbe.
Story: After two years of non-receipt of Russian funds, R' Avraham of Kalisk wrote general letters in winter 5565 complaining that he had received nothing from Russia and announcing the appointment of R' Mordechai of Lechovitch to manage the EY funds collected in Russia. R' Mordechai in turn appointed R' Aharon and R' Yisrael of Ostravna as general gabbaim. The split was triggered by malicious emissaries who had spread false rumors.
Tags: avraham of kalisk, mordechai of lechovitch, eretz yisrael fund, russia, split

Title: R' Avraham of Kalisk on the troubles from separating Volhynia and Russia
Summary: R' Avraham of Kalisk wrote that great harm followed the separation of Volhynia's Hasidim from Russia's in the fundraising system.
Story: In 5565 (1805), R' Avraham of Kalisk wrote that 'from the day the people of Volhynia were separated from the people of Russia, all the problems came out into the open, and great damage came from this.' Nevertheless, although collections in Europe remained organized separately by region, when the funds reached Eretz Yisrael they all passed through his hands. The letter is preserved in Yagdil Torah.
Tags: avraham of kalisk, letter, volhynia, russia, fundraising

Title: Rabbi Aryeh Leib of Volochisk carries Berditchever pidyon funds to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: In summer 5565, Rabbi Aryeh Leib of Volochisk carries funds from Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev to his Chassidim in Eretz Yisrael during his own aliyah.
Story: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev maintained a fund for his Chassidim in Eretz Yisrael, parallel to the Alter Rebbe's similar effort. In summer 5565, he sent that year's contribution with Rabbi Aryeh Leib of Volochisk, who was making his own journey to the land. The Chozeh of Lublin referenced the transfer in a letter to Rabbi Levi Yitzchak from that same season.
Tags: aryeh leib of volochisk, levi yitzchak of berditchev, chozeh of lublin, eretz yisrael, tzfat, pidyon

Title: Separate Chabad fund for Eretz Yisrael is founded
Summary: In 5565 the Alter Rebbe established a separate fund for Chabad chassidim living in Eretz Yisrael, distinct from the older joint kollel.
Story: Whereas the Alter Rebbe had previously served as nasi over Eretz Yisrael funds in general, sent through the chief gabbai R' Yaakov of Smilyan and distributed in the Land by R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and then R' Avraham of Kalisk, in 5565 he founded a dedicated kollel fund for Anshei Chabad. This created the institutional framework that would evolve into Kollel Chabad of Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: kollel chabad, alter rebbe, eretz yisrael, tzedakah

Title: Tanya reprinted in Zhalkva
Summary: The Tanya was again reprinted in Zhalkva in 5565 (1805).
Story: The 73-folio Zhalkva 5565 edition is another in a series of early Galician reprints that diffused the Tanya across Eastern Europe in the decade following the 1797 Slavita first edition.
Tags: alter rebbe, tanya, zhalkva

Title: Tzemach Tzedek begins recording hanachot
Summary: Around 5566 (1805) the fifteen-year-old Tzemach Tzedek began recording hanachot from his grandfather the Alter Rebbe's chassidic discourses.
Story: At about age fifteen, the future Tzemach Tzedek began writing down hanachot of the discourses he heard from his grandfather the Alter Rebbe. Manuscript 1116 in the library archive contains his hanachot of an Alter Rebbe maamar 'Shema Yisrael' delivered in 5566 (1805-1806), preserved in his youthful handwriting.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, alter rebbe, hanachot, manuscript, chassidut

Title: Passing of R. Pinchas Horowitz, the Baal Haflaah, in Frankfurt
Summary: R. Pinchas Horowitz, the Baal Haflaah, rabbi of Frankfurt-am-Main, passed away on 24 Tammuz 5565 after more than thirty-three years in the position.
Story: The Baal Haflaah had taken his Frankfurt seat at the start of 5532, after passing through Brod. His son R. Zvi Hirsch Halevi Horowitz eulogized him in Sefer Lachmei Todah, noting that he had taught Torah in Frankfurt 'more than thirty-three years.' His earlier praise of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch is one of the key indicators dating the Alter Rebbe's halachic work.
Tags: pinchas horowitz, haflaah, frankfurt, yahrzeit

Title: Passing of Rabbi Meir, son of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev
Summary: Rabbi Meir, son of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, passes away in Kislev 5566; the Alter Rebbe sends a letter of consolation later printed as Iggeret HaKodesh chapter 28.
Story: Rabbi Meir, son of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, passed away in Kislev 5566. The Alter Rebbe wrote a letter of consolation to his in-law that was later included as Iggeret HaKodesh chapter 28 in Tanya. His death is thought to have delayed the major Berditchev–Liadi marriage of his son, eventually held in summer 1807 after the year of mourning.
Tags: meir of berditchev, levi yitzchak of berditchev, schneur zalman, iggeret hakodesh

Title: Pidyon HaBen of Rabbi Baruch Shalom with the Alter Rebbe's discourse
Summary: On Erev Chanukah 5566, a pidyon haben was performed for the infant Baruch Shalom, son of the Tzemach Tzedek, at which the Alter Rebbe delivered a chassidic discourse.
Story: The Alter Rebbe delivered a chassidic discourse at the pidyon haben feast for his grandson Baruch Shalom on Erev Chanukah 5566 (December 1805). The discourse is preserved in Maamarei Admur HaZaken 5566. Because Baruch Shalom was a 'safek bechor' (doubtful firstborn), the pidyon was performed from doubt — a notable halachic detail in the family record.
Tags: alter-rebbe, baruch-shalom, tzemach-tzedek, pidyon-haben, discourse

Title: R' Mordechai of Lechovitch letter on new EY gabbaim
Summary: On 11 Kislev 5566 R' Mordechai of Lechovitch wrote confirming R' Aharon and R' Yisrael of Ostravna as the trusted treasurers for EY funds.
Story: R' Mordechai of Lechovitch wrote on 11 Kislev 5566 urging that whoever is for God should ensure their tzedakah is given to the appointed treasurers - R' Aharon of Ostravna and his colleague R' Yisrael. This formalized the new fund-collection structure established under R' Avraham of Kalisk's leadership outside the Alter Rebbe's network.
Tags: mordechai of lechovitch, aharon of ostravna, yisrael of ostravna, eretz yisrael fund

Title: R' Baruch ben Eliyahu prints Tanya in Shklov
Summary: The printer R' Baruch ben Eliyahu issued an edition of Tanya in Shklov in 5566.
Story: In 5566 (1806) the Shklov printer R' Baruch ben Eliyahu, working with his partner R' Yitzchak ben Shmuel, brought Tanya to press. Earlier authorities mistakenly identified this printer as a grandson of the Alter Rebbe (son of Freida); in fact he was the well-known printer who had previously worked in Shklov, Dubrovna and Ladi.
Tags: tanya, shklov, alter rebbe, printing

Title: Sixth edition of Tanya printed in Shklov with revised Igeret HaTeshuva
Summary: The Shklov 1806 edition of the Tanya included the Alter Rebbe's revised Igeret HaTeshuva, also issued separately as its own booklet.
Story: For this 5566 (1806) Shklov printing—the sixth edition within roughly a decade—the Alter Rebbe re-edited Igeret HaTeshuva and entrusted it to press together with the Tanya. The reworked Igeret HaTeshuva also appeared as a 20-folio standalone booklet in Shklov the same year.
Tags: alter rebbe, tanya, shklov, igeret hateshuva

Title: Tanya printed in Shklov
Summary: Tanya was printed in Shklov in 5566 (1806).
Story: The Shklov print shop, operated by R' Mordechai HaLevi Horowitz, produced this edition of Tanya. It was one of several editions of the Alter Rebbe's writings issued in Russia before 1826.
Tags: tanya, shklov, alter rebbe, russia

Title: Passing of R' Shalom Shachna, father of the Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: Rabbi Shalom Shachna, father of the Tzemach Tzedek, passed away in the summer of 5567.
Story: Rabbi Shalom Shachna died in the summer of 5567 (1807), as established in the Igrot Kodesh of the Alter Rebbe. The dating became halachically relevant because the Tzemach Tzedek's son Baruch Shalom was born in 5566, before his namesake grandfather's death — a fact that complicates the Ashkenazi custom against naming a child for a living relative.
Tags: shalom-shachna, tzemach-tzedek, schneersohn, ancestry

Title: Passing of R' Shalom Shachna, son-in-law of the Alter Rebbe
Summary: R' Shalom Shachna, the Alter Rebbe's son-in-law and partner in the Slavita print shop, passed away in 5567 (1807).
Story: From 1800 until his death, R' Shalom Shachna had occupied himself with printing the Talmud and Tur in Slavita on behalf of the Alter Rebbe, partnering with the Rebbe's brother R' Mordechai of Orsha. He likely also collaborated on printing the original Tanya in 1796–1797.
Tags: shalom shachna, alter rebbe, slavita, printing

Title: Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev family unites with Alter Rebbe family
Summary: R' Yekutiel Zusman, grandson of R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, marries the Alter Rebbe's granddaughter in Sivan 5567.
Story: In Sivan 5567 R' Yekutiel Zusman, grandson of R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, married a granddaughter of the Alter Rebbe. The two rebbes had been calling each other 'mechutan' (in-law) in earlier letters in anticipation of the match. R' Levi Yitzchak had stood with the Alter Rebbe through the dispute with R' Avraham of Kalisk, both regarding chassidic doctrine and regarding fundraising for the Land of Israel.
Tags: alter rebbe, levi yitzchak of berditchev, yekutiel zusman, marriage, mechutanim

Title: The grand Zhlobin wedding unites the Berditchev and Liadi dynasties
Summary: The famous 'Zhlobiner chasunah' takes place around Parshat Naso 5567, joining a grandchild of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev to Sarah, daughter of the Mitteler Rebbe.
Story: Around Parshat Naso in summer 5567, the celebrated 'Zhlobiner chasunah' was held in Zhlobin, drawing thousands of Chassidim from across Russia. The bride was Sarah, daughter of Rabbi Dovber (the future Mitteler Rebbe); the groom was a son of Rabbi Meir, son of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev. The match had been arranged by 5564 but was delayed by Rabbi Meir's death in 5566 and the subsequent mourning year.
Tags: zhlobin, marriage, levi yitzchak of berditchev, schneur zalman, mitteler rebbe, sarah

Title: Likutei Moharan printed in Ostroh
Summary: Likutei Moharan, the central work of Rabbi Nachman of Breslov, was printed in Ostroh in 5568.
Story: Likutei Moharan, the foundational chassidic text of the Breslov movement by Rabbi Nachman of Breslov, was first printed in Ostroh in 5568 (1808), during the author's lifetime.
Tags: nachman of breslov, likutei moharan, ostroh

Title: Vilna Gaon students immigrate to Safed and Tiberias
Summary: Opponents of the chasidic movement, the Perushim, made aliyah to Safed and Tiberias.
Story: The arrival of the Vilna Gaon's students brought the European divisions between chasidim and their opponents into Eretz Yisrael, intensifying communal tensions in the Holy Land.
Tags: mitnagdim, vilna-gaon, safed, tiberias, aliyah

Title: Second Berditchev–Liadi marriage links the dynasties
Summary: Rabbi Yekutiel Zalman, grandson of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, marries Rebbetzin Rivka, daughter of the Mitteler Rebbe, in the winter of 5568.
Story: Months after the grand Zhlobin wedding, a second match further tied the two dynasties: Rabbi Yekutiel Zalman, son of Rabbi Yosef Bunem and grandson of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, married Rebbetzin Rivka, daughter of the Mitteler Rebbe. The Tzemach Tzedek—their future brother-in-law—noted in a manuscript a discourse delivered by the Alter Rebbe on the second night of Parshat Yitro 5568, identifying it with this winter wedding.
Tags: marriage, yekutiel zalman, rivka, mitteler rebbe, levi yitzchak of berditchev

Title: Passing of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev
Summary: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, fellow disciple of the Maggid and close associate of the Alter Rebbe, passes away on 25 Tishrei 5570 after some 25 years leading the Berditchev community.
Story: On 25 Tishrei 5570, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev passed away after leading the Berditchev community since around 5545. The Alter Rebbe traveled to Berditchev for the consolation of mourners and remained in Volhynia through the winter of 5570. At the widow's request, he spent Pesach in Rabbi Levi Yitzchak's home and personally conducted the seder; during his stay there he was also asked to weigh in on one of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak's final halachic rulings on sirchot.
Tags: levi yitzchak of berditchev, yahrzeit, berditchev, ukraine, schneur zalman, volhynia

Title: Alter Rebbe describes separate Chabad fund for Tzfat exiles
Summary: In a 5570 letter the Alter Rebbe describes raising and sending funds separately to the Chabad chassidim displaced from Tiberias to Tzfat.
Story: In a 5570 letter the Alter Rebbe writes that he is sending separate support 'to revive the spirit of the lowly and crushed' Chabad community that had moved from Tiberias to Tzfat to escape harassment. Followers of R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev who had also fled to Tzfat stood with the Chabad chassidim. The Alter Rebbe coordinated with R' Levi Yitzchak's trusted messenger to transmit the funds.
Tags: alter rebbe, tzfat, tiberias, kollel chabad, levi yitzchak of berditchev, fundraising

Title: Charity assessment in Rohatchov signed by Alter Rebbe
Summary: A charity assessment in Rohatchov in winter 5570 was signed by the Alter Rebbe, with R' Shmuel listed as 'mo"tz'.
Story: In the winter of 5570 (1810) a tzedakah assessment for the town of Rohatchov was issued, bearing the signature of the Alter Rebbe. R' Shmuel, later the maggid of Hebron, appears on it as 'mo"tz' (moreh tzedek), reflecting his earlier rabbinic role in that town.
Tags: chabad, rohatchov, alter rebbe, tzedakah, russia

Title: Fire at Alter Rebbe's home destroys Shulchan Aruch manuscript
Summary: A fire at the Alter Rebbe's home in Liadi consumed his autograph manuscript of the Shulchan Aruch he had authored.
Story: In 5570 (1810), a fire broke out at the home of Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, the founder of Chabad. The blaze destroyed the autograph manuscript of his Shulchan Aruch HaRav, the legal code he had composed. It was the first of two devastating fires that struck his household in his final years.
Tags: alter rebbe, liadi, shulchan aruch, fire, manuscripts

Title: Fire destroys Alter Rebbe's home in Liadi
Summary: A large fire struck the Alter Rebbe's home in Liadi in 5570 (1810).
Story: According to his sons' later account, this blaze together with a second fire in 1812 consumed the Alter Rebbe's own holograph manuscripts of the Shulchan Aruch. The disasters meant the eventual printed Shulchan Aruch had to be reconstructed from disciples' copies.
Tags: alter rebbe, liadi, fire, manuscripts lost

Title: Great fire at the Alter Rebbe's home in Liadi
Summary: A major fire struck the Alter Rebbe's home in Liadi in 5570, evidently destroying his original manuscript of the Tanya.
Story: In 5570 (1810), a great fire struck Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi's home in Liadi. The original manuscript of the Tanya is believed to have been consumed in this fire, though a corrected manuscript of Iggeret HaTeshuvah in his hand survived in the Chabad library archives.
Tags: alter rebbe, liadi, fire, tanya manuscript

Title: Great fire destroys Alter Rebbe's house in Lyadi
Summary: A sudden fire consumed the Alter Rebbe's home in Lyadi while he was traveling in Volhynia, destroying valuable books and manuscripts.
Story: At the end of winter 5570 (early 1810), a small spark ignited a sudden blaze in the Alter Rebbe's large house in Lyadi while he was on a journey through the Volhynia provinces. Within minutes the entire roof and interior were engulfed, and nothing could be saved — not the costly seforim, household possessions, jewelry, nor pledged valuables that had been kept in the home. Most painful was the loss of the Rebbe's own manuscript glosses on the four sections of Shulchan Aruch.
Tags: lyadi, fire, manuscripts, alter rebbe, volhynia

Title: Great fire in Liadi destroys Alter Rebbe's autograph Shulchan Aruch
Summary: The great fire in Liadi in 5570 (1810) destroyed the autograph manuscript of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch along with other writings such as his teshuvah on mechiras chametz.
Story: The fire consumed the Alter Rebbe's own handwritten Shulchan Aruch and other manuscripts that consequently never reached print. Among the lost works is the kuntres explaining all the details of the bill of sale for chametz, referenced in his general letter on the subject. The Tzemach Tzedek later searched for this teshuvah but could not locate it.
Tags: alter rebbe, liadi, fire, shulchan aruch, manuscript loss

Title: Passing of Rabbi Nachman of Breslov in Uman
Summary: Rabbi Nachman of Breslov, great-grandson of the Baal Shem Tov, passed away in Uman in 5571.
Story: Rabbi Nachman of Breslov (5532–5571 / 1772–1810), great-grandson of the Baal Shem Tov, passed away in Uman, where his gravesite remains a major pilgrimage destination for his followers.
Tags: nachman of breslov, uman, breslov

Title: R' Baruch of Mezhibuzh appoints leaders of Tiberias Chasidim
Summary: After R' Avraham of Kalisk's passing in 5570, R' Baruch of Mezhibuzh appointed R' Tzvi Hirsch Segal of Harki and R' Meir of Bychov to lead the Tiberias Chasidic community.
Story: Following the death of R' Avraham of Kalisk in 5570, the leadership of the general Chasidic community of Tiberias was reorganized by R' Baruch of Mezhibuzh. He asked the community to unify behind R' Tzvi Hirsch Halevi, with R' Meir of Bychov serving alongside him. The appointment letter, preserved in Yagdil Torah, asked the community to 'be one bound bundle in love, brotherhood, peace and friendship.'
Tags: baruch of mezhibuzh, avraham of kalisk, meir of bychov, tzvi hirsch segal, tiberias

Title: R. Levi Yitzchok of Berditchev passes away
Summary: R. Levi Yitzchok of Berditchev passed away in 5570 (1810), after which questions on his lenient ruling on sirkhot were sent to the Alter Rebbe.
Story: Late in life R. Levi Yitzchok had permitted certain sirkhot via squeezing, generating controversy among Berditchev rabbis. After his passing the queries on his ruling were referred to the Alter Rebbe, who defended R. Levi Yitzchok's psak in several responsa.
Tags: levi yitzchok of berditchev, yahrtzeit, sirkhot, alter rebbe

Title: R. Shmuel Segal of Rogatchov listed in Alter Rebbe's charity assessment
Summary: R. Shmuel Segal, moreh tzedek of Rogatchov, was first mentioned in a charity assessment signed by the Alter Rebbe.
Story: In the winter of 1810, R. Shmuel Segal was first recorded as 'moreh tzedek of the community of Rogatchov' in a charity assessment signed by the Alter Rebbe. He served as moreh tzedek in Rogatchov for some fifteen years before making aliyah to the Land of Israel in 1824.
Tags: rogatchov, russia, alter rebbe, shmuel segal, charity

Title: Tikkunei Zohar printed in Kapust by Yehuda Yaffe
Summary: The Tikkunei Zohar was printed in Kapust in 5570 at the press of Yehuda son of A.S. Feivush Yaffe.
Story: This authentic Kapust edition of the Tikkunei Zohar carried a censor's approval dated 1810. Years later, a clandestine reprint forged a title page dated 5585 (1825) but copied this same 1810 censor approval, revealing the forgery. The Yaffe family press was a leading Hebrew printer in White Russia during the early nineteenth century.
Tags: kapust, kabbalah, tikkunei zohar, yehuda yaffe, russia, belarus

Title: Mitteler Rebbe sends circular letter about the Lyadi fire
Summary: Rabbi Dovber wrote a general letter to chassidim describing the devastation of the Lyadi fire.
Story: In Nisan-Iyar 5570 (April-May 1810), shortly after the great fire in Lyadi, the Mitteler Rebbe sent a circular letter to the wider community of chassidim describing the loss. He underscored particularly the destruction of his father's manuscripts of glosses on the four sections of Shulchan Aruch, alongside books, household goods, and pledged valuables that had been kept in the house. He warned chassidim of the terrible blow this would be to his elderly father when he returned.
Tags: lyadi, fire, letter, mitteler rebbe, manuscripts

Title: Alter Rebbe writes Tishrei 1811 epistle on polished shechitah knives
Summary: Late in his life, in 5571 (1811), the Alter Rebbe wrote a major epistle defending the chassidic enactment of polished shechitah knives.
Story: The letter (Iggeret 61) reports R. Chaim of Volozhin's 1803 disclosure and lists the many regions and communities that had by then accepted the polished knives — including Ukraine, parts of Poland, Volyn, and the Holy Land. The enactment, instituted at the Maggid's beit midrash, eventually became universal Jewish practice.
Tags: alter rebbe, shechita, polished knives, mezeritch, letter, 1811

Title: Alter Rebbe writes to rabbis of Vilna on polished knives and peace
Summary: In the week of Parshat Nitzavim 5571 the Alter Rebbe wrote to the rabbis of Vilna concerning the chassidic practice of slaughtering with polished knives and the history of the disputes.
Story: The letter, printed as Iggeret 61 in volume one of his published correspondence, was addressed to the great rabbis of Vilna and asked them to deal mercifully with the chassidim under their authority. The Alter Rebbe acknowledged the rabbis' authority and urged that 'all the people will have peace.'
Tags: alter rebbe, vilna, nitzavim, 5571, polished knives, shechita

Title: Alter Rebbe writes to Vilna scholars on polished shechita knives
Summary: In 5571 the Alter Rebbe wrote to the rabbis of Vilna explaining why Chassidim used polished knives for shechita.
Story: In 5571 the Alter Rebbe addressed a letter to the rabbis of Vilna detailing the reasons Chassidim insisted on polished shechita knives. In a handwritten note in the margin he asked R' Yehuda Leib of Kraz and the other learned Anash of Vilna to study the relevant gemara and poskim carefully so they could respond to objections. The letter shows that an active Chabad scholarly group remained in Vilna into the second decade of the 19th century.
Tags: vilna, shechita, yehuda leib of kraz, halacha, alter rebbe

Title: Marriage testimony for Mitteler Rebbe's daughter and R' Yaakov Yisrael of Cherkas
Summary: A signed testimony document followed the marriage of Rabbi Yaakov Yisrael of Cherkas to a daughter of the Mitteler Rebbe.
Story: On 7 Shevat 5571 (February 1, 1811), a 'zichron edut' testimony document was drawn up concerning the marriage of Rabbi Yaakov Yisrael of Cherkas to a daughter of Rabbi Dovber, the Mitteler Rebbe. The document records the name of the Mitteler Rebbe's wife as Shaina daughter of R' Yaakov, providing one of the few clear sources for identifying his father-in-law by name.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, cherkas, marriage, family, shaina

Title: Alter Rebbe flees Liadi as Napoleon's army advances
Summary: During Napoleon's invasion of Russia, the Alter Rebbe fled Liadi with his family, and the rebbe's house was destroyed by fire.
Story: When Napoleon's army advanced into Russia in 1812, the Alter Rebbe and his family abandoned Liadi to escape the French. The entire Bais HaRav in Liadi was consumed by fire in the aftermath. This destruction left the family destitute and later prompted a special ma'amad collection organized to rebuild a home for the rebbe's family in Lubavitch.
Tags: napoleon, war, liadi, russia

Title: Alter Rebbe flees Liadi during Napoleon's invasion of Russia
Summary: At the end of 5572 the Alter Rebbe fled his home in Liadi as Napoleon's forces advanced through Russia.
Story: During the French invasion of Russia in 1812, Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi abandoned his home and possessions and joined the retreating Russian populace. A second fire struck the household during these upheavals. The Alter Rebbe was carried from place to place along the way, never to return home.
Tags: alter rebbe, liadi, napoleon, war, russia, flight

Title: Alter Rebbe flees Liadi with family ahead of French advance
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi abandoned his home, library, and possessions to flee deep into Russia rather than remain under French rule.
Story: In 1812, as Napoleon's army advanced into Belarus and neared Dubrovna, Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi abandoned his spacious home, valuable library, and all possessions in Liadi, fleeing with his family and close followers — including his son DovBer — into the Russian interior out of loyalty to the Russian throne. The French subsequently looted and burned the family's property, inflicting a 60,000-ruble loss. The family wandered through Kursk province for about six months in severe destitution, a period that ended with the Alter Rebbe's passing in Haditch in Poltava province.
Tags: alter-rebbe, napoleon, 1812-war, liadi, dubrovna, russia, exile, kursk

Title: Death of the Alter Rebbe
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, founder of Chabad, passed away while fleeing Napoleon's invading army.
Story: In 1812, Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, the founder of Chabad and first Lubavitcher Rebbe, passed away while fleeing from Napoleon's invading army through Russia. His son Rabbi Dovber succeeded him and the following year settled in Lubavitch, establishing the town as Chabad's capital. The Alter Rebbe's flight reflected his strong opposition to Napoleon's potential influence on Jewish life.
Tags: russia, alter rebbe, schneur zalman, napoleon, death

Title: Passing of Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi
Summary: The Alter Rebbe, founder of Chabad, passed away in 1812.
Story: His passing came during the chaotic retreat of the Russian population fleeing Napoleon's invasion. He was succeeded by his son, Rabbi Dov Ber, the Mitteler Rebbe.
Tags: alter rebbe, schneur zalman of liadi

Title: Passing of the Alter Rebbe
Summary: Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi passed away on 24 Tevet 5573 in Piena.
Story: Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi, founder of Chabad chassidut, passed away on 24 Tevet 5573 (1812) in the town of Piena during the flight from Napoleon's invading army. He was succeeded by his son, Rabbi Dov Ber, the Mitteler Rebbe.
Tags: alter rebbe, piena, yud tet kislev, tevet

Title: Passing of the Alter Rebbe during the French invasion
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi died in 1812 during his flight from the Napoleonic invasion of Russia.
Story: After fleeing Liadi ahead of Napoleon's advancing army, the Alter Rebbe died in the course of the wartime journey. His passing left the Chasidim of White Russia without their guiding teacher amid the devastation of the war, setting the stage for his son's succession the following year.
Tags: alter rebbe, shneur zalman of liadi, napoleon, war of 1812, white russia, passing

Title: Passing of the Alter Rebbe of Lubavitch
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, founder of Chabad, passes away on 24 Tevet 5573.
Story: On 24 Tevet 5573 the Alter Rebbe, founder of Chabad chassidut, passed away during the flight from Napoleon's invading armies. His son Rabbi Dovber Schneuri (the Mittler Rebbe) succeeded him as leader of Chabad. The Mittler Rebbe continued his father's practice of collecting and sending funds to the Chabad community in Tzfat, in coordination with R' Yisrael of Pikov, son of R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev.
Tags: alter rebbe, schneur zalman of liadi, death, chabad, lubavitch, russia

Title: R' Yissachar Ber Horowitz studies with MaharI"L in Yanovich
Summary: MaharI"L of Yanovich taught R' Yissachar Ber Horowitz in 5572, confirming he was settled in Yanovich by that year.
Story: R' Yissachar Ber Horowitz, who later served ten years as rabbi of Lubavitch, recorded that he heard a particular teaching from MaharI"L 'while studying with him in 5572.' This testimony fixes the earliest documented year for MaharI"L's residence in Yanovich, where he served as moreh tzedek.
Tags: mahari"l, yanovich, lubavitch, students

Title: R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz studies with MaHaRiL of Yanovich
Summary: In 5572 the young R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz, later moreh tzedek of Lubavitch, studied under R. Yehuda Leib of Yanovich.
Story: After marrying into a Yanovich family, R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz settled there as a melamed and studied Torah with the Alter Rebbe's brother, the MaHaRiL of Yanovich, in 5572 (1812). Years later he would cite halachic teachings he heard from MaHaRiL during this period in his own responsa.
Tags: yissachar ber horowitz, maharil of yanovich, yanovich

Title: Schneur Zalman of Liadi passes away
Summary: The first Lubavitcher Rebbe and founder of Chabad Chasidism passes away.
Story: His freedom from czarist prison in 1798 had launched a new stage of public chasidic teaching, a development the Rebbe Rayatz pointed to when expanding the dissemination of Chasidut to wider audiences in Riga.
Tags: alter-rebbe, schneur-zalman, passing

Title: Second fire destroys manuscripts as Alter Rebbe flees Napoleon
Summary: A second fire late in 5572 (1812), during the Alter Rebbe's flight from Napoleon's advance, destroyed remaining Shulchan Aruch manuscripts.
Story: As the Alter Rebbe fled with his household during the Napoleonic invasion, fire consumed what remained of his autograph Shulchan Aruch manuscripts. Only copies in students' hands survived, becoming the basis for the eventual posthumous printed edition.
Tags: alter rebbe, napoleon, fire, war, manuscripts lost

Title: Tzemach Tzedek defines the scope of Torah Or
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek wrote that Torah Or contains the Alter Rebbe's maamarim from 5556 (1795/6) through the end of 5572 (1812).
Story: In a letter, the Tzemach Tzedek explained that Torah Or specifically draws from the Alter Rebbe's maamarim of this period because it was during these years that the Chabad explanations of his thought were elaborated in depth. The Mitteler Rebbe similarly dated the regular flow of public discourses as beginning around 1795/6.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, torah or, alter rebbe, maamarim

Title: War of 1812 destroys Rabbi Schneur's property in Lyady
Summary: The enemy destroyed Rabbi Schneur Zalman's property during the war of 1812, causing losses estimated at 60,000 rubles.
Story: During Napoleon's 1812 invasion of Russia, the property of Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi was destroyed by the enemy, with damages reaching 60,000 rubles according to his own account. He subsequently traveled from Kremenchug to Shklov collecting donations to cover these losses, and his associates continued the fundraising effort afterward. These collected funds, totaling 35,000 rubles, later became central evidence in the 1825 investigation against his son Rabbi DovBer.
Tags: russia, napoleonic war, kremenchug, shklov, property loss, alter rebbe

Title: Alter Rebbe flees Lyadi with family ahead of Napoleon's invasion
Summary: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul the Alter Rebbe and his family fled Lyadi to Krasna as the French army approached.
Story: On Friday, Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5572 (around August 7, 1812), as Napoleon's army advanced on White Russia, Rabbi Schneur Zalman traveled with his entire household to Krasna. The following Friday they had to flee further from the French. The Mitteler Rebbe recorded that they escaped with only two wagons carrying twenty-eight souls — leaving all heavy possessions behind, despite the elderly Rebbe's frailty and the harshness of the journey.
Tags: napoleon, war, lyadi, krasna, flight, alter rebbe

Title: Alter Rebbe arrives in Piena after months of wartime wandering
Summary: After months on the road as a refugee, the Alter Rebbe reached the town of Piena on Erev Shabbat Vayishlach.
Story: On Erev Shabbat parashat Vayishlach 5573 (December 1812), Rabbi Schneur Zalman reached the town of Piena, exhausted and elderly. The Tzemach Tzedek records that the harshness of the winter, the cold, and the constant displacement were far beyond what the aged Rebbe could bear physically. Yet he had refused under any circumstance to remain even one day under French rule, declaring he would not live under Napoleon's government.
Tags: napoleon, war, piena, alter rebbe, flight

Title: Alter Rebbe of Chabad passes away on 24 Tevet
Summary: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, the Alter Rebbe and founder of Chabad, passed away on 24 Tevet 5573.
Story: The Alter Rebbe died on 24 Tevet 5573, during the flight from Napoleon's invasion of Russia. His grandson the future Tzemach Tzedek was 23 years old at the time. Almost all of the Tzemach Tzedek's surviving halachic writings date from after this date, making the rare manuscript in which he still refers to his grandfather as living an unusually early specimen.

Title: Passing of the Alter Rebbe

Title: Family homes in Lyadi reported burned in war's aftermath

Title: Liadi destroyed by fire as Alter Rebbe flees Napoleon's advance

Story: After the Alter Rebbe's passing in late 1812, news arrived that the family's homes in Liadi had been destroyed by fire — described as the 'returning flame' of war. Title: Lubavitch becomes the center of Chabad
Summary: The town of Lubavitch became the worldwide center of Chabad in 5574 with the arrival of the Mitteler Rebbe.
Story: In 5574 (1813/14) the Mitteler Rebbe established his court in Lubavitch, and the town began its 102-year run as the headquarters of the worldwide Chabad movement. Four successive Rebbes would reside there: the Mitteler Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek, the Rebbe Maharash, and the Rebbe Rashab. Alongside the Rebbe the town always had its own moreh tzedek (community rabbi) for everyday halachic questions.

Title: Mitteler Rebbe accepts leadership and a 35,000-ruble fund
Summary: White Russian Chasidim called Rabbi Dovber Schneuri to succeed his late father, pledging to support him and rebuild his property destroyed in the war.
Story: In 1813 the Jews of White Russia summoned Berke Shneur—Rabbi Dovber, the Mitteler Rebbe—to take his father's place as their rebbe. They promised to compensate the family for losses sustained when the enemy destroyed their assets and to provide dignified support through voluntary donations. He gathered 35,000 rubles, distributed among relatives, personal needs, and synagogue construction—an act later cited as evidence in the government's investigation of him.

Title: Mitteler Rebbe and Tzemach Tzedek settle in Lubavitch
Summary: At the end of 5573 and beginning of 5574, the Mitteler Rebbe and his nephew/son-in-law the future Tzemach Tzedek established their court in the town of Lubavitch.

Title: Mitteler Rebbe settles in Lubavitch

Story: In the summer of 1813, Rabbi Dovber, the second Chabad Rebbe, settled in the town of Lubavitch. Title: Mitteler Rebbe settles in Lubavitch as the new Chabad center
Summary: Following the end of the Napoleonic war, the Mitteler Rebbe settled in Lubavitch and made it the center of the Chabad movement.
Story: Shortly after the Alter Rebbe's passing and the conclusion of the Napoleonic war in 5573 (1813), Rabbi Dovber, the second Rebbe of Chabad, established himself in the small White Russian town of Lubavitch. For the next 102 years Lubavitch served as the central seat of the worldwide Chabad movement under successive Rebbes — and from this town the movement took its enduring name.

Title: Mitteler Rebbe settles in the town of Lubavitch
Summary: Rabbi Dovber, the Mitteler Rebbe, settled in the town of Lubavitch in late 5573 and built a home, large synagogue, and library there.
Story: Following the passing of his father in early 5573, the Mitteler Rebbe took up the leadership of Chabad. At the end of that same year (1813) he settled in the small town of Lubavitch. There he constructed a home, a large beit knesset, and a library that became the new center of the movement.

Title: Mitteler Rebbe undertakes fundraising journey through Ukraine and Lithuania
Summary: Rabbi DovBer travelled across Volhynia, Ukraine, Little Russia, and Lithuania to raise funds to rebuild after the family's 1812 losses.
Story: After his father's passing and the family's wartime ruin, in 1813 Rabbi DovBer travelled through the Volhynia, Ukraine, Little Russia, and Lithuania regions to gather support for rebuilding homes, a large synagogue for gatherings and discourses, and household necessities. Communities along the route — both Chassidic and non-Chassidic — convened assemblies and contributed substantial sums, and Belarus communities followed through on the pledges they had sent to him in Kremenchug. In total roughly 35,000 rubles were collected and distributed among family members for housing, clothing, books, and about six months of living expenses.

Title: Mittler Rebbe establishes the Chabad center in Lubavitch

Summary: Rabbi Dovber, the second Chabad Rebbe, settled in Lubavitch in late summer 5573, inaugurating the town's century as Chabad world headquarters.

Title: Passing of the Alter Rebbe
Summary: The Alter Rebbe, Shneur Zalman of Liadi, passed away in 5573 (1812–1813).
Story: Throughout his life, the Alter Rebbe had refused to print his other works, including the Shulchan Aruch. Only after his passing did his sons bring the Shulchan Aruch to press. His maamarim, recorded by various scribes, formed the basis of subsequent Chabad teachings.

Title: Tzemach Tzedek asks Alter Rebbe a Yevamot question
Summary: A note on tractate Yevamot in manuscript 1024 records the young Tzemach Tzedek asking his grandfather the Alter Rebbe about a difficult halacha.
Story: In manuscript 1024 (folio 133a), later printed in Tzemach Tzedek Milu'im vol. 5 §59, the young Menachem Mendel records a question on tractate Yevamot that he asked 'before my grandfather and teacher the Gaon.' Title: Passing of the Alter Rebbe in the village of Piena

Story: Forced to flee Liadi during Napoleon's 1812 campaign, the Alter Rebbe was carried from town to town and village to village for several months. Title: Passing of the Alter Rebbe, Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, founder of Chabad, passed away on 24 Tevet 5573 while in flight from Napoleon's army.
Story: On Motzaei Shabbat, 24 Tevet 5573, after months of displacement following his flight from Liadi, the Alter Rebbe passed away at the age of 66. He was buried in the town of Haditch. Communities of his followers everywhere observed deep mourning.

Title: Passing of the Alter Rebbe in Piena
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi passed away in Piena on the night of 24 Tevet.
Story: On Motzei Shabbat parashat Shemot, the beginning of 24 Tevet 5573 (around January 8, 1813), at approximately 11 o'clock at night, the Alter Rebbe passed away in the town of Piena. His grandson the Tzemach Tzedek described the event as the ark of holiness being taken captive — the light of Israel and the anointed of Hashem summoned to the heavenly academy. He died as a wartime refugee, having refused to remain under Napoleonic rule.

Title: Passing of the Alter Rebbe
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, founder of Chabad, passed away on 24 Tevet 5573 after fleeing the Napoleonic war.

Title: Passing of the Alter Rebbe on 24 Tevet 5573
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, the Alter Rebbe of Chabad, passed away on 24 Tevet 5573, corresponding to January 1813.
Story: The Alter Rebbe died on 24 Tevet 5573 while in flight from the Napoleonic war, leaving his Shulchan Aruch still unprinted. Leadership of Chabad passed to his son, the Mitteler Rebbe, who would oversee posthumous publication of his father's halachic and chassidic works.

Summary: Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi, founder of Chabad, passed away on 24 Tevet 5573 in Pyena after fleeing the advancing French army.
Story: After abandoning his home in Liadi during Napoleon's 1812 invasion, the Alter Rebbe died in flight, leaving his household possessions consumed by fire. Title: Mitteler Rebbe organizes Ma'amad fund distribution
Summary: In Tevet 5574 the Mitteler Rebbe organized the distribution of 35,000 rubles collected to rebuild the Rebbe's household after the war.
Story: Following his father's passing, the Mitteler Rebbe needed to rehabilitate the family after the destruction of the Liadi home. He entrusted the distribution to senior chassid Reb Pinchas Shick of Shklov, with Reb Shlomo Freides and Reb Zalman Roizes as overseers. Two-thirds went to relatives of the Alter Rebbe; one-third was used by the Mitteler Rebbe to build his home and synagogue in Lubavitch. Title: Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch first edition

Story: In 5574 (1814), the first edition of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch was published in Kapust. The work compiles Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi's revised rulings on Jewish law. The Lubavitch Library preserves a copy of this edition.

Title: Construction begins on the Mittler Rebbe's great synagogue in Lubavitch
Summary: In 5574 (1814) the Mittler Rebbe began constructing a large wooden synagogue in his courtyard in Lubavitch, a project that continued for a year or two.
Story: After purchasing a wooden house from the local nobleman Krauer, the Mittler Rebbe built a sizable synagogue in the courtyard. According to the tsarist investigator Korbitsky's later report, it measured roughly 21 by 13 meters; the Rebbe Rayatz recorded much larger dimensions. The site reportedly stood where the Alter Rebbe had studied with R' Yissachar Ber decades earlier.

Title: Construction of large wooden synagogue begins in Lubavitch
Summary: The Mittler Rebbe began building a large wooden synagogue in the Lubavitch courtyard in 5574, taking one to two years to complete.
Story: The synagogue measured roughly 21 by 13 meters with a vestibule open on two sides and a central bimah. According to investigator Korbitzky's 1826 court report, the building also housed Torah scrolls written by the Yanovich scribe, menorahs ordered from Petersburg, and a library of 611 books kept in four cabinets and available for lending.

Title: First edition of Alter Rebbe's Hilchos Pesach printed
Summary: In 5574 (1814) the first printed edition of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch Hilchos Pesach appeared, including the nusach of Seder Mechiras Chametz and the general letter to the chassidim.
Story: Printed years after the great Liadi fire and after the Alter Rebbe's own passing, this edition preserved the public-facing portions of his rulings on selling chametz. The accompanying kuntres explaining the details of the sale was not included; it had not been printed in the Siddur or the Shulchan Aruch and is presumed lost in the Liadi fire of 5570.

Title: First volumes of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch printed in Shklov-Kapust
Summary: The first edition of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch began appearing across 1814–1816 in six volumes printed in Shklov and Kapust.
Story: Roughly a year after the Alter Rebbe's passing, his sons brought the long-awaited Shulchan Aruch to press, drawing on student manuscripts to replace the holograph copies lost in the fires. The first volumes, including hilchot Pesach and the laws of niddah, appeared in 5574 (1814).

Title: Mitteler Rebbe arranges distribution of maamad funds after the Alter Rebbe's passing
Summary: At the end of the first year after the Alter Rebbe's passing, the Mitteler Rebbe organizes distribution of 35,000 rubles in maamad funds among the Alter Rebbe's descendants.
Story: In Tevet 5574 (December 1813–January 1814), one year after the passing of the Alter Rebbe on 24 Tevet 5573, the Mitteler Rebbe arranged the distribution of 35,000 rubles in maamad funds. The funds had been collected from chasidim to rebuild the household of the rebbe in Lubavitch after the original household in Liadi was destroyed by fire when the family fled Napoleon's invasion. The Mitteler Rebbe entrusted the distribution to Reb Pinchas Shick of Shklov, with Reb Shlomo Freidin and Reb Zalman Roizes Slonim of Shklov as oversight, allocating shares to his brothers, sisters, children, stepmother, and other relatives of the Alter Rebbe.

Title: Mitteler Rebbe letter to Meisels and Itinga on aliyah plans
Summary: The Mitteler Rebbe wrote to R. Moshe Meisels and R. Baruch Mordechai Itinga advising against their planned aliyah at that time.
Story: Around 13 Iyar 1814, the Mitteler Rebbe wrote a counsel-letter to two prominent Vilna chassidim, R. Moshe Meisels (author of Shirat Moshe) and R. Baruch Mordechai Itinga (son-in-law of the Vilna av beit din), advising them against their plan to ascend to the Land of Israel. He warned that they would not enjoy long life there, citing reasons known to him. He added that if they nevertheless decided to settle, they should choose Jerusalem rather than Safed or Tiberias, and that the chassidic fund would allocate fifty gold coins annually for their support.

Title: Mittler Rebbe sends three foundational letters to Anash including Kuntres HaHispaalus
Summary: In 5574 (1814), his second year of nesius, the Mittler Rebbe sent three sequential letters to the chassidim, the second of which became Kuntres HaHispaalus.
Story: Manuscript evidence in the Library identifies the date as 5574 for all three letters. The first served as introduction, the second became the famous Kuntres HaHispaalus on the levels of emotional response in avodah, and the third was later printed as Shaar HaYichud (Kuntres HaHisbonenus). They were published in reverse order across the following decades.

Title: R' Moshe Meisels asks Mitteler Rebbe about aliyah
Summary: R' Moshe Meisels consulted the Mitteler Rebbe about emigrating to Eretz Yisrael in 1814-1815.
Story: Between 1814 and 1815, R' Moshe Meisels asked the Mitteler Rebbe about settling in Eretz Yisrael. The Rebbe advised against the move at the time and said he would not allocate Chassidic charity funds beyond fifty gold coins for travel expenses for him and R' Baruch Mordechai, rabbi of Bobruisk.

Title: R. Avraham David Wahrman becomes rabbi of Buchach
Summary: Rabbi Avraham David Wahrman moved from Yazlovich to the rabbinate of Buchach in 5574 (1814).
Story: After twenty-four years in Yazlovich, R. Avraham David transferred to the rabbinate of Buchach in 1814, where he remained for the rest of his life. He continued his daily practice of writing chiddushim across all areas of Torah. None of his writings were printed during his lifetime.

Title: Shulchan Aruch HaRav (Hilchot Pesach) printed in Shklov
Summary: An edition of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch covering the Laws of Passover appeared in Shklov in 5574.
Story: This volume bore an authentic Kapust rabbinical censor's stamp with the signature of Rabbi Nachum Yaffe of Kapust beside it. The genuine stamp would later help historians distinguish authentic Russian-Jewish printings from the wave of forgeries that followed the 1837 ban on Hebrew presses.

Title: Sons of Alter Rebbe publish expanded Tanya
Summary: In 5574, after the Alter Rebbe's passing, his sons published an expanded edition of the Tanya adding Iggeret HaKodesh and Kuntres Acharon.
Story: In 5574 (1814), one year after the passing of the Alter Rebbe on 24 Tevet 5573, his holy sons published a new edition of the Tanya. They added two additional sections: Iggeret HaKodesh and Kuntres Acharon. From this edition onward, all printings of the Tanya have contained these five parts.

Title: Tanya and Shulchan Aruch HaRav printed in Shklov
Summary: Another edition of Tanya and the Shulchan Aruch HaRav were printed in Shklov in 5574 (1814).
Story: The year after the Alter Rebbe's passing, his sons brought his Shulchan Aruch to press in Shklov. This edition appeared alongside a new printing of Tanya at the same print shop.

Title: Tanya reprinted in Shklov by the Alter Rebbe's sons with new sections
Summary: In 1814 the Alter Rebbe's sons reprinted the Tanya in Shklov, adding Igeret HaKodesh and Kuntres Acharon for the first time.
Story: This 5574 (1814) Shklov edition, prepared by the author's sons after his death, established the canonical five-part structure—Tanya, Shaar HaYichud VehaEmuna, Igeret HaTeshuva, Igeret HaKodesh, and Kuntres Acharon—that all subsequent Tanya editions would follow.

Title: Mitteler Rebbe distributes ma'amad bais harav funds
Summary: One year after his father's passing, the Mitteler Rebbe organized distribution of 35,000 rubles in ma'amad funds among his family.
Story: In Tevet 5574, one year after the Alter Rebbe's passing, the Mitteler Rebbe arranged the distribution of the ma'amad bais harav fund. He appointed R. Pinchas Schick of Shklov to administer the distribution, with R. Shlomo Freides and R. Zalman Reuzes of Shklov as overseers. Of the 35,000 rubles collected, two-thirds went to descendants of the Alter Rebbe and one-third was used by the Mitteler Rebbe to build his own home, a synagogue in Lubavitch, and to purchase seforim.

Title: Mitteler Rebbe's letter about distribution of Maamad funds
Summary: Rabbi DovBer Schneuri wrote a letter in Tevet 5574 concerning the division of Maamad support funds among family members after his father's passing.
Story: Following the passing of the Alter Rebbe, his son Rabbi DovBer documented the allocation of donor funds collected for the rebbe's household (the maamad). The letter assigned half-yearly living expenses and gifts to relatives. Title: Arbitration agreement before the Mitteler Rebbe between Litoslavsky and Averba
Summary: Landowner Ivan Litoslavsky and Yeshaya Averba sign an arbitration agreement to have a 7,000-ruble debt judged by the Mitteler Rebbe in Lubavitch.
Story: On 24 May 1814, landowner Ivan Litoslavsky and Yeshaya Berkovich Averba of Surazh district, Vitebsk province, signed an agreement in Lubavitch placing their 7,000-ruble debt dispute before the Mitteler Rebbe for binding arbitration. The agreement, witnessed by the Vilna merchant Shmaryahu Benyaminovich Berkin, declared that both parties would accept the rebbe's ruling without appeal. The document was later submitted as evidence to prove that the rebbe had violated Russian law by acting as arbitrator between a Jew and a non-Jew.

Title: Arbitration contract signed before the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: An arbitration agreement was concluded before Rabbi DovBer Schneuri of Lubavitch, showing his role as a recognized adjudicator.
Story: The contract documents a binding arbitration before the Mitteler Rebbe in his role as a religious-legal authority. Such documents were later cited by Khovansky as evidence the Rebbe overstepped purely religious functions by handling civil disputes between Jews and Christians.

Title: Imperial amnesty manifesto of 30 August 1814
Summary: The Tsar issued a general amnesty manifesto on August 30, 1814, pardoning offenses committed prior to that date.
Story: This sweeping amnesty later became the formal grounds on which Governor-General Khovansky recommended not punishing the Mitteler Rebbe for his 1813 fundraising. Despite Khovansky's view that the collection violated the Jewish Constitution, the 1814 manifesto covered actions taken before its issuance.

Title: Standalone teshuva of the Alter Rebbe published in Kapust

Story: The 10-folio Kapust 5575 (1815) quarto presented one of the Alter Rebbe's responsa on its own, alongside other teshuvot that would be embedded into the Shulchan Aruch volumes. It would later be regathered into the Zhitomir 1847 responsa collection.

Title: Approbation of Maharil printed in Tehillim, Shklov
Summary: Maharil, brother of the Alter Rebbe, gave an approbation to a Tehillim printed around 5576 in Shklov.
Story: Rabbi Yehuda Leib of Yanovich (Maharil), the Alter Rebbe's brother, was author of She'erit Yehudah. Among his approbations is one to a Tehillim with anthologized commentaries and Zohar selections, printed in Shklov around 1816. He wrote that he was lending his name 'to strengthen those who hold fast to G-d's Torah.'

Title: Final volumes of Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch issued in Kapust
Summary: The first edition of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch was completed in 1816 with further Kapust volumes covering Orach Chaim.
Story: By 5576 (1816), the Kapust press had issued the additional Orach Chaim, hilchot Shabbat, and hilchot Eruvin volumes that completed the six-part first edition of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch begun two years earlier.

Title: Mitteler Rebbe directs Chassidim to make aliyah
Summary: The Mitteler Rebbe instructed several of his Chassidim, including R' Moshe Meisels, to emigrate to Eretz Yisrael in 1816-1817.
Story: In 1816-1817 (תקע"ו-ז), the Mitteler Rebbe directed several of his Chassidim to settle in Eretz Yisrael. R' Moshe Meisels was among them, and he initially settled in Tzfat after making aliyah.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, aliyah, moshe meisels, tzfat

Title: Mitteler Rebbe founds Chabad settlement in Hebron
Summary: The Mitteler Rebbe established the Chabad community settlement in Hebron.
Story: Between 1816 and 1819, in response to deepening tensions that had developed since 1805 between the general chassidic community of Safed and Tiberias and the local Chabad chassidim, the Mitteler Rebbe founded a separate Chabad yishuv in Hebron. Until this settlement was established, the Mitteler Rebbe had counseled chassidim planning aliyah to settle in Jerusalem instead.
Tags: hebron, chabad, mitteler rebbe, aliyah, yishuv

Title: Mitteler Rebbe prints Siddur Im Da"Ch and Biurei HaZohar in Kapust
Summary: The Mitteler Rebbe issued in Kapust in 1816 his father's siddur supplemented with chassidic discourses, alongside the first edition of Biurei HaZohar.
Story: Following his father's passing, the Mitteler Rebbe brought to press in Kapust the Siddur Im Da"Ch—pairing the Alter Rebbe's siddur with related chassidic discourses—and the 139-folio first edition of Biurei HaZohar. These two volumes anchored the early posthumous publication of the Alter Rebbe's chassidic teachings.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, alter rebbe, kapust, siddur im dach, biurei hazohar

Title: Mitteler Rebbe writes coded letter on the state of Chassidut
Summary: Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch wrote a cryptic letter to close Chassidim addressing a faction claiming the Alter Rebbe had no successor.
Story: In 5576 (1816), early in his leadership, the Mitteler Rebbe sent a heavily coded letter to confidants — including Pinchas Shick of Shklov — about a group of Chassidim who circulated the claim that after the Alter Rebbe's passing there was no rabbi to fill his place and that Chassidut had ceased. The Rebbe acknowledged Pinchas's earlier 'prophecy' that this struggle would arise and pass, and observed that even as Chassidut was being denigrated, the practice of fundraising continued to spread. The letter was later seized from Pinchas Shick's estate and used by an informer as part of the case against the Rebbe.
Tags: mitteler-rebbe, chassidut, internal-dissent, pinchas-shick, shklov, succession

Title: Mittler Rebbe prints Siddur with Chassidus and Biurei HaZohar in Kapust
Summary: In 5576 (1816) the Mittler Rebbe published a Siddur with discourses from his father (Pirush HaMillos) and the volume Biurei HaZohar in Kapust.
Story: Drawing on his own manuscript collection and copies circulating among chassidim, the Mittler Rebbe assembled the Alter Rebbe's discourses on the siddur and on the Zohar. Both volumes were printed in Kapust in 1816. These remain core published texts of the Alter Rebbe's Chassidus.
Tags: mittler-rebbe, kapust, siddur, biurei-hazohar, alter-rebbe

Title: R' Yisrael Yaffe of Kapust prints Shulchan Aruch HaRav
Summary: The Yaffe brothers in Kapust published the first three volumes of Shulchan Aruch HaRav, Orach Chaim.
Story: In 5576 (1816), the brothers R' Yehuda and R' Yisrael Yaffe, sons of the late R' Alexander Sender Feivish Yaffe, printed volumes 1-3 of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim, at their press in Kapust. This R' Yisrael Yaffe is distinct from R' Yisrael ben Yitzchak Yaffe, also a printer in Kapust who later settled in Hebron. Both Yaffes eventually made aliyah and lived in Hebron.
Tags: yisrael yaffe, yehuda yaffe, shulchan aruch harav, kapust, printing, alter rebbe

Title: R. Moshe Meisels makes aliyah to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: R. Moshe Meisels, longtime trustee of the Vilna community, immigrated to the Land of Israel.
Story: Around 1816, R. Moshe Meisels, author of Shirat Moshe and former trustee of the Vilna kehilla, ascended to the Land of Israel. Although the Mitteler Rebbe had earlier advised against this move, in 1816-1817 he instructed several of his chassidim to make aliyah. When the Mitteler Rebbe later founded the Chabad community in Hebron, Meisels became one of its leading members and signed most communal documents between 1827 and 1844.
Tags: moshe meisels, vilna, hebron, aliyah, chabad

Title: Siddur of the Alter Rebbe printed in Kapust
Summary: The Alter Rebbe's Siddur was printed in Kapust in 5576 (1816).
Story: The Kapust print shop, also associated with R' Mordechai HaLevi Horowitz, published the Alter Rebbe's siddur. Kapust would later become an important Chabad center.
Tags: siddur, kapust, alter rebbe, russia

Title: Document confirming Mitteler Rebbe's standing issued in Vitebsk
Summary: Duke Alexander of Württemberg, military governor of White Russia, issued the Mitteler Rebbe a document attesting to his good standing and right to travel and teach.
Story: On March 3, 1816, the former military governor of White Russia, Duke Alexander of Württemberg, gave Rabbi Dovber Schneuri a formal document parallel to the one his father had received in 1801. It described him as an honest man enjoying the full respect of the Jewish community, traveling to teach ethics and beneficial conduct—though, as Khovansky later noted, it conferred no right to collect money.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, dovber schneuri, duke alexander of württemberg, white russia, lubavitch

Title: Imperial decree restricting voluntary donations to signed lists
Summary: An imperial decree of June 14, 1816, required all charitable collections to be backed by signed declarations of consent submitted to the provincial government.
Story: This decree narrowed the definition of 'voluntary donations' under Russian law: only contributions from individuals who had registered written consent with the provincial government could be lawfully collected. Khovansky later cited this 1816 decree to argue that the Mitteler Rebbe's fundraising—lacking signatures or registered authorization—was illegal.
Tags: russia, law, fundraising, tsar

Title: Colel Chabad formally named
Summary: The fund created by Rabbi Schneur Zalman in 1788 received its formal name, Colel Chabad.
Story: Initially established to support chasidic families in the Holy Land, the organization formalized its identity in 1817. Successive Chabad Rebbes used it to channel European Jewish support to the growing community in Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: colel-chabad, charity

Title: Sefer Lachmei Todah published in Offenbach
Summary: R. Zvi Hirsch Halevi Horowitz published Sefer Lachmei Todah in Offenbach in 5577 (1817), containing his eulogy for his father R. Pinchas Horowitz of Frankfurt.
Story: The volume preserves the son's hesped describing the Baal Haflaah's more than thirty-three years of teaching Torah in Frankfurt. This precise phrasing allows historians to pin the Baal Haflaah's tenure to between summer 5531 and summer 5532. Lachmei Todah thus indirectly anchors the dating of the Alter Rebbe's editing of Hilchos Tzitzis and Pesach.
Tags: lachmei todah, offenbach, zvi hirsch horowitz, frankfurt, germany

Title: Sha'ar HaTeshuvah printed in Shklov
Summary: The Mitteler Rebbe's Sha'ar HaTeshuvah V'HaTefilah appeared in Shklov in 5577.
Story: After issuing his father's works in his first years of leadership, the Mitteler Rebbe began printing his own writings. Sha'ar HaTeshuvah V'HaTefilah was published in Shklov in 1817, the first of nearly a yearly publication schedule.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, shklov

Title: Three-judge din Torah in Lubavitch
Summary: A din Torah convened in Lubavitch in 5577 with MaharI"L, the Mitteler Rebbe, and R' Chaim Avraham.
Story: In 5577 (1816/17) a rabbinical court sat in Lubavitch composed of MaharI"L of Yanovich, the Mitteler Rebbe, and his brother R' Chaim Avraham. The proceedings, preserved in the genizah, illustrate how MaharI"L continued to anchor halachic decision-making in the Chabad center even after the Alter Rebbe's death.
Tags: lubavitch, mitteler rebbe, mahari"l, halacha

Title: Imperial Russian library founded with legal-deposit law
Summary: The major Russian imperial library (later Saltykov-Shchedrin) was founded, with a legal-deposit law requiring every printed book to be sent there.
Story: In 5578 (1818), the major Russian imperial library was founded in St. Petersburg, later renamed Saltykov-Shchedrin. From the date of its founding, Russian law required every published book in the empire to be deposited at the library. This made it a near-complete repository of Hebrew printings, including early Chabad publications that emissaries searched there in 1991.
Tags: library, russia, saltykov-shchedrin, leningrad, legal deposit, imperial library

Title: R' Yehuda Leib Zalkind appointed rabbi of Dinaburg
Summary: R' Yehuda Leib Zalkind, the 'Batlan,' was called from Wilkomir to serve as rabbi in Dinaburg around 5578 (1818).
Story: R' Yehuda Leib Zalkind, author of 'Zecher Yehuda,' was a leading disciple of the Alter Rebbe and study-partner of the Tzemach Tzedek. After serving in Wilkomir (Vilna district), he was called around 5578 (1818) to the rabbinate of Dinaburg, first in the old quarter and later in the central new district.
Tags: dinaburg, latvia, rabbinate, zecher-yehuda, wilkomir

Title: Tzemach Tzedek begins responding to halachic questions
Summary: Around 5578, at age 28, the Tzemach Tzedek began answering halachic questions on a regular basis.
Story: While he had written occasional novellae earlier, the Tzemach Tzedek began responding to halachic queries with regularity around 5578, while his great-uncle Maharil of Yanovitch was still the primary respondent in the Chabad community. Responsum §349 in Yoreh Deah and others can be dated to this year, marking the beginning of his fifty-year career as a posek.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, halacha, responsa, career milestone

Title: Derech Chayim printed in Kopust
Summary: Derech Chayim by the Mitteler Rebbe was printed in Kopust in 5579.
Story: Derech Chayim V'Tochachat Mussar HaSechel, an ethical-Chassidic work by the Mitteler Rebbe, appeared in Kopust in 1819. It opened a long series of Mitteler Rebbe publications issued from Kopust.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, kopust

Title: Earliest extant dated Tzemach Tzedek responsum
Summary: The earliest precisely dated responsum reaching us, printed in Yoreh Deah §8, was written in 5579.
Story: Internal evidence in the responsum (which refers to 'last year, 5578') places its composition in 5579. The original autograph has not survived; only a copy in manuscript 1041 with the Tzemach Tzedek's own glosses remains, with a header noting it was 'copied from volume 3 with annotations.' This is currently the oldest dated piece of his responsa literature in our hands.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, responsa, yoreh deah, manuscript 1041

Title: French translation of the Haggadah by David Drach printed in Metz
Summary: David Drach's French translation of the Haggadah, following both Ashkenazic and Sephardic customs, was printed in Metz.
Story: In 5579 (1819), David Drach's French translation of the Haggadah was issued in Metz, following both Ashkenazic and Sephardic customs. The Hebrew original and French translation were printed page-by-page, with a separate French title page. The 127-page work served the French-speaking Jewish community emerging in post-revolutionary France.
Tags: haggadah, french, metz, france, david drach

Title: Volume 1 of Tzemach Tzedek's responsa bound
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek bound the first volume of his collected responsa around 5579.
Story: In his early years the Tzemach Tzedek bound his question-and-answer correspondence into numbered volumes (chelek 1, 2, 3, etc.). Volume 1, containing responsa from his earliest period, was bound around 5579. This volume, like most of the first fourteen, was later lost or destroyed in a fire in Lubavitch.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, responsa, manuscripts, binding

Title: Donation pledges to R. Aharon of Staroshele's Maamad fund
Summary: Nissan Shlomovitch of Chertkov pledges 50 silver rubles annually to R. Aharon Halevi of Staroshele's Maamad fund.
Story: On 12 June 1819 (Tammuz), Nissan Shlomovitch of Chertkov signed a pledge to give 50 silver rubles annually to Rabbi Aharon Halevi of Staroshele, the founder of the breakaway Strashelye branch of Chabad. He also contributed 25 rubles cash at that time. The records of these donations represent a fragment of Maamad-style fundraising for the parallel chassidic court that arose after the passing of the Alter Rebbe.
Tags: staroshele, aharon halevi, maamad, fundraising, vitebsk

Title: Passing of Esther Miriam, daughter of the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: Esther Miriam, a daughter of the Mitteler Rebbe, passed away in Tammuz 5579.
Story: In Tammuz 5579 (July 1819), Esther Miriam, a daughter of the Mitteler Rebbe, passed away. Her matzeva, identified only relatively recently, describes her as 'the modest and honored woman,' a phrasing suggesting she was already married at the time of her death. According to one reconstruction she may have been a first wife of Rabbi Aharon of Kremenchug, before he later married Chaya, daughter of Rebbe Nachman of Breslov.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, family, death, lubavitch, matzeva

Title: Birz kehillah and Chabad chassidim sign shochet agreement
Summary: On 7 Cheshvan 5580 the kehillah of Birz and the local Chabad chassidim signed a formal agreement permitting the chassidim their own shochet alongside the town's two existing shochtim.
Story: Following the Alter Rebbe's ruling requiring polished knives for shechita, chassidim across Lithuania sought their own shochtim. In Birz, where mitnagdic bans had targeted the practice, the two camps reached a written settlement allowing a chassidic shochet provided he submitted to the town rav and shared revenue. The agreement was signed by R. Yitzchak Isaac, mara d'asra of Birz, and the shamash R. David.
Tags: birz, lithuania, shechita, polished knives, 5580, 7 cheshvan, agreement

Title: Aliyah of R' Yisrael Yaffe (the younger) of Kapust
Summary: R' Yisrael Yaffe (the younger, son of A.S. Feivish) made aliyah to Eretz Yisrael from Kapust.
Story: In 5580 (1820), R' Yisrael Yaffe — son of Alexander Sender Feivish Yaffe and one of the Kapust printers of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch — made aliyah and settled in Hebron. The 5599 census recorded him as 64 years old, having come from Kapust in 5580. He is distinct from R' Yisrael ben Yitzchak Yaffe, also of Kapust, who arrived in 5583.
Tags: yisrael yaffe, kapust, hebron, aliyah, printer

Title: Mikdash Melech printed in Sudilkov
Summary: The kabbalistic work Mikdash Melech was printed in Sudilkov in 5580.
Story: Like the Shklov Shulchan Aruch HaRav, this edition bore the authentic Kapust censor's stamp accompanied by Rabbi Nachum Yaffe's signature. It is one of only three known volumes preserving both the genuine stamp and the rabbi's handwritten name, contrasting with later forgeries that copied only the stamp.
Tags: sudilkov, kabbalah, mikdash melech, ukraine

Title: Mitteler Rebbe publishes Ner Mitzvah u'Torah Or in Kapust
Summary: The Mitteler Rebbe issued the first edition of his Ner Mitzvah u'Torah Or in Kapust in 5580 (1820).
Story: This 1820 Kapust printing was among the first books of the Mitteler Rebbe's own discourses to reach press. It would be followed in the next two years by Ateret Rosh, Imrei Bina, and Sha'arei Orah, all printed in Kapust.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, kapust, ner mitzvah, first edition

Title: Ner Mitzvah V'Torah Or printed in Kopust
Summary: The Mitteler Rebbe's Ner Mitzvah V'Torah Or was printed in Kopust in 5580.
Story: Continuing the steady stream of his published works, the Mitteler Rebbe issued Ner Mitzvah V'Torah Or in Kopust in 1820.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, kopust

Title: R' Moshe ben David Yaffe immigrates from Shklov
Summary: R' Moshe ben David Yaffe immigrated to Eretz Yisrael from Shklov in 5580.
Story: According to the 5599 census, R' Moshe ben David, then aged 30, had immigrated from Shklov to Eretz Yisrael in 5580. He was married with two sons at the time of the census and would later serve as an emissary for the Hebron Chabad community and subsequently for the chassidim of Tiberias.
Tags: shklov, hebron, yaffe, aliyah

Title: Shaar HaYichud printed in Kapust as part of Ner Mitzvah V'Torah Or
Summary: In 5580 (1820) the third of the Mittler Rebbe's 1814 letters was printed in Kapust as Shaar HaYichud in the volume Ner Mitzvah V'Torah Or.
Story: Although written in 1814, the third letter was the first of the three to reach print. It appeared in 1820 under the title Shaar HaYichud as part of the published Ner Mitzvah V'Torah Or in Kapust. Kuntres HaHispaalus and the introductory letter would only follow in print decades later.
Tags: mittler-rebbe, kapust, ner-mitzvah-vetorah-or, shaar-hayichud

Title: Aliyah of R' Mordechai of Shklov to Hebron
Summary: R' Mordechai of Shklov made aliyah and settled in Hebron, where his son R' Yisrael joined him two years later.
Story: R' Mordechai made aliyah from Shklov in 5581 (1821), as recorded in the 5599 census. His son R' Yisrael Yaffe joined him in Hebron in 5593 (1833). R' Mordechai signed the 5594 shadar document and the 5603 power-of-attorney for Jerusalem adjudication.
Tags: mordechai of shklov, shklov, hebron, aliyah

Title: Chabad settlement reestablished in Hebron
Summary: Between 5581 and 5583, Chabad chasidim established their settlement in Hebron.
Story: Following the founding of Kollel Chabad in 5565, organized Chabad settlement in Hebron took shape between 5581 and 5583. This community would form the institutional base of Kollel Chabad until the central council later operated from there during the mid-19th century.
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, settlement

Title: Imrei Binah and Ateret Rosh printed in Kopust
Summary: The Mitteler Rebbe published both Imrei Binah and Ateret Rosh in Kopust in 5581.
Story: In 1821 the Mitteler Rebbe issued two volumes from the Kopust press: Imrei Binah, a major Chassidic treatise, and Ateret Rosh. They were part of his prolific publication output during his sixteen years of leadership.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, kopust

Title: Imrei Binah first edition published in Kapust
Summary: The first edition of Imrei Binah by the Mitteler Rebbe was published in Kapust in 5581.
Story: In 5581 (1821), the first edition of Imrei Binah by Rabbi Dovber Schneuri, the Mitteler Rebbe, was published in Kapust. The book is a major Chassidic discourse work by the second Chabad Rebbe. A copy is preserved in the Lubavitch Library.
Tags: imrei binah, mitteler rebbe, kapust

Title: Imrei Binah printed in Kapust
Summary: Imrei Binah was printed in Kapust in 5581.
Story: This volume is one of three known editions to bear both the authentic Kapust censor's stamp and Rabbi Nachum Yaffe's accompanying signature. Such authentic Kapust printings serve as the comparison standard against which later clandestine forgeries can be detected.
Tags: kapust, imrei binah, chabad, russia

Title: Mitteler Rebbe directs Chabad chassidim to settle in Hebron
Summary: Between 5581 and 5583 the Mitteler Rebbe instructed his chassidim in the Holy Land to relocate from Tzfat to Hebron.
Story: Having earlier settled in Tzfat between 5560 and 5565, Chabad chassidim were directed by the Mitteler Rebbe to move to Hebron during 5581-5583. Hebron became the principal Chabad center in the Holy Land for the next century. A handful remained in Tzfat until the 1837 earthquake.
Tags: hebron, mitteler rebbe, tzfat, settlement
