Title: Mitteler Rebbe's Ateret Rosh and Imrei Bina printed in Kapust
Summary: First editions of the Mitteler Rebbe's Ateret Rosh and Imrei Bina were published in Kapust in 5581 (1821).
Story: These two volumes appeared together in 1821 as part of the Mitteler Rebbe's intensive publication campaign at the Kapust press, expanding the printed corpus of Chabad chassidic discourses well beyond what the Alter Rebbe had issued in his lifetime.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, kapust, ateret rosh, imrei bina

Title: R' Leib of Sena emigrates to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: R' Leib of Sena (Chitrik) made aliyah in 1821 according to the Montefiore census of 1839.
Story: The Montefiore census of 1839 records that R' Leib of Sena, known as Chitrik, emigrated to Eretz Yisrael in 1821 and settled in Hebron. He may have stopped in Istanbul on his journey, where he made acquaintances who later helped forward correspondence to Europe.
Tags: leib of sena, chitrik, aliyah, hebron, tzfat, istanbul

Title: R' Shimon Shmerling departs as first Chabad shadar from Hebron
Summary: R' Shimon Shmerling of Shklov leaves Hebron in summer 5581 as the first Chabad emissary from the city.
Story: In summer 5581 R' Shimon Shmerling, originally of Shklov, departed Hebron as the first Chabad shadar sent from the Hebron community to the diaspora. He returned to Hebron after Pesach 5583. On his journey he registered communities such as Dubna for annual donations.
Tags: shimon shmerling, hebron, shklov, shadar, chabad, kollel

Title: R' Shimon Shmerling's shlichus to Lubavitch for Hebron settlement
Summary: In summer 5581 R' Shimon Shmerling traveled as Hebron's first shaliach to Lubavitch to establish the Chabad settlement in Hebron.
Story: R' Shimon Shmerling, founder of the Chabad community in Hebron and its first emissary, traveled from Hebron to Lubavitch in summer 5581 specifically to coordinate the establishment of the Chabad settlement in Hebron. He is recorded in the Montefiore census as having immigrated in 5581, suggesting he and his family came to Eretz Yisrael around this time.
Tags: shimon shmerling, hebron, shaliach, lubavitch, mitteler rebbe

Title: Volume 3 of Tzemach Tzedek responsa bound
Summary: Volume 3 of the Tzemach Tzedek's bound responsa was completed around 5581.
Story: Volume 3, containing responsa such as Even HaEzer 2 §145 (explicitly written in 5581), was bound around that year. Like most of the early numbered volumes, the original is lost; we know its contents only through summaries the Tzemach Tzedek later copied into other manuscripts when preparing a mehadura batra reorganized by the sections of the Shulchan Aruch.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, responsa, manuscripts

Title: First Hebron Chabad shadar journey rejected by Tzfat kollel
Summary: In summer 1821, the head of the Tzfat Chassidic kollel obstructed a Hebron shadar mission to the diaspora.
Story: In summer 1821 (קיץ תקפ"א), the head of the Tzfat Chassidic kollel, R' Gershon Margolies, opposed a shadar sent on behalf of the new Hebron Chabad community to the diaspora. He intercepted some of the propaganda letters intended to support the new Chabad settlement in Hebron.
Tags: hebron, tzfat, shadar, gershon margolies, chabad kollel

Title: Bill of sale of four amot in Hebron for Chabad settlement
Summary: In 5582 R' Shimon Shmerling signed the bill of sale of four amot of land in Hebron, formalizing the new Chabad settlement.
Story: The 5582 bill of sale of four amot in Hebron marked a foundational step in establishing the permanent Chabad community in the city. R' Shimon Shmerling, one of the founders, was a signatory. In the same year, EY support funds from Russia were sent through R' Yitzchak of Radvil, son of R' Yechiel Michel of Zlotchov.
Tags: hebron, shimon shmerling, land purchase, chabad settlement

Title: Conflict in Shklov over Karliner takeover of main synagogue
Summary: Major friction erupts in Shklov after chassidim take over a room in the main synagogue; the mitnagdim prepare to file a complaint with the government.
Story: In 1822, Simcha Keysin found 'great confusion' in Shklov when chassidim took control of a room in the city's main synagogue. The mitnagdim prepared a complaint to the high government, but R. Pinchas Schick of Shklov, a senior chassidic leader, intervened and pledged to persuade Rabbi DovBer to ease pressure on the mitnagdim. As surety, R. Pinchas handed Keysin the Rebbe's handwritten document about Maamad fund distribution.
Tags: shklov, synagogue, mitnagdim, pinchas schick, russia

Title: Document of sale of Hebron land to chassid R. Yechiel Michel of Birz
Summary: In 5582 four amot of land in Hebron were sold to the Birz chassid R. Yechiel Michel Zusnitz when the Mitteler Rebbe founded the Chabad settlement in Hebron.
Story: Photographed and printed in the history of Chabad in Eretz Yisrael, the deed reflects the Mitteler Rebbe's broader initiative to establish a Chabad presence in Hebron. R. Yechiel Michel, a shochet from Birz, was among the supporters of the new settlement.
Tags: hebron, mitteler rebbe, birz, yechiel michel zusnitz, 5582, settlement

Title: MaharI"L approbates Kapust edition of the Siddur
Summary: In 5582 MaharI"L gave his approbation to the Kapust printing of the Alter Rebbe's siddur.
Story: The 5582 (1822) Kapust edition of the Alter Rebbe's siddur, produced by the printer R' Yisrael Yaffe, carried MaharI"L's published haskama. The approbation was one of MaharI"L's continuing roles as guardian of his late brother's textual legacy.
Tags: mahari"l, kapust, siddur, approbation

Title: Mitteler Rebbe's Sha'arei Orah published in Kapust
Summary: The first edition of the Mitteler Rebbe's Sha'arei Orah was published in Kapust in 5582 (1822).
Story: Sha'arei Orah completed an extraordinary three-year run of major chassidic works issued by the Mitteler Rebbe at the Kapust press between 1820 and 1822.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, kapust, sha'arei orah, first edition

Title: Second wave of Jewish expulsions from Russian villages begins
Summary: Imperial policy launched a renewed campaign to expel Jews from rural villages across the Mogilev and Vitebsk provinces.
Story: In 5582 (1822) the second wave of expulsions of Jews from villages began, displacing families across the Mogilev and Vitebsk provinces and leaving them without homes or means of livelihood. The crisis prompted the Lubavitch fair assembly of 1824, in which Chassidic leaders coordinated a province-wide relief fund and Petersburg lobbying effort under the guidance of the Mitteler Rebbe.
Tags: russia, expulsion, village-jews, mogilev, vitebsk

Title: Shaarei Orah printed in Kopust
Summary: The Mitteler Rebbe's Shaarei Orah appeared in Kopust in 5582.
Story: Shaarei Orah, a discourse on Chanukah and Purim themes, was published by the Mitteler Rebbe in Kopust in 1822.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, kopust

Title: Mogilev Chassidim sign agreement for new synagogue and mikveh
Summary: The Chassidic community of Mogilev empowered five trustees to build a synagogue on newly purchased land and operate the attached bathhouse and mikveh.
Story: On 17 July 1822 (11 Menachem Av 5582), members of the community identified as 'Chassidim of the Lubavitcher Rebbe' in Mogilev signed a binding agreement appointing Wolf Rashel, Shlomo Dankin, and Aizik Cohen, together with community elders Yosef Cohen and Yeshaya Mirkin, as trustees to oversee construction of a new synagogue on land purchased from Rasse Oleshevskaya. The trustees received full discretion over revenues, seat sales, and accounting, with no obligation to render reports. Any shortfall during construction would be advanced personally or borrowed, then repaid from future income of the adjoining bathhouse and mikveh, the synagogue's ground-floor rentals, and seat sales.
Tags: mogilev, synagogue, mikveh, bathhouse, construction, trustees, chabad-community

Title: Mogilev community signs synagogue and mikvah trustee agreement
Summary: Chassidim of Mogilev formalized an agreement appointing gabbaim for their synagogue and mikvah, ratified the same day in the local magistrate court.
Story: On 11 Menachem-Av 5582, Chabad chassidim in Mogilev signed a formal trustee agreement governing their synagogue and mikvah. The agreement was deposited the same day at the Mogilev district peace court, giving it legal standing. The arrangement reflects the institutional organization of Chabad communal life that opponents like Kissin viewed as encroachment.
Tags: mogilev, synagogue, mikvah, gabbaim

Title: Mogilev court ratifies Lubavitch synagogue-building regulation
Summary: A regulation of the Chabad community of Rabbi DovBer (Berke Schneur) of Lubavitch authorizing trusted men to oversee synagogue construction without accountability was signed in the Mogilev peace court.
Story: On July 17, 1822, the chassidic community of Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch formalized a takanah empowering specially trusted individuals to manage the construction of a synagogue, exempting them from any obligation to render accounts of income or expenses, both during construction and afterward. The document was written in Russian on three-ruble stamped paper and notarized as an official document before witnesses at the Mogilev peace court. This regulation later surfaced as evidence in the 1825-1827 investigation against the Mitteler Rebbe.
Tags: lubavitch, synagogue, mogilev, mitteler rebbe, chabad community

Title: Mohilev court confirms Lubavitch community's power of attorney
Summary: The Mohilev peace court formally registers and confirms a power of attorney from the Chabad community of Lubavitch on behalf of Jewish residents of Mohilev.
Story: The power of attorney from the Chasidic community of the Rebbe of Lubavitch, representing the brotherhood of Jewish residents of Mohilev, was presented and entered into the register of the Mohilev peace court as number 51. Signed by Mohilev residents including Litman Avramovich Makrievich, Leib Pevzner, Chaim Shimenovich Bichavski, and Shilem Movshovich Shainin, it was certified by the court with the government seal and witnessed by the mayor and councilmen.
Tags: lubavitch, mohilev, chabad community, power of attorney, russia

Title: Mitteler Rebbe sends R' Shmerling to establish Hebron settlement
Summary: In Tishrei 5583 the Mitteler Rebbe dispatched R' Shimon Shmerling to establish the Chabad settlement in Hebron, instructing him to marry off his son en route.
Story: According to tradition recorded in family histories, in Tishrei 5583 the Mitteler Rebbe sent R' Shimon Shmerling to found the Chabad settlement in Hebron. His son R' Moshe was engaged to Chana Devorah, and the Rebbe instructed him to travel via her town, not dismount the wagon, ask whether she would join them to Eretz Yisrael, arrange the wedding immediately, and bring her along - which he did.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, shimon shmerling, hebron, chabad settlement, moshe shmerling

Title: Aliyah of R' Yisrael Yaffe the Kapust printer
Summary: R' Yisrael ben Yitzchak Yaffe, the senior Kapust printer, made aliyah and settled in Hebron.
Story: In 5583 (1823), R' Yisrael ben Yitzchak Yaffe of Kapust — a signatory of the 5556 Liozna takanot and one of the founders of the Hebron Yishuv — made aliyah to Eretz Yisrael. He soon served as a shadar before 5587 and held a yechidut with the Alter Rebbe documented in Igrot Kodesh. He passed away before Shvat 5589 (early 1829).
Tags: yisrael yaffe, kapust, hebron, aliyah, printer

Title: Chabad community founded in Hebron
Summary: Chasidim who had earlier immigrated to Safed and Tiberias established a Chabad community in Hebron.
Story: In 1823, Chasidim who had first settled in Safed and Tiberias moved to Hebron, founding the Chabad community there. Rabbi Dovber, the second Rebbe, purchased a property for a synagogue, and his daughter Rebbetzin Menucha Rochel later immigrated to join the community.
Tags: hebron, chabad, eretz yisrael, safed, tiberias

Title: Hebron Chabad synagogue established
Summary: Rabbi Dov Ber, the second Chabad Rebbe, encouraged his Chasidim to relocate to Hebron, where they established a synagogue still standing today.
Story: In response to disagreements within the chasidic community in Eretz Yisrael, the Mitteler Rebbe directed his followers to settle in Hebron. The synagogue they founded there in 1823 anchored the growing Chabad community in the patriarchal city.
Tags: hebron, synagogue, mitteler-rebbe, dov-ber

Title: Joint psak by Tzemach Tzedek and MaharI"L in Lubavitch
Summary: In Elul 5583 the Tzemach Tzedek and MaharI"L of Yanovich co-signed a halachic ruling in Lubavitch.
Story: A teshuva and psak written and co-signed in Lubavitch in Elul 5583 (August-September 1823) by MaharI"L and the Tzemach Tzedek, printed in Shearit Yehuda Even Haezer §5, documents their collaborative halachic work during the Mitteler Rebbe's tenure.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, mahari"l, lubavitch, halacha

Title: Mitteler Rebbe forwards Chernobyl agunah case to Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: In summer 5583 the Mitteler Rebbe transferred a difficult agunah case from the Chernobyl beis din to his son-in-law and Maharil.
Story: The Mitteler Rebbe, his father-in-law, directed the young Tzemach Tzedek along with his great-uncle Maharil to examine an agunah case (Even HaEzer §§347–348) referred to him by the Chernobyl beis din. In the resulting responsum the two write that 'it was our master's command... and although we know our small worth, that we have not reached the stature to take up the name and respond from afar, nevertheless one does not refuse a greater.'
Tags: mitteler rebbe, tzemach tzedek, maharil of yanovitch, agunah, chernobyl, ukraine

Title: Mitteler Rebbe requests stipend for R. Shmuel Segal's aliyah
Summary: The Mitteler Rebbe wrote to chassidim of Rogatchov and neighboring towns requesting an annual stipend of thirty gold coins for R. Shmuel Segal's aliyah.
Story: Around 1823, as R. Shmuel Segal prepared to leave Rogatchov for Hebron, the Mitteler Rebbe addressed a letter to the chassidim of Rogatchov, Bobruisk, Paritch, Zhlobin and their surrounding settlements. He requested they collectively pledge an annual stipend of thirty gold coins — ten from Rogatchov, five from Zhlobin, three from Stareshin, and ten from Bobruisk-Paritch — to enable Segal to devote himself to Torah and divine service in the Land of Israel.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, rogatchov, bobruisk, paritch, zhlobin, shmuel segal, stipend

Title: R. Shaul ben Yaakov Mordechai Twer born
Summary: R. Shaul, son of R. Yaakov Mordechai Twer, was born around 1823 (5583), per the 1839 Montefiore census record.
Story: Listed in the Montefiore census as age sixteen, married, and a student, R. Shaul made aliyah with his father in 1832. His descendants would adopt the surname Saulson and form one of the well-known Chabad-Hebron families.
Tags: shaul twer, saulson, hebron, chabad family

Title: R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz asks halakhic question of MaHaRIL
Summary: R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz of Rogatchov submitted a halakhic query to the MaHaRIL mentioning Segal's two-week absence in Mohilev seeking a passport for aliyah.
Story: In the summer of 1823, R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz of Rogatchov — who would later serve as moreh tzedek in Lubavitch — sent a halakhic question to the MaHaRIL. The question mentioned that R. Shmuel Segal had already been away two weeks in Mohilev attempting to obtain a passport for travel to the Land of Israel and had been preparing for nearly a year for the journey.
Tags: rogatchov, mohilev, yissachar ber horowitz, passport, aliyah

Title: R' Moshe Meisels moves from Tzfat to Hebron
Summary: R' Moshe Meisels relocated from Tzfat to Hebron in winter 1823, joining the new Chabad community there.
Story: In the winter of 1823 (חורף תקפ"ג), R' Moshe Meisels moved from Tzfat to Hebron, becoming one of the leading administrators of the new Chabad settlement there. He signed many of the community's communal documents over the following two decades.
Tags: moshe meisels, tzfat, hebron, chabad kollel

Title: Dubna community settles annual Hebron pledge with emissary
Summary: On 12 Av 5583 the council of Dubna records settling its annual 200-zehuvim pledge to Hebron with a visiting emissary.
Story: The Dubna kahal pinkas records that on Sunday 12 Av 5583 an emissary arrived from Hebron carrying a register of communal pledges, showing Dubna obligated to send 200 zehuvim annually. The community settled all accumulated dues, exempting future leaders from the obligation, and the emissary signed the pinkas. It is unclear whether the messenger was R' Shimon Shmerling, R' Leib of Belz, or another shadar 'connected to Hebron.'
Tags: dubna, hebron, shadar, fundraising, poland, volhynia, kahal

Title: Communal fundraising campaign for Petersburg shtadlanim
Summary: Chasidic leaders meeting in Lubavitch in 1824 apportioned 1,720 rubles between Mohilev and Vitebsk provinces to fund delegates intervening for Jewish causes in Petersburg.
Story: Representatives of Mohilev and Vitebsk Jews gathered in the town of Lubavitch to coordinate a special levy for delegates traveling to Petersburg on behalf of the community. They assigned 1,030 rubles to Mohilev province (60%) and 690 rubles to Vitebsk (40%). Khovansky later used this episode as evidence that 'voluntary' donations under the Mitteler Rebbe's leadership were in fact compulsory levies imposed by a few leaders.
Tags: russia, fundraising, shtadlanut, lubavitch, mohilev, vitebsk, petersburg

Title: Fire at Beshen destroys over forty manuscripts of the Alter Rebbe
Summary: A fire in 5584 (1824) at the home of R' Beshen destroyed over forty volumes of the Alter Rebbe's own handwriting that were held there.
Story: According to the Rebbe Rayatz citing his grandfather the Rebbe Maharash, the Alter Rebbe would entrust his manuscripts to the chassid R' Yisrael Yaffe of Kapust, who circulated them among chassidim for study and copying. A vast cache held at R' Beshen's home was lost in the 1824 fire. Only two volumes from 5566-5567 that were on loan to the Mittler Rebbe survived intact.
Tags: beshen, fire, manuscripts, alter-rebbe, mittler-rebbe

Title: Mogilev and Vitebsk Jews fund delegation to Petersburg
Summary: Jews of Mogilev and Vitebsk gubernias enacted a takanah in the Lubavitch region to collect funds for emissaries traveling to Petersburg on communal advocacy matters.
Story: In 1824, a regulation was formulated in the Lubavitch area by Jewish leaders of Mogilev and Vitebsk to fund a delegation traveling to Petersburg for shtadlanut on public affairs. Mogilev was assessed 1,030 rubles and Vitebsk 690 rubles for the emissaries' expenses. The takanah also affirmed that the chachamim, elders, heads of thousands and heads of hundreds named in the document were of equal authority, and the document later became evidence in the case against Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch.
Tags: mogilev, vitebsk, lubavitch, petersburg, shtadlanut, delegation

Title: R' Shmuel Segal arrives in Holy Land from Rohatchov
Summary: R' Shmuel Halevi Segal, later first rabbi of the Chabad community in Hebron, immigrated to the Land of Israel from Rohatchov.
Story: Per the 1839 census, R' Shmuel Halevi, then 64 years old, made aliyah from Rohatchov in 5584 (1824). Prior to his immigration he had served as a moreh tzedek (mo"tz) in Rohatchov and was a signatory on a charity assessment there in winter 5570 with the Alter Rebbe. After his arrival he became the leading rabbinic figure of the Chabad community in Hebron.
Tags: chabad, hebron, rohatchov, aliyah, rabbi

Title: R. Shmuel Segal makes aliyah from Rogatchov to Hebron
Summary: R. Shmuel Segal, the longtime moreh tzedek of Rogatchov, immigrated to Hebron and became a leader of the Chabad community there.
Story: In 1823-1824, R. Shmuel Segal left his fifteen-year post as moreh tzedek of Rogatchov and ascended to the Land of Israel. He settled in Hebron and became rabbi, maggid mesharim, and first appointed leader of the Chabad community established there by the Mitteler Rebbe. The Mitteler Rebbe wrote to chassidim of Rogatchov and surrounding towns requesting an annual stipend of thirty gold coins to support him.
Tags: rogatchov, hebron, chabad, shmuel segal, aliyah, mitteler rebbe

Title: R. Shmuel Segal of Rohatchov travels to the Land of Israel
Summary: The moreh tzedek of Rohatchov, R. Shmuel Segal, made aliyah in 5584 after obtaining a passport in Mohilev.
Story: R. Shmuel Segal, moreh tzedek of Rohatchov, prepared for nearly a year before traveling to Eretz Yisrael in 5584 (1824). He spent several weeks in Mohilev obtaining a passport, leaving R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz and other local rabbis to handle pressing halachic questions in his absence. His departure precipitated R. Yissachar Ber's increased involvement in Rohatchov's rabbinical affairs.
Tags: shmuel segal, rohatchov, aliyah, eretz yisrael

Title: Lubavitch fair assembly raises funds for Jews expelled from villages
Summary: Representatives from Mogilev and Vitebsk provinces gathered at the Lubavitch fair to organize aid and lobbying for Jews expelled from villages.
Story: On Wednesday evening, 20 Adar I 5584 (20 February 1824), Jewish leaders from towns across the Mogilev and Vitebsk provinces convened at the annual Lubavitch fair to address the plight of fellow Jews recently expelled from village settlements and left without means of livelihood. They resolved to send delegates to St. Petersburg to lobby imperial officials, allocating 60% of the funding burden to Mogilev province and 40% to Vitebsk. Trustees were elected — Alexander Ziskind of Dubrovna and Moshe Yehuda Leibowitz Poponia of Shklov for Mogilev (acting in consultation with Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch), and Binyamin Beinish Nachumowitz of Vitebsk and Binyamin Beinish Zussamowitz of Polotsk for Vitebsk.
Tags: russia, mogilev, vitebsk, lubavitch, expulsion, fundraising, village-jews, petersburg-lobbying

Title: Vitebsk leaders ratify trustee list for expelled-Jews relief fund
Summary: Vitebsk province delegates reaffirmed the 690-ruble apportionment and replaced a trustee who declined the role with Chaim Simcha Ginzburg.
Story: Three days after the main Lubavitch assembly, on Motzaei Shabbat into Sunday, 23 February 1824 (Adar I 5584), Vitebsk-area delegates signed a follow-up agreement in Vitebsk. They reaffirmed the 690-ruble share owed by their province, broke down the contribution by district, and replaced Binyamin Beinish Nachumowitz — who declined the trusteeship — with the prominent Chaim Simcha Ginzburg. The agreement was copied by Mendel the scribe and signed by representatives from Vitebsk and Polotsk.
Tags: russia, vitebsk, polotsk, expulsion, fundraising, village-jews

Title: Wedding of Maharil of Kapust, son of the Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: On 14 Cheshvan 5585, the Tzemach Tzedek's son Rabbi Yehuda Leib (later the Maharil of Kapust) married the daughter of Rabbi Shlomo Freides of Shklov, who gave 40 volumes of his transcripts of the Alter Rebbe's teachings as dowry.
Story: The Mitteler Rebbe recorded delivering a discourse 'at the wedding of my grandson Yehuda Leib, 14 Cheshvan 5585.' Rabbi Shlomo Freides, a major chronicler of the Alter Rebbe's teachings, presented forty volumes of his transcripts as the dowry. The Tzemach Tzedek subsequently annotated and expanded these manuscripts, though most were later lost in the great Lubavitch fire.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, maharil, kapust, mitteler rebbe, wedding

Title: First agreement between Hebron Sephardic and Chabad communities
Summary: The Sephardic and Chabad communities of Hebron reached a first agreement dividing Hebron's share of the Pekuam funds.
Story: In 5585 (1825), the Sephardic and Chabad communities of Hebron concluded their first agreement, dividing Hebron's portion of the Pekuam Amsterdam funds between the two communities. The Pekuam committee did not accept their compromise, however, and additional negotiations were required regarding shdarus to other lands. These discussions ultimately produced the broader 5590 agreement.
Tags: hebron, sephardic kollel, chabad kollel, pekuam, agreement

Title: First Chabad–Sephardic agreement in Hebron
Summary: In 5585 the Chabad and Sephardic communities of Hebron sign their first agreement, setting Chabad's contribution at 1,000 grush per year.
Story: The first agreement obligated the Chabad community in Hebron to pay 1,000 grush annually to the Sephardic kollel to share city expenses, including protection payments to the tyrant Sheikh Abdul Rahman who held Hebron under his patronage. Two subsequent agreements would lower this amount as Chabad argued that its own direct payments to the sheikh deserved credit.
Tags: hebron, chabad, sephardim, kollel, abdul rahman, protection payments

Title: Investigator Korbitsky files court report on Mittler Rebbe's court and library
Summary: In 5586 (1825) the tsarist investigator Korbitsky submitted a report to the court describing the synagogue, books, and ritual objects in the Mittler Rebbe's courtyard in Lubavitch.
Story: Korbitsky's report catalogued the synagogue's dimensions, Torah scrolls, menorahs from Petersburg, candlesticks, curtains, and a library of 611 books in four cabinets available for loan to townspeople. The report is a primary source for understanding the Mittler Rebbe's court at Lubavitch in this period. It was later cited in the published account of the Mittler Rebbe's arrest and release.
Tags: mittler-rebbe, russia, tsarist, investigation, library, lubavitch

Title: Liberation of the Mitteler Rebbe on Yud Kislev
Summary: On 10 Kislev 5586 Rabbi DovBer Schneuri was released from detention and returned home to Lubavitch.
Story: The first stage of the Mitteler Rebbe's liberation came when Khovansky freed him to return home after the initial interrogations concluded. This date became Yud Kislev, the Chassidic festival of redemption commemorating his release. The legal case, however, was far from over: Khovansky immediately referred the file to the Mogilev provincial authorities for full trial proceedings.
Tags: yud kislev, lubavitch, khovansky, liberation

Title: Maharil of Yanovitch passes away
Summary: Rabbi Yehuda Leib (Maharil) of Yanovitch, the Alter Rebbe's brother, passed away in early 5586.
Story: Maharil of Yanovitch had served as the primary halachic respondent for the Chabad community after the Alter Rebbe's passing in 5573. With his death at the start of 5586, the responsibility shifted increasingly to his great-nephew the Tzemach Tzedek, who had already been building a responsa practice for roughly eight years.
Tags: maharil of yanovitch, alter rebbe, yahrzeit, halachic transition

Title: Pekidim VeAmarkalim begin uniform EY fund distribution
Summary: From 5585 onward the Pekidim VeAmarkalim of Amsterdam distributed all incoming EY funds among the four kollels in the holy cities.
Story: Starting in 5585 the Chevrat Terumat HaKodesh in Amsterdam (Pekidim VeAmarkalim) systematically distributed all donations among the four kollels - Sephardim, Perushim, Chassidim, and Chabad. Funds were sent four times yearly, usually via Beirut. This system continued until disputes arose with the later-established HoD kollel.
Tags: pekoam, amsterdam, eretz yisrael fund, kollelim, distribution

Title: Rabbi DovBer travels abroad to Karlsbad for medical treatment
Summary: Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch (the Mittler Rebbe) travels to the healing springs of Karlsbad for medical treatment.
Story: In the summer of 1825 (Tammuz-Av 5585), Rabbi DovBer Schneuri traveled outside Russia to Karlsbad to seek treatment at its therapeutic springs. While he was away, Simcha Keysin's denunciations were being delivered to Governor Khovansky in Vitebsk, setting in motion the chain of events that would culminate in the Rebbe's arrest and trial later that year.
Tags: mittler rebbe, karlsbad, travel, health

Title: Shlomo of Layev sends 1000 rubles to the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: On 18 Shvat 5585, Shlomo of Layev forwarded a 1000-ruble contribution to Rabbi DovBer Schneuri.
Story: The transfer documented a large single donation to the Rebbe's treasury earlier in 1825, months before Shimcha Kissin filed his denunciations. Such gifts later figured in Khovansky's calculations of the Rebbe's annual income, which the governor claimed reached 10,000-14,000 rubles per year.
Tags: fundraising, maamad, donations

Title: Tzemach Tzedek responsa to R. Avraham Sheines of Shklov
Summary: Responsa Even HaEzer §§297–298, written in 5585, were sent to R. Avraham Sheines of Shklov to settle a dispute among major rabbis.
Story: According to Beis Rebbi (p. 120), R. Avraham son of R. Tzvi Sheines of Shklov brought before the Tzemach Tzedek a dispute among R. Aharon Halevi of Strashelye, R. Gershon of Shklov, R. Nechemiah of Dubrovna, the author of Beis Ephraim, and others. The Tzemach Tzedek's responses are recorded in Even HaEzer §§297–298, dated 5585.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, shklov, aharon halevi of strashelye, gershon of shklov, beit ephraim, halachic dispute

Title: Volume 7 of Tzemach Tzedek responsa bound
Summary: Volume 7 of the Tzemach Tzedek's responsa, manuscript 233, contains responsa written between 5582 and 5585.
Story: Manuscript 233 is one of only three early bound volumes of the Tzemach Tzedek's responsa that survives. It collects question-and-answer exchanges from 5582 to 5585. Together with manuscripts 1019 and 1050 it provides our chief evidence for the structure of the lost volumes 1–14.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, responsa, manuscript 233

Title: Michael ben Shlomo of Nikolayev sends 1000 rubles to the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: A chassid from Nikolayev encloses 1000 rubles for the Mitteler Rebbe and promises more before Passover.
Story: On 18 Shevat 5585, Michael ben Shlomo of Nikolayev wrote to the Mitteler Rebbe (Admur HaEmtzaei) enclosing 1000 rubles in support, with a promise to send the additional sum by mail before Passover. The letter is one of many surviving documents showing the network of financial support flowing from chassidim across the Russian Empire to the Rebbe's court.
Tags: nikolayev, russia, mitteler rebbe, financial support, maamad

Title: First denunciation against Chabad by Shimcha Kissin
Summary: Shimcha Kissin submitted a general denunciation portraying Chassidim as a destructive sect exploiting youth and seizing community institutions.
Story: Kissin's first letter to Governor Khovansky targeted the Chassidic movement broadly without yet naming the Mitteler Rebbe personally for embezzlement. He alleged the sect ("Karliner") manipulated young men, controlled charity coffers, monopolized shechita, and ran printing presses producing books of miracle tales. The letter demanded the authorities suppress Chassidism, setting in motion the events that led to the Rebbe's arrest.
Tags: shimcha kissin, informers, khovansky, russia, vitebsk

Title: Second denunciation by Shimcha Kissin
Summary: Kissin submitted a second letter, this one personally accusing Rabbi DovBer of misappropriating community funds.
Story: Following his general broadside, Kissin escalated by leveling direct financial charges against the Mitteler Rebbe himself. The accusation centered on funds allegedly collected from communities and distributed among the Rebbe's relatives as personal gifts. This shifted the case from a religious-policy complaint to a criminal allegation of embezzlement under the 1804 Jewish Statute.
Tags: shimcha kissin, informers, khovansky

Title: Second informer letter submitted against the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: Simcha Kisin submitted a second informer letter against the Mitteler Rebbe and the chassidic movement in June 1825.
Story: In late Sivan to Tammuz 5585 (June 1825), Simcha Kisin filed his second informer letter portraying the chassidic movement as greedy exploiters of naive young Jews who seized control of communal funds, charity boxes, shechita, and printing houses. He attached a 1814 distribution letter regarding the ma'amad bais harav as supposed evidence that the Mitteler Rebbe was amassing vast personal wealth. The denunciation demanded the persecution and destruction of the chassidic movement.
Tags: simcha kisin, malshinus, informer, russia, mitteler rebbe

Title: Simcha Keysin's letter to authorities denouncing the Chabad chassidim of Shklov
Summary: Simcha Keysin writes to Russian authorities accusing the 'Karliner sect' (chassidim) of seizing synagogues, printing Asiatic-rite prayer books, and oppressing 'true Jews.'
Story: In June 1825, Simcha Keysin submitted a denunciation to a high Russian official, complaining that the chassidic movement led by the late Rabbi Shneur Zalman and now his son Rabbi DovBer was expanding its influence, seizing parts of the main Shklov synagogue, controlling printing presses for chassidic-rite siddurim, and forcing 'true Jews' to use their kosher meat. He framed the chassidim as an illegitimate sect harming the Jewish community.
Tags: mitnagdim, russia, shklov, simcha keysin, karlin, synagogue, denunciation

Title: First Chabad-Sephardic agreement in Hebron
Summary: The first agreement between the Chabad and Sephardic communities in Hebron was concluded in Tammuz 1825.
Story: In Tammuz 1825 (תמוז תקפ"ה), the Chabad and Sephardic communities of Hebron reached their first formal agreement governing shadar territories and fundraising. The text of this initial agreement has not survived, but it predated the more detailed 1830 agreement.
Tags: hebron, sephardim, chabad kollel, fundraising, agreement

Title: Shimcha Kissin files an informer's complaint against the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: Vitebsk resident Shimcha Kissin denounces the Mitteler Rebbe to Governor-General Khovansky, triggering an investigation.
Story: In July 1825, the Jew Shimcha Kissin of Vitebsk submitted a petition to Governor-General Khovansky accusing the chassidic sect ("Karliners") and its leader Rabbi Berke Schneur (the Mitteler Rebbe) of pressuring traditional Jews and collecting large sums via emissaries for the Rebbe's personal benefit. He attached a Yiddish distribution document and two letters as evidence. The complaint launched the entire investigation that culminated in the Mitteler Rebbe's arrest.
Tags: kissin, vitebsk, khovansky, informer, mitteler rebbe, chassidim, karliner

Title: Simcha Kisin denounces Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch to authorities
Summary: A Jew named Simcha Kisin submitted a denunciation to Governor-General Khovansky accusing Rabbi DovBer (Berke Schneur) of Lubavitch of illegally collecting funds from his followers.
Story: In July 1825, Simcha Kisin delivered a formal denunciation to Prince Nikolai Khovansky, Governor-General of Vitebsk, Mogilev, Smolensk and Kaluga, alleging that Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch — the Mitteler Rebbe — was illegally raising money from his chassidim. This informer's report cited documents including a fund-distribution sheet and correspondence between the Rebbe and his associates. The denunciation triggered the formal criminal investigation that would lead to the Rebbe's arrest and eventual acquittal nearly two years later.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, kisin, informer, khovansky, vitebsk, lubavitch

Title: Simcha Kisin files denunciation against the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: Vitebsk resident Simcha Kisin submitted a denunciation to Governor-General Khovansky accusing the Chasidic 'sect' and Rabbi Berke Shneur of pressuring traditional Jews and illegally collecting funds.
Story: In July 1825, the Jew Simcha Kisin of Vitebsk lodged a complaint with Governor-General Khovansky alleging that the Chasidim—whom he called 'Karliners'—were oppressing 'authentic Jews of the old faith,' and that their rebbe, Berke Shneur, was amassing wealth through dedicated emissaries. As evidence, Kisin produced an original Hebrew document of fund distribution along with a Russian translation and two letters from the Rebbe—the materials that launched the long investigation.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, dovber schneuri, denunciation, simcha kisin, vitebsk, khovansky, informer

Title: Simcha Kissin submits denunciations against Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: In Tammuz-Av 5585 the informer Simcha Kissin handed three denunciation letters about the Mitteler Rebbe to Governor Khovansky in Vitebsk.
Story: Kissin's denunciation portrayed the Chassidic movement as exploiting youthful followers for money and seizing control of communal funds, slaughter, and printing. He attached a copy of the Mitteler Rebbe's 1814 Ma'amad distribution letter, attempting to prove that the Rebbe had amassed roughly 140,000 rubles. The Mitteler Rebbe was traveling abroad at the Carlsbad spa at the time and would be summoned upon his return.
Tags: simcha kissin, mitteler rebbe, denunciation, vitebsk, khovansky

Title: Third denunciation by Shimcha Kissin
Summary: Kissin filed a third denunciation against the Mitteler Rebbe, completing his trio of accusations to Governor Khovansky.
Story: The third installment of Kissin's denunciations reached Khovansky in July 1825. Together with the two earlier letters, it supplied Governor Khovansky of Vitebsk with the pretext to summon the Rebbe for interrogation in early autumn. Kissin's central exhibit remained the 1813 letter on Maamad distribution that he had obtained through Pinchas Schick of Shklov.
Tags: shimcha kissin, informers, khovansky

Title: Third denunciation letter by Simcha Keysin against Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch
Summary: Simcha Keysin submits his third denunciation letter to Governor Khovansky against Rabbi DovBer (the Mittler Rebbe) over collection of Maamad funds.
Story: In July 1825, the mitnaged Simcha Keysin of Shklov submitted a third denunciation to the governor of Vitebsk, alleging that the Maamad funds collected from chassidim by Rabbi DovBer Schneuri were being used for personal pleasures rather than communal needs. The letter attached a document from 1813 detailing distribution of these funds, supposedly written by the Rebbe himself. This denunciation, along with earlier ones, triggered the criminal investigation of the Mittler Rebbe.
Tags: mitnagdim, russia, vitebsk, simcha keysin, mittler rebbe, denunciation, shklov

Title: Governor Khovansky orders Rabbi DovBer brought to Vitebsk for interrogation
Summary: Governor Khovansky in Vitebsk orders police officials to bring Rabbi DovBer from Lubavitch for criminal investigation.
Story: In September 1825 (Tishrei 5586), Governor Khovansky of Vitebsk ordered the regional police to detain Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch and bring him to Vitebsk to face investigation arising from Simcha Keysin's denunciations. The escort traveled from Vitebsk to Lubavitch and detoured through Shklov so it could pick up two chassidic witnesses to bring along for questioning.
Tags: khovansky, mittler rebbe, vitebsk, russia, arrest, lubavitch

Title: Khovansky orders police to bring the Mitteler Rebbe for interrogation
Summary: Governor Khovansky dispatched police official Korbicki to Lubavitch to summon Rabbi DovBer to Vitebsk for interrogation.
Story: Order No. 4767 instructed Korbicki, together with Chevkin and another officer, to travel via Lubavitch, Babinovichi, and Shklov to bring the Rebbe to Vitebsk. Khovansky framed the summons as a private meeting on "several matters" rather than an arrest warrant. According to Beis Rebbi, the Rebbe was actually taken from his home in Lubavitch immediately after Sukkot 5586.
Tags: khovansky, korbicki, vitebsk, lubavitch, arrest

Title: Mitteler Rebbe taken to Vitebsk for interrogation
Summary: On Isru Chag Sukkot 5586 (October 1825) the Mitteler Rebbe was taken to Vitebsk, seat of Governor Khovansky, to face the investigators.
Story: Governor Nikolai Khovansky ruled the provinces of Vitebsk, Mohilev, Smolensk and Kaluga. He ordered the police to bring the Rebbe immediately after the holiday. The case opened with the Rebbe verifying that the attached documents were in his hand, and his confidants Reb Zalman Roizes and Reb Shlomo Freides were summoned for parallel questioning.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, vitebsk, khovansky, arrest, russia

Title: Morozov dismissed from the investigation against the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: Two weeks after appointing three investigators, Khovansky dismisses Major Morozov, leaving Loginov and Markov alone to investigate the rebbe.
Story: About two weeks after assigning Loginov, Markov, and Morozov on 2 October 1825 to investigate the denunciation against the Mitteler Rebbe, Khovansky relieved Morozov of the assignment (document 18). The investigation thereafter continued under Colonel Loginov and Court Counselor Markov alone, who carried it forward to its conclusion.
Tags: russia, khovansky, morozov, loginov, markov, investigation

Title: Investigation against the Mitteler Rebbe formally opened
Summary: The case file against the Mitteler Rebbe was formally received for investigation on October 2, 1825.
Story: After Kisin's denunciation, Khovansky assigned two of his officials to conduct a formal inquiry. The case was officially received on October 2, 1825, with the investigation findings presented to Khovansky on November 10 and forwarded to the Mohilev provincial administration on November 17—beginning the multi-year legal proceedings.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, dovber schneuri, investigation, khovansky, vitebsk

Title: Khovansky assigns investigators to Kisin's denunciation against the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: Governor-General Khovansky formally assigns Colonel Loginov, Court Counselor Markov, and Major Morozov to investigate Kisin's denunciation accusing Rabbi Dovber Schneuri of illegally collecting funds from chasidim.
Story: On 2 October 1825 (document no. 4831), Khovansky formally tasked three officials with investigating the denunciation lodged in June 1825 by a Vitebsk Jew named Kisin against 'Berke Schneur,' the rebbe of the Chasidic sect, accusing him of extorting large sums from Jews loyal to the 'old faith.' Kisin had produced an 1813 Hebrew distribution document showing 35,000 rubles allegedly divided among the rebbe's relatives, and claimed the rebbe was violating the 9 December 1804 Jewish Statute (§52) forbidding rabbis from accumulating wealth. Khovansky ordered the investigators to verify the document's authenticity, examine the sources of the funds, and summon the rebbe for formal questioning.
Tags: russia, vitebsk, denunciation, kisin, khovansky, loginov, markov, morozov, chasidim

Title: Khovansky assigns investigators to lead the inquiry against Rabbi DovBer
Summary: Governor Khovansky formally transfers the investigation of Rabbi DovBer to designated state investigators.
Story: On 2 October 1825 (2 Marcheshvan 5586), Governor Khovansky handed responsibility for the inquiry to his special officials, Colonel Loginov and Court Counselor Markov, to gather evidence on the alleged illegal collection of funds by Rabbi DovBer. This marked the formal opening of the state's criminal investigation against the Mittler Rebbe.
Tags: khovansky, investigation, vitebsk, russia

Title: Khovansky orders investigation of Mitteler Rebbe's fundraising
Summary: Governor-General Khovansky directed Colonel Loginov and Court Counselor Markov to investigate Kisin's denunciation against Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch.
Story: On October 2, 1825, Prince Khovansky issued an order to Colonel Loginov and Court Counselor Markov to conduct a formal inquiry into the accusations brought by Simcha Kisin against the Mitteler Rebbe. They were instructed to determine the source of the sums Rabbi Schneur had distributed among his relatives, whether they came from communal taxes, who collected them, under what legal authority, and whether accountings had been rendered. The investigators summoned the Rebbe along with Lubavitch resident Lavut and the Shklov townsmen Zalman Reizin and Shimon Freidin.
Tags: khovansky, loginov, markov, vitebsk, investigation, mitteler rebbe

Title: Interrogation of R. Zalman Slonim about the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: Khovansky's investigators questioned R. Zalman Slonim as part of the case against the Rebbe.
Story: Slonim was among the close chassidim summoned for testimony in Vitebsk. His interrogation preceded the Rebbe's own first interview by two days. Investigators sought corroboration of Kissin's claims about communal fundraising and money distribution among the Rebbe's relatives.
Tags: zalman slonim, interrogation, vitebsk

Title: Rabbi DovBer asked to authenticate documents attached to denunciation
Summary: Rabbi DovBer is asked to confirm whether the documents attached to the denunciation are in his own handwriting; two chassidim are also interrogated.
Story: On 5 October 1825 (5 Marcheshvan 5586), investigators in Vitebsk asked Rabbi DovBer to confirm that the attachments to Simcha Keysin's denunciation were written in his own hand. The same day, two of his chassidim, R. Zalman Roizes of Slonim and R. Shlomo Freides of Shklov, were also brought before the investigators and interrogated as part of the gathering of evidence.
Tags: mittler rebbe, vitebsk, investigation, shklov, witnesses

Title: Reb Zalman Slonim testifies about the Mitteler Rebbe's maamad funds
Summary: Reb Zalman Leizerovich Slonim of Shklov testifies to investigators about how the Mitteler Rebbe collected and distributed maamad funds after Napoleon's invasion.
Story: On 5 October 1825, Reb Zalman Slonim of Shklov, a 53-year-old chasid who had been appointed by the Mitteler Rebbe (together with Pinchas Shick and Shlomo Freidin) to oversee distribution of maamad funds, gave sworn testimony. He recounted how in spring 1813 the rebbe arrived in Shklov with his family, gathered prominent chasidim, and described his impoverishment after the French looting and burning of his Liadi properties. Slonim confirmed that contributions were freely given by chasidim according to ability, that the 35,000-ruble distribution document was indeed in the rebbe's handwriting, and that another rebbe, Aharon of Starosselye, also received voluntary support nearby.
Tags: russia, shklov, testimony, zalman-slonim, pinchas-shick, maamad, chasidim

Title: First interrogation of Rabbi DovBer in Vitebsk
Summary: The first formal interrogation of Rabbi DovBer Schneuri begins before Russian state investigators in Vitebsk.
Story: On 7 October 1825 (7 Marcheshvan 5586), Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch underwent his first official interrogation in Vitebsk in connection with Simcha Keysin's denunciations. The investigators questioned him about the collection and use of Maamad funds, the relations between chassidim and mitnagdim, and the authenticity of the documents Keysin had submitted as evidence.
Tags: mittler rebbe, vitebsk, interrogation, russia

Title: First interrogation of the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: Rabbi DovBer Schneuri underwent his first interrogation in Vitebsk by Colonel Loginov and court counselor Markov.
Story: On 7 Cheshvan 5586 the Rebbe answered the first round of questions from Khovansky's two appointed investigators. They focused on whether he had written and signed the 1813 financial document presented by Kissin, what portion of the funds went to relatives, and on what legal basis the money was collected. Two days later the Rebbe submitted written answers to their queries.
Tags: khovansky, vitebsk, loginov, markov, interrogation

Title: First interrogation of the Mitteler Rebbe by the provincial commission
Summary: The provincial investigative commission formally presented eleven questions to Rabbi DovBer Schneuri about an internal fund-distribution document.
Story: On 7 October 1825 (7 Marcheshvan 5586), the commission established by the provincial governor delivered eleven written questions to the Mitteler Rebbe regarding a document — already confirmed to be in his own handwriting — that distributed 35,000 rubles among his relatives. The interrogators Colonel Loginov, Court Counselor Markov, and Major Morozov pressed him on the source of the funds, why he collected money from Chassidim beyond his official salary, the meaning of the 'shtar iska' (rabbinic workaround for interest-bearing loans), and the secrecy surrounding the document. They demanded answers without delay.
Tags: mitteler-rebbe, arrest, interrogation, russia, informer, fundraising, chalukah-document

Title: Khovansky orders treasury to reimburse travel costs of escort to Lubavitch
Summary: Khovansky directs the Vitebsk treasury to reimburse his adjutant and the police officers who escorted Rabbi DovBer from Lubavitch via Shklov.
Story: On 7 October 1825, Governor Khovansky wrote to the Vitebsk Provincial Treasury ordering it to reimburse Lieutenant Chevkin, district police officer Korvitsky, and another officer for the costs of the round-trip carriage journey from Vitebsk to Lubavitch and on to Shklov to fetch Rabbi DovBer and witnesses. They had used 6 horses on the way out and 9 on the return, since two more chassidim were added in Shklov.
Tags: khovansky, vitebsk, lubavitch, shklov, treasury, russia

Title: Mitteler Rebbe submits written answers to the interrogators
Summary: Rabbi DovBer Schneuri responded point-by-point to all eleven questions, detailing the family's 1812 losses and the structure of Chassidic donations.
Story: On 9 October 1825 (9 Marcheshvan 5586), the Mitteler Rebbe submitted detailed written answers explaining that the 35,000 rubles in question were one-time donations gathered after the family's 60,000-ruble loss when the French burned their property in Liadi during the 1812 invasion. He described fleeing with his father to inner Russia, his father's death in Haditch, and the appeal of Belarus Jews who reached him in Kremenchug asking that he succeed his father as their rabbi. He insisted Chassidim's gifts are voluntary and never fixed taxes, protested that a translator had inflated the sum to 140,000 rubles, and asked to see the original Hebrew document to identify the error. He signed in Hebrew, with Yehuda Yaffe of Kopust signing the Russian version on his behalf.
Tags: mitteler-rebbe, arrest, interrogation, russia, alter-rebbe, 1812-war, haditch, kremenchug, kopust

Title: Mitteler Rebbe's answers on Lubavitch synagogue construction
Summary: The Mitteler Rebbe details to the investigation committee that the Lubavitch synagogue cost 6,000 rubles, with thousands more spent on Torah scrolls, furnishings, and books.
Story: In his written response to the committee's questions, the Rebbe specified that the large synagogue in Lubavitch had cost 6,000 rubles to build. Four Torah scrolls of the five books of Moses written on parchment cost 1,500 rubles, while crystal chandeliers, arks and other interior furnishings came to 500 rubles. Religious books reached roughly 3,000 rubles. The Rebbe stressed that since construction occurred over time, he could not state with certainty how much came from the collected funds versus later income.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, lubavitch synagogue, torah scrolls, religious books, investigation, russia

Title: Mitteler Rebbe's second interrogation on synagogue and book costs
Summary: The investigation committee questions the Mitteler Rebbe in detail about the construction of the Lubavitch synagogue and the purchase of religious books.
Story: The committee of investigators — Colonel Loginov, Court Counselor Markov, and Major Morozov — pressed the Rebbe to specify how much of the collected funds went to building the large Lubavitch synagogue and acquiring sacred books. Distrusting his answers, the governor would soon dispatch a special investigator to Lubavitch to verify the responses on the ground. The Rebbe's written replies were given the same day, with the on-site verification mission departing four days later.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, dovber schneuri, lubavitch synagogue, interrogation, russia, loginov, markov, morozov

Title: Second interrogation of Rabbi DovBer in Vitebsk
Summary: Rabbi DovBer undergoes a second interrogation in Vitebsk on the same denunciation case.
Story: On 15 October 1825 (15 Marcheshvan 5586), Rabbi DovBer was brought again before the state investigators in Vitebsk for a second interrogation. The session continued the inquiry into the collection of Maamad funds and the allegations made by Simcha Keysin, building the formal record that would later be reviewed by higher courts.
Tags: mittler rebbe, vitebsk, interrogation, russia

Title: Second interrogation of the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: The Mitteler Rebbe was questioned a second time and submitted further written answers the same day.
Story: The investigators pressed the Rebbe with follow-up questions on 15 Cheshvan 5586. The same day he provided written responses, a pattern of careful, documented answers maintained throughout the inquiry. The next day Khovansky reassigned the third investigator to other duties, leaving Loginov and Markov to complete the case.
Tags: interrogation, vitebsk, khovansky

Title: Investigator Morozov reassigned from Mitteler Rebbe investigation
Summary: Khovansky removes Major Morozov from the Mitteler Rebbe investigation team to focus on an unrelated criminal probe, leaving Loginov and Markov to complete the inquiry.
Story: About two weeks into the month-long investigation that ran from early Cheshvan to early Kislev, Major Morozov was reassigned to a separate criminal case involving misuse of treasury funds. Khovansky formally released Morozov from the joint inquiry and instructed Loginov and Markov to complete the entire investigation without him, urging them to make every effort to bring out the truth. The two remaining investigators carried the case forward together.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, morozov, loginov, markov, khovansky, investigation, russia

Title: Investigator Korbitsky sent to inspect Lubavitch synagogue and library
Summary: Investigator Korbitsky was dispatched from Vitebsk to Lubavitch to verify the Mitteler Rebbe's testimony about the cost of building the synagogue and acquiring its sacred books and Torah scrolls.
Story: Acting on Governor Khovansky's order, the private investigator Korbitsky traveled to Lubavitch on October 19, 1825 — his second such mission. He measured and inventoried the wooden synagogue (built in 1814–1815 by the landowner Kruger for about 4,000–5,000 rubles), priced its furnishings at roughly 1,258 rubles, and catalogued 611 books in four cabinets in the Rebbe's home. Local Jews swore the building was financed by donations from the Rebbe's followers, but could not provide further details; Korbitsky recommended further investigation of Kruger and the scribe of Yanovich.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, lubavitch, synagogue, russia, korbitsky, khovansky, kruger, yanovich scribe

Title: Khovansky orders Adjutant Vlasenko sent to fetch R. Aharon of Starashele
Summary: Khovansky proposes that the treasury fund Adjutant Vlasenko's travel to Starashele to bring R. Aharon Halevi to Vitebsk for questioning.
Story: On 19 October 1825, Governor-General Khovansky directed the Vitebsk treasury chamber to pay Adjutant Captain Vlasenko's travel expenses for a mission, accompanied by a policeman of the Mogilev province, to the town of Starashele. The trip was to bring R. Aharon Halevi of Starashele to Vitebsk to be questioned in connection with the Kissin informer affair. Five days later the treasury reported the cost at 119 rubles 52 kopeks.
Tags: khovansky, vlasenko, starashele, r aharon halevi, vitebsk, investigation

Title: Third interrogation of Rabbi DovBer; investigators sent to Lubavitch and Strashelye
Summary: Third interrogation of Rabbi DovBer; same day, special agents are dispatched to verify his statements in Lubavitch and to bring Rabbi Aharon of Staroshele in for questioning.
Story: On 19 October 1825 (19 Marcheshvan 5586), Rabbi DovBer faced his third interrogation in Vitebsk. The same day, the authorities dispatched a special investigator to Lubavitch to verify the Rebbe's testimony against local realities, and sent a separate officer to Strashelye to bring Rabbi Aharon Halevi of Staroshele for questioning in the same broader inquiry into chassidic fundraising.
Tags: mittler rebbe, aharon halevi, lubavitch, staroshele, vitebsk, interrogation

Title: Third interrogation of the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: A third round of interrogation took place on 19 Cheshvan 5586, followed again by the Rebbe's written replies.
Story: By the third interrogation, the questioning had narrowed onto specific financial details and the Rebbe's role in Jewish arbitration. The Rebbe acknowledged accepting cases of debt disputes between Christian and Jewish parties, which Khovansky later cited as exceeding the religious-only scope assigned to rabbis by Section 52 of the 1804 statute.
Tags: interrogation, vitebsk, khovansky

Title: Third interrogation of the Mitteler Rebbe in Vitebsk
Summary: In his third interrogation, the Mitteler Rebbe was questioned about a list of donations to R. Aharon of Strashelye found in his home, which he denied ever seeing.
Story: Investigators presented the Mitteler Rebbe (Rabbi DovBer Schneuri of Lubavitch) with a list of yearly donations pledged by various people for the support of a rebbe, found among his papers. He testified that he had never seen the list and did not know how it had come into his home. It is presumed the list was actually seized at the home of R. Aharon of Strashelye, who was arrested around the same time, and was mistakenly attributed to the Rebbe.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, dovber schneuri, russia, vitebsk, interrogation, ma'amad, r. aharon of strashelye, markov

Title: Interrogation of R. Aharon of Strashelye
Summary: From 21-28 October, Khovansky's officials interrogated Rabbi Aharon of Strashelye in connection with the case.
Story: Rabbi Aharon HaLevi of Strashelye, the Alter Rebbe's senior disciple turned rival rebbe, was drawn into the inquiry for over a week. His earlier letters with Rabbi DovBer were among the materials Kissin had appended to his denunciation. Despite their well-known dispute, R. Aharon's testimony did not yield material that strengthened the case against Rabbi DovBer.
Tags: aharon of strashelye, strashelye, interrogation

Title: Interrogation of R. Aharon of Strashelye in Vitebsk
Summary: R. Aharon HaLevi of Strashelye, brought as a witness rather than a defendant, was interrogated in Vitebsk about donations collected for the Mitteler Rebbe.
Story: Aharon Movshovich HaLevi of Drizin, age 58, testified that he did not recognize a list of donations collected for the support of a rebbe. He stated he supported himself and his family on contributions of up to 3,000 rubles a year from Jews. In a follow-up session on October 28 he confirmed knowing some donors named in the ma'amad lists, and authenticated a letter sent to Simcha Kissin jointly with the Mitteler Rebbe. He was released around Rosh Chodesh Kislev, after less than two weeks in custody.
Tags: r. aharon of strashelye, mitteler rebbe, russia, vitebsk, interrogation, ma'amad, simcha kissin

Title: Interrogation of Rabbi Aharon Halevi of Staroshele
Summary: Rabbi Aharon Halevi of Staroshele is interrogated in Vitebsk over a week-long period as part of the wider inquiry into chassidic fundraising.
Story: From 21 to 28 October 1825 (21–28 Marcheshvan 5586), Rabbi Aharon Halevi of Staroshele, founder of the Strashelye chassidic court, was interrogated in Vitebsk by Russian state investigators. The questioning related to the parallel Maamad fundraising in his branch of Chabad and was part of the broader probe arising from Simcha Keysin's denunciations against Rabbi DovBer.
Tags: staroshele, aharon halevi, vitebsk, interrogation

Title: Reb Aharon of Staroselye interrogated in Vitebsk
Summary: Between 21 and 28 Cheshvan 5586 Reb Aharon of Staroselye was brought to Vitebsk and interrogated as part of the same case.
Story: On 19 Cheshvan a special officer had been dispatched to summon Reb Aharon, a leading disciple of the Alter Rebbe who led his own circle in Staroselye. His interrogation extended the inquiry beyond the Mitteler Rebbe's immediate circle, signaling that Khovansky was probing the Chassidic movement more broadly.
Tags: aharon staroselye, vitebsk, interrogation, chassidut

Title: Release of Rabbi DovBer on Yud Kislev (Chag HaGeula of the Mittler Rebbe)
Summary: Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch is released from Vitebsk on 10 Kislev 5586, the date later marked as his personal Chag HaGeula.
Story: On 10 Kislev 5586 (late November 1825), Rabbi DovBer Schneuri was released from his detention in Vitebsk. The date became established in Chabad tradition as Yud Kislev, the Chag HaGeula (Festival of Liberation) of the Mittler Rebbe, observed annually as a day of celebration, farbrengens, and study of his teachings.
Tags: mittler rebbe, yud kislev, geulah, vitebsk, chag hageula

Title: Mitteler Rebbe petitions Governor Khovansky for release
Summary: On 6 Kislev 5586 the Rebbe submitted a written request to Khovansky asking to be freed from detention.
Story: Having endured three rounds of interrogation and roughly a month of confinement, Rabbi DovBer formally petitioned Governor Khovansky for release. Six days later the investigators delivered their summary of the inquiry to Khovansky. The Rebbe's release on 10 Kislev followed shortly thereafter, marking the first of what would become three stages of liberation.
Tags: khovansky, vitebsk, petition

Title: Mitteler Rebbe submits release request to Governor Khovansky
Summary: On 6 Kislev 5586 (4 November 1825) the Mitteler Rebbe formally petitioned Governor Khovansky for release to his home.
Story: With the active interrogation phase concluded, the Rebbe asked to be released pending the formal trial. The petition was granted four days later, sending the Rebbe home while his case moved into the provincial court system.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, khovansky, vitebsk

Title: Mitteler Rebbe's petition to Governor Khovansky requesting release
Summary: Days before his release, the Mitteler Rebbe submitted a short petition to Governor Khovansky pleading for a speedy decision in his case, citing his deteriorating health.
Story: After the conclusion of his interrogations and shortly before his release, the Mitteler Rebbe wrote a brief memorandum to Governor Khovansky. He expressed confidence that justice would prevail and that the false denunciation against him would be exposed, but appealed to the governor's sense of fairness to expedite a decision because his fragile health was steadily worsening. A longer follow-up petition was later printed in the kuntres 'Bad Kodesh.'
Tags: mitteler rebbe, dovber schneuri, khovansky, russia, vitebsk, petition, imprisonment

Title: Rabbi DovBer submits request to Khovansky to be released home
Summary: Rabbi DovBer formally petitions Governor Khovansky to release him from detention in Vitebsk and allow him to return home.
Story: On 4 November 1825 (6 Kislev 5586), with his interrogations concluded, Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch submitted a written request to Governor Khovansky asking to be released from Vitebsk and allowed to return home. The petition came after weeks of questioning, and the governor granted the release a few days later.
Tags: mittler rebbe, khovansky, vitebsk, release

Title: Mitteler Rebbe released on Yud Kislev
Summary: On 10 Kislev 5586 the Mitteler Rebbe was released from his Vitebsk interrogation and allowed to return home.
Story: Though strictly only an interim release pending trial, this date became commemorated in Chabad as Yud Kislev, the festival of the Mitteler Rebbe's redemption. The eventual judicial acquittal would unfold in three further stages over the next two years; the Mitteler Rebbe himself never lived to see the final Senate confirmation.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, yud kislev, release, vitebsk

Title: Release of the Mitteler Rebbe on 10 Kislev 5586
Summary: Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch, the Mitteler Rebbe, was freed from Russian arrest on 10 Kislev 5586, three days before the Loginov-Markov summary report was issued.
Story: On 10 Kislev 5586 (approximately November 8, 1825) the Mitteler Rebbe was released from imprisonment, a date that became the annual chassidic festival of Yud Kislev. The summary report by investigators Loginov and Markov, compiling all the interrogations and seized documents, was written three days after this release. Although the Rebbe was freed in body, the case formally continued through the Russian courts for another fifteen months until his final acquittal.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, 10 kislev, redemption, vitebsk, lubavitch

Title: Investigators submit summary of investigation to Khovansky
Summary: The state investigators write up a summary of their interrogation findings and submit it, along with supporting documents, to Governor Khovansky.
Story: On 10 November 1825 (12 Kislev 5586), the investigators handling the case against Rabbi DovBer wrote a comprehensive review of the interrogations and evidence gathered, and turned the file over to Governor Khovansky. This summary became the basis for the subsequent transfer of the case to the Mohilev provincial authorities for formal judicial proceedings.
Tags: khovansky, vitebsk, investigation, mittler rebbe

Title: Investigators submit summary of Vitebsk interrogations to Khovansky
Summary: The investigators in Vitebsk submitted to Governor Khovansky a summary of the results of their interrogations of the Mitteler Rebbe and related witnesses.
Story: On 12 Kislev 5586 the Vitebsk investigators compiled and submitted their formal review of the inquiry into the Mitteler Rebbe to the governor-general, Prince Nikolai Khovansky. The document incorporated the findings of Korbitsky's on-site investigation in Lubavitch concerning the synagogue and the Rebbe's library, alongside the responses given by the Rebbe and witnesses such as R. Aharon of Strashelye during the Vitebsk interrogations.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, khovansky, russia, vitebsk, interrogation, investigation summary

Title: Loginov and Markov submit summary report on Mitteler Rebbe case
Summary: Colonel Loginov and Court Counselor Markov filed their comprehensive report to Khovansky compiling all interrogations and documents in the case against Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch.
Story: On November 10, 1825, the investigators Loginov and Markov submitted their final report to Governor-General Khovansky summarizing every interrogation conducted in Vitebsk, the search at Lubavitch by officer Korbitsky, and every document supplied by the informer Kisin or seized from the Rebbe. The report addressed the disputed distribution of 35,000 rubles, the Rebbe's role as arbiter, his correspondence about chassidic affairs, and the synagogue-building takanah. It was received by Khovansky's office the following day and forwarded to the Mogilev gubernia administration a week later.
Tags: loginov, markov, khovansky, investigation, mitteler rebbe, kisin

Title: Case transferred to Mogilev provincial government for trial
Summary: Khovansky sent the file with his findings to the Mogilev provincial government, demanding that the accused be judged with full severity.
Story: Order No. 10265 forwarded the entire investigation, including Loginov and Markov's reports, to Mogilev's provincial government on 19 Kislev 5586. Khovansky concluded that the Rebbe collected 10,000-14,000 rubles annually for personal use and acted as a civil arbitrator, both in violation of Section 52 of the 1804 statute. Mogilev province routed the case to the Babinovichi peace court, which initiated further investigations in Kapust, Orsha, Shklov, and Mogilev.
Tags: khovansky, mogilev, courts, trial

Title: Khovansky forwards Mitteler Rebbe case to Mogilev gubernia
Summary: Khovansky sent the Loginov-Markov investigation file to the Mogilev gubernia administration for legal processing.
Story: On November 17, 1825, after reviewing the investigators' report, Prince Khovansky forwarded the case against Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch to the Mogilev gubernia administration under reference numbers 5849 and 5850. This transfer began the lengthy judicial phase, in which the matter would be routed first to the Babinovichi peace court and ultimately to the Mogilev High Court. Khovansky later cited this directive when pressing officials for updates on the case.
Tags: khovansky, mogilev, mitteler rebbe, vitebsk, case transfer

Title: Khovansky transfers case to Mohilev province for trial
Summary: Governor Khovansky forwards the case file to the Mohilev provincial government so that the case can be tried in the appropriate provincial court.
Story: On 17 November 1825 (19 Kislev 5586), Khovansky transferred the entire investigative file on Rabbi DovBer to the government of Mohilev province, since Lubavitch and Babinovich fell under that jurisdiction. He simultaneously assigned the chief prosecutor of Mohilev to supervise the trial that would follow.
Tags: khovansky, mohilev, lubavitch, babinovich, trial

Title: Khovansky transfers case to Mohilev provincial government
Summary: On 19 Kislev 5586 Governor Khovansky forwarded the case file to the Mohilev provincial government for trial.
Story: Since Lubavitch lay in the Babinovichi district of Mohilev province, jurisdiction now passed there. The provincial authorities in turn sent the file to the Babinovichi peace court, which dispatched officers to Lubavitch and ordered parallel inquiries in Kapust, Orsha, Shklov and Mohilev to verify the Rebbe's account of how Ma'amad funds were collected.
Tags: khovansky, mohilev, babinovichi, russia, courts

Title: Prosecutor of Mogilev confirms receipt of Khovansky's order in the rebbe's case
Summary: Provincial Prosecutor Smolaninov of Mogilev formally acknowledges Khovansky's directive to oversee the legal proceedings against the Mitteler Rebbe.
Story: On 2 December 1825, Smolaninov, the General Prosecutor of Mogilev Province, sent report no. 2292 to Governor-General Khovansky in Vitebsk acknowledging receipt of Khovansky's 17 November order (no. 5850). The order had instructed him to supervise the provincial government's transfer of the investigation against Rabbi Dovber Schneuri to the appropriate court, and to ensure proper application of the law in handling the defendants. The acknowledgement was received in Vitebsk on 5 December 1825.
Tags: russia, mogilev, khovansky, smolaninov, prosecutor

Title: Mogilev provincial government transfers the rebbe's case to Babinavichi court
Summary: The Mogilev provincial government reports to Khovansky that it has forwarded the investigation against the rebbe to the magistrate's court in Babinavichi district.
Story: On 16 December 1825, the Mogilev provincial government (signed by Civil Governor Maksimov and Counselors Butovich, Kishkovich, and Chitozhribsky) reported to Khovansky on action taken in response to his 17 November order (no. 5849). The report summarized findings against Rabbi Dovber Schneuri — including the 35,000-ruble post-1812 collection, ongoing annual collections of 10,000-14,000 rubles, and his serving as arbitrator between Jews and Christians — all allegedly contrary to §§51-52 of the 1804 Jewish Statute. Per §110 of provincial law, the file (no. 872) was forwarded to the magistrate's court in Babinavichi district, which contained Lubavitch, for prosecution.
Tags: russia, mogilev, babinavichi, lubavitch, khovansky, courts, maksimov

Title: Case forwarded to the Babinovitsy peace court
Summary: The Mohilev government transferred the investigation against the Mitteler Rebbe to the peace court of the town of Babinovitsy on December 19, 1825.
Story: Following Khovansky's order, the Mohilev provincial administration sent the case materials to the peace court at Babinovitsy for further examination. The Babinovitsy court ultimately deliberated for six months before issuing its decision in June 1826.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, dovber schneuri, investigation, babinovitsy, court

Title: Mitteler Rebbe case transferred to Babinovichi peace court
Summary: Following standard legal procedure, the case file on Rabbi DovBer was sent from the Mogilev gubernia administration to the Babinovichi peace court.
Story: On December 19, 1825, the case against Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch — concerning allegedly illegal fundraising from his chassidim — was transmitted to the peace court of the town of Babinovichi for adjudication. The court would begin substantive work on the file in mid-January 1826. This routing through a local peace court was the standard procedure before the matter could rise to the Mogilev High Court for review.
Tags: babinovichi, mogilev, mitteler rebbe, court, case transfer

Title: Mohilev provincial government sends case to Babinovich peace court
Summary: The Mohilev provincial government routes the file to the Babinovich peace court for completion of the pre-trial investigation.
Story: On 19 December 1825 (21 Tevet 5586), Mohilev authorities determined that the pre-trial inquiry was not yet complete and sent the file to the peace court in Babinovich, the jurisdiction to which Lubavitch belonged. The Babinovich court was tasked with finishing the questioning of witnesses before the case could go to formal trial.
Tags: mohilev, babinovich, lubavitch, trial

Title: Case file arrives at Babinovich peace court
Summary: The case file against Rabbi DovBer reaches the Babinovich peace court.
Story: On 23 December 1825 (25 Tevet 5586), the case file concerning Rabbi DovBer's alleged illegal collection of Maamad funds was formally received at the Babinovich peace court. Weeks would pass before the court actually began processing it, in part because of bureaucratic delays in assigning supervision.
Tags: babinovich, court, mittler rebbe

Title: Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch reprinted in Sudilkov
Summary: The Alter Rebbe's complete Shulchan Aruch was reissued as a unified six-part series in Sudilkov in 1826.
Story: This 5586 (1826) Sudilkov printing was the first to bring the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch out as a single complete series, departing from the volume-by-volume issuance of the 1814–1816 first edition.
Tags: alter rebbe, sudilkov, shulchan aruch

Title: Crown Rabbinate established in Russia
Summary: The Russian government established the system of 'Crown Rabbis' (rabbanim mitaam) between 1826 and 1835.
Story: Russia required rabbis to maintain official registers of births, marriages, and deaths and to communicate with the government in Russian. Since most traditional rabbis could not fulfill these requirements, a system of state-approved 'Crown Rabbis' arose alongside the religious rabbinate, creating a dual rabbinate that persisted until the fall of the Tsarist regime.
Tags: russia, crown rabbinate, rabbanut mitaam, tsarist government

Title: Death of MaharI"L of Yanovich
Summary: MaharI"L of Yanovich died between late 5585 and the end of Adar I 5586.
Story: MaharI"L's death can be bracketed by two letters: a responsum the Tzemach Tzedek addressed to him in late summer 5585, and a letter from R' Yissachar Ber Horowitz dated 28 Adar I 5586 (March 1826) that already refers to him as 'the late.' He was buried in Yanovich, where local residents long revered his memory.
Tags: mahari"l, yanovich, death

Title: Mitteler Rebbe writes to R. Sh., R. Y., and R. M. about the investigations
Summary: During the investigations the Mitteler Rebbe writes a confidential letter outlining strategy and pleading for chassidic unity in petitions to the authorities.
Story: Around Adar–Nissan 5586 (spring 1826), in the midst of the Khovansky investigations, the Mitteler Rebbe wrote to three chassidim (R. Shmuel, R. Yosef Yitzchak, and R. Menachem Mendel) discussing the delicate political situation. He laid out a strategy whereby the rank-and-file chassidim themselves would petition the courts, attesting that chassidic and non-chassidic Jews lived in halachic unity, and pleaded with R. Tzvi of Polotsk not to separate himself from the chassidic community.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, letter, investigation, r tzvi of polotsk, chassidim, court

Title: Mogilev high court acquits the Mitteler Rebbe (11 Kislev 5587)
Summary: On 11 Kislev 5587 the Mogilev provincial high court ruled to acquit Rabbi DovBer of all charges.
Story: The second stage of liberation came when the Mogilev high court, after reviewing the Babinovichi peace court's findings from investigations in multiple towns, formally cleared the Rebbe of every accusation. The verdict closed the case at the provincial level, but it still required ratification by Governor Khovansky. He instead lodged an appeal to the Senate in St. Petersburg, prolonging the legal struggle by another year.
Tags: mogilev, courts, acquittal, yud-aleph kislev

Title: Passing of Rabbi Yehuda Leib of Yanovich, brother of the Alter Rebbe
Summary: Rabbi Yehuda Leib of Yanovich, the Alter Rebbe's brother and author of Shearit Yehuda, passed away in winter 5586.
Story: Rabbi Yehuda Leib, brother of the Alter Rebbe and rabbi of Yanovich, passed away in the winter of 5586 (1826). He was the author of Shearit Yehuda and had served as a senior halachic authority in Chabad. His passing is noted in the introductions to the Tzemach Tzedek's responsa.
Tags: maharil, yehuda leib, yanovich, alter rebbe brother, shearit yehuda

Title: Pekidim VeAmarkalim letter volumes 1826-1829
Summary: The Pekidim VeAmarkalim of Amsterdam maintained extensive correspondence with kollel heads, with letters from 5586-5589 later published.
Story: The Pekidim VeAmarkalim corresponded extensively with the kollel heads and gabbaim in every city, keeping copies in special letter ledgers. Fifteen large volumes are preserved at the Yad Ben Zvi library. The first three volumes covering 5586-5589 were printed between 5725 and 5739 in the series 'Igrot HaPekidim VeHaAmarkalim MeAmsterdam.'
Tags: pekoam, amsterdam, letters, kollelim, yad ben zvi

Title: R' Yehuda Asad accepted as dayan in Sardhel
Summary: R' Yehuda Asad was appointed dayan in Sardhel on the recommendation of his teacher R' Aharon Suditz-Bichler and the Chasam Sofer.
Story: In the year 5586, R' Yehuda Asad (later author of Yehuda Yaaleh) was received as dayan in the Hungarian community of Sardhel. His appointment came through the recommendations of R' Aharon Suditz-Bichler, the Chasam Sofer, and R' Mordechai Banet.
Tags: yehuda asad, sardhel, chasam sofer, aharon suditz-bichler, hungary, rabbinate

Title: R. Shmuel Segal departs Hebron on emissary mission
Summary: After settling in Hebron, R. Shmuel Segal departed on an emissary mission abroad.
Story: Following his 1824 aliyah to Hebron, R. Shmuel Segal was sent abroad on an emissary mission in 1826-1827 on behalf of the Chabad community. He resumed his communal leadership in Hebron upon his return, where he served for decades and signed nearly all communal documents from 1830 onward.
Tags: hebron, shadar, shmuel segal, chabad

Title: Shulchan Aruch HaRav printed in Sadilkov with haskamos
Summary: The Shulchan Aruch of the Alter Rebbe was printed in Sadilkov in 5586 (1826), after the printer received haskamos for this edition.
Story: R' Mordechai HaLevi Horowitz, after years of printing in Kapust and Shklov, traveled to Sadilkov to produce this edition of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch. He secured rabbinic approbations specifically for this printing.
Tags: shulchan aruch harav, sadilkov, alter rebbe, haskamos, ukraine

Title: Simcha Kisin denounces the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: Simcha Kisin, a relative of the Mitteler Rebbe, denounced him to the authorities in 5586.
Story: Simcha Kisin — son of R' Lipman Kisin, parnas of Vitebsk and cousin of the Alter Rebbe's wife Sterna — turned informant against the Mitteler Rebbe in 5586 (1826). The denunciation led to the well-known arrest and release recorded in Maasar U'Geulat Admur Ha'emtza'i, despite the family's earlier closeness to the Rebbe's household.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, informant, vitebsk, kisin, russia

Title: Torat Chayim printed in Kopust
Summary: Torat Chayim by the Mitteler Rebbe was printed in Kopust in 5586.
