Story: Torat Chayim, a collection of the Mitteler Rebbe's discourses on Genesis and Exodus, was published in Kopust in 1826, two years before his passing.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, kopust

Title: Tsarist search at Mitteler Rebbe's home documents 611-volume library
Summary: A house search by Russian authorities at the Mitteler Rebbe's home in Lubavitch in 5586 recorded a library of 611 volumes in four cabinets.
Story: In 5586 (1826) Tsarist authorities conducted a search of the Mitteler Rebbe's home in Lubavitch. Their detailed inventory recorded a personal library of 611 books arranged in four cabinets. This document provides the earliest concrete glimpse of the size of the Chabad library in its second generation.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, lubavitch, tsarist, arrest, library, search

Title: Yosef David Ayash sent as shadar to Italian cities for Hebron
Summary: Yosef David Ayash began a four-year shlichut from Hebron through the cities of Italy.
Story: Starting in 5586 (1826), Yosef David Ayash traveled through the cities of Italy as a shadar on behalf of Hebron, continuing until 5590. His shlichut was conducted independently because the Pekuam committee did not handle fundraising in Italy. Ayash later left the Jewish people, but his shlichut is described in detail in Sheluchei Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: yosef david ayash, shadar, italy, hebron, sephardic kollel

Title: Chief prosecutor delegates oversight to Babinovich court inspector
Summary: Mohilev's chief prosecutor delegates judicial oversight of the case to the inspector of the Babinovich district court.
Story: On 9 January 1826 (13 Shevat 5586), the chief prosecutor of Mohilev province handed over day-to-day supervision of the case against Rabbi DovBer to the inspector of the Babinovich district court, since the trial venue had shifted. This step set the stage for the actual investigative work in Babinovich to begin.
Tags: babinovich, mohilev, prosecutor, court

Title: Prosecutor General transfers oversight of the Mitteler Rebbe's case to Babinovich
Summary: Mogilev Prosecutor General Smolaninov orders the Babinovich district court inspector to conduct the inquiry into the charges against the Mitteler Rebbe.
Story: On 9 January 1826 (13 Shevat 5586), Mogilev Prosecutor General Smolaninov reported to Governor-General Khovansky that he had instructed the inspector of the Babinovich district court to examine the file on Rabbi Berke Schneur (Mitteler Rebbe) of Lubavitch and reach a swift, lawful decision. This formally moved the case from Khovansky's officials into the regular court system.
Tags: khovansky, babinovich, mogilev, smolaninov, investigation, court

Title: Babinovich court begins work on the case
Summary: The Babinovich peace court begins actively processing the case file against Rabbi DovBer.
Story: On 13 January 1826 (17 Shevat 5586), nearly a month after receiving the file, the Babinovich peace court began actively working on the case against Rabbi DovBer. Within days the court would dispatch a police officer to Lubavitch with written questions for the Rebbe.
Tags: babinovich, court, mittler rebbe

Title: Babinovichi peace court begins hearing Mitteler Rebbe case
Summary: The Babinovichi peace court started its formal review of the file concerning Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch's alleged illegal fundraising.
Story: On January 13, 1826, the Babinovichi peace court opened its examination of the case against Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch. The court would labor over the file for more than six months before issuing its decision in July 1826. Its conclusions were then forwarded to the Mogilev High Court for review, eventually leading to the Rebbe's complete acquittal.
Tags: babinovichi, mitteler rebbe, court, investigation

Title: Officer sent to Lubavitch with written questions for Rabbi DovBer
Summary: The Babinovich court dispatches a police officer with written questions for Rabbi DovBer in Lubavitch.
Story: On 16 January 1826 (20 Shevat 5586), the Babinovich peace court dispatched a police officer to Lubavitch carrying a list of written questions for Rabbi DovBer. The Rebbe's written answers would have been used to fill out the formal court record without bringing him back to Babinovich in person.
Tags: babinovich, lubavitch, mittler rebbe, interrogation

Title: Court inspector Kilikovsky reports delays in Mitteler Rebbe case
Summary: District inspector Kilikovsky informed Governor-General Khovansky that the Babinovich peace court was mishandling the case against Rabbi DovBer.
Story: On 23 January 1826 (27 Shvat 5586), Inspector Kilikovsky of the Babinovich district court reported to Governor-General Khovansky that the case against Rabbi Berke Schneur of Lubavitch had stalled. The file had arrived at the peace court on 23 December 1825 and sat unexamined; only on 15 January 1826 did officials review it, opting on 16 January to send written questions via a constable to the rabbi and the Jewish communities — bypassing proper procedure, which required summoning the rabbi for direct questioning. Kilikovsky reported the irregularity and noted that the secretary Zhuravkovich had already been dismissed by the Mogilev provincial administration for misconduct.
Tags: mitteler-rebbe, babinovich, russia, court, khovansky, kilikovsky

Title: Acting court inspector reports on Mitteler Rebbe case progress
Summary: Acting district court inspector Dobravolski reports to Governor-General Khovansky on the slow progress of the Mitteler Rebbe's case at the Babinovich peace court.
Story: Following Khovansky's order while passing through Babinovich, the acting court inspector took charge of expediting the case against Rabbi DovBer Schneuri of Lubavitch. The inspector found that the case had reached the peace court on December 23, 1825, but progress had been slow. Inquiries sent to the Rebbe were lost in transit, forcing a second messenger to be dispatched. The court then resolved to take sworn testimony from Jewish communities in Orsha, Kopust and Shklov regarding their alleged 1813 invitation to the Rebbe to succeed his father.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, dovber schneuri, russia, investigation, babinovich peace court, khovansky, dobravolski

Title: Court issues investigation orders to Kapust, Orsha, Shklov and Mohilev
Summary: Babinovich court instructs courts in Kapust, Orsha, Shklov and Mohilev to interrogate local chassidim about the Maamad funds.
Story: On 12 February 1826 (17 Adar I 5586), the Babinovich peace court, dissatisfied with the evidence it could gather locally, sent instructions to courts in Kapust, Orsha, Shklov and the lower court of Mohilev. Each was ordered to interrogate the chassidim in its town about the collection and distribution of Maamad funds, expanding the geographic scope of the inquiry considerably.
Tags: babinovich, kapust, orsha, shklov, mohilev, chassidim

Title: Khovansky reports Babinovich court mismanagement to Mohilev government
Summary: Governor-General Khovansky proposes to the Mohilev provincial government that the Babinovich peace court be publicly punished for mishandling the Mitteler Rebbe's case.
Story: Khovansky relayed the district court inspector's findings that the Babinovich peace court had failed to bring the Rebbe in for sworn interrogation as the law required, instead sending a policeman with questions who had not yet returned. The inspector attributed the delays to the court officials' incompetence and ignorance of proper procedure. Khovansky proposed publicly punishing the court for deviating from legal procedure and noted that the secretary Zhuravkovich had already been dismissed for misconduct, calling for a reliable replacement so the case could not be further stalled.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, khovansky, babinovich peace court, judicial misconduct, zhuravkovich, russia

Title: Investigation continues with sworn testimony from Jewish communities
Summary: Court inspector Kilikovski reports that the Babinovich court is gathering sworn testimony from Jewish communities in Orsha, Kopust and Shklov about their 1813 invitation to the Rebbe.
Story: Inspector Kilikovski reported that on February 8 the policeman sent to question the Rebbe had returned admitting he had lost the Rebbe's responses on the road from Lubavitch to Babinovich. A second messenger was dispatched and brought back responses on February 10. The court then resolved to obtain sworn testimony from communities in Orsha and Kopust, and from chasidim in Shklov, to verify whether they had written to the Rebbe in Kremenchug in 1813 promising to compensate his losses from the French invasion and to support his family if he succeeded his father as their rabbi.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, kilikovski, orsha, kopust, shklov, russia, investigation

Title: Mohilev government fines Babinovich court over investigation conduct
Summary: The Mohilev provincial government fines the Babinovich peace court for illegal leniencies in handling the investigation and orders speedier collection of chassidic testimony.
Story: On 3 March 1826 (6 Adar II 5586), the government of Mohilev province imposed a fine on the Babinovich peace court, citing illegal leniency in how the investigation was being run. At the same time, it ordered the courts in Kapust, Orsha, Shklov and Mohilev to accelerate gathering chassidic testimony in the case against Rabbi DovBer.
Tags: mohilev, babinovich, court, fines

Title: Khovansky orders Mohilev prosecutor to oversee Rebbe's case
Summary: Khovansky instructs the General Prosecutor of Mohilev province to closely supervise the handling of the Mitteler Rebbe's case and ensure rapid execution of court demands.
Story: Building on his earlier reports about the disorder at the Babinovich peace court, Khovansky directly instructed the provincial General Prosecutor to ensure the proposals issued to Mohilev province were carried out. The order emphasized swift execution of the Babinovich court's requests, and parallel cooperation from the lower court of Mohilev province, all to be done promptly and without delay.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, khovansky, general prosecutor, mohilev, russia

Title: Khovansky reports lost responses and orders fast case resolution
Summary: Khovansky reports to the Mohilev government on the lost interrogation responses and demands the responsible parties be punished and the case completed urgently.
Story: Following the latest district court inspector's report, Khovansky relayed that the policeman sent with questions to the Rebbe had lost the responses on the road from Lubavitch to Babinovich. He proposed punishing those responsible at the Babinovich peace court for sending a policeman instead of bringing the Rebbe in for proper interrogation. Khovansky also instructed the Orsha and Kopust town councils and the Mohilev lower court to expedite the requested testimony, and reiterated his earlier call for a competent secretary to be appointed.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, khovansky, babinovich peace court, russia, investigation

Title: Mohilev General Prosecutor reports on Rebbe's case to Khovansky
Summary: General Prosecutor Smolaninov reports to Khovansky that the Mohilev provincial government has done nothing to expedite the Mitteler Rebbe's case.
Story: Smolaninov informed Khovansky that despite the demand for a quick legal resolution, the provincial government had taken no action. He summarized the latest developments: the lost interrogation responses, the second messenger who retrieved them on February 10, and the decision to gather sworn testimony from communities in Orsha, Kopust and Shklov. Smolaninov reported that he had personally ordered the district court inspector to ensure the required testimony was gathered promptly and that no further delay would be tolerated.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, smolaninov, general prosecutor, mohilev, babinovich peace court, russia

Title: Mohilev provincial government orders continued interrogation of the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: The Mohilev provincial government reported to Governor-General Khovansky that the magistrate court of Babinovich had been fined for procedural irregularities in the Mitteler Rebbe's case and was ordered to resume formal interrogations without delay.
Story: Civil Governor Maksimov and his councillors reported that the Babinovich magistrate court had bypassed proper procedure by sending a policeman with questions to the Rebbe instead of summoning him to a hearing — an evident leniency. A fine of 10 rubles was imposed on the responsible officials, and the court was ordered to investigate the Rebbe thoroughly on the charge of collecting large sums from his followers and to punish the accused with full severity. Oversight was placed in the hands of the district court inspector and the provincial prosecutor.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, mohilev, khovansky, babinovich court, russia, investigation

Title: District court inspector reports delays in Mitteler Rebbe investigation
Summary: District court inspector Kilikovsky reported to Khovansky that the case against the Mitteler Rebbe was stalled because the courts of Orsha and Mohilev had not yet returned the required investigation results.
Story: Inspector Kilikovsky of the Babinovich district court informed Governor-General Khovansky that the case against Rabbi Berke Schneur of Lubavitch was being held up because the courts in Orsha and Mohilev had not delivered the inquiry results requested on February 12. The Mohilev provincial administration had issued an urgent reminder on March 3, and Kilikovsky himself had pressed the inspectors of those districts on February 24 and again on March 17.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, khovansky, babinovich court, orsha, mohilev, russia, investigation

Title: Mohilev provincial report on continued investigations in Kapust, Orsha, and Mohilev
Summary: The Mohilev provincial government updated Khovansky on continuing inquiries into the Mitteler Rebbe, including a policeman who lost the Rebbe's written answers and sworn testimony being gathered from Jewish communities in Orsha, Kapust, and Shklov.
Story: The provincial government detailed how the Babinovich court had relied on a policeman who returned having lost the Rebbe's responses, then dispatched a second courier and ordered sworn testimony to be collected from the Jewish communities of Orsha, Kapust, and Shklov. The investigators sought to verify a claim that in 1813 the people of Kremenchug had invited Rabbi Schneur to succeed his father, promising to compensate his property losses from the French invasion and to support his entire family. Officials were fined for procedural lapses, and the courts were ordered to complete depositions and rule on the case as swiftly as possible.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, mohilev, khovansky, kapust, orsha, babinovich court, shklov, kremenchug, russia, ma'amad

Title: District court inspector reports completion of Mitteler Rebbe inquiries
Summary: Inspector Kilikovsky reported to Khovansky that the required investigations from various localities in the Mitteler Rebbe's case had finally reached the Babinovich magistrate court and been reviewed.
Story: In a brief dispatch dated 17 Iyar 5586, Kilikovsky, inspector of the Babinovich district court, informed the governor-general that all the depositions and inquiries needed for the case concerning Rabbi Berke Schneur of Lubavitch's alleged unlawful activities had been received from the various localities. The materials had been added to the case file and surveyed, advancing the proceedings toward a decision.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, babinovich court, khovansky, russia, investigation

Title: Provincial prosecutor reports collected testimony in Mitteler Rebbe case
Summary: The provincial prosecutor of Mohilev reported to Khovansky that the necessary depositions, including testimony of Chassidim in Shklov, had been forwarded to the Babinovich magistrate court for swift adjudication of the Mitteler Rebbe's case.
Story: Prosecutor Smolaninov of Mohilev province informed Governor-General Khovansky that reports from the magistrate courts of Orsha and Kapust, as well as the lower court of Mohilev, had reached the Babinovich court, along with the depositions of Chassidim in Shklov needed for the case. He had sent a written demand urging Babinovich to rule promptly on the alleged unlawful actions of Rabbi Berke Schneur of Lubavitch, and informed the district court inspector accordingly.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, mohilev, khovansky, orsha, kapust, shklov, babinovich court, russia, investigation

Title: Babinovitsy peace court rules on Mitteler Rebbe's case
Summary: The peace court at Babinovitsy issued its decision in the Mitteler Rebbe's case on June 20, 1826, after further investigation.
Story: After receiving the case in late 1825, the Babinovitsy peace court conducted additional inquiries and reached its decision on June 20, 1826. The case was then forwarded on August 3 to the First Department of the Mohilev Supreme Court for review—the body that would ultimately acquit the Rebbe.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, dovber schneuri, babinovitsy, court, ruling

Title: R' Mordechai Banet writes recommendation for R' Yehuda Asad
Summary: R' Mordechai Banet of Nikolsburg wrote a letter to R' Aharon, av beis din of Sardhel, recommending support for R' Yehuda Asad.
Story: Dated 16 Sivan 5586, the letter from the elderly R' Mordechai Banet of Nikolsburg praises R' Yehuda Asad's diligence and mastery of halacha, urging R' Aharon to strengthen his standing in the community. The letter was part of the process that led to R' Asad's appointment as dayan.
Tags: mordechai banet, yehuda asad, nikolsburg, sardhel, rabbinate, hungary

Title: Babinovich Peace Court rules in favor of the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: The Babinovich peace court issues its decision in the case against the Mitteler Rebbe.
Story: On 20 July 1826, the peace court of Babinovich rendered its decision in the case opened against the Mitteler Rebbe on the basis of Shimcha Kissin's denunciation. The court concluded that contributions to the Rebbe were freely given and could not be considered illegal, dismissing the charges. The verdict was the first of several rulings exonerating the Rebbe.
Tags: babinovich, court, verdict, exoneration, mitteler rebbe

Title: Babinovich peace court rules on the case
Summary: The Babinovich peace court issues its decision on the case against Rabbi DovBer.
Story: On 20 July 1826 (27 Tammuz 5586), the Babinovich peace court formally issued its decision on the case after months of investigation. The ruling and supporting file were then prepared for transfer to the higher provincial court in Mohilev, which would issue the final verdict.
Tags: babinovich, court, mittler rebbe, verdict

Title: Babinovichi peace court issues decision on Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: The Babinovichi peace court reached its final decision in the case against Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch and submitted it for review by the Mogilev High Court.
Story: On July 20, 1826, after roughly half a year of deliberation, the Babinovichi peace court concluded its work on the case concerning Rabbi DovBer's alleged illegal collection of funds from his chassidim. The decision was then presented for re-examination by the First Department of the Mogilev High Court. The High Court's inspector, Kilikovsky, reported the transfer to Prince Khovansky on July 31, 1826.
Tags: babinovichi, mogilev high court, mitteler rebbe, verdict

Title: Case returned to Mohilev higher court with Babinovich recommendation
Summary: Following the close of the investigation, the case file is returned to the Mohilev higher court along with the Babinovich peace court's recommendation.
Story: On 3 August 1826 (12 Av 5586), with the local investigation complete, the file was sent back to the higher court of Mohilev province, accompanied by the recommendation of the Babinovich peace court. The higher court would now deliberate on a final, binding verdict in the case against Rabbi DovBer.
Tags: babinovich, mohilev, court, mittler rebbe

Title: Imperial amnesty manifesto of 22 August 1826
Summary: A new imperial amnesty was issued on August 22, 1826, shortly after Nicholas I's coronation.
Story: Nicholas I's coronation amnesty pardoned a wide range of prior offenses. Together with the 1814 manifesto, it became one of the two reasons Governor-General Khovansky cited for not pursuing punishment against the Mitteler Rebbe despite his contention that the 1813 fundraising had been unlawful.
Tags: russia, amnesty, manifesto, tsar nicholas i

Title: Mitteler Rebbe denounced and brought to Vitebsk
Summary: At the end of Tishrei 5587, the Mitteler Rebbe was informed against and immediately taken to the city of Vitebsk.
Story: At the end of Tishrei 5587 (October 1826), informers' charges against the Mitteler Rebbe escalated and he was promptly brought to Vitebsk for investigation. There the case fell under the jurisdiction of General-Governor Khovansky of Vitebsk province. The arrest opened months of investigation into the ma'amad collection and the chassidic movement before the Rebbe's eventual full acquittal.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, vitebsk, arrest, malshinus, khovansky

Title: Mitteler Rebbe writes petition to Governor Khovansky
Summary: In Cheshvan or early Kislev 5587 the Mitteler Rebbe wrote a petition to Vitebsk's Governor Khovansky asking that he personally judge the case.
Story: While held in Vitebsk between Cheshvan and the beginning of Kislev 5587 (October-November 1826), the Mitteler Rebbe composed a written petition to General-Governor Khovansky. He requested that the governor personally adjudicate his case, drawing on kabbalistic and chassidic principles the Alter Rebbe had earlier presented before Czar Paul. The petition built on the framework relating fear of Heaven to fear of an earthly king and argued that a king's vision penetrates more truthfully than that of any subordinate judge.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, khovansky, vitebsk, petition, kabbalah, chassidus

Title: Mogilev High Court acquits the Mitteler Rebbe on 11 Kislev 5587
Summary: The First Department of the Mogilev High Court ruled to acquit Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch of the charges of illegal fundraising from his followers.
Story: On November 29, 1826 — 11 Kislev 5587 — the First Department of the Mogilev High Court issued its verdict in favor of Rabbi DovBer (Berke Schneur) of Lubavitch, finding that the charges of unlawful collection of money from his chassidim could not stand. The decision was reached without opposition from the gubernia prosecutor general. This judgment, while not formally confirmed by higher authorities for several more months, secured the Rebbe's freedom from criminal jeopardy.
Tags: mogilev high court, mitteler rebbe, 11 kislev, acquittal, verdict

Title: Mogilev High Court's First Chamber upholds the Mitteler Rebbe's acquittal
Summary: The First Chamber of the Mogilev High Court rules that the Mitteler Rebbe is not guilty.
Story: On 29 November 1826, the First Chamber of the Mogilev High Court ruled in the case of Rabbi Berke Schneur. It found that the donations he received were given voluntarily by his followers and that no criminal offense had occurred, agreeing with the earlier Babinovich verdict. The decision was later presented to Governor-General Khovansky, who disagreed and appealed it to the Ruling Senate.
Tags: mogilev, court, verdict, exoneration, mitteler rebbe

Title: Mohilev High Court acquits the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: On 11 Kislev 5587 the Mohilev provincial high court cleared the Mitteler Rebbe of all charges.
Story: Inquiries in Kapust, Orsha, Shklov and Mohilev had confirmed that chassidim had voluntarily invited the Rebbe to return from Kremenchug and pledged to support him. The court concluded that Ma'amad contributions were voluntary gifts to a non-salaried rabbi, not communal taxes, and so did not violate the 1805 Jewish charter. The verdict was sent to the prosecutor general and then to Governor Khovansky for confirmation.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, mohilev, acquittal, ma'amad

Title: Mohilev higher court acquits Rabbi DovBer
Summary: The Mohilev higher court rules to acquit Rabbi DovBer and forwards the verdict to the provincial chief prosecutor for review.
Story: On 29 November 1826 (11 Kislev 5587), after completing its deliberations, the Mohilev higher court issued a verdict acquitting Rabbi DovBer of the charges that had been brought against him. The case file together with the ruling was passed to the chief prosecutor of Mohilev province for the legally required review and confirmation.
Tags: mohilev, court, mittler rebbe, acquittal

Title: Mohilev Supreme Court acquits the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: On November 29, 1826, the First Department of the Mohilev Supreme Court ruled to acquit Rabbi Dovber Schneuri of all charges of illegal fundraising.
Story: The court concluded that the Mitteler Rebbe had been freely chosen by the Chasidim as their religious teacher, that the donations he received were voluntary and unforced, and that even Jews of other provinces sent contributions without compulsion. It held that no one could be forbidden from giving a legal donation or disposing of private property, and that the Rebbe's arbitration work did not amount to exercising judicial authority. The ruling cleared him of all wrongdoing.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, dovber schneuri, mohilev, supreme court, acquittal

Title: Cantonist conscription law begins for Russian Jewry
Summary: The Tsar's cantonist decree imposed conscription quotas on Jewish communities, sending young boys to the Russian army for 25 years.
Story: From 5587 (1827) onwards, the cruel cantonist law forced Jewish communities to supply fixed quotas of Jewish children — sometimes as many as 30 per thousand Jews — who were dispatched to the army for 25 years and completely cut off from their parents and Jewish life. When communities could not meet the quotas, khappers were sent to seize Jewish children from the streets amidst the cries of children and parents.
Tags: cantonists, russia, conscription, tsar nicholas i, khappers

Title: Founding of Kollel Chabad as a fourth separate kollel in Eretz Yisrael
Summary: In 5587 Kollel Chabad was constituted as a fourth distinct kollel, alongside the Sephardim, Perushim, and Chassidim kollelim.
Story: Building on the dedicated Chabad fund founded by the Alter Rebbe two decades earlier, Kollel Chabad emerged as an independent kollel structure in 5587. Over the following 40 years the four general kollelim subdivided into dozens of subsidiary kollelim corresponding to towns and regions of origin, until the 5626 merger created the Vaad HaKollel HaKlali.
Tags: kollel chabad, eretz yisrael, kollel structure, hebron

Title: Kollel Chabad in Hebron formally established with first leadership
Summary: In 5587, Kollel Chabad in Hebron took its definitive form with three named overseers: R' Tzvi Hirsh Lifshitz, R' Ephraim Yaffe, and R' Moshe Meizlish.
Story: These three men signed as appointees on the shadarut documents of 5587, the founding year of Kollel Chabad as a formal entity. Alongside them, R' Leib Chitrik of Sena was appointed ne'eman (treasurer/bookkeeper). They styled themselves the 'appointees of the community of Ashkenazim called Chabad in Hebron.'

Title: Mittler Rebbe travels to Haditch to visit Alter Rebbe's grave
Summary: At the start of 5588 (1827) the Mittler Rebbe set out from Lubavitch on a long journey to prostrate himself at his father's grave in distant Haditch.
Story: The Mittler Rebbe undertook the demanding trip to Haditch, where the Alter Rebbe was buried, in the autumn of 1827. He would not reach Lubavitch alive on the return. The trip ended in his own passing in Nezhin.

Title: Moses Montefiore's first visit to Palestine
Summary: The prominent British Jewish leader Moses Montefiore made the first of seven trips to the Holy Land.
Story: Montefiore, a confidant of Queen Victoria, would become one of the most influential nineteenth-century advocates for Jews worldwide. His trips to Palestine, Russia, Romania, Rome, and Morocco shaped Jewish diplomatic history.

Title: Passing of Rabbi Dov Ber, the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: The Mitteler Rebbe, second Lubavitcher Rebbe, passed away in 1827.
Story: His passing led to the leadership of his son-in-law and nephew, Rabbi Menachem Mendel, the Tzemach Tzedek. The Mitteler Rebbe's extensive chasidic discourses remained an enduring legacy.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, dov ber

Title: Passing of Rabbi DovBer, the Mittler Rebbe
Summary: Rabbi DovBer Schneuri, the Mittler Rebbe, passes away on 9 Kislev 5588.
Story: On 9 Kislev 5588 (late November / early December 1827), Rabbi DovBer Schneuri, the Mittler Rebbe, passed away. His passing came mid-way through the Senate's appeal proceedings concerning the Khovansky case; the Senate did not yet know of his death when it issued its ruling on the case days later. The date 9 Kislev is now marked annually as his yahrzeit, just one day before his Chag HaGeula on 10 Kislev.
Tags: mittler rebbe, histalkus, yahrzeit, niezhin

Title: Passing of the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: Rabbi DovBer Schneuri, the Mitteler Rebbe, passed away on 9 Kislev 5588, the day before what would have been the first formal celebration of Yud Kislev.
Story: The Mitteler Rebbe's histalkus occurred on 9 Kislev 5588, just days before the Senate's final ratification of his acquittal. Because his passing fell one day before what would have been the inaugural Yud Kislev celebration, the festival was not established as widely as it might otherwise have been. Different traditions place the Rebbe's liberation in 5586, 5587, or 5588, reflecting the three distinct stages of his juridical exoneration.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, dovber schneuri, niftar, 9 kislev, nyezhin

Title: Passing of the Mittler Rebbe in Nezhin
Summary: On 9 Kislev 5588 (late 1827) the Mittler Rebbe passed away in Nezhin on his return journey from Haditch and was buried there.
Story: After visiting his father's grave in Haditch, the Mittler Rebbe fell ill on the way home. He passed in Nezhin on 9 (or 10) Kislev 5588, ending fifteen years of nesius. His resting place in Nezhin became, with Haditch and Rostov, one of the key Chabad pilgrimage sites in the former Russian Empire.
Tags: mittler-rebbe, nezhin, passing, dovber, kislev

Title: R' Leib Chitrik begins service as Hebron Kolel Chabad administrator
Summary: R' Yehuda Leib Chitrik of Sienna begins signing as a trustee of Hebron Kolel Chabad, a role he holds through 1844.
Story: R' Leib Chitrik was among the earliest administrators of Hebron's Chabad community. From 1827 he signed emissary credentials and community letters on behalf of Kolel Chabad in Hebron, continuing in that role until 1844. The 1827 emissary document identifies him as 'Yehuda Leib son of Wolf, trustee of the holy city of Hebron.'

Title: Tzemach Tzedek accepts Chabad leadership in Lubavitch
Summary: Following the passing of the Mittler Rebbe in 5588, Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneersohn accepted the leadership of Chabad and continued the movement from Lubavitch.
Story: The Tzemach Tzedek, both nephew and son-in-law of his predecessor, would lead the movement for nearly forty years from Lubavitch. In his early years he regularly toured Chassidic communities, having visited more than thirty towns by 5597. Lubavitch under his leadership became the cornerstone to which all Chabad communities turned.
Tags: tzemach-tzedek, schneersohn

Title: Tzemach Tzedek accepts leadership of Chabad
Summary: Following the passing of the Mitteler Rebbe in 5588, Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Lubavitch, the Tzemach Tzedek, assumed the leadership of Chabad.
Story: He was nephew and son-in-law of his predecessor, and had lived in Lubavitch alongside him since 1813. For nearly four decades he led Chabad from Lubavitch, traveling each year to a different region of chassidic communities, and writing the more than one thousand responsa of the Tzemach Tzedek series.

Title: Gubernia prosecutor approves Mitteler Rebbe acquittal verdict
Summary: The gubernia prosecutor general of Mogilev formally approved the High Court's verdict acquitting Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch.
Story: On February 1, 1827, corresponding to 16 Shevat 5587, the Mogilev gubernia prosecutor general endorsed the High Court verdict that acquitted Rabbi DovBer of all charges in the illegal-fundraising case. Eight days later the court submitted the approved judgment to Governor-General Khovansky for final ratification. This prosecutorial concurrence removed the last administrative obstacle within the gubernia to formal recognition of the Rebbe's innocence.
Tags: mogilev, prosecutor, mitteler rebbe, acquittal, verdict approval

Title: Mohilev chief prosecutor confirms the acquittal verdict
Summary: The chief prosecutor of Mohilev province formally approves the higher court's acquittal of Rabbi DovBer.
Story: On 1 February 1827 (16 Shevat 5587), the chief prosecutor of Mohilev province endorsed the higher court's ruling acquitting Rabbi DovBer of the charges brought via Simcha Keysin's denunciations. The approved verdict was then sent on to Governor Khovansky in Vitebsk for his confirmation.

Title: Acquittal verdict forwarded to Khovansky for confirmation
Summary: The approved acquittal verdict is sent from Mohilev to Governor Khovansky in Vitebsk for his final confirmation.
Story: On 9 February 1827 (24 Shevat 5587), the verdict acquitting Rabbi DovBer, now approved by the Mohilev chief prosecutor, was forwarded to Governor Khovansky in Vitebsk. Khovansky was expected to confirm the ruling, but instead would choose to appeal to the Senate in St. Petersburg.
Tags: khovansky, mohilev, verdict, mittler rebbe

Title: Formal acquittal verdict sent to Governor Khovansky
Summary: The Mogilev high court formally notified Governor Khovansky of its final acquittal of the Rebbe.
Story: On 24 Shvat 5587 the high court delivered written confirmation of its acquittal ruling to Vitebsk. Khovansky responded by requesting the full file with a summary, then attempted to delay through a series of procedural demands. Within weeks he resolved to escalate the case to the Governing Senate in Saint Petersburg.
Tags: mogilev, courts, acquittal, khovansky

Title: Mogilev High Court reports Mitteler Rebbe acquittal to Khovansky
Summary: Judges of the Mogilev High Court formally reported to Governor-General Khovansky that Rabbi DovBer had been acquitted and remained at liberty.
Story: On February 9, 1827, the First Department of the Mogilev High Court — judges Felix Marzhevsky, Porfiry Karpilovich, and Matvei Dekterev — submitted their verdict in the case of the Mitteler Rebbe to Khovansky for approval. They reported that no objection had been raised by the gubernia prosecutor and that 'Mr. Berke Schneur remains at his liberty.' Khovansky would subsequently request the full case file with a summary, which the court forwarded on March 22, 1827.
Tags: mogilev high court, khovansky, mitteler rebbe, acquittal

Title: Mitteler Rebbe's case presented to Governor-General Khovansky
Summary: The case file on the Mitteler Rebbe is forwarded to Governor-General Khovansky for review.
Story: On 12 February 1827, the Mogilev High Court's decision in favor of the Mitteler Rebbe was forwarded to Governor-General Khovansky. Khovansky considered the acquittal unjust and prepared an appeal, with his own legislative proposals concerning Jewish rabbis, to be submitted to the Ruling Senate.
Tags: khovansky, mogilev, court, mitteler rebbe

Title: Khovansky requests Mitteler Rebbe case file with summary
Summary: Governor-General Khovansky returned the High Court verdict and demanded the full case file accompanied by a brief summary and survey.
Story: On March 2, 1827, from Vitebsk, Khovansky directed the First Department of the Mogilev High Court to send him the verdict in the Mitteler Rebbe case together with the original file and a concise summary as soon as possible. The court initially responded on March 22 with the requested materials, but Khovansky pressed again on March 29 before being informed on April 13 that everything had already been dispatched. The case would eventually be escalated to the Senate in Petersburg on appeal.

Title: Khovansky appeals acquittal of Rabbi DovBer to the Senate in St. Petersburg
Summary: Refusing to confirm the verdict, Khovansky escalates the case by appealing the acquittal of Rabbi DovBer to the Senate of the Empire in St. Petersburg.
Story: On 15 May 1827 (Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5587), Governor Khovansky declined to confirm the Mohilev court's acquittal of Rabbi DovBer and instead lodged an appeal with the Senate in St. Petersburg. He also attached broader policy proposals affecting the status and rights of rabbis throughout Russia, which the Senate said it would consider separately.
Tags: khovansky, saint petersburg, senate, appeal, mittler rebbe

Title: Khovansky appeals the acquittal of the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: Governor-General Khovansky signed his appeal to the Governing Senate on May 15, 1827, in Vitebsk, challenging the Mohilev Supreme Court's acquittal of the Mitteler Rebbe.
Story: Prince Khovansky, Governor-General of Vitebsk, Mohilev, Smolensk and Kaluga, prepared a lengthy report to the Senate's Fifth Department arguing that the lower court's reasoning was unfounded and that the Mitteler Rebbe had in fact violated multiple provisions of the 1804 Jewish Constitution. While conceding that the imperial amnesties of 1814 and 1826 precluded actual punishment, he recommended barring the Rebbe from continuing as rabbi of the Chasidim and proposed broader restrictions on rabbinic authority in Russia. The appeal was filed in Vitebsk on May 15, 1827.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, dovber schneuri, khovansky, governing senate, vitebsk, appeal

Title: Khovansky appeals the acquittal to the Senate in St. Petersburg
Summary: Governor Khovansky filed an appeal to the Governing Senate in St. Petersburg challenging the Rebbe's acquittal.
Story: Refusing to accept the Mogilev verdict, Khovansky on Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5587 lodged a formal appeal with the Senate. He simultaneously instructed the Mogilev court to forward the case file to Petersburg. Khovansky's hope was to have the Rebbe brought to the capital for renewed proceedings, but the appeal would ultimately fail.
Tags: khovansky, senate, saint petersburg, appeal

Title: Mitteler Rebbe's case submitted to the Ruling Senate
Summary: Khovansky's appeal of the Mitteler Rebbe's acquittal reaches the Ruling Senate.
Story: On 15 May 1827, Governor-General Khovansky's appeal in the case of Rabbi Berke Schneur was submitted to the Ruling Senate in St. Petersburg, together with his proposals concerning the conduct of Jewish rabbis. The Senate would deliberate for six months before issuing its final ruling later that year.
Tags: senate, st petersburg, khovansky, mitteler rebbe, appeal

Title: Khovansky orders Mohilev court to send case file to the Senate with his appeal
Summary: Khovansky writes the Mohilev higher court instructing it to forward the case file together with his appeal to the Senate.
Story: On 31 May 1827 (Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5587), writing from Kaluga, Khovansky directed the first department of the Mohilev higher court to ship the 16-page case file (no. 553) along with his official opinion to the ruling Senate. This formally placed the acquittal of Rabbi DovBer in the hands of the highest judicial body of the Russian Empire.
Tags: khovansky, mohilev, senate, saint petersburg, appeal

Title: R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz becomes moreh tzedek of Bychov Chadash
Summary: In 5587, R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz was appointed moreh tzedek of the town of Bychov Chadash.
Story: After several years of teaching and engaging in halachic rulings in Rohatchov, R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz formally took up the moreh tzedek post in Bychov Chadash in 5587 (1827). By 27 Sivan 5587 he was writing responsa from his new post on questions such as tefillin parchment, sending them to the Tzemach Tzedek and other leading rabbis. He would remain there until his next post in Lubavitch.

Title: Hebron Chabad sends shadar R' Yitzchak Ashkenazi to Babylonia
Summary: The Chabad community of Hebron sent R' Yitzchak b"R Shlomo Ashkenazi as a shadar to Babylonia and Basra in summer 1827.
Story: In summer 1827 (קיץ תקפ"ז), the Chabad community of Hebron sent R' Yitzchak b"R Shlomo Ashkenazi to 'the cities of Babylonia and Basra and their surroundings.' Though the shadar was a Sephardic Jerusalem resident, he was dispatched by the Ashkenazi Chabad community, reflecting their isolation from traditional Russian funding streams.

Title: Mittler Rebbe's passing and Tzemach Tzedek's nesius
Summary: On 9 Kislev 5588 (November 1827) the Mittler Rebbe passed, and the Tzemach Tzedek accepted the Chabad nesius for the next 38 years.
Story: Following the passing of his father-in-law the Mittler Rebbe on 9 Kislev 5588 (November 1827), R. Menachem Mendel Schneersohn assumed the leadership of Chabad chassidut. He served as Rebbe for 38 years, until his own passing on 13 Nisan 5626 (1866).

Title: Passing of Mitteler Rebbe (Rabbi Dovber)
Summary: The Mitteler Rebbe passed away on 9 Kislev 5588, leaving Chabad without a confirmed successor.
Story: On 9 Kislev 5588 (late November 1827) the Mitteler Rebbe, Rabbi Dovber Schneuri, passed away in Niezhin. His son-in-law Rabbi Menachem Mendel (the future Tzemach Tzedek) was the natural successor, but for an extended period he refused to formally accept the leadership of Chabad. During this transitional time the chassidim of the movement were unsettled about who would lead them.

Title: Passing of the Mitteler Rebbe (9 Kislev)
Summary: Rabbi Dovber Schneuri, the Mitteler Rebbe, passed away on 9 Kislev 5588.
Story: His passing came twelve days before the Senate in Petersburg confirmed his judicial acquittal. The proximity of his passing to Yud Kislev — what would have been the first major celebration of his redemption — meant that the day was never widely established as a festival during his lifetime, contributing to historical confusion about whether the release occurred in 5586 or 5587.

Title: Mitteler Rebbe passes away on 9 Kislev
Summary: Rabbi Dov Ber of Lubavitch, the Mitteler Rebbe, passed away on 9 Kislev 5588.
Story: The Mitteler Rebbe led Chabad for fifteen years, from 1813 until his passing on 9 Kislev 5588 (1827). His tenure was marked by an extraordinary publication output, with nearly one volume issued each year.

Title: Passing of the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: Rabbi DovBer Schneuri, the Mitteler Rebbe, passed away on 9 Kislev 5588.
Story: The Mitteler Rebbe, Rabbi DovBer Schneuri, passed away on 9 Kislev 5588, just days before the Russian Senate's final verdict in his case. His passing came after a year of investigations stemming from Simcha Kisin's denunciation and his arrest in Vitebsk. The Senate's acquittal would arrive twelve days after his death.

Title: Passing of the Mittler Rebbe
Summary: Rabbi Dovber Schneuri, second rebbe of Chabad, passes away on 9 Kislev 5588.
Story: On 9 Kislev 5588 the Mittler Rebbe passed away. His son-in-law and nephew Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneersohn, the Tzemach Tzedek, succeeded him as leader of Chabad. The Tzemach Tzedek continued sending funds to the Chabad community in Hebron, one of the three primary support channels for the Hebron chassidim alongside the Pekidim of Amsterdam and the joint Italy emissaries.

Title: Ruling Senate exonerates the Mitteler Rebbe of all charges
Summary: The Ruling Senate dismisses the case, declaring the Mitteler Rebbe innocent of all charges.
Story: On 28 November 1827, the Ruling Senate decreed that Kissin's denunciation had no legal basis and that Rabbi Berke Schneur was not guilty of any criminal offense, ordering him fully cleared. Khovansky's accompanying proposals regarding Jewish rabbis were referred to the First Chamber of the Senate for separate review. The Senate's decree was communicated to the Mogilev provincial government, formally ending the legal proceedings.

Title: Senate confirms acquittal of the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: The Governing Senate in St. Petersburg upheld the Mogilev court's acquittal of the Rebbe, rejecting Khovansky's appeal.
Story: On 21 Kislev 5588 the Senate dismissed Khovansky's appeal and confirmed the Mogilev high court's verdict. This third and final stage of liberation came only days after the Rebbe's passing on 9 Kislev. The Mogilev court received notification on 7 Shvat 5588, and the question of trial expenses remained the subject of further correspondence into 1828.

Title: Senate confirms acquittal of the Mittler Rebbe
Summary: The Senate in St. Petersburg confirms the Mohilev acquittal of Rabbi DovBer, closing the criminal proceedings.
Story: On 28 November 1827 (21 Kislev 5588), the ruling Senate in St. Petersburg upheld the Mohilev higher court's acquittal of Rabbi DovBer, formally closing the criminal case that had been opened against him in 1825 following Simcha Keysin's denunciations. At the time of its ruling, the Senate was unaware that the Mittler Rebbe had passed away on 9 Kislev, just twelve days earlier.
Tags: senate, saint petersburg, mittler rebbe, acquittal

Title: Senate in Petersburg confirms acquittal of Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: On 21 Kislev 5588 the Petersburg Senate rejected Governor Khovansky's appeal and confirmed the Mitteler Rebbe's full acquittal.
Story: Khovansky had appealed in 1827, arguing that uncollected Ma'amad contributions were destabilizing and could divert tax revenue. The Senate sided with the Mohilev court, ruling Ma'amad legal as voluntary support for a non-salaried rabbi. The decision arrived twelve days after the Rebbe's passing and permanently legitimized Ma'amad as the financial basis of the Chabad dynasty.
Tags: senate, petersburg, mitteler rebbe, acquittal, ma'amad

Title: Senate in Petersburg upholds acquittal of the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: The Governing Senate in St. Petersburg rejects Khovansky's appeal and affirms the Mogilev high court's acquittal of the Mitteler Rebbe.
Story: On 28 November 1827, the Governing Senate in Petersburg issued its decision on Khovansky's 25 May appeal of the Mogilev high court ruling acquitting Rabbi Dovber Schneuri of charges of illegal fundraising. Reviewing testimony from the Babinavichi community, 5 other communities, and 160 sworn witnesses — all confirming that the 30,000-ruble post-1812 collection and ongoing support were given voluntarily, and that the rebbe served as a preacher rather than as a salaried, tax-collecting rabbi — the Senate found Kisin's denunciation legally unfounded. It ordered the rebbe fully acquitted and referred Khovansky's broader proposals on Russian rabbis to its First Department. The decree was received in Mogilev on 12 December 1827.

Title: Passing of the Mittler Rebbe in Nezhin
Summary: Rabbi Dovber, the second Chabad Rebbe, passed away on 10 Kislev 5588 in Nezhin while returning from a visit to his father's resting place in Haditch.
Story: At the start of 5588 the Mittler Rebbe traveled to prostrate himself at the grave of his father the Alter Rebbe in distant Haditch. On the return journey he stopped in Nezhin, where he passed away on the tenth of Kislev. He is buried there, and his son-in-law the Tzemach Tzedek subsequently assumed the leadership of Chabad.

Title: Senate acquits Mitteler Rebbe of all charges
Summary: On 21 Kislev 5588 the Russian Supreme Senate acquitted the Mitteler Rebbe and legitimated the ma'amad bais harav system.
Story: On 21 Kislev 5588, just twelve days after the Mitteler Rebbe's passing, the Supreme Senate in Petersburg upheld the Mohilev high court's acquittal and rejected Governor Khovansky's appeal. The ruling accepted that ma'amad donations were voluntary and that the Rebbe was not an official salaried rabbi, placing the practice outside the 1804 Jewish Statute's prohibitions. This decision legalized ma'amad as the financial foundation supporting Chabad rebbes for generations to come.

Title: Apei Moshe printed in Livorno
Summary: The collected sermons of R. Moshe Yisrael were printed posthumously in Livorno under the title Apei Moshe.
Story: Nearly ninety years after his death in Alexandria, the sermons of R. Moshe Yisrael were gathered and published in Livorno in 1828 under the title Apei Moshe. The book was one of three posthumous publications of his work, alongside his responsa Mishat Moshe printed in Constantinople.

Title: Passing of the Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: The Mitteler Rebbe passed away in 5588, two years after sending support funds to Hebron through R' Ephraim Yitzchak Epstein and his son-in-law would later send in 5590.
Story: The Mitteler Rebbe, R' Dovber Schneuri, passed away in 5588. He had instituted yearly support quotas for every chassid - rich and poor alike - for Eretz Yisrael through tzedakah boxes in every home. This obviated the need for special emissaries from Hebron to come rally Russian support.

Title: R. Yisrael ben Yaakov Mordechai Twer born
Summary: R. Yisrael, son of R. Yaakov Mordechai Twer, was born around 1828 (5588).
Story: His birth date is reconstructed from the 1839 Montefiore census of the Chabad community of Hebron, which records him at age 11. He and his brothers adopted the family name BeRiMaT (ben R. Mordechai Twer).

Title: Tzemach Tzedek begins nesius in Lubavitch
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Mendel (the Tzemach Tzedek) began his leadership of Chabad from Lubavitch in 5588.
Story: Following the Mitteler Rebbe's passing in late 5588, the Tzemach Tzedek eventually took up the mantle of Chabad leadership in Lubavitch. His nesius would extend until 5626 (1866). Under him Lubavitch became a major center of halachic responsa and chassidic teaching.

Title: Mogilev high court forwards Senate acquittal decree to Khovansky
Summary: The First Department of the Mogilev high court sends Khovansky a copy of the Senate's decree acquitting the Mitteler Rebbe.
Story: On 11 January 1828, the First Department of the Mogilev high court (signed by Chief Judge Felix Marzhevsky and Counselor Porfiry Karpilavich) forwarded Khovansky a copy of the Senate's 28 November 1827 decree, which had reached the department on 2 January 1828. Because the Senate had sent its ruling directly to the Mogilev provincial government rather than to Khovansky (who had filed the appeal), the high court provided him with the official copy. The transmittal (no. 54) closed Khovansky's involvement in the case begun by his 18 September 1825 proposal (no. 4425).
