Title: R. Nathan Halevi of Polotzk urges Tzemach Tzedek to accept leadership
Summary: Less than three months after the Mitteler Rebbe's passing, R. Nathan Halevi Horowitz of Polotzk wrote a halachic responsum to Tzemach Tzedek hinting that he should accept the nesius.
Story: On the eve of Rosh Chodesh Adar 5588 (February 1828) R. Nathan Halevi Horowitz of Polotzk sent a halachic she'eilah to Rabbi Menachem Mendel. He closed it with the unusual chassidic phrase 'prepared to obey him, desirous of his success,' and signed using his mother's name ('Nathan Halevi son of Chayena') as one would in a pidyon-nefesh to a Rebbe. The letter was thus both a halachic query and a coded plea that Tzemach Tzedek accept the leadership of Chabad.
Tags: nathan halevi horowitz, polotzk, tzemach tzedek, succession, responsa

Title: Vitebsk treasury asks who should reimburse adjutant's travel costs
Summary: The Vitebsk treasury chamber petitions Khovansky to determine from whom to recover the 119 rubles spent on Vlasenko's mission.
Story: On 17 March 1828, following the Senate's exoneration of the Mitteler Rebbe, the Vitebsk treasury chamber wrote to Governor-General Khovansky asking how the 119 rubles 52 kopeks paid for Adjutant Vlasenko's 1825 trip to Starashele should be recovered. Since the Senate had found no one guilty, the funds would eventually have to be written off as a state expense. The exchange continued through September 1828.
Tags: vitebsk, treasury, vlasenko, expenses, mitteler rebbe

Title: Corrected translation submitted in Mitteler Rebbe fundraising probe
Summary: An accurate Russian retranslation of a disputed Hebrew passage from the Rebbe's records is submitted to the investigation committee, refuting claims of a 140,000 ruble sum.
Story: During the Rebbe's interrogation, investigators relied on a mistranslated Hebrew passage to claim he had collected roughly 140,000 rubles, of which only 35,000 had been distributed. The Rebbe insisted the translation was falsified and requested access to the original. A new accurate translation was prepared by the Rebbe's translator, the chasid Yehuda Yaffe of Kopust, who certified its accuracy alongside the Rebbe before Court Counselor Markov. The corrected text showed the disputed phrase referred to a portion of the total 35,000 rubles, not an additional sum.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, dovber schneuri, translation, yehuda yaffe, markov, fundraising, russia

Title: Compromise on EY fund distribution: Chabad gets 9/101
Summary: In 5589 a compromise was reached giving Kollel Chabad nine parts of 101 of the Ashkenazic kollels' share of Pekoam funds.
Story: The Ashkenazic kollels' portion of Pekoam funds was divided into 101 equal parts, of which Kollel Chabad received 9 parts. This 5589 compromise remained the basis for Chabad's share even after the later HoD kollel was carved out in 5597, with Chabad still receiving 9/101 of the reduced Ashkenazic share.
Tags: pekoam, kollel chabad, distribution, compromise, kollelim

Title: Death of R' Yisrael ben Yitzchak Yaffe of Kapust
Summary: R' Yisrael ben Yitzchak Yaffe, founding settler of the Chabad community in Hebron, passed away before Shvat 5589.
Story: R' Yisrael ben Yitzchak Yaffe of Kapust, one of the founding settlers of the Chabad community in Hebron, passed away before Shvat 5589 (January 1829). He had served as a shadar and signatory on key documents of the community. His son R' Ephraim later succeeded him as memuneh (administrator) of the Chabad kollel in Hebron.
Tags: yisrael yaffe, hebron, passing, printer

Title: First Haggadah printed in Warsaw
Summary: The first Haggadah ever printed in Warsaw appeared in 5589 with the commentary Birkat HaShir.
Story: In 5589 (1829), the first Haggadah in Warsaw was printed with the commentary Birkat HaShir by Rabbi Aryeh Leib Zintz, issued from the press of Avigdor ben Yoel Lebensohn. Warsaw would later become one of the major centers of Hebrew printing in the world.
Tags: haggadah, warsaw, poland

Title: R' Yitzchak Yaakov accepted as additional rabbi in Romny
Summary: R' Yitzchak Yaakov ben Moshe was received as a second rabbi in the Chassidic town of Romny.
Story: Romny, a Chassidic town in the Poltava region near Haditch (burial place of the Alter Rebbe), already had R' Menachem Nachum as rabbi when R' Yitzchak Yaakov was added in 5589. He would later correspond with the Tzemach Tzedek on halachic matters.
Tags: yitzchak yaakov, romny, ukraine, rabbinate, chabad

Title: New Italy/Spain shadarus compromise in Hebron
Summary: A new compromise on shadar missions to Italy and Spain between Hebron's Chabad and Sephardic communities took effect on Rosh Chodesh Elul 1829.
Story: On Rosh Chodesh Elul 1829 (ר"ח אלול תקפ"ט), a new compromise between the Chabad and Sephardic communities in Hebron came into effect regarding shadar missions to Italy and Spain. This compromise resolved disputes that had not been settled in the first 1825 agreement.
Tags: hebron, italy, spain, shadar, sephardim, chabad kollel

Title: Tzemach Tzedek still refusing to accept pidyonot
Summary: As late as Tishrei 5590 Tzemach Tzedek crossed out R. Nathan's mother's name from a responsum, signalling he was not yet receiving pidyonot.
Story: On 8 Tishrei 5590 (October 1829) R. Nathan Halevi again signed a responsum to Tzemach Tzedek with his mother's name. Tzemach Tzedek struck the word 'Chayena' from the autograph, refusing to receive the letter as a pidyon-nefesh. A few weeks later he again deleted the honorifics 'light of our eyes' and 'his servant' from another of Nathan's letters, evidence that he had not yet fully assumed the role of Rebbe.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, nathan halevi horowitz, polotzk, pidyon nefesh, succession

Title: Agreement between Chabad and Sephardic communities in Hebron
Summary: In 5590 a formal agreement was concluded between the Chabad and Sephardic communities in Hebron, signed by R' Shimon Shmerling among others.
Story: In 5590 the two communities in Hebron - Chabad and Sephardic - reached a formal agreement, signed by R' Shimon Shmerling. The agreement governed the relationship between the two settlements at a time when both shared the burden of protection payments to the local ruler Abd al-Rahman.
Tags: hebron, shimon shmerling, sephardim, agreement, kollelim

Title: EY support sent via R' Ephraim Yitzchak Epstein
Summary: In 5590 support funds were sent to Eretz Yisrael through R' Ephraim Yitzchak Epstein and his son-in-law R' Yosef Yehuda Leib of Shiof.
Story: The 5590 receipt records that the support funds for Eretz Yisrael were transmitted through R' Ephraim Yitzchak Epstein and his son-in-law R' Yosef Yehuda Leib ben R' Chaim of Shiof. According to the 5599 Montefiore census, both immigrated to Eretz Yisrael themselves in 5590 - two years after the Mitteler Rebbe's passing.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, ephraim yitzchak epstein, yosef yehuda leib, shiof, eretz yisrael fund

Title: First Chabad-Sephardi agreement in Hebron
Summary: The Chabad and Sephardi communities of Hebron signed an agreement in 5590 addressing the heavy protection-money demands of Sheikh Abdul Rahman.
Story: In 5590 the two Jewish communities of Hebron, Chabad and Sephardi, formalized an inter-communal agreement signed by R' Shmuel Halevi among others. The agreement documents the exorbitant 'protection' payments demanded by Sheikh Abdul Rahman, the local ruler known as 'the Black Rabbi.' This was the first of several such accords as the communities tried to share the burden imposed by the local strongman.
Tags: hebron, chabad, sephardim, abdul rahman, protection money

Title: Hebron agreement: shdarus to Italy, Sephard, and Persia
Summary: Sephardic and Chabad communities of Hebron formalized joint shdarus arrangements for Italy, Persia, and Sephardic lands.
Story: In 5590 (1830), the Sephardic and Chabad communities of Hebron signed a detailed agreement governing joint shdarus operations to Italy ('Frankia'), Persia ('Urmili and Arabistan'), and other lands. Italy's proceeds were to be divided 80% to Sephardim and 20% to Ashkenazim, while collections from Sephardic and Persian cities, fundraised by Ashkenazi shadarim, would be divided three-quarters to Ashkenazim and one-quarter to Sephardim. This agreement formalized cooperation alongside the Pekuam's centralized fundraising in Amsterdam.
Tags: hebron, sephardic kollel, chabad kollel, shadarim, italy, persia

Title: Hebron Ashkenazi and Sephardic communities sign formal agreement
Summary: The two communities of Hebron sign a formal agreement, with R' Leib Chitrik among the Ashkenazi signatories.
Story: In 1830 the Sephardic and Ashkenazi communities of Hebron concluded a formal accord governing communal matters. R' Leib Chitrik, a senior trustee of Kolel Chabad, was one of the Ashkenazi signatories. The agreement was one of several inter-community arrangements that shaped Hebron's Jewish life in the 19th century.
Tags: hebron, ashkenazi, sephardi, kolel chabad

Title: Hebron Chabad-Sephardic agreement signed
Summary: In 5590 an agreement was signed between the Chabad community and the Sephardic community in Hebron.
Story: Among the Chabad signatories were R' Moshe Meizlish, joined by R' Shmuel Segal, R' Yehuda Leib Sener, and others — without R' Tzvi Hirsh Lifshitz or R' Ephraim Yaffe of the original 5587 trio. The agreement allocated a quarter of all Chabad collections in Sephardic regions to the Hebron Sephardic community.
Tags: hebron, sephardim, agreement, kollel chabad

Title: R' Yosef Halevi appointed assistant gabbai in Hebron
Summary: R' Yosef Halevi was appointed as assistant and successor to his father R' Chaim Halevi as Hebron's gabbai.
Story: In 5590 (1830), after R' Chaim Yaakov Halevi ibn Yakar's 42 years of service as gabbai and pakid of the Hebron community, his son R' Yosef Halevi was appointed as his deputy and successor. The appointment was described as 'a sign of trust and honor' to the elder Halevi. R' Chaim Halevi was the first signatory on the 5590 inter-community agreement.
Tags: yosef halevi, chaim halevi, hebron, sephardic kollel

Title: R' Yosef Yehuda Leib m'Shyuf and R' Ephraim Yitzchak Epstein make aliyah from Shklov
Summary: R' Yosef Yehuda Leib m'Shyuf and his father-in-law R' Ephraim Yitzchak Epstein made aliyah from Shklov to settle in Chevron in 5590.
Story: In 5590, R' Ephraim Yitzchak Epstein traveled from Shklov to Chevron with his wife, son Zalman, daughter, son-in-law R' Yosef Yehuda Leib m'Shyuf, and their four-year-old son Yaakov Zevulun. Hearing of their journey, the Tzemach Tzedek entrusted them to deliver the Russian Chabad support funds to the Chevron community. They arrived in Kislev 5591 after road troubles delayed them past Rosh Hashanah.
Tags: yosef yehuda leib, ephraim yitzchak epstein, shklov, chevron, aliyah

Title: Second Chabad–Sephardic Hebron agreement lowers payment
Summary: A revised agreement in 5590 reduces Chabad's annual contribution to the Sephardic kollel from 1,000 to 900 grush.
Story: Chabad argued that since they also paid Sheikh Abdul Rahman one riyal every Rosh Chodesh and additional gifts at weddings and at the arrival of emissaries, those sums should count toward shared protection payments. The 5590 agreement reduced their annual obligation to 900 grush, paid each year upon the ship's arrival to the head pakid R' Chaim HaLevi. The agreement explicitly named Sheikh Abdul Rahman as 'sar ha'ir' (ruler of the city).
Tags: hebron, chabad, sephardim, kollel, abdul rahman, chaim halevi

Title: Tzemach Tzedek travels to Rogachev, Zhuravichi and Dribin
Summary: In the winter of 5590 (1829–1830) the Tzemach Tzedek traveled to the towns of Rogachev, Zhuravichi and Dribin to deliver Chassidic discourses.
Story: Although the Tzemach Tzedek generally remained in Lyubavichi writing Chassidus, he periodically traveled to outlying towns to deliver maamarim publicly and to receive Chassidim in yechidus. This particular winter tour is reconstructed from headings on his maamarim, which routinely recorded the date and place of delivery. The journey is among the earliest documented in the registry of his discourses.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, russia, travel, rogachev, zhuravichi, dribin

Title: Second Chabad-Sephardic agreement in Hebron
Summary: The second formal agreement between Hebron's Chabad and Sephardic communities was concluded in Elul 1830.
Story: In Elul 1830 (אלול תק"צ), the Chabad and Sephardic communities of Hebron concluded their second formal agreement. It specifically covered shadar missions to Germany, Italy, Spain, and neighboring countries, building on the earlier 1825 understanding.
Tags: hebron, sephardim, chabad kollel, agreement, italy, germany, spain

Title: Russian Chabad support funds arrive in Chevron
Summary: The Russian Chabad support funds for 5590 reached Chevron in Kislev 5591, carried by R' Ephraim Yitzchak Epstein and R' Yosef Yehuda Leib m'Shyuf.
Story: Originally expected by Rosh Hashanah 5591, the emissaries were delayed and arrived in Chevron only in Kislev 5591. A 14 Kislev 5591 letter from the Chevron Chabad community thanked the Tzemach Tzedek for arranging the early dispatch despite the late delivery. The same letter records that 'the road went wrong and an hour of emergency caused them to be delayed.'
Tags: chevron, kolel chabad, tzemach tzedek, support funds

Title: Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch reissued in Sudilkov
Summary: Another full edition of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch appeared in Sudilkov in 1831.
Story: By the early 1830s the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch was well-established across White Russia and Poland, prompting repeated reprints such as this 5591 (1831) Sudilkov edition.
Tags: alter rebbe, sudilkov, shulchan aruch

Title: Hebron Chabad letter to the Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: In 5591 Hebron's Chabad leaders wrote to the Tzemach Tzedek acknowledging support funds, with R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin signing last as the youngest at 29.
Story: The letter from Hebron Chabad leaders confirmed receipt of support funds sent by the third Lubavitcher Rebbe. R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, who would later become Hebron's Chabad rav, signed last as the youngest of the signers and identified himself as 'son of R' Moshe shochet,' showing his trade was shechita while he was also active in community affairs.
Tags: hebron, lubavitch, tzemach tzedek, shimon menashe chaikin

Title: Letter to Tzemach Tzedek signed by R' Shimon Shmerling
Summary: In 5591 R' Shimon Shmerling was a signatory on a letter from the Chabad community in Hebron to the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: R' Shimon Shmerling, one of the founders of the Chabad community in Hebron, signed the 5591 letter from Hebron to the Tzemach Tzedek. This was part of regular correspondence between the Hebron community and the Lubavitcher leadership in Russia, reporting on the situation and requesting continued support.
Tags: shimon shmerling, tzemach tzedek, hebron, kollel chabad

Title: Muhammad Ali sends Ibrahim Pasha to conquer Eretz Yisrael and Syria
Summary: In 5591 the Egyptian ruler Muhammad Ali sent his son Ibrahim Pasha to conquer Eretz Yisrael and Syria.
Story: In 5591 Muhammad Ali of Egypt dispatched his son Ibrahim Pasha to conquer Eretz Yisrael and Syria. Ibrahim Pasha conducted a successful military campaign and became the general governor of the conquered territory from 5593 until 5600, profoundly affecting the Jewish communities under his rule.
Tags: muhammad ali, ibrahim pasha, egypt, conquest, eretz yisrael, syria

Title: Tzemach Tzedek defends R. Yissachar Ber against removal in Bychov Chadash
Summary: In 5591 townspeople of Bychov Chadash sought to replace R. Yissachar Ber, and the Tzemach Tzedek issued a sharp responsum defending him.
Story: In 5591 (1831) residents of Bychov Chadash attempted to install a new moreh tzedek in place of R. Yissachar Ber after they brought in a relative for the position. The Tzemach Tzedek responded with a stern ruling (Yoreh Deah 343) that custom across Israel held a moreh tzedek's appointment to be permanent and that it was absolutely forbidden to remove a qualified scholar without cause. Despite this, R. Yissachar Ber left for Lubavitch within two years.
Tags: yissachar ber horowitz, tzemach tzedek, bychov chadash, rabbinate dispute

Title: Tzemach Tzedek travels to Bobruisk, Paritch and Rogachev
Summary: In the winter of 5591 (1830–1831) the Tzemach Tzedek visited the towns of Bobruisk, Paritch and Rogachev.
Story: Reconstructed from the headings of his Chassidic discourses, this winter tour brought the Tzemach Tzedek to important Chassidic centers in White Russia. Such trips combined public maamarim, private yechidus, and the strengthening of local Chassidic communities. The journey is documented in the chronological registry of his maamarim.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, russia, travel, bobruisk, paritch, rogachev

Title: Volume 13 of Tzemach Tzedek responsa bound
Summary: Volume 13, manuscript 1019 — a book of summaries of earlier responsa — was bound around 5591.
Story: Manuscript 1019 (volume 13) is a survivor of the early numbered series. It contains short summaries of responsa written in earlier volumes, citing them as chelek 1, 2, 3, 4, etc. Although undated internally, the responsa it digests can be matched to known dates, placing its compilation around 5590–5591.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, responsa, manuscript 1019, summaries

Title: Aliyah of R. Yaakov Mordechai Twer and family to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: In 5592 (1832) R. Yaakov Mordechai Twer made aliyah from Mogilev with his sons Shaul, Yisrael and Leib, settling in Hebron's Chabad community.
Story: Aged 38 at the time of aliyah, R. Yaakov Mordechai descended from MaHaRIL, the brother of the Alter Rebbe. His family became the root of the Brimat, Saulson, Singer, and Grossman families in the Holy Land; his eldest son R. Schneur Zalman remained behind in Mogilev and later emigrated separately.
Tags: yaakov mordechai twer, aliyah, hebron, chabad, eretz yisrael, mogilev

Title: R' Menachem Aryeh arrives in Hebron from Rohatchov
Summary: R' Menachem Aryeh, son of R' Shmuel Halevi, immigrated to the Holy Land from Rohatchov together with his 16-year-old son R' Yisrael Yosef.
Story: According to the 1839 Hebron census, R' Menachem Aryeh (also called Nachum Aryeh Leib) made aliyah from Rohatchov in 5592 (1832) at age 40. He came together with his already-married 16-year-old son R' Yisrael Yosef. He later served as administrator of the Chabad kollel, dayan, and head of yeshiva, signing the 1834 Tzemach Tzedek correspondence and other communal documents.
Tags: hebron, chabad, rohatchov, aliyah, kollel

Title: R. Issachar Ber Hurwitz appointed Rav of Lubavitch
Summary: R. Issachar Ber HaLevi Hurwitz served as Rav of Lubavitch from 5592 to 5603 (1832-1843), working closely with the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: From 5592 to 5603 (1832-1843), R. Issachar Ber HaLevi Hurwitz held the rabbinate of Lubavitch. He maintained close halachic contact with the Tzemach Tzedek, frequently routing inquiries to him and binding the resulting responsa into volumes preserved in the library.
Tags: lubavitch, issachar ber hurwitz, rabbinate, tzemach tzedek

Title: Rabbi Yissachar Ber Halevi Horowitz appointed Rabbi of Lubavitch
Summary: Rabbi Yissachar Ber Halevi Horowitz began serving as Rabbi of the town of Lubavitch in 5592.
Story: Horowitz served as town rabbi during much of the Tzemach Tzedek's leadership era. He was followed in the position by Rabbi Avraham son of Avigdor Hakohen. These local rabbinic appointments operated alongside the Chabad leadership presence in the town's main courtyard.
Tags: rabbinic-appointment, horowitz

Title: Rabbi Yissachar Ber Hurwitz appointed rabbi of Lubavitch
Summary: From 5592 Rabbi Yissachar Ber Halevi Hurwitz served as the town rabbi of Lubavitch.
Story: He held the post throughout most of the Tzemach Tzedek's tenure, and was later succeeded by Rabbi Avraham son of Avigdor HaKohen. The town rabbinate was distinct from the Rebbe's role; the Tzemach Tzedek himself was never the salaried communal rabbi of Lubavitch.
Tags: lubavitch, rabbinate, yissachar ber hurwitz

Title: Responsum 353 with conditional psak formula
Summary: In responsum §353, written in 5592, the Tzemach Tzedek refuses to rule alone on a serious matter and demands two or three other prominent poskim concur.
Story: The Tzemach Tzedek wrote in §353 (5592) that 'because of the gravity of the matter, I do not want anyone to rely on me alone, but only with the concurrence of two famous poskim or at least one famous moreh hora'ah, and if [the case develops further], then... it appears to me to permit her, if three great poskim concur.' The responsum is a paradigmatic illustration of his halachic humility, the dominant feature of his style.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, humility, psak halacha, co-decisors

Title: Tzemach Tzedek travels to Ula, Polotsk, Ushatch and Chashniki
Summary: In the winter of 5592 (1831–1832) the Tzemach Tzedek made a circuit through Ula, Polotsk, Ushatch and Chashniki.
Story: This northern circuit of the Tzemach Tzedek is recorded in the maamarim he delivered along the way, which were dated and inscribed with their location of delivery. The trip extended his presence into Vitebsk-region towns and helped consolidate Chabad influence in the area. The journey appears in the chronological registry of his discourses.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, russia, travel, polotsk, ula, ushatch, chashniki

Title: R' Tzvi Hirsh Lehrin notifies Hebron Chabad of Mindel's London oil endowment
Summary: On 18 Elul 5592 the head of the Amsterdam Pekuam wrote to Hebron Chabad about Mrs. Mindel's 25-pound permanent fund for synagogue oil, secured through R' Asher ben Shimshon of London.
Story: R' Tzvi Hirsh Lehrin, who headed the Pekidim and Amarkalim in Amsterdam, informed the Hebron Chabad leadership of a new fund obtained through his London trip that summer. Mrs. Mindel daughter of Yehudah of London consecrated 25 pounds as keren kayemet whose interest would purchase oil for lamps in the community's synagogue and beit midrash. The arrangement was made through R' Asher ben Shimshon, a regular benefactor of Hebron Chabad.
Tags: hebron, london, pekuam, asher ben shimshon, mindel, synagogue, oil, amsterdam

Title: Pekuam letter to Hebron Chabad leaders praising unity
Summary: The Pekuam committee wrote to Hebron's Chabad leaders expressing satisfaction at the renewed peace with the Sephardic pakid.
Story: On 18 Elul 5592 (September 14, 1832), the Pekuam Amsterdam committee wrote to the rabbis and administrators of the Chabad kollel in Hebron. They expressed great satisfaction with a recent letter announcing peace and unity between Chabad and the Sephardic pakid R' Chaim Yaakov Halevi ibn Yakar. The letter was published in Bezalel Landau's Kerem HaChasidut.
Tags: pekuam, hebron, chabad kollel, sephardic kollel, letter, unity

Title: Aliyah of R' Yisrael ben Mordechai from Shklov to Hebron
Summary: R' Yisrael ben Mordechai made aliyah from Shklov to join his father in Hebron.
Story: In 5593 (1833), R' Yisrael ben Mordechai, age 25 and married with a son and daughter, made aliyah from Shklov to Hebron. His father R' Mordechai had preceded him by two years, arriving in 5581. This R' Yisrael Yaffe of Shklov is the third Hebron-based figure of that name in the period.
Tags: yisrael yaffe, shklov, hebron, aliyah

Title: Founding of Chevrat Trumat HaKodesh in USA
Summary: Chevrat Trumat HaKodesh was founded in the United States, on the model of the Amsterdam Pekuam.
Story: In early 5593 (1833), the Chevrat Trumat HaKodesh society was established in the United States, modeled on the Amsterdam Pekuam. Like its European counterpart, it sought to consolidate American Eretz Yisrael fundraising and discourage independent shadarim, withholding allocations from communities that hosted unauthorized envoys. The organization later interacted closely with the Pekuam and the Hebron Chabad kollel.
Tags: chevrat trumat hakodesh, usa, fundraising, pekuam, shadarim

Title: Ibrahim Pasha becomes governor of Eretz Yisrael
Summary: From 5593 Ibrahim Pasha served as governor general of Eretz Yisrael and Syria under Egyptian rule.
Story: Following the successful conquest, from 5593 until 5600 Ibrahim Pasha served as the general governor of the territory conquered by Egypt. His rule brought significant changes to the Jewish communities of Eretz Yisrael, though it would later be marred by the violent suppression of local rebellions including the events of 5594 in Hebron.
Tags: ibrahim pasha, egypt, eretz yisrael, governance

Title: R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz appointed moreh tzedek of Lubavitch
Summary: In 5593 R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz took up the rabbinical post in Lubavitch, where he served for ten years.
Story: After leaving Bychov Chadash in 5593 (1833), R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz established his residence in Lubavitch as the town's moreh tzedek. He served there for a decade alongside the Tzemach Tzedek, engaging in extensive halachic correspondence with the Rebbe and serving as a conduit for questions from rabbis throughout the region. Many of these responsa have since been published in Kovetz Yagdil Torah.
Tags: yissachar ber horowitz, lubavitch, rabbinate

Title: Tzemach Tzedek travels to Shklov and Tzarei
Summary: In the winter of 5593 (1832–1833) the Tzemach Tzedek visited Shklov and Tzarei.
Story: Shklov was historically a stronghold of the Misnagdic camp, making the Rebbe's visit there significant for Chabad–Misnagdic relations. The trip is documented through the dated headings of maamarim he delivered in those towns. It forms part of the chronological registry of his discourses reconstructed from manuscript sources.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, russia, travel, shklov, tzarei

Title: Volume 14 of Tzemach Tzedek responsa bound
Summary: Volume 14 was bound around 5593 and is lost; later manuscripts repeatedly reference it.
Story: Volume 14 contained a published responsum (Even HaEzer §48) explicitly written in 5593, and manuscripts 1050 and 1021 cite it repeatedly with notes such as 'copied here with corrections from chelek 14.' The volume itself, along with most of the volumes numbered 1–14, did not reach us — many believed lost in a fire in Lubavitch.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, responsa, lost manuscripts

Title: Abd al-Rahman rebellion against Egyptian rule
Summary: In early summer 5594 the local ruler Abd al-Rahman of Hebron rebelled against Ibrahim Pasha, prompting an Egyptian military response.
Story: In early summer 5594 Abd al-Rahman, the local ruler of Hebron who had previously collected protection money from both the Sephardic and Chabad communities, rebelled against Ibrahim Pasha. In Tammuz, Ibrahim Pasha brought his army to crush the rebellion - with catastrophic consequences for the Jewish communities of Hebron.
Tags: abd al-rahman, ibrahim pasha, hebron, rebellion, egypt

Title: Birth of Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn, the Rebbe Maharash
Summary: The Rebbe Maharash, fourth Lubavitcher Rebbe, was born in 1834.
Story: The Maharash was known for his sharp intellect and the saying 'lechatchila ariber,' urging chasidim to overcome obstacles from above. He led Chabad during the Industrial Revolution and times of growing Jewish migration.
Tags: maharash, shmuel schneersohn

Title: Birth of Rebbe Maharash (Rabbi Shmuel) in Lubavitch
Summary: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn, the future fourth Chabad Rebbe known as the Maharash, was born on 2 Iyar 5594 in Lubavitch.
Story: The Maharash is the only Chabad Rebbe to have been born, lived his entire life, and passed away in Lubavitch. He would assume Chabad leadership in 5626 following the passing of his father the Tzemach Tzedek. His birth in the town further entrenched Lubavitch as the dynastic seat of the movement.
Tags: maharash, shmuel, schneersohn

Title: Hebron Chabad community letters and shadarut documents
Summary: In 5594 the leaders of the Hebron Chabad community signed letters to the Tzemach Tzedek and shadarut commissions for fundraising abroad.
Story: During 5594 (1834) R' Shmuel Halevi and his son R' Menachem Aryeh signed multiple official Hebron Chabad documents, including correspondence to the Tzemach Tzedek and credentials for emissaries (shadarim) sent to raise funds abroad. These documents form the earliest preserved record of the community's institutional activity, reflecting the burdens of supporting the Hebron yishuv under Sheikh Abdul Rahman's exactions.
Tags: hebron, chabad, tzemach tzedek, shadarut, fundraising

Title: Manuscript of Alter Rebbe's discourses copied by Zalman Leib of Liubavitch
Summary: In 5594 (1834), Zalman Leib b. R' Yid of Liubavitch-Riskin copied a major manuscript of the Alter Rebbe's discourses arranged by Torah portion.
Story: The manuscript (Ms. 633) is notable for its careful headings identifying the dates and circumstances when each discourse was delivered, including maamarim from as early as 5554 (1794). It represents a serious early effort to catalog the chronology of Chabad maamarim.
Tags: manuscript, liubavitch, alter rebbe, zalman leib riskin

Title: R' Natan Amram appointed joint shadar to Italy and Europe
Summary: R' Natan Amram, later rabbi of Alexandria, was appointed as a joint shadar from Hebron's Sephardic and Chabad communities to Italy and Europe.
Story: In Nissan 5594 (1834), R' Natan Amram — later rabbi of Alexandria, Egypt — was designated to travel as a joint shadar from the Sephardic and Chabad communities of Hebron through Italy and surrounding European countries. His departure was delayed by the pogroms and earthquake, and his mission was expanded. The expanded shlichut letter, signed primarily by Chabad leaders, was preserved in Sarid V'Palit.

Title: Senate rejects most of Khovansky's proposed reforms on Jewish status
Summary: In winter 5594, the Senate informs Khovansky that it has rejected most of his proposals regarding the legal status of Russian Jewry, accepting only a few details.
Story: In the winter of 1834 (5594), after years of delay, the Senate responded to Governor Khovansky's policy proposals that had been attached to his 1827 appeal in the Mittler Rebbe's case. The Senate decided to reject most of his suggestions concerning the status and rights of rabbis and Jewish communities, accepting only a few minor points, while informing him that a comprehensive new statute on Jews was already being prepared.
Tags: senate, khovansky, russia, jewish status, legislation

Title: Tzemach Tzedek purchases land for his Lubavitch courtyard
Summary: Around 5594 the Tzemach Tzedek bought the plot of land in Lubavitch on which he built his home.
Story: The parcel later became the site of the great Tomchei Temimim study hall. His first house stood at the northwestern corner of the courtyard with the synagogue beside it; both were destroyed in the great fire of 1856-1858, after which a much larger compound was rebuilt.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, lubavitch, courtyard

Title: Petersburg Senate replies to Khovansky on rabbinic authority
Summary: The Governing Senate told provincial authorities to enforce existing 1804 statutes against unregulated rabbinic donations and civil adjudication.
Story: On 25 January 1834 (27 Shvat 5594), the Governing Senate in Petersburg responded to Governor-General Khovansky's three recommendations on rabbis. The first — that rabbinic pay require provincial approval — was deferred to the comprehensive Jewish statute then in deliberation at the State Council, citing an 1828 prohibition on new Jewish laws until the general code was complete. The second and third — barring extra donations to rabbis and barring them from civil adjudication — were not enacted as new law but issued as administrative directives to enforce Sections 49, 51, and 52 of the 1804 Jewish Constitution.
Tags: russia, petersburg, senate, khovansky, rabbis, jewish-law, 1804-statute

Title: Senate responds to Khovansky on rabbinic appointments
Summary: The Senate replied to Khovansky's recommendations regarding the appointment of rabbis, closing out the long arc of his anti-Chassidic initiatives.
Story: Seven years after the Rebbe's acquittal, the Senate addressed Khovansky's lingering proposals about regulating rabbinic appointments. The Mogilev high court forwarded copies of his recommendations to the Senate in February, and Khovansky relayed the response to the Mogilev provincial government. The exchange marks a final administrative coda to the policy program Kissin's denunciations had originally tried to advance.
Tags: senate, khovansky, rabbinate, russia

Title: Mohilev High Court relays Senate recommendations on rabbinic conduct
Summary: The Mohilev High Court forwards to Khovansky its 1827 recommendations to the Senate on illegal fundraising by Rabbi DovBer Schneuri and the proper role of rabbis.
Story: Seven years after Khovansky submitted his original recommendations to the Senate, the Mohilev High Court's criminal division relayed a copy back to him. The document recommended dismissing the Mitteler Rebbe from his rabbinic post since he could not read or write Russian, Polish, or German as required by section 10 of the Jewish statute. It further proposed barring rabbis from organizing fundraising drives and from adjudicating civil disputes between Jews, restricting them to compensation set under provincial supervision.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, russia, senate, rabbinic authority, tsarist law, fundraising ban, mohilev

Title: Senate ban on rabbinic fundraising and civil arbitration relayed
Summary: Khovansky transmits to the Mohilev and Vitebsk governments the Senate's order forbidding rabbis from collecting voluntary donations or adjudicating civil disputes.
Story: Acting on Khovansky's 1827 recommendation, the Senate had referred the matter to the Minister of the Interior, who cited an 1828 directive forbidding new specific laws about Jews until the general Jewish statute was finalized. Instead, the minister called for strict enforcement of the existing 1804 statute's sections 49, 51, and 52. The Senate adopted this view in late January 1834, instructing Khovansky to notify Jews of Mohilev and Vitebsk that they must not donate to rabbis or use rabbis to settle civil disputes, but instead refer such matters to the established courts.
Tags: russia, senate, rabbinic authority, fundraising ban, civil arbitration, mohilev, vitebsk, khovansky

Title: Birth of Rebbe Maharash in Lubavitch
Summary: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn, the fourth Chabad Rebbe (Maharash), was born in Lubavitch on 2 Iyar 5594.
Story: Rabbi Shmuel was the youngest son of the Tzemach Tzedek and would become the only Chabad Rebbe born, living his entire life, and passing away in Lubavitch. His birth on 2 Iyar 5594 (1834) coincides with the day Chasidim later mark as a special date connected to him. He would later succeed his father as the fourth Rebbe of the Chabad-Lubavitch dynasty.
Tags: maharash, lubavitch, russia, birth, schneersohn

Title: Earthquake in Hebron
Summary: On 16 Iyar 5594 a major earthquake struck Hebron, collapsing many houses in the Jewish courtyard and forcing residents to flee to the fields for a week.
Story: On Sunday 16 Iyar 5594 a great earthquake shook Hebron, collapsing several homes in the Jewish courtyard. The Jews fled their dwellings and stayed for a full week in the fields among armed Arabs - 'like sheep among wolves' - while aftershocks continued every hour. Lesser tremors continued for about four weeks afterward, leaving the community traumatized.
Tags: hebron, earthquake, natural disaster, jewish community

Title: Hebron Arab rebellion against Egyptian forces, Jews killed
Summary: On 9 Iyar 5594 the Arabs of Hebron and surrounding villages rebelled against the Egyptian commander, killing several Chabad chassidim.
Story: On Sunday 9 Iyar 5594 the Arabs of Hebron and surrounding villages rebelled against the Egyptian deputy commander stationed there. Several Chabad chassidim were killed in the attack, while about 400 others were trapped inside the citadel (kala) for weeks until starvation forced their surrender. The community endured constant threats of being burned alive and was saved only through massive ransom payments demanded by local officials.
Tags: hebron, rebellion, violence, kollel chabad, jewish casualties

Title: Arab revolt against Egyptian deputy reaches Hebron Jews
Summary: On 9 Iyar the Arabs of the Hebron region rebel against the Egyptian deputy ruler, putting the local Jews in mortal danger.
Story: On Sunday 9 Iyar the Arabs of the Hebron region rebelled against the deputy of the king. For weeks they threatened the Jews of Hebron with cruel and unusual deaths. Only the intervention of certain notables saved the community from immediate harm during this initial period of unrest.
Tags: hebron, ibrahim pasha, peasants revolt, egyptian rule, arab revolt

Title: Earthquake strikes Hebron
Summary: On 16 Iyar an earthquake collapses walls in Hebron's Jewish quarter, forcing residents to flee to open fields.
Story: On Sunday 16 Iyar an earthquake struck Hebron, collapsing several walls in the Jewish courtyard. Residents abandoned their dwellings and fled, spending seven days and nights in the open fields in great fear. They returned to the city only when the immediate danger passed, awaiting the arrival of Ibrahim Pasha's forces — which would bring far worse violence within weeks.
Tags: hebron, earthquake, natural disaster, jewish quarter

Title: Pogroms during the Peasants' Revolt against Hebron's Jewish community
Summary: Arab rebels rose against Hebron and threatened the Jewish community with daily violence on 9 Iyar.
Story: On 9 Iyar 5594 (May 17, 1834), Arabs in Hebron rebelled against the regional ruler, and for many days threatened the Jewish community with cruel deaths. R' Chaim Halevi, the pakid, used his standing with local nobles and significant payments to secure their protection. The pogroms were followed by an earthquake, both of which were described in a fundraising letter signed by the Chabad kollel leaders sent with shadar R' Natan Amram.
Tags: hebron, pogrom, peasants revolt, 1834, natan amram, chaim halevi

Title: Ibrahim Pasha sacks Hebron - massacre and desecration
Summary: On 28 Tammuz 5594 Ibrahim Pasha's army entered Hebron, conducting a brutal sack with killings, rapes, desecration of Torah scrolls and destruction of homes.
Story: On Monday 28 Tammuz 5594 the deputy commander arrived with his army and conquered Hebron. Despite Jewish hopes, the soldiers were given license to plunder. Homes were burned and ransacked for hidden treasures; oil was spilled and vessels shattered. Many women were violated and Torah scrolls were burned, torn, and spread on the ground with Torah scrolls rolled in blood. Two women, a child by the mikveh, and Sephardic sages were killed.
Tags: ibrahim pasha, hebron, massacre, rape, torah desecration, egypt, kollel chabad

Title: Pogroms and earthquake strike Hebron
Summary: Hebron suffered pogroms and an earthquake in summer 1834, prompting urgent appeals from the Chabad community.
Story: In summer 1834 (קיץ תקצ"ד), pogroms and an earthquake devastated Hebron. The Chabad community wrote desperate letters to their supporters abroad, which the Pekidim u'Amarkalim of Amsterdam later reproduced in printed circulars to encourage greater donations.
Tags: hebron, earthquake, pogroms, chabad kollel, disaster

Title: Hebron Chabad community letter to Tzemach Tzedek on Hebron events
Summary: On 8 Elul 5594 the heads of the Chabad community in Hebron wrote to the Tzemach Tzedek describing the year's catastrophes and pleading for emergency aid.
Story: Following the earthquake, the rebellion, and the brutal sack of Hebron, on 8 Elul 5594 the community leaders - R' Chaim Avraham (son of the Alter Rebbe) and R' Nachum (son of the Mitteler Rebbe) - wrote to the Tzemach Tzedek detailing the year's horrors. They begged him to publicize their suffering, noting that prices had tripled and they were borrowing food and money at interest to keep starving Jews alive.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, hebron, chaim avraham, nachum schneuri, ibrahim pasha, appeal for aid

Title: Ibrahim Pasha's army sacks Hebron's Jewish community
Summary: On 28 Tammuz the Egyptian deputy enters Hebron with his army and his soldiers loot, rape, and murder Jews.
Story: On Monday 28 Tammuz the deputy of the king (Ibrahim Pasha) entered Hebron with his army, having defeated the Arab rebels. The soldiers were given license to destroy: Jews were killed by sword and arrow, women were raped, Torah scrolls were torn apart and trampled, tefillin batim were smashed open in search of hidden treasure, and synagogue vessels and curtains were looted. Survivors were forced to carry the plunder on their shoulders to the army camp two hours' journey from the city.
Tags: hebron, ibrahim pasha, pogrom, massacre, egyptian rule, torah scrolls, tefillin

Title: Letter to Tzemach Tzedek from R' Shmuel of Tzfat
Summary: R' Shemayah, a Chabad chassid in Tzfat, wrote to the Tzemach Tzedek in winter 5595 about plans to relocate to Hebron.
Story: In the winter of 5595 R' Shemayah wrote to the Tzemach Tzedek explaining that after Pesach, once the rains stopped, he intended to settle in Hebron among his Chabad brethren. He noted that R' Shmuel Halevi specifically advised him to join the Hebron community. The letter is preserved in Migdal Oz and indirectly confirms R' Shmuel's role as the de facto rabbi of Hebron.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, tzfat, hebron, chabad, letter

Title: New Russian Jewish charter promulgated
Summary: A new Russian statute regulating Jewish life was published in 5595, replacing the 1805 charter.
Story: The Senate had informed Governor Khovansky that his earlier proposals for regulating the rabbinate would be subsumed under a wider planned overhaul. The 1835 charter became the legal framework under which the Tzemach Tzedek and other Russian Jewish leaders operated, including the rules that conditioned the great surveillance campaign against him in the 1840s.
Tags: russia, jewish charter, law, nicholas i

Title: New Russian statute on the Jews published
Summary: The Russian Empire publishes its new statute regulating the status of the Jews, the second such code after the 1804/5 statute.
Story: In 5595 (1835), the Russian government published a new statute on the Jews, the second comprehensive code of its kind after the original statute of 5565 (1804/5). The legislation governed key aspects of Jewish communal life, the role of rabbis, residence rights, and other matters that had been at the center of Khovansky's earlier proposals and of the legal pressures on the chassidic movement throughout the 1820s and 1830s.
Tags: russia, legislation, jewish status, nicholas i

Title: R. Leib ben Yaakov Mordechai Twer born
Summary: R. Leib, youngest son of R. Yaakov Mordechai Twer, was born in Eretz Yisrael around 1835 (5595).
Story: Recorded at age 4 in the 1839 Montefiore census of the Chabad community of Hebron, R. Leib was the first of the Twer brothers born after the family's aliyah. He too adopted the family name Brimat.
Tags: leib twer, brimat, hebron

Title: Tzemach Tzedek tours Borisov, Minsk, Korenitz, Vilna and Polotsk
Summary: In the summer of 5595 (1835) the Tzemach Tzedek made an extensive tour reaching as far as Vilna.
Story: This summer journey was unusually broad, taking the Tzemach Tzedek into Lithuania proper, including Minsk, Vilna, and Polotsk. According to the report of Captain Yurkovsky six years later, during this stay in Minsk the Rebbe delivered public sermons and explained passages from Kabbalah and the Talmud. The trip is reconstructed from the headings of his maamarim.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, russia, travel, minsk, vilna, borisov, polotsk, korenitz

Title: Tzemach Tzedek visits Vilna and delivers Chassidic discourses
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek visited Vilna, where he delivered Chassidic discourses and received people in yechidus.
Story: In the summer of 5595 (1835), the Tzemach Tzedek visited Vilna. The visit was documented by Shmuel Yosef Fuenn, a maskil of that generation, who described the Rebbe delivering a Chassidic discourse with eyes closed and an expression of awe. Fuenn recorded that the Rebbe did not raise his hand, modulate his voice, or pause, as if a holy spirit spoke from his throat.

Title: Nicholas I signs expanded Jewish charter
Summary: On 13 April 1835 (26 Nissan 5595) Tsar Nicholas I signed an expanded 'Jewish charter' replacing the 1804 law.
Story: Nicholas I's reign brought a stream of new decrees affecting Russian Jewry. A more elaborate Jewish charter was prepared during 5595 and signed on 13 April 1835. The text was printed in Hebrew that same year as 'Chok al Odot Yehudim' in Vilna and Grodno.
Tags: russia, nicholas i, jewish charter, legislation

Title: R' Eliyahu writes to Tzemach Tzedek about Romny rabbinate transition
Summary: R' Eliyahu ben Meshulam Feivish wrote to the Tzemach Tzedek explaining the controversy that forced his in-law R' Menachem Nachum to leave Romny for Chechersk.
Story: Dated 28 Nissan 5595, the letter recounts how six years of communal dispute in Romny led R' Menachem Nachum to accept a position in Chechersk. R' Eliyahu reluctantly agreed to temporarily serve as moreh tzedek in Romny until a permanent replacement could be found, and posed Pesach-related halachic questions to the Tzemach Tzedek.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, eliyahu naaman, menachem nachum, romny, chechersk, machlokes, chabad

Title: R' Natan Amram departs Hebron as shadar
Summary: R' Natan Amram left Hebron on Erev Shavuot 1835 as a shadar to Italy and Turkey on behalf of the Chabad and Sephardic communities.
Story: On the eve of Shavuot 1835 (ערב חג השבועות תקצ"ה), R' Natan Amram departed Hebron as a joint Chabad-Sephardic shadar. Although a request had been made to also include Germany, Holland, France, and England, those territories remained off-limits per the Pekidim u'Amarkalim agreement.
Tags: hebron, natan amram, shadar, italy, turkey, fundraising

Title: R' Natan Amram arrives in Livorno
Summary: R' Natan Amram arrived in Livorno at the end of Av 1835 to begin his fundraising mission in Italy and Turkey.
Story: At the end of Av 1835 (שלהי מנ"א תקצ"ה), R' Natan Amram reached Livorno, beginning a five-year shadar journey through many cities in Italy and Turkey on behalf of the Hebron Chabad community in partnership with the Sephardic kollel.
Tags: natan amram, shadar, livorno, italy, hebron

Title: Tzemach Tzedek visits Vilna
Summary: In Av 5595 the Tzemach Tzedek arrived in Vilna to teach Chassidus, receive chassidim in yechidus, and meet with the local rav R. Avraham Avli of Pasvalys.
Story: News of the visit reached the chassidim of Vilna at the end of Sivan or beginning of Tammuz. When the Rebbe arrived in Av, he delivered a public maamar in the great Ashkenazi beis medrash that drew leading mitnagdim, and he held learned discussions with R. Avraham Avli. The young maskil Shmuel Yosef Fuenn, then sixteen, attended the maamar and described it in print years later.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, vilna, 5595, av, avraham avli, yechidus

Title: R' Menachem Tzvi Hirsch visits Lubavitch seeking the Tzemach Tzedek's help
Summary: R' Menachem Tzvi Hirsch of Krutsa visited the Tzemach Tzedek in Tishrei 5596, receiving a loan, blessings, and recommendation letters.
Story: Struggling with poverty and poor health, R' Menachem Tzvi Hirsch sought guidance from the Tzemach Tzedek about finding a rabbinic position. The Rebbe lent him money to cover debts, blessed him to find a fitting position, and wrote a recommendation to R' Peretz Chen of Beshenkovichi.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, menachem tzvi hirsch, lubavitch, krutsa, rabbinate, chabad

Title: Dispute between R. Shimon Zarchi and R. Yosef Ashkenazi of Yakobstadt
Summary: In 5596 R. Yosef Ashkenazi disputed several rulings of R. Shimon Zarchi, rabbi of Yakobstadt, and both sides wrote to the Tzemach Tzedek for arbitration.
Story: R. Shimon Zarchi, author of Nachalas Shimon and rabbi of Yakobstadt, and R. Yosef Ashkenazi, author of Ohel Yosef and then a rosh metivta in Yakobstadt, clashed in 5596 over several halachic matters. They submitted their reasoning to the Tzemach Tzedek, who responded with multiple rulings adjudicating between them (Orach Chaim §§43, 75; Yoreh Deah §217; Choshen Mishpat §85).
Tags: shimon zarchi, yosef ashkenazi, yakobstadt, nachalat shimon, ohel yosef, halachic dispute

Title: Passing of Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler of Vilna
Summary: Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler, av beit din of Vilna, passed away in 5596.
Story: Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler, who served as av beit din of Vilna, passed away in 5596 (1836). He had been born in 5524 (1764) in Posval. Several volumes of his responsa and novellae written from Vilna in 5593–5594 survived in the Chabad library archives.
Tags: vilna, posveler, rabbinate

Title: R' Shlomo Kugel lives in Kiskoriene near Pleshchenitsy
Summary: In 1836 R' Shlomo Kugel lived in the village of Kiskoriene near Pleshchenitsy in the Minsk region, beginning the Chassidic presence in the area.
Story: According to a 5716 memoir by Mariasha Badana Putrefas, in 1836 (5596) a Jew named R' Shlomo Kugel lived in the village of Kiskoriene near Pleshchenitsy in the Minsk gubernia. Known as R' Shlomo Kiskoriener, his sons Hendel, Yosef and Gershon later spread Chassidut from the surrounding villages into the strongly mitnagdic town of Pleshchenitsy.
Tags: pleshchenitsy, kiskoriene, minsk, kugel family, white russia

Title: Tsarist decree shuts down Hebrew printing presses in Russia
Summary: The 1836-1837 (5597) decree of Tsar Nicholas I ordered the closure of Hebrew printing presses in Russia and inspection of existing Jewish books.
Story: Under Nicholas I, the regime moved against Jewish printing, closing presses and requiring every existing Jewish book in private hands to be inspected and stamped by an authorized rabbi-censor. The decree drove Hebrew printing — including Chabad printing — underground. Several Chabad works appeared in the following years from a clandestine press with falsified imprints.
Tags: russia, tsarist, censorship, printing, decree, nicholas-i

Title: Tzemach Tzedek tours Ukraine; visits graves of Alter Rebbe and Mitteler Rebbe
Summary: In the summer of 5596 (1836) the Tzemach Tzedek made a far-reaching tour through Ukraine, visiting the graves of his grandfather and father-in-law and attending his son's wedding.
Story: This extensive summer journey took the Tzemach Tzedek through Bayov, Shklov, Zhlobin, Bobruisk, Hlusk, Paritch, Chernigov, Nezhin (to prostrate at the grave of his father-in-law the Mitteler Rebbe), Priluk, Kremenchug, Chernobyl, Brahin, Haditch (to prostrate at the grave of his grandfather the Alter Rebbe), Panitch, and Hornostaypil (for the wedding of his son R. Yosef Yitzchak). The trip is documented through the dated headings of maamarim he delivered in each town. It is one of the most extensive recorded journeys of his nesi'us.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, russia, ukraine, travel, haditch, nezhin, chernobyl, wedding, yosef yitzchak

Title: HoD residents protest EY fund distribution
Summary: In Adar 5596 residents from Holland and Germany (HoD) protested the existing distribution arrangement, having established a separate fifth kollel in Eretz Yisrael.
Story: In Adar 5596 the HoD residents (Holland and Deutschland), having established a separate fifth kollel in Eretz Yisrael, contested the distribution arrangement. Though their immigrants were few, they argued that since most Pekoam funds came from their home countries, they deserved a larger share than per-capita allocation would yield. The dispute would persist until 5608.
Tags: hod kollel, holland, germany, pekoam, distribution dispute, kollelim

Title: R' Menachem Tzvi Hirsch writes letter from Romny rabbinate
Summary: From his new post in Romny, R' Menachem Tzvi Hirsch wrote to the Tzemach Tzedek thanking him and detailing his journey to obtain semicha and a position.
Story: Dated 7 Adar 5596, the letter recounts how R' Menachem Tzvi Hirsch travelled from Lubavitch through Beshenkovichi, Vitebsk (with R' Yitzchak Isaac), Mohilov (with R' Meir Berlin), and finally Homel where R' Yitzchak Isaac Epstein recommended him for the Romny position. He sought to repay the loan and asked for blessings for healing.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, menachem tzvi hirsch, romny, yitzchak isaac epstein, homel, vitebsk, mohilov, chabad

Title: Radal of Bichov replies to Lubavitch rabbi on get question
Summary: On 11 Av 5596, R. David Luria of Bichov sent a halachic response to R. Yissachar Ber HaLevi Horowitz, rabbi of Lubavitch.
Story: R. Yissachar Ber HaLevi Horowitz, rabbi of Lubavitch, wrote to the Radal about a get question because the Tzemach Tzedek was away from home. The Radal replied briefly on Monday 11 Menachem-Av 5596, apologizing for the haste due to fast-day weakness and asking not to be troubled with further questions, given his resolution to refrain from issuing responsa for several years. He suggested the question be put again to the Tzemach Tzedek on his return.
Tags: david luria, radal, bichov, lubavitch, yissachar ber horowitz, responsa, get

Title: Tzar's decree closes Jewish printing presses in Russia
Summary: On 5 Marcheshvan 5597 (27 October 1836), the Russian Minister of the Interior announced the Tzar's decree to inspect all Jewish books in Russia, burn suspicious ones, and close all Hebrew printing presses except two — one in Vilna and one in Zhitomir.
Story: The decree, recounted by the Rebbe Rayatz, ordered a sweeping inspection of Jewish books throughout Russia, with suspicious volumes to be burned. By Tevet 5597 all Hebrew presses in Russia were shuttered, leaving only the Romm partnership press in Vilna operating. This crippled Chasidic publishing for decades and is cited as a major reason why so few of the Tzemach Tzedek's writings were printed in his lifetime.
Tags: russia, tzarist decree, censorship, hebrew printing, vilna, zhitomir

Title: R' Leib Baal HaYisurim of Hebron dies in Tzfat
Summary: R' Leib of Hebron, known as the 'baal hayisurim' (man of sufferings), passed away in Tzfat on 15 Cheshvan 5597.
Story: R' Leib, one of the founders of the Chabad settlement in Hebron alongside R' Shimon Shmerling, moved to Tzfat late in life and died there as an old man. According to 'Shaarei Yerushalayim,' he instructed before death that anyone in distress should prostrate on his grave for aid, a practice that continued for generations. His tombstone identifies him as 'R' Leib of Hebron, baal hayisurim, died 15 Cheshvan 5597.'
Tags: hebron, tzfat, leib baal hayisurim, chabad chassidim, gravesite

Title: R' Leib Baal HaYisurin passes away in Tzfat
Summary: R' Leib Baal HaYisurin, who moved to Tzfat in his final years, died there on 15 Cheshvan 5597.
Story: R' Leib Baal HaYisurin, one of the early Chabad chassidim in the Holy Land, relocated to Tzfat in his final years. He passed away there on 15 Cheshvan 5597, only weeks before the great earthquake claimed the lives of others of the small Chabad community in the city.
Tags: tzfat, leib baal hayisurin

Title: HoD kollel begins receiving Pekoam share
Summary: From 5597 the HoD (Holland-Deutschland) immigrants in Eretz Yisrael were given their share among the kollels in the Pekoam distribution.
Story: After many had begun immigrating from Holland and Germany to settle in Eretz Yisrael, from 5597 onward the Pekidim VeAmarkalim included them in the kollel distribution. The HoD share was carved out of the existing Ashkenazic portion, gradually evolving toward the formula codified in 5610.
Tags: hod kollel, holland, germany, pekoam, distribution, kollelim

Title: Kapust press closes mid-printing of Torah Ohr
Summary: Following the Tzarist closure of Hebrew presses in Tevet 5597, the Kapust press was shut down having only completed the first volume of Torah Ohr by the Alter Rebbe.
Story: When the Russian government closed nearly all Jewish printing houses in early 5597, the Kapust press was among those shuttered. It had managed to print only the first part of Torah Ohr, the Alter Rebbe's chasidic discourses; the second volume's publication was delayed for over a decade. This loss shaped the trajectory of Chabad publishing for generations.
Tags: russia, kapust, torah ohr, alter rebbe, censorship

Title: Pogroms and earthquake devastate Tzfat
Summary: Tzfat was struck by two pogroms and a major earthquake during 5594–5598, devastating the Jewish community including the family of R' Uri of Slonim.
Story: In the disasters of 5594–5598 ('the two pillages and the earthquake'), Tzfat's Jewish population was repeatedly attacked and then struck by the Galilee earthquake of 1837. R' Uri of Slonim lost his father, three of his children, and all his property. The killing of his daughter Tzipa Leah is confirmed by the 'List of Tzfat Casualties' published years later.
Tags: tzfat, earthquake, pogrom, 1837 galilee earthquake

Title: R' Aharon Alexandrov brings Torah Or to press
Summary: Rabbi Aharon Alexandrov brought the sefer Torah Or, edited by the Tzemach Tzedek, to the printing press.
Story: In 5597 (1837), Rabbi Aharon ben Moshe Chaim Alexandrov brought the sefer Torah Or to press. This volume of the Alter Rebbe's chassidic discourses was edited and arranged for publication by the Tzemach Tzedek, who attested on the title page that the Alter Rebbe himself had reviewed and corrected many of these maamarim during his lifetime in his own hand and language.
Tags: torah or, tzemach tzedek, alter rebbe, chassidut

Title: R. Yosef Ashkenazi appointed dayan in Novi Aleksandrovsky
Summary: R. Yosef Ashkenazi, author of Ohel Yosef, was appointed dayan in Novi Aleksandrovsky in 5597.
Story: After his disputes with R. Shimon Zarchi the previous year, R. Yosef Ashkenazi was appointed in 5597 to serve as moreh tzedek in the town of Novi Aleksandrovsky, leaving his position as rosh metivta in Yakobstadt.
Tags: yosef ashkenazi, ohel yosef, novi aleksandrovsky, appointment, russia

Title: Russian decree against Hebrew presses
Summary: The Russian government issued the gezeirat hadefusim in תקצ"ז, drastically restricting Hebrew printing presses in the empire and pushing chassidic publishing to Prussian border towns.
Story: The תקצ"ז decree (gezeirat hadefusim) shuttered most Hebrew presses inside Russia. In response, Hebrew presses sprang up in Prussian towns near the Russian border — Königsberg, Johannisberg, Memel, Danzig — producing sefarim aimed primarily at the Russian Jewish market. Books were smuggled in with disguised title pages, omitting place and printer or even falsifying the year, so as to claim if seized to be old volumes legally predating the decree.
Tags: russia, censorship, tzarist, gezeirat hadefusim, hebrew printing

Title: Russian decree restricting Hebrew printing presses
Summary: In 5597 the tsarist government shut down most Jewish presses across Russia, requiring all subsequent Hebrew printing to receive a rabbinical censor's stamp.
Story: The decree triggered a wave of clandestine printing inside Russia in which presses imitated the look of older Kapust and other authentic editions, often forging both title pages and the rabbinical censor's stamp. At least five such forgeries imitating the late Kapust press were printed after this decree, four of them works of Chabad Chassidut, suggesting the underground printer was himself a Chabad chassid.
Tags: russia, censorship, printing, samizdat

Title: Russian government closes nearly all Jewish presses
Summary: In 1837 the Russian authorities shut down nearly every Jewish printing house in the empire, leaving only one operating press in Vilna.
Story: The 5597 (1837) decree halted Hebrew publishing in Russia and forced Chabad and other publishing efforts abroad—notably to Warsaw. The lone Vilna press could not keep up with demand, opening the way for the Zhitomir chassidic press a decade later.
Tags: russia, censorship, tsarist decree, vilna press

Title: Torah Or printed in Kopust
Summary: The Alter Rebbe's discourses were issued as Torah Or in Kopust in 5597 (1837), edited by the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: The Tzemach Tzedek collected and edited an anthology of his grandfather the Alter Rebbe's chassidic discourses, which was published as Torah Or in Kopust in 5597 (1837). A teshuvah preserved in manuscript 227 discusses the preparation of this volume.
Tags: kopust, torah or, alter rebbe, tzemach tzedek, chassidut

Title: Tzemach Tzedek sends Torah Or to print
Summary: In 5597 the Tzemach Tzedek sent Torah Or, the Alter Rebbe's discourses, to press.
Story: In 1837 the Tzemach Tzedek sent Torah Or to the printer, having edited his grandfather the Alter Rebbe's discourses for the volume. Printing began but was halted when government decrees closed many presses in Russia, leaving the second part unprinted at that time.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, alter rebbe, torah or

Title: Tzemach Tzedek travels to Bayov, Rogachev, Dubrovna and Smiljan
Summary: In the summer of 5597 (1837) the Tzemach Tzedek traveled to Bayov for a wedding, then on to Rogachev, Dubrovna and Smiljan.
Story: This summer journey began with a wedding in Bayov, continued through Rogachev to Dubrovna and Smiljan, and ended with a return to Dubrovna. The route is reconstructed from the dated headings of maamarim that the Rebbe delivered along the way. It exemplifies how the registry of his discourses preserves not only Torah content but also family events and biographical detail.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, russia, travel, dubrovna, rogachev, wedding, bayov, smiljan

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's Torah Or completed and printed in Kapust
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek completed editing the first volume of his grandfather's discourses—the Torah Or on Bereishit and Shemot—and printed it in Kapust in 5597 (1837).
Story: After gathering and selecting from many copies of the Alter Rebbe's discourses, the Tzemach Tzedek prepared the Torah Or volume covering Genesis and Exodus and brought it to press in Kapust in 1837. The intended second volume was delayed when Russia shut down its Jewish presses that same year.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, alter rebbe, kapust, torah or

Title: 1837 Galilee earthquake kills Chabad chassidim in Tzfat
Summary: The 24 Tevet 5597 earthquake in Tzfat killed members of the small surviving Chabad community there, including R' Shemaya and R' Lapidot Chalavna with his son.
Story: Even after most Chabad chassidim had relocated to Hebron, a handful remained in Tzfat. The catastrophic Galilee earthquake of 24 Tevet 5597 (January 1, 1837) killed several of them, including R' Shemaya and R' Lapidot Chalavna and his son Shalom Aharon. After the earthquake only a few Chabad families lingered in Tzfat for another two years.
Tags: tzfat, earthquake, 1837, shemaya, lapidot chalavna

Title: Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch reprinted in Warsaw
Summary: A Warsaw edition of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch was published between 1838 and 1840 by Rabbi Avraham Mordechai Alter, son of the Chiddushei HaRim of Gur.
Story: With Russia's Jewish presses shuttered, the Alter Rebbe's halachic code was reprinted in Warsaw during 5598–5600 (1838–1840), notably edited by a future Gerrer rebbe. The edition reflected the spread of the Alter Rebbe's halachic authority into Poland.
Tags: alter rebbe, warsaw, shulchan aruch, gur

Title: First Haggadah printed with literal German translation in Cologne
Summary: The first Haggadah with a literal German translation was printed in Cologne, including musical notation at the end.
Story: In 5598 (1838), a Haggadah with a German translation rendered word-for-word was printed in Cologne. The 91-page volume marked a milestone as the first appearance of the Haggadah with this style of vernacular German translation. Musical notation for the Seder songs was appended at the end of the work.
Tags: haggadah, german translation, cologne, germany, musical notation

Title: Montefiore barred from Me'arat Hamakhpelah
Summary: Despite the Turkish sultan's permission, local Muslim leaders blocked Sir Moses Montefiore from entering the Tomb of the Patriarchs.
Story: Judith Montefiore wrote in her memoir of the 1838 attempt that a 'turbulent throng of Mussulmans' had gathered inside the mosque and a 'raving dervish' raged at the prospect of their entry. The couple decided it would be prudent to retreat without attempting further entrance.
Tags: moses-montefiore, hebron, meorat-hamachpelah

Title: Tzemach Tzedek answers responsum to R' Aharon of Kremenchug
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek wrote a halachic responsum on Orach Chaim addressed to his cousin Rabbi Aharon of Kremenchug.
Story: On 22 Sivan 5598 (June 1838), Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneersohn — the Tzemach Tzedek — wrote a responsum on Orach Chaim, printed as siman 102 in his Shu't Tzemach Tzedek, in reply to a question from his relative Rabbi Aharon of Kremenchug. R' Aharon was a grandson of the Alter Rebbe through his daughter Freida, and was a son-in-law of both the Mitteler Rebbe and of Rebbe Nachman of Breslov.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, kremenchug, responsum, halacha, family

Title: Dr. Eliezer HaLevi sees Asher ben Shimshon's silver menorah in Hebron
Summary: On 15 Menachem Av 5598 Dr. Eliezer HaLevi recorded seeing a beautiful silver menorah donated by R' Asher Shimshon of London hanging before the Holy Ark in Hebron.
Story: Writing for 'Mevaseret Tzion' (Tobolsk 1847), Dr. Eliezer HaLevi described arriving for the afternoon prayer in Hebron and being shown an elegant silver menorah hanging before the holy ark. The inscription identified its donor as R' Asher Shimshon of London, described as a long-standing benefactor of Eretz Israel residents.
Tags: hebron, synagogue, asher ben shimshon, london, eliezer halevi

Title: Hebron census taken for Montefiore
Summary: At Moses Montefiore's request, Hebron's Jewish community took a comprehensive census of its Sephardi and Chabad populations in 5599.
Story: On Sunday during Montefiore's visit to Hebron in Tammuz 5599, the community delivered to him a census of the entire Jewish population, with Sephardim and Ashkenazi-Chabad counted separately. The census, preserved in the Montefiore Archive in London, became a primary source for the genealogy of the Hebron Chabad community. It records details of residents including R' Shmuel Halevi (age 64) and his son R' Menachem Aryeh (age 40).
Tags: hebron, montefiore, census, chabad, sephardim

Title: Max Lilienthal opens first German-style Jewish school in Riga
Summary: Adherent of the German Haskalah Max Lilienthal establishes Russia's first German-style Jewish secular school in Riga.
Story: Riga's small Jewish community invited him seeking a secular Jewish school, possibly under pressure from the Russian government. From Riga, Lilienthal attempted to transform Jewish education throughout Russia, laying groundwork for the secular orientation the Rebbe later encountered.
Tags: lilienthal, haskalah, riga, secular, enlightenment

Title: Max Lilienthal opens first German-style Jewish secular school in Riga
Summary: Max Lilienthal, an adherent of the German Haskalah, arrives in Riga and establishes the first German-style Jewish secular school in Imperial Russia.
Story: At the time, there were fewer than a thousand Jews in Riga. According to Jewish Museum director Ilja Lensky, the community wanted a secular Jewish school, possibly under Russian government pressure for a less religious education system. From that beachhead Lilienthal attempted to transform Jewish education throughout Russia, and by 1927 secular-oriented Jewish schools dominated Riga.
Tags: lilienthal, haskalah, riga, russia, germany

Title: Montefiore census records Twer family in Chabad Hebron community
Summary: The 5599 (1839) Montefiore census recorded the Twer family among the Chabad Jews of Hebron, listing R. Mordechai (45), Saul (16), Israel (11), and Leib (4).
Story: The census itself constitutes a major demographic event for the Old Yishuv, providing the most detailed snapshot of the Chabad community of Hebron in the early nineteenth century. The Twer family entries allow reconstruction of birth years, family composition, and migration date for what would become several major Chabad families.
Tags: montefiore census, hebron, chabad, 1839, twer, demographics

Title: R' Uri Ornstein leaves Tzfat for Hebron
Summary: R' Uri Ornstein, the last prominent Chabad chassid in Tzfat, moved to Hebron in 5599.
Story: R' Uri Ornstein lived in Tzfat until 5599 (1839), when he too relocated to Hebron. His departure essentially ended the Chabad presence in Tzfat for the next several decades; no Chabad chassidim are recorded there from 5600 through 5630.
Tags: tzfat, hebron, ornstein, migration

Title: Montefiore's second visit to the Holy Land begins
Summary: Sir Moses Montefiore and his entourage began their second visit to the Holy Land, lasting from late Iyar to late Tammuz 5599.
Story: Montefiore's second trip to the Holy Land lasted about two months, from the end of Iyar through the end of Tammuz 5599. The party first toured Tzfat, Tiberias, and surrounding villages. They then traveled to Jerusalem, where due to a plague and quarantine they pitched their tents on the Mount of Olives opposite the Temple Mount.
Tags: montefiore, holy land, tzfat, tiberias, jerusalem

Title: Hebron Chabad sends delegation to greet Montefiore in Jerusalem
Summary: On 28 Sivan 5599 the Hebron Chabad community received Montefiore's letter and dispatched a delegation to Jerusalem with an invitation.
Story: When Montefiore wrote from Jerusalem to the heads of the Hebron community about the purpose of his visit, the letter arrived in Hebron on 28 Sivan. That same day the Chabad community wrote a letter of invitation asking him to visit their city, sent through a special delegation of two community leaders who traveled to Jerusalem to escort him personally to Hebron.
Tags: hebron, chabad, montefiore, jerusalem, delegation

Title: Hebron delegates arrive at Montefiore's camp on Mount of Olives
Summary: On the eve of Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5599, the Hebron Chabad delegation reached Montefiore's encampment on the Mount of Olives.
Story: The Hebron delegation arrived at Montefiore's camp on the Mount of Olives on the night of erev Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5599. Lady Judith Montefiore notes in her diary that the messengers came to thank them for coming to the Land of Israel and stayed overnight. Dr. Eliezer Halevi's memoirs likewise mention these Hebron visitors who came to greet them.
Tags: hebron, chabad, montefiore, mount of olives, jerusalem

Title: Montefiore census of Tzfat after the disasters
Summary: Sir Moses Montefiore conducted a census of the Tzfat Jewish community in Erev Shavuot 5599 during his visit.
Story: On his visit to Tzfat at Erev Shavuot 5599, Montefiore registered the surviving Jewish residents after the earthquake and pogroms. R' Uri of Slonim, a Chabad chasid, was registered with the Perushim kollel since there was no Chabad kollel in Tzfat at the time. He signed a contemporaneous letter from the remaining Perushim community as 'Uri Chabad.'
Tags: montefiore, tzfat, census, 1839

Title: First Chevron Chabad letter to Montefiore signed by R' Yosef Yehuda Leib
Summary: On 28 Sivan 5599 the Chevron Chabad community sent the first of six summer letters to Sir Moses Montefiore.
Story: Six letters were sent by the leaders of the Chevron Chabad community to Montefiore during summer 5599, the first dated 28 Sivan 5599. R' Yosef Yehuda Leib son of R' Chaim signed all of them. Notably, he already signed using the phrase 'son of the late' two days before the actual death of R' Chaim the Jerusalem shochet, demonstrating that the Jerusalem shochet was not actually his father.
Tags: yosef yehuda leib, montefiore, chevron, kolel chabad

Title: Hebron Chabad community's letter to Montefiore on agricultural plan
Summary: Leaders of the Hebron Chabad community wrote to Sir Moses Montefiore on 4 Tammuz responding to his plan for agricultural settlement in Eretz Yisrael.
Story: Sir Moses Montefiore traveled to Eretz Yisrael with a plan to lease land from Mohammed Ali for fifty years and settle Jews in agricultural villages. The Hebron Chabad community responded with an elaborately phrased letter dated 4 Tammuz endorsing the plan in principle but explaining that most of their members were elderly Torah scholars unsuited for farming, and that direct financial support would be a greater mitzvah for their community.
Tags: montefiore, hebron, agricultural settlement, mohammed ali, eretz yisrael, kollel chabad

Title: Montefiore departs Jerusalem for Hebron
Summary: Two days after the Hebron delegation arrived, Montefiore's party set out from Jerusalem to Hebron in the early morning.
Story: On Friday morning, two days after the Hebron delegation reached him, Montefiore and his entourage departed Jerusalem for Hebron. After a brief stop at Rachel's Tomb they continued on, arriving near Hebron toward evening. Hundreds of Hebron residents came out to meet them, dancing and singing Psalms in their honor, and escorted them to an olive grove near the city where they pitched their tents.
Tags: montefiore, jerusalem, hebron, rachel's tomb

Title: Montefiore prays at Chabad synagogue in Hebron
Summary: On Shabbat during their Hebron visit, Montefiore prayed Mincha at the Chabad synagogue in the Jews' courtyard.
Story: During the Shabbat of Montefiore's visit, his party remained in their tents in the field. For the prayer services they went into the synagogues in the Jewish courtyard, and at Mincha Montefiore prayed in the Chabad synagogue. The community would later memorialize this event in a formal deed transferring his prayer spot in the synagogue to him as an eternal possession.
Tags: montefiore, hebron, chabad, synagogue, shabbat

Title: Hebron Chabad issues four honorary deeds to Montefiore
Summary: On 4 Tammuz 5599 the Hebron Chabad leaders signed and delivered four honorary deeds to Sir Moses and Lady Judith Montefiore.
Story: The four documents were signed on 4 Tammuz by the leaders of the Hebron Chabad community and delivered to Montefiore that same day. They granted him and his wife places in the synagogue, appointed Sir Moses as patron and head of the Talmud Torah society, and appointed Lady Judith as patron of the Bikur Cholim and Hachnasat Kallah societies. The deeds bound the community to send accountings to her each year.
Tags: hebron, chabad, montefiore, synagogue, tzedakah

Title: Death of R' Chaim ben R' Moshe m'Shklov, first Ashkenazi shochet of Jerusalem
Summary: R' Chaim ben R' Moshe m'Shklov, the first shochet of the Ashkenazi community in Jerusalem, died on Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5599.
Story: The chevra kadisha records of Jerusalem give the death date of R' Chaim ben R' Moshe m'Shklov as Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5599 (not 5591, as one secondary source has it). He served as the first shochet for the Ashkenazi community of Jerusalem. The author uses this correct date to demonstrate that he could not have been the father of R' Yosef Yehuda Leib m'Shyuf, who had already signed as 'son of the late' two days before this date.
Tags: chaim ben moshe shklov, jerusalem, shochet, ashkenazim

Title: Montefiore census of Chevron
Summary: Sir Moses Montefiore conducted a census of the Chevron Jewish community on 4 Tammuz 5599.
Story: On 4 Tammuz 5599 Montefiore registered the Jews of Chevron during his visit. The Chevron Chabad community optimistically registered R' Uri of Slonim as a resident, though he was still in Tzfat at the time and only intended to move. The inaccurate details in his Chevron entry (wrong children's names, ages, and aliyah year) reflect that the community recorded him in absentia.
Tags: montefiore, chevron, census, 1839

Title: Birth of R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum in Pleshenitz
Summary: R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum, son of R. Dovber, of Pleshenitz was born approximately in the year 5600 (1840).
Story: R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum was born around 5600 (1840) in Pleshenitz, Belarus. As a young married man he was already studying in the court of the Tzemach Tzedek, and later became a devoted chassid of the Rebbe Maharash. He earned a living as a businessman while maintaining an active Torah correspondence with leading rabbis of his generation.
Tags: avraham chaim rosenbaum, pleshenitz, russia, biography, chabad chassid

Title: End of Ibrahim Pasha's rule in Eretz Yisrael
Summary: Ibrahim Pasha's rule over Eretz Yisrael ended in 5600 after seven years as governor general.
Story: After conquering Eretz Yisrael and Syria for his father Muhammad Ali, Ibrahim Pasha served as governor general from 5593 until 5600. His rule, which encompassed the catastrophic events of 5594 in Hebron, ended in 5600, returning the region to Ottoman control.
Tags: ibrahim pasha, egypt, eretz yisrael, ottoman empire

Title: Nicholas I orders special ministerial committee on Jewish affairs
Summary: At the end of 1840 (start of 5601) Tsar Nicholas I ordered the establishment of a special ministerial committee to fundamentally 'reform' Jewish life.
Story: The committee included Minister of Interior Stroganov, Minister of Education Uvarov, Minister of Finance Vrontchenko, and Bludov of the legislative ministry, chaired by Count Kiselev; the head of the Third Section, General Dubelt, was later added. Uvarov took on the mission of 'enlightening' the Jews and allied with the Maskilim to compel the opening of state-style Jewish schools. He appointed Dr. Max Lilienthal of Riga as his intermediary with the Jewish population.
Tags: russia, nicholas i, jewish affairs, haskalah

Title: Ottoman expulsion of Egyptian governor from the Land of Israel
Summary: In 5600 the Ottomans expelled the Egyptian ruler from the Land of Israel, after which Sheikh Abdul Rahman returned to terrorize Hebron.
Story: After the Ottoman authorities drove the Egyptian governor out of the Land of Israel in 5600, Sheikh Abdul Rahman resumed his rule over Hebron and its surroundings. He intensified his oppression of the Jews, imposing separate ransom payments on each of the two Jewish communities. The situation forced the diaspora kollel administrators to formally allocate him a share in the kollel's distribution list under the name 'the Black Rabbi.'
Tags: ottoman, egypt, hebron, abdul rahman, war

Title: Death of R. Avraham David of Buchach
Summary: R. Avraham David Wahrman's rabbinate in Buchach ended in 5601 (1841).
Story: The Buchach rabbinate of R. Avraham David ended in 1841 after twenty-seven years. Across his fifty years of rabbanus in two communities he had filled tens of thousands of pages with chiddushim that remained in manuscript. Printing would begin only forty-five years later.
Tags: galicia, buchach, avraham david of buchach, passing

Title: Maskilim denounce Tzemach Tzedek; police search his home
Summary: In 5601 maskilim denounced the Tzemach Tzedek for opposing the government's plan to compel Jewish children to study secular subjects.
Story: A special officer was sent to Lubavitch, interrogated the Rebbe, and searched his home. The shock caused the Rebbe to fall ill and take to his bed. The episode opened years of continuous secret surveillance and culminated in his being summoned to the 1843 Petersburg rabbinical conference.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, maskilim, haskalah, russia, lubavitch

Title: Maskilim inform on Tzemach Tzedek; police search his home
Summary: Maskilim denounced the Tzemach Tzedek to the Russian government in 5601 for opposing forced Haskalah education of Jewish children, leading to a police search of his Lubavitch home.
Story: A special police officer came to Lubavitch to interrogate the Rebbe and search his home, and the Tzemach Tzedek fell ill from the shock. The incident triggered ongoing secret surveillance by the Russian secret police, which continued until the spring of 5607.
