The denunciation was part of a broader Haskalah-driven government effort to compel Jewish children into state-run secular education.
Tags: maskilim, russia, haskalah, tzemach-tzedek, education

Title: R' Uri sent as Hebron Chabad emissary
Summary: R' Uri served as an emissary of the Hebron Chabad community in 5601.
Story: From 5601 onward R' Uri is known as an emissary of the Hebron Chabad community, one of several shaderim sent abroad in that period to collect funds and convey the community's needs to Diaspora donors.
Tags: hebron, uri, shadar, fundraising

Title: Shearit Yehuda published in Vilna by MaharI"L's grandson
Summary: Shearit Yehuda, MaharI"L's halachic work, was brought to press by his grandson R' Ze'ev Wolf in 5601.
Story: In 5601 (1841), R' Ze'ev Wolf, grandson of MaharI"L (through his son R' Yeshaya), brought to press Shearit Yehuda — MaharI"L's collected rulings on melicha together with extensive responsa, glosses on his brother the Alter Rebbe's writings, and oral teachings transmitted in his name.
Tags: mahari"l, shearit yehuda, publication, yanovich

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's good-conduct resolutions
Summary: Between 5601 and 5603 (1841-1843) the Tzemach Tzedek recorded a list of personal good-conduct resolutions, written under Russian secret-police surveillance.
Story: Manuscript 1124 preserves a list of 'good practices' the Tzemach Tzedek set for himself, addressed in the style of a man speaking to himself. Internal evidence places it in 5601-5603 (1841-1843), a period during which he was subjected to surveillance by the Russian secret police, which deeply affected his health.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, secret police, personal resolutions, russia

Title: Maskilic denunciation of Tzemach Tzedek published in German-Jewish press
Summary: On 5 February 1841 (26 Shevat 5601) an article in 'Israelitische Annalen' denounced the Tzemach Tzedek as the chief opponent of government educational reform.
Story: The article, published in the German-Jewish weekly Israelitische Annalen issue 6, was sent from Vilna by Maskilim and named 'Mendel of Lyubavichi' as the leader of the Chassidim of Vitebsk and Mogilev. It claimed the Chabad movement was working to obstruct the government's educational plans and called for excluding Chassidim from communal leadership. The article was then submitted by Maskilim to Minister of Education Uvarov to provoke official action.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, haskalah, maskilim, denunciation, lilienthal, russia

Title: Lilienthal urges harsh suppression of Chassidic opposition
Summary: Dr. Max Lilienthal wrote to the Education Ministry urging the government to suppress Chassidic opposition to Jewish education reforms.
Story: On 11 March 1841 (Rosh Chodesh Nissan 5601), shortly after being appointed to oversee Jewish education, Dr. Max Lilienthal wrote to official Dukst-Dushinsky in the Education Ministry. He reported that his negotiations with the Chassidim of Minsk and Vitebsk revealed they would mount strong and consistent opposition. He urged the government to intervene and crush them in the harshest manner possible.
Tags: russia, haskalah, lilienthal, chassidim, minsk, vitebsk

Title: Lilienthal requests permission to write the Tzemach Tzedek officially
Summary: Lilienthal requested official permission to write a formal letter to the Tzemach Tzedek concerning Jewish education reforms.
Story: On 17 March 1841 (7 Nissan 5601), six days after his initial letter, Lilienthal again wrote to the Education Ministry. He asked for permission to address Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Lubavitch in a formal capacity to learn his position on the proposed reforms. The official Dukst-Dushinsky replied that Lilienthal could write only as a private individual, not officially.
Tags: russia, haskalah, lilienthal, tzemach tzedek, lubavitch

Title: Uvarov requests intelligence on the Tzemach Tzedek from Stroganov
Summary: On 28 March 1841 (18 Nissan 5601) Minister of Education Uvarov wrote to Interior Minister Stroganov requesting information on 'Mendel of Lyubavichi.'
Story: Acting on the German-Jewish article and Maskilic agitation, Uvarov asked Stroganov whether the Ministry of Interior held any information on Mendel of Lyubavichi, his personality and the extent of his influence over the Jews and especially the Chassidim. This launched a year-long secret investigation involving the Third Section, the governor-general of Vitebsk-Mogilev, and gendarmerie officers across three provinces. The correspondence became the documentary backbone for the build-up to the 1843 Rabbinical Conference.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, uvarov, stroganov, russia, haskalah, denunciation

Title: Uvarov requests Third Section investigation of Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: On 30 March 1841 (20 Nissan 5601) Uvarov wrote a confidential letter to Count Benckendorff, head of the Third Section, requesting an investigation of the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: Two days after his letter to Stroganov, Uvarov turned to the head of the secret police with the same request. He cited the Israelitische Annalen article and its respected editor Dr. Jost as warranting confidence in the report. Uvarov asked Benckendorff to collect detailed information on the Tzemach Tzedek's character, conduct, opinions, contacts and influence over the Jews, formally initiating the Third Section's investigation.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, uvarov, benckendorff, third section, russia, secret police

Title: Benckendorff orders provincial investigations of Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: On 5 April 1841 (26 Nissan 5601) Count Benckendorff ordered Governor-General Dyakov and gendarmerie commander Freigang to gather covert intelligence on the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: Acting on Uvarov's 30 March request, Benckendorff dispatched orders to Governor-General Dyakov of Vitebsk-Mogilev and to General Freigang, commander of the Fourth District of the gendarmerie. They were instructed to discreetly investigate the character, conduct, opinions, contacts and influence of the Jew Mendel of Lyubavichi. The order set in motion the parallel investigations that would shape the Third Section's eventual report.
Tags: benckendorff, tzemach tzedek, third section, russia, vitebsk, mogilev

Title: Stroganov confirms Tzemach Tzedek's great influence among Jews
Summary: On 7 April 1841 (28 Nissan 5601) Minister of Interior Stroganov replied to Uvarov confirming the Tzemach Tzedek's strong influence over Jews in White Russia and Lithuania.
Story: Stroganov reported he had no specific file on 'the Lyubavichi rabbi' but acknowledged that 'the Jewish rabbi Mendel of Lyubavichi who dwells in White Russia and belongs to the Chassidim sect, is truly respected by the Jews and has great influence on them, especially on the inhabitants of White Russia and Lithuania.' The confirmation gave official weight to the Maskilim's claims and intensified the case for direct surveillance.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, stroganov, uvarov, russia

Title: Freigang orders gendarmerie officers to investigate Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: On 12 April 1841 (3 Iyar 5601) General Freigang instructed gendarmerie officers in Mogilev, Vitebsk and Minsk to investigate the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: Following Benckendorff's directive, Freigang relayed orders to Colonels Kutsinsky and Wojciech and Captain Yurkovsky. Wojciech of Mogilev would personally travel to Lyubavichi to interview the Rebbe under cover of investigating the local synagogue. The coordinated three-province inquiry generated the most detailed contemporary external descriptions of the Tzemach Tzedek's personality, household and influence.
Tags: freigang, tzemach tzedek, gendarmerie, russia, mogilev, vitebsk, minsk

Title: Colonel Wojciech reports on his investigation of the Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: On 29 May 1841 (21 Sivan 5601) Colonel Wojciech submitted his report on his visit to the Tzemach Tzedek in Lyubavichi.
Story: Earlier, during the February fair in Lyubavichi, Wojciech had entered the Rebbe's home on the pretext of inquiring about the synagogue, finding him studying from a book and conversing in halting Russian. He described the Tzemach Tzedek as over fifty, physically weak, living in poverty with six sons and two daughters, registered as a third-guild merchant but leaving trade to his family. Wojciech concluded the Rebbe was a 'simple man with limited intellect,' morally above reproach, who declined the title of rabbi inherited from his ancestors and wished only to live quietly with his books.
Tags: wojciech, tzemach tzedek, lyubavichi, russia, gendarmerie, interrogation

Title: Dyakov reports to Benckendorff on Tzemach Tzedek's character and influence
Summary: On 9 June 1841 (2 Tammuz 5601) Governor-General Dyakov reported to Benckendorff on the Tzemach Tzedek's residence, conduct and standing among the Jews.
Story: Dyakov identified the man in question as Mendel Schneersohn, registered as a third-guild merchant in Babinovichi but residing permanently in Lyubavichi since 1813. He described the Rebbe as approximately fifty years old, of weak health and rarely leaving his home, possessing good character and conduct with no opinions contrary to the laws. Dyakov noted that Jews — Chassidim and even Misnagdim — turned to him from many places to resolve religious questions, and that he was honored as a descendant of great rabbis, including his grandfather of Liadi who 'was known in Petersburg due to some matter.'
Tags: dyakov, tzemach tzedek, russia, lyubavichi, secret police

Title: Freigang submits combined gendarmerie report on Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: On 12 June 1841 (5 Tammuz 5601) General Freigang submitted a consolidated report from three provinces on the Tzemach Tzedek to Count Benckendorff.
Story: Freigang summarized the parallel reports of Colonel Kutsinsky from Vitebsk, Colonel Wojciech from Mogilev and Captain Yurkovsky from Minsk. The reports broadly agreed that the Tzemach Tzedek lived simply and modestly, was regarded by his followers as a great scholar and held strong influence over them, while showing no signs of disloyalty. Yurkovsky's Minsk report uniquely recounted the Rebbe's 1835 visit to Minsk and noted that 'Zalman, the grandfather of Mendel of Lyubavichi' had been summoned to Petersburg around 1802 on suspicion of belonging to a harmful sect but was cleared and returned home shortly afterwards.
Tags: freigang, tzemach tzedek, benckendorff, russia, gendarmerie

Title: Benckendorff reports findings on Tzemach Tzedek to Uvarov
Summary: On 18 June 1841 (11 Tammuz 5601) Count Benckendorff reported the consolidated investigation findings on the Tzemach Tzedek to Minister of Education Uvarov.
Story: Having received the field reports through Dyakov and Freigang, Benckendorff forwarded the intelligence to Uvarov and requested a decision on next steps. The Third Section had now built a documentary file on the Tzemach Tzedek's character, family, conduct, and influence over the Jews of Vitebsk, Mogilev and Minsk. This concluded the surveillance phase and set the stage for the next move — pressuring the Rebbe to participate in the Rabbinical Conference.
Tags: benckendorff, uvarov, tzemach tzedek, russia, secret police

Title: Benckendorff reports on Mendel Schneersohn to Education Minister Uvarov
Summary: Third Section head Benckendorff sent the Education Minister a report on Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneersohn of Lubavitch, suspected of opposing government plans for the Jews.
Story: On 25 June 1841 (18 Tammuz 5601), Count Benckendorff, head of the Third Section (secret police), forwarded a gendarmerie report on the Tzemach Tzedek to Education Minister Uvarov. The report described Schneersohn as the head of the Chassidic sect in Vitebsk and Mogilev, allegedly opposing the government's plans for Jewish education. Benckendorff requested the document be returned when no longer needed.
Tags: russia, tsarist surveillance, third section, benckendorff, uvarov, tzemach tzedek, lubavitch

Title: Uvarov orders covert surveillance of the Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: Education Minister Uvarov directed that secret surveillance be placed on Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Lubavitch despite finding no unlawful conduct.
Story: On 7 July 1841 (Rosh Chodesh Av 5601), Count Uvarov replied to Benckendorff that although Schneersohn had not committed unlawful acts and seemed harmless, secret surveillance should still be imposed on him. This was especially needed while the government implemented its new Jewish education plans. The two papers about Mendel were returned with the directive.
Tags: russia, tsarist surveillance, uvarov, benckendorff, tzemach tzedek, haskalah

Title: Third Section orders Mogilev gendarmes to spy on the Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: The Third Section ordered Colonel Voytsekh of the Mogilev gendarmerie to conduct covert surveillance of Rabbi Mendel Schneersohn of Lubavitch.
Story: On 21 July 1841 (15 Av 5601), the head of the Third Section formally instructed Colonel Voytsekh of the gendarmerie in Mogilev province to secretly monitor Mendel Schneersohn's conduct and views. The order cited suspicions that he and his followers opposed the government's plans for the Jews. This launched what would become a six-year covert surveillance operation.
Tags: russia, tsarist surveillance, gendarmerie, mogilev, lubavitch, tzemach tzedek

Title: First Haggadah printed in Eretz Yisrael
Summary: The first Haggadah printed in the Land of Israel was issued in Jerusalem in 5602.
Story: In 5602 (1842), the first Haggadah ever printed in the Land of Israel was issued in Jerusalem. It included necessary laws for the Seder night, the Ma'ariv prayer, and the order of counting the Omer.
Tags: haggadah, jerusalem, eretz-yisrael

Title: Lilienthal visits the Tzemach Tzedek in Lubavitch
Summary: Dr. Max Lilienthal traveled to Lubavitch to meet personally with the Tzemach Tzedek about joining the planned Petersburg rabbinic commission.
Story: In 5602, Lilienthal reported to the Education Ministry that he had sent a warm letter to the Rebbe and then traveled to Lubavitch to meet him. He described the Rebbe as about forty-five years old, not tall, and of utterly simple bearing. Lilienthal proposed that the Tzemach Tzedek join the planned rabbinic commission in Petersburg, but the Rebbe initially refused, citing his fragile health since the search and interrogation he had endured.
Tags: russia, haskalah, lilienthal, tzemach tzedek, lubavitch, rabbinic commission

Title: Passing of R. Yehoshua, Rabbi of Horki
Summary: In the summer of 5602 the Chasid R. Yehoshua, Rabbi of Horki, passed away.
Story: During the early years of the Tzemach Tzedek's leadership, the Rabbi of Horki was the Chasid R. Yehoshua. He passed away in the summer of 5602 and was succeeded by R. Yehoshua Eliyahu ben R. Yosef, who served at least until 5610 (1850).
Tags: horki, russia, rabbinate

Title: R' Yehoshua of Horki passes away
Summary: R' Yehoshua, rabbi of Horki and correspondent of the Tzemach Tzedek, passed away in the summer of 5602.
Story: R' Yehoshua served as rabbi of Horki in the early years of the Tzemach Tzedek's leadership. His final psak was issued on Erev Shabbos in Nissan 5602, and the Tzemach Tzedek's responsa to him appear in Even HaEzer. He was succeeded by R' Yehoshua Eliyahu ben Yosef.
Tags: yehoshua horki, tzemach tzedek, horki, rabbinate, chabad

Title: Renewed Chabad-Sephardi agreement in Hebron
Summary: A renewed inter-communal agreement was signed in Hebron in 5602 documenting separate ransom burdens imposed by Sheikh Abdul Rahman.
Story: Following the Ottoman return to power and Abdul Rahman's renewed exactions, the Chabad and Sephardi communities of Hebron updated their inter-communal agreement in 5602. The new accord, signed by R' Shmuel Halevi and R' Menachem Aryeh among others, formalized the separate 'ransom for souls' that the sheikh demanded from each community. This necessitated allocating him a fixed share in the Chabad kollel's distributions abroad.
Tags: hebron, chabad, sephardim, abdul rahman, protection money

Title: Second Hebron inter-community agreement expanding shdarus reach
Summary: Hebron's Sephardic and Chabad communities renewed their agreement, expanding the joint shdarus territories to include Turkey and North Africa.
Story: In 5602 (1842), the Hebron Sephardic and Chabad communities signed another agreement renewing the joint shdarus arrangements. The terms largely matched the 5590 agreement, but added Turkey and the Maghreb (North Africa, inner and outer) to the list of joint shlichut territories alongside Italy, Persia, and Sephardic lands. The expansion reflected growing fundraising operations across the Mediterranean and Ottoman lands.
Tags: hebron, sephardic kollel, chabad kollel, turkey, north africa, agreement

Title: Sefer Avodas HaLevi by Rabbi Aharon HaLevi of Staroshelye published
Summary: First edition of Avodas HaLevi by Rabbi Aharon HaLevi of Staroshelye was published in Lvov.
Story: Rabbi Aharon HaLevi of Staroshelye was a leading disciple of the Alter Rebbe whose writings became foundational texts of Chabad chassidus. This first edition of Avodas HaLevi was printed in Lvov in 5602 (1842) and is now displayed in the Library's exhibition of works by the great Chabad chassidim.
Tags: lvov, aharon halevi, staroshelye, chassidus

Title: Third Chabad–Sephardic Hebron agreement at 500 grush
Summary: A third agreement in 5602 reduces Chabad's annual payment to the Sephardic kollel to 500 grush, effective from Tishrei 5603.
Story: By 5602 Sheikh Abdul Rahman had increased his protection demands and required separate payments from each kollel directly. The third agreement therefore reduced the Chabad contribution to general Hebron expenses from 900 to 500 grush per year, effective Tishrei 5603 onward. The text acknowledges that the Sephardim were the original Jewish settlers under whose communal umbrella the Chabad community had arrived in Hebron.
Tags: hebron, chabad, sephardim, kollel, tzemach tzedek, abdul rahman, protection payments

Title: Tzemach Tzedek receives Honorary Citizen status from Tsar Nicholas I
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Lubavitch received the certificate of Honorary Citizen, signed by Tsar Nicholas I.
Story: In 5602 (1842), the Tzemach Tzedek received the title of Honorary Citizen by certificate signed by the Tsar. This title was a recognition of social standing under Russian estate law. It would later play a role in the lifting of his secret surveillance and in his recognition by the regime.
Tags: russia, nicholas i, honorary citizen, tzemach tzedek

Title: Latest dated responsum in Mehadura Batra Even HaEzer manuscript
Summary: Manuscript 1050, the Even HaEzer mehadura batra, contains a final dated responsum from 5603.
Story: In later years the Tzemach Tzedek began reorganizing his responsa according to the sections of the Shulchan Aruch, possibly to prepare them for print. Manuscript 1050 — labeled in his own hand 'Responsa Even HaEzer, mehadura batra, chelek 2' — was bound around the time of its latest dated responsum, 5603.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, mehadura batra, manuscript 1050, even haezer

Title: Lilienthal Enlightenment education conference
Summary: Max Lilienthal organized a government-backed conference in St. Petersburg to secularize Jewish education in Russia.
Story: In 1843, German Enlightenment activist Max Lilienthal, backed by education minister Sergei Uvarov, organized a St. Petersburg conference to overhaul Jewish education in Russia. The third Chabad Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek, played a pivotal role in blocking Lilienthal's plans.
Tags: max lilienthal, haskalah, st petersburg, uvarov, tzemach tzedek

Title: Petersburg Rabbinical Conference on Jewish education
Summary: During the summer of 5603 the Tzemach Tzedek participated in the Petersburg conference on Jewish education called by the Russian government.
Story: The conference, proposed by the maskilim and convened by the Minister of Education, aimed to pressure leading rabbis to consent to government 'enlightenment' schools for Jewish youth. The Rebbe initially pleaded that his post-interrogation illness made travel impossible, but ultimately agreed that his attendance was essential to block undesirable resolutions. Following the conference he was granted the imperial title of Honorary Citizen for life.
Tags: petersburg, rabbinical conference, tzemach tzedek, haskalah, uvarov

Title: Power of attorney to litigate in Jerusalem
Summary: In 5603 R' Shmuel Halevi signed a power of attorney authorizing litigation in Jerusalem on behalf of the Hebron Chabad community.
Story: Among the official acts of R' Shmuel Halevi as head of the Hebron Chabad community was a formal power of attorney from 5603 authorizing representation in legal proceedings in Jerusalem. The document is part of a series of signed instruments from his tenure as rabbi and maggid of Hebron. It reflects the community's regular need to handle disputes outside the city through proxies.
Tags: hebron, chabad, jerusalem, legal

Title: R' Ephraim Yaffe returns to Hebron Kollel leadership
Summary: In 5603, R' Ephraim Yaffe rejoined the Hebron kollel leadership after a 13-year absence from the signature list.
Story: From 5590 to 5602 he had not signed kollel documents, but starting in 5603 his name appeared again among the first signatories. He served alongside R' Shmuel Segal and R' Yehuda Leib of Sena until 5606.
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, ephraim yaffe, shmuel segal

Title: R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov sent as Hebron Chabad emissary
Summary: Around 5604 the Hebron Chabad community sent R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov of Shklov abroad as their emissary, charged with collecting funds and conveying their hardships.
Story: Around 5604 the Hebron Chabad community appointed R' Yosef Yehuda Leib Mashiov of Shklov as their emissary to collect previously gathered donations and to inform Diaspora Jewry of the suffering they had endured in those years. The mission also reflected his personal need, as his son had reached marriageable age. He served two years on this mission, returning in the summer of 5606.
Tags: hebron, mashiov, shklov, fundraising, kollel chabad, shadar

Title: R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz becomes moreh tzedek of Konotop
Summary: In 5603 R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz left Lubavitch to take up the rabbinate of Konotop, where he remained until his death.
Story: After ten years as moreh tzedek of Lubavitch, R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz accepted the post of moreh tzedek in Konotop in 5603 (1843). He continued his halachic correspondence from there, including extensive teshuvot reflecting on his earlier years. He became known posthumously as 'the Rav of Konotop,' and the Tzemach Tzedek referred to him as such in marginal notes on his old responsa.
Tags: yissachar ber horowitz, konotop, lubavitch

Title: Rabbinic Vaad on Jewish education convenes in Russia
Summary: A government-convened conference on Jewish education met during the summer of 5603, with the Tzemach Tzedek among the participating rabbinic leaders.
Story: The maskilim had proposed the conference to pressure rabbinic leaders into agreeing to open Haskalah schools for Jewish youth. Initially the Tzemach Tzedek declined to attend due to ill health following the 5601 search, but it was ultimately decided that his presence was crucial to prevent harmful resolutions. Following the conference the Russian government issued him a certificate of honored citizenship for his descendants.
Tags: maskilim, haskalah, russia, tzemach-tzedek, vaad, petersburg-conference

Title: Tzemach Tzedek instructs family members to settle in Hebron
Summary: Around 5604 the Tzemach Tzedek directed several relatives to make aliyah and settle in Hebron, becoming the foundation of the Chabad community there.
Story: Around 5604 the Tzemach Tzedek instructed several members of his family to immigrate to Eretz Yisrael and settle in Hebron. Three granddaughters of the Alter Rebbe came from Lubavitch with their families: Menucha Rachel (daughter of the Mitteler Rebbe) with R' Yaakov Slonim, Sarah Rivka with R' Nachum Yosef Schneersohn, and Rachel with R' Moshe Tzvi Pundeminsky. They became the cornerstone of the Chabad settlement in Hebron.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, hebron, aliyah, slonim family, schneersohn family, alter rebbe descendants

Title: Tzemach Tzedek summoned to Petersburg rabbinic conference
Summary: In the summer of 5603 the Tzemach Tzedek was summoned to a rabbinic conference in Petersburg.
Story: In summer 1843 the Tzemach Tzedek was called by the Russian government to a rabbinical conference in Petersburg, where he stayed several months. He took along a list of books for study during free time; some volumes still contain blank pages he had inserted to record new chiddushim.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, petersburg, russia, rabbinic conference, tsarist government

Title: Chaim Ginzburg lobbies for the Tzemach Tzedek to attend Petersburg commission
Summary: Chassidic activist Chaim Ginzburg wrote to Lilienthal that all Chassidim wanted the Tzemach Tzedek as their representative at the Petersburg commission.
Story: On 10 February 1843 (22 Adar I 5603), the activist R. Chaim Ginzburg wrote to Dr. Lilienthal that the entire Chassidic community wanted the Tzemach Tzedek to travel to Petersburg as their representative. Although the Chassidim had initially selected R. Yitzchak Aizik of Orsha as their delegate, opinion shifted toward the Rebbe himself. The letter helped shape the government's eventual invitation.
Tags: russia, haskalah, lilienthal, tzemach tzedek, petersburg, rabbinic commission, chaim ginzburg

Title: Hebron Chabad community signs authorization for kollel emissaries
Summary: On 15 Shvat 5603 the leaders of the Hebron Chabad community signed a power of attorney appointing R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov and R' Moshe Shmerling to litigate against the Perushim community.
Story: The administrators and overseers of the Chabad community in Hebron, joined by the seven communal trustees, formally appointed R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov and R' Moshe Shmerling as their representatives to negotiate and litigate with the Perushim kollel leadership in Jerusalem regarding shared funds from Hungary and Vienna. They were also empowered to settle outstanding claims with the community's own emissary R' Moshe ben David Yaffe.
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, perushim, fundraising, montefiore funds

Title: Lilienthal officially invites the Tzemach Tzedek to the Petersburg commission
Summary: Dr. Lilienthal formally notified the Tzemach Tzedek that he was invited to the rabbinic commission in Petersburg.
Story: On 19 February 1843 (Rosh Chodesh Adar II 5603), Dr. Lilienthal formally notified Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Lubavitch of his invitation to the Petersburg commission on Jewish education. Three days later Lilienthal wrote to the Education Ministry recommending the Tzemach Tzedek as the most important rabbi among the Russian Jews. He argued that the Rebbe's agreement with government policy would carry binding weight for the Chassidim of Vitebsk, Mogilev, Chernigov, Kiev, Kherson, and Minsk.
Tags: russia, lilienthal, petersburg, rabbinic commission, tzemach tzedek

Title: Uvarov instructs Governor-General to summon the Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: Education Minister Uvarov instructed Governor-General Diakov to invite Mendel Schneersohn to the Petersburg rabbinic commission.
Story: On 14 March 1843 (24 Adar II 5603), Count Uvarov wrote to Pyotr Diakov, Governor-General of Vitebsk, Smolensk, and Mogilev provinces. He advised that one of the Chassidic rabbis must be included on the commission, given the Chassidim's prominence in Belorussia and Lithuania. He requested Diakov to notify Mendel Schneersohn to travel to Petersburg, calling him a man of moral merit and sound mind.
Tags: russia, uvarov, diakov, petersburg, rabbinic commission, tzemach tzedek

Title: Tzemach Tzedek requests travel permits for his assistants to Petersburg
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek petitioned Governor Diakov to allow him to bring R. Shmaria Paytelson and his son R. Yehuda Leib as assistants to Petersburg.
Story: On 17 April 1843 (29 Nissan 5603), the Tzemach Tzedek wrote to Governor Diakov from Vitebsk. He requested that his travel pass be expanded to include Shmaria son of Mordechai Paytelson, needed to translate since he spoke only Yiddish, and his son Leib Schneersohn, needed to assist due to his weak health. He attached the passports and asked to be permitted to arrive in time for the commission's opening.
Tags: russia, petersburg, rabbinic commission, shmaria paytelson, yehuda leib schneersohn, tzemach tzedek

Title: Rabbinical Conference convenes in Petersburg
Summary: From 18 Iyar to Elul 5603 (May–September 1843) the Rabbinical Conference summoned by the Russian government was held in Petersburg, with the Tzemach Tzedek in attendance.
Story: After the Third Section's 1841 investigation and Dr. Max Lilienthal's personal visit to Lyubavichi, the government insisted on the Tzemach Tzedek's attendance to neutralize his anticipated opposition to its educational reforms. The Rebbe brought along one of his sons and a Chassid, and packed some thirty seforim with paper to record chiddushim during his stay. The conference's deliberations were kept secret — Beis Rebbi records that the Tzemach Tzedek refused to disclose what transpired, saying he 'had not been given permission to reveal' them.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, petersburg, rabbinical conference, haskalah, lilienthal, russia

Title: Petersburg rabbinic commission convenes
Summary: The Petersburg rabbinic commission on Jewish education opened, with the Tzemach Tzedek among its members.
Story: On 6 May 1843 (18 Iyar 5603), the rabbinic commission convened in Petersburg. The Tzemach Tzedek traveled there with R. Shmaria Paytelson as his translator and his son R. Yehuda Leib for medical assistance. The commission continued through August 1843 (Elul 5603), discussing Jewish educational reforms in great secrecy; the Rebbe later said the details could not be revealed.
Tags: russia, petersburg, rabbinic commission, tzemach tzedek, haskalah

Title: R. Binyamin Wolf Loew of Verbov writes to Maharia Asad on religious decline
Summary: R. Binyamin Wolf Loew, av beis din of Verbov, wrote to R. Yehuda Asad lamenting the breaches in Jewish observance and seeking guidance.
Story: In a letter dated to the week of Parshas Nitzavim 5603, R. Binyamin Wolf Loew of Verbov poured out his anguish to R. Yehuda Asad over the spread of Reform and the loss of an older generation of rabbinic leaders who had stood in the breach. He confessed that the situation pained him daily and pressed Asad to share any practical strategy he might have for resisting the modernist breach-makers. The letter is the earliest of three surviving responses to Asad's outreach campaign for strengthening religious life in Hungary.
Tags: hungary, verbov, reform-movement, yehuda-asad, binyamin-wolf-loew

Title: Slonim family arrives in Hebron
Summary: Rabbi Yaakov and Rebbetzin Menucha Rochel Slonim, the daughter and son-in-law of the Mitteler Rebbe, immigrated to Hebron.
Story: Their arrival significantly bolstered the Chabad community in Hebron. Their descendants would play a central role in Hebron Jewish life, including the tragic 1929 massacre, when grandson Eliezer Don Slonim was killed.
Tags: hebron, slonim-family, mitteler-rebbe

Title: Rabbinical assembly in Paks to strengthen Orthodox observance
Summary: Leading Hungarian rabbis convened in Paks to coordinate opposition to the Reform movement and the planned modernist seminary.
Story: On 3 Elul 5604, prominent Hungarian rabbis gathered in Paks to strengthen Orthodox observance against the inroads of the Reform movement. Among the issues debated was the proposed founding of a modernist rabbinical seminary promoted by the reformers, which the Ksav Sofer later reported had been successfully blocked. In follow-up correspondence, the Ksav Sofer counseled that ongoing resistance to the reformers should be conducted discreetly rather than through further public assemblies.
Tags: hungary, paks, reform-movement, ksav-sofer, yehuda-asad, rabbinical-seminary

Title: Ksav Sofer writes to Maharia Asad about the Paks assembly's outcome
Summary: The Ksav Sofer reported to R. Yehuda Asad that the threat of a modernist seminary had been quashed and counseled discreet ongoing resistance.
Story: Writing from Pressburg on 5 Cheshvan 5605, R. Avraham Shmuel Binyamin Sofer (Ksav Sofer) updated R. Yehuda Asad on developments since the Paks assembly. He confirmed that the magnates had withdrawn support for the reformers' seminary and the danger had passed, crediting community askanim who had worked tirelessly to defeat it. He recommended against convening a further public rabbinical council in Pressburg, urging that resistance proceed quietly until the controversy subsided.
Tags: hungary, pressburg, ksav-sofer, yehuda-asad, rabbinical-seminary, reform-movement

Title: Letter of Rabbi Yisrael Dov Twersky of Vilednik to Rabbi Aharon Lifshitz
Summary: Rabbi Yisrael Dov of Vilednik writes to Rabbi Aharon Lifshitz of Belinitz on a Tuesday of Parashat Vayishlach 5605.
Story: In a letter dated Tuesday of Parashat Vayishlach 5605, the Rebbe of Vilednik acknowledges Rabbi Aharon Lifshitz's letter about a marital question. He declines to rule and directs the questioner to 'the great rabbi of Lubavitch' — the Tzemach Tzedek — instead, illustrating how Ukrainian chasidic rebbes referred difficult halakhic cases to Lubavitch.
Tags: vilednik, belinitz, twersky, ukraine, halakhic-consultation, tzemach-tzedek

Title: R. Yechezkel Banet of Neitra writes to Maharia Asad on monitoring reformers
Summary: R. Yechezkel Banet of Neitra told R. Yehuda Asad that he had posted watchers to detect new modernist moves before the government committee.
Story: In a letter dated the 6th day of Chanukah 5605 from Neitra, R. Yechezkel Banet expressed pain over the continuing troubles being caused to Torah scholars by the reformers. He informed R. Yehuda Asad that he had stationed informants to alert him the moment any modernist proposal was placed before the government committee, at which point he would dispatch a special messenger so that a coordinated response could be prepared. The letter reflects the underground intelligence network the Hungarian rabbinate maintained in the wake of the Paks assembly.
Tags: hungary, neitra, yechezkel-banet, yehuda-asad, reform-movement

Title: Rebbetzin Menucha Rochel immigrates to Hebron
Summary: Rebbetzin Menucha Rochel, daughter of the Mitteler Rebbe, immigrated to Hebron.
Story: In 1845, Rebbetzin Menucha Rochel, daughter of the second Chabad Rebbe Rabbi Dovber, immigrated to Hebron. Her descendants maintained a close connection with the Rebbes in Lubavitch, traveling there regularly and anchoring the Chabad presence in Hebron for generations.
Tags: menucha rochel, hebron, chabad, immigration

Title: Tzemach Tzedek receives Hereditary Honorary Citizen status
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek received the certificate of Hereditary Honorary Citizen for himself and his descendants.
Story: In 5605 (1845), the Tzemach Tzedek received the elevated status of Hereditary Honorary Citizen. Per the Hayom Yom and other sources, this enhanced his standing in Russian society. The title was tied to his subsequent acquisition of an estate in his name.
Tags: russia, hereditary honorary citizen, tzemach tzedek

Title: Young Maharash buys Hebrew books from a Lubavitch bookseller
Summary: In Elul 5605, a bookseller visited Lubavitch and the young Rabbi Shmuel asked his father, the Tzemach Tzedek, for 30 rubles to buy books.
Story: According to a memoir of the Rebbe Rayatz, during the Tzemach Tzedek's monthly tests of his son and other cheder students, prizes were monetary, which Rabbi Shmuel saved together with a weekly ruble to buy seforim. In Elul 5605 (1845) a bookseller came to Lubavitch and the young Maharash requested 30 rubles from money his father held for him; his father gave him the sum plus 10 rubles as a gift, allowing him to buy a substantial collection of books.
Tags: maharash, books, lubavitch, tzemach-tzedek, childhood

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's sons write R' Aharon Lifshitz on the clothing decree
Summary: On 24 Tammuz 5605 the three sons of the Tzemach Tzedek wrote R' Aharon Lifshitz of Belinitch about the Tsarist clothing decree.
Story: Tsar Nicholas I's 1845 decree forced Jews to abandon traditional garb, with a transitional tax (korobka) levied on those still wearing long coats. Because the Tzemach Tzedek was under secret-police surveillance, his sons — the future rebbes of Kopust, Liadi, and Niezhin — wrote to R' Aharon Lifshitz, dayan of Belinitch, asking how the tax collection there with the Mohilev governor's office had been handled, hoping to learn from it for Lubavitch.
Tags: clothing decree, tzemach tzedek, russia, mohilev, belinitch, korobka tax

Title: Sir Moses Montefiore transfers 600 rubles to Hebron Chabad
Summary: In Kislev 5606 emissary R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov routed 600 rubles for Hebron Chabad through Vilna to Sir Moses Montefiore and on to Damascus.
Story: During Kislev 5606, the Hebron Chabad emissary R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov forwarded 600 rubles, equivalent to about 200 guineas, from Shklov via Vilna to Sir Moses Montefiore. The funds were to be transmitted to Damascus and from there to the Chabad community in Hebron, demonstrating the cross-continental philanthropic network supporting the kollel.
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, montefiore, vilna, damascus, fundraising

Title: Letter to Rabbi Avraham Chaim Gagin
Summary: R' Shmuel Halevi signed a letter to R' Avraham Chaim Gagin, Rishon LeTzion, in 5606.
Story: In 5606 R' Shmuel Halevi, maggid of Hebron, signed an official letter addressed to R' Avraham Chaim Gagin (the AGaN), Sephardi chief rabbi of Jerusalem. The letter is preserved in Migdal Oz and is one of the last documents bearing his signature before his death sometime between 5609 and 5615. It illustrates the ongoing institutional relationship between the Hebron Chabad community and the Sephardi rabbinic establishment of Jerusalem.
Tags: hebron, chabad, jerusalem, sephardim, rabbinate

Title: Mohammed Pasha conquers Hebron from Abdul Rahman
Summary: In 5606 the Ottoman governor of Jerusalem, Mohammed Pasha, conquered Hebron from Sheikh Abdul Rahman, with widespread looting following.
Story: After a long internal war between Abdul Rahman and his brothers, Mohammed Pasha, the Ottoman governor of Jerusalem, marched on Hebron in 5606 and captured it from the rebellious sheikh. During the conquest the city was given over to murder and plunder until the governor signaled a halt; the looters did not distinguish between Jews and gentiles. The Sephardi rabbis described how 'sons of Belial' stripped the entire city, while later accounts emphasize that during this second plunder lives were spared and the looting lasted only half a day.
Tags: hebron, ottoman, abdul rahman, war, looting

Title: Montefiore meets Czar Nicholas I in St. Petersburg
Summary: Moses Montefiore traveled to St. Petersburg to urge the czar to improve conditions for Russian Jews.
Story: Montefiore's intervention with Czar Nicholas I became a model the Rebbe Rayatz later invoked when urging JDC leaders to use their influence on behalf of Soviet Jewry. Montefiore returned to Russia for a second visit in 1876.
Tags: moses-montefiore, russia, czar-nicholas-i, diplomacy

Title: R' Moshe Yaffe travels as Tiberias chassidim emissary
Summary: In 5606 R' Moshe ben David Yaffe undertook an additional emissary mission, this one on behalf of the chassidim of Tiberias.
Story: R' Moshe ben David Yaffe, listed in the 5609 census as a talmid chacham and emissary, undertook a second mission in 5606. This later mission was on behalf of the chassidic community of Tiberias rather than Hebron, as documented in 'Shluchei Eretz Yisrael' p. 788.
Tags: tiberias, hebron, yaffe, shadar, fundraising

Title: Hebron Chabad letter on famine and war
Summary: Hebron's Chabad leaders wrote a letter on 13 Shevat 1846 describing severe famine and war that prevented food imports.
Story: On 13 Shevat 1846 (י"ג שבט תר"ו), Chabad leaders in Hebron wrote a desperate appeal describing a heavy famine in the Holy Land. War between local rulers had been ongoing for nearly a year, preventing the import of grain, leaving women and children begging for bread. The letter was later reproduced by the Pekidim u'Amarkalim in their fundraising circulars.
Tags: hebron, famine, war, chabad kollel, pekidim amarkalim, fundraising

Title: R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov's Pesach letter from Shklov
Summary: On Erev Pesach 5606 the Hebron emissary R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov wrote from Shklov to Dr. Eliezer Halevi, Montefiore's secretary, reporting his fundraising progress.
Story: From Shklov on Erev Pesach 5606, the Hebron Chabad emissary R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov wrote to Dr. Eliezer Halevi, secretary to Sir Moses Montefiore (letter published in Kerem Chabad vol. 2). He reported that he had already, in the previous Kislev, transmitted via Vilna to Sir Moses some 600 rubles (roughly 200 guineas) intended to reach Hebron via Damascus, and announced his plan to return home after the festival.
Tags: hebron, shklov, mashiov, montefiore, damascus, fundraising

Title: R' Moshe Shmerling joins Hebron Kollel leadership
Summary: On 5 Menachem Av 5606, R' Yehuda Leib Sener stepped down from the Hebron kollel leadership and R' Moshe Shmerling replaced him.
Story: R' Yehuda Leib appears to have retired due to old age — his successor R' Moshe Shmerling, son of Shimon, joined R' Shmuel Segal and R' Ephraim Yaffe on the kollel board. R' Yehuda Leib lived past 5609.
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, moshe shmerling, yehuda leib sener

Title: R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin joins Hebron Kollel
Summary: On 6 Elul 5606, R' Ephraim Yaffe retired from the Hebron kollel leadership and R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin was added in his place.
Story: R' Ephraim Yaffe apparently retired due to old age and died between 5606 and 5609. His successor, R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, would go on to become the central figure in Hebron Chabad leadership for nearly half a century.
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, shimon menashe chaikin, ephraim yaffe

Title: Chabad chasidim move from Chevron to Jerusalem
Summary: R' Ephraim Yitzchak Epstein, R' Yosef Yehuda Leib m'Shyuf, and other Chabad settlers moved from Chevron to settle in Jerusalem in 5607.
Story: An 5609 letter from the Chevron Chabad community to Montefiore explicitly says 'two years ago we settled in Jerusalem,' dating their move to 5607. This established the Chabad presence in Jerusalem alongside Chevron. R' Uri of Slonim, who had been an emissary in Chevron, also relocated to Jerusalem around this time.
Tags: chevron, jerusalem, kolel chabad

Title: Chabad chassidim begin migrating from Hebron to Jerusalem
Summary: In 5607 Chabad families began migrating from Hebron to Jerusalem, founding the Chabad presence in the holy city.
Story: Suffering under pressure from local landlords and the harsh treatment of gentile neighbors, Chabad families began leaving Hebron for Jerusalem in 5607 (1847). They rented homes in the northern Old City along Harat al-Wad — which Ashkenazim soon nicknamed 'Chevronim Street' (Hebron Street) — laying the foundation for the Chabad community in Jerusalem.
Tags: hebron, jerusalem, migration, chevronim street

Title: Chabad community established in Jerusalem
Summary: The Chabad community in Jerusalem was established in the year 5607.
Story: The founding of the Chabad presence in Jerusalem marked the beginning of an institutional infrastructure that would soon include trustees, census records, and ties to philanthropists abroad. By 5609 a formal census listed Rabbi Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin and Rabbi Uri Orenstein as appointed trustees. They would also sign the 5609 letter to Sir Moses Montefiore as the trustees of Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, settlement

Title: Chabad community settles in Jerusalem
Summary: Chabad chasidim settled in Jerusalem in 5607.
Story: Several leaders of the Chabad community in Jerusalem, including R' Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin, R' Ephraim Yitzchak Epstein, R' Uri Ornstein, R' Yosef Yehuda Leib Mishyov, and R' Tzvi Hirsch Fundaminsky, settled in the holy city in 5607. They later joined signatories on community petitions addressed to Sir Moses Montefiore.
Tags: jerusalem, chabad, settlement, eretz yisrael

Title: Chabad settlement established in Jerusalem
Summary: In 5607, Chabad chasidim established their organized settlement in Jerusalem.
Story: Following the Hebron settlement of 5581–83, Chabad presence was formally established in Jerusalem in 5607. This expansion broadened Kollel Chabad's footprint across the Holy Land and led to a Jerusalem-based administrative branch that worked alongside the Hebron council.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, settlement

Title: First responsa collection of the Alter Rebbe issued in Zhitomir
Summary: The Alter Rebbe's previously scattered responsa were gathered into a single booklet appended to the 1847 Zhitomir Shulchan Aruch.
Story: For the Zhitomir 5607 (1847) Shulchan Aruch edition, all the Alter Rebbe's known responsa—previously printed in their respective halachic contexts—were recollected and issued as a standalone 44-folio supplement. The collection was reprinted with every subsequent Shulchan Aruch edition.
Tags: alter rebbe, zhitomir, responsa, shu"t

Title: Government removes secret surveillance from Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: In the spring of 5607 the Russian authorities concluded there was no fault in the Tzemach Tzedek's conduct and lifted the secret surveillance imposed on him.
Story: The continuous secret-police watch had begun after the 5601 denunciation by maskilim and continued for some six years. After concluding no improper conduct, the government discontinued the surveillance. Documentation of the episode was later published in Pardes Chabad volume 4.
Tags: russia, tzemach-tzedek, surveillance, haskalah

Title: Hebron Chabad families relocate to Jerusalem
Summary: Beginning in 5607, several Hebron Chabad families migrated to Jerusalem due to oppression by local Muslim rulers.
Story: Unable to bear the burden of Sheikh Abdul Rahman's exactions and post-conquest hardship, several Chabad families left Hebron for Jerusalem starting in 5607. They settled in the northern part of the Old City on a street the Arabs called 'Harat al-Wad,' which became known among Ashkenazim as 'Rechov HaChevronim' — the Hebronites' Street — for the very families who settled there. In 5609 they described their motives in a moving letter to Montefiore.
Tags: hebron, chabad, jerusalem, abdul rahman, hebronim

Title: R' Asher ben Shimshon of London donates 1000 grush for Hebron mikveh
Summary: In 5607 R' Asher ben Shimshon of London donated 1000 grush via the Pekuam toward constructing a mikveh for Hebron's Chabad community after years of discussion.
Story: After lengthy debate about building a ritual bath in Hebron, the wealthy London philanthropist R' Asher ben Shimshon donated 1000 grush through the Amsterdam Pekidim and Amarkalim in 5607. Difficulties securing a suitable site led local administrators to request the funds be redirected, which the Pekuam refused without the donor's explicit consent.
Tags: hebron, london, mikveh, pekuam, asher ben shimshon

Title: R' Yechiel Cohen sent as joint shadar to USA from Hebron
Summary: R' Yechiel Cohen traveled to the United States as a shadar bearing letters from both Hebron communities.
Story: In 5607 (1847), R' Yechiel Cohen was sent as a shadar to the United States, carrying credentials from both the Sephardic and Chabad communities of Hebron. He stopped in London on the way and met the philanthropist R' Asher b'R' Shimshon. The Pekuam later sought clarification from the Chabad kollel about the trip's fundraising results.
Tags: yechiel cohen, shadar, usa, hebron, sephardic kollel, chabad kollel

Title: Rabbi Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin settles in Jerusalem
Summary: Rabbi Rivlin, a Chasid of the Alter Rebbe, settled in Jerusalem and became rabbi of the local Chasidim.
Story: His arrival helped establish an additional Chabad community in Jerusalem, complementing the Hebron settlement. His great-great-grandson Reuven Rivlin later served as Israel's president.
Tags: jerusalem, rivlin, chabad-community

Title: Russian government rabbinical schools established
Summary: The Russian government established 'rabbinical schools' in Vilna and Zhytomyr to train crown rabbis.
Story: In 1847, the czarist government opened state-run rabbinical schools in Vilna and Zhytomyr to formalize the crown rabbinate. The schools were heavily influenced by the Enlightenment, and their graduates were poorly regarded by the Jewish public; the schools eventually closed, but the crown rabbi institution persisted.
Tags: vilna, zhytomyr, crown rabbis, haskalah, russia

Title: Russian government removes surveillance on Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: In the spring of 5607 the Russian government lifted the continuous secret-police surveillance imposed on the Tzemach Tzedek after the 1841 denunciation.
Story: After roughly six years of constant watch, the authorities concluded that there was no fault to be found in the Rebbe's conduct. The decision closed the chapter of harassment that had begun with the maskilim's denunciation and the police search of his home.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, lubavitch, secret police, surveillance

Title: Zhitomir edition of Shulchan Aruch published with sons' approbations
Summary: A re-edited Shulchan Aruch with additional material and a preface by the Alter Rebbe's son R. Chaim Avraham was issued at the newly opened chassidic press in Zhitomir from 1847.
Story: When Russia's second Jewish press—the chassidic Zhitomir house—opened in 5607, the Tzemach Tzedek's circle entrusted it with a new Shulchan Aruch edition. The 1847–1848 Zhitomir printing added newly discovered material, a preface by R. Chaim Avraham, and approbations from the senior Chabad rabbis.
Tags: alter rebbe, zhitomir, shulchan aruch, chassidic press

Title: Count Orlov writes to Governor Golitsyn about lifting Tzemach Tzedek surveillance
Summary: Count Orlov, new head of the Third Section, wrote to Governor Golitsyn proposing to lift covert surveillance of the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: On 20 January 1847 (15 Shvat 5607), Count Orlov, who had succeeded Benckendorff as head of the Third Section, wrote to Prince A.M. Golitsyn, Governor-General of Vitebsk, Mogilev, and Smolensk. He noted that Schneersohn lived quietly, was uninvolved in conflicts, and had received the title of Honorary Citizen. Orlov asked Golitsyn for his opinion on whether the surveillance imposed in 1841 could now be lifted.
Tags: russia, tsarist surveillance, orlov, golitsyn, tzemach tzedek

Title: Governor Golitsyn endorses lifting Tzemach Tzedek's surveillance
Summary: Governor-General Golitsyn replied to Orlov endorsing the removal of covert surveillance from the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: On 7 March 1847 (2 Nissan 5607), Prince Golitsyn replied from Vitebsk to Count Orlov. He reported that State Councillor Gamalin had confirmed Schneersohn's title as Honorary Citizen and that the six-year gendarmerie surveillance found his conduct exemplary. Golitsyn formally endorsed lifting the secret watch that had begun in 1841.
Tags: russia, tsarist surveillance, golitsyn, orlov, tzemach tzedek

Title: Orlov asks Uvarov to consent to lifting Tzemach Tzedek surveillance
Summary: Count Orlov wrote to Education Minister Uvarov seeking his approval to halt the Tzemach Tzedek's covert surveillance.
Story: On 14 March 1847 (9 Nissan 5607), Count Orlov wrote to Count Sergey Uvarov, the Education Minister. He summarized Golitsyn's report and asked Uvarov, whose 1841 letter had triggered the surveillance, to formally consent to its removal. He noted that the local government's report seemed sufficient grounds to end the watch.
Tags: russia, tsarist surveillance, orlov, uvarov, tzemach tzedek

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's covert surveillance is officially lifted
Summary: Education Minister Uvarov consented to the formal termination of the secret surveillance on the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: On 19 March 1847 (14 Nissan 5607), the Education Ministry issued document number 2643. Count Uvarov informed Count Orlov that he fully agreed to terminate the gendarmerie's covert surveillance on Honorary Citizen Rabbi Mendel Schneersohn. The six-year covert watch that had begun on 21 July 1841 was thus officially closed.
Tags: russia, tsarist surveillance, uvarov, orlov, tzemach tzedek

Title: Tzemach Tzedek released from secret-police surveillance
Summary: In Nisan 5607 the Tzemach Tzedek's secret-police surveillance, in place during the clothing-decree period, came to an end.
Story: During the years surrounding the 1845 clothing decree the Tzemach Tzedek lived under the watch of the Tsarist secret police and feared writing letters in his own name on sensitive halachic matters, leaving such correspondence to his sons. The surveillance ended in Nisan 5607, after which he could resume more open conduct of his nesius.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, okhrana, russia, surveillance

Title: Pekuam refuses to redirect Hebron mikveh donation without donor consent
Summary: On 15 Elul 5607 the Amsterdam Pekuam wrote Hebron Chabad refusing to reassign R' Asher ben Shimshon's 1000-grush mikveh donation to other charities without his approval.
Story: Heads of the Pekidim and Amarkalim responded to Hebron Chabad's request to redirect the stalled mikveh donation toward a free-loan fund or bikur cholim. R' Asher had insisted any unused sum be returned to him to capitalize a different kollel, with interest funding synagogue lamp oil. The Pekuam declined to act without his decision.
Tags: hebron, mikveh, pekuam, amsterdam, asher ben shimshon

Title: Pekuam queries Hebron Chabad on R' Yechiel Cohen's American mission
Summary: The Pekuam wrote on 15 Elul to ask Hebron's Chabad leaders for accounting of R' Yechiel Cohen's American collections.
Story: On 15 Elul 5607 (August 27, 1847), the Pekuam Amsterdam committee wrote to the heads of Hebron's Chabad kollel inquiring about R' Yechiel Cohen's shadarus to America. The philanthropist R' Asher b'R' Shimshon of London had told them Cohen claimed to represent both Hebron kollelim. The Pekuam wanted to know exactly how much had been collected and what share Chabad had received.
Tags: pekuam, yechiel cohen, hebron, chabad kollel, usa, letter

Title: Ewald reports 16 Hebron Jewish families have relocated to Jerusalem
Summary: A letter by F.C. Ewald dated October 4, 1847 reported 16 Jewish families totaling 53 souls had moved from Hebron to Jerusalem.
Story: F.C. Ewald wrote on October 4, 1847 (published in London's Jewish Intelligence, January 1848) that since his previous report on the persecuted Jews of Hebron, 16 families had left and settled in Jerusalem, forming their own community of 53 souls. The letter is the earliest external attestation of the Hebron-to-Jerusalem migration of Chabad chassidim.
Tags: jerusalem, hebron, ewald, jewish intelligence, missionary observer

Title: First edition of Likkutei Torah printed in Zhitomir
Summary: The first edition of Likkutei Torah — the Alter Rebbe's chassidic discourses on Vayikra, Bamidbar, Devarim and Shir HaShirim — was brought to press in Zhitomir in תר"ח by the brothers R' Yehuda Leib and R' Chaim Shneur Zalman, sons of the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: The Likkutei Torah collected the Alter Rebbe's chassidic discourses on the latter three Chumashim and Shir HaShirim. Two of the Tzemach Tzedek's sons — the future Maharil of Kopust and R' Chaim Shneur Zalman — funded and oversaw the first printing in Zhitomir in תר"ח, with their names appearing on the title page and in the haskamos.
Tags: zhitomir, likkutei torah, tzemach tzedek, alter rebbe, chassidus

Title: Government rabbinical seminaries founded in Vilna and Zhitomir
Summary: The Russian government established two seminaries for rabbis and teachers in Vilna and Zhitomir in 1848.
Story: These seminaries emphasized secular studies and minimized traditional learning, with the government's aim of distancing students from Talmud study and traditional Jewish belief. They became the foundation for training future Crown Rabbis, though most graduates went on to attend universities rather than serve in the rabbinate.
Tags: russia, vilna, zhitomir, rabbinical seminary, haskalah

Title: HoD-Chabad distribution dispute resolved
Summary: The dispute between Kollel Chabad and Kollel HoD over Pekoam fund distribution shares dragged on until 5608 when it was finally resolved.
Story: The protracted dispute between Kollel Chabad and Kollel HoD over their respective shares of Pekoam funds, which had generated multiple rabbinical rulings both ways, finally ended in 5608. The Pekidim VeAmarkalim addressed the matter in numerous letters between the parties before the final compromise.
Tags: hod kollel, kollel chabad, pekoam, dispute resolution

Title: Likutei Torah printed by the Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek published the Alter Rebbe's Likutei Torah in 5608 (1848), with his own appended glosses.
Story: In 5608 (1848) the Tzemach Tzedek brought to press Likutei Torah, his curated anthology of his grandfather the Alter Rebbe's chassidic discourses. He added two manuscript volumes of his own hagahot (manuscripts 1101-1102) supplementing the printed text.
Tags: likutei torah, alter rebbe, tzemach tzedek, chassidut

Title: Likutei Torah printed in Zhitomir
Summary: In 5608 the second volume of the Alter Rebbe's discourses, edited by the Tzemach Tzedek, was printed at the newly licensed Zhitomir press under the title Likutei Torah.
Story: After the Zhitomir press received government approval in 5607 (1847), publishers turned to printing the long-delayed second volume of Torah Ohr. It appeared in 5608 (1848) under the new title Likutei Torah, becoming one of the foundational works of Chabad chasidic literature. The Tzemach Tzedek had spent decades collecting, editing, and annotating the manuscripts that made up the volume.
Tags: zhitomir, likutei torah, alter rebbe, tzemach tzedek

Title: Mendelstam visits the Tzemach Tzedek to push new curriculum
Summary: Maskil Arye Leib Mendelstam came to Lubavitch to urge the Tzemach Tzedek to approve new cheder textbooks.
Story: In the winter of 5608 (1848), Arye Leib Mendelstam, who had replaced Lilienthal at the Education Ministry, arrived in Lubavitch. He sought the Rebbe's approval for newly edited anthology textbooks meant for use in chadarim. The Tzemach Tzedek explained at length why these compilations should not be introduced into traditional Jewish elementary schools.
Tags: russia, haskalah, mendelstam, tzemach tzedek, cheder, lubavitch

Title: R' Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin makes aliyah to Jerusalem
Summary: The Gaon R' Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin, future overseer of Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem, immigrated to the Land of Israel in 5608.
Story: The 5615 census records R' Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin as having immigrated in 5608 (1848). Rabbinic approbations to his Ohalei Yosef (Jerusalem 5626) note he 'pitched his tent of Torah in Jerusalem for some eighteen years' until his passing on 12 Tammuz 5625. He became one of the lead signatories on the founding documents of Jerusalem's Chabad community.
Tags: jerusalem, rivlin, kollel chabad, aliyah

Title: Russian government establishes Rabbinical Commission
Summary: Russia established an official Rabbinical Commission in 1848 to convene periodically in Petersburg on religious matters affecting Russian Jewry.
Story: The commission was a state body that met in the capital approximately every several years to address questions concerning Russian Jewish religious life. Between its founding and the fall of the Tsarist regime, it convened six times, each session lasting one to four months and shaping policy on the rabbinate, education, and communal affairs.
Tags: russia, rabbinical commission, petersburg, tsarist government

Title: Tzemach Tzedek issues Likutei Torah in Zhitomir
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek published the second volume of his grandfather's chassidic discourses—renamed Likutei Torah—at the Zhitomir press in 5608 (1848).
Story: A decade after Russian censorship had blocked the planned sequel to Torah Or, the Tzemach Tzedek brought the Vayikra–Devarim and Shir Hashirim volume to the new Zhitomir chassidic press. Censorship constraints required a name change—Likutei Torah—and the two volumes thereafter circulated as a paired set.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, alter rebbe, zhitomir, likutei torah

Title: Tzemach Tzedek synagogue founded in Old City
Summary: A Chabad synagogue named for the third Rebbe was founded in the Jewish Quarter of the Old City of Jerusalem.
Story: Land was purchased in 1850 with help from Sir Moses Montefiore, and a building was erected. It became the only synagogue in the Jewish Quarter not destroyed by the Jordanian occupation between 1948 and 1967, and remains a vibrant center on Chabad Street today.
Tags: jerusalem, old-city, synagogue, tzemach-tzedek

Title: Tzemach Tzedek refuses to travel to Minsk to meet Mendelstam
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek wrote on 13 Adar I that he could not travel to Minsk and would not retreat from positions agreed at the 1843 commission.
Story: On 13 Adar I 5608, the Tzemach Tzedek replied to Mendelstam's invitation to come to Minsk for further talks. He wrote that he could not travel under any circumstance and that nothing in the curriculum agreed at the 1843 commission should be diminished. He reiterated that the structure they had set for Torah study was an absolute necessity for the children.
Tags: russia, haskalah, mendelstam, tzemach tzedek, cheder, minsk

Title: Hebron Chabad locates Cave of Othniel for mikveh site
Summary: On 8 Nisan 5608 the Pekuam celebrated word from Hebron Chabad that a suitable mikveh location—identified as the Cave of Othniel ben Kenaz—had been recovered from non-Jews.
Story: After receiving reports from Hebron Chabad dated 2 Kislev and 9 Iyar that a suitable mikveh site had been found, the Pekuam relayed the news to R' Asher ben Shimshon in London. He responded with an additional 550 grush to cover the increased cost. The Pekuam praised the recovery of the Cave of Othniel ben Kenaz from strangers but declined to solicit further donations due to widespread economic distress among former donors.
Tags: hebron, mikveh, pekuam, asher ben shimshon, cave of othniel

Title: Tzemach Tzedek again rejects Mendelstam's educational program
Summary: On 24 Nissan the Tzemach Tzedek wrote again to Mendelstam, firmly maintaining his earlier rejection of the new curriculum.
Story: On 24 Nissan 5608, the Tzemach Tzedek replied to Mendelstam's letter of Rosh Chodesh Nissan, received on 9 Nissan. He explained that after a month of deliberation, his view remained the same as what he had already conveyed on 13 Adar I and at the original commission. He pressed Mendelstam to accept his answer, written, he said, in truth and love.
Tags: russia, haskalah, mendelstam, tzemach tzedek, cheder

Title: R' Shlomo Zalman Kovelkin joins Hebron Kollel signatories
Summary: On 22 Iyar 5608, the Hebron Pekuam administrators directed the two remaining overseers to choose a third co-signer.
Story: By summer 5608, R' Shlomo Zalman ben Shmuel Sender Kovelkin was named alongside the two remaining overseers. Born in Polotsk in 5548, he was a regular signatory but not formally counted among the appointees in the 5609 census.
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, shlomo zalman kovelkin

Title: R. Baruch Mordechai Ettinga of Bobruisk receives haskamah on Likutei Torah
Summary: R. Baruch Mordechai Ettinga, Av Beis Din of Bobruisk, signed his approbation on the Likutei Torah on 17 Sivan 5608.
Story: R. Baruch Mordechai Ettinga served as rabbi of Bobruisk for some fifty years before making aliyah. His haskamah on Likutei Torah, dated 17 Sivan 5608, marks the last time he is documented outside of Eretz Yisrael. Shortly thereafter he prepared for his long-anticipated move to Jerusalem.
Tags: likutei torah, bobruisk, baruch mordechai ettinga, haskamah

Title: Death of R' Shmuel Halevi, first Chabad rabbi of Hebron
Summary: R' Shmuel Halevi Segal, first rabbi of the Chabad community in Hebron, died between 5609 and 5615.
Story: R' Shmuel Halevi Segal, who had served as maggid and de facto rabbi of the Hebron Chabad community since his arrival in 5584, died at some point between 5609 and 5615. In the 5609 census he is still listed among the community appointees, but in the 5615 census only his widow appears. His son R' Menachem Aryeh succeeded him as a leading figure of the community and served as a dayan.
Tags: hebron, chabad, rabbi, maggid

Title: Hebron Kollel leadership recorded in 5609 census
Summary: The 5609 Montefiore census formally listed the leadership of Hebron's Chabad community: Shmuel Segal, Avigdor, Shimon Menashe Chaikin, Avraham Dovber Chitrik, and Nachum Aryeh Halevi.
Story: These five men were registered as 'sages, rabbis, leaders, appointees and overseers' of the Hebron Chabad community. The same individuals signed the power-of-attorney document to Montefiore that year. R' Yosef Yehuda Leib Shmerling was listed separately as 'engaged in kollel matters.'
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, montefiore census, shmuel segal, shimon menashe chaikin

Title: Jerusalem Chabad community petitions Montefiore for a synagogue
Summary: In 5609 the founding Chabad settlers in Jerusalem wrote to Moses Montefiore describing their flight from Hebron and asking for funds to purchase a synagogue building.
Story: The early Chabad settlers in Jerusalem, numbering some 30 baalei batim, sent a letter to Sir Moses Montefiore in 5609. They described their forced migration from Hebron two years earlier, the absence of a fixed beis midrash and mikveh, and asked for support to acquire a property they had found, available on a 12,000-grush mashkanta. Twelve heads of the community, led by R' Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin, signed the appeal.
Tags: jerusalem, montefiore, synagogue, mikveh, kollel chabad

Title: Jerusalem Jews tell Montefiore agricultural plan is no longer viable
Summary: During Montefiore's 5609 visit, Jerusalem leaders explained that Egyptian rule had ended and farming the villages was now too dangerous.
Story: On Montefiore's return visit in 5609, the Jerusalem community informed him that conditions had reversed: with the end of Egyptian rule over Eretz Yisrael, weapons had returned to local hands and the countryside had become too dangerous for Jewish agricultural settlement. The letter was signed by several Chabad leaders in Jerusalem including R' Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin, R' Ephraim Yitzchak Epstein, and R' Uri Ornstein.
Tags: montefiore, jerusalem, agricultural settlement, ottoman empire, eretz yisrael

Title: Kollel Chabad letter to Montefiore signed by Jerusalem trustees
Summary: Rabbis Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin and Uri Orenstein signed as trustees of Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem in the letter to Montefiore.
Story: The 5609 census listed Rabbi Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin and Rabbi Uri Orenstein as the trustees of Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem. The same two trustees signed the kollel's letter to Sir Moses Montefiore that year. Their formal role marked early institutional recognition of the Chabad community within Jerusalem's Ashkenazi communal landscape.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, montefiore, rivlin, orenstein

Title: Letter from Hebron migrants to Montefiore
Summary: In 5609 Chabad family heads who had relocated from Hebron to Jerusalem wrote to Montefiore describing their reasons for leaving.
Story: Two years after relocating to Jerusalem, leaders of the migrant families wrote to Sir Moses Montefiore in 5609. They described the crushing oppression of the local rulers in Hebron and the influx of new arrivals which only intensified the burdens. They explained that the special share allocated to Abdul Rahman in the Chabad kollel's distributions consumed funds intended for their own livelihood, forcing them to thin out the Hebron community.
Tags: hebron, chabad, jerusalem, montefiore, abdul rahman

Title: Montefiore's second visit to Eretz Yisrael with community census
Summary: Moses Montefiore visited Eretz Yisrael and ordered a detailed census of every Jewish community in every city.
Story: This was one of six Montefiore visits to the Holy Land. On each (except 5617, too close to the previous) he commissioned censuses listing every Jew by community, plus the community's institutions and leaders. The originals are preserved in his London archive, with photocopies in the Jerusalem library.
Tags: montefiore, census, eretz yisrael, hebron, jerusalem

Title: New EY fund distribution order established
Summary: In 5609 a new distribution formula was instituted dividing Pekoam funds into 168 parts: 67 to the Sephardim and 101 to the Ashkenazic kollels.
Story: From 5609 the distribution formula was fixed: after expenses, funds were divided into 168 parts. The Sephardic kollels received 67/168. From the remaining 101/168, the HoD kollel took a third, and the remaining two-thirds was divided into 101 parts, of which Kollel Chabad in Hebron received 9/101.
Tags: pekoam, distribution, kollelim, kollel chabad, sephardim, hod

Title: R' Yechiel Cohen sent again to USA from Beit El kabbalists
Summary: R' Yechiel Cohen was sent again to America, this time from the Beit El kabbalist beit midrash in Jerusalem, while still apparently linked to Chabad's kollel.
Story: In 5609 (1849), R' Yechiel Cohen was sent again to America, this time on behalf of the Beit El kabbalists' beit midrash in Jerusalem. Despite the change of sender, the Chabad kollel of Hebron remained connected to the mission, as seen in subsequent Pekuam correspondence. The journey extended for several years.
Tags: yechiel cohen, shadar, usa, beit el, jerusalem, chabad kollel

Title: Hebron Chabad petitions Montefiore for a Jewish hospital in Jerusalem
Summary: Hebron Chabad leaders wrote to Montefiore in Menachem Av 5609 urging the urgent construction of a Jewish hospital in Jerusalem.
Story: The letter warned that without a Jewish hospital, sick Jews would be forced to seek care at the missionaries' hospital. The writers also asked that the Jerusalem doctor be authorized to travel to Hebron when called, since the town was too small to support its own physician at that time.
Tags: montefiore, hospital, hebron, jerusalem, missionaries, kollel chabad

Title: R' Moshe Meisels of Hebron passes away
Summary: R' Moshe Meisels, a senior figure of the Hebron Chabad community, died in Menachem Av 5609.
Story: R' Moshe Meisels was one of the leading signatories of Hebron Chabad emissary documents in the 1840s. He passed away in the month of Menachem Av 5609, a fact later used to redate undated communal documents bearing his signature to before that point.
Tags: hebron, meisels, kollel chabad

Title: R' Moshe Meisels passes away in Hebron
Summary: R' Moshe Meisels, author of 'Shirat Moshe' on the 613 commandments and a Chabad leader in Hebron, passed away on 24 Menachem Av 1849.
Story: R' Moshe Meisels, author of 'Shirat Moshe' on the 613 commandments, passed away in Hebron on 24 Menachem Av 1849. A longtime trustee of the Vilna community who later spied for Czar Alexander I against Napoleon and met Napoleon personally twice, he settled in Tzfat circa 1816 and moved to Hebron in 1823, where he became one of the leading administrators of the Chabad kollel.
Tags: moshe meisels, hebron, petira, shirat moshe, 613 mitzvot

Title: R' Yehoshua Eliyahu signs Horki community takkanos
Summary: R' Yehoshua Eliyahu ben Yosef signed community regulations for Horki on 3 Teves 5610.
Story: As rabbi of Horki, R' Yehoshua Eliyahu signed takkanos for the community on 3 Teves 5610, published in Ohalei Shem. He had succeeded R' Yehoshua of Horki, who died in 5602, and would later be succeeded by R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark.
Tags: yehoshua eliyahu, horki, takkanos, rabbinate, chabad

Title: Apatov chassidic shul founded in Vilna
Summary: The Apatov synagogue at 21 Vilenskaya Street in Vilna was founded around 5610.
Story: Apatov served as a Chassidic house of prayer in Vilna for decades before it was acquired by Chabad. Its existence within a city long associated with the misnagdim made it a logistical anchor for Chabad activity in Lithuania. The shul would later host both a major rabbinical conference and a branch of Tomchei Tmimim.
Tags: vilna, apatov, chassidic synagogue, lithuania

Title: Apatov synagogue built in Vilna
Summary: Around 5610 the wealthy R. Yehuda Apatov built a large synagogue and beis tefilah in his courtyard on Wileńska Street in Vilna.
Story: Apatov endowed an entire courtyard to maintain the building and support scholars worthy of rabbinic ordination, registering the gift under imperial law to secure its permanence. The building would later become the central Chabad synagogue of Vilna.
Tags: vilna, apatov, yehuda apatov, 5610, synagogue

Title: Government publishes Rambam excerpts under guise of Rebbe's approval
Summary: The Petersburg government published abridged Rambam halacha booklets for chadarim, framed as if with the Tzemach Tzedek's approval.
Story: In 5610 (1850), the Russian government in Petersburg printed condensed study booklets, 'Some Laws from the Yad Hachazaka of the Rambam,' for use in chadarim. The title page falsely implied the Rebbe's approval by referencing his responsa. This contradicted the Tzemach Tzedek's clear opposition to teaching such anthologies, which he considered useless to the children.
Tags: russia, haskalah, petersburg, rambam, cheder, tzemach tzedek

Title: Pekidim VeAmarkalim compromise settlement document
Summary: In 5610 the Pekidim VeAmarkalim summarized the distribution outcomes in a formal compromise settlement document.
Story: The 5610 compromise document of the Pekidim VeAmarkalim summarized the evolution of Eretz Yisrael fund distribution from 5585 onward through the various adjustments favoring HoD, ending with the formula codified in 5609 that remained in force at the time of writing.
Tags: pekoam, settlement document, distribution, kollelim

Title: R' Shmuel Segal dies, leadership reshuffled
Summary: In the summer of 5610, R' Shmuel Segal's name was dropped from the Hebron kollel leadership, around the time of his death.
Story: His passing left R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, R' Avigdor, and R' Uri Volabriker on the kollel board. The reshuffling marked another step in R' Shimon Menashe's gradual rise to becoming the dominant figure in Hebron Chabad affairs.
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, shmuel segal, uri, avigdor

Title: R' Baruch Mordechai Itigna immigrates to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: R' Baruch Mordechai Itigna, longtime moreh tzedek of Bobruisk, made aliyah and settled in Jerusalem.
Story: After serving as moreh tzedek of Bobruisk until 5611, R' Baruch Mordechai Itigna immigrated to the Holy Land and settled in Jerusalem. His departure opened the way for R' Hillel of Paritch to be appointed as sole rabbi of Bobruisk, including over the misnagdic community.
Tags: baruch mordechai itigna, bobruisk, jerusalem, aliyah, eretz yisrael, chabad

Title: R. Baruch Mordechai Ettinga makes aliyah to Jerusalem
Summary: R. Baruch Mordechai Ettinga, after fifty years as rabbi of Bobruisk, fulfilled his lifelong dream and settled in Jerusalem in 5611.
Story: Already in 5574-5 R. Baruch Mordechai had asked the Mitteler Rebbe about settling in Eretz Yisrael. Although he was instructed to remain in Bobruisk and continued there for another 35 years, in 5611 he finally made the move. By then the Chabad community in Jerusalem had grown, and he chose to settle there rather than in Hebron or Tzefas.
Tags: jerusalem, bobruisk, aliyah, baruch mordechai ettinga, russia

Title: R. Baruch Mordechai Itinga settles in Jerusalem
Summary: After many years serving as rabbi of Bobruisk, R. Baruch Mordechai Itinga ascended to the Land of Israel and settled in Jerusalem.
Story: Around 1851, more than thirty-five years after the Mitteler Rebbe had advised against his aliyah, R. Baruch Mordechai Itinga finally ascended to the Land of Israel and settled in Jerusalem. He had served for an extended period as rabbi of Bobruisk in the intervening years. He died in Jerusalem just over a year later, on 14 Elul 1852.
Tags: jerusalem, bobruisk, baruch mordechai itinga, aliyah

Title: Rabbi Baruch Mordechai of Babruysk moves to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: Rabbi Baruch Mordechai, longtime rav of Babruysk, departs for the Holy Land circa 5611.
Story: Around 5611, the chassidic gaon Rabbi Baruch Mordechai left his rabbinate in Babruysk to settle in Eretz Yisrael. Following his departure the townspeople accepted Rabbi Hillel of Paritch as their rav and av beis din.
Tags: baruch mordechai, babruysk, eretz yisrael, aliyah, rabbinate

Title: Tzemach Tzedek adds discourses to Likutei Torah
Summary: In 5611 the Tzemach Tzedek issued additional discourses for Likutei Torah.
Story: Continuing to edit his grandfather's discourses, the Tzemach Tzedek published a set of supplements to Likutei Torah in 1851.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, likutei torah

Title: Vienna Haggadah with Italian translation in Latin characters
Summary: The first Haggadah with the Italian translation printed in Latin characters was issued in Vienna in 5611 by Meir Ranbarger.
Story: In 5611 (1851), a Haggadah with an Italian translation in Latin script, printed opposite the Hebrew, was issued in Vienna by Meir Ranbarger. Earlier Haggadot had printed the Italian translation in Hebrew characters, making this a milestone in vernacular Haggadah typography.
Tags: haggadah, vienna, italian-translation, ranbarger

Title: R' Menachem Aryeh Segal replaces R' Avigdor in kollel
Summary: In mid-winter 5611, R' Avigdor stepped down from the Hebron kollel leadership and R' Menachem Aryeh ben Shmuel Segal took his place.
Story: The administrators reported that R' Avigdor had withdrawn due to old age and wished him renewed vigor. They welcomed his replacement R' Menachem Aryeh — son of the late R' Shmuel Segal — citing 'the threefold cord that is not quickly broken.'
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, menachem aryeh segal, avigdor

Title: Maharil of Kopust writes to R' Aharon of Belnitz about Bobruisk rabbinate
Summary: Maharil of Kopust wrote to R' Aharon Lipschitz of Belnitz urging him to travel with Bobruisk lay leaders to finalize his appointment as their rabbi.
Story: Dated 24 Sivan 5611, this letter from the son of the Tzemach Tzedek to R' Aharon Lipschitz indicates that Bobruisk's leaders had come to receive him as rav. The appointment ultimately did not materialize, and R' Hillel of Paritch was chosen instead.
Tags: maharil kopust, aharon lipschitz, belnitz, bobruisk, rabbinate, chabad

Title: Pekuam complains about R' Yechiel Cohen's prolonged American mission
Summary: On 25 Tammuz, the Pekuam wrote that New York donors had instructed them not to give Hebron a penny because of R' Yechiel Cohen's continued shadarus.
Story: On 25 Tammuz 5611 (July 24, 1851), the Pekuam wrote to Hebron's Chabad kollel that on several occasions they had received donations from New York with explicit instructions not to give a single penny to Hebron — because R' Yechiel Cohen was still touring America after a very long time. The letter is preserved in Pinkas 11 of the Pekuam records.
Tags: pekuam, yechiel cohen, hebron, usa, letter

Title: Passing of Rabbi Aharon David Gordon in Shklov
Summary: Rabbi Aharon David Gordon, stepson of Rabbi Avraham Avli of Vilna, died in Shklov on 12 Av 5611.
Story: Rabbi Aharon David Gordon (Shklover), stepson of Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler of Vilna, passed away in Shklov on 12 Av 5611 (August 9, 1851). He and his brother had organized about sixty of Rabbi Avraham Avli's responsa, intending to publish them as Be'er Avraham, though that edition never appeared.
