After his death the manuscripts passed to his son.
Tags: shklov, gordon, posveler, manuscripts

Title: Pekuam further correspondence about R' Yechiel Cohen
Summary: The Pekuam continued discussing R' Yechiel Cohen's American shadarus in a letter of 28 Tishrei.
Story: On 28 Tishrei 5612 (October 23, 1851), the Pekuam wrote another letter to Hebron continuing to discuss R' Yechiel Cohen's prolonged American shadarus and its impact on New York donations. The letter is recorded in Pinkas 11 of the Pekuam records.
Tags: pekuam, yechiel cohen, hebron, usa, letter

Title: Abd al-Rahman escapes Jerusalem prison and resumes ruling Hebron
Summary: In early 1852 Hebron's persecutor Abd al-Rahman was briefly chained in Jerusalem's seraglio, then escaped over the city wall and reinstalled himself as mutasallim, immediately fining the Jewish community.
Story: Captured by the Ottoman government, Abd al-Rahman was held briefly in chains in Jerusalem's seraglio before being permitted to walk freely with three guarantors. He escaped one night carrying his chains, jumping from the city wall, and reinstalled himself as mutasallim of Hebron. He immediately began imposing heavy fines on the population, especially the Jews.
Tags: hebron, ottoman empire, abd al-rahman, persecution, mutasallim

Title: Latest dated responsum in Mehadura Batra Orach Chaim manuscript
Summary: Manuscript 1017, the Orach Chaim mehadura batra, was bound around 5612, the date of its latest responsum.
Story: Manuscript 1017 contains the Tzemach Tzedek's reorganized Orach Chaim responsa, drawing on lost volumes 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 14 (the source volumes likely lost in the Lubavitch fire). Its latest internal date, 5612 (folio 276a), establishes the rough binding date.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, mehadura batra, manuscript 1017, orach chaim

Title: R. Baruch Mordechai Itinga dies in Jerusalem
Summary: R. Baruch Mordechai Itinga, son-in-law of the av beit din of Vilna, died in Jerusalem on 14 Elul 1852.
Story: On 14 Elul 1852, R. Baruch Mordechai Itinga passed away in Jerusalem, just over a year after settling there. He had been a prominent Vilna chassid and son-in-law of R. Shmuel, av beit din of Vilna, and served as rabbi of Bobruisk for many years before his aliyah.
Tags: jerusalem, baruch mordechai itinga, death, 14 elul

Title: Sheikh Abd al-Rahman terrorizes Hebron Jews
Summary: Beginning in 5612, Sheikh Abd al-Rahman tormented the Hebron Jewish community with violent extortion until the early 5614s.
Story: The 5618 shadarut letter described how the 'wicked Gentiles of Hebron' imposed a heavy yoke on the Jews, extracting money through false accusations and lawless violence. The sheikh was eventually arrested and taken to Istanbul in iron chains, where he received a death sentence.
Tags: hebron, abd al-rahman, ottoman, persecution

Title: Third edition of Siddur with Da"Ch printed in Königsberg
Summary: The third edition of the Alter Rebbe's Siddur with Chassidic explanations was printed in Königsberg, Prussia in תרי"ב at the press of A. Zamter, with most copies disguised as a much older Berditchev printing to evade Russian censorship.
Story: Following the תקצ"ז decree against Hebrew presses in Russia, presses in Prussian border towns — Königsberg, Johannisberg, Memel, Danzig — produced sefarim for the Russian market. Books destined for smuggling bore disguised title pages omitting the printer and bearing a falsely earlier date. Most copies of this siddur read 'printed in Berditchev' with the year encoded as תקצ"א, but a small batch made for Königsberg's local Jews received a second title page openly declaring 'Königsberg... at the press of A. Zamter, in the year ועבדתם את ה' בכל לבבכם.'
Tags: koenigsberg, siddur im da'ch, alter rebbe, prussia, censorship, smuggling

Title: Tzemach Tzedek acquires the Sederin estate as Hereditary Citizen
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek formally acquired the Sederin estate, securing Hereditary Honorary Citizen status for himself and his descendants.
Story: In 5612 (1852), Bet Rebbi records that the Tzemach Tzedek secured from the government the inherited citizenship title (Potomstvennoe) for himself and his descendants. As part of this status he purchased the Sederin estate in the Bobruisk area of Minsk province, registered in his name. Reports linked the elevation to his role in encouraging Jewish agricultural settlement.
Tags: russia, hereditary honorary citizen, sederin, bobruisk, minsk, tzemach tzedek, agriculture

Title: Death of R' Nechemiah of Dubrovna, gabbai of Kollel Chabad
Summary: R' Nechemiah of Dubrovna, first general gabbai for the Tzemach Tzedek's Eretz Yisrael fund, died on 15 Shevat.
Story: R' Nechemiah of Dubrovna, author of Divrei Nechemiah, served as the general gabbai appointed by the Tzemach Tzedek to receive funds in the diaspora destined for the Chabad community in Eretz Yisrael. After his death on 15 Shevat 5612, the position passed to R' Zev of Retzitzeh and R' Avraham, rabbi of Drogichov. His death is recorded in Beis Rebbi.
Tags: nechemiah of dubrovna, kollel chabad, tzemach tzedek, divrei nechemiah, russia, fundraising

Title: Consul James Finn intervenes during Hebron extortion crisis
Summary: On 9 August 1852 British Consul James Finn received reports of severe disturbances in Hebron and traveled there to restrain Abd al-Rahman's outrages against the Jews.
Story: Reports reached the British consulate that Abd al-Rahman intended to extort 40 purses (about 200 pounds) from Hebron's Jewish quarter that very morning. Finn traveled to Hebron where the European hospital doctor confirmed the news. Finn described the Jews' terror—pale faces and darting eyes, hanging on every word and movement. His presence temporarily restrained the persecutor, though the depredations resumed after Finn left.
Tags: hebron, british consul, james finn, abd al-rahman, persecution

Title: R. Baruch Mordechai Ettinga passes away in Jerusalem
Summary: After roughly a year in the Holy City, R. Baruch Mordechai Ettinga died in Jerusalem on 14 Elul 5612.
Story: R. Baruch Mordechai had only enjoyed his long-awaited residence in Jerusalem for about a year before his passing. Letters from the Pekuamim sent in advance of Rosh Hashanah 5613 still presumed him living, and the funds dispatched arrived after his death. His matzevah, copied in Yerushalayim vol. 1, mistakenly led some later researchers to place his death in 5617.
Tags: jerusalem, baruch mordechai ettinga, bobruisk

Title: Maharash's first dated chassidic discourse manuscript
Summary: The earliest dated chassidic discourse hanacha in Maharash's hand is from Parshat Beshalach, Motzaei Menucha, 5613.
Story: Among the manuscripts inherited and produced by Maharash, the first dated hanacha (transcript) in his own handwriting is titled 'Beshalach, Motzaei Menucha, 5613.' These transcripts recorded discourses of his father, the Tzemach Tzedek, and would form a core part of the Chabad manuscript collection later catalogued by his descendants.
Tags: maharash, chassidus, manuscripts, hanachos, beshalach

Title: R' Shneur Zalman Epstein joins Hebron Kollel
Summary: In the summer of 5613, R' Uri left the Hebron kollel leadership and R' Shneur Zalman ben Ephraim Yitzchak Epstein was named in his place.
Story: Curiously, R' Shneur Zalman Epstein was registered as a Jerusalem resident in all the censuses, suggesting that the senior Jerusalem leader was also listed among the Hebron appointees because Hebron was then the seat of the central Kollel Chabad council.
Tags: hebron, jerusalem, kollel chabad, shneur zalman epstein

Title: Rebbe Maharash begins recording his father's discourses
Summary: Rebbe Maharash recorded hanachot of his father's discourses in 5614.
Story: Few people wrote down hanachot of the Tzemach Tzedek's discourses because he generally recorded them himself. Among those who did was his son the future Rebbe Maharash, whose 1854 transcript survives in the library archive.
Tags: rebbe maharash, tzemach tzedek, hanachot

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's letter to Avrutch
Summary: In 5614 (1854) the Tzemach Tzedek wrote a letter to his son, the future Rebbe of Avrutch.
Story: Among the Tzemach Tzedek's preserved correspondence is a 5614 (1854) letter to his son R. Yisrael Noach, later Rebbe of Avrutch. It was published as Igeret 58 in the Tzemach Tzedek's Igrot Kodesh.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, avrutch, rebbe rayatz, letter

Title: Consul Finn halts Salama's persecution of Hebron Jews
Summary: On 8 February 1854 Consul James Finn ended the harassment that Salama, brother of Abd al-Rahman, was inflicting on Hebron's Jewish community.
Story: James Finn recorded in his diary: 'In Hebron I succeeded in ending the harassment which Salama, brother of Abd al-Rahman Amr, was inflicting on the Jews.' His interventions in Hebron during 1853-1856 were later documented in his book 'Stirring Times, or Records from Jerusalem Consular Chronicles' (London 1878), an important record of the persecutions endured by Hebron's Jewish community.
Tags: hebron, british consul, james finn, salama, persecution

Title: British Consul Finn reports on Abdul Rahman's extortion
Summary: On 28 August 1854 British Consul James Finn wrote to Lord Stratford de Redcliffe detailing Sheikh Abdul Rahman's extortion of Hebron Jewry.
Story: In late summer 5614, British Consul James Finn in Jerusalem wrote to Lord Stratford de Redcliffe describing the Hebron Jews' suffering at the hands of Abdul Rahman. He reported a unique feature of the sheikh's extortion: collecting a fixed share of the seasonal halukkah donations from European Jewry on which the Hebron Jews depended. His name was entered in the kollel ledgers as a stipend recipient, and he would send representatives to collect three days before the scheduled distribution.
Tags: hebron, abdul rahman, british consul, chabad, extortion

Title: R' Yissachar Ber Melamed writes a veksel in Lubavitch
Summary: On Friday, 12 Mar Cheshvan תרט"ו, R' Yissachar Ber Melamed signed a veksel — an open promissory note — in the town of Lubavitch, payable to the bearer for three silver rubles by mid-Adar.
Story: Open promissory notes (vekslach) were widely used in shtetl commerce: merchants could pay for goods with them, and sellers could pass them on as cash. The bearer would collect from the original signer on the appointed day. This veksel, written in Lubavitch by R' Yissachar Ber son of Meir Melamed, is one of three surviving shtarot from the town between תרט"ו-תרח"י.
Tags: lubavitch, veksel, commerce, shtar

Title: Montefiore census documents Chabad synagogues in Jerusalem and Hebron
Summary: The 5615 Montefiore census recorded the synagogues and study halls of Chabad communities in Jerusalem and Hebron.
Story: The 5615 Montefiore census, published as 'Luach Shemos HaBatei Knesios D'Chabad,' documented Chabad's synagogues and study halls in Jerusalem and Hebron. It described a Jerusalem beis midrash named 'Dat Moshe ViYehudis' (after Montefiore) where twelve bachurim studied gemara, poskim and chassidus under R' Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin.
Tags: montefiore, jerusalem, hebron, census, synagogue

Title: Montefiore's third visit and Hebron Bikur Cholim record
Summary: Montefiore's 5615 census recorded Hebron's Bikur Cholim society as providing 'doctor, medicines and lodging' for the sick.
Story: There was still no resident physician in Hebron, so the society either transported patients to Jerusalem or brought the Jerusalem doctor down. The Bikur Cholim entry is one of the earliest documented Hebron Chabad welfare institutions.
Tags: montefiore, census, hebron, bikur cholim

Title: R' Dan Tomarkin appointed gabbai of Kollel Chabad
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek appointed R' Dan Tomarkin of Rogachov as gabbai of Kollel Chabad in 5615.
Story: In 5615 the Tzemach Tzedek appointed the wealthy chasid R' Dan Tomarkin of Rogachov as a gabbai of Kollel Chabad, a position he held for over thirty years. He initially served alongside others on the committee and later became the general gabbai, transferring funds to the Tzemach Tzedek for distribution. Because R' Dan lived in Rogachov, the committee that became known as the 'Rogachov Vaad' was established in that city.
Tags: dan tomarkin, kollel chabad, tzemach tzedek, rogachov, fundraising

Title: R' Dan Tomarkin of Rogachov serves as chief gabbai of Kollel Chabad
Summary: From around 5615 R' Dan Tomarkin of Rogachov was appointed by the Tzemach Tzedek as chief gabbai of Kollel Chabad, a role he held for over thirty years.
Story: Joining the existing gabbaim R' A. of Rogachov and R' Yitzchok Aizik of Bichov, Tomarkin became the dominant figure in administering Kollel Chabad's overseas fundraising. The Tzemach Tzedek himself prepared the lists of distribution recipients, and after the Rebbe's passing in 5626 Tomarkin continued under the leadership of the Tzemach Tzedek's sons. He led the Rogachover Vaad that prepared the distribution lists in the decades that followed.
Tags: rogachov, dan tomarkin, kollel chabad, tzemach tzedek, gabbai

Title: R' Hillel of Paritch declines to serve as borer due to a vow
Summary: R' Hillel of Paritch refused appeals from the Tzemach Tzedek and his son to be the borer in the MaHaRiL's din Torah, citing a 31-year-old vow never to serve as judge or arbitrator, only as a deciding shalish.
Story: The Tzemach Tzedek and his son MaHaRiL both wrote to the famed mashpia R' Hillel of Paritch (author of Pelach HaRimon) asking him to serve as their borer. Hillel replied that 31 years earlier he had taken a vow on da'as ha-makom never to act as dayan or borer, only as a deciding shalish — a safeguard he refused to lift even for the Rebbe's family. He had instituted this restriction because borerim sometimes act 'shelo k'das' by advocating only for the side that chose them.
Tags: hillel of paritch, tzemach tzedek, maharil of kopust, vow, halacha

Title: R' Shneur Zalman Schneersohn added to Hebron Kollel
Summary: In 5615, R' Shneur Zalman ben Menachem Yosef Schneersohn — known by the initials SHZBNY — was added to the Hebron kollel leadership.
Story: Like R' Shneur Zalman Epstein before him, SHZBNY was registered as a Jerusalem resident in the censuses. His inclusion among the Hebron overseers reinforces the pattern that senior Jerusalem leaders were named to the central Hebron council during this period.
Tags: hebron, jerusalem, kollel chabad, schneersohn family

Title: Tzemach Tzedek pens responsum seeking to release R' Hillel's vow
Summary: In response to R' Hillel of Paritch's refusal, the Tzemach Tzedek composed a teshuvah seeking a halachic path to permit annulment of Hillel's vow against serving as borer, later printed in Shu"t Tzemach Tzedek Yoreh Deah siman 181.
Story: When R' Hillel cited his old vow as blocking his service as borer, the Tzemach Tzedek personally researched whether the vow could be released. He drafted a responsum on the question, joined by responsa from R' Yitzchak Aizik of Homel (author of Chana Ariel) and R' Shneur Zalman of Vielizh. The Tzemach Tzedek's reply was eventually published in Shu"t Tzemach Tzedek, Yoreh Deah siman 181.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, responsa, yoreh deah, hillel of paritch, vow, halacha

Title: Y.Y. Benyamin publishes a map of the Land of Israel
Summary: Y.Y. Benyamin issued a map of the Land of Israel in 5615 (1855).
Story: Among the antique maps of the Holy Land preserved in the library is this 1855 production by Y.Y. Benyamin, a mid-nineteenth-century traveler-cartographer.
Tags: map, land of israel, benyamin

Title: MaHaRiL writes to R' Aaron of Belinitz seeking him as judge
Summary: R' Yehuda Leib (later Admur of Kopust) wrote to R' Aharon of Belinitz on the night of 15 Menachem Av תרט"ו, requesting that he serve as a judge (borer) in a din Torah on his behalf.
Story: While his father the Tzemach Tzedek was still alive, the future MaHaRiL of Kopust faced a major din Torah and needed to choose an arbitrator. On the night of 15 Av תרט"ו he wrote to R' Aharon Lipshitz, moreh tzedek of Belinitz, declaring his settled intent to choose him. The letter is one of four surviving epistles documenting the affair, and represents the start of a months-long negotiation over the choice of arbitrator.
Tags: maharil of kopust, aharon of belinitz, din torah, tzemach tzedek, bechirah

Title: MaHaRiL switches choice of borer from R' Hillel to R' Aharon
Summary: On the night of 4 Mar Cheshvan תרט"ז, MaHaRiL wrote to R' Aharon of Belinitz that — given Hillel's refusal — he and his father had decided that Aharon should now serve as borer, and pressed him urgently to accept.
Story: Months of correspondence with R' Hillel of Paritch failed to produce his acceptance as borer. On 4 Mar Cheshvan תרט"ז the MaHaRiL wrote definitively to R' Aharon of Belinitz that the decision had been made to switch back to him, promising to cover travel costs and a fitting honorarium, and stressing 'I have no one else fit for this matter.' The location of the din Torah was still undetermined, perhaps near Berditchev.
Tags: maharil of kopust, aharon of belinitz, hillel of paritch, din torah

Title: R' Avraham Dovid Lavut moves from Romanovka to Nikolaev
Summary: In 5616, the chassidic scholar R' Avraham Dovid Lavut — later the Rebbe's grandfather — left Romanovka, where he had run a yeshiva and talmud Torah, to take up the rabbinate of Nikolaev.
Story: Lavut, author of Kav Naki, headed a yeshiva and talmud Torah in Romanovka and was its mora d'asra. A surviving letter of support signed by the Tzemach Tzedek's sons R' Chaim Shneur Zalman, R' Yehuda Leib and R' Yisrael Noach urging anash to back this yeshiva must therefore date between 5605 and 5615. In 5616 (1856) Lavut relocated to Nikolaev, a move that brackets the latest possible date of the letter.
Tags: avraham dovid lavut, romanovka, nikolaev, rebbe's grandfather, yeshiva

Title: R' Avraham Dovid Lavut moves to Nikolayev as rabbi
Summary: Rabbi Avraham Dovid Lavut, author of Kav Naki and Shaar HaKollel, moved from Romanovka to serve as rabbi of Nikolayev in 5616.
Story: In 5616, Rabbi Avraham Dovid Lavut, the grandfather of the Rebbe (Ramash) and author of Kav Naki and Shaar HaKollel, moved from his rabbinic post in Romanovka to become rabbi of Nikolayev. He would serve as rabbi of Nikolayev until his passing in 5650.
Tags: lavut, nikolayev, romanovka, rabbinate

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's Shulchan Aruch printed in Zhitomir
Summary: In 5616 R. Avraham haKohen of Lubavitch was among the rabbis approving the Zhitomir printing of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch.
Story: The Lubavitch moreh tzedek R. Avraham b. Avigdor haKohen joined the approbations for the 5616 (1856) Zhitomir edition of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch. He served as moreh tzedek of Lubavitch throughout most of the later years of the Tzemach Tzedek, occasionally co-signing responsa or signing in the Rebbe's stead.
Tags: shulchan aruch harav, zhitomir, abraham hacohen, lubavitch

Title: R' Aharon of Belinitz formally agrees to serve as MaHaRiL's borer
Summary: By Monday of parshat Naso תרט"ז, R' Aharon of Belinitz had sent his consent to serve as borer for MaHaRiL, who replied that the news had 'revived our soul.'
Story: The negotiation dragged on for nearly a year. Only at the start of summer תרט"ז did R' Aharon respond affirmatively, his reply delivered by his son. MaHaRiL responded warmly on yom beis parshas Naso, promising to share with him the responsa from the Tzemach Tzedek, R' Yitzchak Aizik of Homel, and R' Shneur Zalman of Vielizh.
Tags: maharil of kopust, aharon of belinitz, din torah

Title: R' Yaakov 'Kuli' Slonim passes away in Hebron
Summary: R' Yaakov (Kuli) Slonim, husband of Menucha Rachel and a leader of the Hebron community, died on 2 Tevet 5617.
Story: R' Yaakov Slonim, married to Menucha Rachel daughter of the Mitteler Rebbe, served as gabbai of the Hebron synagogue and chazzan on the High Holidays. He headed both the Chevra Kadisha and the Gemilut Chasadim society in Hebron. He passed away on 2 Tevet 5617, leaving three sons and three daughters.
Tags: hebron, slonim family, chevra kadisha, gemilut chasadim

Title: Fire in Lubavitch destroys responsa manuscripts
Summary: A fire in Lubavitch between 5616 and 5618 destroyed many of the Tzemach Tzedek's bound responsa volumes.
Story: Compilers' notes at the end of the printed Tzemach Tzedek responsa state that 'our holy master wrote many responsa on this, and in the last fire, woe to us, the book was burned and only this responsum remained.' The Rebbe's notes, citing manuscripts datable to 5608–5616, place the fire between roughly 5616 and 5618. The disaster accounts for the loss of most of volumes 1–14.
Tags: lubavitch, fire, manuscripts, tzemach tzedek, lost works

Title: First Haggadah printed in the United States
Summary: One of the earliest American Haggadot, with English translation, was printed in New York in 5617.
Story: Around 5617 (1857), Henry Frank printed one of the first Haggadot in the United States, in New York. The 72-page volume featured an English translation opposite the Hebrew and included illustrations.
Tags: haggadah, united-states, new-york, english-translation

Title: Great fire destroys Tzemach Tzedek's courtyard in Lubavitch
Summary: Between 5616 and 5618 a great fire in Lubavitch destroyed the Tzemach Tzedek's home, the synagogue, and much of his library and manuscripts.
Story: The Rebbe relocated to the estate of a local nobleman outside town while the courtyard was rebuilt on a more spacious scale. A letter from his son Rabbi Chaim Schneur Zalman (later the Rebbe of Liadi) survives, dated 8 Iyar, appealing to chassidim to contribute toward the rebuilding effort. The expanded compound included an enlarged synagogue and dedicated prayer halls within the Rebbe's own house.
Tags: lubavitch, tzemach tzedek, fire, library

Title: Great fire of Lubavitch destroys Tzemach Tzedek manuscripts
Summary: A great fire swept through Lubavitch in 5617, burning much of the town including the Tzemach Tzedek's home and many of his unpublished manuscripts in both nigleh and chasidus.
Story: The fire devastated Lubavitch including the Tzemach Tzedek's residence and the homes of chasidim who held his manuscripts on loan. Twenty volumes were lost at the home of Rabbi Avraham, the local moreh tzedek, including the missing siman additions to the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch. The Rebbe lamented he no longer had the strength in his old age to rewrite them. Sources variously date the fire to 5616, 5617, or 5618.
Tags: lubavitch, fire, tzemach tzedek, manuscripts, loss

Title: Montefiore's fourth visit to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: Montefiore returned to Eretz Yisrael in 5617 without commissioning a new census.
Story: This visit followed close on the 5615 census, so the existing records were considered sufficient. The visit is the only one of Montefiore's six tours of the Holy Land not associated with a fresh communal survey.
Tags: montefiore, eretz yisrael

Title: Shadarut shaliach sets out to North Africa
Summary: At the beginning of 5618, R' Shaul Ashkenazi set out as the shaliach of Kollel Chabad to Egypt and North Africa.
Story: He carried a shadarut document signed by Chabad leaders in both Hebron and Jerusalem. His route went through Izmir, where he received a recommendation from R' Chaim Palagi in Marcheshvan, before continuing to Alexandria, Tunisia, Tripoli, Algeria, Oran, and Tlemcen — an unusual mission since these were traditionally Sephardic donor territories.
Tags: hebron, jerusalem, kollel chabad, shadarut, north africa, shaul ashkenazi

Title: R' Chaim Palagi endorses Chabad shaliach in Izmir
Summary: In Marcheshvan 5618, R' Chaim Palagi of Izmir gave R' Shaul Ashkenazi a letter of recommendation for his mission to North Africa.
Story: On his way to Egypt and North Africa, R' Shaul stopped in Izmir to obtain endorsement from the renowned Sephardic posek R' Chaim Palagi. This recommendation was important because the shaliach was traveling to traditionally Sephardic communities on behalf of an Ashkenazic kollel.
Tags: izmir, shadarut, chaim palagi, kollel chabad

Title: Chassidim sign debt note to the Tzemach Tzedek in Lubavitch
Summary: On the night of 5 Tevet תרח"י the chassidim R' Yitzchak Chaim Dovber Wilensky and R' Aryeh Leib son of R' Nachum Noach signed a shtar in Lubavitch acknowledging a 15-ruble debt to the Tzemach Tzedek, due within a month and a half.
Story: The shtar may record a loan from the Tzemach Tzedek to two chassidim staying in Lubavitch, or possibly a ma'amad obligation pledged to the Rebbe. R' Yitzchak Chaim Dovber HaLevi Wilensky was among the great chassidim of the era, active in the courts of the Tzemach Tzedek, the Maharash, and the Rashab. He had arrived in Lubavitch shortly after his marriage around age 18-19.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, lubavitch, ma'amad, loan, wilensky

Title: R' Yehuda Leib Zalkind of Dinaburg passes away
Summary: R' Yehuda Leib Zalkind, second rabbi of Dinaburg and author of 'Zecher Yehuda,' died on 23 Kislev 5618.
Story: After roughly four decades as rabbi of Dinaburg, R' Yehuda Leib Zalkind passed away on 23 Kislev 5618 (December 1857). A disciple of the Alter Rebbe and contemporary of the Tzemach Tzedek, he had corresponded with the latter in halachic responsa from their youth.
Tags: dinaburg, latvia, rabbinate, zecher-yehuda

Title: Loan note to Tzemach Tzedek due 5 Tevet
Summary: A loan note from Rabbi Yitzchak Chaim Dov Ber Wilensky and Aryeh Leib was due to the Tzemach Tzedek by 5 Tevet 5618.
Story: Two prominent Chassidim signed a debt obligation to the Tzemach Tzedek with a repayment date of 5 Tevet 5618 (Dec 22, 1857). The note may have covered either a personal loan from the Rebbe or a commitment of maamad support.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, loan, wilensky, maamad

Title: Abd al-Rahman taken in chains to Constantinople and sentenced to death
Summary: In 5618 the Hebron persecutor Abd al-Rahman was finally captured by the government and taken in iron chains to Constantinople, where he was sentenced to death.
Story: After years of tormenting Hebron's Jewish community, Abd al-Rahman was finally seized in 5618. R' Moshe Risher recorded in 'Tevuot HaAretz' (5626/1866) that 'God in His mercy, eight years ago, seized him and took him to Constantinople in iron chains and there gave him the sentence of death.' The community treated his demise as deliverance from a sustained persecution.
Tags: hebron, ottoman empire, abd al-rahman, constantinople, persecution

Title: Beis Menachem synagogue purchased in Jerusalem
Summary: The Chabad community in Jerusalem bought the building that became the Beis Menachem synagogue and immediately added a small upper room.
Story: The upstairs space served as a study hall for talmidei chachamim and a children's Talmud Torah. A full second floor was already part of the long-term plan, as shown by the synagogue stamp on later Montefiore censuses, but the plan would take more than two decades to execute.
Tags: jerusalem, synagogue, beis menachem, kollel chabad

Title: Chabad community in Jerusalem acquires Beit Menachem synagogue
Summary: From 5618 onward the Chabad community in Jerusalem took possession of the Beit Menachem synagogue on a mashkanta arrangement.
Story: After being 'wanderers without a synagogue,' as the 5626 Montefiore report put it, the Chabad community in Jerusalem acquired the Beit Menachem synagogue starting in 5618 (1858). They added a study room on its roof, where the Dat Moshe ViYehudis beis midrash later hosted 20 bachurim and 15 baalei batim.
Tags: jerusalem, beit menachem, synagogue, mashkanta

Title: R' Noach Moshe records debt for Likkutei Torah purchase in Lubavitch
Summary: On 16 Shevat תרי"ח R' Noach Moshe son of Binyamin signed in Lubavitch a debt note for six silver rubles for a Likkutei Torah purchased for the Lubavitcher minyan of the town of Dokshitz.
Story: The new Likkutei Torah of the Tzemach Tzedek had become a prized acquisition for chasidic communities. R' Noach Moshe, while visiting Lubavitch, bought a copy on behalf of the Lubavitcher shul of Dokshitz, signing a debt note to be paid 'when the seller is in Dokshitz.' The shtar is a small witness to early Likkutei Torah distribution.
Tags: lubavitch, likkutei torah, dokshitz, shul, shtar

Title: Sasson donation enables acquisition of the Beis Menachem synagogue
Summary: The Chabad community in Jerusalem secured the Beis Menachem synagogue courtyard via a mortgage funded by David Sassoon's 100-pound-sterling donation, commemorated on 20 Sivan 5618.
Story: Lacking a synagogue, the Chabad community in Jerusalem received 100 lira sterling from David Sassoon of India as a key-money donation to take the courtyard under a four-year mortgage. The courtyard contained a synagogue, women's section, mikveh, and other facilities. A commemorative inscription was installed on 20 Sivan 5618 honoring Sassoon's generosity.
Tags: jerusalem, beit menachem, tzemach tzedek, synagogue, david sasson, india

Title: Dutch translation of Sephardic Haggadah 'Kol Yaakov' printed in Amsterdam
Summary: Jacob Lopes Cardozo published a Sephardic-rite Haggadah translated into Dutch with notes in Amsterdam.
Story: In 5619 (1859), Jacob ben David Lopes Cardozo published 'Sefer Kol Yaakov' in Amsterdam, a Sephardic-custom Haggadah newly translated into Dutch with annotations. The 53-page edition served the Dutch-speaking Sephardic community of the Netherlands. It represented a fresh translation effort aimed at making the Seder accessible in the local vernacular.
Tags: haggadah, dutch, sephardic, amsterdam, netherlands

Title: Judeo-Arabic Haggadah 'Chukat HaPesach' printed in Livorno
Summary: The 'Chukat HaPesach' Haggadah, with laws and instructions in Egyptian Judeo-Arabic, was printed in Livorno.
Story: In 5619 (1859), 'Chukat HaPesach' was published in Livorno by Agudat Ezov, organized into three sections containing legal novellae, the Haggadah with Seder laws in Egyptian-dialect Judeo-Arabic, and a new commentary on Pirkei Avot called 'Avot u'Gevurot'. The 202-page volume also included readings for Rosh Chodesh Nissan, the offerings of the tribal princes, and the burning of leaven. It served the Arabic-speaking Sephardic communities of North Africa.
Tags: haggadah, judeo-arabic, livorno, italy, egypt, agudat ezov

Title: Tzemach Tzedek moves into rebuilt home in Lyubavichi
Summary: At the start of the Hebrew year 5620 (autumn 1859), the Tzemach Tzedek moved back into his newly rebuilt home in Lyubavichi.
Story: After spending time in the courtyard of the town's landowner following the fire, the Tzemach Tzedek and his sons returned to live in their newly rebuilt buildings in Lyubavichi at the beginning of 5620. Shortly afterwards, in Kislev of that same year, he became seriously ill. The episode is recorded in Beis Rebbi, part 3, chapter 6.
Tags: lyubavichi, tzemach tzedek

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's Even HaEzer §41 written between Chanukah and Sivan 5619
Summary: Responsum Even HaEzer §41 references 'Sivan 5618... Chanukah 5619 past,' placing its composition between Chanukah and Sivan 5619.
Story: Internal evidence in Even HaEzer §41 — its opening refers to 'Sivan 5618 past... Chanukah 5619 past' — locates the responsum between Chanukah 5619 and Sivan 5619, late 1858 to spring 1859. This and Yoreh Deah §42 establish that the entire manuscript 2143 ('Book 5619') was written in that year, the latest extant Tzemach Tzedek responsa volume.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, even haezer, responsa, manuscript 2143

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's homes rebuilt after fire
Summary: During 5619 (1858–1859) the Tzemach Tzedek's homes in Lyubavichi were rebuilt after the fire that had destroyed them.
Story: Following the fire that consumed the Tzemach Tzedek's home in Lyubavichi (which also destroyed many of his responsa written between 1848–1856), he had moved temporarily into the local landowner's courtyard. During the year 5619 the buildings for him and his sons were reconstructed. The family then prepared to return to their newly built homes at the start of the following Hebrew year.
Tags: lyubavichi, tzemach tzedek, fire, reconstruction

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's final illness begins in Kislev
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek became gravely ill in Kislev 5620, beginning a six-year illness that lasted until his passing.
Story: In Kislev 5620 the Tzemach Tzedek fell seriously ill and remained so for more than six consecutive years until his passing. During this period he could no longer hold full audience and answered questions submitted through his attendants on small notes, replying briefly in person or in writing. Manuscripts in his hand from these years are scarce and show a trembling script.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, menachem mendel schneersohn, illness, lubavitch

Title: Pinkas of the Malbish Arumim clothing-the-poor society renewed in Lubavitch
Summary: On 18 Marcheshvan 5620 in Lubavitch, a fire-damaged clothing-the-poor society was reconstituted with a new ledger, endorsed by the Tzemach Tzedek and pledged to by his sons and grandsons.
Story: An earlier Malbish Arumim chevra in Lubavitch had collapsed after fire destroyed its pinkas, ending weekly donations that had clothed poor children, especially those attending cheder. On 18 Cheshvan 5620 (November 14, 1859), townsmen reorganized the society in a new pinkas, with the Tzemach Tzedek adding his haskama and his sons and grandsons — including R' Menachem (son of Maharash), R' Baruch Shalom, R' Yehuda Leib of Kopust, R' Chaim Shneur Zalman of Ladi and others — pledging annual contributions.
Tags: lubavitch, tzedakah, malbish arumim, tzemach tzedek, chevra

Title: Tzemach Tzedek becomes gravely ill
Summary: In Kislev 5620 the Tzemach Tzedek became gravely ill, an illness that lasted more than six years.
Story: Beis Rebbi records that the Tzemach Tzedek 'became very ill in the month of Kislev 5620 and was ill for more than six straight years.' During this period he transferred most halachic answering to his son R. Yisrael Noach (Maharin), who would present harder cases back to his father.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, illness, kislev, succession

Title: Tzemach Tzedek falls seriously ill in Lyubavichi
Summary: In Kislev 5620 (late 1859) the Tzemach Tzedek became gravely ill shortly after returning to his newly rebuilt home.
Story: Only weeks after moving back into the rebuilt buildings in Lyubavichi at the start of 5620, the Tzemach Tzedek fell seriously ill in the month of Kislev. The illness is noted as a major episode in his later years, recorded in the family chronicle Beis Rebbi (part 3, chapter 6).
Tags: lyubavichi, tzemach tzedek, illness

Title: Tzemach Tzedek falls severely ill
Summary: In Kislev 5620 the Tzemach Tzedek fell gravely ill in his rebuilt Lubavitch home.
Story: The illness came shortly after the courtyard's reconstruction and his return from the nobleman's estate. He continued to lead the movement for several more years until his passing in 1866.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, lubavitch, illness

Title: Birth of Rabbi Sholom Dovber Schneersohn, the Rashab
Summary: The Rashab, fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe, was born in 1860.
Story: The Rashab built Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim, transforming Chabad education. He led the movement through pogroms, World War I, and the early years of Soviet rule, dying in Rostov in 1920.
Tags: rashab, sholom dovber schneersohn

Title: Birth of Rebbe Rashab in Lubavitch
Summary: Rabbi Shalom Dovber Schneersohn, the future fifth Chabad Rebbe known as the Rashab, was born on 20 Marcheshvan 5621 in Lubavitch.
Story: The Rashab was born to the Maharash and Rebbetzin Rivkah. He would later found the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lubavitch in 5657 and lead the movement through the upheavals of World War One. His birth in the courtyard further confirmed Lubavitch as the dynastic center.
Tags: rashab, shalom-dovber, schneersohn

Title: Pinkas Malbish Arumim opened in Lubavitch
Summary: The Lubavitch society Malbish Arumim opened its ledger in 5620 (1860) with the Tzemach Tzedek's signed endorsement.
Story: The Pinkas of the Malbish Arumim chevrah in Lubavitch dates its founding to 5620 (1860). It records the establishment of the society, includes a written endorsement and signature from the Tzemach Tzedek, and bears annual pledges signed by his sons and grandsons.
Tags: lubavitch, malbish arumim, tzemach tzedek, tzedakah, chevrah

Title: Sheterna Riza and R' Shalom Kaznovsky make aliyah to Hebron
Summary: In 5620-5621 Sheterna Riza Slonim and her husband R' Shalom Kaznovsky immigrated to Hebron by order of the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: Sheterna Riza, eldest daughter of Menucha Rachel and R' Yaakov Slonim, had married R' Shalom Kaznovsky abroad before her parents' aliyah. In 5620-5621, following the directive of the Tzemach Tzedek, the couple themselves made aliyah to Hebron. Their son R' Eliezer Shimon was already married at the time and remained abroad temporarily.
Tags: hebron, aliyah, slonim family, kaznovsky, tzemach tzedek

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's sons recommend R. M.Z. Neimark to Horki community
Summary: On 15 Tevet 5620 the sons of the Tzemach Tzedek wrote to the Horki community urging them to retain R. Mushulam Zalman Neimark.
Story: The sons of the Tzemach Tzedek sent a letter to the leaders of the Horki community asking them to strengthen the salary of R. Mushulam Zalman Neimark, their moreh tzedek, lest he look elsewhere. They emphasized that competent halachic authorities expert in Chasidus were rare in those times.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, horki, moreh tzedek, neimark, russia

Title: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark receives recommendation as rabbi of Horki
Summary: The sons of the Tzemach Tzedek wrote to the Horki community urging them to firmly support R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark with a permanent salary.
Story: Dated 15 Teves 5620, the joint letter from Maharil of Kopust, R' Chaim Shneur Zalman of Liadi, and R' Yisroel Noach of Niezhin praised R' Meshulam Zalman as 'a renowned moreh tzedek both in psak and in chassidus' and urged the community to retain him with a strengthened salary.
Tags: meshulam zalman neumark, maharil kopust, horki, chassidus, rabbinate, chabad

Title: Birth of Rebbe Rashab in Lubavitch
Summary: Rabbi Shalom DovBer Schneersohn, the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe, was born in Lubavitch on 20 Marcheshvan.
Story: Rabbi Shalom DovBer Schneersohn (Rashab) was born in Lubavitch on 20 Marcheshvan 5621. He was the son of Rebbe Maharash. He would later become the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe and founder of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva system.
Tags: rashab, lubavitch, russia, birth

Title: Birthday of the Rebbe Rashab recalled in 1944 diary
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab, fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe, was born Monday Chaye Sarah, 20 Marcheshvan 5621, at 9 AM.
Story: In his 5705 diary the Rebbe Rayatz noted that 20 Marcheshvan was the birthday of his father, the Rebbe Rashab, who was born on Monday of parashat Chaye Sarah, 20 Marcheshvan 5621 (5 November 1860), at the ninth hour of the morning. The Rayatz recorded a dream that night in which his father appeared in Shabbat garments on the 84th anniversary of his soul's descent.
Tags: rashab, birth, chaye sarah

Title: Emancipation of Russian serfs
Summary: The Russian Empire emancipates its serfs, giving peasants land that would later be seized for Soviet collectivization.
Story: The land-ownership pattern that emerged was overturned by Soviet collectivization, which forced the creation of farming collectives, dropped productivity, and contributed to the famine the Rebbe later confronted with his matzah campaign.
Tags: russia, serfs, peasants, emancipation

Title: Chabad community purchases Beis Menachem synagogue outright
Summary: With additional donations and a 250-Napoleon loan, the Chabad community of Jerusalem acquired the Beis Menachem synagogue courtyard permanently in 5622.
Story: After four years on a mortgage backed by Sassoon's donation, the community faced losing the property when the seller wanted his money back. A donor from Kherson contributed 150 lira sterling, additional gifts came in, and they took a permissible-interest loan to reach the full 600 lira sterling purchase price. The acquisition secured the synagogue for the Jerusalem Chabad community permanently.
Tags: jerusalem, beit menachem, tzemach tzedek, synagogue, fundraising

Title: Prince of Wales granted access to Hebron tomb
Summary: The Turkish sultan ordered the ban on non-Muslim entry to Me'arat Hamakhpelah lifted for the Prince of Wales.
Story: The visit was one of a very small number of rare exceptions to the centuries-long ban barring Jews and other non-Muslims from the Tomb of the Patriarchs. Even royal access did not extend to the actual cave beneath the Herodian structure.
Tags: hebron, meorat-hamachpelah, british-royalty

Title: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark moves from Horki to Starodub
Summary: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark left his Horki rabbinate to serve as rav in Starodub, where R' Chaim Shimon Dov Zhivov succeeded him in Horki.
Story: After approximately a decade in Horki, R' Meshulam Zalman moved to Starodub around 5622. The Horki position was filled by R' Chaim Shimon Dov Zhivov, later author of Shivim Tmarim, who would serve there for about 25 years.
Tags: meshulam zalman neumark, horki, starodub, chaim shimon dov zhivov, rabbinate, chabad

Title: R. Mushulam Zalman Neimark moves from Horki to Starodub rabbinate
Summary: Around 5622 R. Mushulam Zalman Neimark left the rabbinate of Horki to assume the rabbinate of Starodub.
Story: After serving in Horki from approximately 5610, R. Mushulam Zalman Neimark transferred to Starodub around 5622, where he served until about 5646. He was succeeded in Horki by the Chasid R. Chaim Shimon Dov Zivov, author of Shivim Temarim. He later also served in Vitebsk and Nevel.
Tags: neimark, horki, starodub, russia, rabbinate

Title: Tzemach Tzedek adds more discourses to Torah Or
Summary: Additional discourses for Torah Or were issued by the Tzemach Tzedek in 5622.
Story: In 1862 the Tzemach Tzedek issued a supplement containing additional discourses on Genesis and Exodus, including selections for Chanukah, Purim and Pesach, expanding Torah Or further.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, torah or

Title: Tzemach Tzedek responsum delivered by his son Maharin
Summary: Orach Chaim §85, dated 5622, was delivered through R. Yisrael Noach (Maharin), reflecting the Tzemach Tzedek's late-life delegation of halacha to his son.
Story: From around 5620 onward, chassidim brought their questions through attendants who relayed them to the bedridden Tzemach Tzedek. He appointed his son R. Yisrael Noach (Maharin) to answer most halachic queries, occasionally forwarding harder ones to his father. Orach Chaim §85 (5622) is one of the late responsa explicitly mediated by Maharin.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, maharin, yisrael noach schneersohn, responsa, transition

Title: Chiddushei HaRim of Gur certifies a shochet's sharpened knife
Summary: The Chiddushei HaRim writes from Gur on 7 Adar Sheni 5622 attesting that he examined a shochet's knife and found him expertly skilled in honing it.
Story: Rabbi Yitzchak Meir Alter, the first Gerrer Rebbe and author of Chiddushei HaRim, wrote to his chossid Rabbi Meir Shachna Reich on Sunday, 7 Adar Sheni 5622. He confirmed having tested the shochet's blade himself—finding the man sensitive to even the finest pgima and capable of restoring the knife to proper condition.
Tags: chiddushei harim, yitzchak meir alter, gur, shochet, meir shachna reich, poland

Title: Letter from Maharchash"z of Lyady on 24 Nisan 5622
Summary: Rabbi Chaim Schneur Zalman of Lyady writes from Lyady asking Reb Aba Pershan of Krasłowa to organize support, on 24 Nisan 5622.
Story: This letter, one of seven from Rabbi Chaim Schneur Zalman of Lyady — son of the Tzemach Tzedek — was written while his father was still alive but in great weakness. It asks longtime supporters in Krasłowa, through Reb Dan and Rabbi Shneur Zalman, to repeat their previous year's fundraising effort on his behalf.
Tags: lyady, krasłowa, schneersohn, fundraising, tzemach-tzedek

Title: Wedding of Nachum Mordechai of Chortkov in Potik
Summary: Rabbi David Moshe of Chortkov's son Nachum Mordechai marries the daughter of Rabbi Shalom Yosef of Sadigura on the Shabbat after Shavuot 5622.
Story: Rabbi David Moshe of Chortkov, son of the Ruzhiner Rebbe, sent a circular letter from Potik in 5622 announcing the wedding of his son Nachum Mordechai to his niece, daughter of his brother Rabbi Shalom Yosef of Sadigura. The wedding was scheduled for the Shabbat after Shavuot, and the letter — addressed to chasidim in Kalisz, Kotarid, Miyaskovke, Krati, Nemirov, and Krasna — requested contributions to defray its substantial costs.
Tags: chortkov, sadigura, ruzhin, potik, wedding

Title: Chevrah Mefitzei Haskalah (Chamah) founded
Summary: Wealthy Russian Jews founded Chevrah Mefitzei Haskalah to promote secular Jewish education and assimilation.
Story: In 1863, backed by some of Russia's wealthiest Jews including the Gunzburg dynasty, the Society to Promote the Enlightenment (Chamah) was established. Its mission was to promote Jewish assimilation into Russian society, and by 1900 it had grown to 150 schools.
Tags: chamah, haskalah, gunzburg, russia, assimilation

Title: R' Eliezer Orlozarow begins rabbinate in Romny
Summary: R' Eliezer Orlozarow, author of Hagahos Eliezer, began his rabbinate in Romny in 5623.
Story: Succeeding earlier rabbis of the Chassidic town, R' Eliezer Orlozarow served as rabbi of Romny for nearly four decades. He would continue in this position until his passing in 5661.
Tags: eliezer orlozarow, romny, hagahos eliezer, rabbinate, chabad

Title: R' Feivel Rappaport of Dinaburg passes away
Summary: R' Feivel Rappaport, the third rabbi of Dinaburg, died around 5623 (1863).
Story: R' Feivel Rappaport, a Chassidic scholar, served as the third rabbi of Dinaburg. He passed away around 5623 (1863), making way for R' Aryeh Leib Zivov of Smilevitz to assume the rabbinate.
Tags: dinaburg, latvia, rabbinate

Title: Society for Spreaders of Enlightenment founded in Russia
Summary: The 'Society of Spreaders of Enlightenment' was founded in Russia in 1863 to spread secular learning among Russian Jews.
Story: Originally named 'Chevra Marbei Haskalah,' the society later changed its name to 'Chevra Mefitzei Haskalah.' It established a wide network of schools and Talmud-Torah institutions across the Pale of Settlement, employing Maskilic teachers and aiming to draw Jewish children toward secular learning and away from traditional observance. The Rebbe Rashab viewed it as a grave spiritual threat and organized sustained opposition against it.
Tags: russia, haskalah, chevra mefitzei haskalah, maskilim

Title: Tzemach Tzedek summer 5623 responsum on Yoreh Deah
Summary: Yoreh Deah §337 was written in summer 5623.
Story: Yoreh Deah §337, written in summer 5623, is one of the few responsa preserved from the years after the Tzemach Tzedek became gravely ill. Most halachic work had passed to his son Maharin by this point; this responsum is among the small set still authored personally.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, yoreh deah, summer, responsa

Title: Zhitomir 'Seder HaTefilah' with Chabad Chassidic discourses by Alter Rebbe
Summary: A two-volume Seder HaTefilah following the Arizal nusach with Chabad Chassidic discourses by the Alter Rebbe was printed in Zhitomir.
Story: In 5623-5624 (1863-1864), a Seder HaTefilah containing all annual prayers according to the Arizal nusach was printed in Zhitomir, accompanied by Divrei Elokim Chayim Chassidic discourses by the Chabad Alter Rebbe Schneur Zalman. The two-volume quarto edition came to a total of 310 leaves. It became a foundational printed Siddur for the Chabad community.
Tags: chabad, zhitomir, alter rebbe, siddur, ari

Title: Tzemach Tzedek chiddushim in half Shevat 5623
Summary: A chiddush in Chiddushim folio 232d is dated to mid-Shevat 5623.
Story: Among the very few late writings from the Tzemach Tzedek's years of illness is a chiddush dated mid-Shevat 5623 (early February 1863). It is one of fewer than a half-dozen dated pieces preserved from after his collapse in Kislev 5620.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, chiddushim, shevat, late writings

Title: Rebbe Maharid of Ladi writes Avraham Avli Person on business and family
Summary: On 12 Kislev 5624, R' Yitzchak Dovber of Ladi, son of R' Chaim Shneur Zalman and grandson of the Tzemach Tzedek, wrote to the chassid Avraham Avli Person with business counsel and family news.
Story: The future Admor Maharid of Ladi, author of Siddur Maharid, encouraged Person to keep faith despite slow earnings and to actively seek commissions. He recounted a visit from R' Moshe and his only son, who agreed to set up a shop, and asked Person to send him a commission. He also reported that the Tzemach Tzedek and his own father R' Chaim Shneur Zalman were both in good health.
Tags: maharid of ladi, yitzchak dovber, tzemach tzedek, maharchash zalman of ladi, avraham avli person, commerce

Title: Death of R' Yeshaya Halevi Horowitz of Beshenkovichi
Summary: R' Yeshaya Halevi Horowitz, a leading chasid of the Tzemach Tzedek in Beshenkovichi, died in 5624.
Story: R' Yeshaya was a prominent chasid of the Tzemach Tzedek and the husband of Bila, niece of the Rebbe. His death left her widowed with five young orphans, leading to her eventual aliyah to Tzfat with her sons. The family became foundational to the renewed Chabad community in Tzfat.
Tags: beshenkovichi, tzemach tzedek, chasidim, russia

Title: Illustrated Italian-translation Haggadah printed in Trieste
Summary: An illustrated Haggadah with an Italian translation was printed in Trieste.
Story: Around 5624 (1864), a 66-page illustrated Haggadah with Italian translation was issued in Trieste. The folio volume served the Italian-speaking Jewish community of the Habsburg port city. It represented the Italian-Jewish tradition of richly produced Haggadot.
Tags: haggadah, italian, trieste, italy, illustrated

Title: Lvov Haggadah 'Gevurot Yisrael' (Maggid of Kozhnitz) and 'Mateh Moshe'
Summary: A Pardes-style Haggadah with 'Gevurot Yisrael' by Yisrael of Kozhnitz and 'Mateh Moshe' by Moshe Eliyakum Briya was issued in Lvov.
Story: Around 5624 (1864), a Haggadah was published in Lvov featuring two commentaries on the Pardes pattern: 'Gevurot Yisrael' by the Maggid Rabbi Yisrael of Kozhnitz, and 'Mateh Moshe' by his son Moshe Eliyakum Briya. Additional drashot on Pesach, the four cups, and 'Kadesh U'Rechatz', plus drashot on Sefirat HaOmer and a commentary on Chad Gadya by Rebbe Mordechai of Chernobyl, were included. The 34-leaf quarto edition was printed by Sh.L. Flecker.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, kozhnitz, lvov, yisrael of kozhnitz, chernobyl

Title: Publication of Shivchei HaRav, early biography of the Alter Rebbe
Summary: Shivchei HaRav, an early printed biography of the Alter Rebbe, was published in Lvov in 5624.
Story: In 5624 (1864) the small biographical work Shivchei HaRav appeared in Lvov. It collected and edited oral traditions about the life of the Alter Rebbe that Chasidim had long preserved in private manuscripts. It became one of the foundational printed sources for the Alter Rebbe's biography.
Tags: alter rebbe, biography, lvov, shivchei harav

Title: R' Aryeh Leib Zivov assumes Dinaburg rabbinate
Summary: R' Aryeh Leib 'Smilevitzer' Zivov, a leading disciple of the Tzemach Tzedek, became rabbi of Dinaburg around 5624 (1864).
Story: R' Aryeh Leib Zivov, who had previously served in Smilevitz and earlier in Homil, was a senior chassid and emissary of the Tzemach Tzedek. He took up the Dinaburg rabbinate around 5624 (1864) and served until approximately 5647 (1887).
Tags: dinaburg, latvia, rabbinate, smilevitz, tzemach-tzedek

Title: Tzemach Tzedek winter 5624 responsum on Orach Chaim
Summary: Orach Chaim §114, written in winter 5624, is among the latest extant Tzemach Tzedek responsa.
Story: Orach Chaim §114 was composed in the winter of 5624, after more than four years of the Tzemach Tzedek's illness. Such late responsa appear only sporadically; the vast majority of halachic work during this period was answered by his son Maharin, with the Tzemach Tzedek consulted only on the most difficult cases.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, orach chaim, winter, late responsa

Title: Wedding invitation from the Chiddushei HaRim
Summary: On 7 Adar Sheni 5624 the Chiddushei HaRim of Ger married his grandson Pinchas Menachem Mendel of Pilcz to his granddaughter Hendel Leah (sister of the Sfas Emes).
Story: From Gur on Rosh Chodesh Adar II 5624, the Chiddushei HaRim wrote a wedding invitation for the union of his grandson Pinchas Menachem Mendel of Pilcz to his granddaughter Hendel Leah, sister of the future Sfas Emes. The invitation was addressed to R' Meshulam Reich, who was a son-in-law of the Rebbe Rashab the elder (son of the Tzemach Tzedek) and later served as a shadar of Kolel Chabad — through whom the letter eventually reached the archive of the Lubavitch rebbeim.
Tags: chiddushei harim, ger, gur, pilcz, wedding, tzemach tzedek family

Title: R. Mordechai Shneur Zalman Schneersohn responds to R. Yosef Tumarkin
Summary: On 21 Adar I 5624 (1864), R. Mordechai Shneur Zalman Schneersohn of Zhitomir wrote a halachic response to R. Yosef Tumarkin of Kremenchug.
Story: R. Mordechai Shneur Zalman Schneersohn — son of the Rebbe of Avruch and grandson of the Tzemach Tzedek — served as a posek in Zhitomir. On 21 Adar I 5624 he replied to R. Yosef Tumarkin of Kremenchug on issues of hafrashas terumah and chalah, the copying costs of some manuscripts, and a question on the Ohr HaChaim to parshas Vayeira. He died young, and most of his writings have been lost.
Tags: mordechai shneur zalman schneersohn, yosef tumarkin, zhitomir, kremenchug, halacha, ohr hachaim

Title: Passing of Rabbi Hillel of Paritch in Cherson
Summary: The famed chossid Rabbi Hillel of Paritch passes away on 11 Menachem Av 5624 during a journey, in the city of Cherson.
Story: During one of his travels, Rabbi Hillel of Paritch—author of Pelach HaRimon and longtime av beis din of Babruysk—passed away in Cherson on 11 Menachem Av 5624. An ohel was built over his grave, and many chassidim journeyed there to prostrate themselves at his resting place.
Tags: hillel of paritch, cherson, yahrtzeit, ohel, ukraine

Title: R' Hillel of Paritch passes away
Summary: R' Hillel of Paritch, the renowned chassid and rabbi of Bobruisk, passed away on 11 Menachem Av 5624.
Story: R' Hillel had succeeded R' Baruch Mordechai Itigna as rabbi of Bobruisk after the latter made aliyah in 5611. He served as sole rabbi over the entire community, including the misnagdic faction who held his words in awe, until his passing on 11 Av 5624.
Tags: hillel paritch, bobruisk, chassid, chabad

Title: Dinaburg adopts dual-rabbi structure
Summary: Starting in 5625 (1865), Dinaburg had two rabbis simultaneously — one Chassidic, one Misnagdic.
Story: From 5625 (1865) onward, the Jewish community of Dinaburg was served by two rabbis at the same time, one chosen by the Chassidim and one by the Misnagdim. The Misnagdic community first brought R' Aharon Shaul Zelig HaKohen of Pruzhana to fill their post.
Tags: dinaburg, latvia, mitnagdim, chassidim, rabbinate

Title: Engagement contract of Rashab and Shterna Sara
Summary: An engagement contract was written between the young Rashab and his cousin Shterna Sara at the urging of Rabbi Menachem Mendel.
Story: In 1865, Shterna Sara visited Lubavitch from her hometown of Ovruch as a young girl. Seeing his two grandchildren standing together in his home, Rabbi Menachem Mendel (the Tzemach Tzedek) declared, 'Bride and groom!' That year, while both children were still young, their parents wrote a tena'im, the formal engagement contract that would lead to their marriage a decade later.
Tags: lubavitch, ovruch, engagement, rashab, shterna sara, tzemach tzedek

Title: Engagement of Maharashab to Sterna Sarah finalized by the Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: The shidduch between the four-and-a-half-year-old Maharashab and Sterna Sarah, daughter of the Rebbe of Ovruch, was finalized by the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: In 5625 (1865), the Tzemach Tzedek finalized and signed the tenaim between his grandson Sholom DovBer (Maharashab), then aged four and a half, and Sterna Sarah, daughter of his son Yosef Yitzchak, Rebbe of Ovruch. The agreement stipulated that the wedding would take place ten years later in 5635 (1875).
Tags: maharashab, sterna sarah, tzemach tzedek, yosef yitzchak of ovruch, shidduch

Title: Hungarian Hoizman brothers settle in Hebron from Liska
Summary: In 5625 R' Alexander Zisha Hoizman emigrated with his family from Liska via Trieste to Hebron, where he joined his brother R' Aryeh Leib, beginning the Hungarian community there.
Story: R' Alexander Zisha Hoizman, born in Hungary in 5578, emigrated in 5625 with his wife Bat-Sheva and three children—Shimon, Menachem Manes, and Tzvi Hersh—via Trieste, where he met his brother R' Aryeh Leib also bound for Eretz Israel. The two Karlin Chassidim families initially worshipped with the Chabad community but eventually founded 'Kahal Ungarit' with its own synagogue as their families grew and intermarried with other non-Chabad families.
Tags: hebron, hungary, liska, hoizman family, karlin chassidim, trieste

Title: R' Meir Tzvi Hershler immigrates from Hungary to Eretz Israel
Summary: R' Meir Tzvi Hershler, born 5615, immigrated from Hungary in 5625 and later married Sarah Mendelsohn of Hebron, settling there between 5630-5634.
Story: R' Meir Tzvi Hershler arrived from Hungary in 5625 at age 10 and later married Sarah, daughter of R' Yonatan Zeev Wolf Mendelsohn of Hebron. He settled permanently in Hebron between 5630-5634. Decades later he would represent the non-Chabad communities during the 5647 din torah between the kollels and serve as their representative on Hebron's Vaad HaKlali.
Tags: hebron, hungary, meir tzvi hershler, mendelsohn family, jerusalem

Title: Rabbi Aryeh Leib Zivav appointed rabbi of Dvinsk-Dinaburg
Summary: Rabbi Aryeh Leib Zivav assumes the rabbinate of Dvinsk-Dinaburg around the year 5625, succeeding Rabbi Yehuda Leib Batlan.
Story: After serving as rav in Babruysk, Smilovitch and Homel, Rabbi Aryeh Leib Zivav was appointed rav of Dvinsk-Dinaburg around 5625, following Rabbi Yehuda Leib Batlan. He was a leading talmid of the Tzemach Tzedek and Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homel and a recognized posek in his region, especially in the laws of writing gittin.
Tags: aryeh leib zivav, dvinsk, dinaburg, rabbinate, latvia

Title: Tnaim signed between Rebbe Rashab and Rebbetzin Sterna Sara
Summary: On 10 Sivan 5625 the engagement contract was written between the four-and-a-half-year-old Rebbe Rashab and his cousin Sterna Sara, with the Tzemach Tzedek personally inscribing the opening line and a financial pledge.
Story: On 10 Sivan 5625, while the future Rebbe Rashab was just four and a half years old, his tnaim were signed with his cousin Sterna Sara, daughter of the Admor Maharin of Ovruch. The Tzemach Tzedek — grandfather of both bride and groom and just ten months before his own passing — personally inscribed the opening blessing on both copies and added on the reverse a pledge to give the couple 50 rubles every year, totaling 500 rubles. The contract stipulated that the wedding itself would take place in Jerusalem in the summer of 5635.
Tags: rebbe rashab, sterna sara, tnaim, tzemach tzedek, ovruch, lubavitch

Title: Rebbe Rashab's engagement signed on 10 Sivan
Summary: The engagement contract of Rebbe Rashab was signed on 10 Sivan 5625.
Story: On 10 Sivan 5625 (June 4, 1865), when Rebbe Rashab was four and a half years old, his tenaim were written. The Tzemach Tzedek personally added the opening line and a closing line of obligation, signing 'Menachem Mendel,' less than a year before his own passing.
Tags: rebbe rashab, engagement, tzemach tzedek

Title: Amsterdam Pekoa"M directs Hebron trustees to share funds with Jerusalem Chabad chassidim
Summary: On 26 Tishrei 5626 the Amsterdam Pekoa"M wrote to the Hebron trustees endorsing distribution of Kollel Chabad funds to chassidim in Jerusalem.
Story: The Amsterdam Pekudei Eretz Yisrael had sent funds to Hebron on the understanding that they would be distributed to Kollel Chabad members across the land. The trustees confirmed that since the regular kollel income was already feeding Jerusalem chassidim, they had now allocated the new donation accordingly, drawing it from the Hebron portion. This exchange illustrates Hebron's role as the Kollel Chabad center distributing funds throughout the four holy cities.
Tags: amsterdam, pekudei eretz yisrael, hebron, jerusalem, kollel chabad, chalukah

Title: Pekuam letter names new Hebron Kollel leadership
Summary: On 26 Tishrei 5626, the Pekuam administrators addressed a letter to R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, R' Shneur Zalman, and R' Dov Ber ben Naftali Hirsch as heads of the Hebron Chabad community.
Story: This is the latest surviving Pekuam letter to the Hebron leadership. The three named men headed the community administration; R' Dov Ber ben Naftali Hirsch may have been R' Dover of Lobki, registered in the 5626 census as a member of R' Shimon Menashe's beit din.
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, shimon menashe chaikin, dov ber

Title: 'Sod Kedoshim' Haggadah of the Alter Rebbe and Aharon HaLevi of Strashelye
Summary: A 'Sod Kedoshim' Haggadah with commentaries by the Chabad Alter Rebbe and his disciple Aharon HaLevi of Strashelye was published.
Story: In 5626 (1866), the Haggadah 'Sod Kedoshim' was published — possibly in Königsberg or Warsaw — featuring two commentaries: one by the Chabad Alter Rebbe Schneur Zalman of Liadi, and one by his disciple Rabbi Aharon HaLevi of Strashelye. The 49-leaf quarto edition transmitted core Chabad teachings on the Passover Seder. It became a foundational Chabad Haggadah commentary.
Tags: chabad, alter rebbe, strashelye, warsaw, konigsberg, sod kedoshim

Title: Jerusalem census lists Yehoshua Natkin and Zalman Epstein as trustees
Summary: The 5626 census recorded Yehoshua Natkin of Jacobstadt and Zalman Epstein as trustees of Kollel Chabad.
Story: Periodic Jerusalem censuses recorded the leadership of Kollel Chabad as it evolved. The 5626 entry identified two trustees serving the community, illustrating the continuity of the kollel administrative structure across decades. Such records form a primary source for reconstructing Chabad institutional history in Jerusalem.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, census, yehoshua natkin, zalman epstein

Title: Kol Aryeh published in Jerusalem
Summary: R' Shneur Zalman Mendelovitch published Kol Aryeh in Jerusalem in 5626.
Story: While serving as a Kollel Chabad emissary to the eastern lands, R' Shneur Zalman ben R' Menachem Mendel Mendelovitch obtained a major donation from the Sassoon family in Bombay for the Chabad synagogue in Jerusalem. He documented the trip in the introduction to his book Kol Aryeh, published in Jerusalem in 5626.
Tags: shneur zalman mendelovitch, jerusalem, kol aryeh, kollel chabad, shadar

Title: Maharash of Lubavitch begins his nesi'ut
Summary: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn (Maharash) becomes Rebbe of Lubavitch in 5626.
Story: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn, son of the Tzemach Tzedek, began leading as Rebbe of Lubavitch in 5626 and continued until his passing in 5643. His tenure is referenced in a recommendation letter from Rabbi Mordechai of Loyev that mentions a 'great rabbi of Lubavitch' (either the Maharash or his son the Rashab) who interceded on behalf of a chasid seeking to settle in the Land of Israel.
Tags: lubavitch, maharash, schneersohn, succession

Title: Marquis of Bute visits Me'arat Hamakhpelah
Summary: The Marquis of Bute was one of the rare non-Muslims granted access to the Tomb of the Patriarchs.
Story: His visit followed the Prince of Wales's 1862 access. These exceptional admissions were granted only at the insistence of the Turkish sultan and remained extremely rare.
Tags: hebron, meorat-hamachpelah, british-aristocracy

Title: Montefiore's fifth visit; Hebron now has a resident physician
Summary: The 5626 census recorded Hebron's first resident Jewish doctor, R. Yisrael Nachum of Chernobyl, age 66, who had immigrated in 5622.
Story: Bikur Cholim was by then paying 4,000 grush a year for the doctor's salary plus 2,000 in other expenses. The census also showed the Chabad synagogue had built a small upstairs room for a Talmud Torah and study hall, with plans drawn for a full second floor.
Tags: montefiore, census, hebron, yisrael nachum, chernobyl

Title: Or HaGanuz printed with Tzemach Tzedek approbation
Summary: Or HaGanuz by Rabbi Yehuda Leib HaKohen of Anipoli was issued in 5626 with a rare approbation from the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: Or HaGanuz appeared in 1866 with an unusual haskama from the Tzemach Tzedek and his sons. It is the only book to which the Tzemach Tzedek lent his name—he made the exception because the author's grandfather, Rabbi Yehuda Leib, had given an approbation to the Alter Rebbe's Tanya.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, yehuda leib hakohen, anipoli, haskama

Title: Passing of the Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek passed away in 1866.
Story: After his passing, his sons divided into separate chasidic dynasties. His youngest son, the Rebbe Maharash, succeeded him as the fourth Lubavitcher Rebbe.
Tags: tzemach tzedek

Title: Passing of the Tzemach Tzedek in Lubavitch
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneersohn, the Tzemach Tzedek, passed away on 13 Nisan 5626 in Lubavitch, the first Chabad Rebbe buried there.
Story: He had instructed in his will that no structure of brick or wood be built over his grave. Out of concern that gentiles might dig the grave searching for buried gold, an ohel of high walls without a roof was constructed around the resting place. A study hall was later added on the southern side, making the spot a place of study and prayer.
Tags: tzemach-tzedek, schneersohn, lubavitch-cemetery

Title: R' Chaim Shmuel Schmerling migrates from Hebron to Jaffa
Summary: R' Chaim Shmuel Schmerling's move from Hebron to Jaffa in 5626 founded the Chabad — and largely the Ashkenazi — settlement there.
Story: The Chabad settlement in Jaffa, and to a significant degree the broader Ashkenazi community there, originated with R' Chaim Shmuel Schmerling's relocation from Hebron in 5626 (1866). He founded the public institutions of the Ashkenazi community and lived in Jaffa for nearly thirty years.
Tags: jaffa, hebron, schmerling, ashkenazi community

Title: R' Chaim Shmuel Shmerling moves to Jaffa to found Chabad settlement
Summary: In 5626 R' Chaim Shmuel Shmerling moved from Hebron to Jaffa and founded the Chabad settlement there.
Story: R' Chaim Shmuel Shmerling, son of R' Moshe and grandson of R' Shimon Shmerling, moved to Jaffa in 5626 and founded the Chabad community there. His move extended the Shmerling family's role as founders of Chabad settlements - from his grandfather establishing the Hebron community to his own founding of the Jaffa community.
Tags: chaim shmuel shmerling, jaffa, hebron, chabad settlement

Title: Rabbi Shmuel becomes Rebbe Maharash
Summary: Rabbi Shmuel became the fourth Lubavitcher Rebbe in Lubavitch following his father's passing, while his brothers established rival Chabad courts.
Story: In 1866, following the passing of his father Rabbi Menachem Mendel (the Tzemach Tzedek), Rabbi Shmuel became the fourth Lubavitcher Rebbe in Lubavitch. His brothers established rival Chabad courts in nearby towns: Rabbi Yehuda Leib in Kopust, Rabbi Chaim Schneur Zalman in Liadi, and Rabbi Yisrael Noach in Nizhyn. For the next half a century, Chabad Chasidim would be divided between these different Chabad Rebbes.
Tags: lubavitch, russia, rebbe maharash, tzemach tzedek, succession

Title: Rebbe Maharash accepts Chabad leadership
Summary: Following the passing of his father in 5626, Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn became the fourth Chabad Rebbe.
Story: The Maharash's leadership continued the Chabad center in Lubavitch and saw major rebuilding of the courtyard after the 5628 fire. He would lead until his own passing in 5643. His era saw significant expansion of structures in the Lubavitch courtyard, including a large new hall and additional family residences.
Tags: maharash, shmuel, schneersohn

Title: Rebbe Maharash begins nesius in Lubavitch
Summary: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn (Maharash) assumed Chabad leadership from Lubavitch in 5626.
Story: After the passing of the Tzemach Tzedek in 5626 (1866), his son Rabbi Shmuel became the new Rebbe of Chabad. He continued to reside and lead from Lubavitch until his own passing in 5643 (1882). During this period R. Avraham Zeligsohn served as the town's moreh tzedek.
Tags: maharash, shmuel schneersohn, lubavitch, nesius

Title: Second edition of Likkutei Torah printed in Zhitomir
Summary: The second edition of Likkutei Torah was brought to press in Zhitomir in תרכ"ו by the mashpia R' Shmuel Betzalel Sheftil (Rashbatz), funded by the sons of the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: The summer of תרכ"ו saw a reprinting of Likkutei Torah, this time managed by the famed mashpia R' Shmuel Betzalel Sheftil. Because it appeared only months after the Tzemach Tzedek's passing, the title page omitted the names of his sons who had financed it and named only the Rashbatz. The third edition (Vilna תרל"ח) later clarified that the second edition too had been funded for the benefit of the Tzemach Tzedek's family.
Tags: zhitomir, likkutei torah, rashbatz, maharil of kopust, tzemach tzedek

Title: Sons of Tzemach Tzedek announce family unity pact
Summary: In summer 5626, the sons of the Tzemach Tzedek issued a public letter committing to peace and joint custody of their father's manuscripts.
Story: After the Tzemach Tzedek's passing earlier that year, his sons issued a circular letter to chassidim describing their pact of peace and a weekly gathering in their father's birth-room. They explained that the surviving forty manuscript volumes — twenty in nigleh and twenty in chassidus — could not be divided, because the nigleh works were destined for printing. The Rebbe Maharash twice added a personal note saying he strongly wished all the writings to be printed and his father's wellsprings to spread outward, citing the Baal Shem Tov's famous letter.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, schneersohn family, unity, manuscripts, rebbe maharash, succession

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's testament to the Rebbe Maharash
Summary: In 5626 (1866) the Tzemach Tzedek wrote a testament instructing his son the Rebbe Maharash on guiding chassidim and reviewing chassidut.
Story: In the final year of his life, the Tzemach Tzedek addressed a testament to his son R. Shmuel, the future Rebbe Maharash, directing him to listen to chassidim, advise them, and review chassidic discourses before them. It appears as Igeret 78 in the Tzemach Tzedek's Igrot Kodesh and offers a sample of his handwriting in its final form.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, rebbe maharash, testament, succession

Title: Tzemach Tzedek, third Chabad Rebbe, passes away
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneersohn passed away, prompting a split among Chabad streams.
Story: His passing led to multiple branches of Chabad emerging in Russia, including Kopust. The same division was mirrored within the Chabad community in Jerusalem and shaped Colel Chabad's governance for decades.
Tags: tzemach-tzedek, menachem-mendel, succession

Title: Vaad HaKlali unites all Ashkenazi kollelim in Jerusalem
Summary: In 5626 the various Ashkenazi kollelim in Jerusalem united under the Vaad HaKlali, established to address the fragmentation of the yishuv.
Story: Seeing that the Ashkenazi community had splintered into many particular kollelim, each looking after its own interests while the community as a whole declined, the rabbis and trustees of Jerusalem established a unified Vaad to oversee shared communal needs and represent the community to the Ottoman authorities. Both Perushim and Chassidim subdivisions participated, with one trustee from each kollel sitting on the Vaad.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel structure, ashkenazim, perushim, chassidim, kollel chabad

Title: Passing of the Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: The third Lubavitcher Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek (R' Menachem Mendel Schneersohn), passed away on 13 Nissan תרכ"ו.
Story: The Tzemach Tzedek's passing on 13 Nissan תרכ"ו shaped subsequent Chabad publishing history. When his sons brought a second edition of Likkutei Torah to press in the summer that followed, they declined to put their names on the title page out of mourning, leaving only R' Shmuel Betzalel Sheftil — the manager of the project — credited.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, lubavitch, passing

Title: Passing of the Tzemach Tzedek; Maharash assumes Chabad leadership
Summary: On 13 Nissan 5626 the Tzemach Tzedek passed away in Lubavitch, and his son Rabbi Shmuel (Maharash) accepted leadership of the Chabad movement there.
Story: After the Tzemach Tzedek's passing on 13 Nissan 5626 (1866), his younger son Rabbi Shmuel became the fourth Rebbe in Lubavitch. His brothers — also prominent rabbis — established branches of Chabad in towns such as Kopust, Liadi, Nizhin, and Ovruch. The succession defined the geographical structure of post-Tzemach-Tzedek Chabad in Tsarist Russia.
Tags: tzemach-tzedek, maharash, lubavitch, succession, schneersohn

Title: Passing of the Tzemach Tzedek (13 Nissan)
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek passed away on 13 Nissan 5626 in Lubavitch, where he is buried.
Story: He was the first Chabad Rebbe to live in Lubavitch from start of leadership to his last day. His will forbade any structure of brick or wood over his grave, but his family built a roofless wall around it out of fear that gentiles would dig in search of buried gold. A study hall was later added on its southern side. His passing precipitated the succession crisis that would split Chabad into several branches.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, lubavitch, succession

Title: Tzemach Tzedek passes away on 13 Nisan
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Mendel, the Tzemach Tzedek, passed away on 13 Nisan 5626.
Story: The Tzemach Tzedek led Chabad for nearly four decades. He passed away on 13 Nisan 5626 (March 29, 1866). His sons divided several of his personal effects, including a black sirtuk whose surviving portion is preserved in the library archives.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, yahrzeit, 13 nisan

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's passing on 13 Nisan
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek passed away on 13 Nisan 5626 (March 30, 1866) in Lubavitch.
Story: After 38 years of Chabad leadership, the Tzemach Tzedek passed away on 13 Nisan 5626 (March 30, 1866). He was succeeded as Rebbe of Lubavitch by his son R. Shmuel, the Rebbe Maharash.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, 13 nisan, lubavitch, hilula, rebbe maharash

Title: R' Yosef Kogel writes RA"Ch about R' Maharash's succession
Summary: R' Yosef Kogel of Pleshchenitz writes to RA"Ch describing notes from the Tzemach Tzedek confirming his son R' Shmuel (Maharash) as successor.
Story: Soon after the Tzemach Tzedek's passing, Chassidim in Pleshchenitz had accepted the Maharash's leadership. On 8 Av 5626 R' Yosef Kogel wrote to RA"Ch relaying news from R' Meir Amtsizer in Orsha, who had seen copies of tzettlach written by the Tzemach Tzedek to his son R' Shmuel — 'open your mouth and your words will illuminate hidden things' — confirming his succession. Kogel adds that most of the world is now drawn after the Maharash, telling 'wonders' about him.
Tags: maharash, tzemach tzedek, pleshchenitz, succession, rebbe maharash, letter, yosef kogel

Title: MaHaRiL of Kopust sends Rashbatz funds and instructions for printing
Summary: On 21 Menachem Av תרכ"ו the Maharil of Kopust wrote to the Rashbatz enclosing 100 silver rubles toward his share of the Likkutei Torah printing along with a long list of detailed instructions.
Story: Among the last letters of the Maharil of Kopust — written about two and a half months before his passing — was this note to R' Shmuel Betzalel Sheftil enclosing his share of the printing costs of the second edition of Likkutei Torah, plus a 'long memo' detailing the printing specifics. The letter highlights the close working partnership between the rebbe and his publishing manager.
Tags: maharil of kopust, rashbatz, likkutei torah, zhitomir

Title: Passing of MaHaRiL of Kopust
Summary: R' Yehuda Leib Schneersohn, the Admur of Kopust (MaHaRiL), passed away on 3 Mar Cheshvan תרכ"ז.
Story: The MaHaRiL of Kopust, eldest son of the Tzemach Tzedek and founder of the Kopust line, passed away on 3 Mar Cheshvan תרכ"ז, about two and a half months after his last letter to the Rashbatz concerning the Likkutei Torah second edition. He had served as Rebbe briefly following his father's passing in Nissan of that year.
Tags: maharil of kopust, kopust, passing

Title: Maharil of Kopust passes away
Summary: R' Yehuda Leib Schneersohn, the Maharil of Kopust and son of the Tzemach Tzedek, passed away on 3 Cheshvan 5627.
Story: The Maharil, a son of the Tzemach Tzedek, was one of the founders of the Kopust branch of Chabad after his father's passing. He had been involved in many rabbinic appointments across Chabad communities, including those in Bobruisk, Romny, and Horki.
Tags: maharil kopust, yehuda leib schneersohn, tzemach tzedek, chabad, kopust

Title: Sephardic Chief Rabbi appeals to Tzemach Tzedek's sons for kollel support
Summary: On 25 Shevat 5627 Rishon LeTzion R' Chaim David Chazan wrote to the Tzemach Tzedek's sons urging them to continue their late father's support of the Hebron and Jerusalem Chabad kollels.
Story: Following the Tzemach Tzedek's passing, Hebron and Jerusalem Chabad communities feared the loss of their crucial support. Sephardic Chief Rabbi Chaim David Chazan dispatched R' Yehuda Leib Slonim to Lubavitch with his letter urging the rebbe's sons to assume their father's role. He warned that without their oversight Chabad communities would become 'like sheep without a shepherd' and praised how splendid the kollelot had been until then.
Tags: hebron, jerusalem, lubavitch, chaim david chazan, tzemach tzedek, yehuda leib slonim, kollel chabad

Title: R. Shmuel HaLevi Levin serves as moreh tzedek of Lubavitch
Summary: By 15 Tammuz 5627 R. Shmuel b. Shlomo HaLevi Levin was serving briefly as moreh tzedek of Lubavitch.
Story: After R. Avraham haKohen's tenure, R. Shmuel b. Shlomo Tzvi HaLevi Levin briefly served as moreh tzedek of Lubavitch. A receipt he issued to a shochet on 15 Tammuz 5627 (July 1867) preserves his title. He was nicknamed 'the Rav of Lubavitch' for the rest of his life, though his actual tenure was short, ending when R. Avraham Zeligsohn was installed in the post.
Tags: shmuel levin, lubavitch, rabbinate

Title: Death of R' Yaakov Zevulun m'Shyuf at age 42
Summary: R' Yaakov Zevulun m'Shyuf, son of R' Yosef Yehuda Leib, died in 5628 at age 42.
Story: Born around 5586 and brought to Eretz Yisrael as a four-year-old in 5590, R' Yaakov Zevulun m'Shyuf died in 5628 at age 42. He was the eldest son of R' Yosef Yehuda Leib m'Shyuf, who had made aliyah from Shklov to Chevron with his father-in-law's family.
Tags: yaakov zevulun shyuf, jerusalem

Title: Fire destroys the Lubavitch courtyard
Summary: In the summer of 5628 fire again consumed the entire Lubavitch courtyard and all the buildings standing upon it.
Story: Just two years into the Maharash's leadership, the wooden buildings of the Rebbe's courtyard were destroyed. The disaster forced major rebuilding decisions, including whether the Maharash could lawfully build his residence on the site of his father's home given the Tzemach Tzedek's will against such use. The rebuilding produced the large hall and new family residences that would characterize the courtyard for the remaining decades.
Tags: fire, lubavitch-courtyard

Title: Hebron Chabad-Sephardic agreement of 5628
