Summary: In 5628, R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, R' Levi Yitzchak Slonim, and R' Shneur Zalman Pundaminski signed an agreement on behalf of Kollel Chabad in Hebron.
Story: This marked the formal entry of R' Levi Yitzchak Slonim into kollel leadership. He would soon dominate Hebron Chabad affairs, with later agreements stating that 'no significant matter could be concluded without R' Levi Yitzchak as long as he was the chosen representative of Chabad.'
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, levi yitzchak slonim, shneur zalman pundaminski

Title: Kuntres HaHispaalus printed as introduction edition in Warsaw
Summary: In 5628 (1868) the introductory letter of the Mittler Rebbe's 1814 trilogy was printed in Warsaw as the preface to Kuntres HaHispaalus.
Story: Although written in 1814, the introductory letter was the last of the three to see print. It appeared in Warsaw in 1868 as the preface to a new edition of Kuntres HaHispaalus. With this, all three of the 1814 letters to Anash were finally in circulation.
Tags: mittler-rebbe, warsaw, kuntres-hahispaalus, letters

Title: Likkutei Biurim on Kuntres HaHispaalus by Rabbi Hillel of Paritch published
Summary: First Warsaw edition of Likkutei Biurim on Kuntres HaHispaalus by Rabbi Hillel of Paritch was printed in 5628.
Story: Rabbi Hillel of Paritch, a foremost chassid of the Mitteler Rebbe and Tzemach Tzedek, wrote extensive commentaries on the Rebbeim's chassidic discourses. His Likkutei Biurim on Kuntres HaHispaalus was first printed in Warsaw in 5628 (1868).
Tags: warsaw, hillel paritch, chassidus

Title: Maamar HaShiflus VeHaSimcha by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil published
Summary: First edition of Maamar HaShiflus VeHaSimcha by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil appeared in 5628.
Story: Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil was a leading chassid of the Alter Rebbe, Mitteler Rebbe, and Tzemach Tzedek. His Maamar HaShiflus VeHaSimcha, an explication of chassidic teachings on lowliness and joy, was first printed in 5628 (1868) and is now exhibited at the Lubavitch Library.
Tags: yitzchak aizik homil, chassidus

Title: Maharash travels to Marienbad for health treatment
Summary: Due to his fragile health, Maharash traveled to the healing springs of Marienbad on doctors' recommendation.
Story: Already in 5628 (1868), Rebbe Maharash was very weak and traveled to Marienbad and other curative springs. Physicians instructed him to engage in physical exercise and manual work, regimens that continued for years afterward and were the subject of his brother's solicitous inquiries in correspondence.
Tags: maharash, marienbad, health, spa

Title: Second great fire destroys the Lubavitch courtyard
Summary: In the summer of 5628 the entire Lubavitch courtyard and its houses burned down again, forcing reconstruction.
Story: Two years after Maharash took up leadership, in summer 5628 (1868), the Chabad courtyard in Lubavitch suffered another major fire, destroying the houses and many of the Tzemach Tzedek's seforim and manuscripts. This created a legal-halachic dilemma because the Tzemach Tzedek's will had stipulated that none of his descendants live in his house — only Torah study or a beis midrash should occupy the site.
Tags: lubavitch, fire, maharash, tzemach-tzedek, russia

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's house in Lubavitch burns
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek's house in Lubavitch burned in 5628 (1868), two years after his passing.
Story: The home of the Tzemach Tzedek burned in 1868, two years after his death. The manuscripts of his Torah writings survived because they had been moved to and preserved in the home of his son the Rebbe Maharash. The fire is mentioned in Igros Kodesh of the Rebbe Maharash, letter 41.
Tags: lubavitch, tzemach tzedek, fire, manuscripts, rebbe maharash

Title: Agreement among Ashkenazi Kollelim in Eretz Yisrael over Siberian shlichim revenue
Summary: Heads of all Ashkenazi Kollelim in Eretz Yisrael signed a binding agreement assigning donations from five Siberian cities and Smolensk exclusively to Kollel Reisin.
Story: On 19 Tammuz 5628, leaders of the Perushim, Volyn Chassidim, and Chabad kollelim in Jerusalem, Hebron, Tzfat and Tiberias formalized in writing that revenue from Chita, Verkhneudinsk, Petrovsky Zavod, Barguzin and Achinsk would belong solely to Kollel Reisin. Chabad signatories Shimon Menashe Chaikin, Levi Yitzchak Slonim and Shneur Zalman Pundaminsky signed on behalf of Kollel Chabad of Hebron. The text was preserved in the Kollel Chabad letter register and copied again in 5662 when the kollel debated dispatching dedicated shlichim to Siberia.
Tags: jerusalem, hebron, siberia, kollel chabad, kollel reisin, perushim, shadar, fundraising

Title: Crown Prince of Prussia visits Hebron tomb
Summary: The Crown Prince of Prussia gained access to the Tomb of the Patriarchs.
Story: His visit was another of the rare exceptions to the Muslim ban on non-Muslim entry. Each such visit typically required direct intervention from the Turkish sultan.
Tags: hebron, meorat-hamachpelah, european-royalty

Title: Passing of Rabbi Baruch Shalom Schneersohn
Summary: Rabbi Baruch Shalom, eldest son of the Tzemach Tzedek, passed away on 16 Shevat 5629 and was buried near his father's grave in Lubavitch.
Story: Rabbi Baruch Shalom — 'safek bechor' (a doubtful firstborn) per a note by his brother Maharash — passed away on 16 Shevat 5629 (late January 1869), four years after his father the Tzemach Tzedek. He was interred about 4.5 cubits from his father's grave inside the ohel built in Lubavitch. The dating of his birth and death is used in halachic literature to discuss Ashkenazi customs regarding naming a child after a living relative.
Tags: baruch-shalom, tzemach-tzedek, lubavitch, russia, schneersohn

Title: Chabad settlement in Tzfat renewed
Summary: Around 5630, the Chabad community in Tzfat was reestablished by R' Yisrael Dover Yaffe and his son-in-law R' Asher Yechezkel Horowitz.
Story: R' Yisrael Dover Yaffe, son of one of the Hebron Kollel Chabad administrators, relocated from Hebron to Tzfat to live near his father-in-law R' David Yehuda Leib. Around the same time, the widow Mrs. Bila, niece of the Tzemach Tzedek, immigrated to Tzfat with her five orphaned sons. The two families merged through marriage and became the nucleus of the renewed Chabad community in Tzfat.
Tags: tzfat, eretz yisrael, settlement, yisrael dober yaffe, asher yechezkel horowitz

Title: Mrs. Bila immigrates to Tzfat with orphaned sons
Summary: Mrs. Bila, niece of the Tzemach Tzedek, immigrated to Tzfat with her five orphaned sons around 5630.
Story: After her husband R' Yeshaya Halevi Horowitz of Beshenkovichi died in 5624, Bila returned to her uncle the Tzemach Tzedek's home with her five young orphans. The Tzemach Tzedek corresponded with R' Aharon of Karlin and R' Aharon of Chernobyl, and together they agreed to support her settlement in the Holy Land. She then made aliyah to Tzfat with her sons, joining the renewed Chabad community there.
Tags: tzfat, tzemach tzedek, bila horowitz, widows, aliyah

Title: Russian translation of the Haggadah by Moshe Goldstein printed in Vilna
Summary: Moshe ben Yaakov Goldstein's Russian translation of the Haggadah was printed in Vilna.
Story: Around 5630 (1870), Moshe ben Yaakov Goldstein produced a Russian translation of the Haggadah, accompanied by annotations in Russian, printed in Vilna. The 70-page work featured the original Hebrew and Russian translation page-by-page. It marked an early example of a Russian-language Haggadah for the Russian Empire's Jews.
Tags: haggadah, russian, vilna, russia, moshe goldstein

Title: Joint Hebron sages letter printed in HaMagid
Summary: A joint letter signed by Hebron's Sephardic and Ashkenazi Chabad sages was printed in HaMagid following its dating in Tevet 1870.
Story: In Tevet 1870 (טבת תר"ל), the leading rabbis of Hebron - both Sephardic and Chabad Ashkenazim - signed a joint appeal describing the community's plight. The letter was published as a supplement in HaMagid on 15 Adar I 1870, urging Jewish donors to contribute generously to support the suffering Holy Land communities.
Tags: hebron, hamagid, chabad kollel, sephardim, famine, fundraising

Title: Letter from Rebbe Maharaitz of Ovruch to his brother Maharash
Summary: Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak of Ovruch wrote to his brother Rebbe Maharash about the latter's health and gifts purchased for the betrothed children Maharashab and Sterna Sarah.
Story: In the summer of 5630 (1870), Yosef Yitzchak of Ovruch sent a letter to his brother Maharash of Lubavitch inquiring about his health, his milk-drinking and gymnastics regimen, the status of the shadarim collecting funds for Eretz Yisrael and Maamad, and the progress of printing the Tzemach Tzedek responsa. He also asked Maharash to deliver, on his behalf, a gift he had bought in Petersburg to his son Maharashab (then nine years old), and to send a gift to his betrothed Sterna Sarah.
Tags: yosef yitzchak of ovruch, maharash, maharashab, sterna sarah, correspondence, russia

Title: Attached letter to Avraham Zalman Ginzburg of Vitebsk for tea from Moscow
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak of Ovruch asked the wealthy Avraham Zalman Ginzburg to order Gulubkov tea from Moscow for him, since he could not drink the Kiev tea.
Story: On 27 Tammuz 5630 (26 July 1870), in Ovruch, the Rebbe of Ovruch wrote to the philanthropist R' Avraham Zalman Ginzburg of Vitebsk asking him to arrange that four pounds of Gulubkov tea be shipped from Moscow to Ovruch. He explained that although tea was available in nearby Kiev, he could not drink that tea. Ginzburg would later become a mechutan of Maharash when his son married Devorah Leah.
Tags: yosef yitzchak of ovruch, avraham zalman ginzburg, vitebsk, moscow, ovruch

Title: First volume of Shu"t Tzemach Tzedek printed in Vilna
Summary: The first volume of the Tzemach Tzedek's responsa was published in Vilna after years of editorial work.
Story: After the Tzemach Tzedek's passing, his manuscripts were entrusted to two Chabad rabbis, R' Chaim Yaakov Widrevitz and R' Shimon ben Dovid, to prepare the responsa and novellae for publication. They worked on the material for several years, and the first volume was finally printed in Vilna in 5631 (1871).
Tags: tzemach tzedek, responsa, vilna, chaim yaakov widrevitz, shimon ben david

Title: First volume of Tzemach Tzedek's responsa printed
Summary: In 5631 the first volume of the Tzemach Tzedek's responsa — Even HaEzer — was published, beginning the multi-decade project of releasing his halachic writings.
Story: Five years after the Tzemach Tzedek's passing, editors completed the first volume of his responsa, covering Even HaEzer. The series would take another thirteen years to complete and was given the name Tzemach Tzedek (gematria of Menachem Mendel). From the publication of these volumes onward, the Rebbe himself became known as 'the Tzemach Tzedek.'
Tags: tzemach tzedek, responsa, even haezer, shu"t

Title: Hebron Romano land purchase deed
Summary: In 1871 (5631) a deed was registered for a parcel of Hebron land purchased on behalf of Markado Romano of Istanbul.
Story: In 1871 a deed in Arabic was executed recording the purchase of a Hebron parcel for 'Markado the Jew of Constantinople residing in al-Khalil' from Khalil, son of the late Ibrahim Abu-Amar Siyaj, for 4,000 grush. The Romano family used such purchases to begin building outside the walls of the Jewish quarter, breaking the ghetto pattern. The grand Romano mansion that resulted was constructed over the following years and completed in 5638.
Tags: hebron, romano, real estate, istanbul

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's first edition published in Vilna
Summary: The first edition of the responsa work 'Tzemach Tzedek' was published in Vilna in 5631.
Story: In 5631 (1871), the first edition of the responsa work 'Tzemach Tzedek' by Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneersohn was published in Vilna. The book gathered the halachic responsa of the third Chabad Rebbe. A copy of this first edition is preserved in the Lubavitch Library.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, vilna, responsa

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's responsa begin publication
Summary: Editing and printing of the Tzemach Tzedek's responsa began in 5631 (1871) and continued through 1884.
Story: Following the brothers' 1866 commitment to publish their father's manuscripts, the Tzemach Tzedek's responsa were sent to editors and printed serially from 1871 through 1884. His chassidic discourses were not printed in this period; they only appeared many years later in the Ohr HaTorah series.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, responsa, shut tzemach tzedek, rebbe maharash

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's responsa printed in Vilna
Summary: The first edition of the Tzemach Tzedek's responsa, Tzemach Tzedek, was printed in Vilna in 1871.
Story: This 5631 (1871) Vilna printing brought the third Chabad rebbe's halachic correspondence into print, anchoring his halachic legacy alongside his already-published chassidic and kabbalistic works.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, vilna, first edition, responsa

Title: Tzemach Tzedek's Shu"t Even Ha'ezer Volume 1 printed in Vilna
Summary: The first volume of the Tzemach Tzedek's responsa on Even Ha'ezer was printed in Vilna, with proceeds going to his sons and grandsons.
Story: The volume bore the notation that it was brought to press by the Tzemach Tzedek's sons and grandsons, who received the income from sales. The publication was managed by R. Refael Mordechai Schneersohn and R. Meshulam Shilem Reich. After printing, copies were distributed among descendants for sale.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, vilna, responsa, even haezer

Title: Wedding of R' Menachem Tzvi b. R' Shmuel Dovber of Borisov in Lubavitch
Summary: The wedding of R' Menachem Tzvi, son of the famed Chassid R' Shmuel Dovber of Borisov, takes place in Lubavitch in Adar.
Story: In Adar 5631 the wedding of R' Menachem Tzvi son of R' Shmuel Dovber (RShD"M) of Borisov was held in Lubavitch. RA"Ch sent a gift to the father of the groom in advance, and RShD"M acknowledged it in a letter that also mentioned an unspecified request that RA"Ch wished him to bring before the Maharash.
Tags: lubavitch, borisov, shmuel dovber borisov, wedding, menachem tzvi

Title: R' Shmuel Dovber of Borisov acknowledges RA"Ch's wedding gift
Summary: RShD"M of Borisov writes to RA"Ch thanking him for his gift and promising to intercede on his behalf with the Maharash.
Story: On 26 Shevat 5631, in the run-up to his son's wedding in Lubavitch, R' Shmuel Dovber of Borisov wrote to RA"Ch thanking him for the gift and the blessing. He added that he would not be lax in raising RA"Ch's request before the Maharash, though the specific nature of the request is not preserved in the surviving correspondence.
Tags: borisov, shmuel dovber borisov, lubavitch, letter, maharash

Title: Maharash builds large hall in Lubavitch courtyard
Summary: In 5632 the Maharash erected a large hall of roughly 21 by 21 meters on the site of his father's former residence in the Lubavitch courtyard.
Story: The hall featured an unusually high ceiling and tall, wide windows on three sides. It was used for High Holiday prayers and large farbrengens whenever sizable crowds of Chassidim came to Lubavitch. It later hosted major family celebrations including the 5652 Hornstein wedding, the 5653 bar mitzvah, and the 5657 wedding of the Frierdiker Rebbe.
Tags: maharash, construction, lubavitch-courtyard

Title: Maharash builds the Large Hall on the Tzemach Tzedek's house site
Summary: In 5632 Maharash built the 30-by-30-cubit Ulam HaGadol on the site of his father's burnt house, designated for prayer during large gatherings.
Story: After the 1868 fire, Maharash addressed his father's halachic will by erecting in 5632 (1872) a large hall (30 cubits square) on the site of the Tzemach Tzedek's former house. The hall served for Yamim Noraim prayers and major chassidic gatherings, where in later years the Rebbe Rayatz's bar mitzvah and his wedding to Rebbetzin Nechama Dina would also be held.
Tags: lubavitch, maharash, synagogue, ulam-hagadol, tzemach-tzedek

Title: R' Yehuda Leib Slonim joins Hebron Kollel leadership
Summary: In 5632, R' Yehuda Leib Slonim was added to the Hebron Chabad leadership team.
Story: He joined the existing trio of R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, R' Levi Yitzchak Slonim, and R' Shneur Zalman Pundaminski. The four men together appeared as overseers in the 5635 census, alongside R' Yeshaya Ornstein, who served as the kollel's scribe while living in Jerusalem.
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, slonim family, yehuda leib slonim

Title: Wedding of Moshe Aryeh Leib Ginzburg and Devorah Leah, daughter of Maharash
Summary: Moshe Aryeh Leib Ginzburg, son of Avraham Zalman Ginzburg of Vitebsk, married Devorah Leah, daughter of Rebbe Maharash.
Story: In the summer of 5632 (1872), R' Moshe Aryeh Leib Ginzburg, son of the philanthropist Avraham Zalman Ginzburg of Vitebsk, married Devorah Leah, daughter of the Rebbe Maharash of Lubavitch. The match sealed a family connection between the Schneersohn dynasty and a leading Vitebsk merchant family.
Tags: maharash, devorah leah, moshe aryeh leib ginzburg, avraham zalman ginzburg, vitebsk

Title: Agreement uniting Kollel Chabad with other Jerusalem kollels signed
Summary: Heads of the Perushim, Volhynia, and Chabad kollels signed a ten-point agreement in Jerusalem on 14 Iyar 5632 unifying fundraising from Russia and Siberia.
Story: After the earlier 5628 (1868) understanding failed to specify each kollel's share, leaders of all Ashkenazi kollels in the Holy Land negotiated a detailed pact dividing donations from Russia and Siberia—four parts to Perushim and Volhynia and one-fifth to Chabad. The document established joint signatories on receipts, banned unilateral fundraising letters, and required all monies to pass through four designated rabbis. It was signed for Kollel Chabad by Shimon Menashe Chaikin, Levi Yitzchak Slonim, Shneur Zalman Pundiminsky, and Yehuda Leib Slonim, all based in Hebron.
Tags: jerusalem, hebron, kollel chabad, perushim, volhynia, fundraising, russia, siberia, levi yitzchak slonim

Title: Rebbe Maharash advises chassid Shmuel Dovber of Borisov on Pleshchenitz trade
Summary: During Chanukah 5633, the Rebbe Maharash, through his secretary, instructed the chassid R' Shmuel Dovber of Borisov (the Reshadam) to travel to Pleshchenitz and proceed with a merchandise purchase.
Story: The Reshadam had written to ask whether to travel to Pleshchenitz to buy goods at a favorable price. The Rebbe's reply, sent through Levi Yitzchak Idelevitz on the 7th day of Chanukah 5633 (December 1872), told him to set the merchant's letter aside and make the trip. The exchange shows how the Maharash gave concrete commercial guidance to chassidim engaged in trade.
Tags: maharash, reshadam, shmuel dovber, borisov, pleshchenitz, commerce, levi yitzchak idelevitz

Title: Reshadam writes Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum of Pleshchenitz about a halachic question
Summary: On 6 Tevet 5633, R' Shmuel Dovber of Borisov wrote R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum of Pleshchenitz to reconcile a written Pesikta source with an oral ruling Rosenbaum had transmitted.
Story: Writing on motzaei Shabbat, 6 Tevet 5633 (December 1872), the Reshadam tells Rosenbaum that the Pesikta passage just received from the post and an oral ruling reported in Rosenbaum's name appear to contradict one another. He treats the printed source as 'halacha v'ein morin kein' because of the risk involved, and asks for a clear practical clarification before an awaited visitor arrives for the last days of Chanukah.
Tags: reshadam, avraham chaim rosenbaum, pleshchenitz, borisov, correspondence, commerce

Title: First record of Rogachov committee in Kollel Chabad ledger
Summary: The earliest documented mention of the Rogachov committee appears in the Kollel Chabad financial ledger of 5633.
Story: The 'Rogachov Vaad' served as the central committee receiving funds for Kollel Chabad in the diaspora. The earliest extant mention appears in a Kollel Chabad accounting ledger of 5633 noting 'sent from Rogachov.' The committee likely was established earlier, perhaps by the Tzemach Tzedek himself.
Tags: rogachov, kollel chabad, fundraising, dan tomarkin

Title: Hebron Chabad beit din bans modern schools
Summary: In 5633 R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin and his Hebron beit din signed a ruling forbidding the new modern schools, following the 5631 Jerusalem rabbis' ruling.
Story: Following the 5631 ruling by Jerusalem's rabbis against the new haskalah-influenced modern schools, the Hebron Chabad rav R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin signed a parallel prohibition with his beit din of R' Chaim Yaakov and R' Shaul. Hungarian Chassidim of Hebron including R' Alexander Zushe Hoizman, his son R' Shimon, and R' Aryeh Leib also added their signatures. The ban appears in 'Maaseh Avot' (Jerusalem 1901).
Tags: hebron, modern schools, haskalah, shimon menashe chaikin, ban, hungarian chassidim

Title: Kollel Chabad funds Tzfat Beit Midrash
Summary: In 5633, Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem allocated funds for the Tzfat Beit Midrash as the community there began to develop again.
Story: The Chabad Beit Midrash in Tzfat dated back to the pre-5583 Chabad settlement there. As the community redeveloped in 5633, Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem began allocating funds for its upkeep, recognizing the resurgent presence of Chabad in the holy city.
Tags: tzfat, beit midrash, kollel chabad, jerusalem

Title: R' Eliezer Shimon Kaznovsky and family settle in Hebron
Summary: In 5633 R' Eliezer Shimon Kaznovsky immigrated with his family to Hebron, accompanied by his grandson R' Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov.
Story: R' Eliezer Shimon Kaznovsky, son of Sheterna Riza Slonim, made aliyah from abroad with his family in 5633 and settled in Hebron. His grandson R' Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov (known as Shila) came with him and would go on to become a leader of the Hebron community, its rabbi, and an administrator of Kollel Chabad from 5663 onward.
Tags: hebron, aliyah, kaznovsky, eliezerov

Title: Rabbi Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld immigrates to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: The future leader of the Eidah HaChareidis immigrated to the Holy Land.
Story: Sonnenfeld, a student of the Ktav Sofer of Pressburg, worked closely with Rabbi Yehuda Leib Diskind, rabbi of Jerusalem's Ashkenazi community. He would later become a central voice opposing Zionist secularization in the city.
Tags: sonnenfeld, jerusalem, aliyah

Title: Wedding of Maharash's son Raza in the Small Hall
Summary: At the start of winter 5634, the wedding of Maharash's son Rabbi Zalman Aharon (Raza) was held in the newly built Small Hall in Lubavitch.
Story: Maharash had stipulated when building the Small Hall (Ulam HaKatan) on the site of the former beis midrash that he could use it for any purpose he wished. At the start of winter 5634 (1873), because the Large Hall was unheated, the wedding feast of his son Raza was held in the Small Hall with klezmer music, with Maharash citing that original stipulation.
Tags: lubavitch, maharash, raza, wedding, ulam-hakatan

Title: Wedding of Rabbi Zalman Aharon Schneersohn (Raza) in Lubavitch
Summary: The wedding of the Maharash's son Rabbi Zalman Aharon, the Raza, was celebrated at the start of 5634 in the small hall of the Lubavitch courtyard.
Story: Because the wedding fell in winter and the large hall was unheated, the celebration meal was held in the heated small hall instead. The Maharash had reserved the right to use the small hall for any purpose at his discretion. This was the first major family celebration in the rebuilt Lubavitch courtyard.
Tags: raza, schneersohn, wedding

Title: Maharash sells chametz to R. Avraham Zeligsohn
Summary: A surviving 5634 chametz-sale document records the Maharash transferring his chametz to R. Avraham Zeligsohn before Pesach.
Story: A document from 5634 (1874) preserves the Rebbe Maharash's sale of chametz to R. Avraham b. Yosef Zeligsohn, who served as moreh tzedek of Lubavitch throughout the Maharash era. The document is reproduced in Tikunei Mikvaot Le-Takanat Rabbeinu, p. 185.
Tags: maharash, avraham zeligsohn, lubavitch, chametz, pesach

Title: Russian universal military conscription law published
Summary: The Russian government published the Ustav (decree) on military obligation, requiring every young Jewish male to serve four years in the army.
Story: In 5634 (1874), the Russian government issued a booklet titled 'Der Ustav (gezetz) vegen militer pflicht', instituting universal conscription. Every Jewish youth was required to serve four years in the Russian army, prompting widespread Jewish efforts to obtain exemptions and triggering periodic crackdowns when the authorities discovered such efforts.
Tags: russia, conscription, draft, ustav

Title: Yoreh Deah responsa of the Tzemach Tzedek printed
Summary: In 5634 the three volumes of the Tzemach Tzedek's Yoreh Deah responsa were printed, including supplementary teshuvos on niddah and mikvaos as omissions in the third volume.
Story: The Yoreh Deah set appeared in 5634 as part of the ongoing publication of the Tzemach Tzedek's halachic corpus. After printing the second volume, three additional responsa on the laws of niddah and mikvaos were discovered and added as 'omissions' at the end of the third volume — an early instance of the pattern of supplements and addenda that would characterize the entire series.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, responsa, yoreh deah

Title: Agreement between Kollel Chabad and other kollelim in Hebron
Summary: In 5635 the Chabad and other Ashkenazi kollelim in Hebron agreed to share funds incoming to Kollel Chabad equally.
Story: In 5635 the Chabad community in Hebron reached an agreement with the other Ashkenazi kollelim there that all funds entering Kollel Chabad's coffers in the name of the Hebron Ashkenazi community would be shared equally with members of the other kollelim. Oversight of the fund remained exclusively with Kollel Chabad's Hebron managers, with the official name being 'Kollel Ashkenazim Chabad of Hebron.'
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, ashkenazi kollelim, fundraising

Title: Jerusalem census records trustees of Kollel Chabad
Summary: The 5635 census listed Avraham Statzeres, Aharon Lipkin, and the scribe Yeshaya Orenstein as Kollel Chabad trustees.
Story: Avraham Statzeres, born in Navaradok in 5565, had made aliyah in 5621. Aharon Lipkin, born in Tolzin in 5593, had made aliyah in 5607. Yeshaya Orenstein, born in Eretz Yisrael in 5595, served alongside them as the scribe of the trusteeship.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, census, statzeres, lipkin, orenstein

Title: Marriage of Rashab and Shterna Sara
Summary: Rabbi Shalom Dovber Schneersohn married his cousin Shterna Sara, who moved from Ovruch to Lubavitch.
Story: In 1875, Rabbi Shalom Dovber (the Rashab) married his cousin Rebbetzin Shterna Sara, fulfilling an engagement contract drawn up in 1865 when both were young children. Shterna Sara moved four hundred miles from her hometown of Ovruch, Ukraine, to Lubavitch following the marriage. The match had been suggested by Rabbi Menachem Mendel, who saw the two grandchildren together and declared them 'Bride and groom!'
Tags: lubavitch, ovruch, ukraine, marriage, rashab, shterna sara

Title: Montefiore 1875 census lists the three Brimat brothers in Hebron
Summary: The 5635 (1875) Montefiore census of the Chabad community of Hebron records the three Twer brothers — Saul, Leib, and Israel — under the family name 'Brimat'.
Story: By 1875 the patriarch R. Yaakov Mordechai had already passed, and only his three Hebron-resident sons were enumerated, each under the BeRiMaT (ben R. Mordechai Twer) surname they had adopted. The census documents the consolidation of the family identity in the Old Yishuv.
Tags: montefiore census, hebron, 1875, brimat, chabad

Title: Montefiore's sixth and final visit to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: Montefiore's 5635 visit produced one final round of community censuses for the Yishuv.
Story: Like its predecessors, the 5635 census recorded each community's institutions and leadership separately. The records remain a primary source for the demography of the mid-19th century Yishuv, with the originals in London and a working card index compiled by Yehoshua Mondshine.
Tags: montefiore, census, eretz yisrael

Title: Wedding of Rebbe Rashab in Ovruch
Summary: On Motzaei Shabbos 11 Elul 5635, the Rebbe Rashab married Rebbetzin Sterna Sara in Ovruch rather than the originally planned Jerusalem.
Story: Although the tnaim of 5625 had set the wedding for Jerusalem in summer 5635, the actual wedding of the future Rebbe Rashab to Rebbetzin Sterna Sara took place on Motzaei Shabbos 11 Elul 5635 in the city of Ovruch. The Rebbe Maharash did not attend, for various reasons; he was known to have wanted the wedding held specifically in Lubavitch, arguing that if not Jerusalem as stipulated, then Lubavitch.
Tags: rebbe rashab, sterna sara, wedding, ovruch, maharash

Title: R' Yisrael Dover Yaffe dies of plague in Tzfat
Summary: R' Yisrael Dover Yaffe, a founder of the renewed Chabad community in Tzfat, died of plague on 27 Tishrei 5636.
Story: After several years supporting his son-in-law R' Asher Yechezkel Horowitz at his table, R' Yisrael Dover Yaffe died from the plague. His death left R' Asher Yechezkel as head of the family and the emerging Chabad community in Tzfat, a leadership role he would hold for decades.
Tags: tzfat, plague, yaffe family

Title: Death of Rabbi Menachem Nachum Twersky of Loyev
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Nachum Twersky of Loyev, a Chernobyl dynasty rebbe, passes away in 5636.
Story: Rabbi Menachem Nachum of Loyev, father of Rabbi Mordechai of Loyev, died in 5636. After his passing, his son Mordechai signed letters as 'son of the deceased Menachem Nachum,' a signature change that helps date the surviving correspondence of the Chernobyl-Rachmistrivka rabbinic family.
Tags: chernobyl, loyev, twersky, ukraine

Title: Death of Rabbi Yitzchak Yosef Twersky of Ovrutch
Summary: Rabbi Yitzchak Yosef of Ovrutch, son-in-law of the Tzemach Tzedek, passes away in 5636.
Story: Rabbi Yitzchak Yosef Twersky of Ovrutch, son-in-law of the Tzemach Tzedek of Lubavitch, died in 5636. He was succeeded by his son Nachum Dov ('Maharanad'), who led the Ovrutch chasidic court until his own death in 5654 and was also the brother-in-law of the Rebbe Rashab.
Tags: ovrutch, twersky, tzemach-tzedek, ukraine

Title: Imrei Noam by Rabbi Hillel of Paritch published in Vilna
Summary: First edition of Imrei Noam by Rabbi Hillel of Paritch was printed in Vilna in 5636.
Story: Rabbi Hillel of Paritch wrote his own chassidic discourses and commentaries on those of the Rebbeim. Imrei Noam was first printed in Vilna in 5636 (1876) and is displayed at the Lubavitch Library exhibition of the great Chabad chassidim.
Tags: vilna, hillel paritch, chassidus

Title: Montefiore's second visit to Russia
Summary: Moses Montefiore returned to Russia three decades after his first meeting with the czar.
Story: The visit continued his lifelong diplomatic effort on behalf of Russian Jews. The Rebbe Rayatz would later cite Montefiore's interventions as a model when urging American Jewish leaders to advocate with the Soviet regime.
Tags: moses-montefiore, russia, diplomacy

Title: R' Shimon Engel of Zelichov born
Summary: R' Avraham Shimon Engel-Horowitz was born in 5636 in the town of Zelichov.
Story: After marriage he initially preferred to earn his living by selling vinegar rather than accept rabbinic positions, only consenting to teach after losing his money. He went on to teach in Tzanz, Krzanov, Stolin and ultimately Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw.
Tags: zelichov, shimon engel zelichover, birth

Title: R. Yosef Kugel of Plescenice passes away
Summary: The well-known chossid R. Yosef Kugel of Plescenice passes away around Adar 5636.
Story: R. Shmuel Dovber of Borisov, writing to R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum on 26 Adar 5636 (1876), reacts with shock to the sudden news of the passing of 'our friend, the God-fearing R. Yosef.' Earlier letters from 5 and 18 Adar of that year had still sent regards to R. Yosef and his nephew R. Gershon Leib, showing how unexpected the loss was for the chassidic circle of Plescenice.
Tags: plescenice, kugel, chassidim, shmuel dovber of borisov

Title: Toldot Amudei HaChabad published in Königsberg
Summary: Michael Levi Radkinson's Toldot Amudei HaChabad, a biographical work on the Chabad Rebbes, was published in Königsberg in 5636.
Story: In 5636 (1876), the writer Michael Levi Radkinson published Toldot Amudei HaChabad in Königsberg. The book gathered and reworked the existing biographical traditions of the Chabad Rebbes for a wider reading public. It served as a precursor to later, more rigorous works such as Beit Rebbi.
Tags: radkinson, biography, konigsberg, chabad history

Title: Zikhron Yerushalayim published in Jerusalem
Summary: R' Shneur Zalman Mendelovitch published Zikhron Yerushalayim in Jerusalem in 5636.
Story: In 5636 R' Shneur Zalman Mendelovitch published Zikhron Yerushalayim in Jerusalem, which included a description of the Chabad Ashkenazi synagogue in Jerusalem. He recorded that the synagogue was founded with donations from Sir Abdullah Meir Sassoon and his brothers Eliyahu, Reuven, Avraham Shalom, and Sliman — sons of Sir David Sassoon — through the intermediation of the author and R' Zalman ben R' Nachum Yosef.
Tags: shneur zalman mendelovitch, jerusalem, zikhron yerushalayim, sassoon, chabad synagogue

Title: R' Yosef Kugel of Pleshchenitsy dies
Summary: The Chassid R' Yosef Kugel of Pleshchenitsy died around Adar 5636, mourned in a letter by R' Shmuel Dovber of Borisov.
Story: R' Yosef Kugel, brother of the mashpia R' Hendel Kugel, was one of the leading Chassidim of Pleshchenitsy. He died around Adar 5636, prompting R' Shmuel Dovber of Borisov to write to R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum on 26 Adar 5636 (22 March 1876) lamenting 'sudden news from Rebbi Z.R. of his camp of the passing of our beloved, God-fearing and trembling R' Y.'
Tags: pleshchenitsy, kugel family, r yosef kugel, r shmuel dovber of borisov

Title: Frumkin describes plight of Hebron's Jews in Chabatzelet
Summary: Yisrael Dov Frumkin published a report in Chabatzelet on 9 Marcheshvan describing the degraded state of Hebron's Jewish community.
Story: The editor of Chabatzelet, Yisrael Dov Frumkin, described how Hebron's Jews lived in conditions worse than Jews of other Palestinian cities. He depicted them as outnumbered by Turks of low moral standing, with weak local government and constant harassment — a Jew dared not even respond to insults lest a mob accuse him of insulting the religion and beat him severely.
Tags: hebron, chabatzelet, frumkin, ottoman empire, abuse

Title: Knesses Yisrael yeshivah founded in Slabodka
Summary: Rabbi Nosson Tzvi Finkel founded Yeshivas Knesses Yisrael in Slabodka, originally as a kollel for married men.
Story: In 1877, Rabbi Nosson Tzvi Finkel established Knesses Yisrael in Slabodka as a kollel for married men. It soon became a full yeshivah and introduced systematic study of musar, sparking the controversy that would lead opponents to open the rival Knesses Beis Yitzchak in 1897.
Tags: slabodka, nosson tzvi finkel, musar, kollel

Title: Maamar Yetzias Mitzrayim by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil published
Summary: First Vilna edition of Maamar Yetzias Mitzrayim by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil was printed in 5637.
Story: This discourse on the Exodus by the great chassid Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil was first printed in Vilna in 5637 (1877). It is one of several of his works exhibited in the Lubavitch Library's Rabboseinu exhibition.
Tags: vilna, yitzchak aizik homil

Title: R. Avraham Chaim decides to sell his share of the liquor business
Summary: In the summer of 5637 R. Avraham Chaim resolved to sell his portion of the yayin saraf (whiskey) enterprise he held jointly with his mechutan R. Hendel, sparking a dispute over how to divide it.
Story: R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum had been a partner with the mashpia R. Hendel in a whiskey and tavern business in Pleshchenitz. In the summer of 1877 he decided to liquidate his share, but he and R. Hendel could not agree on terms of the split. Both wrote their arguments to the Rebbe Maharash, who ultimately issued a binding compromise.
Tags: pleshchenitz, liquor business, avraham chaim rosenbaum, r. hendel, partnership dispute, belarus

Title: R. Chaim Yaakov Widrewitz becomes rabbi of Moscow
Summary: In 5637 R. Chaim Yaakov Widrewitz left the Kupishok rabbinate to become rabbi of Moscow, and R. Avraham Tzvi Brodno succeeded him in Kupishok.
Story: Widrewitz had served as rabbi of Kupishok during the era of the Tzemach Tzedek. In 5637 (1877) he was accepted as rabbi of Moscow, and R. Avraham Tzvi Brodno was appointed in his place in Kupishok.
Tags: widrewitz, moscow, kupishok, brodno, rabbinate

Title: R. Gershon Yehuda Leib Kugel passes away in Vilna
Summary: R. Gershon Yehuda Leib Kugel passes away on Sunday after nightfall, Parshas Nitzavim 5637, and is buried in Vilna on 18 Elul.
Story: His son R. Shlomo recorded in manuscript 584 that his father R. Gershon Yehuda Leib died on Motzaei Shabbos Parshas Nitzavim 5637 (1877) and was honored with burial in Vilna on 18 Elul, after midday. The yahrzeit is observed on 18 Elul. With his passing and the earlier move of the mashpia R. Hendel Kugel to Lubavitch, leadership of the Plescenice chassidim passed to R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum.
Tags: vilna, kugel, plescenice, chassidim

Title: Vilna publication of 'Maamar Yetziat Mitzrayim' by Yitzchak Aizik of Homil
Summary: Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik HaLevi Epstein of Homil's 'Maamar Yetziat Mitzrayim' Chabad commentary was published in Vilna.
Story: In 5637 (1877), 'Maamar Yetziat Mitzrayim' — a Chassidic Chabad commentary by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik HaLevi Epstein of Homil — was published in Vilna. The 29-leaf quarto edition expounded the inner meaning of the Exodus narrative according to Chabad Chassidic teaching. It served as a key text for Chabad students of the early Russian period.
Tags: chabad, homil, vilna, yitzchak aizik of homil, yetziat mitzrayim

Title: Letter from R. Shmuel Dovber of Borisov conveying the Maharash's compromise ruling
Summary: On 7 Elul 5637 R. Shmuel Dovber of Borisov wrote to R. Hendel transmitting the Rebbe Maharash's compromise between him and R. Avraham Chaim over their joint whiskey venture.
Story: After spending three Shabbosos in Lubavitch alongside R. Avraham Chaim and his brother, R. Shmuel Dovber of Borisov was directly entrusted by the Rebbe Maharash to relay his ruling in the partners' dispute. The psak gave R. Hendel a binary choice: retain the krechma and let R. Avraham Chaim sell his mill to anyone (even a non-Jewish license holder), or relinquish the krechma in exchange for 300 rubles. The Rebbe also advised R. Hendel to consult three trusted men if he could not decide on his own.
Tags: maharash, shmuel dovber of borisov, r. hendel, psak, liquor business, krechma, lubavitch, din torah

Title: R' Gershon Yehuda Leib Kugel buried in Vilna
Summary: R' Gershon Yehuda Leib Kugel was buried in Vilna on 18 Elul 5637.
Story: After dying just after Shabbat Parshat Nitzavim 5637, R' Gershon Yehuda Leib Kugel was buried in the Jewish community of Vilna on 18 Elul 5637 (28 August 1877). His yahrzeit was set for 18 Elul.
Tags: vilna, kugel family, r gershon leib kugel, burial

Title: R' Gershon Yehuda Leib Kugel dies
Summary: R' Gershon Yehuda Leib Kugel, son of R' Hendel Kugel and father of R' Shlomo, died after Shabbat Parshat Nitzavim 5637.
Story: As recorded by his son R' Shlomo in manuscript 584, R' Gershon Yehuda Leib Kugel died after the conclusion of Shabbat Parshat Nitzavim 5637 (September 1877). He was buried in Vilna on 18 Elul 5637 after midday, with his yahrzeit observed on 18 Elul.
Tags: pleshchenitsy, kugel family, vilna, r gershon leib kugel

Title: Murder of Rachamim Turgeman in Hebron
Summary: Hebron Jewish notable Rachamim Turgeman died from beating injuries, reported in Chabatzelet on 14 Tevet 5638.
Story: Rachamim Turgeman, a notable of the Hebron Jewish community and a British protégé, was severely beaten by a local Turk and died seven days later. The Hebron community alerted the governor, and because he was under British protection a commission including the British consul's representative and Dr. Chaplin came from Jerusalem, performed an autopsy confirming the cause of death, and arrested the assailant for trial.
Tags: hebron, murder, rachamim turgeman, british consulate, ottoman empire

Title: Birth of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson
Summary: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, father of the seventh Lubavitcher Rebbe, was born in 5638.
Story: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, son of Baruch Schneur Schneersohn and father of the Rebbe Menachem Mendel (the seventh Chabad Rebbe), was born in 5638 (1877/78). He descended from Rabbi Baruch Shalom, eldest son of the Tzemach Tzedek, through Baruch Schneur — a lineage Maharash's family tradition noted explicitly.
Tags: levi-yitzchak, schneerson, ramash-father, russia

Title: Chiddushim on the Talmud of the Tzemach Tzedek printed
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek's chiddushim on the Talmud were printed in 5638 as part of the ongoing release of his halachic writings.
Story: Published roughly in the middle of the multi-decade Tzemach Tzedek printing project, the chiddushim on Shas included editorial cross-references to teshuvos prepared for the Choshen Mishpat volume — suggesting that volume was already ready for press, though Russian censors refused to permit its publication.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, chiddushim, talmud

Title: Latvian authorities permit second Riga synagogue
Summary: In 1878 the Latvian authorities allowed an additional synagogue to be built within the Chassidic shul building in Riga.
Story: In 5638 (1878) the Latvian authorities permitted the construction of an additional synagogue building within the Riga Chassidic shul complex. From then on, three minyanim — all called 'Draisin' minyanim — operated under one roof: a mixed Chabad minyan, one exclusively for Lubavitch chassidim, and a larger one for Kapust chassidim.
Tags: riga, latvia, synagogue, draisin

Title: R' Yeshayahu Berlin settles in Riga
Summary: R' Yeshayahu Berlin, a leading supporter of Tomchei Tmimim, settled in Riga around 5638 (1878).
Story: R' Yeshayahu Berlin, a wealthy benefactor and one of the main supporters of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lubavitch as well as other activities of the Rebbe Rashab, established himself in Riga around 5638 (1878). His arrival anchored the growing Chabad community in the Latvian capital.
Tags: riga, latvia, tomchei-tmimim, philanthropy

Title: Rashab exempted from army draft
Summary: At age eighteen, the Rashab was exempted from the army draft after a medical examiner discovered he had tuberculosis.
Story: In 1878, at the age of eighteen, Rabbi Shalom Dovber (the Rashab) was examined for the Russian army draft. The medical examiner discovered he had tuberculosis, leading to his exemption from military service. Professor Zacharov told the Rashab's younger brother Mendel that the Rashab had just two months to live, a prognosis that proved dramatically incorrect as he lived for another forty-two years.
Tags: russia, rashab, army draft, exemption, tuberculosis, czarist russia

Title: Rebbe Maharash receives Tzemach Tzedek manuscript as gift
Summary: In 5638 (1878) the Rebbe Maharash gifted a Tzemach Tzedek chiddushim manuscript to his son, the future Rebbe Rashab.
Story: Manuscript 226, containing the Tzemach Tzedek's chiddushim and Even HaEzer responsa, was given by the Rebbe Maharash to his son, the future Rebbe Rashab, in 5638 (1878). A gold-tooled inscription on the binding records the gift.
Tags: rebbe maharash, rebbe rashab, tzemach tzedek, manuscript, gift

Title: Romano courtyard construction completed
Summary: Construction of the Romano mansion in Hebron was completed in 5638, immediately triggering a major dispute.
Story: After years of planning and building, Markado Romano's grand mansion in Hebron was completed in 5638. The completion immediately sparked a controversy when Romano had a dispute with one of the builders, who brought the matter before R' Eliyahu Mani, Sephardi rabbi of Hebron. When Mani ruled against Romano, Romano accused him of favoritism, igniting a years-long communal conflict that drew in the entire Holy Land Jewish community.
Tags: hebron, romano, real estate, controversy

Title: Small Chabad community established in Riga
Summary: A modest Chabad community takes root in Riga, with a few synagogues including one with three sanctuaries for Lubavitch, Liadi, and Kopust branches.
Story: The Riga Chabad community grew slowly until enhanced by Russian emigration in the early twentieth century. In the Jewish ghetto, one Chabad synagogue housed three adjacent sanctuaries for the varied Chabad sub-groups. But there was no yeshivah to bring a youthful spirit to the city, a far cry from Lubavitch's vibrant ethos.
Tags: riga, latvia, chabad, synagogue, ghetto

Title: Third edition of Likkutei Torah printed in Vilna
Summary: The third edition of Likkutei Torah was printed in Vilna in תרל"ח, including a notice clarifying that publication rights belonged to the grandsons of the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: The Vilna תרל"ח edition of Likkutei Torah included a printed statement that the haskamot of the great rabbis of the generation forbade reprinting without the permission of the Tzemach Tzedek's grandchildren, the sons of his son R' Menachem Mendel. The notice retroactively clarified that the prior תרכ"ו edition had also been undertaken for the Tzemach Tzedek's family.
Tags: vilna, likkutei torah, tzemach tzedek

Title: Yehudah V'Yerushalayim published mentioning Aharon Lipkin's role
Summary: R. Yoel Moshe Solomon's 1878 work described how funds from England for Jerusalem's kollelim flowed through Aharon Lipkin for Chabad.
Story: In Yehudah V'Yerushalayim, Yoel Moshe Solomon recounted that money received from England by the General Vaad of Jerusalem's kollelim was distributed to each kollel separately. The Chabad portion was delivered to R. Aharon Lipkin, identified as their trustee. The account confirms Lipkin's continuing leadership role through the 1870s.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, yoel moshe solomon, aharon lipkin

Title: Yonah Wolf Mendelsohn sent from Hebron to America as shadar
Summary: R. Yonah Wolf Mendelsohn was sent from Hebron to America in 5639 as emissary of the city's Jewish community.
Story: HaChavatzelet of 11 Cheshvan 5639 reported the shedarut as undertaken 'by the community of Israel residents of Hebron from the Sephardic and Ashkenazi congregations.' No indication ties it to the broader Kollel Chabad system. The article noted that Hebron's communities had never authorized the Jerusalem rabbinate to send emissaries on their behalf.
Tags: hebron, shadar, america, yonah wolf mendelsohn

Title: Cornerstone laid for Beis Menachem second floor
Summary: The cornerstone for the second floor of the Beis Menachem synagogue was laid in 5639, with plans drawn by the architect Schick.
Story: Binyamin ben Shlomo Yechezkel, a Sasson family relative, set the first stone. The community elder Shneur Zalman Mendelovitz prayed for the donor's late wife Leah bat Parchi and blessed the entire Sasson family in Bombay, London and Calcutta. The plaque on the upper floor names the building Knesset Eliyahu.
Tags: jerusalem, synagogue, beis menachem, kollel chabad, schick, sasson

Title: R' Aharon Shaul Zelig HaKohen passes away in Dinaburg
Summary: R' Aharon Shaul Zelig HaKohen of Pruzhana, author of 'Teshuvot LaShoel' and 'Magen Shaul,' died in 5639 (1879).
Story: Brought from Pruzhana around 5625 (1865) as Misnagdic rabbi of Dinaburg, R' Aharon Shaul Zelig HaKohen authored 'Teshuvot LaShoel' and 'Magen Shaul.' He served the community until his death in 5639 (1879).
Tags: dinaburg, mitnagdim, pruzhana, teshuvot-lashoel, magen-shaul

Title: R' Elimelech Siminawski first travels to America
Summary: R' Elimelech Siminawski of Sosnitsa was in America for the first time at the beginning of 5640 (autumn 1879).
Story: R' Elimelech Siminawski traveled from Sosnitsa to America at the start of 5640, during the wave of departures triggered by Russian pogroms. He later recounted that the Rebbe Maharin of Nezhin, when asked whether one should flee to America, replied that if there were any place to escape from the Holy One he would flee there himself. His testimony helped frame the early Chabad community's ambivalent view of the chasidim who emigrated west.
Tags: united states, russia, sosnitsa, emigration, anash

Title: R' Reuven HaLevi Levin succeeds him in Dinaburg
Summary: R' Reuven HaLevi Levin filled the Misnagdic rabbinic chair of Dinaburg from 5639 (1879).
Story: After R' Aharon Shaul Zelig HaKohen's death in 5639 (1879), R' Reuven HaLevi Levin assumed the Misnagdic rabbinate of Dinaburg. He served in that position until his own death in 5647 (1887).
Tags: dinaburg, mitnagdim, rabbinate

Title: Rebbetzin Shterna Sara's dream of three Rebbes
Summary: On Simchat Torah 1879, Rebbetzin Shterna Sara received a prophetic dream of three previous Rebbes promising her a son.
Story: On Simchat Torah 1879, Rebbetzin Shterna Sara was distressed after her father-in-law Rabbi Shmuel overlooked her when bestowing blessings on the family. That night, she dreamed of a Jew who promised her a son if she would give eighteen rubles to charity. Rabbi Shmuel later identified the dream visitors as the first three Lubavitcher Rebbes: the Tzemach Tzedek, the Mitteler Rebbe, and the Alter Rebbe. Ten months later, she gave birth to Yosef Yitzchak.
Tags: lubavitch, russia, dream, simchat torah, shterna sara, tzemach tzedek, mitteler rebbe, alter rebbe

Title: Second story added to Jerusalem Chabad synagogue
Summary: An additional level was constructed atop the Tzemach Tzedek synagogue in the Jewish Quarter.
Story: A plaque dedicated by the Sassoon family of Mumbai marking the addition remains prominently displayed in the building today.
Tags: jerusalem, tzemach-tzedek-shul, old-city

Title: Wedding of Brachah Slava Rosenbaum to Shlomo Kugel
Summary: R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum's daughter Brachah Slava married Shlomo, son of R' Gershon Yehudah Leib Kugel and grandson of the mashpia R' Hendel Kugel.
Story: The wedding took place during Parshas Terumah 5639 (early 1879). R' Avraham Chaim invited his close friend R' Shmuel Dovber of Borisov, who responded on 25 Adar with a mazal-tov letter explaining why he had been unable to attend. The match linked the Rosenbaum family with the Kugel family of Pleshchenitsy.
Tags: pleshchenitsy, kugel family, rosenbaum, wedding

Title: Wiener buys handwritten Tanya manuscript in Borisov
Summary: Shmuel ben Yermiyahu Wiener purchased a handwritten manuscript of the Tanya in the town of Borisov.
Story: In 5639 (1879), bibliophile Shmuel ben Yermiyahu Wiener acquired a handwritten Tanya manuscript in Borisov. The manuscript was missing its first page and conclusion, containing only up to chapter 37. Wiener's inscription on the inner cover documented the purchase. The manuscript was found in 1991 by Chabad emissaries in Leningrad's Asiatic Institute, in the Friedland collection.
Tags: tanya, manuscript, borisov, wiener, shmuel wiener, belarus

Title: Wedding of R' Shlomo Kugel and Bracha Slava Rosenbaum
Summary: R' Shlomo Kugel married Bracha Slava, daughter of R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum of Pleshchenitsy, during Parshat Terumah 5639.
Story: R' Shlomo, son of R' Gershon Yehuda Leib Kugel, married Bracha Slava, daughter of R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum of Pleshchenitsy, in the week of Parshat Terumah 5639 (February 1879). R' Shmuel Dovber of Borisov, unable to attend in person because he was in Lubavitch, sent a mazal-tov letter on 25 Adar 5639.
Tags: pleshchenitsy, kugel family, rosenbaum family, wedding

Title: Binyamin Aba grandson of R' Leib of Belz dies
Summary: Binyamin Aba ben R' Meir, identified in 'Avnei Zikaron' as grandson of the holy R' Leib of Belz, passed away on 21 Adar 5639.
Story: The record in 'Avnei Zikaron' chapter 12 of Binyamin Aba's death on 21 Adar 5639 has been cited in the scholarly discussion attempting to identify R' Leib of Belz with R' Leib Baal HaYisurim of Hebron, though the connection remains unproven.
Tags: belz, leib of belz, hebron, avnei zikaron

Title: Death of R' Uri Ornstein of Slonim
Summary: R' Uri Ornstein of Slonim, son-in-law of the 'Keren Orah,' died in Jerusalem on 17 Adar 5639.
Story: R' Uri Ornstein, a Chabad chasid who had made aliyah from Slonim, served two terms as a Chevron Chabad emissary totaling twelve years. He died in Jerusalem on 17 Adar 5639. His wife Zisil, daughter of R' Yitzchak of Karlin, died seven years later on 12 Adar II 5646.
Tags: uri ornstein, slonim, jerusalem, keren orah

Title: R. Avraham Chaim hears 'Tze'enah uRe'enah' discourse from Rebbe Maharash in Lubavitch
Summary: On Shavuot 5639 R. Avraham Chaim was in Lubavitch and heard the Rebbe Maharash deliver the maamar 'Tze'enah uRe'enah,' afterwards entering yechidus to ask about its content.
Story: R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum traveled to Lubavitch for Shavuot 5639, during the lifetime of the Rebbe Maharash. He heard the discourse 'Tze'enah uRe'enah' on the source of Kerias Shema in the Giving of the Torah, and in yechidus asked the Rebbe how this fit with the standard Kabbalistic mapping of positive and negative mitzvos to the divine name. He preserved the Rebbe's brief answer in writing for future study.
Tags: lubavitch, shavuot, maharash, avraham chaim rosenbaum, yechidus, chassidic discourse

Title: RA"Ch hears a 'Tze'enah Ure'enah' maamar from the Maharash on Shavuos
Summary: RA"Ch is in Lubavitch for Shavuos and hears the Maharash deliver the maamar beginning 'Tze'enah Ure'enah', later entering for yechidus.
Story: RA"Ch wrote to his nephew R' Shmuel Rosenbaum that on Shavuos 5639, during the Maharash's lifetime, he was in Lubavitch and heard an important maamar beginning 'Tze'enah Ure'enah'. He entered yechidus to ask about it, received the Rebbe's holy reply, and noted that another Chassid had also asked a question on the same maamar — material RA"Ch promised to relate in a later letter.
Tags: lubavitch, maharash, shavuos, yechidus, chassidus, maamar

Title: Eliyahu Sasson of Bombay donates 200 pounds for Jerusalem synagogue expansion
Summary: HaChavatzelet of Tammuz 5639 reported Eliyahu Sasson's 200-pound donation to expand the Jerusalem Chabad synagogue in memory of his wife.
Story: Overcrowding had forced worshipers into the courtyard, especially on the High Holidays, with reports of illness from the summer sun. Sasson's gift, secured through intermediary Shneur Zalman Mendelovitz, would fund a full second floor named Knesset Eliyahu in honor of the donor.
Tags: jerusalem, synagogue, sasson, bombay, kollel chabad, fundraising, hachavatzelet

Title: Maharashab receives permanent exemption from Russian military service
Summary: At age 18, Maharashab was registered for the 1877 conscription cohort, examined, and ruled permanently unfit for military service.
Story: On 25 July 1879, during the summer of 5639, the Vitebsk Gubernia conscription office issued certificate no. 1645 to 'the Vitebsk merchant's son Sholom Berke Shmuilov Schneersohn', recording that he had presented himself for service under the 1877 draft. Following medical examination he was declared wholly unfit for military service and granted a permanent exemption. He was registered as a Vitebsk resident — likely to ease obtaining the exemption — reflecting his father's property holdings in that city.
Tags: maharashab, russia, conscription, exemption, orsha, vitebsk

Title: Rebbe Maharash sends business and shidduch advice via secretary Levi Yitzchak Idelevitz
Summary: On 17 Av 5639, the Rebbe Maharash dictated a reply through his secretary to the chassid R' Yaakov Ayerov, endorsing a proposal from the town of Kalk and reporting on his improving health.
Story: The Rebbe Maharash often communicated with chassidim through his secretary R' Levi Yitzchak Idelevitz. In this letter, written on Wednesday 17 Menachem Av 5639 (1879), the Rebbe advises Yaakov Ayerov — likely on a match for one of his sons — that the proposal from Kalk seems good and that he should look into it carefully. The note also reports that the Rebbe's health has improved, helping fix the dating to 5639.
Tags: maharash, levi yitzchak idelevitz, yaakov ayerov, correspondence, kalk

Title: Rebbe Maharash travels to Switzerland for medical treatment
Summary: Rabbi Shmuel of Lubavitch, the Rebbe Maharash, traveled to Switzerland in autumn 5640 on doctors' orders for his health.
Story: On the instruction of his physicians, the Maharash departed Lubavitch in Tishrei 5640 (October 1879) and traveled westward through Europe. He stayed in Vevey until 19 Cheshvan, then moved to Montreux on Lake Geneva. In a letter to the chasid Shmuel Dovber of Borisov dated 27 Cheshvan, he reported that the climate was helping him and that he planned to continue to Biarritz before returning home via Paris.
Tags: maharash, switzerland, vevey, montreux, health, travel

Title: Birth of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn (the Rebbe Rayatz)
Summary: The sixth Chabad rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, was born in 5640 (1880).
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz, who would lead Chabad through the Soviet repression and the Holocaust era and eventually settle the movement in New York, was born in 5640. His 120th birth-anniversary in summer 2000 prompted a dedicated library exhibition of his belongings and writings.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, birth, yosef yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Birth of Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn in Lubavitch
Summary: The future sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, was born on 12 Tammuz in the town of Lubavitch.
Story: Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak (the Rayatz) was born on 12 Tammuz 5640 in Lubavitch, the town that gave Chabad its name. He was the only son of the Rebbe Rashab and would later succeed him as the sixth Rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch. The date of his birth would later become doubly significant as the same date on which he was released from Soviet imprisonment in 1927.
Tags: rayatz, lubavitch, russia, birth

Title: Chabad expansion across Europe begins after Russian pogroms
Summary: Following the pogroms in Russia from 5640 onward, Chabad began spreading across European countries.
Story: Beginning in 5640 (1880), as a result of pogroms in Russia, Chabad communities began establishing footholds in countries across Europe. This was the first significant wave of Chabad expansion beyond the Russian Empire.
Tags: europe, russia, pogroms, chabad-expansion

Title: Birth of Gil Kugel
Summary: Gil Kugel, son of R' Shlomo Kugel, was born on Tuesday 4 Nisan 5640 in Pleshchenitsy.
Story: As recorded in the Kugel family register (manuscript 584), R' Shlomo Kugel's son Gil was born on Tuesday, 4 Nisan 5640 (16 March 1880) in Pleshchenitsy. The entry was kept by his father along with the dates of all five of his children's births.
Tags: pleshchenitsy, kugel family, birth

Title: Birth of Gil Kugel in Pleshchenitsy
Summary: Gil Kugel, son of R' Shlomo Kugel and Brachah Slava, was born in Pleshchenitsy on 4 Nisan 5640.
Story: Recorded by his father Shlomo Kugel on the inside cover of manuscript no. 584 in the library, Gil was the first of several children born to the couple in Pleshchenitsy. The family register lists births of multiple siblings across the 1880s and into 5651.
Tags: pleshchenitsy, kugel family, birth

Title: Sir Eliyahu Sasson dies with synagogue construction unfinished
Summary: Sir Eliyahu Sasson, the Bombay donor of the Jerusalem Chabad synagogue's second floor, died on 12 Iyar 5640.
Story: HaChavatzelet reported that the shell of the new floor stood complete, but interior plaster, windows and doors were still missing. Work had been suspended for months due to lack of funds, and the obituary implied the family would need to complete what he had started.
Tags: sasson, bombay, jerusalem, synagogue, obituary, hachavatzelet

Title: Wedding of Chaim Meir Yechiel in Sadigura
Summary: Grandson of Rabbi Avraham Yaakov of Sadigura marries the daughter of Rabbi Yitzchak of Bohush on the Shabbat after Shavuot 5640.
Story: Rabbi Avraham Yaakov of Sadigura, son of the Ruzhiner, sent a circular letter from Sadigura in 5640 announcing the wedding of his grandson Chaim Meir Yechiel — son of his son-in-law Rabbi Aviezri Zelig — to Bat-Sheva, daughter of his nephew Rabbi Yitzchak of Bohush. The letter was carried by emissaries Reb Gedalia the shochet and Reb Chaim Kwashis of Kamenetz, who invited chasidim to attend.
Tags: sadigura, bohush, ruzhin, wedding, kamenetz

Title: Birth of Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn
Summary: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, who would become the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, was born in Lubavitch on 12 Tamuz 5640.
Story: On June 30, 1880 (12 Tamuz 5640), Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was born in Lubavitch to Rabbi Shalom Dovber (the Rashab) and Rebbetzin Shterna Sara. His birth followed a vivid dream in which his mother was reassured by three previous Lubavitcher Rebbes that she would bear a son. At his circumcision, his grandfather Rabbi Shmuel served as sandek and prophetically declared that the child would become a Rebbe.
Tags: lubavitch, russia, birth, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, rashab, shterna sara

Title: Rebbe Rayatz born in Lubavitch
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz, Yosef Yitzchak, was born in Lubavitch on 12 Tammuz 5640.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, was born on 12 Tammuz 5640 (1880) in Lubavitch. He would later become the sixth Rebbe of Chabad. His birthday of 12 Tammuz would also become significant as the date of his liberation from Soviet imprisonment decades later.
Tags: birth, lubavitch, rebbe rayatz

Title: Birth of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn in Lubavitch
Summary: The future sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, was born in Lubavitch, Russia.
Story: Born on 12 Tamuz 5640, he would grow up to succeed his father, the Rashab, as the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe. His birthday, 12 Tamuz, later coincided with his release from Soviet imprisonment in 1927, making the date a celebrated chasidic holiday.
Tags: yosef yitzchak schneersohn, lubavitch, russia, rayatz

Title: Birth of Shmuel Kugel
Summary: Shmuel Kugel was born on 10 Teves 5641 to R' Shlomo Kugel and Brachah Slava.
Story: His birth is recorded in the family register inside manuscript 584 owned by his father R' Shlomo Kugel of Kotzieli. The note lists him as the second son, born on Friday Parshas Vayechi.
Tags: pleshchenitsy, kugel family, birth

Title: Arrest of R. M.Z. Neimark and 80 Jews of Starodub
Summary: In 5641 R. Mushulam Zalman Neimark and eighty Jews of Starodub were arrested following an informer's denunciation over efforts to exempt Jewish children from Russian military conscription.
Story: Acting under the guidance of the Rebbe Maharash, R. Mushulam Zalman Neimark of Starodub had worked to secure exemptions for Jewish children from service in the Russian army. After the maskil Dov Lazarov denounced him, he and eighty Starodub Jews were arrested. The yeshiva in Starodub was shut by the police and even the Rebbe Maharash himself was nearly indicted, with Chasidim interrogated about their travels to Lubavitch.
Tags: neimark, starodub, russia, kantonisten, maskilim, dov lazarov, arrest, informer

Title: Arrests of Rabbi Meshulam Zalman Neimark and Starodub Jews
Summary: Rabbi Meshulam Zalman Neimark and many Jews of Starodub were arrested for helping evade conscription and imprisoned for two full years.
Story: In 5641 (1881), the Russian authorities discovered the conscription-evasion efforts of Rabbi Meshulam Zalman Neimark along with many Starodub Jews. They were arrested and held in custody for two full years, an episode documented in the Igrot Kodesh of the Maharash.
Tags: starodub, meshulam zalman neimark, conscription, arrest, russia

Title: Assassination of Czar Alexander II of Russia
Summary: Czar Alexander II was assassinated, ending his era of reforms and ushering in repressive policies under his son Alexander III.
Story: Alexander II's assassination led directly to a wave of anti-Jewish repression. His son Alexander III rolled back his father's reforms and intensified oppression of Russian Jews. The assassination set the stage for decades of state-sponsored anti-Semitism.
Tags: russia, czar, alexander ii, assassination

Title: Czar Alexander II assassinated
Summary: Czar Alexander II of Russia was assassinated, ushering in a more repressive era for Jews.
Story: The assassination of Czar Alexander II in 1881 brought his son Alexander III to the throne. The new czar rolled back his father's reforms and increased oppression of Russian Jews, setting the stage for the May Laws the following year.
Tags: russia, czar, alexander ii, assassination

Title: Death of Rabbi Yeshaya Meshulam Zusya Twersky
Summary: Rabbi Yeshaya Meshulam Zusya Twersky, son of Rabbi Aharon of Chernobyl, passes away in 5641.
Story: Rabbi Yeshaya Meshulam Zusya of the Chernobyl dynasty died in 5641. Letters he co-signed with his brother Baruch Asher and his nephew Mordechai of Loyev are therefore dateable to the window 5636–5641 — after Menachem Nachum of Loyev's death but before his own.
Tags: chernobyl, twersky, ukraine

Title: Eliyahu Shusterman born in Lohin, Volhynia
Summary: Eliyahu ben Achiezer Shusterman, father of the author, was born in 5641 in the small town of Lohin near Korosten in the Volhynia region.
Story: Eliyahu Shusterman, the author's father, was born in the year 5641 (1880/1881) in the small Volhynian town of Lohin, near Korosten in the Berdichev region. He later studied in Vyetka near Homel, a town known as a seat of sharp Talmudic scholars. His Yiddish accent remained 'Litvish' from his upbringing in Belorussia, unlike his brother David who spoke in a 'Polish' Volhynian dialect.
Tags: shusterman family, lohin, volhynia, ukraine, birth

Title: Pogroms erupt in southern Russia after Alexander II's assassination
Summary: In the spring of 1881, anti-Jewish pogroms swept through southern Russia in the wake of the assassination of Tsar Alexander II.
Story: The unrest devastated dozens of communities in the Pale of Settlement and gave the new tsar, Alexander III, a pretext to appoint Interior Minister Nikolai Ignatiev. Ignatiev would draft the punitive 'Temporary Regulations' of 1882, blaming the Jews themselves for the violence directed against them.
Tags: russia, pogroms, alexander ii, southern russia, ukraine

Title: Polish translation of the Haggadah by Fabius Strauch printed in Warsaw
Summary: Fabius Strauch's Polish translation of the Haggadah was printed in Warsaw.
Story: Around 5641 (1881), Fabius Strauch's translation of the Haggadah into Polish was issued in Warsaw. The 96-page volume made the Seder ritual accessible to Polish-speaking Jews who had become more integrated with the local language. It represented part of the broader 19th-century movement to render Jewish liturgical texts into local European languages.
Tags: haggadah, polish, warsaw, poland

Title: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark arrested in Starodub with 80 Jews
Summary: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark was arrested in Starodub along with 80 other Jews and imprisoned for two years.
Story: In 5641, R' Meshulam Zalman and 80 fellow Jews of Starodub were arrested and held in prison for two years (5641-5643). The Rebbe Maharash corresponded about the situation in letters preserved in his Igros Kodesh.
Tags: meshulam zalman neumark, starodub, arrest, imprisonment, russia, chabad

Title: Rebbe Maharash hanachot from 5641
Summary: A bound volume of Rebbe Maharash's 5641 discourses survives in his own handwriting.
Story: Rebbe Maharash's manuscripts include a volume of discourses he composed in 1881, three years before his passing. These hanachot remain in the library archive.
Tags: rebbe maharash, drushim, hanachot

Title: Starodub Jews remain imprisoned for two years
Summary: From 5641 to 5643 R. M.Z. Neimark and the arrested Starodub Jews remained in prison while community efforts sought their release.
Story: The arrested Starodub Jews remained imprisoned for two years (5641-5643). The Rebbe Maharash sent a short letter of encouragement to Neimark in prison, dispatched his secretary R. Levi Yitzchak Idelevitz to Starodub to assess the situation, and corresponded in code with the prisoners. Activists in Riga, Velizh, Starodub and Kiev coordinated to retain top defense attorneys in Kiev.
Tags: neimark, starodub, russia, imprisonment, maharash

Title: Warsaw map of the Land of Israel printed
Summary: A map of the Land of Israel was printed in Warsaw in 5641 (1881).
Story: The 1881 Warsaw map is part of the library's collection of antique Holy Land cartography spanning the seventeenth through nineteenth centuries.
Tags: map, land of israel, warsaw

Title: Birth of Rebbetzin Nechama Dina Schneersohn in Kishinev
Summary: Nechama Dina Schneersohn, future wife of the Rayatz, was born in Kishinev to Rabbi Avraham Schneersohn.
Story: Nechama Dina was the daughter of Rabbi Avraham Schneersohn, a second cousin of the Rebbe Rashab. Her birth date corresponds to 17 Tishrei 5642. She would later marry Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn (the Rayatz) and become rebbetzin of the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe.
Tags: nechama dina, kishinev, schneersohn family

Title: Nechama Dina Schneersohn is born
Summary: Nechama Dina Schneersohn, future wife of the Rayatz, was born in Kishinev.
Story: Nechama Dina Schneersohn was born on 17 Tishrei 5642 (October 24, 1881) in Kishinev to Rabbi Avraham Schneersohn, a second cousin of the Rebbe Rashab. She would later be selected as the bride for the Rashab's only son, the Rayatz.
Tags: nechama dina, kishinev, birth

Title: BILU sends first Zionist settlers to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: BILU, an early Russian Zionist group, sent its first settlers to Eretz Yisrael.
Story: BILU was one of the earliest Russian Zionist organizations. In 1882 it dispatched its first settlers to Eretz Yisrael, marking the beginning of organized secular Zionist settlement and an emerging ideological challenge to traditional Jewish life.
Tags: zionism, bilu, eretz yisrael, russia, migration

Title: May Laws restrict Russian Jewish life
Summary: Czar Alexander III instituted the May Laws, severely restricting Jewish residency, economy, and education.
Story: In 1882, Alexander III enacted the discriminatory May Laws, prohibiting Jews from leasing land outside the Pale, restricting high school and university attendance, and limiting mortgages. These laws were a major catalyst for mass Jewish emigration to America and the West.
Tags: russia, may laws, pale of settlement, anti-semitism, alexander iii

Title: Mitteler Rebbe's Shnei HaMeoros published in Lvov
Summary: Shnei HaMeoros, a collection of the Alter Rebbe's discourses transcribed by the Mitteler Rebbe, was printed in Lvov in 1882.
Story: The 48-folio Lvov 5642 (1882) edition presented hanachot—written transcriptions—of the Alter Rebbe's chassidic discourses as recorded by his son and successor, expanding the documented corpus of the Alter Rebbe's Torah.
Tags: alter rebbe, mitteler rebbe, lvov, shnei hameoros

Title: Moshe Wittenberg makes aliyah to Jerusalem from Vitebsk
Summary: R. Moshe Wittenberg made aliyah from Vitebsk to Jerusalem in 5642, later assuming a central financial role for Kollel Chabad.
Story: Wittenberg was a known upright and reliable man, a Torah scholar and prominent Chabad chassid. After settling in Jerusalem, his stature led the Rebbeim and senior charity overseers abroad to propose elevating him to manage Kollel Chabad funds for Eretz Yisrael. His arrival from Vitebsk would prove foundational for the kollel's modern financial structure.
Tags: jerusalem, vitebsk, moshe wittenberg, aliyah

Title: Passing of Rabbi Shmuel, the Rebbe Maharash
Summary: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn, the fourth Lubavitcher Rebbe, passed away in Lubavitch three days after Yom Kippur 1882.
Story: In 1882, three days after Yom Kippur, Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn, the Rebbe Maharash and fourth Lubavitcher Rebbe, passed away in Lubavitch at the age of forty-eight. On the eve of Rosh HaShanah that year, he had cryptically told his wife that she would rise up thirty-two steps physically while he would rise spiritually, alluding to his impending passing. He had been Rebbe for a little more than sixteen years, leaving his youngest daughter just four years old.
Tags: lubavitch, russia, rebbe maharash, death, tishrei

Title: Passing of Rebbe Maharash in Lubavitch
Summary: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn, the Maharash, passed away in Lubavitch on 13 Tishrei 5643.
Story: He was buried in the ohel that had been constructed for his father the Tzemach Tzedek in the Lubavitch cemetery. The Maharash was the only Chabad Rebbe to live his entire life in the town. His passing brought his son the Rashab to the leadership of Chabad.
Tags: maharash, schneersohn, lubavitch-cemetery

Title: Passing of the Rebbe Maharash
Summary: The Rebbe Maharash passed away in 1882.
Story: His passing came during an era of accelerating change for Russian Jewry. He was succeeded after a transitional period by his son, the Rashab.
Tags: maharash

Title: R' Shmuel Dovber of Borisov writes RA"Ch on 'the fallen Sukkah of David'
Summary: In Kislev RShD"M of Borisov writes RA"Ch that he has much to share about contemporary events and 'the fallen Sukkah of David'.
Story: Dating from the period immediately after the Maharash's passing, a letter from R' Shmuel Dovber of Borisov to RA"Ch in Kislev 5643 hints at unsettled times among the Chassidim, alluding to the 'fallen Sukkah of David'. The letter signals that he has 'much, much to inform' RA"Ch about current events affecting Chabad.
Tags: borisov, shmuel dovber borisov, letter, chassidic correspondence

Title: R' Shneur Zalman Schneersohn (Shazbani) passes away
Summary: R' Shneur Zalman ben Nachum Yosef Schneersohn, author of Nimukei Shazbani, died in the winter of 5642 leaving young orphans.
Story: R' Shneur Zalman ben Nachum Yosef Schneersohn (known by his initials Shazbani), author of Nimukei Shazbani and other works, died in the winter of 5642 in Hebron. He left behind several adult daughters and minor orphan sons. The beit din, together with his brothers Chaim Tzvi and Pinchas, appointed two trustees over his estate to act on behalf of the orphans, including reaching settlements with his daughters.
Tags: hebron, schneersohn, shazbani, orphans, estate

Title: Rabbi Shmuel, fourth Chabad Rebbe, passes away
Summary: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn, the Rebbe Maharash, passed away in Lubavitch.
Story: Shortly before his passing, an Alexandria Jew brought his grandson to Rabbi Shmuel along with first fruits, asking for a blessing. Rabbi Shmuel promised that one day the grandson would bring fruit to his own grandson — a blessing fulfilled when that grandson welcomed the Rebbe Rayatz to Alexandria in 1929.
Tags: rabbi-shmuel, lubavitch, succession

Title: Rebbe Rashab accepts Chabad leadership
Summary: Some time after the passing of his father in 5643, Rabbi Shalom Dovber Schneersohn assumed the leadership of Chabad.
Story: The Rashab's leadership inaugurated the final phase of Lubavitch as Chabad's world center. His most lasting institutional contribution was the founding of Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lubavitch in 5657. He would lead the movement through the trauma of forced exile from Lubavitch in World War One.
Tags: rashab, shalom-dovber

Title: Rebbe Rashab begins nesius in Lubavitch
Summary: Rabbi Sholom Dovber (Rashab) became Rebbe of Chabad in Lubavitch in 5643.
Story: Upon the passing of the Maharash in 5643 (1882), his son Rabbi Sholom Dovber Schneersohn (Rashab) assumed leadership of Chabad. He remained in Lubavitch for the next three decades, founding the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva and corresponding extensively with the town's moreh tzedek R. Dovid Yakobson.
Tags: rashab, sholom dovber schneersohn, lubavitch, nesius

Title: Russian May Laws restrict Jewish residency and economic life
Summary: Czar Alexander III instituted the discriminatory May Laws restricting Jewish residency, education, and commerce.
Story: The May Laws prohibited Jews from leasing land outside the Pale of Settlement, restricted high school and university attendance, and limited mortgages on land. They were expanded in 1885 and became a major catalyst in Jewish emigration from Russia to America and other countries.
Tags: russia, may laws, alexander iii, pale of settlement, antisemitism

Title: Sons of Prince of Wales visit Hebron tomb
Summary: The sons of the Prince of Wales were granted exceptional access to Me'arat Hamakhpelah.
Story: Their visit followed their father's own admission two decades earlier. Such exceptions to the Muslim ban remained rare and tightly controlled.
Tags: hebron, meorat-hamachpelah, british-royalty

Title: Ignatiev's 'Temporary Regulations' tighten the Pale of Settlement
Summary: The Committee of Ministers adopted Ignatiev's 'Temporary Regulations,' barring Jews from rural residence and from holding rural property even within the Pale.
Story: The regulations prohibited Jews from living outside cities and towns within the fifteen Pale provinces and outlawed Jewish-held sales, mortgages and leases on rural real estate beyond the Pale. Although labeled 'temporary,' they remained in force for 33 years until the middle of World War I, devastating Jewish livelihood and packing Jews into overcrowded urban districts.
Tags: russia, pale of settlement, ignatiev, temporary regulations, alexander iii

Title: Death of R. Zev Wolf b. Yeshayahu, buried in Chabad section of Mount of Olives
Summary: R. Zev Wolf b. R. Yeshayahu, a grandson of the brother of the Admur of Yanovich, died on 6 Elul 5642 and was buried in the Chabad plot on the Mount of Olives.
Story: His name and date are recorded in 'Avnei Zikaron' chelek 12 (copied in 'Oholei Lyubavitch' vol. 3 p. 75 ff.). The entry establishes the presence of MaHaRIL's family descendants in nineteenth-century Eretz Yisrael and confirms their continued affiliation with the Chabad community.
Tags: mount of olives, burial, chabad, mahril, yanovich

Title: Passing of Rebbe Maharash in Lubavitch
Summary: Rabbi Shmuel of Lubavitch (Maharash) passed away on 13 Tishrei 5643 and was buried in the ohel he had built for his father, the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: Maharash died in Lubavitch on 13 Tishrei 5643 (late September 1882), having served continuously since 1866 despite chronic weakness in his final years. He was laid to rest in the ohel he had constructed years earlier for his father the Tzemach Tzedek. His yahrzeit remains observed as a major day in the Chabad calendar.
Tags: maharash, lubavitch, ohel, tzemach-tzedek, schneersohn

Title: Histalkus of Rebbe Maharash
Summary: Rebbe Maharash passed away on 13 Tishrei 5643, leaving his 22-year-old son Rashab.
Story: On 13 Tishrei 5643, Rebbe Shmuel Schneersohn (Maharash) passed away. His son Rashab was still in his 22nd year. Though he composed maamarim and recorded them, Rashab did not yet agree to formally accept the leadership of the Chabad movement.
Tags: maharash, lubavitch, passing

Title: Rashab's first public maamar on Sukkos
Summary: Rashab delivered his first public maamar 'Keser Yitnu Lecha' on the second day of Sukkos 5643.
Story: On the second day of the festival of Sukkos in 5643, Rashab delivered his first public Chassidic discourse, beginning 'Keser Yitnu Lecha.' This marked his first public teaching following his father Maharash's passing earlier that month.
Tags: rashab, maamar, sukkos, lubavitch

Title: Chabad elders convene to address succession
Summary: Prominent Chabad rabbis gathered in Lubavitch to urge the Rashab and his brother to assume leadership after their father's passing.
