Story: On Shabbat, October 21, 1882 (8 Cheshvan 5643, Parashas Lekh Lekha), Chabad elders convened in the home of Rebbetzin Rivkah Schneersohn to address the future of the movement following Rabbi Shmuel's passing. Prominent rabbis including Rabbi Zalman Pinsker, Rabbi Dan Tumarkin, and Reb Chaim Yaakov Viderevitz attended. The two older sons, Rabbi Zalman Aharon and Rabbi Shalom Dovber, initially refused to sit with the rabbis, but eventually agreed to recite maamarim, tacitly stepping into their father's role.
Tags: lubavitch, russia, succession, rashab, raza, chabad elders

Title: Birth of R' Yeshaya Halevi Horowitz of Tzfat
Summary: R' Yeshaya Halevi Horowitz, future rabbi of the Chabad community in Tzfat, was born in 5643.
Story: Son of R' Asher Yechezkel Horowitz, he was named for his paternal grandfather. He would later serve as rabbi of the Chabad community in Tzfat from 5669 to 5684, before relocating to the United States.
Tags: tzfat, horowitz family, rabbi

Title: R' Yechiel Heilprin among yoshvim during mourning year
Summary: R' Yechiel Heilprin was among the yoshvim in Lubavitch in 5643, the year of mourning for the Rebbe Maharash.
Story: R' Yechiel Heilprin was among the yoshvim in Lubavitch during 5643 (1883), which was the year of mourning of the Rebbe Rashab for his father, the Rebbe Maharash. From 5660 onwards, R' Yechiel served as a shadar (emissary) for Tomchei Tmimim, raising funds for the yeshiva.
Tags: yoshvim, lubavitch, heilprin, maharash

Title: Rebbe Maharash passes away; Rashab begins delivering maamarim
Summary: After Rebbe Maharash's passing in 5643, his son Rebbe Rashab began delivering and writing Chassidic discourses.
Story: Rebbe Maharash passed away in 1883. Although Rebbe Rashab did not formally accept the Chabad leadership until 1894, he began saying and writing Chassidic discourses immediately. A volume of his discourses from this first year, 5643, survives.
Tags: rebbe maharash, rebbe rashab, yahrzeit, lubavitch

Title: Trial acquits Rabbi Zalman Neimark and Chassidim in Staradub
Summary: After two years awaiting trial, Rabbi Zalman Neimark and other Chassidim were acquitted in the Staradub case in the winter of 5643.
Story: Rabbi Zalman Neimark and a group of Chassidim from Staradub had been imprisoned and held over for trial for two years. The trial finally took place in the winter of 5643 (1883), ending with their full acquittal. Shortly after the verdict, Rabbi Neimark left Staradub and was soon invited to serve as rabbi of Vitebsk.
Tags: staradub, russia, trial, persecution, rabbi zalman neimark

Title: Letter on the Four Sons of the Haggadah from Pleshchenitsy
Summary: On 8 Marcheshvan 5644, R' Avraham Chaim wrote from Pleshchenitsy to R' Yehoshua Lipman explaining the order of the Four Sons by kabbalistic principles.
Story: Writing from Pleshchenitsy on 8 Marcheshvan 5644, R' Avraham Chaim addressed his prospective in-law R' Yehoshua Lipman. The letter unfolds a kabbalistic exposition of the Four Sons of the Passover Haggadah, mapping them onto the four worlds Atzilut–Beriah–Yetzirah–Asiyah and the four 'fierce ones' of Reish Lakish, and asks Lipman to clarify three differing orderings found in Pri Eitz Chaim and the siddur. He closes by inviting Lipman to bring the agreed wedding-gift sum in person.
Tags: pleshchenitsy, avraham chaim rosin, haggadah, kabbalah, four sons, matchmaking

Title: Birth of R. Shmuel Levitin
Summary: R. Shmuel Levitin was born in Pahar in 5644.
Story: R. Shmuel Levitin, future rabbi of Rakishok and later chief mashpia of Tomchei Tmimim in New York, was born in 5644 (1884) in Pahar. He went on to study at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch.
Tags: levitin, pahar, birth

Title: Likkutei Torah with Rebbe Maharash's annotations published
Summary: Likkutei Torah on three parshiyos with annotations of the Rebbe Maharash was printed in Vilna in 5644.
Story: In 5644 (1884), an edition of Likkutei Torah on three parshiyos was printed in Vilna incorporating annotations of Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn, the Rebbe Maharash. The Lubavitch Library preserves a copy of this edition. The work transmits Chassidic discourses of the Alter Rebbe with later commentary.
Tags: likkutei torah, rebbe maharash, vilna

Title: Likutei Torah on three Parashiyos printed in Vilna
Summary: An edition of Likutei Torah on three Parashiyos was issued in Vilna in 1884, associated with the Rebbe Maharash.
Story: This 5644 (1884) Vilna printing was among the chassidic works connected to the Rebbe Maharash, the fourth Chabad rebbe, and broadened distribution of the Alter Rebbe's discourses on these portions.
Tags: rebbe maharash, vilna, likutei torah

Title: R' Mordechai Margolios appointed rabbi of Disna
Summary: R' Mordechai Margolios was received as rabbi of Disna in 5644.
Story: Following the long tenure of R' Mordechai, a chassid of the Tzemach Tzedek who had served in Kamin and then Disna, R' Mordechai Margolios was appointed rabbi of Disna in 5644.
Tags: mordechai margolios, disna, rabbinate, chabad

Title: Tzemach Tzedek responsa and Piskei Dinim series completed
Summary: In 5644, eighteen years after the Tzemach Tzedek's passing, the final volumes — Orach Chaim responsa and two volumes of Piskei Dinim — were printed, completing the original series.
Story: After 13 years of editorial work and printing, the series was completed in 5644. Newly discovered teshuvos and chiddushim were appended to the Piskei Dinim volume. The publishers gave the entire series the name 'Tzemach Tzedek' (gematria of Menachem Mendel), and from this point the Rebbe himself was named after his book. Choshen Mishpat responsa were blocked by Russian censors who opposed rabbinic adjudication.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, responsa, piskei dinim, orach chaim

Title: Vilna mitnagdim alter Tzemach Tzedek's text on the Gra
Summary: In 5644 mitnagdim at the Vilna press altered a passage in Tzemach Tzedek's Piskei Dinim that called a Vilna Gaon argument 'no proof'.
Story: Piskei Dinim III, 69c originally read of an argument of the Vilna Gaon, 'this is no proof.' At the Vilna printing in 5644, soon after the passing of the Rebbe Maharash and during an interregnum in the Chabad leadership, type-setters substituted 'and I in my poverty have not merited to understand his holy words.' The Frierdiker Rebbe later recounted to the Rebbe that as soon as the forgery was discovered in Lubavitch, the offending pages were reprinted with the original wording, though some falsified copies could not be recalled.
Tags: vilna, mitnagdim, vilna gaon, piskei dinim, censorship, printing, maharash

Title: Yosef Yitzchak begins formal education
Summary: Four-year-old Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn began formal schooling with master educator Rabbi Yekusiel Aizik.
Story: In 1884, when Yosef Yitzchak was four years old, he began his formal education in cheder. On his first day, his father and uncle Rabbi Zalman Aharon celebrated by tossing candies that they said came from the angel Mikhael, continuing a family tradition from the Tzemach Tzedek. His teacher, Rabbi Yekusiel Aizik, was a master educator descended from Chasidim of the Alter Rebbe, known for his enthusiastic storytelling about the Baal Shem Tov.
Tags: lubavitch, russia, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, cheder, yekusiel aizik, education

Title: Family travels to Yalta for Rashab's health
Summary: The Rashab and family traveled to Yalta for six months for his health, with five-year-old Yosef Yitzchak studying under Schneur Zalman Slonim.
Story: In fall 1885, the Rashab and his family traveled almost one thousand miles south from Lubavitch to Yalta for six months, where the warm climate would benefit his health. Five-year-old Yosef Yitzchak accompanied them and studied under Rabbi Schneur Zalman Slonim from Hebron, who had come to Lubavitch for an extended stay. The family took daily walks together and the Rayatz later described it as an idyllic period spent with his parents.
Tags: yalta, russia, rashab, shterna sara, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, schneur zalman slonim

Title: May Laws expanded under Alexander III
Summary: The May Laws were expanded, further tightening restrictions on Russian Jews.
Story: In 1885, three years after their initial enactment, Czar Alexander III expanded the May Laws. The reinforced restrictions on residency, education, and economic activity accelerated mass Jewish emigration from Russia to the United States and other Western countries.
Tags: may laws, russia, alexander iii, anti-semitism, pale of settlement

Title: Pittsburgh Platform issued by Reform movement
Summary: The American Reform movement issued its founding principles, repudiating classical Jewish beliefs.
Story: The platform questioned the divinity of the Torah and the obligation to observe mitzvot, foregrounding ethical living instead. The Rebbe Rayatz would later challenge this ideology directly in his American visit, arguing that fulfillment of practical mitzvot was the true key to connection with the Divine.
Tags: reform-judaism, united-states, pittsburgh-platform

Title: R' Yehuda Leib Slonim makes his last trip to Lubavitch
Summary: In 5645 R' Yehuda Leib Slonim of Hebron made his final journey to Lubavitch in his capacity as administrator of Kollel Chabad.
Story: R' Yehuda Leib Slonim, who along with his brothers managed Kollel Chabad after R' Shimon Menashe took on rabbinic duties, made numerous trips to Lubavitch to coordinate the kollel's affairs over decades. His last trip in 5645 is documented in a letter from Rebbe Rashab (vol. 1, letter 4). He died eight years later in 5653.
Tags: hebron, lubavitch, yehuda leib slonim, kollel chabad, rashab

Title: R. Shneur Zalman Slonim arrives at Lubavitch
Summary: In summer 5645 (1885), the Rebbe Rashab's cousin R. Shneur Zalman Slonim arrived in Lubavitch from Hebron.
Story: R. Shneur Zalman, son of R. Mordechai Dov Slonim of Hebron, came to Lubavitch and remained a substantial time. He later accompanied the Rebbe Rashab to Yalta for the winter and, on returning to Eretz Yisrael, was tasked with locating Chassidic manuscripts there.
Tags: slonim, hebron, eretz yisrael, lubavitch, manuscripts

Title: Rebbe Rashab winters at Yalta healing waters
Summary: Throughout the winter of 5646 (1885–1886) the Rebbe Rashab stayed at the Yalta healing waters, accompanied by R. Shneur Zalman Slonim.
Story: The Rebbe traveled to the Crimean resort of Yalta for medical reasons and remained the entire winter. His cousin R. Shneur Zalman Slonim was with him throughout the stay, returning to Eretz Yisrael at the start of summer 5646.
Tags: yalta, crimea, health, slonim

Title: Death of R' Avraham Mertzbacher, owner of major Munich book collection
Summary: On 21 Sivan 5645, R' Avraham Mertzbacher of Munich died, leaving his son a collection of 156 manuscripts, 4,332 antique books, and 43 incunabula.
Story: Mertzbacher had built his renowned bibliophile collection from 1866-1885 through Rabbi Raphael Nathan Rabinowitz, who used the books for his Dikdukei Sofrim project. After his death, his son Dr. Isaac Mertzbacher sought to sell the collection, which would later attract Rebbe Rashab's interest as a potential Jewish library acquisition.
Tags: mertzbacher, munich, library, bibliophile

Title: Death of R. Avraham Mertzbacher of Munich
Summary: R. Avraham Mertzbacher, who built a rare collection of 156 manuscripts and 4,332 books in Munich, died on 21 Sivan 5645.
Story: Mertzbacher had assembled his important collection between 1866 and 1885, including 43 incunabula printed before 1500. After his death, his son Dr. Yitzchak Eizik Mertzbacher inherited the library and later sought to sell it, prompting interest from the Rebbe Rashab.
Tags: munich, germany, library, bibliophile, mertzbacher

Title: Birth of Shmuel Kugel
Summary: Shmuel Kugel, son of R' Shlomo, was born on Friday 10 Tevet 5646 in the week of Parshat Vayechi.
Story: R' Shlomo Kugel recorded the birth of his son Shmuel on Friday, 10 Tevet 5646 (18 December 1885), during the week of Parshat Vayechi. The note appears in the family register in manuscript 584.
Tags: kugel family, birth

Title: Death of Rabbi Yehuda Tzvi of Rozdol
Summary: Admor Yehuda Tzvi Eichenstein of Rozdol, of the Kaliver chassidic dynasty, passed away in 5646.
Story: Rabbi Yehuda Tzvi ben Shlomo Eichenstein of Rozdol, a Kaliver rebbe, passed away in 5646 (1886). He had famously prayed from a siddur once owned by the Baal Shem Tov, an inscription on which dates it to before his death.
Tags: rozdol, kaliv, eichenstein, siddur

Title: Eshel Avraham first edition printed in Lvov
Summary: Mahadura kamma of Eshel Avraham by R. Avraham David of Buchach was published in Lvov in 5646 (1886).
Story: The first edition of Eshel Avraham — chiddushim on Shulchan Aruch by R. Avraham David of Buchach — appeared in Lvov in 1886, forty-five years after the author's passing. The manuscripts had been preserved by his great-grandson R. Yisrael Aryeh Leib Wahrman, who copied them in unsystematic order.
Tags: lvov, eshel avraham, avraham david of buchach, galicia

Title: Hungarian translation Haggadah printed in Vienna
Summary: An illustrated Haggadah with Hungarian translation in parallel pages was printed in Vienna.
Story: Around 5646 (1886), a Haggadah was issued in Vienna with a Hungarian translation displayed page-by-page opposite the Hebrew original. The volume included illustrations, with the laws printed in Yiddish using Tzene-Rene script and in Ladino in square letters. The 31-page edition catered to the multilingual Jewish communities of the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
Tags: haggadah, hungarian, vienna, austria, illustrated

Title: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark appointed rabbi of Vitebsk
Summary: After the death of R' Zalman Ostrovner, R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark was appointed rabbi of Vitebsk.
Story: Following R' Zalman Ostrovner's passing in 5646-7 in Vitebsk, R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark moved from Starodub to take the position. He would serve only about two years before moving on to another Belarusian community.
Tags: meshulam zalman neumark, vitebsk, zalman ostrovner, rabbinate, chabad

Title: Death of Zisil Ornstein, daughter of R' Yitzchak of Karlin
Summary: Zisil Ornstein, wife of R' Uri Ornstein and daughter of R' Yitzchak of Karlin, died on 12 Adar II 5646.
Story: Recorded in 'Avnei Zikaron' volume 12, Zisil's death is noted as 12 Adar II 5646. She was the daughter of R' Yitzchak the rabbi of Karlin and outlived her husband R' Uri by seven years. Together they had been part of the Slonim contingent that settled in the Chabad communities of Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: zisil ornstein, karlin, jerusalem

Title: Peace agreement ends Hebron rabbinic dispute
Summary: In Tammuz 5646 a peace agreement was signed ending the long Hebron rabbinic dispute, with R' Eliyahu Mani as chief rabbi and R' Rachamim Yosef Franko as Av Beit Din.
Story: After years of bitter dispute over the Hebron rabbinate, prompted by Markado Romano's conflict with R' Eliyahu Mani, the Jerusalem rabbis brokered a reconciliation. In Tammuz 5646 a peace agreement was signed, with both R' Eliyahu Mani and R' Rachamim Yosef Franko among the signatories. The accord established Mani as the Sephardi chief rabbi of Hebron and Franko (the Charif) as Av Beit Din.
Tags: hebron, sephardim, rabbinate, eliyahu mani, rachamim franko

Title: Lag BaOmer dinner in Kharkiv
Summary: The Rashab and family stopped in Kharkiv on Lag BaOmer, where local Chasidim organized a large welcome dinner.
Story: In May 1886, returning from Yalta to Lubavitch, the Rashab and his family stopped in Kharkiv on Lag BaOmer. Local Chasidim organized a large dinner to welcome them, with rabbis, prominent Chasidim, and community members crowding the room to the rafters. When the Rashab taught a maamar, Chasidim crowded around to listen. During the event, young Yosef Yitzchak found his mother crying privately and conveyed her concerns about his father's health back to the Rashab.
Tags: kharkiv, russia, lag baomer, rashab, maamar, chasidic gathering

Title: Rebbe Rashab writes to R. Shabsai Shaftil seeking Alter Rebbe manuscripts
Summary: On 11 Sivan 5646 the Rebbe Rashab wrote to the famed mashpia R. Shabsai Shaftil inquiring about the holy autograph manuscripts of the Alter Rebbe.
Story: In letter 555 the Rebbe expressed his intense longing for the writings of the Alter Rebbe and asked Shaftil to update him on their status. The fate of these particular manuscripts remained unknown; a year later Shaftil sent him a manuscript of the Mitteler Rebbe instead.
Tags: manuscripts, alter rebbe, shaftil, chassidic texts

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter to Rashaz Slonim about manuscripts in geniza
Summary: On 8 Elul 5646, Rebbe Rashab writes to Rashaz Slonim instructing him to discreetly safeguard small-format manuscripts belonging to him found in a geniza.
Story: This letter (Igros #556) marks the early phase of Rebbe Rashab's lifelong project of collecting manuscripts of his ancestors. He repeatedly emphasized that manuscripts in small format belonged to him personally. The correspondence with Rashaz Slonim about manuscript acquisition would continue for over 25 years.
Tags: manuscripts, rashab, rashaz slonim, geniza, letters, russia

Title: First lithograph of the Tzemach Tzedek portrait approved by Vilna censor
Summary: The earliest printed portrait of the Tzemach Tzedek, a lithograph by N. Metz, received Vilna censor approval on 30 October 1886.
Story: In the winter of 5647, N. Metz of Vilna issued the first widely distributed lithograph of the Tzemach Tzedek, captioned in Hebrew 'Tzaddik for an everlasting memory: portrait of the holy gaon Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Lubavitch' and in Russian as 'Portrait of the Lubavitcher rabbi Mendel Schneersohn.' Censor approval was granted in Vilna on 30 October 1886. It became the basis for many subsequent reproductions of the Tzemach Tzedek's likeness.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, portrait, lithograph, vilna, n. metz, russia

Title: First lithograph portrait of Tzemach Tzedek approved by censor
Summary: On October 30, 1886, the Russian censor in Vilna approved the first lithograph of the Tzemach Tzedek's portrait.
Story: The lithographer N. Metz in Vilna produced the first printed portrait of the Tzemach Tzedek, captioned in Hebrew and Russian. The censor's approval is dated October 30, 1886, and the print appeared the following year as part of an exhibit of the Rebbe in his white garment.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, lithograph, vilna, censor, portrait

Title: Death of R. Schneur Zalman b. Yaakov Mordechai (Singer/Grossman ancestor)
Summary: R. Schneur Zalman b. Yaakov Mordechai — eldest son of the Twer patriarch — died on 14 Kislev 5647 and was buried on the Mount of Olives.
Story: Named for the Alter Rebbe, he was likely born around 1814, married young, and remained in Mogilev when his father and brothers made aliyah in 1832, joining them only many years later. His descendants include R. Yaakov Mordechai Singer (rabbi/shochet of Rishon LeTzion) and the Grossman family of Jerusalem.
Tags: schneur zalman, mount of olives, singer, grossman, mogilev, alter rebbe

Title: Mordechai Shlonk appointed as Kollel Chabad trustee
Summary: R. Mordechai Shlonk was appointed as a Kollel Chabad trustee in 5647 by order of the Kapuster Rebbe.
Story: In his Tumat Yesharim pamphlet of 1913, Shlonk wrote that he had served as a kollel trustee for 26 years. His appointment in 5647 came by directive of the Kapuster Rebbe alongside Michel Baruch Reizes. Shlonk's long tenure made him a key continuity figure during the leadership transitions of the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, mordechai shlonk, kapust dynasty

Title: R' Meir Simcha HaKohen of Dvinsk appointed
Summary: R' Meir Simcha HaKohen, future author of 'Or Sameach' and 'Meshech Chochmah,' became Misnagdic rabbi of Dvinsk in 5647 (1887).
Story: On the passing of R' Reuven HaLevi Levin in 5647 (1887), R' Meir Simcha HaKohen was selected to fill the Misnagdic rabbinic chair in Dinaburg/Dvinsk. He would become world-famous as the author of 'Or Sameach' and 'Meshech Chochmah.'
Tags: dvinsk, or-sameach, meshech-chochmah, rabbinate

Title: R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin appointed rav of Hebron Chabad
Summary: R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin made aliyah from Konstantinograd and was appointed rabbi of Hebron's Chabad community.
Story: In 5647 (1887), the elderly R' Shmuel Menachem Chaikin, then 85, sought a deputy. That year, R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin, formerly rabbi of Konstantinograd in Ukraine, made aliyah and settled in Hebron. After examining Levin's learning, Chaikin and the leading scholars of Hebron unanimously appointed him as rabbi, signing a formal kesav of acceptance.
Tags: yehuda leib shaul levin, shmuel menachem chaikin, hebron, chabad kollel, rabbinate, aliyah

Title: Rabbi A.D. Lavut re-edits and prints the Siddur Torah Or in Vilna
Summary: Rabbi A.D. Lavut reissued the Alter Rebbe's siddur as Siddur Torah Or in Vilna in 1887, scrubbing later printing errors.
Story: By 5647 (1887), various siddur reprintings had accumulated textual corruptions. Rabbi Lavut's Vilna edition restored the nusach to its early Shklov-Kapust form and added Shaarei Tefillah, a commentary explaining the precise wording. The edition was reprinted multiple times in 1889, 1890, and 1892.
Tags: alter rebbe, vilna, siddur torah or, lavut

Title: Rabbi Zalman Neimark appointed rabbi of Vitebsk
Summary: Following the death of Rabbi Zalman Ostrovner around 5646-7, Rabbi Zalman Neimark was appointed rabbi of Vitebsk.
Story: After Rabbi Zalman Ostrovner died in Vitebsk in approximately 5646-7 (1886-7), the community appointed Rabbi Zalman Neimark in his place. He served there only about two years before being invited to a different community in White Russia.
Tags: vitebsk, russia, rabbi zalman neimark, rabbi zalman ostrovner

Title: Wiener buys 1490 Soncino Rambam in Yekaterinoslav
Summary: Shmuel Wiener purchased a 1490 Soncino incunabulum Rambam in Yekaterinoslav.
Story: In the summer of 5647 (1887), Shmuel Wiener acquired a precious Soncino 1490 incunabulum edition of the Rambam in Yekaterinoslav (now Dnipro). His inscription documented the purchase. The book was located by Chabad emissaries in 1991 in the Asiatic Institute's collection, which holds roughly 60 incunabula.
Tags: rambam, soncino, incunabula, wiener, yekaterinoslav, ukraine

Title: Birth of Tzvi Hirsch Kugel
Summary: Tzvi Hirsch Kugel, son of R' Shlomo, was born on Friday 18 Tevet 5647.
Story: R' Shlomo Kugel recorded that his son Tzvi Hirsch was born on Friday, 18 Tevet 5647 (13 January 1887), in the week of Parshat Shemot. The entry appears in his family register in manuscript 584.
Tags: kugel family, birth

Title: Birth of Tzvi Hirsch Kugel
Summary: Tzvi Hirsch Kugel, son of R' Shlomo and Brachah Slava, was born on 18 Teves 5647.
Story: Recorded by his father in the family register on manuscript 584, Tzvi Hirsch was born on Friday Parshas Shemos. He was a grandson of R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum and great-grandson of R' Hendel Kugel.
Tags: pleshchenitsy, kugel family, birth

Title: Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan Spektor grants smicha to Rafael of Amdur
Summary: Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan Spektor of Kovno issues a rabbinic ordination certificate to Rabbi Rafael ben Shimshon of Amdur.
Story: On 23 Tevet 5647, the famed posek and av beis din of Kovno, Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan Spektor (author of Be'er Yitzchak), tested Rabbi Rafael of Amdur and found him fluent in Shas and capable of original Torah insights. He issued a full kabbalas smicha—yoreh yoreh, yadin yadin—stating that any community that accepts him as rav will derive pride and nachas from him.
Tags: yitzchak elchanan spektor, rafael of amdur, kovno, lithuania, smicha, rabbinic ordination

Title: Passing of Rabbi Aryeh Leib Zivav, rav of Dvinsk
Summary: Rabbi Aryeh Leib Zivav, longtime rav of Dvinsk and chossid of the Tzemach Tzedek, passes away on erev Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5647.
Story: Born around 5570-5571 and ordained by the Tzemach Tzedek at age eighteen, Rabbi Aryeh Leib Zivav served in the rabbinate of Babruysk, Smilovitch, Homel and finally Dvinsk-Dinaburg. He passed away on Monday, erev Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5647. Most of his responsa never reached our hands; only a small bundle written during his Homel years was preserved in manuscript.
Tags: aryeh leib zivav, dvinsk, yahrtzeit, chabad rabbis

Title: Rabbi Yochanan of Rachmistrivka endorses Rabbi Eliyahu Posek's appointment in Ravna
Summary: Rabbi Yochanan of Rachmistrivka writes to the community of Ravna in 5647 endorsing their selection of Rabbi Eliyahu Posek as rabbi.
Story: Dated Sunday of Parashat Behaalotecha 5647, the letter expresses joy that the Ravna community accepted Rabbi Eliyahu Posek — author of Mor V'Ohalot — as rabbi without controversy. Rabbi Yochanan urges holdouts to add their signatures and instructs the community to pay both the rabbi and the shochet on time so the rabbi can study undisturbed.
Tags: rachmistrivka, ravna, eliyahu-posek, rabbinical-appointment, ukraine, mor-veohalot

Title: Spektor declines to issue an amulet, sends blessing for Yitzchak Yaffe's daughter
Summary: Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan Spektor responds that he does not give amulets and instead sends a healing blessing for the ailing daughter of Yitzchak Yaffe.
Story: Writing from Kovno on 20 Sivan 5647 in reply to a letter of 17 Sivan, Rabbi Spektor explains that he has never given amulets and that it is simply not his way. In their stead he extends a heartfelt blessing for the full recovery of Yitzchak Yaffe's daughter. He closes by noting that his weakened eyes make writing difficult.
Tags: yitzchak elchanan spektor, kovno, amulets, blessings, yitzchak yaffe

Title: Mrs. Bila Horowitz dies in Tzfat
Summary: Mrs. Bila Horowitz, niece of the Tzemach Tzedek and matriarch of the Tzfat Chabad community, died on 4 Tammuz 5647.
Story: Bila had immigrated to Tzfat around 1870 with her five orphaned sons, becoming a foundational figure in the renewed Chabad community there. Her descendants, listed as 'sons of Bila' in the Kollel Chabad distribution records, remained prominent in the Tzfat community after her death.
Tags: tzfat, horowitz family, tzemach tzedek

Title: Hebron arbitration ruling establishes joint Ashkenazi Vaad
Summary: Arbitrators in Jerusalem ruled on 20 Tammuz 5647 to create a joint Vaad of Ashkenazi communities in Hebron.
Story: After disputes arose between Kollel Chabad in Hebron and the other Ashkenazi kollelim, both sides turned to the Jerusalem beis din under R' Shmuel Salant. The arbitrators Zalman Chaim Rivlin and Yoel Moshe Salomon, with R' Shmuel Salant's approval, ruled on 20 Tammuz 5647 that two Chabad representatives and one from the other kollelim would form a three-man 'Vaad of the Ashkenazi communities in Hebron' with shared seal and shared distribution of communal funds.
Tags: hebron, vaad, kollel chabad, shmuel salant, ashkenazi kollelim, arbitration

Title: HaChavatzelet reports Montefiore estate distribution in Hebron
Summary: HaChavatzelet reports that trustees of Moshe Montefiore's estate continue funding Hebron, with the Ashkenazi share distributed at 40 piasters per person.
Story: After Moshe Montefiore's death at 101, his estate's trustees continued to send funds to the Holy Land. The 15 Av 5647 (1887) issue of HaChavatzelet described how Hebron's portion was split between the Sephardic and Ashkenazi communities by population, with a three-man Ashkenazi committee dividing the money at 40 piasters per soul.
Tags: hebron, montefiore, chavatzelet, philanthropy, ashkenazi

Title: R' Yehuda Leib Levin's letter on his Hebron rabbinate
Summary: R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin wrote to his family from Hebron on the 4th day of Selichot describing his new rabbinic appointment.
Story: On the 4th day of Selichot 5647 (September 1887), R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin wrote to his family from Hebron, describing the elderly R' Shmuel Menachem Chaikin and the process by which Levin had been examined and accepted as rabbi by the city's scholars. The letter is preserved in Sinai journal volume 87.
Tags: yehuda leib shaul levin, hebron, letter, rabbinate

Title: Rebbe Rashab writes to R. Avraham Dovid Lavut requesting manuscript
Summary: On 8 Tishrei 5648 the Rebbe Rashab thanked R. Avraham Dovid Lavut for a holy autograph page and asked for the responsa manuscript of the Tzemach Tzedek's son.
Story: The Rebbe wrote to the noted Chabad gaon Lavut — author of Kav Naki and Shaar HaKollel — expressing joy at receiving a page of holy autograph manuscript via Lavut's grandson R. M. A. Sh. He further requested that the grandson send the autograph responsa of R. Y. L. (Maharil) for the same reasons of preservation.
Tags: lavut, kav naki, shaar hakollel, manuscripts, responsa

Title: Spektor acknowledges donations from Zekharia Lifshitz for fire victims
Summary: Rabbi Spektor confirms receipt of funds donated and collected by Rabbi Zekharia Lifshitz for victims of a fire.
Story: On 24 Elul 5647, days before the new year, Spektor wrote from Kovno acknowledging the money Lifshitz contributed and gathered for those left destitute by fire. He invoked the blessing of the perishing upon Lifshitz and offered an effusive year-end wish for him and his family to be inscribed and sealed for good life and abundant divine favor.
Tags: yitzchak elchanan spektor, kovno, charity, fire victims, zekharia lifshitz, tzedakah

Title: Hebron Joint Vaad publicly announced in Chabatzelet
Summary: An announcement in Chabatzelet on 3 Marcheshvan 5648 informed world Jewry of the new Hebron unified Vaad and its three elected leaders.
Story: Following the arbitration ruling, the new joint Vaad published an announcement in Chabatzelet on 3 Marcheshvan 5648 declaring that all disputes between Chabad chasidim and the other Ashkenazi kollelim of Hebron were ended. The three elected leaders — R' Baruch Mordechai Halevi Gloiberman, R' Binyamin Rivlin, and R' Meir Tzvi Hershler — would receive all donations for the Hebron Ashkenazi community.
Tags: hebron, vaad, chabatzelet, baruch mordechai gloiberman, binyamin rivlin, meir tzvi hershler

Title: Arrest of R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum in Pleshchenitsy
Summary: Chassid R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum was arrested in Pleshchenitsy for involvement in evading conscription and imprisoned for three years.
Story: In 5648 (1888), the chassid R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum was arrested in Pleshchenitsy for helping Jews evade Russian military conscription. He remained in custody for three years, his ordeal recorded in 'Toldot Avraham Chaim'.
Tags: avraham chaim rosenbaum, pleshchenitsy, conscription, arrest, russia

Title: Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum begins imprisonment in Smolensk
Summary: Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum arrives at the Smolensk prison in the summer of 5648 and is permitted to bring sacred ritual items with him.
Story: Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum, a Chabad chassid and scholar in halacha, kabbalah and Hebrew grammar, was sentenced to imprisonment in Smolensk. He arrived at the prison in the summer of 5648 (1888), where he was initially put to hard labor alongside violent criminals serving lifetime sentences of exile. Despite the harsh conditions, the authorities allowed him from the outset to bring ritual articles into his confinement.
Tags: imprisonment, smolensk, russia, avraham chaim rosenbaum

Title: Direct postal collection replaces traveling shadarim
Summary: From 5648 onward Kollel Chabad shifted from collecting support via traveling shadarim to direct postal transfer.
Story: Funds were no longer entrusted to traveling emissaries but were mailed by each community directly to the 'ba'al ha'adres' in Jerusalem. The reform aimed to reduce avoidable expense and risk of misappropriation associated with the older shadar model. R. Moshe Wittenberg was appointed as the first ba'al ha'adres to oversee the new system.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, fundraising, shadarim, postal

Title: Fire in Nevel scatters Rabbi Neimark's books
Summary: A fire struck Nevel in summer 5648, leaving Rabbi Zalman Neimark's books displaced thereafter.
Story: In a letter dated 9 Nisan 5649, Rabbi Neimark wrote from Nevel that 'last summer there was the present fire here, since which time the books have been moved from corner to corner.' The fire occurred in summer 5648 (1888) and continued to disrupt his study and books long afterward.
Tags: nevel, fire, white russia

Title: Kollel Chabad center shifts from Hebron to Jerusalem
Summary: Around 5648 the operational center of Kollel Chabad shifted from Hebron to Jerusalem after Jerusalem leaders challenged the Hebron officials' authority.
Story: Jerusalem-based Chabad figures began calling themselves 'heads of Kollel Chabad' and asked donors abroad to send funds directly to them rather than through the Hebron officials or the Rogachover Vaad's general gabbai R. Dan Tumarkin. The Hebron officials under R. Shimon Menashe Chaikin responded with a public kruz, supported by some 50 Hebron and 50 Jerusalem Chabad signatories. Although the Jerusalem activists did not get everything they wanted immediately, by 5651 the ba'al ha'address (the kollel's primary postal point of contact) was already based in Jerusalem, and from then on Jerusalem was effectively the kollel's center.
Tags: jerusalem, hebron, kollel chabad, fundraising, ba'al ha'address

Title: Position of 'ba'al ha'adres' created with Moshe Wittenberg appointed
Summary: Beginning in 5648 the kollel added a 'ba'al ha'adres' role; R. Moshe Wittenberg was the first appointee.
Story: Wittenberg agreed to take the role only on condition that every community abroad send its R'Meir Baal HaNess charity funds directly to Jerusalem rather than through itinerant shadarim. This was meant to eliminate excessive expense and occasional waste. Most communities thereafter mailed their contributions directly to him.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, moshe wittenberg, fundraising, adres

Title: R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum arrested
Summary: R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum of Pleshchenitsy was arrested in 5648 and remained imprisoned until late 5650.
Story: In 5648 (1888) R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum, leader of the Pleshchenitsy Chassidic community after R' Hendel Kugel moved to Lubavitch, was arrested. He remained imprisoned, including in Smolensk, until late 5650 (1890), writing several letters from prison to his friends and family during that period.
Tags: pleshchenitsy, r avraham chaim rosenbaum, smolensk, persecution, russia

Title: R' Avraham Chaim's arrest and imprisonment in Smolensk
Summary: R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum was sentenced to two years in prison in Smolensk for attempting to exempt a young man from the Russian army.
Story: R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum spent two years imprisoned in Smolensk, Russia, after trying to help a Jewish youth avoid Tsarist military conscription. Despite the harsh conditions, he maintained an extensive correspondence on Torah, Kabbalah, Chassidus, grammar, and divine service. His letters from prison reveal both the difficulty of his confinement and his continued spiritual life.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, tsarist conscription, rosenbaum

Title: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark moves to Nevel
Summary: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark moved from Vitebsk to assume the rabbinate of Nevel.
Story: By the start of summer 5648, R' Meshulam Zalman was already serving in Nevel, where a major fire had occurred that summer causing his books to be moved repeatedly. He would serve as rabbi of Nevel until his passing five years later.
Tags: meshulam zalman neumark, nevel, vitebsk, fire, rabbinate, chabad

Title: R' Shalom Mordechai Chaikin publishes pamphlet honoring R' Dan Tomarkin
Summary: In 5648 R' Shalom Mordechai Chaikin printed a proclamation honoring R' Dan Tomarkin's forty years of service to Kollel Chabad.
Story: In 5648 R' Shalom Mordechai Chaikin published a proclamation describing how the Tzemach Tzedek and his sons had ordained R' Dan Tomarkin of Rogachov as gabbai of Kollel Chabad, praising his forty years of trustworthy service in distributing the funds that sustained the Chabad community in Eretz Yisrael. The text was later reprinted in Migdal Oz.
Tags: shalom mordechai chaikin, dan tomarkin, kollel chabad, rogachov, migdal oz

Title: R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum arrested in Plescenice
Summary: R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum is arrested in 1888 over forged documents issued by his assistant R. Chaikel Rapaport to spare Jewish youths from the tsarist army.
Story: As elected elder of Plescenice, Rosenbaum delegated the local administrative office (upravа) to his assistant R. Chaikel Rapaport, entrusting him with his official seal. Rapaport used the seal to issue forged passports and 'false benefits' to save Jewish boys from military conscription; when the authorities discovered this, both men were arrested. Rosenbaum was first held in Borisov for most of 5648 (1888) before being transferred to Smolensk.
Tags: russia, plescenice, borisov, arrest, tsarist, informers, draft evasion

Title: Rabbanit Rivka gifts a leather case to her grandson
Summary: In winter 5648, Rabbanit Rivka gave Rebbe Rayatz a leather paper case that had belonged to Rebbe Maharash.
Story: Rebbe Rayatz inscribed that the leather case for papers in the archive was from his grandfather Rebbe Maharash. He received it as a gift from his great-grandmother Rabbanit Rivka in the winter of 1888.
Tags: rebbe maharash, rebbe rayatz, rabbanit rivka, lubavitch

Title: Rabbi Eliyahu Posek leaves Ravna to become rabbi of Alapolia
Summary: After only one year in Ravna, Rabbi Eliyahu Posek accepts the rabbinate of Alapolia in 5648.
Story: Rabbi Eliyahu Posek's tenure in Ravna proved short-lived; in 5648 he moved to serve as rabbi in Alapolia. He was the author of Mor V'Ohalot and many other works, and Rabbi Yochanan of Rachmistrivka had publicly endorsed his earlier appointment in Ravna the previous year.
Tags: eliyahu-posek, ravna, alapolia, rabbinical-appointment, ukraine

Title: Rabbi Yitzchak Shlomo Yoel Sherman appointed rabbi of Ravna
Summary: Rabbi Yitzchak Shlomo Yoel Sherman, later author of Pitchei Shearim, becomes rabbi of Ravna in 5648.
Story: After Rabbi Eliyahu Posek left Ravna for Alapolia in 5648, the community appointed Rabbi Yitzchak Shlomo Yoel Sherman in his place. He later became known as the author of Pitchei Shearim, published in London in 5720 (1960).
Tags: sherman, ravna, rabbinical-appointment, pitchei-shearim, ukraine

Title: Rabbi Zalman Neimark becomes rabbi of Nevel
Summary: In early summer 5648, Rabbi Zalman Neimark left Vitebsk and took up the rabbinate of Nevel, where he served until his death.
Story: After two years in Vitebsk, Rabbi Zalman Neimark accepted the position of rabbi in Nevel in White Russia. A responsum he wrote from Nevel on 9 Nisan 5649 references a fire 'last summer,' indicating he had already settled there by the start of summer 5648 (1888). He continued to serve as rabbi of Nevel until his death.
Tags: nevel, vitebsk, white russia, rabbi zalman neimark

Title: Rashab writes ethical will for his son
Summary: Concerned about his health, the Rashab wrote an ethical will outlining how his wife should educate young Yosef Yitzchak if he died.
Story: In 1888, when he was just twenty-seven and his son Yosef Yitzchak was eight, the Rashab was deeply concerned about his health and decided to write an ethical will. The will outlined how he wished his wife to educate their son if he passed away. Based on the verse 'Educate a child in accordance to his way,' the document was eventually published in 1943 under the title Chanokh LaNaar.
Tags: lubavitch, russia, rashab, ethical will, chanokh lanaar, education, yosef yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Rebbetzin Rivka gives Maharash's leather portfolio to grandson Rayatz
Summary: In winter 5648 Rebbetzin Rivka gave her grandson, the future Rebbe Rayatz, the leather paper-portfolio that had belonged to her father-in-law the Maharash.
Story: Rebbe Rayatz inscribed a note documenting that the leather portfolio used for holding papers, from the estate of his great-grandfather the Maharash, was given to him as a gift by his grandmother Rebbetzin Rivka in the winter of 5648. The portfolio is preserved with his inscription identifying its provenance.
Tags: maharash, rebbetzin rivka, rayatz, heirloom, wallet

Title: Recovery of Mitteler Rebbe manuscripts via Yisrael Yaffe descendants
Summary: After more than two years of searching, R. Shneur Zalman Slonim located descendants of the printer R. Yisrael Yaffe of Kopust and recovered substantial Mitteler Rebbe manuscripts.
Story: Tasked by the Rebbe Rashab in 1886 to find descendants of R. Yisrael Yaffe, R. Shneur Zalman Slonim located them in Eretz Yisrael after over two years of investigation. Among the recovered manuscripts were large portions of the Mitteler Rebbe's Pirush HaMilos and unpublished sections related to Amrei Binah and Shaar HaTefillin, which the Rebbe Rashab acquired.
Tags: mitteler rebbe, yisrael yaffe, kopust, manuscripts, amrei binah

Title: Romano courtyard registered to R' Rachamim Yosef Franko
Summary: Around 1888 the Romano courtyard in Hebron was formally registered in the name of R' Rachamim Yosef Franko.
Story: After Markado Romano's death in Damascus while returning from visiting his ill son in Istanbul, his Istanbul heirs decided to register the Hebron mansion temporarily in the name of R' Rachamim Yosef Franko. A deed from approximately 1888 records the transfer from 'Markado Effendi son of Ibrahim Romano the Istanbuli' to 'Rachamim Effendi Franko.' The arrangement was not a final sale, since the heirs themselves did not live in the Holy Land.
Tags: hebron, romano, real estate, franko

Title: Rosenbaum imprisoned in Smolensk; permitted religious articles in jail
Summary: Beginning summer 5648, the chassid Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum was incarcerated in Smolensk prison and allowed to bring sacred items into the jail.
Story: In the summer of 5648 (1888), the Chabad chassid Reb Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum was sent to prison in Smolensk. From his arrival the authorities permitted him to bring religious articles into the cell. He would remain there nearly two years, conducting an extensive correspondence with chassidim and family members.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, avraham chaim rosenbaum

Title: Rosenbaum transferred to Smolensk prison
Summary: After about a year in Borisov, R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum is sentenced and transferred to a Smolensk penal company in the summer of 5648.
Story: Following the trial in Borisov, Rosenbaum was sentenced to two years in the 'rastantnaya rota' in Smolensk for signing a document on behalf of an only son seeking exemption from the army. The warden of the Borisov prison personally escorted him out and wept, recognizing that this prisoner was an unusually learned and refined man. Rosenbaum remained in Smolensk from the summer of 5648 (1888) until the summer of 5650 (1890).
Tags: russia, smolensk, borisov, prison, tsarist

Title: RSM Chaikin publishes Chabad kollel proclamation
Summary: R' Shmuel Menachem Chaikin issued a public proclamation regarding Chabad kollel affairs, co-signed by R' Levin.
Story: In 5648 (1888), R' Shmuel Menachem Chaikin continued his active role in Hebron after Levin's appointment, publishing a kruz regarding matters of the Chabad kollel. R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin co-signed the proclamation, marking the new dual rabbinic leadership. The proclamation is preserved in Migdal Oz.
Tags: shmuel menachem chaikin, yehuda leib shaul levin, hebron, chabad kollel, proclamation

Title: Tel Aviv trustees attempt to dismantle Rogachov Vaad and Hebron leadership
Summary: In 5648 the Jerusalem Kollel Chabad trustees moved to abolish R' Dan Tomarkin's appointment, eliminate the shadarim, and shift the center from Hebron to Jerusalem.
Story: Calling themselves "heads of Kollel Chabad," the Jerusalem trustees circulated public notices proposing that every city send its donations directly through the post to Jerusalem, bypassing the overseas shadarim and the Hebron trustees. The Hebron community and many Jerusalemites protested fiercely in a counter-broadside, but the Jerusalem trustees succeeded on all three counts. From this point Hebron lost its place as the administrative center of the kollel.
Tags: jerusalem, hebron, kollel chabad, rogachov, dan tomarkin, shadarim

Title: Tzemach Tzedek portrait printed in Keneset Yisrael (Warsaw)
Summary: An engraving of the Tzemach Tzedek signed by artist Z. Schatz appeared in the journal Keneset Yisrael, vol. 3 (Warsaw 5648).
Story: In 5648 (1888), the Warsaw journal Keneset Yisrael reproduced a portrait of the Tzemach Tzedek in its third volume (cols. 215-216), signed by the artist Z. Schatz. This version differs noticeably from the original painting and from the Metz lithograph, and the author of the present study judges it an unsuccessful attempt unworthy of further analysis.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, portrait, warsaw, keneset yisrael, z. schatz

Title: Tzemach Tzedek portrait reissued in Knesset Yisrael
Summary: A version of the Tzemach Tzedek's portrait was published in Warsaw's Knesset Yisrael 1888 anthology.
Story: Knesset Yisrael, third volume (Warsaw 1888), included a portrait of the Tzemach Tzedek signed by the engraver Z. Shatz. It reproduced an earlier lithograph distributed by Shmaryahu Schneersohn.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, portrait, warsaw, knesset yisrael

Title: R' Levin's letter on the modest salary of the Hebron rabbinate
Summary: On 19 Tevet, R' Levin wrote home that his salary was only 12 rubles a month with no other income.
Story: On 19 Tevet 5648 (January 3, 1888), R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin wrote home that his total salary in Hebron was only 12 rubles a month, with no wedding fees, mechirat chametz revenue, or Purim funds as in the diaspora. He noted that prior to him, the Hebron rabbi had not taken a salary at all. The letter is preserved in Sinai journal.
Tags: yehuda leib shaul levin, hebron, letter, rabbinate, salary

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter about firm pricing for manuscript acquisition
Summary: On 22 Adar 5648, Rebbe Rashab cautions Rashaz Slonim against showing excessive enthusiasm when buying manuscripts, urging measured pricing.
Story: Rashaz Slonim had begun overpaying for manuscripts after recognizing the Rebbe's intense desire for them. In this letter (Igros #562), Rebbe Rashab teaches that internal passion must be limited externally so sellers don't inflate prices. The principle was that emotional restraint preserves the practical ability to keep acquiring.
Tags: manuscripts, rashab, rashaz slonim, letters

Title: R' Levin's letter on Hebron's Jewish court system
Summary: On 22 Sivan, R' Levin wrote that Hebron had abundant Torah-court cases, including disputes between Jews and Muslims who also turned to the beit din.
Story: On 22 Sivan 5648 (June 2, 1888), R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin wrote that din Torah cases in Hebron were numerous because the community did not use gentile courts, and even Jew-Muslim disputes were brought before the Jewish beit din. He explained that despite this, the rabbi received no fees for rulings, only the basic small salary. The letter is preserved in Sinai journal.
Tags: yehuda leib shaul levin, hebron, beit din, letter

Title: Rosenbaum's halachic letter on Birkas HaLevana through a window
Summary: On 13 Elul 5648 Rosenbaum writes a halachic responsum questioning whether one may recite Birkas HaLevana through a closed glass window.
Story: Dated 13 Elul 5648 (1888) and addressed to a scholarly correspondent, the letter explores whether one may bless the new moon through window glass when it is impossible to go outside or open the window – for example in winter or when sewage is being removed nearby. Rosenbaum weighs the Dvar Shmuel's prohibition against the Magen Avraham's ruling permitting the havdalah candle blessing through glass, and proposes distinguishing between covering the viewer's eye and covering the object viewed. He also requests that the addressee acquire him a fine Genoese esrog and three matching hadas branches for Sukkos.
Tags: halacha, birkas halevana, responsum, plescenice

Title: Avraham Chaim writes from prison requesting etrog and lulav
Summary: From the Smolensk prison on 13 Elul 5648, Avraham Chaim asks Rabbi Yehuda Leib Maskil LeEitan to procure a Yanover etrog, a beautiful lulav, and three matched myrtle branches for Sukkot.
Story: On 13 Elul 5648 (August 20, 1888), Avraham Chaim wrote from prison to Rabbi Yehuda Leib Maskil LeEitan asking him to acquire Sukkot articles on his behalf when purchasing his own. He requested a Yanover etrog, a lulav beautiful in appearance and complete in form, and three matched hadassim, with delivery to reach him immediately after Yom Kippur. The letter shows that prison authorities permitted him to receive religious articles within months of his arrival.
Tags: imprisonment, smolensk, sukkot, etrog, lulav, yehuda leib maskil leeitan

Title: Rosenbaum writes from Smolensk prison requesting an etrog for Sukkot
Summary: On 13 Elul 5648 Rosenbaum wrote from prison to Rabbi Yehuda Leib Maskil L'Eitan of Pleschenitz asking him to acquire a fine Yanover etrog, lulav, and three hadasim.
Story: Writing from the Smolensk jail on 13 Elul 5648, Reb Avraham Chaim asked the rabbi of Pleschenitz to purchase a Yanover etrog of fine appearance, a complete lulav, and three properly meshulash hadasim. He requested they reach him immediately after Yom Kippur so he could fulfill the mitzvah of the Four Species inside the prison.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, etrog, sukkot, yehuda leib maskil l'eitan

Title: Birth of Chaya Mushka, daughter of R' Asher Grossman
Summary: Chaya Mushka, second daughter of R' Asher Grossman of Nikolayev, was born in 5649.
Story: In 5649, after many years following the marriage of her elder sister, Chaya Mushka was born to R' Asher Grossman of Nikolayev. She would later marry R' Yosef Shmuel Garfinkel of Pahar in 5666.
Tags: nikolayev, grossman-family, birth

Title: Birth of R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich
Summary: R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich was born in Bakhmut in 5649.
Story: Born in Bakhmut in 5649 (1889), R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich would go on to study in Lubavitch, become one of the 'chozrim' (those who repeated chassidic discourses from memory), and serve as rabbi in several Lithuanian communities.
Tags: chatzkevich, bakhmut, birth

Title: Chassidim of Nikolayev outgrow single beis midrash
Summary: In 5649 the growing Nikolayev Chabad community required a second synagogue, prompting R' Asher Grossman to begin efforts to build one.
Story: By 5649, the Chabad community in Nikolayev had grown so large that a single beis midrash no longer sufficed. R' Asher Grossman began efforts to build an additional synagogue. On 8 Tevet 5649, the city's rabbi, Rabbi Avraham Dovid Lavut, wrote forbidding him from splitting off into a separate minyan now that the decision to build a new shul for the whole community had been made.
Tags: nikolayev, chabad-russia, synagogue, r-asher-grossman

Title: First print of a portrait of the Alter Rebbe
Summary: The first printed image of the Alter Rebbe's likeness, taken from a painted portrait, was issued in 5649 (1889).
Story: This 1889 reproduction is the earliest known printed portrait of the Alter Rebbe; later painters would render new images based on it, several of which the seventh Rebbe received and the library preserves.
Tags: alter rebbe, portrait, iconography

Title: First printing of the Alter Rebbe's portrait with engraver's signature
Summary: The first printed portrait of the Alter Rebbe, signed by engraver Glatzbesky, appeared in 5649.
Story: The earliest known printing of the Alter Rebbe's portrait bears the signature of the engraver Glatzbesky. Below the image are lines in Hebrew and Russian signed by the publishers Rabbi Shmaryahu Schneersohn and Z. Sh"Tz. The print is now displayed at the Lubavitch Library.
Tags: alter rebbe, portrait, glatzbesky, schneersohn

Title: First written account of the Tzemach Tzedek's portrait
Summary: Alexander Zisskind Rabinowitz published the earliest account of the Tzemach Tzedek's surreptitious portrait in HaAsif 5649.
Story: In the 5649 (1889) volume of HaAsif (p. 167), Alexander Zisskind Rabinowitz wrote that the portrait of R. Menachem Mendel of Lubavitch was widespread, having been made by a photographer who stole into his room against the Tzemach Tzedek's will — for Chassidic rebbes refused to leave images of themselves to posterity. This is the earliest published version of the famous tradition about the painting's origins.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, ha'asif, alexander rabinowitz, portrait

Title: Hebron Chabad rabbis issue 5649 kruz
Summary: R' Chaikin and R' Levin co-signed another public proclamation related to the Chabad kollel.
Story: In 5649 (1889), R' Shmuel Menachem Chaikin and R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin co-signed another kruz related to the Hebron Chabad kollel. By this point Levin was consistently signing with the title 'rav and moreh in Hebron,' while Chaikin signed without titles. The signing order — Chaikin first, then Levin — reflected respect for the elder while acknowledging Levin's official rabbinic role.
Tags: shmuel menachem chaikin, yehuda leib shaul levin, hebron, chabad kollel, proclamation

Title: Hebron Vaad in financial crisis as R' Baruch Mordechai resigns
Summary: At the end of Kislev 5650 Hebron community leaders begged the remaining two Vaad members to continue serving despite empty coffers.
Story: By late Kislev 5650 the Hebron Ashkenazi Vaad faced severe financial distress: R' Baruch Mordechai Halevi resigned, doctors and shochtim went unpaid, and the pharmacy ran out of medicine. The community's rabbis and notables wrote to the two remaining members, R' Binyamin Rivlin and R' Meir Tzvi Hershler, urging them to continue managing the Vaad's affairs until new elections on Rosh Chodesh Elul.
Tags: hebron, vaad, baruch mordechai gloiberman, binyamin rivlin, meir tzvi hershler, financial crisis

Title: New harsh labor rules imposed on Smolensk prisoners
Summary: After Pesach 5649, Smolensk prison authorities imposed new rules requiring every prisoner to rise at 4 a.m. and assemble for forced labor selection.
Story: R' Avraham Chaim wrote to R' Hendel Kugel on 20 Iyar 5649 about a new harsh regime in the Smolensk prison: every prisoner had to rise at the bell at 4 a.m. and stand in formation while the warden selected work assignments — a wait of two or three hours during the best part of the day. R' Avraham Chaim himself had been assigned for five days to fence the property of the prison administration.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, forced labor

Title: R' Avraham Chaim describes Pesach in Smolensk prison
Summary: On erev Shabbos of the second day of Chol Hamoed Sukkos 5649, R' Avraham Chaim wrote to R' Eliyahu Rivkin describing how he kept Pesach in prison.
Story: R' Avraham Chaim recounted that the previous Pesach in Smolensk prison, the local Chassid R' Zarchi brought him all his needs for the first day of Pesach and visited with his wife on Yom Tov bringing him beloved foods. Throughout that winter of 5649, he was also able to hire others to perform his mandatory prison labor.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, pesach, rosenbaum

Title: R' Chaim Kavash born in Vyetka
Summary: R' Chaim Kavash was born in Vyetka in 5649.
Story: Born in Vyetka in 5649, Chaim Kavash went on to study in the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lubavitch and to serve as a rabbi in Yochavitch and a refugee community leader in Samarkand. His estate preserved several artifacts of disputed but reputed Baal Shem Tov and early-chassidic provenance.
Tags: chaim kavash, vyetka, russia, biography

Title: Rabbi Zalman Aharon advocates for Avraham Chaim in Smolensk
Summary: On the Rebbe's counsel in 5650, Rabbi Zalman Aharon Schneersohn travels to Smolensk to intercede with the governor and ease Avraham Chaim's prison conditions.
Story: Acting on the Rebbe's instruction from the year 5650 (1889/1890), Rabbi Zalman Aharon Schneersohn (the Raza) traveled to Smolensk to advocate for his imprisoned relative. Although outright release was impossible, he persuaded the governor to exempt Avraham Chaim from hard labor and grant him a separate cell apart from the other prisoners. He also notified the leading members of the local community and Chabad chassidim so they could continue supporting Avraham Chaim, and his intervention paved the way for further leniencies.
Tags: smolensk, zalman aharon schneersohn, imprisonment, russia, governor, rashab

Title: Rosenbaum writes to R. Hendel from prison
Summary: On 20 Iyar 5649 Rosenbaum writes from prison to the mashpia R. Hendel, recalling his Lubavitch youth and reporting on Plescenice chassidic life.
Story: Writing on 20 Iyar 5649 (1889) from Smolensk, Rosenbaum reminisces with R. Hendel Kugel about his student days in Lubavitch alongside R. Chaim Yaakov Widerewitz, whom he had just learned was passing through nearby Smolensk en route to Vitebsk. In a separate letter dated 'Wednesday Parshas Masei 5649,' he rejoices that the shochet R. Reuven Liberman has established regular Chassidus learning in Plescenice and prays that the local chassidic community will flourish in his absence.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, hendel kugel, chaim yaakov widerewitz, plescenice

Title: Yeshivat Magen Avot founded in Hebron
Summary: The Chabad yeshiva 'Magen Avot' was founded in Hebron in 5649, predating Yeshivat Torat Emet by over two decades.
Story: Yeshivat Magen Avot, a Chabad yeshiva in Hebron, was established in 5649. It functioned in Hebron until Yeshivat Torat Emet was founded in 5672. The Rebbe Rashab took particular interest in Magen Avot and reorganized it in 5663 in an effort to deepen Chassidic learning in the Holy Land.
Tags: hebron, chabad, yeshiva, magen avot

Title: Yitzchak Sharion arrives in Jerusalem
Summary: R. Yitzchak Sharion arrived in Jerusalem in 5649 and later recorded the kollel's leadership in his memoirs.
Story: Upon his arrival in Jerusalem in 5649, Sharion noted that Kollel Chabad had two trustees, the senior of whom hailed from Kherson in southern Russia and was known as 'the Khersoner.' Sharion's memoirs, published in Jerusalem in 1943, became a key source for the kollel's mid-19th-century history.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, yitzchak sharion, memoir

Title: HaChavatzelet supplement names Kollel Chabad trustees
Summary: A 23 Shvat 5649 supplement to HaChavatzelet identified Yitzchak Yaakov Shabtai and B.M. Reizes as Kollel Chabad's trustees.
Story: Issue 19's supplement carried the signature 'Yitzchak Yaakov Shabtai and B.M. Reizes, trustees of Kollel Chabad in the Holy City.' Although Sharion had not remembered the names of the trustees of his era, this published notice preserved them. Soon thereafter Michel Baruch Reizes would emerge as senior trustee.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, hachavatzelet, yitzchak yaakov shabtai, reizes

Title: Vilna-censored Warsaw print of Tzemach Tzedek portrait
Summary: A Warsaw-printed copy of the Tzemach Tzedek portrait carrying a Vilna censor approval dated 26 January 1889 is preserved at the National Library in Jerusalem.
Story: The National Library in Jerusalem holds a Warsaw-printed copy of the Tzemach Tzedek portrait stamped with a Vilna censor's permit dated 26 January 1889. It is one of several variants of the portrait circulating after the original Metz lithograph of 1886.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, portrait, warsaw, vilna, censor

Title: R. Avraham Chaim writes essay on sadness vs. bitterness to R. Chanoch Hendel
Summary: On Monday Ki Tisa 5649 R. Avraham Chaim wrote a lengthy chassidic letter to his mechutan R. Chanoch Hendel distinguishing depressive sadness (atzvus) from holy bitterness (merirus).
Story: Responding to news about R. Hendel's grandson, who was engaged in avodas haLev based on Tanya, R. Avraham Chaim explained that the same effort to fulfill 've'ahavta lerei'acha' protects from excessive bodily attachments. He taught that sadness over the state of Klal Yisrael can be transformed into bitterness drawn from gevuros dikedushah — which carries vitality and pleasure — whereas plain atzvus comes from the cold, dry element of earth without any moisture of kedushah. He warned that tears that overflow such bounds must be examined to see whether they are truly an offering to G-d or merely the yetzer's pretext to rob a person of joy.
Tags: tanya, atzvus, merirus, chanoch hendel, avodah, chassidic letters, iggeret hateshuvah

Title: Rosenbaum writes from Smolensk prison about his arrest
Summary: From prison in Smolensk on 27 March 1889, Rosenbaum laments his fate of sitting among 'night robbers and forest murderers' for a single forged signature.
Story: In a letter dated 27.3.89 from his Smolensk cell, Rosenbaum describes the bitterness of being imprisoned in old age among violent criminals, his dignity stripped away. He explains that his only 'crime' was signing on behalf of a sole-son draftee, an act of mercy that had been twisted into an accusation of fraud. The letter offers a rare glimpse into his prison conditions and inner state during the tsarist incarceration.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, letters, tsarist

Title: R. Avraham Chaim writes to R. Chaim Gershon Kogel from Smolensk prison
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Nissan 5649 R. Avraham Chaim wrote from his imprisonment in Smolensk to his old friend R. Chaim Gershon Kogel, thanking him for his words of comfort.
Story: Throughout his imprisonment in Smolensk, R. Avraham Chaim received consoling letters from friends across the Chabad world. On Rosh Chodesh Nissan 5649 he replied to R. Chaim Gershon Kogel, telling him that despite the many waters that had passed between them, the love expressed in his letter had not been extinguished. He observed that a prisoner's spirit cools from the heat of his oppressor when he sees that distant friends share in his sorrow.
Tags: smolensk, prison, avraham chaim rosenbaum, chaim gershon kogel, russian empire, imprisonment, letters

Title: Rosenbaum writes Rosh Chodesh Nissan letter from jail to R' Chaim Gershon Kugel
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Nissan 5649 the imprisoned Rosenbaum thanked R' Chaim Gershon Kugel for words of comfort and friendship that eased his suffering in captivity.
Story: From his cell in Smolensk on 1 Nissan 5649, Reb Avraham Chaim wrote to R' Chaim Gershon Kugel acknowledging the warmth of his letter. He noted that an imprisoned man's spirit is consoled when even distant friends share in his pain. The exchange preserved one of several friendships Rosenbaum maintained from prison.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, chaim gershon kugel

Title: R. Avraham Chaim invites R. Hendel to visit him in Smolensk prison
Summary: On 20 Iyar 5649 R. Avraham Chaim wrote to R. Hendel reversing his earlier objection and inviting him to come visit during the warmer months.
Story: In the winter R. Avraham Chaim had discouraged R. Hendel from making the trip to Smolensk prison, both because of the cold and so the travel funds could be sent home to his family. On 20 Iyar 5649 he wrote that the time was now better for them both, asking R. Hendel to inform him before setting out. During that visit R. Hendel brought a gift for one of the guards, which led to a marked improvement in R. Avraham Chaim's treatment.
Tags: smolensk, prison, r. hendel, avraham chaim rosenbaum, imprisonment, visits

Title: RA"Ch writes from Smolensk prison on his contact with the Rebbetzin
Summary: From his Smolensk imprisonment RA"Ch writes to his mechutan R' Hendel describing letters from Rebbetzin Rivkah on his behalf.
Story: On 20 Iyar 5649 RA"Ch wrote from prison in Smolensk to the mashpia R' Hendel, reporting that R' Avraham Yitzchak Zarchi had visited him and told him of a letter the Rebbetzin (wife of the Maharash, Rebbetzin Rivkah) had sent before Pesach to R' Leib Berlin on RA"Ch's behalf. RA"Ch expressed his distress at troubling her and admiration at her humility.
Tags: smolensk, prison, katorga, rebbetzin rivkah, letter, hendel, russia

Title: Birth of Meir Shalom Kugel during grandfather's imprisonment
Summary: Meir Shalom Kugel was born on 20 Sivan 5649 while his grandfather R' Avraham Chaim was imprisoned in Smolensk.
Story: Born on Wednesday Parshas Korach, Meir Shalom's birth was reported to his imprisoned grandfather R' Avraham Chaim by the mashpia R' Hendel Kugel, who traveled to Pleshchenitsy upon hearing the news. R' Avraham Chaim responded from prison on Parshas Pinchas with a blessing letter to his son-in-law and daughter, including detailed questions about the birth, the mohel, and the celebration.
Tags: pleshchenitsy, kugel family, birth, smolensk, prison

Title: Birth of Meir Shalom Kugel during Rosenbaum's imprisonment
Summary: Meir Shalom, fourth son of R' Shlomo Kugel, was born on 20 Sivan 5649 while his grandfather R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum was imprisoned in Smolensk.
Story: R' Shlomo Kugel recorded the birth of his son Meir Shalom on Wednesday, 20 Sivan 5649 (19 June 1889). The birth came while the child's grandfather R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum was imprisoned in Smolensk; R' Hendel Kugel traveled to Pleshchenitsy for the brit, and R' Avraham Chaim sent congratulations from prison on Sunday Parshat Pinchas.
Tags: kugel family, rosenbaum family, pleshchenitsy, birth

Title: R. Avraham Chaim forbids his wife to visit him in Smolensk
Summary: In a letter of Wednesday Parshas Masei 5649 R. Avraham Chaim told R. Hendel he had refused his wife's request to travel to Smolensk to see him.
Story: R. Avraham Chaim's wife had written that she wished to come to Smolensk for public appearance's sake. He replied that he did not consent: it would mean abandoning the home and shop and placing a week's burden on their son Zalman, with little real benefit. The decision is recorded in his letter to R. Hendel from the week of Parshas Masei 5649.
Tags: smolensk, prison, family, avraham chaim rosenbaum, household, imprisonment

Title: R. Avraham Chaim reports easing of prison conditions after gift to guard
Summary: In a letter dated Sunday Parshas Pinchas 5649, partly written in Aramaic to evade the censor, R. Avraham Chaim described how passing the guard the gift R. Hendel had brought won him quiet treatment.
Story: Fearing the censor's eye, R. Avraham Chaim switched mid-letter into Aramaic to recount his interaction with the prison official. He explained that he had appealed to the guard not to be forced like the other Jewish prisoners to bake and travel to the bathhouse on Shabbos, and the guard had given a half-promise to accommodate him. He noted wryly that those who appear friendly only while they enjoy a benefit do not stand with a man in his time of trouble.
Tags: smolensk, prison, guards, shabbos observance, aramaic, censorship, imprisonment, bathhouse

Title: Rosenbaum forbids wife from visiting him at Smolensk prison
Summary: Around Parshat Masei 5649 Rosenbaum wrote to R' Hendel explaining that he had refused his wife permission to travel to Smolensk and visit him, citing the burden on home and business.
Story: In a letter dated the week of Parshat Masei 5649 to the mashpia Reb Hendel, Reb Avraham Chaim explained why he had rejected his wife's plan to visit him in prison. He felt the trip would force abandonment of their home and store and would burden their son Zalman with running everything for a week without yielding any real benefit.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, family, hendel

Title: Sister-in-law travels to Smolensk to visit Rosenbaum in prison
Summary: In Elul 5649 Rosenbaum's bride-sister-in-law came to Smolensk to visit him, prompting him to send a letter asking her fiancé to purchase a fine tallit katan on his behalf.
Story: During Elul 5649, Rosenbaum's sister-in-law (the bride) traveled to Smolensk to see him. In replying to her, he addressed her fiancé Reb David, asking him to purchase a tallit katan of the highest quality from Kiryat Chana David before the new year. The request reflected both his ritual concerns and his confidence in his future relative's taste.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, family

Title: Letter from prison to Rabbi Yehuda Leib of Pleshchenitsy
Summary: On Sunday of Parshat Noach 5650, R' Avraham Chaim wrote from prison to Rabbi Yehuda Leib Maskil L'Eitan of Pleshchenitsy about his countdown to freedom.
Story: On the Sunday of Parshat Noach 5650, R' Avraham Chaim sent a parallel letter to Rabbi Yehuda Leib Maskil L'Eitan, rabbi of Pleshchenitsy. He repeated his wordplay on the year tarn as encoding mar-dror — bitterness turning to liberation — and described the 240 days remaining of his sentence as days that would be sweetened into glory upon his release.
Tags: imprisonment, letters, pleshchenitsy, avraham chaim rosin, yehuda leib maskil leitan

Title: R' Avraham Chaim begins counting days to redemption from prison
Summary: At the start of 5650, imprisoned R' Avraham Chaim began counting down the days until his anticipated release.
Story: Immediately upon the entry of the year 5650 (autumn 1889), R' Avraham Chaim Rosin, held in the Smolensk fortress prison, began to count the days until his liberation. He expressed this hope in letters to acquaintances, calling the year tarn (תר"נ) a year of mattir asurim ('releaser of the bound'). The countdown framed his correspondence and poetry during the entire year of imprisonment.
Tags: imprisonment, smolensk, avraham chaim rosin, redemption

Title: Rosenbaum permitted to build a sukkah in Smolensk prison courtyard
Summary: For Sukkot 5650 the warden granted Rosenbaum the unusual privilege of building a sukkah inside the prison courtyard.
Story: Although Rosenbaum initially feared he would not even be able to eat a kezayit of bread in a sukkah and lamented his isolation from the community, the prison warden ultimately granted him permission to erect a sukkah in the prison yard for Sukkot 5650. The episode showed the warden's growing regard for him and was preserved in a letter by R' Shlomo Rosenbaum.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, sukkot

Title: Avraham Chaim attends Yom Kippur services during Smolensk imprisonment
Summary: On Yom Kippur 5650, Avraham Chaim is permitted to leave the Smolensk prison to pray at a local synagogue but refuses an aliyah due to the congregation's lax observance.
Story: On Yom Kippur of 5650 (October 5, 1889), Avraham Chaim was allowed out of prison to attend services at a Smolensk synagogue. He declined, however, to accept an aliyah to the Torah, citing that the congregants were Sabbath desecrators and Yom Kippur eaters and that several of the synagogue's Torah scrolls were halachically invalid. The account implies he prayed there regularly while imprisoned but withheld participation in public honors for these reasons.
Tags: imprisonment, smolensk, yom kippur, synagogue

Title: Avraham Chaim permitted to build a sukkah in prison courtyard
Summary: Before Sukkot 5650, the Smolensk prison warden grants Avraham Chaim permission to erect a sukkah in the prison courtyard.
Story: In a letter written between Yom Kippur and Sukkot 5650 Avraham Chaim lamented that he would be cut off from the community for the first nights of the festival, unable to eat even a kezayit of bread in a sukkah. To his relief the warden then granted permission to construct a sukkah in the prison courtyard, as recorded in a letter by Rabbi Shmuel Rosenbaum. The concession reflected the warden's growing regard for him and was one of several leniencies that followed Rabbi Zalman Aharon's earlier intervention.
Tags: imprisonment, smolensk, sukkot, sukkah

Title: Prison letter from R' Avraham Chaim to R' Zev Wolf Kugel
Summary: On 25 Tishrei 5650, R' Avraham Chaim wrote from prison to R' Zev Wolf Kugel describing his hopes of release within roughly eight months.
Story: Writing from the Smolensk prison on 25 Tishrei 5650, R' Avraham Chaim told the grandson of R' Hendel that he could not yet describe his physical state, but that he expected good news within about eight months. He played on the gematria of the Hebrew month-name letters and the phrase mattir asurim, encoding his redemption hope into the date itself.
Tags: imprisonment, letters, smolensk, avraham chaim rosin, kugel

Title: Rosenbaum counts months to release in Rosh Hashanah-period letter
Summary: On 25 Tishrei 5650 Rosenbaum wrote to R' Zev Wolf Kugel calculating that roughly eight months remained until his release and reading the year tav-resh-nun as a hint of redemption.
Story: From the Smolensk jail on 25 Tishrei 5650, Reb Avraham Chaim told the young R' Zev Wolf Kugel that he could not yet share substantive news, but in about eight months he hoped to bring glad tidings. He interpreted the 240 days remaining of his sentence as the gematria of 'mar' (bitterness) that would be transformed into 'dror' (freedom), invoking the blessing 'matir asurim.'
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, zev wolf kugel

Title: R' Avraham Chaim writes from prison about Parshas Lech Lecha maamar
Summary: From his Smolensk prison cell on the eve of 19 Kislev 5650, R' Avraham Chaim responded to R' Hendel Kugel about the Rebbe Rashab's Parshas Lech Lecha maamar.
Story: In early Kislev 5650 (late 1889), R' Hendel Kugel sent R' Avraham Chaim a summary of a maamar the Rebbe Rashab had delivered on Parshas Lech Lecha. On the eve of 19 Kislev, R' Avraham Chaim wrote back from his prison in Smolensk, expressing how precious the teaching was but lamenting that the summary alone was insufficient. He asked that R' Avraham the chozer record full maamarim and mail them to him several at a time.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, maharashab, maamar, chassidus, rosenbaum, hendel kugel

Title: Avraham Chaim leaves prison for Yud-Tes Kislev farbrengen
Summary: On 19 Kislev 5650, the Smolensk prison warden permits Avraham Chaim to spend the entire night at the chassidim's gathering place and to purchase oil for Chanukah lights.
Story: By 19 Kislev 5650 (December 12, 1889) Avraham Chaim had so won over the Smolensk prison warden that he was released for the night to the local chassidim's meeting place, where he remained with fellow chassidim until morning. On the eve of the date he wrote that Rabbi Avraham Yitzchak Zarchi had visited him and that, with the warden's permission, he would travel into the city the next day to buy oil for the Chanukah candles. The leniency was a high point of the cumulative effect of Rabbi Zalman Aharon's advocacy earlier in the year.
Tags: imprisonment, smolensk, yud tes kislev, chanukah, farbrengen

Title: R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum writes Yud-Tes Kislev Torah letter from Smolensk
Summary: On 19 Kislev 5650, R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum sent a detailed Torah letter from Smolensk to R. Chanoch Hendel analyzing chassidic concepts.
Story: On the morning of Yud-Tes Kislev 5650 (December 12, 1889), R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum wrote from Smolensk to his colleague R. Chanoch Hendel. The letter discussed a maamar said on Parshas Lech Lecha concerning the concept of 'goy gadol' and a new creation through good deeds. He raised questions about the conflicting interpretations of the Yerushalmi, the Zohar, Targum Yonatan, and Rashi on the verse 'Hashem yotzei mimekomo,' asking that his doubts be brought before the Rebbe (Maharash) for clarification.
Tags: avraham chaim rosenbaum, smolensk, russia, yud-tes kislev, correspondence, chassidus, chanoch hendel

Title: Rosenbaum receives leave to visit chassidim for 19 Kislev farbrengen
Summary: On the night of 19 Kislev 5650 the warden allowed Rosenbaum to leave the prison and spend the night farbrenging with the chassidim in town.
Story: After R' Raza Schneerson's intervention with the Smolensk governor improved Rosenbaum's prison conditions, on the night of 19 Kislev 5650 the warden permitted him to leave the jail entirely. He spent the whole night at the chassidic gathering with anash, and the following day received leave to go into town to purchase oil for Chanukah lights.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, 19-kislev, chanukah

Title: Birth of R' Shmuel Grossman in Nikolayev
Summary: R' Shmuel Grossman, son of R' Asher of Nikolayev, was born in 5650.
Story: About a year after his sister Chaya Mushka's birth, R' Shmuel Grossman was born in Nikolayev in 5650 to R' Asher Grossman. On 4 Elul 5650, Rashab responded to R' Asher's question about hiring a wet nurse given his wife's weakened state after the births. R' Shmuel would later study in Tomchei Tmimim and serve as shochet.
Tags: nikolayev, grossman-family, birth

Title: Chassidic prayer house built in Libau
Summary: The Chassidic prayer house in Libau (Liepaja) was constructed by the Chassidic community in 5650 (1890).
Story: In 5650 (1890) the Chassidic community of Libau (today Liepaja, Latvia) built their dedicated prayer house. The building was known simply as 'the Chassidishe Minyan' and followed Nusach Ha'Ari prayer rite.
Tags: libau, liepaja, latvia, kurland, synagogue

Title: Family returns to Lubavitch after extended absence
Summary: After years abroad seeking medical care, the Rashab and his wife returned to spend an entire year in Lubavitch with their son.
Story: In 1890, after years of being absent from Lubavitch while seeking medical treatment in Russia and abroad, the Rashab and his wife finally returned home. The Rayatz later wrote that this was 'almost the first in my life that my father spent entirely at home,' as the greater part of previous years had been spent abroad. However, in December 1890, the Rashab fell ill with a high fever for about two months.
Tags: lubavitch, russia, rashab, shterna sara, yosef yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Letter to Pekuam regarding Magen Avot yeshiva in Hebron
Summary: R' Chaikin and R' Levin wrote to the Pekuam regarding the Magen Avot yeshiva in Hebron.
Story: In 5650 (1890), R' Shmuel Menachem Chaikin wrote to the Pekuam Amsterdam committee on behalf of the Magen Avot yeshiva in Hebron, with R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin co-signing as rabbi. The dual signature pattern continued: Chaikin signed first, Levin added the title 'rav and moreh in Hebron.' The yeshiva was a Chabad institution requiring external support.
Tags: shmuel menachem chaikin, yehuda leib shaul levin, hebron, magen avot, yeshiva, pekuam

Title: Prison conditions sharply worsen at end of winter 5650 in Smolensk
Summary: Around the end of winter 5650 the staff at Smolensk prison changed and stringent new restrictions were imposed on prisoners' clothing, food, bedding and use of fire.
Story: At the close of winter 5650 the prison administration was replaced and Rosenbaum wrote to R' Hendel describing harsher rules: only government-issued uniforms, straw pillows instead of feather, no private samovars, food rationed to two meals only, no chests or utensils beyond a single pot and spoon. He worried particularly about Pesach, when reliance on the common kettle would force compromise on chametz and warm food.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison

Title: R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum released from prison
Summary: R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum was released from prison at the end of 5650 after roughly two years of imprisonment.
Story: After his arrest in 5648, R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum remained imprisoned until the end of 5650 (1890). During this period he wrote numerous letters, including one on Thursday Parshat Tzav 5650 in which he discussed plans to travel via Lubavitch upon release, and another describing his elderly father counting the moments until they would meet again.
Tags: pleshchenitsy, r avraham chaim rosenbaum, russia, persecution

Title: R' Raza Schneerson travels to Smolensk to plead for Rosenbaum
Summary: On the Rebbe Maharash's posthumous instruction, in 5650 R' Raza Schneerson came to Smolensk and intervened with the governor to ease Rosenbaum's prison conditions.
