Story: Acting on the late Rebbe Maharash's counsel from the previous years, in 5650 R' Raza Schneerson traveled to Smolensk and presented himself to local leaders and chassidim on Rosenbaum's behalf. Although he could not obtain Rosenbaum's release, his intervention with the governor freed him from hard labor, secured him a separate cell, and won him kindly treatment from the warden including a private stove and a chest of books.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, raza schneerson, rebbe maharash

Title: R. Avraham David Lavut, Rabbi of Nikolayev, passes away
Summary: Rabbi Avraham David Lavut, Rabbi of Nikolayev, passed away in 5650, having designated his grandson to succeed him.
Story: In 5650 (1890), Rabbi Avraham David Lavut, who had served as Rabbi of Nikolayev, passed away. Before his passing he instructed the heads of the community that his grandson Rabbi Meir Shlomo Yanovsky should fill his place. Yanovsky thereupon assumed the Nikolayev rabbinate, a post he would hold until his own passing in 5693.
Tags: lavut, nikolayev, rabbinate, ukraine

Title: R. Meir Shlomo Yanovsky becomes Rabbi of Nikolayev
Summary: Rabbi M.S. Yanovsky, grandfather of the Rebbe, assumed the Nikolayev rabbinate in 5650.
Story: In 5650 (1890), Rabbi Meir Shlomo Yanovsky succeeded his grandfather Rabbi Avraham David Lavut as Rabbi of Nikolayev, on Lavut's deathbed instruction. He held the position until his death on 23 Elul 5693 (1933), after which his son-in-law Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn (uncle of the Rebbe) succeeded him.
Tags: yanovsky, nikolayev, rabbinate, ukraine

Title: Town of Otwock founded by Jewish settlers
Summary: The resort town of Otwock, about thirty kilometers from Warsaw, was founded around 1890 by wealthy Jews on a tract of forest land they had purchased.
Story: Otwock developed rapidly into a large town with a population that was roughly half Jewish. Its clean air and proximity to Warsaw later made it the chosen residence of the Frierdiker Rebbe and the new home of Tomchei Tmimim in 1935. The town's character as a Jewish resort and sanatorium center shaped its role in Chabad history.
Tags: poland, otwock, warsaw-area

Title: Hebron Vaad publishes public appeal for funds
Summary: On 8 Tevet 5650 the two remaining Hebron Vaad members published an appeal to world Jewry for emergency assistance.
Story: After community leaders begged them to continue, R' Binyamin Rivlin and R' Meir Tzvi Hershler published in Chabatzelet on 8 Tevet 5650 a public appeal describing the Vaad's emptied coffers, unpaid communal workers, and inability to pay the doctor and shochet, calling on diaspora Jewry to come to the aid of the Ashkenazi communities of Hebron.
Tags: hebron, vaad, binyamin rivlin, meir tzvi hershler, fundraising

Title: Rosenbaum's 15 Shevat letter from prison anticipating freedom
Summary: On 15 Shevat 5650 Rosenbaum wrote to the rabbi of Pleschenitz that every passing day brought salvation closer, comparing memory of past days to a riddle about yesterday and tomorrow.
Story: From Smolensk on 15 Shevat 5650, Reb Avraham Chaim told R' Yehuda Leib Maskil L'Eitan that he had no real news but that 'salvation draws nearer day by day.' He framed the long days behind bars with a Hebrew riddle: 'What was tomorrow and will be yesterday?'—answer, 'today'—expressing faith that he would yet see redemption.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, yehuda leib maskil l'eitan

Title: Tu B'Shevat prison letter to Rabbi Yehuda Leib of Pleshchenitsy
Summary: On 15 Shevat 5650 R' Avraham Chaim wrote again from prison, expressing that each day brought his salvation closer.
Story: On 15 Shevat 5650, R' Avraham Chaim wrote once more to Rabbi Yehuda Leib of Pleshchenitsy. He thanked God for life and health, saying his days now seemed long but only until they passed, and likened his situation to the riddle that 'today' is yesterday's tomorrow and tomorrow's yesterday.
Tags: imprisonment, letters, pleshchenitsy, avraham chaim rosin, tu bshevat

Title: Prison administration changes and conditions harshen at Smolensk
Summary: At the end of winter 5650, the officers overseeing the Smolensk prison were replaced and the conditions for the prisoners grew significantly harsher.
Story: Toward the end of the winter of 5650, new guards took over the Smolensk prison and tightened the regime. Prisoners were forbidden to smoke, were limited to coarse prison-issue clothing and straw-stuffed pillows, lost access to private samovars, and were restricted to two meals' worth of food at a time. R' Avraham Chaim recorded these privations in his letters.
Tags: imprisonment, smolensk, avraham chaim rosin, prison conditions

Title: Passing of R' Avraham Dovid Lavut, rabbi of Nikolayev
Summary: Rabbi Avraham Dovid Lavut, author of Kav Naki and Shaar HaKollel, passed away on 18 Adar 5650 in Nikolayev.
Story: On 18 Adar 5650, Rabbi Avraham Dovid Lavut, grandfather of the future Rebbe (Ramash), passed away. He left a written request that the chassidim of Nikolayev appoint his grandson Rabbi Meir Shlomo Yanovsky as his successor, and that the chassidim of Romanovka appoint his son-in-law R' Isser Yanovsky. The Nikolayev appointment was carried out; Romanovka instead appointed R' Shaymen Atkin.
Tags: lavut, nikolayev, kav-naki, shaar-hakollel, rabbinate

Title: RA"Ch writes from Smolensk prison about visiting Lubavitch after release
Summary: Nearing the end of his sentence, RA"Ch writes R' Hendel from prison about routing his journey home through Lubavitch.
Story: On Thursday of Parshas Tzav 5650, as his release approached, RA"Ch wrote to R' Hendel that he intended to ask his elderly father in Pleshchenitz for permission, or advice, on whether to travel home via Lubavitch. He notes his father is so weak that he can no longer add greetings in his own hand to family letters and counts the hours until they meet again in life.
Tags: smolensk, prison, katorga, letter, hendel, lubavitch, russia, pleshchenitz

Title: Letter to R' Hendel describing harsh new prison regime
Summary: On Thursday of Parshat Tzav 5650, R' Avraham Chaim wrote to the mashpia R' Hendel about the worsened Smolensk prison conditions and Passover concerns.
Story: On Thursday of Parshat Tzav 5650, R' Avraham Chaim wrote to the mashpia R' Hendel describing in detail the new restrictions imposed by the changed prison administration. He worried especially about Passover, since the prohibition on private samovars made hot water for matzah impossible, and the prison ovens could not be koshered. He noted that only about two and a half months remained of his sentence.
Tags: imprisonment, letters, smolensk, avraham chaim rosin, hendel, mashpia, passover

Title: Rebbe Rashab rebukes Rashaz Slonim for overpaying for a manuscript book
Summary: On 11 Nisan 5650, Rebbe Rashab tells Rashaz Slonim that paying over 100 rubles for a manuscript was excessive and that such buying would deplete any fortune.
Story: After receiving a manuscript book sent via Rashaz's father, Rebbe Rashab expressed astonishment at the price paid (Igros #39). He warned that buying at any price would not only exhaust all means but also prevent assembling the truly essential manuscripts. He reaffirmed his core principle: manuscripts are the very life of his soul, yet acquisition must remain within limits.
Tags: manuscripts, rashab, rashaz slonim, letters

Title: R' Avraham Chaim plans release from Smolensk prison on Parshat Korach
Summary: R' Avraham Chaim expected to be released from the Smolensk prison on Monday of Parshat Korach 5650, planning then to travel to Lubavitch.
Story: In his Parshat Tzav letter, R' Avraham Chaim told R' Hendel that his planned day of departure from the Smolensk prison would be the Monday of Parshat Korach, in late spring 5650. He intended to travel directly to Lubavitch upon release, ending roughly a year of imprisonment.
Tags: imprisonment, smolensk, avraham chaim rosin, lubavitch, release

Title: Rosenbaum released from Smolensk prison around Parshat Korach 5650
Summary: Rosenbaum left Smolensk prison about Monday of Parshat Korach 5650, ending nearly two years of incarceration, and planned to travel directly to Lubavitch.
Story: After almost two years of imprisonment in Smolensk, Reb Avraham Chaim was released around the Monday of Parshat Korach 5650. In his last prison letter he announced the date of his expected freedom and his intention to journey at once to Lubavitch to see the Rebbe Maharash's son and successor circle.
Tags: russia, smolensk, prison, release

Title: Expulsion of Jews from Moscow
Summary: Russian authorities expelled the Jews of Moscow in 1891, forcing Chabad rabbis R' DovBer Efrat and R' Chaim Yaakov Widerwitz to flee.
Story: In 1891 (תרנ"א), the Czarist government issued the Moscow expulsion decree, forcing Jewish residents to leave the city. The two Chabad rabbis serving Moscow at the time, R' DovBer Efrat and R' Chaim Yaakov Widerwitz, both had to depart. Widerwitz emigrated to America, while Efrat made aliyah to Hebron where his grandmother and the Slonim family lived.
Tags: moscow, russia, expulsion, dovber efrat, chaim yaakov widerwitz, chabad rabbi

Title: R' Chaim Eliezer Bichovsky enters the etrog trade for Kollel Chabad
Summary: In 5651 R' Chaim Eliezer Bichovsky took over the Kollel Chabad etrog trade, a cover for the Eretz Yisrael fund.
Story: Bichovsky later recounted in a public reply that he had begun handling "the etrog business" of Kollel Chabad in 5651, the trade serving as a discreet front for the Eretz Yisrael fundraising operation. He partnered with R' Chaim Bagin, and the two ran the renamed Vaad Mesadrei HaReshimah until 5673, when leadership changed again.
Tags: kollel chabad, chaim eliezer bichovsky, etrogim, fundraising

Title: R' Chaim Leib Gar's son R' Tzvi Gar born in Yakobshtadt
Summary: R' Tzvi (Hershl) Gar, future representative of the Rebbe Rayatz in Riga, was born to R' Chaim Leib in Yakobshtadt.
Story: R' Tzvi Gar was born in Yakobshtadt, Kurland — a stronghold of Chabad Chassidism — to his father R' Chaim Leib. He was educated at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch and later served as a mashgiach in the Riga slaughterhouse, becoming the Rebbe Rayatz's contact person in Riga in the early years of his leadership.
Tags: yakobshtadt, kurland, tomchei-tmimim, tzvi-gar

Title: R' DovBer Efrat arrives in Hebron
Summary: R' DovBer Efrat arrived in Hebron at the end of 1891 after leaving Moscow due to the expulsion decree.
Story: R' DovBer Efrat, grandson of Rebbetzin Menucha Rachel Slonim, arrived in Hebron at the end of 1891 (שלהי תרנ"א) after the Moscow expulsion forced him out of Russia. He joined his extended Slonim family already settled there.
Tags: dovber efrat, hebron, aliyah, moscow expulsion, menucha rachel slonim

Title: R. Chaim Avraham Bichowsky begins serving Kollel Chabad
Summary: In 5651 R. Chaim Avraham Bichowsky began his service in Kollel Chabad, as he later recounted in his kruz 'Teshuva LeDorshei HaAddress'.
Story: Bichowsky wrote that when he entered the kollel's service in 5651, the ba'al ha'address was already R. Moshe Wienberg in Jerusalem. After Wienberg's death the post passed jointly to R. Manus Werevoleanski and R. Mordechai Schlank, and when Manus died, R. DovBer Efrat was appointed alongside Schlank. His chronology established that Jerusalem had already been the kollel's central address before 5651.
Tags: kollel chabad, ba'al ha'address, bichowsky

Title: Rosenbaum reaches Frankfurt and opens a dairy shop
Summary: After Shabbat in Warsaw with his brother, Rosenbaum traveled to Frankfurt where one of his sons joined him and they opened a dairy-products store, staying about a year.
Story: Following his flight from Pleschenitz, Reb Avraham Chaim spent Shabbat in Warsaw at his brother's home. He then proceeded to Frankfurt, where one of his sons joined him and together they opened a shop selling dairy foods. They remained in Frankfurt about a year until German authorities expelled him.
Tags: germany, frankfurt, escape, rosenbaum

Title: Rebbe Rashab employs scribe R. Shmuel Rabinovich to copy manuscripts
Summary: On Monday of Parshas Vayakhel 5651 the Rebbe Rashab instructed his scribe R. Shmuel Rabinovich on which Chassidic discourses to copy.
Story: The Rebbe sent a list specifying which texts to copy fully and which to merely examine, requesting the completed copies. He also arranged that R. Yitzchak Noach the shochet would obtain certain Maamarim from R. Baruch Tumarkin for copying, sent ten rubles, and asked Rabinovich to advise on the total fee.
Tags: rabinovich, der shrayber, manuscripts, copying, baruch tumarkin

Title: Birth of Chana Kugel
Summary: Chana, daughter of R' Shlomo Kugel, was born on the eve of Shabbat Tazria, 2 Nisan 5651.
Story: R' Shlomo Kugel recorded in his family register the birth of his daughter Chana on the eve of Shabbat Parshat Tazria, 2 Nisan 5651 (11 March 1891). The entry appears in manuscript 584 in the Lubavitch library.
Tags: kugel family, birth

Title: Birth of Chanah Kugel
Summary: Chanah Kugel was born on Friday Parshas Tazria, 2 Nisan 5651, in Pleshchenitsy.
Story: Recorded by R' Shlomo Kugel in his family register on manuscript 584, Chanah was the fifth child listed in the household. The register documents the family's growth across the 1880s and early 1890s in Pleshchenitsy.
Tags: pleshchenitsy, kugel family, birth

Title: R' Yaakov Himelfarb's father dies in Libau
Summary: R' Yaakov Himelfarb's father passed away on 7 Iyar 5651 in Libau, when his son was eleven years old.
Story: On 7 Iyar 5651 (May 1891) R' Yaakov Himelfarb's father died in Libau, leaving his eleven-year-old son to grow up in the community. The Himelfarb family — father, grandfather, and great-grandfather — were all Chabad chassidim who prayed in Nusach Ha'Ari.
Tags: libau, liepaja, latvia, kurland

Title: R' Levin's final letter from Hebron
Summary: R' Levin wrote his last letter from Hebron on 17 Tammuz, still signing as rav of the city.
Story: On 17 Tammuz 5651 (June 23, 1891), R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin wrote his last preserved letter from Hebron, still signing 'rav and moreh in Hebron.' The following year he relocated to Jerusalem. His letters from Hebron are preserved in Sinai journal volume 87.
Tags: yehuda leib shaul levin, hebron, letter, jerusalem

Title: Yarmarka market and Yosef Yitzchak's arrest in Lubavitch
Summary: Ten-year-old Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was arrested at the Lubavitch market fair after defending Reb Dovid the butcher from a corrupt police sergeant.
Story: During the two-day yarmarka market fair in Lubavitch on June 29-30, 1891, young Yosef Yitzchak encountered a police sergeant beating Reb Dovid the butcher with false accusations of theft. After defending the butcher, Yosef Yitzchak was arrested and locked in a dark cell, where he reviewed Mishnah by heart and prayed Minchah. He was released when officers realized he was the nephew of Rabbi Zalman Aharon Schneersohn, and the butcher was exonerated when the sergeant's actual theft was uncovered.
Tags: lubavitch, russia, white russia, arrest, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, czarist russia

Title: Rosenbaum flees Russia after warning of renewed arrest
Summary: In Tishrei 5652 a friendly investigator warned Rosenbaum that new charges were being prepared, prompting him to host one final Simchat Torah farbrengen and slip out of Pleschenitz that night.
Story: On one of the days of Tishrei 5652-3, Reb Avraham Chaim was secretly told that fresh proceedings were being readied against him and that he must flee abroad. On Simchat Torah he hosted a great gathering for all the local chassidim, farbrenging joyously all day, and at nightfall vanished from town. Opponents who heard of his flight gave chase but failed to overtake him.
Tags: russia, plescenitz, escape, simchat torah

Title: R' DovBer Efrat issues shochet certification in Hebron
Summary: R' DovBer Efrat issued a kosher slaughter certification on 13 Kislev 1891 shortly after arriving in Hebron.
Story: On 13 Kislev 1891 (י"ג כסלו תרנ"ב), R' DovBer Efrat gave a relative a shochet u'bodek certification. The document opens with his statement that the Almighty had granted him to come to the Holy City and notes the duration of his residence there, confirming his arrival shortly before.
Tags: dovber efrat, hebron, shochet, certification

Title: R' Levin moves from Hebron to Jerusalem
Summary: R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin ended his Hebron rabbinate and moved to Jerusalem.
Story: Toward the end of 5652 (1892), R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin moved from Hebron to Jerusalem, ending five years of service as rav of Hebron's Chabad community. His departure is documented in the biographical work Zekher Aviad. The move closed the dual-rabbinate era he had shared with R' Shmuel Menachem Chaikin.
Tags: yehuda leib shaul levin, hebron, jerusalem, rabbinate

Title: R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum leaves Russia
Summary: R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum departed Russia during the years 5652-5653 (1892-1893).
Story: After decades of life as a Chabad chassid and businessman in the Russian Empire, R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum left Russia in the years 5652-5653. The departure came in the early years of the Rebbe Rashab's leadership, as significant numbers of Russian Jews were beginning to seek refuge in the West. He would spend several years in transit before reaching his final destination.
Tags: avraham chaim rosenbaum, russia, emigration

Title: R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz settles in Warsaw after Moscow expulsion
Summary: Following the 1891-1893 expulsion of Jews from Moscow, Chabad chassid R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz relocated to Warsaw.
Story: R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz, son-in-law of R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin, had originally lived in Dokshitz and then Moscow. When the Tsarist government expelled the Jews of Moscow in 5652-5653 (1892-1893), he resettled in Warsaw, becoming one of the earliest Chabad chassidim to establish himself there. He would later head Chabad activity in the city until his death.
Tags: warsaw, moscow expulsion, russia, poland, yosef yozik horowitz

Title: Rosenbaum expelled from Germany and relocates to Amsterdam
Summary: A German police official informed Rosenbaum he could not remain in Germany, and although he refused to consider America he moved instead to Amsterdam.
Story: About a year after his arrival in Frankfurt, a police officer ordered Reb Avraham Chaim to leave German territory. He moved to Amsterdam, intent on avoiding America at all costs. There he conducted some business with the chassid Persson but found no steady livelihood.
Tags: germany, holland, amsterdam, expulsion

Title: Rosenbaum released from Smolensk and flees Russia
Summary: Warned of a new prosecution after Simchas Torah 5652/3, Rosenbaum secretly flees Plescenice via Warsaw to Frankfurt.
Story: After his release, a sympathetic investigating magistrate quietly warned Rosenbaum that fresh charges were pending and hinted that he should escape abroad. On one of the days of Tishrei 5652/5653 (1891/2) he was tipped off that he would be re-arrested the day after Simchas Torah; he hosted a joyous farewell farbrengen for the Plescenice chassidim and vanished that night. He traveled first to Warsaw, where his brother lived, and then to Frankfurt, where he and his son ran a dairy shop for about a year.
Tags: russia, plescenice, warsaw, frankfurt, escape, emigration

Title: Wedding of Chaya Mushka Hornstein in Lubavitch
Summary: The Maharash's daughter Chaya Mushka Hornstein was married in the large hall of the Lubavitch courtyard in the summer of 5652.
Story: This was among the major family celebrations held in the great hall the Maharash had erected in 5632. The large hall, with its high ceiling and wide windows, served as the venue for Chabad's most significant communal occasions when large crowds gathered in Lubavitch. The 5652 wedding was followed a year later by the bar mitzvah of the Frierdiker Rebbe in the same hall.
Tags: wedding, hornstein, schneersohn

Title: Bar Mitzvah of Rebbe Rayatz in Lubavitch
Summary: The bar mitzvah of the Rebbe Rayatz was held in the great hall of the Rebbes' courtyard in Lubavitch.
Story: In summer 5653 (1893), the bar mitzvah of the future Rebbe Rayatz was held in the great hall of the Rebbes' courtyard in Lubavitch. The same great hall would later host his wedding four years later.
Tags: bar mitzvah, lubavitch, rebbe rayatz

Title: Bar Mitzvah of the Frierdiker Rebbe in Lubavitch
Summary: The bar mitzvah celebration of the future Frierdiker Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was held in the great hall of the Lubavitch courtyard in the summer of 5653.
Story: The celebration brought a large gathering of Chassidim to Lubavitch and used the same large hall that had hosted the 5652 Hornstein wedding. Four years later in 5657 the same hall would host the future Frierdiker Rebbe's wedding. This event marked the coming of age of Chabad's next generation of leadership.
Tags: frierdiker-rebbe, bar-mitzvah, yosef-yitzchak

Title: Bar Mitzvah of the future Rayatz in Lubavitch
Summary: In the summer of 5653 the Bar Mitzvah of the future Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak was held in the great hall of the Rebbes' courtyard.
Story: In the summer of 5653 (1893), the Bar Mitzvah of the future Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak was celebrated in the large hall of the courtyard of the Rebbes in Lubavitch, the same hall used for the large communal gatherings of Chabad. The event is documented in Sefer HaMaamarim 5711.
Tags: rayatz, lubavitch, bar mitzvah

Title: Bar Mitzvah of the Rebbe Rayatz in the Large Hall
Summary: The bar mitzvah celebration of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn (Rayatz) took place in the Large Hall of the Lubavitch courtyard in 5653.
Story: According to Rayatz's own memoirs, the Large Hall built by his grandfather Maharash hosted his bar mitzvah celebration in 5653 (1893). The same hall had hosted the wedding of his aunt Chaya Mushka to Rabbi Moshe HaKohen Hornstein, and would also host his own wedding four years later.
Tags: rayatz, lubavitch, bar-mitzvah, ulam-hagadol, schneersohn

Title: City renamed from Dinaburg to Dvinsk
Summary: The Latvian city formerly called Dinaburg was officially renamed Dvinsk.
Story: Daugavpils, the second-largest city in Latvia, southeast of Riga, went through several name changes. Until 5653 (1893) it was known as Dinaburg, after which the authorities renamed it Dvinsk. The city would later be renamed again to Daugavpils.
Tags: latvia, dvinsk, daugavpils, dinaburg, naming

Title: Letter showing Rebbe Maharash books still undivided among heirs
Summary: In 5653, Rebbe Rashab's letter to R' Yitzchak Dovber Vilenski indicates that the printed books from Rebbe Maharash's estate had not yet been divided among the sons.
Story: Following Rebbe Maharash's passing, the printed book collection remained in his house for over a decade before being divided. This letter is one of the data points indicating that division did not happen immediately after his passing.
Tags: rashab, maharash, vilenski, inheritance, books, letters

Title: R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin dies
Summary: In 5653, R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin — rabbi and chief overseer of Hebron Chabad — died, along with R' Yehuda Leib Slonim.
Story: R' Shimon Menashe had served continuously in Hebron Chabad leadership since 5607, becoming the principal overseer in his later years while remaining 'honorary president' due to extreme old age. Active leadership had long since shifted to R' Levi Yitzchak Slonim, but his death ended an era.
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, shimon menashe chaikin, yehuda leib slonim

Title: Rashab assumes leadership of Chabad on Rosh HaShanah
Summary: Rabbi Shalom Dovber Schneersohn formally assumed the position of Rebbe in Lubavitch on Rosh HaShanah.
Story: On Rosh HaShanah 1893, the Rashab formally took on the mantle of Chabad leadership. He used the position to reassert Lubavitch's involvement in Russian Jewish communal affairs after years of relative quiet following the Maharash's passing in 1882.
Tags: rashab, leadership, chabad, rosh hashanah

Title: Rashab formally accepts Chabad leadership
Summary: After eleven years, Rashab accepted the full yoke of Chabad leadership in 5654.
Story: In 5654 (1893/4), Rashab fully accepted the leadership of the Chabad movement, including holding regular yechidus, responding to written queries for guidance, and permitting his Chassidic discourses to be transcribed and distributed. He had hesitated to assume formal leadership for over a decade after his father's passing.
Tags: rashab, leadership, nesius, lubavitch

Title: Rashab formally assumes position of Lubavitcher Rebbe
Summary: On Rosh HaShanah, Rabbi Shalom Dovber Schneersohn (Rashab) formally assumed leadership as the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe.
Story: The Rashab began to reassert Lubavitch involvement in Russian Jewish communal affairs. He challenged the dominance of Enlightenment-aligned representatives like Baron David Gunzburg and asserted leadership on behalf of the chasidic community, drawing on the vast Chabad network across Russia.
Tags: rashab, rosh hashanah, lubavitch, leadership

Title: Rashab fully accepts position of Rebbe
Summary: On Rosh HaShanah 1893, Rabbi Shalom Dovber fully accepted the position of Rebbe, becoming the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe.
Story: On Rosh HaShanah in 1893, the Rashab, then thirty-two, fully accepted the position of Rebbe, becoming the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe. He walked into services and took his father's seat near the holy ark, which had remained vacant since Rabbi Shmuel's passing eleven years earlier. With his acceptance of the position, Chasidim began to flock to Lubavitch in large numbers once again, beginning what the Rayatz called 'the era of the rebirth of Lubavitch.'
Tags: lubavitch, russia, rashab, rosh hashanah, succession

Title: Rashbatz appointed teacher of Yosef Yitzchak
Summary: Rabbi Shmuel Betzalel Sheftel (Rashbatz) was appointed by the Rashab to teach his son Yosef Yitzchak.
Story: A few days after Rosh HaShanah 1893, the Rashab appointed Rabbi Shmuel Betzalel Sheftel, known as the Rashbatz, to teach his son Yosef Yitzchak. The Rashbatz had previously taught the Rashab himself at the behest of Rabbi Shmuel. He remained Yosef Yitzchak's teacher until 1900, and was renowned for his ability to clarify chasidic concepts through parables and his deep knowledge of chasidic teachings from previous generations.
Tags: lubavitch, russia, rashbatz, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, teacher

Title: Rayatz visits Chasid R. Chaim Dover Vilensky in Lubavitch
Summary: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn saw the Chasid R. Chaim Dover Vilensky in Lubavitch during the summer of 5653.
Story: The Rayatz later recalled having seen the noted Chasid R. Chaim Dover Vilensky of Kremenchug two or three times, the last being in Lubavitch in the summer of 5653 (1893). Decades later he sought to commemorate this Chasid by gathering material from Vilensky's son for the Hatamim journal.
Tags: lubavitch, chaim dover vilensky, kremenchug, rayatz

Title: Raza relocates to Vitebsk
Summary: Rabbi Zalman Aharon Schneersohn relocated to Vitebsk, deferring leadership of Chabad to his younger brother the Rashab.
Story: In the summer of 1893, Rabbi Zalman Aharon Schneersohn (the Raza) relocated from Lubavitch to Vitebsk, fifty miles away. The move possibly was meant to keep him out of the limelight, clearing the way for his younger brother the Rashab to emerge as Rebbe. The Raza had declared that 'My brother, the Rashab, was born a Rebbe and is a Rebbe' and may also have been motivated by financial difficulties. He continued to visit Lubavitch often and became a major influence on his nephew Yosef Yitzchak.
Tags: vitebsk, russia, raza, zalman aharon schneersohn, relocation

Title: Rosenbaum expelled from Germany, moves to Amsterdam
Summary: Around 5653, a German police officer orders Rosenbaum to leave Frankfurt, and he relocates reluctantly to Amsterdam.
Story: After roughly a year running a dairy shop in Frankfurt with his son, a police official informed Rosenbaum that he had no right to reside in Germany and ordered him out. He moved to Amsterdam, where he partnered in business with the chossid R. Abba Person of Koenigsberg, who had likewise been forced to leave Russia. Unable to find sustainable income there, he would soon be pushed, against his preference, to consider emigration to America.
Tags: germany, frankfurt, amsterdam, netherlands, police, emigration

Title: Rosenbaum moves from Berlin to Königsberg seeking business
Summary: At the start of summer 5653 Rosenbaum left Berlin for Königsberg to try his hand at business, but his efforts there did not succeed.
Story: In early summer 5653 Reb Avraham Chaim moved from Berlin to Königsberg, pursuing a commercial venture he hoped would establish him. He labored at it all summer without success and confessed that 'the design did not come to fruition because God did not consent to it.'
Tags: germany, konigsberg, berlin

Title: Rosenbaum works as proofreader in Berlin Torah publishing house
Summary: During the winter of 5653 Rosenbaum worked in Berlin preparing a Torah-scholarly journal for press while residing in the home of its publishing rabbi.
Story: In winter 5653 Reb Avraham Chaim worked in Berlin as the editor and proofreader of a Torah-scientific journal, lodging in the home of the rabbi who issued it. From there he wrote to Rabbi Tzvi Tietz, author of Zikhron Yehudah on Eichah, explaining why he had cut a passage from a submitted article on the wording of the bris-milah blessing 'tziva yedidut.'
Tags: germany, berlin, publishing, tzvi tietz

Title: Rosenbaum works as Torah journal editor in Berlin
Summary: During 5653 Rosenbaum lives in Berlin while editing and proofreading a Torah-scholarly journal in the publisher's home.
Story: A surviving undated letter from this period describes Rosenbaum as 'arranging and preparing the words of the wise for print,' lodging in the home of an unnamed rabbinic publisher in Berlin. He used the post to correspond with R. Tzvi Tietz, author of Zikaron Yehuda on Eichah, about the wording of the bris milah blessing 'tziva yedidus,' explaining why he had cut a passage from Tietz's submitted essay.
Tags: germany, berlin, torah journal, editing

Title: Russian law confirms melamdim need no certification
Summary: A Russian law issued in 1893 confirmed that melamdim in the western provinces did not require any certification of secular education.
Story: Despite ongoing pressure from Maskilim and Russian officials to require state certification (tzenz) of melamdim, the law signed by the Minister of Education preserved the right of traditional teachers to operate cheders without such requirements. The Rebbe Rashab worked over many years to defend this status against repeated attempts to alter it.
Tags: russia, melamdim, cheder, tsarist law, tzenz

Title: R' Yaakov Landa born in Kornitz
Summary: R' Yaakov Landa, future rabbi of Libau and Bnei Brak, was born on 5 Iyar 5653 in Kornitz.
Story: R' Yaakov Landa was born on 5 Iyar 5653 (April 21, 1893) in Kornitz to his father R' Moshe Yehuda Leib. He would go on to study at Tomchei Tmimim, serve as rabbi of Kornitz, Libau and finally Bnei Brak.
Tags: kornitz, landa, bnei-brak

Title: HaChavatzelet announces R' DovBer Efrat's rabbinic appointment
Summary: The newspaper HaChavatzelet published the announcement of R' DovBer Efrat's appointment as rabbi of Hebron on 9 Tammuz 1893.
Story: On 9 Tammuz 1893 (ט' תמוז תרנ"ג), the newspaper HaChavatzelet reported that R' DovBer Efrat, formerly one of the rabbis of Moscow, had been chosen as the new rabbi of the Ashkenazi community in Hebron. The notice described him as a 'distinguished guest' passing through Jerusalem.
Tags: dovber efrat, hachavatzelet, hebron, rabbinate, moscow

Title: R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, Hebron Chabad rav, dies at age 92
Summary: R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, who served as head of Hebron's Chabad community for approximately fifty years, died on 29 Sivan 5653 at age 92.
Story: Born in Shklov around 5562, R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin emigrated to Eretz Israel at age 18 in 5580 and moved from Tzfat to Hebron at the Mitteler Rebbe's directive. He served as Av Beit Din of Hebron's Chabad community for some fifty years. Hachavatzelet reported that 'all Hebron's inhabitants, Sephardic and Ashkenazi, streamed in reverence behind his bier and aroused bitter mourning over him.'
Tags: hebron, shklov, shimon menashe chaikin, rabbinate, kollel chabad

Title: Wedding of Rachel Leah of Kopust
Summary: On Friday 9 Tamuz 5653, R' Yaakov Halevi Vishelitzky married Rachel Leah, daughter of the Admor Maharshaz of Kopust (author of Magen Avos).
Story: On Friday 9 Tamuz 5653 in the town of Kopust, R' Yaakov ben Avraham Yeshaya Halevi Vishelitzky married Rachel Leah, daughter of the Admor Maharshaz of Kopust — the author of Magen Avos and the senior leader of the Kopust branch of Chabad. The surviving ketubah was witnessed by Shneur Zalman David ben Moshe and Binyamin ben Shimon.
Tags: kopust, rachel leah, vishelitzky, magen avos, wedding

Title: Death of R' Shimon Menashe; R' DovBer Efrat appointed rabbi of Hebron
Summary: Rabbi Shimon Menashe of Hebron passed away on 29 Sivan 1893, and R' DovBer Efrat was appointed in his place.
Story: Rabbi Shimon Menashe of Hebron died on 29 Sivan 1893 (כ"ט סיון תרנ"ג). R' DovBer Efrat, who had already arrived in Hebron from Moscow following the 1891 expulsion of Jews from that city, was appointed to succeed him as rabbi of the Ashkenazi community in Hebron.
Tags: hebron, shimon menashe, dovber efrat, rabbinate, petira

Title: Yosef Yitzchak's bar mitzvah
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn celebrated his bar mitzvah on Monday, Tamuz 5653, with Chasidim convening from throughout Russia.
Story: On Monday, Tamuz 5653 (June 26, 1893), Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn celebrated his bar mitzvah in Lubavitch. He woke at 6:00 a.m., immersed in the mikveh, and prayed at the gravesites of his ancestors before reciting two of three maamarim he had memorized. The weeklong celebration drew Chasidim from throughout Russia, with the third maamar revealed only privately on the following Shabbat to a select group. His father blessed him that 'You should never be fearful of anything.'
Tags: lubavitch, russia, bar mitzvah, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, rashab, maamar

Title: R' Eliezerov writes blessing letter to new Hebron rabbi
Summary: R' Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov (Shil"a) sent a blessing letter to R' DovBer Efrat on 15 Av 1893 from his shadar journey.
Story: On 15 Av 1893 (ט"ו רחמים תרנ"ג), while serving as a shadar abroad, R' Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov (Shil"a) wrote a heartfelt blessing letter to R' DovBer Efrat congratulating him on his appointment as rabbi of Hebron. The letter wished him strength to lead with justice and uprightness.
Tags: dovber efrat, shlomo yehuda leib eliezerov, hebron, shadar, rabbinate

Title: R' Yehuda Leib Slonim, Kollel Chabad administrator, dies
Summary: R' Yehuda Leib Slonim, principal administrator of Kollel Chabad in Hebron, passed away on 27 Tammuz 5653—just weeks after R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin.
Story: R' Yehuda Leib Slonim, who together with his brothers R' Levi Yitzchak and R' Mordechai Dovber managed Kollel Chabad's affairs in Hebron, traveled repeatedly to Lubavitch to coordinate funds and policy with successive rebbes. His passing on 27 Tammuz 5653, weeks after Hebron's chief rav, marked the end of an era for the community.
Tags: hebron, lubavitch, yehuda leib slonim, kollel chabad, slonim family

Title: Rosenbaum moves from Berlin to Koenigsberg
Summary: In summer 5653 Rosenbaum relocates from Berlin to Koenigsberg, where he weighs and rejects emigrating to America.
Story: By 4 Parshas Tavo 5653 (1893) Rosenbaum was writing from Koenigsberg to R. Ze'ev Wolf and R. Chaim Gershon Kugel about the hardships of resettling in Berlin and then Koenigsberg. He recounts a long reply he received from R. Chaim Yaakov Widerewitz – chief rabbi of the Sephardic Congregation in America, who had emigrated in 5652 – warning that America was good for the strong but harsh for refined and delicate people. Identifying himself with the latter, Rosenbaum decided for the time being not to cross the ocean.
Tags: germany, berlin, koenigsberg, emigration, america

Title: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark passes away in Nevel
Summary: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark, rabbi of Nevel, passed away on 28 Menachem Av 5653.
Story: After serving in Horki, Starodub, Vitebsk, and finally Nevel, R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark passed away on 28 Av 5653. His son R' Yechezkel Feivel succeeded him in the Nevel rabbinate, and his grandson R' Avraham Yaakov Neumark later published Eshel Avraham.
Tags: meshulam zalman neumark, nevel, yechezkel feivel, chabad

Title: Rabbi Zalman Neimark of Nevel dies
Summary: Rabbi Zalman Neimark, rabbi of Nevel, died on 28 Menachem Av 5653, and was succeeded by his son Rabbi Yechezkel Feivel.
Story: After serving as rabbi of Nevel from 5648 onward, Rabbi Zalman Neimark died on 28 Menachem Av 5653 (10 August 1893), as recorded in the introduction to Eshel Avraham. His son, Rabbi Yechezkel Feivel, took his place as rabbi of Nevel.
Tags: nevel, rabbi zalman neimark, rabbi yechezkel feivel

Title: Rosenbaum writes from Königsberg about why he avoids emigrating to America
Summary: On Wednesday of Parshat Ki Tavo 5653 Rosenbaum told the Kugel brothers that R' Chaim Yaakov Widerewitz had warned him from New York that America suited only strong workers, not delicate scholars.
Story: Writing from Königsberg in Parshat Ki Tavo 5653 to R' Zev Wolf and R' Chaim Gershon Kugel, Reb Avraham Chaim quoted at length a letter he had received on 16 Iyar from R' Chaim Yaakov Widerewitz, rabbi of the Sephardic association in America. Widerewitz advised that any family with three or four strong working hands would find livelihood, but 'soft and delicate people' would suffer terribly. Knowing himself to be of the second type, Rosenbaum reluctantly resolved not to cross the ocean.
Tags: germany, konigsberg, america, widerewitz

Title: Czar Alexander III dies; Nicholas II ascends Russian throne
Summary: Alexander III died and was succeeded by his son Nicholas II, who continued and intensified anti-Jewish policies.
Story: Nicholas II would be the last czar of Russia, ruling until his abdication and execution in 1917. He blamed Jews for Russia's problems in personal letters and presided over a period of severe pogroms and repression of Russian Jewry.
Tags: russia, czar, nicholas ii, alexander iii

Title: Death of Czar Alexander III
Summary: Czar Alexander III died and was succeeded by his son Nicholas II, the last Russian czar.
Story: In 1894, Alexander III died after thirteen years of repressive rule. His son Nicholas II succeeded him and continued the anti-Jewish policies of his predecessors, blaming Jews for Russia's troubles and presiding over both the Beilis trial and the eventual collapse of the Romanov dynasty.
Tags: alexander iii, nicholas ii, russia, czar

Title: Death of Rabbi Nachum Dov Twersky of Ovrutch
Summary: Rabbi Nachum Dov of Ovrutch ('Maharanad'), brother-in-law of the Rebbe Rashab, passes away in 5654.
Story: Rabbi Nachum Dov Twersky of Ovrutch, son of Rabbi Yitzchak Yosef of Ovrutch and brother-in-law of the Rebbe Rashab of Lubavitch, died in 5654. Surviving correspondence with chasidim such as Reb Yaakov Ayerov of Kovel includes a letter pleading on behalf of a man whose only son had been taken — likely conscripted into the Russian army.
Tags: ovrutch, twersky, rashab, ukraine

Title: Fifth Rabbinical Commission convenes in Petersburg
Summary: The Fifth Rabbinical Commission convened in Petersburg in the winter of 1894 and agreed to require religious rabbis to hold secular education certificates.
Story: Chaired by Rabbi Tzvi Hirsch Rabinowitz of Kovno, son of Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan Spektor, the commission accepted a proposal that religious rabbis also be required to obtain secular education certification (tzenz) to manage civil registers. The decision was made without consulting other leading rabbis of the generation, and the Rebbe Rashab only learned of it about three years later, prompting his sustained opposition.
Tags: russia, petersburg, rabbinical commission, rabbi tzvi hirsch rabinowitz, kovno

Title: R' Isser Yanovsky appointed rabbi of Krivoy Rog
Summary: R' Isser Yanovsky was appointed rabbi of Krivoy Rog in Kherson province around 5654/5.
Story: Around 5654/5, R' Isser Yanovsky was appointed rabbi of the town of Krivoy Rog in Kherson province, not far from Nikolayev. Rashab's letter of 23 Marcheshvan 5655 references his receipt of letters from both Kremenchug and Krivoy Rog, apparently related to this appointment.
Tags: krivoy-rog, kherson, yanovsky, rabbinate

Title: R' Yosef Eliezer Friedman appointed rabbi of Hadiach
Summary: Rabbi Yosef Eliezer Friedman was appointed rabbi of Hadiach in 5654, after R' Isser Yanovsky's candidacy did not materialize.
Story: In 5654, Rabbi Yosef Eliezer Friedman became rabbi of Hadiach, the city associated with the burial place of the Alter Rebbe. The post had been considered for R' Isser Yanovsky two years earlier, when Rashab wrote on 15 Adar 5652 endorsing such an appointment, but that arrangement never came to fruition.
Tags: hadiach, rabbinate, friedman

Title: Rashab gathers group of bachurim as 'yoshvim'
Summary: In 5654 the Rebbe Rashab gathered 16-17 young men as 'yoshvim' in Lubavitch, the seed that would become Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: In 5654 (1894), the Rebbe Rashab refused requests from Baron Ginzburg and Chovevei Tzion, and instead gathered a group of 16-17 bachurim, sons of chassidic balebatim, who came to Lubavitch as 'yoshvim' to study. This group became the foundation of Tomchei Tmimim, which the Rebbe saw as a vessel that would withstand both the Haskalah and Zionist movements.
Tags: yoshvim, lubavitch, rashab, baron ginzburg

Title: Rashab seeks to print Choshen Mishpat responsa
Summary: In 5654 the Rebbe Rashab wrote to his mechutan Rabbi Meshulam Reich about printing an additional volume of Tzemach Tzedek responsa that would include the censored Choshen Mishpat material.
Story: The Choshen Mishpat responsa had been blocked by Russian censors decades earlier. In 5654 the Rashab attempted to revive the project, corresponding with his mechutan about publication, but the effort did not come to fruition. Further attempts followed in 5660 and 5668, with the Rashab noting in the latter year that the volume was 'already arranged and copied, ready for printing' — yet still it did not appear.
Tags: rashab, tzemach tzedek, choshen mishpat, censorship

Title: Rebbe Rashab formally accepts Chabad leadership
Summary: Rebbe Rashab formally assumed the Chabad leadership in 5654.
Story: Although he had been delivering discourses since 1883, Rebbe Rashab only officially accepted the Chabad leadership in 1894. Throughout his tenure he was unable to publish Chassidic books in Russia, due to Tsarist censorship; his discourses circulated in handwritten and mimeographed copies.
Tags: rebbe rashab, lubavitch, nesius

Title: Passing of R' Chaim Shmuel Shmerling in Jaffa
Summary: R' Chaim Shmuel Shmerling, founder of the Chabad settlement in Jaffa, passed away on 20 Adar I 5654 in Jaffa and was buried in Jerusalem.
Story: R' Chaim Shmuel Shmerling passed away in Jaffa on 20 Adar I 5654 and was buried in Jerusalem. Twenty-eight years after founding the Jaffa Chabad community in 5626, his death marked the end of his role in extending the family's pioneering legacy across the Chabad settlements of Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: chaim shmuel shmerling, jaffa, jerusalem burial, chabad settlement

Title: R' Chaim Shmuel Schmerling passes away in Jaffa
Summary: Founder of Jaffa's Ashkenazi institutions, R' Chaim Shmuel Schmerling died there on 2 Adar 5654.
Story: After nearly three decades building communal life in Jaffa, R' Chaim Shmuel Schmerling passed away on 2 Adar 5654 (February 1894). His biography appears in the Schmerling pamphlet (Tidhar, Tel Aviv 5706) and in Toldos Mishpachas HaRav MiLadi p. 76.
Tags: jaffa, schmerling

Title: Birth of R' Yochanan Gordon in Dokshitz
Summary: R' Yochanan Gordon, who would later serve for many years as the gabbai of 770, was born on 23 Iyar 5654 in Dokshitz to R' Yisrael and Esther.
Story: R' Yochanan Gordon, future longtime gabbai of 770 Eastern Parkway, was born in the town of Dokshitz to his father R' Yisrael and mother Esther. He recorded his birthdate of 23 Iyar 5654 himself on a 'Sefer HaChassidim' registration card filled out 17 Tevet 5723. He would go on to study at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch and become a central figure in Chabad communal life in America.
Tags: dokshitz, yochanan gordon, russia, biography

Title: Letter of Rabbi Menachem Nachum of Tolna for a blind chasid
Summary: The Tolna Rebbe writes to Rabbi Avraham Yechezkel Orlozarov of Kharkov on behalf of Tzvi Surkes, who lost his sight.
Story: Dated Thursday of Parashat Chayei Sarah 5655 in Tolna, the letter introduces Tzvi Surkes — a man who had always supported himself by his own labor until suddenly going blind. The Tolna Rebbe asks Rabbi Orlozarov, a chasid of the Rebbe Rashab, to help Surkes both financially and in securing a consultation with a professor in Kharkov.
Tags: tolna, chernobyl, kharkov, medical, letter-of-recommendation, rashab

Title: Rosenbaum family arrives in New York on the SS Moravia
Summary: On 13 Kislev 5655 / 11 December 1894 Reb Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum, his wife Yetta and sons Zalman and Yosef reached New York on the ship Moravia from Hamburg.
Story: Having finally decided to emigrate, the Rosenbaum family sailed from Hamburg and arrived at the port of New York on 11 December 1894 aboard the SS Moravia. The passenger manifest recorded Abraham (54), Yetta (53), Solomon (21) and Joseph (11). In New York he would settle, deal in diamonds and jewelry at 444 Grand Street, and gather chassidim around him.
Tags: america, new york, immigration, hamburg, rosenbaum

Title: Akedah ceremony at Lubavitch Ohel
Summary: On Yosef Yitzchak's fifteenth birthday, the Rashab brought him to the Ohel and inducted him as a Jewish leader.
Story: On the Rayatz's fifteenth birthday in 1895, the Rashab brought him to the Ohel in Lubavitch and declared he was bringing his son to the akedah, drawing on the biblical binding of Yitzchak. Standing before the open ark, the Rashab transferred to his son the sacred task of working for the public good, recounted 140 years of Lubavitcher Rebbes' communal work, and inducted him as a Jewish leader. From that day, the Rayatz stood by his father's side as his personal secretary and confidant.
Tags: lubavitch, russia, akedah, rashab, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, ohel, communal work

Title: Death of Rabbi Yochanan Twersky of Rachmistrivka
Summary: Rabbi Yochanan of Rachmistrivka, son of Rabbi Mordechai of Chernobyl, passes away in 5655.
Story: Rabbi Yochanan of Rachmistrivka died in 5655. After his death, his son Rabbi David of Zlatopol no longer signed letters as 'son of the master, may he live,' a change that allows researchers to date a surviving emissary-letter of his to before 5655.
Tags: rachmistrivka, twersky, ukraine

Title: R' Dovber Efrat takes over Hebron Chabad leadership
Summary: Around 5655, R' Dovber Efrat arrived in Hebron, became rabbi of the Chabad community, and took over kollel administration.
Story: Following the deaths of R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, R' Yehuda Leib Slonim, and R' Levi Yitzchak Slonim, R' Dovber Efrat was appointed rabbi of Hebron Chabad and took over the kollel administration. He was joined by R' Mordechai Dovber Slonim and R' Binyamin Rivlin in leading the community.
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, dovber efrat, mordechai dovber slonim, binyamin rivlin

Title: R' Levi Yitzchak Slonim dies
Summary: R' Levi Yitzchak Slonim, the dominant figure in Hebron Chabad administration, died in 5655.
Story: He had managed all affairs of Kollel Chabad in Hebron and was considered the de facto head of the community. According to family history, 'nothing was done in Hebron without him during all his days.' His death cleared the way for new leadership under R' Dovber Efrat.
Tags: hebron, kollel chabad, levi yitzchak slonim

Title: R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov arrives in Lubavitch to study
Summary: R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov of Lazovich arrived in Lubavitch in 5655 to learn as one of the 'yoshvim' before Tomchei Tmimim was founded.
Story: Born in Lazovich near Klimovich, R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov came to Lubavitch in 5655 to study. Tomchei Tmimim had not yet been founded, so he learned for two to three years among the 'yoshvim' under the mashpia R. Chanoch Hendel Kugel. He later married into the Horowitz family and settled in Warsaw.
Tags: lubavitch, yoshvim, shraga feivish zalmanov, chanoch hendel kugel

Title: Rashab summers in Bolivke with his son
Summary: The Rashab began six summers of intensive mentorship with his son Yosef Yitzchak in Bolivke beginning in summer 1895.
Story: In the summer of 1895, the Rashab traveled with his wife to the resort town of Bolivke, forty-five miles from Lubavitch. While the official reason was his weakened health, the true motive was to spend time mentoring his son. For six years until 1901, the Rashab took the Rayatz on two-hour daily walks, studying Talmud and chasidic maamarim, sharing personal stories, and preparing him for future leadership.
Tags: bolivke, russia, rashab, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, education, mentorship

Title: Rayatz begins communal work as his father's personal secretary
Summary: At age 15, Yosef Yitzchak began his communal career serving as personal secretary to his father, the Rashab.
Story: This early role gave him intimate access to the affairs of the Chabad movement and prepared him for decades of communal leadership. He would handle correspondence, organizational matters, and represent his father in increasingly significant roles.
Tags: yosef yitzchak schneersohn, rashab, lubavitch

Title: Rayatz represents father at Kovno rabbinic conference
Summary: At age fifteen, the Rayatz represented his father the Rashab at a conference of Jewish religious leaders in Kovno.
Story: In 1895, at just fifteen years old, the Rayatz attended a conference of Jewish religious leaders in Kovno on behalf of his father, the Rebbe Rashab. He simultaneously began serving as the Rashab's private secretary, a role he would hold for 25 years.
Tags: rayatz, kovno, rabbinic conference, leadership

Title: Rayatz represents father at rabbinic conference in Kovno
Summary: At age fifteen, the Rayatz represented the Rashab at a conference of Jewish religious leaders in Kovno.
Story: This was the Rayatz's first major communal role. He formally became active in community affairs that year and began serving as his father's private secretary, a role he would hold for the next twenty-five years until the Rashab's passing in 1920.
Tags: rayatz, kovno, rabbinic conference

Title: Reb Shraga Feivish Zalmanov arrives in Lubavitch
Summary: R' Shraga Feivish Zalmanov first came to study in Lubavitch in 5655, between Pesach and Shavuot.
Story: In 5655 (1895), between Pesach and Shavuot, R' Shraga Feivish Zalmanov arrived in Lubavitch to study among the 'yoshvim'. He later recorded his memories of that period, describing how R' Chanoch Hendel would teach Tanya daily between Mincha and Maariv to the young men. The Rebbe Rayatz mentioned his arrival in Sefer HaSichot 5702.
Tags: yoshvim, lubavitch, zalmanov

Title: Passing of R' Yosef Yehuda Shmerling in Jerusalem
Summary: R' Yosef Yehuda Shmerling, 'firstborn' grandson of R' Shimon Shmerling and signatory of the 5604 Pekoam letter as 'trustee of the kollel,' passed away in Jerusalem on 2 Elul 5655.
Story: R' Yosef Yehuda Shmerling, born around 5581 at the time of his family's immigration to Eretz Yisrael, was known as 'Yosef Yehuda the firstborn.' He signed the 5604 letter to the Pekidim VeAmarkalim as 'trustee of the kollel.' He passed away in Jerusalem on 2 Elul 5655, continuing the Shmerling family's central role in the Chabad settlement of the Holy Land.
Tags: yosef yehuda shmerling, jerusalem, hebron, kollel chabad

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter mentions books still stored in sacks
Summary: On 19 Menachem Av 5655, Rebbe Rashab wrote that 'in my home the books are lying in sacks,' suggesting recent division but not yet shelved.
Story: This letter (Igros #64) indicates that the division of inherited books from Rebbe Maharash's estate had likely occurred during 5655, but the Rebbe had not yet built cabinets and shelved them. The systematic library organization would begin in earnest by 5660.
Tags: rashab, books, lubavitch, letters

Title: Death of R. Shaul Chevroni (Saulson ancestor)
Summary: R. Shaul b. R. Yaakov Mordechai Chevroni died on erev Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan 5656 (Oct 17, 1895) and was buried on the Mount of Olives.
Story: His descendants would adopt the surname Saulson, which would become a well-known family in Hebron and beyond. His death notice is preserved in 'Avnei Zikaron' alongside other members of the Twer family.
Tags: shaul chevroni, saulson, hebron, mount of olives, burial

Title: R' Shaul Ashkenazi dies in Jerusalem
Summary: R' Shaul ben Yaakov Mordechai Chevroni (Brimt/Shaulzon) died on Erev Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan 5656 in Jerusalem.
Story: Born in 5583 in Mohilev, R' Shaul made aliyah with his family in 5592. He taught Tanach and Gemara in Jerusalem according to the 5615 census, returned to Hebron in 5626 to join the kollel leadership, served on R' Shimon Menashe's beit din, and eventually returned to Jerusalem where he is buried. His descendants adopted the surname Shaulzon.
Tags: jerusalem, hebron, shaul ashkenazi, shaulzon, brimt

Title: Author's birth in Zhuravichi
Summary: Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson, author of the memoirs, was born on 3 Kislev in Zhuravichi.
Story: Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson was born on 3 Kislev 5656 (corresponding to 1895) in the town of Zhuravichi to his father Reb Yaakov Leib. He descended from four generations of shochtim in Zhuravichi. The family traced its lineage to the Shlah HaKadosh through nine generations.
Tags: zhuravichi, birth, jacobson family

Title: First printing of the Tzemach Tzedek's portrait in Vilna
Summary: The Tzemach Tzedek's portrait was first printed in Vilna in 5656 with Hebrew and Russian captions.
Story: A printed portrait of the third Lubavitcher Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek, was issued in Vilna in 5656 (1896) with bilingual Hebrew-Russian text beneath. The image is preserved in the Lubavitch Library and exhibited alongside other portraits of the Rebbeim.
Tags: vilna, tzemach tzedek, portrait

Title: Rabbi Dovid Meir Rabinowitz immigrates to United States
Summary: Rabbi Dovid Meir Rabinowitz, a devoted Chabad chasid, immigrated to the United States in 1896 and settled in Boston.
Story: Rabinowitz pioneered traditional Judaism and Jewish education in Boston. In 1927, his daughter received a two-word telegram from the Rebbe's family — 'Tatte arestirt' — and he dispatched his sons Asher and Peretz to Washington, where they enlisted Justice Louis Brandeis to lobby on the Rebbe's behalf.
Tags: boston, america, immigration, rabinowitz

Title: Rabbinic conference in Vilna with Rayatz representing father
Summary: The Rayatz again represented the Rashab at a conference of Jewish religious leaders, this time in Vilna.
Story: Following his first conference in Kovno the previous year, the sixteen-year-old Rayatz attended this Vilna gathering. These meetings began his lifetime involvement with Europe's leading rabbinic figures and prepared him for his later leadership role in Russian Jewish communal affairs.
Tags: rayatz, vilna, rabbinic conference

Title: Rashab seeks medical care in Moscow
Summary: Gravely ill, the Rashab traveled to Moscow for medical care and considered relocating to Eretz Yisrael.
Story: In 1896, the Rashab was gravely ill and traveled with his wife to Moscow for medical care. Doctors gave him a bleak prognosis of just months to live. He suggested to his wife they travel to Eretz Yisrael to spend his last days there, saying their sixteen-year-old son could lead Chabad in his place. Rebbetzin Shterna Sara prevailed on him to remain in Lubavitch, and he ultimately recovered, living another twenty-four years.
Tags: moscow, russia, rashab, illness, shterna sara

Title: Rashab visits ancestral gravesites before founding yeshivah
Summary: The Rashab traveled to the gravesites of the Baal Shem Tov, the Maggid, the Alter Rebbe and the Mitteler Rebbe to pray for guidance.
Story: Pained by the spiritual condition of Russian Jewry, the Rashab visited the gravesites in Mezibuzh, Anipoli, Hadyach, and Nizhyn. Upon returning to Lubavitch he also prayed at the gravesites of his grandfather the Tzemach Tzedek and his father the Maharash. With their blessing, he established the yeshivah the following year.
Tags: rashab, baal shem tov, maggid of mezeritch, alter rebbe, mitteler rebbe, ohel

Title: Rashab visits gravesites of chasidic forebears
Summary: Rashab visited the gravesites of the Baal Shem Tov, the Maggid, the Alter Rebbe, and the Mitteler Rebbe.
Story: In the summer of 1896, troubled by the spiritual state of Russian Jewry, the Rashab traveled to Mezibuzh, Anipoli, Hadyach, and Nizhyn to pray at the graves of the Baal Shem Tov, the Maggid of Mezeritch, the Alter Rebbe, and the Mitteler Rebbe. Upon his return he prayed at the graves of his grandfather and father before establishing Tomchei Temimim.
Tags: rashab, graves, baal shem tov, maggid, alter rebbe, mitteler rebbe

Title: Rayatz attends Vilna rabbinic conference
Summary: The Rayatz again represented his father at a conference of Jewish religious leaders, this time in Vilna.
Story: Following his 1895 appearance in Kovno, the Rayatz traveled to Vilna in 1896 to once more represent the Rashab at a gathering of Jewish religious leaders, deepening his early immersion in Russian Jewish communal affairs.
Tags: rayatz, vilna, rabbinic conference

Title: Siddur Im Shaar HaKollel edition published in Vilna
Summary: A reworked Chabad siddur edition with Shaar HaKollel was published in Vilna in 5656 (1896).
Story: This 1896 Vilna printing reorganized Rabbi Lavut's earlier edition and added Shaar HaKollel, becoming a long-influential template for subsequent Chabad siddur printings.
Tags: alter rebbe, vilna, siddur, shaar hakollel

Title: Yeshivas Rabbeinu Yitzchok Elchonon founded
Summary: The yeshivah that would later become Yeshiva University was founded on New York's Lower East Side.
Story: Initially based on the Lower East Side, the institution became Yeshivah College in 1928 and later Yeshivah University. At the time of the Rebbe Rayatz's 1929 visit, it had recently relocated to Washington Heights and was one of only a handful of Jewish schools in New York.
Tags: yeshiva, united-states, new-york, rietz

Title: Engagement of Rayatz to Nechama Dina in Bolivke
Summary: The Rayatz became engaged to his second cousin Nechama Dina Schneersohn in Bolivke, where the family was spending the summer.
Story: The Rashab and his wife had chosen Nechama Dina over wealthier candidates with large dowries, following the Rayatz's preference for marrying a relative. The tena'im was signed on 28 Sivan 5646 in Bolivke. The Rebbe Rashab undertook all wedding expenses since the bride's family had limited means, and the celebration lasted a week.
Tags: rayatz, nechama dina, bolivke, engagement, schneersohn family

Title: Rayatz becomes engaged in Bolivke
Summary: The Rayatz signed engagement contracts with Nechama Dina Schneersohn in Bolivke.
Story: On 28 Sivan 5656 (June 9, 1896), the tena'im were signed in Bolivke, formally engaging the Rayatz to Nechama Dina. The Rebbe Rashab took on all wedding expenses despite his family's limited means, having chosen Nechama Dina over wealthier matches with large dowries.
Tags: rayatz, nechama dina, bolivke, engagement, tenaim

Title: Shterna Sara writes cousins about Rayatz's bride and wedding delay
Summary: Rebbetzin Shterna Sara wrote her cousins in Hebron describing the chosen bride and explaining the wedding was deferred a year.
Story: Writing on 1 Elul 5646 to Rabbi Mordechai Dovber and Rabbi Schneur Zalman Schneersohn in Hebron, Shterna Sara praised Nechama Dina as 'charming and very observant' and explained that the family had given up major financial benefits to select the most proper young woman. She requested they pray for the family at the holy places before Rosh HaShanah.
Tags: shterna sara, rayatz, nechama dina, hebron, eretz yisrael

Title: Shterna Sara writes to family in Eretz Yisrael
Summary: Rebbetzin Shterna Sara wrote to her Hebron cousins about the choice of Nechama Dina as the Rayatz's bride.
Story: On 1 Elul 5656 (September 1, 1896), Rebbetzin Shterna Sara wrote to Rabbi Mordechai Dovber and Rabbi Schneur Zalman Schneersohn in Hebron, explaining that Nechama Dina was chosen for her piety despite the family forgoing significant dowry offers. She also asked them to pray for the family at the holy gravesites before Rosh HaShanah.
Tags: shterna sara, letter, hebron, nechama dina

Title: Enlightenment activist Mordechai Ben Hillel scouts Lubavitch for a school
Summary: Enlightenment activist Mordechai Ben Hillel scouted Lubavitch to explore opening a secular school targeting the chasidic stronghold.
Story: Ben Hillel reported that Lubavitch was visited by thousands annually and that establishing a school there would influence all of Russian Jewry. With the support of Baron Gunzburg, the school opened with 130 students despite the Rashab's strong opposition. The Rashab would later lament Gunzburg's support at a major farbrengen.
Tags: haskalah, lubavitch, mordechai ben hillel, chevrah mefitzei haskalah

Title: Founding of Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lubavitch
Summary: Rashab founded the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lubavitch in summer 5657.
Story: In the summer of 5657, Rashab established the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lubavitch. The yeshiva initially operated in various rooms of the Rebbe's courtyard. It would continue operating in Lubavitch for over twenty years before relocating during World War I.
Tags: tomchei-tmimim, yeshiva, lubavitch, rashab

Title: Knesses Beis Yitzchak yeshivah founded in Slabodka
Summary: Opponents of musar study founded Knesses Beis Yitzchak as a rival to Slabodka's musar yeshivah.
Story: A major controversy erupted in Slabodka between those who argued that study should focus exclusively on Talmud and those who supported teaching ethics through musar. Those opposed to musar opened Knesses Beis Yitzchak in 1897. In 1904 they hired Rabbi Baruch Ber Leibowitz as rosh yeshivah.
Tags: slabodka, knesses beis yitzchak, musar controversy, lithuanian yeshivah

Title: Knesses Beis Yitzchak yeshivah opens in Slabodka
Summary: Opponents of the Musar movement opened Knesses Beis Yitzchak yeshivah in Slabodka.
Story: In 1897, scholars who objected to the systematic study of musar at Slabodka opened a rival yeshivah called Knesses Beis Yitzchak. The split reflected an ongoing controversy in Lithuanian yeshivas over whether ethics study should be integrated alongside Talmud.
Tags: slabodka, musar, knesses beis yitzchak, lithuania

Title: Louis Lamm receives the Dr. Baer estate of calendars
Summary: After the death of grammarian Dr. Seligman Isaac Baer in 5657, his book-bound estate of calendars passed to Louis Lamm.
Story: Dr. Seligman Isaac Baer of Biebrich, the renowned masoretic scholar, died in 5657 (1897). Following his death, his bound estate of calendars came into the possession of Louis Lamm of Amsterdam. Part of the Chabad library's collection of ancient calendars — over a thousand items in some four hundred varieties — traces back to this Baer estate via Lamm.
Tags: louis lamm, seligman baer, biebrich, calendars, masorah

Title: R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov marries and settles in Warsaw
Summary: Around 5657, R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov married Tzirla, daughter of R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz, and joined his father-in-law in Warsaw.
Story: After studying for several years in Lubavitch, R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov married Tzirla, daughter of R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz, around 5657. The couple settled with the bride's father in Warsaw, where R. Shraga Feivish would later become one of the central leaders of the Chabad community.
Tags: warsaw, marriage, shraga feivish zalmanov, horowitz family

Title: Rebbe Rashab founds Tomchei Temimim Yeshiva
Summary: In 5657 the Rebbe Rashab founded the Tomchei Temimim Lubavitch yeshiva.
Story: In the year 5657 (1897), Rabbi Sholom Dovber Schneersohn (the Rebbe Rashab) founded the yeshiva 'Tomchei Temimim Lubavitch.' Over subsequent years it expanded to dozens of branches across Russia, operating openly at first and then underground after Soviet persecution intensified. The yeshiva became the backbone of Chabad's educational network in Russia.
Tags: tomchei temimim, lubavitch, russia, yeshiva

Title: Rebbe Rashab founds Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim in Lubavitch
Summary: Rabbi Sholom DovBer Schneersohn opens the first chasidic yeshivah, revolutionizing Jewish education.
Story: Yehuda Geberer notes Chabad took the lead in this arena: 'The first who did this was the Rebbe Rashab with the opening of Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim in 1897.' With time, other chasidic groups followed Chabad's lead, establishing their own yeshivas. The seventh Rebbe identified the founding as a major stage in the dissemination of chasidic teachings.
Tags: tomchei temimim, lubavitch, rashab, yeshivah, chasidut

Title: Rebbe Rashab learns of Fifth Commission's decisions
Summary: In 1897 the Rebbe Rashab learned of the Fifth Rabbinical Commission's decision and began years of intense efforts against it.
Story: About three years after the Petersburg commission, the Rebbe became aware that participating rabbis had agreed to require state educational certificates for religious rabbis. He launched a sustained multi-year campaign to prevent the change, arguing that young rabbis with secular certification would be susceptible to heresy and would do more harm than the existing Crown Rabbis.
Tags: russia, rabbi sholom dovber, tzenz, rabbanut mitaam

Title: Rebbe Rashab opens letter campaign to youth
Summary: Before founding the yeshiva in 5657, the Rebbe Rashab issued a general letter to young men and their parents about conduct and study.
Story: In 5657, prior to founding Tomchei Tmimim, the Rebbe Rashab turned to youth and parents in a general letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. 1, letter 68) regarding their conduct and studies. He also waged battle against schools being established by the Society for the Diffusion of Enlightenment and by the ICA. This concern for the next generation motivated the founding of the yeshiva.
Tags: rashab, youth, haskalah, jewish education

Title: Tomchei Temimim founded in Lubavitch
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab established the Tomchei Temimim yeshivah in Lubavitch, beginning with a small group of outstanding students.
Story: Elchonon Morozov was among the first students. He was chosen as the personal study partner for the Rashab's son, the future Rayatz, and later joined the yeshivah faculty before becoming the Rebbe's secretary.
Tags: tomchei-temimim, lubavitch, morozov

Title: Tomchei Temimim moves to Zembin
Summary: After the High Holidays, Tomchei Temimim's students and their mashpia relocated from Lubavitch to Zembin.
Story: Following the Tishrei holidays of 1897, the original cohort of Tomchei Temimim students relocated with Rabbi Shmuel Gronem to Zembin, a small town some 160 miles west of Lubavitch. The smaller setting reduced distractions, and over the year the original group grew to eighteen students.
Tags: zembin, tomchei temimim, belorussia, relocation

Title: Tomchei Temimim opens; Yosef Yitzchak appointed director
Summary: Following his wedding, the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva opened in Lubavitch and the future Rayatz was appointed as its director.
Story: Shortly after his wedding, the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva was opened in Lubavitch under his father the Rebbe Rashab, and the future Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak was appointed to serve as its director. The yeshiva offices occupied the front of his new residence facing the courtyard. This appointment launched his lifelong leadership of Chabad's educational network.
Tags: tomchei temimim, lubavitch, rayatz, yeshiva

Title: Tomchei Temimim yeshivah founded in Lubavitch
Summary: The Rashab established the flagship Chabad yeshivah with a small select group of outstanding scholars.
Story: Among the first students chosen was Elchonon Morozov, born 1877, who excelled to the point that the Rashab selected him as the personal study partner for his son the Rayatz. Tomchei Temimim was a revolutionary accomplishment close to the Rashab's heart — both the key to continuity of chasidic teachings and an incubator for new Jewish leadership. It would remain the last bastion of Jewish scholarship functioning in the Soviet Union.
Tags: tomchei temimim, lubavitch, rashab, morozov

Title: Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva founded
Summary: The Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was founded in Lubavitch.
Story: In the year 5657 (1897), the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was established in Lubavitch by the Rebbe Rashab. The 40th anniversary of this founding would later be marked in 1937 with a special issue of HaTamim dedicated to the history of the yeshiva.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, yeshiva founding

Title: Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva founded in Lubavitch
Summary: Tomchei Tmimim was founded in Lubavitch in 5657, soon developing departments for younger bachurim and for advanced avreichim training to be poskim.
Story: Established by the Rebbe Rashab, Tomchei Tmimim quickly gathered cohorts of select bachurim and provided their full upkeep, including clothing and footwear for poor students. A later department for outstanding avreichim — men close to receiving semicha for hora'ah — was added, with the institution also covering their families' needs. Letters of support from the rabbis of Nikolaev, including the Rebbe's maternal grandfather R' Meir Shlomo Yanovsky, were solicited as enrollment grew and resources tightened.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, rashab, yeshiva, founding

Title: Wedding of Rebbe Rayatz and founding of Tomchei Temimim
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz married and was appointed director of the newly founded Tomchei Temimim yeshiva.
Story: At the end of 5657 (1897), the wedding of the Rebbe Rayatz took place in the great hall of the Rebbes' courtyard in Lubavitch. Immediately after the wedding, the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva was founded, and he was appointed as its director. After the wedding, an additional room was built onto his father's house for his residence.
Tags: wedding, lubavitch, tomchei temimim, yeshiva, rebbe rayatz

Title: Wedding of the Frierdiker Rebbe in Lubavitch
Summary: The wedding of the future Frierdiker Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was celebrated in the great hall of the Lubavitch courtyard in the summer of 5657.
Story: This wedding coincided with the founding of Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in the same summer. The great hall again served as the venue for one of the dynasty's central family events. Together, the founding of the yeshiva and the marriage of the heir-apparent made the summer of 5657 a pivotal moment in Lubavitch history.
Tags: frierdiker-rebbe, wedding, yosef-yitzchak

Title: Wedding of the future Rayatz in Lubavitch
Summary: At the end of 5657, the wedding of the future Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak was held in the great hall of the Lubavitch courtyard.
Story: At the end of 5657 (1897), the wedding of the future Rayatz was celebrated in the great hall of the courtyard of the Rebbes in Lubavitch. After the wedding an additional room was built onto his father's house for the couple, and he later moved into the adjacent house in the southwestern corner of the courtyard.
Tags: rayatz, lubavitch, wedding

Title: Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim founded by Rebbe Rashab
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab establishes the first chasidic yeshivah, a revolutionary institution other chasidic groups would later emulate.
Story: Historian Yehuda Geberer notes this was Chabad's leading response to 'the great crisis' — declining chasidic numbers in the interwar years. The yeshivah balanced talmudic study with chasidic philosophy, creating the model later expanded by the Rayatz across Poland and Lithuania.
Tags: lubavitch, rashab, tomchei-temimim, yeshivah

Title: Marriage of Yosef Yitzchak to Nechama Dina Schneersohn
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn married Nechama Dina Schneersohn on 13 Elul 5657.
Story: The union joined two branches of the Schneersohn family. Nechama Dina would stand by her husband through Soviet persecution, exile, and the eventual escape to America.
Tags: yosef yitzchak schneersohn, nechama dina, marriage

Title: Wedding of the Rebbe Rayatz to Rebbetzin Nechama Dina
Summary: The wedding of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn to Rebbetzin Nechama Dina was held in the Large Hall in Lubavitch in Elul 5657.
Story: Rayatz married Rebbetzin Nechama Dina in Elul 5657 (August/September 1897) in the Large Hall of his grandfather Maharash's Lubavitch courtyard. This was the third major family simcha hosted in that hall, after Maharash's daughter Chaya Mushka's wedding and Rayatz's own bar mitzvah in 5653.
Tags: rayatz, nechama-dina, lubavitch, wedding, ulam-hagadol, schneersohn

Title: Wedding of Rebbe Rayatz and Rebbetzin Nechama Dina
Summary: Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak married Rebbetzin Nechama Dina on 13 Elul 5657.
Story: On 13 Elul 5657, Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, son of Rebbe Rashab and the future sixth Rebbe of Lubavitch, married Nechama Dina, daughter of Rabbi Avraham Schneersohn of Kishinev. The date would later be commemorated annually with gifts and blessings exchanged between the couple. The anniversary became significant in Chabad lore and was marked publicly fifty years later in 5707.
Tags: rayatz, nechama-dina, wedding, 13-elul

Title: Wedding of the Rayatz and Nechama Dina in Lubavitch
Summary: The Rayatz and Nechama Dina were married in Lubavitch two weeks before Rosh HaShanah.
Story: Chasidim streamed to Lubavitch for the celebration. The Rayatz donned a shtreimel and recited Shehechiyanu before the ceremony. The chuppah was held Friday afternoon (13 Elul 5657) in the courtyard of the main synagogue, after which the crowd escorted the couple through town with singing and dancing.
Tags: rayatz, nechama dina, lubavitch, wedding, shtreimel

Title: Wedding of the Rayatz in Lubavitch
Summary: The Rayatz married Nechama Dina in Lubavitch on a Friday afternoon, two weeks before Rosh HaShanah.
Story: On 13 Elul 5657 (September 10, 1897), the Rayatz wed Nechama Dina in Lubavitch. The chuppah was held Friday afternoon in the courtyard of the main synagogue, with the Rayatz donning the customary Lubavitcher shtreimel. Chasidim streamed in from across Russia for the celebrations.
Tags: rayatz, nechama dina, wedding, lubavitch, shtreimel

Title: Founding meeting of Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim
Summary: The Rashab gathered fifty guests at the wedding reception and announced the founding of Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim.
Story: On 15 Elul 5657 (September 12, 1897), the day of the wedding reception, the Rashab unveiled his plan for a new yeshivah integrating Talmud with chasidic philosophy. Despite skepticism from many of the assembled rabbis and philanthropists, the Rebbe pressed forward, and this date became the official founding of Tomchei Temimim.
Tags: tomchei temimim, rashab, rayatz, lubavitch, yeshivah, founding

Title: Founding of Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva
Summary: The Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was founded on 15 Elul 5657 by the Rebbe Rashab, with branches in Lubavitch and Zembin.
Story: On 15 Elul 5657 (September 12, 1897), the Rebbe Rashab founded the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva, with R' Chanoch Hendel overseeing the Lubavitch branch and R' Shmuel Gronem Esterman overseeing the Zembin branch in Minsk province. The yeshiva was established to strengthen young men in Torah study and fear of Heaven amid growing Haskalah and Zionist movements. It became the central Chabad yeshiva network.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, zembin, rashab, yeshiva founding

Title: Rashab unveils plan for Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim
Summary: At a Sunday afternoon meeting of fifty distinguished wedding guests, the Rashab unveiled his plan for a revolutionary yeshivah integrating Talmud and Chasidic philosophy.
Story: Held the day of the Rayatz's wedding reception (15 Elul 5657), the Rashab announced his plan to 'open a yeshivah for our youth, with proper administration, so that they can dedicate themselves exclusively to Torah study.' Most attendees expressed serious reservations about the feasibility. The day of this meeting is considered the founding date of Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim.
Tags: rashab, tomchei temimim, lubavitch, founding, chasidic education

Title: Studies begin at Tomchei Temimim in Lubavitch
Summary: Tomchei Temimim opened its doors with Rabbi Shmuel Gronem as mashpia on the auspicious 18 Elul.
Story: Studies began on 18 Elul 5657 (September 15, 1897), the joint birthday of the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe. The Rashab personally selected the first students from among the yoshvim and appointed Rabbi Shmuel Gronem as the yeshivah's first mashpia, with detailed curriculum instructions.
Tags: tomchei temimim, shmuel gronem, 18 elul, baal shem tov, alter rebbe

Title: Tomchei Temimim begins studies in Lubavitch
Summary: On 18 Elul, birthday of both the Alter Rebbe and Baal Shem Tov, studies began in Lubavitch under mashpia Shmuel Gronem.
Story: The Rashab personally selected the first group of students, many of whom were already yoshvim studying informally in Lubavitch. Rabbi Shmuel Gronem was appointed mashpia with detailed instructions regarding curriculum. After the High Holidays the students relocated to Zembin, a smaller town with fewer distractions.
Tags: tomchei temimim, lubavitch, shmuel gronem, 18 elul, baal shem tov birthday

Title: Czech translation of the Haggadah by Dr. Gustav Weiner printed in Prague
Summary: Dr. Gustav Weiner's Czech translation of the Haggadah was printed in Prague.
Story: Around 5658 (1898), Dr. Gustav Weiner's translation of the Haggadah into Czech was published in Prague. The 79-page volume served the Czech-speaking Jewish community of Bohemia. It reflected the late 19th-century integration of Central European Jewry with the surrounding national languages.
Tags: haggadah, czech, prague, bohemia

Title: Eidah HaChareidis-precursor leadership transferred to Sonnenfeld
Summary: Upon Rabbi Yehuda Leib Diskind's passing, Rabbi Sonnenfeld became head of Jerusalem's Ashkenazi community.
Story: Sonnenfeld had worked closely with Diskind for years. His ascension positioned him to formalize the Eidah HaChareidis in 1921 and lead opposition to Zionist secularization.
Tags: sonnenfeld, jerusalem, ashkenazi-community

Title: Przemyśl Haggadah 'Bet HaYayin' by Meir Yehuda Libush Langerman of Turka
Summary: Meir Yehuda Libush Langerman of Turka published the Haggadah 'Bet HaYayin' incorporating teachings of Avraham Yaakov of Sadigura in Przemyśl.
Story: Around 5658 (1898), the Haggadah 'Sefer Bet HaYayin' by Meir Yehuda Libush Langerman, head of the rabbinical court of Turka, was issued in Przemyśl by Zupnik, Knoller, and Wolf. The 52-leaf quarto featured 'Likkutim Tilpiot' built largely on the teachings of Rebbe Avraham Yaakov of Sadigura. It represented the Sadigura-Ruzhin Chassidic tradition's interpretation of the Passover liturgy.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, sadigura, turka, przemysl, galicia

Title: R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum settles in the United States
Summary: In 5658 (1898), R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum arrived and settled in the United States.
Story: Five to six years after leaving Russia, R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum arrived in the United States in 5658 (1898), where he established his residence.
