He was among the earlier Chabad chassidim to take up permanent residence in America, well before the major waves of Chabad emigration that followed the Russian Revolution. He would live out the last fifteen years of his life there.
Tags: avraham chaim rosenbaum, united states, immigration, america

Title: RA"Ch immigrates with his family to the United States
Summary: In 5658 RA"Ch and his family settle in America, where he goes into the diamond and jewelry trade in New York.
Story: According to R' Dovid Shifrin's account, in 5658 RA"Ch arrived with his family in the United States and established himself as a dealer in diamonds and pearls at 444 Grand Street, 2nd floor, New York. His home became a gathering place for Torah scholars, and he maintained an ongoing correspondence with the Rebbe Rashab back in Russia.
Tags: immigration, new york, usa, diamonds, grand street, chabad in america

Title: Rashab names yeshivah 'Tomchei Temimim' on Simchat Torah
Summary: During Simchat Torah hakafot at approximately 4 a.m., the Rashab named the new yeshivah Tomchei Temimim.
Story: After dancing intensely around the bimah, the Rashab paused the singing and declared: 'The yeshivah that was established by the grace of G-d doesn't have a name. Now I am naming it Tomchei Temimim.' The name derived from the verses recited during the seventh hakafah. Students and alumni would henceforth be called 'temimim.'
Tags: rashab, tomchei temimim, simchat torah, naming, hakafot

Title: Rayatz appointed head of Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak was appointed to lead Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim, the central Chabad yeshiva founded by his father.
Story: This role placed him at the helm of Chabad's flagship educational institution at age 18. Tomchei Temimim would become his lifelong project, with branches eventually established across Russia, Poland, and ultimately North America.
Tags: tomchei temimim, lubavitch, yeshiva

Title: Yeshiva relocated from Zembin to Lubavitch
Summary: On the night of Simchas Torah 5659, the Rebbe Rashab announced that the yeshiva's main location was being moved from Zembin to Lubavitch.
Story: On the night of Simchas Torah 5659 (1898), during the hakafot, the Rebbe Rashab publicly announced that the yeshiva, which had until then been based in Zembin in Minsk province, would henceforth be established in Lubavitch. In its first year, the main yeshiva had been in Zembin under R' Shmuel Gronem, while a smaller group of students remained in Lubavitch.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, zembin, simchas torah

Title: Yeshivah named Tomchei Temimim on Simchat Torah
Summary: During Simchat Torah hakafot, the Rashab formally named the yeshivah Tomchei Temimim.
Story: On Simchat Torah 1898, as the seventh hakafah began around 4 a.m., the Rashab paused the dancing and announced that the new yeshivah would be named Tomchei Temimim, derived from the hakafot verse 'Tomekh temimim, hoshiya na.' Its students would forever be known as temimim.
Tags: simchat torah, tomchei temimim, naming, hakafot

Title: Rabbi Yisrael Shalom Yosef of Mezhibuzh appoints Asher Zelig Muterperel as rabbi of Michelfaliye
Summary: From Mezhibuzh, Rabbi Yisrael Shalom Yosef writes to the leaders of Michelfaliye endorsing Asher Zelig Muterperel as their new rabbi.
Story: Dated Parashat Acharei 5658 in Mezhibuzh, the letter approves Asher Zelig Muterperel — son of Rabbi Shalom of Ba'ar — to succeed his late father-in-law as rabbi of Michelfaliye. The rebbe instructs the community to support him generously so 'no stranger shall sit on his throne' and so he can devote himself to study.
Tags: mezhibuzh, michelfaliye, muterperel, rabbinical-appointment, ruzhin

Title: Hebron Vaad letter signed by four gabbaim
Summary: A Hebron Vaad letter dated 5 Tammuz 5658 was signed by Mordechai Dovber Slonim, Binyamin Rivlin, Yaakov Slonim, and Levi Eliezer Klansky.
Story: By 5 Tammuz 5658 the Vaad of the Ashkenazi community in Hebron was led by four signatories: Mordechai Dovber Slonim, Binyamin Rivlin, Yaakov Slonim, and Levi Eliezer Klansky. The same first two signed Vaad documents in 5663 and 5669, when Chaim Avraham Fundaminsky was added, all stamping with the seal 'Zechus Avos LeBanim Tizkor — Seal of the Vaad HaKlali of the Ashkenazi Communities of Hebron.'
Tags: hebron, vaad, mordechai dovber slonim, binyamin rivlin, yaakov slonim, levi eliezer klansky

Title: Rayatz appointed director of Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim
Summary: At age eighteen, the Rayatz assumed the position of director of Tomchei Temimim on 24 Elul 5659.
Story: A group of Chasidim led by Rabbi Asher Grossman approached the Rayatz to take the role, citing his wisdom, motivation, and energy. After he demurred, they appealed to the Rashab, who endorsed the idea. The Rayatz immediately faced complex tasks of fundraising, hiring staff, and managing the yeshivah's growth.
Tags: rayatz, tomchei temimim, lubavitch, director, fundraising

Title: Rayatz becomes director of Tomchei Temimim
Summary: On 24 Elul 5658, the eighteen-year-old Rayatz was appointed director of Tomchei Temimim.
Story: After Chasidim led by Rabbi Asher Grossman of Nikolayev urged the Rayatz to lead the yeshivah and the Rashab endorsed the idea, the Rayatz assumed the directorship on 24 Elul 5658 (September 11, 1898). He immediately took on fundraising, faculty management, and expansion of the institution.
Tags: rayatz, tomchei temimim, director, 24 elul

Title: Farbrengen on 19 Kislev decries Lubavitch maskil school
Summary: At a 19 Kislev farbrengen, the Rashab bitterly denounced Baron Gunzburg for supporting an Enlightenment school in Lubavitch.
Story: On 19 Kislev 5659 (December 3, 1898), the Rashab spoke about a major farbrengen, lamenting that Baron Gunzburg had refused his plea to 'give me Yavneh' and spare Lubavitch from a maskil-funded school. The school had nonetheless opened with 130 students.
Tags: 19 kislev, haskalah, gunzburg, lubavitch, yavneh

Title: R' Eliezer Moshe Madievsky sent to Machzikei HaDat in Kovno
Summary: In the summer of 1899 the Rebbe Rashab's emissary R' Eliezer Moshe Madievsky was stationed at the Machzikei HaDat office in Kovno.
Story: Madievsky was sent on behalf of the Rebbe Rashab to coordinate with the Machzikei HaDat office headed by R' Yaakov Lifshitz and R' Z. Landa, called by the secular press 'the Black Bureau.' The mission was to unite all 'God-fearing' Jews—rebbes, rabbis, and observant Maskilim—in a counter-offensive against the Zionist movement.
Tags: kovno, machzikei hadat, rabbi eliezer moshe madievsky, anti-zionism, rabbi yaakov lifshitz

Title: Society for Promotion of Enlightenment opens school in Lubavitch
Summary: The Society for Promotion of Enlightenment opened a school in Lubavitch in the winter of 5659 (1898-99) despite the Rebbe's strenuous opposition.
Story: Society representative Mordechai Ben-Hillel HaKohen had investigated and recommended Lubavitch as the historic cradle of Chasidism where a Maskilic school could influence the entire Chasidic population. The school first opened in rented quarters with Gedalyahu Weinstein as principal. The Rebbe Rashab personally traveled to Petersburg to plead with Baron Ginzburg to spare Lubavitch this 'shame,' but the appeal failed.
Tags: lubavitch, chevra mefitzei haskalah, school, russia, baron ginzburg, gedalyahu weinstein

Title: Death of R. Moshe Wittenberg
Summary: R. Moshe Wittenberg, ba'al ha'adres of Kollel Chabad, died on 27 Nissan 5659.
Story: HaChavatzelet reported that on the third day of Chol HaMoed Pesach 5659 the renowned philanthropist Moshe ben Reuven Wittenberg, born and raised in Vitebsk, passed away childless. He had loved Jerusalem and made it his home for about eighteen years. After his death R. Manish Verovlanski and R. Mordechai Shlonk were jointly appointed to the address role.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, moshe wittenberg, obituary

Title: Rebbe Rashab writes letter against Zionism
Summary: On 10 Tammuz 5659 (June 18, 1899) the Rebbe Rashab wrote his detailed letter setting out the case against the Zionist movement.
Story: The letter, preserved as Igrot Kodesh letter 86, articulated the Rebbe's opposition to the political Zionist movement on religious and ideological grounds. It was written the same summer that he dispatched his emissary R' Eliezer Moshe Madievsky to the Machzikei HaDat office in Kovno to help unite traditional Jewish leadership against both Zionism and the Haskalah.
Tags: zionism, rabbi sholom dovber, letter 86, russia

Title: Rashab writes letter denouncing Zionism
Summary: The Rashab wrote a major letter sharply criticizing Zionism's secular nationalist program.
Story: On 10 Tamuz 5659 (July 22, 1899), the Rashab penned a sharp critique of Zionism, denouncing proponents who sought to replace Torah-based Jewish identity with secular nationalism. The letter became a foundational statement of the Chabad position on the early Zionist movement.
Tags: rashab, zionism, letter, secular nationalism

Title: Rebbe Rashab prepares Vilna edition of Tanya
Summary: In Elul 5659 (September 1899), Rebbe Rashab wrote the first of his letters to R' Asher Grossman of Nikolayev directing corrections for the Vilna Tanya edition.
Story: Rebbe Rashab entrusted R' Asher, a chossid and shochet from Nikolayev, with proofreading the Tanya against early manuscripts and prints for the new Rom press edition. The Rebbe personally reviewed the proposed corrections and resolved unresolved questions, finalizing the text for the new edition.
Tags: tanya, vilna, rashab, rom press, asher grossman, nikolayev

Title: R' Shneur Zalman Slonim arrives in Yafo
Summary: R' Shneur Zalman Slonim arrived in Yafo on Wednesday, 13 Kislev 5660, to assume the Chabad rabbinate there.
Story: His arrival was reported in the HaTzvi newspaper on 15 Kislev, noting that the new rabbi had been brought from Hebron at the request of chasidim and prominent householders. A reception followed on Shabbat with representatives of Bnei Brit, Achva, and Bnei Yisrael societies, lasting through the night.
Tags: yafo, shneur zalman slonim, rabbinate

Title: Dedication poem in Vilna Tanya for Rebbe Rashab
Summary: Dated 19 Kislev 5660 (11 December 1899), R' Asher composed an acrostic poem honoring Rebbe Rashab and placed it on the final page of the Vilna Tanya.
Story: The poem's first letters spelled out 'Shalom DovBer ni' and the closing letters 'b'Rabi Shmuel ziya'. When the first copy reached Rebbe Rashab on 22 Tevet, he was displeased: he had not approved the poem and instructed that copies not be sold until R' Asher signed the dedication openly. The page was later torn from most copies.
Tags: tanya, vilna, rashab, asher grossman, 19 kislev

Title: R' Asher Grossman signs introduction to Vilna Tanya
Summary: On the first day of Chanukah 5660 (18 December 1899), R' Asher Grossman signed the bibliographic introduction to the new Vilna Tanya in Vilna.
Story: His introduction details the painstaking emendation process — collating manuscripts held by descendants of the Tzemach Tzedek — and credits R' Moshe Weiler of Krislave for collecting numerous addenda to Iggeres HaKodesh. The introduction was attributed publicly only after Rebbe Rashab insisted R' Asher's name be added.
Tags: tanya, vilna, asher grossman, moshe weiler, chanukah

Title: Alter Rebbe's Tanya printed in Vilna
Summary: In 5660 the Rebbe Rashab arranged the printing of the Tanya in Vilna, conducted through the chassid R. Anshil Aronovich at the Romm press.
Story: All correspondence with the printers was handled by R. Anshil Aronovich, who served as the Rashab's representative in Vilna. The same arrangement was used four years later for the printing of Likutei Torah.
Tags: tanya, vilna, 5660, anshil aronovich, romm press, rashab

Title: Beginning of Chabad settlement in the United States
Summary: Chabad settlement in America begins in 5660.
Story: The companion volume 'Toldot Chabad B'Artzot HaBrit' opens with the first Chabad settlement in the United States in 5660 (1900), tracing the movement's growth in America through 5710 (1950).
Tags: united states, settlement, immigration

Title: Chabad community in Jaffa appoints its own rabbi
Summary: In 5660 the growing Chabad community of Jaffa brought in their own dedicated rabbi.
Story: As Chabad's presence in Jaffa expanded year by year, the community took the step in 5660 (1900) of installing its own dedicated rabbi. The move marked the maturation of what had begun as a single family's migration in 1866 into a self-governing kehillah.
Tags: jaffa, chabad, rabbi

Title: Chamah's Enlightenment schools reach 150
Summary: By 1900, the Society to Promote the Enlightenment (Chamah) had established 150 schools across Russia.
Story: Founded in 1863 with backing from the Gunzburg family, Chamah's network of schools, which minimized Jewish instruction and promoted Russian-language secular education, had expanded to 150 institutions by 1900. The Rashab regarded the growth as a serious threat to traditional Jewish education.
Tags: chamah, haskalah, russia, assimilation

Title: Government-rabbi conference in the Kherson colonies
Summary: Moshe Krebs, government rabbi of the Kherson Jewish colonies, organized a conference of crown rabbis and presented its conclusions to the Interior Minister in early 1900.
Story: Krebs's initiative set the stage for a broader gathering of government-appointed rabbis in Nikolaev and alarmed the traditional rabbinic leadership. Religious authorities feared that resolutions adopted by reform-minded crown rabbis would be stamped with state authority and used against traditional Judaism.
Tags: kherson, crown rabbis, government rabbis, krebs, interior ministry

Title: JCA pledges one million francs to Enlightenment schools
Summary: The Jewish Colonial Association in Paris pledged one million francs to develop Enlightenment schools in Russia.
Story: In 1900, the Paris-based JCA committed one million francs toward Enlightenment-oriented schooling for Russian Jews. The Rashab, assisted by the Rayatz, organized an international rabbinic lobbying effort that ultimately blocked a follow-up 600,000-franc allocation and redirected funds toward Jewish economic development.
Tags: jca, paris, haskalah, russia, funding

Title: Jewish Colonial Association pledges 1 million francs for Haskalah schools
Summary: The Jewish Colonial Association in Paris pledged 1 million francs to support Enlightenment schools in Russia.
Story: Chamah's campaign to open secular schools expanded with this major funding pledge. The Rashab, with the Rayatz's help, organized an international lobbying effort with prominent rabbis in Russia and France to petition the JCA to withhold the funds. They succeeded in blocking a second allocation of 600,000 francs.
Tags: jca, paris, haskalah, chevrah mefitzei haskalah, fundraising

Title: Marriage of R. Levi Yitzchak Schneerson and Rebbetzin Chana
Summary: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, father of the Rebbe, married Rebbetzin Chana in summer 5660.
Story: In the summer of 5660 (1900), Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, father of the Rebbe, was married to Rebbetzin Chana (Yanovsky). The date is documented in a letter of Rebbe Rashab (Igros Kodesh vol. 3, letter 656). It is suggested that during the years 5658–5660 he may have briefly studied at Lubavitch.
Tags: levi yitzchak, chana, marriage, nikolayev

Title: Passing of the Maharshaz of Kopust, author of Magen Avos
Summary: The Admor Shlomo Zalman of Kopust, author of Magen Avos and son of the Admor Maharil of Kopust, passed away in the year 5660.
Story: The Admor Shlomo Zalman of Kopust, son of the Admor Maharil and grandson of the Tzemach Tzedek, lived until 5660. Known for his work Magen Avos, he had assumed his father's place in Kopust from 5627 onward and was the senior figure of the Kopust branch of Chabad.
Tags: kopust, magen avos, maharshaz, obituary

Title: Publication of the corrected Tanya edition (Vilna 5660)
Summary: Rashab issued the corrected edition of Tanya printed in Vilna 5660, edited by R' Asher Grossman of Nikolayev.
Story: In 5660, Rashab published a corrected edition of the Tanya in Vilna. The proofreading was performed by R' Asher Grossman, shochet of Nikolayev, whom Rashab called 'the chief compiler' in letters of that year. R' Asher's signed 'Modaa Rabba' notice has appeared in every subsequent edition of the Tanya.
Tags: tanya, vilna, r-asher-grossman, rashab

Title: R' Dovid Shifrin departs for America with Rebbe Rashab's notice
Summary: Around 5660, R' Dovid Shifrin came to inform the Rebbe Rashab of his planned move to America, though not to ask permission.
Story: Around 5660, before leaving for America, R' Dovid Shifrin of Pleshchenitsy (resident in Zembin) visited the Rebbe Rashab and said, 'Rebbe, I am going to America' — explaining that he had not come to ask permission, since his sons were already there and his ticket was bought, but that he did not want to be like a student who flees the cheder without telling his teacher. Shifrin became the central organizer of anash in America without title, office, or formal role, operating purely on personal bonds of chasidic brotherhood.
Tags: rebbe rashab, shifrin, pleshchenitsy, zembin, united states, emigration

Title: R' Shneur Zalman Slonim appointed rabbi in Yafo
Summary: In 5660, the Lublin Gaon (Toras Chesed) ordered R' Shneur Zalman Slonim to leave his Hebron affairs and accept the Chabad rabbinate in Yafo.
Story: R' Shneur Zalman submitted to the Lublin Gaon's directive and moved to Yafo to serve the Chabad community. His first task was building a kosher mikveh for women in Neve Shalom, since the existing one was in dangerous and remote old Yafo. He also organized shechita, built a Chabad synagogue, and gave weekly chassidus discourses.
Tags: yafo, hebron, shneur zalman slonim, tzaddik of lublin

Title: R. Baruch Shalom Cohen settles in Warsaw
Summary: Around 5660, the chassid R. Baruch Shalom Cohen settled in Warsaw, joining the small but growing Chabad community there.
Story: R. Baruch Shalom Cohen took up residence in Warsaw around the year 5660 (~1900). He remained there until 5672, when he relocated to nearby Volomin to open a branch of Tomchei Tmimim.
Tags: warsaw, baruch shalom cohen

Title: R. Manish Verovlanski appointed ba'al ha'adres by the Rebbe Rashab
Summary: R. Manish Verovlanski of Lazna was named ba'al ha'adres of Kollel Chabad in 5660 on the Rebbe Rashab's instruction.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab wrote to R. Mendel Slonim on 3 Menachem Av 5660 expressing his preference that funds be sent to Verovlanski because this would establish proper order. The Rebbe Rashab later wrote that Verovlanski's appointment came by his own selection. Verovlanski served only three years before his death.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, manish verovlanski, rebbe rashab, lazna

Title: Rashab declares mission of Tomchei Temimim as 'soldiers of King David'
Summary: Three years after founding, the Rashab laid out a mission statement comparing the temimim to King David's devoted soldiers.
Story: On Simchat Torah, the Rashab told the students they should 'divorce' themselves from worldly concerns and make spiritual development their priority. He charged them with disseminating chasidic teachings outward, recalling the Baal Shem Tov's vision of bringing redemption through spreading the wellsprings.
Tags: rashab, tomchei temimim, simchat torah, mission statement, lubavitch

Title: Rashab travels to Worishofen for medicinal waters
Summary: In winter 5661, the Rebbe Rashab traveled abroad to the medicinal waters at Worishofen, where he met Dr. Yitzchak Eizik Mertzbacher about purchasing his late father's library.
Story: During this trip the Rashab encountered Dr. Mertzbacher, who wished to sell his father's important book and manuscript collection. The Rashab became interested in acquiring the collection to establish a Jewish library under religious ownership.
Tags: rashab, worishofen, germany, health, travel

Title: Rashbatz appointed chief mashpia
Summary: In summer 5660, R' Shmuel Betzalel Sheftel was appointed chief mashpia at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch.
Story: In the summer of 5660 (1900), following the passing of R' Chanoch Hendel Kugel, R' Shmuel Betzalel (Rashbatz) Sheftel was appointed chief mashpia at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch. He had previously taught the Rebbe Rashab's son in Lubavitch from 5654 onwards. Rashbatz served until his passing on 15 Sivan 5665.
Tags: rashbatz, sheftel, tomchei tmimim, mashpia

Title: Rebbe Rashab writes long letter to JCA Paris committee
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab wrote a long letter (Igrot Kodesh 102) to the JCA Paris committee arguing that funds should support Jewish economic life rather than secular schools.
Story: The Rebbe described the spiritual ruination caused by Mefitzei Haskalah schools and argued that JCA's true mission—aid to suffering Russian Jews—called for establishing factories and employment in the Pale of Settlement, not secular schools for religious children. He proposed redirecting the one-million-franc allocation toward economic relief, and the letter became the foundation document of a years-long lobbying campaign.
Tags: jca, ica, paris, letter 102, chevra mefitzei haskalah, economic relief

Title: Simchat Torah mission statement for Tomchei Temimim
Summary: On Simchat Torah, the Rashab laid out the mission of Tomchei Temimim, calling its students 'soldiers of King David.'
Story: On Simchat Torah night 1900, three years after the yeshivah's founding, the Rashab compared the temimim to soldiers of King David who set worldly concerns aside for a higher mission. He charged them with disseminating chasidic teachings and standing strong as Jewish leaders against the temptations of the era.
Tags: simchat torah, tomchei temimim, mission, soldiers of king david

Title: Vilna edition of Tanya printed by Tomchei Temimim
Summary: In 5660 (1899/1900), the Vilna Tanya appeared as the official edition of Tomchei Temimim, published by the Rom press.
Story: The print run included 3,400 standard copies and 1,400–1,600 quality 'regal' paper copies. The cover declared the edition was issued by Tomchei Temimim, and the proceeds beyond expenses were dedicated to supporting the yeshiva's students. This was the first major scholarly edition of Tanya.
Tags: tanya, vilna, rashab, tomchei temimim, rom press, asher grossman

Title: Zembin branch moves to Kovlitz after fire
Summary: About two weeks before Shavuot 5660, the entire town of Zembin burned down, forcing the yeshiva branch to relocate to Kovlitz.
Story: About two weeks before Shavuot 5660 (1900), a terrible fire destroyed the entire town of Zembin where the yeshiva branch was located. All houses, study halls and lodgings burned, and students fled to Lubavitch. After requests from several towns to host the yeshiva, lots were drawn and Kovlitz was chosen. Immediately after Shavuot the students relocated to Kovlitz with R' Shmuel Gronem.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, zembin, kovlitz, fire

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter from Charkov on shelving books
Summary: On 22 Tevet 5660, Rebbe Rashab wrote from Charkov to his son in Lubavitch asking whether the books had been placed on shelves and about a Petersburg book shipment.
Story: By 5660, Rebbe Rashab had begun the active phase of completing missing volumes and organizing books in cabinets (Igros #90). This represents the beginning of the systematic Lubavitch library construction that would continue for two decades.
Tags: rashab, charkov, library, books, shelving, letters

Title: Rebbe Rashab reports completion of Vilna Tanya proofing
Summary: On 15 Teves 5660 (7 January 1900), Rebbe Rashab wrote to his son the Rayatz that, after one more careful review of the printed Tanya, he found eight typographical errors.
Story: Eight replacement pages were reprinted on a separate sheet and inserted at the back of the volume, with a buyer's notice instructing readers to substitute the corrected pages for the original ones at pages 14, 21, 33, 43, 76, 140, 143, and 152.
Tags: tanya, vilna, rashab, rayatz, corrections

Title: Rebbe Rashab letters about the dedication page incident
Summary: On 22 and 24 Teves 5660 (14–16 January 1900), Rebbe Rashab wrote to the Rayatz and to R' Asher demanding that the unauthorized dedication poem be openly signed as a personal addition.
Story: Rebbe Rashab made clear that he was distressed by the addition and would not allow distribution until the poem was clearly attributed to R' Asher rather than appearing as part of the book itself. The matter was resolved by tearing the page from nearly all copies.
Tags: tanya, vilna, rashab, asher grossman, rayatz

Title: Death of R' Chanoch Hendel Kugel
Summary: R' Chanoch Hendel Kugel, mashpia in Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch, passed away on 21 Tevet 5660.
Story: R' Chanoch Hendel Kugel, who served as mashpia for the Lubavitch branch of Tomchei Tmimim from its founding, passed away on 21 Tevet 5660 (1900). His role was filled in the summer of 5660 by R' Shmuel Betzalel (Rashbatz) Sheftel as chief mashpia. The Rebbe Rashab was at the medicinal springs in Kharkov at the time and corresponded with his son about the appointment.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, mashpia, kugel

Title: Public letter confirms Slonim's Yafo appointment
Summary: On 23 Adar I 5660, R' Yitzchak Shmerling published an open letter in HaTzvi affirming that the Lublin Gaon had personally appointed R' Shneur Zalman Slonim to Yafo.
Story: Some had questioned whether the Lublin Gaon had truly directed Slonim's move to Yafo. R' Yitzchak Shmerling responded with an open letter to HaTzvi, stating that he had spoken with the Gaon directly and heard from him that he had chosen R' Shneur Zalman to take the Yafo rabbinate.
Tags: yafo, shneur zalman slonim, tzaddik of lublin, hatzvi

Title: R' Zev Wolf Lewitin appointed mashgiach
Summary: At the start of Adar Rishon 5660, R' Zev Wolf Lewitin was appointed mashgiach over nigleh studies in Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: At the start of the month of Adar Rishon 5660, by call of the menahel, R' Zev Wolf Lewitin, son-in-law of R' Gershon Dov, came to Lubavitch and was appointed mashgiach over the bachurim's study of nigleh. He served as mashgiach until his passing in 5670. R' Yehuda Leib Bodnevitz was simultaneously appointed mashgiach for chassidut studies and R' Michoel Bliner as additional mashpia.
Tags: lewitin, tomchei tmimim, mashgiach, nigleh

Title: Hamelitz reports Baron Ginzburg secured one million francs from JCA
Summary: On 1 Adar II 5660 (March 2, 1900) the Hamelitz newspaper reported that Baron David Ginzburg had secured one million francs from JCA in Paris for Mefitzei Haskalah schools.
Story: The young Baron David Ginzburg traveled to Paris and persuaded the Jewish Colonization Association (JCA), founded by Baron Maurice de Hirsch, to allocate a million francs for schools run by the Society for Promotion of Enlightenment in Russia. When the Rebbe Rashab read of this in Hamelitz, he launched a sustained campaign to redirect the funds away from Maskilic schools and toward economic relief.
Tags: baron ginzburg, jca, ica, paris, chevra mefitzei haskalah, hamelitz, press

Title: Krebs publishes call for crown-rabbi assembly in HaMelitz
Summary: On 8 Adar II 5660, Moshe Krebs published a proclamation in HaMelitz announcing a planned April 1900 assembly of government-appointed rabbis in Nikolaev.
Story: Krebs reported he had already conveyed the conclusions of his Kherson colony rabbinical conference to the Interior Minister. Participation was limited to government-approved rabbis and assistants, fueling fears among the traditional rabbinate that the gathering would yield religiously hostile resolutions endorsed by the state.
Tags: russia, kherson, krebs, hamelitz, crown rabbis, nikolaev

Title: R. Chaim Ozer warns of risk from crown-rabbi assembly
Summary: On 27 Adar II 5660, R. Chaim Ozer Grodzinski wrote to R. Eliezer Moshe Madeyevsky urging vigilance over the planned crown-rabbi assembly.
Story: Chaim Ozer asked Madeyevsky to investigate the matter inside the Interior Ministry and to ensure that the assembly's recommendations could not damage traditional Jewish life. He requested a personal meeting in Vilna on Madeyevsky's return to coordinate strategy.
Tags: russia, chaim ozer, crown rabbis, interior ministry, madeyevsky, vilna

Title: Twenty-five crown rabbis convene in Nikolaev
Summary: On 2 Iyar 5660, twenty-five government-appointed rabbis met in Nikolaev under official authorization, alarming the traditional rabbinate.
Story: Fear spread that the assembly would adopt resolutions hostile to traditional Judaism backed by the imprimatur of the Interior Ministry. The Slonimer Rebbe Shmuel Weinberg and R. Yosef Slifer urgently dispatched R. Eliezer Yosef Klatzky to the Rebbe Rashab, who endorsed the immediate organization of a counter-assembly of traditional rabbis and rebbes.
Tags: russia, nikolaev, crown rabbis, krebs, rashab, slonim

Title: Rebbe Rashab encourages Slonim's Yafo rabbinate
Summary: On 3 Menachem Av 5660, the Rebbe Rashab wrote to R' Mordechai Dovber Slonim to encourage his son in his new Yafo rabbinate.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab acknowledged that the family had endured distress over the Yafo arrangement but explained that since the Lublin Gaon had directed it, they should trust in Hashem. He expressed confidence that R' Shneur Zalman would succeed in his new post.
Tags: rashab, yafo, shneur zalman slonim, mordechai dovber slonim

Title: Rebbe Rashab writes letter on JCA schools to R' Moshe Avigdor Chaikin
Summary: On 21 Av 5660 (August 16, 1900) the Rebbe Rashab wrote to R' Moshe Avigdor Chaikin in England about the JCA schools.
Story: The Rebbe described the spiritual damage of the Mefitzei Haskalah schools—including the newly opened school in Lubavitch funded with 5,000 rubles from JCA—and detailed his plan to address the JCA committee in Paris. He asked R' Chaikin to translate his letter into French with the care of one whose soul was engaged in the cause, and revealed that he had personally traveled to Petersburg two weeks earlier to strategize against the schools.
Tags: jca, rabbi moshe avigdor chaikin, england, lubavitch school, chevra mefitzei haskalah

Title: Rebbe writes to R' Yeshaya Berlin on JCA campaign strategy
Summary: On 11 Elul 5660 (September 5, 1900) the Rebbe Rashab wrote to R' Yeshaya Berlin urging that an emissary be sent to the Paris JCA committee.
Story: The Rebbe argued that since Russian Jews desperately needed economic aid—not educational support—JCA had been deceived by the Petersburg committee. He proposed dispatching their own messenger to Paris to make the case directly, expressing cautious optimism that the request could succeed if pressed firmly.
Tags: jca, paris, rabbi yeshaya berlin, chevra mefitzei haskalah

Title: Rayatz letter recounting Maharash's construction of the Large Hall
Summary: At the beginning of Kislev 5661 (November 1900), Rayatz wrote letter no. 4619 documenting Maharash's reasoning for building the Large Hall over the Tzemach Tzedek's home site.
Story: In a letter dated to the beginning of Kislev 5661, the Rebbe Rayatz preserved family tradition about why Maharash, fearing the future neglect of his father's will, deliberately built the 30-by-30-cubit hall as a place of prayer and Torah on the site of the Tzemach Tzedek's home. This letter is among the primary sources for the early architectural history of the Lubavitch chatzer.
Tags: rayatz, letters, lubavitch, maharash, tzemach-tzedek

Title: R' Avraham Avli Persson dispatched to lobby JCA
Summary: On 16 Cheshvan 5661 (November 8, 1900) the Rebbe wrote that R' Avraham Avli Persson would travel through Vilna, Brisk, and Lodz before heading to Paris on behalf of the JCA campaign.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab chose R' Avraham Avli Persson of Konigsberg to lead the JCA lobbying effort. Persson was to visit Vilna's R' Chaim Ozer Grodzinski, Brisk's R' Chaim Soloveitchik, and Lodz's R' Eliyahu Chaim Meisel to obtain their letters to JCA, then continue to Frankfurt, Karlsruhe, Halberstadt, Fulda, Baden, and finally Paris itself.
Tags: jca, rabbi avraham avli persson, konigsberg, paris, vilna, brisk, lodz

Title: Rebbe Rashab requests Rabinowitz catalog for Mertzbacher purchase
Summary: On the 5th day of Chanukah 5661, Rebbe Rashab wrote from abroad asking his son to send him the Rabinowitz book catalog and his personal book list.
Story: Following his meeting with Dr. Mertzbacher, Rebbe Rashab needed reference materials to evaluate the collection's worth (Igros #677). The Rabinowitz catalog was particularly valuable because its pricing was considered authoritative. This launched the years-long negotiations over the Munich library.
Tags: rashab, mertzbacher, munich, library, letters

Title: Rebbe Rashab travels to Worishofen for medical waters
Summary: In winter 5661, Rebbe Rashab traveled to the healing springs of Worishofen, where he met Dr. Isaac Mertzbacher and learned of the available Munich collection.
Story: During this medical trip abroad, Rebbe Rashab encountered the son of the late R' Avraham Mertzbacher, who wished to sell his father's library. This chance meeting sparked Rebbe Rashab's multi-year effort to purchase the Munich collection and create a Jewish library in observant hands.
Tags: rashab, worishofen, travel, medical, germany

Title: Rashab requests Rabinowitz catalog from his son for Mertzbacher library evaluation
Summary: On 5 Chanukah 5661, the Rashab wrote from abroad to his son (the future Rebbe Rayatz) in Lubavitch asking him to find and send the Rabinowitz book catalog urgently.
Story: The Rashab needed the catalog of R. Rafael Nata Rabinowitz to help evaluate the prices of the Mertzbacher collection he was negotiating to buy. He stressed the urgency and also asked for a list of his own books.
Tags: rashab, frierdiker rebbe, library, mertzbacher, rabinowitz catalog

Title: Birth of Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka
Summary: The Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka was born in 5661; the Rashab sent a mazal tov letter to mark her birth.
Story: The Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, future wife of the seventh Rebbe, was born in 5661 (1901). Her grandfather, the Rebbe Rashab, wrote a personal mazal tov letter on the occasion of her birth, which is preserved and displayed at the Lubavitch Library exhibition on family purity and Chabad life events.
Tags: rebbetzin chaya mushka, rashab, russia

Title: Branch opened in Nevel
Summary: In early summer 5661 a branch of Tomchei Tmimim was opened in Nevel under R' Yehuda Leib Bodnevitz.
Story: In early summer 5661 (1901), a new branch of Tomchei Tmimim was opened in the town of Nevel. About twenty students were selected and sent with the mashgiach R' Yehuda Leib (Tzites) Bodnevitz, who hailed from Nevel and thus was suited to lead this branch. The Nevel branch lasted about a year and a half before closing in late summer 5662.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, nevel, bodnevitz

Title: Inauguration of yeshiva's large hall
Summary: On 8 Tammuz 5661 the renovated Great Hall in the Rebbe's courtyard was inaugurated as the yeshiva's study hall.
Story: On the third day, 8 Tammuz 5661 (1901), the Great Hall (30 amos by 30 amos, originally built in 5632 as a prayer space) was renovated and inaugurated as the study hall of Tomchei Tmimim. The funds were donated by R' Yeshaya Berlin, one of the yeshiva's main supporters. The dedication ceremony was held with great splendor.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, berlin, zal hagadol

Title: R' Chizkiyah Medini settles in Romano house
Summary: When R' Chizkiyah Medini came to Hebron in 5661, the Romano family hosted him in their mansion, where he completed his Sdei Chemed.
Story: R' Chizkiyah Medini, author of the Sdei Chemed, arrived in Hebron in 5661 and was housed by the Romano family in their stately mansion. He used the building, which contained a synagogue called the Istanbuli Beit Knesset, as his base for Torah study and teaching. There he completed his monumental Sdei Chemed before dying on 24 Kislev 5665. The 'Yeshivat Sdei Chemed' was later established in the same building in his memory.
Tags: hebron, sdei chemed, medini, romano, yeshiva

Title: R' Eliezer Orlozarow passes away in Romny
Summary: R' Eliezer Orlozarow, longtime rabbi of Romny, passed away in 5661.
Story: After nearly four decades serving as rabbi of Romny since 5623, R' Eliezer Orlozarow died in 5661. He was succeeded by R' Chaim Yeshaya Schneersohn (descendant of the Tzemach Tzedek through the Maharil of Kopust), with R' Akiva Yankilevsky (Orlozarow's son-in-law) appointed as additional moreh tzedek.
Tags: eliezer orlozarow, romny, rabbinate, chabad

Title: R' Yeshayahu Berlin opens additional Riga Chabad minyan
Summary: R' Yeshayahu Berlin opened an additional Chabad minyan in Riga in 5661 (1901).
Story: Building on his earlier work in Riga, R' Yeshayahu Berlin opened an additional Chabad minyan in the city in 5661 (1901). The synagogue at 22/24 Mills Street later carried his name as a memorial to his role.
Tags: riga, latvia, synagogue, yeshayahu-berlin

Title: R. Chaim Yeshaya Schneersohn becomes rabbi of Romen
Summary: R. Chaim Yeshaya Schneersohn, great-grandson of the Tzemach Tzedek, was installed as rabbi of Romen in 5661.
Story: R. Chaim Yeshaya Schneersohn — son of the rebbe of Retchitsa, grandson of the Kapuster rebbe R. Yehuda Leib, and great-grandson of the Tzemach Tzedek — assumed the rabbinate of Romen in 5661 (1900/1901). He would serve the town for over twenty-five years and was among the senior anash figures in the city who endorsed the local petition to the 1910 St. Petersburg rabbinical conference. He held the position until his passing in late 1927.
Tags: russia, romen, chaim-yeshaya-schneersohn, schneersohn-family

Title: Rayatz opens textile mill in Dubrovno
Summary: The Rayatz opened a Shabbat-observant textile mill in Dubrovno using JCA funds.
Story: In 1901, tasked by his father, the Rayatz spent a year setting up a textile mill in Dubrovno some sixty miles from Lubavitch. Built with JCA funds redirected from Enlightenment schools, the mill closed on Shabbat and eventually employed two thousand local Jews, removing the stigma of factory work.
Tags: dubrovno, textile mill, rayatz, employment, jca

Title: Rayatz opens textile mill in Dubrovno using diverted JCA funds
Summary: The Rayatz spent a year setting up a textile mill in Dubrovno using JCA funds redirected toward Jewish economic opportunity.
Story: With help from the Polyakov brothers, the Rashab convinced the JCA to divert Haskalah funds toward creating economic opportunities for Russian Jews. The factory, located sixty miles from Lubavitch, was closed on Shabbat and eventually provided gainful employment for two thousand local Jews, removing social stigma from factory work.
Tags: rayatz, dubrovno, textile mill, jca, economic development

Title: Rayatz travels to Vilna, Brisk, Lodz, and Koenigsberg
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak traveled across Eastern Europe to establish the Dubrovna factory.
Story: The trip was part of his communal economic work, organizing infrastructure that could support Jewish life and community in the region. He visited major Jewish centers including Vilna, Brisk, Lodz, and Koenigsberg in pursuit of the project.
Tags: vilna, brisk, lodz, koenigsberg, dubrovna, factory

Title: Rebbe Rashab appeals to the JCA for industrial relief in the Pale
Summary: Rebbe Rashab wrote to the Jewish Colonization Association describing catastrophic Jewish poverty in Russia and urging it to build factories in the Pale rather than fund Maskilic schools.
Story: In a long, anguished letter (Igrot Kodesh #102), the Rebbe portrayed families starving from the combined effects of Pale residency restrictions and the new state monopoly on liquor sales. He argued that funding industrial infrastructure inside the Pale would allow Jews to earn a living where they were trapped by law, rather than supporting the Society for the Diffusion of Enlightenment.
Tags: russia, rashab, jca, jewish colonization association, poverty, pale of settlement, liquor monopoly

Title: Tomchei Tmimim classes move to renovated great hall
Summary: By 5661 the growing enrollment of Tomchei Tmimim required relocating classes into the great hall, which was being renovated for year-round yeshiva use.
Story: The great hall, originally built only for summer use, lacked heating and had simple wooden walls that had deteriorated. Renovation began with installation of stoves, new foundations and flooring, and new windows, continuing until 5663. Eighteen large tables seating up to ten students each filled the hall, with a central bimah holding two tables for the mashgichim.
Tags: tomchei-tmimim, lubavitch-courtyard, rashab

Title: Tomchei Tmimim expands into main hall
Summary: Tomchei Tmimim student numbers grew enough to require using the main hall (Zal) in 5661.
Story: In 5661, the number of students at Tomchei Tmimim had grown sufficiently that classes began being held in the main hall (Zal) of the courtyard in Lubavitch.
Tags: tomchei-tmimim, yeshiva, lubavitch

Title: Wiener's bibliography of Haggadot published in St. Petersburg
Summary: Shmuel Wiener published his pioneering bibliography of 909 Haggadot in St. Petersburg in 5661.
Story: In 5661 (1901), the bibliographer Shmuel Wiener published in Petersburg his Reshimat Haggadot-Pesach Shenidpesu B'Khol Artzot Tevel — a list of 909 editions of the Haggadah printed worldwide between 1500 and 1900. It became the foundational bibliographic reference for the Haggadah.
Tags: bibliography, haggadah, wiener, st-petersburg

Title: Yeshaya Berlin donates for refurbishment of Tomchei Temimim zal
Summary: Philanthropist Yeshaya Berlin of Riga gave a large gift enabling refurbishment of the study hall and construction of a dining room.
Story: With enrollment growing rapidly, the Rayatz approached Berlin for a major gift. The study hall known as the zal was refurbished and additional facilities were built. Berlin was a successful businessman married to a granddaughter of the third Rebbe and remained close to the Chabad Rebbes throughout his life.
Tags: yeshaya berlin, riga, tomchei temimim, philanthropy, lubavitch

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter to R' Yeshaya Berlin about Mertzbacher collection
Summary: On 4 Shevat 5661, Rebbe Rashab estimated the Munich collection price at 35,000-40,000 rubles and tried to enlist R' Yeshaya Berlin of Riga as funder.
Story: In this letter (Igros #691), Rebbe Rashab described the pricing methodology based on the Rabinowitz catalog. He noted that Baron David Ginzburg would acquire such manuscripts at any cost without hesitation. The goal was to keep this Jewish treasure in observant hands rather than letting it pass to secular collectors.
Tags: rashab, yeshaya berlin, riga, mertzbacher, library

Title: Rebbe summarizes Persson's tour of European rabbis
Summary: On 22 Tevet 5661 (January 13, 1901) the Rebbe summarized R' Persson's two-month tour of Russian and German rabbis on behalf of the JCA campaign.
Story: The Rebbe reported on visits to R' Chaim Ozer Grodzinski (whose letter to JCA was strong), R' Chaim Soloveitchik (whose letter was too harsh against committee members), and R' Eliyahu Chaim Meisel (where Persson stayed over two weeks). Persson was now traveling to Berlin and onward to Frankfurt, Karlsruhe, Halberstadt, Fulda, and Baden to gather support from German Orthodox rabbis before continuing to Paris.
Tags: jca, rabbi avraham avli persson, rabbi chaim soloveitchik, rabbi chaim ozer grodzinski, rabbi eliyahu chaim meisel, germany

Title: Rashab writes to R. Yeshaya Berlin about funding Mertzbacher library purchase
Summary: On 4 Shvat 5661, the Rashab wrote to the wealthy chassid R. Yeshaya Berlin of Riga estimating the Mertzbacher collection price at 35,000-40,000 rubles and pressing him to commit to funding the purchase.
Story: The Rashab compared prices using the Rabinowitz catalog and argued that Baron David Ginzburg would surely buy the manuscripts and early printings at any price if he knew. He pressed R. Berlin to decide, noting that hesitation prevented serious negotiations with Mertzbacher.
Tags: rashab, yeshaya berlin, riga, library, mertzbacher, philanthropy

Title: Rebbe Rashab requests catalog return after Mertzbacher silence
Summary: On 26 Shevat 5661, Rebbe Rashab reported that Hirshenger of Munich had requested his catalog back on Dr. Mertzbacher's behalf, pressing for a decision.
Story: The lack of response was puzzling the Munich seller. Rebbe Rashab needed Yeshaya Berlin's definitive answer—whether he intended to fund the purchase or had abandoned the idea (Igros #697). The acquisition negotiations were stalling.
Tags: rashab, mertzbacher, munich, hirshenger, letters

Title: Rebbe writes from Worishofen healing springs on JCA effort
Summary: On 25 Shevat 5661 (February 14, 1901) the Rebbe Rashab, recuperating at Worishofen's healing springs, met with R' Persson to plan the next phase.
Story: The Rebbe had traveled to Worishofen for medical treatment and Persson came to him to coordinate strategy. Together they prepared additional letters needed for Persson's mission and discussed how to manage the campaign going forward.
Tags: jca, worishofen, rabbi avraham avli persson, germany

Title: Rashab presses for decision on Mertzbacher purchase
Summary: On 26 Shvat 5661, the Rashab wrote again to R. Yeshaya Berlin after receiving a letter from Hirschenger in Munich requesting the return of the catalog and an answer from Mertzbacher.
Story: Mertzbacher had wondered why the Rashab was not communicating about the purchase. The Rashab pressed Berlin to give a definite yes or no so he could respond appropriately, since negotiations could not proceed without the funder's commitment.
Tags: rashab, yeshaya berlin, library, mertzbacher, hirschenger

Title: R' Persson recalled from Paris for Pesach
Summary: On 9 Nisan 5661 (March 29, 1901) the Rebbe wrote to R' Persson to return home to Konigsberg for Pesach before resuming the Paris mission.
Story: Persson had spent five weeks in Paris meeting with R' Tzadok Kahn, R' Shmuel Altmann, R' Shlomo Cohen, and JCA president M. Leven, struggling to overturn the Mefitzei Haskalah grant. The Rebbe instructed him to return home for the holiday and then travel back to Paris after Pesach for the JCA committee's late-April session, when the Rebbe himself would also travel to Paris.
Tags: jca, paris, rabbi avraham avli persson, rabbi tzadok kahn, rabbi shmuel altmann

Title: Branch opened in Horodishtch
Summary: R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin arrived in Horodishtch on 20 Iyar 5661 to lead a new branch of Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: On 20 Iyar 5661 (1901), R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin arrived in Horodishtch to head a new branch of Tomchei Tmimim, with 20 students under his care. The Rashbatz had been sent ahead by the menahel to organize matters. The branch operated until 5671, when Havlin moved to Hebron to open the Toras Emes yeshiva.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, horodishtch, havlin

Title: Rebbe Rashab instructs son on guarding manuscripts during Kamenka trip
Summary: On 27 Iyar 5661, Rebbe Rashab wrote to his son Rebbe Rayatz with detailed instructions for appointing guards over the manuscripts before traveling to a Kamenka wedding.
Story: Rebbe Rashab took manuscript security with utmost gravity (Igros #737). He asked his son to appoint constant guards with full devotion to protecting the manuscripts, including from theft. He also asked the family matriarch to oversee security generally.
Tags: rashab, rayatz, manuscripts, kamenka, security, letters

Title: Rebbe Rashab pushes for rabbinical assembly on JCA funding crisis
Summary: On 1 Sivan 5661, Rebbe Rashab wrote to R. Avraham Avli Perlson urging him to press leading rabbis to convene over the JCA donations being directed to Maskilic schools in Russia.
Story: The JCA (Jewish Colonization Association) had begun channeling funds to schools of the Mefitzei Haskalah society, threatening traditional Jewish education in Russia. Rebbe Rashab considered the matter so urgent that he sought to organize a rabbinical assembly to formulate a response. He worked behind the scenes through R. Avraham Avli Perlson, asking the great rabbis (such as the Telshe Rav) to take ownership of the cause publicly while he supported them from the background.
Tags: russia, rashab, jca, haskalah, rabbinical assembly, avraham avli perlson

Title: Rebbe Rashab summarizes failed JCA Paris campaign
Summary: On 19 Sivan 5661 (June 6, 1901) the Rebbe Rashab summarized the failure of the Paris JCA campaign to R' Eliezer Moshe Madievsky.
Story: The Rebbe described how Baron Ginzburg had retained the JCA committee's full confidence, dismissing the rabbinic protest as 'Chasidism,' and how JCA president Leven had broken his promise to consult Polyakov independently. Although the committee acknowledged the schools' teachers were harmful, they refused to act on the rabbis' protest and merely forwarded the complaints to Petersburg. The Rebbe resolved to convene an assembly of Russian rabbis to escalate the effort.
Tags: jca, paris, baron ginzburg, rabbi tzadok kahn, rabbi avraham avli persson, polyakov

Title: Rebbe Rashab follow-up letter on manuscript security
Summary: On 20 Menachem Av 5661, Rebbe Rashab pressed his son for immediate confirmation on who had been appointed to guard the manuscripts.
Story: Rebbe Rashab noticed his son had failed to mention manuscript security arrangements in previous letters (Igros #765). He demanded immediate reply on who was guarding them and where the keys had been entrusted. The intensity reflects how central the manuscript archive was to his life's work.
Tags: rashab, rayatz, manuscripts, security, letters

Title: Passing of grandfather R. Avraham Shlomo, shochet of Zhuravichi
Summary: The author's paternal grandfather R. Avraham Shlomo, shochet of Zhuravichi, passed away on 25 Elul.
Story: R. Avraham Shlomo, who had been a chasid of the Tzemach Tzedek, the Maharash, and the Rashab, passed away on 25 Elul 5661. He had served as shochet in Paritch before being pressed by his family to return to Zhuravichi after his father's death. He left behind his widow Bracha and three sons: Yaakov Leib, Yisrael Yeshaya, and Yosef Hillel.
Tags: zhuravichi, shochet, jacobson family

Title: Rebbe Rashab laments rabbinic inaction against Russian religious decline
Summary: On 14 Tevet 5662 the Rebbe Rashab wrote that the absence of rabbinic mobilization while the Maskilim worked aggressively was 'terrifying,' and that he could rely only on R. Menachem Mendel Chein for assistance.
Story: After repeated failed attempts to convene a rabbinical assembly in summer 5661, the Rebbe Rashab expressed bitter frustration in a letter to R. Eliezer Moshe Modayevsky. He reported informing R. Chaim Ozer Grodzinski of Vilna that the rabbis should no longer rely on him and must act independently, while he himself stood ready to travel for any assembly that would actually convene. Although R. Chaim Ozer was passionate about the cause, the Rebbe felt the man lacked the power to effect internal change.
Tags: russia, rashab, haskalah, rabbinical assembly, eliezer moshe modayevsky

Title: Admor R' Shmuel of Slonim visits Rebbe Rashab
Summary: In 1902 Admor R' Shmuel Weinberg of Slonim traveled to the Rebbe Rashab to discuss founding the Machzikei HaDat society.
Story: R' Shmuel of Slonim and Rabbi Yosef Shlifer of Slonim had previously sent an emissary, R' Eliezer Yosef Klatzky, in late winter 5660 to engage the Rebbe Rashab. In Tevet 5662 R' Shmuel himself came to Lubavitch to plan a general organization called Machzikei HaDat that would unite multiple Chasidic and rabbinic factions in defense of traditional Judaism.
Tags: machzikei hadat, rabbi shmuel weinberg, slonim, rabbi yosef shlifer

Title: Berditchev publication of Magen Avot drashot by Rebbe Mahara'sh of Kapust
Summary: The Magen Avot drashot of Rebbe Shlomo Zalman of Kapust (the Mahara'sh of Kapust) on Sefer Vayikra were published in Berditchev.
Story: In 5662 (1902), 'Magen Avot' — drashot of the Chabad-Kapust Rebbe Shlomo Zalman (Mahara'sh of Kapust) on Sefer Vayikra — was published in Berditchev. The 50-leaf folio edition preserved the teachings of the Kapust branch of Chabad, which split from the main Lubavitch line. It served the Kapust-Chabad community in the Russian Empire.
Tags: chabad, kapust, berditchev, magen avot, mahara'sh of kapust

Title: Berlin edition of Orchot Chaim part two
Summary: Rabbi M. Schlesinger published part two of Orchot Chaim with an introduction in Berlin in 5662.
Story: In 5662 (1902), Rabbi M. Schlesinger published part two of Orchot Chaim in Berlin. In his introduction he explained the existence of two recensions of the work, noting that in the second edition — completed after the author reached Majorca and studied under Rabbi Shem Tov Falco — Rabbi Shem Tov is cited about fifteen times in part two alone.
Tags: berlin, orchot chaim, schlesinger

Title: Birth of Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson, the seventh Rebbe
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson, the seventh Lubavitcher Rebbe, was born in 1902.
Story: Born in Nikolaev to the Schneerson family of rabbinic descent, he later married the Rayatz's daughter Chaya Mushka. After a lifetime of preparation, he accepted leadership in 1951 and led Chabad until his passing in 1994.
Tags: menachem mendel schneerson, seventh rebbe

Title: Kitchen and dining hall built for Tomchei Tmimim students
Summary: In 5662 a kitchen and dining facility was built in the Lubavitch courtyard to serve the students of Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: The growing yeshiva required dedicated food-service infrastructure within the courtyard. The kitchen and dining hall sufficed for several years until further expansion forced construction of a larger building. The expanded yeshiva also accommodated cheder students who had come to study in Lubavitch.
Tags: tomchei-tmimim, lubavitch-courtyard

Title: Police raid on Tomchei Tmimim hall
Summary: In summer 5662, the Mohilev district director and police raided the yeshiva hall following malicious denunciations.
Story: After Shavuot 5662 (1902), on a Friday afternoon, the district director from Mohilev province arrived at the yeshiva hall with the local police chief and secret police, after denunciations claimed over 200 students were studying illegally. Only about 30 students were present, and the director was impressed by their appearance, but ordered the hall sealed pending official permits. Within a day, after the menahel telegraphed Mohilev, the seal was removed.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, informers, police, haskalah, mohilev

Title: Publication of Beit Rebbi, comprehensive Chabad biographical history
Summary: Rabbi Chaim Meir Hillman's Beit Rebbi, the major early biographical work on the Chabad dynasty, was published in Berditchev in 5662.
Story: In 5662 (1902) Rabbi Chaim Meir Hillman published Beit Rebbi in Berditchev. The work greatly expanded earlier accounts of the lives of the Chabad Rebbes and drew on many oral and written sources. It became the standard reference for Chabad biographical history for generations.
Tags: beit rebbi, hillman, berditchev, chabad history, biography

Title: R' Dovber Efrat moves to Jerusalem; R' Shiloh takes Hebron
Summary: In late 5662, R' Dovber Efrat moved to Jerusalem and R' Shiloh assumed the Hebron rabbinate and kollel administration.
Story: R' Dovber Efrat relocated to Jerusalem at the end of 5662. R' Shiloh succeeded him in both the rabbinate and kollel leadership in Hebron, working alongside R' Mordechai Dovber Slonim and R' Binyamin Rivlin until World War I.
Tags: hebron, jerusalem, kollel chabad, dovber efrat, shiloh aharon

Title: Rayatz travels to St. Petersburg for communal matters
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak traveled to St. Petersburg to handle communal matters on behalf of Russian Jewry.
Story: St. Petersburg, as the imperial capital, was a key center for Jewish advocacy with government officials. The Rayatz repeatedly traveled there throughout the early 1900s, work that ultimately led to his being arrested four times between 1902 and 1911.
Tags: st petersburg, russia

Title: Rayatz's second arrest over secular school accusations
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was arrested a second time due to accusations from teachers at the secular school in Lubavitch.
Story: In 1902, Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn faced his second arrest, brought about by accusations leveled by teachers at the secular school in Lubavitch. This arrest reflected ongoing tensions between traditional Chabad education and the secular educational system pushed by reformers. It was one of seven arrests he would experience over his lifetime under czarist and later Communist rule.
Tags: lubavitch, russia, arrest, secular school, yosef yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Romanian translation of the Haggadah by Avraham Shlomo Gold printed in Craiova
Summary: The third revised edition of Avraham Shlomo Gold's Romanian translation of the Haggadah, with musical notation, was printed in Craiova.
Story: Around 5662 (1902), Avraham Shlomo Gold issued the third revised edition of his Romanian translation of the Haggadah, with many additions, in Craiova. The 83-page work included annotations and musical notation. It served the Romanian-speaking Jewish community of the Balkans.
Tags: haggadah, romanian, craiova, romania, musical notation

Title: Shaarei Zedek Hospital founded in Jerusalem
Summary: Dr. Moshe Wallach founded Jerusalem's Shaarei Zedek Hospital with Shabbat observance and Jewish tradition built into its protocols.
Story: Wallach, a religious German Jew known for piety and dedication to patients, would later sail home alongside the Rebbe Rayatz from Alexandria in 1929 and nurse the Rebbe back to health after he fell ill upon learning of the Hebron massacre. The hospital remains one of the premier medical centers in Israel.
Tags: shaarei-zedek, jerusalem, wallach, hospital

Title: Tomchei Tmimim builds dedicated kitchen and dining hall
Summary: A kitchen and dining hall were built in the Lubavitch courtyard for yeshiva students in 5662.
Story: In 5662, a kitchen and dining hall were constructed in the Lubavitch courtyard to serve Tomchei Tmimim students. This facility lasted for several years until the yeshiva grew further and required additional building expansion.
Tags: tomchei-tmimim, lubavitch, infrastructure

Title: Rabbi Chaim Mordechai Aizik Hodakov born in Beshankovich
Summary: The future chief of staff to the seventh Rebbe is born in the Russian town of Beshankovich.
Story: Hodakov's family moved to Riga when he was two, where he studied under Rabbi Yoel Barantchik of the Novardok Musar movement. He became an ardent Chasid when the Rebbe arrived in 1928 and later founded the Derech Eretz school at eighteen.
Tags: hodakov, birth, beshankovich, russia

Title: Rashab signs printing contract for fifth edition of Likkutei Torah
Summary: On 19 Adar I תרס"ב the Rebbe Rashab signed a contract with a Vilna printing house to produce the fifth edition of Likkutei Torah, with the plates remaining his property.
Story: The Rashab personally oversaw a new, carefully corrected fifth edition of Likkutei Torah. He signed the printing contract on 19 Adar I תרס"ב, with the printing plates remaining his property. He aimed to lower the price from 5-6 silver rubles per copy to roughly 2 rubles, so that even middle-class Jews could afford the set. The Rebbe and R' Shmuel Sofer (Rabinowitz) personally proofed the text.
Tags: rashab, likkutei torah, vilna, romm press

Title: Kollel Chabad writes Rebbe Rashab on Siberian shlichim, citing 1868 agreement
Summary: Kollel Chabad officials wrote to Rebbe Rashab on 10 Adar I 5662 about sending dedicated shlichim to Siberia, citing the existing pesher with the Perushim.
Story: When the Kollel Chabad officials in Jerusalem debated dispatching their own emissaries to the cities of Siberia, they wrote to Rebbe Sholom DovBer of Lubavitch explaining that they were bound by an earlier pesher with the Perushim Vaad HaKlali. They attached a copy of the 1868 agreement which had been preserved in the kollel's letter register. The letter is the earliest known reference to that agreement in Chabad correspondence.
Tags: siberia, kollel chabad, kollel reisin, shadar, fundraising

Title: Rashab discusses renewed Mertzbacher library negotiations
Summary: On 25 Adar 5662, the Rashab informed R. Yeshaya Berlin that Mertzbacher was again willing to sell after a year's delay and asked Berlin for a final decision.
Story: After Mertzbacher had earlier refused to sell, three weeks earlier he had written that he wanted to sell. The Rashab also revealed he had proposed the purchase to R. Yaakov Horowitz of Riga in Hamburg, and suggested perhaps Berlin and Horowitz could form a partnership.
Tags: rashab, library, mertzbacher, yeshaya berlin, yaakov horowitz, riga

Title: Rashab writes RA"Ch directing the organization of NY anash
Summary: On 24 Adar I 5662 the Rebbe Rashab replies to RA"Ch, instructing NY anash to meet thrice weekly for Chassidus study and to fix tefillah and mitzvah observance.
Story: Responding to RA"Ch's report on the life of anash in New York, the Rebbe Rashab on 24 Adar I 5662 (Igrot Kodesh vol. 1, letter 114) acknowledged a $100 contribution and urged the immigrants to organize. He directed them to gather at least three times weekly — Thursday night, Shabbos, and motzaei Shabbos — for fixed study of Chassidus, and to make 'tikkunim' in the conduct of public prayer and mitzvah observance in their new setting.
Tags: rashab, new york, usa, anash, chassidus, tefillah, igrot kodesh, shiurim

Title: Rebbe Rashab proposes Riga as home for Mertzbacher library
Summary: On the eve of 25 Adar 5662, Rebbe Rashab urged R' Yeshaya Berlin to purchase the Munich library and house it in 3-4 rooms of his Riga home for Torah study.
Story: Rebbe Rashab clarified his vision: the priority was that an important Jewish library exist in observant hands, even if located in Riga rather than Russia or Lubavitch (Igros #782). He proposed dedicating 2-3 rooms for books and one for study. He also approached R' Yaakov Horowitz of Riga as a possible co-funder.
Tags: rashab, yeshaya berlin, riga, mertzbacher, munich, library

Title: Rebbe Rashab encourages New York anash via letter through Rosenbaum
Summary: On 24 Adar I 5662 the Rebbe Rashab replied to Rosenbaum, acknowledging a 100-ruble donation and urging the New York chassidim to gather thrice weekly to study Chassidut, daven with kavanah and strengthen mitzvah observance.
Story: Receiving Rosenbaum's report on the New York group together with 100 rubles, on 24 Adar I 5662 the Rebbe Rashab wrote a long letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. 1 #114). He praised the men of the Rebbe Maharash's circle for retaining their spiritual life in a distant land, urged them to meet on Thursday nights, Shabbat and motzaei Shabbat to learn Chassidut together, and to correct shortcomings in their tefillah and observance.
Tags: america, new york, rebbe rashab, torah study

Title: R. Shneur Zalman of Lublin, author of Toras Chesed, passes away
Summary: The renowned posek R. Shneur Zalman of Lublin, author of Toras Chesed, died on 5 Nisan 5662 in Jerusalem.
Story: R. Shneur Zalman of Lublin lived in a house in Jerusalem purchased for him by R. Yeshaya Berlin and dedicated to Kollel Chabad. His passing on the night of 5 Nisan 5662 prompted the Jerusalem trustees to propose using his house as a new Chabad yeshiva. This proposal was the catalyst for the multi-year discussion that culminated in establishing Chabad yeshivas in Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: jerusalem, torat chesed, shneur zalman of lublin, kollel chabad

Title: Rashab announces affordable Likkutei Torah project
Summary: On 6 Iyar תרס"ב the Rebbe Rashab wrote that the new Likkutei Torah edition would cost no more than 2 rubles — down from 5-6 — so it would become accessible even to chassidim of modest means.
Story: In a letter dated 6 Iyar תרס"ב the Rashab explained the motivation behind the fifth edition: existing copies cost chassidim 5-6 silver rubles with great difficulty in obtaining them, while the new edition would be priced around 2 rubles and well-proofed. The project reflected his broader concern with making Chabad chassidic texts widely available.
Tags: rashab, likkutei torah, affordable, chassidim

Title: Branch in Dokshitz opened
Summary: Following a council in Sivan 5662, a small branch of Tomchei Tmimim was opened in Dokshitz under R' Yehoshua Lein.
Story: On 17 Sivan 5662 (1902), founders of the yeshiva society met with the Rebbe Rashab at the country house and decided to open a small branch of Tomchei Tmimim in Dokshitz at the urging of its residents. The avreich R' Yehoshua Lein was appointed as teacher. The branch is mentioned in correspondence through Erev Tisha B'Av 5666.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, dokshitz, lein

Title: Kolel Chabad holds lottery for two Montefiore-fund beneficiaries
Summary: Kolel Chabad trustees draw lots for two Jerusalem members to receive that year's share of the Montefiore estate fruits.
Story: On 19 Sivan 5662 (June 24, 1902), the trustees of Kolel Chabad notified the Vaad Klalli that a lottery — held before them and other notables — had selected R' David Gilel and R' Noach son of R' Chaim Ber to enjoy that year's distribution from Sir Moshe Montefiore's estate. Names of winners were sent to the London executors, who paid each recipient directly.
Tags: jerusalem, hebron, montefiore, kolel chabad, vaad klalli

Title: Rebbe Rashab vision of Torah library in Riga
Summary: On 10 Menachem Av 5662, Rebbe Rashab argued that since secular Jews maintain great libraries for ulterior motives, a G-d-fearing man should spend a few thousand to enable Jewish study.
Story: Rebbe Rashab pushed Yeshaya Berlin to dedicate part of his large Riga home to a Jewish library where observant Jews could come and learn. He emphasized this would be 'a benefit to him and a benefit to the world.' Despite extensive negotiations, the Mertzbacher acquisition ultimately fell through.
Tags: rashab, yeshaya berlin, riga, library, torah study

Title: Rashab's letter on building a Jewish library in Riga
Summary: On 10 Menachem Av 5662, the Rashab sent the Mertzbacher catalog with supplement to R. Ze'ev Wolf, instructing him to negotiate a price of 30,000-35,000 rubles and outlining his vision for a Jewish library in Riga.
Story: The Rashab urged that since maskilim maintained great libraries for non-religious purposes, a God-fearing Jew should fund this acquisition. He proposed that R. Yeshaya Berlin dedicate 3-4 rooms of his large house in Riga for the library and a study hall, so observant Jews could come to learn. The purchase ultimately did not materialize.
Tags: rashab, library, mertzbacher, riga, ze'ev wolf, hirschenger

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter to Jerusalem trustees on schools and chalukah
Summary: On 21 Av 5662 the Rebbe Rashab decreed that Kollel Chabad members sending children to secular schools or shaving their beards must be denied chalukah.
Story: Reacting with anguish to news that some Kollel Chabad members were sending their children to modern schools, the Rebbe Rashab insisted that the kollel was founded for those engaged in Torah and avodah in Eretz Yisrael, not for supporting those undermining traditional Jewish life. He ruled that beard-shavers and parents enrolling children in such schools must be cut from the chalukah lists, a position the Jerusalem trustees only partially implemented after a year of dispute.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, rashab, schools, shkoleh, shaving, religious decline

Title: R' DovBer Efrat leaves Hebron rabbinate for Jerusalem
Summary: R' DovBer Efrat left the Hebron rabbinate after nine years to remarry and settle in Jerusalem in summer/Elul 1902.
Story: After nine years as rabbi of Hebron's Ashkenazi community, R' DovBer Efrat left in summer 1902 (קיץ תרס"ב) and settled in Jerusalem in Elul of that year after taking a new wife there. He explained in HaChavatzelet that the heavy burden of communal duties had become too much for him in his advancing age.
Tags: dovber efrat, hebron, jerusalem, marriage, rabbinate

Title: Rabbi Dovber Efrat of Hebron remarries in Jerusalem
Summary: Around Tishrei 5663 the Rabbi of Hebron, R. Dovber Efrat, married in Jerusalem and remained there, leaving Hebron Chabad without a rabbi.
Story: Through the winter of 5663 the Hebron Chabad community debated whether to import a new rabbi from elsewhere or appoint one of its own members. By early summer they decided on Rabbi Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov, a respected local scholar then living in Hebron.
Tags: hebron, jerusalem, dovber efrat, rabbinate

Title: R' DovBer Efrat appointed Chabad administrator in Jerusalem
Summary: Following the death of R' Manish Wirowlianski on 21 Cheshvan 1902, R' DovBer Efrat was appointed Chabad kollel administrator in Jerusalem.
Story: On 21 Cheshvan 1903 (כ"א מ"ח תרס"ג), R' Manish Wirowlianski, the administrator of the Chabad kollel in Jerusalem, passed away. The Jerusalem Chassidim appointed R' DovBer Efrat in his place, a role he held for nearly a decade until his death.
Tags: dovber efrat, jerusalem, chabad kollel, manish wirowlianski, petira

Title: Death of R. Manish Verovlanski; Dov Ber Efrat appointed as ba'al ha'adres
Summary: On 21 Cheshvan 5663 R. Manish Verovlanski died and R. Dov Ber Efrat was appointed in his place.
Story: Following Verovlanski's death the kollel's leadership convened unanimously on Friday and chose R. Dov Ber Efrat as his successor. By tradition the appointment required approval from the network of overseas overseers, so confirmation by telegram was sought before printing new envelopes. R. Yehuda Leib Menuchin, the kollel bookkeeper, wrote that the appointment had been by full consensus.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, manish verovlanski, dov ber efrat, succession

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter on Kollel Chabad bookkeeping
Summary: A 16 Kislev 5663 letter from the Rebbe Rashab referred to R. Yehuda Leib Menuchin as the kollel's bookkeeper.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab wrote that R. Leib Menuchin was at the time serving as bookkeeper of the kollel. The reference establishes Menuchin's formal position within the institutional structure of Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem at the start of the 20th century.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, rebbe rashab, yehuda leib menuchin

Title: Cheder department opened in Tomchei Tmimim
Summary: In 5663-5664 a formal cheder department was opened in Tomchei Tmimim for younger boys.
Story: While initial discussions about opening a cheder began in summer 5662 with R' Menachem Mendel Diskin teaching eight boys, the cheder department was formally opened in 5663-5664. The Rebbe Rashab sent his brother Rashaz to Mohilev to obtain a permit assuring no government oversight of studies in the cheder. Within three years, the cheder grew into two shiur classes and three chadarim.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, cheder, diskin

Title: Hebron Yeshiva Magen Avot renewed
Summary: With the renewal of Magen Avot yeshiva in Hebron in 5663, the idea immediately arose to affiliate it with Tomchei Tmimim of Lubavitch.
Story: Upon the renewal of yeshiva Magen Avot in Hebron in 5663, R' Yaakov Yosef Slonim of Hebron raised with the future Rebbe Rayatz the possibility of affiliating it with the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva network. The Rayatz, then practical director of Tomchei Tmimim, initially deferred the idea due to upheavals in Russia, though the affiliation was implemented several years later.
Tags: hebron, magen avot, yeshiva, tomchei tmimim, rayatz

Title: Homel pogrom
Summary: Ten Jews were murdered, many wounded and significant property looted in the late-summer 1903 pogrom in Homel.
Story: Like Kishinev earlier that spring, the Homel violence enjoyed at least tacit government backing while officials blamed Jewish revolutionary activity. The two pogroms loomed over the Petersburg assembly of Jewish notables the following winter, with Plehve invoking them as an implicit threat of further violence.
Tags: belarus, homel, pogrom, tsarist russia

Title: JCA halts Mefitzei Haskalah funding mid-grant
Summary: In Adar 5663 (early 1903) the Rebbe Rashab heard that JCA had withheld the remaining 600,000 francs of the million-franc grant to Mefitzei Haskalah.
Story: After three years of sustained protest, JCA stopped releasing funds, retaining 600,000 of the original million francs allocated for the Society for Promotion of Enlightenment's schools. The Rebbe speculated in a follow-up letter that the long campaign of rabbinic protests against Mefitzei Haskalah may finally have moved the committee.
Tags: jca, ica, chevra mefitzei haskalah, paris, baron ginzburg

Title: Kishinev pogrom
Summary: Approximately 50 Jews were murdered, hundreds wounded and extensive property destroyed in the spring 1903 pogrom in Kishinev.
Story: The Russian government blamed the Jews themselves, framing the violence as a response to Jewish involvement in revolutionary movements, particularly the socialist Bund. Local officials openly or covertly encouraged the rioters, and Interior Minister Plehve later cited Kishinev as a warning to Jewish notables in St. Petersburg.
Tags: bessarabia, kishinev, pogrom, plehve, tsarist russia

Title: Lublin Haggadah 'Sefer HaZmanim' by Yaakov Leiner of Izbica
Summary: Yaakov ben Mordechai Yosef Leiner of Izbica's 'Sefer HaZmanim', including a Haggadah commentary based on the Arizal, was printed in Lublin.
Story: In 5663 (1903), Yaakov ben Mordechai Yosef Leiner of Izbica published 'Sefer HaZmanim' in Lublin, printed by Moshe Schneidmesser and the widow Nechama Hershenhorn. The first part contained essays and homilies on the month of Nissan and its laws, an explanation of the Haggadah according to the Arizal's text, and material on dew, Sefirat HaOmer, the entire Passover holiday, Iyyar, and Pesach Sheni. The 55-leaf quarto reflected the teachings of the Izbica Chassidic dynasty.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, izbica, yaakov leiner, lublin, poland

Title: Publication of Chukei Chevrat Binyan Yehuda VehaGalil
Summary: In 5663 the Jerusalem society for building shelters for needy Kollel Chabad members in Jerusalem and Hebron published its bylaws, documenting the Ohel Yitzchak gift.
Story: In Jerusalem 5663 a small 18-page pamphlet entitled 'Sefer Chukei Chevrat Binyan Yehuda VehaGalil' was published, setting out the rules of the society that built shelters for the poor of Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem and Hebron. The booklet records R' Yitzchak ben Aharon's donations for the Ohel Yitzchak beit medrash in Meah Shearim and for four adjacent kollel houses, distributed to families by lottery every three years.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, ohel yitzchak, binyan yehuda, meah shearim

Title: Rebbe Rashab reorganizes Yeshivat Magen Avot
Summary: In 5663 the Rebbe Rashab reorganized Yeshivat Magen Avot in Hebron in an attempt to revive Chassidic learning in the Holy Land.
Story: Distressed by the near-total absence of Chassidut study in the Holy Land, particularly among younger married men, the Rebbe Rashab in 5663 personally undertook to reorganize Yeshivat Magen Avot in Hebron. He hoped this would address the spiritual gap he had observed among otherwise pious students. In a letter from Elul 5663 he explained that even ardent Torah scholars in the Land knew almost nothing of Chassidut and were utterly distant from it.
Tags: hebron, chabad, rashab, yeshiva, magen avot

Title: Rebbe Rashab's internal Russian passport issued
Summary: Rebbe Rashab's internal Russian passport, recording his travels from 5663 onward, is preserved in the archive.
Story: An internal Russian passport belonging to Rebbe Rashab survives in the library archive, documenting his travels within Russia from 1903 onward.
Tags: rebbe rashab, russia, passport

Title: Renovations of great hall completed for Tomchei Tmimim
Summary: The multi-year renovation of the great hall in the Lubavitch courtyard for year-round yeshiva use was completed in 5663.
Story: Stoves had been installed, foundations and flooring renewed, and new windows fitted to make the building usable in winter. The renovated hall could now host the yeshiva's growing enrollment around its eighteen large study tables. The project transformed what had been a summer-only celebration space into the daily home of Chabad's flagship yeshiva.
Tags: tomchei-tmimim, lubavitch-courtyard

Title: Russian internal passport issued to Maharashab
Summary: The Orsha district police issued Maharashab an internal Russian passport recording his status as a hereditary honorary citizen and second-guild merchant.
Story: On 2 January 1903 (16 Tevet 5663), the Orsha district police of Mogilev Gubernia issued Sholom Berke ben Shmuel Schneersohn an internal Russian passport. The document recorded him as a hereditary honorary citizen and second-guild merchant of Orsha, aged 48, residing permanently in the town of Lubavitch. The passport's validity was restricted to the Pale of Settlement and would document his subsequent travels through 1917.
Tags: maharashab, passport, orsha, lubavitch, russia

Title: Rebbe Rashab rebukes Warsaw chassidim over splitting the minyan
Summary: On 13 Tevet 5663, the Rebbe Rashab wrote to R. Yosef Yozik objecting to his founding a separate Chabad minyan in Warsaw.
Story: When R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz established a second Chabad minyan in Warsaw apart from the existing one, the Rebbe Rashab disapproved. On 13 Tevet 5663 he wrote to him, expressing how heavily the split weighed on him because he sensed it would lead to division of hearts and machloket. The two minyanim would later become the well-known shuls at Franciscan 30 and Dzika 8.
Tags: warsaw, rebbe rashab, minyan dispute, yosef yozik horowitz

Title: Maharashab travels to Vitebsk
Summary: Maharashab's passport was stamped in Vitebsk on 4 Shevat 5663.
Story: Two and a half weeks after his passport was issued, on 19 January 1903 (4 Shevat 5663), Maharashab's internal Russian passport was stamped in Vitebsk, his first recorded trip on this document.
Tags: maharashab, vitebsk, passport, travel

Title: R' Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov becomes rabbi of Hebron
Summary: R' Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov (Shil"a) was accepted as permanent rabbi of Hebron at the beginning of Iyar 1903.
Story: At the beginning of Iyar 1903 (תחילת אייר תרס"ג), R' Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov was accepted as the permanent rabbi of Hebron, succeeding R' DovBer Efrat who had moved to Jerusalem. On 25 Iyar, R' DovBer Efrat printed a notice in HaChavatzelet redirecting all donations to be sent to the new rabbi.
Tags: shlomo yehuda leib eliezerov, shila, hebron, rabbinate, dovber efrat

Title: Jerusalem trustees report partial implementation of Rashab's school ruling
Summary: On 4 Nisan 5663 the Jerusalem trustees informed the gabbaim abroad that beard-shavers and parents sending children to secular schools received only one-third of their chalukah.
Story: After a year of correspondence about how strictly to apply the Rebbe Rashab's ruling, the Jerusalem trustees reported that those violating the standards had now received only a third of their normal portion. They pushed back on the gabbaim's complaint that these recipients had been paid before God-fearing poor families, asserting that the God-fearing poor had in fact been paid first.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, rashab, schools, chalukah, yaakov ornstein

Title: Rebbe Rashab approves Eliezerov as Rabbi of Hebron
Summary: On 21 Iyar 5663 the Rashab wrote to the Sdei Chemed in Hebron formally approving Rabbi Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov as Rabbi of the Hebron Chabad community.
Story: The Rashab had earlier received a petition from Hebron residents demanding a rabbi from outside the city; though he disagreed, he had stepped back rather than impose his choice.
