When the community itself converged on Eliezerov, he sent an immediate telegram of approval and a long letter the next day to Eliezerov himself.
Tags: hebron, eliezerov, rashab, sdei chemed, rabbinate

Title: Rebbe Rashab declines to move Slonim from Yafo
Summary: On 22 Iyar 5663, the Rebbe Rashab wrote that R' Shneur Zalman Slonim could not be moved from Yafo to lead a new Jerusalem yeshiva.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab had wanted to appoint R' Shneur Zalman to oversee a new Chabad yeshiva in Jerusalem, but worried that leaving Yafo after three years of intense work there would unravel everything he had built. He concluded that pulling him out would undo the essential reforms he had instituted.
Tags: rashab, yafo, jerusalem, yeshiva, shneur zalman slonim

Title: Chabad community of Jaffa announces construction of its synagogue
Summary: On 24 Iyar 5663 the heads of Kollel Chabad announced that the Anash synagogue in Jaffa had been built up to and including the dome.
Story: On 24 Iyar 5663, leaders of Kollel Chabad recorded in the kollel pinkas that 'in Jaffa Anash are building a beis midrash, and it is already complete up to and including the dome; finishing touches remain.' This was the first synagogue dedicated to Chabad chassidim in Jaffa.
Tags: jaffa, synagogue, kollel chabad

Title: Report on attendance at Ohel Yitzchak beit medrash
Summary: In mid-Tamuz 5663 Kollel Chabad director R' Yehuda Leib Menuchin reported that only five Anash plus about ten other Jews were studying at Ohel Yitzchak.
Story: R' Yehuda Leib Menuchin, the administrator of Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem, wrote in mid-Tamuz 5663 that he had sent the shamash Shalom Yaakov to Ohel Yitzchak the previous Shabbat to attend R' Yaakov ben Tzvi Trisspolsky's class and report on activity there. The report counted five Chabad members and more than ten other Jews regularly present in the beit medrash. Attendance would later grow significantly as Jews moved from the Old City to the new neighborhoods.
Tags: jerusalem, meah shearim, ohel yitzchak, kollel chabad, menuchin

Title: Tsarist secret committee opens review of Jewish laws
Summary: A secret committee under the Minister of the Interior was formed to review Russia's Jewish laws; a circular went out in August 1903 soliciting opinions from provincial governors.
Story: On the eve of Sukkot 5664, the Rebbe Rashab wrote to R. Yeshaya Berlin urging him to use his contacts to influence the governors' replies before the October 1 deadline. The committee, chaired by Interior Minister Vyacheslav Plehve, convened in early January 1904 to weigh partial easings of the Pale alongside new restrictions.
Tags: russia, plehve, pale of settlement, interior ministry, rashab

Title: Eliezerov publishes public appeal for Hebron Chabad institutions
Summary: In Elul 5663 the new Rabbi Eliezerov and the Sdei Chemed issued a printed appeal warning that the Hebron community was on the brink of collapse.
Story: The flyer described Hebron Jews silently bearing extreme poverty, without the energetic shadarim that other communities sent abroad. The signers begged donors to support the Magen Avos yeshiva, the children's Talmud Torah, and homes of shelter for the destitute who could not afford rent.
Tags: hebron, eliezerov, sdei chemed, fundraising, poverty, magen avos

Title: Rashab general letter on Jerusalem yeshiva leadership
Summary: On 14 Elul 5663, the Rebbe Rashab issued a general letter announcing that R' Shneur Zalman Slonim would supervise the Jerusalem yeshiva's studies.
Story: After deliberating throughout the summer, the Rebbe Rashab decided to prioritize the Jerusalem yeshiva over the Yafo rabbinate. In his general letter to chasidim, he announced that R' Shneur Zalman would oversee both the nigleh and chassidus learning. For unknown reasons, however, the plan never came to fruition.
Tags: rashab, jerusalem, yeshiva, shneur zalman slonim

Title: Rashab's letter on the decline of Chassidus study in Eretz Yisrael
Summary: In an epistle dated 14 Elul 5663, the Rashab lamented the collapse of Chassidus study among Chabad avreichim in Eretz Yisrael and welcomed the new initiative to open Chabad yeshivas in Jerusalem and Hebron.
Story: The Rashab described how Chassidus study in Eretz Yisrael had reached its lowest ebb, with young Chabad avreichim studying in Perushim yeshivas instead. He expressed deep distress at the situation but rejoiced that a spirit of purification had stirred his followers there to establish Chabad yeshivas in Jerusalem and Hebron. This letter contextualizes the simultaneous push to found dedicated Chabad institutions in the Holy Land.
Tags: rashab, eretz yisrael, chassidus, kollel chabad, yeshiva

Title: Maskilic press attacks planned Grodno rabbinical assembly
Summary: Throughout Cheshvan-Kislev 5664, the Hebrew newspaper Ha-Melitz (issues 228, 242, 255) and the Russian Novosti published protests and articles attacking the planned Grodno Orthodox rabbinical assembly.
Story: When word of the planned Grodno assembly reached Haskalah circles, they launched a press campaign to discredit it, publishing protests in Ha-Melitz, Novosti, and other outlets. The Rebbe Rashab described the Hebrew papers as 'shouting and barking,' while R. Eliyahu Akiva Rabinovich answered the attacks in the journal Ha-Peles (Tevet 5664). The Maskilim also planted false reports that prominent rabbis like the Lodzer Rav Maizel and rabbis of Dvinsk and Plotsk were withdrawing from the assembly.
Tags: russia, grodno, haskalah, ha-melitz, novosti, rabbinical assembly

Title: R' Sh.Y.L. Eliezerov leaves Hebron for Europe and Russia
Summary: Hebron Ashkenazi chief rabbi Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov leaves Hebron for what was announced as a several-month fundraising trip abroad.
Story: On 26 Marcheshvan 5664 (November 15, 1903), Hebron Ashkenazi rabbi Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov departed his city to travel abroad on behalf of Hebron's institutions, especially the Magen Avot yeshiva. R' Yaakov Yosef Slonim's farewell address in HaChavatzelet spoke of a few months' absence, but the trip in fact lasted over two years. Eliezerov went first to Lubavitch to consult the Rashab on improving Hebron's material and spiritual state.
Tags: hebron, eliezerov, shadar, lubavitch, magen avot

Title: Eighty rabbis invited to Grodno religious assembly
Summary: By early winter 5664 (around 5 Kislev), serious preparations were underway for an official assembly of approximately eighty Orthodox rabbis in Grodno, formally convened by R. Eliyahu Akiva Rabinovich of Poltava.
Story: After years of failed attempts, real preparations finally materialized in 5664 to convene an assembly of Orthodox rabbis under government authorization in Grodno. R. Eliyahu Akiva Rabinovich of Poltava served as the official convener, and the proposal had the backing of R. Chaim Soloveitchik of Brisk. The Rebbe Rashab proposed a preliminary smaller gathering of senior rabbis to define an agenda before the main assembly.
Tags: russia, grodno, rashab, rabbinical assembly, eliyahu akiva rabinovich, poltava

Title: Baron Ginzburg intervenes to block Grodno assembly
Summary: In Tevet 5664 (early January 1904), Baron Naftali Hertz Ginzburg met with the Russian Minister of the Interior on behalf of Haskalah circles, successfully derailing authorization for the Grodno rabbinical assembly.
Story: When press attacks and denunciations failed to block the Grodno assembly, Haskalah leaders dispatched Baron Naftali Hertz Ginzburg to lobby the Minister of the Interior directly. According to Ginzburg's report, he had turned the minister against the assembly by arguing that the invitees were rabbis from minor towns. Rebbe Rashab lamented in letters dated 3-8 Tevet that this exposed how far the power of those opposed to Orthodox interests had grown.
Tags: russia, grodno, naftali hertz ginzburg, minister of interior, haskalah, rabbinical assembly

Title: R. Shmuel Zalmanov born in Warsaw
Summary: R. Shmuel Zalmanov was born in Warsaw on the 8th of Tevet 5664.
Story: Shmuel Zalmanov, who would later become a senior figure in Tomchei Tmimim, editor of Hatamim, and head of Nichoach in New York, was born in Warsaw on 8 Tevet 5664. He first attended the yeshiva only for Chassidus studies when it opened in summer 5681, and entered as a full student in summer 5684.
Tags: warsaw, poland, shmuel zalmanov, biography

Title: Rashab delivers 19 Kislev 1903 discourse (later printed in Torat Shalom)
Summary: On 19 Kislev 5664 (Dec 1903) the Rebbe Rashab discussed the letter of R. Levi Yitzchok about the Maggid's high regard for the Alter Rebbe.
Story: The Rashab cited the letter and noted its unusual phrasing — 'I did not hear' rather than 'I do not know' — calling it a wonder. The discourse was later printed in 'Torat Shalom' and is the source of an enduring puzzle about R. Levi Yitzchok's wording.
Tags: rashab, torat shalom, 19 kislev, alter rebbe, levi yitzchok of berditchev

Title: Hebron Vaad correspondence dated 14 Kislev
Summary: Hebron Vaad stationery preserved in the Shila Archive bears a letter dated 14 Kislev 5664.
Story: A photograph of the Hebron Vaad's letterhead from the Shila Archive includes a letter dated 14 Kislev 5664 that appears unrelated to the Vaad itself. The stationery printed the official name of the Vaad and the address of the Ashkenazi rabbi.
Tags: hebron, vaad, shila archive

Title: Denunciations sent against Grodno rabbinical assembly
Summary: By 17 Kislev 5664, two written denunciations had reached the Grodno governor's office, sent from Kovno and Bialystok, accusing the assembled rabbis of seeking to bring 'darkness' upon the world.
Story: Opponents of the Orthodox rabbinical assembly escalated their resistance by sending official denunciations to Grodno authorities. Rebbe Rashab condemned the audacity, noting that beyond the threat to the assembly itself, the rabbis were being publicly disgraced before the gentiles. Despite this, the bureaucratic process for authorization continued; the governor had requested files on each registered participant and the permit was expected within roughly two weeks.
Tags: russia, grodno, rashab, kovno, bialystok, denunciation, rabbinical assembly

Title: Death of R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum's wife in America
Summary: R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum's wife died in 5664 in America, leaving him with his youngest son Yosef.
Story: R' Yehoshua Kastrel wrote a letter of condolence to R' Avraham Chaim in 5664 (1904), noting that he presumed Avraham Chaim was now living with his youngest son Yosef, who had married in America. Kastrel admitted he barely knew either the deceased wife or Yosef personally.
Tags: america, new york, rosenbaum, death

Title: Death of Yetta Rosenbaum in New York
Summary: In 5664 Yetta Rosenbaum, wife of Reb Avraham Chaim, died after four months of severe illness, in a year of major financial losses for the family.
Story: In the course of 5664 Reb Avraham Chaim's wife Yetta lay ill for about four months before she died, and he expended over 1,000 dollars on her medical care. In the same year his diamond business lost nearly 2,000 dollars when merchandise from Germany failed to arrive, together amounting to roughly three-quarters of his savings in his old age.
Tags: america, new york, death, family, rosenbaum

Title: Fifth edition of Likkutei Torah printed in Vilna
Summary: The Rashab's carefully corrected fifth edition of Likkutei Torah was printed at the Romm press in Vilna in תרס"ד, with extensive new hagahot and a 'mode'ah rabbah' explaining the proofing effort.
Story: After two years of intensive proofing — by R' Shmuel Sofer (Rabinowitz) and the Rashab personally, drawing on original manuscripts and reliable copies — the fifth edition appeared in Vilna in תרס"ד. A 'mode'ah rabbah' was inserted noting newly added hagahot that had been omitted from earlier editions due to copyist errors, and a corrections list (luach hatikun) was added at the end of part two.
Tags: rashab, likkutei torah, vilna, romm press, shmuel sofer

Title: Knesses Beis Yitzchak hires Rabbi Baruch Ber Leibowitz
Summary: Rabbi Baruch Ber Leibowitz was hired as rosh yeshivah of Knesses Beis Yitzchak in Slabodka.
Story: In 1904, Knesses Beis Yitzchak in Slabodka hired Rabbi Baruch Ber Leibowitz to lead the yeshivah. He would later relocate the yeshivah to Vilna in 1921 and to Kamenitz in 1926, becoming one of the most influential Lithuanian roshei yeshivah of the era.
Tags: baruch ber leibowitz, knesses beis yitzchak, slabodka, rosh yeshivah

Title: Ladino Haggadah with Hebrew commentary printed in Livorno
Summary: An illustrated Ladino-translation Haggadah, including Maariv prayers and Shir HaShirim, was printed in Livorno.
Story: In 5664 (1904), Shlomo Belforte & Co. printed a Haggadah in Livorno with Ladino translation and several illustrations. Maariv prayers were appended along with Shir HaShirim. The 42-leaf volume served the Ladino-speaking Mediterranean Sephardic community.
Tags: haggadah, ladino, livorno, italy, sephardic, shir hashirim

Title: Likutei Torah printed in Vilna
Summary: In 5664 the Rebbe Rashab oversaw the printing of Likutei Torah in Vilna at the Romm press, again through R. Anshil Aronovich.
Story: Aronovich, who worked at the Romm printing house, conducted all the negotiations on the Rashab's behalf. His role as the Rebbe's representative in Vilna would later be formally acknowledged in the 'Modaah Rabbah' notice printed in later Tanya editions.
Tags: likutei torah, vilna, 5664, anshil aronovich, rashab, romm press

Title: Persian translation Haggadah 'Chukat HaPesach' for Bukharian Jews printed in Jerusalem
Summary: Shimon Hakham translated the 'Chukat HaPesach' Haggadah into Persian to serve the Bukharian Jewish community of Jerusalem.
Story: In 5664 (1904), 'Chukat HaPesach' was printed in Jerusalem by Shmuel HaLevi Zuckerman, featuring readings for the entire month of Nissan, the Korban Pesach with an extract from Shimshon of Ostropoli, and a Persian translation of the Haggadah by Shimon Hakham. The 68-page work also included tales and songs related to Pesach intended to benefit the Bukharian Jewish community. A separately titled Persian translation of Shir HaShirim was appended at the end.
Tags: haggadah, persian, jerusalem, bukhara, shimon hakham

Title: RA"Ch's wife dies after long illness in New York
Summary: In 5664 RA"Ch's wife of his youth passes away after roughly four months of severe illness, depleting much of his savings.
Story: Writing on Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni 5665, RA"Ch recounts that in the preceding year, 5664, his wife of his youth had died after lying on a sickbed for some four months, with over a thousand dollars spent on her care. Earlier that same year he had lost nearly two thousand dollars when goods from Germany failed to arrive, together amounting to roughly three-quarters of the savings he had built up in his old age.
Tags: new york, usa, family, illness, widower

Title: Rabbi Avraham Yitzchak Kook becomes rabbi of Jaffa
Summary: Rabbi Kook moved from Russia to Eretz Yisrael, becoming rabbi of Jaffa.
Story: Kook, whose mother came from a Chabad family, was known for his scholarship and his efforts to bridge Jews of all backgrounds. He would later be appointed the first chief rabbi by the British Mandate in 1929.
Tags: rav-kook, jaffa, aliyah

Title: Rabbi Baruch Ber Leibowitz appointed rosh yeshivah of Knesses Beis Yitzchak
Summary: Rabbi Baruch Ber Leibowitz was hired as rosh yeshivah of Knesses Beis Yitzchak in Slabodka.
Story: Rabbi Baruch Ber became one of the most influential Lithuanian rosh yeshivos of his era. He would later move the yeshivah to Vilna in 1921 and to Kamenitz in 1926, where it became known as the famed Kamenitz yeshivah.
Tags: baruch ber leibowitz, knesses beis yitzchak, slabodka, lithuanian yeshivah

Title: Russo-Japanese War breaks out
Summary: War broke out between Russia and Japan over control of Manchuria and Korea, drafting thousands of Jewish soldiers.
Story: In 1904, conflict erupted between Russia and Japan, conscripting thousands of Jewish soldiers into the Russian army for two years before an inglorious Russian defeat. The Rashab and Rayatz launched a campaign to provide Passover supplies to the Jewish troops on the Far East front.
Tags: russia, japan, war, manchuria, korea, jewish soldiers

Title: Russo-Japanese War breaks out over Manchuria and Korea
Summary: War broke out between Japan and Russia over control of the Far East regions of Manchuria and Korea.
Story: Thousands of Jewish soldiers were enlisted in the Russian army and fought for two years before Russia's inglorious defeat. The Rashab was concerned about Jewish soldiers far from home with no food or matzah for Passover, prompting him to launch initiatives to provide for their religious needs.
Tags: russia, japan, war, manchuria, korea

Title: Birth of Rebbetzin Sheina, daughter of Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: Rebbetzin Sheina, youngest daughter of the Rebbe Rayatz, was born on the night of Shabbat Shemot, 21 Tevet 5664.
Story: The 5705 Motzaei Shabbat Shemot diary entry records the birth of the Rebbe Rayatz's daughter Sheina forty-one years earlier, on the night of Shabbat Kodesh Shemot 5664 (January 1904), at the twelfth hour of the night. The Rebbe spent three hours that night reconstructing every detail of her birth in his memory, then wept over not knowing where Sheina and her husband Menachem Mendel — son of his cousin Chaya Mushka — then were, and prayed for their safety among the rest of Israel.
Tags: sheina, rayatz, birth, parshat shemot

Title: R' Yehoshua Kostral writes from San Remo consoling Rosenbaum
Summary: On 7 Shevat 5664 R' Yehoshua Kostral wrote from San Remo consoling Rosenbaum on his wife's death and gently suggesting that he ought to consider remarriage.
Story: From San Remo on 7 Shevat 5664, R' Yehoshua Kostral acknowledged Rosenbaum's letter informing him of Yetta's passing. He admitted he scarcely knew the deceased or Rosenbaum's American household and so could hardly comfort him, yet he urged that 'you are not yet old' and that sitting alone is impossible—he should seek a second match.
Tags: italy, san remo, yehoshua kostral, consolation

Title: R' Yehoshua Kostral writes RA"Ch a letter of consolation
Summary: From San Remo, R' Yehoshua Kostral writes RA"Ch a letter of consolation on the loss of his wife and broaches the question of remarriage.
Story: On 7 Shevat 5664, from San Remo, Italy, R' Yehoshua Kostral wrote to RA"Ch to console him on the death of his wife, lamenting that he hardly knew who shared RA"Ch's home in America — perhaps his younger son R' Yosef who had married there. He gently raised the question of remarriage, noting RA"Ch was not yet old enough to live alone.
Tags: yehoshua kostral, san remo, italy, letter, consolation, remarriage, yosef rosenbaum

Title: Plehve rebukes Jewish notables in St. Petersburg
Summary: Interior Minister Plehve summoned ten leaders of the Petersburg Jewish assembly, led by Baron Ginzburg, and warned that another Kishinev-style pogrom could recur.
Story: Plehve rebuked the delegation over Jewish youth involvement in revolutionary movements, the alienating effect of Russian schooling on Jewish students, and the agitation of the foreign Hebrew press. He linked any easing of residency laws to internal Jewish reform and explicitly threatened a repeat of the 1903 Kishinev and Homel pogroms. The Rebbe Rashab, then in Paris, received the verbatim transcript with alarm and demanded active community response.
Tags: russia, plehve, petersburg, baron ginzburg, kishinev, homel, zionism, rashab

Title: Rashab appoints R' Eleazar Moshe Madiyevsky to head Hebron committee
Summary: On 15 Shvat 5664 the Rashab writes asking R' Eleazar Moshe Madiyevsky to head a Russia-based committee for Hebron.
Story: On 15 Shvat 5664 (February 1, 1904), the Rashab dispatched R' Sh.Y.L. Eliezerov to R' Eleazar Moshe Madiyevsky with a personal letter asking him to head a new Russia-based committee dedicated to improving conditions in Hebron. The discussions stretched on for a year and a half before the Vaad Chevroni was finally constituted in the summer of 1905.
Tags: rashab, madiyevsky, hebron, vaad chevroni

Title: Slonim writes Shiloh on remaining in Yafo
Summary: On 2 Adar 5664, R' Shneur Zalman Slonim wrote to R' Shiloh that he had concluded he must remain in Yafo despite earlier plans to move to Jerusalem.
Story: R' Shneur Zalman had initially expected to relocate to Jerusalem per the Rebbe's decision, but was told not to move without explicit instruction from the Rebbe himself. He recounted the hardships of his arrival in Yafo, observed that the community now had a clear path forward, and accepted that his lot was to remain in Yafo.
Tags: yafo, jerusalem, shneur zalman slonim, shiloh

Title: Slonim notes lack of confirmation on Jerusalem move
Summary: On 18 Iyar 5664, R' Shneur Zalman Slonim wrote again to R' Shiloh that he had still received no clarifying word about relocating to Jerusalem.
Story: Although he had been told the Rebbe Rashab had decided he should settle in Jerusalem, he was also instructed not to move until receiving definitive word. By 18 Iyar 5664 no such word had come, confirming that he would remain in Yafo as rabbi.
Tags: yafo, jerusalem, shneur zalman slonim, shiloh

Title: R' Leib Menuchin letter on Tzfat yeshiva proposal
Summary: On 15 Sivan 5664, R' Leib Menuchin wrote to Kollel Chabad administrators abroad opposing R' Asher Yechezkel Horowitz's plan to open a yeshiva in Tzfat.
Story: R' Asher Yechezkel hoped to open a Chabad yeshiva in Tzfat headed by his son R' Yeshaya. R' Leib Menuchin advised the kollel's overseas administrators that the kollel's funds should not be used for this venture. The yeshiva ultimately did not come to fruition.
Tags: tzfat, yeshiva, kollel chabad, asher yechezkel horowitz

Title: Romm Vilna invoice for printing Likkutei Torah issued
Summary: The Romm publishing house in Vilna issued an invoice on 7 June 1904 (8 Menachem Av תרס"ד) totaling 2,801.71 rubles for the printing of Likkutei Torah on Vayikra, Bamidbar, Devarim and Shir HaShirim.
Story: The detailed invoice from Romm's Vilna press itemized paper costs for 1,900 and 1,500 copies of the two volumes, printing fees, plate costs, binding (covers), and corrections. Against advance payments totaling 1,100 rubles in 1902-1903, a balance of 1,701.71 rubles remained owed as of the invoice date.
Tags: vilna, romm press, likkutei torah, rashab

Title: Rayatz writes to Yaakov Yosef Slonim about buying books in Eretz Yisrael
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz writes the first of several letters to R. Yaakov Yosef Slonim arranging the purchase of rare seforim through dealers in the Holy Land.
Story: On the Tuesday of Parashas Pinchas 5664, Rayatz sends Slonim a list of 47 books he is willing to buy from a Jerusalem dealer for 92 rubles and 40 kopeks, asking him to negotiate the prices down. He emphasizes interest specifically in old editions and requests that the seller send lists of antique seforim, not new ones. He also asks Slonim to obtain addresses of dealers in Algiers, where he had heard cheap acquisitions were possible.
Tags: library, rayatz, eretz-yisrael, letters, book-collecting

Title: R' Alter Simchowitz comes to Lubavitch to study
Summary: In Cheshvan 5665 R' Chaim Alter Nisan Shimon Simchowitz arrived in Lubavitch to study at Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: Born in Pochep around 5650, Simchowitz had first studied at the yeshiva of R' Tzvi Netta Gnessin in Pochep, whose graduates often progressed to Tomchei Tmimim. After arriving in Lubavitch he spent time in the preparatory program in Horodisht before joining the main yeshiva hall.
Tags: lubavitch, alter simchowitz, horodisht, tzvi netta gnessin

Title: Maharashab travels to Petersburg
Summary: Maharashab traveled to Petersburg, his passport recording the stamp dated 8 Kislev 5665.
Story: On 3 November 1904 (8 Kislev 5665), Maharashab's passport was stamped in Petersburg. Petersburg lay outside the Pale of Settlement, and his repeated visits there reflect his merchant status that allowed him such travel.
Tags: maharashab, petersburg, passport, travel

Title: Death of R' Chizkiyah Medini (Sdei Chemed)
Summary: R' Chizkiyah Medini, author of the Sdei Chemed, died on 24 Kislev 5665 in the Romano mansion in Hebron.
Story: R' Chizkiyah Medini died on 24 Kislev 5665 in the Romano mansion in Hebron, where he had lived and taught since his arrival in 5661. He passed away while still engaged in his Torah study and writing. His monumental halachic encyclopedia, the Sdei Chemed, was completed during his years in that house, and the yeshiva later established there was named in his honor.
Tags: hebron, sdei chemed, medini

Title: Rayatz forwards Nachum Etrog's Jerusalem book list to Slonim
Summary: On erev Shabbos Vayetze 5665, Rayatz sends R. Yaakov Yosef Slonim a long list of seforim he wants to purchase from the Jerusalem dealer Nachum Etrog.
Story: Rayatz writes that he has obtained an extensive list from Nachum Etrog in Jerusalem and is sending it to Slonim with prices marked according to his own knowledge and his various catalogs. He explains his priorities: the chief interest is rare books from first printings, with Kabbalah works first, then responsa, then poskim. He also urges Slonim to search the genizah of Jerusalem — and especially Chevron — for manuscripts of the Chabad Rebbes, particularly the Mitteler Rebbe.
Tags: library, jerusalem, rayatz, letters, book-collecting, nachum-etrog

Title: Eliezerov reports cholera outbreak in Caucasus from Samarkand
Summary: Writing from Samarkand on 3 Tevet 5665, Eliezerov reports a cholera outbreak in the Caucasus disrupting his mission.
Story: From Samarkand in Bukhara on 3 Tevet 5665 (December 11, 1904), Eliezerov wrote to his brother-in-law R' M.M. Naeh that this trip had been the hardest of his four missions combined. He had agreed to take on the Caucasus mission for the Sephardic community but cholera had broken out there, forcing him to plan a return route via Baku and Georgia if possible, otherwise straight back to Lubavitch as the Rashab had instructed.
Tags: samarkand, bukhara, caucasus, cholera, eliezerov, shadar

Title: Chinese Matzah Campaign for Russian soldiers
Summary: The Rashab and Rayatz secured permission and supplies to ship Passover matzah to Jewish soldiers in the Far East.
Story: Building on a limited 1904 attempt, in 1905 the Rashab and Rayatz mounted a far larger effort to provide Passover matzah and supplies to Jewish soldiers fighting on the Russo-Japanese front. Despite anti-Semitic government obstruction and immense logistical challenges, they obtained permission and distributed supplies across the Far East front.
Tags: passover, matzah, russo-japanese war, soldiers, far east

Title: Covert rabbinic meeting in St. Petersburg over Russian pogroms
Summary: The Rayatz participated in a covert summer meeting of prominent rabbinic leaders in St. Petersburg to strategize against the wave of pogroms across Russia.
Story: The 25-year-old Rayatz was dispatched to Western Europe to meet famous statesmen of Germany and Holland, persuading them and foreign bankers to apply pressure and economic sanctions on the Russian government. He proved himself as a modern shtadlan capable of advocacy on the international Jewish scene.
Tags: st petersburg, pogroms, rabbinic meeting, rayatz

Title: Covert rabbinic strategy meeting in St. Petersburg
Summary: The Rayatz attended a covert rabbinic strategy meeting in St. Petersburg to address the wave of pogroms.
Story: In the summer of 1905, the Rayatz joined a clandestine meeting of prominent rabbinic leaders in St. Petersburg to develop a response to the pogroms erupting across Russia. He was subsequently dispatched to Western Europe to enlist German and Dutch statesmen and foreign bankers to pressure the Russian government.
Tags: st petersburg, pogroms, rabbinic meeting, rayatz

Title: Matzah campaign delivers Passover supplies to Jewish soldiers in Far East
Summary: After failed efforts the previous year, the Rashab and Rayatz secured permission and shipped Passover supplies to Jewish soldiers throughout the Far East front.
Story: Facing obstacles of an anti-Semitic regime, the need for a broad Jewish coalition, logistical nightmares of shipping thousands of miles, and securing funding, the Rashab and Rayatz intensified the effort. After much work, czarist permission was obtained and Passover supplies were distributed to soldiers dispersed across a vast geographical area.
Tags: passover, russo-japanese war, soldiers, matzah, rashab, rayatz

Title: R' Chaim Aba Veil begins shul attendance in Dvinsk
Summary: R' Chaim Aba Veil began praying as a child in Dvinsk's 'Painters' Synagogue' in 5665 (1905).
Story: In 5665 (1905) the young Chaim Aba Veil started accompanying adults to the 'Farbershe Minyan' — the Painters' Synagogue on the Zhitomir Street in the Pletzer district of Dvinsk. Founded originally by the city's painters, it had become by then a leading Chabad shul, and existed until the Nazi destruction.
Tags: dvinsk, latvia, painters-minyan, childhood

Title: R' Shneur Zalman Rosenbaum's American shliach mission for Tomchei Tmimim
Summary: R' Shneur Zalman Rosenbaum was sent by the Rebbe Rashab to America to fundraise for the Tomchei Tmimim yeshivos.
Story: R' Avraham Chaim wrote on Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni 5665 (1905) that his brother R' Shneur Zalman had arrived in New York as an emissary of the Lubavitcher Rebbe to raise funds for the yeshivos. R' Shneur Zalman traveled through New York, Philadelphia, New Haven, Hartford, Springfield, and Boston, and R' Avraham Chaim asked whether he should also visit Rochester. The mission supported the four-city yeshiva network that had been founded six years earlier.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, america, new york, fundraising, shliach, rosenbaum

Title: Rabbinic conference establishes 'Vaad HaChevronim' to expand pushke network
Summary: In summer 5665 prominent Chabad rabbis convened on the affairs of the Rambahn fund; Rebbe Rashab decided to create a dedicated 'Chevronim' vaad to oversee Eretz Yisrael donations.
Story: The conference, later described by Rebbe Maharayatz, sought ways to improve the income flowing to Kollel Chabad through R. Meir Baal HaNes pushkes. Rebbe Rashab concluded that a specialized oversight body, named the 'Chevronim', was needed to closely monitor donations. The vaad's first priority was to install pushkes in every Jewish home across Russia.
Tags: chevronim, rambahn, fundraising, pushke, shoferos

Title: Rashab founds Va'ad HaChevroni to protect Hebron Chabad community
Summary: In summer 5665 the Rebbe Rashab founded the Va'ad HaChevroni abroad to defend Hebron's share of Kollel Chabad funds against Jerusalem's growing dominance.
Story: After the kollel's center shifted from Hebron to Jerusalem, the Hebron Chabad community declined economically as Jerusalem-based administrators favored their own city. The Rashab established the Va'ad HaChevroni to advocate for Hebron's rights abroad and demanded that a Hebron representative be included among the official signatories receiving kollel funds. He saw protecting Hebron as essential to maintaining the legacy of his predecessors who had specifically chosen Hebron.
Tags: hebron, rashab, kollel chabad, fundraising, jerusalem rivalry

Title: Rayatz organizes Passover fund for Russian troops in the Far East
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak helped organize a fund to provide Passover supplies for Jewish soldiers in the Russian army deployed to the Far East.
Story: During the Russo-Japanese War, Jewish soldiers serving far from home faced enormous difficulty observing Passover. The Rayatz participated in organizing logistical and financial support to bring matzah and other holiday needs to these troops.
Tags: passover, russo-japanese war, russian army, jewish soldiers

Title: Reshag becomes chief mashpia in Lubavitch
Summary: Around summer 5665, R' Shmuel Gronem (Reshag) Esterman moved from Zembin to Lubavitch as chief mashpia.
Story: Following the passing of the Rashbatz on 15 Sivan 5665, R' Shmuel Gronem (Reshag) Esterman was appointed chief mashpia of Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch in summer 5665 (1905). The Rebbe Rashab wrote on 15 Menachem-Av 5665 that with Reshag's arrival in Lubavitch, the study of chassidut rose to new heights. He served until his passing in 5681.
Tags: esterman, reshag, tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, zembin

Title: Royal decree on religious tolerance
Summary: On 17 Tevet 5665 the Tsar issued a decree with eight clauses, the sixth dealing with religious tolerance.
Story: On 17 Tevet 5665 (1905), the Russian Tsar issued an eight-clause decree, the sixth clause of which directed administrative measures to remove obstacles to religious practice for various faiths. This decree raised hopes for the Rebbe Rashab that the Yavneh society he wished to establish to legalize Tomchei Tmimim would now be approved, though it ultimately was not.
Tags: russia, religious tolerance, tomchei tmimim

Title: Tzemach Tzedek additions printed in Vilna Shulchan Aruch
Summary: A new Vilna edition of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch was printed in 5665, including additional Tzemach Tzedek responsa across all four chelkei Shulchan Aruch that had been discovered in the intervening twenty years.
Story: Between 5645 and 5665, additional responsa of the Tzemach Tzedek covering all four sections of Shulchan Aruch came to light. Rather than issue a separate supplement, the editors of the 5665 Vilna edition of Shulchan Aruch HaRav incorporated them as an appendix to that printing — making the new Vilna edition an essential reference for halachic researchers.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, shulchan aruch harav, vilna

Title: Rashab urges second Petersburg assembly to prioritize material relief
Summary: On 17 Shevat 5665, Rebbe Rashab wrote that delegates to Baron Ginzburg's new Petersburg assembly must demand residency and land-purchase rights rather than university access.
Story: The Rebbe warned that the assembly's lawyers and freethinkers would prioritize educational equality while neglecting Jews' physical survival. He pressed instead for the right to live anywhere in Russia, including villages, and for every Jew to be allowed to purchase at least fifty desyatinas of land in any locality.
Tags: russia, petersburg, baron ginzburg, pale of settlement, rashab

Title: Future Rebbe Rayatz defers Hebron yeshiva affiliation due to Russian unrest
Summary: On 5 Adar II 5665 the future Rebbe Rayatz wrote R' Yaakov Yosef Slonim of Hebron that adding another branch to Tomchei Tmimim was difficult given internal Russian upheavals.
Story: In response to a Hebron request to add Magen Avot as a branch of Tomchei Tmimim, the Rayatz explained that the present year's 'great storms in our country, from within and from without'—a reference to the 1905 Russian Revolution upheavals—made expansion impossible. He expressed hope that with God's help fruitful approaches would emerge.
Tags: lubavitch, hebron, rayatz, tomchei tmimim, yaakov yosef slonim, russia

Title: Rayatz sends Slonim third book list extending to letter mem
Summary: On the 2nd of Adar Sheni 5665, the Rebbe Rayatz sends Slonim the continuation of book lists, now covering through letter mem.
Story: This third surviving letter in the Slonim correspondence shows that Rayatz's book-acquisition project in the Holy Land was systematic and alphabetical. The lists were being worked through letter by letter, with only the first installment (alef to ches) preserved in detail and this letter extending the project through mem.
Tags: library, rayatz, letters, book-collecting

Title: RA"Ch describes year of financial and personal losses
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni 5665 RA"Ch writes describing the preceding year's losses — his wife's death and major business setbacks.
Story: In a letter dated Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni 5665, RA"Ch reflects on a punishing previous year: the death of his wife after a four-month illness on which he spent over a thousand dollars, and a separate loss of nearly two thousand dollars in his business when goods failed to arrive from Germany. Together, he writes, these consumed about three-quarters of all the savings he had accumulated in his later years.
Tags: new york, usa, loss, letter, business, germany imports

Title: Rosenbaum recounts losses and widowhood in Rosh Chodesh Adar II letter
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Adar II 5665 Rosenbaum wrote describing the death of his wife and major business losses, and reported on his brother R' Zalman's fundraising tour for Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: On Rosh Chodesh Adar II 5665 Reb Avraham Chaim summarized the previous year: his wife of his youth had died after a four-month illness costing over 1,000 dollars, his diamond business had lost nearly 2,000 more, and he had been visited by his brother R' Shneur Zalman Rosenbaum, dispatched by the Rebbe Rashab as an emissary for the Tomchei Tmimim yeshivas. He noted with pride his brother's success in raising funds in New York and Philadelphia.
Tags: america, new york, rosenbaum, tomchei tmimim

Title: Death of R. Dov Ber Fradkin
Summary: R. Dov Ber Fradkin, son of the author of Torat Chesed, died on 17 Adar Sheni 5665.
Story: Fradkin had been added to the roster of kollel trustees as an honorary member, signing letters of the kollel out of respect for the institution's prestige. His role brought distinction without operational responsibilities, as he was not directly engaged in the kollel's affairs. His death further consolidated the active leadership around Shlonk, Efrat, Menuchin, and Ornstein.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, dov ber fradkin, torat chesed

Title: Death of Rashbatz Sheftel
Summary: R' Shmuel Betzalel (Rashbatz) Sheftel, chief mashpia at Tomchei Tmimim, passed away on 15 Sivan 5665.
Story: R' Shmuel Betzalel (Rashbatz) Sheftel passed away on 15 Sivan 5665 (1905), after serving as chief mashpia at Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch for five years. Following his death, R' Shmuel Gronem Esterman (Reshag) from Zembin was appointed in his place. The Zembin branch was simultaneously closed.
Tags: rashbatz, sheftel, tomchei tmimim, mashpia

Title: R' Moshe Mordechai Chaikin visits Hebron for father-in-law's yahrzeit
Summary: On 27 Sivan 5665 Moshe Mordechai Chaikin wrote from Hebron noting his annual arrival with his mother for R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin's yahrzeit.
Story: R' Moshe Mordechai Chaikin, stepson and son-in-law of R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, came each year from Jerusalem with his mother Devorah for the yahrzeit. His 27 Sivan 5665 letter to ShILA from Hebron mentioned the upcoming yahrzeit on the eve of 1 Tammuz. Moshe Mordechai later published R' Akiva Yosef Schlesinger's 'Brit Olam' with his own annotations in Jerusalem 5662-5663.
Tags: hebron, chaikin family, shimon menashe chaikin, tcharnostre

Title: Eliezerov spends Shavuot with the Rashab in Lubavitch
Summary: R' Sh.Y.L. Eliezerov spends Shavuot 5665 in Lubavitch, after which the Rashab dispatches him with letters of recommendation to Riga.
Story: On Shavuot 5665 (June 9, 1905), Eliezerov was in Lubavitch, where the Rashab gave him letters of recommendation to the wealthy chassidim of Riga. The trip was tied to the purchase of Hatzer Romano in Hebron and other matters strengthening the Chabad settlement there. He then returned to Lubavitch to help organize the Vaad Chevroni in Tammuz.
Tags: lubavitch, shavuot, rashab, eliezerov, riga

Title: Vaad Chevroni established in Lubavitch
Summary: After a year and a half of discussion, the Vaad Chevroni — a Russia-based committee for Hebron's welfare — is established in Tammuz 5665.
Story: In Tammuz 5665 (summer 1905), the Vaad Chevroni was finally established in Lubavitch under R' Eleazar Moshe Madiyevsky, with the Rashab's encouragement. R' Sh.Y.L. Eliezerov had spent Shavuot in Lubavitch and remained to help organize the committee, whose purpose was to attend continuously to improving Hebron's material and spiritual conditions.
Tags: lubavitch, hebron, vaad chevroni, rashab, madiyevsky

Title: Passing of maternal grandfather R. Avraham Nachum of Alkov
Summary: The author's maternal grandfather R. Avraham Nachum of Alkov passed away on 29 Tammuz.
Story: R. Avraham Nachum, a well-off villager in Kanave near Zhuravichi who operated a water mill and a wool processing factory, passed away on 29 Tammuz 5665. He left behind his wife Rachel Dvasha, five sons, and one daughter (the author's mother). His will included his son-in-law Yaakov Leib among the heirs, and arrangements for dividing the estate followed.
Tags: alkov, kanave, jacobson family

Title: Notes on mezuzah on the right and Chanukah candle on the left
Summary: On Chanukah 5666, R' Avraham Chaim recorded his own kabbalistic reasoning for placing the mezuzah on the right and the Chanukah lamp on the left.
Story: Marked 'Chanukah 5666,' R' Avraham Chaim's note works through the seeming paradox that the mezuzah, identified with the lower sefirot vav-heh, is placed on the right, while the Chanukah lamp, identified with the higher chochmah-binah, is placed on the left. He resolves it via the doctrine that the recipient can outrank the giver in or chozer, citing the Gemara's eleven blessings for one who appeases a poor man and parallels in tefillin placement.
Tags: chanukah, mezuzah, kabbalah, avraham chaim rosin, chasidic thought

Title: Rebbe Rashab appoints R. Menachem Mendel Nae as Kollel Chabad bookkeeper
Summary: On 6 Kislev 5666 the Rebbe Rashab informed R. Nae of his appointment as the kollel's accountant.
Story: The Rebbe instructed Rabbi Nae to request his predecessor R. Leib Menuchin to transfer all accounting documents addressed to the Rebbe's son. Nae was directed to send subsequent financial reports to designated central overseers including R. Chaim Bagin. The appointment came at a time of reorganization of the kollel's senior administration.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, menachem mendel nae, rebbe rashab, bookkeeper

Title: R' Yitzchak ben Aharon of Königsberg, donor of Ohel Yitzchak, dies
Summary: R' Yitzchak ben Aharon, the Königsberg shochet who funded the Ohel Yitzchak beit medrash in Meah Shearim, passed away on 15 Kislev 5666.
Story: R' Yitzchak ben Aharon, a shochet from Königsberg, together with his wife Breina, donated the funds to build the magnificent Ohel Yitzchak beit medrash in Meah Shearim, named for him. He also funded four kollel houses adjacent to it that were allotted by lottery to needy Chabad families every three years. He passed away on 15 Kislev 5666 as recorded in 'Avnei Zikaron' vol. 12.
Tags: jerusalem, meah shearim, ohel yitzchak, kollel chabad, philanthropy

Title: Author begins studying with Rav Baruch Rabinowitz in Zhuravichi
Summary: At about age 11, the author began studying Talmud with Rav Baruch Rabinowitz, the Ashkenazi rabbi of Zhuravichi, during the winter of 5667.
Story: In the winter of 5667 (late 1906 / early 1907), at approximately age 11, the author's father placed him to study with Rav Baruch Rabinowitz, the Ashkenazi rabbi of Zhuravichi. They learned Tractate Bava Basra together, and the rabbi found favor in him. However, lacking a study partner, the need to travel to a yeshiva became clear.
Tags: zhuravichi, torah study

Title: Donation for Beis Avraham veRachel building
Summary: In Adar 5666, the gevir R' Avraham Rosenzweig pledged 8,000 rubles for a stone building for Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: Around 16 Adar 5666 (1906), the wealthy R' Avraham Rosenzweig donated 8,000 rubles to build a stone building in Lubavitch called 'Beis Avraham veRachel', housing the chadarim and a dining hall. Construction was delayed by pogroms and the revolutionary upheaval but resumed and was completed around 5671.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, rosenzweig, construction

Title: Eshel Avraham second edition printed in Buchach
Summary: Mahadura tinyana of Eshel Avraham was published in Buchach in 5666 (1906).
Story: A second edition of Eshel Avraham appeared in Buchach in 1906, twenty years after the Lvov first edition. Much later, a third edition drawn from the surviving manuscripts in the Chabad library was progressively printed in the Shulchan Aruch HaShalem of Machon Yerushalayim.
Tags: buchach, eshel avraham, avraham david of buchach, galicia

Title: Hebron Sephardic and Ashkenazi communities agree on Montefiore split
Summary: Hebron's two communities reach an agreement on how to divide their share of the Montefiore estate funds.
Story: In 5666 (1906) the Sephardic and Ashkenazi communities of Hebron formalized how the Montefiore estate funds reaching the city would be divided between them. A receipt preserved in the SY"L Archive documents that on 22 Elul 5666 (September 12, 1906) one beneficiary received five pounds sterling as his share of the estate's fruits.
Tags: hebron, montefiore, ashkenazi, sephardi

Title: Husiatin firm prints Otzar Klei Chemdah manuscript catalog
Summary: In 5666, the Husiatin partnership of R' L. Shvager and R' D. Frenkel printed a catalog called 'Otzar Klei Chemdah' listing rare manuscripts on parchment and paper for sale.
Story: The booksellers and manuscript dealers issued this catalog to market rare manuscripts. Rebbe Rashab obtained a copy and marked 22 manuscripts with stars indicating those he wished to purchase, with handwritten notes on the descriptions. The catalog itself is preserved in the Chabad library.
Tags: husiatin, shvager, frenkel, manuscripts, catalog

Title: Levitin marries and becomes rabbi of Rakishok
Summary: In 5666 R. Shmuel Levitin married the daughter of Rakishok's rabbi R. Asher Margolios and succeeded him in the rabbinate.
Story: In 5666 (1906), Levitin married Mrs. Sheina, the daughter of R. Asher Margolios, rabbi of Rakishok, and was appointed in his father-in-law's place as rabbi of Rakishok.
Tags: levitin, rakishok, margolios, marriage, rabbinate

Title: Major donation received for Tomchei Tmimim expansion
Summary: An important donation arrived in 5666 to fund expansion of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva facilities in Lubavitch.
Story: The donation enabled construction over subsequent years of two brick buildings in the eastern portion of the courtyard. These housed a study hall for the lower shiurim, a special dining hall for Passover, and a tea station for the yeshiva students. The expansion accommodated both the growing enrollment of Tomchei Tmimim and the cheder students who studied alongside them.
Tags: tomchei-tmimim, donation, lubavitch-courtyard

Title: Marriage of Chaya Mushka Grossman to R' Yosef Shmuel Garfinkel
Summary: Chaya Mushka Grossman married R' Yosef Shmuel Garfinkel of Pahar, a Tomchei Tmimim alumnus, in 5666.
Story: In 5666, Chaya Mushka, daughter of R' Asher Grossman of Nikolayev, married R' Yosef Shmuel Garfinkel of Pahar, a student of Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch. On 6 Av 5666 Rashab wrote R' Asher congratulating him on the engagement. After their wedding, R' Yosef became shochet in Kislovodsk.
Tags: nikolayev, kislovodsk, garfinkel, grossman-family, marriage

Title: Poalei Tzion attack at yeshiva office
Summary: On Motzaei Shabbat after Purim 5666, members of Poalei Tzion attacked the yeshiva office in Lubavitch, firing pistols.
Story: On Motzaei Shabbat after Purim 5666 (1906), after a student named Dovber Davzik who had joined Poalei Tzion was expelled and his belongings confiscated, a group of about 40 men and women from Poalei Tzion came to the courtyard, shooting pistols at the office window. The bullet passed by a guest rabbi from Romanov who was leaning over the table — miraculously no one was hurt. The Rabbanit Rivka (mother of the Rebbe) heard the shots from her nearby home.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, poalei tzion, violence, shootings

Title: Poalei Tzion raid the Rashab's summer home in Bolivke
Summary: Six to eight armed Poalei Tzion members raided the Rashab's summer home in Bolivke, terrorizing his family.
Story: A few months after the yeshivah attack, Poalei Tzion intruders broke into the Rashab's Bolivke summer home with revolvers drawn, destroying furniture and ransacking the house in front of the Rayatz's young daughters and their grandmother. The Rashab was forced to hire security guards; his brother the Raza eventually negotiated a settlement from Vitebsk.
Tags: poalei tzion, bolivke, rashab, violence, security

Title: Poalei Tzion raids Rashab's summer home in Bolivke
Summary: Six to eight armed Poalei Tzion members raided the Rashab's summer home in Bolivke, destroying furniture and ransacking the property.
Story: Brandishing revolvers and exclaiming 'We'll show you!', the intruders frightened the Rayatz's young daughters and the Rebbetzin. They blocked the road to prevent police from arriving. The Rashab was forced to hire security guards. His brother the Raza, living in Vitebsk, eventually negotiated an agreement with Poalei Tzion.
Tags: poalei tzion, rashab, bolivke, violence, marxist zionism

Title: Rashab publishes kuntres defending Hebron's primacy in Kollel Chabad
Summary: At the start of 5667 the Rashab released a lengthy kuntres explaining why Hebron deserves priority over Jerusalem in Chabad's communal support.
Story: The Rashab argued that although Jerusalem possesses greater inherent holiness, the present spiritual quality of Hebron was higher because Jerusalem had become contaminated by sinners while Hebron remained pure under vigilant rabbinic leadership. He cited the Mitteler Rebbe and Tzemach Tzedek's deliberate choice of Hebron and urged Torah scholars to settle there. He also announced plans for a new society called Chevronim to strengthen Hebron, though the previous year's troubles had delayed its launch.
Tags: hebron, rashab, jerusalem, kollel chabad, chevronim

Title: Rayatz lobbies German and Dutch bankers to stop pogroms
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak traveled to Germany and Holland to persuade bankers to use their financial leverage to stop pogroms in Russia.
Story: Following the wave of pogroms that swept Russia in 1905-1906, the Rayatz sought international economic pressure as a tool for protecting Jewish communities. He approached prominent bankers in Germany and Holland, asking them to use their leverage with the Russian government.
Tags: germany, holland, pogroms, advocacy, bankers

Title: Rayatz's St. Petersburg arrest over military exemption efforts
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was arrested in St. Petersburg over his efforts to exempt rabbis from military service.
Story: In 1906, Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was arrested in St. Petersburg after working to secure exemptions for rabbis from compulsory military service in the Russian army. His advocacy for protecting Jewish religious leaders from conscription was viewed as obstructionist by czarist authorities. This was one of his early imprisonments under the czarist regime.
Tags: st. petersburg, russia, arrest, military draft, rabbis, yosef yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Rayatz's third arrest in Poalei Tzion conflict
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was arrested a third time after a conflict with Poalei Tzion activists in Lubavitch.
Story: In 1906, Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was arrested following a confrontation with Poalei Tzion, a Labor Zionist organization active in Lubavitch. The clash reflected the broader ideological battles between traditional Chabad Chasidism and emerging Jewish political movements in early twentieth-century Russia. This was one of multiple arrests he endured under czarist rule.
Tags: lubavitch, russia, arrest, poalei tzion, yosef yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Rebbe Rashab's 5666 maamarim circulated
Summary: Discourses of Rebbe Rashab from 5666 circulated in handwritten and mimeographed copies.
Story: Two editions of Rebbe Rashab's 1906 (5666) discourses are exhibited—one mimeographed, the other handwritten by the well-known Chassid R. Zalman Idel Zislin. Tsarist restrictions prevented formal publication, so discourses circulated in multiple copies among Chassidim.
Tags: rebbe rashab, drushim, mimeograph, samizdat

Title: Rebbe Rashab's siyum-pidyon at zaide's tziyun
Summary: During 5666, the Rebbe Rashab wrote pidyonot at the graves of his grandfather and father seeking protection from Poalei Tzion threats.
Story: During the Poalei Tzion crisis of 5666 (1906), the Rebbe Rashab wrote pidyonot at the tziyunim of his grandfather the Tzemach Tzedek and his father the Rebbe Maharash. He prayed for great mercy upon himself, his son Yosef Yitzchak, and the students of Tomchei Tmimim, who were being threatened with murder by Poalei Tzion if their financial and personnel demands were not met.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, rashab, tzemach tzedek, pidyon

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter to trustees defining Kollel Chabad's purpose
Summary: On 27 Tevet 5666 the Rebbe Rashab wrote to the Jerusalem trustees defining the kollel's purpose as supporting Torah and avodah, not merely settling the land.
Story: The Rebbe articulated his understanding that the holy fathers had founded the Eretz Yisrael fund specifically because the land was uniquely suited to Torah and avodah, and not for the sake of artisans and businessmen lacking the yoke of Torah. He returned to this theme in many later letters, in ongoing tension with the Jerusalem trustees who maintained a broader yishuv-support mission.
Tags: kollel chabad, rashab, jerusalem, torah and avodah, ideology

Title: Maharayatz letter describes founding of 'Chevronim' vaad and new shadar
Summary: On 18 Shvat 5666 Rebbe Maharayatz wrote a letter recounting the 1905 conference, the founding of the Chevronim vaad, and the appointment of new shadarim.
Story: The letter describes how the Chevronim vaad was tasked with expanding pushke placements 'in every place'. R. Meir Leib Horowitz had just been appointed as a new emissary to Russian cities, and R. Zalman Yitzchak Walshanik of Riga was named the dedicated gabbai for Eretz Yisrael funds. The decisions overrode an earlier proposal to abolish traveling shadarim in favor of mailing funds directly to Jerusalem, which Rebbe Rashab had opposed.
Tags: chevronim, kollel chabad, shadar, meir leib horowitz, zalman yitzchak walshanik, rambahn

Title: Maharashab travels to Moscow
Summary: Maharashab's passport was stamped in Moscow on 2 Adar 5666.
Story: On 14 February 1906 (2 Adar 5666), Maharashab's internal Russian passport was stamped in Moscow, documenting one of his several trips to the imperial cities outside the Pale of Settlement.
Tags: maharashab, moscow, passport, travel

Title: Rebbe Rashab issues general letter on Eretz Yisrael donations and shadar Horowitz
Summary: On 19 Shvat 5666 Rebbe Rashab issued a circular to Anash on the mitzvah of supporting Eretz Yisrael and introducing R. Meir Leib Horowitz as his new shadar.
Story: The Rebbe extolled the founding role of the Alter Rebbe in establishing the mitzvah of tzedakas Eretz Yisrael in Russia, and lamented that in recent years the practice had weakened in many towns. He instructed Anash to welcome Horowitz, install pushkes in homes lacking them, and follow detailed procedures spelled out in an accompanying letter from his son Maharayatz. A second circular soon clarified that the new pushkes were for the kollel as a whole and not specifically for Hebron.
Tags: chevronim, shadar, meir leib horowitz, pushke, rambahn, anash

Title: Rebbe Rashab selects R. Meir Leib Horowitz as kollel emissary
Summary: On 19 Shvat 5666 the Rebbe Rashab announced he had chosen R. Meir Leib Horowitz as shaliach for the holy task.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab held that emissary travel remained essential to invigorate R'Meir Baal HaNess collections, despite the move to postal collection. He explained in several Shvat 5666 letters that personal travel was needed to gather accumulated sums and to strengthen future giving by appointing local collectors. Horowitz was selected as 'shaliach mitzvah' for this great mitzvah.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, rebbe rashab, meir leib horowitz, fundraising

Title: Poalei Tzion attacks Tomchei Temimim
Summary: Armed Poalei Tzion members confronted the Rayatz at the yeshivah and later shot at the building.
Story: On March 22, 1906, Marxist Zionist Poalei Tzion members marched into Tomchei Temimim demanding the release of teenage student Berel Davzik. Three days later they returned with weapons, threw stones, and fired bullets at the yeshivah, narrowly missing Rabbi Moshe Klatzkin of Romanov. Students drove them off, but the Rayatz forbade reprisal.
Tags: poalei tzion, marxism, zionism, tomchei temimim, berel davzik, lubavitch

Title: Poalei Tzion confronts Rayatz with weapons over student Berel Davzik
Summary: Members of Marxist Zionist group Poalei Tzion confronted the Rayatz at the yeshivah with weapons, demanding student Berel Davzik be allowed to stay.
Story: The Rayatz had telegrammed the parents of underage student Davzik, who had become active in Poalei Tzion. On Thursday night, group members marched in with weapons threatening the Rayatz, who responded fearlessly. Three days later they returned, shooting at the yeshivah and narrowly missing Rabbi Moshe Klatzkin of Romanov. Yeshivah students drove them off.
Tags: poalei tzion, rayatz, lubavitch, tomchei temimim, berel davzik, marxist zionism

Title: Death of R. Michel Baruch Reizes
Summary: R. Michel Baruch ben David Reizes, trustee of Kollel Chabad, died on 4 Nissan 5666.
Story: Reizes had come to Jerusalem from Poltava in Russian Ukraine. He had served as senior trustee of Kollel Chabad in the late 19th century, in succession to the Khersoner. His death is recorded in Avnei Zikkaron volume 12.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, michel baruch reizes, poltava, obituary

Title: Eliezerov returns to Hebron after over two years abroad
Summary: R' Eliezerov returns to Hebron at the end of winter 5666, ending a mission that had lasted more than two years.
Story: HaChavatzelet of 9 Nisan 5666 (April 3, 1906) reported that Rabbi Shlomo Leib Eliezerov, Ashkenazi av beit din of Hebron, had arrived in Jerusalem on Rosh Chodesh Nisan returning from his trip to Russia, and continued to Hebron on 3 Nisan. Soon after, the Sephardic community issued him a formal release certifying his fourth mission had been the most profitable yet.
Tags: hebron, eliezerov, shadar, chavatzelet

Title: Pyotr Stolypin appointed Russian interior minister and prime minister
Summary: Pyotr Stolypin was appointed interior minister and prime minister under Czar Nicholas II.
Story: Stolypin's anti-Semitic agenda would prompt the Rayatz's covert mission to St. Petersburg to subvert a planned decree against the Jewish community. Stolypin served until his assassination in 1911.
Tags: russia, stolypin, nicholas ii, antisemitism

Title: Poalei Tzion attack at Rebbe's summer dacha
Summary: On 7 Menachem Av 5666, Poalei Tzion members raided the Rebbe Rashab's summer dacha demanding ransom.
Story: On the night of 7 Menachem Av 5666 (1906), six to eight Poalei Tzion members from Vitebsk came to the Rebbe Rashab's dacha with revolvers, destroyed the dining shed, broke tables, cabinets, and door glass. The Rebbetzin asked to take her terrified children outside but was forced back into the house at gunpoint. The attackers demanded 3,000 rubles. Eventually a settlement and ransom payment was reached during Elul.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, poalei tzion, violence, rashab, ransom

Title: Rebbe Rashab appoints R' Yisrael Dovber Frumkin as Kollel Chabad trustee
Summary: On 21 Menachem Av 5666 the Rebbe Rashab notified Jerusalem trustees that he had appointed R' Yisrael Dovber Frumkin as an additional trustee.
Story: Hoping that Frumkin's character and standing would help reform the kollel's distribution practices in line with the policy he had set out the same day in a parallel letter to Frumkin, the Rebbe instructed the existing trustees to admit Frumkin to the vaad and make no decisions without him. The Jerusalem trustees and the rebbes of Lyadi and Bobruisk resisted the appointment, and after months of dispute it was unclear whether Frumkin ever effectively served.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, rashab, yisrael dovber frumkin, trustees

Title: R' Gershon Chen temporarily appointed mashgiach
Summary: At the start of 5667, student R' Gershon Chen was appointed acting mashgiach when R' Zev Wolf Lewitin fell ill.
Story: At the start of 5667 (autumn 1906), when the mashgiach R' Zev Wolf Lewitin fell ill, the student R' Gershon Chen was temporarily appointed in his place. A letter from the Rebbe Rayatz dated 5 Marcheshvan 5667 announced that Chen would supervise order in the Great Hall. When Lewitin recovered, he resumed his post.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, chen, lubavitch, mashgiach

Title: R' Avraham Chaim donates lottery winnings to the Rebbe Rashab
Summary: R' Avraham Chaim won 5,000 rubles in an American lottery and sent 1,000 to the Rebbe Rashab, who acknowledged it on 12 Tishrei 5667.
Story: On 12 Tishrei 5667 (October 1906), the Rebbe Rashab wrote to R' Avraham Chaim from Lubavitch confirming receipt of 1,000 rubles along with a record of how the money was distributed. The Rebbe blessed him with success and the means to continue doing tzedakah. A month later, on 18 Marcheshvan, the Rebbe advised him to invest the remaining funds in a house that would produce income.
Tags: lottery, tzedakah, rosenbaum, maharashab, america

Title: Rosenbaum sends 1,000 rubles of lottery winnings to Rebbe Rashab
Summary: After winning 5,000 rubles in a New York lottery, Rosenbaum sent 1,000 to the Rebbe Rashab, who acknowledged receipt on 12 Tishrei 5667.
Story: Reb Avraham Chaim won 5,000 rubles in a lottery and immediately sent 1,000 of them to the Rebbe Rashab. On 12 Tishrei 5667 (1 October 1906) the Rebbe wrote from Lubavitch confirming arrival of the money, enclosing a distribution list, and praying that Rosenbaum continue to merit livelihood and the ability to do tzedakah.
Tags: america, new york, rebbe rashab, tzedakah, lottery

Title: Rebbe Rashab kuntres clarifies new pushkes are for entire kollel, not Hebron alone
Summary: A Cheshvan 5667 kuntres by Rebbe Rashab reiterated that the new shoferos were intended for the entire kollel and not solely for the Hebron community.
Story: Some had interpreted the Chevronim vaad's expanded fundraising as specifically aiding Chabad's Hebron yishuv, prompting Rashab to publish a clarifying kuntres. He restated his earlier kruz that 'it never occurred to me that the new shoferos would be for Hebron alone.' The clarification reaffirmed that all new income belonged to the general kollel infrastructure.
Tags: chevronim, pushke, hebron, kollel chabad, fundraising

Title: Rebbe Rashab advises Rosenbaum to invest lottery winnings in a house
Summary: On 18 Cheshvan 5667 the Rebbe Rashab advised Rosenbaum that the prudent use of his prize money would be to purchase a stone house yielding income proportionate to his needs.
Story: Continuing the conversation about Rosenbaum's lottery winnings, the Rebbe Rashab wrote from Lubavitch on 18 Cheshvan 5667 that 'in my opinion it is correct that he buy a stone house from which he will have income according to his needs.' He blessed him that God should send him a good and successful property and prosperity in body and soul.
Tags: america, rebbe rashab, investment, lottery

Title: Rayatz investigated by authorities over Lubavitch radical youth riots
Summary: The Rayatz was investigated due to riots in Lubavitch by radical youth, which he proved were not part of the yeshivah.
Story: Coming after the 1905 revolution when political tensions ran high, this was one of four arrests of the Rayatz between 1911 and 1916. He proved the rioters were not connected to the yeshivah and was released with a stern warning. These detentions did not deter him from his communal work.
Tags: rayatz, lubavitch, arrest, 1905 revolution

Title: Rayatz investigated over Lubavitch riots
Summary: The Rayatz was investigated by Russian authorities in December 1906 over radical-youth riots in Lubavitch.
Story: In December 1906, in the aftermath of the 1905 revolution's political tensions, the Rayatz was investigated about riots in Lubavitch by radical youth. He proved the rioters were not part of the yeshivah and was released after a brief detention.
Tags: rayatz, arrest, lubavitch, riots, 1905 revolution

Title: Decision to go to Lubavitch instead of Lida
Summary: En route to Lida yeshiva, the author and his father were dissuaded by two travelers and instead chose Lubavitch.
Story: While waiting at the Molodechno train station to transfer to Lida, the author's father was approached first by a fundraiser for the Lida yeshiva who warned about lax standards among older students, and later by a venerable bearded man who denounced Rabbi Reines for sharing a stage with a partially uncovered woman and urged: 'If you want your son to remain an honest Jew, take him to Lubavitch.' After much inner turmoil, the boy chose Lubavitch and they boarded the train for Lubavitch instead.
Tags: lubavitch, lida, tomchei tmimim, yeshiva

Title: Lubavitch mikvah rebuilt in courtyard
Summary: After earlier plans were blocked by local opposition, the Lubavitch courtyard mikvah was rebuilt and reached the spring waters in Elul 5667.
Story: Following a failed attempt in 5666 to build a mikvah on one side of the courtyard due to opposition from non-Jewish neighbors near their church, Rashab rebuilt the existing mikvah at a deeper level during summer 5667. On 5 Elul 5667 he wrote of his joy that the diggers had reached the spring waters.
Tags: mikvah, lubavitch, construction, rashab

Title: Rashab corresponds with R. Dovid Yakobson on Lubavitch mikveh
Summary: In 5667 the Rashab wrote at length to the Lubavitch moreh tzedek about the laws of the town's newly built mikveh.
Story: When a new mikveh was constructed in Lubavitch in 5667 (1907), the Rashab and the town's moreh tzedek R. Dovid b. Bentzion Yakobson exchanged a series of substantial halachic letters on the laws of mikvaot. These letters are preserved in Igrot Kodesh of the Rashab, vol. 1, nos. 167-171. R. Yakobson was the son-in-law of R. Avraham Zeligsohn and had inherited the post despite his relatively young age.
Tags: rashab, dovid yakobson, mikveh, lubavitch, halacha

Title: Tomchei Tmimim funding collapses in Russia after 1905 pogroms
Summary: In a summer 5667 fundraising letter Rosenbaum reported that the recent Russian pogroms had severely weakened Russian donors and left Tomchei Tmimim's roughly 500 students in dire need.
Story: Writing to R' Gershon Kapilowitz in summer 5667, Rosenbaum described Tomchei Tmimim, founded by the Rebbe Rashab in Lubavitch, with some 500 outstanding students supplied with all their needs. Until then Russian philanthropists had given tens of thousands of rubles per year, but the recent pogroms and disturbances had crippled their ability to give. American donors now had to step in with fixed annual pledges to keep the yeshivas functioning.
Tags: russia, tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, pogroms, fundraising

Title: Tomchei Tmimim fundraising crisis after 1905 Russian pogroms
Summary: R' Avraham Chaim wrote letters in summer 5667 urging American Chassidim to support Tomchei Tmimim after Russian pogroms cut off traditional funding.
Story: In a summer 5667 (1907) letter to R' Gershon Kopilovitz, R' Avraham Chaim explained that some 500 yeshiva students studied at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch under the direct supervision of the Rebbe Rashab. With Russian pogroms devastating the donor base, the yeshiva faced terrible shortages, and R' Avraham Chaim called on American supporters to commit to regular annual pledges.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, pogroms, russia, fundraising, america, yeshiva

Title: Wooden synagogue built in Kostroma
Summary: The small wooden synagogue of Kostroma's tiny Jewish community was constructed in 1907.
Story: By the time the Rebbe arrived in exile in 1927, the synagogue had been closed by Soviet authorities. Services moved to the large home of local shochet Yerachmiel Kugel, where the Rebbe and his entourage stayed. In recent years the Jewish community in Kostroma has undergone a rebirth.
Tags: kostroma, synagogue, russia

Title: SILA writes to Rebbe Rashab about Bukhara shlichut
Summary: On 14 Tevet 5667, SILA (R' Shneur Zalman Ladier) wrote to Rebbe Rashab seeking permission for a Bukhara emissary mission.
Story: Less than a year after returning to Chevron, R' Shneur Zalman Ladier ('SILA') wrote to the Rebbe Rashab on 14 Tevet 5667 explaining that disputes over Kolel Chabad leadership and personal pressures made permanent settlement in Eretz Yisrael impossible. He asked permission to undertake another shlichut, this time for the Sephardi community to Bukhara. He estimated the mission would take eight months.
Tags: shneur zalman ladier, rebbe rashab, bukhara, chevron, shadar

Title: Rebbe Rashab approves SILA's Bukhara shlichut
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Adar 5667 Rebbe Rashab approved SILA's request for the Bukhara shlichut.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab responded on Rosh Chodesh Adar 5667 that 'the matter is necessary for him and cannot be postponed.' He also approved SILA's parallel travel to Lubavitch to discuss community affairs in person. The Rebbe blessed his journey with 'good and true reasons.'
Tags: rebbe rashab, shneur zalman ladier, bukhara

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter to son on Husiatin manuscript purchases
Summary: On 11 Nisan 5667, Rebbe Rashab directed his son which kabbalistic manuscripts to prioritize from the Husiatin catalog, including Sefer HaKavanot and Livnat HaSapir.
Story: The Rebbe identified specific manuscripts worth pursuing (Igros #961), suspecting Livnat HaSapir might be the autograph of R' Avraham Saba based on a marginal signature. Eighteen of the marked manuscripts were ultimately acquired and now hold catalog numbers 1972-1989 in the library. Each purchased volume bears Rebbe Rayatz's notation: 'This we bought.'
Tags: rashab, rayatz, husiatin, manuscripts, kabbalah, letters

Title: Letter to Rabbi Tzirelson of Ludmir on Eretz Yisrael fundraising
Summary: Secretary Yaakov Kapil Zeliksohn wrote to Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Tzirelson of Ludmir regarding Eretz Yisrael fundraising.
Story: On 20 Adar 5667, writing on the Rebbe Rayatz's stationery from Lubavitch, secretary Yaakov Kapil Zeliksohn sent a postcard to Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Tzirelson, rabbi of Ludmir (Vladimir-Volynsky). The letter urged Tzirelson to follow the model of the Kovel community in collecting Ramban funds for the Anash community in Hebron. At that time the future Rebbe Rayatz served as director of Tomchei Temimim and chairman of the Hebron Vaad.
Tags: rayatz, tzirelson, ludmir, eretz-yisrael, ramban-funds, tomchei-temimim, russia

Title: Rashab writes from Lubavitch that Rayatz's books are intact
Summary: On 11 Nissan 5667, Rebbe Rashab writes to his son Rayatz from Lubavitch reassuring him that his personal book collection is intact and in order.
Story: Both the Rashab and the Rayatz spent most of 5667 abroad. The Rashab returned to Lubavitch for Pesach and wrote on 11 Nissan that 'your books are intact and stand in order as they were.' He repeated the reassurance about Rayatz's separate personal library on 24 Nissan, underlining that father and son maintained distinct collections in the Lubavitch library.
Tags: library, rashab, rayatz, letters, lubavitch

Title: Rebbe Rashab confirms broader rabbinic consensus around Kollel Chabad reform
Summary: On 8 Iyar 5667 the Rebbe Rashab wrote to his son the Rayyatz that the rebbes of Lyadi, Bobruisk and Retzitza all now agreed to Frumkin's appointment.
Story: Writing to the future Rebbe Rayyatz, the Rashab reported that R' Yeshaya Berlin had received word from the Rebbe of Lyadi confirming consensus around Frumkin, with the rebbes of Bobruisk and Retzitza also agreeing. He hoped this would finally settle the matter so that the land might be quiet, though as he wrote a week later he could only hope it was truly so.
Tags: kollel chabad, rashab, yisrael dovber frumkin, lyadi, bobruisk, retzitza

Title: SILA departs Lubavitch for Bukhara
Summary: SILA departed Lubavitch for Bukhara on 8 Iyar 5667, traveling via Moscow with an acquaintance from Samarkand.
Story: After spending Pesach and several weeks in Lubavitch consulting with the Rebbe Rashab, SILA left for Bukhara on 8 Iyar 5667. A letter from the Rebbe Rashab that day notes 'today our relative R' Shneur Zalman traveled to Bukhara via Moscow.' He was accompanied by a Samarkand resident who had been waiting for him in Moscow.
Tags: shneur zalman ladier, rebbe rashab, bukhara, moscow, samarkand

Title: Rashab inquires after Rayatz's manuscript and book purchases
Summary: On 24 Nissan 5667, Rashab writes Rayatz again about books and asks for news of manuscript and book acquisitions, including from Husiatyn.
Story: In addition to repeating that Rayatz's books in Lubavitch are still in their place, Rashab inquires about the status of manuscripts being sought from Husiatyn and asks whether the list sent to Eretz Yisrael has produced any response. This pattern of detailed book-purchase oversight runs through many of the Rashab-Rayatz letters of this period.
Tags: library, rashab, rayatz, letters, manuscripts, husiatyn

Title: Uncles emigrate to America after Shavuos
Summary: The author's uncles R. Yisrael Yeshaya and R. Yosef Hillel emigrated from Zhuravichi to America after Shavuos 5667.
Story: After Shavuos of 5667 (1907), uncles Yisrael Yeshaya and Yosef Hillel left Zhuravichi for America, partly to escape Russian army conscription which required a 300-ruble fine for those who emigrated without reporting. They had corresponded with their uncles already in America, who sent them travel tickets and described American prosperity. The family escorted them out of town on the Motzaei Yom Tov following the holiday.
Tags: america, emigration, jacobson family, military

Title: Kolel Chabad purchases building adjacent to Beit Menachem synagogues
Summary: A printed appeal from Tammuz 5667 announces the purchase of a large adjacent courtyard to save Jerusalem's Chabad synagogues from being shut.
Story: In Tammuz 5667 (July 1907), Kolel Chabad of Jerusalem issued a printed appeal explaining that the Beit Menachem synagogues — founded fifty years earlier by the Tzemach Tzedek opposite the Hurva ruin — were about to be sealed because the adjoining three-story courtyard with its shops was about to be sold to a Muslim buyer. One of the signatories donated 4,000 rubles personally and the community borrowed another 12,000 rubles to buy the courtyard and dedicate its income to needy Chabad scholars in perpetuity.
Tags: jerusalem, beit menachem, kolel chabad, tzemach tzedek

Title: Death of R. Yehuda Leib Menuchin
Summary: R. Yehuda Leib Menuchin, former bookkeeper of Kollel Chabad, died on 10 Menachem Av 5667.
Story: Menuchin had served as the kollel's bookkeeper in the early years of the 20th century until his role was transferred to R. Menachem Mendel Nae in late 5666. After his death, the active leadership of the Jerusalem kollel narrowed to Shlonk and Efrat as the address holders, with Yeshaya Ornstein as scribe and Nae as bookkeeper.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, yehuda leib menuchin, bookkeeper

Title: R' Avraham Chaim sends Tzemach Tzedek manuscript to the Rebbe Rashab
Summary: On 11 Elul 5667, the Rebbe Rashab wrote from Würzburg requesting that R' Avraham Chaim send him the autograph signature of the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: Writing from Würzburg on 11 Elul 5667 (1907), the Rebbe Rashab thanked R' Avraham Chaim for a 100-mark donation and discussed two books to be sent. Most precious, the Rebbe wrote, was the handwriting of the Tzemach Tzedek, which he requested be sent by registered mail to Lubavitch. The Rebbe Rayatz later recounted this gift in a letter dated 12 Tishrei 5696.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, manuscripts, maharashab, wurzburg, rosenbaum

Title: Rebbe Rashab writes from Würzburg accepting Tzemach Tzedek manuscript
Summary: On 11 Elul 5667 the Rebbe Rashab wrote to Rosenbaum from Würzburg asking him to send the Tzemach Tzedek's handwritten power-of-attorney to Lubavitch by registered mail.
Story: From Würzburg on 11 Elul 5667 the Rebbe Rashab acknowledged receipt of 100 marks Rosenbaum had sent on his behalf, and turned to a more precious offer. He told Rosenbaum that the Tzemach Tzedek's autograph was 'dearer to us than any wealth,' and asked him to send it by registered mail to Lubavitch, while books should go via Königsberg.
Tags: germany, wurzburg, rebbe rashab, tzemach tzedek, manuscripts

Title: Departure from Zhuravichi toward yeshiva
Summary: On Motzaei Shabbos Bereshis, 28 Tishrei 5668, the author and his father left Zhuravichi by wagon to seek a yeshiva.
Story: On the night of 28 Tishrei 5668, the author and his father set out from Zhuravichi by wagon, first arriving in Rogachev on Sunday morning. That evening they continued by covered wagon some 60 versts to Bobruisk, arriving Monday morning, to consult the father's uncle R. Tuvia the shochet about whether to send the boy to the Lida yeshiva or to Lubavitch.
Tags: zhuravichi, rogachev, bobruisk, travel

Title: Author arrives in Lubavitch to begin yeshiva studies
Summary: The young author arrived in Lubavitch with his father on Wednesday, Rosh Chodesh Marcheshvan 5668, and stayed at the home of his relative, the shochet R. Shlomo Chaim Kutain.
Story: On Wednesday, the eve of Rosh Chodesh Marcheshvan 5668 (corresponding to early October 1907), the author and his father arrived in Lubavitch. They lodged with their relative R. Shlomo Chaim Kutain, a shochet who trained students in ritual slaughter, including the Rayatz. Roughly ten students at a time learned the craft under him.
Tags: lubavitch, tomchei-tmimim, shlomo-chaim-kutain, shochet

Title: Author's first yechidus with the Rebbe Rashab
Summary: On Thursday, 2 Marcheshvan 5668, the author entered the Rebbe Rashab's chamber for the first time and was directed to the yeshiva administration.
Story: On Thursday, 2 Marcheshvan 5668, the author and his father were received in yechidus by the Rebbe Rashab — the author's first encounter with a Lubavitcher Rebbe. The Rebbe instructed that the boy be referred to the yeshiva administration. The next day he was examined by R. Yechiel Komisar and R. Yechezkel Himmelstein and admitted to R. Leib Babin's class.
Tags: rashab, yechidus, tomchei-tmimim, lubavitch

Title: Rebbe Rashab delivers maamar in the small zal, Shabbos Noach
Summary: On Shabbos Parshas Noach 5668, the Rebbe Rashab delivered a maamar of Chassidus in the small zal of the Lubavitch beis medrash.
Story: After Kabbalas Shabbos on Parshas Noach, the Rebbe Rashab entered the kleiner zal where he then customarily said Chassidus. The Rayatz arrived first in Shabbos garb and shtreimel, and bachurim sang niggunim including the famed Yedid Nefesh of Lubavitch. Sudden silence fell as the Rebbe entered and delivered the maamar — the author's first such experience.
Tags: rashab, rayatz, maamar, kleiner-zal, lubavitch

Title: Chafetz Chaim writes about sales of completed Mishnah Berurah
Summary: On Sunday Parshat Vayetze 5668, the Chafetz Chaim wrote that with God's help he had completed the Mishnah Berurah on the full Shulchan Aruch Orach Chaim and listed prices for his works.
Story: He sent his emissary R. Yitzchak ben Yisrael Yosef of Cizevo to distribute his books in towns near Warsaw, asking Jews to assist him. He specified prices for each volume: Mishnah Berurah parts 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 at 1.20 rubles each, part 4 at 90 kopeks bound, with 6.60 rubles for the complete set.
Tags: chafetz chaim, mishnah berurah, radin, book pricing

Title: Author's first entry into the Rashab's chamber
Summary: On 3 Cheshvan 5668, the author entered the chamber of the Rebbe Rashab in Lubavitch for the first time.
