Story: On Tuesday, 3 Cheshvan 5668 (1907), the young Yisrael Jacobson entered the holy chamber of the Rebbe Rashab in Lubavitch for the first time. Fifty years later, on the corresponding date in 5718, he marked the anniversary by entering the chamber of the Rebbe (Rayatz's successor). It was at that 5718 yechidus that he was directed to begin writing his memoirs.
Tags: lubavitch, rashab, yechidus, tomchei tmimim

Title: Babinovitch branch opens
Summary: In summer 5668 a branch of Tomchei Tmimim was opened in Babinovitch under R' Zev Wolf Lewitin and R' Shlomo Risen.
Story: In summer 5668 (1908), a Tomchei Tmimim branch opened in Babinovitch as an intermediate stage between the chadarim/shiurim and the Great Hall. R' Zev Wolf Halevi Lewitin oversaw nigleh and R' Shlomo Ben Dovid Risen oversaw chassidut. The Rebbe Rashab corresponded about it from Marienbad. The branch later relocated to Shchedrin.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, babinovitch, marienbad

Title: Bichawski publishes circular defending the adres system
Summary: The general overseas gabbai R. Chaim Aharon Bichawski printed a circular titled 'Tshuva LeDorshei HaAdres' in 5668.
Story: Bichawski urged donors not to wait for the arrival of traveling emissaries before remitting R'Meir Baal HaNess funds. Communities should send their contributions directly several times per year, and to avoid depriving the emissary of his livelihood, pay him a percentage of the sums collected and forwarded. The circular reflected the gradual shift away from purely shadar-based fundraising.
Tags: kollel chabad, chaim aharon bichawski, fundraising, adres

Title: Birth of R. Yosef Avraham Cohen (Friedman) in Rechitsa
Summary: R. Yosef Avraham Cohen, later chief secretary of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw, was born in Rechitsa, Russia in 5668 under the name Yosef Avraham Friedman.
Story: Yosef Avraham Friedman was born in Rechitsa in 5668 (1908). He would later cross into Poland, study at Tomchei Temimim Warsaw, and become a key administrator of the yeshiva office.
Tags: rechitsa, russia, yosef avraham kagan, biography

Title: Death of R' Isser Yanovsky, rabbi of Krivoy Rog
Summary: R' Isser Yanovsky, rabbi of Krivoy Rog and great-uncle of the Rebbe (Ramash), passed away in winter 5668.
Story: In winter 5668, R' Isser Yanovsky passed away. He had served as rabbi of Krivoy Rog for about fifteen years and had traveled to Carlsbad for medical treatment in 5666 with Rashab's support. On 21 Adar I 5668, Rashab wrote his father-in-law R' Asher requesting that any valuable items, especially writings from Rebbeim, found in R' Isser's estate be sent to him.
Tags: krivoy-rog, yanovsky, rabbinate

Title: Fire breaks out in the small zal of Lubavitch yeshiva
Summary: In mid-winter 5668, a fire erupted in the kleiner zal of the Lubavitch yeshiva and was extinguished by the students with water from courtyard wells.
Story: During the harsh winter of 5668 (early 1908), sparks were seen escaping the chimney of the heavily stoked stove in the small zal. Within a half hour the fire spread; with no modern firefighting equipment available, the students hauled water in large barrels from two wells in the courtyard and quenched the blaze. For some months afterward davening did not take place in the small zal, and the Rebbe Rashab began saying Chassidus in the large zal.
Tags: lubavitch, fire, kleiner-zal, tomchei-tmimim, winter

Title: Marienbad summer conference of Chassidic Rebbes
Summary: In the summer of 5668 the Rebbe Rashab, the Gerrer Rebbe, and other leaders convened a conference in Marienbad to coordinate preparations for the planned rabbinical gatherings in Vilna and Petersburg.
Story: Outside the reach of Russian government scrutiny, leading Orthodox figures including Rebbe Rashab and the Gerrer Rebbe (R. Avraham Mordechai Alter) met in the Bohemian spa town of Marienbad. They discussed the preparations for the upcoming Vilna assembly and the Petersburg Rabbinical Conference. The Gerrer Rebbe asked Rashab to clarify the situation in Petersburg through the special emissary being sent to the capital.
Tags: marienbad, rashab, gerrer rebbe, petersburg conference, rabbinical assembly

Title: R' Alchanan Dov Morozov appointed mashgiach for chassidut
Summary: Mid-winter 5668, R' Alchanan Dov Morozov was appointed mashgiach for chassidut in the Great Hall.
Story: In the middle of winter 5668 (early 1908), R' Alchanan Dov Morozov was appointed mashgiach for chassidut studies in the Great Hall at Tomchei Tmimim. The appointment was announced through a letter from the Rebbe Rashab read by office manager R' Eliezer Kaplan. Morozov later served as secretary to the Rebbe Rayatz and was executed in Petersburg in 5698 (1938).
Tags: tomchei tmimim, morozov, mashgiach, chassidut

Title: R' Yaakov Landa enters Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch
Summary: R' Yaakov Landa began studying at the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lubavitch in 5668 (1908).
Story: R' Yaakov Landa entered the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lubavitch in 5668 (1908). He continued his studies there until 5672 (1912), receiving a full Chabad chassidic and Talmudic education.
Tags: lubavitch, tomchei-tmimim, landa, yeshiva

Title: R. Avraham Chaim drafts his first will and sends it to the Rebbe Rashab
Summary: In 5668 R. Avraham Chaim prepared a will and dispatched a copy to the Rebbe Rashab for his review.
Story: Sensing the need to set his affairs in order, R. Avraham Chaim composed a will in 5668 and forwarded a copy to the Rebbe Rashab. The text of that first will has not survived, but the Rebbe's acknowledgement letter from Marienbad is preserved, praising him for arranging his matters as a G-d-fearing and prudent man should.
Tags: will, tzava'ah, rashab, avraham chaim rosenbaum, estate planning

Title: R. Elchanan Dov Marozov appointed mashgiach of Chassidus
Summary: In mid-winter 5668, R. Elchanan Dov Marozov was appointed mashgiach of Chassidus in the large zal of Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: Earlier in the year R. Shlomo Risin of Rogachov had served as mashgiach of Chassidus in the great hall. Mid-winter 5668 saw R. Elchanan Dov Marozov appointed in his stead. R. Eliezer Kaplan, head of the yeshiva office, came to the large zal to read aloud a letter from the Rebbe Rashab announcing the appointment.
Tags: tomchei-tmimim, lubavitch, elchanan-dov-marozov, mashgiach

Title: R. Shmaryahu Yehuda Leib Medalia appointed rabbi of Vitebsk
Summary: R. Shmaryahu Yehuda Leib Medalia was appointed rabbi of Vitebsk in Tishrei 5669.
Story: R. Shmaryahu Yehuda Leib Medalia took up the rabbinate of Vitebsk in Tishrei 5669, with his appointment documented in correspondence of the Rebbe Rashab. Within roughly a year and a half he would serve as Vitebsk's delegate to the 1910 St. Petersburg rabbinical conference, where he carried the city's anash petitions on chinuch and rabbinic credentials. Medalia would later become one of the most prominent Chabad rabbinic figures of the Soviet period.
Tags: russia, vitebsk, shmaryahu-medalia, rebbe-rashab

Title: Rashab acquires Beit Romano in Hebron
Summary: After years of effort, the Rashab completed the purchase of Beit Romano and an adjacent property in Hebron.
Story: By 1908, the Rashab had raised the funds and navigated the legal hurdles to acquire Beit Romano, a large mansion originally built by an affluent Istanbul Jew. Combined with an adjacent property, it would serve as the base for Toras Emes, the first chasidic yeshivah in the Jewish homeland.
Tags: hebron, beit romano, rashab, real estate, eretz yisrael

Title: Rashab becomes owner of Beit Romano complex in Hebron
Summary: After years of effort, the Rashab acquired the large Beit Romano property and an adjacent property in Hebron.
Story: Originally owned by an affluent Jew from Istanbul, the mansion was put up for sale by his children. The Rashab raised the necessary funds and navigated complicated legal steps over several years to acquire it. The Rayatz was intimately involved. The combined property became the base for the new yeshivah and gave the Rashab a strong foothold in Hebron.
Tags: rashab, hebron, beit romano, eretz yisrael, real estate

Title: Rayatz participates in organizing the Vilna Conference
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak helped organize the Vilna Conference addressing the state of Russian Jewry.
Story: The Vilna Conference gathered rabbinic and communal leaders to address pressing challenges facing Russian Jewry. The Rayatz's involvement reflected his growing stature as a communal organizer.
Tags: vilna, conference, russian jewry

Title: Rebbe Rashab purchases Hebron building for future yeshiva
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab purchased a large multi-story building in Hebron in Av 5668.
Story: In Av 5668 the Rebbe Rashab of Lubavitch purchased a large multi-story stone building in Hebron containing eighteen dwellings, three large water cisterns, surrounding land suitable for additional construction, and a khan rented for two hundred rubles annually. The building would later house the Toras Emes yeshiva established in 5672.
Tags: hebron, rashab, toras emes, real estate, av

Title: Rebbe Rashab purchases Romano courtyard in Hebron
Summary: In late summer 5668 the Rebbe Rashab purchased the Romano courtyard in Hebron from Avraham Romano, son of Markado Romano.
Story: At the end of summer 5668 the Rebbe Rashab acquired the famous Romano courtyard in Hebron from Avraham, son of the late Markado Romano. The grand mansion had been built outside the Jewish ghetto in the 1870s and had hosted prominent visitors, including R' Chizkiyah Medini, the Sdei Chemed, who lived and died there. After the purchase the building would become a central Chabad property in Hebron.
Tags: hebron, chabad, rashab, romano, real estate

Title: Rebbe Rashab writes about plans for new Hebron yeshiva
Summary: In Cheshvan 5669 the Rebbe Rashab wrote that the existing Hebron yeshiva was inadequate and outlined plans for a new institution.
Story: In a letter from Cheshvan 5669 the Rebbe Rashab explained that although a Chabad yeshiva already existed in Hebron, it was 'small and not what we truly intend.' He envisioned a yeshiva that would attract God-fearing avreichim devoted to Torah study under proper supervision. This vision would be realized three years later with the founding of Yeshivat Torat Emet.
Tags: hebron, chabad, rashab, yeshiva, torat emet

Title: Russian government approves Knesset Yisrael Orthodox organization
Summary: In the winter of 5668 the Russian government formally authorized the Orthodox organization Agudat Knesset Yisrael, headed by R. Chaim Ozer Grodzinski.
Story: After years of failed assemblies, the Charedi community achieved a major institutional milestone when the Russian government recognized Agudat Knesset Yisrael in winter 5668. R. Chaim Ozer Grodzinski of Vilna headed the organization, which became the legal framework that would later make a Vilna rabbinical assembly possible under its statute (paragraph 39). R. Eliezer Gordon of Telshe was deeply involved in the new body.
Tags: russia, knesset yisrael, chaim ozer grodzinski, agudah

Title: Rebbe Rashab inquires after SILA in Bukhara
Summary: On 7 Adar II 5668 the Rebbe Rashab wrote to SILA in Bukhara asking how much longer his mission would take.
Story: Still in Bukhara nearly a year after his arrival, SILA received a letter from the Rebbe Rashab on 7 Adar II 5668 expressing his strong desire that SILA return home. The Rebbe asked for a detailed report on his welfare and the duration of his remaining stay. SILA would not return to Chevron until Shevat 5669.
Tags: rebbe rashab, shneur zalman ladier, bukhara

Title: Author remains in Lubavitch for Pesach 5668
Summary: Refused permission to travel home, the young author spent Pesach 5668 in Lubavitch and afterward began receiving yeshiva support as a 'gola' bachur.
Story: As Pesach 5668 approached, the author wrote home asking for travel funds, but the mashgiach R. Yechezkel Himmelstein denied him leave. After Pesach his father informed him that supporting him was a hardship, and he should seek yeshiva stipends. The Rebbetzin Shterna Sarah's 'krupnik' meals, lodging arrangements, and modest cash from the yeshiva and bachurim's fund began his life as an exile-student.
Tags: lubavitch, pesach, tomchei-tmimim, yeshiva-life

Title: Maharashab travels to Moscow
Summary: Maharashab's passport was stamped in Moscow on 11 Iyar 5668.
Story: On 29 April 1908 (11 Iyar 5668), Maharashab traveled again to Moscow, where his internal Russian passport received an entry stamp.
Tags: maharashab, moscow, passport, travel

Title: Postponed Lag BaOmer rabbinical assembly in Vilna
Summary: R. Eliezer Gordon of Telshe scheduled a general rabbinical assembly for Lag BaOmer 5668 in Vilna under the auspices of Knesset Yisrael, but it had to be postponed when it was realized that the proper governmental authorization had not yet been obtained.
Story: Acting with great urgency, R. Eliezer Gordon scheduled a general rabbinical assembly for Lag BaOmer 5668 in Vilna, conflating it with the affairs of the newly authorized Knesset Yisrael. Rabbis across the region had already begun gathering in district capitals to consult, but it became clear that a general assembly required the Minister of the Interior's permission rather than the local governor's. The organizers were forced to publicly announce the postponement via newspapers and telegrams.
Tags: russia, vilna, lag baomer, eliezer gordon, telshe, knesset yisrael, rabbinical assembly

Title: Rebbe Rashab delivers Shavuos maamar at Rebbetzin Rivka's home
Summary: On Shavuos 5668, the Rebbe Rashab said a deep maamar at the seudah held in his mother Rebbetzin Rivka's home in Lubavitch.
Story: At Rebbetzin Rivka's dining room a long table was set for the Shavuos seudah, with the Rebbe Rashab at its head. Expecting a short, accessible maamar like the prior year's 'Keshe'alah Moshe LaMarom,' students crowded in, but this time the Rebbe delivered a deep maamar continuing the themes of the two days of Yom Tov. Older bachurim teased the younger ones about whether they had managed to follow it.
Tags: rashab, shavuos, rebbetzin-rivka, maamar, lubavitch

Title: Death of R. Yaakov Ornstein
Summary: R. Yaakov Ornstein, scribe of Kollel Chabad, died on 22 Sivan 5668.
Story: Ornstein was succeeded by R. Moshe Ornstein, who first appears in the kollel's correspondence on 14 Menachem Av 5669 alongside trustees Dov Ber Efrat and Mordechai Shlonk. His death marked a generational transition in the scribal office of the kollel.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, yaakov ornstein, scribe

Title: Pesher allocates Siberian-city revenue 41% Chabad, 59% Kollel Reisin
Summary: A Tammuz 5668 Kollel Chabad letter records the existing split of donations from Petrovsky Zavod, Chita, Verkhneudinsk and Barguzin: 41% to Chabad, 59% to Kollel Reisin.
Story: Per a longstanding pesher with the Vaad HaKlali, four of the five Siberian cities were treated as shared between Kollel Reisin and Kollel Chabad rather than belonging to Reisin exclusively. The Tammuz 5668 entry in the Kollel Chabad letter register pinpoints the division as Chabad 41% and Reisin 59%. The fifth city, Achinsk, is not mentioned in this allocation.
Tags: siberia, kollel chabad, kollel reisin, fundraising, petrovsky zavod, chita, barguzin

Title: Rashab purchases rare books for Lubavitch library
Summary: In a July 1908 letter, the Rashab describes purchasing four rare books that summer for his library.
Story: Rabbi Sholom Dovber Schneersohn (the Rashab) actively expanded his library throughout his life. A letter from July 1908 documents the purchase of four rare books that summer that did not appear on the earlier 1905 catalog, evidence later used to argue the collection had grown to roughly 7,000 titles by 1915.
Tags: library, rashab, books, lubavitch, schneersohn-collection

Title: Rebbe Rashab purchases books in Königswart
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab purchased rare Prague-printed books from a synagogue caretaker in Königswart.
Story: On 10 Tammuz 5668 (July 9, 1908), the Rebbe Rashab wrote from Marienbad about visiting the small nearby town of Königswart with R' N. Gur-Aryeh and R' Z. Persitz. They found an old synagogue with an ancient Torah scroll, and from the caretaker he purchased several Prague-printed books including Chok L'Yisrael, Mesorat HaBrit HaKatan, Gevul Binyamin, and Horeh Gever.
Tags: library, books, marienbad, königswart, czechia

Title: Rebbe Rashab accepts Rosenbaum's first will from Marienbad
Summary: On 23 Tammuz 5668 the Rebbe Rashab wrote from Marienbad acknowledging a copy of Rosenbaum's will and praising him for ordering his affairs as a God-fearing person should.
Story: Reb Avraham Chaim drafted a will in 5668 and sent a copy to the Rebbe Rashab. On 23 Tammuz 5668 the Rebbe replied from Marienbad commending him for arranging his affairs—'as a God-fearing and sensible man should do'—and blessing him with long life, livelihood, peace of mind for Torah and avodah, and good health.
Tags: czech, marienbad, rebbe rashab, wills

Title: Rebbe Rashab replies from Marienbad acknowledging R. Avraham Chaim's will
Summary: On 23 Tammuz 5668 the Rebbe Rashab wrote from Marienbad to R. Avraham Chaim affirming the propriety of his will and blessing him with long life, livelihood, and health.
Story: Receiving the copy of R. Avraham Chaim's will at his home, the Rebbe Rashab — then in Marienbad on the advice of Professor Berlin for his own health — responded on 23 Tammuz 5668. He commended the chassid for arranging his affairs as a G-d-fearing and discerning person should, and blessed him with longevity, parnassah, success, and the ability to engage in Torah and avodah in peace. The Rebbe also mentioned that he himself awaited a complete recovery among all of Israel.
Tags: rashab, marienbad, will, tzava'ah, blessings, avraham chaim rosenbaum, health

Title: Czernowitz Conference declares Yiddish 'glue' of Jewish life
Summary: At the Czernowitz Conference, secular Yiddish leaders declare Yiddish to be 'the glue to hold Jewish life together.'
Story: The Yiddish movement believed using Yiddish would be a barrier to assimilation, rejecting classic Jewish religious beliefs and observance. Many of its early schools were strongly anti-Zionist, though most later became supportive of Zionism. Yiddish schools spread across Russia, Europe, the US, and Canada, but most had closed by the early 1970s.
Tags: yiddish, czernowitz, secularism, peretz, conference

Title: Czernowitz Conference declares Yiddish a Jewish national language
Summary: Leaders at the Czernowitz Conference proclaim Yiddish 'the glue to hold Jewish life together.'
Story: The Yiddish movement's secular philosophy rejected classic Jewish religious observance and aimed to build Jewish identity around language alone. It spread to Russia, Europe, and North America before fading in the late twentieth century.
Tags: yiddishism, czernowitz, secular, language

Title: Kollel reports damage to Tzfat Chabad Beit Midrash
Summary: On 25 Elul 5668, Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem wrote that the Tzfat Beit Midrash had cracked and required government-mandated repairs costing twenty napoleons.
Story: The Tzfat Chabad community appealed for help after government-ordered repairs to their damaged Beit Midrash cost twenty napoleons. Kollel Chabad arranged for Jerusalem and Hebron to cover ten napoleons and forwarded the additional request to overseas administrators, illustrating the poverty of the small community.
Tags: tzfat, beit midrash, kollel chabad, ottoman government

Title: Confidential meeting of Chabad-aligned rabbis to plan rabbinic conference
Summary: The Rashab asked the Rayatz to organize a confidential meeting of rabbis closely aligned with Chabad to strategize for the upcoming St. Petersburg conference.
Story: With the Russian government convening a major rabbinic conference and the first Duma elections approaching, the Rashab needed to develop a consensus position. The agenda also included determining 'the manner and extent of our involvement in preparation for the elections in the forthcoming duma.'
Tags: rashab, rayatz, rabbinic conference, duma elections

Title: Confidential pre-conference rabbinic meeting
Summary: The Rashab asked the Rayatz to organize a confidential meeting of Chabad-aligned rabbis to set strategy.
Story: In October 1908, anticipating the St. Petersburg rabbinic conference, the Rashab tasked the Rayatz with convening a small confidential meeting of Chabad-aligned rabbis to develop a consensus on government engagement and prepare for the forthcoming Duma elections.
Tags: rabbinic strategy, chabad, duma, elections, rayatz

Title: Conference of Chabad rabbanim and wealthy chassidim in Lubavitch
Summary: In Marcheshvan 5669, prominent Chabad rabbanim and wealthy chassidim gathered in Lubavitch for an unusual conference referenced later by the Frierdiker Rebbe.
Story: Around Parshas Vayera in Marcheshvan 5669, a notable assembly of senior Chabad rabbanim and wealthy chassidim convened in Lubavitch — alluded to by the Rayatz in a later sicha of Pesach 5694. The author saw R. David Tzvi Chen of Chernigov and R. Yaakov Mordechai Bezpalov of Poltava for the first time. The aliyos in shul that Shabbos required special direction from the Rebbe Rashab himself.
Tags: chabad-rabbanim, lubavitch, david-tzvi-chen, yaakov-mordechai-bezpalov, rashab

Title: Conference of Chabad rabbis convenes in Lubavitch at the Rashab's invitation
Summary: A special assembly of Chabad rabbis gathers in Lubavitch during Cheshvan 5669 at the personal invitation of the Rebbe Rashab.
Story: In Cheshvan 5669, Rabbi Sholom DovBer of Lubavitch (the Rebbe Rashab) summoned a special conference of Chabad rabbis. Among the attendees was Rabbi Yaakov Mordechai Bezpolov, rav of Poltava, who remained at the gathering at least until 17 Cheshvan, as reflected in the published Igros Kodesh of the Rebbe Rashab.
Tags: rashab, lubavitch, chabad rabbis, conference, yaakov mordechai bezpolov

Title: Lubavitch convenes preparatory assembly of Chabad rabbis
Summary: In mid-Cheshvan 5669 the Rebbe Rashab convened an assembly of Chabad rabbis and lay leaders in Lubavitch, establishing a permanent bureau to prepare for the upcoming Vilna rabbinical assembly.
Story: As preparations for the Vilna assembly intensified, the Rebbe Rashab gathered Chabad rabbis and community activists in Lubavitch itself for a strategic conference. The gathering established a standing committee to handle the preparatory work for the Vilna assembly. The Chabad assembly also decided to seek the Gerrer Rebbe's approval to send two Chabad representatives, R. Menachem Mendel Chein of Nezhin and R. Shmaryahu Leib Medalia of Vitebsk, to participate in the upcoming assembly of Polish rabbis.
Tags: lubavitch, rashab, chabad, rabbinical assembly, vilna assembly

Title: Passing of the Raza, elder brother of the Rebbe Rashab
Summary: In the week of Parshas Vayera 5669, R. Zalman Aharon (Raza), elder brother of the Rebbe Rashab, passed away in Vitebsk.
Story: The Raza, who lived in Vitebsk, passed away during the week of Parshas Vayera 5669. The family withheld the news from the elderly Rebbetzin Rivka, who was still alive. When she insisted on traveling to Vitebsk after a week without letters from her son, an elder of the town, R. Dovber 'Bere Avremkes,' gently told her there was no longer reason to go, and the horses were returned to the stable.
Tags: raza, vitebsk, rashab, rebbetzin-rivka, lubavitch

Title: Poltava community appoints Adermann as kosher meat overseer
Summary: Rabbi Yaakov Mordechai Bezpolov and the Poltava community committee formalize a contract appointing Rabbi Shemaya Adermann to supervise the porging and sale of kosher meat in Poltava.
Story: On Monday, 29 Marcheshvan 5669, the Poltava rav Rabbi Yaakov Mordechai Bezpolov together with the community's elected committee signed an agreement with Rabbi Shemaya Adermann, who undertook to uphold the full set of regulations they enacted to safeguard the kashrus of meat in the city. The document carries the rav's stamp and the signatures of community officers including Aharon HaKohen Glezer, Chaim Zissel Chernigover and others. A puzzling secondary date of 2/11/1903 is appended at the bottom of the signatures.
Tags: poltava, yaakov mordechai bezpolov, kashrut, shechita, menaker, ukraine

Title: Assembly of Polish rabbis convenes
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5669 an assembly of Polish rabbis convened to address the same governmental questions about religious affairs that prompted the Vilna gathering.
Story: Russian-ruled Poland organized its own rabbinical assembly on Rosh Chodesh Kislev to respond to the preparatory questions for the Petersburg Rabbinical Conference. Two Chabad representatives, R. Menachem Mendel Chein of Nezhin and R. Shmaryahu Leib Medalia of Vitebsk, attended at the invitation of the Gerrer Rebbe. They reported the assembly's discussions and decisions back to the Rebbe Rashab, who immediately relayed the details to his son, the Rayatz, who was overseeing preparations for the Vilna assembly.
Tags: poland, warsaw, gerrer rebbe, menachem mendel chein, shmaryahu leib medalia, petersburg conference, rabbinical assembly

Title: Author's bar mitzvah in Lubavitch
Summary: The author marked his bar mitzvah on 3 Kislev 5669 in Lubavitch, having studied a maamar of the Rebbe Maharash with R. Mordechai Leib Rabinowitz.
Story: On 3 Kislev 5669 the author turned thirteen. His relative R. Mordechai Leib Rabinowitz learned with him the maamar 'Ein HaKadosh Baruch Hu Ba BiTrunya' from 5648, which he reviewed thoroughly. The bar mitzvah came soon after a difficult period in which his protests over class placement nearly resulted in expulsion from Tomchei Tmimim.
Tags: bar-mitzvah, lubavitch, tomchei-tmimim, mordechai-leib-rabinowitz

Title: Permit secured for Vilna rabbinical assembly via Ministry of Interior
Summary: By 3 Kislev 5669 the Rebbe Rashab obtained Russian government authorization for a 25-rabbi consultative assembly in Vilna, leveraging Dr. Krebs's questions about preparations for the Petersburg Rabbinical Conference.
Story: When Dr. Krebs, the 'Learned Jew' at the Ministry of the Interior, circulated preparatory questions for the upcoming Petersburg Rabbinical Conference, the Rebbe Rashab seized the opportunity. Through the wealthy Petersburg askan R. Shmuel Michel Treinin, a petition signed by Yitzchak Liubinsky was submitted requesting permission for twenty-five named Orthodox rabbis to meet in Vilna to consult on the upcoming conference's religious questions. The director of the relevant department signed the permit, ending years of failed attempts to obtain authorization.
Tags: russia, vilna, ministry of interior, dr. krebs, shmuel michel treinin, yitzchak liubinsky, petersburg conference, rabbinical assembly

Title: Rebbe Rashab denounces Baron Ginzburg in 19 Kislev address
Summary: On 19 Kislev 5669 (December 12, 1908) the Rebbe Rashab spoke with great bitterness about Baron Ginzburg and the Maskilic school in Lubavitch.
Story: In his 19 Kislev address the Rebbe denounced 'the architect of the movement in government circles,' Baron Hertz Ginzburg, and recounted that he had pleaded with him 'give me Yavneh'—asking that at least Lubavitch be spared a Mefitzei Haskalah school—and that the baron refused even this minimal concession.
Tags: yud-tes kislev, baron ginzburg, lubavitch school, chevra mefitzei haskalah

Title: 19 Kislev farbrengen 5669 closed to younger students
Summary: At the 19 Kislev 5669 farbrengen, the Rebbe Rashab spoke sharply against state-language primary schools being established in the Pale of Settlement.
Story: The Tomchei Tmimim administration barred cheder-level students from attending the 19 Kislev 5669 farbrengen with the Rebbe Rashab in the large zal. The Rebbe spoke with great bitterness against the founding of Russian-language 'shkoles' for Jewish children, condemning the initiative's patron Baron Horace Ginzburg, who had refused his plea to spare at least Lubavitch. The author later heard that the baron died around Purim that winter.
Tags: yud-tes-kislev, rashab, lubavitch, schools, baron-ginzburg

Title: Chabad chassidim in Vilna purchase the Apatov synagogue
Summary: In the winter of 5669, Chabad chassidim in Vilna bought the Apatov synagogue at 21 Vilenskaya Street.
Story: The purchase gave Vilna's Chabad community a permanent base and is documented in a letter of Rebbe Rayatz (Igrot Kodesh vol. 1, letter 25). The same building would later host the Vilna branch of Tomchei Tmimim. Its acquisition came just months before a major rabbinical conference convened in the city.
Tags: vilna, apatov, chabad, lithuania, rashab

Title: Chabad chassidim of Vilna purchase the Apatov synagogue
Summary: In the winter of 5669 the Chabad chassidim of Vilna purchased the Apatov synagogue building for fifty thousand rubles, later renaming it 'Beis Knesses Lubavitch'.
Story: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak (later the Frierdiker Rebbe) wrote that the chassidim acquired the large brick building together with its sixty-year-old beis knesses, intending to install their own shochet as well. The building served as the heart of Chabad life in Vilna until the Holocaust.
Tags: vilna, apatov, 5669, rashab, synagogue, lubavitch

Title: Chabad purchases Hebron property under Rebbe Rashab
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab oversaw the purchase of a large Hebron property where Chabad opened a yeshivah.
Story: Rabbi Shlomo Leib Eliazrov assisted the Rashab in the purchase of Beit Romano. The site of the new Hebron neighborhood traces back to this acquisition, which expanded Chabad's institutional presence in the city.
Tags: hebron, rashab, yeshiva, beit-romano

Title: Cholera outbreak in the Vitebsk province
Summary: During the summer of 5669, a cholera epidemic struck the Vitebsk region and nearby provinces, prompting government orders to drink only boiled water.
Story: In the summer of 5669 the dreaded cholera 'dever' spread through the Vitebsk province and surrounding regions. The Russian authorities ordered that only boiled water be drunk throughout the affected provinces. Large cauldrons of boiling water were kept in the yeshiva at all times, and even the drinking barrel in the zal was filled exclusively from boiled water.
Tags: cholera, vitebsk, lubavitch, russia, epidemic

Title: Election of 42 delegates to the Petersburg Rabbinical Conference
Summary: Forty-two delegates were elected from the various gubernias of Russia for the Petersburg Rabbinical Conference, most of them God-fearing rabbis.
Story: The election campaign concluded with 42 delegates chosen from across the gubernias of Russia, the majority of whom were observant rabbis. The Rebbe Rashab himself was elected as one of seven members of the conference's organizing committee. This represented a major victory for the religious camp after intensive campaigning.
Tags: russia, rabbinical conference, petersburg, tsarist russia, elections

Title: Founding of Agudat HaTmimim
Summary: At the start of 5670, the Agudat HaTmimim was founded for alumni of the yeshiva.
Story: Agudat HaTmimim was founded at the start of 5670 (1909) as a support network for married alumni of Tomchei Tmimim who had taken positions as rabbis, shochtim, merchants and activists. About 45 alumni attended the founding meeting in Lubavitch with the Rebbe Rayatz as chairman. By 14 Tevet 5670, a pamphlet listed about 200 members.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, alumni, agudat hatmimim

Title: Lubavitch mikvah building reconstruction
Summary: Rashab built a stone structure over the rebuilt mikvah during summer 5669.
Story: In summer 5669, Rashab oversaw construction of a stone wall building over the Lubavitch mikvah, with internal partitions of timber. This mikvah served the community until the family's evacuation to Rostov in 5676.
Tags: mikvah, lubavitch, construction

Title: Maskilic counter-assembly convenes in Kovno
Summary: Around the time of the Vilna rabbinical assembly, the Maskilim and government-appointed rabbis (rabbanim mi-ta'am) convened their own authorized 'Assembly of Jewish Public Activists' in Kovno, producing a roughly two-hundred-page volume of proposals that was submitted to the Ministry of Interior.
Story: Determined not to cede the field to the Orthodox rabbinate, the modernist faction and government-appointed rabbis organized a parallel assembly in Kovno called the 'Assembly of Jewish Public Activists.' They recorded all their proposals in a volume of roughly two hundred pages, submitted it to the Ministry's religious affairs department, later published a printed collection of the speeches and proposals, and established a standing bureau to prepare for the Petersburg Rabbinical Conference.
Tags: russia, kovno, haskalah, askanim, petersburg conference

Title: R' Yochanan Gordon studies at Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch
Summary: R' Yochanan Gordon entered Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch in 5669, where he studied for eight years until 5677.
Story: According to a self-recorded registration card, R' Yochanan Gordon learned in the Lubavitcher yeshiva Tomchei Tmimim from 5669 through 5677. This placed him at the central Chabad yeshiva during the final years of Rebbe Rashab's leadership and into the turbulent World War I period.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, yochanan gordon, russia

Title: R. Levi Yitzchak Schneerson appointed Rabbi of Yekaterinoslav
Summary: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson was accepted as Rabbi of Yekaterinoslav in 5669, when the Rebbe was seven years old.
Story: In 5669 (1908–1909), Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, father of the Rebbe, was accepted as Rabbi of Yekaterinoslav. The Rebbe, born in Nikolayev, was seven years old at the time of the move. In subsequent years he would travel back to Nikolayev at the end of each summer to stay several weeks with his maternal grandparents.
Tags: levi yitzchak, yekaterinoslav, nikolayev, rabbinate, ukraine

Title: R. Yehoshua Arsh begins teaching at Tomchei Temimim Lubavitch
Summary: In the winter of 5670 R. Yehoshua Arsh was accepted for the first time as a Rosh Mesivta at Tomchei Temimim in Lubavitch.
Story: The memoirist studied that winter under R. Yehoshua Arsh, who had just been hired. The class learned tractate Kiddushin together with all of Tosafot over the course of the winter through Pesach, mastering the material thoroughly.
Tags: lubavitch, tomchei temimim, yehoshua arsh

Title: R. Zalman Dov of Dribin appointed Rosh Mesivta in Shchedrin
Summary: R. Zalman Dov of Dribin, a noted Chabad scholar, was appointed Rosh Mesivta for the Tomchei Temimim branch in Shchedrin.
Story: R. Zalman Dov, a great talmid of R. Tzvi Neta Gnessin of Pochep, was selected from among the outstanding learners of Chabad chassidim. R. Shaul Dov Zislin was chosen as mashpia and director of the Shchedrin branch.
Tags: shchedrin, tomchei temimim, zalman dov dribin

Title: Rayatz travels to Germany to confer with communal leaders
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak traveled to Germany for consultations with Jewish communal leaders.
Story: His travels in 1909 continued his pattern of seeking international Jewish coordination on issues facing Russian Jewry. Germany hosted significant Jewish philanthropic and political networks that the Rayatz worked to engage.
Tags: germany, jewish leadership

Title: Rebbe Rashab elected delegate from two Russian provinces
Summary: In late 5669/early 5670 the Rebbe Rashab personally traveled to Mogilev and Chernigov to campaign and was elected as a delegate to the Petersburg Rabbinical Conference from both provinces.
Story: Departing from his usual practice, the Rebbe Rashab personally undertook campaign travel to the cities of Mogilev (whose province included Lubavitch) and Chernigov to ensure that pious rabbis were selected as delegates to the Petersburg conference. He stood as a candidate himself and was elected from both provinces, an event later recorded in Zikaron LiVnei Yisrael as 'the campaign' he undertook. He acknowledged the burden weighed heavily upon him but felt he could not refuse.
Tags: russia, rashab, mogilev, chernigov, petersburg conference, elections

Title: Rebbe Rashab travels to Mohilev for delegate elections
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab personally traveled to Mohilev to campaign for the selection of observant delegates, staying at the home of philanthropist Reb Yehoshua Rozinkin.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab journeyed to Mohilev to lead what was termed in local parlance a 'campaign' for delegate elections. The wealthy Reb Yehoshua Rozinkin built a new brick home for him with all new furnishings and even new silk bed coverings. Dignitaries of the city greeted the Rebbe at the train station with a carriage drawn by horses, as was customary for nobility.
Tags: russia, mohilev, elections, r' yehoshua rozinkin, rabbinical conference

Title: Tomchei Temimim branch moves from Bobinovich to Shchedrin
Summary: At the beginning of 5670 (late 1909), the Tomchei Temimim branch in Bobinovich relocated to Shchedrin.
Story: The branch served as an intermediate level between the chadarim and the main Lubavitch yeshiva, with roughly sixty students in three classes. The town's householders agreed that about forty students would be supported by hosting meals ('teg'), while twenty would be supported wholly or partly by the Lubavitch yeshiva fund. Students traveled from Lubavitch to Shchedrin after Sukkot 5670.
Tags: shchedrin, bobinovich, tomchei temimim, russia

Title: Tomchei Tmimim branch founded in Babinovitch
Summary: In 5669 a Tomchei Tmimim branch was established in Babinovitch as an intermediate stage between the Lubavitch cheders and the great hall.
Story: In 5669 the yeshiva opened a branch in Babinovitch to bridge the gap between the cheder-level shiurim in Lubavitch and the senior bachurim of the large zal. R. Zev Wolf Levitin supervised the nigleh studies and R. Shlomo b. David Risin oversaw Chassidus. A separate group of bachurim continued learning in Horodishtch under R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin.
Tags: tomchei-tmimim, babinovitch, zev-wolf-levitin, shlomo-risin, horodishtch

Title: SILA returns to Chevron from Bukhara
Summary: SILA returned to his home in Chevron in Shevat 5669 after his extended Bukhara shlichut.
Story: Winter 5669 saw SILA in Lubavitch, and he reached his home in Chevron in Shevat 5669. The Rebbe Rashab welcomed him back with letters of 26 Shevat 5669 expressing relief at his safe arrival via Odessa and Jaffa. Rebbe Rayatz's 8 Adar 5669 letter reports that the family had been anxious during the journey's 20-day delay.
Tags: shneur zalman ladier, bukhara, chevron

Title: Maharashab travels to Vilna
Summary: Maharashab's passport was stamped in Vilna on 12 Iyar 5669.
Story: On 20 April 1909 (12 Iyar 5669), Maharashab visited Vilna, the great Lithuanian center of Jewish learning, with his passport stamped there.
Tags: maharashab, vilna, passport, travel

Title: Preliminary rabbinical conference in Baranovich
Summary: From 9-11 Iyar 5669 a preliminary closed conference of senior rabbis convened in Baranovich, immediately prior to the main Vilna assembly, to align agendas and positions.
Story: Following the Rebbe Rashab's longstanding insistence that any major rabbinical assembly be preceded by a smaller preparatory conference of selected senior figures, a three-day gathering was held in Baranovich. This allowed the leading Orthodox rabbis to clarify positions, narrow disagreements, and agree on what would be proposed publicly before the broader twenty-five-rabbi convention in Vilna began two days later.
Tags: russia, baranovich, vilna assembly, rabbinical assembly

Title: Pre-conference meeting of 25 leading rabbis in Vilna
Summary: Twenty-five leading rabbis convened in Vilna with government permission to set an agenda for the upcoming national conference.
Story: The meeting was made possible through efforts of the Rashab in coordination with Rabbi Chaim Ozer Grodzinski of Vilnius. The Rayatz was named secretary of the meeting. The participants worked to develop a unified rabbinic position ahead of the contentious St. Petersburg conference.
Tags: vilna, chaim ozer grodzinski, rayatz, rabbinic conference

Title: Rabbinical assembly held in Vilna
Summary: A rabbinical assembly was convened in Vilna in Iyar 5669 (May 1909) on the question of the Crown Rabbinate.
Story: After more than a decade of failed attempts to organize a general rabbinical convention against the proposed reform of the Russian rabbinate, an assembly was finally held in Vilna in Iyar 5669. It addressed the dual-rabbinate question that had occupied the Rebbe Rashab and other leading rabbis since the Fifth Rabbinical Commission's decision.
Tags: vilna, rabbinical assembly, rabbanut mitaam

Title: Rabbinical conference convenes in Vilna in Iyar 5669
Summary: A rabbinical conference was held in Vilna from 12 to 20 Iyar 5669, with the Rebbe Rashab among its conveners and leading participants.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab was one of the conveners and chief figures of the gathering, whose details are recorded in Igrot Kodesh of the Rashab (vol. 4, letter 1029, with introduction p. 26). Beyond formal sessions, the visit brought the Rebbe Rashab into the newly acquired Apatov shul on Lag BaOmer, where he delivered a chassidic discourse.
Tags: vilna, rabbinical conference, rashab, lithuania

Title: Rebbe Rashab delivers maamar at Apatov synagogue on Lag B'Omer
Summary: On Lag B'Omer 5669 the Rebbe Rashab visited the newly acquired Apatov synagogue in Vilna and delivered a Chassidic discourse.
Story: The Frierdiker Rebbe later recalled in a 5684 letter that the building was already being called 'Beis Knesses Lubavitch' when his father, the Rashab, said Chassidus there on Lag B'Omer. The visit cemented the synagogue's identity as the chassidic center of the city.
Tags: vilna, rashab, lag b'omer, 5669, apatov, maamar

Title: Vilna pre-conference of leading rabbis
Summary: Twenty-five leading rabbis met in Vilna to set the agenda for the upcoming St. Petersburg conference.
Story: In May 1909, through coordination between the Rashab and Rabbi Chaim Ozer Grodzinski of Vilna, the Russian government permitted twenty-five leading rabbis to gather in Vilna. The Rayatz was named secretary of the meeting, which set the agenda for the 1910 national conference in St. Petersburg.
Tags: vilna, rabbinic conference, chaim ozer grodzinski, rayatz

Title: Vilna rabbinical assembly convenes under Rebbe Rashab
Summary: After nine years of effort, Rebbe Rashab succeeded in convening an officially-authorized rabbinical assembly in Vilna in Iyar 5669.
Story: Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak later described it as 'the great Vilna assembly, the like of which had not been held in a hundred years.' Authorized by the Interior Ministry strictly for matters of religious strengthening, it nevertheless adopted a resolution to the ministry connecting religious decline to the economic catastrophe of the Pale of Settlement.
Tags: vilna, rashab, rabbinical assembly, religious strengthening, pale of settlement

Title: Historic Vilna rabbinical assembly convenes
Summary: From 12-20 Iyar 5669 (May 3-11, 1909) twenty Orthodox rabbis convened the major Vilna rabbinical assembly, described as the first such united gathering in approximately one hundred years.
Story: After nearly a decade of failed attempts, the official Vilna rabbinical assembly finally took place over ten days in Iyar 5669, with the Gerrer Rebbe (R. Avraham Mordechai Alter) joining for part of the proceedings. Twenty of the twenty-five authorized rabbis attended. The assembly resolved to dispatch traveling rabbis and preachers to towns across Russia to strengthen religious observance, organize Torah study circles, and establish local educational committees (Vaadei Chinuch) of pious learned men to supervise schooling. The Rayatz, designated by the Rebbe Rashab to handle all operational details, prepared the formal protocol that was submitted via the governor to the Ministry of Interior's religious affairs department.
Tags: russia, vilna, rashab, rayatz, gerrer rebbe, chaim ozer grodzinski, rabbinical assembly, education

Title: Rebbe Rashab visits the Apatov shul in Vilna on Lag BaOmer 5669
Summary: On Lag BaOmer 5669, while in Vilna for the rabbinical conference, the Rebbe Rashab visited the Apatov shul and delivered a maamar there.
Story: The visit is recorded in a letter of the Rebbe Rayatz (Igrot Kodesh vol. 1, letter 171). Coming during the Iyar 5669 rabbinical conference, it strengthened the standing of the newly acquired Chabad synagogue in Vilna. The discourse left a lasting impression on the local Chabad community.
Tags: rashab, vilna, apatov, lag baomer, maamar

Title: Great Hall at Lubavitch closed after roof beams cracked
Summary: After dancing on the second night of Rosh Hashanah 5670 caused the roof beams to crack, the Great Hall at Lubavitch was closed.
Story: During dancing on the second night of Rosh Hashanah 5670, the roof beams of the Great Hall began to give way. Immediately after Rosh Hashanah the hall was closed, and after Sukkot additional support beams were installed from floor to ceiling to brace the structure.
Tags: lubavitch, tomchei temimim, building

Title: Rosh Hashanah prayers held in Great Hall at Lubavitch
Summary: On Rosh Hashanah 5670 (1909), roughly 150 minyanim gathered for prayers in the Great Hall at Lubavitch.
Story: In 5669 prayers had been held in the Small Hall, but in 5670 a much larger crowd—approximately 150 minyanim—prompted moving the High Holiday services to the Great Hall. During dancing on the second night of Rosh Hashanah after the chassidus discourse, the roof beams began to crack.
Tags: lubavitch, tomchei temimim, rosh hashanah, rebbe rashab

Title: Petersburg Rabbinical Conference elections in Russian provinces
Summary: Beginning in Tishrei 5670, elections were ordered across Russian provinces to select two delegates per province for the upcoming Petersburg Rabbinical Conference, prompting the Rebbe Rashab to publish kol koreh broadsides and personally travel to campaign.
Story: After the holidays in Tishrei 5670, the government ordered elections for delegates to the Petersburg Rabbinical Conference, with two representatives to be chosen per province through a multi-stage process. The Rebbe Rashab immediately issued a kol koreh, dispatched R. Moshe Rosenblum to coordinate with the gedolim, and obtained additional kol koreh letters from R. David Friedman of Karlin and R. Chaim Ozer Grodzinski. Thousands of copies were distributed to synagogues. Dr. Krebs at the Ministry of Interior actively lobbied against electing Orthodox rabbis, citing precedents where ministers had selected only one or two religious rabbis to past commissions.
Tags: russia, petersburg conference, rashab, rayatz, dr. krebs, elections, kol koreh

Title: Rebbe Rashab promises 'Reid' and Maamar that became Kuntres HaAvodah
Summary: On Simchat Torah 5670, unable to continue the farbrengen due to crowding, the Rebbe Rashab promised to deliver a 'reid' and maamar that later became Kuntres HaAvodah.
Story: Overcome by heat and pressure of the crowd at the Simchat Torah 5670 farbrengen, the Rebbe Rashab stood and told the chassidim he would not release them until he gave them a 'reid' as Tomchei Temimim required, and a maamar. The discourse was eventually published in 5671 (1910/11) as Kuntres HaAvodah, though it was also called Kuntres 5669.
Tags: rebbe rashab, kuntres haavodah, tomchei temimim, simchat torah

Title: Simchat Torah farbrengen of Rebbe Rashab in Small Hall, 5670
Summary: On Simchat Torah 5670 the Rebbe Rashab held a farbrengen in the Small Hall at Lubavitch, speaking emotionally about his father, the Rebbe Maharash.
Story: Because the Great Hall was closed, the Simchat Torah daytime farbrengen took place in the crowded Small Hall, with the Rebbe Rashab entering through a door from the Maharash's adjoining room. He spoke at length and wept while recalling his father's Simchat Torah and 19 Kislev. Crushing pressure broke tables and benches; his elderly mother Rebbetzin Rivkah and his wife Rebbetzin Sterna Sarah came to plead with him not to overexert himself.
Tags: lubavitch, rebbe rashab, simchat torah, rebbetzin rivkah, kuntres haavodah

Title: R' David Leib Yaffe of Hebron passes away in Jerusalem
Summary: R' David Leib ben Moshe Yaffe, born in Eretz Yisrael to a Hebron Chabad family, died in Jerusalem on 3 Cheshvan 5670.
Story: R' David Leib was the son of the emissary R' Moshe ben David Yaffe of Hebron and was born in Eretz Yisrael, listed as a child of three in the 5599 census and as age 31 in the 5626 census. He later moved to live in Jerusalem, where he passed away on 3 Cheshvan 5670, his death recorded in 'Avnei Zikaron' vol. 12.
Tags: hebron, jerusalem, yaffe family

Title: Compromise agreement on Chernigov delegates
Summary: Yitzchak Schneersohn proposed and reached an agreement with the Rebbe Rashab to split the two Chernigov gubernia delegate seats — one for each camp.
Story: On the morning of the assembly, Yitzchak Schneersohn came to the Rebbe Rashab's home immediately after prayers and proposed a compromise to avoid conflict: each side would get one delegate. The Rebbe's candidate Rabbi Mendel Chen of Nezhin would be elected, alongside one candidate from the opposing camp. The Rebbe, calculating the uncertainty of his less reliable supporters, accepted on the spot. Both delegates were subsequently elected from Chernigov gubernia.
Tags: russia, chernigov, elections, rabbi mendel chen, compromise

Title: District elections in Chernigov gubernia
Summary: Elections of delegates in the remaining districts of Chernigov gubernia were held, with Rabbi Menachem Mendel Chen elected from Nezhin.
Story: The week after the elections in the city of Chernigov, the remaining districts (uyezds) of the Chernigov gubernia held their elections. Attached to the Rebbe Rayatz's letter dated the night of 27 Cheshvan was the list of elected delegates, which included Rabbi Menachem Mendel Chen, son of the Rad"tz, chosen from his town of Nezhin. He would later play a major role in the conference.
Tags: russia, chernigov, elections, nezhin, rabbi mendel chen

Title: Election of two delegates from Chernigov gubernia
Summary: Rabbi David Tzvi Chen and Yitzchak Schneersohn were elected as the two delegates from the city of Chernigov for the upcoming Rabbinical Conference.
Story: The city of Chernigov elected two delegates to the rabbinical conference: Rabbi David Tzvi (the Rad"tz) Chen, the religious rabbi of the city, and Mr. Yitzchak Schneersohn, the government-appointed rabbi (Rabbiner). The Rebbe Rashab wrote on the night of 25 Cheshvan that the government rabbi of Chernigov was not aligned with their camp, while the Rad"tz had only been chosen from Chernigov itself, with further district elections still pending.
Tags: russia, chernigov, elections, rabbinical conference, rabbi david tzvi chen, yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Rebbe Rashab travels to Chernigov for delegate selection
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab traveled personally to Chernigov to lead the campaign for selecting two observant rabbis as gubernia representatives to the conference.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab journeyed to Chernigov, accompanied by his son (the future Rebbe Rayatz), to manage the campaign for delegate selection. Knowing his own nephew Yitzchak Schneersohn was a candidate but not sufficiently God-fearing, he insisted that in matters of holiness, family ties carry no weight. He met with each rabbi and delegate individually to hear their views before sharing his own.
Tags: russia, chernigov, elections, mohilev, rabbinical conference

Title: Schneersohn elected as delegate from shtetl Nevel
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab was elected as a delegate from the shtetl of Nevel in the Vitebsk gubernia, despite efforts by secularists to block his selection.
Story: During preparations for the Petersburg Rabbinical Conference, electors in the shtetl of Nevel (Vitebsk gubernia) unanimously voted to send the Rebbe Rashab (Rabbi Sholom DovBer Schneersohn) as their delegate. Secular activists tried to introduce a break in the voting and lobby against his candidacy, but failed. Nevel was the locality from which he was officially chosen.
Tags: russia, vitebsk, nevel, elections, rabbinical conference, tsarist russia

Title: Last known appointment of Hebron Joint Vaad
Summary: On 15 Kislev 5670 seventy-five Hebron heads of household signed the last known appointment of the joint Vaad.
Story: The last known appointment document of the Hebron joint Vaad is dated 15 Kislev 5670 and bears the signatures of seventy-five heads of family in Hebron. The names of the three elected members were not specified in the document, which simply addressed them as 'three who walk uprightly chosen by majority to manage the Vaad HaKlali.'
Tags: hebron, vaad, appointment

Title: Boys' division opened for Rostov children
Summary: In Tevet 5670 a new department opened in Lubavitch for 11-12 year-old boys from Rostov.
Story: On 7 Tevet 5670 (December 1909), the Rebbe Rashab approved opening a new younger department in Lubavitch, primarily for a group of children from Rostov aged 11-12. This addressed Rostov chassidim's request that their children be educated in Lubavitch, with a special melamed assigned. The Rashab saw this as building Jewish education in Rostov as well.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, rostov, young students

Title: Encouraging election results reported in Tevet
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab wrote that the bitter inter-party election struggle was producing favorable results, with the majority of those being elected being observant rabbis.
Story: In Tevet, the Rebbe Rashab wrote to Rabbi Shilo (Hareshil"a) that the conflict between the parties was very intense, but that — God willing — the observant camp would prevail in the elections with a majority of kosher delegates. He noted that even the few elected were accomplishing much, and that opponents were also working hard from outside, requiring great effort on their part to rouse and act.
Tags: russia, elections, rabbinical conference, tsarist russia

Title: Rebbe Rayatz dates Tzemach Tzedek manuscript
Summary: In Teves 5670 the Rebbe Rashab wrote a letter reconsidering the authorship of a small manuscript whose cover bore the inscription 'Adkaru lei yoma d'tilga,' concluding it was likely the Tzemach Tzedek's handwriting rather than the Mitteler Rebbe's.
Story: In Kuntres Etz HaChaim the Rashab had cited the inscription with uncertainty about which Rebbe had written it. In his Teves 5670 letter he reconsidered and concluded it was more likely the Tzemach Tzedek's hand. The manuscript was later catalogued as item 29 in the Rayatz's collection but was lost during World War II along with many other bichlach.

Title: First published list of Tomchei Tmimim graduates
Summary: The first known list of Tomchei Tmimim graduates was published on 14 Tevet 5670.
Story: On 14 Tevet 5670 (December 26, 1909), a list of Tomchei Tmimim graduates was published — the first such roster of alumni. It was later reprinted in 'MiBeit HaGenazim' and represents the earliest documented effort to catalog the yeshiva's students.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, alumni list, russia

Title: Author moves to Shchedrin branch after Shavuot 5670
Summary: After Shavuot 5670, the memoirist relocated to the Shchedrin branch of Tomchei Temimim to continue his studies.
Story: At Shchedrin he heard a shiur in nigleh from R. Moshe Mordechai Amrami (Poharelsky) of Pochep on tractate Bava Batra. The two classes were combined under R. Shaul Dov Zislin's direction, and the mashgiach for nigleh was R. Yaakov Baruch Krasik.
Tags: shchedrin, tomchei temimim, moshe mordechai poharelsky

Title: Examinations at Tomchei Temimim attended by Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: In spring 5670, examinations of younger students at Tomchei Temimim were conducted by senior bochurim, with the Rebbe Rayatz entering during the test.
Story: The memoirist and his brother-in-law Alter Beilin were tested by R. Raphael Cohen of Germanovitch and R. Avraham Eli Plotkin in Ketubot 74b. The exam took place Friday morning of erev Shabbat, and the Rebbe Rayatz, then director of Tomchei Temimim, entered during the testing. The author notes the awe his presence inspired and that they passed successfully.
Tags: lubavitch, tomchei temimim, rebbe rayatz, raphael cohen

Title: Founding of Gemach Shomrei Shabbos in New York
Summary: The 'Shomrei Shabbos' free-loan society was founded in the year 5670, with its office at the Tzemach Tzedek shul on 184 Henry Street in New York.
Story: The Shomrei Shabbos gemach (free-loan society) was established in 5670 and based at the Tzemach Tzedek synagogue at 184 Henry Street, a three-story stone building in a Jewish neighborhood of New York. Although little is known of its earliest years, the institution's location at the Chabad shul suggests it may have been founded from the outset as a Chabad chassidic gemach. R' Gershon Simson served as its first chairman.

Title: Mazkir R' Reuven Liberman writes letter on state of Pleshchenitsy
Summary: On the eve of Shabbat Parshat Chukat 5670, R' Reuven Liberman wrote to R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum lamenting how Pleshchenitsy had declined.
Story: R' Reuven Liberman, leader of the Pleshchenitsy Chassidim after R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum's emigration, wrote on the eve of Shabbat Parshat Chukat 5670 (1910) describing how the town's glory had vanished. He contrasted the flourishing time when Rosenbaum lived there with its present decline, and longed to see him again even for a moment.
Tags: pleshchenitsy, r reuven liberman

Title: Move of Shchedrin students delayed; learning in Great Hall
Summary: After Pesach 5670, students bound for Shchedrin were forced to remain in Lubavitch and learn in the Great Hall until after Shavuot.
Story: Although the students were supposed to leave for Shchedrin after Pesach, the host town was not ready to receive them. They remained in Lubavitch, studying in the Great Hall under supervision of R. Yosef Friedman of Rogachov for nigleh and R. Moshe of Zembin for chassidus.
Tags: lubavitch, shchedrin, tomchei temimim

Title: National rabbinic conference convenes in St. Petersburg
Summary: The Russian government hosted an unprecedented national conference of rabbis and community leaders in St. Petersburg.
Story: Traditional rabbis, crown rabbis, and community leaders gathered to seek consensus on community leadership and education. The Rashab was named as one of the conference organizers, with the Rayatz at his side throughout. Rabbi Chaim Ozer Grodzinski's compromise position on secular knowledge for rabbis was adopted by majority. The conference concluded with a disrespectful meeting with Prime Minister Stolypin.
Tags: st petersburg, rabbinic conference, crown rabbis, stolypin, chaim ozer grodzinski, chafetz chaim

Title: National rabbinic conference in St. Petersburg
Summary: The government convened a national conference in St. Petersburg to resolve issues of community leadership and education.
Story: In 1910, the Russian government held an unprecedented rabbinic conference in St. Petersburg with the Rashab among the organizers. Debates centered on whether community rabbis needed secular education; Rabbi Chaim Ozer's compromise prevailed. The conference concluded with a disrespectful meeting with Prime Minister Pyotr Stolypin.
Tags: st petersburg, crown rabbis, stolypin, rabbinic conference, education

Title: R' Avraham Zaltzman arrives in Lubavitch
Summary: R' Avraham Zaltzman arrived to learn at Tomchei Tmimim around Rosh Hashanah 5671.
Story: R' Avraham Zaltzman recorded in a letter to his sons that he arrived in Lubavitch around Rosh Hashanah 5671 (1910). He progressed through the chadarim — studying with the Vietker melamed, then with Itzcheh, then with the Sener melamed, then with R' Yechiel, then with the Dvinsker R' Yehoshua Arsh, then with R' Shmuel Borisover — before being sent to study in Shchedrin.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, zaltzman, cheder

Title: Rashab considers opening Tomchei Temimim branch in Eretz Yisrael
Summary: The Rashab began to seriously consider opening a branch of the yeshivah in Eretz Yisrael, focused on Hebron.
Story: Jerusalem's historically religious character was being transformed by non-religious Zionist immigrants, while Hebron remained a spiritual oasis. To bolster the impoverished Chabad community there, the Rayatz established Chevronim, a special fund to help Hebron's Jews. The community leaders asked the Rashab to purchase Beit Romano.
Tags: rashab, hebron, eretz yisrael, toras emes, chabad expansion

Title: Rashab from Menton objects to merging Rayatz's books into his library
Summary: While in Menton, France in winter 5670, Rashab responds to Rayatz's plan to add his personal books to his father's collection, expressing mixed feelings.
Story: While the Lubavitch books were being arranged in cabinets during the winter of 5670, Rayatz wished to fill out his father's collection from his own private holdings. Rashab, writing from Menton, replies that while he enjoys the completion, he is concerned that books be available in Rayatz's own room for casual learning. The episode marks the formal occasion when Rayatz instructed his bookbinder to emboss his initials 'yud-shin' in gold on the spines of his volumes to distinguish his collection.

Title: Rayatz arrested in St. Petersburg over conscription advocacy
Summary: The Rayatz was briefly imprisoned in St. Petersburg for advocating military exemptions for young men.
Story: In 1910, czarist authorities arrested the Rayatz in St. Petersburg for his efforts to exempt young Jewish men from military service. As with his other arrests between 1911 and 1916, the detention was brief and ended with a stern warning when no incriminating evidence was found.
Tags: rayatz, arrest, st petersburg, military service

Title: Rayatz imprisoned in St. Petersburg over military exemption efforts
Summary: The Rayatz was imprisoned in St. Petersburg because of his efforts to exempt young men from Russian military service.
Story: This was one of four arrests of the Rayatz between 1911 and 1916. All detentions were brief, since government inquiries found nothing incriminating. He was released each time with a stern warning, but these incidents spurred him to even greater communal efforts. He was imprisoned again in 1916 for the same cause.
Tags: rayatz, st petersburg, arrest, military exemption

Title: Rayatz involved in preparing the Rabbinical Conference
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak helped prepare a major Rabbinical Conference addressing Russian Jewish religious affairs.
Story: The conference was part of ongoing efforts to defend traditional Jewish practice in the face of Russian government interference. Between 1902 and 1911, his communal advocacy resulted in four arrests in Moscow and St. Petersburg.
Tags: rabbinical conference, russia

Title: Rayatz's St. Petersburg arrest over rabbis' conference
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was arrested in St. Petersburg following an informer's report about planning for a rabbis' conference.
Story: In 1910, Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was arrested in St. Petersburg after an informer alerted authorities about his role in planning a rabbinic conference. Such gatherings were viewed as politically threatening by czarist authorities monitoring Jewish religious leadership. This was the fourth in his series of arrests under the Russian regime.
Tags: st. petersburg, russia, arrest, informer, rabbinic conference, yosef yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Rebbe Rashab and Rabbi Chaim Soloveitchik return to Petersburg
Summary: In Iyar, the Rebbe Rashab and Rabbi Chaim Soloveitchik returned to Petersburg, where communal needs required them to remain until late Sivan.
Story: During the month of Iyar 5670, the Rebbe Rashab and Rabbi Chaim Soloveitchik of Brisk returned together to Petersburg. The state of communal affairs required them to remain in the capital through the end of Sivan. On the second day of Shavuot, Rabbi Chaim joined the Rebbe Rashab for the festive holiday meal, where they discussed words of Torah.
Tags: russia, petersburg, rabbi chaim soloveitchik, communal affairs

Title: Rebbe Rashab publishes 'Cheshbon Katzar' on Petersburg Conference
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab published a pamphlet 'Cheshbon Katzar' giving a detailed account of the Petersburg Rabbinical Conference and explaining the minority's reasoning.
Story: At the conclusion of the conference, the Rebbe Rashab printed a booklet titled 'Cheshbon Katzar from the Petersburg Rabbinical Conference at the Rabbis' Assembly, 5670.' In the introduction he wrote that he wished to present to his brethren a short accounting of the conference's actions and clarify the various decisions and their reasoning. The pamphlet was published over the course of the summer of 5670.
Tags: russia, petersburg, rabbinical conference, pamphlet

Title: Rebbe Rashab travels to Petersburg in Cheshvan 5671
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab journeyed to Petersburg in Cheshvan 5671 to make final corrections to the Petersburg Conference protocol before its submission to the Interior Ministry.
Story: After the official protocol was prepared, Baron David Gunzburg signed it and prepared to submit it, but fell ill with his final illness. The question arose of who would deliver the protocol to the head of the Religious Affairs Department at the Interior Ministry, and several corrections were still required. The Rebbe Rashab traveled to Petersburg in Cheshvan 5671 to handle these matters; the protocol was apparently submitted at that time.
Tags: russia, petersburg, baron david gunzburg, rabbinical conference

Title: Sighet Haggadah with 'Tzemach Hashem L'Tzvi' commentary by Tzvi Hirsh of Nadvorna
Summary: A new Haggadah commentary 'Tzemach Hashem L'Tzvi' by Tzvi Hirsh of Nadvorna, with his father Shalom Zelig's pamphlet, was printed in Sighet.
Story: In 5670 (1910), the Haggadah with the new commentary 'Tzemach Hashem L'Tzvi' by Tzvi Hirsh of Nadvorna was published in Sighet by Avraham Kaufman and Sons. The 39-leaf duodecimo edition included a 'Divrei Shalom' pamphlet by the author's father, Shalom Zelig. It served the Galician Nadvorna Chassidic community.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, nadvorna, sighet, tzvi hirsh, shalom zelig

Title: SILA's sixth Russia journey to advance Chevron Chabad projects
Summary: In late 5670 SILA traveled to Russia to transfer Chevron property to the Rebbe Rashab's name, restore the minyan at the Avraham Avinu synagogue, and establish the Toras Emes yeshiva.
Story: SILA's sixth Russia trip pursued three major Chevron Chabad initiatives: registering a Chevron property in the Rebbe Rashab's name, renewing the minyan at the historic Avraham Avinu synagogue, and founding the Toras Emes yeshiva. He remained in Lubavitch for most of 5671 and much of 5672 working on these projects. The Toras Emes yeshiva would become a landmark institution of Chabad education in Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: shneur zalman ladier, chevron, rebbe rashab, toras emes, avraham avinu synagogue

Title: Three-way split on Russian rabbinic status at Petersburg Conference
Summary: The Petersburg Rabbinical Conference split into three factions over what educational requirements should apply to officially recognized rabbis in Russia.
Story: The central debate at the conference concerned the legal status of rabbis in Russia, who had not been government-recognized as spiritual leaders. The majority, led by Rabbi Chaim Ozer Grodzinski of Vilna, favored limited secular education and Russian language proficiency, with the rabbi also managing birth certificates. A twelve-member modernist minority led by the lawyer H. Sliozberg demanded broader secular education and refined Russian. An eight-member minority led by the Rebbe Rashab insisted that rabbis need only know Torah, with a separate clerk handling birth certificates. The conference elected a committee of three, including the Rebbe, to draft conclusions for the Interior Ministry's Religious Department.
Tags: russia, petersburg, rabbinical conference, rabbi chaim ozer, henry slozberg, government rabbis

Title: Rebbe Rashab discusses division of father's books with son Rayatz
Summary: On 18 Tevet 5670 the Rebbe Rashab wrote to his son the Rayatz about identifying books inherited from his father, the Rebbe Maharash.
Story: In letter 282 the Rebbe Rashab described how the books from the Rebbe Maharash's private study could be identified by their bindings, and referenced an old list of how the books were divided among the brothers, which R. Nissan Skvolla still held. The autograph manuscripts had gone entirely to him as successor.

Title: Maharashab travels to Petersburg
Summary: Maharashab's passport was stamped in Petersburg on 28 Adar I 5670.
Story: On 24 February 1910 (28 Adar I 5670), Maharashab arrived in Petersburg, the first of three trips he would make to the capital that year.

Title: Petersburg rabbinical conference debates rabbinic credentials and chinuch
Summary: A government-convened rabbinical conference in St. Petersburg debated requiring secular-education certificates for rabbis and reforming cheder studies.
Story: In Adar 5670, leading rabbis of the Russian Empire assembled in St. Petersburg for a rabbinical conference whose agenda included the proposed requirement that rabbis hold a secular-education certificate, the future of the kazyonny (crown) rabbinate, and the place of secular studies in the cheder system. The Rebbe Rashab invested years of preparation in shaping the lineup of attendees and their positions, urging opposition to mandatory secular credentials and to the modernist reforms championed by the maskilic attorney Henry Slosberg. Communities such as Vitebsk and Romen submitted petitions backing the Rashab's positions, several of which were preserved in his archive.
Tags: russia, petersburg-rabbinical-conference, rebbe-rashab, kazyonny-rabbi, haskalah, slosberg

Title: Sixth Rabbinical Commission convenes in Petersburg
Summary: The Sixth Rabbinical Commission convened in Petersburg in Adar Sheni 5670 (March 1910) to address Russian Jewish religious affairs.
Story: The Sixth Commission was the final meeting of the state-convened Rabbinical Commission before the fall of the Tsarist regime. Like its predecessors it addressed matters of the rabbinate, but no change was made to the law on Crown Rabbis; the dual-rabbinate system continued until the Communist takeover.
Tags: petersburg, rabbinical commission, rabbanut mitaam

Title: Petersburg Rabbinical Conference convenes
Summary: The Petersburg Rabbinical Conference began on 4 Adar Sheni and ran for about a month until 6 Nissan, with the Rebbe Rashab effectively leading the proceedings.
Story: The Conference lasted approximately one month from 4 Adar Sheni to 6 Nissan 5670. The Rebbe Rashab dominated as the true leader, setting the tone and effectively directing the assembly despite formally remaining in the background. Because sessions had to be conducted in Russian and his fluency was limited, his views were articulated by Rabbi Mendel Chen of Nezhin, who excelled in Russian oratory, Talmudic learning, and piety. Henrich Sliozberg later wrote in his memoirs that the young Rebbe rarely spoke much, but every word demonstrated mastery over the masses; he was as immovable as stone on religious matters.
Tags: russia, petersburg, rabbinical conference, rabbi chaim ozer, henry slozberg, rabbi mendel chen

Title: Petersburg Rabbinical Conference of 1910
Summary: From 4 Adar II to 6 Nisan 5670 (March 15 to April 15, 1910) the official Russian Rabbinical Conference convened in Petersburg for approximately one month, with Dr. Krebs serving as the government representative.
Story: After two years of intensive preparation, the official Rabbinical Conference (Ravvinskaya Komissiya) convened in Petersburg under the auspices of the Ministry of the Interior's religious affairs department. The conference was the culmination of years of effort by Rebbe Rashab and the Orthodox rabbinate, who had finally succeeded in ensuring that this iteration of the periodic government rabbinical commission would consist primarily of pious Orthodox rabbis from across the empire, including the Polish provinces. The conference proper lasted about a month, with follow-up work continuing through the end of 5670.
Tags: russia, petersburg, ministry of interior, dr. krebs, rabbinical conference, rashab

Title: Vitebsk cheder teachers petition Petersburg conference against secular studies
Summary: Fifteen Vitebsk cheder teachers and principals petitioned the Petersburg rabbinical conference to bar secular studies for children under thirteen.
Story: On 17 Adar Sheini 5670, fifteen melamdim and principals of cheders in Vitebsk signed a letter, led by R. Dov Nachman Horowitz, to the rabbis assembled in St. Petersburg. They warned from experience that exposing young children to Russian-language schoolbooks and gymnasium classes hollowed out their faith and led them to reject Chassidus and prayer. They proposed barring admission to Russian-language schools before age thirteen, requiring melamdim to teach mussar works approved by rabbis, and ensuring religious instruction in state schools be given only by Orthodox rabbis. The letter was conveyed to the conference through Vitebsk's rabbi, R. Shmaryahu Yehuda Leib Medalia.

Title: Maharashab travels to Petersburg
Summary: Maharashab's passport was stamped in Petersburg on 16 Iyar 5670.
Story: On 12 May 1910 (16 Iyar 5670), Maharashab returned to Petersburg, with his internal passport receiving another official stamp.

Title: Rosh Hashanah 5671 journey from Shchedrin to Lubavitch
Summary: For Rosh Hashanah 5671, the new Shchedrin students traveled together to Lubavitch despite the yeshiva refusing travel expenses.
Story: Eighteen students obtained permission to travel only after depositing five rubles each for return travel. Joined by chassidim from Bobruisk-area towns, they rented a dedicated train car from Zlobin to Orsha and spent the journey singing chassidic niggunim. R. Shaul Dov Zislin led the lively farbrengen on the train, drawing curious onlookers from other cars.

Title: Maharashab travels to Petersburg
Summary: Maharashab's passport was stamped in Petersburg on 16 Cheshvan 5671.
Story: On 5 November 1910 (16 Cheshvan 5671), Maharashab travelled to Petersburg for the third time that calendar year, with his passport again stamped at the capital.

Title: Kollel Chabad publishes detailed fundraising accounts
Summary: In Kislev 5671 Kollel Chabad's trustees printed an itemized account of their etrog-trade-linked support in HaModia.
Story: The supplement to HaModia presented a detailed list of remittances from hundreds of towns abroad for fiscal year 5670. Most communities were marked as having sent funds directly to Jerusalem rather than through shadarim. About one hundred towns were listed as collected by R. Ber Reich and roughly forty by R. Hirsch Tomerkin, indicating the surviving network of itinerant emissaries.

Title: Assassination of Russian Prime Minister Pyotr Stolypin
Summary: Pyotr Stolypin, Russia's interior minister and prime minister, was assassinated.
Story: Stolypin had been the target of the Rayatz's covert St. Petersburg mission to subvert his planned anti-Jewish decree. He had served Czar Nicholas II since 1906. Earlier in 1910, he had met disrespectfully with rabbinic leaders at the conclusion of the national rabbinic conference, blaming them for the Bund's anti-government activities.

Title: Death of R' Gershon Dov of Driben
Summary: In 5671 the rosh yeshiva of Tomchei Tmimim Shchedrin, R' Zalman Dov of Driben, passed away.
Story: In 5671 (1911), the rosh yeshiva of Tomchei Tmimim in Shchedrin, the gaon R' Zalman Dov 'der Dribiner', passed away. The yeshiva placed advertisements in newspapers seeking a replacement, and various candidates came to deliver test shiurim before the staff and senior students, but none were chosen.

Title: Death of R' Michoel Bliner
Summary: R' Michoel Bliner ('Reb Michoel der Alter'), mashpia in Tomchei Tmimim, passed away on Motzaei Shabbat Toldot 5672.
Story: R' Michoel Bliner, known as 'Reb Michoel der Alter', served as an additional mashpia in Tomchei Tmimim from 5660 until his death on Motzaei Shabbat Toldot 5672 (November 1911). He was renowned for his extreme devotion and once shared with Ben-Zion Dinur how he had crossed the broken Dnieper ice three times to reach the Tzemach Tzedek before Pesach 5625.

Title: Death of Rabbi Mordechai Twersky of Loyev
Summary: Rabbi Mordechai of Loyev, son of Rabbi Menachem Nachum, dies in 5671.
Story: Rabbi Mordechai of Loyev died in 5671, providing the latest possible date for his surviving letter of recommendation on behalf of a chasid seeking to settle in the Land of Israel. That letter, addressed to communities including Brahin, Layev, Mazyr, Rechitsa, and Bobruisk, also references the 'great rabbi of Lubavitch' (Maharash or Rashab) who interceded for the petitioner.

Title: Derech Mitzvosecha and early Tzemach Tzedek chasidic works printed
Summary: Beginning in 5671, the Tzemach Tzedek's chasidic works — Derech Mitzvosecha, Derech Emunah (Sefer HaChakirah), Yahel Ohr, and the first volume of Or HaTorah — were printed in the generation after his passing.
Story: Some 45 years after the Tzemach Tzedek's passing, his chasidic writings began to appear in print. The works printed between 5671 and 5678 included Derech Mitzvosecha (on mitzvos), Derech Emunah (philosophical investigation), Yahel Ohr (on Tehillim), and the first volume of Or HaTorah. The majority of his chasidic corpus — the Or HaTorah series — would only see print in the seventh generation.

Title: Lawyer Ibsen completes memorandum on rabbinic status
Summary: The Petersburg lawyer Ibsen finished preparing a memorandum on the status of rabbis in late Iyar 5671 after persistent prodding by the Rebbe Rashab.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab had commissioned the Petersburg lawyer Ibsen to prepare a separate memorandum (doklad), apparently concerning rabbinic status, for submission to the Religious Affairs Department. The work dragged on until late Iyar 5671. Throughout the winter, the Rebbe repeatedly pressed Ibsen to finish, working through his son, Rabbi Shmuel Gourary, and Rabbi Menachem Mendel Chen. After completion, additional corrections were needed before submission to Chanan, head of the Religious Department.

Title: R' Alter Simchowitz sent to found Yeshivat Toras Emet in Hebron
Summary: At the beginning of 5672, R' Alter Simchowitz was chosen as one of seven students sent by the Rebbe Rashab to establish Yeshivat Toras Emet in Hebron.
Story: The Rashab dispatched seven Tomchei Tmimim students to the Holy Land to seed a Chabad yeshiva in Hebron. Simchowitz returned to Lubavitch at the end of that same year and continued studying there until 5680, serving as a chozer who transmitted the maamarim of the Rashab.

Title: R' Gershon Chen leaves Lubavitch for Alexandria
Summary: In 5671, R' Gershon Chen left Lubavitch to fill his late father-in-law's rabbinical post in Alexandria.
Story: In 5671 (1911), R' Gershon Chen's father-in-law R' Chaim Leib Atkin, rabbi of Alexandria, passed away, and Chen left Lubavitch to fill the rabbinical position there. In 5679 he opened a branch of Tomchei Tmimim in Alexandria, as recorded in Toldot Chabad b'Russia haSovietit.

Title: R' Yaakov Boruch Krasik becomes mashgiach
Summary: At the start of 5672, R' Yaakov Boruch Krasik was appointed mashgiach over nigleh in Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: At the start of 5672 (autumn 1911), R' Yaakov Boruch Krasik, who had previously been mashgiach over nigleh in Shchedrin, was appointed mashgiach over nigleh at Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch. He retained this position until the yeshiva moved to Kremenchug in 5678, where he continued until his death in 5681.
