Title: R' Yehoshua Arsh becomes Rosh Yeshiva at Zal Hakatan
Summary: R' Yehoshua Arsh was accepted as Rosh Yeshiva of the Zal Hakatan in Lubavitch in 5671 (1911).
Story: R' Yehoshua Arsh, who had been head of the Dvinsk yeshiva endowed by the wealthy R' Moshe Weitenberg, was accepted in 5671 (1911) as Rosh Yeshiva of the Zal Hakatan ('small hall') of Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch. At the request of R' Dovid Volovich of Dvinsk, he brought his son Chaim Aba Veil along to study in Lubavitch.

Title: Rebbe Rayatz instructs R' Shimon Hauzman to prepare Hebron quarters
Summary: In Tammuz 5671 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to prepare rooms in Hebron for the new yeshiva's mashpia and students.
Story: In Tammuz 5671, as the decision was reached to send students from Lubavitch to Hebron, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Shimon Hauzman, who managed the Hebron building, asking him to prepare five rooms in the property — three on the upper floor for the mashpia and yeshiva office, and two on the lower floor for the visiting students. A parallel letter went to R' Yitzchak Chen, who had settled in Hebron that year.

Title: Rosenbaum writes his will mentioning the Tzemach Tzedek's tallis
Summary: In his 5671 will, Rosenbaum records that the Tzemach Tzedek's tallis is in his wife's keeping and that he is afraid to wear it.
Story: Writing his will in 5671 (1911), Rosenbaum noted that he still possessed the tallis of the Tzemach Tzedek, acquired in full payment from the meshulach R. Madil after he personally identified it as the one in which the Rebbe had prayed. He admitted uncertainty whether the tzitzis on it were the originals or replacements made by R. Madil, and explained that out of awe he could not bring himself to wear another tzaddik's tallis in this world.

Title: Search for new Rosh Mesivta in Shchedrin in 5671
Summary: In 5671 the Shchedrin branch searched for a new Rosh Mesivta but could not find a suitable candidate.
Story: Among the candidates was Nachum Eliezer of Paritch, a brilliant scholar with semicha from the Rogatchover Gaon. Although he delivered two impressive shiurim, he was not hired due to a health concern. Several other candidates were tried unsuccessfully.

Title: Seder HaAvodah siddur issued in Vilna
Summary: The Seder HaAvodah Chabad siddur was issued in Vilna in 5671 (1911).
Story: This 1911 Vilna siddur would later serve as the photographic base for the first 1945 Tehillas Hashem edition, with corrections directed by the Rebbe Rayatz.

Title: Tefilot LeKol HaShanah with Chinuch HaDat introduction printed in Vilna
Summary: A Tefilot LeKol HaShanah following the Arizal nusach with laws drawn from the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch was printed in Vilna.
Story: In 5671 (1911), 'Tefilot LeKol HaShanah' was printed in Vilna following the Arizal nusach with laws drawn from the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch, marginal notes by 'Torah Or', reading marks, tagim and other details. It opened with an essay titled 'Chinuch HaDat V'HaLashon' (Religious and Linguistic Education). The 168-leaf octavo edition served the Chabad community of Lithuania before World War I.

Title: Tomchei Temimim Tomchei Tmimim founds Toras Emes yeshiva in Hebron
Summary: In summer 5671, the Rebbe Rashab announced the founding of a yeshiva in Eretz Yisrael, dispatching R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin with students to Hebron.
Story: After Shavuot 5671 (1911) it became known that the Rebbe Rashab was establishing a yeshiva in the Holy Land, choosing Hebron as its location. R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin traveled with five selected students—R. Yechezkel Feigin, R. Alter Simchovich, R. Hillel of Pochep, R. Yisrael Zalman of Yanovich, and R. Tzvi Katzav of Hadiach—along with three volunteers who joined them.
Tags: hebron, eretz yisrael, toras emes, rebbe rashab, shlomo zalman havlin

Title: Tomchei Tmimim 'Toras Emes' yeshiva opens in Hebron
Summary: The Toras Emes yeshiva opened in Hebron at the start of 5672.
Story: At the start of 5672 a branch of Tomchei Tmimim, the Toras Emes yeshiva, opened in Hebron and operated for nearly three years. Studies began in the house donated by R' Shneur Zalman Berlin, which had previously housed the Magen Avos yeshiva, and were later moved to the Romano courtyard. Sleeping quarters for students and the mashpia's family were assigned in the large building purchased by the Rebbe Rashab in 5668.
Tags: hebron, toras emes, tomchei tmimim, rayatz, rashab, yeshiva

Title: Toras Emes yeshivah established in Hebron
Summary: The Rashab sent a group of outstanding students led by Rabbi Zalman Havlin to Hebron to establish Toras Emes, the first chasidic yeshivah in the Jewish homeland.
Story: Considered a branch of Tomchei Temimim in Lubavitch, the new yeshivah aimed to invigorate the study of chasidic teachings in Eretz Yisrael and create a new cadre of Jewish leaders there. Just as the Rashab hoped Tomchei Temimim graduates would set a new direction for Russian Jewry, he hoped Toras Emes graduates would do so in the Holy Land.
Tags: hebron, toras emes, zalman havlin, eretz yisrael, chasidic yeshivah

Title: Toras Emes yeshivah founded in Hebron
Summary: The Rashab sent students led by Rabbi Zalman Havlin to Hebron to establish Toras Emes, the first chasidic yeshivah in the Jewish homeland.
Story: In 1911, the Rashab dispatched a group of outstanding Tomchei Temimim students led by Rabbi Zalman Havlin to Hebron to establish Toras Emes. As a branch of Tomchei Temimim, it was intended to invigorate chasidic study in Eretz Yisrael and produce a new cadre of Jewish leaders for the land.
Tags: toras emes, hebron, zalman havlin, eretz yisrael, branch yeshivah

Title: Yeshiva Toras Emes founded in Hebron
Summary: The Chabad yeshiva Toras Emes was established in Hebron at the start of 5672, surviving roughly two and a half years until WWI shut it down.
Story: The yeshiva Toras Emes was founded in Hebron in early 5672 (late 1911). It operated for some two and a half years until the outbreak of World War I forced the mashpia-director and students — Russian subjects in an enemy state — to return to Russia. The yeshiva would lie dormant for seven years until being refounded in Jerusalem.
Tags: hebron, toras emes, rashab, havlin, yeshiva

Title: Yeshivat Torat Emet founded in Hebron
Summary: At the start of 5672 the Rebbe Rashab founded Yeshivat Torat Emet in Hebron, sending a mashpia and seven select Tomchei Temimim students.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab established Yeshivat Torat Emet in Hebron at the beginning of 5672. To launch it he dispatched a dedicated mashpia along with seven of the finest students from Yeshivat Tomchei Temimim in Lubavitch. In a general letter to chassidim in winter 5672 he explained that the lack of a proper yeshiva in their kollel had left even those drawn to Torah study without support, and announced the new institution as the realization of the founders' true vision.
Tags: hebron, chabad, rashab, yeshiva, torat emet, tomchei temimim

Title: Yeshivat Torat Emet founded in Hebron with seven Tomchei Tmimim students
Summary: Seven elite Tomchei Tmimim students are sent to Hebron to found the Torat Emet yeshiva there.
Story: Seven select students of Tomchei Tmimim — among them Alter Simchovitz, Hillel Pevzner, Tzvi Hirsch Katzav, Yechezkel Feigin, Menachem Krasik, Avraham Eli Asherov, and Yisrael Zalman Asnas — were dispatched in 1911 to found Yeshivat Torat Emet in Hebron. Nine additional students from Hebron and Jerusalem joined them. R' Shimon Glitzenstein later recalled enrolling in the yeshiva's first year, at the end of summer 5672.
Tags: hebron, torat emet, tomchei tmimim, rashab, frierdiker rebbe

Title: R' Yosef Friedman appointed mashgiach
Summary: By Shevat 5671, R' Yosef Friedman of Rogachov had been appointed mashgiach replacing R' Zev Wolf Lewitin.
Story: After the passing of R' Zev Wolf Lewitin, R' Yosef Friedman of Rogachov was appointed mashgiach over nigleh at Tomchei Tmimim, as mentioned in a letter dated 15 Shevat 5671 (1911). He later became rabbi of Ostrovna. R' Yisrael Jacobson recalled him as filling the role of the departed R' Zev Wolf Halevi.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, friedman, rogachov, mashgiach

Title: Tomchei Tmimim funds Magen Avot students in Hebron
Summary: On the eve of 1 Adar 5671 R' Shneur Zalman Landau of Lubavitch sent 200 rubles and a stipend list for Magen Avot students, formalizing the yeshiva's affiliation with Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: The accompanying receipt template had each student in Hebron acknowledge that his stipend came 'from the association Tomchei Tmimim of Lubavitch, under the leadership of the Rebbe.' Each student signed individually. The disbursements covered Tammuz and Menachem Av 5670, marking a concrete step in establishing Lubavitch's institutional presence in the Land of Israel before the founding of Torat Emet.
Tags: hebron, magen avot, tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, shila, stipends

Title: R. Avraham Chaim writes a private will for his son Yaakov
Summary: On 2 Iyar 5671 R. Avraham Chaim wrote a detailed private will for his son Yaakov covering burial arrangements, distribution of his tallesim and estate, and a 1,050-shekel gift to the Rebbe Rashab.
Story: In ten clauses R. Avraham Chaim instructed Yaakov to bury him in his New York chevra's plot — warning him not to be swayed by the New Haven offer — and forbade any public hesped or newspaper notice. He detailed his prepared linen tachrichim from Germany, his Shabbos and weekday tallesim (including one inherited from the Tzemach Tzedek that he was afraid to wear in the next world), and asked that the bottom of the casket be broken so his body would touch the earth, per the Zohar in Parshas Vayechi and Terumah. He also charged Yaakov to forward 1,050 shekels of his estate as tzedakah to the Rebbe Rashab through his brother R. Z., to say kaddish, daven before the amud, and learn mishnayos throughout the year.
Tags: will, tzava'ah, burial, new york, new haven, yaakov rosenbaum, tachrichim, kaddish, rashab, tzedakah

Title: Rosenbaum writes private will for son Yaakov, designating burial in New York
Summary: On 2 Iyar 5671 Rosenbaum wrote a private will instructing his son Yaakov that he be buried in the New York chevra plot and that 1,050 dollars be transmitted as tzedakah to the Rebbe Rashab.
Story: On 2 Iyar 5671 (April 30, 1911) Reb Avraham Chaim wrote a personal will to his son Yaakov. He insisted on burial in the New York chevra plot, refusing offers from New Haven where R' David Schifrin lived. He also reminded his son that 1,050 dollars from the estate were earmarked as tzedakah for the Rebbe, to be sent through his brother R' Zalman.
Tags: america, new york, rosenbaum, wills, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rashab decides to send Tomchei Temimim students to expand Hebron yeshiva
Summary: On the night of 25 Iyar 5671, after a three-hour meeting with Tomchei Temimim leadership, the Rashab resolved to send select students and a mashpia to strengthen the Magen Avos yeshiva in Hebron.
Story: After more than a year of discussion, the Rashab convened the directors of Tomchei Temimim on 25 Iyar 5671 for over three hours to plan support for Hebron. He decided to dispatch outstanding avreichim, including a mashpia in Chassidus, to establish the Magen Avos yeshiva on a sound footing and to make it an open branch of Tomchei Temimim. The decision was reported in letters Shilo sent to Hebron on 9-10 Sivan.
Tags: hebron, torat emet, magen avot, tomchei temimim, rashab, yeshiva

Title: Chatzkevich becomes rabbi of Ponimonek
Summary: By 29 Sivan 5671 (June 25, 1911), R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich had been installed as rabbi of Ponimonek, as announced in the Tomchei Tmimim journal 'HaAch'.
Story: In 5671 (1911) Chatzkevich succeeded his father-in-law R. Yitzchak Moshe Weiler as rabbi of Ponimonek. The Tomchei Tmimim journal 'HaAch' (29 Sivan 5671) congratulated him, calling him a beloved chossid and yarei shomayim and wishing him further elevation.
Tags: chatzkevich, ponimonek, weiler, haach-journal

Title: Maharashab travels to Moscow
Summary: Maharashab's passport was stamped in Moscow on 20 Elul 5671.
Story: On 31 August 1911 (20 Elul 5671), shortly before Rosh Hashanah, Maharashab traveled to Moscow, the visit documented by a passport stamp.
Tags: maharashab, moscow, passport, travel

Title: Author begins learning at Great Hall Lubavitch, 5672
Summary: For Rosh Hashanah 5672 (fall 1911) the memoirist's class moved to learn in the Great Hall at Lubavitch.
Story: R. Shilem Koratin was appointed mashgiach for chassidus that winter, with R. Yaakov Baruch Krasik supervising nigleh and R. Shmuel Gronem Esterman serving as mashpia. They learned Derech Mitzvotecha until R. Gronem fell ill with eye trouble and had to travel for extended treatment, after which the students learned on their own from the Rebbe Rashab's maamarim.
Tags: lubavitch, tomchei temimim, shilem koratin, shmuel gronem

Title: Hebron Tomchei Tmimim mashpia and students depart Lubavitch
Summary: Mashpia Shneur Zalman Havlin received written instructions from both Rebbeim before leaving Lubavitch for Hebron on 2 Cheshvan 5672.
Story: The Rashab told Havlin his sole focus in Hebron must be the yeshiva itself, apart from supervising Chabad properties. The Rayatz, as head of Tomchei Tmimim, formally appointed Havlin to the central vaad and as the local mashpia and representative, instructing him to commission an official institutional seal bearing the Tomchei Tmimim name.
Tags: hebron, tomchei tmimim, rashab, rayatz, havlin

Title: Rebbe Rashab affirms Slonim-Shlank as Kollel Chabad address
Summary: Rebbe Rashab wrote that the official address for Kollel Chabad donations should remain 'Slonim Shlank'.
Story: On 26 Cheshvan 5672 (Nov 1911), the Rebbe Rashab wrote in letter 349 affirming that the official mailing address for Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem should be 'Slonim Shlank' – the names of administrators R. Mordechai Dovber Slonim and R. Mordechai Shlank. This was meant to maintain the existing administrative structure of the kollel.
Tags: rashab, kollel chabad, jerusalem, mordechai dovber slonim, shlank

Title: Passing of R. Michoel Bliner, mashpia of Tomchei Temimim
Summary: R. Michoel Bliner, mashpia at Tomchei Temimim, passed away on Motzaei Shabbat 28 Cheshvan 5672 in Lubavitch.
Story: On Yom Kippur 5672 R. Michoel had asked to be brought into the Great Hall where the Rebbe Rashab prayed, with his bed placed against the wall between the hall and the second room. The Rebbe Rashab spoke with him on Yom Kippur, discussing whether he was permitted to forgo fasting, though he chose to fast anyway. The Rebbe Rashab attended the funeral that Motzaei Shabbat through deep mud, and the Rebbe Rayatz carried the bier, losing a galosh in the mire en route to the cemetery.
Tags: lubavitch, tomchei temimim, michoel bliner, rebbe rashab, rebbe rayatz

Title: Hebron yeshiva officially renamed 'Toras Emes'
Summary: In a letter to mashpia R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin dated Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5672, the Rebbe Rayatz formally designated the new Hebron yeshiva 'Toras Emes'.
Story: Following the Rashab's decision to send a contingent of avreichim to Hebron, the mashpia R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin and his group arrived in the city. The Rebbe Rayatz then wrote to him on Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5672 instructing that the yeshiva be called 'Toras Emes'. This name change reflected not only renaming but a reorganization absorbing the existing Magen Avos yeshiva.
Tags: hebron, torat emet, magen avot, rayatz, shlomo zalman havlin, yeshiva

Title: Hebron yeshiva renamed Toras Emes
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5672, one day after the students arrived in Hebron, the Rayatz announced the new yeshiva would be called Toras Emes rather than Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: The Rayatz sat down to write a twelve-page letter the moment the safe-arrival telegram came in. The name change reflected a strategic decision to separate the new institution from the central Tomchei Tmimim treasury, so it would draw its own donors rather than burden the Lubavitch yeshiva network.
Tags: hebron, toras emes, tomchei tmimim, rayatz

Title: Rayatz letter outlines Hebron yeshivah purpose
Summary: The Rayatz wrote a long letter to Rabbi Havlin and his students laying out the purpose of the Hebron yeshivah.
Story: On 3 Kislev 5672 (November 24, 1911), the Rayatz sent a detailed letter to Rabbi Zalman Havlin and his Hebron students. It articulated the mission of Toras Emes: invigorating chasidic study in Eretz Yisrael and producing new Jewish leadership for the land, parallel to Tomchei Temimim's mission in Russia.
Tags: rayatz, zalman havlin, letter, toras emes, hebron

Title: Rayatz letter to Havlin outlining purpose of Hebron yeshivah
Summary: The Rayatz wrote a long letter to Rabbi Havlin and his students in Hebron outlining the purpose of the new yeshivah.
Story: Dated 3 Kislev 5672, the letter detailed the curriculum and vision for Toras Emes. The Rayatz was intimately involved in setting up the program, giving detailed instructions for curriculum and student acceptance, while expecting Rabbi Havlin would ultimately take full administrative responsibility.
Tags: rayatz, zalman havlin, hebron, toras emes

Title: Toras Emes declares full financial independence from Tomchei Tmimim
Summary: A Chanukah 5672 kuntres signed by Havlin and Eliezerov declared that Toras Emes Hebron had no fiscal connection whatsoever to Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch.
Story: The pamphlet warned supporters not to confuse the two institutions or shift donations between them, since each had its own vaad and shadarim. The Rashab issued a parallel general letter to Anash announcing Toras Emes and listing the dedicated emissaries he was sending to raise its funds.
Tags: hebron, toras emes, tomchei tmimim, havlin, eliezerov, fundraising

Title: R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie is born in Kremenchug
Summary: On the first night of Chanukah 5672 R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie was born in Kremenchug.
Story: On the first night of Chanukah 5672 (approximately 16 December 1911) R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie was born in Kremenchug. He was the son of R' Natan Gurarie and the younger brother of R' Yechiel Tzvi. His early years coincided with the upheavals of revolution and civil war in Russia.
Tags: shneur-zalman-gurarie, kremenchug, ukraine, russia, birth

Title: Chana Ariel by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil published in Berditchev
Summary: First edition of Chana Ariel by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil was printed in Berditchev in 5672.
Story: Chana Ariel is a major chassidic work by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil, an outstanding disciple of the first three Chabad Rebbeim. The first edition appeared in Berditchev in 5672 (1912) and is exhibited at the Lubavitch Library.
Tags: berditchev, yitzchak aizik homil, chassidus

Title: Dr. Nissan Mindel born in Riga
Summary: Nissan Mindel, future secretary to two Lubavitcher Rebbes and translator of the Tanya, is born in Riga.
Story: He met the Rebbe as a young man on the Rebbe's arrival from Russia. He earned a master's at Manchester and a doctorate in Semitic languages at Columbia, before serving as secretary in Otwock and accompanying the Rebbe on the 1940 voyage to America.
Tags: mindel, birth, riga

Title: Older bochurim assigned to learn Chassidus with younger students at Tomchei Tmimim
Summary: A new study arrangement at Tomchei Tmimim paired senior bochurim with younger students to deepen their Chassidus learning.
Story: At the start of 5673, after the mashpia R. Shilem Kuratin suspected that several students were not committing themselves to learning Chassidus, a new arrangement was instituted in Tomchei Tmimim. A few of the senior bochurim were paired with younger students to study Chassidus together. The author was assigned to R. Nota Pinski.
Tags: lubavitch, tomchei tmimim, russia, shilem kuratin, nota pinski

Title: R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov sent to help establish Yeshivas Toras Emes in Hebron
Summary: Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov, a Tomchei Tmimim student, was among those sent to help found Yeshivas Toras Emes in Hebron.
Story: In 5672 (1912), R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov of Surazh, who had studied at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch, was part of the group sent to establish Yeshivas Toras Emes in Hebron. He later returned to Russia during World War I, eventually serving as rabbi of Drivin and then emigrating to Riga.
Tags: ashurov, yeshivas toras emes, hebron, tomchei tmimim

Title: R' Menachem Mendel Naeh appointed Kollel Chabad trustee
Summary: In the summer of 5672 R' Menachem Mendel Naeh became a trustee of Kollel Chabad and received instructions from the Rebbe Rashab.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab wrote to Naeh asking him to undertake reforms in the kollel concerning prayer and Torah study, so that it would at least partially correspond to the holy intent of its founders. The appointment came amid a broader period of transition in the kollel leadership, including the death of R' Dovber Efrat on Erev Rosh Chodesh Tammuz that same summer.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, menachem mendel naeh, rashab

Title: R' Shilem Kuratin appointed mashgiach for chassidut
Summary: In winter 5672, R' Shilem Kuratin of Disna was appointed mashgiach for chassidut studies at Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: In winter 5672 (early 1912), R' Shilem Kuratin from Disna was appointed mashgiach for chassidut studies at Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch. He was known for his deep meditation in prayer and his ability to repeat the Rebbe Rashab's chassidic discourses verbatim. He continued in his role when the yeshiva moved to Kremenchug, until his passing in early Elul 5679.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, kuratin, disna, mashgiach

Title: R' Shimon Glitzenstein enrolls at Yeshivat Torat Emet in Hebron
Summary: R' Shimon Glitzenstein joins Yeshivat Torat Emet at the end of summer 5672, replacing Alter Simchovitz who had returned to Lubavitch.
Story: At the end of summer 5672 (1912), R' Shimon Glitzenstein enrolled at Yeshivat Torat Emet in Hebron in its first year of operation. He replaced R' Alter Simchovitz, who had returned to Lubavitch over the course of that summer. Glitzenstein would later document the yeshiva's early years in writings published in Bitaon Chabad.
Tags: hebron, torat emet, glitzenstein

Title: R. Baruch Shalom Cohen moves to Volomin and opens Tomchei Tmimim branch
Summary: In 5672, R. Baruch Shalom Cohen relocated from Warsaw to nearby Volomin, where he opened a branch of Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: After living in Warsaw for over a decade, R. Baruch Shalom Cohen moved to the nearby town of Volomin in 5672 (1912). There he founded a branch of Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim, extending the yeshiva network beyond Lubavitch itself into the Polish-Russian border region.
Tags: volomin, warsaw region, tomchei tmimim, baruch shalom cohen

Title: Rashab founds Torat Emet yeshiva as independent Chabad institution
Summary: In 5672 the Rebbe Rashab established the Torat Emet yeshiva as a separate institution outside the umbrella of Kollel Chabad.
Story: Until then Kollel Chabad had served as the overarching organization for all Chabad activity in the Holy Land, with private institutions operating under its supervision. The Rashab broke this pattern by founding Torat Emet as an independent yeshiva, marking the beginning of a new institutional model for Chabad in Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: rashab, torat emet, yeshiva, kollel chabad, hebron

Title: Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva founded in Hebron
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab established the Torat Emet yeshiva in Hebron in 5672, dispatching a mashpia and top Lubavitcher students.
Story: In 5672 (1911/12), the Rebbe Rashab founded the Torat Emet yeshiva in Hebron, sending a special mashpia and several outstanding students from Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch to lead it. The yeshiva would later close during the deportations of World War I.
Tags: hebron, torat-emet, rashab, yeshiva, eretz-yisrael

Title: Toras Emes opens branch in Jerusalem
Summary: Following the founding of Toras Emes in Hebron in 5672, a branch of the yeshiva opened in Jerusalem with the gaon R. Tzvi Pesach Frank as rosh yeshiva.
Story: After Toras Emes was established in Hebron, a Jerusalem branch was opened the same year. R. Tzvi Pesach Frank served as the rosh yeshiva of the Jerusalem branch. Only fragmentary information about this branch has reached us.
Tags: jerusalem, torat emet, tzvi pesach frank, yeshiva

Title: Vilna 'Siddur with Likutei Torah' of Chabad's Alter Rebbe
Summary: A Siddur with selected Chassidic discourses (Likutei Torah) from the Alter Rebbe's writings, arranged by the order of prayer, was issued in Vilna.
Story: In 5672 (1912), a Siddur was published in Vilna containing Likutei Torah—Chassidic discourses drawn from the writings of the Chabad Alter Rebbe Schneur Zalman of Liadi, arranged according to the order of the prayers. The 360-leaf octavo edition made the Alter Rebbe's Chassidic teachings accessible alongside the daily liturgy. It served the Chabad community of Lithuania and beyond in the years before the Russian Revolution.
Tags: chabad, vilna, alter rebbe, likutei torah, siddur

Title: Volomin branch founded
Summary: In 5672, a Tomchei Tmimim branch was established briefly in Volomin near Warsaw.
Story: In 5672 (1912), R' Boruch Sholom HaKohen moved to Volomin near Warsaw, where he committed to fund half the expenses of the local yeshiva if a manager from Lubavitch was sent. The Rebbe Rashab sent R' Mordechai Perlov to lead the yeshiva. Students began preparing to travel to Lubavitch, but the outbreak of World War I in summer 5674 ended the project.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, volomin, warsaw, poland

Title: World Agudath Israel founded at Katowice conference
Summary: Jewish religious leaders establish Agudath Israel in Katowice, Poland, in response to secularization and Zionism.
Story: The movement unified many chasidic groups with the Lithuanian yeshivah world, though Chabad did not join. Agudath Israel later won seats in the Latvian Saeima and became a major presence in Israel and the US.
Tags: agudath-israel, katowice, poland, orthodoxy

Title: World Agudath Israel founded in Katowice, Poland
Summary: Jewish religious leaders establish World Agudath Israel at a Katowice conference as a response to secularization and Zionism.
Story: The Agudah unified many chasidic groups with the Lithuanian yeshivah community, though Chabad did not join. In Latvia, Agudath Israel became a major influential party, winning two Saeima seats in 1922 and 1925, falling to one in 1928, and regaining two in 1931. After the 1934 Latvian coup, multi-party elections did not resume until 1990.
Tags: agudath israel, katowice, poland, religious zionism, lithuanian yeshivot

Title: Yeshivat Torat Emet founded in Hebron
Summary: At the beginning of 5672 the Chabad Yeshivat Torat Emet was founded in Hebron after extended preparations.
Story: Following years of efforts to build a Chabad yeshiva presence in Eretz Israel—including the affiliation of Magen Avot with Tomchei Tmimim—Yeshivat Torat Emet was founded in Hebron at the beginning of 5672. The yeshiva would become a major center for Chabad learning in the Land of Israel and was supervised by Rebbe Rashab from Lubavitch.
Tags: hebron, torat emet, yeshiva, lubavitch, rashab

Title: Magen Avos yeshiva absorbed into Toras Emes
Summary: By Lag B'Omer 5672, Shilo instructed that funds sent from Russia for Magen Avos belonged to Toras Emes, confirming the older yeshiva's full absorption.
Story: In a Lag B'Omer letter to his brother-in-law R. Menachem Mendel Nae, Shilo specified that the 40 ruble donation from Meir Vozlinski for Magen Avos in fact belonged to Toras Emes. He further warned not to hand over funds from Russia to the Magen Avos gabbaim without his knowledge. This documents how Magen Avos was administratively folded into the newly established Toras Emes.
Tags: hebron, torat emet, magen avot, yeshiva

Title: R' Dovber Efrat passes away
Summary: R' Dovber Efrat, a Jerusalem trustee and ba'al ha'adres of Kollel Chabad, passed away on Erev Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5672.
Story: Efrat had been one of the Jerusalem trustees and also served as a ba'al ha'adres handling the Chabad fund's mail address. His death left two key positions vacant. The Rebbe Rashan of Bobruisk wrote to Jerusalem proposing that the elderly R' Gershon Lipschitz be appointed as trustee in his stead.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, dovber efrat, trustees, ba'al ha'adres

Title: R' DovBer Efrat passes away in Jerusalem
Summary: R' DovBer Efrat, longtime Chabad rabbi and administrator in Hebron and Jerusalem, passed away on 1 Tammuz 1912.
Story: R' DovBer Efrat passed away on 1 Tammuz 1912 (א' תמוז תער"ב) in Jerusalem. He had served nine years as rabbi of Hebron and nearly ten more years as administrator of the Chabad kollel in Jerusalem after the death of R' Manish Wirowlianski.
Tags: dovber efrat, jerusalem, petira, chabad kollel

Title: Birth of Yisrael Yehuda Levin in Zhivotov
Summary: Yisrael Yehuda Levin, author of the memoir Zichronotai, was born on Shabbat 7 Tammuz 5672 in Zhivotov, Ukraine.
Story: Levin was born to Ephraim Shmuel ben Yosef and Leah Beila (daughter of the Dashov shochet Yisrael Bilenki) in the small town of Zhivotov in Vinnitsa province. His memoir, written across 35 years beginning around 1960, would document his life under Soviet rule and his eventual escape. The town was a religious community where his father served as a melamed.
Tags: zhivotov, ukraine, vinnitsa, birth, yisrael yehuda levin

Title: Bobruisk Rebbe writes about Kollel donations after R. Dovid Aharon's passing
Summary: The Rebbe of Bobruisk wrote that etrog donations should now be sent in the names of Slonim and Shlank.
Story: In a letter dated 5 Menachem Av 5672 (July/Aug 1912), the Bobruisker Rebbe instructed the local administrators to publish in HaModia news of the passing of R. Dovid Aharon and direct that those sending money for etrogim send it under the names of Shlank and Slonim. The letter was preserved in several public circulars of the time.
Tags: bobruisk, kollel chabad, etrogim, address

Title: Jerusalem Anash hold elections, install three new Kollel administrators
Summary: A group of 76 Anash in Jerusalem held elections and chose three new administrators for Kollel Chabad.
Story: On 15 Tammuz 5672 (July 1912), 76 members of Anash gathered in Jerusalem and ran their own election for kollel administrators, choosing R. Shmuel Halevi Levin, R. Gershon Lapshitz, and R. Moshe Kazarnovsky. The move was undertaken without the consent of the Rebbe Rashab and ultimately led to a years-long split in Kollel Chabad.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, elections, shmuel halevi levin, gershon lapshitz, moshe kazarnovsky

Title: Rebbe Rashab appoints R. Menachem Mendel Naeh as Kollel administrator
Summary: Rebbe Rashab wrote to R. Menachem Mendel Naeh asking him to accept appointment as a Kollel Chabad administrator.
Story: On 16 Elul 5672 (Aug/Sept 1912), the Rebbe Rashab wrote letter 341 (vol. II) asking R. Menachem Mendel Naeh, an experienced accountant who had managed Kollel finances for years, to formally accept the title of administrator. Naeh had previously refused the title in 5669 but agreed to participate informally. He now accepted out of deference to the Rebbe.
Tags: rashab, menachem mendel naeh, kollel chabad, jerusalem

Title: R' Meir Heilperin letter on book selection for Rashab
Summary: Book dealer R' Meir Heilperin wrote about cataloging books for selection by the Rebbe Rashab.
Story: On 16 Elul 5672 (August 29, 1912), book dealer R' Meir Heilperin wrote requesting that R' M. Rabinowitz catalog all available books, both new and old half-quires, not just rare ones, so he could select what the Rebbe Rashab needed. The letter suggests Heilperin had already visited Lubavitch and examined the library during summer 5672.
Tags: library, books, meir heilperin, bibliography

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter to Rashaz Slonim acknowledging manuscript shipment
Summary: On 22 Elul 5672, Rebbe Rashab confirmed receipt of a precious manuscript including Birkat Chatanim by the Mitteler Rebbe, calling it deeply meaningful.
Story: After 25 years of correspondence with Rashaz Slonim about manuscript collection (Igros #344), Rebbe Rashab expressed his desire that Rashaz continue sending such precious materials regularly. The Birkat Chatanim manuscript was catalogued as #1194 and printed in Maamarei Admur Ha'emtza'i Droshei Chatuna Vol. 1, p. 146.
Tags: rashab, rashaz slonim, manuscripts, birkat chatanim, letters

Title: Rashab tells Slonim not to leave Yafo for Hebron
Summary: On 22 Elul 5672, after Toras Emes opened in Hebron, the Rebbe Rashab told R' Shneur Zalman Slonim not to abandon Yafo for his hometown.
Story: Following the founding of Yeshivas Toras Emes in Hebron, R' Shneur Zalman wished to lay down his Yafo burdens and return to Hebron. The Rebbe Rashab replied that he could not abandon Yafo after all the effort and toil he had invested to bring the community to its current state.
Tags: yafo, hebron, toras emes, rashab, shneur zalman slonim

Title: Simchas Torah 5673 Rayatz farbrengen with the Tzarske familye remark
Summary: The Rayatz farbrenged Simchas Torah 5673 and dubbed R. Shilem and R. Elchanan Dov a "royal family" not to be touched.
Story: On Simchas Torah the Rayatz farbrenged in the same apartment, in the room of R. Nachman the meshares (then occupied by R. Shlomo Leib Eliezerov). R. Elchanan Dov Morozov made a witty barb at R. Shilem, who quoted "sent forth his hand against him." The Rayatz responded by calling them "tzarske familye" (royal family), and someone added in Russian: "He will lie many klaftern deep, but tzarske familye — don't touch the royal family."
Tags: simchas torah, rayatz, elchanan dov morozov, shilem kuratin, shlomo leib eliezerov, lubavitch

Title: R. Mordechai Mentlik born in Minsk
Summary: R. Mordechai Mentlik was born in Minsk on 19 Cheshvan 5673.
Story: R. Mordechai Mentlik was born in Minsk on 19 Cheshvan 5673 (October 30, 1912). He later studied at Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw from 1925, was selected to study in Riga in 1931, and became a maggid shiur in the preparatory program in 1934.
Tags: mordechai mentlik, minsk, biography, russia

Title: Eretz Yisrael Anash ratify R. Menachem Mendel Naeh's appointment
Summary: Anash throughout the Holy Land ratified the Rebbe's appointment of R. Menachem Mendel Naeh as Kollel administrator.
Story: At the beginning of Marcheshvan 5673 (Oct/Nov 1912), the public of Anash from all parts of Eretz Yisrael affirmed the Rebbe Rashab's appointment of R. Menachem Mendel Naeh and signed letters confirming the new administrative arrangement. This was documented in the kuntres 'Tumas Yesharim'.
Tags: menachem mendel naeh, kollel chabad, anash, eretz yisrael

Title: R. Shainfinkel reports finding Kollel Chabad accounts in order to Bobruisker Rebbe
Summary: On 27 Cheshvan 5673 R. Shalom Simcha Shainfinkel wrote to Rebbe Shemarya Noach of Bobruisk that he had audited the Kollel Chabad cashbox and found the accounts trustworthy.
Story: Following accusations of embezzlement against the Jerusalem officials, Rebbe Rashab of Lubavitch and Rebbe Shemarya Noach of Bobruisk had asked the wealthy laymen R. Shalom Simcha Shainfinkel and R. Gershon Lifshitz to inspect the kollel's books. Shainfinkel reported that he had visited the kollel office repeatedly, examined the cashbox and ledgers, and found administration 'in proper and upright order' with no grounds to doubt the officials' integrity. Lifshitz participated only on condition that this not be construed as accepting any formal appointment.
Tags: kollel chabad, jerusalem, shainfinkel, gershon lifshitz, etrog trade, audit

Title: Maharashab travels to Petersburg
Summary: Maharashab's passport was stamped in Petersburg in late 5673.
Story: On 22 November 1912, Maharashab's internal passport was stamped in Petersburg during one of his trips to the Russian capital.
Tags: maharashab, petersburg, passport, travel

Title: 19 Kislev 5673 farbrengen and maamar with Rebbe Rashab
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab led a marathon 19 Kislev celebration with the four-levels sicha, a 40-minute niggun, and a maamar from the Hemshech Tarav.
Story: 19 Kislev 5673 fell on a Friday, with the main celebration and meal held Motzei Shabbat in the great hall. The Rebbe Rashab came at about 10 PM and delivered the famous two-hour sicha on the four levels of tzaddik, yashar, tamim, and chassid, followed by the niggun for forty minutes and the 19 Kislev maamar from the Hemshech Tarav. He spoke of being an etzem unaffected by higher or lower, and said that leaving Lubavitch (for medical travel abroad) was "like separating from life" since his whole vitality was speaking Chassidus.
Tags: 19 kislev, yud tes kislev, rebbe rashab, rayatz, hemshech tarav, lubavitch, shmuel aba dulitzky

Title: Shainfinkel and Chagiz confirm to Rebbe Rashab that Kollel Chabad books are accurate
Summary: On 7 Tevet 5673 Shainfinkel and Yitzchak Chagiz wrote to Rebbe Rashab confirming that accounts 1–20 sent by Kollel Chabad matched the office's day-book with no discrepancies.
Story: Their certification, attached to Rashab's later circular, vouched that the figures aligned with the kollel's 'tagebuch' which was largely signed by recipients upon receipt of funds. Chagiz added his own confirmation that he too had reviewed the accounts and the ledgers and found everything correct. The document became a key piece of evidence in defending the Jerusalem officials against the gabbaim abroad.
Tags: kollel chabad, jerusalem, audit, shainfinkel, yitzchak chagiz, etrog trade

Title: Maamar on Kabbalas Shabbos of 10 Teves 5673
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab delivered a maamar at Kabbalas Shabbos of 10 Teves, with students listening from outside the window in the snow.
Story: 10 Teves 5673 fell on Friday erev Shabbos. The Rebbe Rashab davened Kabbalas Shabbos at home, and announced that students could eat something and then he would deliver a maamar. The doors were closed by the time the author and others returned; they stood outside the window in the bitter cold and snow listening to the maamar delivered b'kol ram, and R. Shimshon Vitebsker was let in mid-maamar through a chain of doors opened by the Rayatz's daughter Chana.
Tags: 10 teves, asarah b'teves, rebbe rashab, maamar, shimshon vitebsker, shilem kuratin, lubavitch

Title: Author's first yechidus with the Rebbe Rashab
Summary: The author entered his first yechidus with the Rebbe Rashab, who guided him on tefillah b'peirush hamilos.
Story: In the winter of 5673 the author entered his first yechidus with the Rebbe Rashab, marking his entry among the bochurim devoted to inner avodah. He had prepared with intense Krias Shema al hamita and committed to at least six hours of Chassidus study daily plus extended tefillah. The Rebbe instructed him to daven b'peirush hamilos and to connect the themes of Pesukei D'Zimra and Birchos Yotzer, which would open the heart.
Tags: yechidus, rebbe rashab, tefillah, lubavitch, avodah

Title: Author's sister Sasha Hinde emigrates to the United States
Summary: The author's sister emigrated to the United States in summer 5673, prompting a yechidus over travel home.
Story: In summer 5673 the author's sister, Mrs. Sasha Hinde, traveled to the United States. The father asked the Rebbe Rashab for permission for the author to come home from yeshiva to bid her farewell, but the Rebbe questioned the trip in the middle of zman. During the same yechidus the author received approval to begin laying Rabbeinu Tam tefillin upon turning 18 that Kislev.
Tags: united states, emigration, rebbe rashab, rabbeinu tam tefillin, lubavitch

Title: Beilis affair derails planned rabbinic conference
Summary: A second government-organized rabbinic conference scheduled for the winter of 5674 was derailed by the outbreak of the Beilis blood libel trial.
Story: The Russian government had been preparing for a follow-up rabbinic conference to be held in the winter of 5674 (1913-1914). However, the Beilis blood libel affair erupted and threw the Jewish world into turmoil. The matter dragged on through the end of 5674, when World War I broke out, and the second rabbinic conference never materialized.
Tags: russia, beilis affair, blood libel, rabbinic conference

Title: Beilis blood libel trial in Kiev
Summary: Mendel Beilis was tried in Kiev on trumped-up blood libel charges in a case that drew worldwide attention.
Story: Beilis was accused of killing a 12-year-old boy whose body was found near the brick factory he managed. Prosecutors tried to link him and ritual murder to the Chabad community through his friendship with a man named Feivel Schneersohn. The Rashab and Rayatz played a major behind-the-scenes role, with the Rayatz enlisting attorney Oscar Gruzenberg to spearhead the masterful defense.
Tags: beilis, kiev, blood libel, oscar gruzenberg, rashab, rayatz

Title: Berditchev Siddur 'Seder Tefilah' with Maharid of Liadi's commentary
Summary: A Seder Tefilah Siddur with the Maharid of Liadi's Chassidic 'Pirush HaMilot' commentary was printed in Berditchev.
Story: In 5673 (1913), a Seder Tefilah following the Arizal nusach as composed by the Alter Rebbe was published in Berditchev, accompanied by a Chassidic 'Pirush HaMilot' commentary by Rebbe Yitzchak Dovber Schneersohn (Maharid of Liadi). The two-volume octavo edition came with 217 plus 231 leaves of teachings. It supplemented the Chabad liturgical canon with the Maharid's distinctive interpretation.
Tags: chabad, liadi, berditchev, maharid, siddur, pirush hamilot

Title: Founding of separate 'Kollel Chabad HaMeyuchad'
Summary: A formal separate kollel called 'Kollel Chabad HaMeyuchad' was founded, splitting Kollel Chabad in two.
Story: In the summer of 5673 (1913), the three new administrators – Lapshitz, Kazarnovsky and Levin – decided to formally constitute a separate kollel, named 'Kollel Chabad HaMeyuchad'. They explained their decision in two kuntreisim, 'Tzedek u-Mishpat u-Meisharim' and 'Divrei Shalom v'Emes'. This separate kollel persisted for roughly ten years before reunification.
Tags: kollel chabad hameyuchad, split, jerusalem, gershon lapshitz, moshe kazarnovsky

Title: Group of lax students expelled from Tomchei Tmimim, most readmitted
Summary: Students dismissed from Tomchei Tmimim for laxity in seder were mostly readmitted after pleading and commitments to improve.
Story: During 5673 a group of students grew lax with seder, rushing through tefillah in 35–40 minutes after Chassidus shiur to get to nigleh learning. R. Shilem Kuratin spoke with the Rebbe Rashab, who said he preferred dozens of proper students to hundreds of indifferent ones. The students were expelled, and after a week or more of pleading and promises most were readmitted, though one left Lubavitch entirely.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, discipline, shilem kuratin, rebbe rashab

Title: Louis Lamm acquires R. Akiva Eiger oil portrait
Summary: Amsterdam dealer Louis Lamm purchased the oil portrait of R. Akiva Eiger from the Eiger family inheritance for 25 marks in 1913.
Story: Louis Lamm, an Amsterdam book dealer and publisher, acquired the oil portrait of R. Akiva Eiger — said to originate from Russia and from the Eiger family inheritance — in 1913 for 25 Reichsmark. He kept it for over two decades before it was sold to the Rayatz in 1936, eventually entering the Chabad library archive.
Tags: amsterdam, louis lamm, rabbi akiva eiger, portrait, art

Title: Meah Shearim published in Berditchev
Summary: Meah Shearim, a collection of one hundred discourses and letters of the Alter Rebbe, Mitteler Rebbe, and Tzemach Tzedek, was published in Berditchev in 1913.
Story: The 5673 (1913) Berditchev printing bundled chassidic discourses and correspondence of the first three Chabad rebbes with the Alter Rebbe's siddur, giving the latter the popular name Siddur Meah Shearim.
Tags: alter rebbe, mitteler rebbe, tzemach tzedek, berditchev, meah shearim

Title: Mendel Beilis blood libel trial
Summary: Mendel Beilis was tried in Kiev on blood libel charges; defense attorney Oscar Gruzenberg won acquittal.
Story: In 1913, Kiev Jew Mendel Beilis was accused of murdering twelve-year-old Andrei Yushchinksy for ritual purposes. The Rayatz, dispatched by the Rashab, enlisted leading attorney Oscar Gruzenberg, who orchestrated a masterful defense culminating in a Shema declaration. Beilis was acquitted, but the trial drew worldwide attention to Russian anti-Semitism.
Tags: beilis, blood libel, kiev, gruzenberg, chabad, antisemitism

Title: Pesach seudah at Tomchei Tmimim
Summary: On 23 Nissan 5673, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote about the Pesach seudah at Tomchei Tmimim with 139 students.
Story: In a letter dated 23 Nissan 5673 (1913), the Rebbe Rayatz described the customary Acharon Shel Pesach seudah at Tomchei Tmimim. The Rebbe Rashab, the menahel, mashgichim, mashpiim, melamdim and office workers ate together with 139 students that year (excluding the younger shiur and cheder students). The meal continued until close to 10 PM the previous evening.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, pesach, rashab

Title: R' Avraham Dovid Pevzner becomes mashpia
Summary: In late 5673, R' Avraham Dovid Pevzner was accepted as a mashpia at Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: Approximately at the end of 5673 (1913), R' Avraham Dovid Pevzner was accepted as a mashpia at Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch. R' Yisrael Jacobson described him as humble and soft-spoken, but at farbrengens he spoke with great warmth and tailored his words to each listener's spiritual state.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, pevzner, lubavitch, mashpia

Title: R' Shneur Zalman Rosenbaum travels to America for Tomchei Tmimim
Summary: Around 5673, R' Shneur Zalman Rosenbaum obtained the Rebbe Rashab's reluctant permission to travel to America, ostensibly to fundraise for Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: Approximately in 5673, R' Shneur Zalman Rosenbaum traveled to America under the pretext of raising funds for Tomchei Tmimim. A letter later shown to the author from R' Yehoshua Kastrol in Trieste characterized the move as Rosenbaum's personal wish to reach America, for which he had persuaded the Rebbe Rashab to consent. The dating is anchored by the fact that the parallel Toras Emes yeshiva was founded just after Sukkos 5672.
Tags: rebbe rashab, rosenbaum, tomchei tmimim, fundraising, united states

Title: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz born in Poland
Summary: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz was born in Kintsk, Poland in 5673.
Story: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz was born in Kintsk, Poland in 5673 (1912-1913). He studied at Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw from 1925 to 1933 and then served as a maggid shiur in the preparatory program in Warsaw and worked in the yeshiva office.
Tags: moshe pinchas katz, kintsk, poland, biography

Title: Shmuel Wiener invited to Lubavitch to help organize the library
Summary: The renowned bibliographer Shmuel Wiener was invited to Lubavitch to assist in organizing the Rebbe Rashab's library.
Story: Around 5673 (1913), the famous bibliographer Shmuel Wiener was brought to Lubavitch specifically to help arrange the library. According to R' Chaim Liberman's account, Wiener was given two weeks off from his work, and the Rebbe Rayatz asked him to come for a short time to view the books. He ended up staying only about a week.
Tags: library, lubavitch, shmuel wiener, bibliography

Title: Zhuravichi delegation to Rebbe Rashab over land sold to non-Jews
Summary: A delegation from Zhuravichi petitioned the Rebbe Rashab to intervene after chassidim sold the town's pastureland.
Story: In summer 5673 the author's father came with R. Zev Brulin, secretary of the Zhuravichi kehilla, on a special mission to the Rebbe Rashab. The wealthy chassidim R. Shmuel Trainin of Petersburg and R. Yehoshua Rosenkin of Mogilev had bought the courtyard and land surrounding Zhuravichi from non-Jewish landowners and were now reselling it, leaving the town with no pasture for its cattle; the delegation asked the Rebbe to intervene on behalf of the town's poor.
Tags: zhuravichi, russia, shmuel trainin, yehoshua rosenkin, mogilev, petersburg, rebbe rashab

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter on starting library catalog
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab expressed satisfaction that work had begun on organizing books and making a catalog.
Story: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Shevat 5673 (January 1913), the Rebbe Rashab wrote to his son expressing pleasure that the books had been organized and a catalog made. He instructed that a copy of the list should be sent to Shmuel Wiener, who had assisted the Rebbe in selecting valuable books for the library.
Tags: library, lubavitch, catalog, shmuel wiener

Title: Bobruisker Rebbe describes growing rift in Kollel Chabad
Summary: The Bobruisker Rebbe wrote a public letter describing the growing split between the old and new Kollel administrators.
Story: In Adar 5673 (Feb/March 1913), the Bobruisker Rebbe published a circular describing how R. Gershon Lapshitz had proposed forming a separate kollel. He recounted that the old administrators threatened poor recipients with loss of stipends if they accepted money from the new ones, but in the end the breach widened. The letter was circulated under the title 'Copy of Letters of the Bobruisker Rebbe Regarding Etrog Trade'.
Tags: bobruisk, kollel chabad, etrogim, gershon lapshitz, split

Title: Chol HaMoed Pesach 5673 Rayatz farbrengen in the Raza's rooms
Summary: The Rayatz farbrenged with senior bochurim Chol HaMoed Pesach 5673, teaching that each day must surpass the previous.
Story: During Chol HaMoed Pesach 5673 the Rayatz farbrenged with the senior bochurim in the rooms of the RaZ"A (R. Zalman Aharon). He told how the Rashbatz had once made him pay six kopecks for whiskey and two for cake to hear a chassidishe vort, then delayed telling it: the parable of the wagon driver's apprentice who, after a fast on 17 Tammuz, said "today is not yesterday" — meaning each day must be better than the last.
Tags: pesach, rayatz, raza, rashbatz, lubavitch, tomchei tmimim

Title: Bobruisker Rebbe formally approves separate Kollel under Lapshitz-Kazarnovsky
Summary: The Bobruisker Rebbe wrote that he had approved formation of a separate vaad under Lapshitz and Kazarnovsky.
Story: In Iyar 5673 (May 1913), the Bobruisker Rebbe issued a letter stating that a gathering of important Kollel members had concluded that a separate vaad must be established and that he had consented. He directed that any money sent in their names would reach the poor efficiently.
Tags: bobruisk, kollel chabad, split, gershon lapshitz, moshe kazarnovsky

Title: R. Naeh reports formation of rival Lapshitz-Kazarnovsky vaad
Summary: R. Menachem Mendel Naeh wrote to his brother-in-law describing the formation of a separate Lapshitz-Kazarnovsky vaad.
Story: On 13 Iyar 5673 (May 1913), R. Menachem Mendel Naeh wrote that on Sunday, Gershon Lapshitz and Moshe Kazarnovsky had gathered ten men at the home of R. Shmuel Levin and signed a paper agreeing to form their own vaad. This is the earliest dated documentation of the formal organizational split.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, gershon lapshitz, moshe kazarnovsky, menachem mendel naeh

Title: Rebbe Rashab circular endorses Jerusalem etrog officials amid public controversy
Summary: In Tammuz 5673 Rebbe Rashab issued a printed circular defending the Jerusalem etrog officials as trustworthy and directing donors to continue using the Slonim-Schlank address.
Story: Amid public uproar over fresh accusations, Rashab told Anash that the Eretz Yisrael etrog officials were honest and that the auditors Shainfinkel and Chagiz had testified their accounts were entirely straight. The circular was distributed via mimeograph together with Shainfinkel's audit letter and signed by hand at the opening and close. It instructed senders to use the established 'Slonim Schlank' address for kessef hakodashim.
Tags: kollel chabad, etrog trade, jerusalem, schlank, slonim, audit

Title: Rayatz asks Eliyahu Simpson for weekly written summaries of Rashab's maamarim
Summary: On 20 Tammuz 5673, Rayatz writes from his travels to chozer R. Eliyahu Simpson asking for weekly written summaries of his father's Shabbos maamarim.
Story: While traveling and unable to hear Rashab's discourses himself, Rayatz writes Simpson to send him each week a brief outline of the Shabbos maamar — the opening, the conclusion, and the connective content, rather than a full hanachah. He asks Simpson to coordinate with fellow chozrim Alter and Yerucham to ensure the reports arrive consistently at the address provided.
Tags: chassidus, rayatz, rashab, letters, chozrim, eliyahu-simpson

Title: Rashab letter to Shmuel Treinin about Beilis trial
Summary: The Rashab wrote to Shmuel Treinin explaining why he had decided against personally testifying at the Beilis trial.
Story: Dated 17 Elul, the Rashab cited concerns that his testimony might draw too much attention and could strengthen the prosecution's case. He was also concerned about elucidating obtuse theological concepts in 'modern terms.' Despite not testifying, the Rashab remained deeply involved behind the scenes in trial preparations.
Tags: rashab, beilis, shmuel treinin

Title: R' Yaakov Landa appointed rabbi of Kornitz
Summary: R' Yaakov Landa was appointed rabbi of Kornitz on 21 Elul 5673 (September 1913), succeeding his father.
Story: At the end of 5673 (September 1913), R' Yaakov Landa was appointed to the rabbinate of Kornitz, filling the position of his late father R' Moshe Yehuda Leib. The appointment was formalized on 21 Elul 5673. He was forced to leave during World War I.
Tags: kornitz, landa, rabbinate

Title: Passing of R. Shmuel HaLevi Levin in Jerusalem
Summary: R. Shmuel HaLevi Levin, formerly moreh tzedek of Lubavitch, passed away on 18 Marcheshvan 5674 in Jerusalem.
Story: R. Shmuel b. Shlomo Tzvi HaLevi Levin, the former Lubavitch moreh tzedek, died on 18 Marcheshvan 5674 (November 1913) in his Jerusalem home, having purchased his burial plot three years earlier. He was buried in the Old Cemetery (har hazeitim). The Kolel Chabad chevra kadisha register identifies him as 'the elder, who was called the Rav of Lubavitch.'
Tags: shmuel levin, jerusalem, chabad, lubavitch

Title: Rashab sends Tzemach Tzedek's citizenship certificates to attorney Gruzenberg
Summary: Rabbi Sholom Dovber of Lubavitch sent the Tzemach Tzedek's Russian citizenship documents to defense attorney Oscar Gruzenberg during the Beilis trial.
Story: On 3-4 Marcheshvan 5674 (late October/early November 1913), the Rashab wrote to Oscar Gruzenberg, lead defense counsel in the Mendel Beilis blood libel trial. Having read in the newspapers Gruzenberg's reference to the Tzemach Tzedek, he sent him the Hereditary Honorary Citizen certificate issued by Tsar Nicholas I, along with the earlier Honorary Citizen certificate. The Rashab believed these documents would help demonstrate the integrity of Russian Jewish leadership in the Tsar's eyes.
Tags: russia, beilis trial, gruzenberg, rashab, tzemach tzedek, honorary citizen

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter acknowledging additional manuscript shipment
Summary: On 14 Cheshvan 5674, Rebbe Rashab acknowledged with deep gratitude another shipment of manuscripts received complete from Rashaz Slonim.
Story: In this letter (Igros #1044), Rebbe Rashab praised the shipment as a great matter and credited Rashaz with great merit for his role. The lifelong manuscript-collection partnership remained productive into the years just before World War I.
Tags: rashab, rashaz slonim, manuscripts, letters

Title: Rebbe Rashab travels abroad for health reasons, early Kislev 5674
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab left Lubavitch for medical treatment abroad in early Kislev 5674, returning only after Pesach.
Story: Due to his weakened health, the Rebbe Rashab left for abroad around the week of Parshas Vayetzei, in the beginning of Kislev 5674, so that he was not in Lubavitch for 19 Kislev that year. Wealthy chassidim later traveled to be with him for Purim 5674. He did not return to Lubavitch until after Pesach 5674.
Tags: rebbe rashab, health, europe, lubavitch, travel

Title: Mrs. Devorah Chaikin, widow of Hebron Chabad rav, dies
Summary: Mrs. Devorah, second wife of R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin and granddaughter of R' Wolf of Tcharnostre, passed away on 13 Kislev 5674.
Story: Mrs. Devorah—a widow with son Moshe Mordechai whom R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin married after his first wife Zissel died between 5626-5635—passed away on 13 Kislev 5674. Through her first marriage her son Moshe Mordechai was a descendant of R' Wolf of Tcharnostre buried in Tiberias, and later became son-in-law of R' Akiva Yosef Schlesinger.
Tags: hebron, chaikin family, tcharnostre, devorah chaikin

Title: Rayatz letter to Havlin on entrepreneurial management approach
Summary: The Rayatz wrote to Rabbi Havlin articulating Chabad's management approach of empowering individuals with full responsibility.
Story: Dated 3 Kislev 5674, the letter stated: 'Our approach is to appoint individuals and entrust them with the management, and they are responsible for the projects given over to them.' This entrepreneurial model would become emblematic of Chabad expansion in the decades to come, used by both the Rayatz and the seventh Rebbe.
Tags: rayatz, zalman havlin, management philosophy, chabad

Title: Bris milah of R. Shilem Kuratin's son on 19 Kislev 5674
Summary: Shneur Zalman, son of R. Shilem Kuratin, had his bris on 19 Kislev 5674 with the Rayatz as sandek.
Story: A son was born to the mashgiach R. Shilem Kuratin, with the bris milah held on 19 Kislev 5674. The child was named Shneur Zalman, and the Rayatz was honored with sandekaus. The Rebbe Rashab was abroad that year, so the 19 Kislev celebrations were led by mashpi'im and anash.
Tags: bris milah, shilem kuratin, rayatz, 19 kislev, yud tes kislev, lubavitch

Title: Death of R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum in America
Summary: R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum, the former leader of Pleshchenitsy Chassidim, died in the United States on 25 Kislev 5674.
Story: Born around 5600, R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum had spent his youth at the court of the Tzemach Tzedek and later became a leading Chassid of the Maharash and the leader of the Pleshchenitsy Chassidic community. After emigrating and settling in America in 5658, he died there on 25 Kislev 5674 (24 December 1913), as recorded in the Rebbe's footnote in Sefer HaSichot Kayitz 5700.
Tags: united states, r avraham chaim rosenbaum, pleshchenitsy

Title: Passing of R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum in America
Summary: R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum passed away on 25 Kislev 5674 (December 24, 1913) in the United States.
Story: R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum passed away on 25 Kislev 5674, the first night of Chanukah, corresponding to December 24, 1913. He died in the United States, where he had settled some fifteen years earlier. A chassid who had been close to both the Tzemach Tzedek and the Rebbe Maharash, his surviving Torah correspondence preserves valuable insights into the chassidic thought of late nineteenth-century Russia.
Tags: avraham chaim rosenbaum, united states, passing, yahrzeit, chanukah

Title: Passing of Rabbi Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum on first night of Chanukah
Summary: Rabbi Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum passes away on 25 Kislev 5674, the first night of Chanukah, after declining the standard deathbed confession in favor of Patach Eliyahu.
Story: In his final years Avraham Chaim suffered paralysis of his left arm, losing movement and sensation. When a visitor brought him a Torah Or siddur with the order of viduy for a dying person, he refused it, calling it a 'misnagdic viduy,' and instead recited Patach Eliyahu, the kabbalistic introduction said before Friday Mincha, from beginning to end with great sweetness. He passed away on 25 Kislev 5674 (December 24, 1913), the first night of Chanukah, his yahrzeit observed on that date.
Tags: passing, yahrzeit, chanukah, avraham chaim rosenbaum, patach eliyahu

Title: Hidden Chanukah farbrengen at a tinsmith's house, Nun Hei of Chanukah 5674
Summary: R. Shmuel Gronem held a hidden farbrengen for 30 bochurim on the 5th night of Chanukah 5674 and taught a new niggun.
Story: On the 5th night of Chanukah 5674 a secret farbrengen was held with R. Shmuel Gronem Esterman. Because doctors had forbidden him whiskey due to eye trouble, the gathering was kept hidden; the talmid Yitzchak Raskin had bought a menorah at a tinsmith's workshop near Chochlukeh Street and arranged to use the place. About thirty bochurim attended; R. Gronem taught them the niggun "Mipnei mah yarda haneshama" and spoke discreetly about shemiras habris.
Tags: chanukah, shmuel gronem esterman, yitzchak raskin, niggun, shemiras habris, lubavitch

Title: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand sparks World War I
Summary: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria ignited the winds of war across Europe.
Story: Germany declared war on Russia that summer and invaded the following year. The war disrupted the Toras Emes yeshivah in Hebron, as Russian students were considered enemy aliens under Ottoman rule and forced to return to Russia. The conflict would eventually force the Rashab to abandon Lubavitch.
Tags: world war i, franz ferdinand, austria, europe

Title: Hebron Chabad settlement disrupted by World War I
Summary: In 5674 the First World War broke out and the Chabad settlement in Hebron ceased functioning.
Story: The Hebron Chabad community had been led for nearly twenty years by R' Dovber Efrat (until 5662) and then by R' Shiloh together with R' Mordechai Dovber Slonim and R' Binyamin Rivlin. When World War I began in 5674, the Chabad presence in Hebron came to a halt.
Tags: hebron, world war i, kollel chabad, war

Title: Henry Morgenthau visits Me'arat Hamakhpelah
Summary: The Jewish US ambassador to the Turkish Empire was granted exceptional access to the Tomb of the Patriarchs.
Story: Morgenthau's admission was among the rare instances when the Muslim ban was lifted at the sultan's insistence. Like other dignitaries before him, he was given access only to the Herodian structure, not the cave beneath.
Tags: hebron, meorat-hamachpelah, morgenthau, united-states, ottoman-empire

Title: Munkacs Haggadah 'Tiferet Banim' by Tzvi Hirsch Shapira
Summary: The Haggadah 'Tiferet Banim' with Pardes-style commentary by Tzvi Hirsch Shapira of Munkacs was published in Munkacs.
Story: In 5674 (1914), the Haggadah with a Pardes-style commentary called 'Tiferet Banim' by Tzvi Hirsch Shapira, head of the Munkacs rabbinical court, was published in Munkacs by Kahn and Fried. The 82-leaf octavo edition represented the Munkacs Chassidic and rabbinical tradition. It contributed to the rich tradition of Carpathian Chassidic Haggadah commentaries.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, munkacs, tzvi hirsch shapira, carpathian

Title: Passing of Rebbetzin Rivkah in Lubavitch
Summary: Rebbetzin Rivkah, wife of the Maharash, passed away in 5674 and was buried beside her husband in the Lubavitch ohel.
Story: Her resting place was placed adjacent to the Maharash's grave alongside the ohel originally built for the Tzemach Tzedek. The Lubavitch cemetery also contained a separate ohel for the Chabad rebbetzins, including the wives of the Alter Rebbe, the Mittler Rebbe, and the Tzemach Tzedek. Her passing came on the eve of the upheavals that would soon end Lubavitch's role as Chabad's center.
Tags: rebbetzin-rivkah, lubavitch-cemetery

Title: R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz passes away in Warsaw
Summary: At the start of 5675, R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz, one of the earliest Chabad settlers in Warsaw, passed away.
Story: R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz, who had built up Chabad life in Warsaw from the 1890s onward, died at the start of 5675 (autumn 1914). Leadership of the Warsaw Chabad community then passed to his son-in-law R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov, his brother-in-law R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin, and his nephew R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin.
Tags: warsaw, yosef yozik horowitz, death

Title: Rostov delegation brings 12 students to Tomchei Tmimim
Summary: The Rostov kehilla, beyond the Pale of Settlement, sent 12 children to train at Tomchei Tmimim as future klei kodesh.
Story: In 5674 a delegation came from the Rostov-on-Don kehilla to evaluate the yeshiva. Since Rostov was beyond the Pale of Settlement, the community lacked shochtim, rabbanim, mohalim and other religious functionaries, so they decided to send their children to be trained as future klei kodesh. After visiting several yeshivos, they were impressed by Lubavitch and enrolled twelve students, hiring R. Moshe Rosenblum as their melamed.
Tags: rostov, pale of settlement, tomchei tmimim, moshe rosenblum, russia, education

Title: Six-member delegation arrives in Jerusalem to audit Kollel Chabad accounts
Summary: In early summer 5674 a six-member delegation arrived in Eretz Yisrael — three each from Lubavitch and Bobruisk — to audit Kollel Chabad's books and adjudicate the conflict.
Story: Lubavitch sent R. Eliezer Moshe Modyevsky of Kharol, R. Yitzchak Yoel Rapaporowitz and R. Nosson Gurary of Kremenchug; Bobruisk sent R. Menachem Mendel (son of the Bobruisker Rebbe), R. Yitzchak Shmuel Luria and R. Shemarya Mekler. The gabbaim Bichowsky and Bagin also came to face beis-din proceedings with the Eretz Yisrael officials. The visit triggered roughly a month of intensive ledger review and public testimony in Jerusalem.
Tags: kollel chabad, jerusalem, audit, lubavitch, bobruisk, modyevsky, rapaporowitz, gurary

Title: Toras Emes yeshiva closes in Hebron
Summary: The Toras Emes yeshiva ceased operating in Hebron at the end of 5674.
Story: After nearly three years of operation in Hebron, the Toras Emes yeshiva ceased functioning at the end of 5674. The yeshiva had operated first in the home donated by R' Shneur Zalman Berlin and later in the Romano courtyard, with student housing in the Rebbe Rashab's large property.
Tags: hebron, toras emes, tomchei tmimim, yeshiva, world war

Title: Torat Emet opens Jerusalem branch under R' Tzvi Pesach Frank
Summary: Torat Emet opens a Jerusalem branch with R' Tzvi Pesach Frank — later a chief rabbi of Jerusalem — as its rosh metivta.
Story: Following discussions about absorbing Jerusalem avreichim into the yeshiva, Torat Emet opened a Jerusalem branch in 5674 (1913–14). The Frierdiker Rebbe's letter of 3 Kislev 5674 to R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin asked for accounts of the new branch. The rosh metivta of the Jerusalem branch was R' Tzvi Pesach Frank, who would later become one of Jerusalem's leading rabbinic authorities.
Tags: jerusalem, torat emet, tzvi pesach frank, frierdiker rebbe

Title: World War I devastates Hebron's Jewish community
Summary: The outbreak of WWI shook Hebron's Jewish settlement, cutting off charitable distribution funds and triggering hunger and disease.
Story: When World War I broke out in 5674/1914, Hebron's Jewish community was severely shaken. Fears of Turkish military conscription, the cessation of chalukah funds reaching the yeshivot, and a collapse of incoming support from emissaries (shadarim) forced many Jews to flee. Hunger and disease drove residents to seek refuge wherever they could find it.
Tags: hebron, wwi, ottoman empire, famine

Title: World War I erupts in Europe
Summary: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand triggered World War I; Germany declared war on Russia that summer.
Story: In 1914, the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria ignited World War I. Germany declared war on Russia that summer and invaded the following year, setting the stage for the upheaval that would eventually force the Rashab to flee Lubavitch.
Tags: world war i, franz ferdinand, germany, russia, war

Title: WWI begins; Russian Jews expelled from Eretz Yisrael
Summary: With the outbreak of World War I in summer 5674, all Russian citizens were expelled from Eretz Yisrael, sending SILA on another shlichut to Bukhara.
Story: The summer 5674 outbreak of WWI brought the Ottoman expulsion of Russian subjects from Eretz Yisrael. SILA, a Russian citizen, was forced to leave and used the opportunity for another emissary mission to Bukhara. He reportedly opened a yeshiva in Samarkand during his exile, where he is documented in Kislev 5677.
Tags: world war i, russia, expulsion, chevron, bukhara

Title: WWI forces Torat Emet shluchim back to Russia
Summary: With the outbreak of World War I in 5674, the mashpia and student shluchim of Yeshivat Torat Emet returned from Hebron to Russia.
Story: When World War I began in 5674 (1914), the mashpia and the student shluchim who had been sent from Lubavitch to staff Yeshivat Torat Emet in Hebron were forced to return to Russia. The yeshiva's original Hebron operation effectively shut down. The institution would later be reopened in Jerusalem, where it continues to operate today.
Tags: hebron, chabad, torat emet, world war i, russia

Title: 200+ Chabad members in Eretz Yisrael publicly remove gabbaim Bichowsky and Bagin
Summary: In Tevet 5674 over 200 Chabad members across Eretz Yisrael published a kruz declaring the gabbaim Bichowsky and Bagin removed from their posts.
Story: Responding to accusations and a unilateral decision by the gabbaim abroad to dismiss the Jerusalem-based officials, 204 signatories from Jerusalem, Hebron, Tzfat and Tiberias issued a 'Moda'a Rabba' from the Kollel Chabad etrog office. They declared the two gabbaim and their faction removed, and asked that all funds be sent only to the established address of R. Mordechai Dov Slonim and R. M. Schlank. Bichowsky soon published 'HaTaynos VeHa'ashomos' detailing his charges, and the officials responded in the kuntres 'Tumas Yesharim'.
Tags: kollel chabad, etrog trade, bichowsky, bagin, jerusalem, slonim, schlank

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter on book duplicates and library organization
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab wrote to his son about handling duplicate books in the library and identifying volumes inherited from his father.
Story: In Tevet 5674 (January 1914), the Rebbe Rashab wrote multiple letters to his son the Rebbe Rayatz about library matters. He addressed which duplicate books could be sold to R' Meir Lubak on behalf of R' M.G., emphasizing that books inherited from his father, the Rebbe Maharash, should not be sold. He requested a list of duplicates with prices be sent to the buyer.
Tags: library, lubavitch, books, rebbe rashab

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter on book spacing in library shelves
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab wrote that library books should not be packed too tightly on shelves to prevent damage.
Story: On 15 Tevet 5674 (January 13, 1914), the Rebbe Rashab wrote to his son expressing satisfaction with the library organization. He instructed that books should not stand crowded and crammed together, as this damages them by preventing air circulation. While they need not be as spaciously arranged as Wiener had set them, they should not be packed tightly.
Tags: library, lubavitch, books, preservation

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter on cataloging library books by subject
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab requested a topical catalog be made of the library's contents.
Story: On 21 Tevet 5674 (January 19, 1914), the Rebbe Rashab wrote to his son expressing his long-standing desire for a subject-based catalog of the library. He wanted a list showing which general topics appeared in which books, such as the category of Torah. He hoped Moshe Chaim could create such a list, and had originally wanted Wiener to do it.
Tags: library, lubavitch, catalog, bibliography

Title: Passing of Rebbetzin Rivka, wife of Maharash
Summary: Rebbetzin Rivka, wife of Rebbe Maharash, passed away on 10 Shevat 5674 and was interred beside her husband at the Lubavitch ohel.
Story: Rebbetzin Rivka, daughter of Rabbi Aharon of Aleksandrov and wife of Maharash, died on 10 Shevat 5674 (1914) — a date later doubly significant in Chabad history. She was laid to rest near her husband Maharash adjacent to the Tzemach Tzedek's ohel in Lubavitch. A separate ohel in the cemetery housed graves of earlier rebbetzins of the Chabad dynasty.
Tags: rivka, maharash, lubavitch, ohel, schneersohn

Title: Passing of Rebbetzin Rivka, wife of the Maharash, 10 Shevat 5674
Summary: Rebbetzin Rivka, wife of the Maharash, passed away in Lubavitch on 10 Shevat 5674 while her son was in Menton.
Story: Rebbetzin Rivka, wife of the Rebbe Maharash, passed away on Friday morning, 10 Shevat 5674. She had caught a cold earlier in the week, which developed into pneumonia; Dr. Lieberman of Vitebsk was summoned, and on Thursday night R. Nachum Glass traveled to Vitebsk to bring oxygen, but she died that Friday morning. The Rebbe Rashab was in Menton at the time and the Rayatz led the levaya, choosing a plot opposite the ohel of the Tzemach Tzedek and the Maharash, conditional on the Rebbe Rashab's approval.
Tags: rebbetzin rivka, maharash, rebbe rashab, rayatz, menton, vitebsk, levaya, lubavitch

Title: Passing of Rebbetzin Rivka, wife of the Rebbe Maharash
Summary: Rebbetzin Rivka, wife of Rebbe Maharash, passed away on Friday 10 Shevat 5674.
Story: The Rebbetzin's yahrzeit on 10 Shevat is observed by the Frierdiker Rebbe leading prayers before the amud. The date is referenced in the narrative of the Frierdiker Rebbe's 10 Shevat 5690 prayers in Crown Heights, when Michael Feder traveled from Philadelphia to be present.
Tags: rebbetzin rivka, maharash, yud shevat, yahrzeit, 1914

Title: Rayatz travels abroad to console his father after Rebbetzin Rivka's passing
Summary: The Rayatz left for Germany after Shabbos to console his father, who ordered round-the-clock learning in his mother's room.
Story: On Motzei Shabbos following the levaya, the Rayatz traveled to Germany to comfort his father the Rebbe Rashab and to report on the funeral arrangements. When someone pointed out that his hat was not properly placed, he replied that he never paid attention to such things, certainly not now. From abroad the Rebbe Rashab sent a telegram instructing that ten bochurim study around the clock for the entire shloshim in his mother's room.
Tags: rayatz, rebbe rashab, rebbetzin rivka, germany, shloshim, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter to son on manuscript security via R' Elchanan
Summary: On 11 Adar 5674, Rebbe Rashab instructed his son to entrust manuscript security to R' Elchanan, who should sleep in the manuscript room with other yeshiva students.
Story: Continuing his pattern of manuscript security instructions during his absences (Igros #428), Rebbe Rashab insisted on having designated guardians physically present overnight. The yeshiva students would sleep in the manuscript room to ensure continuous protection.
Tags: rashab, rayatz, manuscripts, security, letters

Title: Purim 5674 farbrengen abroad with wealthy chassidim
Summary: Wealthy chassidim traveled abroad for a long Purim 5674 farbrengen with the Rebbe Rashab.
Story: For Purim 5674, while the Rebbe Rashab was still abroad for medical treatment, wealthy chassidim of anash traveled to be with him. There was a long farbrengen with wondrous teachings. The Rebbe returned to Lubavitch only after Pesach 5674.
Tags: purim, rebbe rashab, europe, anash, farbrengen

Title: Rebbe Rashab returns to Lubavitch after Pesach 5674
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab returned to Lubavitch after Pesach 5674 and resumed his Tarav Hemshech on Shavuos.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab returned to Lubavitch after Pesach 5674, ending the absence that had begun the previous Kislev. On Shavuos he resumed delivering the Hemshech that he had begun on Shavuos Tarav ("BeSha'a SheHikdimu"), continuing without break until Shabbos Parshas Vayera 5676.
Tags: rebbe rashab, pesach, lubavitch, hemshech tarav, shavuos

Title: 'Emet MeEretz Titzmach' clears Jerusalem officials and invites public claims
Summary: At the end of Iyar 5674 the Lubavitch delegates published the kruz 'Emet MeEretz Titzmach' affirming the trustworthiness of officials Slonim, Schlank and Naeh.
Story: After nearly a month of daily review, the delegates announced they had examined every ledger of income from every place and individual, and found all properly recorded with matching orders, talons and receipts. They had posted notices inviting anyone with a complaint to come forward — even offering a reward to whoever could prove a missing share — and received only generic complaints about small allowances rather than evidence of misappropriation. They concluded with full confidence in the integrity of the kollel officials Slonim, Schlank and Naeh.
Tags: kollel chabad, jerusalem, audit, slonim, schlank, naeh, lubavitch

Title: Bichowsky faction founds breakaway 'Kollel Chabad HaMeyuchad' in Jerusalem
Summary: On 24 Iyar 5674 Bichowsky, Luria and Mekler convened a meeting of 'Bnei Kolleinu Chabad HaMeyuchad', formalizing a permanent split in the kollel.
Story: When the unity proposal required retaining the existing Jerusalem managers, members of the Bichowsky group refused, citing past suffering at the hands of those managers. The next day they published a kruz announcing the founding of 'Kollel Chabad HaMeyuchad' as a separate body, and stating that the din torah against the previous managers would be conducted only once R. Chaim Bagin — who was ill — arrived. The split between the two kollelim from this point became final.
Tags: kollel chabad meyuchad, bichowsky, luria, mekler, jerusalem, split

Title: Rebbe Rashab resumes Hemshech Tarav on Shavuos 5674
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab resumed his Hemshech Tarav on Shavuos 5674 with maamarim on tohu and tikkun.
Story: On Shavuos 5674 the Rebbe Rashab resumed delivering the Hemshech he had begun on Shavuos Tarav ("BeSha'a SheHikdimu"). The maamarim of summer 5674 dealt with the themes of tohu and tikkun, offering deep and luminous explanations. The series continued without interruption until Parshas Vayera 5676.
Tags: shavuos, rebbe rashab, hemshech tarav, tohu and tikkun, maamar

Title: Shabbos Beha'aloscha 5674 at the Zaalshe dacha
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab at the Zaalshe dacha spoke on the root of middos above seichel on Shabbos Beha'aloscha 5674.
Story: On Shabbos Parshas Beha'aloscha 5674 the author was at the Rebbe Rashab's summer dacha at Zaalshe. The Rebbe spoke about the root of the middos that transcends the intellect. The author would visit Zaalshe again that summer for Parshas Pinchas and Parshas Ki Setze.
Tags: zaalshe, dacha, rebbe rashab, beha'aloscha, middos, summer

Title: Din torah opens before Jerusalem Beis Din Tzedek between Kollel officials and gabbaim
Summary: On 11 Tammuz 5674 both sides appeared before the Ashkenazi Beis Din Tzedek of Jerusalem, which heard the parties before the gabbaim withdrew.
Story: After Bagin arrived, the parties presented their claims before the Beis Din Tzedek. The gabbaim ultimately refused to continue litigating before that beis din, and the dispute dragged on for two months. The gabbaim returned abroad at the start of Elul, and on 16 Elul the beis din published its ruling 'Emet UMishpat Kasuv' siding with the Jerusalem officials.
Tags: kollel chabad, beis din tzedek, jerusalem, bichowsky, bagin

Title: Shabbos Pinchas 5674 at the Zaalshe dacha
Summary: A Shabbos at the Zaalshe dacha on Parshas Pinchas 5674 drew the mashgiach and prominent guests from Warsaw.
Story: On Shabbos Parshas Pinchas 5674 the author was again at Zaalshe, joined by R. Shilem Kuratin the mashgiach on Chassidus and guests including the maskil R. Pesach Frenkel and the tamim R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov of Warsaw-Klimovich, son-in-law of R. Yosef Yuzik Horowitz of Warsaw.
Tags: zaalshe, dacha, rebbe rashab, pinchas, shilem kuratin, shraga feivish zalmanov, warsaw

Title: Maharaitz visits Lubavitch on yeshiva business
Summary: On 9 Elul 5674, Maharaitz travelled alone to Lubavitch for Tomchei Temimim matters and stayed until 11 Elul.
