Title: Rebbe Rashab writes blessing to mother from Slavyansk
Summary: Rebbe Rashab penned a handwritten note to a mother, blessing her son to walk in the good and upright path.
Story: While residing in Slavyansk during the upheavals of World War I, Rebbe Sholom DovBer of Lubavitch wrote a brief handwritten response to a mother who had sought his blessing. He acknowledged receipt of her letter and prayed that G-d grant her son a good heart to walk in the good and upright way. The note is dated Monday of the week of Parshat Re'eh, 5677.
Tags: rashab, slavyansk, blessing, letter, russia

Title: Maharashab travels to Moscow
Summary: Maharashab's final recorded passport stamp was issued in Moscow on 26 Menachem Av 5677.
Story: On 1 August 1917 (26 Menachem Av 5677), in the volatile months between the February and October Revolutions, Maharashab's internal Russian passport received its final recorded stamp, in Moscow. This visit marked the last documented journey in this passport during the closing months of imperial and revolutionary Russia.
Tags: maharashab, moscow, passport, wwi, russian revolution

Title: R' Zev Wolf Bronstein dies in Spanish flu epidemic
Summary: R' Zev Wolf Bronstein, father of the Bronstein brothers of Cherkassy, succumbed to the Spanish flu between Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur 5678.
Story: The epidemic claimed R' Zev Wolf Bronstein during the Ten Days of Repentance in 5678. He was the father of the well-known Bronstein brothers of Cherkassy — Chaim Ezra, Nosson, Mordechai, and Hershka — and later father-in-law of R' Shlomo Chaim Kesselman, who became a mashpia in Tomchei Temimim Lod.
Tags: bronstein, rostov, spanish flu, death, tcherkassy

Title: Russian rabbis officially receive military exemption
Summary: By Erev Rosh Hashanah 5678 the rabbis' draft exemption was officially confirmed and publicized in the Kiev press.
Story: In letter 1071 the Rebbe Rashab announced the news, noting publication in Kiev newspapers that all rabbis — regardless of seniority or grade — held equal exemption rights. He praised the recognition of rabbinic status itself as a great good.
Tags: russia, provisional government, kiev, rabbinate, military exemption

Title: Spanish flu epidemic strikes Chabad community in Rostov
Summary: A devastating Spanish flu epidemic struck during Rosh Hashana 5678 in Rostov, incapacitating roughly forty people who could not attend the Rebbe's services.
Story: The Spanish flu, accompanied by severe vomiting and diarrhea, swept through Rostov during Rosh Hashana 5678. The narrator himself was struck on the first night of the holiday. About forty people were unable to attend the Rebbe Rashab's Torah reading and shofar blowing, lying instead in the lower quarters of the building.
Tags: rostov, spanish flu, epidemic, illness, 5678

Title: Yeshiva students travel to Rostov for Rosh Hashana with Rebbe Rashab
Summary: All the bochurim of the great hall traveled from Lubavitch to Rostov to be with the Rebbe Rashab for Rosh Hashana 5678.
Story: For Rosh Hashana 5678 the entire student body of the main study hall traveled to Rostov to spend the High Holy Days with the Rebbe Rashab. The narrator stayed with his previous host R' Mordechai Gertzulin on Staraya Pochtovaya 122. This was part of an established pattern of Tomchei Temimim students gathering with the Rebbe for major holidays.
Tags: rostov, rosh hashana, tomchei tmimim, rebbe rashab, 5678

Title: Calabrian etrog mix-up at Rebbe Rashab's home on Sukkos
Summary: During Chol Hamoed Sukkos 5678 the Rebbe Rashab's personal Calabrian etrog was mistakenly handed to Pesach Wolf of Zhitomir, prompting a halachic discussion.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab had several Calabrian etrogim that Sukkos, designating one for the chassidim to use for the blessing. When Pesach Wolf arrived mid-Chol Hamoed from Zhitomir, the attendant R' M.M. mistakenly brought him the Rebbe's own etrog. This sparked a subsequent halachic discussion about whether the blessing had been fulfilled or had to be repeated.
Tags: rebbe rashab, sukkot, etrog, calabria, rostov

Title: Rebbe Rashab's Simchas Torah farbrengen on lengthy prayer
Summary: An exceptional Simchas Torah 5678 farbrengen in Rostov centered on the necessity of avodah and lengthy prayer, lasting until late at night.
Story: The Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah farbrengens of 5678 in Rostov were extraordinary, all focused on the imperative of avodah and lengthy davening — the core mission of Lubavitch. Sichos from the farbrengen are preserved in transcripts and the printed Toras Shalom. The Rebbe also engaged Polish chassidic refugees of Ger and Alexander who were present, and the daytime farbrengen continued until near midnight with dancing through the house.
Tags: rebbe rashab, simchat torah, farbrengen, rostov, avodah, torat shalom

Title: Bolshevik October Revolution begins, sparking Russian civil war
Summary: At the start of 5678 the Red Revolution erupted in Russia, triggering shortages, civil war, and German advances into Jewish areas.
Story: The Bolshevik Revolution at the start of 5678 unleashed widespread shortages of food and goods across Russia and ignited civil war. With the Russians ceasing combat, German forces advanced rapidly into the Jewish heartland of the western empire. The crisis directly threatened Tomchei Temimim in Lubavitch, prompting plans to relocate the yeshiva.
Tags: russia, revolution, bolshevik, civil war, world war i

Title: Bolsheviks overthrow Kerensky and ban Jewish religious parties
Summary: The Bolshevik seizure of power dissolved the Provisional Government and annulled the religious Jewish parties and societies that had organized after the February Revolution.
Story: Throughout 1917, in the freedom that followed the February Revolution, chassidim and other observant Jews had been organizing politically, urged on by the Rebbe Rashab, to win representation in the new communal structures. The planned all-Russian Jewish assembly never met. The Bolshevik overthrow of Kerensky's government ended these efforts entirely: the new regime invalidated the religious parties and disbanded the societies that had taken shape under the Provisional Government.
Tags: bolsheviks, kerensky, russia, jewish politics, communism

Title: Rebbe Rashab caught in Moscow during October Revolution
Summary: Traveling toward Petrograd at the end of Marcheshvan 5678, the Rebbe was forced by the October Revolution to halt in Moscow and return to Rostov.
Story: Invited by the Ministry of Religions for consultations in Petrograd, the Rebbe also planned to meet R. Chaim Ozer Grodzinski there to discuss a general rabbis' assembly. While en route the Bolshevik October Revolution broke out; he stayed Shabbos in Moscow and afterward returned to Rostov.
Tags: russia, october revolution, bolshevik, moscow, petrograd, rostov

Title: City authorities seize Lubavitch courtyard buildings
Summary: After the last yeshiva students left Lubavitch, the city authorities took over the Rebbes' courtyard.
Story: At the end of 5678 (1918), after the last Tomchei Temimim students left Lubavitch, the municipality seized the courtyard. The great hall was converted into the city theater, the Rashab's house became the court building, the Maharash's rooms became the city council, the Rayatz's rooms became municipal offices, and the brick house became the city school.
Tags: lubavitch, soviet, communism, courtyard, yeshiva

Title: Father released from army, reopens cheder in Zhivotov
Summary: Ephraim Shmuel returned from military service in 1918 and reopened his Torah school for children and youth in Zhivotov.
Story: After his release following the fall of the Tsar, Ephraim Shmuel resumed teaching Torah to the youth of Zhivotov. The political climate had changed dramatically: Russia was now a republic, parties were forming, and secular movements were drawing young Jews away from religion. The first public political address in the synagogue by a young woman shocked the elders and ignited communal conflict.
Tags: zhivotov, cheder, ukraine

Title: Final Tomchei Temimim students leave Lubavitch
Summary: By the end of summer 5678, the last group of Tomchei Temimim students departed Lubavitch.
Story: Although the Rashab left Lubavitch in late 1915, the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva students remained behind to learn for another two and a half years. Before the final group departed at the end of summer 5678 (1918), they organized the belongings left behind and buried valuables deep in the cellar of the Rebbe's house for safekeeping. The move ended Lubavitch's centuries-long role as the seat of Chabad.
Tags: tomchei temimim, lubavitch, yeshiva, russia

Title: Last Tomchei Temimim students leave; municipality seizes the Lubavitch courtyard
Summary: At the end of 5678 the last yeshiva students departed Lubavitch, and the municipality took over the courtyard of the Rebbes for civic uses.
Story: At the end of 5678 (1918), the last students of the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva left Lubavitch. The local municipality then seized the courtyard of the Rebbes: the great hall became the municipal theater, the Rashab's house became the courthouse, the Rebbe Maharash's rooms housed the municipal leadership committee, the Rayatz's rooms became the municipal officials' building, and the stone house was turned into the city school.
Tags: tomchei temimim, lubavitch, soviet, russia, exile

Title: Latvia declares independence from Russia
Summary: Latvians overthrow Russian rule and establish an independent republic.
Story: Independence enabled Jewish political participation and party activity; the Rebbe later noted that the community should have established yeshivot from this point on but failed to do so.
Tags: latvia, independence, politics

Title: Latvia declares independence from Russian rule
Summary: The Latvians overthrow Russian rule and become independent, ushering in active Jewish political participation.
Story: Latvian independence lasted until the German invasion in July 1941. The Rebbe later said that since 1918, an effort should have been made to establish Torah institutions. In an election held shortly after the Rebbe's 1927 arrival, Latvian Jews won six parliamentary seats divided among religious parties, Zionists, and the Bund.
Tags: latvia, russia, independence, parliament

Title: Pelach HaRimon by Rabbi Hillel of Paritch published in Vilna
Summary: First edition of Pelach HaRimon by Rabbi Hillel of Paritch printed in Vilna in 5678.
Story: Pelach HaRimon, one of Rabbi Hillel of Paritch's major chassidic compositions, was first printed in Vilna in 5678 (1918). The volume is displayed at the Lubavitch Library exhibition celebrating the great Chabad chassidim.
Tags: vilna, hillel paritch, chassidus

Title: Rashab purchases courtyard property at Bratsky Pereulok 44 in Rostov
Summary: Amid revolution and nationalization, the Rashab bought a large two-story house with courtyard at Bratsky Pereulok 44.
Story: After two years in the Pushkinsky apartment, in 5678 the Rashab moved to buy a substantial building — roughly 16 by 32 meters, two stories with a basement — at Bratsky Pereulok 44. The purchase fell during the chaotic onset of the Russian Civil War and Bolshevik nationalization of property; the down payment of 50,000 was made in January, and the Rashab wrote on 28 Adar that confirmation of the deed and the renovations were uncertain. The deal was nonetheless completed, and by the end of that summer the family moved in, with public prayers held there from Tishrei 5679 onward.
Tags: rashab, rostov, bratsky pereulok, russian revolution, civil war

Title: Rebbe Rashab photographed for emigration passport
Summary: After the Bolshevik takeover, Rebbe Rashab permitted a photograph for a passport in 5678.
Story: In 1918, following the Bolshevik conquest of Russia, Chabad leaders worried they might be forced to emigrate. For passport purposes, Rebbe Rashab permitted a photograph of himself seated in his yechidus room in Rostov. It remains the only photograph of him.
Tags: rebbe rashab, rostov, bolsheviks, russia, portrait

Title: Rebbe writes about hunger in wartime Vilna
Summary: In the summer of 5678 the Rebbe Rashab wrote describing the severe hunger suffered in Vilna during World War I, including by his own representative R. Anshil Aronovich.
Story: After receiving a letter brought out by a traveler, the Rashab wrote that the chassidim of Vilna, including Aronovich, had endured terrible hunger, though conditions had since improved somewhat. The letter is preserved as Iggeret 1097 in volume five of his correspondence.
Tags: vilna, world war i, anshil aronovich, 5678, hunger, rashab

Title: Rostover Siddur printed in Rostov
Summary: The Rostover Siddur, an edition of Tehillas Hashem incorporating corrections directed by the Rebbe Rashab, was printed in Rostov in 5678 (1918).
Story: Photographed from the earlier Tefillas Kol Peh, the Rostov 1918 siddur incorporated many revisions ordered by the Rebbe Rashab and would later serve as the photo-master for the 1947 New York Tehillas Hashem.
Tags: rebbe rashab, rostov, siddur tehillat hashem

Title: Soviet rule begins in Russia
Summary: Soviet rule begins in 5678, opening the era covered by Toldot Chabad in Soviet Russia.
Story: The Soviet regime took hold in 5678 (1918), launching a generation of underground Chabad activity. The companion volume 'Toldot Chabad B'Russia HaSovietit' covers the movement under Soviet rule from this year through 5710.
Tags: russia, soviet, communism

Title: Tanya manuscript catalogued in Wiener private collection
Summary: The Tanya manuscript bought in 1879 was catalogued as item 225 in Wiener's private collection.
Story: In 1918, the Tanya manuscript Wiener had purchased decades earlier in Borisov was catalogued as item 225 in his personal collection. This cataloguing inscription remained visible to Chabad emissaries who examined the manuscript at the Asiatic Institute in Leningrad in 1991.
Tags: tanya, manuscript, wiener, catalog, private library

Title: Ten thousand dollars raised in Kremenchug for Tomchei Temimim
Summary: Per the Rebbe Rashab's directive, ten thousand dollars was collected in Kremenchug during spring 5678 for the yeshiva.
Story: Following the narrator's return from Rostov, the Kremenchug chassidim raised the 10,000 dollars the Rebbe Rashab had mandated to sustain Tomchei Temimim. The daughters of R' Nosson Gurary — Perla and Leah — personally whitewashed the walls and scrubbed the floors of the new yeshiva quarters in preparation for the students.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, kremenchug, fundraising, gourary

Title: Tomchei Temimim shiur students relocated to Oryol
Summary: The younger shiur students were transferred from Lubavitch to Oryol amid worsening conditions and German advances during 5678.
Story: As the financial and security situation in Lubavitch deteriorated under the new Bolshevik regime, the yeshiva's junior shiur students were sent to Oryol. There they were hosted by the shochet R' Yaakov Pantelyev and supported by the wealthy chassid Mr. Shmulevitch. Three older bochurim — Shmuel Chaim Shechtman of Zlobin, Abba of Bolhakov, and apparently R' Yisrael Zuber — accompanied them.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, oryol, relocation, civil war

Title: Tomchei Temimim yeshiva students leave Lubavitch for safer towns
Summary: In 5678 (1918) the yeshiva students left Lubavitch to study in other towns farther from the war zone near the front.
Story: With Lubavitch sitting close to the WWI front, the yeshiva could no longer operate safely there. The students dispersed to study in interior towns. This was a key step in the institutional unraveling of Lubavitch as Chabad's center.
Tags: tomchei-tmimim, wwi, lubavitch, yeshiva

Title: Tomchei Tmimim relocates from Lubavitch
Summary: After over 20 years in Lubavitch, Tomchei Tmimim relocated to Kremenchug and other cities in 5678.
Story: In 5678, Tomchei Tmimim left Lubavitch after operating there for over twenty years. The yeshiva relocated to Kremenchug and other Russian cities as the wartime disruption continued. The Lubavitch era of the yeshiva had come to an end.
Tags: tomchei-tmimim, kremenchug, lubavitch, wwi, evacuation

Title: Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva leaves Lubavitch
Summary: In the summer of 5678 (1918), the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva left Lubavitch, ending the Chabad presence there for over seventy years.
Story: The Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva departed Lubavitch in the summer of 5678 (1918). After the departure, the entire Rebbeim's courtyard burned down following the histalkus of the Rebbe Rashab, as recounted in the Frierdiker Rebbe's letters; the surviving wooden buildings on the property all postdate that fire. By 1991 a new brick post-office building was being constructed in the middle of the old courtyard.
Tags: lubavitch, tomchei tmimim, yeshiva, tarach, world war i, russia, rashab

Title: Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva relocates from Lubavitch to Kremenchug
Summary: After two and a half years operating without the Rebbe in residence, Tomchei Tmimim relocated from Lubavitch to Kremenchug in late summer 5678.
Story: The final students dug deeply into the cellar of the Rebbe's residence to hide possessions before departing. They gathered for a bitter farbrengen marking their separation from Lubavitch, still hoping the move was temporary. With the Soviet anti-religious campaign that followed, the yeshiva eventually retreated underground across dozens of Russian towns.
Tags: tomchei-tmimim, kremenchug, lubavitch

Title: Yeshiva relocation from Lubavitch begins
Summary: During 5678, the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva relocated in stages from Lubavitch to Kremenchug.
Story: Following the Rebbe Rashab's departure from Lubavitch in early 5676 and worsening conditions during World War I, the yeshiva students remained until 5678 (1918). The shiurim moved first under R' Yehoshua Arsh to Oryol for about a year and then to Kremenchug, while the Great Hall (Zal) remained until students gradually relocated to Kremenchug. The last farbrengen in Lubavitch took place on Shabbat Mevarchim Elul.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, kremenchug, world war 1, exile

Title: Yeshivah Torah Vodaath founded in Williamsburg
Summary: Torah Vodaath was established in Brooklyn's Williamsburg neighborhood.
Story: At the time of the Rebbe Rayatz's 1929 visit, Torah Vodaath and Yeshivas Rabbeinu Yitzchok Elchonon were the principal yeshivot in New York. Only twelve percent of Brooklyn's Jewish children received any Jewish education in the 1920s.
Tags: yeshiva, brooklyn, williamsburg, united-states

Title: Zionist Office census records 757 Jews in Hebron
Summary: A census conducted by the Zionist Organization's Palestine Office in 5678 found 757 Jews in Hebron, roughly half the pre-war population.
Story: After the British conquest, the Palestine Office of the Zionist Organization conducted a census in 5678 (1918). It tallied 256 Ashkenazim, 444 Sephardim, and 57 Maghrebi and Yemenite Jews — a total of 757 souls. This was roughly half the Jewish population recorded a decade earlier.
Tags: hebron, census, demographics, british mandate

Title: Elections to the All-Jewish General Congress
Summary: Religious lists succeeded in the January 1918 (Shevat 5678) elections to the All-Jewish General Congress, but the Congress never convened.
Story: Chabad's bloc 'Achdut' — number 3 on the ballot — was formed by merging with the religious lists 'Netzach Yisrael' and 'HaMasoret VeHaCheirut,' with the Rebbe's approval. In some places the Orthodox ran separately as 'Adas Yisrael' with a platform he composed. Despite electoral success, the subsequent consolidation of Bolshevik rule prevented the Congress from ever meeting.
Tags: russia, jewish congress, achdut bloc, edas yisrael, elections

Title: Yeshiva fundraisers depart Lubavitch on night of 13 Adar
Summary: On the night of 13 Adar 5678 the narrator and R' Leib Krasik left Lubavitch for Moscow as part of an emergency fundraising mission to save the yeshiva.
Story: With Tomchei Temimim collapsing financially, senior figures were dispatched to Russia's major Jewish centers. R' Shilem Kuratin went to Petersburg, R' Eliezer Kaplan to Vitebsk and Nevel, and the narrator with R' Leib Krasik were sent to Moscow. They read the megillah on the eve of 13 Adar and boarded the train that night, planning to daven and read megillah again in Moscow.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, fundraising, moscow, purim, civil war

Title: Eighteen thousand rubles raised in Moscow for Tomchei Temimim on Purim
Summary: On Purim day 5678 the magnate R' Zalka Persitz and R' Baruch Shalom Kahan helped raise 18,000 rubles in a single day in Moscow for the yeshiva.
Story: After arriving in Moscow on Purim eve and being hosted at R' Baruch Shalom Kahan's home, the fundraisers were taken the next morning to the office of the magnate R' Zalka Persitz. Through phone calls throughout the day they collected 18,000 rubles. The emissaries sewed 9,000 rubles into each of their garments and returned to Lubavitch.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, fundraising, moscow, purim, persitz, kahan

Title: Germans capture Lubavitch region just before Pesach
Summary: German forces entered the Lubavitch area immediately before Pesach 5678, cutting civilian rail travel and isolating the town.
Story: Following the Brest-Litovsk treaty, German forces advanced into the area encompassing Lubavitch right before Pesach 5678. Civilian rail traffic was halted — only military trains ran — preventing the narrator from returning from Kremenchug. The occupation persisted through the summer, with German authorities installing local Ukrainian rulers under their suzerainty.
Tags: lubavitch, germany, world war i, occupation

Title: Rebbe Rashab delivers maamar 'Hachodesh Hazeh' in Rostov
Summary: On Shabbos Parshas Hachodesh 5678 the Rebbe Rashab said the maamar 'Hachodesh Hazeh' in Rostov, before a yechidus with the visiting emissary.
Story: Following his fundraising trip to Moscow, the narrator traveled to Rostov to ask the Rebbe Rashab's guidance on the future of Tomchei Temimim. He arrived before Shabbos Parshas Hachodesh 5678 and heard the Rebbe deliver the maamar 'Hachodesh Hazeh' that Shabbos. Motzaei Shabbos he had a forty-minute yechidus in which the Rebbe gave his ruling that the students should remain in Lubavitch.
Tags: rebbe rashab, maamar, parshas hachodesh, rostov, 5678

Title: Rebbe Rashab rules yeshiva should remain in Lubavitch
Summary: In a Motzaei Shabbos yechidus in Rostov, the Rebbe Rashab ruled that despite German advances Tomchei Temimim students should stay in Lubavitch.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab gave three reasons in yechidus: he believed the Germans would not capture Lubavitch; even if captured the area would not be fully controlled, allowing small group study; and even at worst the border would be porous enough to cross. He concluded that relocating Lubavitch itself was impossible — 'the light will be missing' — and a telegram was sent to halt the evacuation. By then it was too late and most students had already left.
Tags: rebbe rashab, tomchei tmimim, lubavitch, rostov, yechidus, world war i

Title: 13 Nissan farbrengen at the Gurary shul in Kremenchug
Summary: A farbrengen was held on 13 Nissan 5678 in the Gurary shul of Kremenchug, led by R' Elchonon Dov Morozov.
Story: While stranded in Kremenchug arranging accommodations for the shiur students, the narrator attended a 13 Nissan farbrengen in the Gurary synagogue. R' Elchonon Dov Morozov was the principal speaker, with the meshulach R' Yechiel Halperin and others present. The gathering was part of the consolidation of the Tomchei Temimim community in its new wartime home.
Tags: kremenchug, farbrengen, morozov, halpern, 13 nissan

Title: Narrator returns to Lubavitch from Kremenchug around Rosh Chodesh Iyar
Summary: Around Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5678 the narrator carried 10,000 rubles back to Lubavitch, crossing the German–Russian border on foot at Orsha at night.
Story: Around Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5678 the narrator left Kremenchug for Lubavitch with 10,000 rubles hidden in his stockings. At Orsha he had to walk roughly three miles between the German and Russian customs posts in the dark, assisting an elderly Jewish woman who could not keep pace. He arrived in Lubavitch via Krasna in the morning.
Tags: lubavitch, kremenchug, orsha, german occupation, border crossing

Title: Twelve Tomchei Temimim students arrested as suspected spies in Poltava
Summary: Twelve Lubavitcher bochurim en route from Lubavitch to Kremenchug were arrested at Poltava station on suspicion of espionage and nearly executed.
Story: Rumors reached Kremenchug on a Friday that twelve Tomchei Temimim students had been killed at Poltava station. In fact they had been detained as suspected spies — triggered by Zalman Birnbaum's Polish-style cap and rapid movements. R' Tzvi Gurary used his military contacts to telephone the Poltava war chief, and R' Mordechai Aharon Friedman traveled by military train to obtain rabbinic guarantees from R' Duber Greenpress and R' Eliyahu Akiva Rabinowitz that freed them.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, poltava, kremenchug, civil war, arrest, espionage, gourary

Title: Acharon shel Pesach farbrengen at R' Tzvi Gurary in Kremenchug
Summary: On Acharon shel Pesach 5678 a farbrengen was held at R' Tzvi Gurary's home in Kremenchug, lasting late into the night.
Story: The narrator spent Pesach 5678 in Kremenchug as a guest of R' Nosson Gurary, whose home was open to all. On the last day of Pesach the local chassidim gathered at R' Tzvi Gurary's house for a farbrengen that extended until late at night, even as 10,000 dollars was being raised for Tomchei Temimim per the Rebbe Rashab's instruction.
Tags: kremenchug, farbrengen, gourary, pesach, acharon shel pesach

Title: Rebbe Rashab stays at Slavyansk healing waters
Summary: From 9 Tammuz to 10 Elul 5678 the Rebbe stayed at the Slavyansk healing waters under harsh wartime travel conditions.
Story: Amid the Russian Civil War, when travel was nearly impossible, the Rebbe made the one known journey of the period to the Slavyansk spa, arriving the eve of 9 Tammuz 5678 and remaining through 10 Elul. He wrote of overcrowded train cars, the unavailability of seat reservations, and dread about the return trip.
Tags: slavyansk, russia, civil war, health, travel hardship

Title: Rashab reports on stereotype plates in Rostov during WWI
Summary: On 21 Menachem Av תרע"ח, writing from Rostov during WWI, the Rashab informed his son the Rayatz that the stereotype plates of Likkutei Torah and Tanya, and the printing house generally, were intact.
Story: During the displacement of WWI the Rashab settled in Rostov-on-Don. From there, on 21 Av תרע"ח, he wrote to his son the future Rebbe Rayatz that the stereotype plates of Likkutei Torah and Tanya and the rest of the press equipment had survived intact — a fact that would later enable a sixth edition to be printed from those plates in תרפ"ח.
Tags: rashab, rostov, wwi, stereotype plates, likkutei torah, tanya

Title: Farewell farbrengen at R' Shmuel Gronem on Shabbos Mevorchim Elul
Summary: On Shabbos Mevorchim Elul 5678, before leaving Lubavitch, a farewell farbrengen was held at R' Shmuel Gronem's home with wine from the Rebbe's cellar.
Story: Before evacuating Lubavitch the remaining bochurim and senior figures held a final farbrengen at the Rashag's home on Shabbos Mevorchim Elul 5678. They drew bottles of wine from the cellar of the Rebbe Rayatz's father-in-law R' Avraham. The atmosphere of taking leave of Lubavitch — even with hope of return — was overwhelming, despite reassuring news from Kremenchug and Rostov.
Tags: lubavitch, farbrengen, shmuel gronem, tomchei tmimim, departure

Title: Tomchei Temimim center relocates from Lubavitch to Kremenchug
Summary: Near Elul 5678 the final group left Lubavitch via Bryansk and a night border crossing to reach Kremenchug, ending the yeshiva's presence in Lubavitch.
Story: After hiding the Rebbe's household vessels in a deep cellar, the last twelve bochurim and senior families departed Lubavitch via Rudnia toward Bryansk. From Klintsy they used peasant wagons through a neutral zone, paying off Russian soldiers and German border guards along the way. After bribery, beatings, and a tense night in no-man's land, they reached Gomel and continued to Kremenchug — formally ending the yeshiva's residence in Lubavitch.
Tags: lubavitch, kremenchug, tomchei tmimim, relocation, civil war, german occupation, bryansk

Title: Tomchei Tmimim students travel to Rostov for Rosh Hashanah 5679
Summary: All the Tomchei Tmimim students traveled to Rostov to spend Rosh Hashanah 5679 with the Rebbe Rashab.
Story: The chassidim prayed in the Shaalash, a wooden structure built in the courtyard of the Rebbe Rashab's home on Bradsky Pereulok 44 in Rostov, which he had purchased after the move from Lubavitch. R' Yechiel Halpern served as chazzan. This was the first Rosh Hashanah of the Tomchei Tmimim student body following the relocation from Kremenchug for the chag.
Tags: rostov, rosh hashanah, tomchei tmimim, rashab, shaalash, yechiel halpern

Title: Wedding of Chaim Kavash officiated by the Rebbe Rashab in Rostov
Summary: Between Yom Kippur and Sukkot 5679, R' Chaim Kavash of Vyetka married a relative of Rebbetzin Sterna Sarah, with the Rebbe Rashab serving as mesader kiddushin.
Story: The Rebbe Rashab stood at the entrance of the Shaalash while the chuppah was held in the courtyard. For the bracha of 'Asher Bara' he honored a religious German army officer who was lodging in the Rebbe's home. Witnesses noted that during the blessings the Rebbe held his hands raised, fingers spread above his eyebrows.
Tags: wedding, rashab, rostov, rebbetzin sterna sarah, chaim kavash

Title: Calabrian etrog identified by the Rebbe Rashab on Erev Sukkot 5679
Summary: On Erev Sukkot 5679 the Rebbe Rashab studied a single etrog brought from Calabria for about two hours before confirming its origin.
Story: The etrog was sent by R' Shmuel Gurary and delivered by R' Dovber Ganzburg of Odessa amid wartime disruption of supply routes. Throughout Sukkot the Rebbe permitted every chassid to bless the etrog but allowed no one — not even his son the Rayatz — to perform na'anuim with it, and asked each person whether their hands were dry. He sat in the sukkah from 6 to 10 a.m. each day attending to the chassidim.
Tags: sukkot, etrog, calabria, rashab, shmuel gurary, dovber ganzburg, odessa

Title: Simchat Torah 5679 farbrengen with the Rebbe Rashab in Rostov
Summary: On the night of Simchat Torah 5679 the Rebbe Rashab attended kiddush at the home of his son the Rayatz before hakafot, delivering rare personal remarks.
Story: The Rebbe spoke about Moshiach coming through wealthy supporters and about the founding of Tomchei Tmimim, declaring 'I am a sichli' and that he would not be moved by externalities. When he discussed connection to the House of David he turned to the Rayatz and said 'Yitzchak, hear this — it concerns you.' Hakafot were not held that night, and the Rebbe Rashab uncharacteristically danced with the assembled chassidim, something he had previously done only with his son.
Tags: simchat torah, rashab, rayatz, rostov, moshiach, tomchei tmimim, davidic lineage

Title: Author's final yechidus with the Rebbe Rashab
Summary: After Sukkot 5679 the author entered for what would be his final yechidus with the Rebbe Rashab, presenting two shidduch proposals.
Story: He raised concerns about premature deaths in the family of the proposed bride suggested by his future brother-in-law R' Aharon Eliezer Zeitlin. The Rebbe Rashab repeated three times 'nito vos tzu choshesh zein' — there is nothing to fear — and closed with 'Hashem should protect you from everything,' the last words the author would ever hear from him in person.
Tags: yechidus, rashab, shidduch, rostov, aharon eliezer zeitlin

Title: 19 Kislev 5679 farbrengen in Rostov
Summary: The 19 Kislev 5679 farbrengen was held in Rostov with R' Shaul Dov Zislin repeating a maamer 'Devash V'chalav Tachas Leshonech.'
Story: Chassidim of Kremenchug including R' Shmuel Kuratin tried to travel to Rostov for the chag but could not obtain train tickets and had to return home as the rail network was in disarray. Witnesses recalled that as R' Shaul Dov Zislin chazered the maamer 'honey and milk flowed from his mouth.'
Tags: yud tes kislev, rostov, shaul dov zislin, kremenchug

Title: Gurarie family relocates to Rostov, near the Rebbe's home
Summary: At the start of 5680 the Gurarie family moved to Rostov, settling near the home of the Lubavitcher Rebbe.
Story: At the start of 5680 (autumn 1919) the Gurarie family relocated to Rostov, settling close to the residence of the Rebbeim. R' Shneur Zalman was then about eight years old. The proximity allowed close contact with the Rebbes' court during a formative period of his life.
Tags: rostov, russia, gurarie-family, rebbe-rashab, rebbe-rayatz

Title: Hebrew Theological College founded in Chicago
Summary: The Hebrew Theological College, also called Beis HaMidrash LaTorah, was founded in Chicago.
Story: It became a major center of Jewish learning. During the Rebbe Rayatz's 1930 visit to Chicago, its rosh yeshivah Rabbi Nachman Bar was personally challenged by the Rebbe to expand his impact beyond the yeshivah walls.
Tags: chicago, htc, yeshiva, united-states

Title: Martyrdom of Moshe Yehoshua Bzhilianski (Alter of Teplik), Breslov Chassid
Summary: Moshe Yehoshua Bzhilianski, known as Alter of Teplik and compiler of the 'Or Zoreach' Breslov Haggadah, was killed sanctifying God's name.
Story: In 5679 (1919), during the turbulent post-revolutionary period in Ukraine marked by widespread pogroms, the Breslov Chassid Moshe Yehoshua Bzhilianski — known as Alter of Teplik — was killed in sanctification of God's name. He had been working on a Breslov Haggadah called 'Or Zoreach' based on the writings of Rabbi Nachman of Breslov. The Haggadah was eventually published posthumously in Jerusalem in 1927 by his Breslov colleagues.
Tags: breslov, teplik, ukraine, pogroms, martyrdom, alter of teplik

Title: Rebbe Rashab letter on destruction in Lubavitch
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab wrote about the seizure and destruction of property in the Lubavitch courtyard.
Story: On Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni 5679 (1919), the Rebbe Rashab wrote about events in Lubavitch: the courtyard and houses had been confiscated and great destruction wrought. Book crates, cabinets, and furniture had been taken and much was broken. Valuable utensils worth great sums were left behind, and they had reportedly turned the brick house into a club out of spite.
Tags: lubavitch, soviet, destruction, courtyard

Title: Soviet ministry approves grant to Habima theater
Summary: Despite Yevesektzia leader Dimenstein's protest, the Soviet ministry of culture approved a grant to the Hebrew-language Habima theater.
Story: Dimenstein argued the grant indulged 'the whim of the bourgeoisie' and pursued Hebrew culture as anathema to Jewish Communism. A public debate was held in Moscow in 1920. The episode illustrated that the Yevesektzia routinely exceeded Soviet government policy.
Tags: habima, yevesektzia, dimenstein, moscow

Title: Ukrainian pogroms of 5679–5680 kill roughly 300,000 Jews
Summary: During 5679 and 5680 anti-Jewish pogroms by White Army, Petliura, and Makhno forces killed approximately 300,000 Jews across Ukraine.
Story: Rival armies competing for control of Ukraine after the German withdrawal openly permitted their soldiers to attack Jewish communities. Kremenchug suffered an incursion by Petliura's troops for about a week, with house searches and several casualties; chassidim hid in cellars. Later the Makhnovist forces, who had killed R' Menachem Mendel of Bobruisk in Yekaterinoslav, besieged Kremenchug from across the Dnieper at Kraukov until Red Army artillery drove them back across the bridge.
Tags: pogroms, ukraine, russian civil war, petliura, makhno, denikin, kremenchug

Title: Rebbe Rashab dispatches secret emissary to Vitebsk and Lubavitch
Summary: In Shevat 5679 the Rebbe sent a special emissary to Vitebsk, Petrograd and Moscow to learn the fate of his family and chassidim under Soviet rule.
Story: By Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni 5679 the emissary had still not returned. The Rebbe described in letter 1103 how he had heard nothing from his sister and brother-in-law in Vitebsk for nine months, that the Lubavitch courtyard and homes had been confiscated, libraries and furniture seized or smashed, and that the synagogue had been turned into a clubhouse 'out of vengeance.'
Tags: civil war, vitebsk, lubavitch, shaliach, communist, expropriation

Title: Jerusalem Beis Din Tzedek reaffirms trust in Kollel Chabad officials during WWI
Summary: On 20 Adar I 5679 the Jerusalem Beis Din published a further ruling defending the Kollel Chabad vaad amid wartime accusations from Anash abroad.
Story: Critical letters had circulated in the Diaspora attacking the Jerusalem vaad under Rebbe Rashab's nesius, sowing discord and discouraging donors. The beis din declared that it knew the officials well as honest and trustworthy men, and that whenever funds arrived from America and England — Russian remittances having been cut off by the war — they were distributed to the poor of the kollel in Jerusalem, Hebron, Tzfat, Tiberias, Yafo and the moshavot. The pesak became a recurring touchstone in the kollel correspondence of 5681–5682.
Tags: kollel chabad, beis din tzedek, jerusalem, world war i, america, england

Title: Chafetz Chaim writes to Rabbi Moshe Madeyevski about relocating to Charal
Summary: On Sunday Parshat Emor 5679, the Chafetz Chaim wrote to the rabbi of Charal asking help to find lodging there because of terrible food prices where he was then living.
Story: He sent a beloved student ahead to find a residence and necessities, noting he had no acquaintances in Charal. The famine of the period during his Russian exile forced him to consider moving to find a place where prices were not so high.
Tags: chafetz chaim, charal, famine, russia, madeyevski

Title: Tomchei Tmimim opens a branch in Charol
Summary: After Pesach 5679 the Kremenchug branch of Tomchei Tmimim sent a contingent of its shiurim students to establish a class in the town of Charol.
Story: The author traveled to Charol ahead of the move to arrange housing for the students and confer with the local rabbinate. He stayed with R' Shmuel Gurary, the town's dayan, while R' Moshe Madayevsky served as rav. The move was driven by the worsening shortages and disorder around Kremenchug.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, charol, kremenchug, shmuel gurary dayan, moshe madayevsky

Title: Haidamak pogroms reach Zhivotov
Summary: At the start of summer 1919 Haidamak pogromist bands arrived in Zhivotov, beginning a long campaign of robbery, forced labor, and murder.
Story: Petliura and Denikin forces were fighting their civil war across Ukraine, and successive bands of pogromists — including those of Tyutyunyk and Sokolov — passed through the area. They imposed taxes on the Jewish community, conscripted men like Ephraim Shmuel to dig defensive trenches, and increasingly turned to murder. Local Ukrainian peasants joined the violence as the months wore on.
Tags: pogrom, haidamaks, ukraine, zhivotov, civil war, petliura, denikin

Title: Author's tenaim signed on 16 Tammuz 5679 in Zhuravichi
Summary: On the night of 16 Tammuz 5679 the author's engagement to the daughter of R' Yehoshua Heshel Levin was finalized in Zhuravichi.
Story: The father-in-law-to-be traveled to the author's parents in Zhuravichi for Shabbat 14 Tammuz, and the kishrei hatena'im were arranged after Shabbat. The kallah was not present, remaining in Gomel; a dowry of ten thousand rubles was committed, though the currency was already badly devalued by the upheaval.
Tags: tenaim, engagement, zhuravichi, yehoshua heshel levin, gomel

Title: Death of R' Shilem Kuratin
Summary: R' Shilem Kuratin, mashgiach for chassidut, passed away in Kremenchug on 5 Elul 5679.
Story: R' Shilem Kuratin, mashgiach for chassidut studies at Tomchei Tmimim from winter 5672, continued in his post when the yeshiva moved to Kremenchug. He passed away on 5 Elul 5679 (1919) in Kremenchug at a relatively young age. The Rebbe Rashab was not told of his passing. R' Alter Simchowitz was later appointed in his place.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, kuratin, kremenchug, mashgiach

Title: Rebbe Rashab distributes banknotes on Sukkot 5680
Summary: Rebbe Rashab gave out banknotes as gifts and segulot during Sukkot 5680, his final Sukkot.
Story: On Sukkot of 5680, Rebbe Sholom DovBer of Lubavitch distributed banknotes either as gifts or as a segulah (spiritual remedy). The dates were inscribed in the margins by his secretary, Rabbi Elchonon Dov Marozov. This was the Rebbe Rashab's final Sukkot before his passing on 2 Nissan 5680.
Tags: rashab, sukkot, segulah, banknote, russia

Title: Death of R' Asher Grossman of Nikolayev
Summary: R' Asher Grossman, longtime shochet of Nikolayev and editor of Tanya, passed away on 15 Marcheshvan 5680.
Story: R' Asher Grossman, shochet of Nikolayev and one of the leading chassidim of Rashab and Maharash, passed away on 15 Marcheshvan 5680. He had served as shochet of Nikolayev until at least 5678 and edited Rashab's corrected Tanya edition. Before his death he left dowry funds with Rashab for his still-unmarried daughter Chaya Frieda, which transferred to Rayatz after Rashab's passing months later.
Tags: nikolayev, r-asher-grossman, tanya-editor, passing

Title: Yahrzeit of Rebbetzin Yocheved bat Leah
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz's mother-in-law, Rebbetzin Yocheved bat Leah, passed away on 16 Marcheshvan 5680.
Story: The 5705 diary records that 16 Marcheshvan was the yahrzeit of the Rebbe Rayatz's mother-in-law, Rebbetzin Yocheved bat Leah, who passed away on 16 Marcheshvan 5680 (9 November 1919). The Rebbe marked the day by preparing a Yiddish maamar on 'Hayta li dim'ati' for the Kriah V'Kedushah journal.
Tags: yahrzeit, mother-in-law, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rashab gives Mazal Tov gift on 19 Kislev 5680
Summary: On the Chag HaGeulah of 19 Kislev 5680, Rebbe Rashab distributed a banknote inscribed with a Mazal Tov blessing.
Story: On 19 Kislev 5680, the festival commemorating the Alter Rebbe's liberation, Rebbe Sholom DovBer of Lubavitch presented a banknote bearing the inscription 'Mazal Tov, 19 Kislev 5680' to a chassid. The annotation in the margin was recorded by his secretary, Rabbi Elchonon Dov Marozov. This was one of the final such gifts of the Rebbe Rashab's life, given mere months before his passing.
Tags: rashab, 19-kislev, chag-hageulah, russia

Title: Decision to transfer Schneersohn library to Rumyantsev Museum
Summary: On 16 December 1919, Soviet authorities ruled regarding the disposition of the Schneersohn library that would lead to its transfer to the Rumyantsev Museum.
Story: This was one of two key decisions cited by the Soviet Scientific Council, the other being 21 May 1921, that resulted in the library being given by Narkompros to the Rumyantsev Museum, later renamed the Russian State Library named after Lenin.
Tags: soviet, library, frierdiker rebbe, rumyantsev museum, narkompros, nationalization

Title: Author's wedding on 8th day of Chanukah 5680 in Belitsa
Summary: On the eighth day of Chanukah 5680 the author married in Belitsa near Gomel, amid acute famine and political collapse.
Story: The original tenaim date had been advanced once his future brother-in-law saw the father-in-law's failing health and the spreading famine. The author's mother brought three or four pounds of meat, an uncle obtained a small amount of wheat flour for challos, and a brother-in-law procured a pound of sugar. About ten chassidim joined for sheva brachos on Shabbat, where the author began to chazer a maamer but stopped midway, overwhelmed by the surrounding conditions.
Tags: wedding, belitsa, gomel, famine, russian civil war, chanukah

Title: Defiant Purim farbrengen in Rostov under Bolshevik police visit
Summary: The Rashab led a 12-hour Purim celebration that continued despite a curfew and visits from Bolshevik police officers.
Story: Despite government bans on meetings and a 9 p.m. curfew, the Rashab encouraged singing and sent for additional liquor. When three police officers entered during a maamar, the Rashab declared 'We have to say chasidut, and they will be batul' and continued teaching about evil as a false reality. The officers gazed silently and left. The farbrengen lasted until morning light.
Tags: rashab, purim, rostov, bolsheviks, farbrengen

Title: Final volume of Rebbe Rashab's discourses
Summary: Rebbe Rashab's last year of recorded discourses is 5680.
Story: A volume of Rebbe Rashab's discourses from 1920—his final year—is preserved in the archive. It marks the close of nearly four decades of teaching.
Tags: rebbe rashab, drushim, rostov

Title: Founding of Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek in Jerusalem
Summary: Kolel Chabad founded Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek in the Chabad synagogue of the Old City of Jerusalem in 5680, soon after WWI ended.
Story: Following WWI, the managers of Kolel Chabad established Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek in the Chabad synagogue in Jerusalem's Old City in 5680, with Yeshivat Midrash Shmuel founded subsequently. By this period most of the Chabad community had relocated to the New City and prayed primarily at the 'Ohel Yitzchak' synagogue. R' Avraham Zalman remained living inside the Old City synagogue throughout the war years.
Tags: tzemach tzedek yeshiva, jerusalem, kolel chabad, old city

Title: Massacre at Tetiev synagogue burning
Summary: In winter 1920 the Jews of nearby Tetiev (Titov) were gathered into their synagogue and burned alive by pogromists, reducing the community of 8,000 to under 2,000.
Story: While fleeing Zhivotov through the fields, the Levin family watched a column of smoke rising from Tetiev in the distance. They later learned that pogromists had locked the Jews of Tetiev inside the synagogue and set it on fire. Tetiev was a deeply religious Chernobyl chassidic town of about 8,000 souls; fewer than 2,000 survived, most of them young orphans.
Tags: pogrom, tetiev, titov, ukraine, synagogue, massacre

Title: Mufti of Jerusalem organizes Balfour-protest riots
Summary: Mohammed Amin al-Husseini organized Palestine riots to protest the Balfour Declaration.
Story: Al-Husseini, later appointed mufti of Jerusalem by the British Mandate, would go on to instigate the 1929 Hebron massacre and lead the 1936 Arab Revolt. During World War II he traveled to Berlin, where he met with Hitler and other top German officials and encouraged the Holocaust.
Tags: mufti, husseini, palestine, balfour-declaration, arab-riots

Title: Passing of Rebbe Rashab in Rostov
Summary: In 5680 (1920) the Rebbe Rashab passed away in Rostov-on-Don, far from his original home in Lubavitch.
Story: Displaced by the war and unable to return to Lubavitch, the Rashab eventually settled in Rostov, where he passed away in 1920. His son and successor, the Rebbe Rayatz, would lead Chabad through Soviet repression. The Rashab's resting place in Rostov became an important pilgrimage site.
Tags: rashab, rostov, russia, passing

Title: Passing of the Rashab in Rostov
Summary: The Rashab passed away in Rostov in 1920.
Story: His passing in Soviet Rostov launched the succession of his son, the Rayatz, as sixth Rebbe. The Rashab left explicit instructions for the succession, easing what could have been a fraught transition.
Tags: rashab, rostov, russia

Title: Passing of the Rebbe Rashab in Rostov
Summary: Rabbi Shalom Dovber Schneersohn, the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe, passed away in Rostov after a brief illness.
Story: Two weeks after the Purim farbrengen, the Rashab fell ill on a Friday and was diagnosed with typhoid. On the following Shabbat night, after blessing each of his granddaughters and the Rayatz, he whispered the words 'bekhol levavkha uvekhol nafshekha' of Shema and his soul ascended, thrusting the Rayatz into the leadership of Chabad.
Tags: rashab, rostov, typhoid, rayatz, leadership succession

Title: Passing of the Rebbe Rashab in Rostov-on-Don
Summary: Two weeks after Purim, the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe passed away from typhoid after blessing his children and reciting Shema.
Story: Diagnosed with typhoid on Sunday after a Friday onset of illness, the Rashab's condition deteriorated through the week. Late at night he asked to be moved to his study, telling Chasidim 'I am going to heaven, and I am leaving you my manuscripts.' After blessing each of his daughters and his son, he passed at dawn while whispering 'with all your heart and all your soul' from the Shema.
Tags: rashab, rostov, passing, rayatz, leadership transition

Title: Pogromist Sokolov extorts Zhivotov, kills ten
Summary: The pogromist Sokolov entered Zhivotov in late winter 1920, demanded tribute, and had ten Jews killed including the rabbi's wife.
Story: When Sokolov's band approached Zhivotov, the town's elders went out to greet him with bread, water, and a Torah scroll, begging him to restrain his men. He agreed but said ten Jews would die regardless. Among the dead was the wife of the town's rabbi, Reb Chaim. The town considered itself spared compared to neighboring Tetiev.
Tags: pogrom, sokolov, zhivotov, ukraine

Title: Polish-Bolshevik war reaches Lipovets
Summary: In summer 1920 Polish troops occupied Lipovets, demanding flour and lodging from Jewish residents before being driven out by the advancing Soviet army.
Story: Unlike the pogromists, the Polish soldiers did not murder, but they demanded that locals bake bread for them and house their men. The Levin family hosted a Polish soldier and baked from flour the army provided. Soviet forces eventually captured the Poles or drove them back, and Lipovets quieted from major fighting.
Tags: polish-soviet war, lipovets, ukraine

Title: R' Alter Simchowitz sent to direct Tomchei Tmimim branch in Shchedrin
Summary: In the summer of 5680 the Rebbe Rashab sent R' Alter Simchowitz to direct the Shchedrin branch of Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: The Rashab arranged for Simchowitz to travel from Lubavitch to Shchedrin with full instructions and orientation. The branch operated until 5678 when the yeshiva and its branches were relocated to Kremenchug, after which Simchowitz served there as supervisor of chassidus studies.
Tags: shchedrin, russia, tomchei tmimim, alter simchowitz, rashab

Title: R. David Stockhamer arrives in United States
Summary: R. David Stockhamer arrived in the US with his wife and three daughters around 5680.
Story: Around 5680 (1919-1920), the chassid R. David Stockhamer arrived in the United States with his wife and three daughters and settled in Newark, New Jersey. He later became distressed at the lack of suitable chassidic young men for his daughters in America, leading him to consult the Rebbe Rayatz.
Tags: david stockhamer, newark, new jersey, immigration, chassidim

Title: Rabbi Mordechai Dubin establishes Derech Eretz School in Riga
Summary: Latvian parliamentarian Rabbi Mordechai Dubin founds the Derech Eretz School, an Orthodox school teaching both religious and secular subjects.
Story: The school laid the foundation for educational change in Riga. Its founding dean was an eighteen-year-old Rabbi Chaim Mordechai Aizek Hodakov. The opportunity to fulfill the Rebbe's later mission of transforming Jewish education in Latvia came in 1934, when Hodakov was appointed chief inspector of all Jewish schools.
Tags: dubin, derech eretz, riga, latvia, torah im derech eretz

Title: Rashab buried in Rostov Jewish cemetery
Summary: Rabbi Sholom DovBer Schneersohn, the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe, was buried in Rostov hours after his Saturday night passing.
Story: The casket was carried to the cemetery by yeshivah students and elders of anash, with the whole Jewish community of the city present. Standing at his father's fresh grave, the Rayatz publicly appointed three rabbis as a beit din and declared he was purchasing the plot conditionally, reserving the right to later reinter the Rashab in the ancestral burial ground in Lubavitch. The German invasion and the revolution had prevented the return to Lubavitch.
Tags: rashab, rostov, funeral, russia, rayatz

Title: Rashab's final Purim farbrengen in Rostov
Summary: Defying Bolshevik curfew, the Rashab led a twelve-hour Purim farbrengen as police looked on without intervening.
Story: At the 1920 Purim celebration in Rostov, the Rashab insisted on a full farbrengen despite the 9 p.m. curfew. When Bolshevik officers entered the room, the Rashab continued teaching a maamar on evil as a false reality. The officers stood silently and then departed, and the farbrengen continued until morning light.
Tags: purim, rostov, rashab, farbrengen, bolshevik police

Title: Rayatz accepts position of sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe
Summary: Following the passing of his father, the Rashab, in Rostov, Yosef Yitzchak accepted the role of sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe.
Story: The Rashab left explicit instructions that his son succeed him, easing the succession. The Rayatz took on leadership during one of the most perilous periods in Russian Jewish history, as Bolshevik anti-religious campaigns intensified.
Tags: rostov, rashab, succession, russia

Title: Rayatz delivers first maamar to Rivkin at end of shivah
Summary: The Rayatz privately recited a chasidic discourse to Berel Rivkin in his father's Rostov study at the close of the shivah.
Story: On the Shabbat that ended his week of mourning for his father, the Rayatz invited Berel Rivkin into the Rashab's study and recited a maamar his father had said on Purim, adding insights of his own. He asked Rivkin to keep it private, but news of the discourse soon spread among the Chasidim. It was his first step toward accepting the position of sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe.
Tags: rayatz, rostov, maamar, succession

Title: Rayatz organizes Rashab's manuscripts during the year of aveilus
Summary: Throughout the mourning year 5680-5681, the Rebbe Rayatz organizes Rashab's manuscripts and prepares detailed indexes.
Story: Rayatz arranged the maamarim chronologically, one binder per year, adding a handwritten label to each binder and compiling a detailed index of openings. These bound binders are now numbered 2541-2585 in the Library archive. He likewise organized Rashab's letters, and on 19 Marcheshvan 5681 recorded in his diary the count of maamarim and letters then in his possession.
Tags: manuscripts, rayatz, rashab, ksav-yad, cataloging

Title: Rayatz recites maamar publicly on first day of Passover
Summary: After a private recitation arranged with Rivkin, Chasidim listened from outside the door as the Rayatz delivered a maamar for nearly an hour on Passover.
Story: On the first day of Passover, the Rayatz again told Rivkin he wished to recite a maamar privately. Rivkin arranged for Chasidim to gather outside the door of the Rashab's study; they cracked open the doors and listened. A week later, at the end of Passover, the Chasidim entered the room itself while he spoke.
Tags: rayatz, rostov, passover, maamar

Title: Rayatz's Rostov arrest by Yevsektzia
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was arrested in Rostov following accusations from the Yevsektzia, the Jewish section of the Communist Party.
Story: In 1920, in Rostov, Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was arrested after the Yevsektzia, the Jewish section of the Communist Party, leveled accusations against him. The Yevsektzia became a primary opponent of religious Jewish life in the early Soviet period, targeting Chabad activities. This marked the sixth of his seven arrests and his first under Communism.
Tags: rostov, russia, arrest, yevsektzia, communism, yosef yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Rebbe Rashab passes away in Rostov
Summary: Rabbi Sholom DovBer Schneersohn, the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe, passes away, leaving leadership to his son.
Story: His passing forced his son Yosef Yitzchak to begin again from scratch — the first of three such restarts in his life. Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim, which the Rashab had founded in 1897, became a key inheritance.
Tags: rashab, rostov, passing

Title: Rebbe Rayatz assumes leadership of Chabad
Summary: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn assumed the position of sixth Rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz took over leadership after the passing of his father, the Rebbe Rashab. He would not wear the traditional shtreimel again until his daughter Chaya Mushka's wedding in 1928, a symbolic gesture marking a new era of Chabad.
Tags: succession, leadership

Title: Rebbe Rayatz draws the Menorah of Chassidus
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz drew a seven-branched menorah summarizing the seven generations of Chassidic leadership from the Baal Shem Tov to his father.
Story: During his year of mourning, Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak drew a seven-branched Menorah of Chassidus for himself, each branch dedicated to one of the founders of Chassidus and the Rebbeim of Chabad across the seven generations. Each Rebbe was inscribed with his name, years of leadership, yahrtzeit, and in some cases burial location. The drawing was framed by verses about the seven lamps illuminating Israel and the soul of man standing on four pillars: love, feeling, knowledge, and faith.
Tags: rayatz, menorah, chassidus, seven-generations, baal-shem-tov

Title: Rebbe Rayatz organizes his father's manuscript archive
Summary: In 5680, after his father's passing, Rebbe Rayatz organized Rebbe Rashab's manuscripts by year and prepared comprehensive indexes for the collection.
Story: Rebbe Rayatz catalogued 1,173 maamarei Chassidus surviving in Rebbe Rashab's own handwriting and documented an estimated 700-800 additional maamarim recorded only by the chozrim. He preserved hundreds of original letters and acquired letters from their recipients, eventually amassing some 2,000 letters of his father by 1927. Twenty-five volumes of these maamarim were eventually published as Sefer HaMaamarim 5643-5680.
Tags: rayatz, rashab, manuscripts, archive, indexing

Title: Rebbe Rayatz secludes himself during mourning for his father
Summary: Following the passing of his father Rebbe Rashab, Rebbe Rayatz sat secluded in his room, alone with his Creator.
Story: After Rebbe Sholom DovBer passed away on 2 Nissan 5680, his son Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak entered a period of intense seclusion. As he later described in his letters, from the first day he felt as a man struck by thunder, finding no rest except in his thrice-daily prayers, and remaining closed in his room without speaking. This period of withdrawal and inner reckoning shaped his early nesius.
Tags: rayatz, rashab, mourning, rostov, seclusion

Title: Yeshivah relocates from Kremenchuk to Rostov
Summary: Facing starvation in Ukraine, Tomchei Temimim moved to Rostov to be near the new Rebbe.
Story: During the war the yeshivah had been transferred from Lubavitch to Kremenchuk, but with key Jewish supporters fleeing the city, students were forced to ration bread to every other day. The Rayatz declared, 'I want Tomchei Temimim to be next to me,' and within two weeks roughly eighty boys arrived, many ill and in torn clothing. Rabbi Shmuel Gurary borrowed funds and sold personal property to keep the yeshivah afloat.
Tags: tomchei temimim, rostov, kremenchuk, famine

Title: Yeshivah Tomchei Temimim relocates to Rostov
Summary: Tomchei Temimim moved from Kremenchuk in Ukraine to Rostov in the winter of 1920 amid extreme food shortages.
Story: After fleeing Lubavitch during the war, the yeshivah had landed in Kremenchuk, where students rationed bread to once every two days. The new Rebbe brought the yeshivah to Rostov, saying he wanted Tomchei Temimim next to him. Conditions remained dire, but Rabbi Shmuel Gurary borrowed funds and sold personal property to sustain it.
Tags: tomchei-temimim, rostov, kremenchuk, yeshivah, famine

Title: Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek founded in Jerusalem
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Nae founded Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek in Jerusalem for kollel avreichim to study Chassidus two hours daily.
Story: After WWI, exiles of Eretz Yisrael returned home, with Hebron's community largely resettling in Jerusalem. Upon his return from Egypt, Rabbi Menachem Mendel Nae launched the yeshiva as part of his repair work for Kollel Chabad. The yeshiva convened in the Beit Menachem Tzemach Tzedek synagogue, fulfilling the Rebbe Rashab's wish to bind kollel scholars to regular Chassidus study.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, menachem mendel nae, yeshiva tzemach tzedek, post-wwi

Title: Bolsheviks take control of Rostov
Summary: Bolshevik forces took control of Rostov in January, ending consideration of emigration from Russia for the Rebbe's household.
Story: In January 1920, the Bolsheviks consolidated control over Rostov. The new regime's arrival ended discussions in the Rashab's household about relocating outside Russia entirely. The Rashab curtailed public activities to avoid drawing the regime's attention.
Tags: rostov, bolsheviks, communism, russia

Title: Bolsheviks take control of Rostov-on-Don
Summary: The Bolsheviks took control of Rostov, prompting the Rashab to curtail his public activities.
Story: Not wanting to draw the attention of the new regime, the Rashab asked Chasidim to limit visits to him for services, maamarim, or private audiences. Only a small group joined him for services afterward. The idea of relocating out of Russia entirely had been raised earlier but faded after the Bolshevik takeover.
Tags: bolsheviks, rostov, russia, communist revolution

Title: Colel Chabad Jerusalem board pledges allegiance to Rebbe Rashab
Summary: In Tevet 5680, Colel Chabad's Jerusalem-based board officially decided to place itself under the direction of the Lubavitcher Rebbe.
Story: The decision marked a shift from the Kopust branch's sway over the organization back to the main Chabad-Lubavitch line. After the Rashab's passing, the board reaffirmed the pledge to the Rebbe Rayatz, though tensions over governance and finances persisted until the Rayatz visited in 1929.
Tags: colel-chabad, jerusalem, rashab, governance

Title: Kollel Chabad reorganized with Va'ad HaMoetza after WWI
Summary: At the end of Tevet 5680 Chabad anash in Jerusalem elected three administrators and a four-member advisory council to lead Kollel Chabad pending the Rebbe's involvement.
Story: With the Hebron Chabad community dissolved by war and Russian income cut off after the Revolution, only the local administrators remained of the old kollel structure. By secret ballot, anash chose three memunim and a four-member Va'ad HaMoetza, explicitly declaring the kollel under the patronage of the Lubavitcher Rebbe and stipulating that all decisions were temporary until contact with the Rebbe could be restored. This arrangement lasted nine years until the Rayatz formally accepted the kollel's presidency.
Tags: kollel chabad, jerusalem, post-war, rayatz, elections

Title: Post-WWI Kollel elections install three administrators and four-man council
Summary: After WWI displacement, Kollel Chabad held secret-ballot elections for three administrators and a four-man council.
Story: At the end of Tevet 5680 (Jan 1920), after most Anash had returned from wartime exile and one of the administrators (R. Mordechai Dovber Slonim) had passed away, the surviving members of Kollel Chabad held elections by secret ballot. They selected three administrators and four council members to jointly manage the kollel, explicitly declaring the kollel under the authority of the Rebbe of Lubavitch.
Tags: kollel chabad, post-war, jerusalem, wwi, elections

Title: Father-in-law R' Yehoshua Heshel Levin passes away
Summary: The author's father-in-law R' Yehoshua Heshel Levin passed away on 28 Tevet 5680.
Story: He had long suffered from a debilitating leg ailment but could no longer travel to therapeutic spas because of the civil war. After the wedding his son brought him from Gomel to Belitsa, where he was bedridden until his death several weeks later. The author was then beginning to peddle small quantities of salt and tobacco between cities to support his family.
Tags: yehoshua heshel levin, belitsa, gomel, famine

Title: Rashab summons Rayatz to discuss future under Communist rule
Summary: In a candle-lit study, the Rashab told the Rayatz that the Jewish people were entering a period of dark clouds lasting at least 22 years.
Story: On Friday 8 Adar, with Purim approaching, the Rashab summoned his son. Studying Pri Etz Chaim on Mordechai and Esther, the Rashab made extraordinary predictions about Lenin's strange death, Trotsky's exile and execution, Stalin adapting to the times, and the eventual fall of the Soviet regime. He charged the Rayatz with mesirat nefesh to spread Torah, which proved prophetic when the Rayatz's father passed weeks later.
Tags: rashab, rayatz, rostov, purim, soviet predictions, mesirat nefesh

Title: Rashab's prophetic Purim-eve conversation with the Rayatz
Summary: In a candlelit study, the Rashab entrusted the Rayatz with combatting Soviet anti-religious oppression at the cost of self-sacrifice.
Story: On 8 Adar 5680 (February 27, 1920), the Rashab summoned the Rayatz into his candlelit study. He foretold at least twenty-two years of dark clouds for Russian Jewry, predicted the eventual fall of the Soviet regime and specific fates for Lenin, Trotsky, and Stalin, and charged his son with self-sacrifice to defend Torah and Judaism.
Tags: rashab, rayatz, rostov, communism, prophecy, mesirat nefesh

Title: Levin family flees Zhivotov for Lipovets
Summary: After Purim 5680 the Levin family hired a wagon and fled Zhivotov for Lipovets, arriving just before Pesach.
Story: The roads were thick with mud, forcing the family to repeatedly dismount and help push the wagon. They traveled several days, sleeping at the wagon-driver's village home along the way. All six members of the family arrived safely in Lipovets days before Passover 1920, where Rabbi Shlomo Sternberg and shochet Reb Levi helped them settle.
Tags: zhivotov, lipovets, ukraine, pogrom, flight

Title: Passing of Rebbe Rashab in Rostov
Summary: Rabbi Shalom Dovber Schneersohn, the Rashab, passed away on 2 Nisan 5680 in Rostov-on-Don and is buried there.
Story: He had been forced from Lubavitch four and a half years earlier by the German advance in World War One. His passing in Rostov marked the definitive end of the Lubavitch era of Chabad. His son the Frierdiker Rebbe assumed the leadership under the increasingly hostile conditions of early Soviet Russia.
Tags: rashab, shalom-dovber, rostov

Title: Rebbe Rashab instructs Havlin to revive Toras Emes at first opportunity
Summary: On Purim 5680 in Rostov, the Rebbe Rashab directed R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin to return to the Holy Land and refound the Toras Emes yeshiva at the first possible opportunity.
Story: Before his passing, the Rebbe Rashab spoke with R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin on Purim 5680 in Rostov, instructing him that as soon as travel became possible he must return to the Land of Israel — without regard to obstacles — to resume directing Yeshiva Toras Emes as before. The instruction is preserved in a 5684 letter of the Rebbe Rayatz (Igros Kodesh vol. 1, no. 134).
Tags: rashab, havlin, toras emes, rostov, purim

Title: Pavel Papov reports on the Schneersohn book collection in Moscow
Summary: On March 1, 1920, Pavel Papov files a report on the Schneersohn collection stored at the Kokorev warehouses in Moscow.
Story: Papov reports that the Schneersohn crates are intact except for one damaged by customs officials, that each crate weighs roughly 15 pud, and that at least 12 wagons would be needed to move the collection. The books are on the third floor accessible only by a manual hoist, and lacking funds to operate it, Papov seals the rooms. The report sets the stage for transfer of the collection from the nationalized Kokorev warehouses to the Rumyantsev Library (later the Lenin Library).
Tags: library, moscow, kokorev-warehouses, soviet, rumyantsev-library, russia

Title: Histalkus of Rashab in Rostov
Summary: Rashab passed away in Rostov on 2 Nissan 5680.
Story: On 2 Nissan 5680, Rebbe Shalom DovBer Schneersohn passed away in Rostov-on-Don. His passing transferred leadership of Chabad to his only son, Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn (Rayatz). At the time of his passing, Rashab held funds entrusted by R' Asher of Nikolayev for his unmarried daughter's dowry.
Tags: rashab, rostov, passing

Title: Passing of R' Moshe Rosenblum in Rostov
Summary: The scribe and chassid R' Moshe Rosenblum, who departed Lubavitch with the Rebbe, passed away on 2 Nisan 5680 in Rostov.
Story: R' Moshe Rosenblum, a distinguished sofer and yerei shamayim, accompanied the Rashab's exile from Lubavitch in 5676. As they left the town he expressed hope to be reunited soon, and the Rebbe replied that he hoped it would be by Pesach. In the event Rosenblum remained in Rostov and died there on 2 Nisan 5680.
Tags: rostov, moshe rosenblum, sofer, petira

Title: Passing of Rebbe Rashab in Rostov
Summary: On Motzaei Shabbos Vayikra, the night of 2 Nissan 5680 at 3:30 AM, the Rebbe Rashab passed away in Rostov.
Story: After years of organizing his father's manuscripts during the civil war, the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe — Sholom Dovber Schneersohn — passed away in the early hours of 2 Nissan 5680 (March 21, 1920) and was buried in Rostov-on-Don. His son and successor, the Rebbe Rayatz, assumed the leadership of Chabad.
Tags: rostov, rashab, yahrzeit, passing, nissan

Title: Passing of the Rebbe Rashab on 2 Nissan 5680
Summary: Rabbi Sholom DovBer Schneersohn, the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe, passed away on 2 Nissan 5680 in Rostov.
Story: The news reached the author in Gomel only on Erev Shabbat Parshat Shemini, when R' Akiva Trachtenberg told him at a cobbler's shop and he returned home weeping. That Shabbat the Gomel chassidim gathered at the Lubavitch shul for Mincha, where elders including R' Shlomo, R' Moshe and R' Shneur Zalman Tomarkin and R' Aharon Eliezer Zeitlin declared the Rebbe Rayatz as successor, danced together, and resolved to write a collective letter of hiskashrus.
Tags: rashab, rostov, histalkus, hiskashrus, rayatz, gomel, tomarkin, shneur zalman schneersohn

Title: Rebbe Rashab passes away in Rostov
Summary: The Rebbe Rashab passed away in Rostov on the night of 2 Nissan 5680.
Story: On Motzaei Shabbos Vayikra, the early morning of Sunday 2 Nissan 5680 (March 21, 1920) at 3:30 AM, the Rebbe Rashab passed away in Rostov-on-Don. In his final years he had occupied himself extensively with arranging the manuscript collection of his ancestors. Shortly before his passing he told the surrounding chassidim 'I am going to heaven, the writings I leave to you.'
Tags: rostov, passing, rebbe rashab, yahrzeit

Title: Rebbe Rashab's passing on 2 Nissan 5680
Summary: Rabbi Sholom Dovber Schneersohn, the Rebbe Rashab, passed away on 2 Nissan 5680.
Story: Rabbi Sholom Dovber Schneersohn, the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe known as the Rebbe Rashab, passed away on 2 Nissan 5680 (March 21, 1920). His son, the Rebbe Rayatz, subsequently recorded a chart of all the Chabad Rebbeim's lifespans and resting places. He had marked the place where he had stopped learning in a sefer some ten days before his passing.
Tags: rebbe rashab, yahrzeit, rostov

Title: Rayatz arrested at synagogue in Rostov
Summary: Three Cheka officers entered the synagogue and escorted the Rebbe, still in mourning for his father, to a police interrogation.
Story: Brought before fifteen armed officers around a long table, the Rebbe was interrogated about Judaism and Kabbalah. When one officer threatened him with a pistol, the Rebbe replied that he had one G-d and two worlds, while they had one world and many gods. The Cheka eventually issued his release on August 8, 1921.
Tags: cheka, rostov, interrogation, rayatz

Title: Rayatz arrested by Cheka during morning prayers
Summary: Three Cheka officers brought the Rayatz from the Rostov synagogue to a police station for interrogation about Judaism and Kabbalah.
Story: During the year of mourning for his father, the Rayatz was confronted by three armed officers, two of them Jewish Yevsektzia members, who demanded he remove his tallit and tefillin and come with them. At the police station, fifteen armed officers sat around a conference table to intimidate him. When one threatened with his gun, the Rayatz replied that 'this toy' impresses only those with no faith — 'we have one G-d and two worlds.'
Tags: rayatz, cheka, yevsektzia, rostov, interrogation

Title: Yiddishes Tageblatt predicts end of Chabad
Summary: Jonathan Mark's New York Yiddish newspaper wrote that the Rashab left no fitting successor in his son.
Story: Following the Rashab's passing, Jewish newspapers worldwide predicted the end of Chabad. In the Yiddishes Tageblatt, Jonathan Mark opined that the Rashab's son lacked the aptitude to follow in his place. Seven years later, Mark reversed course and praised the new Rebbe in his book Gedolim Fun Unzer Tzeit.
Tags: obituary, rashab, rayatz, new york, jonathan mark

Title: Levin parents recover from typhus
Summary: Late in summer 1920 Ephraim Shmuel and Leah Beila contracted typhus along with all their children; only eight-year-old Yisrael Yehuda remained well, and the family recovered by Tishrei 5681.
Story: With both parents and siblings bedridden, the young Yisrael Yehuda was the family's only able body, though he was too small to help much. The parents nevertheless fasted on Yom Kippur despite their weakness. By the end of the High Holidays the family had recovered completely.
Tags: typhus, illness, lipovets, yom kippur

Title: R' Asher Yechezkel Horowitz dies in Tzfat
Summary: R' Asher Yechezkel Horowitz, head of the Tzfat Chabad community and kollel administrator, died on 24 Elul 5680.
Story: R' Asher Yechezkel had led the renewed Tzfat Chabad community for decades and managed the Kollel Chabad distribution in Tzfat. After his death, his son R' Yeshaya succeeded him in administering the kollel's affairs in the city.
Tags: tzfat, kollel chabad, horowitz family

Title: Ephraim Shmuel opens large cheder in Lipovets
Summary: After Simchas Torah 5681 the family moved into a three-room apartment in Lipovets and Ephraim Shmuel opened what became the town's largest cheder.
Story: The new apartment was rented from the widow of the melamed Reb Gedalyahu Shmuel. Ephraim Shmuel taught Chumash with Rashi to a large group of children, and Leah Beila assisted by teaching them Hebrew writing and arithmetic. This was the largest cheder in Lipovets.
Tags: lipovets, cheder, ukraine

Title: Rayatz records inventory of manuscripts in his diary
Summary: On 19 Marcheshvan 5681, Rayatz records in his diary the count of maamarim and letters from his father that are in his possession.
Story: Following his year-long project of cataloging Rashab's manuscript output, Rayatz committed the inventory totals to writing in his personal diary. This count became one of the reference points for tracking what manuscripts existed in the Rebbe's collection at that moment in the early Soviet period.
Tags: manuscripts, rayatz, diary, ksav-yad, inventory

Title: Rebbe Rayatz compiles inventory of his father's manuscripts
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz compiled a detailed list of the maamarim, chozrim, and letters left by his father Rebbe Rashab.
Story: On 19 Mar-Cheshvan 5681, during his year of mourning for his father, Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak compiled a detailed catalogue of every Chassidic maamar that remained in his father Rebbe Rashab's own handwriting. He also recorded the names of the chozrim who transmitted maamarim delivered orally, and summarized the collection of letters left behind. The list was later printed at the end of Kuntres Chanoch LaNaar.
Tags: rayatz, rashab, manuscripts, chassidus, chozrim

Title: Bolsheviks requisition rooms in the Rashab's Rostov home
Summary: In the week before 3 Kislev 5681, Soviet authorities seized rooms in the Rebbe's house.
Story: Writing on the eve of 3 Kislev 5681, the Rashab reported that the previous week a 'rekvizitsia' had been carried out on his home — the two upper and lower wings, plus the room beside his hall and the corner room facing his bedroom. With great effort he managed to retain his own room, but his son's household lost their granddaughter Chana's room. 'We are now surrounded by neighbors,' he wrote; intervention had been useless.
Tags: rashab, rostov, communists, rekvizitsia, nationalization

Title: Rayatz falls ill from typhus in Rostov
Summary: On 28 Marcheshvan, the Rayatz became too ill to lead evening services as the typhus epidemic intensified in Rostov.
Story: The typhus epidemic struck the Rebbe's household; soon his mother Rebbetzin Shterna Sara and his three daughters also caught the disease. Doctors said his survival was unlikely. A rabbinical court convened and students pledged years of their own lives for the Rebbe's recovery.
Tags: rayatz, rostov, typhus, illness

Title: Rayatz falls ill with typhus in Rostov
Summary: The Rayatz became too weak to lead evening services as the typhus epidemic struck his household.
Story: On the night of 28 Marcheshvan 5681, the Rebbe could no longer lead services. In the following days his mother Rebbetzin Shterna Sara and his three daughters also fell ill. Doctors gave him little chance of surviving, with Professor Milsalavski telling Goldin that medically there was no cure.
Tags: typhus, rostov, rayatz, epidemic

Title: Rayatz says maamar despite illness on Shabbat Toldot
Summary: On Shabbat Parshat Toldot, between bouts of typhus, the Rayatz mustered strength to deliver a maamar.
Story: Shortly after first falling ill, the Rebbe had enough strength to say a maamar on Shabbat Toldot. The illness then intensified, and his situation became grave; Professor Milsalavski said there was no medical cure, but believed the Rebbe might recover.
Tags: rayatz, rostov, typhus, maamar

Title: Birth of the author's daughter Sarah on 19 Kislev 5681
Summary: The author's eldest daughter Sarah was born on 19 Kislev 5681 in Gomel.
Story: She arrived during the height of the post-civil-war famine, as Ukrainian refugees lay swollen with hunger in the streets and Jews in Gomel were reduced to eating bran, oil-seed residue, and potato peels. The rabbinate permitted kitniyos that Pesach because of the shortages, and the family relied on supplies the author hauled back and forth from the village of Zhuravichi.
Tags: birth, yud tes kislev, gomel, sarah, famine

Title: Rayatz begins recovery from typhus
Summary: After roughly three weeks of grave illness, the Rebbe's condition began to improve on 19 Kislev.
Story: Chasidim led by Reb Itche der Masmid prayed repeatedly at the Ohel of the Rashab, and Goldin telegrammed Chasidim in Lubavitch, Nizhyn, and Hadyach to pray at the graves of earlier Rebbes. The improvement coincided with 19 Kislev, the chasidic festival marking the Alter Rebbe's release from czarist prison in 1798.
Tags: rayatz, rostov, 19-kislev, typhus, recovery

Title: Rayatz begins recovery from typhus on 19 Kislev
Summary: The Rebbe's condition turned the corner on the Chasidic festival commemorating the Alter Rebbe's release from czarist prison.
Story: After about three weeks of grave illness, the tide turned on 19 Kislev — the day marking Rabbi Schneur Zalman's 1798 release from prison and regarded as the New Year of Chabad Chasidism. Yeshivah students had been praying at the Rashab's ohel led by Reb Itche der Masmid, and a rabbinical court collected written pledges from students donating years of their lives, reportedly totaling thirty years.
Tags: typhus, 19 kislev, recovery, rostov

Title: Anti-religious Chanukah parade mocks Avraham Hanoch's cheder in Lipovets
Summary: On Chanukah 5681, Soviet activists led a public parade through Lipovets caricaturing the author's father teaching Torah and ridiculing Chanukah lights and his cheder.
