Story: Yevsektsiya operatives marched students and elders wearing red ties through the streets in an anti-Jewish demonstration, drawing cartoons of the father instructing his pupils and mocking the family cheder. The author's family experienced for the first time a threat aimed not only at their bodies but at their souls. The mother responded that being publicly linked with G-d and Torah was a great merit.
Tags: lipovets, ussr, yevsektsiya, chanukah, anti-religious-campaign, ukraine

Title: Chabad yeshivah opens in Warsaw with twelve students
Summary: While the Rebbe is still in Rostov, a Chabad yeshivah opens in Warsaw with twelve students on the first yahrzeit of the Rebbe Rashab.
Story: The Rebbe referred to this time as 'days of light and days of joy,' even as the yeshivah in Rostov was being forcibly closed and the Chabad educational network in Russia went underground. He appointed a board of five members, instructing them to 'focus on discussions of ethical behavior, instilling a G-d-fearing spirit, and acquiring good character traits.' By 1928 the yeshivah had grown to 250 students.
Tags: warsaw, poland, tomchei temimim, rashab, yahrzeit

Title: Chafetz Chaim decides to leave Russia and return to Radin
Summary: In Adar 5681, the Chafetz Chaim left Snovsk to return to Radin after Soviet authorities forced public Sabbath desecration on the whole town including his yeshiva students.
Story: He wrote that the authorities imposed labor on the entire city on weekdays and Shabbat, including yeshiva students from the beis medrash whom he could not save. He concluded one must leave a place where God's name is publicly desecrated, even considering travel to Eretz Yisrael via Odessa, though he first returned to Radin.
Tags: chafetz chaim, snovsk, radin, soviet, religious persecution, yeshiva

Title: City of Dvinsk renamed Daugavpils
Summary: Dvinsk received its current Latvian name, Daugavpils, in 5681 (1921).
Story: After Latvia gained independence, the city known as Dvinsk under Russian rule was officially renamed Daugavpils in 5681 (1921). This was the third name for the city, following Dinaburg and Dvinsk. It remains the country's second-largest city.
Tags: latvia, dvinsk, daugavpils, naming

Title: Court of the Rebbes in Lubavitch burned to the ground
Summary: In 5681 (1921) the entire courtyard complex of the Rebbes in the town of Lubavitch was destroyed by fire.
Story: After WWI and the upheavals of the Russian Revolution, the historic court of the Chabad Rebbes in Lubavitch was consumed by fire in 1921. The buildings that had served as the seat of the dynasty for over a century were lost. The town ceased to function as a Chabad center from this point onward.
Tags: lubavitch, fire, destruction

Title: Death of R' Yaakov Boruch Krasik
Summary: R' Yaakov Boruch Krasik, mashgiach of Tomchei Tmimim, passed away in Kremenchug in 5681.
Story: R' Yaakov Boruch Krasik, who served as mashgiach over nigleh in Tomchei Tmimim throughout its years in Lubavitch and continued in Kremenchug after the move in 5678, passed away in Kremenchug in 5681 (1921). His brother R' Eliezer Krasik later wrote a memoir about him in Bitaon Chabad.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, krasik, kremenchug, mashgiach

Title: Eidah HaChareidis formally established
Summary: Rabbi Sonnenfeld formalized the traditional Orthodox Chareidi community in Jerusalem.
Story: The Eidah HaChareidis emerged as a counterweight to Zionist and Reform-influenced communal structures. It continues to exist today as a distinct traditional Orthodox community.
Tags: sonnenfeld, jerusalem, eidah-hachareidis, orthodox

Title: Fire destroys the houses of the Lubavitch courtyard
Summary: At the beginning of Nissan 5681, fire consumed all the houses in the courtyard of the Rebbes in Lubavitch within half an hour.
Story: At the beginning of Nissan 5681 (1921), one year after the passing of the Rebbe Rashab, a fire from heaven destroyed all the houses in the courtyard of the Rebbes in Lubavitch within half an hour. Whatever was stored in the cellars was looted and broken by non-Jews. The physical heart of Chabad's home town was effectively erased.
Tags: lubavitch, fire, courtyard, russia

Title: Marriage of R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky to Chaya Frieda Grossman
Summary: R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky married Chaya Frieda Grossman in 5681 after consulting Rayatz and visiting the Ohel.
Story: In 5681, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky (born Mogilev 5657, studied in Lubavitch 5671-5677) married Chaya Frieda Grossman, youngest daughter of R' Asher of Nikolayev. He inquired about the shidduch from Rayatz, who instructed him to travel to the Ohel to ask Rashab. After the wedding, he received the dowry funds R' Asher had entrusted before his death.
Tags: kazarnovsky, grossman-family, marriage, rayatz

Title: MKva restoration funds sent to Lubavitch
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz sent funds to Lubavitch for the restoration of the destroyed mikvah.
Story: At the start of 5682 (1921), after the mikvah building in Lubavitch had been destroyed in the fire, the Rebbe Rayatz sent the remaining community a sum of money for its restoration. At that time several chassidim still lived in Lubavitch and had moved the synagogue to the brick house.
Tags: lubavitch, mikvah, restoration

Title: Narkompros authorizes return of Schneersohn library (permit 670)
Summary: In winter 5681, the Soviet Narkompros education commissariat issues permit number 670 authorizing return of the Schneersohn library to its owner.
Story: Following an appeal from the Committee of Jewish Synagogues, the scientific libraries department of Narkompros formally resolved to return the books. The authorization carried the number 670, but Rayatz lacked the means to physically remove the books from storage and had nowhere to house them. The crates remained in Moscow and the original permit document was subsequently lost, becoming the centerpiece of a multi-year struggle as later officials disclaimed knowledge of it.
Tags: library, soviet, narkompros, moscow, russia, permits

Title: R. Boruch Ber moves yeshivah to Vilna
Summary: Rabbi Baruch Ber Leibowitz relocated his Slabodka yeshivah to Vilna.
Story: In 1921, Rabbi Baruch Ber Leibowitz moved Knesses Beis Yitzchak from Slabodka to Vilna. He would later move it again to Kamenitz in 1926, where it became one of the great Lithuanian yeshivas of the interwar period.
Tags: baruch ber leibowitz, vilna, knesses beis yitzchak, lithuania

Title: Rabbi Avraham Chaim Nae returns to Jerusalem to rebuild Yeshivat Torat Emet
Summary: Returning to Jerusalem, R. Avraham Chaim Nae took the initiative to reestablish Yeshivat Torat Emet there.
Story: Rabbi Avraham Chaim Nae joined SiLA and R. Moshe Aryeh Leib Shapira to issue a public appeal to revive the yeshiva originally established by the Rebbe Rashab in Hebron. Rabbi Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov, who had returned from his wartime exile, was enlisted to lead the yeshiva based on the Rebbe Rashab's mandate. The appeal stressed completing what they had begun in the holy work of rebuilding Torat Emet.
Tags: jerusalem, yeshiva torat emet, avraham chaim nae, post-wwi

Title: Rayatz establishes Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim in Warsaw
Summary: The Rayatz established a branch of Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim in Warsaw and launched a program to strengthen Judaism in Soviet Russia.
Story: With the original Lubavitch yeshiva network under attack from Soviet authorities, opening a Warsaw branch provided a relatively safe haven outside Russia. Simultaneously, the Rayatz launched an extensive underground network to sustain Jewish education and observance inside the USSR.
Tags: warsaw, poland, tomchei temimim, yeshiva

Title: Rayatz farbrengs for hours on Purim after fast collapse
Summary: Though he fainted observing the Fast of Esther, the Rebbe recited a maamar for two and a half hours on Purim.
Story: Still recuperating from typhus, the Rebbe asked his doctor whether he could farbreng and say a maamar on Purim. The doctor allowed it but instructed him to limit the maamar to fifteen minutes. The next day the Rebbe spoke for two and a half hours and remained with the Chasidim for more than three additional hours.
Tags: purim, maamar, farbrengen, rostov

Title: Rayatz fasts and farbrengs on Purim despite illness
Summary: Still recovering from typhus, the Rayatz fainted on the Fast of Esther but completed the fast and led a long Purim farbrengen the next day.
Story: The doctor permitted the Rebbe a fifteen-minute maamar; he instead recited one for two and a half hours and sat with Chasidim for three more. Many yeshivah students were also ill, and the financial strain of medical bills was mounting. Reb Shmuel Gurary's death exacerbated the crisis.
Tags: rayatz, rostov, purim, illness

Title: Rayatz prepares chronological registry of Rashab's discourses
Summary: In 5681 (1921) the Rebbe Rayatz prepared a chronological registry of his father the Rashab's discourses from his nesi'us years 1883–1920.
Story: This was the first systematic chronological list of the maamarim of a Rebbe organized by year of delivery. The Rayatz prepared it together with a general overview of the discourses of the Rashab's forty-year nesi'us. The methodology established here became the model for later registries of other Rebbeim's maamarim.
Tags: rayatz, rashab, maamarim, registry

Title: Rayatz sends funds to repair the Lubavitch mikvah
Summary: At the start of 5682 the Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak sent money to the remaining Jews of Lubavitch to rebuild the destroyed mikvah.
Story: After the fire destroyed the courtyard and the mikvah, some members of Anash still living in Lubavitch relocated the synagogue into the stone house. At the start of 5682 (1921), the Rayatz sent them a sum of money to repair the mikvah, as documented in Igrot Kodesh vol. 14.
Tags: rayatz, lubavitch, mikvah, russia

Title: Schneersohn library confiscated by Soviet government
Summary: The Soviet government nationalized the Schneersohn library of Lubavitch rebbes' books and manuscripts.
Story: In 1921 the Russian government confiscated the Schneersohn library, which would later become the focus of decades-long Chabad efforts to recover the texts. Culture Minister Gubenko cited this 1921 nationalization in his December 1990 letter refusing to return the collection to Agudas Chassidei Chabad. The confiscation set the stage for the Didan Notzach campaign decades later.
Tags: russia, soviet union, schneersohn library, nationalization, didan notzach

Title: Solovki Islands monastery converted to first Soviet political prison camp
Summary: The fifteenth-century monastery on the Solovki Islands in the White Sea was converted into the Soviet Union's first political prison camp.
Story: Solovki operated as a notorious labor camp from 1921 until the onset of war in 1939. It was the site to which the GPU first sentenced the Lubavitcher Rebbe before international pressure forced commutation to internal exile in Kostroma.
Tags: solovki, soviet union, prison, white sea

Title: Soviet authorities close Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Rostov
Summary: In 5681 the Soviet authorities forced the closure of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Rostov.
Story: With the central yeshiva shut down by Soviet authorities, the Rebbe Rayatz opened a new branch of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw and dispatched R' Alter Simchowitz from Russia to direct its spiritual program. This effectively shifted the institutional center of gravity for Lubavitch yeshiva education out of Russia.
Tags: rostov, russia, soviet, tomchei tmimim, closure

Title: Tomchei Tmimim central yeshiva relocates from Kremenchug to Rostov
Summary: In the winter of 5681 the central Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva moved to Rostov, where R' Alter Simchowitz was appointed mashpia.
Story: The yeshiva had previously been headquartered in Kremenchug. The Rostov tenure was short-lived, as Soviet authorities forced the yeshiva to close that same year, prompting the Rebbe to redirect his educational resources to Warsaw.
Tags: rostov, kremenchug, russia, tomchei tmimim, alter simchowitz

Title: Tomchei Tmimim founded in Warsaw
Summary: Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was established in Warsaw in 5681.
Story: In 5681 (1920-1921), the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was established in Warsaw, Poland. This Polish branch would later become the central yeshiva after the Rebbe Rayatz settled in Poland, growing to include multiple branches across Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, warsaw, poland, yeshiva founding

Title: Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw operates at Franciscan St. 30
Summary: During 5681–5682 the Warsaw branch of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva studied in the synagogue at Franciscan Street 30.
Story: In the years 5681–5682 (approximately 1920–1922) the Warsaw branch of Tomchei Tmimim was housed in the synagogue at Franciscan Street 30. The yeshiva was still in its early formative period in Poland and used existing study halls before later expansions. This location preceded its move to a more spacious house of study on the same street.
Tags: warsaw, poland, tomchei-tmimim, yeshiva, franciscan-street

Title: Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva founded in Warsaw
Summary: The Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was founded in Warsaw in 5681, eventually growing to ten branches across Poland.
Story: Tomchei Tmimim was established in Warsaw in 5681 (1921). Over the next 19 years it expanded to ten branches throughout Poland, until it was destroyed during the Holocaust.
Tags: warsaw, poland, tomchei-tmimim, yeshiva

Title: Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva in Rostov closed by Soviet authorities
Summary: In late winter 1921, Soviet authorities shut down Tomchei Tmimim in Rostov, arrested its leaders, expelled students, and confiscated the Rebbe's property.
Story: The closure marked the beginning of the underground period for the Tomchei Tmimim network across Russia. At the very same moment that the Russian network was being driven underground, a new branch was being founded in Warsaw, Poland, beginning what would become the central Tomchei Tmimim of the interwar period.
Tags: russia, rostov, soviet, tomchei-tmimim, persecution

Title: Warsaw branch of Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim opens
Summary: On the first anniversary of the Rashab's passing, twelve students inaugurate the Warsaw branch of the chasidic yeshivah.
Story: The Rebbe called this 'days of light and days of joy.' He appointed an oversight board and instructed them to focus on ethics, G-d-fearing spirit, and character. By 1927 it had 157 students; by 1928, 250. It eventually relocated to Otwock and became the incubator for postwar Chabad rabbis.
Tags: warsaw, poland, yeshivah, tomchei-temimim

Title: Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim founded in Warsaw
Summary: In 5681, Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim was founded in Warsaw under the leadership of R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov, R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin, and R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin.
Story: Building on the established Chabad community of Warsaw, Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim was founded there in 5681 (1921). At its head stood the three central Warsaw Chabad leaders: R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov, R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin, and R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin. The yeshiva became a major hub of Chabad education in interwar Poland.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, shraga feivish zalmanov, shneur zalman shmotkin, dovber moshe shmotkin

Title: Vitebsk cheder show trial halted by 5,000 protesters
Summary: Thousands of local Jews protested a Yevsektzia staged trial of the traditional cheder in Vitebsk.
Story: Five thousand local Jews came out shouting to stop the trial and threatening to close the cinema where it was being held, while thousands more assembled in local synagogues. Uneasy Yevsektzia members called off the trial after physical threats, but they regrouped soon after. A second trial was held in which the cheder was sentenced to be liquidated.
Tags: vitebsk, yevsektzia, cheder, show trial, protest

Title: Vitebsk show trial against cheder canceled by protests
Summary: Five thousand local Jews shut down a Yevesektzia show trial of a traditional Vitebsk cheder.
Story: Thousands more gathered in synagogues to protest, and the Yevesektzia organizers were physically threatened. They later regrouped and staged a second trial that sentenced the cheder to liquidation.
Tags: vitebsk, cheder, show-trial, protest

Title: R. Aryeh Leib Sheinin sent to influence Vilna and Minsk towns
Summary: By 17 Shevat 5681 the Rebbe was directing R. Aryeh Leib Sheinin of Zembin to travel through the Vilna and Minsk provinces promoting Torah and chassidus study.
Story: Sheinin, one of the foremost Tomchei Tmimim students in Lubavitch, was sent by the Rebbe in the winter of 5681 as a mashpia in the towns of the Vilna and Minsk regions. On 17 Shevat 5681 the Rebbe wrote (Igros Kodesh vol. 16, letter 5723) singling him out as a model emissary urging communities to establish fixed Torah-study times in nigleh and chassidus.
Tags: sheinin, zembin, vilna, minsk, kvius-itim, chassidus

Title: Kollel Chabad accepts Rebbe Rayatz as Nasi after Rashab's passing
Summary: Upon news of Rebbe Rashab's passing, the Kollel Chabad community signed a statement accepting Rayatz as Nasi.
Story: In Shvat 5681 (Feb 1921), as the time for the kollel's annual elections arrived, the shocking news of the Rebbe Rashab's passing reached Jerusalem. Most members of the kollel gathered and signed a document accepting Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak (Rayatz) as their rebbe in spiritual guidance and as Nasi of the kollel, and asked the existing administrators to continue for another year.
Tags: rayatz, rashab, kollel chabad, succession, jerusalem

Title: Yevesektzia stages show trial against Lubavitch yeshivah
Summary: The Yevesektzia organized a show trial in Rostov demanding the closure of Tomchei Temimim and conscription of its students into the labor army.
Story: Following a similar staged trial against a Vitebsk cheder in January, the Yevesektzia targeted Lubavitch in Rostov. They forced their way into the Rebbe's home, seized inherited household goods and silver, and imprisoned three students plus the Rebbe's future son-in-law Shmaryahu Gurary for five days before he negotiated their release.
Tags: yevesektzia, rostov, show-trial, tomchei-temimim

Title: Yevsektzia stages show trial against Lubavitch yeshivah
Summary: A trial in Rostov demanded the closure of Tomchei Temimim and conscription of its students into the workforce.
Story: The Yevsektzia 'testified with lies' and forcefully demanded that the yeshivah be closed and that its students be added to the army of workers. During this period they also forced their way into the Rebbe's home, seizing household goods, clothing, and silver inherited from his father. Three students and the Rebbe's future son-in-law Rabbi Shmaryahu Gurary were imprisoned for five days.
Tags: yevsektzia, rostov, tomchei temimim, show trial

Title: Chafetz Chaim moves yeshivah back to Poland
Summary: Rabbi Yisrael Meir Kagan, in his early eighties, returned his Radin yeshivah from Russia to Poland.
Story: Leaving Russia, the Chafetz Chaim stopped in Minsk and told local rabbi Nissan Telushkin that he had no strength left to battle the Communists and the renegades within. Later in life he reportedly regretted leaving, saying a Jew must be ready to sacrifice himself for Judaism.
Tags: chafetz-chaim, radin, poland, minsk, emigration

Title: Chafetz Chaim transfers yeshivah back to Poland
Summary: Rabbi Yisrael Meir Kagan, in his early eighties, moved his Radin yeshivah out of Soviet Russia.
Story: Having transferred the yeshivah to Russia in 1915 at the start of World War I, the Chafetz Chaim moved it back to Poland in 1921. Stopping in Minsk, he told the local rabbi Nissan Telushkin that he had no strength left to battle the malicious government and 'the evil renegades' forcing yeshivah students to desecrate Shabbat. Later in life he reportedly regretted leaving.
Tags: chafetz chaim, radin, poland, yeshivah relocation, minsk

Title: Entire Lubavitch courtyard burns down
Summary: At the start of Nisan 5681 fire destroyed the entire Lubavitch courtyard of the Rebbes, ending the town's role as Chabad's center.
Story: The fire came one year after the passing of the Rashab in Rostov and three years after the yeshiva's departure for Kremenchug. With the courtyard gone and the Rebbe's family long departed, the town ceased to function as the movement's headquarters. The buildings of the great hall, the small hall, the residences, and the yeshiva facilities all perished.
Tags: fire, lubavitch-courtyard

Title: Fire destroys all buildings in Lubavitch courtyard
Summary: All the buildings in the Rebbes' courtyard in Lubavitch burned down at the start of Nissan 5681.
Story: In the early days of Nissan 5681 (April 1921), one year after the passing of the Rebbe Rashab and between his yahrzeit and that of the Tzemach Tzedek, fire destroyed all the buildings in the Rebbes' courtyard in Lubavitch. The fire consumed everything within half an hour, including the beis midrash with all its Torah scrolls, and spread to the market and many streets. When the Rebbe Rayatz visited in summer 5682, he was shocked by the desolate scene.
Tags: lubavitch, fire, destruction, courtyard

Title: Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva founded in Warsaw
Summary: On 2 Nissan 5681, the first yahrzeit of the Rebbe Rashab, Tomchei Tmimim was founded in Warsaw with twelve students drawn from local Chabad chassidim.
Story: The founders included R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin, R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov, and R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin. The yeshiva opened at the Lubavitch beis midrash at Franciszkańska 30 after Pesach, with R. Baruch Friedman of Russia soon appointed as mashpia. The founding effectively transferred the center of the Tomchei Tmimim network from Soviet Russia to Poland.
Tags: warsaw, poland, tomchei-tmimim, founding, rashab-yahrzeit, franciszkanska

Title: Second Soviet decision concerning the Schneersohn library
Summary: On 21 May 1921, Soviet authorities issued a second ruling that, together with the 16 December 1919 decision, transferred the Schneersohn library to the Rumyantsev Museum.
Story: These two decisions formed the legal basis the Soviet Scientific Council cited in 1924 when refusing to return the library to the Frierdiker Rebbe, even though he had earlier received a positive response from the libraries department of Narkompros.
Tags: soviet, library, rumyantsev museum, narkompros

Title: Wedding of Chana Schneerson and Rabbi Shmaryahu Gurary in Rostov
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz's older daughter Chana married Rabbi Shmaryahu Gurary in a very modest ceremony in Rostov.
Story: At the time, Rostov was suffering from typhus and famine, and the Yevsektzia had forcibly closed the Lubavitch yeshivah. The secret police broke into the Rebbe's home before the wedding and seized property including the wedding dress. With limited finances, only light refreshments of cake and drinks were served to guests.
Tags: rostov, russia, gurary, famine, typhus, yevsektsia

Title: Sasonkin writes from Rostov to Axelrod in Zembin
Summary: Secretary Nochum Shmaryahu Sasonkin wrote from Rostov to Rabbi Avraham Eliyahu Axelrod with fundraising directives for Tomchei Temimim.
Story: On 13 Sivan 5681, writing from Rostov-on-Don, Rebbe Rayatz's secretary Nochum Shmaryahu Sasonkin wrote to the recently married Axelrod in Zembin. He acknowledged a letter from Axelrod's father in America and directed Axelrod to urge his father to mobilize donations to Tomchei Temimim through newspaper appeals. He listed contacts in Vienna, Iași (Romania), Warsaw, and Riga who could relay funds, noting that foreign currency would be worth two thousand times more in their home country.
Tags: sasonkin, axelrod, rostov, zembin, tomchei-temimim, fundraising, russia

Title: Rebbe Rayatz sends detailed organizational instructions for Warsaw yeshiva
Summary: In the days after learning of the Warsaw founding, the Rebbe sent two detailed letters laying out the name, structure, leadership committee, admissions, and daily schedule of the new yeshiva.
Story: The Rebbe instructed that the institution be called 'Merkezet Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch in Warsaw' and named R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin, R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov, and R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin as the core of a five-member governing committee. The letters specified standards of yiras shamayim, character development, and daily conduct expected of the Tmimim.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-tmimim, letter, rostov

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe writes celebratory letter to Warsaw yeshiva
Summary: On 11 Tammuz 5681, the Rebbe Rayatz, then still in Rostov, wrote an exuberant letter to the students of the newly founded Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: Word of the Warsaw founding had reached the Rebbe only at the beginning of Tammuz, smuggled across the closed Soviet border by special messenger. He spent days speaking of his joy and called the students his sons, praying that the yeshiva would grow and spread its light. The next day he wrote a follow-up letter to R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-tmimim, letter, rostov

Title: Cheka issues release document for Rayatz
Summary: The secret police formally attested to the release of Rabbi Schneersohn weeks after the interrogation.
Story: Following the previous summer's interrogation in Rostov, the Cheka issued a document attesting to the Rebbe's release. It was just one act in a years-long drama of conflict with the Yevsektzia that would culminate in arrest and exile six years later.
Tags: cheka, rayatz, rostov, release

Title: Chicago Sentinel reports starving Lubavitch students
Summary: The American Jewish newspaper described starvation among yeshivah students who had evacuated Lubavitch for Rostov.
Story: The Sentinel reported that 'the yeshivah students who have evacuated Lubavitch for Rostov-on-Don are starving.' The financial pressures, famine, and disease prompted some students to leave the yeshivah and return home. Once one of the great centers of European Jewish scholarship, the yeshivah was whittled down to just forty students in Rostov.
Tags: sentinel, chicago, famine, rostov, tomchei temimim

Title: Chicago Sentinel reports starving Lubavitcher students
Summary: The Chicago-based Sentinel reported that yeshivah students who had evacuated Lubavitch for Rostov were starving.
Story: By mid-1921, financial pressures, famine, and disease drove many students to leave Rostov for home. The grand yeshivah of Lubavitch had been whittled down to roughly forty students in Rostov, making it among the last bastions of traditional Torah scholarship in Russia.
Tags: chicago, sentinel, media, rostov, famine

Title: Chafetz Chaim's letter from 5 Selichot 5681
Summary: On 5 Selichot 5681, the Chafetz Chaim wrote reflecting on his six years of wandering in Russia, in Smilavitchi, Shumyatch and Snovsk, and his return.
Story: He described how God had finally fulfilled their wish to leave Russia after the Soviet authorities imposed forbidden labor on all, even yeshiva students. He thanked the communities that had supported the yeshiva splendidly throughout the exile.
Tags: chafetz chaim, radin, russia, yeshiva, exile

Title: R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin departs Rostov for the Holy Land
Summary: In mid-Elul 5681 R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin set out from Rostov with his family for the Land of Israel to refound the Toras Emes yeshiva.
Story: Sent by the Rebbe Rayatz to renew Toras Emes, R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin departed Rostov with his family in mid-Elul 5681. The Rebbe wrote on 16 Elul 5681 to Shila on Havlin's behalf and on 19 Cheshvan 5682 reported having received word that Havlin was in Tiflis awaiting passage from Batum. The journey ended up taking nearly four months.
Tags: havlin, rostov, toras emes, rayatz, travel

Title: Sheinin appointed rabbi of Dokshytsy
Summary: In Tishrei 5682 the Rebbe sent R. Aryeh Leib Sheinin to serve as rabbi of the chassidic community in Dokshytsy.
Story: In Tishrei 5682 (autumn 1921), the Rebbe Rayatz dispatched Sheinin to take up the rabbinate of the chassidic community in Dokshytsy. R. Yochanan Gordon, the town's shochet, later wrote of Sheinin's profound personal qualities and devotion to the Rebbe.
Tags: sheinin, dokshytsy, vilna-region

Title: Decision to found Tomchei Tmimim branch in Homel
Summary: On Simchat Torah 5682, Chabad chassidim gathered in Homel resolved to establish a local branch of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva.
Story: Travel to the central yeshiva in Lubavitch had become unsafe under the new Soviet regime, leaving students wandering with no stable place to study. At a Simchat Torah gathering in the home of R' Shmuel Biale 'der zeiger macher,' the chassidim of Homel decided to open their own branch of Tomchei Tmimim. They wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz requesting permission and a rosh yeshiva, and he approved, granting the new institution the name 'Tomchei Tmimim of Lubavitch in Homel.'
Tags: homel, tomchei tmimim, russia, simchat torah, shmuel biale

Title: Rayatz launches Toras Emes yeshiva in Jerusalem
Summary: On 19 Cheshvan 5682 the Rayatz wrote to Havlin directing him to establish the yeshiva first in Jerusalem rather than Hebron.
Story: Havlin selected a property in the Brand courtyard in the Beis Yisrael neighborhood (today the Karlin shtibel). The Rayatz prescribed four daily hours of Chassidus on the Tomchei Tmimim model, with the rest of the day devoted to nigleh in a strict schedule.
Tags: jerusalem, toras emes, havlin, rayatz, beis yisrael

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes to father-in-law about R' Alter's mission
Summary: On 19 Cheshvan 5682 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin reporting that his son-in-law R' Alter was still in Minsk on his way to Warsaw.
Story: The letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. 1, letter 95) reported that Alter remained in Minsk after Sukkot but was likely to travel on to R' Shraga Feivish, since the Warsaw founders had pleaded for an experienced mashpia and supervisor. The correspondence shows the Rebbe coordinating an international transfer of personnel under difficult conditions.
Tags: minsk, warsaw, alter simchowitz, shlomo zalman havlin, letter

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes to RashZ Hablin about Yeshivat Torat Emet
Summary: On 19 Cheshvan 5682 the Rebbe Rayatz informed RashZ Hablin he was being sent to direct Yeshivat Torat Emet in Jerusalem.
Story: Anash in America had inquired about the signatories of the public appeal to rebuild Torat Emet and whether the Rebbe was still its director. The Rebbe Rayatz replied that the signatories were former students of the institution and that RashZ Hablin had been dispatched to Eretz Yisrael to take charge of Torat Emet. The letter clarified institutional authority during the transition.
Tags: jerusalem, yeshiva torat emet, rashaz hablin, rebbe rayatz

Title: Kollel administrators ask Rebbe Rayatz to formally accept Nesius
Summary: Kollel Chabad administrators wrote to Rebbe Rayatz formally asking him to accept the Nesius of the kollel.
Story: On 10 Kislev 5682 (Dec 1921), administrators Menachem Mendel Naeh and Moshe Ornstein wrote to Rebbe Rayatz describing the post-war renewal of the kollel and the community's vote in Shvat 5681 to accept him as Nasi. They asked him to confirm and direct the next round of elections.
Tags: rayatz, kollel chabad, menachem mendel naeh, moshe ornstein

Title: Rebbe writes to Minsk arranging funds for R' Alter's journey
Summary: On 5 Kislev 5682 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote authorizing up to two million in funds for R' Alter Simchowitz in Minsk and laying out the logistics of his move to Warsaw.
Story: The Rebbe instructed that Alter would first need to be issued a rabbinic certification by a Warsaw synagogue, which would help him secure travel papers. He would travel alone immediately and have his family follow about a month later; the Rebbe stressed that 'the time is precious.'
Tags: minsk, warsaw, alter simchowitz, letter, funding

Title: Rebbe writes to Warsaw Chabad leaders about R' Alter's arrival
Summary: On 6 Kislev 5682 the Rebbe wrote to several Warsaw chassidim including R' Feivush Zalmanov, R' Bezpalov and R' Yehuda Leib Raskin promising central support once R' Alter arrived.
Story: The Rebbe assured them that once Alter Simchowitz reached Warsaw and the yeshiva's affairs were organized, central Chabad would provide a subsidy for the yeshiva's operating expenses.
Tags: warsaw, alter simchowitz, feivush zalmanov, letter

Title: Rebbe urges R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin to expedite R' Alter's arrival
Summary: On 7 Kislev 5682 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin in Warsaw urging that R' Alter from Pochep arrive as quickly as possible.
Story: Shmotkin was directing the founding of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw, and the Rebbe pressed him to do whatever was needed to bring Alter in without delay. The exchange documents how closely the Rebbe was managing both finances and personnel during the relocation.
Tags: warsaw, shneur zalman shmotkin, alter simchowitz, letter

Title: Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva opens in Homel
Summary: On Chanukah 5682, the Homel branch of Tomchei Tmimim opened with R' Yechezkel Feigin as rosh yeshiva and a single student.
Story: After receiving the Rebbe Rayatz's approval, the Homel chassidim engaged R' Yechezkel Feigin — who had recently moved from Kremenchug to his mother-in-law's home — to serve as rosh yeshiva, with his salary paid in flour because of the famine. The yeshiva opened on Chanukah in the Babushkin shul, the only synagogue willing to host the students out of fear they would break the windows and benches. For its first three weeks the only student was Hillel Sklyar, son of R' Avraham Yaakov Sklyar of Zlobin.
Tags: homel, tomchei tmimim, yechezkel feigin, hillel sklyar, chanukah, babushkin shul

Title: Family moves near the kloiz at the Bashtun in Lipovets
Summary: In early winter 5683 the family relocated next to the Bashtun kloiz, where the father resumed teaching a large group of children in the home.
Story: A G-d-fearing cooper was their neighbor at the new dwelling. More observant parents who still clung to Yiddishkeit entrusted their sons to the author's father, and a sizable cheder gathered in a large room of the home. The move offered modest stability during the worsening Soviet anti-religious climate.
Tags: lipovets, ussr, ukraine, underground-cheder

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe requests release of library to Rostov
Summary: In summer 5682, the Frierdiker Rebbe submitted a renewed request to be permitted to take his library from the Moscow warehouses to his home in Rostov.
Story: Earlier he had been unable to retrieve the books because he lacked a place to store them. Though Narkompros had approved his request in principle, that year the books were still not returned to him.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, rostov, library, moscow, soviet

Title: Lubavitch yeshivah relocates to Poltava
Summary: Forty students of Tomchei Temimim moved by horse and wagon from Rostov to Poltava, where local Chasidim agreed to underwrite the yeshivah.
Story: Unable to secure rail authorization, the students traveled four hundred miles by wagon. Poltava had a strong, diverse community of about twenty thousand Jews and a less aggressive Yevesektzia. That summer the Rebbe appointed Rabbi Yechezkel Feigin as administrator.
Tags: tomchei-temimim, poltava, ukraine, yechezkel-feigin

Title: R' Natan Gurarie passes away
Summary: In 5682 R' Natan Gurarie, father of R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie, passed away in Rostov.
Story: In 5682 (1921/22) R' Natan Gurarie, father of R' Shneur Zalman and R' Yechiel Tzvi, passed away. He left a widow, Mrs. Esther, and his sons, who continued in their father's path. R' Shneur Zalman was then about ten years old.
Tags: natan-gurarie, rostov, russia, gurarie-family

Title: R' Yosef Goldstein joins Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw at age 14
Summary: In summer 5682, 14-year-old Yosef Goldstein was admitted to Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw through a workaround, since he was considered too young.
Story: Goldstein had been studying at Yeshivat Toras Chaim when he and several other boys decided to transfer to Chabad. Because he was only 14 the yeshiva refused him at first, so he arranged private study with R' Avraham Ziskind and R' Moshe Yehuda Reichman until he was gradually absorbed into the yeshiva. Shmuel Zalmanov served as his mentor; the total enrollment at that point was 15 students.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, yosef goldstein, shmuel zalmanov, students

Title: R. Natan Gurary passes away in Rostov
Summary: In 5682, the chassid R. Natan Gurary passed away in Rostov, leaving his widow Esther and sons Yechiel Tzvi Hirsch and Shneur Zalman.
Story: R. Natan Gurary died in Rostov in 5682 (1922). Three years later, his widow Esther and sons would leave Soviet Russia, with his elder son Yechiel Tzvi Hirsch eventually settling in Warsaw and becoming one of the leaders of Polish Chabad.
Tags: rostov, russia, natan gurary, death

Title: R. Yosef Avraham Friedman smuggled across border to Poland
Summary: In 5682 the future Tomchei Temimim secretary smuggled himself across the Soviet-Polish border and assumed the name Alter Kagan.
Story: In 5682 (1922), Yosef Avraham Friedman illicitly crossed from Russia into Poland. He officially adopted the name Alter Kagan, though unofficially he continued to be known as Yosef Avraham Kagan.
Tags: russia, poland, yosef avraham kagan, border, soviet

Title: Rafael Cohen elected rabbi of Nevel
Summary: In 5682, R. Rafael Cohen was elected rabbi of Nevel, succeeding R. Yechezkel Faivish Neimark.
Story: After serving in Osvet from his marriage in 5671 and then in Shchedrin following R. Yehuda Leib Esterin's death in Adar 5672, Cohen took the Nevel rabbinate. He served there until forced to flee after the 5689 arrests of Chabad rabbis in Nevel.
Tags: rafael-cohen, nevel, rabbinate, soviet-russia

Title: Rayatz establishes Rabbinical Committee for Russian Jewry
Summary: Departing from historical decentralization, the Rebbe convened a national rabbinical body with himself as chair, advocating for rabbis under Yevesektzia pressure.
Story: By 1922 the Rebbe was in contact with communities across Russia about schools, mikvaot, rabbis, and shochtim. The Rabbinical Committee leveraged the inconsistency between formally permissive Soviet law and the aggressive Yevesektzia, lobbied the Soviet Bar Association for clarification on religious schooling, and defended teachers in court.
Tags: rabbinical-committee, russia, advocacy, yevesektzia

Title: Rayatz petitions Rumyantsev Library director for return of books
Summary: During a six-week stay in Moscow in summer 5682, Rayatz writes the Rumyantsev Library director requesting return of his confiscated books.
Story: Lodging at the home of R. Meir Yaakovson during a stay focused on klal work, Rayatz petitions the library director, recounting the 1921 Narkompros decision in his favor and explaining that the collection had migrated from the nationalized Kokorev warehouses to the Rumyantsev Library only because he had lacked storage. The petition was not honored, and the books remained in the library's possession.
Tags: library, soviet, moscow, rumyantsev-library, rayatz, russia

Title: Rayatz's final visit to Lubavitch
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz traveled to Lubavitch for the final time to pray at the graves of his predecessors.
Story: In 1922, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn made his final pilgrimage to the town of Lubavitch to pray at the graves of the Lubavitcher Rebbes interred there. The visit came years after his father had left during World War I, and the town was no longer the spiritual capital it had once been. This was the last visit by a Lubavitcher Rebbe to the historic town.
Tags: lubavitch, soviet union, pilgrimage, yosef yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Rayatz's only return visit to Lubavitch as Rebbe
Summary: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5682, the Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak traveled to Lubavitch to pray at the Ohel of his predecessors.
Story: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5682 (1922), the Rayatz traveled to Lubavitch to prostrate himself at the Ohel of his predecessors. While there he delivered a Chassidic discourse in the synagogue that had been relocated to the stone house. This was the only time he visited Lubavitch after assuming the leadership of Chabad.
Tags: rayatz, lubavitch, ohel, russia

Title: Rebbe Rayatz reopens Torat Emet yeshiva in Jerusalem
Summary: In 5682, the Rebbe Rayatz re-established the Torat Emet yeshiva in Jerusalem after its closure in WWI.
Story: After the Torat Emet yeshiva of Hebron had closed during World War I, the Rebbe Rayatz reopened it in Jerusalem in 5682 (1922). It has continued to operate there to the present day, with a branch also opened at the time in Jaffa.
Tags: jerusalem, torat-emet, rayatz, yeshiva, eretz-yisrael

Title: Tomchei Temimim relocates to Poltava
Summary: Forty students traveled four hundred miles by horse and wagon to a more hospitable Ukrainian city.
Story: Unable to obtain authorization to travel by train, the students made the long trip by wagon. The Rebbe appointed Rabbi Yechezkel (Chatche) Feigin as administrator of the central yeshivah in Poltava. The local Chabad community of some twenty thousand Jews was diverse and better organized, and the Yevsektzia had less influence there.
Tags: poltava, ukraine, rostov, tomchei temimim, yechezkel feigin

Title: Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw relocates to Franciscan St. 8
Summary: In the years 5683–5685 the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim moved to a more spacious house of study at Franciscan Street 8.
Story: Between 5683 and 5685 (approx. 1922–1925) the yeshiva relocated within Warsaw to a roomier beit midrash at Franciscan Street 8. The move reflected steady growth in student numbers as the institution's reputation spread across Poland and neighboring countries. It remained at this address until the next, larger move in 5686.
Tags: warsaw, poland, tomchei-tmimim, yeshiva, franciscan-street

Title: Toras Emes reconstituted in Jerusalem
Summary: Rabbi Zalman Havlin returned to Eretz Yisrael and reestablished Toras Emes in Jerusalem.
Story: Following the Rashab's instruction before his passing, Rabbi Zalman Havlin returned to Eretz Yisrael in 1922 and reconstituted Toras Emes in Jerusalem, where it continues to flourish as a center of chasidic scholarship to this day.
Tags: toras emes, jerusalem, zalman havlin, eretz yisrael

Title: Toras Emes reopened in Jerusalem after WWI
Summary: After the First World War's disruption, Yeshivas Toras Emes was reopened in 5682, this time based in Jerusalem rather than Hebron.
Story: The First World War interrupted operations of the Toras Emes yeshiva in Eretz Yisrael. In 5682, after the war ended, the yeshiva was reestablished, now centered in Jerusalem rather than Hebron. This re-founding is documented in detail in the following chapter of the source.
Tags: jerusalem, torat emet, war, yeshiva, post-wwi

Title: Toras Emes yeshivah reconstituted in Jerusalem
Summary: Rabbi Zalman Havlin returned to Eretz Yisrael and reconstituted the Toras Emes yeshivah in Jerusalem.
Story: Before his passing in 1920, the Rashab had instructed Havlin to return to Eretz Yisrael as soon as possible. The yeshivah, originally founded in Hebron in 1911 but disrupted by World War I, was now re-established in Jerusalem. Today it remains a flourishing center of Jewish scholarship.
Tags: toras emes, jerusalem, zalman havlin, eretz yisrael

Title: Torat Emet yeshiva opens in Jerusalem
Summary: In 5682 the Torat Emet yeshiva opened a branch in Jerusalem, maintaining its status as an institution independent of Kollel Chabad.
Story: Following the model established by the Rashab when he originally founded Torat Emet in 1912, the yeshiva's Jerusalem branch operated outside the Kollel Chabad framework. This continued the trend of creating standalone Chabad institutions rather than placing all activity under the kollel umbrella.
Tags: torat emet, jerusalem, yeshiva, kollel chabad

Title: Yeshivat Torat Emet reestablished in Jerusalem
Summary: Yeshivat Torat Emet was reopened in Jerusalem in 5682 after its Hebron branch had been completely disbanded.
Story: Kollel Chabad's leadership wrote to R. D.M. Rabinovitch of Boston that the Hebron Torat Emet yeshiva had ceased entirely and could not yet be reconstituted there. Rabbi Eliezerov together with two distinguished avreichim were establishing the yeshiva anew in Jerusalem according to the Rebbe Rashab's original plan. Donors were urged to support the renewed institution.
Tags: jerusalem, yeshiva torat emet, hebron, kollel chabad

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes lengthy response to Kollel administrators
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz wrote a detailed reply to the 10 Kislev letter, but it was delayed in transit for months.
Story: On 24 Tevet 5682 (Jan 1922), Rebbe Rayatz composed a long reply to Naeh and Ornstein about kollel management, but the original letter has not survived. Its contents are known only through later correspondence in which he summarized it. The letter took roughly four months to arrive in Jerusalem.
Tags: rayatz, kollel chabad

Title: R' Havlin arrives in Jerusalem to refound Toras Emes
Summary: R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin reached Jerusalem on Friday 6 Tevet 5682, refounding the Toras Emes yeshiva there.
Story: After a circuitous four-month journey from Rostov through Tiflis, Batum and Constantinople, R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin arrived in Jerusalem on erev Shabbos 6 Tevet 5682. R' Menachem Mendel Naeh recorded his arrival in a 15 Tevet letter to the Rebbe. Toras Emes was reestablished in Jerusalem, where it continues to operate.
Tags: jerusalem, havlin, toras emes, rayatz

Title: Rayatz writes to R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin about Kollel matters
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin acknowledging news from Jerusalem about the kollel.
Story: On 10 Shvat 5682 (Feb 1922), Rebbe Rayatz wrote letter 106 to R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin in Jerusalem, thanking him for regular updates and expressing hope that the kollel was being run faithfully along the lines his late father had outlined in tarav. He also referenced his 24 Tevet letter to Naeh, which Havlin had not yet seen.
Tags: rayatz, shlomo zalman havlin, kollel chabad

Title: Rebbe Rayatz announces opening of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw
Summary: On 8 Shevat 5682 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote, via his secretary Elchanan Dober Marozov, announcing that a branch of Tomchei Tmimim had opened in Warsaw with about 25 talented students.
Story: The letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. 14, letter 5136) explained that the Warsaw branch had been founded on the suggestion of the Rebbe's son-in-law. R' Alter Simchowitz, who had previously directed the Shchedrin branch, was being dispatched to run it. The opening marked the formal re-establishment of Lubavitch yeshiva infrastructure outside Soviet Russia.
Tags: warsaw, poland, tomchei tmimim, elchanan dober marozov, alter simchowitz, letter

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe issues detailed organizational plan for Torat Emet
Summary: On 10 Shvat 5682 the Frierdiker Rebbe writes R' Sh.Z. Havlin a lengthy letter prescribing how to organize Torat Emet in three divisions.
Story: On 10 Shvat 5682 (February 8, 1922), the Frierdiker Rebbe sent R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin a long and detailed letter laying out how to organize Yeshivat Torat Emet into three divisions, defining the student types, the rashei yeshiva to be hired, and the order of study. Havlin then recruited R' Moshe Aryeh Leib Shapira as a rosh metivta and R' Shimon Glitzenstein as secretary — both alumni of Torat Emet's original Hebron cohort — who would serve in these roles for decades.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, torat emet, hebron, havlin

Title: Rayatz reflects in letter on assuming leadership
Summary: On 10 Shevat 5682 the Rayatz wrote of his shock at reading his father's instruction that he assume the leadership.
Story: The Rayatz revealed that his eyes 'darkened' when he read that the leadership of the community was placed on him. He became deeply ill from the weight of the responsibility but was restored to life and committed to following his father's sacred instructions. Decades later, 10 Shevat would become the date of his own passing in 1950.
Tags: rayatz, succession, letter, igrot kodesh

Title: Rebbe Rayyatz reaffirms Kollel Chabad is for Torah scholars only
Summary: On 29 Shvat 5682 the Rebbe Rayyatz wrote that Kollel Chabad exists solely for those who dwell in the tent of Torah.
Story: Echoing his father the Rashab's earlier letter, the Rayyatz declared that he could not extend his hand to anyone who wished to maintain the kollel for the sake of general yishuv-support. The kollel was created for those sitting in Torah, he insisted, and they were its essential beneficiaries. This continued a multi-decade debate over the kollel's purpose.
Tags: kollel chabad, rayyatz, ideology, yoshvei ohel

Title: Confrontation between Tomchei Tmimim and Novardok yeshivas in Homel
Summary: Shortly before Purim 5682, Novardok students confronted the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Homel over students who had transferred from their school.
Story: Novardok students had been founding small yeshivas across Soviet Russia, including one in Homel, but their unstructured curriculum and idiosyncratic mussar exercises — recording 'peulos' of humility such as asking shopkeepers for absurd goods — caused many students to transfer to the better-ordered Tomchei Tmimim. Two senior Novardok students, including Meir of Brisk, demanded that R' Yechezkel Feigin return their students or cease teaching. The author and Feigin physically escorted them out, and the matter was later argued with R' Avraham Yafen, then rosh yeshiva of Novardok in Homel.
Tags: homel, novardok, tomchei tmimim, avraham yafen, mussar, meir of brisk

Title: Tomchei Tmimim Homel adds assistant rosh yeshiva
Summary: At the beginning of Adar 5682 the growing Homel yeshiva engaged Rabbi Yosef Baruch as assistant rosh yeshiva.
Story: Students gradually streamed into the Homel branch of Tomchei Tmimim, and by the start of Adar a second teacher was needed. Rabbi Yosef Baruch was hired as assistant to R' Yechezkel Feigin, and the student Meir Shor of Padobranka was appointed deputy mashgiach. Although other shuls now offered space, the chassidim remained at the Babushkin shul on grounds of hazakah and were granted permission to set up long study tables throughout the building.
Tags: homel, tomchei tmimim, yosef baruch, meir shor

Title: R' Alter Simchowitz reaches Warsaw after losing foot crossing border
Summary: Before Pesach 5682, R' Alter Simchowitz finally arrived in Warsaw after his foot was amputated in a Vilna hospital following a frostbitten illegal border crossing.
Story: On his way from Russia to Poland, Simchowitz had smuggled himself across the border on foot through a forest, where the severe cold caused his foot to freeze. He was taken to a Vilna hospital where the foot was amputated, and only then continued to Warsaw, arriving just before Pesach to take up his post as mashpia.
Tags: warsaw, vilna, alter simchowitz, border crossing, tomchei tmimim

Title: R. Naeh writes that Rebbe's 24 Tevet letter has not arrived
Summary: R. Naeh wrote to Rayatz expressing concern that the long-awaited 24 Tevet letter had been lost in the mail.
Story: On 7 Nissan 5682 (April 1922), R. Menachem Mendel Naeh wrote to Rebbe Rayatz expressing anxiety that the substantial letter of 24 Tevet had not arrived after such a long delay. He worried that the postal route had encountered some disaster and that the letter was lost.
Tags: menachem mendel naeh, rayatz, postal delays

Title: Rabbi Rafael Mordechai Barshansky arrested in Homel
Summary: Rabbi Rafael Mordechai Barshansky was jailed after publicly defending religion at a Soviet-organized debate in Homel.
Story: When Soviet authorities convened a public assembly to attack religion, Rabbi Rafael Mordechai Barshansky — a powerful preacher — rose to refute them. Unable to defeat him in open debate, the authorities trumped up charges, with one of his former servants among the judges, and imprisoned him. After great efforts he was freed and subsequently emigrated to America.
Tags: homel, rafael mordechai barshansky, soviet, persecution, america

Title: Soviet decrees against religion intensify in the Homel region
Summary: After Pesach 5682 the Soviet authorities launched their first organized campaign of decrees against yeshivas and chadarim in the Homel area.
Story: Following Passover, the Bolshevik regime escalated its persecution of religious institutions, issuing decrees aimed at closing yeshivas and chadarim. The chassidim, not yet familiar with Soviet tactics, were caught off guard as the authorities convened public meetings to attack religion and recruited informers — including former servants of rabbis — to act against the community.
Tags: soviet, persecution, homel, yeshivas, chadarim

Title: Warsaw students meet R' Alter at Acharon shel Pesach farbrengen
Summary: On Acharon shel Pesach 5682 the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim students first met R' Alter Simchowitz at a kiddush and farbrengen that ran into the following day.
Story: The gathering, hosted at the home of R' Zalman Shmotkin, continued nonstop into the next day, and Alter delivered the maamar 'V'henif yado al hanahar.' With his arrival the yeshiva's level of study in nigleh and chassidus rose markedly and an elevated atmosphere took hold among the students.
Tags: warsaw, alter simchowitz, shneur zalman shmotkin, farbrengen, tomchei tmimim

Title: R. Naeh responds to Rayatz's letter on Kollel's mission
Summary: After receiving the long-delayed 24 Tevet letter, R. Naeh replied affirming the kollel's mission to support scholars.
Story: On 18 Sivan 5682 (June 1922), R. Naeh wrote a substantive reply to Rebbe Rayatz's recently-received letter. He agreed with the Rebbe's vision that the original purpose of the RMBN (Rabbi Meir Baal HaNes) fund was to support scholars in Eretz Yisrael, while acknowledging that since the era of the Tzemach Tzedek, simple working families had also been supported.
Tags: menachem mendel naeh, rayatz, kollel chabad, rmbn

Title: Letter to Rebbe Rayatz describing founding of Tzemach Tzedek yeshiva
Summary: R. Menachem Mendel Nae wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz detailing the founding and program of Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek in Jerusalem.
Story: Writing on 18 Sivan 5682, Rabbi Nae reported he had returned to his post at the kollel in Tevet 5680 and secured a 15 pound sterling monthly budget. The funds enabled avreichim and bachurim from various Jerusalem yeshivot to gather twice daily at Beit Menachem Tzemach Tzedek for structured Chassidus study. The yeshiva was thereby named Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, menachem mendel nae, yeshiva tzemach tzedek, rebbe rayatz

Title: Kollel Chabad signs agreement with Tzemach Tzedek yeshiva managers
Summary: Yeshiva managers signed an agreement with Kollel Chabad's leadership regulating fundraising for the yeshiva and the kollel.
Story: On 25 Sivan an agreement clarified that the gathering of scholars studying Chassidus daily at Beit Menachem—founded by the kollel in 5680—would remain the kollel's institution and property. It would continue to be called Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek as printed in the yearly calendar. All internal and external affairs would be conducted under the kollel managers' directives.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, yeshiva tzemach tzedek, agreement

Title: Rebbe Rayatz makes first return visit to Lubavitch
Summary: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5682, the Rebbe Rayatz visited Lubavitch for the first time since assuming the leadership of Chabad.
Story: After travel restrictions were lifted, the Rebbe Rayatz traveled to Lubavitch on Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul, delivering a maamar in the brick shul — the other synagogues having burned — and praying at the Ohel before departing for Moscow with R' Shmuel Aba Dulitzky. A delegation from Homel led by the author met him on the platform at the Krasna station, and the author received a yechidus on the train. The Rebbe likened his renewed journey to Lubavitch to a horse finally breaking loose from its tether, signifying the renewal of the bond with the town since he had assumed the nesius.
Tags: lubavitch, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, krasna, ohel, shmuel aba dulitzky

Title: Rebbe Rayatz visits Lubavitch to pray at ancestral graves
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz visited Lubavitch on Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5682 to pray at the ancestral graves.
Story: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5682 (August 24, 1922), the Rebbe Rayatz traveled to Lubavitch to pray at the holy graves of his ancestors. During his stay, he delivered a chassidic discourse in the synagogue located in the brick house. This was the only time he visited Lubavitch after assuming the leadership of Chabad.
Tags: lubavitch, ohel, graves, rebbe rayatz

Title: R. Naeh notes long correspondence delays before Sukkos 5683
Summary: R. Naeh wrote that multiple summer letters had not been acknowledged, and promised to send a copy.
Story: Erev Sukkos 5683 (Oct 1922), R. Naeh wrote to Rebbe Rayatz that he had sent multiple letters that summer with no acknowledgment, and that he was puzzled by the Rebbe's failure to receive his 18 Sivan response. He promised to send a carbon copy of the letter after the holiday.
Tags: menachem mendel naeh, rayatz, postal delays

Title: R. Naeh sends Rayatz a carbon copy of his Sivan letter
Summary: R. Naeh sent Rebbe Rayatz a carbon copy of his 18 Sivan letter after the original failed to arrive.
Story: On 4 Marcheshvan 5683 (Oct/Nov 1922), R. Naeh fulfilled his Erev Sukkos promise and sent Rebbe Rayatz a copy of the long letter he had written on 18 Sivan, enclosing the carbon. This is illustrative of how slowly correspondence flowed between Eretz Yisrael and Soviet Russia in this period.
Tags: menachem mendel naeh, rayatz, kollel chabad

Title: Cheshvan 5683 census finds only 413 Jews remaining in Hebron
Summary: By Cheshvan 5683 a precise count found only 413 Jews in Hebron, with the Chabad community essentially gone.
Story: Yisrael Kaplan reported in HaTor (issue 31) that a careful census in Cheshvan 5683 found just 413 Jews in Hebron — 306 Sephardim and 107 Ashkenazim. The Chabad kollel, once first in seniority and stature with 165 souls in 5678, had nearly ceased to exist; only nine remaining families received a meager distribution administered from Jerusalem.
Tags: hebron, census, demographics, chabad, decline

Title: R' Aleksander Sender Yudasin appointed rabbi of Krivoy Rog
Summary: R' Aleksander Sender Yudasin, a Tomchei Tmimim alumnus, was appointed rabbi of Krivoy Rog with rabbinical certificate dated 14 Marcheshvan 5683.
Story: After approximately fifteen years without clear succession following R' Isser Yanovsky's death, R' Aleksander Sender Yudasin was appointed rabbi of Krivoy Rog in early 5683. His rabbinical certificate is dated 14 Marcheshvan 5683. Yudasin was an alumnus of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva.
Tags: krivoy-rog, yudasin, tomchei-tmimim, rabbinate

Title: Brothers light menorah and play Chanukah kvitlach in Lipovets
Summary: During Chanukah 5683 the author and his older brother prayed Hallel daily, lit the menorah with their father, and played kvitlach at night.
Story: Each day of the festival the boys walked to shul together to daven and recite Hallel. In the evenings, after their father kindled the lights and their mother fried latkes, they played the traditional Chanukah kvitlach game, providing a small island of warmth amid the harsh anti-religious environment.
Tags: lipovets, chanukah, family, ussr

Title: Bar mitzvah of Rabbi Shlomo Sternberg's only son in Lipovets
Summary: In the summer of 5683 the only son of Rabbi Shlomo Sternberg of Lipovets celebrated his bar mitzvah, with the author's brother and their melamed seated alongside the celebrant.
Story: The author's brother Yosef had befriended Mordechai, son of Rabbi Sternberg, and a private melamed was teaching the two boys Gemara with Rashi and Tosafot. At the bar mitzvah seudah the brother sat beside the bar mitzvah boy together with their teacher, a rare moment of communal Jewish celebration in the increasingly hostile shtetl.
Tags: lipovets, sternberg, bar-mitzvah, ukraine

Title: Chofetz Chaim passes through Homel en route to Poland
Summary: Around 5683, when Polish nationals living in Russia were granted permission to return to Poland, the Chofetz Chaim passed through Homel and lodged with R' Shmuel Yitzchak Luria.
Story: When the Soviets permitted Polish nationals residing in Russia to return home, the Chofetz Chaim left the town of Snovsk, where he had been living with his students, and made his way toward Poland. En route he passed through Homel, staying as a guest in the home of R' Shmuel Yitzchak Luria. This was the only time the author met him, describing him as 'a very pious Jew.'
Tags: chofetz chaim, homel, shmuel yitzchak luria, snovsk, poland, repatriation

Title: Facsimile reproduction of the Soncino Haggadah published in Leipzig
Summary: A facsimile reproduction of the c. 1485 Soncino Haggadah was published in Leipzig with illustrations supplied by Albert Frisch.
Story: Around 5683 (1923), a facsimile reproduction of the Haggadah extracted from the c. 1485 Soncino Machzor was issued in Leipzig. Illustration plates were supplied by Albert Frisch, with the title and printing notes hand-lettered by Franziska Baruch. Two copies were produced, one on slightly larger paper.
Tags: haggadah, facsimile, leipzig, soncino, germany, incunabula

Title: Famine and Joint-supplied food relief reach Lipovets
Summary: In 5683 a terrible famine struck and the Soviet government distributed cooked food and bread, almost certainly supplied by the Joint Distribution Committee.
Story: Residents stood on long queues to receive a portion of cooked food, bread and meat from a local official. Because the official's sons studied in the family's cheder, the author and his brother were able to obtain the bread ration with little waiting. The episode reflects the dire hunger gripping Ukrainian shtetls during this period.
Tags: famine, joint, lipovets, ussr, ukraine, relief

Title: Last Chabad breakaway dynasty ends
Summary: With the passing of Rabbi Shmaryahu Noach Schneersohn of Bobruysk in 1923, the last breakaway Chabad dynasty came to an end.
Story: In 1923, Rabbi Shmaryahu Noach Schneersohn of Bobruysk passed away, marking the end of the last of the breakaway Chabad dynasties that had emerged after Rabbi Menachem Mendel's passing in 1866. At that point, all Chabad Chasidim accepted Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn as the sole Chabad Rebbe. This consolidation followed the establishment of Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim in Lubavitch, which had drawn students from across the various Chabad streams.
Tags: bobruysk, russia, shmaryahu noach schneersohn, kopust, chabad unification, yosef yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Passing of the Maharshan of Bobruisk
Summary: The Admor Shmaryahu Noach of Bobruisk, who had succeeded his brother as leader of the Kopust line, passed away in 5683.
Story: The Admor Shmaryahu Noach of Bobruisk, brother of the Maharshaz of Kopust, took his brother's place after the latter's passing in 5660 and continued to lead until his own death in 5683. He represented the Bobruisk-Kopust continuation of the Tzemach Tzedek's offspring dynasty alongside the main Lubavitcher line.
Tags: bobruisk, maharshan, kopust, obituary

Title: R' Avraham Naftali Hirtzka Goldberg joins as ram in Warsaw
Summary: In winter 5683 R' Avraham Naftali Hirtzka Goldberg was hired as an additional ram at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw to teach the class below R' Shimon's.
Story: Known as 'der Klobutzker' for the small town near Lodz where he grew up and studied, Goldberg later lived in Wielun before being brought to Warsaw. He was a classic Polish lamdan who loved pilpul; R' Shmuel Zalmanov reported to the Rebbe that his style was not quite the Chabad approach but that students were inspired by the vitality of his teaching.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, avraham naftali goldberg, klobuck, wielun

Title: R' Avraham Shimon Engel of Zelichov appointed rosh yeshiva in Warsaw
Summary: In 5683 R' Avraham Shimon Engel-Horowitz of Zelichov was appointed rosh yeshiva at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw with the Rebbe Rayatz's approval.
Story: Engel was renowned for encyclopedic mastery of Talmud and skill in explaining Rishonim; his opening shiur in Bava Metzia reportedly analyzed twenty-eight different Rishonic approaches. He had previously taught in yeshivot in Tzanz, Krakow, Krzanov and Stolin before joining Tomchei Tmimim. R' Shmuel Zalmanov reported to the Rebbe both his brilliance and his weakness in giving over the deeper analytical reasoning that students needed.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, shimon engel zelichover, rosh yeshiva

Title: R. Yechiel Meir Blumenfeld appointed rav at Tachkemoni in Warsaw
Summary: In 5683, R. Yechiel Meir Blumenfeld, a co-founder of the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim, was appointed as a rav at the Mizrachi rabbinical seminary Tachkemoni.
Story: Blumenfeld's family had been expelled from Poland to Russia during World War I, where they encountered Chabad and became sympathizers. After returning to Warsaw he helped establish Tomchei Tmimim and gave shiurim there in Maseches Shabbos before his Tachkemoni appointment.
Tags: warsaw, blumenfeld, tachkemoni, mizrachi, tomchei-tmimim

Title: Rabbi Eliyahu Simpson immigrates to the United States
Summary: Rabbi Eliyahu Simpson, a chozer of the Rashab's discourses, immigrated to the US and served as rabbi of the Chabad synagogue in Boro Park.
Story: In 1927, Simpson was among the American Chasidim who scrambled to secure funds for the Rebbe's relocation. After the arrival of the Rebbe Rayatz in 1940, he became one of his secretaries and a key figure in the development of Chabad in the United States.
Tags: america, boro park, simpson, immigration

Title: Rebbe Rayatz sends R' Aryeh Leib Shainin to Dokshitz
Summary: In 5683 the Rebbe Rayatz dispatched R' Aryeh Leib Shainin — a top student of Tomchei Tmimim — to serve as rabbi and mashpia in Dokshitz.
Story: In 5683 the Rebbe Rayatz sent R' Aryeh Leib Shainin to the town of Dokshitz to serve as its rabbi and mashpia. Shainin had been one of the most outstanding talmidim of Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch — the Rebbe Rashab reportedly said that the entire founding of Tomchei Tmimim had been worthwhile for him alone. Shainin lived in Dokshitz until the Second World War and was murdered there in the Holocaust.
Tags: leib shainin, dokshitz, rebbe rayatz, rav, mashpia, soviet union

Title: Rebbe Rayatz's 5683 maamar circulated by mimeograph
Summary: A maamar from 5683 was distributed by mimeograph among Chassidim.
Story: During the early Soviet years Rebbe Rayatz transmitted his discourses by mimeograph rather than print. A 1923 maamar circulated in this fashion and is preserved in the exhibit.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, russia, mimeograph, samizdat

Title: Soviet authorities impose a kehilla council on Homel
Summary: During 5683 the Soviet authorities compelled Homel's Jews to form an official community council, with R' Shmuel Yitzchak Luria chosen as chairman.
Story: As anti-religious decrees mounted — synagogues being seized through forced signature campaigns and mikvaot closed under hygienic pretexts — the government ordered the Jews of Homel to establish a community council. R' Shmuel Yitzchak Luria was elected chairman and worked closely with the younger tmimim, defying the protests of older communal figures. Through their efforts a new mikveh was built, and the Rebbe Rayatz sent Luria a long letter pledging support from his vast network of institutions despite carrying personal debts of tens of thousands of dollars.
Tags: homel, soviet, shmuel yitzchak luria, kehilla, mikveh, synagogue closures

Title: Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw moves to Franciszkanska 8
Summary: In 5683 Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw, having grown to around 100 students, relocated from Franciszkanska 30 to a more spacious building at Franciszkanska 8.
Story: The new site, a beit midrash of the Strikov chassidim, had two large halls plus a kitchen, dining area and dormitory rooms; a Jewish neighbor across the way cooked for the yeshiva. The yeshiva remained there through 5685, moving to Mlawska 7 in 5686.
Tags: warsaw, poland, tomchei tmimim, franciszkanska, expansion

Title: Rebbe instructs R' Alter to train students to speak chassidus publicly
Summary: On 15 Iyar 5683 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Alter Simchowitz directing him to select short maamarim and train Warsaw students to deliver them publicly.
Story: The Rebbe wrote that even shy students must be pushed to overcome their reluctance to speak, since training them this way would yield great benefit over time. He closed with strong encouragement, invoking his late father's spirit and reminding Alter that the work of spreading Torah is done 'not by might and not by power, but by knowing Him.'
Tags: warsaw, alter simchowitz, chassidus, public speaking, letter

Title: Yechidus in Rostov on emigration to America
Summary: During Shavuot 5683 the Rebbe Rayatz, then residing in Rostov, advised the author to consider emigrating to America.
Story: The author traveled to the Rebbe Rayatz in Rostov for Shavuot 5683, where the Rebbe delivered chassidus and R' Yechezkel Feigin served as chozer at the chazarah following Shacharis. In a yechidus after the holiday, after noting that his parents and siblings had already emigrated to the United States, the author received the Rebbe's answer that going to America was 'very right, one must travel, do not be ashamed.'
Tags: rostov, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, shavuot, emigration, america, yechezkel feigin

Title: Rebbe writes again to R' Alter pressing for expansion and student development
Summary: At the end of Sivan 5683 the Rebbe again wrote to R' Alter, complaining of poor reporting and urging that students give chassidus publicly and that the institution be expanded.
Story: The Rebbe noted he had received no updates since his Iyar letter and reiterated that students must repeat chassidus in public. He told Alter and the staff that the duty of rebuilding Tomchei Tmimim 'as it once was' rested on them, promising that a portion of the donations from overseas chassidim would be allocated to Warsaw's needs.
Tags: warsaw, alter simchowitz, chassidus, tomchei tmimim, funding, letter

Title: Ramash meets Chaya Mushka for first time in Kislovodsk
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson (Ramash) met his future wife Chaya Mushka in the resort town of Kislovodsk, escorted by matchmaker Rabbi Eliyahu Chaim Althaus.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz confided to Althaus that summer that he wished to marry off his daughter to the Ramash, and asked him to act as shadkhan. Althaus escorted the twenty-one-year-old groom on the 600-mile trip from Yekaterinoslav to Kislovodsk. The Ramash stayed two weeks before returning to Rostov with the Rebbe.
Tags: kislovodsk, russia, caucasus, althaus, shidduch

Title: Rebbe writes 'Hilkhot Mendel' letter to Chaya Mushka
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his daughter alluding to the Ramash's recent visit and hinting he wanted to see her again.
Story: A week after the Ramash returned to Rostov, the Rebbe wrote to Chaya Mushka, who remained in Kislovodsk, that he had been studying 'Hilkhot Mendel' (the subject of Mendel) for several hours each day. He noted that the Ramash had left with a pleasant impression of the Caucasus and would like another excursion in the mountains.
Tags: letters, shidduch, caucasus

Title: Rayatz writes to Agudath Israel about home schooling
Summary: The Rebbe wrote to Agudath Israel leaders in the United States about ongoing local harassment of religious home schooling.
Story: After the Rabbinical Committee blocked a 1923 proposal by the People's Commiserate of Justice to close loopholes permitting religious home instruction, the Rebbe acknowledged the partial victory. Despite the formal ruling allowing private religious instruction for up to six children, local authorities continued to harass teachers. The letter is preserved in Igrot Kodesh.
Tags: agudath israel, homeschooling, soviet law, harassment

Title: Threat to nationalize the Rashab's Rostov home in summer 1923
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Elul 5683 the Rayatz reported that authorities wished to nationalize the family's Rostov house.
Story: In a letter dated Rosh Chodesh Elul 5683, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn relayed his mother's news that the authorities intended to nationalize the Rostov home. In the event, no further confiscation occurred that summer, and the Rebbe's household remained in the building another half year. The episode underscored the constant precariousness of Chabad's headquarters under Soviet rule.
Tags: rayatz, rostov, communists, nationalization

Title: Rebbe deploys Chatzkevich across Lithuania and Latvia
Summary: On 9 Elul 5683 the Rebbe Rayatz tasked R. Chatzkevich with traveling Lithuania and Latvia to write rousing letters and establish chassidus shiurim.
Story: On 9 Elul 5683 the Rebbe wrote to Chatzkevich (Igros Kodesh vol. 14, letter 5178), formally charging him with founding chassidus-study groups in the provinces of Kovno, Vilna, and Dvinsk. The Rebbe also wrote to anash in those regions (letter 5181), asking them to support Chatzkevich and establish written and oral shiurim in every place anash lived.
Tags: chatzkevich, kovno, vilna, dvinsk, chassidus, shiurim

Title: Cheder branch of Torat Emet founded in Jaffa
Summary: The Rebbe Rayyatz instructed R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin to establish a cheder in Jaffa as a branch of the Torat Emet yeshiva in Jerusalem.
Story: In a letter dated Rosh Chodesh Marcheshvan 5684, the Rebbe Rayyatz responded to pleas from Chabad chassidim in Jaffa about their dire spiritual situation and instructed Havlin, director of Torat Emet in Jerusalem, to organize a children's cheder and yeshiva there under the Torat Emet name. R' David Patash, a prominent member of the Tel Aviv chareidi community who had recently arrived from Russia, helped lead the effort. The Rebbe also wrote directly to Patash a few weeks later seeking his help to support the new institution.
Tags: jaffa, tel aviv, torat emet, chabad, yishuv, rayyatz, shlomo zalman havlin

Title: Joseph Yitzchak Schneersohn convenes covenant on 19 Kislev in Rostov
Summary: On 19 Kislev, the Rebbe charged Chasidim in Rostov to fan out to every city, establish places of study, and hire teachers.
Story: Volunteers stepped forward and the Rebbe promised to make a pact with them. A few months later he formalized the secret covenant in Moscow with a quorum of ten.
Tags: rostov, 19-kislev, covenant, education

Title: Rebbe Rayyatz writes to R' David Patash about the Jaffa cheder
Summary: The Rebbe Rayyatz wrote to R' David Patash on 3 Tevet 5684 urging him to assist in founding a talmud torah and yeshiva in Jaffa.
Story: Having received a letter from Chabad chassidim in Jaffa describing the spiritual ruin of their community, the Rebbe explained that Torat Emet of Jerusalem lacked resources to open a branch. Since Patash, recently arrived from Russia, was known for his devotion to Torah causes, the Rebbe asked him to take up the project. The letter set the stage for Patash to become a central supporter of the new institution.
Tags: jaffa, tel aviv, david patash, rayyatz, kollel chabad, yishuv

Title: Agudas Chasidei Chabad founded in the United States
Summary: Agudas Chasidei Chabad of America was established in summer 5684 following the Rebbe Rayatz's directives.
Story: In summer 5684 Rabbi Mendel Leib Lukshin of Krivoyrog reached America carrying lengthy guidance from the Rebbe Rayatz, with whom he had spoken at length in Rostov about establishing the new society. The office was set up behind a partition in the back of the Kremer brothers' wholesale trouser shop at 687 Broadway. R' Moshe Eliezer Kremer accepted the presidency at R' Dovid Shifrin's invitation, while Shifrin served as organizer and secretary.
Tags: united states, lubavitch, agudas chasidei chabad, anash, lukshin, kremer

Title: Agudas Chassidei Chabad established in America
Summary: Agudas Chassidei Chabad was formalized in America in 1924, predating similar formal organizations in other countries.
Story: Many Jews had emigrated from the chasidic heartland in Russia to new communities worldwide. Some were ardent Chasidim, others merely nostalgic. While America formalized Chabad in 1924, in many other countries the connections remained informal. The Rebbe encouraged his Chasidim to expand their vision and take responsibility for all Jews.
Tags: america, agudas-chassidei-chabad

Title: Agudas Chassidei Chabad established in New York
Summary: Chabad synagogues across North America united under Agudas Chassidei Chabad.
Story: Founded by figures including Max Kramer, the organization was still in its infancy when news of the 1927 arrest reached America. It eventually became Chabad's world headquarters and the home of the priceless library the Rebbe brought from Russia.
Tags: new york, america, chabad, agudas chassidei chabad

Title: Agudas Chassidei Chabad established in the United States
Summary: Agudas Chassidei Chabad was founded to strengthen the bond between roughly 150 Chabad-associated immigrant congregations in America.
Story: Led by Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson, the organization operated as a loose confederation of immigrant synagogues whose members were linked largely by sentimental attachment to Chabad rather than active chasidic practice. Though it had not matured into a major national body by 1939, it became the institutional vehicle through which the rescue of the Sixth Rebbe was organized.
Tags: united states, new york, agudas chassidei chabad, yisrael jacobson, congregations

Title: Agudas Chassidei Chabad founded in the United States
Summary: A national Chabad organization was founded in the US to coordinate the small but growing community.
Story: Still in its infancy at the time of the Rebbe Rayatz's 1929 visit, the organization connected with roughly forty Chabad synagogues in New York City and many more across the country. Yehuda Lokshin was its director when the Rebbe wrote to him in January 1929 about plans to visit America.
Tags: agudas-chassidei-chabad, united-states, chabad

Title: Alter Rebbe micrographic portrait copyrighted in Washington
Summary: A micrographic portrait of the Alter Rebbe formed of letters of his Tanya was copyrighted in Washington in 1924.
Story: Artist Natanel Chazan created a portrait of the Alter Rebbe in which the image is composed entirely of the letters of his Tanya. The print was copyrighted in Washington, D.C. in 1924 and is now part of the Lubavitch Library's exhibition of portraits of the Rebbeim.
Tags: washington dc, alter rebbe, portrait, tanya, natanel chazan

Title: Bobruysk Chabad dynasty ends with passing of Rabbi Shmaryahu Noach
Summary: Rabbi Shmaryahu Noach Schneersohn of Bobruysk, the last leader of the breakaway Chabad branches, passed away; his Chasidim gravitated to the Rayatz.
Story: After the 1869 passing of the third Rebbe Menachem Mendel, four of his sons established themselves as Rebbes in other Russian towns alongside Rabbi Shmuel in Lubavitch. Those dynasties eventually petered out. With Shmaryahu Noach's death, Chabad Chasidim from Kopust, Bobruysk, and elsewhere united behind the new Lubavitcher Rebbe.
Tags: bobruysk, kopust, schneersohn, dynasty

Title: Facsimile of Moshe ben Natan HaKohen's Haggadah for the Chatam Sofer published in Berlin-Leipzig
Summary: A facsimile of the manuscript Haggadah created in 1816 for the Chatam Sofer by Moshe ben Natan HaKohen was published in Berlin-Leipzig by B. Cohen.
Story: In 5684 (1924), B. Cohen published in Berlin-Leipzig a precise facsimile reproduction of an illustrated Haggadah manuscript originally created in 1816 by Moshe ben Natan HaKohen for the renowned halakhic authority Moshe Sofer, the Chatam Sofer.
