The 19-leaf quarto reproduction featured colorful illustrations alongside the Yiddish translation in Tzene-Rene script. The work was printed by B.G. Teubner.
Tags: haggadah, facsimile, berlin, leipzig, chatam sofer, moshe ben natan hakohen, illustrated

Title: Founding of Agudath Chassidei Chabad in America
Summary: Agudath Chassidei Chabad of America was founded in 5684 as the principal support organization for Chabad activity in Europe.
Story: In 5684 (1924) Agudath Chassidei Chabad was established in the United States. It became the primary funder of Chabad's activities in Russia, Riga, and Poland, supporting the network of Tomchei Temimim yeshivos, the Rebbe Rayatz's household and secretariat, and the acquisition of books for the Lubavitch library.
Tags: usa, agudath-chassidei-chabad, fundraising

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe moves to Leningrad
Summary: In early summer 1924, R. Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn moved from Rostov to Leningrad, where he now had room to store the long-confiscated library.
Story: This relocation prompted his subsequent declaration to Soviet authorities requesting the library be sent to his new Leningrad address. He explained he could now store the books, having previously lacked space.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, leningrad, rostov, soviet

Title: Gentiles seal the Rashab's underground mikvah in Rostov
Summary: In summer 5684, after the Rayatz's departure, the mikvah built in the Rostov house was sealed and floored over.
Story: Following the Rayatz's forced relocation in Nissan 5684, the new occupants of the Bratsky Pereulok house sealed up the ritual bath that the Rashab had constructed in the basement and laid the basement floor over it. The mikvah — a 'mikvah on mikvah' design the Rashab had personally specified in detailed letters from Slavyansk — would remain hidden for more than seventy years.
Tags: rostov, mikvah, communists

Title: Jaffa branch of Torat Emet officially opens
Summary: During the summer of 5684 the Chabad cheder opened in Jaffa as a branch of the Torat Emet yeshiva of Jerusalem.
Story: Following months of planning and the Rebbe Rayyatz's letters from late 5683 and early 5684, the cheder finally opened in Jaffa during the summer of 1924. By Elul of that year the Rebbe was already referring to it as an established branch in a fundraising letter for Torat Emet. R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin oversaw the institution from Jerusalem, with local support led by Patash, R' Yaakov Malkov, and R' Zalman Aharon Menevitch.
Tags: jaffa, tel aviv, torat emet, chabad, yishuv

Title: JDC begins diverting funds for Russian Jewish 'cultural work'
Summary: The American Joint Distribution Committee began allocating funds to support the Rebbe's Rabbinical Committee, education, and religious activities.
Story: JDC representative Dr. Joseph Rosen, who admired the Rebbe, helped overcome critics inside the Jewish community and pressure from Communist officials to direct money to the Rebbe's projects. The funds supported both home-based industrial training for urbanized Jews and underground religious activities.
Tags: jdc, joseph-rosen, funding, cultural-work

Title: JDC creates the Agro-Joint subsidiary
Summary: The Joint Distribution Committee created a corporation to resettle Soviet Jews on communal farms in cooperation with the Communist regime.
Story: Under Dr. Joseph Rosen, the program operated for fourteen years, ultimately transforming roughly 200,000 Soviet Jews from urban dwellers to peasants. The Rebbe Rayatz repeatedly questioned the wisdom of the project and pushed for the JDC to instead support home-based industries and religious life.
Tags: jdc, agro-joint, soviet-union, colonization, rosen

Title: Levitin appointed to lead rabbinical school in Nevel
Summary: In 5684 the Rebbe Rayatz appointed Levitin to found and direct a beis midrash for rabbinical training in Nevel.
Story: After roughly ten years in Kutaisi, Levitin was appointed by the Rebbe Rayatz in 5684 (1924) to establish and direct a beis midrash for rabbinical training in Nevel, attracting men in their 20s, 30s, and 40s to study laws of practical halacha.
Tags: levitin, nevel, rabbinical-school

Title: Moshe Leib Rotstein marries Kayla Chanovich in Globoke
Summary: R. Moshe Leib Rotstein married Kayla, daughter of the shochet R. Yisrael Chanovich of Globoke, in 5684.
Story: In 5684 (1924), R. Moshe Leib Rotstein — born Zusya Shifrin in Russia around 5660 — married Kayla, daughter of R. Yisrael Chanovich, the shochet of Globoke. Rotstein had fled Russia after WWI and the Revolution, adopting a forged identity. His new father-in-law passed away the following year.
Tags: marriage, globoke, moshe leib rotstein, kayla chanovich, secretary

Title: Nine Chasidim take oath with the Rebbe
Summary: In 1924 nine Chasidim, including Bentzion Shemtov, took an oath with the sixth Rebbe that would mark them as trusted activists for decades.
Story: The 1924 oath bound a small group of Chasidim to the Rebbe's mission during the harshest years of Soviet anti-religious persecution. Members of this group, like Shemtov, were later deployed in the postwar era to build Chabad infrastructure in Western countries.
Tags: nine chasidim, oath, bentzion shemtov, rayatz

Title: R' Alter Simchowitz leaves Warsaw to return to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: At the start of 5685, R' Alter Simchowitz was compelled to leave Warsaw to serve as mashpia at Yeshivat Toras Emet in Eretz Yisrael.
Story: After roughly three years directing Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw's spiritual life, Simchowitz returned to Eretz Yisrael at the Rebbe's direction to take a mashpia role at Toras Emet. He would later be briefly recalled to Warsaw in 5689 before returning again to Jerusalem permanently.
Tags: warsaw, eretz yisrael, toras emet, alter simchowitz

Title: R' Alter Simchowitz leaves Warsaw yeshiva for Eretz Yisrael
Summary: R' Alter Simchowitz, mashpia at the Warsaw yeshiva, contracted tuberculosis at the start of 5685 and was forced to leave Poland for Eretz Yisrael to serve as mashpia at Yeshivas Toras Emes.
Story: At the beginning of 5685 (autumn 1924), R' Alter Simchowitz fell ill with tuberculosis, attributed to his damp, dilapidated lodgings in Warsaw. Doctors advised that Jerusalem's air would be better for his health than Poland's humid climate. He left Poland to take up the position of mashpia at Yeshivas Toras Emes in Eretz Yisrael, and his departure significantly weakened the spiritual atmosphere of the Warsaw yeshiva.
Tags: alter simchowitz, warsaw, eretz yisrael, tomchei tmimim, toras emes, poland, illness, tuberculosis

Title: R' Chaim Meir Lis appointed mashpia in Warsaw yeshiva
Summary: R' Chaim Meir Lis accepted the position of mashpia at Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw after receiving a personal handwritten letter from the Rebbe encouraging him to take the role.
Story: After R' Alter Simchowitz left for Eretz Yisrael, R' Chaim Meir Lis was appointed as one of the mashpi'im in the Warsaw yeshiva. He initially refused the position, wanting to support himself through his own labor, but accepted after receiving a second handwritten letter from the Rebbe explaining the role of tmimim as 'lanterns of light.' He served as mashpia until after Purim 5687 (1927).
Tags: chaim meir lis, warsaw, tomchei tmimim, mashpia, rebbe rashab, rayatz

Title: R' Dovber Rivkin travels to Eretz Yisrael as Rosh Mesivta of Toras Emes
Summary: R' Dovber Rivkin traveled to Eretz Yisrael at the start of 5685 to take up the position of Rosh Mesivta at Yeshivas Toras Emes.
Story: Around the same time that R' Alter Simchowitz left for Eretz Yisrael, R' Dovber Rivkin also traveled there. He was appointed Rosh Mesivta (R"M) at Yeshivas Toras Emes, while R' Alter Simchowitz served as mashpia at the same institution.
Tags: dovber rivkin, toras emes, eretz yisrael, rosh mesivta

Title: R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin appointed senior teacher at Torat Emet
Summary: R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin, newly arrived in Jerusalem from abroad, is appointed a senior teacher at the expanding Torat Emet.
Story: In summer 5684 (1924) Torat Emet expanded and needed an additional rosh metivta. Just then R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin made aliyah and settled in Jerusalem. The Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to him on 2 Elul approving his joining the yeshiva, and to Havlin on Erev Rosh Chodesh Marcheshvan 5685 instructing that distinguished students be placed under his guidance. He served in that role for about three years before relocating to America.
Tags: rivkin, torat emet, jerusalem, frierdiker rebbe

Title: R' Shneur Zalman Schneersohn considers Chicago rabbinate
Summary: During 5684 R' Shneur Zalman Schneersohn deliberated whether to accept a call from Chicago to serve as a Chabad rabbi in America.
Story: R' Shneur Zalman Schneersohn — son of the Retziter Rebbe and a senior great-grandson of the Alter Rebbe — received papers from Chicago inviting him to serve as rabbi and Chabad leader there, with an apartment and a gabbai already prepared. R' Chaim Eliezer Bichovsky urged him to accept, citing a tradition that chassidus would spread in the lower hemisphere before the coming of Mashiach; his brother R' Chaim Schneersohn of Bremen advised him instead to settle in Eretz Yisrael. The author, consulted on the matter, also recommended America, noting that the wave of emigrants from Russia in those years consisted largely of Torah-observant Jews seeking religious freedom.
Tags: shneur zalman schneersohn, chicago, america, chabad, emigration, chaim eliezer bichovsky

Title: R' Yeshaya Horowitz leaves Tzfat for America
Summary: Around mid-winter 5684, R' Yeshaya Halevi Horowitz left his post as rabbi of Chabad in Tzfat and emigrated to the United States.
Story: After serving as rabbi of the Chabad community in Tzfat since 5669 and managing the kollel's distribution there after his father's death, R' Yeshaya departed for America. From this point his name no longer appeared in the Tzfat distribution lists of Kollel Chabad.
Tags: tzfat, america, emigration, horowitz family

Title: R' Yitzchak Zalman Posner murdered by anti-Bolshevik bands
Summary: R' Yitzchak Zalman Posner of Karop was killed together with twelve other Jews when anti-Bolshevik bandits seized a riverboat near Makoshin station.
Story: R' Yitzchak Zalman Posner — father of R' Shalom Posner — was a regular guest of the author in Homel, traveling there roughly every two weeks to purchase wares for his store in Karop in Chernigov province. After refusing the author's invitation to stay for Shabbos so he could return for an unusual second trip the following week, he set out by train to Makoshin and then by riverboat. On Friday morning anti-Bolshevik bands boarded the boat and murdered thirteen Jews on board, claiming they were Bolsheviks, then dumped the bodies into the river. His mother in America was never informed of his death.
Tags: yitzchak zalman posner, homel, karop, anti-bolshevik bands, murder, desna

Title: R' Yosef Blumenfeld appointed mashgiach in Warsaw yeshiva
Summary: At the start of 5685, R' Yosef Blumenfeld of Dombrowa was appointed as a new R"M and mashgiach in the Warsaw yeshiva with the Rebbe's approval.
Story: At the beginning of 5685, the Warsaw yeshiva received a new appointment of R"M and mashgiach with the Rebbe's consent: R' Yosef Blumenfeld of Dombrowa, who had studied for two years at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch. He later served as R"M in the Radomsk Chassidic yeshivas 'Keter Torah,' then as rabbi in Krolewska Huta, and in winter 5695 immigrated to Eretz Yisrael where he served on the beis din in Tel Aviv.
Tags: yosef blumenfeld, warsaw, tomchei tmimim, mashgiach, dombrowa

Title: Rabbi Avraham Eliyahu Axelrod emigrates to Baltimore
Summary: Rabbi Avraham Eliyahu Axelrod emigrated from Soviet Russia to the United States, settling in Baltimore.
Story: In 5684 Rabbi Avraham Eliyahu Axelrod, a noted Tomchei Temimim alumnus who had been living in Zembin since 5681, emigrated from Soviet Russia to America and settled in Baltimore. He would serve as a rabbi there for nearly three decades. His departure was later praised by Rebbe Rayatz's secretary Marozov as an escape from the spiritual darkness of Soviet life.
Tags: axelrod, baltimore, emigration, america, soviet-union

Title: Rabbi Moshe Chaim Yehoshua Schneersohn-Twerski immigrates to US
Summary: Rabbi Moshe Chaim Yehoshua Schneersohn-Twerski, a descendant of the second Rebbe, immigrated to the United States in 1924.
Story: Born in 1867, he settled on Eastern Parkway near what would become the sixth Rebbe's shul. A distant relative and close confidant of the sixth Rebbe, his naturally joyous disposition made him the one who could console the Rebbe after the Holocaust photographs incident of May 1945.
Tags: moshe chaim yehoshua schneersohn-twerski, united states, eastern parkway, rebbe dovber

Title: Rabbinical Committee secures JDC funding
Summary: The American Joint Distribution Committee began diverting funds to 'cultural work' supporting the Rebbe's network.
Story: Funding was critical to the Rabbinical Committee's success, and Dr. Joseph Rosen, the JDC representative in Russia, directed money to the Rebbe for educational projects. The 'cultural work' label was code for religious education and the activities of the committee of rabbis. Allocations also supported home-based industry job training for urban Jews.
Tags: jdc, joseph rosen, funding, rabbinical committee

Title: Rayatz forced to leave Rostov and relocate to St. Petersburg
Summary: Forced from Rostov, the Rayatz relocated to St. Petersburg, intensified Jewish life efforts in Russia, and established Agudas Chassidei Chabad in the US.
Story: Bolshevik pressure made Rostov untenable, but the Rayatz refused to abandon Russian Jewry. From St. Petersburg, he expanded the underground religious network. He also founded Agudas Chassidei Chabad in the United States as a base for international support.
Tags: rostov, st petersburg, leningrad, russia, soviet union, agudas chassidei chabad

Title: Rayatz relocates from Rostov to Leningrad
Summary: Following the near-arrest in Rostov, the Rebbe moved his court to a large apartment on the corner of Machovaya and Fantilamanskaya streets in Leningrad.
Story: The apartment had belonged to a baron from Kass, the governor of Bessarabia, who was banished from Leningrad in June 1924 and signed the dwelling and much of its furniture over to the Rebbe. Without an official permit for prayer assemblies, Chasidim gathered in a large room similar to the Lubavitch hall. The city's chief rabbi was the respected David Tevel Katzenellenbogen.
Tags: leningrad, st-petersburg, rayatz, katzenellenbogen

Title: Rayatz works to repair the Lubavitch Ohel
Summary: In 5684 the Rayatz worked to arrange repairs to the destroyed Ohel of the Rebbes in Lubavitch.
Story: When the courtyard was destroyed, the Ohel covering the Rebbes' graves was also destroyed, the attached study hall was ruined, and non-Jews stole the stones of the surrounding fence. In 5684 (1924), the Rayatz worked to arrange repairs to the Ohel, as recorded in Igrot Kodesh vol. 1. The overall situation, however, continued to deteriorate.
Tags: rayatz, lubavitch, ohel, russia

Title: Rebbe Rayatz moves from Rostov to Leningrad
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz relocated from Rostov to Leningrad, bringing the family library and manuscripts.
Story: In 5684 (1924), the Rebbe Rayatz emigrated from Rostov to Leningrad, taking with him the books and manuscripts inherited from his father the Rashab. This was the first of a series of moves that carried the Lubavitch library across Europe before it eventually reached New York.
Tags: russia, rostov, leningrad, library, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz moves residence to Leningrad
Summary: In 5684 the Rebbe Rayatz relocated his residence to Leningrad, from where he managed Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw by correspondence.
Story: In 5684 (1923/24) the Rebbe Rayatz moved from his prior location to Leningrad. From there he maintained a steady correspondence with the Tomchei Tmimim administration in Warsaw on all matters of the yeshiva. The Warsaw committee — R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin, R' Tzvi Gurarie and R' Shmuel Zalmanov's father — handled day-to-day affairs while reporting regularly to him.
Tags: rebbe-rayatz, leningrad, russia, soviet-union

Title: Rebbe relocates from Rostov to Leningrad
Summary: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn moved his residence from Rostov to Leningrad (Petrograd).
Story: In 5684, the Frierdiker Rebbe transferred his seat from Rostov to Leningrad. Soon after the move, the bibliographer Shmuel Wiener approached him with an offer to sell his celebrated private library. This move set the stage for the foundational acquisition of what would become the Lubavitch Library.
Tags: russia, rostov, leningrad, petrograd, rayatz

Title: Rebbe's home in Rostov searched by Yevsektzia
Summary: Yevsektzia officers searched the Rebbe's house and threatened arrest, prompting the eventual move to Leningrad.
Story: Returning from meetings in Moscow, the Rayatz was met outside Rostov by his secretary Rabbi Morozov with ominous news that the Yevsektzia had searched his house. The search ended at four a.m., and only intervention by influential locals prevented arrest. Soon afterward, the Rebbe relocated to Leningrad.
Tags: rostov, yevsektzia, search, leningrad

Title: Rebbetzin's third Rebbe predecessor dies in Bobruysk
Summary: Rabbi Shmaryahu Noach Schneersohn of Bobruysk, last leader of the rival Chabad dynasties, passed away.
Story: After the 1869 passing of the third Rebbe Rabbi Menachem Mendel (Tzemach Tzedek), four of his sons established themselves as competing Rebbes in other towns while his youngest, Rabbi Shmuel, became Rebbe in Lubavitch. Those rival dynasties petered out without successors. With Rabbi Shmaryahu Noach's passing, the last of those branches ended and his Chasidim gravitated to the Rebbe Rayatz.
Tags: bobruysk, shmaryahu noach, kopust, succession

Title: Secret covenant of nine Chasidim in Moscow
Summary: The Rayatz convened nine confidants in Moscow to swear an oath to sustain Judaism under Soviet rule even at the cost of their lives.
Story: Building on a 19 Kislev 5684 address in Rostov calling for emissaries to every city, the Rebbe formalized a clandestine covenant the next winter. The nine became generals of an underground network of schools, yeshivot, synagogues, and mikvaot that lasted until the Soviet collapse. Among the known members were Elchonon Morozov, Bentzion Shemtov, Simon Yakovshvili, and Yerachmiel Binyaminson.
Tags: moscow, underground, kritat-brit, shemtov, morozov, yakovshvili

Title: Secret covenant of ten in Moscow
Summary: The Rayatz convened nine Chasidim to form a clandestine network to preserve Judaism under Soviet rule.
Story: In the winter of 1924, with decrees against Torah students and Jewish schools intensifying, nine temimim gathered in Moscow and the Rebbe completed the quorum of ten. They swore an oath to defiantly fortify Judaism under the Soviet regime, even to the point of mesirat nefesh. The known members included Elchonon Dov Morozov, Bentzion Shemtov, Simon Yakovshvili, and Yerachmiel Binyaminson; classes were held in cold, windowless dungeons dug into the ground.
Tags: kritat brit, moscow, underground, morozov, shemtov, jacobson

Title: Sheinin tours Vilna-region towns to spread chassidus
Summary: In 5684 the Rebbe sent Sheinin to visit communities in the Vilna region and strengthen public learning of chassidus.
Story: After Sheinin reported in Shevat 5684 on his travels, the Rebbe responded (Igros Kodesh vol. 1, letter 171) urging more correspondence with chassidim, dedicated trips, and Tanya recitation in Donilovich. The same day the Rebbe also wrote to R. Yeshaya Friedman, shochet in Donilovich, and to R. Shraga Faivish Bronstein of Kurnits, both of whom had begun teaching Tanya publicly thanks to Sheinin.
Tags: sheinin, donilovich, vilna, tanya, chassidus

Title: Shmuel Zalmanov enters Tomchei Tmimim as full student
Summary: In summer 5684, Shmuel Zalmanov entered Tomchei Tmimim as a regular enrolled student after previously attending only for Chassidus studies.
Story: Shmuel Zalmanov had been coming to the Warsaw yeshiva for Chassidus studies since its opening in summer 5681. In summer 5684 he was officially enrolled as a full student of the yeshiva, and was already noted in records as highly capable and qualified for rabbinic ordination.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, shmuel zalmanov

Title: Soviet Jewish agricultural-colony resettlement project launched
Summary: The Soviet land-resettlement project is launched, relocating Jews to communal farms in Ukraine and Crimea.
Story: Yevsektzia leader Semyon Dimenstein had advocated this in conferences as early as 1918. Authorities relocated Jewish families, sometimes forcibly, in the hope of 'productizing' Jews into farmers. Before they ended their support in 1938, the JDC invested $16 million ($238 million today) in helping the Communists move Jews to agricultural settlements.
Tags: soviet, agricultural colonies, ukraine, crimea, yevsektzia, joint distribution committee

Title: Soviet land resettlement project launched to 'productize' Jews
Summary: The USSR begins relocating Jewish families to communal farms in Ukraine and Crimea to transform them into farmers.
Story: Driven by Semyon Dimenstein and the Yevsektzia, the project displaced traditional Jewish economic roles. The JDC financially supported the plan despite the Rebbe's warnings that it lacked religious infrastructure and served Soviet anti-religious ends.
Tags: russia, soviet, agricultural-colonies, yevsektzia, ukraine, crimea

Title: Soviet officials respond to Rayatz with two earlier library transfer decisions
Summary: In response to Rayatz's renewed petition, officials cite a December 16, 1919 and May 21, 1921 decision transferring the library to the Rumyantsev Museum, now the Lenin State Library.
Story: The denial referenced decisions of 16 December 1919 and 21 May 1921 by which Narkompros had transferred the Schneersohn library to what had become the Lenin State Public Library, and refused on that basis to return it to Yosef Sholom Berkovich Schneersohn.
Tags: library, soviet, rumyantsev-library, lenin-library, narkompros

Title: Soviet seizure of Rashab's library transferred to Russian National Library
Summary: In 1924 the Soviet government transferred the seized portion of the Rashab's library, stored in Moscow since 1915, to the Russian National Library.
Story: After the Rebbe Rashab evacuated Lubavitch in 1915, the bulk of the combined libraries was stored in Moscow while priceless manuscripts were taken to Rostov. With the fall of the czarist government the Moscow books were seized. Authorities agreed to repatriate the collection in 1921 but reneged, again in 1925. The Rebbe Rayatz pursued the library's return throughout his life.
Tags: moscow, russia, library, rashab, soviet-seizure

Title: Tomchei Tmimim central yeshiva operates in Kharkov
Summary: By 5684 the central Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was based in Kharkov under the direction of R' Yechezkel Feigin.
Story: Following the dispersion of Tomchei Tmimim under Soviet pressure, the central yeshiva relocated to Kharkov by 5684. R' Yechezkel Feigin, who had earlier been called from Homel to lead the institution in Poltava, now served as mashgiach and manager of the Kharkov yeshiva, dispatching emissaries such as R' Shneur Gorelik and R' Yisrael Matmid to fundraise across the region.
Tags: kharkov, tomchei tmimim, yechezkel feigin, soviet

Title: Trotsky leadership conflict briefly eases anti-religious persecution
Summary: Toward the end of 5684, internal Communist Party strife around Trotsky temporarily quieted the campaign against Jewish religious life in Lipovets.
Story: The author attributes a noticeable lull in anti-religious pressure to factional struggles at the top of the Communist Party. The respite was short-lived, but it gave families like his room to breathe and to resume modest Torah study at home. The episode illustrates how Kremlin politics directly affected daily Jewish life in the shtetls.
Tags: ussr, trotsky, communist-party, ukraine, yevsektsiya

Title: Warsaw yeshiva expands to additional apartment on Franciszkanska Street
Summary: At the beginning of 5685, the Warsaw yeshiva rented a second apartment at 6 Franciszkanska Street to supplement its existing space at number 8.
Story: Having moved to 8 Franciszkanska Street at the start of 5683, the Warsaw yeshiva outgrew the space by the beginning of 5685 and rented an additional nearby apartment at 6 Franciszkanska. The shiurim and main gathering remained at number 8, while the shiur lectures and Chassidus learning that couldn't fit took place in the shul at number 6.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, franciszkanska, expansion, poland

Title: Wiener transfers his private library to the Frierdiker Rebbe
Summary: Shmuel Wiener handed over his entire private library to the Frierdiker Rebbe.
Story: In 1924, Shmuel Wiener transferred his entire personal collection of books and manuscripts to the Frierdiker Rebbe (Rayatz), making them part of the Chabad library. One Tanya manuscript was apparently not transferred and remained behind, later showing up in the Friedland collection in Leningrad.
Tags: wiener, library, rayatz, schneersohn library, collection transfer

Title: Yevesektzia search of Rebbe's home in Rostov
Summary: Returning from Moscow, the Rayatz found that Yevesektzia officers had searched his Rostov home and intended to arrest and exile him.
Story: His secretary Rabbi Elchonon Morozov met him outside the city with the warning. After ten days back in Moscow he returned to Rostov, where the house was surrounded; an extensive overnight search nearly ended in arrest, prevented only by influential locals. The Rebbe then decided to relocate to Leningrad.
Tags: yevesektzia, rostov, rayatz, secret-police

Title: Zalman Shazar immigrates to Palestine
Summary: Zionist leader Zalman Shazar (born Schneur Zalman Rubashov to a Chabad family) immigrated to Palestine in 1924.
Story: Born in 1889 in Mir near Minsk to a Chabad family, Shazar became active in the Zionist Poalei Tzion movement before settling in Palestine to take a leadership role in Zionist activities. He would later play a part in the planning of Kfar Chabad with the sixth Rebbe.
Tags: zalman shazar, palestine, zionism, poalei tzion

Title: Death of Soviet leader Vladimir Lenin
Summary: Lenin died at age 53 after repeated strokes and medical complications.
Story: His death fulfilled the Rashab's 1920 prediction that 'Lenin will die in a strange fashion.' As Lenin's health had deteriorated, Stalin had been consolidating power. The Rayatz noted the accuracy of his father's predictions about Soviet leaders in his diary entries.
Tags: lenin, soviet union, russia

Title: Death of Vladimir Lenin
Summary: Soviet leader Vladimir Lenin died at age 53 after repeated strokes, fulfilling the Rashab's 1920 prediction.
Story: In January 1924, three and a half years after the Rashab's prediction to the Rayatz, Lenin died at age fifty-three following multiple strokes and medical complications. His death set off a power struggle from which Stalin would emerge dominant.
Tags: lenin, soviet union, russia

Title: Lenin dies; St. Petersburg renamed Leningrad
Summary: Vladimir Lenin died in January 1924, prompting the renaming of St. Petersburg to Leningrad.
Story: The renaming of the former Russian capital came just before the Rebbe Rayatz was compelled to relocate there. The Rebbe later moved to Leningrad in May 1924 after being ordered by the political police to leave Rostov.
Tags: russia, leningrad, st-petersburg, communism

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Raskin on dispatching mashpiim
Summary: In mid-Tevet 5684 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Yehuda Leib Raskin about appointing traveling mashpiim for towns in Poland and Lithuania.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz outlined a plan to assign select chassidim as shadarim who would travel a regular circuit through Poland and Lithuania to strengthen Chassidic life. Among those named was R. Shimon Noach Nimoitin, who would be deployed wherever proved most useful. The letter is preserved as Igros Kodesh vol. 14, no. 5197.
Tags: mashpiim, lithuania, poland, shluchim, tevet, yehuda-leib-raskin

Title: Rayatz receives Tzemach Tzedek portrait from R.M.A. Stillerman
Summary: On 4 Shevat 5684 the Rebbe Rayatz received a printed Tzemach Tzedek portrait from R.M.A. Stillerman.
Story: On 4 Shevat 5684 (10 January 1924), R.M.A. Stillerman gave the Rebbe Rayatz a print of the Tzemach Tzedek's portrait. The print is one of the earliest preserved in the Chabad library and exhibits more of the Rebbe's chair, feet and bookcase than the well-known Metz lithograph, suggesting both derive from a still-earlier original.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, portrait, stillerman, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz orders comprehensive alumni list
Summary: On 18 Shevat 5684 the Rebbe Rayatz instructed R. Sholom Dovber Halevin to prepare a list of all Tomchei Tmimim students from 1897-1924.
Story: On 18 Shevat 5684 (January 24, 1924), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Sholom Dovber Halevin requesting a comprehensive list of all yeshiva students from Tomchei Tmimim and its branches — Lubavitch, Zembin, Kovlitz, Horodishtz, Shchedrin, Romny, Cherson, Hebron, Kremenchug, Poltava, Warsaw, Kutaisi, Nevel, and Jerusalem — from 5657 to 5684. A mimeographed list was reportedly prepared in Rostov-Leningrad, though no copies have been found.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, alumni list, sholom dovber halevin, branches

Title: Rebbe Rayatz urges Shmotkin to find a full-time fundraiser for Warsaw yeshiva
Summary: At the end of Shevat 5684 the Rebbe wrote to R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin urging him to find a dedicated administrator to grow the Warsaw yeshiva.
Story: The Rebbe (Igrot Kodesh vol. 1, letter 179) offered generous percentage compensation to anyone who would take on Warsaw's fundraising and growth as a full-time mission, arguing the institution could easily be five or six times larger than its current state. He warned that 'a thing that stands in place is truly going down.'
Tags: warsaw, shneur zalman shmotkin, fundraising, tomchei tmimim, letter

Title: Rayatz writes to R. Zalman Yitzchak Volshanik of Riga about Kollel
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Zalman Yitzchak Volshanik of Riga about Kollel finances and supporting Torah scholars.
Story: On 3 Adar Sheni 5684 (March 1924), Rebbe Rayatz wrote letter 191 to R. Zalman Yitzchak Volshanik of Riga. He explained that he had purposely refrained from replying earlier, overwhelmed by his struggle to sustain Torah scholars under Soviet conditions, and emphasized that the kollel must focus on supporting scholars rather than on the schism between the two kollels.
Tags: rayatz, riga, kollel chabad, zalman yitzchak volshanik, rmbn

Title: R' Azriel Zelig Slonim sent as Kollel Chabad emissary to America
Summary: On 24 Adar Sheni 5684 the Kollel Chabad administrators signed a contract dispatching R' Azriel Zelig Slonim to the United States as the kollel's fundraising emissary.
Story: Three administrators—R' Yisrael Asher Liba, R' Mordechai Kazarnovsky, and R' Moshe Ornstein—signed the agreement preserved in the kollel's letter ledger. The mission reflected the post-war effort to rebuild Kollel Chabad's finances after Russian funding had collapsed. Shadar missions to America became increasingly important during the interwar period.
Tags: kollel chabad, fundraising, shadar, america, jerusalem

Title: House search and arrest threat force Rayatz to leave Rostov
Summary: On 11 Nissan 5684 Soviet agents searched Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak's home and offered exile in lieu of arrest.
Story: On 11 Nissan 5684, authorities conducted a search of the Rayatz's Rostov home and prepared to arrest him. The matter was resolved by an agreement that he would avoid imprisonment if he left Rostov for another city. The Rayatz and his family relocated to Leningrad shortly thereafter, and the Bratsky Pereulok house passed to local tenants, ending nearly a decade as the center of Chabad.
Tags: rayatz, rostov, leningrad, kgb, communists, arrest

Title: Rayatz appoints five trusted men to oversee Kollel matters
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz appointed five trusted associates to evaluate Kollel Chabad and report back to him.
Story: On 7 Iyar 5684 (May 1924), after two more years of inconclusive correspondence, Rebbe Rayatz appointed a committee of five trusted associates: R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin, R. Shiloh, R. Yitzchak Shmuel Luria, R. Menachem Mendel Naeh and R. Moshe Dov Rivkin. He asked them to examine the kollel's true situation so he could direct its restoration.
Tags: rayatz, kollel chabad, shlomo zalman havlin, yitzchak shmuel luria, menachem mendel naeh, moshe dov rivkin

Title: Rebbe forced from Riga to St. Petersburg under Yevsektzia pressure
Summary: In May 1924, threats from the Yevsektzia compelled the Sixth Rebbe to leave Riga and relocate to St. Petersburg.
Story: It was one in a series of forced relocations the Rebbe later catalogued at his Riga farewell — Rostov to St. Petersburg, out of Russia in 1927, then Warsaw, Otwock, back to Riga, and finally America — each driven by danger or duty rather than personal choice.
Tags: riga, st petersburg, russia, soviet union, yevsektzia

Title: Rebbe Rayatz relocates from Rostov to Leningrad
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz was forced to leave Rostov for Leningrad by order of the Soviet political police.
Story: As he later described it, 'I was compelled to leave by the order of the political police.' His family followed shortly thereafter. The Ramash visited Leningrad regularly, also attending classes at the local university and being drawn deeper into the Rebbe's affairs.
Tags: rostov, leningrad, russia, yevsektsia, political-police

Title: Five-man committee proposes formalizing Rayatz's Kollel Nesius
Summary: Rayatz's five appointees wrote to the Kollel administrators proposing government recognition of his Nesius.
Story: On 12 Sivan 5684 (June 1924), the five-man committee wrote to the kollel administrators proposing that they formalize Rebbe Rayatz's Nesius through official government recognition, granting him authority to manage all kollel matters via his representative and to amend its bylaws. The administrators replied affirmatively, contingent on Rayatz's formal acceptance.
Tags: rayatz, kollel chabad, nesius

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe submits declaration in Leningrad demanding return of library
Summary: In June 1924, the Frierdiker Rebbe submitted a formal declaration from Leningrad arguing that his library, never abandoned and used for scholarly work, must be returned to him under Soviet law.
Story: He argued that Soviet law did not nationalize private libraries, especially those used by scholars, that the books had always been under his supervision, and that prior Narkompros approval proved the library had never been ownerless. He stressed the books were religious texts relevant only to a narrow circle of Jewish religious specialists.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, leningrad, library, soviet, narkompros, kokorov

Title: Rayatz renews request for library return from Leningrad
Summary: In June 1924, having moved to Leningrad, Rayatz renews his application for return of the library now that he has space to house it.
Story: In this petition (Beis HaGenazim ch. 63) Rayatz reminds officials of the Narkompros decision in his favor and explains that the obstacle to executing it — lack of housing for the books — has now been removed. He argues that the collection, by its sectarian content, would only interest a narrow circle of Jewish religious scholars, and asks for its return.
Tags: library, soviet, leningrad, rayatz, russia

Title: Rebbe Rayatz uproots from Rostov to Leningrad
Summary: At the beginning of summer 5684, the Rebbe Rayatz was forced to leave Rostov and settled in Leningrad.
Story: Mounting Soviet pressure forced the Rebbe Rayatz to uproot his household from Rostov and move to Leningrad (formerly Petrograd) at the start of summer 5684. By that point the central Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was situated in Kharkov, with R' Yechezkel Feigin serving as mashgiach and director.
Tags: rostov, leningrad, petrograd, yosef yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Soviet Scientific Council refuses to return Schneersohn library
Summary: On 23 June 1924, the Soviet Scientific Council informed the Frierdiker Rebbe that they could not fulfill his request because the library had already been transferred to the Rumyantsev Museum, now the Russian State Public Library named after Lenin.
Story: The response cited decisions of 16 December 1919 and 21 May 1921 as basis for the transfer by Narkompros. It was signed by Pinkevich, acting chairman of the Scientific Council, and Zinkov, chairman of scientific libraries. This refusal prompted the Rebbe to file another similar request in winter 5685.
Tags: soviet, frierdiker rebbe, rumyantsev museum, library, lenin library, narkompros

Title: Visit to the Lipovets Jewish cemetery on Tisha B'Av 5684
Summary: On Tisha B'Av 5684 the author, his brother and Rabbi Sternberg's son walked the rural roads outside Lipovets to visit the town's Jewish cemetery.
Story: Reaching the beit hachaim required a long trek along village roads far from town. The author later recalled it as the first and only outing he ever took with religious boys his age. The episode evokes the shrinking circle of observant peers available to him as Soviet pressure mounted.
Tags: lipovets, tisha-bav, cemetery, sternberg, ukraine

Title: Author travels to Leningrad for Rosh Hashanah 5685
Summary: Despite financial hardship, the author borrowed money and traveled from Homel to Leningrad to spend Rosh Hashanah with the Rebbe Rayatz.
Story: The author's financial situation was strained, so he borrowed funds collected for ma'amad after R. Yosef the temimid's departure and bought a train ticket to Leningrad. His wife baked challahs and roasted two chickens for the journey. He stopped in Neveil to visit his brother-in-law R. Meir Simcha Chen and to see the famous chassidic town for the first time, lodging with relatives near the Rebbe.
Tags: russia, leningrad, rosh hashanah, rayatz, rebbe rayatz, homel, neveil

Title: R. Shimon Noach Nimoitin appointed mashpia of Vilna
Summary: On 2 Elul 5684 the Rebbe Rayatz formally appointed R. Shimon Noach Nimoitin to teach Chassidus to anash in Vilna and surrounding towns.
Story: The Rebbe wrote on 2 Elul 5684 to R. Shimon Noach Nimoitin directing him to repeat maamarei Chassidus before anash of Vilna and to travel periodically to nearby towns to encourage fixed Torah study and chavrusa learning. On the same day he wrote to the anash of Vilna asking them to receive R. Shimon Noach warmly and set up a venue for him to deliver Chassidus.
Tags: vilna, lithuania, mashpiim, shimon-noach-nimoitin, elul

Title: Havlin reports over 100 students at the Jaffa cheder
Summary: On 15 Elul 5684 R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin wrote that more than 100 children of immigrants were studying at the new Jaffa cheder.
Story: In a letter to R' Yehuda Leib Horowitz, Havlin described how he was compelled to fulfill the Rebbe Rayyatz's instruction to establish the cheder after the chassidim of Jaffa pleaded with the Rebbe to provide schooling for their children. He reported that more than one hundred children of immigrants, who otherwise had no place for traditional Torah education, were now learning in the cheder.
Tags: jaffa, tel aviv, torat emet, shlomo zalman havlin, immigrants

Title: Erev Rosh Hashanah encounter with Elye Chaim Althaus in Leningrad
Summary: On Erev Rosh Hashanah at the Rebbe Rayatz's apartment in Leningrad, the author was awakened to chassidic responsibility by R. Elye Chaim Althaus.
Story: After Selichos and Shacharis, the author entered the Rebbe's apartment at Machovaya 12 and was shocked to find the prayer hall unprepared with no benches set up. When he asked R. Elye Chaim Althaus about it, Althaus repeated the question back to him, awakening the author to the fact that he himself bore responsibility for the Rebbe's house. The author said this moment 'made him ten years older.'
Tags: leningrad, machovaya 12, elye chaim althaus, rosh hashanah, chassidic responsibility

Title: Thirty minyanim of Temimim gather for Rosh Hashanah 5685 with the Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: Approximately thirty minyanim of Temimim, mostly Tomchei Temimim students, traveled to Leningrad for Rosh Hashanah 5685 with the Rebbe Rayatz.
Story: Around thirty minyanim of Temimim, the overwhelming majority students of Tomchei Temimim, came to Leningrad to be with the Rebbe Rayatz for Rosh Hashanah. Even R. Leib Bagad, a balebatish figure from Lubavitch generally distant from chassidus, prayed there and embraced the visiting Temimim like brothers. The warmth and bond among the visitors was deeply felt throughout the holiday.
Tags: leningrad, tomchei temimim, rosh hashanah, rebbe rayatz, leib bagad

Title: Tmimim emigration pact made on Rosh Hashana 5685
Summary: On Rosh Hashana 5685 the Tmimim resolved that every alumnus who reached the West would work to bring out his fellows from Russia.
Story: Gathered for Rosh Hashana 5685, the chevrah of Tomchei Tmimim alumni committed that anyone who succeeded in leaving Soviet Russia for another country must labor on behalf of fellow Tmimim trying to follow. This compact shaped the rescue work of Agudas HaTmimim through the next decade. The author later operated under this mandate to secure visa affidavits and travel funds for many comrades — work which became sharply harder after the Rebbe Rayatz's 1929 American visit.
Tags: soviet union, emigration, tmimim, rescue, rosh hashana

Title: Temimim assembly resolves to send students from Russia to America
Summary: After Rosh Hashanah 5685, an assembly of Temimim in Leningrad decided to send representatives abroad to help bring more students out of Russia.
Story: Following Rosh Hashanah, the Temimim convened and resolved by majority vote that they must campaign to leave Russia, sending one or two emissaries to foreign countries who would then help bring additional students from Russia to safety. The author was the only one at the assembly preparing to travel to America, and the responsibility for the American mission was placed on him. The decisions were submitted to the Rebbe Rayatz.
Tags: russia, america, emigration, tomchei temimim, leningrad, yisrael jacobson

Title: Death of R. Yisrael Chanovich, shochet of Globoke
Summary: R. Yisrael Chanovich, shochet of Globoke and father-in-law of R. Moshe Leib Rotstein, passed away on 19 Marcheshvan 5685.
Story: R. Yisrael Chanovich, who served as the shochet of Globoke, passed away on 19 Marcheshvan 5685, one year after his daughter Kayla's marriage to R. Moshe Leib Rotstein. He left behind sons Chaim, Shmuel Avraham, and Gershon, and several daughters.
Tags: globoke, shochet, yisrael chanovich, death

Title: Contract signed to purchase Shmuel Wiener's library
Summary: The Frierdiker Rebbe signed a written contract to purchase the Wiener library for $5,000 in monthly $50 installments.
Story: On 8 Cheshvan 5685 the Frierdiker Rebbe and bibliographer Shmuel Wiener executed a signed agreement transferring Wiener's massive bibliographic collection — including some 400 Haggadah editions, 140 Kinnos volumes, sixty Siddur recensions, machzorim, and Yiddish Tchines — to the Rebbe. The purchase price of $5,000 was to be paid in monthly installments of $50 over many years. About 4,000 unbound items came with the collection and would be bound after delivery.
Tags: russia, leningrad, shmuel-wiener, library, rayatz, bibliography

Title: Bar mitzvah of R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie in Nevel
Summary: On Chanukah 5685 R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie celebrated his bar mitzvah while a student at Tomchei Tmimim in Nevel.
Story: On Chanukah 5685 (December 1924) R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie reached bar mitzvah while studying at the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Nevel. Shortly afterward he, his mother Esther, and his older brother R' Yechiel Tzvi left Soviet Russia and settled in Warsaw. There he enrolled at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw and received personal study direction from the Rebbe Rayatz.
Tags: shneur-zalman-gurarie, nevel, russia, tomchei-tmimim, bar-mitzvah

Title: R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin reports to R' Dovber Rivkin on Warsaw yeshiva
Summary: On the 7th day of Chanukah 5685, R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin wrote to R' Dovber Rivkin inquiring about the state of Yeshivas Toras Emes and reporting on the Warsaw yeshiva.
Story: On the 7th of Chanukah 5685, R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin sent a letter to R' Dovber Rivkin in Eretz Yisrael, asking about R' Alter Simchowitz's arrival, his health, and the state of Yeshivas Toras Emes in both quantity and quality, in physical and spiritual matters. The same letter described the recent appointment of R' Yosef Blumenfeld as mashgiach in the Warsaw yeshiva.
Tags: shneur zalman shmotkin, dovber rivkin, warsaw, tomchei tmimim, chanukah, correspondence

Title: Rebbe Rayatz acquires Shmuel Wiener's collection
Summary: In Kislev 5685, the Rebbe Rayatz purchased Shmuel Wiener's collection of about 5,000 rare books, including roughly 400 Haggadot.
Story: In Kislev 5685 (December 1924), the Rebbe Rayatz acquired the collection of bibliographer-collector Shmuel Wiener. The acquisition of approximately 5,000 rare books — including some 400 Haggadot — formed a cornerstone of the Lubavitch library's renowned holdings.
Tags: rayatz, library, wiener, haggadah, bibliography

Title: Wiener library acquired in Kislev 5685
Summary: In Kislev 5685 the Frierdiker Rebbe formally took possession of the Wiener bibliographic collection, the founding nucleus of the Lubavitch Library.
Story: Following negotiations begun the previous year, the Rebbe completed the purchase of Wiener's library in Kislev 5685 under terms of long-term monthly payments. The collection had been stored in Wiener's flooded basement and was rescued and dried in the upper floor of a factory rented by R. Eliyahu Chaim Althoz during the Soviet NEP era. The library would become the cornerstone of the future Lubavitch collection.
Tags: russia, leningrad, shmuel-wiener, library, rayatz

Title: Author secures Soviet exit visas for the Gurary family in Homel
Summary: During winter 5685 the author arranged Soviet exit visas in Homel for the Gurary family, including the widow and children of R. Tzvi Hirsch Gurary.
Story: R. Shmarya Gurary asked the author whether he could arrange foreign-travel passports through Homel for the family of R. Tzvi Hirsch Gurary, offering 250 rubles (25 chervontses). After Nochum Gurelnik came to verify the possibility, R. Nosson Gurary brought the family to Homel, where they were registered in residents' household books. By winter's end the author had obtained exit permits for R. Tzvi's entire family, for R. Nosson's wife Esther, and for R. Shmarya Gurary.
Tags: homel, russia, exit visa, gurary family, nochum gurelnik, tzvi hirsch gurary, nosson gurary

Title: Berlin Haggadah illustrated by Y. Liberman published by Gunzer and Levin
Summary: An illustrated Haggadah by Y. Liberman was published by Gunzer and Levin's bookstore in Berlin.
Story: Around 5685 (1925), the book firm of Gunzer and Levin issued an illustrated Haggadah in Berlin with art by Y. Liberman. Printed by Rudolf Grätz, the 48-page folio included a special German title page but no German translation. The Yiddish translation occupied a separate 23-page section.
Tags: haggadah, berlin, germany, y. liberman, illustrated

Title: Branch of Torat Emet opens in Rishon LeZion
Summary: A second branch of the Torat Emet network opened in Rishon LeZion during 5685, the year after the Jaffa branch.
Story: Building on the precedent set in Jaffa, a further branch was opened in Rishon LeZion. The Rebbe Rayyatz referred to both branches in his letter of 2 Shvat 5686 to R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin, asking for more detailed reports from Tel Aviv and Rishon LeZion.
Tags: rishon lezion, torat emet, chabad, yishuv

Title: Family moves to Rabbi Levi the shochet's house in Lipovets
Summary: For the winter of 5686 the family moved into the home of R' Levi the shochet, filling its cellar with potatoes to last through Pesach.
Story: The cellar storage of their potato harvest from the small plot they had worked outside town secured the family's food supply through winter and Pesach. The move also provided the moral support of living beside an observant shochet at a time when religious neighbors were increasingly rare in Lipovets.
Tags: lipovets, ukraine, shochet

Title: Jacobson delivers maamar at bris of Chaim Eliezer Horowitz in Moscow
Summary: Jacobson repeated the Rebbe Rashab's maamar 'Hareini Es Mareich' in Yiddish at the bris of Tomim Chaim Eliezer 'Velizer' Horowitz in Moscow.
Story: During his Moscow stay he was honored to chazer Chassidus at the bris. Accustomed in Homel to chazering in Yiddish so that the balebatim could understand, he did the same in Moscow—drawing critique from the Moscow Tmimim, who considered the audience refined enough for Chassidus in Loshon HaKodesh and remarked that he was 'translating' Chassidus.
Tags: moscow, bris, maamar, yiddish, chaim-eliezer-horowitz

Title: Jacobson granted yechidus with Rebbe Rayatz in Moscow
Summary: During his six-week stay in Moscow awaiting payment of his American steamship ticket, Jacobson received yechidus and a parting blessing from the Rebbe Rayatz.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz visited Moscow while Jacobson was lodged in the Abramov family's apartment. The yechidus was held at the home of one of the Tmimim—either the shochet R. Chaim Zalman Gordon or R. Shimon Yaakobson—with Sender Rappaport, son-in-law of Shimon Yaakobson, managing entries and exits. The local circle of Anash and Tmimim included craftsmen and stocking-makers but also pnimi'usdike chassidim with deep grasp of Chassidus, gathering Shabbos mornings for two hours of Chassidus study followed by avoda-style davening.
Tags: moscow, rayatz, yechidus, tmimim, israel-jacobson

Title: JDC begins curtailing funding to the Rebbe's Russian network
Summary: After supporting the Rebbe's operations on and off, the JDC began winding down its support for his work in Russia.
Story: The retreat from funding Jewish education and religious life under Soviet conditions deepened the financial crisis facing the Rebbe Rayatz's underground network. It would become the central motivation for his 1929 American journey.
Tags: jdc, soviet-jewry, funding, religious-education

Title: Krasov ketubah enters the Rebbe Rayatz's archive
Summary: In 5685 the bibliographer R' Shmuel Wiener transmitted the 5440 Krasov ketubah to the Rebbe Rayatz, where it was added to the library archive.
Story: In 5685, the bibliographer R' Shmuel Wiener — known for his scholarly catalogues of Jewish manuscripts — transmitted an extraordinary ketubah from 5440 Crimea to the Rebbe Rayatz. It eventually became part of the Lubavitcher library's collection of more than fifty antique ketubot of over a century in age.
Tags: shmuel wiener, rebbe rayatz, ketubah, archive, crimea

Title: Leningrad Jewish Religious Community gains state recognition
Summary: LERO became the formally recognized central Jewish communal body in Leningrad under Lev Gurewicz.
Story: Gurewicz, a Zionist lawyer with limited Jewish education, led LERO and harbored ambitions to unite all of Russian Jewry in a national congress. In the summer of 1925 he met the Rebbe for the first time and proposed a partnership. The Rebbe was lukewarm, sensing risks that would later prove justified.
Tags: lero, leningrad, gurewicz, soviet recognition

Title: LERO formally recognized in Leningrad
Summary: The Leningrad Jewish Religious Community (LERO), led by Lev Gurewicz, received formal Soviet recognition.
Story: Gurewicz, a Zionist with a law degree, would soon propose a national congress of Russian Jewish communities, secretly backed by the Yevesektzia, to create a lay-led structure that could supplant the Rebbe's leadership. The Rebbe met Gurewicz that summer and responded coolly to the idea.
Tags: lero, leningrad, gurewicz, yevesektzia

Title: R' Yehiel Tzvi Gurarie emigrates from Russia to Warsaw
Summary: In 5685 R' Yehiel Tzvi Gurarie escaped Soviet Russia and settled in Warsaw, soon joining the Tomchei Tmimim leadership.
Story: In 5685 (1924/25) R' Yehiel Tzvi Gurarie succeeded in escaping Soviet Russia and settling in Warsaw. He joined the three-man directing committee of the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim, replacing R' Dov Moshe Shmotkin who had emigrated to the Holy Land. Together with R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin and R' Shmuel Zalmanov's father, he bore the burden of running the yeshiva.
Tags: warsaw, russia, soviet-union, tzvi-gurarie, emigration, tomchei-tmimim

Title: R' Yisrael Jacobson arrives in America at Ellis Island
Summary: R' Yisrael Jacobson arrives at Ellis Island with his family and is processed by immigration officials before entering New York City.
Story: Arriving with his wife and two children, Jacobson was held at Ellis Island where his daughter Rachel Dvasha (age 1.5) was secretly coming down with measles that went undetected by the inspectors. After questioning about his finances (he had only one dollar) and rabbinic duties, the synagogue representatives Mr. Benjamin (president), Mr. Siegel (secretary), and his uncle Yosef Hillel came to vouch for him. The next Thursday morning they took the Third Avenue elevated train into Manhattan, passing through Wall Street which his uncle described as the richest place in the world.
Tags: america, immigration, ellis island, new york, yisrael jacobson, zhuravichi

Title: R. Yechiel Tzvi Hirsch Gurary settles in Warsaw
Summary: In 5685, R. Yechiel Tzvi Hirsch Gurary left Soviet Russia with his mother and brother and settled in Warsaw, joining the Chabad yeshiva leadership.
Story: R. Yechiel Tzvi Hirsch Gurary, son of R. Natan Gurary and son-in-law of the Radzyn Rebbe R. Mordechai Yosef Eliezer Leiner, left Soviet Russia in 5685 (1925). Together with his mother Esther and his younger brother Shneur Zalman, he settled in Warsaw. Immediately upon arrival he was appointed to the management board of the yeshiva, joining R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov and R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin at the head of Warsaw Chabad.
Tags: warsaw, yechiel tzvi gurary, leaving russia, radzyn

Title: Rabbi of Lipovets relocates to Kiev
Summary: At the end of 5685 the rabbi of Lipovets moved to Kiev, after which the local dayan filled the rabbinic role and the Yevsektsiya intensified its work.
Story: With the rav gone, a less stalwart replacement appeared in public debates with Yevsektsiya activists, and the position of religious Jewry in Lipovets weakened sharply. The Yevsektsiya summoned the new rabbinic representative to a public disputation in the town club, where he conceded much of the anti-religious argument. The author, then a youth, attended and was deeply shaken.
Tags: lipovets, kiev, rabbinate, ukraine

Title: Roster of 78 students compiled at Warsaw yeshiva
Summary: At the end of 5685 a detailed roster of 78 students of the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was compiled, recording family details, talents, and diligence.
Story: Toward the end of 5685, a list of 78 students of the Warsaw yeshiva was compiled and preserved in the archives. It included family details, abilities, and the diligence of each student, as well as the year each had been accepted, providing a record of the student body for the years 5682-5685. Of those listed, 54 were currently studying and 24 had already completed their studies.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, students, records, poland

Title: Sponsoring synagogue closes immediately after Jacobson's arrival
Summary: The small storefront synagogue that filed immigration papers to bring Jacobson to America closes the Sunday after his first Shabbos.
Story: The synagogue that had submitted the official request papers to bring Jacobson to America met in a rented storefront established by a small group of men. The Shabbos after his arrival he prayed there, but the very next day the synagogue closed permanently. This made clear that the shul had been founded specifically as a vehicle of divine providence to bring him to America.
Tags: america, new york, immigration, synagogue, divine providence

Title: Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva opens in Romny under R' Yani Gurarie
Summary: R' Shneur Zalman Yisroel Yaakov ('Yani') Gurarie arrived in Romny to open and head a Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva.
Story: Having earlier lived in Kremenchug, R' Yani Gurarie came to Romny in 5685 to establish an underground branch of Tomchei Tmimim during the Soviet anti-religious crackdown. The yeshiva operated for three years amid escalating harassment from the Yevsektsiya.
Tags: yani gurarie, shneur zalman gurarie, romny, tomchei tmimim, yeshiva, soviet union, chabad

Title: Warsaw Haggadah with Sfat Emet and Tiferet Shlomo commentaries
Summary: A Haggadah combining the 'Sfat Emet' (Yehuda Aryeh Leib of Gur) and 'Tiferet Shlomo' (Shlomo HaKohen of Radomsk) commentaries was printed in Warsaw.
Story: In 5685 (1925), a Haggadah featuring the 'Sfat Emet' commentary by Rebbe Yehuda Aryeh Leib Alter of Gur and the 'Tiferet Shlomo' by Rabbi Shlomo HaKohen, head of the Radomsk court, was issued in Warsaw by Yitzchak Meir Alter. The 83-leaf octavo edition was printed by Kupferstoch and Kramarsh. Leaves 2-4 apparently were never printed.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, gur, radomsk, warsaw, sfat emet, tiferet shlomo

Title: Kol Yisrael article exposes Tel Aviv municipality's pressure on Chabad cheder
Summary: R' Yaakov Malkov published an article in Kol Yisrael on 6 Tevet 5685 exposing the Tel Aviv municipality's hostility toward the Chabad cheder.
Story: After a donor offered to fund a building for the cheder, Malkov reported that the Tel Aviv municipality demanded either Hebrew-only instruction under municipal supervision, or a 40-pound permit fee. The municipality referred the matter to Ahad Ha'am, who refused to support the institution while it taught in Yiddish. Malkov framed this as religious persecution dressed in linguistic guise and a painful absurdity for Jewish life in Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: tel aviv, jaffa, torat emet, kol yisrael, yaakov malkov, dizengoff, yiddish, hebrew, ahad ha'am

Title: Rayatz petitions Soviet scientific council for library return
Summary: On 11 Shevat 5685, Rayatz petitions the scientific department council, again emphasizing his lawful ownership of the library now housed in the former Rumyantsev Museum.
Story: Rayatz describes how the library had been transferred from the former Kokorev warehouses to the museum about a year earlier and still sat in the original Lubavitch crates. He explains that since moving to Leningrad he now has both the space and the need to resume scholarly use of his collection. The appeal is structured around his earlier Narkompros authorization, which library administrators were claiming they could not locate.
Tags: library, soviet, leningrad, rayatz, russia

Title: Lenin Library refuses to return Schneersohn collection
Summary: On 2 Adar 5685, library administrators issue a refusal citing missing registration, scholarly value, and the advice of librarian Shmuel Eisenstadt.
Story: The refusal letter listed several pretexts: the owners had failed to register the library with the Narkompros libraries department; absent registration it had been handed to the Rumyantsev Museum; librarian Shmuel Eisenstadt had opined the books were of special importance and should not be returned; the library's Jewish section was poor and would be enriched by the collection; and the books would otherwise serve only a narrow circle. The real obstacle was that officials could not locate the 1921 Narkompros authorization. Eisenstadt, a Zionist who later emigrated to Eretz Yisrael, was identified as the personal antagonist behind the refusal.
Tags: library, soviet, lenin-library, eisenstadt, yevsektsiya

Title: GPO agents search author at Homel train station after Purim
Summary: In the week after Purim 5685 the author was detained and searched by GPO agents while boarding a train in Homel for Leningrad.
Story: As the author boarded a train in Homel headed to Leningrad in the week after Purim, two GPO agents signaled him to follow them. They led him to their building next to the station and searched his clothing, body, and belongings. Among the searchers was a man who himself had smuggled goods for him from Minsk, but they found nothing and he managed to catch his scheduled train.
Tags: soviet union, gpo, kgb, homel, russia, secret police

Title: Author arrives in Leningrad on 21 Adar to seek audience with the Rebbe
Summary: The author arrived in Leningrad on Tuesday 21 Adar 5685, traveling on behalf of R. Yisrael Magidsohn and to seek the Rebbe's guidance on his own emigration.
Story: The author arrived in Leningrad on Tuesday, 21 Adar. The Rebbe Rayatz was not present, having traveled to Moscow, and only returned home the following day, Wednesday. The author was traveling both as an emissary for R. Yisrael Magidsohn, who feared GPO surveillance after a search at his government workplace, and to receive the Rebbe's guidance on his own preparations to leave Russia.
Tags: leningrad, moscow, rebbe rayatz, yisrael magidsohn, 21 adar

Title: Yechidus appoints author mashpia in Homel and emissary to Rostov
Summary: On Thursday night after 21 Adar 5685 the Rebbe Rayatz instructed the author to serve as mashpia in Homel and to travel to Rostov for the 2 Nisan yahrzeit.
Story: In Thursday night yechidus the author first presented R. Yisrael Magidsohn's situation and then his own, and the Rebbe told him to begin preparations for the journey to America. The Rebbe also asked him to serve as mashpia in Homel for 40 rubles per month until his departure, regardless of his daytime occupation. Finally the Rebbe appointed him as emissary to travel to Rostov for the Rebbe Rashab's yahrzeit on 2 Nisan, which fell that year on Friday.
Tags: leningrad, homel, rostov, mashpia, yechidus, rebbe rayatz, rebbe rashab, yahrzeit

Title: Second yechidus: pidyonos and instructions for the Rostov Ohel
Summary: On Sunday before his trip the Rebbe Rayatz gave the author pidyonos to place at the Rebbe Rashab's Ohel and detailed instructions for handling the Rebbe's personal pidyon.
Story: At 6pm Sunday yechidus the Rebbe summarized the Shabbos maamar and gave the author a bundle of pidyonos to place at the Ohel. He instructed that his own pidyon be read only once, only at the Ohel, never copied or shown to anyone, with no leniency. The Rebbe also sent the author to his mother, Rebbetzin Shterna Sarah, who gave him a pidyon and details about their former Rostov home at Bradsky Pereulok 44.
Tags: leningrad, rostov, ohel, pidyon nefesh, rebbe rashab, yahrzeit, shterna sarah

Title: Author makes pilgrimage to Rostov Ohel for 2 Nisan yahrzeit
Summary: On Friday 2 Nisan 5685 the author visited the Rebbe Rashab's Ohel in Rostov as the Rebbe Rayatz's emissary, marking the fifth yahrzeit.
Story: Arriving in Rostov the author felt the city's emptiness, no longer the holy place that had drawn him in earlier years. He prayed Maariv with the local Temimim in the Rebbe's former home, where the absence of the tzaddik cried out from every corner. On Friday, the yahrzeit, he went to the Ohel and carried out the Rebbe Rayatz's instructions precisely, remaining in Rostov for Shabbos before returning home.
Tags: rostov, ohel, rebbe rashab, yahrzeit, 2 nisan, five year yahrzeit

Title: Marozov writes to Axelrod in Baltimore
Summary: Secretary Elchonon Dov Marozov wrote to Axelrod in Baltimore acknowledging a donation and reflecting on the spiritual oppression in Soviet Russia.
Story: On 2 Iyar 5685, secretary Elchonon Dov Marozov acknowledged receipt of three shekalim from a donor through Axelrod, who had by then emigrated to Baltimore. Marozov described how despite difficult material conditions in Soviet Russia they had celebrated Pesach with joy, lamenting that no acquaintance had bread or peace of mind. He praised Axelrod for having escaped 'the darkness here where the air is full of heresy and apostasy, enforced with a strong hand.'
Tags: marozov, axelrod, baltimore, soviet-union, kefirah, emigration

Title: Funeral of R' Moshe Eliezer Kremer; presidency passes to his sons
Summary: At his graveside on 6 Iyar 5685, the sons of R' Moshe Eliezer Kremer pledged to continue his work in Agudas Chasidei Chabad.
Story: At the cemetery on 6 Iyar 5685, before R' Moshe Eliezer Kremer was lowered into the grave, R' Mendel Leib Lukshin halted the burial to extract a handshake commitment from the sons that they would continue their father's work as leaders of Agudas Chasidei Chabad. As eldest, R' Chaim Zalman Kremer (CHZK) thereby inherited the presidency. The agudah's office remained behind the family's wholesale trouser shop on Broadway.
Tags: united states, agudas chasidei chabad, kremer, lukshin

Title: Eliyahu Shusterman travels to Rebbe Rayatz in Leningrad
Summary: For Shavuot 5685, Eliyahu Shusterman traveled to the Rebbe Rayatz in Leningrad intending to leave his shamash position in Zhlobin, but was instructed to remain.
Story: For Shavuot 5685 (1925) — the 'matzaim' holiday — Eliyahu Shusterman traveled from Zhlobin to Leningrad to see the Frierdiker Rebbe. He intended to leave his post as shamash and relocate to Kharkov. The Rebbe did not agree and instructed him to continue in the shamash role at the Karmer Shul in Zhlobin.
Tags: leningrad, rayatz, shusterman family, shamash, zhlobin

Title: Rebbe Rayatz sends maamar to Warsaw students from Russia
Summary: On 25 Iyar 5685, the Rebbe Rayatz sent the maamar 'Ein HaKadosh Baruch Hu Ba B'Truniya' from Russia to the students of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw, instructing them to learn it by heart.
Story: On 25 Iyar 5685, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote from Russia to the students of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw, sending them the maamar 'Ein HaKadosh Baruch Hu Ba B'Truniya Im Briyosav' as a gift, with instructions to study it and know it by heart. He urged them to strengthen themselves in Torah study, both nigleh and Chassidus, and in avodah of prayer and refinement of character, promising Heaven's help in rising spiritually and materially.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, warsaw, tomchei tmimim, maamar, russia, iyar, correspondence

Title: R. Israel Jacobson receives Soviet exit papers in Homel
Summary: On 15 Sivan 5685, Jacobson received his Soviet passport and set out from Homel with his family for Moscow en route to America.
Story: Jacobson's parents in America had sent him a rabbinic invitation from a synagogue in their Brooklyn neighborhood, which the U.S. consul in Riga needed to verify before issuing a visa. With the passport in hand, he boarded a carriage to the train station with his wife and daughters Chaya Sara and Rachel Dvasha, and was seen off at the station by Anash including his brother-in-law R. Aharon Eliezer and R. Zalman Chasdan. He traveled with French Line, hoping the company would extend him credit toward Riga since he still lacked the full ticket fare.
Tags: russia, homel, emigration, soviet-union, israel-jacobson, french-line

Title: Toras Emes purchases land in Givat Shaul
Summary: On 22 Sivan 5685 the Rayatz endorsed Havlin's plan to buy land in Givat Shaul for a permanent Toras Emes building.
Story: Havlin had raised an initial $3,000 toward the project, with the Rayatz's earlier approval. By 2 Shevat 5686 the land had been acquired and the Rayatz wrote back with congratulations, calling it a mazal tov.
Tags: jerusalem, toras emes, givat shaul, havlin, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes JDC philanthropists about settlements
Summary: On 25 Sivan 5685, the Rebbe wrote to the JDC board expressing concerns over the Russian resettlement project.
Story: This was among the Rebbe's earliest written interventions on the agricultural colonies. He raised concerns about religious services on the farms and the wisdom of forcibly moving Jews to Ukraine, and asked the JDC to support home-based industries instead.
Tags: jdc, rayatz, soviet-jewry, agricultural-colonies

Title: Letter to JDC qualifiedly endorsing agricultural colonies
Summary: The Rebbe acknowledges Dr. Rosen's colonies but warns of the missing religious infrastructure: mikvaot, teachers, shochtim, synagogues.
Story: Reading at a JDC board meeting in English translation, the Rebbe asked, 'What about the thousands who cannot work in agriculture, or move from their homes?' He urged the JDC to help them through urban home-based industry instead.
Tags: jdc, agricultural-colonies, russia, letter

Title: Rebbe writes qualified endorsement of agricultural colonies to JDC
Summary: While still in Russia, the Rebbe writes the JDC leadership in New York with a qualified endorsement of the Jewish agricultural colonies.
Story: He wrote, 'It was gratifying to hear from Dr. Rosen about the establishment of the agricultural colonies,' but raised concerns about the 'lack of attention to religious institutions, mikveh, teachers, shochtim, rabbis, synagogues.' He encouraged the JDC to also help the thousands who could not work in agriculture. The letter was translated into English and read at the JDC board meeting.
Tags: joint distribution committee, agricultural colonies, russia, letter

Title: Jacobson family crosses Soviet–Latvian border at Sebezh
Summary: At the end of Tammuz 5685, Jacobson and his family escaped Soviet Russia by train through Sebezh into Latvia.
Story: The crossing came at sunset, and only when Latvian officials and railway staff boarded the train did the family begin to grasp that they were physically out of the Soviet Union. Even then the dread of being seized back on some pretext lingered—it could not yet be felt in the heart that the escape from Bolshevik rule was real.
Tags: soviet-union, latvia, emigration, sebezh, border-crossing, israel-jacobson

Title: Jacobson family arrives in Riga
Summary: The Jacobson family arrived in Riga on Rosh Chodesh Menachem Av 5685, beginning a near five-month wait for an American visa.
Story: French Line first lodged them in an emigrant hotel and then moved them to a quarantine residence required for travelers transiting Latvia for overseas voyages. The U.S. consul in Riga—since Washington did not yet recognize the Soviet government—required at least six weeks to verify the authenticity of the Brooklyn shul's invitation before considering a visa.
Tags: latvia, riga, emigration, us-consulate, french-line

Title: R' Yisrael Jacobson arrives in Riga
Summary: R' Yisrael Jacobson arrived in Riga from Russia on Rosh Chodesh Menachem Av 5685, en route to the United States.
Story: On Rosh Chodesh Menachem Av 5685 (July 22, 1925), R' Yisrael Jacobson reached Riga as part of his journey out of Soviet Russia toward the United States. He was held there awaiting an American entry visa, and during his stay delivered chassidic discourses in the Bazaar Berg synagogue.
Tags: riga, latvia, emigration, russia, jacobson

Title: Daughter Chaya Sara hospitalized with scarlet fever in Riga
Summary: Jacobson's four-and-a-half-year-old daughter Chaya Sara fell ill with scarlet fever in early Elul 5685 and was confined to a Riga municipal hospital for six weeks.
Story: The American consul, on hearing of the contagion, warned that any entry to the consulate within three months would permanently void the visa. The municipal hospital had little warmth for Jewish refugees, so the parents could only visit at a window each day—including on Rosh Hashanah—bringing a hard-to-find orange and listening to their daughter beg to be taken home.
Tags: latvia, riga, illness, scarlet-fever, us-consulate, chaya-sara-jacobson

Title: Simchat Torah farbrengen with Riga Tmimim
Summary: On Simchat Torah 5686, Jacobson farbrenged in Riga with the local Tmimim and R. Mordechai Dubin, with hakafos running late into the night.
Story: The gathering included R. Mordechai Chefetz Hy"d, his brother R. Michoel Leib Hy"d, R. Tzvi Gor (son-in-law of the chazan R. M.M. Volosov), R. Yaakov Horowitz of Liepaja Hy"d, and R. Mordechai Dubin. The Riga Tmimim had also received the Rebbe Rayatz's Rosh Hashanah 5686 maamarim, which Jacobson learned with the local chavurah during his five-month stay.
Tags: latvia, riga, simchat-torah, farbrengen, tmimim, mordechai-dubin, mordechai-chefetz

Title: Letter to Agudas Harabonim on agricultural colonies
Summary: The Rebbe urges American Orthodox rabbis to lobby the JDC for religious infrastructure in the Soviet agricultural colonies.
Story: He asked them to ensure the colonies were provided 'with the religious institutions necessary for every Jew,' arguing that without synagogues, mikvaot, and schools, the resettlements would sever Jews from their tradition.
Tags: jdc, agudas-harabonim, agricultural-colonies, letter

Title: Rebbe writes Agudas Harabonim urging religious infrastructure in colonies
Summary: While still in Russia, the Rebbe writes the New York-based Union of Orthodox Rabbis urging them to lobby the JDC for religious institutions in the colonies.
Story: He pressed US rabbis to ensure the JDC 'provide the agricultural colonies with the religious institutions necessary for every Jew.' Without publicly criticizing the JDC, the Rebbe believed Jews would be far better served by remaining in the cities near family and community.
Tags: agudas harabonim, agricultural colonies, russia, letter

Title: Rebbe proposes home-based industries plan to JDC board
Summary: The Rebbe writes the JDC board proposing home-based industries for Russian Jews as an alternative to agricultural resettlement.
Story: He asked the JDC to provide Russian Jews with the tools, training, and financial support necessary to establish home-based factories and small businesses. This would give them greater economic freedom and allow the option of not working on Shabbat. The Rebbe argued such industries 'would provide the Jews with a respectable income and sense of dignity.'
Tags: joint distribution committee, russia, home industries, shabbat, letter

Title: Jacobson departs Riga for America on 19 Kislev
Summary: After his visa came through, Jacobson left Riga on motzaei Shabbat 19 Kislev 5686, taking leave during R. Mordechai Chefetz's 19 Kislev seudah.
Story: Mid-seudah at the shochet R. Mordechai Chefetz's home, Jacobson received parting blessings from his friends and set out via Kovno, Königsberg, Berlin, Paris, and Le Havre. A planned reunion in Berlin with his friend Alter Beilin—who held his own American visa and would later become his brother-in-law—failed because Beilin's departure was on a different schedule and neither yet knew how to easily locate the other in a foreign city.
Tags: latvia, riga, emigration, 19-kislev, chag-hageulah, mordechai-chefetz, alter-beilin

Title: R' Yisrael Jacobson departs Riga for America
Summary: R' Yisrael Jacobson left Riga on 19 Kislev 5686 after months of stays with the city's Chabad community.
Story: Mid-Yud-Tes Kislev Farbrengen on 5686 (December 6, 1925) at the home of the shochet R' Mordechai Chefetz, R' Yisrael Jacobson received parting blessings from his Riga friends and departed. He had spent several months in the city after leaving Russia, joining its tmimim for farbrengens and study of chassidus.
Tags: riga, latvia, jacobson, emigration, yud-tes-kislev

Title: Rabbi David Tzvi Hirsch Chen (the Radatz) passes away in Jerusalem
Summary: The Radatz, rabbi of Chernigov and grandfather of the poet Zelda, died on 24 Kislev 5686 in Jerusalem and was buried on the Mount of Olives.
Story: Rabbi David Tzvi Hirsch Chen, known as the Radatz, served as rabbi of Chernigov before emigrating to the Land of Israel and settling in Jerusalem. Less than a year after his aliyah he passed away on 24 Kislev 5686. He was buried on the Mount of Olives, leaving behind his daughter Rachel and granddaughter Zelda.
Tags: jerusalem, har hazeitim, chen family, chernigov, passing

Title: Jacobson family boards SS Paris at Le Havre
Summary: On the sixth night of Chanukah 5686, Jacobson and his family boarded the SS Paris at Le Havre for the Atlantic crossing to America.
Story: After about a week in Le Havre, the family embarked on Wednesday, the sixth Chanukah candle. The ship took on additional passengers via tender at an English coast before heading into open sea; Jacobson's wife was bedridden with seasickness from that stop onward, and elder daughter Chaya Sara also suffered, while a Friday-evening storm sent waves cresting over the ship's roof.
Tags: france, le-havre, ss-paris, chanukah, emigration

Title: Jacobson family arrives in America at Ellis Island
Summary: The Jacobson family reached the American shore on Tuesday 5 Tevet 5686 and were processed at Ellis Island.
Story: After the stormy Atlantic crossing on the SS Paris, the ship docked on 5 Tevet. All the passengers, Jacobson and his family among them, were transferred to Ellis Island for immigration processing—closing out a journey from Homel that had taken roughly six months by way of Moscow, Riga, Kovno, Königsberg, Berlin, Paris, and Le Havre.
Tags: usa, new-york, ellis-island, emigration, israel-jacobson

Title: Author's brother begins studying at Rabbi Morgenstern's yeshiva in Kiev
Summary: In the summer of 5686 Yosef left Lipovets for the Morgenstern yeshiva in Kiev, after his friend Mordechai Sternberg wrote that the yeshiva accepted bachurim from age 18.
Story: The yeshiva was headed by Rabbi Morgenstern under the oversight of Kiev's chief rabbi, Rav Chaim Matasov, and admitted only older bachurim. Yosef boarded with R' Shlomo Telingator in Podol, a Boyan chassid and old friend of the author's father. Soon a Komsomol infiltrator with a fake beard arrived at the (Litvish) yeshiva to corrupt the students.
Tags: kiev, yeshiva, morgenstern, matasov, sternberg, ukraine

Title: Boneh Yerushalayim published in Jerusalem
Summary: Boneh Yerushalayim, a collection of the Alter Rebbe's discourses, was published in Jerusalem in 1926.
Story: The 180-page Jerusalem 5686 (1926) printing extended publication of the Alter Rebbe's chassidic teachings to the Land of Israel.
Tags: alter rebbe, jerusalem, boneh yerushalayim

Title: Detailed yeshiva report sent to the Rebbe Rayatz in Leningrad
Summary: On 5 Chayei Sarah 5687, R. Shmuel Zalmanov sent a detailed report to the Rebbe Rayatz in Leningrad describing the organization and class structure of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw.
Story: Immediately upon assuming his role as general supervisor, Zalmanov reported in detail on yeshiva conditions to the Rebbe Rayatz, who was then living in Leningrad. The report described three divisions plus the main hall, with approximately 170 students, listing teachers, study material, and pedagogical structure. A follow-up report was sent on Parshas Va'eira covering academic progress through Kesubos daf 71.
Tags: warsaw, leningrad, tomchei tmimim, shmuel zalmanov, rayatz

Title: Elul 5686 Agudas HaTmimim meeting commits funds to print Likkutei Torah
Summary: In Elul 5686 the author convened Agudas HaTmimim at his home; members pledged to raise the funds needed to reprint Likkutei Torah in Warsaw.
Story: After receiving word from Warsaw that Likkutei Torah could be reprinted there for roughly six hundred dollars, the author hosted a meeting of Agudas HaTmimim in Elul 5686. Members pledged sums proportionate to their means — some five dollars, some ten. The amount still fell short of even a down payment, and serious progress only came months later with the Tevet seudah.
Tags: likkutei torah, warsaw, tomchei tmimim, fundraising

Title: Habima theater troupe departs Russia for tour
Summary: The Hebrew-language Habima Theater left the Soviet Union on a government-sanctioned tour and never returned.
