Story: Established in 1917 with state recognition, Habima had been a Yevsektzia target since Dimenstein protested its 1919 grant from the Soviet ministry of culture. The whole troupe departed in 1926 and relocated to Tel Aviv. In 1958 Habima became the official national theater of Israel.
Tags: habima, hebrew, zionism, yevsektzia, tel aviv

Title: Habima theater troupe leaves Russia
Summary: The Hebrew-language Habima theater departed on a government-sanctioned international tour and never returned.
Story: Habima had been founded in 1917 and received a government grant in 1919 over Yevesektzia leader Dimenstein's objections. After years of Yevesektzia harassment, the troupe relocated to Tel Aviv. In 1958 it became the official national theater of Israel.
Tags: habima, hebrew, yevesektzia, tel-aviv

Title: Jacobson accepted as rabbi of Anshei Bobruisk in Brownsville
Summary: After a two-week trial period, R' Yisrael Jacobson is hired as rabbi of the Anshei Bobruisk synagogue at 228 Christopher Street in Brownsville.
Story: Through the advocacy of fellow Zhuravichi townspeople including R' Zev Chaikin, and after R' Memel Lukshin spoke with R' Shneur Zalman Chavkin (deputy chair of the Brownsville branch), Jacobson was given a two-week trial period and then hired as rabbi. The parent society in Manhattan opposed hiring a rabbi due to one maskil member's objection, so his salary was paid directly by individual congregants and the Mishnayos study society rather than the official society. Members who initially opposed him gradually came to embrace him, attending his home and shul on Yud-Tes Kislev, Purim, and other festive days.
Tags: america, brownsville, new york, yisrael jacobson, anshei bobruisk, christopher street

Title: Jacobson becomes baal tokea at Anshei Bobruisk
Summary: Before the month of Elul, the Anshei Bobruisk congregants ask Jacobson to serve as their baal tokea, beginning a 24-year tenure in that role.
Story: Before Elul 5686, the congregants asked Jacobson to serve as their baal tokea, despite his protest that he had almost never blown the shofar before. After practicing and finding the task within his ability, he purchased a new shofar. He went on to serve as the shul's baal tokea for twenty-four years, until he eventually left the position.
Tags: rosh hashanah, shofar, baal tokea, brownsville, anshei bobruisk

Title: Jacobson moves into apartment at 204 Christopher Street
Summary: Shortly before Passover, R' Yisrael Jacobson rents an apartment at 204 Christopher Street near his Brownsville synagogue.
Story: Around Passover, Jacobson moved into an apartment at 204 Christopher Street near the Anshei Bobruisk synagogue, and later relocated to 276 Christopher Street. His father warned him that questions of kashrus on poultry — especially 'pakin' blemishes in the intestines — would arise before Pesach, particularly in Brownsville, which was then called 'the Jerusalem of America.' His father came frequently in those days to support him through the first such she'eilos.
Tags: brownsville, new york, yisrael jacobson, christopher street, passover

Title: R' Chaim Kavash receives rabbinic appointment in Yochavitch
Summary: In 5686 R' Chaim Kavash, a Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch alumnus, became rabbi of Yochavitch in the Polotsk district.
Story: After studying in Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch, R' Chaim Kavash was appointed rabbi of Yochavitch in the Polotsk district in 5686. As Soviet pressure on rabbis in small towns mounted, he fled first to Nevel and, when the Germans invaded, deeper into Russia to Samarkand.
Tags: chaim kavash, yochavitch, polotsk, russia, tomchei tmimim alumnus

Title: R' Yosef Rosen returns to Dvinsk rabbinate
Summary: The Rogatchover Gaon returned to Dvinsk in 5686 (1926) and resumed his rabbinate.
Story: After more than a decade in Russia, R' Yosef Rosen returned to Dvinsk in 5686 (1926) and resumed serving as rabbi of the city's Planover Minyan. He continued in that role until 5696 (1936).
Tags: dvinsk, rogatchover, rabbinate

Title: R. Boruch Ber moves yeshivah to Kamenitz
Summary: Rabbi Baruch Ber Leibowitz relocated his yeshivah from Vilna to Kamenitz.
Story: In 1926, Rabbi Baruch Ber Leibowitz moved Knesses Beis Yitzchak from Vilna to Kamenitz, where it would remain one of the leading Lithuanian yeshivas until the Holocaust.
Tags: baruch ber leibowitz, kamenitz, yeshivah

Title: R. Shmuel Zalmanov appointed chief supervisor of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw
Summary: At the start of 5687, R. Shmuel Zalmanov received a handwritten letter of appointment from the Rebbe Rayatz as general supervisor and coordinator of Nigleh studies across all branches of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva.
Story: R. Shmuel Zalmanov, then one of the senior students, was appointed by the Rebbe Rayatz to supervise and centralize the study of Nigleh in every division of the yeshiva and to test the students. Soon after, he was also given responsibility for administrative management, including organizing funding sources. He remained in this role until his marriage in 5693 (1933).
Tags: warsaw, poland, tomchei tmimim, shmuel zalmanov, rayatz

Title: Ramash hides from Bolsheviks in Luga
Summary: Fearing detention by the Bolsheviks, the Ramash took refuge for several months in the home of Rabbi Chanoch Henoch Etkin in Luga, on the outskirts of Leningrad.
Story: At the time the Ramash was engaged, the Bolsheviks began investigating him. He hid in Etkin's home for a few months, spending his time studying and learning Talmud daily with his host. Etkin had regular employment and was not harassed by the authorities.
Tags: luga, leningrad, russia, bolsheviks, etkin

Title: Rayatz records Rashab's prediction of Soviet collapse
Summary: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak recorded in his diary the prediction his father, the Rebbe Rashab, had made three weeks before his passing.
Story: The Rashab told his son there would be difficult times requiring actual self-sacrifice, but that the Communist government would eventually disintegrate. The fall of the Soviet Union in the early 1990s, and the flourishing of Chabad activity in its wake, was understood by Chasidim as the fulfillment of this prophecy.
Tags: rashab, rayatz, diary, prediction, communism, mesirat nefesh

Title: Shmuel Zalmanov begins teaching Chassidus to younger students
Summary: In 5686, R. Shmuel Zalmanov began giving Chassidus shiurim to younger students at Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw.
Story: By summer 5686, Zalmanov was noted as excelling in both Nigleh and Chassidus, studying Likkutei Torah with one group in the morning and Hemshech Ayin-Beis with the Tmimim in the evening. He reviewed Chassidus well and spent extended time in prayer, foreshadowing his later leadership roles.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, shmuel zalmanov, chassidus

Title: Tomchei Tmimim branch founded in Otwock
Summary: A preparatory branch of Tomchei Tmimim was founded in Otwock in 5686 (1926).
Story: Founded by R. Meir Blizinski shortly after his wedding, the Otwock branch opened after Pesach 5686 with three classes meeting at Beis Medrash Rindorf. It served as a feeder yeshiva for the central Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw, but lasted only one year before closing in spring 5687 (1927) due to funding cuts.
Tags: poland, otwock, tomchei tmimim, yeshiva ketana, branch

Title: Rebbe sends Zelig Slonim on first mission to England
Summary: In January 1926 the Rebbe dispatched Rabbi Zelig Slonim from Soviet Russia to England as his emissary to teach and inspire London Chasidim.
Story: While locked in spiritual combat with the Yevesektzia, the Rebbe still attended to overseas Chasidim. Slonim's mission included finding positions for Chabad rabbis and shochtim. He worked to install Rabbi Mordechai Gutnick at London's Nusach Ari synagogue despite congregational opposition, and the Rebbe coached him to bypass recalcitrant leaders by appealing directly to members.
Tags: england, london, slonim, shadar, nusach-ari, gutnick

Title: Rabbi Shalom Shlomo Schneersohn passes away in Jerusalem
Summary: Rabbi Shalom Shlomo Schneersohn, uncle of the Lubavitcher Rebbe and rabbi of Shiroka, died on 7 Shevat 5686 in Jerusalem.
Story: Rabbi Shalom Shlomo Schneersohn was the brother of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneersohn and served as rabbi of Shiroka before fleeing to Chernigov during the Russian Revolution. He later made aliyah with his father-in-law the Radatz but died on 7 Shevat 5686 in Jerusalem, less than a year after arriving. He was buried on the Mount of Olives, survived by his wife Rachel and daughter Zelda.
Tags: jerusalem, har hazeitim, schneersohn family, shiroka, passing

Title: R. Meir Blizinski marries on 1 Nisan
Summary: R. Meir Blizinski married on Rosh Chodesh Nisan 5686, the day he turned nineteen.
Story: In a letter dated 13 Shevat 5737 to his grandson R. S. Heber, Blizinski recalled marrying on Rosh Chodesh Nisan 5686 at age nineteen. Soon after, he moved to Otwock and resolved to establish a yeshiva there, which became the first Tomchei Tmimim branch outside Warsaw.
Tags: meir blizinski, poland, otwock

Title: Hilula farbrengen for Rebbe Rashab with Basi LeGani maamar
Summary: Anash gather at Tzemach Tzedek shul on 184 Henry Street for the Rashab's yahrzeit, where Jacobson delivers a Basi LeGani maamar sent from Russia by the Rayatz.
Story: Following instructions from the Rayatz, Anash held a farbrengen on 2 Nissan at the Tzemach Tzedek synagogue at 184 Henry Street to mark the yahrzeit of his father, the Rebbe Rashab. As a guest, Jacobson was honored to deliver chassidus and repeated the maamar 'Basi LeGani,' which the Rayatz had sent from Russia specifically to be studied by Anash on the yahrzeit that year. The maamar was very well received, and Anash from Brownsville subsequently began coming to Jacobson's own shul for Seudah Shlishis.
Tags: yahrzeit, rashab, rayatz, basi legani, tzemach tzedek shul, henry street, maamar, new york

Title: Wedding of R' M. Blizinski in Warsaw
Summary: R' M. Blizinski married on 2 Nisan 5686, shortly before the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim moved into its new building.
Story: On 2 Nisan 5686 (around mid-March 1926) R' M. Blizinski was married in Warsaw. He later recalled the date precisely in a 1977 letter to his grandson, noting that the wedding took place just before the yeshiva left Franciscan St. 8 and moved to its new building. The detail helped establish the exact timing of the yeshiva's relocation.
Tags: warsaw, blizinski, wedding

Title: Otwock yeshiva opens after Pesach with three classes
Summary: The Otwock yeshiva opened immediately after Pesach 5686 with three classes at Beis Medrash Rindorf.
Story: R. Meir Blizinski enlisted a local bachur named Naftali Tzuker, who already had a small study group, and added two additional classes. Blizinski personally taught Tanya nightly to the upper class while shouldering most of the budget from his dowry savings and the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim leadership.
Tags: poland, otwock, tomchei tmimim, naftali tzuker, shlomo tziley

Title: Rebbe Rayatz directs R' S. Z. Gurarie's course of study
Summary: On 27 Nisan 5686 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the young R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie laying out his study program at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw.
Story: On 27 Nisan 5686 (April 1926) the Rebbe Rayatz, writing from Petersburg, instructed the teenage R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie that his principal study was to be Talmud with deep iyun. He asked the boy to inform him in detail which tractates he knew, including Tosafot, so that the studies could be properly arranged. The letter is preserved in Igrot Kodesh vol. 11, letter 3795.
Tags: rebbe-rayatz, shneur-zalman-gurarie, warsaw, tomchei-tmimim, letter

Title: Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw moves to Mlawska 7 / Sapuzinski 17
Summary: In spring 5686 Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw moved to a three-story rented building at Mlawska 7 (corner Sapuzinski 17), where it remained for ten years.
Story: After Pesach 5686 the rapidly growing yeshiva — with nearly three hundred students drawn from Poland and abroad — left Franciscan Street and moved into a far larger leased building at Mlawska 7 / Sapuzinski 17. The three-story former flour-mill complex, fitted out as kitchen, dining hall, five large classrooms, dormitory attic and a prayer hall, was renovated with a grant from Mr. Bernhard Cohen of the Joint Distribution Committee's reconstruction fund. The yeshiva remained at this address until autumn 5696 (1935), when it relocated to Otwock.
Tags: warsaw, poland, tomchei-tmimim, yeshiva, joint-distribution-committee

Title: Agudas HaTmimim founded in Manhattan on Motzei Shabbos Shemini
Summary: On Motzei Shabbos Shemini 5686, Tomchei Tmimim alumni in America met at R' A. Simpson's home and founded Agudas HaTmimim.
Story: On the night of Saturday parshas Shemini 5686, the Tomchei Tmimim alumni then in America assembled at R' A. Simpson's residence at 137 W. 116th Street in New York and formally established Agudas HaTmimim. R' Yitzchak Sneiderman and the shochet R' Avraham Ram joined the society. Its early meetings focused on supporting Maamad Beis Chayeinu (sending one thousand dollars in one campaign), securing affidavits to bring Tmimim from Russia, and founding a properly observant cheder.
Tags: new york, tomchei tmimim, agudas hatmimim, simpson, anash

Title: Rayatz writes condolence letter on the passing of Rabbi Shalom Shlomo Schneersohn
Summary: The Rayatz wrote a letter of consolation from Leningrad on 4 Iyar 5686 to Rebbetzin Rachel Schneersohn after her husband's passing.
Story: Upon learning of the death of his relative Rabbi Shalom Shlomo Schneersohn, the Rayatz wrote a condolence letter on 4 Iyar 5686 to the widow Rebbetzin Rachel. He noted that he had not shared the news with his mother Rebbetzin Shterna Sarah to spare her grief, and offered prayers and blessings for the family's wellbeing.
Tags: leningrad, condolence, rayatz, schneersohn family

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes long letter to Felix Warburg
Summary: On 27 Iyar 5686, the Rebbe wrote a detailed letter to JDC chair Felix Warburg about the Russian settlements.
Story: Without expressing direct opposition, the Rebbe raised important questions about religious services and asked the JDC to provide three things: facilities and religious services in the settlements, training in home-based industries for urban Jews, and subsidies for rabbis. Warburg ultimately rejected the religious priorities.
Tags: jdc, warburg, rayatz, agricultural-colonies, soviet-jewry

Title: Rayatz writes Agudas HaTmimim in America accepting their offer to help recover books
Summary: On 12 Tammuz 5686, Rayatz writes to the newly founded Agudas HaTmimim 'Beis Rebbi' in the United States, welcoming their initiative to help recover the books taken from Moscow.
Story: Members of Agudas HaTmimim in America had informed Rayatz they had organized a society called 'Beis Rebbi' as a memorial to past Rebbes, whose aim was to help retrieve the books that had been improperly seized in Moscow. Rayatz responds with encouragement, urging them to consult lawyers and well-connected figures of standing and predicting that their effort would succeed with G-d's help.
Tags: library, rayatz, agudas-hatmimim, america, letters

Title: JDC report counts 15,000 children in secret schools
Summary: A confidential aide-memoire described the underground Jewish education system operating across the USSR.
Story: The confidential report sent to the JDC in New York stated that some fifteen thousand children were being educated in a growing number of secret schools. In Moscow alone, three hundred children studied in groups of three, hiding in cellars and venturing to the woods in summer. Each teacher was paid thirty rubles a month, with another thirty rubles paid to a watchman keeping lookout for authorities.
Tags: jdc, underground, report, moscow, secret schools

Title: Warsaw leadership absorbs Otwock yeshiva as Tomchei Tmimim branch
Summary: In Elul 5686, the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim hanhalah visited Otwock and formally adopted the yeshiva as a branch.
Story: R. Feivel Zalmanov, R. Zalman Shmuktin and R. Tzvi Gurary HY"D came to Otwock on a Shabbos in Elul 5686, informed the teachers the yeshiva was now Tomchei Tmimim Otwock, and planned to bring in around twenty out-of-town students. R. Chaim Meir Liss was sent as mashpia while Blizinski remained gashmi administrator handling salaries, lodging and meals.
Tags: poland, otwock, warsaw, feivel zalmanov, zalman shmuktin, tzvi gurary, chaim meir liss

Title: Rebbe Rayatz speaks on mesirus nefesh of Avraham Avinu vs. Rabbi Akiva
Summary: On Simchas Torah 5687 in Russia, the Frierdiker Rebbe explained to R' Yechezkel Feigin the distinction between Rabbi Akiva's and Avraham Avinu's approaches to mesirus nefesh.
Story: Just after Simchas Torah 5687, R' Yechezkel Feigin wrote to the author conveying what the Frierdiker Rebbe had told him: Rabbi Akiva sought mesirus nefesh as an opportunity to fulfill the verse, whereas Avraham Avinu sought to publicize Hashem's existence in the world — accepting prison or being thrown into a furnace only as incidental consequences of that mission. The statement framed the Rebbe's own underground work in Soviet Russia and foreshadowed his arrest months later.
Tags: simchas torah, russia, yechezkel feigin, mesirus nefesh

Title: Resignation of LERO religious minority in Leningrad
Summary: Ten religious board members resigned from LERO after discovering reforms to Jewish education and religious practice being implemented behind their backs.
Story: LERO had twenty-four board members split between traditionalists and modernizers; the majority secretly pushed reforms before being exposed. The ten resigning members convened at Leningrad's main synagogue, applied for recognition as a separate community, and confronted Rabbi Katzenellenbogen, who had been misled by Gurewicz.
Tags: lero, leningrad, reform, katzenellenbogen, gurewicz

Title: Ten religious members resign from LERO board
Summary: The traditionalist minority quit LERO after the reformist majority secretly implemented religious changes.
Story: The board of LERO had twenty-four members split between those wanting to retain classic Jewish education and those wishing to modernize. After reformers were exposed implementing unilateral changes, the ten religious members resigned in October 1926 accusing LERO of acting unethically. Weeks later they petitioned the government for recognition of a new religious organization.
Tags: lero, leningrad, schism, reformers

Title: Rebbe Rayatz instructs R' S. Z. Gurarie to study Mishnayot by heart
Summary: On 28 Tishrei 5687 the Rebbe Rayatz directed R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie to learn Mishnayot by heart, beginning with Seder Taharot.
Story: On 28 Tishrei 5687 (October 1926) the Rebbe Rayatz wrote again to R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie, instructing him to learn Mishnayot by heart starting from Seder Taharot. The pace was to be no more than one chapter every two days, with thorough memorization and calm review. The letter is found in Igrot Kodesh vol. 11, letter 3800.
Tags: rebbe-rayatz, shneur-zalman-gurarie, warsaw, mishnah, letter

Title: Korosten conference of rabbis
Summary: About one hundred rabbis convened in Korosten, Ukraine; though skeptical, the Rayatz was unanimously named honorary chairman.
Story: Led by Rabbi Zev Kipnis, the conference was government-sanctioned as a divide-and-conquer maneuver to weaken the Rebbe ahead of the Leningrad community conference. The Rebbe secretly sent the young Bentzion Shemtov to steer the agenda. When his telegram was read, the rabbis stood in respect; alarmed authorities later arrested Shemtov and Kipnis.
Tags: korosten, ukraine, rabbinical-conference, kipnis, shemtov

Title: Korosten rabbinical conference in Ukraine
Summary: Nearly one hundred rabbis gathered in Korosten; Rayatz was unanimously elected honorary chairman.
Story: The Rebbe was skeptical the conference would be productive but believed the noble intentions of organizer Rabbi Zev Kipnis would prevent harm. He dispatched Bentzion Shemtov to ensure an agenda strengthening Jewish education. When the Rebbe's telegram was read aloud, all the rabbis stood in respect — but the esteem displayed alarmed the Communist authorities, who had hoped the conference would divide Russian Jewry.
Tags: korosten, ukraine, rabbinical conference, shemtov, kipnis

Title: Rabbinical Conference in Korosten
Summary: The first rabbinical conference of the Korosten, Zhitomir and Shepetovka districts met in Korosten on 18-20 Cheshvan 5687 (26-28 October 1926).
Story: From 26 to 28 October 1926 (18-20 Cheshvan 5687), seventy-two Soviet-era rabbis convened in Korosten with about thirty additional unofficial participants — 101 men in all are numbered in the surviving group photograph. The official list of delegates includes communal rabbis from Malin, Korosten, Zhitomir, Ovruch, Berdichev and other towns, with guests from Kiev, Leningrad, Odessa, Vinnitsa and elsewhere; the photograph was first published by the author in 1989 in 'Toldot Chabad B'Russia HaSovietit.'
Tags: korosten, ukraine, soviet union, rabbis, communism, religious community

Title: Rebbe Rayatz blesses Tomchei Tmimim students for Yud-Tes Kislev
Summary: On 12 Kislev 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the students of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw with blessings for the upcoming festival of Yud-Tes Kislev.
Story: In a letter dated 12 Kislev 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz blessed the students of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw, along with their mashpi'im, mashgichim, and administrators, in advance of Yud-Tes Kislev. He invoked the path of the Rebbeim who had given their souls to disseminate Chassidus, and prayed they would elevate themselves and strengthen the world's pillars through Torah and mitzvos.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, rayatz, yud tes kislev, blessing

Title: Rayatz writes to Katzenellenbogen urging caution
Summary: The Rebbe asked the chief rabbi of Leningrad not to act unilaterally on plans for a national conference.
Story: Gurewicz had been traveling Russia falsely claiming the Rebbe's endorsement for a national congress. In a personal handwritten letter to Rabbi David Tevel Katzenellenbogen dated 23 Cheshvan 5687, the Rayatz wrote that the idea required further consideration and urged consultation with other rabbinic leaders. The chief rabbi was being misled by LERO's leadership.
Tags: katzenellenbogen, leningrad, conference, letter

Title: Rayatz letter to R' Eliyahu Simpson about library
Summary: In December 1926 the Rayatz wrote to Rabbi Eliyahu Simpson in New York reporting the books were still in the church building beside the former Rumyantsev (Lenin) Museum.
Story: Writing to a leader of the Lubavitch community in New York, the Rayatz confirmed the books were lodged in the ex-church annex of what had been the Rumyantsev Museum—now the Lenin Library—and that the Yevsektsia had failed to take them. He laid out a strategy for lobbying the Soviet government from the United States to compel their return.
Tags: library, rayatz, simpson, moscow, rumyantsev, lenin-library, new-york

Title: Toras Emes architectural plans approved by Rayatz
Summary: On 7 Tevet 5687 the Rayatz received and approved the detailed building plans for the Toras Emes yeshiva on its new Givat Shaul plot.
Story: He authorized Havlin to publicize the plans and solicit Anash and the broader Jewish community to fund the construction, promising spiritual reward to all donors. Despite the campaign and the cleared land, the building was never actually built.
Tags: jerusalem, toras emes, givat shaul, rayatz, construction, fundraising

Title: Rayatz urges American Tmimim to mobilize scholarly petition for library
Summary: On 21 Teves 5687, Rayatz writes Eliyahu Simpson with strategy for a coordinated international campaign of scholars and synagogues to pressure for library return.
Story: Rayatz reports that his books are currently housed in a former church attached to the Rumyantsev Museum (renamed for Lenin) and that the Yevsektsiya in Belarus has been falsely claiming the library was given to them in perpetuity. He outlines a plan to involve bibliophile associations, prominent scholars in the world of Jewish studies, and synagogue leadership writing to influential figures — particularly to a person whose intervention with Soviet authorities would carry weight — to formally request access to his library for scholarly work.
Tags: library, rayatz, agudas-hatmimim, america, rumyantsev-library, lenin-library, yevsektsiya, joint

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes about Yevsektsia bid for library
Summary: On 21 Tevet 5687 the Sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe wrote about reports the Yevsektsia in Belarus had been granted the Schneersohn library.
Story: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn (the Rayatz) addressed rumors that the Yevsektsia—the Jewish section of the Communist Party in Belarus—had received ownership of the Lubavitch library. He insisted the books were still held in Moscow and instructed his followers to keep pressing for their return.
Tags: library, yevsektsia, rayatz, soviet, belarus, moscow

Title: Alter Rebbe yahrzeit seudah on 24 Tevet 5687 launches Likkutei Torah reprint
Summary: On 24 Tevet 5687 the author held a seudah for the Alter Rebbe's hilula at which several hundred dollars were raised to begin printing Likkutei Torah.
Story: On 24 Tevet 5687 the author convened a seudah at his home in honor of the Alter Rebbe's yahrzeit; after delivering a maamar, he spoke before bentching about the Alter Rebbe, Likkutei Torah, and the Warsaw yeshiva's offer. Donors pledged on the spot in amounts of $25 and $50, raising several hundred dollars and finally enabling the print run. Total printing costs eventually reached over $800.
Tags: alter rebbe, likkutei torah, yahrzeit, fundraising, new york

Title: American Chassidim lobby for Rebbe Rayatz's release
Summary: Agudas Chassidei Chabad in America organized advocacy and fundraising to free the imprisoned Frierdiker Rebbe, working through Senator Borah in Washington.
Story: Once word of the arrest arrived in the U.S., the chevra gathered to plan a response. Attorney Kramer engaged Senator Borah, an influential American politician whose voice carried weight even abroad. The American community's organized strength was weak, however, and the fundraising effort fell short of the urgency — Avraham Dov Levin der Malach even denied the whole story, reasoning that anything printed in the newspapers must be false.
Tags: agudas chassidei chabad, usa, senator borah, lobbying, fundraising

Title: Anash in Vilna establish a Tomchei Tmimim branch at the Apatov shul
Summary: In early spring 5687, chassidim in Vilna moved to found a branch of Tomchei Tmimim inside the Apatov synagogue.
Story: The initiative is described in HaTamim issue 2, p. 133. It was driven by local Chabad askanim and would be staffed in time by figures including Eliyahu Weitz, Shneur Zalman Zeligson, Moshe Katzenelson and Chaim Shpreiregen. The Rebbe Rayatz responded with a letter of encouragement weeks after the project was launched.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, vilna, apatov, rayatz, lithuania

Title: Arrest and release of the Frierdiker Rebbe
Summary: The Frierdiker Rebbe was arrested and released during the summer of 5687.
Story: Schusterman recalls that the arrest and release of the Rebbe occurred during the summer of 5687, while he was studying in Suraz. The Suraz community was unaware of events at the time; Rabbi Axelrod may have known but feared to publicize it, as the Yevsektzia had begun operating in Suraz as well.
Tags: rayatz, frierdiker-rebbe, soviet, kgb, arrest, yevsektzia

Title: Arrest of Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: In 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz is arrested for his work strengthening Torah and Jewish observance in Soviet Russia.
Story: During the imprisonment, Rayatz worried in his cell about whether the manuscripts in his home would be seized by the authorities. Simultaneously, the future Rebbe — then his son-in-law — quickly distributed the manuscripts among trusted chassidim to hide them, returning them after the liberation. The episode is recorded in Rayatz's prison diary in Likutei Dibburim vol. 4 p. 1246.
Tags: rayatz, soviet, arrest, gpu, russia

Title: Arrest of Rebbe Rayatz with house search in Petersburg
Summary: In 5687, Soviet authorities arrested Rebbe Rayatz in Petersburg, conducting a house search where investigators examined manuscripts and antique books in the library.
Story: During the search, officials did not open the cabinets containing the Rebbeim's manuscripts but inquired whose handwriting they were. They showed particular interest in one cabinet of antique manuscripts including Livnat HaSapir by R' Avraham Saba and the Shemoneh Shearim by R' Shmuel Vital, plus first-edition printed books like the 1476 Ralbag and 1489 Ramban. The interest, however, was only superficial.
Tags: rayatz, arrest, petersburg, soviet, ussr, kgb, library, manuscripts

Title: Author begins importing Calabria esrogim to North America
Summary: At the start of 5688, the author launched what would become a multi-decade enterprise of importing Calabria esrogim to America for Sukkos.
Story: After Shavuos 5687 the author wrote to Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw and to R' Yechezkel Feigin in Riga, asking them to ship ten Calabria esrogim to America in time for Sukkos 5688. Six were taken by named recipients, four remained unsold because of cosmetic flaws. By 5689 he was importing twenty in individual cardboard boxes, and the operation grew from there — he later credited himself as the first to bring Calabria esrogim to the Western Hemisphere.
Tags: calabria, esrogim, warsaw, riga, trade, sukkos

Title: Author travels alone from Lipovets to study at the Kiev cheder katan
Summary: After Pesach 5687 the 14-year-old author traveled by wagon and train from Lipovets to Kiev to learn in the underground cheder katan run by R' Yaakov der Beker under R' Benyamin Gorodetzky.
Story: Reaching the Podol address of R' Shlomo Telingator (already departed for Eretz Yisrael), he was guided to Morgenstern's yeshiva, which refused him as underage at 14. He was instead accepted into the small Lubavitch yeshiva ketana effectively run by R' Yaakov der Beker, with Rabbi Benyamin Gorodetzky overseeing it from the Chabad shul on Shchekavitskaya St. R' Yaakov Konotoper served as his maggid shiur, teaching Perek HaMafkid.
Tags: kiev, lipovets, yeshiva-ketana, gorodetzky, podol, ukraine

Title: Avraham Padabranker studied at the Lithuanian yeshiva in Kiev
Summary: Avraham Padabranker learned at the Lithuanian yeshiva in Kiev led by Rabbi Morgenstern under Rabbi Mattasov of Podol.
Story: In 5687 (1926/27), Avraham Padabranker studied in Kiev at the Litvish yeshiva. The Rosh Mesivta was Rabbi Morgenstern, who served under the leadership of Rabbi Mattasov, the chief rabbi of Podol. Years later he was encountered in Chernigov, having held onto some connection to Yiddishkeit unlike many of his peers who broke under Soviet pressure.
Tags: kiev, ukraine, lithuanian-yeshiva, avraham-padabranker, rabbi-morgenstern, rabbi-mattasov, podol

Title: Breslov Haggadah 'Or Zoreach' arranged by Moshe Yehoshua Bzhilianski, killed in 1919
Summary: The Breslov Haggadah 'Or Zoreach' based on Rebbe Nachman's writings was published in Jerusalem, compiled by Moshe Yehoshua Bzhilianski (Alter of Teplik), who was killed sanctifying God's name in 1919.
Story: In 5687 (1927), the Breslov community in Jerusalem published the Haggadah 'Or Zoreach', based on the writings of Rabbi Nachman of Breslov and arranged by the late Moshe Yehoshua Bzhilianski known as Alter of Teplik, who was killed sanctifying God's name in 5679 (1919). The 53-page octavo edition brought Rebbe Nachman's distinctive interpretation of the Haggadah to a wide audience. It served as a foundational text for the Breslov Chassidic community.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, breslov, jerusalem, rebbe nachman, or zoreach, martyrdom

Title: Chabad library shipped from Russia to Latvia
Summary: When the Rebbe left Russia in 1927, he succeeded in exporting his library despite Soviet opposition.
Story: A Soviet investigator who understood the value of Jewish books urged the government to block the export. Mordechai Dubin arranged a second investigator who lacked such knowledge and authorized the license. The library, augmented in 1925 by a 5,000-volume collection from Shmuel Weiner, traveled with the Rebbe to Latvia, separate from the bulk stored in Moscow that the Soviets had refused to return.
Tags: russia, latvia, library, dubin, soviet-export

Title: Death of Shaina (Sania) Schusterman in Zlobin
Summary: The memoirist's sister Shaina (Sania) died young in summer 5687 (1927), prompting his parents to move to a new house in the center of Zlobin.
Story: After Shaina's untimely death in summer 1927, the memoirist's mother no longer wished to remain in the family home. The father bought a larger house in the center of Zlobin and went into debt as a result, leaving the family in difficult straits when the memoirist later took ill with pleurisy.
Tags: zlobin, schusterman family

Title: Epidemic in Zhlobin disrupts yeshiva studies in Surazh
Summary: At the end of summer 5687 a contagious disease in Zhlobin prevented the author and other boys from returning to the yeshiva ketana in Surazh founded by R. Moshe Axelrod.
Story: When R. Moshe Axelrod moved to Surazh and established a yeshiva ketana there, Eliyahu Shusterman had taken his son's entire class — seven boys, all under bar-mitzvah age — and brought them to study and board in Surazh. At the end of summer 5687 (1927) a contagious disease spread through Zhlobin and the boys could not return; they remained in Zhlobin, where Rabbi Binyaminsohn taught them Bava Metzia and the elderly R. Yitzchak Matles taught them Tanach and Hebrew grammar in the evenings.
Tags: zhlobin, surazh, epidemic, yeshiva ketana, moshe axelrod

Title: Felix Warburg visits the Soviet Union
Summary: The JDC chairman traveled to Russia, met the Rebbe and a delegation of rabbis twice, and toured the Jewish agricultural colonies.
Story: Warburg was impressed by Communist-staged farm towns named after him, Warburg-4 and Warburg-5, and returned a champion of forced collectivization. He promised the Rebbe help that did not materialize, and his biographer Ron Chernow later described the settlements as 'a bizarre hybrid of Park Avenue charity and Marxist agriculture.'
Tags: warburg, jdc, soviet-union, agricultural-colonies

Title: Founding of the small Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Suraz
Summary: Rabbi Moshe Axelrod founded a small yeshiva in Suraz upon assuming the rabbinate there, drawing seven students from Zlobin plus three locals.
Story: Schusterman's father brought seven twelve-year-old students from Zlobin, including the author, and arranged their lodging and meals. Three additional local students brought the total to ten. Rabbi Yeshaya Alewski, the shochet, served as magid shiur teaching Gemara Gittin. Axelrod insisted the boys read Torah publicly despite being below bar mitzvah age.
Tags: suraz, moshe-axelrod, tomchei-tmimim, yeshiva-katanah

Title: Founding of Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Vilna
Summary: In 5687 anash of Vilna founded the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva, with R. Shimon Noach Nimoitin on the executive committee.
Story: The Chabad community of Vilna established a branch of Tomchei Tmimim in 5687. R. Shimon Noach Nimoitin, the mashpia for Vilna and its environs, served as a member of the yeshiva's governing committee.
Tags: vilna, lithuania, tomchei-tmimim, yeshiva, shimon-noach-nimoitin

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe arrested by Soviet authorities in Leningrad
Summary: In 5687, the Frierdiker Rebbe was arrested in Soviet Russia for his clandestine work to strengthen Yiddishkeit, an event that reverberated through Chabad communities worldwide.
Story: News of the arrest reached America only with significant delay. American Chassidim were caught off-guard and largely unaware of the mortal danger — they had not lived under the Soviet terror firsthand. Attorney Mr. Kramer turned to Washington through Senator Borah, who carried influence with the U.S. government and across the Atlantic, to seek the Rebbe's release.
Tags: russia, soviet union, kgb, leningrad, imprisonment

Title: Kazarnovsky family emigrates from Russia to USA
Summary: After several years in Russia, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky and family emigrated to the United States in 5687.
Story: In 5687, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky and his family emigrated from Russia to the United States. They first settled in Rochester, New York, where he served as rabbi of the Ein Yaakov synagogue, before moving to New York.
Tags: kazarnovsky, emigration, russia, usa, rochester

Title: Leipzig facsimile of the Darmstadt Haggadah manuscript
Summary: A facsimile of the Darmstadt Haggadah manuscript was published in Leipzig with a separate text volume edited by Bruno Italianer.
Story: In 5687 (1927) and 5688 (1928), a facsimile of the Darmstadt Haggadah manuscript was issued in Leipzig in two volumes. The text-volume — featuring introduction and German commentary by Bruno Italianer — was 313 pages, while the facsimile-volume issued the following year reproduced 56 leaves of the original manuscript. Together they constituted one of the major early 20th-century scholarly publications of an illuminated medieval Haggadah.
Tags: haggadah, facsimile, leipzig, darmstadt, manuscript, italianer

Title: Levin leaves to learn at Kiev yeshiva
Summary: In summer 1927 the fifteen-year-old Yisrael Yehuda Levin traveled to Kiev to study in yeshiva, where he first learned of the underground Tomchei Tmimim network.
Story: This trip marked the start of a decade of wandering through Soviet underground yeshivos. Levin would move between Vitebsk, Pereyaslav, Kiev, Baku, Kutaisi, Kulashi, Moscow, Chernigov, Malachovka, Leningrad, Voronezh, Krivoy Rog, and Kharkov as yeshivos were repeatedly shut down by the secret police. He lived without proper papers or with forged ones.
Tags: kiev, yeshiva, tomchei tmimim

Title: R' Mordechai Dubin secures Rebbe Rayatz's exit visa via Latvian parliament
Summary: R' Mordechai Dubin used Latvia's swing vote on recognizing the Soviet government to negotiate the Frierdiker Rebbe's release from Russia together with his manuscripts and library.
Story: Newly independent Latvia operated as a democratic parliament whose vote on Soviet recognition was finely split. R' Mordechai Dubin, an Agudas Yisroel delegate with influence over several non-Jewish parliamentarians, traveled to Russia and promised that if the Rebbe were permitted to leave, he would help deliver Latvian recognition. After the Rebbe insisted at the Ohel in Rostov that he would not leave without his ksavim and seforim, Dubin returned and secured that concession as well.
Tags: latvia, soviet union, agudas yisroel, mordechai dubin, diplomacy

Title: R' Shmuel Schneiderman, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky, and Chazzan Shmuel Kantroff arrive in USA
Summary: Over the years 5686–5688, several Lubavitcher Tmimim including R' Shmuel Schneiderman, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky, and Chazzan Shmuel Kantroff arrived in America.
Story: During the period 5686–5688, a small wave of Tmimim reached the United States. R' Schneiderman settled in Philadelphia and remained there until his passing in 5715. Chazzan Kantroff moved between several towns before settling in Brooklyn, and R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky took a rabbinic position in Rochester before eventually being recruited as secretary and director of Agudas Chassidei Chabad.
Tags: usa, philadelphia, rochester, tmimim, immigration

Title: R' Yaakov Landa leaves Russia and settles in Libau
Summary: R' Yaakov Landa left Soviet Russia at the start of 5688 and settled with relatives in Libau.
Story: At the beginning of 5688 (1927), R' Yaakov Landa exited Soviet Russia, where he had served as rabbi in the Rebbe Rashab's court in Rostov and headed Tiferes Bachurim in Moscow. He settled with relatives in Libau (Liepaja), Latvia, with the Rebbe Rayatz personally directing him to assess the local community's needs.
Tags: libau, liepaja, latvia, landa, emigration, russia

Title: R' Yosef Blumenfeld receives rabbinical ordination
Summary: R' Yosef Blumenfeld received semicha for the rabbinate in 5687, with the ordination noting he was Rosh Mesivta in Warsaw.
Story: R' Yosef Blumenfeld received his rabbinical ordination in 5687 (1927), which was later printed at the beginning of his commentary on the Kaftor VaFerach. The semicha noted that he had served as Rosh Mesivta in Warsaw.
Tags: yosef blumenfeld, semicha, warsaw, rabbinate

Title: Rabbi Binyaminson accepts the Zlobin rabbinate
Summary: Rabbi Yerachmiel Binyaminson came from Shtchedrin to serve as rabbi of Zlobin after gaining the elder rabbi's consent, ending factional strife in the town.
Story: Binyaminson refused to enter a town divided by factional 'sides.' He first visited the elder Rabbi Wilda for his blessing, declaring he would not come if opposed. The elder rabbi agreed, the factions dissolved, and the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote praising the peace established (Sefer HaMaamarim 5687, supplement p. 269). Schusterman's father served as matchmaker for the arrangement.
Tags: zlobin, yerachmiel-binyaminson, shtchedrin, rabbinate, peace

Title: Rabbi Moshe Axelrod leaves Zlobin for Suraz
Summary: Rabbi Moshe Axelrod, the young Chasidic rabbi of Zlobin, left in 5687 to accept the prestigious rabbinate of Suraz.
Story: Axelrod had filled the position of his brother-in-law Rabbi Menachem Mendel Dubrawsky in Zlobin. The Frierdiker Rebbe wrote a letter of blessing upon his acceptance of the Suraz rabbinate, noting that 'from of old, men of name have sat there.' His departure opened the way for Rabbi Yerachmiel Binyaminson to come to Zlobin.
Tags: zlobin, suraz, moshe-axelrod, rabbinate, rayatz

Title: Rashab publishes diary entries after leaving Soviet Union
Summary: After leaving the Soviet Union, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn began publishing his diary entries with chasidic history and lore.
Story: In 1927, after leaving the Soviet Union following his arrest and death sentence, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn began publishing the diary entries he had been compiling since his youth in Lubavitch. He had been writing down stories, chasidic lore, and customs heard from Chasidim and his father from a young age, encouraged by his teacher Reb Nissan. These publications became foundational sources for chasidic history and tradition.
Tags: soviet union, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, diary, publication, chasidic history

Title: Rayatz arrested in Leningrad; manuscripts hidden by chassidim
Summary: During his 1927 arrest in Leningrad, the Rayatz distributed bundles of chassidic manuscripts to his followers for safekeeping.
Story: When Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was arrested by Soviet authorities in 1927, he entrusted manuscript bundles (bichlach) to several chassidim to conceal until the danger passed. The Seventh Rebbe later clarified that the manuscripts were returned almost immediately and that authorities had not, in fact, formally confiscated them.
Tags: rayatz, leningrad, soviet, arrest, manuscripts, bichlach

Title: Rayatz arrested, sentenced to death, exiled, and expelled from Russia
Summary: After establishing yeshivas in Bukhara, the Rayatz was arrested by Soviet authorities, sentenced to death, exiled to Kostroma, and forced to leave Russia for Latvia.
Story: Soviet secret police arrested the Rayatz for his clandestine religious work, initially sentencing him to death. International pressure commuted the sentence to exile in Kostroma and ultimately expulsion from the USSR. He departed for Riga, Latvia, where he would establish his next base of operations.
Tags: soviet union, kgb, gpu, arrest, exile, kostroma, latvia, bukhara

Title: Rayatz leaves Soviet Russia for Riga
Summary: At the end of Tishrei 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz leaves Soviet Russia and settles in Riga, Latvia.
Story: Forced out at the beginning of 5688 after his imprisonment and exile, Rayatz immediately resumed efforts to recover the library — now from outside Russia. On Rosh Chodesh Marcheshvan he wrote to the Soviet embassy in Latvia formally requesting their support in returning the books to him. The Soviet ambassador in Riga promised to intercede, but no concrete result followed in the short term.
Tags: rayatz, soviet, riga, latvia, russia, emigration

Title: Rayatz's St. Petersburg arrest and death sentence
Summary: Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was arrested in St. Petersburg and sentenced to death, eventually freed due to international Jewish pressure.
Story: In 1927, Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was arrested in St. Petersburg and held at the notorious Shpalerka Prison, where Soviet authorities sentenced him to death for his religious activities. World Jewry mounted significant international pressure on the Soviet government, ultimately securing his release. This seventh and final arrest marked the climax of his confrontations with anti-religious authorities in Russia.
Tags: st. petersburg, leningrad, soviet union, arrest, death sentence, shpalerka prison, communism, yosef yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Rebbe arrives in Riga with library
Summary: At the start of 5688 the Frierdiker Rebbe left Russia for Riga, bringing the Wiener library and his manuscripts.
Story: After protracted negotiations and intercession by Dr. Cohen of Berlin and Mordechai Dubin, the Soviet government permitted Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak to emigrate at the beginning of 5688 together with all his printed books and manuscripts. He settled in Riga and began rebuilding his life in exile, still burdened by emigration debts and without permanent quarters.
Tags: riga, latvia, russia, rayatz, library, emigration

Title: Rebbe Rayatz announces plan to visit Warsaw yeshiva
Summary: On the first night of Chanukah 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote that he intended to visit Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw, no earlier than the month of Shevat.
Story: Following the visit of R. Yisrael Pinchas to Riga, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote on the first night of Chanukah 5688 that he planned to visit Tomchei Tmimim of Warsaw. He stated his intention to travel no earlier than the upcoming month of Shevat, beginning preparations for the journey from Riga.
Tags: warsaw, riga, tomchei tmimim, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrested and exiled to Kostroma
Summary: In summer 5687 the Rebbe Rayatz was arrested by Soviet authorities and exiled to Kostroma.
Story: R. Eliyahu Chaim Altheuse accompanied the Rebbe into Kostroma exile, and when the Rebbe later left Russia and settled in Riga, Altheuse left with him. The arrest is referenced as background to Altheuse's lifelong devotion to the Rebbe.
Tags: rayatz, kgb, yevsektsia, kostroma, arrest, soviet

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrested by Soviet authorities
Summary: In the summer of 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz was arrested by Soviet authorities and sentenced to exile.
Story: In summer 5687 (1927), the Rebbe Rayatz was arrested by the Soviet regime. He was sentenced to exile in 'eretz gezeira' before being released on 12 Tamuz. The arrest and subsequent release set in motion his emigration from Russia later that year.
Tags: soviet union, rayatz, arrest, kgb, russia

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrested, exiled, and forced to leave Soviet Russia
Summary: In 5687 Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was arrested by Soviet authorities, sentenced to exile, released, and forced to leave Russia.
Story: In 5687 (1927) the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, was arrested by the Soviet GPU for his work to preserve Jewish life under communism. After being sentenced, his sentence was commuted and he was eventually freed and ordered out of the country. He refused to leave without his library, and only after firm insistence was he permitted to take his collection with him as he relocated the center of Chabad to Riga.
Tags: rayatz, soviet, arrest, exile, russia, riga, library

Title: Rebbe Rayatz emigrates from Russia to Riga
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz left Soviet Russia for Riga in 5688, bringing the family library with him.
Story: Following his arrest and release, the Rayatz emigrated from the Soviet Union to Riga, Latvia, in 5688 (late 1927). He carried with him the books and manuscripts saved from Rostov and Leningrad, continuing to safeguard the inheritance of the Chabad Rebbeim through political upheaval.
Tags: russia, riga, latvia, library, rayatz, emigration

Title: Rebbe Rayatz invited to settle in Warsaw upon leaving Russia
Summary: At the end of Tishrei 5688, immediately upon the Rebbe Rayatz's exit from Russia, the leaders of the Chassidic community in Warsaw invited him to settle there, but he declined.
Story: Upon leaving Russia at the end of Tishrei 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz was invited by Warsaw's Chassidic leaders to take up residence in the city. He replied that various weighty reasons made this impossible, but expressed his intention to visit Warsaw at a designated future time.
Tags: warsaw, russia, rayatz, emigration

Title: Rebbe Rayatz leaves Russia
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz was forced to leave the Soviet Union at the beginning of 5688, settling first in Riga.
Story: At the start of 5688 (late 1927), the Rebbe Rayatz was compelled to leave the Soviet Union. He resided for several years in Riga before later relocating his household to Warsaw and then Otwock.
Tags: rayatz, russia, riga, soviet-union

Title: Rebbe Rayatz released from Soviet imprisonment and exile
Summary: In summer 1927, the Rebbe Rayatz was released from Soviet imprisonment and exile but faced ongoing danger of re-arrest.
Story: After his arrest and exile in Soviet Russia in summer 1927 (5687), Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was freed but remained under threat of further imprisonment. The danger compelled him to seek to leave Russia as quickly as possible. Latvian parliament deputy Mordechai Dubin worked through the summer to secure his exit visa by arranging his appointment as Chief Rabbi of Riga.
Tags: russia, kgb, soviet, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, imprisonment

Title: Rebbe Rayatz requests detailed report on Warsaw yeshiva
Summary: On 25 Marcheshvan 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the yeshiva director R. Shmuel Feivish Zalmanov requesting a detailed report on the state of Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: About a month after declining to relocate to Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the yeshiva administrator requesting that his son Shmuel write a thorough, organized account of the yeshiva's condition. He emphasized his strong desire to know every detail of the institution's affairs.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, rayatz, correspondence

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes a postcard from prison
Summary: During his summer 5687 imprisonment, Rebbe Rayatz was allowed to send one censored postcard home.
Story: While held in his Soviet prison cell in summer 1927, Rebbe Rayatz was permitted to send a single postcard home in Russian, after censorship review. The card survives in the library archive.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, imprisonment, soviet union, kgb

Title: Sixth Rebbe departs Russia after Simchat Torah in Leningrad
Summary: The sixth Rebbe departed Russia in 1927, the day after Simchat Torah in Leningrad, in a memory Mendel Futerfas would invoke from a Soviet interrogation cell two decades later.
Story: Futerfas's last sight of the Rebbe was at the Simchat Torah gathering in Leningrad in 1927. When facing Soviet interrogation on 17 Iyar 5707, he conjured that image and mentally composed a letter requesting a blessing — to which, by mystical coincidence, the Rebbe in New York responded that very day.
Tags: rayatz, leningrad, russia, simchat torah, mendel futerfas

Title: Tomchei Tmimim branch founded in Vilna
Summary: A Tomchei Tmimim branch was founded in Vilna in 5687 (1927).
Story: The Vilna branch joined a growing network of provincial Tomchei Tmimim preparatory yeshivos feeding into the central yeshiva in Warsaw. It would become one of the longest-lasting and most prominent branches, eventually serving as the refuge point when Polish branches collapsed at the outbreak of WWII.
Tags: lithuania, vilna, tomchei tmimim, branch

Title: Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva founded in Vilna
Summary: Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva was established in Vilna less than a year before the Rebbe's first visit there in Adar 5688.
Story: A branch of the Chabad Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was established in Vilna, then under Polish rule, in the period prior to Adar 5688. The Rebbe Rayatz visited the yeshiva during his first trip to Lithuania, addressing the students at the Apatov shul where it was housed.
Tags: vilna, lithuania, tomchei tmimim, yeshiva

Title: Lenin Library again refuses to return Schneersohn books
Summary: In February 1927 the Lenin Library denied a formal request to return the Schneersohn books, despite an authorized return permit.
Story: After lawyer Orinson prepared a formal certificate authorizing the books' return on the grounds they had been improperly seized, the library claimed the document had been lost and refused to act on it. The Rayatz reported the rejection in correspondence to followers in New York.
Tags: library, rayatz, lenin-library, moscow, soviet, orinson

Title: Rayatz nearly arrested at Moscow hotel
Summary: A Yevesektzia officer hunted the Rebbe at his Moscow hotel; he was smuggled out the kitchen entrance and hidden at a second hotel.
Story: Traveling secretly to meet JDC representatives, the Rebbe was spotted on the train by Mark Semyonovitch Bashkov, a senior OGPU member of Belorussian-chasidic descent. A friendly hotel manager warned the Rebbe at midnight and relocated him. Days later, Yevesektzia officer Krotov burst into the new room to arrest him, but Bashkov's OGPU credentials drove the agents off.
Tags: moscow, yevesektzia, ogpu, bashkov, jdc

Title: Yevsektzia raid foiled at Moscow hotel
Summary: A Yevsektzia officer's attempt to arrest the Rayatz at a Moscow hotel was thwarted by a senior OGPU official.
Story: The Rebbe had traveled to Moscow under tight secrecy to meet JDC representatives. After being smuggled between hotels, he met with Mark Semyonovitch Bashkov, an OGPU executive board member he had encountered on the train. When Yevsektzia officer Krotov burst in with armed men, Bashkov produced his credentials — and the would-be arresters 'stood like blocks of wood, as if thunderstruck' and fled.
Tags: moscow, ogpu, bashkov, yevsektzia, krotov

Title: Daughters of Elchonon Morozov arrested for Zionism
Summary: Rachel and Sara Morozov were arrested in Leningrad on charges of belonging to the Zionist organization Dror.
Story: While imprisoned, the sisters learned of their father Elchonon Morozov's own arrest and declared a hunger strike until his treatment improved. On the fifth day he was moved into a cell with Zionist prisoners.
Tags: morozov, leningrad, zionism, dror, secret-police

Title: Morozov's Zionist daughters arrested in Leningrad
Summary: Rachel and Sara Morozov were arrested for belonging to the Zionist organization Dror.
Story: Rabbi Elchonon Morozov's two daughters were drawn from religious observance by the lure of secular Zionism. They were arrested on February 9 for activities in Dror, weeks before their father was also seized. When they learned their father was being mistreated in prison, they declared a hunger strike until his conditions improved.
Tags: morozov, leningrad, zionism, dror, arrest

Title: Rayatz reflects on father's 1920 predictions in Moscow diary entry
Summary: On 10 Adar Alef, while harassed in Moscow by the Yevesektzia, the Rayatz wrote in his diary about his father's prophetic predictions.
Story: The Rayatz woke at 3 a.m. troubled by events in Moscow. After reflecting on the 1920 meeting with his father about the new regime and its leaders' fates, 'I went back to sleep, and my soul was relaxed.' These predictions endowed him with fortitude during the darkest times of Soviet persecution.
Tags: rayatz, moscow, yevsektsia, diary

Title: Elchonon Morozov arrested in Leningrad
Summary: The Rayatz's secretary and chief underground coordinator was arrested, initially accused of attempting to smuggle the Rebbe's books abroad.
Story: Before being taken away, Morozov handed the list of underground yeshivot and schools to his eleven-year-old son. Jailed with hardened criminals, in May he was indicted for helping Jews cross the border illegally, sentenced to three years' exile, and deported to Krasnoyarsk. Rabbi Feigin called the arrest 'terrifying and ominous' for the network.
Tags: morozov, leningrad, underground, krasnoyarsk, exile

Title: Rabbi Elchonon Morozov arrested
Summary: The Rebbe's chief secretary and key underground coordinator was jailed, initially accused of smuggling books abroad.
Story: Morozov was held with the worst political prisoners, creating an ominous atmosphere among the Chabad community. Before being taken, he secretly handed the list of underground yeshivas and schools to his eleven-year-old son, who hid it without the police noticing. In May 1927 he was indicted for helping Jews cross the border illegally and sentenced to three years exile in Krasnoyarsk.
Tags: morozov, leningrad, underground, arrest, siberia

Title: Bentzion Shemtov arrested in Kharkiv
Summary: Following the Korosten conference, Shemtov was detained in Korosten and held in Kharkiv until Passover.
Story: Secret police had uncovered his role at the conference and his organizing across Ukraine's Volhynia region. He was released after about a month, only to be arrested again in Kharkiv in June on the same day the Rebbe himself was arrested in Leningrad.
Tags: shemtov, kharkiv, korosten, secret-police

Title: Fiery Purim farbrengen against the Yevesektzia
Summary: At a mid-March Purim farbrengen in Leningrad, the Rayatz publicly mocked and defied the Yevesektzia in the presence of their spies.
Story: The Rebbe screamed that the Yevesektzia did not frighten him and urged Chasidim to defy the regime to the point of self-sacrifice rather than send children to Communist schools. He told one Chasid that if confronted with the choice of a bonfire or yielding his child, he should accept the flames. Chasidim and informers alike sensed that retribution was imminent.
Tags: leningrad, purim, farbrengen, yevesektzia

Title: Rayatz holds defiant Purim farbrengen in Leningrad
Summary: The Rebbe screamed defiance at the Yevsektzia during a fiery Purim gathering filled with informants.
Story: Rabbi Zalman Duchman described the farbrengen as 'terrifying.' The Rayatz shouted, 'Who is the Yevsektzia? A rabbi's son? A butcher's son? I am not frightened by them!' He urged Chasidim to spread Judaism with self-sacrifice, telling one follower: 'Zalman, if they ever build a bonfire and confront you with the choice of yielding your child to their schools or casting yourself into the flames, let yourself be cast into the flames!'
Tags: purim, leningrad, yevsektzia, farbrengen, spies

Title: Shemtov arrested after Korosten conference work
Summary: Bentzion Shemtov was arrested in Korosten and held in Kharkiv for a month until Passover.
Story: The secret police had discovered Shemtov's activities and his role at the Rabbinical Conference. After release at Passover, he was detained again in June on the same day the Rebbe was arrested in Leningrad. He was held for another thirty days and grilled about the clandestine Chabad system before being released pending trial.
Tags: shemtov, korosten, kharkiv, underground

Title: Secretariat letter recounts collapse of Moscow library negotiations
Summary: On 27 Adar Rishon 5687, the secretariat letter (Iggeres 3806) details how Eisenstadt and the library board ultimately denied the return.
Story: The letter recounts that Rayatz had again obtained a Narkompros authorization through the prominent attorney I. S. Orinson, but when emissary R. Chaim Manesson came to collect the books, library staff confiscated the permit and stalled, eventually claiming the document was lost. When Orinson tried again, no new permit was forthcoming. After more than three years, the library board declared the books were now their property. Eisenstadt — described as acting from personal vengeance against the Rebbe's known anti-Zionist stance — was identified as the driving force.
Tags: library, soviet, moscow, rumyantsev-library, eisenstadt, yevsektsiya

Title: Rebbe Rayyatz urges restoring Tel Aviv cheder as Torat Emet branch
Summary: On 3 Adar Sheni 5687 the Rebbe Rayyatz wrote lamenting the decline of the Tel Aviv cheder and urging its reorganization as a Torat Emet branch.
Story: Responding to a report about the diminished state of the Tel Aviv cheder, the Rebbe expressed sorrow that financial shortfall had shrunk the institution. He emphasized that the original plan was for Torat Emet to plant branches in every city in Eretz Yisrael, and asked the new local manager R' Uri to formally re-establish the Tel Aviv cheder as a branch of Torat Emet under Jerusalem's direction.
Tags: tel aviv, jaffa, torat emet, rayyatz, chinuch

Title: Leningrad conference announced for October
Summary: Just after Passover, the Leningrad community publicly scheduled its long-debated national Jewish congress.
Story: Despite the Rebbe's opposition, LERO pressed ahead with plans for an October conference. The plan was secretly backed by the Yevsektzia, who saw it as a chance to create alternative leadership and divert JDC funds away from the Rebbe's network. With Moscow and Minsk withholding approval, the scheme faltered — making drastic action against the Rebbe a matter of time.
Tags: leningrad, lero, gurewicz, conference, yevsektzia

Title: Leningrad conference of Russian Jewish communities announced
Summary: Just after Passover, LERO announced that its national Jewish congress would convene that October.
Story: Despite Gurewicz's traveling lobbying campaign, the major communities of Moscow and Minsk withheld approval, following the Rebbe's lead. The Yevesektzia, secretly backing the plan, intended to use the new lay-led structure to bypass the Rebbe and divert JDC funding away from his network.
Tags: lero, leningrad, congress, gurewicz, yevesektzia

Title: Otwock branch closes after one year
Summary: The Otwock branch closed before Pesach 5687 after the American Relief organization cut funding to Polish yeshivos.
Story: By spring 5687 the Relief organization had stopped supporting Polish yeshivos, claiming Polish Jewry could sustain them itself. Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim could only fund a reduced two-class operation in Otwock with lowered salaries; Blizinski withdrew, and no Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva existed in Otwock until the central yeshiva relocated there in 5696 (1936).
Tags: poland, otwock, tomchei tmimim, relief, funding crisis

Title: Anash in Vilna write to Rebbe Rayatz proposing Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva
Summary: On 13 Nisan 5687, Chabad chassidim in Vilna wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz in Leningrad asking his blessing to establish a Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in the Apatow Shul.
Story: In early Nisan 5687, Anash of Vilna were inspired to found a branch of Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch in their Apatow synagogue, modeled on the Warsaw yeshiva. A letter signed by the founding committee was sent to the Rebbe Rayatz in Leningrad, requesting his approval, guidance on selecting students, structuring nigleh and chassidus studies, and finding a suitable mashpia. The shaliach R' Lemil from Warsaw also assisted during a visit.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, lithuania, apatow shul, rebbe rayatz, founding

Title: Rebbe Rayatz blesses founding of Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Vilna
Summary: On 27 Nisan 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz replied to the Vilna chassidim with joy and blessing for the new yeshiva, advising that the director be a Tomim familiar with the spirit of Lubavitch.
Story: Responding to the founders' letter, the Rebbe Rayatz expressed great joy and confidence that students from surrounding regions would soon gather. He stressed that the director must be a former Tomchei Tmimim student deeply familiar with the institution's spirit, fully dedicated to admissions and supervising students with sharp insight and a firm hand.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, rebbe rayatz, letter, blessing

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes encouragement letter to the new Vilna yeshiva branch
Summary: On 27 Nisan 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a letter of encouragement and blessing to the chassidim founding the Vilna branch of Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: Published in Igrot Kodesh of the Rayatz (vol. 1, letter 323), the letter responded to the spring 5687 effort by Vilna anash to launch the yeshiva at the Apatov shul. It set the institution on its formal footing under the central Tomchei Tmimim network. The branch's office was eventually housed not in the shul itself but in the office of the I. V. Levin company at 15 Kolejowa Street.
Tags: rayatz, tomchei tmimim, vilna, apatov

Title: R' Reuven Liberman, last of the Pleshchenitsy Chassidim, dies
Summary: R' Reuven Liberman, last of the great Chassidim of Pleshchenitsy, died on Shabbat 28 Nisan 5687 at age seventy.
Story: R' Reuven Liberman, who had served as shochet and leader of Chassidic life in Pleshchenitsy since R' Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum's emigration, died on Shabbat 28 Nisan 5687 (30 April 1927) at age seventy. His son R' Chaim Liberman, then secretary to the Rayatz, traveled from Leningrad immediately after Pesach to attend the funeral, writing afterward that 'such men are gone from us now in every respect.'
Tags: pleshchenitsy, r reuven liberman, r chaim liberman

Title: England severs diplomatic relations with Russia over espionage
Summary: Britain cut diplomatic ties with the Soviet Union after exposing Russian spies operating in the United Kingdom.
Story: At the end of May 1927, Conservative Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin presented Parliament with deciphered Soviet telegrams proving espionage activities by the All-Russian Co-operative Society. The break in diplomatic relations heightened Soviet paranoia. Together with the assassination of ambassador Voykov, it provided pretext for Stalin's wave of internal repression that swept up the Lubavitcher Rebbe.
Tags: uk, russia, espionage, diplomacy, baldwin

Title: Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva opens in Vilna at Apatow Shul
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5687, the Vilna branch of Tomchei Tmimim was inaugurated at the Apatow Shul on 21 Vilner Street with a festive opening assembly.
Story: Following the Rebbe's blessing, the new yeshiva opened with a grand ceremony attended by congregants of both the Apatow and Kirzner Chabad shuls, along with the city's leading rabbis including the renowned Maggid of Vilna, Rabbi Menachem Kasovsky. Thirteen boys aged 14-15 had been gathered from surrounding shtetls; classes opened with Masechet Gittin under Rabbi Zeev Segal as first Rosh Yeshiva and R' Mordechai Leib Grossbein as mashgiach.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, lithuania, apatow shul, founding, rabbi zeev segal, rabbi menachem kasovsky

Title: England severs diplomatic relations with Russia over espionage
Summary: PM Stanley Baldwin presented deciphered Soviet telegrams to the House of Commons after the All-Russian Co-operative Society raid, ending UK-Soviet diplomatic relations.
Story: At the end of May 1927, England severed diplomatic relations with Russia after a police raid on the All-Russian Co-operative Society in the UK uncovered Soviet espionage activities. Conservative Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin presented the House of Commons with deciphered Soviet telegrams as proof. This rupture helped trigger Stalin's broader crackdown on perceived enemies inside Russia, including religious leaders.
Tags: uk, russia, espionage, stanley baldwin, arcos raid

Title: Bentzion Shemtov arrested in Kharkiv same day as Rebbe
Summary: Three months after his Passover-time release, Shemtov was arrested again in Kharkiv and grilled about the underground Chabad network.
Story: He was held for thirty days and revealed nothing, then released pending trial. He later received a three-year sentence to Siberian exile. The Rebbe was arrested on the same day in Leningrad.
Tags: shemtov, kharkiv, siberia, underground

Title: Soviet ambassador Pyotr Voykov assassinated in Warsaw
Summary: A Russian monarchist killed Soviet ambassador Pyotr Voykov at the Warsaw train station in retaliation for his role in the czar's execution.
Story: Voykov, who was Jewish and had been active with Stalin in the Bolshevik party, had been denied accreditation by Canada but accepted as ambassador to Poland. His assassination unleashed Stalin's accusations of a foreign monarchist network tied to Britain, leading to mass executions of former nobles and clergy in the Soviet Union.
Tags: poland, russia, voykov, monarchists, warsaw, assassination

Title: Stalin unleashes wave of executions after Voykov assassination
Summary: Stalin ordered the execution of former nobility and clergy across Russia and empowered the GPU with extrajudicial emergency tribunals.
Story: In response to the Voykov assassination and the British diplomatic break, Stalin claimed a foreign monarchist plot and unleashed widespread repression. Party organizations affirmed the executions at hundreds of factory meetings, and the GPU received emergency authority to expedite cases. The Yevsektsia seized the moment to move against the Lubavitcher Rebbe, their most fiery religious adversary.
Tags: stalin, soviet union, gpu, purges, clergy, nobility

Title: Latvia signs trade agreement with Soviet Union
Summary: Latvia and the Soviet Union signed a friendship and commerce treaty that still required ratification by the Latvian Saeima, where Chabad MP Mordechai Dubin held a swing vote.
Story: On June 2, 1927, Latvia and the Soviet Union signed a trade deal that was economically vital to Latvia but politically important to the diplomatically isolated Russians. Internal Latvian opposition meant the deal had to be ratified by the Saeima, where Chabad Chasid Mordechai Dubin held two seats. Dubin would later leverage his swing vote to pressure Russia into releasing the Rebbe.
Tags: latvia, russia, trade, mordechai dubin, saeima

Title: Latvia signs trade agreement with the Soviet Union
Summary: Latvia signed a commerce treaty with Soviet Russia that still required ratification by the Latvian parliament.
Story: Though Latvia needed the deal more than the Soviets, the Bolsheviks wanted it as a step in peeling the Baltic states away from the West. Internal Latvian opposition meant the trade agreement had to be ratified by the Saeima. Mordechai Dubin's swing vote later became leverage to pressure Moscow into releasing the Rebbe and granting him an exit visa.
Tags: latvia, soviet union, trade, dubin, saeima

Title: Vilna yeshiva reports rapid growth to Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: On 5 Sivan 5687, Vilna yeshiva leaders wrote to the Rebbe reporting over twenty students from surrounding towns and confirming Rabbi Zeev Segal as Rosh Yeshiva.
Story: The Vilna directors reported that students were arriving daily from Disna, Dokshitz, Postov, Koretz and other towns, exceeding twenty in number. Rabbi Zeev Segal, formerly a Rosh Mesivta in Grodno, was appointed Rosh Yeshiva, and R' Mordechai Leib Grossbein was temporarily designated as mashpia in chassidus. Classes were divided by age into two levels studying Gemara with Tosafot.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, rabbi zeev segal, rabbi mordechai leib grossbein, growth

Title: Assassination of Soviet ambassador Pyotr Voykov in Warsaw
Summary: Russian monarchist Boris Koverda shot Soviet ambassador Pyotr Voykov at the Warsaw train station, triggering Stalin's wave of executions and arrests.
Story: In early June 1927, a Russian monarchist assassinated Soviet ambassador to Poland Pyotr Voykov at the Warsaw train station, citing Voykov's role in killing Czar Nicholas. Stalin responded with mass executions of former nobility and broader extrajudicial GPU powers. The Yevesektzia seized this atmosphere of repression to move against the Rebbe.
Tags: russia, poland, voykov, monarchist, stalin, warsaw

Title: Soviet search at Rayatz's Leningrad home
Summary: On 14 Sivan 5687, Soviet authorities searched the Rayatz's residence but took only papers of no value.
Story: According to the Rayatz's own contemporaneous notes, agents who entered his home on 14 Sivan 5687 left with only worthless papers. A separate summer 1927 search in Rostov, however, confiscated a collection of his writings from 1921.
Tags: rayatz, leningrad, soviet, search, gpu

Title: GPU arrests Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn in Leningrad
Summary: Shortly after midnight, GPU agents Mikhail Nachmanson and Grigory Lulov burst into the Rebbe's Leningrad apartment, searched it for an hour and a half, and took him to Shpalerka prison.
Story: Minutes past midnight on June 15, 1927 (14 Sivan 5687), GPU officers Nachmanson and Lulov, both from Chabad families, led a contingent of armed men into the sixth Rebbe's Leningrad apartment. After a tense search lasting an hour and a half during which the Rebbe insisted on first reciting grace and warned the officers they would regret the arrest, he was taken at around 2:20 a.m. to the notorious Shpalerka prison. By taking a wrong corridor inside the prison, the Rebbe miraculously avoided being grouped with twelve other clergy who were summarily shot that night.
Tags: russia, leningrad, gpu, yevesektzia, nachmanson, lulov, arrest, shpalerka

Title: GPU arrests Rebbe Rayatz at his Leningrad apartment
Summary: Just after midnight on June 15, 1927, armed GPU agents burst into Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn's Leningrad apartment and arrested him.
Story: Officers Mikhail Nachmanson and Grigory Lulov, both from Chabad families, led a contingent of armed men in a search lasting an hour and a half. The Rebbe recited grace slowly to allow family members to conceal incriminating documents. Despite his daughters' pleas and his mother Shterna Sara's tearful outburst, he was taken at 2:20 a.m. to the notorious Shpalerka prison.
Tags: leningrad, gpu, yevsektsia, arrest, shpalerka, nachmanson, lulov, 14 sivan

Title: Rayatz and R' Chaim Liberman arrested in Leningrad
Summary: The Rayatz and his secretary R' Chaim Liberman were arrested in Leningrad on the eve of 15 Sivan 5687.
Story: On the eve of 15 Sivan 5687 (14-15 June 1927), the Sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe (Rayatz) and his secretary R' Chaim Liberman were both arrested in Leningrad. After some time in the Leningrad prison, they were sent into exile separately—the Rebbe to Kostroma and Liberman to Tambov.
Tags: leningrad, rayatz, r chaim liberman, kgb, soviet, arrest

Title: Rebbe begins hunger strike in Shpalerka prison demanding tefillin
Summary: After being struck and having his tefillin confiscated, the Rebbe refused food until they were returned.
Story: Following his arrival at Shpalerka, the Rebbe insisted on his right to pray with tefillin and was beaten and pushed down a ladder by a guard. His belt buckle gashed his stomach. When the prison warden told him to forget the 'foolishness,' the Rebbe began a hunger strike that lasted until Friday before sunset.
Tags: shpalerka, leningrad, tefillin, hunger strike, imprisonment

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrested in Leningrad by Soviet authorities
Summary: On 15 Sivan 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz was arrested in Petersburg, beginning the chain of events leading to his exile, redemption, and departure from Russia.
Story: Soon after responding to the Vilna founders, the Rebbe Rayatz was arrested in Petersburg on 15 Sivan and subsequently sent into exile. After his miraculous redemption, efforts began to extract him from Russia entirely. He eventually reached Riga at the end of Tishrei 5688.
Tags: leningrad, petersburg, russia, soviet, arrest, rebbe rayatz, kgb

Title: Rebbe's secretary Chaim Lieberman arrested after burning documents
Summary: GPU agents arrested Rabbi Chaim Lieberman, the Rebbe's secretary, just after he finished burning records of the secret school system.
Story: Warned by Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson that the GPU had raided the Rebbe's home, Lieberman immediately burned all financial records and correspondence related to the underground Jewish school network. The fire had not yet consumed everything when officers knocked at his door, but they found nothing usable. He was arrested anyway and interrogated.
Tags: lieberman, gpu, leningrad, samizdat, underground schools

Title: Rebbe interrogated by GPU officers in Shpalerka prison
Summary: Two nights after his arrest, Nachmanson, Lulov and two others interrogated the Rebbe and threatened him with execution within 24 hours.
Story: The interrogators rested their hands on weapons laid on the table, accusing the Rebbe of counterrevolutionary activity, leading Soviet Jewry, influencing American bourgeois Jews through the JDC, and operating a network of religious institutions. The Rebbe rebuffed them, citing Soviet law that did not ban religious teaching. As the session ended, Lulov declared, 'In twenty-four hours, you will be shot.'
Tags: gpu, interrogation, leningrad, shpalerka, nachmanson, lulov

Title: Rebbe receives tefillin and challah in Shpalerka prison
Summary: After 72 hours of fasting, a Jewish guard delivered the Rebbe's tefillin and books, and challah from home arrived before sunset.
Story: Friday before Shabbat, the Rebbe finally received his tefillin and sefarim. He refused the prison's non-kosher meals and demanded food from home. Just before sunset, three loaves of uncut challah were delivered to his cell, breaking his hunger strike.
Tags: shpalerka, leningrad, tefillin, imprisonment, challah, shabbat

Title: Rebbe receives tefillin and food from home in Shpalerka
Summary: After 72 hours of fasting and resisting beatings, the Rebbe was finally given his tefillin and books and received three loaves of uncut challah from his family.
Story: On Friday June 17, 1927, after two nights and three days of imprisonment, a Jewish guard returned the Rebbe's confiscated tefillin and books. The Rebbe refused the prison's non-kosher meals and demanded food from home. Just before sunset, three loaves of uncut challah were delivered to his cell.
Tags: russia, leningrad, shpalerka, tefillin, hunger strike, challah

Title: Rebbe undergoes second GPU interrogation in Shpalerka
Summary: The Rebbe insisted he was a teacher of chasidic philosophy uninvolved in politics, and confirmed his opposition to the planned Leningrad Jewish conference.
Story: Recovered GPU file no. 898 shows the Rebbe maintained the same position before and after the revolution. He affirmed his opposition to the Yevsektsia-supported conference of Russian Jewish kehillot, which had become the immediate flashpoint for his arrest.
Tags: gpu, interrogation, shpalerka, leningrad, conference

Title: Second GPU interrogation of the Rebbe
Summary: In a second interrogation documented in the GPU file, the Rebbe insisted he was a rabbi and teacher of chasidic philosophy, never involved in politics, and confirmed his opposition to the proposed Leningrad Jewish conference.
Story: On June 21, 1927, GPU investigators questioned the Rebbe again. He stood firm that he had been a rabbi both before and after the revolution and was uninvolved in politics. When asked about the proposed conference for Russian Jewry being organized by the Leningrad community, he confirmed his opposition.
Tags: russia, leningrad, gpu, interrogation, conference

Title: Rebbe's first postcard from prison delivered to family
Summary: A Shabbat postcard from the Rebbe reached his family declaring he was well, despite the beatings he had endured.
Story: On Shabbat June 25, the family received the Rebbe's first written word from Shpalerka. Although he had been repeatedly beaten and was in excruciating pain, his message was upbeat. He requested sefarim including Likkutei Torah and Chumash Bemidbar.
Tags: shpalerka, leningrad, imprisonment, shabbat

Title: Rebbe's postcard from prison reaches family
