Summary: A Shabbat postcard from the imprisoned Rebbe arrived at his home, reporting he was 'well' despite beatings and requesting Likkutei Torah and Chumash Bemidbar.
Story: On Shabbat, June 25, 1927, a postcard the Rebbe had written from Shpalerka was delivered to his family in Leningrad. Despite repeated beatings and excruciating pain, the message was upbeat. He asked his family to send him sefarim, including Likkutei Torah and a Chumash Bemidbar.
Tags: russia, leningrad, shpalerka, prison, sefarim

Title: Rebbe's death sentence commuted to Solovki exile
Summary: Madam Peshkova's intercession and international outcry caused the GPU to replace the Rebbe's death sentence with ten years' exile in Solovki.
Story: On Wednesday June 29, an official informed Rabbi Eliyahu Chaim Althaus that the firing-squad verdict had been commuted to exile in the remote Solovki Islands prison camp. The family was told to bring food and say goodbye. A crowd gathered outside the prison as Lulov tried one last time to extort a public retraction from the Rebbe, who refused.
Tags: gpu, solovki, peshkova, leningrad, althaus

Title: Solovki exile sentence reduced to three years in Kostroma
Summary: After Madam Peshkova's further intervention, the Rebbe's ten-year Solovki sentence was replaced with a three-year exile to Kostroma on the Volga River.
Story: On Thursday, after Madam Peshkova pressured the GPU again, the Rebbe was informed that instead of Solovki he would be exiled for three years to Kostroma. He saw the official document on the desk, with the original 'Death by firing squad' crossed out, replaced by 'Ten years in Solovki', and then by 'Three years in Kostroma.' Guards beat him repeatedly when he refused to stand to hear the sentence.
Tags: russia, kostroma, solovki, exile, peshkova

Title: Rebbe released for home visit and exiled to Kostroma (3 Tamuz)
Summary: After nineteen days in Shpalerka, the Rebbe was permitted six hours at home before boarding a train into three-year exile in Kostroma.
Story: Continued lobbying by Madam Peshkova overturned the Solovki decree, and the sentence was reduced to three years in Kostroma. The Rebbe refused to leave on Thursday because the journey would violate Shabbat; he was kept until Sunday morning July 3. At Leningrad station thousands of Jews formed an honor guard as he gave a defiant speech declaring that only Jewish bodies, not souls, are subject to foreign rule.
Tags: kostroma, exile, leningrad, shpalerka, peshkova, 3 tamuz

Title: Rebbe released from Shpalerka and exiled to Kostroma
Summary: After nineteen days in Shpalerka, the Rebbe was permitted a six-hour visit home and then boarded a train to begin three years of exile in Kostroma.
Story: On Sunday, July 3, 1927 (3 Tamuz 5687), the Rebbe left Shpalerka prison after 18 days, 11 hours, and 15 minutes of imprisonment. He had refused to leave on Thursday because the train would have forced him to desecrate Shabbat; Madam Peshkova's intercession through Premier Rykov and GPU chief Menzhinsky won him a delay until Sunday. After meeting Chasidim at home, an honor-guard of Leningrad Jews lined his path to the train, where he gave a defiant platform speech declaring that 'only our bodies were sent into exile.'
Tags: russia, leningrad, kostroma, exile, 3 tamuz, shabbat

Title: Liberation of Rebbe Rayatz and return of hidden manuscripts
Summary: On 12 Tammuz 5687, with Rayatz's release confirmed, R. Z. Duchman returns the manuscripts he had hidden during the arrest.
Story: Duchman later wrote that he had received a large basket of manuscripts (ksvei-yad-kodesh) to hide and on Tuesday 12 Tammuz at 1:30 PM he brought them back. The future Rebbe — sitting in the western side of the great hall — told him as he handed them over: 'I will pay you for your effort with good news, that the Rebbe will arrive in time for Shabbos.' Years later in 5748, when asked whether some manuscripts may not have been returned, the Rebbe replied definitively: 'They were returned immediately!!'
Tags: rayatz, geulah, yud-beis-tammuz, manuscripts, soviet

Title: Liberation of the Rayatz on Yud-Beis Tammuz
Summary: The Rayatz was freed from Soviet exile on 12-13 Tammuz 5687, the date later commemorated as Yud-Beis Tammuz.
Story: After being arrested on 15 Sivan 5687 and exiled to Kostroma, the Rayatz was freed on 12-13 Tammuz 5687 (12-13 July 1927). The date became the great Chabad festival of liberation; later that fall, in the latter part of Tishrei 5688, he left Russia entirely and settled in Riga.
Tags: rayatz, kostroma, soviet, liberation, yud beis tammuz

Title: Liberation of the Rebbe Rayatz on 12 Tammuz
Summary: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was freed from Soviet imprisonment and exile on 12 Tammuz 5687 (July 1927), the Chabad festival of liberation.
Story: Arrested for his work sustaining Jewish life under Soviet repression, the Rebbe Rayatz was released on 12 Tammuz 5687. The date became a major commemorative occasion in Chabad, marked in 2000 by a library exhibition honoring his 120th birth-year and 73 years since his liberation.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, yud beis tammuz, soviet union, liberation

Title: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn freed from Soviet imprisonment
Summary: Following the Frierdiker Rebbe's release on 12 Tammuz 5687, R' Benyamin Gorodetzky began showing his portrait at the Chabad shul in Kiev and urging Jews to behold it.
Story: The author, then learning at the Kiev cheder katan, observed Rabbi Gorodetzky displaying a photograph of the Rebbe Rayatz to local balebatim and telling them it was a mitzvah to gaze upon him. He did not yet grasp the full significance, but the timing — soon after Yud-Beis Tammuz — places it just after the Rebbe's release from Soviet prison. The episode marks his earliest known exposure to the Frierdiker Rebbe.
Tags: frierdiker-rebbe, yud-bet-tammuz, kiev, ussr, soviet-prison, chabad

Title: Rebbe freed from exile in Kostroma
Summary: On the day of his weekly required check-in with the Kostroma GPU, the Rebbe was informed that a telegram from Moscow had ordered his unconditional release.
Story: On Tuesday, July 12, 1927 (12 Tamuz), the Rebbe came to the GPU headquarters in Kostroma for his mandated weekly appearance. An officer told him papers had arrived freeing him. The international outcry combined with Madam Peshkova's lobbying had overcome the opposition of Leningrad GPU chief Stanislav Messing. The Rebbe marked the day by teaching a maamar on Psalms 118:7, 'G-d aided me'; 12 Tamuz has since been celebrated annually as a Chabad festival of liberation.
Tags: russia, kostroma, 12 tamuz, liberation, peshkova

Title: Rebbe notified of unconditional release from Kostroma exile (12 Tamuz)
Summary: When the Rebbe came for his weekly check-in at GPU headquarters in Kostroma, an officer informed him that orders had arrived from Moscow freeing him.
Story: Sustained pressure from Madam Peshkova, telegrams to President Kalinin and Premier Rykov, and international protests forced Moscow to overturn the exile. On Tuesday July 12, the Kostroma GPU station was closed for a local holiday, but an officer told Althaus the release papers had arrived. The seventh Rebbe would later establish 12 Tamuz as an annual festival of liberation.
Tags: kostroma, 12 tamuz, release, peshkova, althaus

Title: Rebbe Rayatz redeemed on 12 Tamuz
Summary: On 12 Tamuz 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz was redeemed from Soviet imprisonment and exile.
Story: After his arrest in the summer of 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz was released on 12 Tamuz (July 12, 1927). The day was thereafter commemorated as a Chabad chag ha-geulah. The circumstances forced him to leave Russia, and he settled in Riga shortly afterward.
Tags: 12 tamuz, rayatz, redemption, soviet union

Title: Rebbe returns to Leningrad after exile
Summary: Two days after being freed in Kostroma, the Rebbe arrived back in Leningrad despite fears that the local GPU might arrest him again.
Story: On July 14, 1927, the Rebbe arrived back in Leningrad following his liberation from Kostroma exile. The news of his release spread quickly across the Soviet Union, sparking celebrations among Chasidim. On his first Shabbat back he recited the HaGomel blessing of thanksgiving for surviving prison.
Tags: russia, leningrad, kostroma, hagomel

Title: Rebbe returns to Leningrad from Kostroma exile
Summary: Two days after his release, the Rebbe arrived back in Leningrad, despite the GPU's threat to re-arrest him.
Story: Word of the liberation spread quickly across the Soviet Union; in Kharkiv, Rabbi Hillel Levin received a telegram and Chasidim gathered at Rabbi Aharon Tomarkin's home to celebrate. In Leningrad, Stanislav Messing had opposed the release and threatened to arrest the Rebbe again. The Rebbe recited HaGomel that first Shabbat before relocating to Malakhovka outside Moscow.
Tags: leningrad, kostroma, hagomel

Title: Announcement of Rebbe Rayatz's return from Kostroma exile
Summary: Secretary Shneur Zalman Schneersohn announced to Axelrod that the Rebbe Rayatz had safely returned home from Kostroma exile.
Story: On 15 Tammuz 5687, secretary Shneur Zalman Schneersohn wrote with the long-awaited news that 'today is the day we hoped for — our holy father returned home in peace and success.' This announced Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak's release from his Kostroma exile, following his arrest by Soviet authorities, death sentence, and dramatic redemption on 12-13 Tammuz. The release would soon be commemorated annually as Chag HaGeulah.
Tags: rayatz, kostroma, exile, release, 12-tammuz, soviet-union, kgb

Title: Soviet censors approve export of 59 boxes of books
Summary: Soviet foreign-trade and customs officials in Leningrad personally inspected and sealed 59 boxes of Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak's books for transfer to Latvia.
Story: On 5 Menachem-Av 5687, representatives A. Feigelstein of the foreign-trade office and G. Alachbrov of the Leningrad customs office signed off on the inspection and official sealing of fifty-nine book boxes belonging to Y. Schneersohn. After initial Soviet refusal to permit export of the library, intercession by Dr. A. Cohen of Berlin and Latvian parliamentarian Mordechai Dubin secured Moscow's order to allow the books out, with the censor instructed to stamp every crate.
Tags: russia, soviet, censorship, library, rayatz, leningrad, latvia

Title: Riga community petitions Soviets to release Rebbe and books
Summary: The Riga kehillah wrote to the Soviet authorities announcing the Rebbe's appointment as Chief Rabbi of Riga and requesting that he be permitted to bring his ancestors' manuscripts.
Story: On 23 Menachem-Av 5687 the Riga Jewish community council notified the Soviet regime of the Frierdiker Rebbe's appointment as Chief Rabbi of Riga and pleaded that he be allowed to immigrate with all his family and bring along the writings of his holy forefathers and his own manuscripts. The letter was part of the diplomatic pressure that eventually persuaded Moscow to authorize the export of the library.
Tags: riga, latvia, soviet, rayatz, library, mordechai-dubin

Title: Riga Jewish community formally invites Rebbe as chief rabbi
Summary: On 23 Menachem Av, the Riga Jewish community formally invited the Rebbe to serve as its chief rabbi, providing legal cover for an exit visa.
Story: Mordechai Dubin, a Chabad chasid and member of the Latvian Saeima, presented the invitation to Russian officials, who initially rejected it. Simultaneously Dr. Oscar Cohn delivered an invitation from Frankfurt's Jewish community. Dubin then leveraged his swing vote on the unratified Latvia-Soviet trade agreement to extract the exit visa from Moscow.
Tags: riga, latvia, dubin, exit visa, 23 av

Title: Riga Jewish community invites Rebbe to be chief rabbi
Summary: On 23 Menachem Av 5687, the Riga Jewish community sent a formal invitation for the Rebbe to become its chief rabbi, used as leverage to secure his exit visa.
Story: On August 21, 1927 (23 Menachem Av 5687), the Riga Jewish community formally invited the Rebbe to become its chief rabbi. Mordechai Dubin, head of the Riga community and a member of the Latvian Parliament, presented the letter to Russian officials. Combined with Dubin's swing vote on the pending Russia-Latvia trade treaty, the invitation became the key lever for obtaining the Rebbe's exit visa.
Tags: latvia, riga, mordechai dubin, exit visa

Title: Death of Schusterman's sister Shayna in scarlet fever epidemic
Summary: Schusterman's married sister Shayna (Sanya) died on 25 Menachem Av 5687 after five days of illness during a scarlet fever epidemic in Zlobin.
Story: Scarlet fever swept Zlobin, with virtually no household spared. Shayna left a two-year-old son named Achiezer, who was later reported lost in the war. Rabbi Binyaminson's adopted son Alterke also died in the epidemic, as did Chaim, son of the melamed R' Shalom Horowitz, on his thirteenth birthday on Rosh Hashanah.
Tags: zlobin, scarlet-fever, epidemic, death

Title: Feigin writes urgent appeal to American Chasidim for funds
Summary: Rabbi Yechezkel Feigin cryptically pleaded with Eliyahu Simpson and Yisrael Jacobson in America to wire funds for the Rebbe's relocation and the secret school system.
Story: Using code language about 'illness' and 'expert doctors' to evade censors, Feigin warned that miracles do not happen every day and the Rebbe had to be moved to Riga immediately. His letter conveyed both the cost of imprisonment and the ongoing financial demands of keeping underground institutions afloat.
Tags: feigin, america, fundraising, riga, 27 av, underground schools

Title: Bar mitzvah of M. Schusterman in Suraz
Summary: Schusterman became bar mitzvah on Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5687 in Suraz, where he was studying at the small yeshiva.
Story: After Shacharit at the 'rabbi's minyan' a bottle of liquor was placed on the table. Rabbi Axelrod called on the boy to deliver a drasha on tefillin from the verse 'V'shamarta es ha-chukah ha-zos l'mo'adah.' There were no invitations, no dinner, and no chair-lifting — only the minyan's congregants saying 'l'chaim.'
Tags: suraz, bar-mitzvah, moshe-axelrod

Title: 'Kol Korei' published describing the new yeshiva building
Summary: In Elul 5687 the yeshiva published a 'Kol Korei' describing its new three-story building at Mlawska 7.
Story: In Elul 5687 (August–September 1927) Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw issued a printed Kol Korei, describing for donors and the public the spacious accommodations at Mlawska 7 / Sapuzinski 15/17 — six classrooms, a large kitchen, prepared beds and orderly conduct in a dedicated three-story building. A photograph of the document later appeared in Beton Chabad issue 34.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-tmimim, kol-korei, fundraising, mlawska-street

Title: JTA publishes report from Riga on cause of Rebbe's arrest
Summary: The Jewish Telegraphic Agency reported that the Rebbe's arrest stemmed from his opposition to the planned conference of Soviet Jewish kehillot.
Story: The JTA's Riga dispatch said that 'well-informed circles in Moscow' traced the arrest to the Lubavitcher Rebbe's resistance to the Leningrad conference set for October 21, 1927. The conference's initiators, it reported, decided to discredit the Rebbe before Soviet authorities to remove his opposition.
Tags: jta, riga, press, yevsektsia, kehillah conference

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe arrives in Riga, Latvia
Summary: Word reached American Chassidim that the Frierdiker Rebbe and his family had arrived safely in Riga, accompanied by his secretary R' Yechezkel Feigin.
Story: On the Monday following the $4,000 wire transfer, news came that the Rebbe and his household had reached Riga. He was accompanied by his secretary and gabbai R' Yechezkel Feigin, who from Riga maintained an active correspondence with the author about day-to-day matters of the chatzer. Riga would serve as the Rebbe's primary residence for the next several years.
Tags: riga, latvia, yechezkel feigin, exile

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe departs Soviet Russia after Sukkos
Summary: Immediately after Sukkos 5688, the Frierdiker Rebbe and his family left Soviet Russia for Riga, Latvia, ending months of danger that followed his arrest and release.
Story: After the events of Tishrei 5688 in Leningrad, the Frierdiker Rebbe and his household departed Russia just after Sukkos. The exit had been arranged through R' Mordechai Dubin's leverage in Latvian parliament, with permission also granted to bring the Rebbe's manuscripts and library out of the country. American Chassidim received news of the journey only later, in stages.
Tags: russia, latvia, riga, exile, leningrad

Title: Rayatz leaves Russia and settles in Riga
Summary: At the end of Tishrei 5688 the Rayatz left the Soviet Union and settled in Riga, Latvia.
Story: After his liberation on 12-13 Tammuz 5687, the Rayatz remained in Russia for several more months. At the end of Tishrei 5688 (October 1927) he left Soviet Russia and settled in Riga, while his secretary R' Chaim Liberman remained behind in exile in Tambov.
Tags: rayatz, riga, russia, latvia, emigration

Title: Rebbe celebrates last Simchat Torah with Russian Chasidim
Summary: The Rebbe spent his final holiday in the Soviet Union surrounded by Chasidim who packed his Leningrad synagogue beyond capacity.
Story: Despite the risk of arrest, Chasidim flocked from across the country. The room, with a normal capacity of six hundred, swelled with hundreds more. The Rebbe urged each Chasid to influence their community, declaring 'I will be with you.' At the train station thousands lined the platform, and one Chasid, Rabbi Meir Simcha Chein, wept, 'The Rebbe is going, and we are left here.'
Tags: leningrad, simchat torah, russia, departure, farbrengen

Title: Rebbe celebrates last Simchat Torah with Russian Chasidim in Leningrad
Summary: Russian Chasidim packed a Leningrad synagogue, normally holding 600, far beyond capacity for the Rebbe's final Simchat Torah before leaving the Soviet Union.
Story: In October 1927, the Rebbe celebrated his last holiday in Russia, Simchat Torah, with his Chasidim in Leningrad. Despite the risk of arrest, Chasidim flocked from across the country; the synagogue swelled with people packed into every corner. The Rebbe urged them, 'Don't fear anyone,' and consoled them, 'I will be with you,' while one Chasid wept, 'The Rebbe is going, and we are left here.'
Tags: russia, leningrad, simchat torah, farewell

Title: Rebbe forced out of Russia after death sentence
Summary: In October 1927 the Sixth Rebbe was forced to leave the Soviet Union after a death sentence at the hands of the anti-religious regime was commuted to exile.
Story: The Rebbe's expulsion from Russia ended his direct leadership inside the Soviet Union but began two decades of relocations across Latvia, Poland, and eventually the United States while he continued to sustain an underground religious network back in the USSR.
Tags: russia, soviet union, yevsektzia, exile, st petersburg

Title: Rebbe Rayatz leaves Russia for Riga
Summary: The Russian authorities granted approval for the Rebbe and his family to depart Russia for Riga, Latvia, after years of persecution.
Story: The Rebbe insisted his future son-in-law also be permitted to leave. When officials asked, 'Can't you find another son-in-law?' the Rebbe famously replied, 'A son-in-law like him I can't find there.' The move ended the Russian chapter of Chabad leadership.
Tags: riga, latvia, russia, exile

Title: Rebbe Rayatz leaves Soviet Russia
Summary: At the end of Tishrei 5688, Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn left Soviet Russia.
Story: After years of persecution under the Communists, the Rebbe Rayatz departed Russia in late Tishrei 5688. Immediately upon his exit, Chabad chassidim in Warsaw appealed to him to settle in Poland, arguing it would allow them and the chassidim in the Polish-ruled regions of Lithuania (Vilna, Daksht, Dolhinov, Glubokie, etc.) to remain connected to their Rebbe.
Tags: russia, soviet-union, rayatz, emigration, tishrei

Title: Rebbe Rayatz's train stops in Vilna en route to Latvia
Summary: At the end of Tishrei 5688, after leaving Russia for Latvia, the Rebbe Rayatz's train briefly stopped in Vilna where he spoke with the Rosh Yeshiva and mashpia.
Story: As the Rebbe Rayatz traveled from Russia to Latvia, his train passed through Vilna. The yeshiva's bochurim and administration eagerly awaited him at the station. The Rebbe stepped out onto the carriage steps and conversed with the Rosh Yeshiva and mashpia, but the brief stop did not permit longer interaction before the train continued to Riga.
Tags: vilna, latvia, riga, russia, rebbe rayatz, exile

Title: Rebbe sends action plan to disrupt Leningrad conference
Summary: The Rebbe dispatches an organizing plan covering nine key cities with instructions to Chasidim to undermine the Yevsektzia conference.
Story: The plan focused on cities including Moscow, Leningrad, and Kutaisi in Soviet Georgia, with lists of contacts and detailed instructions. The plans succeeded and the conference was never convened.
Tags: yevsektzia, russia, underground, leningrad

Title: Final Soviet approval to ship 66 book crates to Riga
Summary: On erev Yom Kippur 5688 the Soviets issued final clearance for sixty-six crates of books and effects to be shipped to Riga.
Story: Just before the Rebbe's departure, on 5 October 1927, customs and foreign-trade representatives issued the conclusive export authorization covering 66 crates of books and household items destined for Riga. The document noted that the books had been examined and approved for shipment by foreign-ministry officials, completing the long bureaucratic battle to bring the library out of the Soviet Union.
Tags: russia, soviet, censorship, library, rayatz, latvia, riga

Title: Rebbe Rayatz departs Leningrad with family
Summary: On Thursday 24 Tishrei 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz and his family left Leningrad for Latvia.
Story: After months of effort by Mordechai Dubin to secure exit papers, the Rebbe Rayatz departed Leningrad with his family on Thursday morning. Senior Chabad rabbis accompanied him by train to the border station at Pskov. From Pskov they wrote a farewell letter to Latvian Jewry on behalf of the Rebbe.
Tags: russia, leningrad, riga, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, exile

Title: Brooklyn Chassidim wire $4,000 to Riga for the Rebbe's resettlement
Summary: On Erev Shabbos Parshas Bereishis 5688, the author insisted on immediately telegraphing $4,000 to Riga to fund the Rebbe's exit from Russia despite communal hesitation.
Story: Gathered in the Agudas Chassidei Chabad office in the Kramer brothers' factory, the author and R' A. Simpson — with Rabbi Lookstein's qualified support — pressed for an immediate $4,000 wire to R' Mordechai Dubin in Riga. The Kramer brothers initially balked at so large a sum and proposed delay, offering only $1,000, then $1,500. The author refused to leave the factory until the full sum was sent; by day's end the money was wired, and by Monday word arrived that the Rebbe and his family had reached Riga.
Tags: brooklyn, riga, fundraising, kramer brothers, agudas chassidei chabad, a. simpson, lifshitz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Riga from Soviet Russia
Summary: On Friday 25 Tishrei 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Riga, establishing the new center of Chabad activity outside the Soviet Union.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Riga with his family, having been appointed Chief Rabbi of the city, which had enabled his exit from Russia. His arrival expanded the existing Chabad community in Riga and made it the new hub of his work on behalf of Soviet Jewry. He first stayed at the Kommerz Hotel for about a month before securing apartments.
Tags: riga, latvia, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, chabad

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Riga, Latvia after exile from Soviet Russia
Summary: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn arrives in Riga, Latvia, after being forced to leave Soviet Russia.
Story: Two days after Simchat Torah, the Rebbe's train from Leningrad crossed into Latvia. At 7:00 a.m. on 25 Tishrei, 5688 the train pulled into Riga, where thousands gathered at the station and surrounding plaza. The Rebbe and his family slowly navigated the crowd to a local hotel, eventually moving to an apartment in an upscale Jewish neighborhood.
Tags: riga, latvia, russia, exile, soviet, rayatz

Title: Sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe arrives in Riga, Latvia from Russia
Summary: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn arrives in Riga two days after Simchat Torah following expulsion from the Soviet Union.
Story: After enduring arrest and exile in Russia, the sixth Rebbe crossed into Latvia by train, arriving at 7:00 a.m. at Riga station. Thousands of Jews of every background filled the station and surrounding plaza to greet him. He and his family were eventually escorted to a hotel and later to an apartment in an upscale Jewish neighborhood.
Tags: riga, latvia, exile, rayatz, russia

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes thank-you letters to those who secured his release
Summary: On Sunday 27 Tishrei 5688, two days after arriving in Riga, the Rebbe Rayatz began writing thank-you letters to those who worked for his release.
Story: Although exhausted from his journey from Russia and not yet settled in housing, the Rebbe Rayatz immediately sat down to write thanks to the people who had advocated for his release. He had no secretaries at this time, as R. Chaim Lieberman was still in exile in Tambov and R. Yechezkel Feigin had not yet managed to leave Russia.
Tags: riga, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, letters, rescue

Title: Warsaw chassidim invite Rebbe Rayatz to settle in Poland
Summary: On 27 Tishrei 5688, the leaders of Warsaw Chabad wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz urging him to make Poland or Polish-Lithuania his home.
Story: After the Rebbe Rayatz left Soviet Russia and settled in Riga, the heads of Warsaw Chabad — R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov, R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin, and R. Yechiel Tzvi Gurary — wrote on 27 Tishrei 5688 inviting him to relocate to Poland or the Polish-ruled parts of Lithuania. They argued that the bulk of anash and the Tomchei Tmimim students were now concentrated in Poland, and that travel from Riga was very difficult. The Rebbe declined the move but agreed to make a visit.
Tags: warsaw, riga, rayatz invitation, shraga feivish zalmanov, shneur zalman shmotkin, yechiel tzvi gurary

Title: Rebbe composes letter to Chasidim on train from Russia
Summary: On the train leaving Russia, the Rebbe writes to his Chasidim that distance cannot break their essential bond.
Story: Heartbroken by the boisterous Leningrad send-off, the Rebbe composed a letter to the Chasidim while still on the train. He wrote that 'the essential connection between us cannot be broken, nor does the fact that distance stands between us break that bond.' The letter was dated 24 Tishrei, 5688.
Tags: russia, exile, letter, igrot kodesh

Title: Rebbe writes letter to Chasidim during train journey out of Russia
Summary: On the train to Latvia, the Rebbe composes a letter to his followers affirming their unbroken spiritual bond.
Story: Heartbroken at leaving Russia, the Rebbe wrote, 'The essential connection between us cannot be broken, nor does the fact that distance stands between us break that bond.' The letter, written during the journey, was preserved in Igrot Kodesh, volume 1.
Tags: letter, igrot-kodesh, exile, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes 11+ letters from Riga in single day
Summary: On Tuesday 29 Tishrei 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote at least 11 letters to associates in Russia and abroad announcing his safe arrival.
Story: Working alone without secretaries, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote letters to close associates inside Russia and abroad, announcing his arrival, asking about their welfare, and requesting greetings be passed to various figures. Within the first month from Russia, he wrote at least 70 letters, mostly to heads of the Chasidic community in Russia, encouraging them in their difficult situation and directing the continuation of religious activity.
Tags: riga, russia, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, letters

Title: Rayatz petitions Soviet ambassador in Riga for library return
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Marcheshvan 5688, immediately after settling in Riga, Rayatz petitions the Soviet ambassador in Latvia for help returning his library.
Story: The letter closes with a firm request that the ambassador render every possible cooperation toward recovering and transferring the library to Riga. The ambassador subsequently promised to take up the matter, but in his 3 Teves letter to R. David Shifrin, Rayatz reports that no satisfactory answer had yet been received.
Tags: library, rayatz, riga, latvia, soviet, letters

Title: Rebbe declines invitation to relocate to Warsaw
Summary: Responding to the Warsaw community's invitation to settle there, the Rebbe declines for unstated reasons.
Story: Shortly after his arrival in Riga, the Warsaw community wrote inviting the Rebbe to relocate there. He responded that 'their request could not be fulfilled for various reasons,' possibly because of visa or citizenship difficulties. He added that he hoped to visit them soon.
Tags: warsaw, poland, riga, letter

Title: Rebbe writes to Rabbi Zevin urging opposition to Leningrad conference
Summary: Just days after arriving in Riga, the Rebbe writes urging Chasidim to undermine the Yevsektzia-backed Leningrad Jewish conference.
Story: The Rebbe wrote, 'Anyone with a G-d-fearing spirit should protest against the Leningrad conference and undermine those plotting against the values of Torah.' He dispatched a detailed nine-city action plan that successfully prevented the conference from convening.
Tags: letter, yevsektzia, leningrad-conference, russia

Title: Rebbe writes to Zevin urging protest against Leningrad Jewish conference
Summary: From Riga the Rebbe writes Rabbi Shlomo Yosef Zevin urging Russian Chasidim to undermine the planned Leningrad Jewish conference.
Story: Despite the suffering he endured in Russia for opposing the Leningrad Jewish conference, the Rebbe dispatched a detailed action plan from Riga to disrupt it. The conference, organized by the Leningrad Jewish community and surreptitiously supported by the Yevsektzia, targeted nine key cities including Moscow and Kutaisi. The plan succeeded and the conference was never convened.
Tags: russia, leningrad, yevsektzia, conference, underground

Title: Rebbe Rayatz travels to Berlin to meet Joint leadership
Summary: Immediately after moving to his new Riga apartment, the Rebbe Rayatz traveled to Berlin to meet with Jewish leaders about aid for Soviet Jewry.
Story: On the same day he moved into his new apartment, the Rebbe traveled to Berlin to meet with major activists including R. Meir Hildesheimer, the Rogatchover Gaon, R. M.M. Zack of Riga, and Mordechai Dubin to discuss the budget for Torah institutions in Russia. This meeting led to the establishment of a special bureau under his direction for the relief work.
Tags: berlin, joint, russia, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, fundraising

Title: Rebbe directs Rabbi Yakovshvili to study shechitah and work in Kutaisi
Summary: From Riga the Rebbe instructs Rabbi Simon Yakovshvili to travel to Kutaisi and learn shechitah while building Jewish education there.
Story: The Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Simon Yakovshvili directing him to travel to Kutaisi in Soviet Georgia and study the art of shechitah. He told him to defer pursuing a shidduch and to consult with Avraham Levik Slavin and Schneur Zalman Altshuler on educational projects, requesting regular updates on all accomplishments.
Tags: georgia, kutaisi, shechitah, russia, underground

Title: Rebbe writes to Rabbi Yakovshvili about shechitah and Kutaisi
Summary: The Rebbe instructs Rabbi Simon Yakovshvili to return to Kutaisi, learn shechitah, and coordinate Jewish education there.
Story: Despite being in Riga, the Rebbe directed activity in remote Soviet Georgia. He instructed Yakovshvili to consult with Avraham Levik Slavin and Schneur Zalman Altshuler about educational projects and report back regularly.
Tags: letter, kutaisi, georgia, shechitah, russia

Title: Chatzkevich appointed rabbi of Kupishok
Summary: On 15 Cheshvan 5688 the Rebbe Rayatz congratulated R. Chatzkevich and the chassidim of Kupishok on his appointment as their rabbi.
Story: At the start of 5688 (autumn 1927), R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich was accepted as rabbi of Kupishok. The Rebbe wrote two letters dated 15 Cheshvan 5688 (Igros Kodesh vol. 16, letters 5810-5811): one to Chatzkevich blessing his appointment and asking him to set up public shiurim in nigleh and chassidus, and one to the Kupishok chassidim congratulating them on selecting one of the foremost Tomchei Tmimim alumni.
Tags: chatzkevich, kupishok, rabbinate, tomchei-tmimim

Title: Rebbe praises Shimon Bliner for establishing Mishnah and chasidic classes in Moscow
Summary: From Riga, the Rebbe writes to the Chasid Shimon Bliner praising his establishment of underground Mishnah and chasidic philosophy classes in Moscow.
Story: The Rebbe wrote, 'I enjoyed reading that you established classes in Mishnah and chasidic philosophy. I read the names of those involved; please share with them my blessing.' This was one of many letters showing the Rebbe's intimate involvement in underground Russian Jewish activity from his Riga base.
Tags: moscow, russia, underground, mishnah, chasidut

Title: Rebbe writes to Shimon Bliner praising Moscow Torah classes
Summary: The Rebbe lauds Chasid Shimon Bliner for establishing underground classes in Mishnah and chasidic philosophy in Moscow.
Story: The Rebbe wrote that he 'enjoyed reading' about the new classes and asked Bliner to share his blessing with all involved. The letter is preserved in Igrot Kodesh volume 16.
Tags: moscow, russia, underground, letter

Title: First meeting of Vaad Magen UMekhaseh held in Riga
Summary: Two weeks after arriving, the Rebbe convenes prominent rabbis to form the Committee for the Protection and Care of Russian Jewry.
Story: The committee included Rabbi Yosef Rosen (the Rogotchover Gaon), Rabbi Meir Hildesheimer of Berlin, and Rabbi Mendel Zak of Riga. It later gained the backing of Rabbis Yisrael Meir Kagan and Chaim Ozer Grodzinski, and organized worldwide fasts and prayers for Soviet Jewry.
Tags: committee, russian-jewry, rogotchover, hildesheimer

Title: Vaad Magen UMekhaseh founded to protect Russian Jewry
Summary: Two weeks after arriving in Riga, the Rebbe convenes prominent rabbis to create the Committee for the Protection and Care of Russian Jewry.
Story: The first meeting included Rabbi Yosef Rosen (the Rogotchover Gaon), Berlin chief rabbi Dr. Meir Hildesheimer, and Rabbi Mendel Zak. The committee laid out a plan to enlist major Jewish groups like the JDC and Alliance Israélite Universelle. Renowned rabbis including the Chafetz Chaim and Rabbi Chaim Ozer Grodzinski joined the effort.
Tags: russia, underground, joint distribution committee, agudah, rogatchover

Title: Rebbe Rayatz rents two apartments in Riga
Summary: On 27 Cheshvan 5688, after a month in a hotel, the Rebbe Rayatz rented two apartments in Riga to house his family, his mother, and a place of prayer.
Story: After about a month at the Kommerz Hotel, the Rebbe Rayatz secured two small apartments on two floors. The lower floor housed his mother the Rebbetzin and contained the prayer room and part of his library. The upper floor was for the Rebbe and his daughters Chaya Mushka and Sheina, while his daughter Chana and son-in-law Rashag took a separate apartment.
Tags: riga, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, synagogue

Title: Professor Chavkin inspects Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw
Summary: On 5 Tevet 5688, Professor Mordechai Zev (Vladimir) Chavkin inspected Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw and wrote a detailed report on the institution.
Story: Professor Chavkin visited the yeshiva and recorded that 8 teachers aged 35-50 ran four classes plus a self-study fifth class for older students. He counted approximately 250 students aged 10 to 20, of whom 80 lived on-site and received meals; the rest stayed with families. He documented the committee leadership including Zalmanov, Shmotkin, Gurarie, Rothstein, Blum, and Rabbi Yosef Kalisch.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, chavkin, inspection

Title: Ramash departs Riga for Berlin
Summary: Two months after arriving from Russia, the Ramash departed Riga for Berlin, where he would attend lectures and university courses for years to come.
Story: The day after he came to Berlin, the Ramash represented his future father-in-law at a convention of Agudath Israel. In Berlin he attended lectures by Rabbi Yechiel Yaakov Weinberg of the Rabbinical Seminary, and with Weinberg's help registered at Friedrich Wilhelm University for courses in geometry, physics, and higher mathematics.
Tags: berlin, germany, riga, university, weinberg, agudath-israel

Title: Rebbe writes detailed letter to Baruch Rizik about leaving Russia
Summary: Six weeks after his departure, the Rebbe describes the emotional farewell at the Leningrad station and his anguished overnight journey.
Story: In a forthcoming letter to a Chasid in Rostov, the Rebbe described the thousands who filled the station 'full of emotion,' the eighteen-hour overnight train ride, and his prayer for the Jews left behind. The letter survives in Igrot Kodesh, volume 17.
Tags: letter, rostov, igrot-kodesh, exile

Title: Rebbe writes Rizik recounting departure from Russia
Summary: In a forthcoming letter to Baruch Rizik in Rostov, the Rebbe shares the anguish of leaving Russia six weeks earlier.
Story: The Rebbe described thousands filling the Leningrad station, 'full of emotion,' surging toward the train. He wrote of passing 'eighteen hours with anguish in the heart, pain in the soul, the darkness of the night, the ringing of the wheels of the train only adding to the sense of sadness.' His spirits lifted when Latvian Chasidim boarded the train an hour from Riga and sang the joyous melody from his Lubavitch chuppah three decades earlier.
Tags: russia, rostov, leningrad, exile, letter

Title: Passing of R. Chaim Yeshaya Schneersohn, rabbi of Romen
Summary: R. Chaim Yeshaya Schneersohn, longtime rabbi of Romen and descendant of the Tzemach Tzedek, passed away on 15 Kislev 5688.
Story: R. Chaim Yeshaya Schneersohn passed away on 15 Kislev 5688 after more than a quarter-century as rabbi of Romen. A direct descendant of the Tzemach Tzedek through the Kapuster and Retchitsa branches of the dynasty, he had been a leading anash figure in the city during the late Tsarist period. His signature stands at the foot of the 1910 Romen petition to the St. Petersburg rabbinical conference preserved in the Rebbe Rashab's archive.
Tags: russia, romen, chaim-yeshaya-schneersohn, schneersohn-family, yahrzeit

Title: R' Chaim Yeshaya Schneersohn passes away in Romny
Summary: R' Chaim Yeshaya Schneersohn, rabbi of Romny and descendant of the Tzemach Tzedek, passed away on 15 Kislev 5688.
Story: R' Chaim Yeshaya, a great-grandson of the Tzemach Tzedek through the Maharil of Kopust, had served Romny since 5661. His passing left the Romny rabbinate vacant during the harsh Soviet years, eventually leading to R' Yani Gurarie being offered the position.
Tags: chaim yeshaya schneersohn, romny, rabbinate, chabad, kopust

Title: First 19 Kislev farbrengen at the Kiev yeshiva ketana
Summary: Young students in Kiev held their first 19 Kislev farbrengen at the urging of R' Binyamin Gorodetzky.
Story: R' Binyamin Gorodetzky asked the author to collect money from the boys of the underground yeshiva ketana in Kiev to organize a 19 Kislev gathering. The resulting farbrengen was the author's first participation in a Chag HaGeulah celebration, held quietly as Soviet surveillance of the yeshiva was beginning to tighten and synagogues were being closed across Russia.
Tags: kiev, 19-kislev, farbrengen, tomchei-tmimim, russia, binyamin-gorodetzky

Title: Rebbe writes letter to anash and temimim in Russia (19 Kislev)
Summary: From outside Russia, the Rebbe wrote to his Chasidim 'in the country of my birth' saying he had been forced to leave.
Story: Marking the Chabad festival of 19 Kislev, the Rebbe addressed his followers in the Soviet Union, recounting the Yevsektsia's persecution of his efforts to strengthen Torah. 'I was forced to leave Russia,' he wrote. 'My heart and soul are with the anash and temimim in our country.'
Tags: 19 kislev, russia, letter, yevsektsia, exile

Title: Rebbe writes Haffkine about strategizing against Yevsektzia
Summary: The Rebbe writes scientist-philanthropist Waldemar Haffkine in German, urging a secret meeting of Jewish leaders to counter the Yevsektzia.
Story: The Rebbe explained that being just outside Russia's border allowed him to continue his efforts more freely for Russian Jewry. He told Haffkine he had 'not given up on Russia' and now sought to enlist his help in arranging a private meeting of Jewish leaders to find a way to 'extinguish the power of the Yevsektzia.' He emphasized the effort must be conducted with the utmost secrecy.
Tags: yevsektzia, haffkine, russia, underground, berlin

Title: Rebbe writes to Haffkine from Riga about Russian Jewry
Summary: The Rebbe writes in German to scientist Waldemar Haffkine, explaining that Riga allows him broader reach to help Russian Jewry.
Story: The Rebbe told Haffkine, 'I have not given up on Russia. My residence is just outside the border so I can continue my efforts for Russian Jewry.' He explained he could now correspond more freely and proposed strategies against the Yevsektzia.
Tags: haffkine, russia, letter, yevsektzia

Title: Prof. Khavkin writes detailed survey of the Warsaw yeshiva building
Summary: On 5 Tevet 5688 Prof. Mordechai Zev (Vladimir) Khavkin wrote a detailed English-language survey of the Tomchei Tmimim building in Warsaw.
Story: On 5 Tevet 5688 (29 December 1927) Prof. Mordechai Zev (Vladimir) Khavkin penned a detailed report on the Warsaw yeshiva branch, describing its layout — kitchen and dining hall on the ground floor, five spacious classrooms above, a sleeping attic, and an old single-story wing converted to a prayer hall for the public. He noted that the equipment, of the simplest possible kind, was funded by a Joint Distribution Committee reconstruction grant from Mr. Bernhard Cohen. The report was later translated from English and printed in Beton Chabad issues 34–35.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-tmimim, khavkin, joint-distribution-committee, mlawska-street

Title: Anash request the Rebbe relocate from Riga to Poland
Summary: In the winter of 5688, chassidim in Poland and Lithuania formally asked the Rebbe to move his residence from Riga to their region, a request the Rebbe declined.
Story: The Rebbe responded that while their reasons were sound, various weighty considerations made the move impossible at that time. The request would be renewed repeatedly over the following years until the Rebbe finally agreed to move in 1933.
Tags: riga, poland, lithuania, letter, anash

Title: Author begins studies at Polotsk Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva
Summary: The author and his hometown friend Moshe Roxin enrolled for the winter zman at the underground Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Polotsk.
Story: About thirty older bochurim were studying in Polotsk under rosh yeshiva R' Yechezkel Himmelstein (later murdered in Riga) and the celebrated mashgiach R' Shlomo Chaim Kesselman. The author and his fellow townsman Moshe Roxin — son of the Zlobin shochet R' Refoel Eliezer Roxin — were placed in lodgings ('eshel') and joined the shiur on the Bava Metzia mishna 'ha-zahav koneh et ha-kesef.' Two weeks in, the mashgiach told the author he could remain but that Moshe, weaker in learning, must transfer to Vitebsk; the author chose to accompany his friend.
Tags: polotsk, tomchei-tmimim, yeshiva, belarus, soviet-union, yechezkel-himmelstein, shlomo-chaim-kesselman

Title: Author studies Tanach and dikduk with R' Itshe Matlies in Zlobin
Summary: Through the winter of 5688 in Zlobin, the author studied Tanach and Hebrew grammar with the veteran melamed R' Itshe Matlies (Riskin) by night to train as a precise baal koreh.
Story: By day he learned Gemara with Rabbi Benyaminson, and in the evenings R' Itshe taught him Yirmiyahu and dikduk. Toward the end of the term R' Itshe drilled him word-by-word through the opening chapters of Shemos, demanding on which letter the trop fell and why. Half a century later the author still retained the rules of mileil and milra he had learned then.
Tags: zlobin, kriah, dikduk, baal-koreh, evening-study, soviet-era

Title: Jews begin settling in Birobidzhan
Summary: Stalin's Jewish province on the Chinese border opened for settlement, with Yiddish street signs but banned religious practice.
Story: To promote secular Jewish socialism, the Soviet government created a Jewish autonomous province in remote Siberia. Religious practice was banned and the Jewish population never rose above forty-five thousand. Only after the fall of the Soviet Union did Judaism return to Birobidzhan, when Rabbi Mordechai Scheiner became the community's rabbi in 2002.
Tags: birobidzhan, stalin, jewish autonomous oblast, siberia, yiddish

Title: Library visitor publishes description in HaOlam London
Summary: On 22 Elul 5688, the London journal HaOlam published a visitor's account of the Lubavitch library highlighting its manuscript treasures and incunabula.
Story: The visitor described a 440-year-old manuscript by R' Avraham Saba (author of Tzror HaMor), Ralbag's 1476 Torah commentary, and a Ramban printed in Lisbon in 1489. The published descriptions help corroborate which volumes were in the collection at that time, including the eight-volume Shemoneh Shearim autograph by R' Shmuel Vital.
Tags: library, haolam, london, ralbag, ramban, avraham saba, manuscripts

Title: Likkutei Torah reprint completed in Warsaw by Agudas HaTmimim of America
Summary: The Likkutei Torah reprint, sponsored by Agudas HaTmimim of America, was completed in 5688.
Story: One thousand copies were printed; five hundred were given as a gift to Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw and five hundred were shipped to America, bound, and sold for five dollars the set. The title page credited Agudas HaTmimim of America (the alumni of Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch) as sponsor, with the final volume listing every contributor. The printing significantly lifted the morale of anash in America.
Tags: likkutei torah, warsaw, tomchei tmimim, agudas hatmimim

Title: Ma'amad committee founded under R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin in USA
Summary: In summer 5688, a dedicated ma'amad committee was established under Agudas Chassidei Chabad to support the Frierdiker Rebbe's household, with R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin as chairman.
Story: R' Yechezkel Feigin had written from Riga that Havlin and Rivkin would be enlisted to revive ma'amad fundraising in America. Because the Rebbe's household in Riga was under genuine financial strain — only about $300 per month was reaching him — Agudas Chassidei Chabad created a special ma'amad department chaired by R' Rivkin, with the tomim R' Elchonon Fogelman as a board member. A circular was sent to Anash, and the idea that ma'amad was its own primary obligation — not merely a line in the Agudah budget — began to take hold.
Tags: maamad, agudas chassidei chabad, rivkin, fagelman, feigin, fundraising, bais chayeinu

Title: R' Alter Simchowitz reappointed chief mashpia of Warsaw yeshiva
Summary: Before Tishrei 5689 R' Alter Simchowitz visited the Rebbe Rayatz in Riga and was appointed chief mashpia of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw.
Story: The reappointment was short-lived: within a few months Simchowitz had to return again to Eretz Yisrael, where he resumed serving as mashpia at Yeshivat Toras Emet and as mashpia of Anash in Jerusalem.
Tags: riga, warsaw, alter simchowitz, tomchei tmimim

Title: R. Yechezkel Feigin writes about plans to expand Warsaw yeshiva
Summary: On 3 Iyar 5688, secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to R. Yisrael Jacobson in America about plans to expand Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw to two or three times its size.
Story: Feigin reported that the Rebbe Rayatz was deeply moved by the conduct and condition of the Warsaw yeshiva, which had approximately 250 students and was the largest Chabad yeshiva. He noted that there was great financial hardship despite the achievement, and that the Rebbe was determined to take responsibility for substantially expanding the institution materially and spiritually. The director of Agudas Chassidei Chabad in America was being informed in preparation for fundraising efforts.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, yechezkel feigin, yisrael jacobson, expansion

Title: R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevitch appointed mashpia for Lithuania
Summary: In the summer of 5688 the Rebbe Rayatz appointed R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevitch to serve as traveling mashpia for the Kovno, Vilna, and Dvinsk districts.
Story: R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevitch, who served as rav of Kopishok, was commissioned by the Rebbe Rayatz in summer 5688 to travel among the towns of the Kovno, Vilna, and Dvinsk regions, establishing regular shiurim in Chassidus among anash.
Tags: lithuania, kovno, vilna, dvinsk, mashpiim, yisrael-noach-chatzkevitch, kopishok

Title: Rayatz campaigns to send matzah to Soviet Jews
Summary: From his new base outside Russia, the Rayatz organized campaigns to supply matzah to Jews still trapped under Soviet rule.
Story: With Passover observance increasingly difficult in the USSR, the Rayatz mobilized international networks to ship matzah eastward. The effort continued through 1929 and laid groundwork for ongoing covert religious support.
Tags: matzah, passover, soviet union, russia

Title: Rayatz writes to his uncle about Ohel repairs
Summary: At the start of 5689 the Rayatz wrote to his uncle Rabbi Moshe Leib Ginzburg about ongoing efforts to repair the Lubavitch Ohel.
Story: At the beginning of 5689 (1928), the Rayatz wrote a letter to his uncle Rabbi Moshe Leib Ginzburg discussing efforts to make repairs at the Ohel in Lubavitch. The correspondence is preserved in Igrot Kodesh vol. 15. Soviet conditions made such practical work extremely difficult.
Tags: rayatz, lubavitch, ohel, russia, moshe leib ginzburg

Title: Rebbe outlines master plan for an open scholarly library
Summary: In summer 5688 the Frierdiker Rebbe summoned his librarian Chaim Liberman and outlined a fifteen-year plan to build an open scholarly library at Lubavitch.
Story: After Liberman's own emigration from Russia in early summer 5688, the Rebbe shared his vision: rather than a closed private collection, the library would be opened to researchers like the seminary or British Museum libraries. He envisioned modest annual book purchases over about fifteen years, eventual cataloging, and a dedicated building — perhaps named for a wealthy donor — to house the future thousands of volumes.
Tags: riga, library, rayatz, chaim-liberman, bibliography

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Riga and begins publishing kuntreisim
Summary: From 5688 onward, Rebbe Rayatz published his maamarim as Kuntreisim and his sichot as Likutei Dibburim in Riga.
Story: Following his release from Soviet captivity, Rebbe Rayatz settled in Riga in 1928. There he established a publishing program of maamarim in the Kuntres series and sichot in Likutei Dibburim. The Riga period continued through 1933.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, riga, latvia, kuntres, likutei dibburim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz farbrengs with Tomchei Tmimim students on Purim
Summary: On Purim 5688 in Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz held a farbrengen with Tomchei Tmimim students that lasted past 2 a.m.
Story: After the Megillah reading the night of Purim, a select group of Anash dined with the Rebbe Rayatz, who spoke of Chassidus and avodah until past midnight. The following afternoon at 3:30 he came to the yeshiva hall for the Purim seuda, with Anash seated at the tables and students standing in rows singing Chabad melodies. The farbrengen continued until 2 a.m., after which the Rebbe told a chassid in the office that he had not imagined the yeshiva in such an exalted state, calling it 'a piece of my father's work'.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, rayatz, purim, farbrengen

Title: Rebbe Rayatz travels to Warsaw to visit Tomchei Tmimim
Summary: On 28 Shevat 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz departed from Riga for Warsaw to visit Tomchei Tmimim, staying about two weeks.
Story: After preparations begun on the first night of Chanukah, the Rebbe Rayatz traveled to Warsaw on 28 Shevat 5688 and stayed approximately two weeks. The trip combined an inspection of Tomchei Tmimim with visits to Anash in Warsaw and the surrounding region. Detailed accounts were preserved by accompanying chassidim and later published in Sefer HaToldos and the Sefer HaMaamarim and Sichos of 5688.
Tags: warsaw, riga, tomchei tmimim, rayatz, visit

Title: Rebbe Rayatz vacations in Bulduri near Riga
Summary: During summer 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz spent a month in Bulduri near Riga, though he continued working rather than truly resting.
Story: Worn out by imprisonment, exile, and intensive work, the Rebbe Rayatz had been advised to rest. He delayed it until midsummer, when he took a month-long stay in the seaside resort of Bulduri near Riga. By his own account he did nothing for his health there, continuing to work through correspondence each day.
Tags: riga, bulduri, latvia, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, health

Title: Rebbe Rayatz visits Dvinsk en route to Warsaw
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz made a brief visit to Dvinsk in late Shevat 5688, traveling from Riga to Warsaw.
Story: In late Shevat 5688 (February 1928), the Rebbe Rayatz stopped in Dvinsk en route from Riga to Warsaw. He addressed the local anash during this short visit, encouraging the Chabad community of the city.
Tags: dvinsk, rayatz, riga, warsaw, latvia

Title: Rebbe Rayatz visits Vilna yeshiva after Warsaw trip
Summary: In Adar 5688, after visiting Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz traveled to Vilna to visit the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva there.
Story: Following his Warsaw visit during Adar 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz continued to Vilna to personally visit the young Tomchei Tmimim branch. The directors had previously requested he come and also pleaded for a qualified candidate to serve as combined Rosh Yeshiva, mashpia, and mashgiach.
Tags: vilna, warsaw, rebbe rayatz, visit

Title: Rebbe Rayatz's first visit to Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw
Summary: On Thursday of Parshas Tetzaveh 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz visited Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw for the first time, inspecting offices, classrooms, and dormitories.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz toured the entire yeshiva, beginning with the office where he examined account books and student records, then meeting individually with the rosh yeshivas, mashgichim, and mashpi'im. He proceeded through every classroom and the main study hall, telling the chief mashgiach 'fine personal property,' inspected the dormitories and dining hall, and recited Shehecheyanu. He later remarked that the yeshiva was 'an everlasting edifice — but in its inner dimension'.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, rayatz, visit

Title: Reports on the state of mikvaot in Drivin recorded by R' Ashurov
Summary: Documentation about the condition of the mikvaot in Drivin was created in 5688, later published in Toldos Chabad B'Russia HaSovietit.
Story: In 5688 (1928), R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov, then rabbi of Drivin, submitted reports on the state of the local mikvaot. These reports were later published in Sefer Toldos Chabad B'Russia HaSovietit, p. 174.
Tags: drivin, mikvaot, ashurov, russia

Title: Riga library acquisition begins Rebbe's world-class collection
Summary: In the summer of 1928 the Rebbe and librarian Chaim Lieberman began transforming his personal collection into a world-class research library in Riga.
Story: The Rebbe envisioned a public library for research like the British Museum, requiring thousands of books, financing, a facility, and a catalog. The London paper HaOlam soon hailed the collection as a treasure of Jewish artifacts, citing one of the oldest printed siddurim from 1475 and 950 Haggadot. The Rebbe sought books from booksellers as far as Yemen, Australia, and Africa.
Tags: riga, library, lieberman, research, haolam

Title: Romen Tomchei Tmimim shut down just as the author arrives
Summary: In the summer of 5688 the author travelled to Romen to learn in Tomchei Tmimim, only to discover on arrival that the underground yeshiva had just been broken up by Soviet pressure.
Story: The Yevsektsiya was systematically destroying the remaining small yeshivos by arresting or hounding the magidei shiur, since the young bochurim themselves could not be jailed. Romen, a major chassidic centre, still hosted a functioning Tomchei Tmimim, so the author travelled there with Rabbi Benyaminson, who was also exploring a rabbinic post in the town. They arrived to find the yeshiva already dispersed, and the author returned to Zlobin to continue learning with Rabbi Benyaminson through the summer.
Tags: romen, tomchei-tmimim, yevsektsiya, yeshiva-closure, soviet-era

Title: Rotstein becomes secretary at Warsaw yeshiva
Summary: From 5688 onward, R. Moshe Leib Rotstein served as secretary of the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva in Warsaw.
Story: Beginning in 5688 (1928), R. Moshe Leib Rotstein took up the position of secretary at the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva in Warsaw. He continued in this role for years, serving the institution under the Frierdiker Rebbe's leadership.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei temimim, moshe leib rotstein, secretary

Title: Sixth edition of Likkutei Torah printed from existing plates
Summary: The sixth edition of Likkutei Torah was printed in תרפ"ח from the original stereotype plates of the תרס"ד Vilna edition, which had survived WWI intact in the Rashab's possession.
Story: Per his תרס"ב contract with the Vilna printer, the Rashab retained ownership of the stereotype plates of Likkutei Torah. Having confirmed in 1918 that the plates remained whole, the sixth edition could be issued in תרפ"ח directly from those same plates without resetting the type.
Tags: likkutei torah, stereotype plates, rashab

Title: Trotsky banished from Russia to Alma Alta
Summary: Leon Trotsky was banished to remote Alma Alta as Stalin consolidated power.
Story: Trotsky's exile fulfilled the Rashab's 1920 prediction that 'Trotsky will be exiled.' He was deported from Russia entirely two years later and eventually relocated to Mexico after living in European cities. He would be assassinated in 1940 by a Stalinist agent.
Tags: trotsky, soviet union, stalin, exile

Title: Trotsky banished to Alma Ata
Summary: Stalin banished Leon Trotsky to remote Alma Ata in Kazakhstan.
Story: In 1928, fulfilling the Rashab's 1920 forecast that Trotsky would be exiled, Stalin banished his rival to Alma Ata. Two years later, Trotsky would be deported from the Soviet Union entirely.
Tags: trotsky, soviet union, stalin, exile, alma ata

Title: Tzemach Tzedek portrait on the Remigalski Riga calendar
Summary: The 5689 calendar published by Remigalski in Riga featured the Tzemach Tzedek's portrait on its cover, and was also issued as a Shanah Tovah card.
Story: In 5689 (1928-29), the Remigalski publishing house in Riga produced a yearly calendar with the Tzemach Tzedek's portrait on the title page; a copy is in the Chabad library. The same image was distributed as a New Year greeting card, reflecting how widely circulated the Tzemach Tzedek's image had become by the interwar period.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, portrait, riga, latvia, remigalski, shanah tovah

Title: Underground learning in Kiev's upper shiur during winter 5688
Summary: In winter 5688 the author was promoted to the higher class at the Kiev cheder katan and the shiur began meeting clandestinely in shuls and private homes.
Story: Fear of arrest forced the small class to learn in hiding, sometimes in a large shul where the bitter cold made the boys' toes burn, and other times crammed onto a bed in the tiny room of R' Zalman Levin of Kursk. From then on R' Zalman Levin reviewed the shiur with the author, materially strengthening his Gemara study. The author writes that this period brought him to feel the meaning of 'Torah is upheld only by one who kills himself for it,' and that it eventually opened the door to Tomchei Temimim in Vitebsk.
Tags: kiev, yeshiva-ketana, underground, ussr, ukraine, zalman-levin-korsk

Title: Warsaw Haggadah with 'Shem MiShmuel' commentary by Shmuel Bornstein of Sochatchov
Summary: The 'Shem MiShmuel' Haggadah commentary by Rebbe Shmuel Bornstein of Sochatchov was published in Warsaw.
Story: In 5688 (1928), the Haggadah with the 'Shem MiShmuel' commentary by Rebbe Shmuel ben Avraham Bornstein of Sochatchov was published in Warsaw, edited by Chanoch Heinich Falman. Printed by Wegmeister, the 64-leaf octavo edition became one of the central Chassidic Haggadah commentaries of the interwar era. It distilled the Sochatchov Chassidic teachings on Passover.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, sochatchov, warsaw, shem mishmuel, bornstein

Title: Yeshivas Rabbeinu Yitzchok Elchonon becomes Yeshivah College
Summary: The institution evolved from a yeshivah into Yeshivah College, the precursor to Yeshiva University.
Story: The transition reflected the slow emergence of American Jewish higher learning. At the time, serious Jewish scholarship still required travel to Poland, Lithuania, or Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: yeshiva-university, rietz, new-york, united-states

Title: Yisrael Yehuda Levin began service in Tomchei Tmimim Vitebsk
Summary: After Pesach 5688, Yisrael Yehuda Levin began his work in the underground Tomchei Tmimim in Vitebsk together with the bachur Avraham Kvashe.
Story: After Pesach in 5688 (spring 1928), Yisrael Yehuda Levin began serving in the clandestine Tomchei Tmimim network in Vitebsk alongside the bachur Avraham Kvashe (later in Riga). He worked there for the entire stretch of that period before later moving on to similar work in Kiev. This was during the era of intense Soviet persecution of religious education.
Tags: vitebsk, tomchei-tmimim, underground-yeshiva, soviet-russia, avraham-kvashe

Title: Grodner Moment publishes feature on the Rebbe's activity in Riga hotel
Summary: The Polish Yiddish daily Grodner Moment reports on the Rebbe's prayer, audiences, and Shabbat maamarim at his Riga hotel.
Story: The paper described the Rebbe sitting 'day and night in a room designated for prayer and learning,' meeting all types of Jews in the afternoons. On Shabbat, large crowds flooded the hotel to hear the Rebbe recite a maamar, with his voice 'becoming stronger and more flowing, words streaming from his mouth, quotes from the Bible, Talmud, and Zohar woven and seasoned with parables.'
Tags: riga, press, yiddish, grodner moment, poland

Title: Grodner Moment reports on Rebbe's activities in Riga hotel
Summary: The Yiddish daily reports on the masses flocking to the Rebbe's hotel for prayers, blessings, and Shabbat maamarim.
Story: The paper described corridors 'packed with masses of people' awaiting audiences, and Shabbat afternoons when 'the hotel loses its mundane weekday state' as people flooded in to hear the Rebbe recite a maamar weaving Bible, Talmud, and Zohar.
Tags: press, yiddish-press, grodno, riga

Title: Rebbe sends second letter to Haffkine on Russian Jewry strategy
Summary: The Rebbe follows up his earlier German-language correspondence with Haffkine pressing for action against the Yevsektzia.
Story: The Rebbe again emphasized the need for a private meeting of prominent Jews to counter what he called 'the greatest danger and damage to the activities of Russian Jewry.' It appears, however, that the suggestion of such a private meeting did not prove successful in practice.
Tags: haffkine, russia, yevsektzia, underground, letter

Title: Rebbe writes to Haffkine proposing secret meeting against Yevsektzia
Summary: The Rebbe urges Haffkine to help arrange a confidential gathering of Jewish leaders to counter the Yevsektzia.
Story: Calling the Yevsektzia 'the greatest danger and damage to the activities of Russian Jewry,' the Rebbe stressed the meeting must be done 'with the utmost secrecy.' The plan ultimately did not materialize.
Tags: haffkine, yevsektzia, russia, letter

Title: Detroit Jewish Chronicle praises Rebbe's impact on Latvian Jewry
Summary: The Detroit Jewish Chronicle reports that the Rebbe's exile has been a boon for Orthodox Jewry in Latvia.
Story: The paper wrote that 'the Lubavitcher Rebbe had brought a great deal of activity into the life of Orthodox Jewry in Latvia.' It concluded that 'Soviet Russia has thus, by expelling the Lubavitcher Rebbe, done a good turn to the Jews of Latvia.' The story was an early sign that the Rebbe's influence transcended his immediate community.
Tags: press, latvia, detroit, united states, soviet

Title: Detroit Jewish Chronicle reports on Rebbe's impact in Latvia
Summary: The American Jewish paper reports that Soviet Russia inadvertently helped Latvian Jewry by expelling the Lubavitcher Rebbe.
Story: The paper wrote, 'The Lubavitcher Rebbe had brought a great deal of activity into the life of Orthodox Jewry in Latvia. And Soviet Russia has thus, by expelling the Lubavitcher Rebbe, done a good turn to the Jews of Latvia.'
Tags: press, detroit, american-press, riga

Title: Rebbe corresponds with the Rogatchover on 22 Shevat
Summary: On 22 Shevat 5688 the future Rebbe wrote a halachic question to the Rogatchover Gaon.
Story: On 22 Shevat 5688 (Feb 13, 1928), the future Lubavitcher Rebbe wrote a halachic letter to the Rogatchover Gaon. The Rogatchover replied on 24 Shevat, and the Rebbe wrote back again on 21 Adar of that year. The Rebbe later copied the exchange in his Reshimot, notebook 33.
Tags: the rebbe, rogatchover, halacha, correspondence

Title: Rogatchover replies to the Rebbe on 24 Shevat
Summary: The Rogatchover Gaon replied to the Rebbe on 24 Shevat 5688.
Story: Two days after the Rebbe's question, on 24 Shevat 5688 (Feb 15, 1928), the Rogatchover Gaon sent his response. The exchange formed part of a brief halachic correspondence later recorded by the Rebbe.
Tags: the rebbe, rogatchover, halacha, correspondence

Title: Rebbe Rayatz departs Riga for Warsaw visit
Summary: On Sunday 28 Shevat 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz left Riga for Warsaw, responding to the Polish Chabad community's request for a visit.
Story: After the Warsaw Chabad community invited the Rebbe to settle there following his exit from Russia, he replied that this was impossible but he wished to visit. He set out from Riga in the morning, stopping in Dvinsk, Vilna, and other towns en route. The trip combined visits to yeshivas and Chasidim with meetings on Soviet Jewry relief.
Tags: riga, warsaw, poland, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Warsaw for his first visit
Summary: On erev Rosh Chodesh Adar 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Warsaw from Riga for his first major visit to Polish anash.
Story: Leaving Riga on Sunday morning 28 Shvat 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz traveled to Warsaw via Dvinsk, the border stations, and Vilna, where chassidim greeted him at each stop. He reached Warsaw on the morning of erev Rosh Chodesh Adar (Feb 20, 1928), lodging in the home of R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov. Over the following weeks he received thousands of visitors, met with rabbanim and admorim, said maamarim, and traveled briefly to Otwock to visit R. Moshe Hornstein.
Tags: warsaw, rayatz, riga, vilna, dvinsk, first visit

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Warsaw for three-week visit
Summary: On Monday eve of Rosh Chodesh Adar 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Warsaw for a three-week stay, followed by a week in Otwock.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Warsaw on the eve of Rosh Chodesh Adar I. He spent three weeks in the city and nearly a week in Otwock, visiting the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva and meeting with Chasidim. He also held several meetings related to aid for Soviet Jewry, returning via a week-long stop in Vilna.
Tags: warsaw, poland, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, tomchei tmimim, otwock

Title: Rebbe Rayatz returns to Riga after five-week journey
Summary: On 28 Adar 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz returned home from a five-week journey that included visits to the yeshivos in Warsaw and Vilna.
Story: In letters dated 6 and 8 Nissan 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz reported having returned on 28 Adar exhausted but spiritually nourished by his trip. He described the lasting positive impression made on him by Tomchei Tmimim of Warsaw and the yeshiva in Vilna. He resolved upon returning home to personally take on the project of expanding the Warsaw yeshiva.
Tags: riga, warsaw, vilna, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz's first visit to Vilna after leaving Russia
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz visited Vilna for about a week in late Adar 5688, his first visit to Lithuania after leaving Russia.
Story: A few months after leaving Soviet Russia, the Rebbe traveled to Warsaw and on his return to Riga stopped in Vilna at the urgent request of local chassidim and the Tomchei Tmimim students there. Originally planned for two days, he extended his stay to a full week after a further appeal from chassidim in Dolhinov. He delivered a maamar at the Apatov shul where the yeshiva was housed, prayed there on Shabbat, and met with Rabbi Chaim Ozer Grodzinski regarding aid to Russian Jewry.
Tags: vilna, lithuania, poland, rayatz, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rebbe visits Warsaw yeshivah and conducts long Purim farbrengen
Summary: Four months after departing Russia, the Rebbe travels to Warsaw for two weeks, visiting the yeshivah and holding a marathon Purim farbrengen.
Story: The Rebbe met with Warsaw's leading rabbis and communal leaders, deepening awareness of the plight of Russian Jewry, and spent time in yechidut with many Chasidim. The highlight was a long Purim farbrengen with the yeshivah students that began at 3:30 p.m. and did not end until 2:00 a.m. The Warsaw yeshivah had grown to 250 students by that year.
Tags: warsaw, poland, purim, tomchei temimim, farbrengen

Title: Rebbe Rayatz visits Otwock on Shushan Purim
Summary: On Shushan Purim 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz traveled from Warsaw to Otwock to visit his uncle R. Moshe Hornstein.
Story: During his first Warsaw visit, the Rebbe Rayatz traveled on Shushan Purim 5688 (March 7, 1928) to Otwock, the home of his uncle R. Moshe Hornstein, son-in-law of the Rebbe Maharash. Anash and select Tomchei Tmimim students joined him in Otwock for Shabbat Parshat Ki Tisa before he returned to Warsaw for further yechidut sessions.
Tags: otwock, shushan purim, rayatz, moshe hornstein

Title: Rebbe writes again to the Rogatchover on 21 Adar
Summary: On 21 Adar 5688 the Rebbe sent a second letter to the Rogatchover Gaon.
Story: Completing their exchange, the future Rebbe wrote back to the Rogatchover Gaon on 21 Adar 5688 (March 13, 1928). The full set of letters was later published in his Reshimot.
Tags: the rebbe, rogatchover, halacha, correspondence

Title: 'The New Book of Lamentations' published in Hadoar
Summary: An anonymous letter in the US Hebrew newspaper exposes the bleak conditions and anti-religious motives behind the Soviet colonies.
Story: The writer charged that the Soviet government was using colonization 'to break down and destroy the Jewish spirit.' He described hunger, harsh winters, and Potemkin-village shows put on for visiting JDC officials.
Tags: hadoar, agricultural-colonies, russia, yevsektzia

Title: Hadoar publishes 'The New Book of Lamentations' on Soviet Jewish colonies
Summary: The Hebrew US weekly Hadoar publishes an anonymous twelve-page letter describing the dire condition of Jews in Soviet agricultural colonies.
Story: The letter, addressed to JDC Moscow head Dr. Rosen, denounced the Soviet plan to relocate Jews to communal farms as a Yevsektzia scheme 'to break down and destroy the Jewish spirit.' It documented hunger, cold, and religious oppression in the colonies. 'We plow and plant with tears and harvest with despair,' the writer warned.
Tags: hadoar, russia, agricultural colonies, yevsektzia, joint distribution committee

Title: Havlin and Rivkin travel to USA to fundraise for Torat Emet
Summary: In Nisan 5688 R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin and R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin depart the Holy Land for America via Riga to fundraise for Torat Emet.
Story: In Nisan 5688 (April 1928), R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin and R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin departed the Holy Land for the United States. They stopped first in Riga to consult with the Frierdiker Rebbe on the details of their mission. From then on Havlin spent extensive time in America raising funds for the yeshiva's deficit, while Rivkin remained in the US and joined Yeshivat Torah Vodaas as a rosh metivta.
Tags: havlin, rivkin, usa, torat emet, riga, frierdiker rebbe

Title: R' Yani Gurarie sentenced to five months hard labor by Soviet authorities
Summary: After a Soviet show trial during Pesach 5688, R' Yani Gurarie was sentenced to five months of forced labor for running the underground Romny yeshiva.
Story: Following an earlier 5687 prosecution that was commuted by amnesty, the Yevsektsiya brought a fresh protokol against R' Gurarie in Teves 5688 and staged a public show trial (pokazatelni sud) on Pesach. Despite intense efforts, he was sentenced to five months of forced labor, after which the yeshiva closed.
Tags: yani gurarie, romny, tomchei tmimim, yevsektsiya, soviet union, show trial, chabad

Title: Author arrives at Tomchei Tmimim Vitebsk on Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5688
Summary: After Pesach 5688 the author traveled without authorization from Kiev to Vitebsk to join the underground Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva.
Story: Together with Avrahmaleh Kvash and Dovid Green of Kaminetz, the author defied warnings and boarded a train to Vitebsk, the major rail hub serving the Tomchei Tmimim network in Polotsk and Nevel. He arrived on the eve of Rosh Chodesh Iyar and was hosted at the home of R' Berel Yaffe, where he saw for the first time large numbers of religious boys with payos and Lubavitcher tzitzis, writing home that he had reached 'Eretz Yisrael'.
Tags: vitebsk, tomchei-tmimim, russia, berel-yaffe, kaminetz

Title: Yechezkel Feigin reports first-year progress of Vilna yeshiva
Summary: On 3 Iyar 5688, the secretary R' Yechezkel Feigin wrote to R' Israel Jacobson summarizing the Vilna yeshiva's first-year growth to 28 students.
Story: In a letter to R' Israel Jacobson dated 3 Iyar 5688, R' Yechezkel Feigin (secretary to the Rebbe Rayatz) reported that the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim had reached 28 students in its first year and that more were expected to join in the upcoming summer term.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, yechezkel feigin, israel jacobson, growth

Title: Rashag departs Riga for Paris fundraising mission
Summary: On the night of motzei Shabbos 8 Iyar 5688, R. Shmaryahu Gourary (Rashag) left Riga for Paris to raise funds for Soviet Jewry.
Story: After Passover, the Rebbe Rayatz dispatched his son-in-law Rashag to England and France to organize a fundraising effort for Soviet Jewry suffering under anti-religious persecution. In Paris he was joined by R. Alexander Sender Reinin, R. Menachem Mendel Rotshtein of Warsaw, and Mr. Guggenheim of Switzerland.
Tags: paris, france, fundraising, shmaryahu gourary, rashag, russia

Title: R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin and R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin arrive in USA from Yeshivas Toras Emes
Summary: At the end of Iyar 5688, R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin and R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin reached America to establish a dedicated fundraising office for Yeshivas Toras Emes of Eretz Yisroel.
Story: Stopping in Riga en route to receive the Frierdiker Rebbe's guidance, the two arrived in Hoboken at the end of Iyar to set up an independent office for Toras Emes — separate from Agudas Chassidei Chabad. Tension arose with Agudas Chassidei Chabad's chairman R' Chaim Zalman Kramer, who lobbied them to channel all fundraising through the existing umbrella. After weeks of negotiation and a marathon overnight meeting that briefly produced a tentative agreement, Havlin instead rented his own offices on Blake Street and later on Henry Street, installing R' Mordechai Gruner to manage it.
Tags: toras emes, eretz yisroel, hebron, fundraising, tmimim, riga, havlin, rivkin

Title: R' Chaim Liberman departs Tambov for Riga
Summary: R' Chaim Liberman left Tambov on 1 May 1928 (11 Iyar 5688) after the Rayatz secured his release.
Story: After roughly a year of imprisonment and exile, R' Chaim Liberman was released and obtained an exit permit—largely through the efforts of the Rayatz from Riga and the intervention of Latvian Sejm deputy Mordechai Dubin. A photograph in the library archive shows his last day in Tambov, marked '1 May 1928,' corresponding to 11 Iyar 5688. He stopped briefly in Moscow on the advice of fellow Chassidim R' Yaakov Maskalik and R' Shmuel Levitin not to delay his departure.
Tags: tambov, riga, r chaim liberman, rayatz, soviet, emigration

Title: Rashag meets Chief Rabbi of France in Paris
Summary: On Sunday 16 Iyar 5688, Rashag met with French Chief Rabbi Israel Levi and his secretary R. Moshe Lieber.
Story: Rashag's Paris mission included a meeting with French Chief Rabbi Israel Levi and his secretary Moshe Lieber. The following day he met Mr. Warnser, personal secretary to Baron Edmond Rothschild, as well as Mr. Bigart of the Alliance Israélite Universelle and Mr. Unger of JCA, who pledged participation in the work.
Tags: paris, france, fundraising, rashag, israel levi, russia

Title: Rayatz writes Dr. A. Freimann about lost library
Summary: On 16 Iyar 5688, Rayatz writes scholar Dr. A. Freimann that 'the Schneersohn Lubavitch library' remains in government hands but he hopes for return.
Story: Writing from exile in Riga, Rayatz tells the noted Judaica scholar Freimann that the library, internationally known as 'the book treasury of the Lubavitcher Rebbe Schneersohn,' was unlawfully seized by the Soviet government during his Rostov exile, and that he draws strength from the hope that with G-d's help it will eventually be returned.
Tags: library, rayatz, letters, freimann

Title: Rebbe writes Iyar 5688 letters on building the library
Summary: On 16 Iyar 5688 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote letters detailing his plan to enlarge the library by soliciting books from authors and dealers worldwide.
Story: From Riga the Rebbe wrote to bookseller David Frankel of Husiatyn requesting catalogues from booksellers in Yemen, Australia, Africa, France and Italy, and to R. Chaim Hillel Bloch in the Holy Land instructing him to ask authors and Jerusalem institutions to send their publications, forms, calendars and circulars. The strategy aimed to gather books and ephemera cheaply, paying only postage, in order to rebuild the collection lost in Russia.
Tags: riga, library, rayatz, book-collecting, bibliography

Title: R' Yitzchok Matmid leads Lag B'Omer 5688 farbrengen in Vitebsk
Summary: R' Yitzchok Matmid interrupted the Vitebsk shiur on Lag B'Omer 5688 and farbrenged at the home of R' Chaim Shmuel of Lubavitch.
Story: During his stay in Vitebsk's Kleiner Zeit, R' Yitzchok Matmid told R' Avraham Mayorer mid-shiur that the lesson must be shortened so a farbrengen could be held. The gathering took place at the home of R' Chaim Shmuel of Lubavitch, the shamash of the shul where the senior 'par zich' bochurim also took their meals.
Tags: vitebsk, lag-baomer, farbrengen, yitzchok-matmid, kleiner-zeit, tomchei-tmimim

Title: R' Chaim Liberman arrives in Riga
Summary: R' Chaim Liberman arrived in Riga from his Soviet exile on 19 Iyar 5688, where the Rayatz had awaited him.
Story: R' Chaim Liberman arrived in Riga at 10 PM on 19 Iyar 5688 (9 May 1928), eight days after leaving Tambov. The Rayatz wrote that day that 'today one of my secretaries, Mr. Liberman, is arriving here,' describing how Mordechai Dubin had worked for some six months to obtain his exit permit after his arrest at the same time as the Rebbe.
