Tags: riga, tambov, r chaim liberman, rayatz, mordechai dubin, latvia

Title: Rebbe details ordeals in Russia in long letter from Riga
Summary: The Rebbe writes a long letter detailing his suffering in Russia and his sense of loss after exile.
Story: He wrote, 'I fled the bad, but I have not yet found the good.' He continued, 'I was driven from my country and forced to separate from my beloved brothers and friends.' The Rebbe expressed his desire 'to live in our country of Russia, where people are putting their lives on the line for Torah and observance in the midst of deprivation.'
Tags: russia, riga, exile, letter, igrot kodesh

Title: Rebbe writes long letter detailing ordeals in Soviet Russia
Summary: The Rebbe writes that Riga is only 'temporary' and details his suffering in Russia and longing for the country he was forced to leave.
Story: He wrote, 'I fled the bad, but I have not yet found the good. I was driven from my country and forced to separate from my beloved brothers and friends.' His new stationery printed 'Riga' followed by the word 'temporary.'
Tags: letter, russia, igrot-kodesh, exile

Title: Paris assembly convened for Soviet Jewry aid
Summary: On Friday 21 Iyar 5688, Rashag convened a general assembly in Paris bringing together French Jewish leadership for Russian Jewry relief.
Story: The assembly drew Chief Rabbi Israel Levi, Chief Rabbi Eisenstadt, R. Moshe Lieber, Baron Pierre Ginzburg, S. Pollak, Mr. Unger of JCA, Mr. Bigart of the Alliance, Mr. Tedesco of the Paris Consistoire, Mr. Warnser as Baron Rothschild's secretary, and attorney Matieu Miller. The meeting consolidated French support for the Rebbe's work.
Tags: paris, france, fundraising, rashag, russia, alliance, rothschild

Title: R. Akiva Gotmanovich reports lack of chassidim in Widz
Summary: On 23 Iyar 5688 R. Akiva Gotmanovich reported to the Frierdiker Rebbe that he was teaching public classes in Widz but had 'no chassidim to talk with'.
Story: The dispatch reflected a thinning chassidic presence in the small Lithuanian town. Three days later the Frierdiker Rebbe responded urging Gotmanovich to teach short maamarim on avoda before the local crowd, adapting Chassidus to the audience he had.
Tags: widz, lithuania, 5688, 23 iyar, frierdiker rebbe, shiurim

Title: Rebbe writes to R. Ushpal in Kornitz
Summary: On 25 Iyar 5688 the Rebbe Rayatz addressed a letter to R. Shlomo Eliyahu Ushpal, rabbi of Kornitz.
Story: R. Shlomo Eliyahu Ushpal served as rabbi of Kornitz, succeeding R. Yaakov Landa who had earlier held the position in place of his father R. Moshe Yehuda Leib Landa. On 25 Iyar 5688 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote him there.
Tags: ushpal, kornitz, landa, rabbinate

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe responds on teaching Chassidus in Widz
Summary: On 26 Iyar 5688 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to R. Akiva Gotmanovich advising him to teach short maamarim on Chassidic avoda before the people of Widz.
Story: Despite Gotmanovich's complaint that there were no chassidim in Widz, the Frierdiker Rebbe encouraged him to bring Chassidus to ordinary Jews by selecting brief, accessible discourses focused on practical service of G-d.
Tags: widz, frierdiker rebbe, 5688, 26 iyar, shiurim

Title: Rebbe writes letter blaming Voykov reprisals for clergy crackdown
Summary: In a letter dated 19 Iyar 5688, the Rebbe described how Soviet authorities struck out at religious leaders to avenge Voykov's assassination and the British expulsion.
Story: The Rebbe explained that the 1927 wave of repression against clergy of all faiths was tied to two international shocks: the rupture with England and the killing of the Soviet ambassador in Warsaw. The Yevsektsia, he wrote, exploited the moment to act against him.
Tags: letter, voykov, soviet union, clergy, 19 iyar

Title: Shavuos kiddush in Brooklyn unites Lubavitcher community around Toras Emes
Summary: On Shabbos of Shavuos 5688, the author hosted a kiddush in Brownsville that drew local shtieblach into the cause of Yeshivas Toras Emes.
Story: Shavuos 5688 fell on Friday and Shabbos. The author hosted a kiddush with cholent at his home, inviting his own shul's mispallelim and several minyanim of Anash from Brownsville — then considered 'the Yerushalayim of America.' R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin's warmth captivated the crowd, and fundraising drives for Toras Emes were soon organized in several local shuls including the Lubavitcher shtibel on Watkins Street under Rav Tzvi Hirsch Dachowitz.
Tags: brownsville, brooklyn, shavuos, toras emes, havlin, fundraising

Title: Rebbe declares 12 Tamuz a festival of liberation in public letter
Summary: On the first anniversary of his release, the Rebbe published a letter establishing 12 Tamuz as a yearly festival for all who love Torah.
Story: Written from his new residence, the letter framed the anniversary as a celebration not only for the observant but for 'all those who merely bear the name Jew,' since every Jewish heart is bound with God and Torah. Since then, 12 Tamuz has been marked annually in Jewish communities across the world.
Tags: 12 tamuz, letter, release anniversary, 15 sivan

Title: Rebbe writes anniversary letter calling 12 Tamuz a festival of liberation
Summary: A year after his release, the Rebbe published a letter declaring that 12 Tamuz is a 'festival of liberation' for all who love Torah and even for every Jew.
Story: On June 3, 1928 (15 Sivan 5688), the Rebbe issued a public letter explaining that his liberation should be marked annually as a festival for those who love Torah and observe its commands, and indeed for every Jew, 'for the heart of every man of Israel is perfectly bound with G-d and His Torah.' This letter formalized the annual observance of 12 Tamuz across Jewish communities.
Tags: 12 tamuz, igrot kodesh, liberation

Title: Kiddush in Zhlobin marking first anniversary of Rayatz's liberation
Summary: On 12 Tammuz 5688 the Shusterman home in Zhlobin hosted a kiddush marking the first anniversary of the Rebbe Rayatz's liberation, attended by R. Tzemach Horowitz.
Story: On 12 Tammuz 5688 (June 30, 1928), the first anniversary of the Frierdiker Rebbe's liberation, the Shusterman family hosted a kiddush in their Zhlobin home. The chassid R. Tzemach Horowitz, then serving as a mashpia in Zhlobin, participated. The author recalled the event still vividly decades later.
Tags: yud beis tammuz, rayatz, liberation, zhlobin, tzemach horowitz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes to Chief Rabbi Hertz of England
Summary: On 21 Tammuz 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to British Chief Rabbi J.H. Hertz about 20,000 Soviet Jewish children needing Torah education.
Story: The Rebbe described how 20,000 children in the USSR sought religious learning but could not access it primarily for lack of funds, urging European Jewry to mobilize on behalf of Soviet Jews. He argued that the persecution was not the only obstacle — financial means were the decisive missing element.
Tags: england, london, hertz, fundraising, russia, education

Title: Rebbe writes British Chief Rabbi Hertz pleading for Russian Jewry
Summary: The Rebbe pleads with British Chief Rabbi Dr. Yosef Hertz to use his influence to fund Russian Jewish education.
Story: Following the Rashag's earlier diplomatic visit to London, the Rebbe wrote, 'It is not a time for silence or to hold back on action. We must save Russian Jewry.' He told Hertz he knew 'of twenty thousand children in the USSR who wish to study Torah and are unable to – not because of the persecution, but rather the lack of money.'
Tags: england, hertz, russia, twenty thousand children, letter

Title: Rebbe writes to Chief Rabbi Hertz of Britain about Russian Jewry
Summary: The Rebbe implores the British chief rabbi to help save twenty thousand Russian children unable to study Torah for lack of funds.
Story: Thanking Rabbi Hertz for welcoming his son-in-law Rashag, the Rebbe wrote, 'It is not a time for silence or to hold back on action. We must save Russian Jewry. What will future generations say if we do not answer their call in the time of crisis?'
Tags: letter, hertz, england, russian-jewry, fundraising

Title: Rebbe Rayatz advises R' Yani Gurarie on Romny rabbinate
Summary: On 28 Tammuz 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz responded to R' Yani Gurarie endorsing his acceptance of the Romny rabbinate provided it would not cause controversy.
Story: After the Romny yeshiva was shut down and R' Gurarie served his forced labor sentence, the community offered him the vacant rabbinate. The Rebbe Rayatz instructed him to actively pursue accepting the position, provided he was certain it would not become a matter of communal dispute.
Tags: rayatz, yani gurarie, romny, rabbinate, soviet union, chabad

Title: Maamar 'HaYom Haras Olam' in Yiddish received for printing in America
Summary: In Elul 5688, the Frierdiker Rebbe's Yiddish ma'amar 'HaYom Haras Olam' arrived in America for printing and distribution, sponsored by R' Menachem Mendel Kunin.
Story: The shochet R' Menachem Mendel Kunin — described as an exceptionally generous supporter of Lubavitch — personally underwrote the printing of the ma'amar. Its appearance in America was felt as a stirring of renewed Lubavitcher spirit among Anash, signaling that the warmth of the chatzer was reviving on American soil even as the Russian community had been shattered.
Tags: maamar, yiddish, elul, menachem mendel kunin, shochet, usa

Title: Feigin's first appeal to Jacobson for wedding funds
Summary: Rabbi Yechezkel Feigin secretly wrote to Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson in New York imploring American Chasidim for financial help for the upcoming royal wedding.
Story: With the wedding approaching, the financial situation was dire. The Communist revolution had disrupted donations from Russian Chasidim, and few Chasidim lived in Western Europe. Feigin wrote, 'We must put our heads together and find a solution. In the end, a wedding must be made. But with what?'
Tags: feigin, jacobson, new-york, fundraising, wedding

Title: Rebbe Rayatz received Maharash's kippah from R' Shneur Tzvi Schneersohn
Summary: On 3 Elul 5688 Rebbe Rayatz received the white silver-threaded mitznefet of his grandfather the Maharash as a gift.
Story: A handwritten note by Rebbe Rayatz, later discovered in a Russian archive, recorded that the mitznefet (kippah) of his grandfather the Maharash was given to him as a gift by his relative R' Shneur Tzvi Schneersohn, grandson of R' Chaim Avraham, on 3 Elul 5688. The kippah, woven with silver threads and bearing a small tail, eventually entered the Chabad library's artifact archive after the 'didan notzach' books trial of 5746–47.
Tags: maharash, kippah, heirloom, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes letter on Colel Chabad reforms
Summary: On 13 Elul 5688, the Rebbe wrote that he viewed Colel Chabad as 'a sacred obligation' but required reform of its governance and finances.
Story: The Rebbe made his acceptance of Colel Chabad's leadership conditional on a proper understanding of its finances. The reforms he requested were ultimately codified in a new charter in 1933.
Tags: colel-chabad, rayatz, governance, finance

Title: First Yiddish maamar published in Riga in over a century
Summary: The Rebbe publishes the maamar Kinyan HaChaim, the first chasidic discourse printed in Yiddish since the eighteenth century.
Story: Published before the High Holidays, this was the Rebbe's first maamar since leaving Russia. Printing in Yiddish rather than Hebrew made chasidic teachings accessible to a wider lay audience, marking a major step in disseminating Chasidut.
Tags: maamar, yiddish, kinyan-hachaim, dissemination

Title: R' Yehuda Eber tests Vitebsk Tomchei Tmimim students in Elul 5688
Summary: In Elul 5688 R' Yehuda Eber examined the Vitebsk talmidim and grouped the youngest top boys into a new advanced shiur.
Story: During Elul review the rosh yeshiva R' Yehuda Eber came to Vitebsk to test the bochurim, with R' Avraham Mayorer and the mashgiach deciding in advance how to combine them into examination groups. The author was tested alongside Avrahmaleh Kvash, Meir Zarchi, Yosef Sushtarvitz, and Shimon Shtilerman, the youngest and most capable bochurim, and the group was earmarked to form a new advanced class for the coming winter.
Tags: vitebsk, tomchei-tmimim, yehuda-eber, avraham-mayorer, exams

Title: Rebbe publishes first maamar since leaving Russia, in Yiddish
Summary: Weeks before the High Holidays, the Rebbe publishes maamar Kinyan HaChaim in Yiddish, breaking with eighteenth-century Hebrew-only convention.
Story: It was the first maamar printed not in Hebrew but in Yiddish since the eighteenth century, making chasidic teachings accessible to a broader public. In its introduction, the Rebbe addressed those who had drifted from chasidic roots: 'Remember your historical roots, your parents and grandparents.' He urged parents to 'instill these teachings in your children.'
Tags: maamar, yiddish, kinyan hachaim, riga, dissemination

Title: Rebbe Rayatz travels to Berlin to meet Joint executives
Summary: In mid-Elul 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz traveled to Berlin to negotiate continuing Joint Distribution Committee support for Russian Torah work.
Story: The Joint had funded the Rebbe's Soviet activities since 1922, but signaled they would not continue funding Torah work in Europe for 5689. In Berlin the Rebbe met with R. Aharon Teitelbaum, head of Central Relief, along with Hildesheimer, Mr. Cohen, Mr. Rosen, and Hildesheimer to argue for continued support specifically for Russia.
Tags: berlin, joint, rosen, teitelbaum, fundraising, russia

Title: R' Alter Simchowitz arrives in Riga for the Days of Awe
Summary: R' Yechezkel Feigin notified R' Israel Jacobson that R' Alter Simchowitz had come from Jerusalem to spend Tishrei with the Rebbe Rayatz in Riga.
Story: Following the Rebbe Rayatz's late-winter 5688 visit to Warsaw Tomchei Temimim, he resolved to overhaul the yeshiva's staffing. The chance arose when R' Alter Simchowitz of Jerusalem, who had served as mashpia in Warsaw from 5682-5685, traveled to Riga for the Days of Awe. On 18 Elul 5688, the Rebbe's secretary R' Yechezkel Feigin informed R' Israel Jacobson of the 'honored guest's' arrival, setting the stage for discussions to bring R' Alter back as chief mashpia.
Tags: riga, warsaw, tomchei-temimim, alter-simchowitz, yechezkel-feigin, israel-jacobson, yamim-noraim

Title: HaOlam reports on the Rebbe's library in Riga
Summary: The London weekly HaOlam published a correspondent's report describing the Frierdiker Rebbe's library in Riga as a rich treasury of Jewish antiquities.
Story: On 22 Elul 5688, HaOlam printed an account by a Yiddishe Shtime correspondent who had visited the library in Riga. The article enumerated such treasures as a 440-year-old manuscript of R. Avraham Saba, a 1475 Venice siddur, 950 Haggadah editions in many languages, 900 selichos volumes, and manuscripts of the Baal Shem Tov and Maggid of Mezeritch, painting a vivid picture of the collection's scope just months after its arrival.
Tags: riga, library, rayatz, haolam, manuscripts, press

Title: R' Yechezkel Himmelstein flees Polotsk to Vitebsk for Rosh Hashanah 5689
Summary: After Soviet authorities closed the Polotsk mikveh, rosh metivta R' Yechezkel Himmelstein came to Vitebsk for Rosh Hashanah 5689.
Story: The closure of the mikveh in Polotsk forced its rosh metivta R' Yechezkel Himmelstein to relocate to Vitebsk for the Yamim Noraim. He prayed together with the Tomchei Tmimim bochurim in the Zaranover shul, an early sign of how Soviet pressure was beginning to splinter the yeshiva network.
Tags: polotsk, vitebsk, mikveh, yechezkel-himmelstein, soviet-repression, zaranover

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Rabbi Aharon Milovski about JDC efforts
Summary: The Rebbe detailed his efforts to secure JDC funding for Russian Jewish religious life in a letter to Rabbi Milovski.
Story: The letter laid out the funding crisis facing Chabad's underground network in Russia. It was part of the broader correspondence that culminated in the Rebbe's decision to travel to the United States.
Tags: jdc, rayatz, soviet-jewry, milovski

Title: Rebbe Rayatz letter on visiting Lubavitch graves
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his uncle about arranging repairs to the ohel in Lubavitch.
Story: On 5 Cheshvan 5689 (September 19, 1928), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his uncle Rabbi Moshe Leib Ginsburg about restoration efforts at the ohel of the Tzemach Tzedek and the Rebbe Maharash. R' Yechiel Chazan had written that the ohel needed major repairs. The Rebbe asked how much the repairs would cost so he could help arrange them.
Tags: lubavitch, ohel, graves, restoration

Title: Rebbe blesses Sylvia Reinen for translating maamar into Yiddish
Summary: The Rebbe writes a special blessing for Sylvia Reinen, who translated the first post-Russia maamar into Yiddish.
Story: In the letter to Alexander Sender Reinen, the Rebbe wrote, 'A special blessing to your wife for her efforts translating the discourse… It will be a great merit that those who don't understand another language are able to study it.' This marked the beginning of an effort to engage women with the intellectual depth of Chabad Chasidut.
Tags: women, yiddish, translation, maamar, reinen

Title: Rebbe thanks Sylvia Reinen for translating maamar into Yiddish
Summary: The Rebbe blesses Sylvia Reinen for her role translating a chasidic discourse, an early step in empowering women in chasidic learning.
Story: Writing to her husband Alexander Sender Reinen, the Rebbe noted, 'It will be a great merit that those who don't understand another language are able to study it.' This was a foundational moment in opening chasidic study to women.
Tags: women, translation, letter, yiddish

Title: R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin appointed spiritual director of Yeshiva Torah Vodaas
Summary: After Sukkos 5689, R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin became menahel ruchni of Yeshiva Torah Vodaas after R' Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz stepped down from that role.
Story: R' Yeshaya Binush Tarshish approached the author with news that Torah Vodaas needed a new menahel ruchni following R' Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz's resignation from that position. The author and Rav Nissan Telushkin advocated for R' Rivkin, who at the time was floundering in an ill-defined ma'amad role. Rivkin was a natural fit — a scholar with yeshiva administrative experience — and his appointment came as Torah Vodaas stood on the threshold of major growth.
Tags: torah vodaas, brooklyn, shraga feivel mendlowitz, rivkin, nissan telushkin, yeshaya binush tarshish

Title: Rebbe Rayatz cites Warsaw activities as a distraction from expansion plans
Summary: On 3 Marcheshvan 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his uncle R. Moshe HaKohen Horenstein that yeshiva and cheder administration in his own country had prevented him from advancing the Warsaw expansion.
Story: Writing to his uncle, the Rebbe Rayatz explained that if properly organized, Tomchei Tmimim of Warsaw could bring real light to the world. He had resolved during his Warsaw visit to take this work upon himself, but upon returning home he was overwhelmed by the burdens of running the yeshivos and chadarim in his own country. Earlier, on 2 Marcheshvan 5689, he had written to the yeshiva administration confirming in writing that the impression made by the institution was beyond description.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, rayatz, moshe horenstein

Title: R' Yaakov Landa's rabbinical writ signed for Libau
Summary: On 17 Tishrei 5689 about forty heads of Libau's Chassidic community signed R' Yaakov Landa's rabbinical writ.
Story: After repeated encouragement from the Rebbe Rayatz to accept the Libau rabbinate, R' Yaakov Landa's rabbinical writ was signed on 17 Tishrei 5689 (October 1, 1928) by some forty heads of the local Chassidic community. The writ formalized his position as rabbi of the Libau Chassidim.
Tags: libau, liepaja, latvia, landa, rabbinate

Title: Rayatz writes R' Ashurov reassuring him over informants' libels
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz wrote R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov assuring him not to worry about denunciations made against him.
Story: On 24 Tishrei 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov of Drivin, reassuring him not to worry about informers who had denounced him. He stated that truth shines and all libels are nullified, and that those who sit in judgment recognize the truth.
Tags: ashurov, informants, drivin, russia

Title: Studies resume at Warsaw Tomchei Temimim with R' Alter as mashpia
Summary: On the first day of Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan 5689, R' Alter Simchowitz began teaching chassidus each morning at the Warsaw Tomchei Temimim.
Story: After Tishrei in Riga, R' Alter Simchowitz traveled to Warsaw to take up his new post. On Sunday, 30 Tishrei 5689, the students began studying chassidus with him at the appointed early hour. About thirty-five students filled the hall; their outward conduct was orderly but they urgently needed steady guidance and clearer instruction on the inner avodah expected of them.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-temimim, alter-simchowitz, mashpia, chassidus

Title: Rebbe Rayatz formally appoints R' Alter chief mashpia of Warsaw yeshiva
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz wrote from Riga to the yeshiva's Va'ad and to R' Alter himself, charging him with general supervision of chassidus and overall yeshiva conduct.
Story: On 2 Marcheshvan 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz sent a letter to the Warsaw Va'ad declaring that he was placing on R' Alter Simchowitz the 'sacred yoke' of overseeing all hashpa'a and hadracha at the yeshiva. In a parallel letter that day to R' Alter, he charged him with ordering the studies, awakening the students' inner point of avodah she'b'lev through chassidic teaching, and producing fruit in middos and conduct.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-temimim, alter-simchowitz, mashpia, appointment

Title: Rebbe offers his uncle R' Moshe Hornstein the Warsaw yeshiva directorship
Summary: On 3 Marcheshvan, the Rebbe Rayatz proposed that his uncle R' Moshe Hornstein of Otwock take charge of administering the Warsaw yeshiva.
Story: Writing from Riga the day after his appointment letters for R' Alter, the Rebbe addressed his uncle R' Moshe Hornstein, who lived in Otwock near Warsaw. He asked him to accept overall management and financial stewardship of Tomchei Temimim, explaining that the institution had to be rebuilt from scratch and that he could now coordinate more easily than before. R' Alter Simchowitz was to convey the practical details, and Hornstein could leave his own business to his wife and son in order to focus on the yeshiva.
Tags: warsaw, otwock, tomchei-temimim, moshe-hornstein, appointment

Title: Feigin's second appeal to Jacobson
Summary: Six weeks before the wedding, Feigin wrote again to Jacobson urging him to enlist Rabbi Shalom Dovber Rivkin and launch an appeal to all Tomchei Temimim alumni.
Story: Feigin explained that European Chasidim could not really help because of the suffering they had endured. 'Finances must come from your country,' he wrote, urging Jacobson to telegram or write to all the Temimim alumni and pleading with him to act swiftly.
Tags: feigin, jacobson, new-york, fundraising, rivkin, temimim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Rabbi Chaim Ozer about American trip
Summary: On 4 Cheshvan 5689, the Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Chaim Ozer Grodzinski, who along with the Chafetz Chaim encouraged the American journey.
Story: Rabbi Chaim Ozer, who corresponded regularly with the Rebbe, had discussed the matter with the Chafetz Chaim in Radin. Their joint encouragement helped solidify the Rebbe's decision to travel to America.
Tags: chaim-ozer, chafetz-chaim, rayatz, united-states

Title: Soviet education minister Lunacharsky attacks Rebbe in NY Times
Summary: Anatoly Lunacharsky publicly declares war on 'Schneersohnovschina' — the religious activities of the Lubavitcher Rebbe.
Story: Lunacharsky told the Times, 'We shall combat the relics of the Middle Ages, the Schneersohnovschina.' The term was thereafter used by Soviet authorities to imprison Chasidim. He declared the Jewish solution lay in 'fusion of the Jews in the great melting pot.'
Tags: soviet, lunacharsky, press, schneersohnovschina

Title: Soviet education minister Lunacharsky targets the Rebbe in NYT
Summary: Soviet Minister of Education Anatoly Lunacharsky declares war on 'Schneersohnovschina' in The New York Times.
Story: Lunacharsky said, 'We shall combat the relics of the Middle Ages, the Schneersohnovschina.' The Times explained the term as 'the religious activities of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, who is now in exile in Latvia.' According to Lunacharsky, the solution lay in 'the fusion of the Jews in the great melting pot of the peoples who inhabit the Soviet Union.'
Tags: soviet, lunacharsky, press, new york times, schneersohnovschina

Title: Warsaw yeshiva Va'ad meets to plan staff reorganization
Summary: The Warsaw Tomchei Temimim Va'ad convened on Sunday 7 Marcheshvan 5689 to shrink the staff and reshape supervision under financial pressure.
Story: R' Alter Simchowitz, R' Shmuel Zalmanov, and the senior administration committee met to plan how to reduce the yeshiva in size without weakening essential study. They resolved to release three staff members—the nigleh supervisor R' Yehoshua Ber, the second-division rosh yeshiva R' Zvi Meir, and the mashpia RSh"L—and proposed installing R' Boruch Friedman as the new nigleh supervisor. They also decided that R' Shmuel Zalmanov would travel to Otwock to formally press R' Moshe Hornstein to accept the directorship.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-temimim, alter-simchowitz, shmuel-zalmanov, vaad

Title: R' Alter Simchowitz reports yeshiva conditions to the Rebbe
Summary: R' Alter wrote on 9 Marcheshvan that fixing the yeshiva hinged on appointing a chief director, but R' Moshe Hornstein's answer was still pending.
Story: On Monday 8 Marcheshvan R' Alter had visited Otwock to relay the Rebbe's proposal to R' Moshe Hornstein, but Hornstein gave only a tentative response pending the Rebbe's letter. Writing on 9 Marcheshvan, R' Alter described being overwhelmed by the disorder—the financial straits, the gap in nigleh supervision, and the absence of mature students to whom hashpa'a could yet be delegated—and stressed that nothing could be set right until a chief director was installed.
Tags: warsaw, otwock, tomchei-temimim, alter-simchowitz, moshe-hornstein

Title: R' Shmuel Zalmanov reports Va'ad and Otwock visit to the Rebbe
Summary: R' Shmuel Zalmanov wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz the night of 10 Marcheshvan 5689 describing the Va'ad's decisions and R' Moshe Hornstein's hesitations.
Story: Zalmanov reported the Va'ad's plan to reduce the institution while replacing the nigleh supervisor with 'our man' R' Boruch Friedman, and to draw senior students into giving hashpa'a in chassidus. He recounted his Monday 8 Marcheshvan trip to Otwock, where Hornstein seemed willing in principle but had unresolved doubts and would only answer after writing the Rebbe himself. The yeshiva's financial state was 'awful and terrifying,' with creditors pressing and no income.
Tags: warsaw, otwock, tomchei-temimim, shmuel-zalmanov, moshe-hornstein

Title: R' Alter writes Rebbe about ill health and yeshiva difficulties
Summary: On 11 Marcheshvan 5689, R' Alter described his weakness and the strain of his daily schedule to the Rebbe Rayatz, still awaiting Hornstein's answer.
Story: R' Alter wrote that he was 'very weak' and that his daily seder was unsustainable: he ate only mezonot before tefilla, taught chassidus until nine, but often could not hold out for davening to conclude after noon. He still hoped R' Moshe Hornstein would accept the directorship within a week and asked the Rebbe for guidance and a berachah for strength to serve b'mesirah amitis.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-temimim, alter-simchowitz, health

Title: Rebbe Rayatz blesses R' Alter Simchowitz with a refuah shleima
Summary: Responding on 15 Marcheshvan 5689, the Rebbe wished R' Alter full recovery and strength to guide the talmidim in the path set by the Rebbe Rashab.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz answered R' Alter's letter with a blessing that Hashem grant him a refuah shleima and a calm, strong mind to teach Torah and avodah she'b'lev. He invoked the inner authority his father, the Rebbe Rashab, had given them, that the students should ascend to the level of halacha through 'the form overpowering the matter'.
Tags: alter-simchowitz, warsaw, tomchei-temimim, health, blessing

Title: Wedding date set for Rebbe Menachem Mendel and Chaya Mushka
Summary: On 16 Cheshvan 5689, the wedding of R. Menachem Mendel Schneerson to Chaya Mushka was set for 14 Kislev in Warsaw.
Story: After waiting in hopes that the groom's father Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneersohn would be granted Soviet permission to attend, the date was finalized for 14 Kislev in Warsaw, with the chuppah at the courtyard of Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva. The father was ultimately denied travel papers. Mass invitations were sent to Chasidim, activists, rabbis, and Rebbes.
Tags: warsaw, menachem mendel schneerson, chaya mushka, wedding, levi yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Soviets shut down yeshiva in Nevel
Summary: Authorities closed the American-subsidized yeshiva in Nevel a year after the Rebbe's arrest.
Story: The Nevel yeshiva, located in a Chabad enclave about 120 miles from Lubavitch, had been an important center of religious learning. Its closure, reported by the JTA on November 2, 1928, was part of the ongoing campaign against Jewish religious education in the Soviet Union.
Tags: nevel, yeshiva, soviet union, jta

Title: Yeshivah in Nevel closed by Soviet authorities
Summary: The JTA reported the closure of the American-subsidized Chabad yeshivah in Nevel, roughly 120 miles from Lubavitch.
Story: On November 2, 1928, the JTA reported that the yeshivah in Nevel — a vibrant Chabad town about 120 miles from Lubavitch — had been shut down by Soviet authorities a year after the Rebbe's arrest. Nevel had been a center of chasidic life with a Jewish population of nearly 5,900 in 1897. The local Jewish community was later annihilated by the Nazis during the Holocaust.
Tags: russia, nevel, yeshivah, jta, american subsidy

Title: Rebbetzin Sterna Sara's letter from Riga about the impending wedding
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5689 from Riga, Rebbetzin Sterna Sara wrote to Rabbi Eliezerov about the family's difficult years in Russia and her impressions of her future grandson-in-law.
Story: On Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5689 from Riga, Rebbetzin Sterna Sara wrote in Yiddish to her relative Rabbi Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov, describing the hardships the family had endured in Soviet Russia and the joyous transition to her granddaughter Chaya Mushka's upcoming wedding. She told him she had recently had the opportunity to meet his nephew the chosson Menachem Mendel and found him 'a quite distinguished young man,' inviting Eliezerov to share in the simcha even from afar.
Tags: sterna sara, riga, wedding, eliezerov, soviet union

Title: Rebbe Rayatz departs Riga for Warsaw wedding
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz left Riga by train for Warsaw, accompanied by his family and the groom, greeted by thousands at the train station.
Story: Two rows of men stretching five hundred feet stood as an honor guard as the Rebbe entered the station. The crowd danced alongside as the train pulled away. Large crowds also gathered in the stations in Dvinsk and Vilnius to wish the Rebbe well during the journey.
Tags: riga, warsaw, poland, train, wedding

Title: Rebbe Rayatz holds chassan mohl for Tomchei Temimim students
Summary: On the eve of the Rebbe's wedding, the Rebbe Rayatz convened a chassan mohl at the Warsaw yeshiva with a maamar, niggunim, and dancing with the students.
Story: On 13 Kislev 5689, the day before his daughter Chaya Mushka's wedding in Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz held a chassan mohl gathering specifically for the talmidim of Tomchei Temimim. He delivered a maamar of chassidus, niggunim of Chabad were sung, and after Birkat HaMazon the Rebbe danced with the students of the yeshiva.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-temimim, wedding, chayya-mushka, maamar, niggun, dancing

Title: Royal Wedding of Chaya Mushka and the Ramash in Warsaw
Summary: The 'royal wedding' of the Rebbe Rayatz's daughter Chaya Mushka to Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson took place at Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim in Warsaw before 5,000 people.
Story: The Rebbe wore his grandfather's shtreimel publicly for the first time since assuming leadership, symbolizing a new era of Chabad's rebirth in Western Europe. The Rebbe taught a maamar starting at 11:00 p.m. and again at 4:00 a.m. The wedding introduced the relatively unknown Ramash to the broader Jewish community, including Rabbi Meir Shapiro, who afterward told the Rebbe, 'You have taken a son-in-law who is a gaon.'
Tags: warsaw, poland, shtreimel, tomchei-temimim, meir-shapiro, royal-wedding

Title: Sefer Ohr HaMeir presented to the Rebbe at his wedding
Summary: At the Rebbe's wedding on 14 Kislev 5689 in Warsaw, Rabbi Meir Shapiro presented his responsa work Ohr HaMeir inscribed as a 'drasha gift.'
Story: At the Rebbe's wedding in Warsaw on 14 Kislev 5689, Rabbi Yehuda Meir Shapiro — founder of Yeshivas Chachmei Lublin and originator of the Daf Yomi — presented his responsa work Ohr HaMeir as a drasha gift. He inscribed it: 'A drasha gift to the choicest of vines, sons of holy supernal fathers, on the wedding day, 3 Vayishlach 5689, in Warsaw.' The Rebbe Rayatz directed his son-in-law to engage Rabbi Shapiro in Torah discussion at the wedding.
Tags: meir shapiro, lublin, daf yomi, ohr hameir, wedding gift, warsaw

Title: Sefer Ohr Sameach presented to the Rebbe at his wedding
Summary: The Gaon R' Meir Simcha HaKohen of Dvinsk presented his Ohr Sameach commentary on the Rambam to the Rebbe at his wedding on 14 Kislev 5689.
Story: Among the books the Rebbe received at his wedding on 14 Kislev 5689 was the Ohr Sameach commentary on the Rambam by R' Meir Simcha HaKohen of Dvinsk. The Rebbe himself inscribed the title page: 'From the books of Menachem Schneersohn, 14 Kislev 5689.'
Tags: meir simcha, dvinsk, ohr sameach, rambam, wedding gift

Title: Wedding of Rayatz's daughter Chaya Mushka in Warsaw
Summary: On 14 Kislev 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz's daughter married the future Rebbe in Warsaw, marking his second visit to the city.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz's second visit to Warsaw took place on 14 Kislev 5689 (November 27, 1928), for the wedding of his daughter to his son-in-law, the future Lubavitcher Rebbe. After the wedding, on the fourth night of Chanukah, the Rayatz wrote a public letter of thanks to all of Polish anash and the temimim for their efforts on behalf of the wedding arrangements.
Tags: warsaw, rayatz, 14 kislev, rebbe wedding, rayatz daughter

Title: Wedding of Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson and Chaya Mushka in Warsaw
Summary: On 14 Kislev 5689 in Warsaw, the future Lubavitcher Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson married Chaya Mushka, daughter of the Rebbe Rayatz.
Story: The chuppah was held in the courtyard of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Warsaw. The groom's father R. Levi Yitzchak Schneersohn, in Soviet Russia, was denied a travel permit and could not attend. The Rebbe's uncle R. Moshe Hornstein and aunt served as unterfirer on the groom's side in place of the father.
Tags: warsaw, poland, menachem mendel schneerson, chaya mushka, wedding, tomchei tmimim

Title: Wedding of Rebbe's daughter; donor offers building for yeshiva
Summary: At a wedding on 14 Kislev 5689, the Warsaw philanthropist R' Avraham HaKohen offered to fund a new yeshiva building.
Story: On 14 Kislev 5689 (27 November 1928) — the date of a wedding in the Rebbe's family — R' Avraham HaKohen, a Warsaw philanthropist, expressed his desire to donate a new building for the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva. The Rebbe Rayatz alluded to the offer days later in a Chanukah letter to him, and pursued the matter through R' Dov Nisan Bezpalov, hoping to acquire property in Warsaw or in nearby Otwock for the yeshiva. The plan ultimately did not come to fruition at that time.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-tmimim, rebbe-rayatz, avraham-hakohen, wedding, fundraising

Title: Wedding of Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka and Rebbe Menachem Mendel in Warsaw
Summary: On 14 Kislev 5689, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, daughter of the Rebbe Rayatz, married the future Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson in Warsaw.
Story: The kabbalat panim was held in the Tomchei Temimim hall and the chuppah in the yeshiva's courtyard. Tomchei Temimim students joined the wedding meal in a separate hall alongside the mashpia R' Alter, whom the Rebbe Rayatz instructed to distribute mashke to the talmidim for l'chaim. The Rebbe then addressed them with a sicha on the principle that 'Torah is preserved only in one who puts himself to death over it,' and afterward danced with the yeshiva's director and supervisors.
Tags: warsaw, wedding, chayya-mushka, rebbe-menachem-mendel, tomchei-temimim, yud-daled-kislev

Title: Wedding of the Lubavitcher Rebbe and Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson married Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, daughter of the Rayatz, in Warsaw on 14 Kislev 5689.
Story: The wedding on 14 Kislev 5689 became one of the most observed dates on the Chabad calendar — the day the Rebbe later called 'the day that bound me to you.' In this diary it is mentioned in passing alongside a 14 Kislev entry as the Rebbe's wedding anniversary, set beside the diarist's own 14 Kislev wedding decades later.
Tags: warsaw, 14-kislev, rebbetzin-chaya-mushka, rayatz

Title: Wedding of the Lubavitcher Rebbe and Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka in Warsaw
Summary: On Tuesday 14 Kislev 5689 the future Lubavitcher Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson married Chaya Mushka, daughter of the Rebbe Rayatz, in Warsaw.
Story: On Tuesday 14 Kislev 5689 in Warsaw, the future seventh Lubavitcher Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson married Chaya Mushka, daughter of the Rebbe Rayatz. R' Yochanan Gordon recalled in a later letter that the Rebbe Rayatz had urged guests to attend by saying, 'Imagine such a wedding where the Rebbe my father will surely be present, and the Maharash and the Tzemach Tzedek and the Mitteler Rebbe and the Alter Rebbe — and perhaps the Baal Shem Tov.'
Tags: rebbe, chaya mushka, rebbe rayatz, warsaw, wedding

Title: Rebbe arranges R' Moshe Hornstein's interim directorship of Warsaw yeshiva
Summary: On 23 Kislev 5689, the Rebbe wrote to R' Shraga Feivish Zalmanov and R' Moshe Hornstein finalizing a three-month engagement for Hornstein to organize the yeshiva.
Story: After traveling with R' Shraga Feivish Zalmanov, the Rebbe Rayatz had persuaded his uncle R' Moshe Hornstein to step in and put the yeshiva in order for about three months. He now asked Zalmanov to send his son Shmuel to Otwock to acquaint Hornstein with the operations, ledgers, and correspondence, and wrote Hornstein himself to confirm the plan. The arrangement does not appear in later sources, suggesting it was never carried out.
Tags: warsaw, otwock, tomchei-temimim, moshe-hornstein, shraga-feivish-zalmanov

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes to R' Avraham HaKohen on Chanukah
Summary: On the fourth day of Chanukah 5689 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Avraham HaKohen alluding to his promised donation for the yeshiva.
Story: On the fourth day of Chanukah 5689 (around 11 December 1928) the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the Warsaw philanthropist R' Avraham HaKohen, gently alluding — without detail — to 'the great good things you wish to do.' The letter referred to Avraham HaKohen's earlier offer at the family wedding to fund a new yeshiva building. It is preserved in Igrot Kodesh vol. 16, letter 6004.
Tags: rebbe-rayatz, warsaw, avraham-hakohen, letter, chanukah

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes to R' Dov Nisan Bezpalov about yeshiva property
Summary: On 3 Tevet 5689 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Dov Nisan Bezpalov exploring purchase of a building or courtyard around Warsaw — preferably in Otwock — for the yeshiva.
Story: On 3 Tevet 5689 (December 1928) the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a confidential letter to R' Dov Nisan Bezpalov, asking him to identify properties around Warsaw suitable for purchase on long-term bank financing, with a preference for towns near Warsaw such as Otwock. He stressed that the matter be kept entirely private and not discussed even with close associates. The letter is found in Igrot Kodesh vol. 16, letter 6016.
Tags: rebbe-rayatz, warsaw, otwock, dov-nisan-bezpalov, letter, property

Title: Ramash begins his Reshimot diary
Summary: The Ramash made his first notation in what would become the Reshimot, a detailed private diary recording his interactions with the Rebbe Rayatz.
Story: The diary included a wealth of chasidic lore, history, and customs, with anecdotes of all the Rebbes back to the Baal Shem Tov. Most of the Reshimot was written in Europe before WWII, with small sections added in Brooklyn in the early 1940s. The notations were discovered in his desk shortly after his passing and published posthumously by Kehot.
Tags: reshimot, diary, torat-menachem, chabad-history

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Toras Emes students upon R' Alter's return
Summary: On 5 Tevet 5689, the Rebbe wrote to the Toras Emes students in Jerusalem announcing R' Alter Simchowitz's safe return journey.
Story: After roughly two months in Warsaw, R' Alter began the return trip to Jerusalem rather than relocating his family. On 5 Tevet 5689 the Rebbe wrote to the students of Toras Emes urging them to give themselves fully to R' Alter's program of study and avodah, signaling that he would now remain permanently in Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: jerusalem, toras-emes, alter-simchowitz

Title: Feigin writes to Axelrod about the custom of mother's name in pidyon
Summary: Secretary Yechezkel Feigin confirmed to Rabbi Axelrod the established custom of writing the mother's name in a pidyon nefesh.
Story: On 6 Tevet 5689, secretary Yechezkel Feigin confirmed receipt of Axelrod's pidyon nefesh and his five-shekel check. He clarified that the established practice is to write the mother's name in a pidyon, citing both the Rebbe Rayatz's statement that the Rebbeim had always written the mother's name and a tradition from Rabbi Hillel of Paritch that in a pidyon one writes the mother's name while in a tzettel one writes the father's name.
Tags: feigin, axelrod, pidyon-nefesh, minhag, hillel-of-paritch

Title: R' Alter Simchowitz reports safe arrival back in Eretz Yisrael
Summary: R' Alter wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz on 14 Tevet 5689 from Eretz Yisrael confirming his safe return.
Story: On 14 Tevet 5689, R' Alter sent the Rebbe a brief report announcing his safe arrival in Eretz Yisrael. The Rebbe later acknowledged the letter and asked for word that he had resumed his work at Toras Emes.
Tags: jerusalem, toras-emes, alter-simchowitz

Title: Matzah operation for Soviet Jewry begins
Summary: On 17 Tevet 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz instructed Rashag and Mordechai Dubin to begin organizing massive shipments of kosher matzah into Soviet Russia.
Story: Reports from across the USSR indicated that Passover flour could not be obtained anywhere. The Rebbe launched an enormous operation to ship 28 train cars of matzah to communities in 17 Soviet towns and 5,689 packages of matzah flour to private addresses in 404 towns. Negotiations with the Soviet embassy in Riga and Berlin over export permits and customs duties dominated the next three months.
Tags: matzah, passover, russia, rashag, dubin, soviet

Title: Arrest of Cherson Tomchei Tmimim faculty and students
Summary: In autumn 5690 (1929), Soviet authorities in Cherson arrested R' Yosef Himelstein, the mashgiach R' Tzemach Gurevitz, and the entire student body of the Tomchei Tmimim branch.
Story: The Chabad yeshiva in Cherson was opened by R' Yosef Himelstein and the mashgiach R' Tzemach HaLevi Gurevitz for the winter term. Before the new arrivals from Zlobin reached the city, the entire faculty and student body had been arrested. They were eventually released under condition not to leave Cherson — and immediately fled the city the moment they were freed.
Tags: cherson, tomchei tmimim, soviet union, arrests, yeshiva

Title: Closure of Tomchei Tmimim branch in Romen
Summary: The Tomchei Tmimim branch in Romen was disbanded in 5689, forcing students including Schusterman to return home.
Story: Schusterman had traveled to Romen to study at the yeshiva but had to return when it closed. The rosh yeshiva, Rabbi Yaakov ('Yana') Gurary, a local of Romen, was left without a position. Some townspeople proposed he assume the vacant rabbinate previously held by Rabbi Chaim Shneerson (grandson of the Tzemach Tzedek), but Rabbi Binyaminson — when offered the post — withdrew upon seeing factions form.
Tags: romen, tomchei-tmimim, yaakov-gurary, soviet

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe's earlier American visit on eve of Wall Street crash
Summary: The Frierdiker Rebbe's prior visit to America took place just before the Wall Street stock market crash, with hundreds of thousands of dollars raised for Soviet Jewry.
Story: Recalling his earlier American visit during the 5699 yechidus, the Frierdiker Rebbe explained that his previous trip had been for the sake of general Jewish life and that he succeeded in that goal, with thanks to G-d. He raised several hundred thousand dollars to aid the Jews of Russia, on the very eve of the Wall Street stock market collapse, with his very presence stirring American Jewry to support his far-reaching activities. His deeper aim, however, had been spiritual: to awaken a feeling of teshuvah in the hearts of American Jewry.
Tags: usa, frierdiker rebbe, soviet jewry, fundraising, wall street crash

Title: Jews expelled from Borisov collective for refusing Shabbat milking
Summary: Jews in new collective settlements in the Borisov region are removed as 'undesirables' for refusing to milk cows on Shabbat.
Story: The case illustrated how the agricultural settlements pushed Jews to choose between livelihood and observance. The synagogue of communal farm town Krivoy Rog was converted into an arts hall where Yiddish ballads mocked traditional pieties.
Tags: borisov, soviet, shabbat, agricultural-colonies

Title: Levitin arrested by the Yevsektzia
Summary: In the winter of 5689 R. Shmuel Levitin was imprisoned by the Yevsektzia in Velikie Luki and sentenced to exile.
Story: In Kislev 5689 the Yevsektzia accused Levitin of disseminating Torah to youth in Nevel. He was placed in harsh imprisonment in Velikie Luki and sentenced to internal exile, leaving the Nevel rabbinical school in crisis.
Tags: levitin, nevel, yevsektzia, soviet-repression, velikie-luki

Title: Lubavitch calendar issued by Remigalsky in Riga
Summary: The 5689 luach published by Remigalsky in Riga featured a Tzemach Tzedek portrait.
Story: In 1929 the Remigalsky publishing house in Riga issued an annual luach whose cover bore a portrait of the Tzemach Tzedek, one of many adaptations of the famous 1886 lithograph.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, riga, latvia, calendar, portrait

Title: Network of Yiddish state schools reaches peak in Soviet Union
Summary: By 1929 there were 1,100 state-run Yiddish schools in the Soviet Union, serving roughly 130,000 students.
Story: Promoted by the Yevesektzia as schools for the 'Jewish proletariat,' they excluded Hebrew, Jewish religion, history, and tradition. Many religious parents sent their children to non-Jewish schools instead to avoid the anti-religious propaganda.
Tags: yiddish, schools, yevesektzia, education-policy

Title: New Toras Or shul built in Ponevezh
Summary: A new, grand Chabad shul (known as Toras Or) was built in Ponevezh in 5689, alongside the existing older shtibel.
Story: Ponevezh had two Chabad shuls in the interwar years. The newer and more elegant one, called Toras Or, was constructed in 5689; the older shtibel was where the tamim R. Shmuel Tzvi Lison, Hy"d, served as mashpia.
Tags: ponevezh, lithuania, synagogue, toras-or

Title: Photograph of Rayatz with future Rebbe before wedding
Summary: A photograph from 5689, evidently taken shortly before the Rebbe's wedding, shows the future Rebbe standing beside his seated father-in-law at a dining-room table, likely in Riga.
Story: Among the library's photographs is one from 5689 (1929), evidently taken close to the Rebbe's wedding — perhaps when he was already a chassan. The future Rebbe stands while his future father-in-law, the Rayatz, sits and holds his hand, beside the dining-room table that was apparently in Riga. A companion image from the same session shows the Rayatz seated at the same table beside his wife Rebbetzin Nechama Dina, studying a book.
Tags: rayatz, rebbe, riga, wedding, photograph

Title: Polotsk yeshiva shut down and R' Shlomo Chaim Kesselman exiled to Poltava
Summary: Shortly after Nevel, Soviet authorities raided Tomchei Tmimim in Polotsk and exiled R' Shlomo Chaim Kesselman to Poltava.
Story: Soon after the Nevel raid, the GPU moved against the Polotsk branch of Tomchei Tmimim, arresting its students and administrators. R' Shlomo Chaim Kesselman was singled out and exiled to Poltava, while the rest of the bochurim fled, most routing through Vitebsk because of its central rail position.
Tags: polotsk, poltava, shlomo-chaim-kesselman, tomchei-tmimim, soviet-repression, vitebsk

Title: Publication of Vayomer Shmuel by R' Shmuel Elbaz in Casablanca
Summary: R' Shmuel Elbaz's halachic work Vayomer Shmuel was published in Casablanca in 5689 (1929).
Story: R' Shmuel Elbaz, son of R' Yitzchak, was the same figure who in 1717 had married Rivkah bat Shem Tov Cohen of Fes and consented to her inheritance waiver. His subsequent work Vayomer Shmuel appeared in print in Casablanca centuries later, in 1929, cementing his reputation among the rabbinic authorities of Morocco.
Tags: morocco, casablanca, shmuel elbaz, vayomer shmuel

Title: R. Elchanan Yakubovitz publishes Even Shimon
Summary: After returning to his native Latvia in 5678, R. Elchanan Yakubovitz published the first volume of his Even Shimon in 5689.
Story: Following his evacuation from Lubavitch and a brief tenure in Russia, R. Elchanan Yakubovitz returned to Latvia in 5678 (1918). He resumed teaching as a rosh mesivta in several yeshivot and in 5689 (1929) printed the first volume of his halachic work Even Shimon, named after his father R. Avraham Shimon.
Tags: elchanan yakubovitz, even shimon, latvia

Title: Rabbi Kook appointed first chief rabbi by British Mandate
Summary: With the establishment of the Chief Rabbinate, Rabbi Kook assumed the position of chief rabbi.
Story: His appointment formalized his stature as the leading Religious-Zionist rabbinic voice in Palestine. The Rebbe Rayatz met with him three times during his 1929 visit, more than with any other figure.
Tags: rav-kook, chief-rabbinate, british-mandate, palestine

Title: Rabbi Slonim sent to South Africa on multi-year mission
Summary: In 1929 the Rebbe sent Rabbi Zelig Slonim from Eretz Yisrael to South Africa for what became a 2.5-year mission.
Story: Feigin wrote that the Rebbe knew little of what was happening in South Africa and asked Slonim to explore employment opportunities for rabbis and shochtim, both to strengthen Jewish life and to facilitate emigration from Russia. Slonim visited communities throughout South Africa and Rhodesia, sending detailed reports back to the Rebbe.
Tags: south-africa, rhodesia, slonim, shadar, immigration

Title: Rayatz visits Eretz Yisrael and the United States
Summary: The Rayatz undertook a historic visit to Eretz Yisrael and the United States, his first time in both countries.
Story: The journey took the Rayatz to the Holy Land, where he visited established and emerging Jewish communities, and then to America, where he met thousands of Jews and laid groundwork for future Chabad activity. The visits reshaped his geographic vision for the movement.
Tags: eretz yisrael, palestine, united states, travel

Title: Rebbe begins yearlong journey to Eretz Yisrael and America
Summary: From his Riga base, the Rebbe undertakes an almost yearlong trip to the Holy Land and the United States.
Story: The travels were aimed at inspiring communities and meeting Jewish leaders to help Russian Jewry. The visit was a turning point for establishing the Rebbe's international stature and for the future of American Chabad.
Tags: america, eretz-yisrael, travel, rayatz

Title: Rebbe launches international matzah campaign for Soviet Jewry
Summary: Facing Soviet famine, the Rebbe coordinates a global emergency campaign to ship matzah into Russia before Passover.
Story: The Rebbe enlisted Mordechai Dubin, the Rashag, and rabbis including Chaim Ozer Grodzinski, Yisrael Meir Kagan, and Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld. Despite Soviet obstruction, 140,000 kilos of matzah reached Russian Jews, proving the Rebbe could marshal global support without the Jewish establishment.
Tags: matzah-campaign, passover, russia, famine, soviet

Title: Rebbe Maharayatz visits Eretz Yisrael and inspects Kollel Chabad
Summary: During his summer 5689 visit to Eretz Yisrael, Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn personally inspected the Kollel Chabad office and its work.
Story: The Rebbe reported being pleased with the kollel's administration and orderly procedures, and witnessed the scope of its activity in supporting Torah scholars, the holy yishuv, widows, orphans and the very poor. He saw the institution as continuing the legacy of his ancestors, and the visit set the stage for his formal acceptance of the kollel's nesius days later. The visit also fell during the summer that included the 1929 Arab riots in Hebron.
Tags: kollel chabad, jerusalem, maharayatz, visit

Title: Rebbe Rayatz instructs founding of Chmielnik yeshiva
Summary: During Tishrei 5690 the Rebbe Rayatz, in Riga, instructed Yosef Goldstein to establish a Tomchei Tmimim branch in Chmielnik.
Story: When Yosef Goldstein traveled to the Rebbe Rayatz in Riga for the High Holidays of 5690, the Rebbe ordered him to found a branch of Tomchei Tmimim in his hometown of Chmielnik under the name 'Toras Emes.' Goldstein returned home, partnered with Avraham Zonstein of the Tmimim association, and the yeshiva was operational within weeks. The name 'Toras Emes' was retained at the Rebbe's insistence even though local authorities preferred the older 'Beis Yosef' designation.
Tags: poland, chmielnik, riga, yosef-goldstein, toras-emes, tishrei

Title: Rebbe Rayatz's first visit to the United States
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz visited the United States for the first time at the end of 5689.
Story: At the close of 5689 the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in America for his first visit, traveling among Jewish communities including St. Louis, where he received $600 from R' Shaul Dovber Zislin's brother toward Zislin's rescue from Russia. After this visit obtaining Soviet exit permits became markedly harder, and the author's rescue work in subsequent years yielded fewer successes. The Rebbe's response to one rescue request was that supernatural intervention would be required to bring the family out.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, united states, visit, st louis, lubavitch

Title: Rebbe's secretariat writes to Shvadron about library effort
Summary: The Frierdiker Rebbe's secretariat wrote to Shvadron with cautious optimism about retrieving the Chabad library, saying 'hope appears for the good.'
Story: Efforts to recover the Chabad library held by Soviet authorities continued throughout the late 1920s. In 1929, the Frierdiker Rebbe's secretariat sent a letter to Shvadron stating that 'hope appears for the good' regarding the library. The letter is documented in the Rebbe Rayatz's published correspondence (vol. 1, p. 538).
Tags: library, soviet union, shvadron, schneersohn library, rayatz

Title: Soviet authorities expel the Polotsk Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva
Summary: Mid-winter 5689 Soviet authorities shut down the underground Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva operating in Polotsk.
Story: The clandestine Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva that had been functioning in Polotsk under R' Yechezkel Himmelstein and R' Shlomo Chaim Kesselman, with about thirty older students, was forcibly closed by Soviet authorities mid-winter. The author had already transferred to the Vitebsk branch a short time earlier, which he later recorded as providential. He completed the winter zman at Vitebsk under R' Gavriel Kagan without disturbance.
Tags: polotsk, tomchei-tmimim, yeshiva, soviet-persecution, belarus, soviet-union

Title: Soviet legislation strips clergy of housing and employment rights
Summary: 1929 Soviet legislation made Shabbat-observant Jews liable for rents up to ten times higher if not officially employed, targeting clergy of all religions.
Story: The law curbed clergy's ability to serve congregations and devastated observant Jews. Reports of growing hunger trickled out, and the Rebbe attempted food shipments. In 1929 he had sent matzah for Passover, but Russian authorities now refused to authorize organized shipments, prompting his shift to the covert package strategy.
Tags: soviet-union, russia, religious-persecution, shabbat-observance, passover

Title: Soviet raid scatters Tomchei Tmimim central yeshiva in Nevel
Summary: Mid-winter authorities came to arrest the Nevel yeshiva and kollel staff, scattering its classes across Leningrad, Vitebsk, and Yekaterinoslav.
Story: Nevel had been the heart of the Tomchei Tmimim network in Russia, housing R' Nissan Nemenov, R' Zalman Kornitzer, R' Yehuda Eber's shiur, and R' Shmuel Levitin's kollel for rabbinical students. When the GPU came to arrest everyone, the entire institution dispersed: the middle and part of the youngest class went to Leningrad with R' Nissan Nemenov, the senior class transferred to Vitebsk, and R' Yehuda Eber's shiur passed through Vitebsk on its way to Yekaterinoslav.
Tags: nevel, tomchei-tmimim, soviet-repression, nissan-nemenov, leningrad, vitebsk, yekaterinoslav, yehuda-eber, kollel

Title: Tomchei Tmimim branch founded in Lodz
Summary: A Tomchei Tmimim branch was founded in Lodz in 5689 (1929).
Story: Added to the growing network of provincial preparatory yeshivos, Lodz grew into one of the largest branches with two classes by 5695 and roughly 150 students before the war. It remained a central pillar of Chabad education in Poland until the Nazi invasion forced its collapse.
Tags: poland, lodz, tomchei tmimim, branch

Title: Tomchei Tmimim Chmielnik 'Toras Emes' founded
Summary: The Chmielnik branch of Tomchei Tmimim, named 'Toras Emes,' was founded in the winter of 5690.
Story: While visiting the Rebbe Rayatz in Riga during Tishrei 5690, Yosef Goldstein, a young shochet and former student of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw, was instructed to establish a branch in Chmielnik called 'Toras Emes.' Together with Avraham Zonstein he gathered about fifteen students, and the yeshiva quickly grew. By the time of its report, three rashei yeshiva taught roughly seventy students across four divisions.
Tags: poland, chmielnik, tomchei-tmimim, toras-emes, yosef-goldstein, rebbe-rayatz

Title: Tomchei Tmimim Romny closes after Soviet persecution
Summary: The Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Romny closed in 5689 amid the Soviet crackdown on Jewish education.
Story: According to the memoirs of R' Mordechai Shusterman, who had traveled to Romny to study, the yeshiva ceased operating in 5689, forcing students to return home. With the yeshiva closed, R' Yani Gurarie was left without a position before being offered the Romny rabbinate.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, romny, yani gurarie, yeshiva, soviet union, chabad

Title: Yiddish school network peaks at 1,100 schools
Summary: The state-run Yiddish school system reached its peak with around 130,000 students.
Story: The Yevsektzia championed Yiddish as the language of the 'Jewish proletariat' while abolishing Hebrew study and Zionist culture. By 1929 there were 1,100 such schools across the Soviet Union. Jewish religion, history, Hebrew, and tradition were excluded from the curriculum, and many religious parents sent children to non-Jewish schools to avoid the anti-religious propaganda.
Tags: yiddish schools, yevsektzia, soviet education, secular

Title: Author begins serving as ba'al koreh in Vitebsk
Summary: Studying at the Vitebsk Tomchei Tmimim, the author began chanting the weekly Torah portion in a local minyan starting from Parashat Bo.
Story: Lodging in the same apartment building as rosh yeshiva R' Gavriel Kagan, with R' Tzemach (son of R' Yitzchak the masmid) serving as mashgiach, the author followed a schedule of Gemara until 8 PM and a half-hour of Tanya. Beginning with Parashat Bo and continuing through Yitro and the rest of the year, he reviewed each parsha after the evening seder and chanted it the next Shabbat at a nearby minyan, training himself into the role of ba'al koreh he would carry for life.
Tags: vitebsk, yeshiva, tomchei-tmimim, belarus, torah-reading, baal-koreh, soviet-union

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe writes about Pandel cheder of sixty pupils
Summary: On 21 Tevet 5689 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to R. Yehuda Leib Bernstein concerning a cheder of sixty pupils in the Lithuanian town of Pandel.
Story: The Rebbe also mentioned a meeting he had held with R. Avraham Levitan of Birz about establishing public shiurim in that town. The letter shows the Frierdiker Rebbe's active oversight of Chabad education in the small Lithuanian communities between the world wars.
Tags: pandel, birz, lithuania, 5689, 21 tevet, cheder

Title: Jacobson receives letter about Rebbe Rayatz's planned visit to America
Summary: R. Yisrael Jacobson receives a letter from R. Yechezkel Feigin announcing that the Rebbe Rayatz plans to visit America the following summer.
Story: In Shevat 5689 (early 1929), R. Yisrael Jacobson received a letter from the Rebbe Rayatz's secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin, informing him that the Rebbe was preparing to travel to the United States that summer on behalf of Russian Jewry. The letter sparked the first wave of preparations among Anash, who were astonished at the prospect but did not initially dare to formally invite the Rebbe themselves. Jacobson notes that it was the Rebbe's own self-sacrifice for Russian Jewry that ultimately drove him to undertake the difficult journey.
Tags: yosef yitzchak schneersohn, yechezkel feigin, yisrael jacobson, america, russia

Title: Tmimim raise emergency ma'amad funds after telegram from R' Feigin
Summary: In mid-winter 5689, an urgent telegram from R' Yechezkel Feigin in Riga prompted twelve Tmimim to pledge emergency ma'amad funds at a meeting at R' Rivkin's home.
Story: Roughly twelve Tmimim gathered at R' Rivkin's house, each pledging no less than $100 — except two who pledged $50, and R' Gershon Simpson who gave $150. The author himself took out a gmach loan he planned to repay $20 per week, though Providence enabled him to repay it sooner. One Tomim publicly demanded all give at least $100 yet ultimately contributed nothing himself and left angry with the author — an episode the author cites to illustrate how strained the Tmimim's finances were.
Tags: maamad, feigin, riga, tmimim, fundraising, gershon simpson

Title: Kazarnovsky becomes rabbi of Bensonhurst congregations
Summary: Kazarnovsky was appointed rabbi of Bnei Yitzchak and Tiferes Yisrael in Bensonhurst, Brooklyn, with Rayatz's blessing on 21 Tevet 5689.
Story: In winter 5689, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky was appointed rabbi of both Bnei Yitzchak and Tiferes Yisrael synagogues in Bensonhurst, Brooklyn, where he served for the rest of his life. On 21 Tevet 5689, Rayatz wrote congratulating him and praying he would succeed in providing proper Torah teaching.
Tags: kazarnovsky, brooklyn, bensonhurst, rabbinate, rayatz

Title: Rayatz writes R' Ashurov about appointing his successor in Drivin
Summary: Before R' Ashurov's planned departure from Russia, the Rebbe asked him to arrange a successor rabbi and shochet for Drivin.
Story: On 26 Tevet 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov regarding the appointment of a rabbi and shochet in Drivin to replace him after his planned departure. The Rebbe urged him to make arrangements for the community before leaving for Riga.
Tags: ashurov, drivin, russia, rabbinate

Title: Rebbe responds to R' Alter on resuming Toras Emes leadership
Summary: On 27 Tevet 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz blessed R' Alter with strength of health to take up his leadership of the Jerusalem yeshiva.
Story: Replying to R' Alter's 14 Tevet letter, the Rebbe gave thanks for his safe arrival and prayed that Hashem strengthen his health so he could diligently lead the Toras Emes yeshiva in Jerusalem. He assumed by then that R' Alter had already re-entered his duties at the yeshiva.
Tags: jerusalem, toras-emes, alter-simchowitz, health

Title: Rebbe Rayatz urges revival of Torah study among Hebron Chabad remnant
Summary: On 4 Shevat 5689 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote urging that Tanya, Likkutei Torah and chassidic review be set up for the remaining Chabad community in Hebron.
Story: Writing to R' Shmuel Yehuda Chaim on 4 Shevat 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz lamented how abandoned the Hebron settlement had become and called for fixed shiurim in Tanya and Likkutei Torah. He named the dedicated chassid R' Moshe Goldsmid as the one who would gladly take on this teaching, if only listeners could be assembled.
Tags: hebron, rayatz, tanya, likkutei torah, moshe goldsmid

Title: Rebbe Rayatz reaffirms R' Alter's mission at Toras Emes
Summary: On 16 Shevat 5689, the Rebbe wrote again to R' Alter with blessings for health and success in fulfilling his role at Toras Emes.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz prayed for R' Alter's strength to fulfill 'his task and his calling' as designated and blessed by his father, the Rebbe Rashab. He invoked the special kochos given to R' Alter for leading and sustaining Tomchei Temimim — but the plan to bring his family to Warsaw was now permanently set aside, and his role at Toras Emes was treated as fixed.
Tags: jerusalem, toras-emes, alter-simchowitz, rashab

Title: Cyrus Adler argues against funding Rebbe's matzah shipment
Summary: JDC leader Cyrus Adler writes Joseph Hyman opposing support for the Rebbe's emergency matzah campaign for Soviet Jews.
Story: Adler argued that 'the Yevsektzia might block the deliveries' and that the shipment might embarrass the Russians. He later reversed position in 1932, writing he was not disposed to surrender Jewish religious practice to the Soviets.
Tags: jdc, matzah-campaign, adler, russia

Title: Cyrus Adler argues JDC should not support Rebbe's matzah campaign
Summary: JDC leader Dr. Cyrus Adler writes Joseph Hyman opposing support for the Rebbe's emergency campaign to ship matzah into the USSR.
Story: Adler warned that the Yevsektzia might block deliveries, embarrass the Russians, or that the Soviets might not agree to allow shipments. Years later, Adler regretted the decision, writing in 1932, 'I am not disposed to take the attitude to completely surrender all Jewish religious practice in Russia to the Soviets.'
Tags: joint distribution committee, matzah, passover, soviet, adler

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes urgent appeal to Aharon Teitelbaum
Summary: On 19 Shevat 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a desperate letter to R. Aharon Teitelbaum, chairman of Central Relief, after a telegram saying budget hopes were lost.
Story: The Rebbe described receiving a telegram from R. Lukshin reading 'no hope for the budget,' which devastated him. A second telegram said Teitelbaum 'gives hope for next week,' indicating the question would return to the table. He spelled out that Soviet institutions were 'flailing between life and death,' with R. Rosen having loaned 15,000 rubles.
Tags: joint, teitelbaum, central relief, russia, fundraising

Title: Rebbe writes Teitelbaum warning that Russian schools face collapse
Summary: The Rebbe writes JDC board member Rabbi Aron Teitelbaum that Russian Jewish schools are 'hanging between life and death.'
Story: He told Teitelbaum, 'The institutions in Russia are hanging between life and death. There are daily requests for funding.' The Rebbe revealed he was taking personal loans to keep Russian institutions afloat, warning that denial of funding would bring victory to the Yevsektzia and demoralize underground activists.
Tags: joint distribution committee, agudas harabonim, russia, underground, teitelbaum

Title: Rebbe writes to Rabbi Teitelbaum about dire Russian Jewish institutions
Summary: The Rebbe describes Russian Jewish institutions 'hanging between life and death' and pleads for JDC funding.
Story: Writing to JDC board member Rabbi Aron Teitelbaum, the Rebbe described schools on the verge of closing and personal loans to keep them afloat. He warned that withdrawing funding would hand victory to the Yevsektzia.
Tags: jdc, russia, teitelbaum, letter, fundraising

Title: Rebbe Rayatz raises possibility of trip to America
Summary: On 20 Shevat 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Agudas Chabad leadership in America that the budget crisis might force him to travel there.
Story: Citing advice from R. Chaim Ozer Grodzinski of Vilna and the Chofetz Chaim, the Rebbe wrote that he might have to make the journey to the United States to put the relief effort for Russian Jewry on a stable footing. The trip would be deferred until after the matzah operation, then take shape via the Holy Land starting Elul.
Tags: usa, agudas chabad, fundraising, russia, chofetz chaim, chaim ozer

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Yehuda Lokshin about US visit plans
Summary: On 20 Shevat 5689, the Rebbe sent the first written indication of his plans to travel to America to Chabad's New York director.
Story: The Rebbe wrote that the JDC's budget cuts were causing him great anguish and that he had consulted with Rabbi Chaim Ozer and the Chafetz Chaim, who encouraged him to go. The chasidic community was informed of the plan a few months later.
Tags: united-states, rayatz, jdc, lokshin, agudas-chassidei-chabad

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe writes to R. Avraham Levitan in Birz
Summary: On 24 Shvat 5689 the Frierdiker Rebbe replied to R. Avraham Levitan with feedback on his report about establishing public Chassidus classes in Birz.
Story: Levitan would continue reporting to the Rebbe on shiurim and farbrengens in Birz over the following decade, including through the late 1930s. He remained a key figure in maintaining Chabad communal life in Birz until the war.
Tags: birz, lithuania, 5689, 24 shvat, avraham levitan, shiurim

Title: Rebbe organizes funds for Levitin's release
Summary: On 24 Shevat 5689 the Rebbe wrote to the chassidim of Rakishok urging them to raise a larger sum toward Levitin's release.
Story: Replying to a letter from the Rakishok chassidim on 24 Shevat 5689 (Igros Kodesh vol. 16, letter 6121), the Rebbe explained that Levitin's situation remained unclear. He told them the sum they had collected was inadequate and pressed them to raise a proper amount so it would be ready when an opportunity arose to bring him to them.
Tags: levitin, rakishok, nevel, ransom-fund

Title: Feigin writes Jacobson urging US Chabad to prepare for Rebbe's visit
Summary: On 26 Shevat 5689, Rabbi Yechezkel Feigin asked Yisrael Jacobson to unite the US Chabad community in preparation for the Rebbe's arrival.
Story: Feigin described the Rebbe's financial difficulties and health challenges, and urged Jacobson to set aside internal differences. 'Leave behind the differences of opinion between you,' he wrote, 'make an effort to come together.'
Tags: feigin, jacobson, rayatz, united-states

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes about Avraham HaKohen's proposed Riga visit
Summary: On 9 Adar II 5689 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote welcoming Avraham HaKohen's proposed visit to Riga to discuss the yeshiva's housing.
Story: On 9 Adar II 5689 (February 1929) the Rebbe Rayatz wrote again to R' Avraham HaKohen, replying to a letter in which the philanthropist had proposed visiting Riga to continue their discussion of housing for the yeshiva. The Rebbe noted that such a visit would be most welcome and asked for the planned timing in detail. The letter is preserved in Igrot Kodesh vol. 16, letter 6153.
Tags: rebbe-rayatz, riga, warsaw, avraham-hakohen, letter

Title: R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin passes away in Eretz Yisrael
Summary: On 12 Adar 5689, the chassid R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin, a leader of Warsaw Chabad who had moved to Eretz Yisrael, passed away.
Story: R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin had relocated from Warsaw to Eretz Yisrael, returning periodically to visit Warsaw. He died on 12 Adar 5689 (Feb 22, 1929) and was buried on the Mount of Olives. On 29 Adar Sheni the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a letter of condolence to his sons and sons-in-law.
Tags: eretz yisrael, mount of olives, dovber moshe shmotkin, death

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes on global anash correspondence
Summary: On 12 Adar 5689 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch and R. Pinchas Mintz of Kovno about systematic correspondence with anash in Lithuania, Brazil, South Africa, and Russia.
Story: The Rebbe instructed his correspondents in Kovno to gather scattered descendants of chassidim, organize letter-writing campaigns to anash who had emigrated to Brazil and South Africa, and engage in carefully worded correspondence with relatives still trapped in Soviet Russia. The letter (Igros Kodesh vol. 16, no. 6154) emphasized the duty to awaken in such Jews their ancestral connection to Chassidus.
Tags: lithuania, brazil, south-africa, russia, kovno, pinchas-mintz, yehoshua-isaac-baruch, adar

Title: Levi Yitzchak and Chana Schneersohn write to Rachel Schneersohn after Rebbe's wedding
Summary: In Adar I 5689 Rabbi Levi Yitzchak and Rebbetzin Chana wrote from Dnepropetrovsk to their sister-in-law Rachel acknowledging her mazel tov for the Rebbe's wedding.
Story: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneersohn and Rebbetzin Chana wrote from Dnepropetrovsk (Yekaterinoslav) in Adar I 5689, thanking Rachel and Zelda for their congratulations on the wedding of their son the Rebbe. Levi Yitzchak explained that they had been unable to attend the wedding for various reasons and described arranging financial support to be sent to Rachel through Rabbi Lakshin.
Tags: dnepropetrovsk, yekaterinoslav, schneersohn wedding, levi yitzchak, rebbetzin chana

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Berlin for matzah operation meetings
Summary: On Sunday 21 Adar I 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Berlin and organized a week of meetings with European delegates on the matzah relief operation.
Story: Through the week, the Rebbe convened representatives from several European countries to coordinate fundraising for the matzah operation. From Berlin he sent a detailed telegram to Riga to sign the contract for matzah baking under the supervision of Rabbi M.M. Zack. He returned to Riga at the end of Adar I.
Tags: berlin, matzah, passover, russia, fundraising

Title: International matzah campaign delivers 140,000 kilos to Soviet Jews
Summary: The Rebbe's emergency campaign successfully ships 140,000 kilos of matzah into the famine-stricken Soviet Union before Passover.
Story: Mordechai Dubin secured Soviet approval through diplomatic channels in Riga while production ran at full force in Riga, Dvinsk, and Berlin. Another 5,689 packages were mailed directly to families in four hundred communities. The campaign cost $88,000 (some $1.3 million today); the JDC contributed $10,000 thanks to Dr. Rosen's urging in Moscow.
Tags: matzah, passover, russia, soviet, dubin, famine, joint distribution committee

Title: Rebbe appeals to R. Kahana-Shapira of Kovno for Levitin
Summary: In Nissan 5689 the Rebbe wrote to R. Avraham Dovber Kahana-Shapira, rabbi of Kovno, asking him to enlist high officials to free Levitin to Lithuania.
Story: In Nissan 5689 the Rebbe wrote (Igros Kodesh vol. 16, letter 6201) to the Kovno rabbi, detailing Levitin's biography and recent imprisonment in Velikie Luki. He asked Kahana-Shapira to intervene through high government officials so that Levitin would be permitted to relocate to Lithuania, specifically to his former rabbinate in Rakishok.
Tags: levitin, kahana-shapira, kovno, soviet-exile, intervention

Title: R' Moshe Katzenelson, Vilna yeshiva committee member, passes away
Summary: R' Moshe ben Eliezer HaKohen Katzenelson, formerly of Polotzk and a founding committee member of the Vilna yeshiva, passed away on 2 Nisan 5689.
Story: R' Moshe Katzenelson was a member of the executive committee of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim from its founding, devoted to the institution with complete faith. Originally from Polotzk, he served on the management board until his passing on 2 Nisan 5689.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, yahrzeit, polotzk

Title: Vilna Tomchei Tmimim management issues first preserved letter
Summary: On 4 Nisan 5689 the management of the Vilna branch of Tomchei Tmimim issued a letter signed by its committee — Weitz, Epstein, Aronowitz, Lueyev, Minkov, secretary Kapelyuvits, and Reltsnik.
Story: The signed letter, on yeshiva letterhead and stamped with the institution's seal, documents the working committee a few years into operations. Eliyahu Weitz served as director, with a multi-member board overseeing the branch from the Levin company offices on Kolejowa Street. The branch was already a recognized communal institution, supported by monthly donations from Vilna and the region and even by an allocation from R' Chaim Ozer Grodzinski's Vaad HaYeshivos.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, vilna, eliyahu weitz, lithuania

Title: Vilna yeshiva committee appeals to Vaad HaYeshivot for aid
Summary: On 4 Nisan 5689, the Vilna yeshiva committee wrote in Yiddish to the Vaad HaYeshivot describing their critical financial situation.
Story: A letter from the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim committee, preserved in the Vaad HaYeshivot file at the YIVO archives, described the yeshiva's dire situation in the Apatow Shul where many poor children were being supported. The committee emphasized that despite the yeshiva's chassidic name, students of all orientations learned there, appealing for funds.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, vaad hayeshivot, yivo, apatow shul, fundraising

Title: Rashag reports to Meisel on Passover matzah campaign progress
Summary: Rabbi Shemaryahu Gurary writes Rabbi Yisrael Meisel in Tel Aviv with extensive details on the international matzah-shipment campaign.
Story: The Rashag described the daily struggle with Russian officials, who repeatedly stalled and shifted authority between Riga, Moscow, and Berlin. He praised Chief Rabbi Hertz's major public announcement in London and the strong support from French Chief Rabbi Levi and Russian immigrant donors in Paris. Committees had been formed across Europe and as far as Shanghai and Harbin.
Tags: matzah, passover, russia, soviet, rashag, meisel

Title: Rashag reports to Meisel on Passover matzah shipment to Soviet Union
Summary: Rabbi Gurary documents the complex diplomatic and logistical struggle behind the international matzah campaign for Soviet Jewry.
Story: The Rashag lamented Russian bureaucracy: 'Every day they say they have no answer. Then they say I must inquire in Moscow.' Ultimately, 140,000 kilos of matzah were shipped plus 5,689 packages, at a total cost of $88,000.
Tags: matzah-campaign, passover, rashag, russia, letter

Title: All 28 matzah cars confirmed arrived in Soviet Russia
Summary: On the night of 12-13 Nisan 5689, word reached the Rebbe Rayatz that all 28 train cars and 5,689 matzah-flour packages had reached their Soviet destinations.
Story: After months of negotiations over export permits and customs rates — initially 5 kopecks per kilo, then a demand of 2 rubles per kilo before settling at half a ruble — 28 train cars of matzah were shipped from Riga and Berlin to 17 Soviet towns. Alongside the cars, 5,689 packages of matzah flour reached private addresses across 404 towns, all arriving by the eve of Passover 5689.
Tags: matzah, passover, russia, soviet, fundraising

Title: Rebbe Rayatz announces trip to America via Holy Land
