Summary: On 27 Nisan 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Agudas Chabad in America agreeing to visit, planning to travel via the Holy Land first.
Story: With travel back to the Soviet Union impossible to visit the graves of his ancestors, the Rebbe decided to route his journey through the Holy Land before reaching America. He targeted early Elul for the trip's beginning. The visit was meant to consolidate funding for Torah work in Russia under intensifying persecution.
Tags: usa, israel, palestine, fundraising, russia, agudas chabad

Title: Rebbe writes to Dalhinov chassidim
Summary: On 28 Nissan 5689 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a warm reply to the chassidim of Dalhinov, sent via their rabbi R. Gedalia Wilensky.
Story: After the Dalhinov chassidim wrote to the Rebbe through their rabbi R. Gedalia Wilensky in late winter 5689, the Rebbe replied on 28 Nissan 5689 (Igros Kodesh vol. 16, letter 5186), blessing the community and their families with abundant life and material and spiritual blessing.
Tags: wilensky, dalhinov, vilna-region

Title: Feigin urges American Chabad to set up maamad fundraising
Summary: Rabbi Yechezkel Feigin describes the Rebbe's spiritual isolation and financial crisis in Riga and urges US Chabad to organize support.
Story: Feigin wrote, 'Spiritually, the Rebbe is suffering. There are few anash here.' He noted the Rebbe lacked resources to establish a yeshivah in Riga and faced mounting debts and medical needs.
Tags: letter, feigin, maamad, fundraising, america

Title: Rabbi Feigin appeals to US Chasidim for fundraising help
Summary: Rabbi Yechezkel Feigin writes Rabbis Simpson and Jacobson urging them to establish a US fundraising program for the Rebbe.
Story: Feigin explained that historic sources of income in Russia were nonexistent in Riga. He described the Rebbe's spiritual suffering: 'There are few anash here. When the Rebbe says a maamar, there are not many who appreciate it.' He noted the Rebbe was burdened by many debts and was unable to establish a yeshivah due to lack of resources.
Tags: feigin, jacobson, united states, maamad, fundraising

Title: Last documented mention of the original Tel Aviv cheder
Summary: On 15 Sivan 5689 R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin wrote from the U.S. to his son about the cheder's building and its administration.
Story: Writing from America, Havlin asked his son to coordinate with R' Yaakov Malkov regarding fundraising and synagogue matters, while keeping the actual cheder and the courtyard and houses under the supervision of his other son Shalom. This is the last reference to the original Tel Aviv cheder in the documented record before it apparently closed.
Tags: tel aviv, torat emet, shlomo zalman havlin, yaakov malkov

Title: Rebbe Rayatz visits Hebron during his 1929 Holy Land trip
Summary: In Tammuz 5689 the Rebbe Rayatz visited Hebron, touring Chatzer Romano and meeting with the local Chabad community.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz visited Hebron in Tammuz 5689, just weeks before the massacre that would destroy the community. He visited the home of R' Yaakov Yosef Slonim, toured Chabad's Chatzer Romano property, repeated a maamar in the synagogue, and called on the Slabodka yeshiva. The visit is described in Sefer HaToldos vol. 4 and in Sefer Chevron.
Tags: hebron, rayatz, yaakov yosef slonim, slabodka, chatzer romano

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Glizenstein about decision to visit Holy Land
Summary: On 1 Tamuz 5689, the Rebbe wrote of his decision to visit the Holy Land in place of his customary visits to ancestral graves in Russia.
Story: Since he could no longer travel to his fathers' graves in Russia, the Rebbe explained, he had decided to visit Eretz Yisrael to pray at the sacred sites. The letter framed the trip's spiritual rationale alongside its political and fundraising goals.
Tags: glizenstein, rayatz, eretz-yisrael, kivrei-tzaddikim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Sonnenfeld about Eretz Yisrael visit
Summary: On 2 Tamuz 5689, the Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld seeking help with visa arrangements.
Story: The Rebbe emphasized to the Eidah HaChareidis leader that the purpose of the trip was personal — 'to visit the holy sites' — and not political. He also wrote to Rabbi Kook with the same request, signaling his intent to avoid the Yishuv's political fault lines.
Tags: sonnenfeld, rayatz, eretz-yisrael, visa

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Slonim and Eliazrov about visit
Summary: On 3 Tamuz 5689, the Rebbe wrote to Chabad leaders in Eretz Yisrael informing them of his impending arrival.
Story: The Rebbe hoped Chasidim would not overburden him given his delicate health, and stated that every possible effort would be made to avoid political entanglements. 'My visit is of a private nature,' he wrote.
Tags: slonim, eliazrov, rayatz, eretz-yisrael, chabad-community

Title: Rebbe Rayatz departs Riga for journey to Eretz Yisrael and the US
Summary: On 23 Tamuz 5689, the Rebbe left Riga with his son-in-law the Rashag for a year-long overseas voyage.
Story: The trip came just months after the Rebbe recovered from a heart attack. His daughter Chaya Mushka and her husband, the Ramash, joined them in Berlin for the train journey through Germany, Czechoslovakia, and Austria to the Italian port of Trieste.
Tags: rayatz, riga, journey, rashag

Title: 1929 Hebron massacre destroys the Jewish community
Summary: In Av 5689 Arab rioters massacred Jews in Hebron; survivors fled and the centuries-old Jewish settlement came to an end.
Story: Just days after the Rebbe Rayatz's visit, the 1929 Hebron massacre fell upon the Jewish community. R' Moshe Goldsmid, the spiritual anchor of Chabad's tiny remnant, was among those slaughtered, hy"d. The surviving Jews abandoned Hebron, ending the Jewish settlement in the city.
Tags: hebron, massacre, 1929 riots, moshe goldsmid, british mandate, arab riots

Title: Rebbe Rayatz enters Me'arat Hamakhpelah in Hebron
Summary: The Rebbe became the only known Jewish rabbinic leader in centuries to enter the Tomb of the Patriarchs.
Story: Eliezer Don Slonim, whose unique relationship with local Arab leaders made the visit possible, escorted the Rebbe with six rabbis. The anti-Semitic mufti of Jerusalem telegrammed local authorities demanding the visit be blocked, but his message arrived after the Rebbe had finished. The Rebbe also dispensed charity to the local Arab poor as he left.
Tags: hebron, meorat-hamachpelah, rayatz, slonim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz boards ship at Trieste
Summary: On 25 Tamuz 5689, the Rebbe boarded a ship at Trieste bound for Alexandria, Egypt.
Story: His daughter Chaya Mushka and son-in-law the Ramash accompanied him as far as the southern Italian port of Brindisi, where they returned to Berlin. The Rashag continued with the Rebbe on the voyage.
Tags: rayatz, trieste, italy, voyage

Title: Ship stops at Brindisi en route to Alexandria
Summary: On 27 Tamuz 5689, the Ramash and his wife disembarked at Brindisi to return to Berlin.
Story: The Rashag continued with the Rebbe Rayatz on the voyage to Alexandria, where they were welcomed by Jewish community leaders and a delegation of Chabad rabbis from Jerusalem.
Tags: rayatz, brindisi, italy, ramash

Title: Anti-Kook flyers distributed at Rebbe Rayatz's Jerusalem arrival
Summary: At the train station, flyers protesting the Rebbe's planned meeting with Rabbi Kook were distributed, sparking a brief fight.
Story: The flyers, signed deceptively as 'Chabad Chasidim of Jerusalem,' attacked Rabbi Kook in disparaging terms. A scuffle broke out, broken up by the British police. The Rashag made a major diplomatic effort to mitigate the damage and finalize the meeting with Rabbi Kook.
Tags: jerusalem, kook, controversy, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Jerusalem
Summary: After a nine-day journey from Riga, the Rebbe arrived at Jerusalem's train station to a crowd of five thousand.
Story: More than ten percent of Jerusalem's Jewish population turned out to welcome him. That same afternoon he made his way through the Old City on foot to the Western Wall, where 1,500 gathered and hundreds more watched from rooftops. 'I cried hot tears,' he wrote his family. 'Standing next to the Wall of the Beit HaMikdash, everything changes.'
Tags: rayatz, jerusalem, eretz-yisrael, western-wall, kook, sonnenfeld

Title: Maharayatz issues public letter endorsing Kollel Chabad
Summary: On 13 Menachem Av 5689 Rebbe Maharayatz wrote a letter of strengthening for Kollel Chabad describing what he had seen at its Jerusalem office.
Story: He praised the kollel's leadership, administration, and orderly procedures, and described the breadth of its work in supporting Torah scholars and the yishuv of Eretz Yisrael. The letter was meant to encourage donors and to recommit the worldwide Chabad community to the kollel's mission. It accompanied his decision in principle to accept the formal nesius of the kollel.
Tags: kollel chabad, maharayatz, jerusalem, tzedakah

Title: Maharayatz formally accepts nesius of Kollel Chabad; appoints Eliezerov as bakoach
Summary: On the eve of 15 Menachem Av 5689 Maharayatz informed the kollel officials that he would assume the nesius and appointed R. Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov as his permanent bakoach.
Story: The Rebbe accepted the nesius on condition that an institutional 'bakoach hanesius' — distinct from the regular officials — be installed to oversee all kollel affairs, sign in the name of the nesius, and handle all correspondence with him. He named his relative R. Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov to that position. The appointment restored the traditional structure of Chabad rebbes serving as nesi'im of the kollel that had been founded in the time of the Alter Rebbe.
Tags: kollel chabad, maharayatz, eliezerov, nesius, jerusalem

Title: Rebbe Rayatz departs Eretz Yisrael for the United States
Summary: After a two-week visit, the Rebbe left the Holy Land via Egypt en route to America.
Story: Fifteen busloads of Chasidim escorted the Rebbe from his Tel Aviv hotel to the Lod train station. 'The Rebbe was very emotional,' wrote Rabbi Shimon Glitzenstein, 'and gave his blessing to each and every person.' The Rebbe distributed a printed maamar so he could depart by sharing words of Torah.
Tags: rayatz, eretz-yisrael, lod, united-states

Title: Hebron massacre
Summary: Arab mobs incited by Jerusalem's mufti murdered sixty-four Jewish men, women, and children in Hebron.
Story: Just days after the Rebbe Rayatz's visit, riots erupted across Palestine using Jewish prayer at the Western Wall as a pretext. Many of those killed in Hebron were Chabad Chasidim, including the American yeshivah student David Shainberg, who had been deeply impressed by the Rebbe just days earlier.
Tags: hebron, arab-riots, massacre, mufti, palestine

Title: R' Eliyahu Nochum Shklyar reaches America from Eretz Yisroel
Summary: R' Eliyahu Nochum Shklyar arrived in America between Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur 5690 with his wife and eldest daughter.
Story: After leaving Russia for Eretz Yisroel and marrying there, R' Eliyahu Nochum Shklyar wished to join his father in America; the author persuaded the family to sponsor him by promising he would find a livelihood. Shklyar arrived between Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur 5690 with his wife and eldest daughter Yehudis. A few days after Sukkos, the author placed him as shochet at the slaughterhouse where his uncle R' Yeshaya Jacobson was head shochet — a post he held for many years.
Tags: shklyar, immigration, shochet, united states, eretz yisroel

Title: R. Feigin and Chaim Lieberman arrive in New York to prepare for Rebbe's visit
Summary: Roughly a week before the Rebbe Rayatz's arrival, his secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin and Chaim Lieberman travel to New York to coordinate the visit.
Story: In early Elul 5689, about a week before the Rebbe Rayatz himself was due to arrive, his secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin and Chaim Lieberman came to America to help organize the visit. They joined the ongoing debate over where the Rebbe would lodge, but no consensus emerged. By default the Rebbe was initially housed at R. Eliyahu Simpson's new apartment above a shul in Boro Park.
Tags: yechezkel feigin, chaim lieberman, america, boro park, eliyahu simpson

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in New York Harbor
Summary: Hundreds of Chasidim and well-wishers greeted the Rebbe as he disembarked, escorted by New York police.
Story: His ten-month sojourn in the US would take him from Boston to St. Louis, with most of his time spent in the Crown Heights and Brownsville sections of Brooklyn and three months in Chicago. The visit would also set the stage for his eventual relocation to America in 1940.
Tags: rayatz, united-states, new-york, voyage

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in America at New York Harbor
Summary: On Wednesday, 13 Elul 5689 (September 18, 1929), the Rebbe Rayatz arrives at New York Harbor for his historic first visit to the United States.
Story: Through the intervention of attorney Yekusiel Kremer, the Rebbe and his entourage were transferred at sea onto a small government vessel at South Ferry, sparing him the ordinary immigration disembarkation. A welcoming delegation that included R. Mordechai Lipa Lokshin, the Kremer brothers, Judge Philip Kleinfeld, and R. Shmuel Eliezer Nelson boarded the cutter to greet him. Despite a torrential downpour and an under-organized reception, the Rebbe was escorted through Manhattan by motorcycle police to R. Eliyahu Simpson's home in Boro Park, where he gave brief opening remarks ("Sadna de'ar'a chad hu") from the balcony.
Tags: yosef yitzchak schneersohn, america, new york, boro park, kremer family, eliyahu simpson, yisrael jacobson, first american visit

Title: Toras Emes flees Givat Shaul after 1929 riots
Summary: Following the 5689 Arab riots the Toras Emes yeshiva abandoned Givat Shaul and relocated inside Jerusalem proper.
Story: Havlin's son wrote on 13 Elul 5689 that the yeshiva had been forced out of its location outside the city and was now suffering severe overcrowding. The Rayatz ruled that the remote Givat Shaul site was unsafe and a more secure location had to be found.
Tags: jerusalem, toras emes, givat shaul, 1929 riots, havlin

Title: Rebbe Rayatz delivers maamar 'Hashkifa' on first Shabbos in America
Summary: On Shabbos Parshas Ki Tavo, days after arriving in America, the Rebbe Rayatz delivers the maamar 'Hashkifa' at R. Eliyahu Simpson's Boro Park shul.
Story: Just three days after disembarking in New York, the Rebbe Rayatz delivered the maamar 'Hashkifa Mim'on Kodshecha' on Shabbos Parshas Ki Tavo 5689. The maamar was later printed. It was given at R. Eliyahu Simpson's Boro Park shul, located below the apartment where the Rebbe was lodged during his first week in the United States.
Tags: yosef yitzchak schneersohn, america, chassidus, maamar, boro park, ki tavo, eliyahu simpson

Title: Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch Łódź founded
Summary: The Łódź branch of Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch was founded on 17 Elul 5689.
Story: According to the letterhead of the yeshiva, the Łódź branch of Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch was founded on 17 Elul 5689 (Sept 22, 1929) at Paludniowa 25. R. Zalman Schneersohn served as chairman and his son R. Dovber Yitzchok as director. The yeshiva initially operated with two divisions and grew steadily under the leadership of Lubavitcher chassidim in Łódź.
Tags: poland, lodz, tomchei-tmimim, yeshiva-branch, zalman-schneerson, dovber-yitzchok-schneerson

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Rabbi Kook from his voyage
Summary: On 21 Elul 5689, the Rebbe wrote that he had become sick from anguish after hearing of the Hebron massacre.
Story: Dr. Moshe Wallach, on the same ship, nurtured the Rebbe back to health. The Rebbe praised Wallach in laudatory terms as 'a wise man with fear of Heaven.'
Tags: kook, rayatz, hebron-massacre, wallach

Title: Ramash leads Sukkot farbrengen in Riga
Summary: While the Rebbe was in the US, the Ramash led a Sukkot farbrengen in Riga that astonished the chasidic community.
Story: Rabbi Eliyahu Chaim Althaus wrote that the Ramash spoke for hours saying words of Chasidut with teachings from the Sages: 'The critics and cynics have been silenced.' News spread so that on Simchat Torah, a huge crowd gathered, and Althaus reported people leaving the farbrengen saying they had never seen or heard anything like it.
Tags: riga, sukkot, simchat-torah, althaus, farbrengen

Title: Rebbe insists books must accompany him out of Russia
Summary: An Althoz letter from motzaei Rosh Hashana 5690 records that the Frierdiker Rebbe had refused to leave Russia if a single book were left behind.
Story: Writing in October 1929, R. Eliyahu Chaim Althoz recounted the Rebbe's earlier insistence — delivered while at the ohel in Rostov — that he would not depart if even one volume had to remain. Mordechai Dubin once again traveled to intercede and succeeded in extracting the export concession, a story the chassid R. Y. Jacobson similarly preserved in his memoir Zikaron Livnei Yisrael.
Tags: russia, soviet, library, rayatz, rostov, althoz

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe leads Rosh Hashana prayers at Anshei Lubavitch shul, Brownsville
Summary: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn led the High Holy Day services at Beis Hamedrash Anshei Lubavitch, 195 Watkins Street, during his first visit to America.
Story: Because the Rebbe's Crown Heights apartment was too small for the anticipated crowd, anash chose the large Anshei Lubavitch shul in Brownsville for his Yamim Noraim prayers. Rosh Hashana night prayers stretched many hours with weeping that listeners would never forget. The Rebbe stayed in the home of Dr. Akin on Stone Avenue, secured through community askan Aaron Siminovsky.
Tags: rayatz, rosh hashana, brownsville, anshei lubavitch, 1929 visit, brooklyn, usa, frierdiker rebbe, aaron siminovsky

Title: Rebbe Rayatz delivers Rosh Hashanah maamar in Brownsville
Summary: For the High Holidays, the Rebbe attended a large Brownsville synagogue where he prayed at great length and recited a maamar.
Story: Years later Yehoshua Greenberg recalled that the shul was packed, with many gathered outdoors. 'The Rebbe's voice was booming,' he said, 'and even those outside heard him.' The maamar 'Zeh HaYom Techilat Maasekha' was later published.
Tags: brownsville, brooklyn, rosh-hashanah, rayatz, maamar

Title: Hyman issues confidential JDC memorandum on the Rebbe
Summary: JDC director Joseph Hyman prepared a confidential memo for Dr. Cyrus Adler in advance of his meeting with the Rebbe.
Story: Hyman raised concerns about transferring funds to Russia and asserted the JDC could help 'on the condition that there be no publicity and no noise. No brass bands.' He noted the Rebbe had created a reliable mechanism to secretly transfer funds and referred to him as 'our friend' without using his name.
Tags: jdc, hyman, adler, rayatz, soviet-jewry

Title: Rebbe writes Rabbi Munk requesting German translation of maamar
Summary: The Rebbe writes Rabbi Meir Munk in Berlin asking him to arrange for a maamar to be translated into German.
Story: This was the first time a chasidic discourse would be published in a European language other than Hebrew or Yiddish. The Rebbe wanted to engage German Jews, many of whom lacked a strong Jewish academic background, and give them the opportunity to appreciate concepts of chasidic philosophy. The Ramash later arranged for another translation in 1936.
Tags: berlin, germany, translation, maamar, munk

Title: Adler-Rebbe Rayatz meeting on JDC support
Summary: Just after Rosh Hashanah, the Rebbe and Dr. Cyrus Adler met to discuss JDC support for Russian Jewish religious life.
Story: Adler, a traditional Jew educated in Orthodox schools, was sympathetic to the Rebbe's mission. In his internal JDC memo, Adler noted the difficulties of Russian Jewish life and was open to legally transferring funds. At a second meeting a month later, he assured the Rebbe the JDC would help significantly and secretly — a commitment that was ultimately not honored.
Tags: jdc, adler, rayatz, soviet-jewry

Title: Simchat Torah celebration in Crown Heights
Summary: A few thousand people joined the Rebbe for a forty-eight-hour holiday celebration in Brooklyn.
Story: Reform Rabbi Stephen S. Wise visited the Rebbe privately during the day, later telling his Manhattan students, 'It is worthwhile for you to visit the chakham, the wise leader of the Jewish people, in Brooklyn.' The celebration continued past sunset with editors, reform rabbis, yeshivah alumni, and Chasidim joining a long farbrengen and series of talks outlining a vision for American Jewry.
Tags: crown-heights, simchat-torah, rayatz, stephen-wise, farbrengen

Title: Famous Simchat Torah 'Eimasai Kaasi Mar' sicha and Stephen Wise visit
Summary: During the Rebbe's first American Simchat Torah, Rabbi Stephen Wise visited and the Rebbe delivered the historic 'Eimasai Kaasi Mar' sicha later printed in three pamphlets.
Story: Hakafos continued until dawn, and at the daytime meal the Rebbe was about to begin his sicha when Reform leader Rabbi Stephen Wise arrived to greet him. Yiddish journalists who were present struggled to capture the deep content; R. Chaim Lieberman, the Rebbe's secretary, stood behind him and transcribed the talk in pencil, later recopying it in ink. The sicha was published in a second edition in 5697 (1937) in three pamphlets.
Tags: rayatz, simchat torah, stephen wise, 1929 visit, brooklyn, usa, frierdiker rebbe, chaim lieberman, journalists

Title: Bar mitzvah of Meir Greenberg sparks beard-removal campaign in Crown Heights
Summary: At the early-Cheshvan bar mitzvah of Meir Greenberg, the boy's father Yehoshua Falk had yechidus, prompting the Rebbe's sharp rebuke over American beard removal.
Story: The author urged the bar mitzvah boy's father to seek the Rebbe's blessing; the father had removed his beard with depilatory cream as was then standard practice. After the visit the Rebbe scolded the author that a beardless Jew was attending his shul, demanding to know how he could eat his bread under such circumstances. This conversation launched a sustained effort to convince Crown Heights congregants to stop removing their beards.
Tags: bar mitzvah, beard, americanization, meir greenberg, yehoshua falk greenberg, brooklyn, yiddishkeit

Title: Memoirist travels to teach at Cherson yeshiva
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan 5690 (3 November 1929) the memoirist set out from Zlobin to teach at the Chabad yeshiva in Cherson, only to find on arrival that the staff and students had been arrested.
Story: The memoirist boarded the train Sunday morning on Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan 5690 with fellow Zlobin native Dovber HaLevi Gurevitch, arriving in Cherson 36 hours later. The R'M R' Yosef Himelstein's wife met them outside in tears: her husband, the mashgiach, and all the students had been arrested. Too frightened to take them in, the residents sent the pair back, and a non-Jewish wagon driver sheltered them overnight before they returned to Kremenchug.
Tags: cherson, tomchei tmimim, zlobin, soviet union, kremenchug

Title: Rayatz writes R' Gutnik in London asking aid for refugee rabbis in Riga
Summary: The Rebbe asked R' Mordechai Zev Gutnik in London to help two refugee Chabad rabbis stranded in Riga.
Story: On 21 Cheshvan 5690, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Mordechai Zev Gutnik, a rabbi in London, requesting help for two students of his stranded in Riga: R' Yaakov Yisrael Zuber and R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov. Both had hoped to emigrate to America but had been rejected by the American consul; the Rebbe asked Gutnik to secure entry permits and positions for them elsewhere.
Tags: gutnik, ashurov, zuber, riga, london, emigration

Title: R' Yaakov Landa marries Mina Rabinowitz
Summary: R' Yaakov Landa married Mrs. Mina Rabinowitz in the winter of 5690, with the Rogatchover officiating.
Story: In the winter of 5690 (1929-1930), R' Yaakov Landa, rabbi of the Libau Chassidim, married Mrs. Mina Rabinowitz. A 9 Kislev 5690 article in the Frimorgn newspaper announced the wedding and noted that the Rogatchover Gaon would serve as the mesader kiddushin.
Tags: libau, liepaja, latvia, landa, rogatchover, marriage

Title: Rebbe Rayatz urges Latvia Anash to expand public Chassidus study
Summary: From America the Rebbe Rayatz wrote an open letter to Anash in Latvia urging dedicated public Chassidus study and announcing a special committee to promote it.
Story: While visiting the United States the Rebbe Rayatz dispatched a general letter (Vol. II, Iggeret 464) to Anash and Chassidic families across Latvia, urging each one to weigh his present spiritual state against the standard of earlier Chassidim and to commit to fixed times of public Chassidus study. He announced the formation of a special committee for this purpose and called on rabbis, ritual slaughterers, and synagogue gabbaim throughout Latvia to join hands in bringing the threefold blessing tied to such study to every town.
Tags: latvia, riga, chassidus, rayatz, letter, anash, united states

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Philadelphia
Summary: The Rebbe began a month-long stay in Philadelphia, where he was welcomed by crowds of thousands.
Story: During the visit, the Rebbe was honored at Independence Hall with an invitation to sit in George Washington's chair, calling the building 'the cradle of American democracy.' Local philanthropists Nathan and Jennie Faggen hosted a major fundraising dinner that raised over fifteen thousand dollars despite the recent stock market crash.
Tags: philadelphia, rayatz, independence-hall, faggen

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe spends 19 Kislev in Philadelphia
Summary: The Rebbe celebrated 19 Kislev 5690 in Philadelphia, drawing the Feder family back to observance.
Story: On his cross-country American tour the Rebbe visited Philadelphia for Yud Tes Kislev. Among those drawn closer was the family of Michael Feder of Nevel, Vitebsk, who kashered their home. Their son Henry began putting on tefillin and briefly worked in the office handling the Rebbe's American visit.
Tags: rayatz, yud tes kislev, philadelphia, 1929 visit, usa, frierdiker rebbe, feder family

Title: Agudas Chassidei Chabad founded for Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia
Summary: Twenty-one Chasidim meet at the Rashag's home during High Holidays to form a union of Chabad communities across the region.
Story: Rashag proposed the organization with the Rebbe's approval. It took on the mandate of strengthening Chabad communities in Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia, providing institutional infrastructure for the dispersed movement.
Tags: agudas-chassidei-chabad, rashag, high-holidays, riga

Title: Di Yisurim Fun Lubavitcher Rebben published in Riga
Summary: An anonymous Yiddish narrative of the Rebbe's Soviet imprisonment, later identified as the work of journalist Elimelech Josselsohn, was published in Riga.
Story: Josselsohn, a religious Zionist who had studied in Jerusalem before returning to Riga to write for Frimorgen, captured the mood and climate of the turbulent era. The book was translated into English for the first time in volume 6 of Likkutei Dibburim (Kehot, 2012).
Tags: yiddish, riga, josselsohn, imprisonment account

Title: Founding of Agudas Chassidei Chabad branches in New York neighborhoods
Summary: During his American visit the Rebbe convened anash leaders, drafted the bylaws of Agudas Chassidei Chabad, and established neighborhood branches across greater New York and other cities.
Story: The Rebbe summoned the chief Chabad askanim and met with them several times in his quarters to draft the agudah's constitution. Greater New York was divided into neighborhoods with appointed gabba'im and ledger books, and the Rebbe wrote a personal blessing in his own hand at the head of each branch's book. At the Rebbe's request Shmuel Hein was appointed secretary of the agudah.
Tags: agudas chassidei chabad, rayatz, 1929 visit, new york, shmuel hein, tomchei tmimim, bylaws

Title: Future Rebbe makes inventory of Rayatz's manuscript holdings
Summary: Around 5690, the future Rebbe (then Rayatz's son-in-law) compiles a three-page list of the manuscripts held by Rayatz.
Story: The list, in the future Rebbe's own hand, notes that pages 1 and 2 are copied from the general index while page 3 records bichlach not found in the index but seen personally — possibly added after the index was compiled. The numbering on the right matches the order arranged by Rashab himself. This list aligns with the 265 bichlach catalogued in Rayatz's general index, suggesting the future Rebbe compiled it after Rayatz entrusted the manuscripts to him.

Title: Jerusalem Haggadah illustrated by A. El-Hanani
Summary: A Haggadah illustrated by A. El-Hanani was printed in Jerusalem.
Story: In 5690 (1930), an illustrated Haggadah by A. El-Hanani was printed by Lipschitz in Jerusalem. The 37-page edition included musical notation. It represented the developing Yishuv artistic tradition of Haggadah illustration in pre-state Palestine.
Tags: haggadah, jerusalem, el-hanani, illustrated, musical notation

Title: Leningrad rabbis arrested including Shimon Lazaroff
Summary: In 1930 Soviet authorities arrested eleven Leningrad rabbis including community head Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff for running underground religious institutions.
Story: The indictment named Lazaroff as head of the religious association Tzemach Tzedek, accusing him of organizing unlawful yeshivas and chadarim funded by foreign capitalists. Sentenced to ten years, he died in a prison camp in 1933. Despite arrests the underground system showed remarkable resilience, with yeshivas closing in one town and reopening in another.
Tags: leningrad, russia, soviet-union, lazaroff, tzemach-tzedek, kgb

Title: Rabbi Eber sent to examine students in Warsaw and Vilna
Summary: In the summer of 5690 (1930) the Rebbe Rayatz dispatched Rabbi Yehuda Eber from Riga to examine the students of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw and Vilna.
Story: While stranded in Riga awaiting an American visa, Rabbi Yehuda Eber received word through Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson and Rabbi Y. Feigin that the Rebbe Rayatz wished him to travel immediately to Warsaw and Vilna to examine all the students of Tomchei Tmimim there. A telegraphic visa was arranged from Warsaw. The journey set in motion his future role as rosh yeshiva of the central yeshiva in Warsaw.
Tags: warsaw, vilna, poland, lithuania, tomchei tmimim, yehuda eber, examinations

Title: Rabbi Yehuda Eber leaves Russia for Riga
Summary: Rabbi Yehuda Eber departed Russia in the winter of 5690 (1930) and arrived in Riga after years of leading underground yeshiva branches.
Story: After serving as a leading rosh yeshiva in the underground Tomchei Tmimim network in Poltava, Rostov, Nevel, and Vitebsk, Rabbi Yehuda Eber received permission to leave Soviet Russia in the winter of 5690. He arrived in Riga intending to continue on to the United States, but was unable to obtain entry papers despite efforts by Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson of Agudas Chabad. He remained stranded with his family in Riga while pursuing the American visa.
Tags: russia, riga, latvia, yehuda eber, tomchei tmimim, emigration

Title: Rayatz launches family purity campaign on first US visit
Summary: During his first US visit in 5690, the Rayatz founded women's leagues for family purity in numerous American towns.
Story: On his first visit to the United States in 5690 (1930), the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe (Rayatz) confronted widespread ignorance of family purity and founded leagues of women in many towns to strengthen observance. This work is described in Toldos Chabad B'Artzos HaBris chapter 11.
Tags: united states, rayatz, family purity, mikvah

Title: Rebbe Rayatz stays in Otwock for Tishrei 5691
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz stayed in Otwock during Tishrei 5691, as reported in the local press.
Story: During Tishrei 5691 (autumn 1930), Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn (the Rebbe Rayatz) stayed in the Polish town of Otwock, as reported by the local 'Otwocker Tzeitung.' The visit drew significant local attention. The Library preserves a copy of the newspaper edition reporting on his stay.
Tags: otwock, poland, rebbe rayatz, tishrei

Title: Roster of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw students compiled
Summary: A detailed roster of the students learning at Yeshivas Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw was compiled for the summer of 5690 (1930), recording family and academic details of each bochur.
Story: The summer 5690 student list documents nearly sixty bochurim studying in the Warsaw yeshiva, with notes on their hometowns, ages, family backgrounds, chassidic affiliations, and academic progress through the yeshiva's classes. The list preserves a rare demographic snapshot of pre-war Polish Chabad youth, including students from Warsaw, Chelm, Lublin, Stopnica, Riga, Romania, and dozens of Polish towns. It serves as a key document for tracing the talmidim of Tomchei Tmimim before the Holocaust.
Tags: warsaw, poland, tomchei tmimim, student roster, yeshiva

Title: Stalin dismantles the Yevsektsia
Summary: Stalin dismantled the Yevsektsia (Jewish section of the Communist Party), killing and exiling many of its leaders and activists.
Story: This fulfilled the Rashab's 1920 prediction that the Communist Jews who fought Judaism would be 'broken and their leaders killed.' A whole generation of Jewish Communists involved in Jewish affairs were liquidated in massive purges. The Yevsektzia had been the greatest threat to religious Jewry in the Soviet Union.
Tags: stalin, yevsektsia, soviet union, jewish communists

Title: Tomchei Tmimim branch founded in Chmielnik
Summary: A Tomchei Tmimim branch was founded in Chmielnik in 5690 (1930).
Story: Chmielnik joined Warsaw, Vilna and Lodz in the expanding Tomchei Tmimim provincial network. It remained active through the late 1930s and was repeatedly listed among the network's stable branches in official accountings.
Tags: poland, chmielnik, tomchei tmimim, branch

Title: Trotsky deported from Russia
Summary: Two years after his banishment to Alma Ata, Leon Trotsky was deported from Russia entirely.
Story: In 1930, having been banished to Alma Ata two years earlier, Trotsky was deported from the Soviet Union altogether. He moved through European cities before eventually settling in Mexico, where he would be assassinated a decade later.
Tags: trotsky, soviet union, exile

Title: Trotsky deported from the Soviet Union
Summary: Trotsky was deported from Russia entirely, two years after his initial banishment to Alma Alta.
Story: After living in European cities, Trotsky eventually relocated to Mexico. In 1937 he was sentenced to death in absentia in a Moscow trial. He was assassinated by a Stalinist agent in his home in Mexico City in 1940.
Tags: trotsky, soviet union, stalin, exile

Title: Vaad formed to bring the Frierdiker Rebbe to settle in America
Summary: Before the Rebbe's summer 1930 departure, anash formed a committee chaired by Max (M.M.) Halbreich to bring the Rebbe to settle permanently in America.
Story: An awakening grew among anash in summer 5690 that the Rebbe should immigrate to the United States. A vaad was chosen with Max Halbreich, brother and son-in-law of Chaim Halbreich, as chairman and R. Nissan Telushkin among its energetic activists, and funds were raised. The Rebbe would later write on 18 Cheshvan 5691 that he did not intend to settle in America.
Tags: rayatz, settlement, max halbreich, nissan telushkin, usa, vaad, immigration

Title: Yevesektzia dismantled by Stalin
Summary: Stalin dissolved the Yevesektzia, and many of its leaders were later killed or exiled during the Great Purge.
Story: The dissolution did not soften the Soviet stance on religion. In the 1930s, after the Yevesektzia was gone, government actions against synagogues and religious leaders became harsher.
Tags: yevesektzia, stalin, great-purge

Title: Yevesektzia dismantled in Soviet purges
Summary: Stalin dismantled the Yevesektzia, killing and exiling its Jewish Communist leaders.
Story: In 1930, the Yevesektzia, the anti-religious Jewish section of the Communist Party that had been a primary persecutor of Soviet Jews, was dismantled. Many of its leaders and activists were killed or exiled in the purges, fulfilling another of the Rashab's 1920 predictions.
Tags: yevesektzia, stalin, soviet union, purges, communism

Title: Yevesektzia dismantled; Soviet state takes over anti-religious campaign
Summary: In 1930 the Soviet government dismantled the Yevesektzia, just as the Rebbe Rashab had foreseen, and the state itself took over religious suppression.
Story: Until 1930 the Rebbe and the Committee of Rabbis had often played government officials against Yevesektzia zealots. With its closure, government restraint ended and persecution became state policy. Stalin's later purges devoured Yevesektzia leaders themselves: Dimenstein was killed in 1938, Litvakov executed in 1937, and Frumkin died in a Kazakhstan prison camp after her 1938 arrest.
Tags: soviet-union, russia, yevesektzia, religious-persecution

Title: Yevsektzia dismantled by Stalin
Summary: Stalin disbanded the Jewish section of the Communist Party; many of its leaders were later killed in the purges.
Story: Established in 1917 to fortify Bolshevik control over Jewish masses, the Yevsektzia had been the Rayatz's primary adversary throughout the 1920s. After 1930 many of its leaders, including Semyon Dimenstein and Moshe Litvakov, were killed or exiled in the Great Purge. After the Yevsektzia was disbanded, government actions against synagogues and religious leaders actually became harsher.
Tags: yevsektzia, stalin, great purge, dimenstein, litvakov

Title: Chabad rabbi leaves Globoke
Summary: The Chabad rabbi of Globoke departed in the winter of 5690, leaving the chassidic community to seek a replacement from the Rebbe.
Story: In the winter of 5690 (1930), the rabbi of the Chabad community in Globoke left the town. The chassidic community (separate from the general kehilla, which had its own rabbi, R. Yosef HaLevi Katz) turned to the Rebbe Rayatz, then in America, asking him to send a Chabad rabbi to replace him.
Tags: globoke, lithuania, rabbinate, vacancy

Title: Rebbe Rayatz meets Justice Louis Brandeis
Summary: In late January, the Rebbe asked the Supreme Court justice to spearhead a coalition of major Jewish groups to help Soviet Jews.
Story: Rabbi Kook had given the Rebbe a letter of recommendation. The Rebbe proposed an alliance with the JDC coordinating colonies while others facilitated emigration and supported religious life, with Brandeis as chair. 'Rabbi Schneersohn impressed me so much,' Brandeis later wrote, but he limited himself to behind-the-scenes work, and the broader coalition floundered.
Tags: brandeis, washington, soviet-jewry, rayatz, coalition

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Baltimore
Summary: The Rebbe began a three-week visit to Baltimore, welcomed by a crowd of three thousand.
Story: During the visit, the Rebbe was presented with the key to the city by the mayor, met with Maryland Governor Albert Richie, and delivered a maamar to roughly 1,500 people challenging the ethics-only theology of liberal Judaism. 'The key to connecting with the Divine,' he taught, 'is through fulfilling the commandments.'
Tags: baltimore, rayatz, maryland, mitzvot

Title: Mordechai Schwei celebrates wedding in Finland
Summary: Rabbi Mordechai Schwei, the sole Chasid in remote Finland, wrote to Zelig Slonim describing how he marked Chaya Mushka's wedding.
Story: Despite his isolation, Schwei wrote, 'I shared in the joy with all the Temimim and the Rebbe.' His letter reflects how Chasidim around the world celebrated the wedding remotely as a moment of collective joy, even in the most distant outposts of the chasidic world.
Tags: finland, schwei, slonim, temimim

Title: Kuperstock visits Globoke for Shabbos Yitro
Summary: At the Rebbe's instruction, R. Menachem Mendel Kuperstock of Fastov visited Globoke for Shabbos Parshas Yisro and made a strong impression on the local chassidim.
Story: From America, the Rebbe Rayatz directed R. Menachem Mendel Kuperstock, the rabbi of nearby Fastov, to visit Globoke. He arrived for Shabbos Parshas Yisro, spoke publicly, repeated chassidic discourses, and left a positive impression on the chassidic community there.
Tags: kuperstock, globoke, fastov, chassidus

Title: Minsk rabbis arrested by Soviet secret police
Summary: A group of rabbis was arrested in Minsk and accused of being a counter-revolutionary organization linked to the Rebbe Rayatz.
Story: The GPU charged Rabbi Pevsner with receiving instructions from the Rebbe in the US about organizing illegal rabbinical seminaries and Hebrew schools. The arrests emboldened JDC leaders, led by Warburg, who opposed funding the Rebbe's activities — they refused further support, fearing association with him might damage their Russian standing.
Tags: minsk, gpu, soviet-jewry, pevsner, rayatz

Title: Rebbe leads amud prayers in Crown Heights for Rebbetzin Rivka's yahrzeit
Summary: On Shabbat 10 Shevat 5690 the Rebbe davened before the amud for the yahrzeit of his grandmother Rebbetzin Rivka, wife of the Rebbe Maharash.
Story: Michael Feder traveled from Philadelphia and spent the entire Shabbat at the Rebbe's home to ease the test of Shabbat observance, davening near the Rebbe with hot tears streaming down. The Rebbetzin Rivka, wife of Rebbe Maharash, had passed away on Friday 10 Shevat 5674.
Tags: rayatz, yud shevat, rebbetzin rivka, yahrzeit, 1929 visit, brooklyn, feder family

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Chicago
Summary: A boisterous crowd of fifteen thousand welcomed the Rebbe at LaSalle Street Station for a three-month stay.
Story: It took police half an hour to make a path for the Rebbe to exit the station. During the Chicago visit, the Rebbe challenged the rosh yeshivah of Hebrew Theological College, Rabbi Nachman Bar, to expand his impact beyond the yeshivah by teaching weekly parashah classes to ordinary Jews — a class Rabbi Bar would teach for the next sixteen years.
Tags: chicago, rayatz, lasalle-station, htc, nachman-bar

Title: Vilna yeshiva reports examination by R' Aryeh Leib Sheinin
Summary: On 23 Shevat 5690, Vilna yeshiva administrators wrote to the Rebbe describing R' Aryeh Leib Sheinin's recent examination of the students.
Story: R' Aryeh Leib Sheinin, rabbi of Dokshitz, visited the Vilna yeshiva and examined the students in their Torah, avodah, and conduct. So impressed was he that he urged the administration to expand beyond their current five classes by adding a higher division for advanced bochurim who would otherwise need to travel elsewhere.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, rabbi aryeh leib sheinin, dokshitz, examination

Title: R' Shneur Zalman Zeligson, Vilna yeshiva co-founder, passes away
Summary: R' Shneur Zalman ben Avraham Aba Zeligson, a co-founder and supporter of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim, passed away on 25 Shevat 5690.
Story: R' Shneur Zalman Zeligson prayed in the building that became the Vilna yeshiva before its founding and was among its founders. He later served as an examiner of the students and a supporter of the institution until his passing on 25 Shevat 5690, as recounted by his student R' Moshe Dreyzin.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, yahrzeit, founding

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Rabbi Rothstein about US indifference
Summary: On 28 Shevat 5690, the Rebbe described the cold attitude toward Russian Jewry he encountered in America.
Story: The Rebbe wrote that the JDC, the Agudas Harabonim, and public opinion in the US were all indifferent to Russian Jews' plight. After months in America, however, he sensed a slight shift: 'The public is waking up slightly and is beginning to feel that something must be done.'
Tags: rayatz, rothstein, jdc, soviet-jewry

Title: Semicha granted to Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw students by Warsaw rabbinic luminaries
Summary: In Adar 5690 (March 1930) leading Warsaw rabbis granted semicha to a group of Tomchei Tmimim students after rigorous examinations.
Story: A landmark celebration marked the awarding of semicha to the first group of Tomchei Tmimim bochurim in Warsaw by major poskim including Rabbi Menachem Zemba, Rabbi Shlomo Dovid Kahane, Rabbi Chaim Leib Yudkovsky, Rabbi Yehoshua Plate, and Rabbi Yitzchak Meir Kanal. Surviving semicha documents from the estate of Rabbi Moshe Pinchas Katz, dated Adar 5690, were issued by Rabbi Shlomo Dovid Kahane, Rabbi Yitzchak Meir Kanal, Rabbi Sholom Shachna Cherniak of Maciejów, and Rabbi Yechezkel Michelson. The achievement demonstrated the high Talmudic level the yeshiva had reached in exile.
Tags: warsaw, poland, semicha, menachem zemba, shlomo dovid kahane, tomchei tmimim

Title: Sheinin reports on 5690 tour of Vilna-region towns
Summary: Writing on the eve of 16 Adar 5690 (תר"צ), Sheinin reported on his Shevat tour through Haloboutchi, Pliesy, Disna, and Vilna, where he energized Tanya and chassidus shiurim.
Story: Sheinin recounted that during Shevat 5690 he visited multiple towns repeating chassidus and urging Tanya shiurim. In Haloboutchi, R. Yeshaya Refael recited chassidus each Shabbos; in Pliesy he prompted R. Yisrael to begin a daily Tanya shiur; in Disna he worked with R. Shemarya Yofeh to begin Tanya after his daily gemara; and in Vilna's Kirzner minyan he prompted R. Elye Weitz to add Tanya to his daily gemara shiur.
Tags: sheinin, vilna, disna, pliesy, haloboutchi, tanya

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Rabbi Rabinowitz of disappointment in JDC
Summary: On 2 Adar 5690, the Rebbe expressed great disappointment over the JDC's repeated broken promises.
Story: 'I trusted naively the words of Dr. Rosen in Riga that the JDC would help,' the Rebbe wrote. The Wall Street crash had hurt fundraising, but he remained undeterred: 'We must break down the wall of indifference. The condition of Russian Jewry is very grave.'
Tags: rayatz, rabinowitz, jdc, rosen

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes coordinated letters blessing the Latvia Chassidus committee
Summary: On 4 Nisan the Rebbe Rayatz sent a series of letters thanking and blessing the new committee in Riga, led by R. Chaim Mordechai Aizik Chodakov, for the spread of Chassidus study.
Story: On 4 Nisan 5690 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a coordinated set of letters: to R. Chaim Mordechai Aizik Chodakov (later his personal secretary) who chaired the Riga committee, to R. Shneur Zalman Yitzchak Wolshonok, to Anash of Riga, and to the General Committee for Expanding Chassidus Study in Latvia. He thanked them for the news that additional batei midrash had opened Chassidus shiurim and proposed that during Chol HaMoed Pesach all of the city's study groups convene in one shul to review a discourse together, strengthen mutual love, and inspire the younger generation.
Tags: latvia, riga, chassidus, rayatz, chodakov, wolshonok, letter

Title: Brandeis writes Israel Thurman about Rebbe's coalition proposal
Summary: Justice Brandeis described the Rebbe's coalition idea and his admiration for him in a letter to Israel Thurman.
Story: 'Rabbi Schneersohn impressed me so much,' Brandeis wrote. David Bressler subsequently attempted to create a joint initiative of the American Jewish Committee, the American Jewish Congress, and the JDC, but the proposal floundered without Brandeis taking a public leadership role.
Tags: brandeis, thurman, soviet-jewry, rayatz

Title: Chodakov reports growing Chassidus shiurim in Riga to Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: R. Chaim Mordechai Aizik Chodakov reported to the Rebbe Rayatz that the Latvia committee had opened new shiurim in synagogues that had not heard Chassidus for years.
Story: Writing on 25 Nisan 5690, Chodakov informed the Rebbe Rayatz that batei midrash which had not heard a Chassidus discourse in living memory now hosted regular shiurim, and that a fresh shiur had just been started in an unexpected beis midrash in Riga. He singled out the contributions of refugee rabbis Israel Zuber, Avraham Eli Asherov, and Yehuda Eber, and especially R. Eli Chaim Althaus, whose enthusiasm and personal commitment to serve as mashpia in one shul made an entire shiur possible.
Tags: latvia, riga, chassidus, chodakov, althaus, zuber, asherov, eber, report

Title: Riga committee meets at Wolshonok's home to plan citywide Chassidus gathering
Summary: Twelve members of the Riga committee met at R. Shneur Zalman Yitzchak Wolshonok's home and resolved to hold a citywide gathering of Chassidus students on Rosh Chodesh Iyar at the Dreyzin shul.
Story: Because the Rebbe Rayatz's instruction to hold the gathering during Chol HaMoed Pesach only reached Riga on the third day of the intermediate days, the committee had to postpone. On 29 Nisan 5690 twelve committee members gathered at R. Wolshonok's home and decided in protocol number 9 to convene the general assembly on Rosh Chodesh Iyar at the middle minyan of the Dreyzin beis midrash.
Tags: latvia, riga, chassidus, wolshonok, dreyzin, meeting, protocol

Title: Citywide farbrengen of Riga Chassidus study groups at Dreyzin shul
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5690 the Riga committee held a large farbrengen of Chassidus study circles at the Dreyzin beis midrash, lasting from 9 pm to 2 am.
Story: Fulfilling the Rebbe Rayatz's proposal, the Riga committee assembled a large gathering of Anash at the middle minyan of the Dreyzin beis midrash for a citywide farbrengen of all the Chassidus study groups. The event ran from 9 pm until 2 am, and Chodakov reported the same day that it would both strengthen existing learners and attract new ones to fixed Chassidus study.
Tags: latvia, riga, chassidus, dreyzin, farbrengen, chodakov

Title: Rebbe Rayatz requests student rosters from Vilna yeshiva
Summary: On 3 Nisan 5690, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the Vilna yeshiva requesting detailed lists of students including names, hometowns, abilities, and class placement.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz wrote asking the Vilna administration to send detailed rosters of all students - names, fathers' names, occupations, hometowns, length of study at the yeshiva, abilities, study habits, class placement, and the committee's plans for each student's upcoming year.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, rebbe rayatz, letter

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes to R' Chaim Ozer Grodzensky on Vilna funding
Summary: On 3 Nisan 5690, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Rabbi Chaim Ozer Grodzensky requesting an increase in the Vaad HaYeshivot subsidy to the Vilna yeshiva from 25 to 50 shekels monthly.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz wrote a warm letter to Rabbi Chaim Ozer Grodzensky thanking him for his support of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim and the Vaad HaYeshivot's monthly subsidy of 25 shekels. He requested that the subsidy be raised to 50 shekels monthly, expressing confidence that Rabbi Chaim Ozer would fulfill this request.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, rabbi chaim ozer grodzensky, vaad hayeshivot, fundraising

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe spends Pesach in Chicago
Summary: On his American tour the Rebbe celebrated Pesach in Chicago, drawing thousands to greet him.
Story: As part of the Rebbe's extensive travel across the United States he visited Chicago for Pesach 5690. In every city he visited, thousands and sometimes over ten thousand Jews came to meet him at the train station. He inspired many families and communities to draw closer to Yiddishkeit.
Tags: rayatz, pesach, chicago, 1929 visit, usa, frierdiker rebbe

Title: Detroit Jewish Chronicle reports arrest of 16 leaders in Minsk
Summary: The paper reports that sixteen Jewish leaders were arrested in Minsk for the counterrevolutionary crime of corresponding with the Rebbe.
Story: The Chronicle reported the leaders 'had been hounded by the secret police for no other reason than being in contact with the Lubavitcher Rebbe.' Communications between the Rebbe and Soviet Jews carried grave personal risk.
Tags: soviet, minsk, arrests, press

Title: Sixteen Jewish leaders arrested in Minsk for corresponding with the Rebbe
Summary: The Detroit Jewish Chronicle reports the arrest of sixteen Jewish leaders in Minsk for the 'counterrevolutionary crime' of corresponding with the Rebbe.
Story: According to the paper, the men 'had been hounded by the secret police for no other reason other than being in contact with the Lubavitcher Rebbe.' The arrests confirmed the very real danger to recipients of the Rebbe's prolific underground correspondence from Riga.
Tags: minsk, russia, soviet, secret police, press

Title: Chadakov writes Rayatz that refugee rabbis are benefiting Riga
Summary: R' Chaim Mordechai Aizik Chadakov wrote the Rebbe describing the benefit Riga drew from rabbis who had arrived from Russia.
Story: On 25 Nisan 5690, R' Chaim Mordechai Aizik Chadakov wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz that the Riga community was benefiting greatly from the rabbis who had come from the valley of weeping (Russia), namely R' Yisrael Zuber, R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov, and now also R' Yehuda Eber.
Tags: chadakov, riga, zuber, ashurov, eber, refugees

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Detroit
Summary: More than ten thousand thronged Michigan Central Station to welcome the Rebbe for a week-long visit.
Story: A police escort conducted the Rebbe to his car, and a procession of more than ten thousand escorted him to Detroit's Emanuel Synagogue. During the visit the Rebbe gave individual audiences and made an unannounced visit to a local Chabad synagogue, where he addressed the Depression and urged congregants not to despair.
Tags: detroit, rayatz, michigan-central, isadore-starr

Title: Rayatz writes letter recalling lifelong passion for collecting books
Summary: Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak (Rayatz) writes in a letter on Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5690 that he has been a collector of books since his youth.
Story: In a letter dated Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5690 (Iggeres 3837), the Rebbe Rayatz reflects on himself, noting that there are those who learn from books, those who read books, and those who collect them — and that he has been a collector since his earliest years. This statement frames a lifelong project of acquiring and preserving Jewish books that paralleled his father Rebbe Rashab's library work in Lubavitch.
Tags: library, rayatz, letters, autobiography

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in St. Louis
Summary: The Rebbe began a ten-day visit to St. Louis, the furthest western city of his American tour.
Story: The Jewish Record reported the crowd was unprecedented in size: 'Such a large crowd consisting of thousands of men, women, and children has never been witnessed at any reception accorded to a Jewish leader visiting our city.' During the visit local women publicly pressed the Rebbe for help building a new mikveh, which he championed.
Tags: st-louis, rayatz, missouri, mikveh

Title: St. Louis mikveh fundraising dinner
Summary: Plans for a new St. Louis mikveh were unveiled at a fundraising dinner held at Congregation B'nai Amoona.
Story: Each attendee received a card with a picture of the Rebbe and a coin he had given for supporters of the mikveh. The Rebbe encouraged the local committee, gave coins to distribute, and remained in contact with the women after returning to Europe.
Tags: st-louis, mikveh, rayatz, women

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe spends Shavuot in the Bronx
Summary: The Rebbe celebrated Shavuot 5690 in the Bronx, praying and delivering a maamar at the East 172nd Street mikveh shul.
Story: On Shavuot the Rebbe prayed in the synagogue attached to the mikveh at 172 East and delivered a maamar. During his US visit he also delivered chassidus on weekdays, including a Tuesday parshat Toldot maamar at Beis Knesses Tzemach Tzedek on Marcy Street in Brooklyn that drew an estimated five thousand people.
Tags: rayatz, shavuot, bronx, new york, 1929 visit, usa, frierdiker rebbe

Title: Rebbe Rayatz returns from America
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz returned to Europe from his trip to the United States in the summer of 5690.
Story: After his historic visit to America, the Rebbe Rayatz returned in the summer of 5690 (1930). Shortly after, the Globoke chassidic community held a special meeting about the rabbinate vacancy and renewed their appeal to him.
Tags: rayatz, usa, travel

Title: Vilna yeshiva confirms $100 stipend from Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: On 4 Tammuz 5690, the Vilna yeshiva administration formally acknowledged receipt of $100 from the Rebbe Rayatz covering the month of Sivan.
Story: Beyond communal donations and the Vaad HaYeshivot subsidy, the Rebbe Rayatz sent a monthly stipend from Riga to support the Vilna yeshiva. The administration's signed receipt for $100 covering Sivan was preserved, demonstrating the ongoing financial lifeline from the Rebbe's office.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, rebbe rayatz, fundraising, riga

Title: Rebbe Rayatz sends $90 Tammuz subsidy to Vilna yeshiva
Summary: On 7 Tammuz 5690, the Rebbe Rayatz sent a check for $90 to Vilna - the regular $100 monthly subsidy minus $10 toward the gemach.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the Vilna yeshiva committee enclosing a check for $90 - the standard monthly $100 stipend, with $10 deducted for the gemach (free-loan fund). This documented one example of the systematic monthly support the Rebbe provided from Riga.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, rebbe rayatz, fundraising, gemach

Title: Rebbe Rayatz meets President Herbert Hoover at the White House
Summary: The Rebbe was received by the US president, accompanied by Rabbis Moshe Kramer, Chaim Fogelman, and Asher Rabinowitz.
Story: The visit was arranged at the last minute. The Rebbe used it to express appreciation for the freedoms granted American Jews and for the US government's assistance to Jews living overseas. The Rashag also thanked the president for his support of Jews in Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: hoover, white-house, washington, rayatz, rashag

Title: Rebbe Rayatz departs the United States
Summary: On 20 Tamuz 5690, the Rebbe sailed for Europe, leaving a crowd at the pier with a new vision for American Jewry.
Story: He proclaimed it was time for American Jews to redefine their role: 'Until this point, you were in the role of givers, supporting Torah institutions in Europe. But now you also have to become takers — adapt the approach of disseminating Jewish learning and strengthening Judaism, and institute it in America. Make America a place of Torah.'
Tags: rayatz, united-states, departure, vision

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe departs America aboard the ship Bremen
Summary: On 21 Tammuz 5690 Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn left the United States after his historic ten-month visit, sailing on the ship Bremen.
Story: Before departure the tmimim gathered at the Rebbe's hotel expecting a farbrengen. The Rebbe prolonged his prayers until 5pm and then delivered over an hour of sharp rebuke. A large crowd including delegations from many cities came to the port to see him off, where the Rebbe addressed them with words of farewell and encouragement.
Tags: rayatz, 1929 visit, usa, frierdiker rebbe, departure, tomchei tmimim, ship bremen

Title: Rayatz departs the United States to return to Europe
Summary: The Rayatz left the United States to return to Europe after his historic American visit.
Story: He set sail on 21 Tamuz 5690, beginning a journey that would take him via Germany to recovery in Marienbad and finally home to Riga. The trip back marked the end of his groundbreaking visit to America, where he had established Agudas Chassidei Chabad's American presence.
Tags: united states, travel, europe

Title: Rayatz arrives in Bremen, Germany
Summary: After leaving New York, the Rayatz arrived in Bremen, Germany.
Story: Bremen, a major German port, served as his entry point back to Europe. From there he traveled to Berlin in time for Tisha B'Av.
Tags: bremen, germany

Title: Rebbe Rayatz's ship docks in Bremen
Summary: On 27 Tamuz 5690, the Rebbe arrived in Bremen, Germany after the transatlantic voyage.
Story: He proceeded to Berlin with his daughter Chaya Mushka and son-in-law the Ramash, then spent three weeks recuperating at the spa town of Marienbad on doctors' orders before continuing home to Riga.
Tags: bremen, germany, rayatz, marienbad

Title: Rebbe arrives in Berlin returning from US trip
Summary: On 1 Menachem Av 5690, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived safely in Berlin on his way back to Riga from his extended trip to the United States.
Story: R. Shmuel Zalmanov reported the arrival to R. Azriel Zelig Slonim, noting that the chassidim were again preparing a formal letter asking the Rebbe to settle in Poland rather than Riga and were hoping he would spend the upcoming High Holidays there.
Tags: berlin, usa, riga

Title: Rayatz spends Tisha B'Av in Berlin
Summary: The Rayatz observed Tisha B'Av in Berlin during his journey back to Riga.
Story: Berlin in 1930 hosted a significant chasidic community, including many émigrés from Russia. The Rayatz's presence for Tisha B'Av brought together local chasidim for a meaningful observance of the fast day.
Tags: berlin, germany, tisha bav

Title: Rebbe declines to come to Warsaw before holiday
Summary: On 28 Menachem Av 5690, the Rebbe wrote to his son-in-law (the future Rebbe) that he could not come to Warsaw before the upcoming Yom Tov.
Story: A second letter on Motzaei Shabbos Re'eh confirmed the same answer to the Warsaw chassidim. Despite repeated invitations and arguments that Riga was not suitable, the Rebbe judged that the timing for relocation had not yet come.
Tags: warsaw, letter, ramash

Title: Agudas Chassidei Chabad founded in Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia
Summary: Twenty-one Chasidim gather at the Rashag's home during the High Holidays and, with the Rebbe's approval, found Agudas Chassidei Chabad.
Story: For the High Holidays of 1930, Chasidim from Poland and Lithuania came to celebrate with the Rebbe in Riga. A group of twenty-one Chasidim convened in the home of the Rashag, who suggested the new organization. With the Rebbe's approval, Agudas Chassidei Chabad took on the mandate of strengthening the Chabad community across the three-country region.
Tags: agudas chassidei chabad, poland, lithuania, latvia, high holidays, rashag

Title: Agudas Chassidei Chabad of Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia founded in Riga
Summary: European Chasidim convened in Riga after Rosh HaShanah 1930 to formally establish Agudas Chassidei Chabad of Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia.
Story: Fearing the Rebbe Rayatz might relocate to the US, Chasidim who had flocked to Riga for the High Holidays met Saturday evening at the Rashag's home. The new organization aimed to unite the Chabad community, reinforce study of chasidic philosophy, and build a financial foundation enabling the Rebbe to relocate to Warsaw. They sent a letter to the Rebbe urging him to settle in Warsaw rather than America.
Tags: riga, poland, lithuania, latvia, agudas-chassidei-chabad, rashag

Title: Bentzion Shemtov weds Esther Golda in Siberian exile
Summary: Shemtov married Esther Golda Futerfus in the small Siberian village of Yanivskiek.
Story: Esther Golda made the long trek from Moscow that summer. Without a mikveh, she immersed in an icy river; without a ring, Shemtov fashioned one from a silver fork. Exiled rabbi Shmuel Levitin officiated. Reb Mendel Futerfus, a legendary underground figure, had suggested the match.
Tags: shemtov, siberia, yanivskiek, exile, wedding

Title: Shemtov marries Esther Golda in Siberian exile
Summary: After three years exile in Siberia, Bentzion Shemtov married his fiancée in a remote village near the Trans-Siberian railroad.
Story: Esther Golda Futerfus made the long trek to Siberia in summer 1930 to join her fiancé. The wedding was held in Yanivskiek, about fifty miles from the railroad; lacking a mikveh, she hacked through an icy river to immerse. With no ring, Shemtov fashioned one from a silver fork, and exiled chasidic rabbi Shmuel Levitin officiated.
Tags: shemtov, siberia, exile, wedding, yanivskiek

Title: Globoke chassidim petition Rebbe to appoint Kuperstock
Summary: Forty-eight Globoke chassidim signed a formal request, dated 14 Elul 5690, appointing delegates to ask the Rebbe to install R. Kuperstock as their rabbi.
Story: On 14 Elul 5690 the chassidic community of Globoke convened and signed a letter to the Rebbe Rayatz, naming three delegates - R. Elyakum Reier, R. Baruch Shalom Tzepeliowitz, and R. Moshe Leib Rothstein - to formally request that R. Menachem Mendel Kuperstock be appointed as their rabbi. The letter expressed satisfaction with his earlier visit and was signed by 48 chassidim with the community's seals.
Tags: globoke, kuperstock, petition, lithuania

Title: Rayatz arrives back in Riga after American journey
Summary: The Rayatz returned to his Riga home on 15 Elul after his American trip and a recuperation stay in Marienbad.
Story: Riga had become his European base following expulsion from the USSR. The arrival concluded his months-long voyage from New York via Bremen, Berlin, and Marienbad.
Tags: riga, latvia

Title: Rebbe Rayatz returns to Riga
Summary: After thirteen months abroad, the Rebbe arrived home to a packed train station of well-wishers.
Story: As soon as the train pulled in, loud 'Baruch haba' calls reverberated through the air. Police created a corridor through the dense crowd to allow the Rebbe's entourage to exit. Chasidim from nearby Poland and Lithuania later flocked to Riga to join him for the High Holidays.
Tags: rayatz, riga, return, homecoming

Title: R. Meir Shlomo Yanovsky writes pre-Rosh Hashanah letter to grandchildren
Summary: Rabbi M.S. Yanovsky and his wife Rachel wrote a Rosh Hashanah blessing letter from Nikolayev to their grandchildren in Riga.
Story: On 24 Elul 5690 (Sept. 17, 1930), Rabbi Meir Shlomo Yanovsky and Rebbetzin Rachel wrote from Nikolayev to their grandchildren — the future Rebbe and Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, and Rebbetzin's brother Yisrael Aryeh Leib. They expressed longing to see them, asked for letters in return, and gave their Rosh Hashanah blessings; this was one of the last letters before Yanovsky's passing three years later.
Tags: yanovsky, nikolayev, letter, rebbetzin chaya mushka, ramash, rashag

Title: Meeting of Anash leaders from Poland, Lithuania and Latvia at Rashag's home
Summary: On Motzaei Shabbos Vayelech, 5 Tishrei 5691, prominent chassidim from Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia gathered at the home of the Rashag in Riga to discuss founding an Agudat Chassidim.
Story: The future Rebbe (Ramash) participated in the meeting. The participants resolved to establish a permanent inter-country committee to support the Rebbe's beis chayeinu, to form an Agudat Chassidim across European countries, and formally to ask the Rebbe to settle in Poland. The minutes were later printed in a 2005 tshura by the Stambler family.
Tags: riga, poland, lithuania, latvia, agudat-chassidim, asifa

Title: Polish, Lithuanian and Latvian Anash send unified letter pleading Rebbe stay
Summary: On 6 Tishrei 5691 the assembled chassidim wrote a formal letter to the Rebbe begging him not to leave them for America and to settle in Poland.
Story: The letter, signed by Anash representatives from Poland, Latvia, Lithuania, and even Russia, had been triggered by rumors that American chassidim were lobbying for the Rebbe's move to the United States. The signatories committed to make all needed preparations to receive him.
Tags: riga, poland, lithuania, latvia, anash, letter

Title: Rebbe endorses Kuperstock as Globoke's Chabad rabbi
Summary: On 8 Tishrei 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a handwritten letter to the Globoke chassidim blessing them and supporting Kuperstock's appointment.
Story: In his handwritten letter of 8 Tishrei 5691 (published in Igros Kodesh vol. 17, letter 275), the Rebbe encouraged the Globoke chassidim who were upholding R. Menachem Mendel Kuperstock's appointment and blessed them with health and abundant livelihood. The letter survives only in part.
Tags: globoke, kuperstock, rayatz-letter

Title: Rebbe rebuffs general rabbi's opposition in Globoke
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz replied on 8 Tishrei 5691 to the general kehilla's rabbi, rejecting his attempts to claim the Chabad rabbinate for his son-in-law.
Story: The general kehilla's rabbi opposed Kuperstock's appointment, wanting to reserve the Chabad rabbinate for his son-in-law. The Rebbe Rayatz, in a letter dated 8 Tishrei 5691 (Igros Kodesh vol. 17, letter 6276), wrote that he had not expected such agitation and stressed that the chassidic community must not surrender its longstanding chazakah over its own rabbinate.
Tags: globoke, rabbinate-dispute, chazaka

Title: Kuperstock accepts the Globoke rabbinate
Summary: On 13 Tishrei 5691 R. Kuperstock wrote to the Rebbe accepting the Globoke rabbinate alongside his Fastov post.
Story: Writing to the Rebbe Rayatz on 13 Tishrei 5691, R. Kuperstock confirmed receipt of the Rebbe's letters and of the formal rabbinic appointment from Globoke. He accepted the role and expressed hope that the disputes around the position would be settled peaceably.
Tags: kuperstock, globoke, fastov, acceptance

Title: Fastov chassidim plead to keep Kuperstock
Summary: Eighteen chassidim of Fastov wrote on 14 Tishrei 5691, asking the Rebbe not to transfer their rabbi to Globoke.
Story: On 14 Tishrei 5691, the chassidim of Fastov sent a signed letter to the Rebbe Rayatz protesting the planned transfer of Kuperstock to Globoke. They asked why their community should be deprived of a rabbi who guided them in the ways of their forebears, given that they too held a longstanding right to his leadership.
Tags: fastov, kuperstock, petition

Title: Rebbe delivers Simchat Torah talk demanding Jewish street outreach
Summary: On Simchat Torah 1930 in Riga, the Rebbe lays out a vision of bold outreach and demands non-observant Jews not stay for dancing.
Story: The Rebbe lamented that Latvia was 'Jewish only in appearance,' tasked Dubin's group with transforming Jewish education, and declared, 'You need to stand on the street corners and pull Jews into a synagogue to study.' He then sternly told those unwilling to put on tefillin to leave before hakafot — a directive later revealed to have foiled a Peretz Communist youth-club plot to disrupt the celebration.
Tags: simchat torah, riga, outreach, tefillin, peretz, achot hatemimim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz reveals Simchat Torah 5691 directive to memorize 12 chapters of Tanya
Summary: On Simchat Torah 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz in Riga disclosed a directive to memorize the first 12 chapters of Tanya including the Hakdama.
Story: A letter from R' Yehuda Eber in Riga reached Vitebsk in the winter of 5691 reporting that on Simchat Torah the Rebbe Rayatz had revealed a 'secret': everyone must memorize the first 12 chapters of Tanya together with the introduction. The directive spread immediately through the underground network, and chassidim and bochurim across Russia began learning Tanya baal peh.
Tags: tanya, simchat-torah, riga, rayatz, yehuda-eber, memorization, soviet-russia

Title: Simchat Torah 5691 sicha and 'Pratz Klub' disruption attempt
Summary: At the Simchat Torah 5691 gathering the Rebbe delivered sharp words to a crowd that included secularists, while members of the 'Pratz Klub' attempted to sabotage the meeting.
Story: The printed sicha records the Rebbe's pointed remarks to the assembled, some of whom were freethinkers. During the gathering the electric lights were briefly extinguished and reignited; the disruptors had actually intended to cut the electric wires. The Rebbe later remarked that at the moment of speaking he did not understand what was forcing the content out of him.
Tags: rayatz, simchat torah, pratz klub, anti-religious, feigin, riga, 1930

Title: Simchat Torah 1930 — Rebbe's stern address foils Peretz disruption
Summary: The Rebbe demands those not observing basics of tradition leave; only later it is revealed the Peretz Communist youth had infiltrated to disrupt the dancing.
Story: On this Simchat Torah, the Rebbe also founded Agudas Chassidei Chabad of Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia, criticized Latvian Jewry as 'Jewish only in appearance,' and called on Chasidim to 'stand on the street corners and pull Jews into a synagogue to study' — the seed of public outreach that would later define Chabad.
Tags: simchat-torah, riga, peretz, outreach, communist-youth

Title: R. Yechezkel Feigin tells Rebbe about 'Pratz Klub' plot
Summary: On Friday 25 Tishrei 5691 R. Yechezkel Feigin entered the Rebbe to disclose that the 'Pratz Klub' had come with malicious intent at the Simchat Torah gathering.
Story: Feigin had initially withheld the information about the disruption attempt and the planned cutting of the electric wires. When he finally told the Rebbe, the Rebbe responded that now he understood what had compelled him to deliver the pointed words he had spoken at the gathering.
Tags: yechezkel feigin, pratz klub, rayatz, anti-religious, 1930, riga

Title: Feigin reveals Peretz plot to Rebbe two days after Simchat Torah
Summary: Rabbi Feigin informs the Rebbe that Peretz infiltrators had planned to cut electricity and break up the hakafot.
Story: When the Rebbe heard the details, he said, 'Now I know that I was justified in speaking that way, though at the time I did not know what pushed me to say it.' The story was preserved in Feigin's letter to Jacobson.
Tags: peretz, feigin, communist-youth, letter, riga

Title: Feigin writes Jacobson revealing Peretz plot against Simchat Torah
Summary: Rabbi Feigin writes to Rabbi Jacobson in the US explaining how the Rebbe's harsh Simchat Torah words foiled a Communist youth-club plot.
Story: Feigin disclosed that members of the local left-wing Peretz youth club had infiltrated the crowd intending to cut the electricity and violently break up the hakafot. 'When the Peretz leaders heard the Rebbe's strident words, they instructed their followers to leave.' When Feigin later informed the Rebbe, he replied, 'Now I know that I was justified in speaking that way.'
Tags: peretz, simchat torah, riga, feigin, jacobson, communist

Title: Violent opposition forces Kuperstock back to Fastov
Summary: On 28 Tishrei 5691 Kuperstock reported to the Rebbe that hostile crowds in Globoke's Lubavitcher and Starasele shuls forced him to flee the town at night.
Story: Kuperstock had traveled to Globoke for Shabbos Bereishis but encountered intense opposition. Youths jeered him in the Lubavitcher shul after Torah reading, and rowdies brandished their fists at him when he tried to speak in the Starasele shul. By nightfall a coalition demanded he leave the town that very night. He wrote to the Rebbe on 28 Tishrei 5691 describing the events, thankful that he had escaped with his life.
Tags: globoke, kuperstock, violence, starasele-shul, lubavitcher-shul

Title: Rayatz announces plan to establish a Torah study circle in Riga
Summary: The Rebbe wrote R' Yehuda Leib Nimoitin announcing his decision to establish a select Torah study circle in Riga.
Story: On 2 Cheshvan 5691, soon after returning to Riga from America, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Yehuda Leib Nimoitin announcing his decision to establish a Torah study circle in Riga for outstanding students of Torah and yiras shamayim. He wished to gather ten select students who would devote themselves wholly to Torah study according to set conditions.
Tags: riga, tomchei tmimim, study circle, nimoitin

Title: Maharayatz to Kollel Chabad: a dedicated staffer for the kollel is essential
Summary: On 7 Cheshvan 5691 Maharayatz wrote to the Kollel Chabad leadership that a dedicated staff person, even part-time, was indispensable to handling its affairs.
Story: After returning from his year-long trip to America, the Rebbe redoubled his involvement in kollel matters, sending shadarim and writing extensively to town gabbaim across Eastern Europe. His letter to the leadership argued that the cost of a dedicated staffer would itself be 'income, not expense', because of how much fundraising and administration it would unlock. The letter is part of an intense burst of administrative reorganization spanning 5690–5691.
Tags: kollel chabad, maharayatz, administration

Title: Rayatz establishes Shulchan HaNesius over Kollel Chabad
Summary: On 7 Marcheshvan 5691 the Rayatz issued letters formalizing the Shulchan HaNesius committee to oversee Kollel Chabad alongside the existing Va'ad HaMoetza.
Story: Having previously appointed R' Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezrov as his personal representative when he accepted the kollel's presidency, the Rayatz now created a Shulchan HaNesius to ensure direct supervision of the kollel's affairs. The committee included rabbis Eliezrov, Menachem Mendel Naeh, Chaim Kam, Yisrael Asher Liba, and Mordechai Reuven Rokeach. Its regulations were sent in a separate document no longer extant.
Tags: rayatz, kollel chabad, shulchan hanesius, eliezrov, jerusalem

Title: Rayatz announces R' Ashurov's appointment as Rosh Yeshiva in Warsaw
Summary: In his general letter of 19 Cheshvan 5691, the Rebbe announced R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov's appointment as Rosh Yeshiva in Warsaw.
Story: On 19 Cheshvan 5691, in a general letter, the Rebbe Rayatz announced that he was sending R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov, described as a great Torah scholar of exceptional talent, to serve as Rosh Yeshiva in one of the divisions of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw. However, this plan was apparently never carried out, as Ashurov remained in Riga.
Tags: ashurov, warsaw, tomchei tmimim, rosh yeshiva, poland

Title: Rebbe Rayatz appoints Yehuda Eber as spiritual director of Tomchei Tmimim Vilna
Summary: On 19 Marcheshvan 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz sent Yehuda Eber — a Tomchei Tmimim director recently extracted from Soviet Russia — to lead the Vilna branch.
Story: Eber, brother of the well-known R' Eliyahu of Krasnoluki, had himself been a senior figure inside the Soviet Tomchei Tmimim network before escaping with his family. The Rayatz's letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. 2, letter 498) introduces him to the Vilna leadership as a great talmid chacham and gifted young man. He served in Vilna until 5693, when he was reassigned as spiritual director of the central yeshiva in Warsaw.
Tags: rayatz, yehuda eber, tomchei tmimim, vilna, russia

Title: Rebbe Rayatz declines move to America, decides to remain in Europe
Summary: In a letter dated 18 Cheshvan 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz informed US Chasidim he would remain in Europe due to spiritual needs and his health.
Story: After his US visit had raised hopes of relocation, the Rebbe wrote his American Chasidim explaining that European communal duties, the yeshivas, and weakness of health made a move premature. Quoting the talmudic principle of not demolishing one synagogue before building another, he implied that leaving Europe would weaken Chabad's work there. He left the door open to a future move with proper preparation.
Tags: america, europe, warsaw, tomchei-temimim, depression

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes to Łódź students about study reports
Summary: On 19 Cheshvan 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the talmidim of Warsaw, Vilna and Łódź expressing pleasure at their study reports.
Story: In a letter dated 19 Cheshvan 5691 (Igros Kodesh vol. 2, no. 498), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the talmidim of Tomchei Tmimim that he had taken great pleasure reading the lectures and study reports from Warsaw, Vilna and Łódź. The letter is the earliest extant reference to the Łódź branch in the Rebbe's correspondence. It documents the regular reporting system maintained between the branches and the Rebbe during his stay in Riga.
Tags: poland, lodz, warsaw, vilna, tomchei-tmimim, rebbe-correspondence

Title: Rebbe writes that he will not settle permanently in America
Summary: In a letter dated 18 Cheshvan 5691 the Rebbe informed anash that he did not plan to immigrate permanently to the United States.
Story: Despite the vaad's efforts to bring him to settle in America, the Rebbe wrote that this was not his intention.
