He later explained to the author in Elul 5699 that the manner of his American visit had been that of a public askan, an area in which he had skill and success but which was not his true work — his work was chassidim and chassidus.
Tags: rayatz, settlement, usa, 1930, letter, vaad

Title: R' Shmuel Zalmanov sends Rayatz overview of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw
Summary: R' Shmuel Zalmanov sent the Rebbe a detailed status report on Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw at the start of the new term.
Story: On 20 Cheshvan 5691, R' Shmuel Zalmanov wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz with a general overview of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw at the start of the new term. He reported 29 new students admitted and 110 students in total studying across three divisions, detailing who was teaching nigleh and chassidus in each class and stressing the continuing need for an inner mashpia.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, shmuel zalmanov, poland, enrollment

Title: Rebbe Rayatz appoints R' Yehuda Eber Rosh Yeshiva in Vilna
Summary: On 19 Marcheshvan 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the Vilna administration appointing R' Yehuda Eber as new Rosh Yeshiva.
Story: Having rescued R' Yehuda Eber from Russia to Riga, the Rebbe Rayatz sent him to head the Vilna yeshiva. In his letter introducing the appointment, the Rebbe described R' Eber as one of the directors of Tomchei Tmimim in Russia, an outstanding talmid chacham of exceptional talent, still young in years.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, rebbe rayatz, rabbi yehuda eber, russia, rescue

Title: Chatzkevich leads Lithuanian delegation to the Rebbe
Summary: In Kislev 5691, R. Chatzkevich headed a delegation of Lithuanian chassidim asking the Rebbe Rayatz to visit Lithuania.
Story: In Kislev 5691 (late 1930), as recorded by the Rebbe's secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin (Sefer HaMaamarim Kuntreisim vol. 1, p. 153a), the chassidim of Lithuania sent a delegation to the Rebbe. R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich of Kupishok headed the group, which formally renewed the request that the Rebbe visit anash in Lithuania and fix a date for the trip.
Tags: chatzkevich, kupishok, lithuania, rebbe-visit, feigin

Title: Rayatz writes Nimoitin that Riga study circle plan still not realized
Summary: The Rebbe wrote Nimoitin that his desire to raise the level of Torah study had still not been realized.
Story: On 14 Kislev 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote again to R' Yehuda Leib Nimoitin, noting that his wish for the good of the students and for raising the level of Torah knowledge had still not come to fruition. The plan to establish a Riga study circle was still encountering difficulties.
Tags: riga, nimoitin, study circle

Title: R' Yehuda Eber sends detailed report to Rebbe on Vilna students
Summary: On Motzaei Shabbos Vayishlach 16 Kislev 5691, R' Yehuda Eber wrote a comprehensive report to the Rebbe Rayatz after examining all students in Vilna.
Story: After his arrival as Rosh Yeshiva, R' Yehuda Eber individually examined every student and sent the Rebbe a detailed roster covering each student's abilities, diligence, and yiras shamayim. He noted that R' Yaakov Hochman, the mashpia, was dedicated to the students' conduct but had not been examining their progress; new procedures were instituted.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, rabbi yehuda eber, rabbi yaakov hochman, report

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe delivers 19 Kislev 5691 maamar on divine influx
Summary: On 19 Kislev 5691 the Rebbe delivered a maamar teaching that divine influence to the souls of Israel flows from the Name Havayah by way of overriding nature.
Story: R. Yechezkel Feigin reported the content of the maamar to the author in a letter from Kislev 5691. The Rebbe taught that the spiritual influence to neshamot Yisrael is drawn from the name Havayah via meavir ha-teva — overriding the natural order.
Tags: rayatz, yud tes kislev, maamar, feigin, 1930, name havayah

Title: Rabbi Teitz of Livenhof requests teacher for the youth
Summary: The Rebbe wrote on 6 Tevet 5691 considering sending Yaakov Landa to Livenhof to teach the local Tiferes Bachurim youth.
Story: In winter 5691 Rabbi Avraham Binyamin Teitz of Livenhof asked the Frierdiker Rebbe to send a teacher for the town's young men. The Rebbe wrote to Yaakov Landa on 6 Tevet 5691 (Igrot vol. 2, no. 516) saying that Livenhof was unusual: even the local balebatim wanted to study, and Rabbi Teitz, while distinguished, was not an outgoing public figure.
Tags: livenhof, livani, latvia, yaakov-landa, tiferes-bachurim, avraham-binyamin-teitz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz plans tour of Latvian towns
Summary: On 6 Tevet 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote that he hoped to visit several places in Latvia and was seeking funds to cover the travel.
Story: In a letter dated 6 Tevet 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz revealed that the idea of personally visiting a number of Latvian communities had occurred to him, and that he was taking on the considerable burden of finding a source to cover the travel expenses. His stated intention was to learn first-hand what was happening in those places and to see whether direct encouragement might accomplish something.
Tags: latvia, rayatz, travel, outreach, letter

Title: Arrest of R' Eliyahu Far, shochet Tzvi Zarchi, and Vitebsk Zal bochurim
Summary: Around the closure of the Vitebsk yeshiva, the GPU arrested the senior Zal bochurim and chassidim R' Eliyahu Far and shochet Tzvi Zarchi.
Story: In Zarutchei the GPU arrested the older bochurim of the Zal, including Michael Teitelbaum, Herzl Minkowitz, and Avraham Aharon Chen. Soon after, they took the chassid R' Eliyahu Far and the shochet R' Tzvi Zarchi, father of Meir Zarchi. Most of the remaining rabbis and prominent chassidim fled, leaving only the suspected collaborator Goldberg as the Russian rav.
Tags: vitebsk, gpu, eliyahu-far, tzvi-zarchi, michael-teitelbaum, soviet-repression, zarutchei

Title: Earliest extant Naeh booklet calendar (5692)
Summary: The oldest surviving copy of R. A.C. Naeh's annual calendar of customs is the 5692 booklet edition.
Story: Before Kollel Chabad began publishing R. Naeh's calendar, he printed it himself as a booklet sent to overseas supporters. The library's earliest preserved copy is titled 'Luach for the year 5692 with the laws and customs of the year, by Rabbi Avraham Chaim Naeh, Jerusalem,' carrying his New Year greeting to donors.
Tags: jerusalem, minhagim, avraham chaim naeh, booklet

Title: GPU closes Vitebsk Tomchei Tmimim before Purim 5691
Summary: Before Purim 5691 the GPU raided the Vitebsk yeshiva, identifying students by their long thin Lubavitcher tzitzit and round yarmulkes.
Story: Soviet agents entered the Kleiner Zeit shul where the bochurim were learning and arrested them along with two adult Jews present. A GPU investigator examined the prisoners' headcoverings and tzitzit: the older balei-batim whose flat yarmulkes and short, thick tzitzit looked different were released, while the boys with round yarmulkes and long thin tzitzit were identified as Lubavitchers. They were released that night but the yeshiva had effectively been broken.
Tags: vitebsk, tomchei-tmimim, gpu, soviet-repression, tzitzit, yarmulke, kleiner-zeit

Title: GPU misreads coded letter on Vitebsk visa list for 15 bochurim
Summary: A coded letter from R' Yehuda Eber requesting Riga visas for 15 bochurim was deciphered by the GPU after an elderly chassid explained the abbreviation.
Story: Shortly before Purim 5691 the Vitebsk hanhala received word from R' Yehuda Eber that visas were being arranged in Riga for 15 bochurim, with the message written in tiny letters as '15 ס.' to disguise the request. The hanhala understood that 'ס' stood for 'simanim' meaning bochurim, but when the GPU showed the letter to imprisoned balei-batim and an elderly chassid foolishly explained the code, the gentile investigator triumphantly identified the plot. The chassidim involved were held in prison for a long time.
Tags: vitebsk, riga, yehuda-eber, gpu, visas, emigration, soviet-repression

Title: Mandelbaum sent to Krakow to teach chassidus
Summary: In the summer of 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz dispatched R. Yitzchak Mandelbaum to Krakow to deliver chassidus shiurim and try to open a Tomchei Tmimim branch.
Story: In summer 5691 (1931), R. Yitzchak Mandelbaum, a Tomchei Tmimim student in Warsaw, was sent by the Rebbe to Krakow for a period to deliver chassidic discourses. He also attempted to open a branch of Tomchei Tmimim in his own town of Matzayov, though that effort did not materialize.
Tags: mandelbaum, krakow, chassidus, tomchei-tmimim, matzayov

Title: Plan to transfer Warsaw 'olam' students to Riga falls through
Summary: In summer 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz planned to transfer senior Warsaw yeshiva students to Riga; the plan did not come to fruition.
Story: In summer 5691 (1931) a plan was developed to move the advanced students of the Warsaw 'olam' to Riga, where the Rebbe Rayatz was then residing. R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie was among those selected for the move. When the plan ultimately failed, the Rebbe instead dispatched Gurarie to a number of towns in Volyn to attempt opening branches of Tomchei Tmimim there.
Tags: warsaw, riga, tomchei-tmimim, shneur-zalman-gurarie, transfer

Title: Połaniec branch of Tomchei Tmimim founded
Summary: The Połaniec (Potshanov) branch of Tomchei Tmimim was founded at the start of 5692 with about 25 students.
Story: At the start of 5692 (fall 1931), at the urging of the Rebbe Rayatz, a small yeshiva was opened in Połaniec as a branch of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw. Beginning with about twenty-five students, the yeshiva grew to over sixty boys divided into five divisions, under the leadership of R. Moshe Aharon Morgel. He taught Gemara and some chassidus to the upper division, with public chassidus shiurim several times a week.
Tags: poland, potshanov, polaniec, tomchei-tmimim, moshe-aharon-morgel, yeshiva-branch

Title: R' Yitzchak Mandelbaum sent on summer mission to Krakow
Summary: In summer 5691 the Rebbe dispatched R' Yitzchak Mandelbaum to Krakow for an extended outreach visit to local bochurim.
Story: Mandelbaum spent time in Krakow connecting with young men and exchanging letters with them. On returning he debriefed the Rebbe, who on 15 Menachem Av asked for fuller particulars — names, addresses, and any continuing correspondence — to follow up on these contacts.
Tags: poland, krakow, tomchei temimim, yitzchak mandelbaum

Title: R. Yechiel Meir Blumenfeld publishes Kol HaMitzvah
Summary: R. Yechiel Meir Blumenfeld, a founder of the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim, printed his sefer Kol HaMitzvah in Warsaw in 5691.
Story: Blumenfeld had been born in 5653 (1893). He combined his role as a Mizrachi rav at Tachkemoni with continued support for Chabad institutions in Warsaw. He would later be murdered in the Warsaw Ghetto on Yom Kippur 5703.
Tags: warsaw, blumenfeld, halacha, sefer

Title: R. Yehuda Eber appointed rosh yeshiva in Warsaw
Summary: At the start of 5692, the Rebbe Rayatz appointed R. Yehuda Eber to head the Warsaw yeshiva and organize Tanya shiurim across the city.
Story: Early in 5692 (autumn 1931) the Rebbe Rayatz appointed R. Yehuda Eber rosh yeshiva of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw. Together with the position came the assignment to organize Tanya classes in batei midrash across the city, a task R. Yehuda delegated in part to a young avreich named Moshe Chaim.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, yehuda eber, rosh yeshiva, tanya shiurim

Title: R. Yitzchok Aryeh Mandelbaum sent to head Łódź yeshiva
Summary: At the start of 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz sent R. Yitzchok Aryeh Mandelbaum to lead the Łódź yeshiva.
Story: Early in 5692 (autumn 1931), the Rebbe Rayatz dispatched R. Yitzchok Aryeh Mandelbaum to Łódź to head the yeshiva. He arrived on the night of Sunday of Parshas Noach and immediately set about examining and organizing students into divisions. Although officially appointed only as ram, the burden of administration also fell on his shoulders since the Schneersohn brothers were occupied with their business.
Tags: poland, lodz, yitzchok-aryeh-mandelbaum, tomchei-tmimim, appointment

Title: R. Yochanan Gordon immigrates to America from Dokshitz
Summary: In 5692 the tamim R. Yochanan Gordon, shochet of Dokshitz, immigrated to America with his family including sons Nissan and Sholom Dovber.
Story: On arrival R. Yochanan replaced his sons' Russian-style caps with American hats. When Sholom Dovber was embarrassed to enter the author's home wearing the new hat during Chol Hamoed Pesach, the author explained how garments of honor change with time and place, citing teachings from both the Rebbe Rashab and the Rebbe Rayatz on the matter.
Tags: yochanan gordon, shochet, dokshitz, immigration, brooklyn, achei tmimim, hat, clothing

Title: Rabbi Yosef Goldstein opens yeshivah in Chmielnik
Summary: At a 1931 Riga farbrengen the Rebbe charged newly married Yosef Goldstein to open a yeshivah in Chmielnik in southern Poland.
Story: Goldstein, twenty-four, was startled when the Rebbe placed a hand on his shoulder and assigned him the mission. With friends including Rabbi Mottel Bryski, he founded a yeshivah that grew to over seventy students and spawned an elementary program. Chaim Meir Bukiet enrolled there at age eleven, transferring later to Warsaw and Otwock.
Tags: chmielnik, poland, goldstein, bryski, bukiet

Title: Rebbe addresses women's gathering in Rokiškis, Lithuania
Summary: A large group of women requests the Rebbe speak to them — an unprecedented event in chasidic history.
Story: Historically chasidic Rebbes only addressed men publicly. In the same visit, the Rebbe lamented declining scholarship, criticized modern integrated schools, and praised the 'old-style cheder' while supporting Tze'irei Agudath Israel as a practical compromise.
Tags: women, rokiskis, lithuania, chasidic-philosophy

Title: Rebbe dispatches Zalman Gurary to open yeshivah in Volhynia
Summary: In 1931 the Rebbe sent the nineteen-year-old Rabbi Zalman Gurary to Volhynia to strengthen Torah study and open a yeshivah.
Story: Locals laughed at Gurary, telling him Novardok had already failed there. The Rebbe had written ahead introducing his "outstanding student" to local Chasidim and synagogues. Gurary persevered, overcoming initial skepticism by emphasizing the goal of educating local students. The success reflected the Rebbe's broader strategy of empowering students as spiritual entrepreneurs.
Tags: volhynia, poland, gurary, novardok

Title: Rebbe Rayatz orders Polish yeshivot alumni list
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz directed the preparation of an alumni list of the yeshivot in Poland in 5691.
Story: In 5691 (1930-1931), the Rebbe Rayatz directed the preparation of a list of graduates of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshivot in Poland. Unlike the earlier lists, this one was apparently not intended for publication and remained an internal record.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, alumni list, poland

Title: Rebbe visits Rokiškis and addresses gathering of women
Summary: A large group of women requests that the Rebbe speak for them during his visit to Rokiškis, Lithuania — historically unprecedented for a chasidic Rebbe.
Story: Rabbi Feigin recorded that 'in the wake of the request, the Rebbe spoke to a gathering of women.' Historically, chasidic Rebbes only addressed men in public; the Rokiškis talk was a deliberate step toward empowering women in Chabad. The same year, the Rebbe lamented the lowered standards of Jewish scholarship in modern integrated schools.
Tags: rokiskis, lithuania, women, achot hatemimim, chasidut

Title: Schneur Gutnick passes away in London
Summary: Rabbi Schneur Gutnick, rabbi of the London Chabad synagogue, passed away in 1931, leaving his eleven-year-old son Chaim an orphan.
Story: Rabbi Yechezkel Abramsky took an interest in the young Chaim Gutnick after his father's death and encouraged his attendance at Telz Yeshiva in Poland. Chaim would later emerge as one of Australia's most influential rabbis.
Tags: schneur gutnick, chaim gutnick, london, england

Title: Soviet famine of 1931–33 begins
Summary: Severe famine engulfed the Soviet Union, prompted by unsuccessful farm collectivization.
Story: Despite the famine's severity, JDC chair Felix Warburg dismissed the Rebbe's appeal to send matzah to Russian Jews in 1932, insisting they had access to flour. His stance reflected misconceptions formed during his staged 1927 visit to the Jewish farm colonies.
Tags: soviet-union, famine, collectivization, stalin

Title: Soviet secret police close Tomchei Tmimim in Vitebsk
Summary: In late winter 5691 the Soviet secret police shut down the underground Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Vitebsk, forcing a group of students to flee to Georgia.
Story: A group including R. Moshe Rubinson, Abraham Kvash, Yosef Goldberg, Michael Rapaport and others escaped to Kutaisi in Georgia, where they continued studying until winter 5693. A subsequent crackdown in Georgia, framed as a border-crossing case, scattered the group again.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, vitebsk, ussr, bolshevik, georgia, kutaisi

Title: Tmimim begin chassidus shiurim that seed Achei Tmimim
Summary: At the start of 5692 the tmimim Avraham M.M. Baranetzki, Yitzchak Kalodny, and Tzvi Schechter began joining the author's chassidus shiurim for yeshiva students.
Story: The three initially found the lessons difficult and came only to socialize, but after a few weeks of informal gatherings they returned to the formal Tanya study. They were later joined by Mordechai Altein, Yitzchak Matashin, Mordechai Fischer, and Zerach Gordon, laying the foundation for the Achei Tmimim organization.
Tags: achei tmimim, tomchei tmimim, shiurim, chassidus, brooklyn, baranetzki, kalodny, schechter, tanya

Title: Yisrael Yehuda Levin in Pereyaslav after fleeing Vitebsk
Summary: After fleeing Vitebsk, Yisrael Yehuda Levin spent time in Pereyaslav and befriended the town rabbi, Yehoshua Zelig Diskin.
Story: In 5691 (1931), after escaping from Vitebsk, the author settled for a time in Pereyaslav. There he became close with the rav demata, Rabbi Yehoshua Zelig Diskin, a great scholar of noble character, with whom he later corresponded. Rabbi Diskin wrote on his behalf to Chief Rabbi Avraham Yitzchok Kook in Eretz Yisrael, helping to set in motion paperwork for emigration to the Holy Land.
Tags: pereyaslav, vitebsk, yehoshua-zelig-diskin, rav-kook, eretz-yisrael, soviet-russia

Title: Library cataloging effort under way in Riga
Summary: On 29 Tevet 5691 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote that work on cataloging the Wiener-based library was ongoing and a full catalogue was expected within a month.
Story: Although the Wiener collection had been at the Rebbe's disposal since 1924, no comprehensive list yet existed because the books had been arriving in bundles. In Tevet 5691 the Rebbe wrote that they were finally organizing the holdings and anticipated completing a catalogue within roughly a month, which he hoped to share with correspondents.
Tags: riga, library, rayatz, shmuel-wiener, cataloging

Title: Rebbe launches food-package operation to Soviet Jews
Summary: In a January 1931 letter to Peter Wiernik, the Rebbe outlined a covert plan to send food and clothing packages to Soviet Jews as if from relatives.
Story: Observant Jews who would not work on Shabbat were denied ration cards, and the Soviet famine of 1932-33 deepened the crisis. The Rebbe organized a global network of "relatives" sending packages from Europe, the US, and beyond. The Rashag coordinated, contacting Jewish leaders as far as Cape Town and Paris. The campaign operated covertly to avoid Soviet interference.
Tags: soviet-union, russia, food-packages, famine, wiernik, rashag

Title: New executive committee elected at Anash gathering in Warsaw
Summary: A general meeting of Anash in Warsaw elected an expanded executive committee for Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: Following a general meeting of Anash held on Motzaei Shabbos Shemos and continued on Motzaei Shabbos Vaera, an expanded executive committee was elected to manage Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw. The committee was reported in a letter dated 2 Shevat 5691 to the Rebbe's son-in-law Rashag, who had been placed in charge of the yeshiva's treasury. Members included R' Mendel Rotstein as honorary chairman and R' Shraga Feivish Zalmanov as chairman.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, poland, anash, vaad, rashag

Title: Agudas Nashim women's society founded in Rakishok
Summary: During his Rakishok visit, the Rebbe Rayatz founded an Agudas Nashim society dedicated to family purity.
Story: On the evening following his arrival, the Rebbe convened a gathering of men and women in Rakishok and spoke about taharas hamishpacha. At that assembly an Agudas Nashim society was founded with a registry book opened with a blessing and signature from the Rebbe himself.
Tags: rakishok, lithuania, women, taharas hamishpacha, agudas nashim

Title: Hanhalla warns Rayatz of severe budget crisis at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw
Summary: The yeshiva's management warned the Rebbe of a severe financial crisis threatening the institution.
Story: On 22 Shevat 5691, the management of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw wrote a desperate letter to the Rebbe Rayatz describing the yeshiva's dire financial condition. The Great Depression had cut income from America, and they considered shrinking the institution by reducing students and staff. They requested guidance and that the Rebbe telegraph New York for emergency support.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, budget, great depression, poland

Title: Rayatz visits Rakshik in Lithuania
Summary: The Rayatz traveled to Rakshik, Lithuania, for nine days to receive local Chasidim.
Story: Many Chasidim in the region could not travel to Riga, so the Rayatz brought himself to them. The visit from 1 Adar to 9 Adar gave Lithuanian Chabad communities a rare opportunity to meet the Rebbe.
Tags: rakshik, lithuania, chasidim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz visits Rakishok in Lithuania
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz visited Rakishok from Rosh Chodesh Adar to 9 Adar 5691, meeting Anash from throughout Lithuania.
Story: After the Lithuanian chassidim sent delegations led by Rabbi Yisrael Noach of Kupishok requesting a visit, the Rebbe traveled to Rakishok for nine days. He received hundreds for yechidus until late at night, addressed yeshiva students from Telz and Ponevezh, met with Yavneh school representatives and Tiferes Bachurim leaders, and delivered several maamarim including 'V'habriach Hatichon' and 'Atah Echad'.
Tags: rakishok, rokiskis, lithuania, rayatz, yechidus

Title: Rebbe founds Agudas Nashim in Rakshik
Summary: During Adar 5691, on his visit to Rakshik, the Rebbe founded a women's organization for strengthening taharas hamishpacha.
Story: A pinkas was opened recording the founding members, with a handwritten introduction and blessing by the Rebbe at its front. The Rebbe wrote that 'every city and settlement where the women establish such an Agudas Nashim - whether by this name or another - whose aim is strengthening taharas hamishpacha, may they, their husbands and offspring be included in the blessing stated here.'
Tags: rayatz, rakshik, agudas-nashim, taharas-hamishpacha, women

Title: Rayatz decides to transfer Warsaw advanced students to Riga
Summary: The Rebbe wrote the Warsaw hanhalla announcing his decision to bring the advanced Ulam students to Riga.
Story: In response to the hanhalla's questions in late Nisan 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz informed Warsaw that he had decided to establish the main Tomchei Tmimim near his residence in Riga. Around 30-35 advanced 'Ulam' students from Warsaw would be selected to move there, while the Warsaw branch would continue only as a preparatory mechina. R' Yehuda Eber was being dispatched to examine and select students.
Tags: warsaw, riga, tomchei tmimim, transfer, poland

Title: Vitebsk chassidic prisoners fast nine days through Pesach 5691
Summary: The arrested Vitebsk chassidim, including R' Eliyahu Far's daughter, fasted nine days through Pesach 5691 rather than eat chametz.
Story: All the imprisoned Vitebsk chassidim, including the daughter of R' Eliyahu Far who later became the wife of R' Michael Lipsker, refused to eat chametz in their cells during Pesach. For nine days they subsisted on a single piece of sugar daily rather than violate the holiday, even as the rest of the Vitebsk yeshiva infrastructure collapsed around them.
Tags: vitebsk, pesach, fasting, chametz, eliyahu-far, michael-lipsker, soviet-repression

Title: Visa effort to bring Rebbe's family to Poland
Summary: On 13 Nissan 5691, R. Shmuel Zalmanov reported that Polish Anash were actively working to obtain visas for the Rebbe's family.
Story: Although no firm decision had yet been made about the move, the chassidim believed that once visas were secured the Rebbe would accept their request. The letter was sent to R. Azriel Zelig Slonim in Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: poland, riga, visas, letter

Title: Warsaw hanhalla again asks Rayatz for direction on reorganization
Summary: The Warsaw management asked the Rebbe how to organize the yeshiva for the coming summer term amid financial uncertainty.
Story: On 26 Nisan 5691, the management of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw again wrote to the Rebbe, awaiting direction on how to arrange the yeshiva for the coming summer term. The financial crisis left them uncertain how to proceed and they urgently sought the Rebbe's guidance.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, poland, reorganization

Title: Yeshiva administration asks Rebbe to appoint R. Yehuda Eber as Rosh Yeshiva in Warsaw
Summary: Members of the Warsaw yeshiva administration wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz asking that R. Yehuda Eber be appointed as mashgiach and rosh yeshiva for nigleh.
Story: On 26 Nisan 5691, the leadership of Tomchei Temimim in Warsaw petitioned the Rebbe Rayatz to bring R. Yehuda Eber on as a leader of the nigleh studies. They believed he would greatly benefit the depth and quality of Talmud study at the yeshiva.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei temimim, yehuda eber, poland

Title: R' Yehuda Eber arrives in Warsaw to examine yeshiva students
Summary: R' Yehuda Eber arrived in Warsaw to examine students for possible transfer to Riga.
Story: On Monday 2 Iyar 5691, R' Yehuda Eber arrived in Warsaw, sent by the Rebbe Rayatz from Riga to examine the students of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw and select those suitable for transfer to a new Ulam being opened in Riga. He immediately began by testing the younger students.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, eber, examinations, poland

Title: R' Eber sends Rayatz first report on Warsaw student examinations
Summary: R' Eber wrote to the Rebbe with detailed lists of students he had examined so far.
Story: On 10 Iyar 5691, R' Yehuda Eber reported to the Rebbe Rayatz on his progress examining students at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw. He had finished testing the younger students in the shiurim taught by R' Naftali and R' Dovid, and had begun examining the older students of the 'Kibbutz' (advanced division), enclosing a detailed list.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, eber, examinations

Title: R' Eber finishes examining Warsaw students and reports to Rayatz
Summary: R' Eber finished examining all Warsaw students and sent the Rebbe a detailed analysis of the planned Riga transfer.
Story: On 13 Iyar 5691, R' Yehuda Eber reported to the Rebbe that he had examined all the students currently in Warsaw and that about 20 would be suitable to transfer to Riga. He recorded his disagreement with the hanhalla's plan to close the lower preparatory class, arguing that new students typically join the younger classes and that chassidic families in the area especially wished their sons to learn at Tomchei Tmimim.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, eber, examinations, riga, transfer

Title: R' Yehuda Eber reports Warsaw yeshiva mashpia shortage to Rebbe
Summary: R' Yehuda Eber wrote on 13 Iyar 5691 that no truly suitable senior mashpia had filled R' Alter's place at Warsaw Tomchei Temimim since his departure.
Story: On 13 Iyar 5691, R' Yehuda Eber reported to the Rebbe Rayatz that the chief weakness at the Warsaw yeshiva, since R' Alter Simchowitz's return to Jerusalem, was the absence of capable senior staff. R' Zalman Shmotkin studied with the students and supervised them, but his other responsibilities prevented him from giving the role the full devotion it required.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-temimim, yehuda-eber, zalman-shmotkin, alter-simchowitz

Title: R' Yehuda Eber's spring report on Warsaw yeshiva staff
Summary: On 13 Iyar 5691 R' Yehuda Eber sent the Rebbe a written assessment of the Warsaw yeshiva's teachers and supervisors.
Story: On 13 Iyar 5691 (30 April 1931) R' Yehuda Eber, sent to examine the Warsaw students, wrote a report to the Rebbe Rayatz evaluating each teacher and the chief mashgiach R' Yehoshua Berl. He praised R' David Teiblum's clear instruction, while observing that R' Yehoshua Berl, though a great scholar, was inclined to talmudic abstractions rather than the simple sense of the Gemara. The report set the stage for the Rebbe's later directive to reduce the Warsaw staff.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-tmimim, yehuda-eber, david-teiblum, report

Title: R' Eber examines Tomchei Tmimim students at the Lodz branch
Summary: R' Eber traveled to Lodz to examine students of the Tomchei Tmimim branch there.
Story: From 17 to 19 Iyar 5691, R' Yehuda Eber, at the Rebbe Rayatz's direction, examined the students at the Tomchei Tmimim branch in Lodz. After completing the examinations, he returned to Warsaw.
Tags: lodz, tomchei tmimim, eber, examinations, poland

Title: Plan to move Rebbe to Poland temporarily shelved
Summary: On 19 Iyar 5691, R. Shmuel Zalmanov wrote that the relocation plan had been deferred and the Rebbe would likely remain in Riga for an extended time.
Story: The letter also noted that the Rebbe was considering founding a Tomchei Tmimim branch in Riga itself, to which a group of senior students would be sent. This Riga plan would also fail to materialize, clearing the way for the eventual move to Otwock.
Tags: poland, riga, letter, tomchei-tmimim

Title: R. Yehuda Eber reports to Rebbe on Łódź yeshiva
Summary: On 22 Iyar 5691 R. Yehuda Eber sent the Rebbe a detailed report on the 52 students of the Łódź yeshiva.
Story: After being dispatched in Iyar 5691 to examine students in Warsaw, Łódź and Vilna, R. Yehuda Eber reported from Warsaw on 22 Iyar (May 9, 1931). He found 52 students at Łódź studying in two divisions, described their daily schedule, and praised the dedication of the Schneersohn brothers — particularly Dovber — who funded the yeshiva from their own pockets. He observed that the city was fertile ground for growth but financial strain limited expansion.
Tags: poland, lodz, yehuda-eber, tomchei-tmimim, warsaw, schneerson-brothers

Title: R' Eber travels to Vilna to examine Tomchei Tmimim students there
Summary: R' Eber traveled from Warsaw to Vilna to examine students at that branch of Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: On Sunday 23 Iyar 5691, R' Yehuda Eber traveled from Warsaw to the Tomchei Tmimim branch in Vilna to examine its students, continuing his survey of yeshiva students across the Polish branches at the Rebbe Rayatz's direction.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, eber, examinations

Title: R' Yehuda Eber reports on Vilna yeshiva class restructuring
Summary: On 1 Sivan 5691, R' Yehuda Eber wrote from Vilna detailing his reorganization of the yeshiva classes after returning from examining students in Warsaw and Lodz.
Story: After visiting Warsaw and Lodz to examine students at the Rebbe Rayatz's request, R' Yehuda Eber returned to Vilna and immediately reorganized the classes. He reported that although the student count had decreased slightly from the winter, the qualitative level had improved. The preparatory class was disbanded, and not a single student was missing from his own advanced class or R' Zeev Segal's top class.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, rabbi yehuda eber, rabbi zeev segal, warsaw, lodz

Title: R' Eber writes Rayatz detailed final report on yeshiva students
Summary: From Vilna on Isru Chag Shavuot, R' Eber sent the Rebbe a detailed final report on enrollment and faculty needs.
Story: On Isru Chag Shavuot (7 Sivan) 5691, R' Yehuda Eber wrote in detail from Vilna to the Rebbe Rayatz, reporting that Warsaw had about 25 students in the Kibbutz, 27 in the older shiur, and 25 in the younger. He warned that two qualified teachers in nigleh and chassidus would urgently be needed if the planned student transfer to Riga did not proceed soon.
Tags: vilna, warsaw, tomchei tmimim, eber

Title: Pinchas Mordechai Teitz founds Yavneh society in Livenhof
Summary: In Sivan 5691 Pinchas Mordechai Teitz visited the Rebbe in Riga and reported on the new Yavneh society for youth Torah study.
Story: During Sivan 5691 Rabbi Teitz's son Pinchas Mordechai Teitz visited the Rebbe in Riga and described the new association 'Yavneh' he had formed to organize the Livenhof youth around study of Tanach, Kitzur Shulchan Aruch, Mishnayos and Aggadah, and to strengthen mitzvah observance.
Tags: livenhof, livani, latvia, yavneh, pinchas-mordechai-teitz

Title: Rebbe blesses Yavneh society of Livenhof
Summary: On 20 Sivan 5691 the Frierdiker Rebbe sent a letter of blessing to the newly founded Yavneh society in Livenhof.
Story: The Frierdiker Rebbe wrote on 20 Sivan 5691 (Igrot vol. 17, no. 6289) expressing joy at Pinchas Mordechai Teitz's report of the founding of Yavneh in Livenhof. He blessed its members for success in their Torah learning program and prayed they would grow in numbers and become a model among Jewish youth.
Tags: livenhof, yavneh, pinchas-mordechai-teitz, latvia

Title: Rayatz departs Riga for tour of Polish yeshiva branches
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz left Riga to visit the three Tomchei Tmimim branches in Poland.
Story: On 9 Tammuz 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz left Riga to visit the three branches of Tomchei Tmimim under his guidance in Poland: Warsaw, Vilna, and Lodz. He arrived in Warsaw on 8 Tammuz, intending to make personal visits to the yeshivas and meet privately with students.
Tags: riga, warsaw, poland, rayatz, travel

Title: Rayatz departs Riga to survey Warsaw yeshiva
Summary: The Rayatz left Riga on 9 Tamuz to spend two weeks in Warsaw assessing the yeshiva and the possibility of relocating there.
Story: Warsaw had become a major center of Chabad activity outside the USSR. The Rayatz wanted to evaluate the Tomchei Temimim branch in person and weigh whether to move his own residence to Poland.
Tags: warsaw, poland, otwock, tomchei temimim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz leaves Riga for Warsaw to visit yeshivos
Summary: On 9 Tammuz 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz left Riga for Warsaw to visit the three yeshivos under his direction.
Story: As recounted in his letter of 5 Menachem Av 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz departed Riga on 9 Tammuz to travel to Warsaw and inspect the three yeshivos in Warsaw, Vilna and Łódź under his administration. During his time in Warsaw in mid-Tammuz, students from the Łódź branch traveled to meet him and were received in yechidus.
Tags: riga, warsaw, lodz, vilna, rebbe-travels, tomchei-tmimim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz visits Tomchei Tmimim branches via Warsaw
Summary: On 9 Tammuz 5691 the Rebbe left Riga for Warsaw to meet students from the Warsaw, Vilna and Lodz Tomchei Tmimim branches.
Story: The Rebbe traveled from Riga to Warsaw to inspect the three Tomchei Tmimim yeshivot under his direction. Students from the Vilna and Lodz branches traveled to Warsaw, where they were received in yechidus during the visit.
Tags: warsaw, vilna, lodz, tomchei tmimim, poland

Title: Rebbe Rayatz visits Warsaw to review Tomchei Temimim yeshivah
Summary: On 9 Tamuz 5691, the Rebbe traveled to Warsaw for a deep internal review of Chabad's flagship yeshivah.
Story: News of the visit electrified students in Warsaw, Vilnius, and Lodz. Thousands of Warsaw Jews welcomed the Rebbe at the yeshivah gates before Shabbat. He delivered maamarim, led a farbrengen marking his prison release, and held private yechidut sessions with each student over two days.
Tags: warsaw, poland, tomchei-temimim, vilnius, lodz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz's third visit to Warsaw
Summary: On 9 Tamuz 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz left Riga to visit the three Tomchei Tmimim yeshivot in Warsaw, Vilna, and Lodz.
Story: On 9 Tamuz 5691 (June 24, 1931), the Rebbe Rayatz left Riga on his third trip to Warsaw, this time to inspect the three Tomchei Tmimim yeshivot under his leadership in Warsaw, Vilna, and Lodz. He summarized the journey in a letter dated 5 Menachem Av of that year.
Tags: warsaw, vilna, lodz, rayatz, yeshiva inspection

Title: 12 Tammuz 5691 farbrengen with R' Binyamin of Minsk in Kiev's Dimievka
Summary: After fleeing Vitebsk, the author attended a warm 12 Tammuz farbrengen led by R' Binyamin of Minsk at the Kiev Tomchei Tmimim in Dimievka.
Story: Following the breakup of the Vitebsk yeshiva, the author and his chavrusa R' Michael Rapoport regrouped in Kiev for Shabbat 12 Tammuz before continuing on to Baku. The senior bochur R' Binyamin of Minsk, the mashpia of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Dimievka, led a warm farbrengen with the bochurim, providing a moment of spiritual encouragement amid the ongoing Soviet repression.
Tags: kiev, 12-tammuz, farbrengen, binyamin-minsk, tomchei-tmimim, dimievka, michael-rapoport

Title: Rayatz spends Chag HaGeula 12-13 Tammuz with yeshiva in Warsaw
Summary: The Rebbe spent Chag HaGeula in Warsaw with the Tomchei Tmimim community, delivering chassidus and meeting students.
Story: On 12-13 Tammuz 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz celebrated his liberation festival with the Tomchei Tmimim community at the yeshiva in Warsaw. He delivered three maamarei chassidus and many sichos during his approximately two-week stay, and met privately in yechidus with virtually every student of the yeshiva.
Tags: warsaw, chag hageula, 12 tammuz, tomchei tmimim, yechidus

Title: Author and Mikhal Rapoport arrested at Gori, Stalin's birthplace
Summary: While riding the train past Gori, Stalin's birthplace, the author and Mikhal Rapoport were detained by the GPU and briefly jailed.
Story: Although they had safely passed major cities like Rostov, Baku, and Tbilisi, the GPU seized them in the small town of Gori because the local secret police were unusually aggressive in Stalin's hometown. They were locked up with a violent Georgian prisoner and demanded their tefillin from the guards in the morning. They were eventually released in Tbilisi after intervention.
Tags: georgia, gori, stalin, gpu, arrest

Title: Chabad students arrive in Kutaisi to establish underground yeshiva
Summary: A group of Chabad yeshiva students reaches Kutaisi, Georgia just before Erev Tishah B'Av after a difficult journey from Kiev via Baku.
Story: After traveling from Kiev to Baku and finding it unsuitable for study, the students continued to Kutaisi. They arrived shortly before Erev Tishah B'Av and were warmly welcomed by local Georgian Chabad chassidim, many of whom had previously studied at Tomchei Tmimim in Vitebsk, Nevel, or Lubavitch. The community helped fund their settlement so a yeshiva could be re-established in the city.
Tags: kutaisi, georgia, soviet union, tomchei tmimim, underground

Title: Rebbe travels from Riga to Warsaw with R. Teitz
Summary: During Tammuz 5691 the Frierdiker Rebbe traveled from Riga to Warsaw, suggesting on the train to R. Teitz that Livenhof open a yeshiva.
Story: In Tammuz 5691 the Frierdiker Rebbe left Riga for Warsaw, riding the train together with Pinchas Mordechai Teitz. During the journey the Rebbe urged Teitz to expand the Yavneh learning groups and try to open a full yeshiva in Livenhof itself.
Tags: riga, warsaw, poland, latvia, pinchas-mordechai-teitz, livenhof

Title: Rebbe visits Warsaw and dispatches students to scout Polish-Volhynian towns
Summary: During his summer 1931 visit to Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz spoke with select students about traveling through Poland and Volhynia to identify towns where additional Tomchei Temimim branches could be opened.
Story: In mid-Tammuz 5691, while in Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz convened several senior students — including R' Shneur Zalman Gurary, R' Yosef Goldstein, R' Meir Glazman and R' Yitzchak Mandelbaum — and tasked them with surveying towns across Poland and the Volhynia region. Each was to assess where it would be feasible to establish new branches of the yeshiva. By mid-Av the students were reporting back, and the Rebbe responded with detailed instructions to each.
Tags: poland, volhynia, warsaw, tomchei temimim, rayatz, shneur zalman gurary, yosef goldstein, meir glazman, yitzchak mandelbaum

Title: Rayatz spends Shabbat in Otwock
Summary: During his Warsaw trip, the Rayatz spent Shabbat 13 Tamuz in Otwock.
Story: Otwock, a resort town near Warsaw, would later become the Rayatz's permanent residence. This early visit foreshadowed its future role as the Chabad center in Poland.
Tags: otwock, poland, shabbat

Title: Rayatz departs Warsaw to travel to Marienbad
Summary: After approximately two weeks visiting the Warsaw yeshiva, the Rebbe departed for Marienbad.
Story: On 22 Tammuz 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz departed Warsaw to travel to Marienbad. His Warsaw stay had been devoted primarily to the yeshiva, with the visit lasting from 8 Tammuz through 22 Tammuz.
Tags: warsaw, marienbad, rayatz, travel

Title: Rayatz travels to Marienbad for recovery
Summary: The Rayatz left Warsaw on 23 Tamuz for an extended stay in Marienbad.
Story: Marienbad's spas were a frequent destination for the Rayatz, who suffered chronic health issues. He stayed until 1 Elul before beginning his journey back to Riga.
Tags: marienbad, czechoslovakia, health

Title: Secretary announces Rebbe will move to Otwock
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Menachem Av 5691, secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote that it was nearly certain the Rebbe would relocate entirely to Poland and settle in Otwock.
Story: Feigin expected the move to occur in mid-Elul. While the full relocation would be delayed by two years due to apartment difficulties, the Rebbe did spend Tishrei 5692 in Otwock as a first trial of the new residence.
Tags: otwock, warsaw, letter, feigin

Title: Rebbe agrees in writing to come to Poland for Elul
Summary: On 3 Menachem Av 5691 the Rebbe wrote to the Warsaw vaad formally agreeing to come to Poland during the upcoming month of Elul.
Story: The Rebbe noted that the exact date could not yet be fixed and that he would notify them in two to three weeks. The letter resolved months of correspondence and set in motion the first Tishrei stay in Otwock.
Tags: warsaw, letter, elul

Title: Rayatz describes purpose of his tour of three Polish yeshivas
Summary: The Rebbe wrote describing his recent journey to visit the three Tomchei Tmimim branches in Poland.
Story: On 5 Menachem Av 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote that on 9 Tammuz he had left Riga for Warsaw to visit the three yeshivas under his guidance in Warsaw, Vilna, and Lodz. The trip had given particular focus to meeting yeshiva students personally.
Tags: warsaw, vilna, lodz, rayatz, tomchei tmimim, poland

Title: Anash informed Rebbe will spend High Holidays in Poland
Summary: On 7 Menachem Av 5691 R. Shmuel Zalmanov shared the good news that the Rebbe had agreed to come to Poland for the upcoming Yamim Noraim.
Story: Zalmanov expressed hope that the visit would lead to a permanent move. The letter was part of the continuing correspondence with R. Slonim documenting the campaign to bring the Rebbe to Poland.
Tags: poland, letter, high-holidays

Title: R' Zalmanov reports to R' Slonim on Rayatz's Warsaw visit
Summary: R' Shmuel Zalmanov wrote to R' Azriel Zelig Slonim describing the Rebbe's recent two-week visit to Warsaw.
Story: On 7 Menachem Av 5691, R' Shmuel Zalmanov wrote to R' Azriel Zelig Slonim about the Rebbe Rayatz's recent visit to Warsaw on his way to Marienbad. The Rebbe stayed two weeks, delivered three maamarim and many sichos, celebrated Chag HaGeula at the yeshiva, took interest in its state, and met privately with nearly every student.
Tags: warsaw, rayatz, shmuel zalmanov, slonim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz commits monthly funding to Łódź yeshiva
Summary: On 7 Menachem Av 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz sent $50 to Łódź — $25 for yeshiva upkeep and $25 for R. Baruch Friedman's salary.
Story: In a letter dated 7 Menachem Av 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz enclosed two checks of $25 each to the directorate of Tomchei Tmimim Łódź. The first was on account of his pledge toward yeshiva expenses, and the second toward the salary of R. Baruch Friedman, who served as the mashpia from 5689 to 5692. The Rebbe requested immediate confirmation of receipt.
Tags: poland, lodz, tomchei-tmimim, baruch-friedman, rebbe-correspondence, funding

Title: Rebbe writes R. Yehuda Eber on Łódź yeshiva's future
Summary: On 14 Menachem Av 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote R. Yehuda Eber that the Łódź yeshiva must offer shiurim only, not a full study hall.
Story: Writing on 14 Menachem Av 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz urged R. Yehuda Eber to spend several days in Łódź to evaluate the situation. He clarified that the Łódź branch was intended to host shiurim only, with no large independent study hall — that role being reserved for Warsaw. The letter reflects the structural division the Rebbe envisioned among the Polish branches.
Tags: poland, lodz, yehuda-eber, tomchei-tmimim, rebbe-correspondence

Title: Feigin writes Jacobson on Rayatz's reasoning for the Warsaw journey
Summary: Secretary R' Yechezkel Feigin wrote R' Yisrael Jacobson about the Rebbe's visit to Poland.
Story: On 15 Menachem Av 5691, the Rebbe's secretary R' Yechezkel Feigin wrote R' Yisrael Jacobson describing how the Rebbe Rayatz had chosen, en route to Marienbad, to visit Poland and especially the yeshiva. The Rebbe had said the situation could no longer continue without a yeshiva nearby, deciding either to transfer part of the yeshiva to Riga or to relocate his own residence to Warsaw.
Tags: warsaw, rayatz, feigin, jacobson, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rebbe asks R' Yehuda Eber to map yeshivas of Polish Lithuania
Summary: On 15 Menachem Av 5691 the Rebbe repeated his request that R' Yehuda Eber compile a list of yeshivas in Polish Lithuania with their locations and student counts.
Story: The Rebbe had originally written the prior winter asking Eber, head of Tomchei Temimim in Vilna, to gather this information. Now he renewed the request, observing that Vilna was a natural base from which such intelligence could be assembled. The data was to feed his broader planning for Tomchei Temimim's expansion across Polish Lithuania.
Tags: polish lithuania, vilna, tomchei temimim, yehuda eber, rayatz

Title: Rebbe sends R' Meir Glazman to survey yeshivas in Lvov and surroundings
Summary: On 15 Menachem Av 5691 the Rebbe instructed R' Meir Glazman to broaden his Lvov mission beyond the Machzikei Lomdei Torah yeshiva to all local Torah institutions.
Story: Responding to Glazman's first report from Lvov, the Rebbe expressed pleasure that he had grasped the broader purpose of the visit. The Rebbe asked him to identify every yeshiva, study circle, and shtiebel where Torah was learned in the city, to record names of contacts for future correspondence, and to extend his survey to the surrounding towns of the Lemberg region for another week.
Tags: poland, lvov, lemberg, machzikei lomdei torah, tomchei temimim, meir glazman

Title: R' Yitzchak Mandelbaum proposes opening a yeshiva in Maciów
Summary: In Av 5691, R' Yitzchak Mandelbaum wrote to the Rebbe relaying an offer from his hometown Maciów of a newly built, well-appointed building suited for a yeshiva.
Story: Mandelbaum forwarded a letter from a young man in Maciów (Volhynia) describing a magnificent stone building, recently completed by a wealthy New York native in memory of his deceased daughter. The donor had built dormitory space, a dining hall, and apartments for the heads of the yeshiva, and pledged ongoing support. The local community urged that a Chabad yeshiva be founded there.
Tags: poland, volhynia, maciów, tomchei temimim, yitzchak mandelbaum

Title: Rayatz settles in Otwock at Shapira hotel for the month of Tishrei
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz arrived from Riga in Otwock to remain there throughout the month of Tishrei.
Story: In Elul 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Otwock from Riga, renting the Shapira hotel as a spacious residence and beis midrash for himself and his family. He instructed that the students of the Lodz yeshiva join him in Otwock for the entire month of Tishrei.
Tags: otwock, rayatz, tishrei, poland, shapira hotel

Title: Rayatz directs preparation of Tomchei Tmimim alumni list
Summary: The Rebbe instructed R' Shmuel Zalmanov to compile a comprehensive list of all alumni from Tomchei Tmimim's first decade.
Story: On 22 Menachem Av 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Shmuel Zalmanov asking the hanhalla to compile a list of all students who had studied at Tomchei Tmimim over its first ten years, including where they were now and what they were doing. The aim, the Rebbe wrote to talmid R' Yitzchak Mandelbaum, was to identify alumni who could be placed as roshei yeshiva, mashpiim, and madrichim to spread Torah.
Tags: alumni, tomchei tmimim, shmuel zalmanov, harbatzas torah

Title: Rebbe asks R' Yosef Goldstein to undertake a Krakow mission
Summary: On 22 Menachem Av 5691 the Rebbe wrote to R' Yosef Goldstein asking whether he could accept a two- to three-week shlichus to Krakow.
Story: Building on his Warsaw conversations about strengthening Tomchei Temimim alumni scattered across Polish towns, the Rebbe noted that Goldstein lived not far from Krakow and might be able to visit the city periodically. He inquired whether Goldstein had already acted on their discussion and whether his schedule allowed him to take on a focused Krakow mission of several weeks.
Tags: poland, krakow, tomchei temimim, yosef goldstein, rayatz

Title: Rebbe sends R' Shneur Zalman Gurary to investigate Maciów yeshiva offer
Summary: On 22 Menachem Av 5691 the Rebbe instructed R' Shneur Zalman Gurary to travel discreetly to Maciów to inspect the building offered for a new yeshiva.
Story: After receiving Mandelbaum's report, the Rebbe wrote both to Mandelbaum and to Gurary on the same day. He asked Gurary to view the buildings, send a detailed description, and act quietly so that no rival groups would seize the opportunity. The Rebbe hoped that once full details were in hand, arrangements could be made to open a yeshiva there.
Tags: poland, volhynia, maciów, tomchei temimim, rayatz, shneur zalman gurary

Title: Zalmanov reports to Rayatz on alumni-tracking project progress
Summary: R' Zalmanov reported he had begun sending circular letters to traceable alumni.
Story: On 27 Menachem Av 5691, R' Shmuel Zalmanov replied to the Rebbe that he had begun the alumni project, sending each known alumnus a circular letter with detailed questions. He included a sample of the letter being sent.
Tags: alumni, tomchei tmimim, shmuel zalmanov

Title: Rebbe inquires about Livenhof and Kreuzburg activity
Summary: On 27 Av 5691 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote that he had heard only second-hand reports from Livenhof and Kreuzburg and requested a detailed update.
Story: The Frierdiker Rebbe wrote on 27 Av 5691 (Igrot vol. 17, no. 6299) complaining that since leaving Riga at the start of Tammuz he had only heard fragmented news 'from afar' about Livenhof and Kreuzburg, and asked Pinchas Mordechai Teitz to send a detailed report on developments there.
Tags: livenhof, kreuzburg, latvia, pinchas-mordechai-teitz

Title: R' Shneur Zalman Gurary visits Maciów to inspect proposed yeshiva building
Summary: On 5 Elul 5691, R' Shneur Zalman Gurary reported from Maciów after touring the proposed yeshiva building and meeting with the local committee.
Story: Gurary described the structure in detail, sketching its layout since the town was too small for him to photograph or measure openly — a bearded bochur arriving in such a small town drew immediate attention. The local committee, prompted by Mandelbaum's letter forwarding the Rebbe's interest, had convened a meeting earlier that week and was actively considering the proposal. Gurary indicated that a formal letter from the committee to the Rebbe was forthcoming.
Tags: poland, volhynia, maciów, tomchei temimim, shneur zalman gurary

Title: Zalmanov updates Rayatz on slow alumni response, plans newspaper notice
Summary: R' Zalmanov reported few alumni had yet responded; nearly 300 names were on file but many addresses were uncertain.
Story: On 6 Elul 5691, R' Shmuel Zalmanov updated the Rebbe Rayatz on the alumni project, noting that responses had so far been few. The hanhalla had nearly 300 alumni names on file, though not all addresses were precise, and planned to publish a notice in newspapers to reach more former students.
Tags: alumni, tomchei tmimim, shmuel zalmanov

Title: Maciów community committee formally proposes hosting a Chabad yeshiva
Summary: On 7 Elul 5691 the rabbi, deputy rabbi, and seven committee members of Maciów's 'Yeshivat Talmud Torah' wrote to the Rebbe offering a hall in their new building for a thirty-student yeshiva.
Story: Signed by Rabbi Shalom Shachna Cherniak, his deputy Rabbi Yosef Lashtshiver, and the seven committee members, the letter described how they had deliberately left the upper story of the building unfinished to prevent secularists from establishing schools there. They offered the Rebbe immediate use of a large, ornate hall sufficient for thirty students, and invited the Rebbe to take an active interest in establishing a major yeshiva in Volhynia at this site.
Tags: poland, volhynia, maciów, tomchei temimim, shalom shachna cherniak

Title: Rayatz returns to Riga via Berlin
Summary: After Marienbad and a short Berlin stop, the Rayatz arrived back in Riga on 7 Elul.
Story: The travel pattern of Riga–Marienbad–Berlin–Riga became familiar over his Latvian years. He would not stay long, however, departing for Poland just two weeks later for the High Holidays.
Tags: riga, berlin, latvia

Title: Riga Anash plead with Rebbe Rayatz not to leave for Warsaw
Summary: More than one hundred Anash in Riga signed a letter on 12 Elul 5691 begging the Rebbe Rayatz to stay through the upcoming Yamim Noraim rather than move to Warsaw.
Story: When word spread that the Rebbe Rayatz planned to relocate from Riga to Warsaw, the Riga community at first refused to believe it. Once the plan was confirmed, over a hundred Chassidim signed a letter on 12 Elul 5691 describing their broken hearts and pleading with the Rebbe to remain among them at least for the coming High Holidays rather than take up the larger discussion at such a sensitive moment in the calendar.
Tags: latvia, riga, warsaw, rayatz, petition, anash, high holidays

Title: Rebbe Rayatz spends Tishrei in Otwock near Warsaw
Summary: During Tishrei 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz stayed in Otwock near Warsaw, close to the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva, before returning to Riga.
Story: Although the move from Riga to Warsaw had been postponed, the Rebbe Rayatz spent the month of Tishrei 5692 in Otwock near Warsaw, where the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva was located. He had earlier hoped to relocate the senior division of the yeshiva from Warsaw to Riga, but when that plan fell through he decided to take up residence near the yeshiva instead.
Tags: poland, otwock, warsaw, rayatz, tishrei, tomchei temimim

Title: Rebbe travels alone to Warsaw before Rosh Hashanah
Summary: On 20 Elul 5691, secretary Feigin reported that the Rebbe would travel to Warsaw the next day, alone, because no apartment was yet available for the family.
Story: The Rebbe spent Rosh Hashanah and the entire month of Tishrei in Otwock. He returned to Riga around 10 Cheshvan after concluding that a suitable apartment could not yet be secured, and stayed in Riga for two more years before the relocation was completed.
Tags: warsaw, otwock, rosh-hashanah, feigin

Title: Rayatz departs Riga for the High Holidays in Poland
Summary: On 21 Elul, the Rayatz left Riga to spend the High Holidays in Poland.
Story: Spending the High Holidays among the Chasidim of Warsaw and Otwock allowed the Rayatz to strengthen his Polish flock. He would remain in Poland through Cheshvan, dividing his time between Warsaw and Otwock.
Tags: riga, poland, high holidays

Title: Underground Rosh Hashanah minyan in Kutaisi for 5692
Summary: Anash and tmimim gathered in R. Yosef's home in Kutaisi for a Rosh Hashanah minyan praying with the devotion of pre-revolutionary Vitebsk.
Story: On Rosh Hashanah 5692 the students held a private minyan in the home of R. Yosef, brother of Chacham Yitzchak who had studied in Lubavitch. R. Eli Chaim the shochet led prayers with tears and dveikut. On motzaei Rosh Hashanah the maamar 'Hashem yechatu merivav' from 5689 was reviewed.
Tags: kutaisi, georgia, rosh hashanah, underground

Title: Decision to keep central yeshiva in Warsaw and expand it
Summary: During Tishrei 5692 it was resolved that the central Tomchei Temimim yeshiva would remain in Warsaw and be expanded with a new mechina division.
Story: After a plan to move the yeshiva closer to the Rebbe in Riga was abandoned, the decision was made during Tishrei 5692 to keep the central yeshiva in Warsaw and grow it. A preparatory mechina division for younger students was added, classes were enlarged, and the staff was expanded.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei temimim, mechina, poland

Title: Mechina preparatory division founded at Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Warsaw
Summary: Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw opened a new Mechina division for bar-mitzvah-age students at the start of 5692.
Story: After deliberations through summer 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz decided in Tishrei 5692 to keep the central Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Warsaw and add a Mechina branch for younger students. Classes opened on Sunday of Parshat Vayera with 10–11 boys, supplementing the existing two shiurim for ages 14–17 and the senior Olam for self-learners. Initial enrollment was limited because the new program was announced late.
Tags: warsaw, poland, tomchei tmimim, mechina, yeshiva, rayatz

Title: Mechina preparatory division opens at Tomchei Temimim Warsaw
Summary: On Sunday of Parshas Vayera 5692, formal studies began in the new mechina preparatory department with 10-11 young students.
Story: The mechina division for younger students officially began learning on Sunday of Parshas Vayera. Only 10-11 students initially enrolled because word had spread late, but more were expected to join in the coming term.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei temimim, mechina, poland

Title: R' Menachem Mendel Schneerson farbrengs publicly for first time, in Otwock
Summary: During Sukkos 5692 in Otwock, R' Menachem Mendel Schneerson (later the Rebbe) delivered his first public farbrengen.
Story: On a night of Simchas Beis HaShoeiva during Sukkos 5692 in Otwock, the Rebbe Rayatz instructed his son-in-law R' Menachem Mendel Schneerson, then called the Ramash, to farbreng with the assembled community. Beginning at 8 PM and continuing until dawn, the Ramash opened on the mishna 'Hevei az kanamer' and astonished the entire crowd with the depth and brilliance of his Torah, drawing on Talmud, Midrash, Zohar, Kabbalah, and chassidic stories. From that moment Anash began to recognize his unique greatness in his own right.
Tags: otwock, ramash, rebbe, farbrengen, simchas beis hashoeiva, sukkos

Title: Rebbe Rayatz returns from Otwock to Riga
Summary: In mid-Marcheshvan 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz returned from Otwock to Riga, where he remained for another two years before finally moving to Warsaw.
Story: After his Tishrei stay in Otwock, the Rebbe Rayatz returned to Riga around the middle of Marcheshvan 5692. He remained there for two more years before the final relocation to Warsaw, and during that period a branch of the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva was also opened in Riga.
Tags: latvia, riga, otwock, rayatz, tomchei temimim

Title: Tomchei Temimim Warsaw opens 5692 school year with 120 students
Summary: The 5692 academic year opened in Warsaw with 120 students: 50 in the main hall, 60 in two classes, and 10 in the newly opened mechina.
Story: At the start of the 5692 school year, Tomchei Temimim Warsaw enrolled approximately 120 students. The faculty included R. Yehuda Eber as rosh yeshiva, R. David Teiblum as r"m, R. Baruch Friedman as mashpia, R. Shmuel Zalmanov as administrator, and R. Eliyahu Moshe Liss and R. Meir Glazman as Chassidus instructors.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei temimim, mechina, enrollment, poland

Title: R. Yehuda Eber appointed Rosh Yeshiva of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw
Summary: R. Yehuda Eber confirmed in a letter to R. Yisrael Jacobson that the Rebbe had appointed him as r"m and mashgiach over nigleh studies in Warsaw.
Story: On 26 Tishrei 5692, R. Yehuda Eber wrote to R. Yisrael Jacobson reporting his new appointment by the Rebbe Rayatz as r"m and mashgiach for nigleh studies at the Warsaw yeshiva. He also noted his expectation that the Rebbe himself would settle permanently in Warsaw.
Tags: warsaw, yehuda eber, tomchei temimim, poland

Title: Rayatz returns from Poland to Riga
Summary: After dividing his post-holiday time between Warsaw and Otwock, the Rayatz returned to Riga on 10 Cheshvan.
Story: The return concluded a months-long Polish stay. Latvia remained his official residence, even as his connections to Polish Chasidic life deepened.
Tags: riga, poland, warsaw, otwock

Title: Rebbe returns from Otwock to Riga
Summary: Around 10 Cheshvan 5692 the Rebbe returned from his first extended stay in Otwock back to Riga.
Story: Although the Rebbe had publicly indicated his decision to settle in Poland, no suitable apartment could be found in the tight Warsaw housing market. He returned to Riga 'for a few months' that turned into two more years.
Tags: otwock, riga, warsaw

Title: R' Yehuda Eber reports founding of Mechina to the Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: On 28 Marcheshvan 5692 rosh yeshiva R' Yehuda Eber wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz confirming the Mechina had begun functioning.
Story: R' Yehuda Eber's report described 10–11 boys learning in the new Mechina, attributing low initial numbers to short notice. He predicted growth in subsequent terms. By 20 Kislev there were 13 talmidim, and from 3 Tevet R' Moshe Chaim was teaching them Tanya daily.
Tags: warsaw, yehuda eber, tomchei tmimim, rayatz, mechina

Title: R. Mandelbaum reports overcrowded conditions at Łódź
Summary: On 8 Kislev 5692 R. Mandelbaum reported the Łódź yeshiva's financial state was dire despite excellent student progress.
Story: In his report of 8 Kislev 5692, R. Mandelbaum described the yeshiva's grave financial situation: income was minimal relative to expenses and the Schneersohn brothers were covering shortfalls from their own pockets. Nonetheless, he was pleased with the students' diligence in both nigleh and chassidus, and reported that the yeshiva had earned a reputation among the yeshivos of Łódź.
Tags: poland, lodz, yitzchok-aryeh-mandelbaum, tomchei-tmimim, rebbe-correspondence, finances

Title: Yochanan Gordon immigrates to America on Rebbe's promise
Summary: Yochanan Gordon immigrated to the US at Chanukah 5692 after the Rebbe promised his children would remain religious and study in his yeshivas.
Story: Gordon had resisted joining his three brothers in America, fearing his children would abandon observance as theirs had. The Rebbe assured him the children would remain religious Jews and learn in his yeshivas. The pledge was fulfilled in 1940 when Gordon's son Shalom Ber became one of the first students at the Rebbe's Brooklyn yeshivah.
Tags: america, immigration, gordon

Title: Chassidus distribution campaign launched in Warsaw
Summary: Beginning in 5692, the Warsaw yeshiva ran a campaign of Tanya shiurim and maamar deliveries in shtieblach and yeshivot across the city.
Story: Under R. Yehuda Eber's direction in 5692, a young avreich named Moshe Chaim was sent into Warsaw shuls and yeshivot to teach Tanya and disseminate Chassidus. He established daily Tanya classes in the Bagne beis midrash (forty students), the Sochaczow Beis Avraham yeshiva (thirty boys for five zlotys a week), and the Franciscan 22 Chabad shul (four Ger chassidim). He also began saying maamarim every Shabbat in the Dzika shul.
Tags: warsaw, hafatzas hama'ayanos, tanya shiurim, yehuda eber, moshe chaim, ger chassidim, sochaczow yeshiva

Title: Mandelbaum sent to head Tomchei Tmimim Lodz
Summary: During 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz appointed R. Yitzchak Mandelbaum to head the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lodz.
Story: Mandelbaum had distinguished himself as a Tomchei Tmimim student in Warsaw, praised in 5686 as 'sharp-minded' with depth in nigleh and chassidus. In 5692 (1932) the Rebbe sent him to lead the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lodz.
Tags: mandelbaum, lodz, tomchei-tmimim, yeshiva

Title: Mechina founded at Dzika 8 shul
Summary: In 5692, the 'Mechina' preparatory program was established in the Agudas Chabad shul on Dzika 8 in Warsaw.
Story: The Agudas Chabad shul on Dzika 8 (possibly also called Zamenhof 8) served the younger Chabad chassidim of Warsaw. In 5692 (1932) it became home to the newly founded Mechina, a preparatory program feeding into the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva.
Tags: warsaw, dzika 8, mechina, agudas chabad shul

Title: R' Shimon Zelichover joins Yeshivat Chochmei Lublin as spiritual supervisor
Summary: In the spring of 5692 R' Shimon Zelichover was accepted as spiritual supervisor at Yeshivat Chochmei Lublin.
Story: Engel had taught the senior shiur at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw at least through the end of 5687 before being recruited by R' Meir Shapiro for Chochmei Lublin. He remained in Lublin until shortly after Shapiro's passing.
Tags: lublin, chochmei lublin, shimon engel zelichover, meir shapiro

Title: R' Yaakov Landa serves as shadar in Latvia
Summary: In early 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz sent R' Yaakov Landa as a Kollel Chabad emissary to the towns of Latvia.
Story: At the start of 5692 (1932), the Rebbe Rayatz dispatched R' Yaakov Landa as a Kollel Chabad shadar (fundraising emissary) to the Jewish communities of Latvia. That same year, his appointment as general rabbi of Libau was also under consideration, prompting correspondence from the Rogatchover.
Tags: landa, kollel-chabad, shadar, latvia, fundraising

Title: R' Yochanan Gordon emigrates to New York
Summary: After living in Dokshitz until 5692, R' Yochanan Gordon emigrated with his family to New York, where he established himself as a shochet u'bodek.
Story: In 5692, R' Yochanan Gordon left his hometown of Dokshitz with his family and emigrated to New York. He set himself up in his new country as a shochet u'bodek (ritual slaughterer and inspector), a trade he had presumably been trained in earlier. This move placed him among the growing community of Lubavitcher chassidim taking root in America.
Tags: immigration, yochanan gordon, new york, dokshitz, shochet

Title: Rebbe appoints Rotstein as his secretary in Druzgenik
Summary: During the summer of 5692 at the Druzgenik convalescent home, the Frierdiker Rebbe appointed R. Moshe Leib Rotstein as his secretary.
Story: In the summer of 5692, R. Moshe Leib Rotstein stayed with the Frierdiker Rebbe at the convalescent home in Druzgenik. It was apparently during this stay that the Rebbe formally appointed him as his secretary, a role he would fulfill in the years to come.
Tags: druzgenik, moshe leib rotstein, secretary, frierdiker rebbe

Title: Rebbe Rayatz visits Vilna in summer 5692
Summary: In the summer of 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz visited Vilna, where many Chabad rabbis of Lithuania gathered to join him for seudah shlishis.
Story: R. Yitzchak Dov Ushpal recalled that during the Rebbe Rayatz's Vilna visit in summer 5692 (1932), after davening the Rebbe went to his hotel where senior Chabad rabbis assembled for seudah shlishis. Among those present were R. Shlomo Eliyahu Ushpal of Kornitz, R. Kuperstock of Fastov, R. Mendelovitz, R. Leib Sheinin of Dokshytsy, and the rabbis of Dalhinov and Radoshkovitz.
Tags: vilna, rebbe-visit, kuperstock, sheinin, ushpal, mendelovitz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz visits Vilna yeshiva late at night
Summary: In early Elul 5692, during his visit to Vilna, the Rebbe Rayatz made a late-night surprise visit to the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva to hear 'the voice of Torah.'
Story: At the conclusion of his Vilna visit in early Elul 5692, the Rebbe Rayatz expressed his desire to visit the yeshiva at a late hour. Finding the students still learning at long tables with open gemaros, the Rebbe declared 'Hakol kol Yaakov - I wish to hear the sound of Torah.' The bochurim resumed learning aloud as the Rebbe walked among the tables gazing at each student before bestowing his blessing.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, rebbe rayatz, visit, elul

Title: Rebbe travels to Druskininkai for leg treatment
Summary: During the summer of 5692 the Rebbe stayed in the spa town of Druskininkai to treat the recurrence of his leg ailment.
Story: From Druskininkai he traveled briefly to visit Anash in Ludmir, Volhynia, and returned to Riga via stops in Warsaw and Vilna. The health challenges that summer foreshadowed a more severe medical crisis the following winter.
Tags: druskininkai, lithuania, health, spa

Title: Rebbe travels to Ludmir with Rotstein as secretary
Summary: On 23 Menachem Av 5692, the Frierdiker Rebbe traveled to visit Anash in Ludmir with R. Moshe Leib Rotstein as his secretary.
Story: On 23 Menachem Av 5692, the Frierdiker Rebbe set out from Druzgenik to visit chassidim in Ludmir. In his diary the Rebbe noted that 'the one traveling with me as secretary is the tamim R. Moshe Leib Rotstein,' formalizing the secretarial role.
Tags: ludmir, moshe leib rotstein, frierdiker rebbe, travel

Title: Tomchei Tmimim branches founded in Patzanow, Riga, Kovel, Baranowicze
Summary: Four new Tomchei Tmimim branches opened in 5692 (1932) in Patzanow, Riga, Kovel and Baranowicze.
Story: While Patzanow became a stable long-term branch, the branches in Riga, Kovel and Baranowicze each lasted only one year. The 1932 expansion reflected the Frierdiker Rebbe's push to seed Chabad education across Poland, Lithuania and Latvia.
Tags: poland, latvia, patzanow, riga, kovel, baranowicze, tomchei tmimim, branch

Title: Wedding of Sheina Schneerson and Mendel Horenstein in Landwarow
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz's youngest daughter Sheina married Rabbi Mendel Horenstein in Landwarow, Poland, with Rabbi Chaim Ozer Grodzinski officiating.
Story: Landwarow was chosen because of visa issues, sitting just over the border from Vilnius. Rabbi Baruch Ber Leibowitz of Kaminetz Yeshivah was also present and had a scholarly discussion with the Ramash. After the wedding, the couple moved to Paris, and a few months later Chaya Mushka and the Ramash joined them there.
Tags: landwarow, poland, lithuania, horenstein, grodzinski, baruch-ber

Title: Yitzchak Goldin arrested for underground educational work
Summary: Goldin was arrested for his role in the Chabad educational underground; an initial death sentence was commuted to exile in Kazakhstan.
Story: Goldin had assisted the Rebbe during his illness in Rostov and helped administer Tomchei Temimim. He escaped Russia in 1946 and eventually moved to Brooklyn.
Tags: goldin, kazakhstan, underground, exile

Title: Łódź yeshiva moves to Pomorska A41 building
Summary: In Shevat 5692 the Łódź yeshiva moved to a larger building at Pomorska A41 with three divisions.
Story: Beginning in Shevat 5692, the Łódź yeshiva relocated from Paludniowa 25 to spacious modern quarters at Pomorska A41. The new building featured central heating, hot water and modern facilities, and housed roughly fifty families including many chassidim. With the move, the yeshiva expanded to three divisions and grew to about one hundred students.
Tags: poland, lodz, tomchei-tmimim, pomorska, yeshiva-building

Title: R. Zalman Levitin arrives in Kutaisi to head the underground yeshiva
Summary: Mid-winter R. Zalman Levitin (the Haditcher) reached Kutaisi and reorganized the underground yeshiva with strong leadership.
Story: In mid-winter R. Zalman 'the Haditcher' Levitin joined the Kutaisi group and began guiding them in chassidus, teaching Shoresh Mitzvas HaTefillah, Haamanas Elokus, and chapters of Derech Mitzvosecha before moving them on to Hemshech 5659 with required memorization. He raised funds and ran the yeshiva with a firm hand, drawing additional bochurim including Moshe Rexin, Ze'ev Zalmanov, and Avraham Kievman.
Tags: kutaisi, georgia, zalman levitin, haditcher, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rebbe sends theological letter to Ramash on Chabad's distinctive focus
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz sent his son-in-law a lengthy letter exploring Chabad's distinctive emphasis on intellectual ideas and spiritual growth as opposed to other chasidic groups' focus on miracles.
Story: The Ramash responded, 'From the depths of my heart, I thank you for this precious gift,' while also writing that he remained 'puzzled' that people still said 'In Chabad, we have no interest in miracles.' The letter was later published in Hatomim, volume 2.
Tags: letters, theology, chasidut, hatomim, miracles

Title: Rayatz sends future Rebbe on mission to Hans Gaslar in Berlin
Summary: On 11 Shevat 5692, Rayatz instructs his son-in-law (the future Rebbe) to enlist Hans Gaslar of Berlin to lobby Minister Weizmann to pressure the Soviets.
Story: Rayatz writes that he can no longer postpone using personal connections and recommendations to recover the library. He provides detailed identification markers: about 5000 catalogued numbers (Shas, Rambam, Tur, Mikraos), each cross-referenced in the list he kept; bindings mostly in distinctive blue, green, or chocolate-colored cloth. He emphasizes the chillul Hashem of the holy books of the Rebbeim — including ones with their marginal notations — sitting in captivity, and the great mitzvah of rescuing them.
Tags: library, rayatz, future-rebbe, berlin, weizmann, soviet, germany

Title: R. Yechezkel Feigin letter on Vilna-region towns
Summary: On 17 Shevat 5692 the Rebbe's secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to R. Yisrael Jacobson noting roughly forty small towns of anash in the Vilna province.
Story: Reporting to R. Yisrael Jacobson, the Rebbe's secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin described plans for a tour of the Vilna province around Adar, mentioning that the region contained nearly forty small towns, most populated by anash. The letter offers one of the clearest contemporary snapshots of Chabad's geographic reach in interwar Lithuania.
Tags: lithuania, vilna, yechezkel-feigin, yisrael-jacobson, shevat

Title: Adler writes Hyman protesting JDC silence on Russian Judaism
Summary: Dr. Cyrus Adler urged the JDC not to remain silent as Jewish religious life was destroyed in Russia.
Story: 'I am not willing to take the attitude that every vestige of Judaism shall be destroyed in Russia with our silence, which means assent,' Adler wrote. He also signed a personal letter of support to the Rebbe on Dropsie College stationery, asking Hyman to send it if the JDC did not object.
Tags: jdc, adler, hyman, soviet-jewry, religious-freedom

Title: Warburg writes Hyman rejecting JDC support for Russian Judaism
Summary: JDC chairman Felix Warburg dismissed efforts to bolster Jewish religious life in Russia as 'stupidity' and 'a waste of time.'
Story: Warburg also rejected the Rebbe's matzah campaign and expressed personal disdain, writing 'I have no confidence in Schneersohn.' His Reform commitments shaped his view that Jewish observance was peripheral and that integrating Jews into Soviet society was the priority.
Tags: warburg, jdc, soviet-jewry, religious-freedom, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz visits Glubokoe and Postov
Summary: In early Adar Sheni 5692 the Rebbe visited small towns in the Vilna region including Glubokoe and Postov for about ten days.
Story: Responding to requests from Anash in the roughly forty small towns of the Vilna region who could not travel to see him, the Rebbe spent about ten days touring the area until Purim. He delivered three maamarim in Postov and was accompanied by Rabbi Menachem Mendel Kupershtok of Postov and Rabbi Mordechai Chefetz. The train broke down en route, requiring a four-hour wait during which he received about fifty people in yechidus.
Tags: glubokoe, postov, vilna region, poland, rayatz

Title: Rayatz visits Lithuanian Chabad communities
Summary: The Rayatz traveled through Lithuania, visiting communities including Glubok and Pastov.
Story: From 30 Adar Alef to 9 Adar Bet, he brought himself to townlets where local Chabad Chasidim could meet him in person. He returned to Riga on March 17.
Tags: lithuania, glubok, pastov

Title: Rebbe presses Łódź for status updates
Summary: On 3 Adar II 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz expressed surprise at receiving no updates from the Łódź yeshiva.
Story: In a letter dated 3 Adar II 5692, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote with surprise that he had heard nothing of the Łódź yeshiva's situation since his recent travels and return. He demanded to know how his earlier instructions had been carried out and asked for a complete update on the current state of affairs.
Tags: poland, lodz, tomchei-tmimim, rebbe-correspondence

Title: Assembly of Latvian rabbis convenes in Riga
Summary: On 20 Adar II 5692 an assembly of Latvian rabbis convened in Riga to strengthen Judaism and Shabbos observance, opened by a short programmatic address from the Rebbe Rayatz.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz urged R. Yaakov Landau to attend the gathering and arranged for him to come to Riga several days early to consult quietly with the organizers, Messrs. Chefetz and Chodakov. The Rebbe's secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote on 26 Adar II to R. Israel Jacobson that the assembly produced concrete resolutions on strengthening Judaism in general and Shabbos observance in particular, and that the Rebbe himself opened the proceedings with a brief but substantive speech laying out a principal foundation for the discussions.
Tags: latvia, riga, rabbis, assembly, shabbos, rayatz, landau, feigin, chodakov

Title: Rebbe writes to NY Agudas Nashim supporting yeshivos
Summary: On 13 Nissan 5692 the Rebbe wrote to the New York Agudas Nashim supporting the yeshivos under his leadership.
Story: The letter shows that beyond the original taharas hamishpacha focus, the women's organizations were taking on additional missions including financial support for Chabad yeshivos. The Rebbe's 5690 visit to America had launched the broader Agudas Nashim initiative.
Tags: rayatz, agudas-nashim, new-york, yeshivos, women

Title: Tnaim of Sheina written in Rebbe Rayatz's own hand
Summary: On Lag B'Omer 5692, the Rebbe Rayatz personally wrote the text of the tnaim for his daughter Sheina's engagement to R' Menachem Mendel Horenstein.

Title: Rebbe approves Livenhof yeshiva and reports 27 students
Summary: On 25 Nissan 5692 the Frierdiker Rebbe encouraged founding a small yeshiva in Livenhof, soon reporting 27 talmidim.
Story: In a Chol HaMoed Pesach letter dated 25 Nissan 5692 the Frierdiker Rebbe told Pinchas Mordechai Teitz that he had discussed strengthening Tiferes Bachurim/Yavneh with R. Chadakov and was thrilled at the possibility of founding a small yeshiva in Livenhof. A subsequent letter celebrated that, with mesirus nefesh, the yeshiva had already enrolled 27 students.

Title: Rayatz travels to Druskenig for medical treatment
Summary: After his daughter's wedding, the Rayatz traveled to Druskenig for about two months of medical treatment for his feet.
Story: Chronic foot problems plagued the Rayatz throughout his life and shaped much of his travel schedule. The spa town of Druskenig provided extended treatment in the summer of 1932.
