Title: Marriage of Sheina Schneersohn to Mendel Horenstein in Landvarov
Summary: The Rayatz's youngest daughter Sheina married Mendel Horenstein in Landvarov, Poland, on 10 Sivan.
Story: The Rayatz left Riga before Shavuot to attend the wedding. Sheina and her husband would later be among the millions murdered in the Holocaust, while her sister Chaya Mushka escaped to America.

Title: Wedding of Sheina daughter of the Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: On Tuesday 10 Sivan 5692, Sheina daughter of the Rebbe Rayatz married her cousin R' Menachem Mendel HaKohen Horenstein, both later murdered in the Holocaust.
Story: On Tuesday 10 Sivan 5692, Sheina daughter of the Rebbe Rayatz married her cousin R' Menachem Mendel HaKohen Horenstein, son of R' Moshe HaKohen Horenstein who had been a son-in-law of the Rebbe Maharash. Their tnaim had been written several weeks earlier on Lag B'Omer of that year, in the Rebbe Rayatz's own hand. Sheina and her husband would later be murdered in the Holocaust, Hashem yikom damam.

Title: Rayatz writes Boston Rabbi Rabinowitz seeking Senator Borah's intervention
Summary: On 23 Sivan 5692, Rayatz writes Rabbi D. M. Rabinowitz of Boston hoping his son Asher will help obtain a letter from Senator Borah to Soviet Foreign Minister Litvinov.
Story: Rayatz asks whether Rabbi Rabinowitz's son Asher can secure a letter from Senator Borah to Soviet Foreign Commissar Litvinov requesting return of the library according to Rayatz's existing inventory. At the time, the US had not yet recognized the Soviet government, and the senator's intervention did not produce the hoped-for result.

Title: 12 Tammuz 5692 farbrengen at the Liebov family home in Kutaisi
Summary: The growing Kutaisi Chabad community marked the chag hageulah of 12 Tammuz 5692 with a farbrengen at the home of R. Yisrael Liebov's father.
Story: By summer 5692 the Liebov family and additional Anash households had moved to Kutaisi, turning the city into a small Chabad settlement. The chag hageulah of 12 Tammuz was celebrated in the home of R. Yisrael Liebov's parents, a gathering that knit together the underground yeshiva students and the established families.

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe writes about Senator Borah's library intervention
Summary: The Frierdiker Rebbe wrote about US Senator Borah's intervention to recover the Chabad library from the Soviets.
Story: In August 1932, the Frierdiker Rebbe (Rayatz) wrote a letter discussing efforts by US Senator William Borah to recover the Chabad library held by Soviet authorities. The letter appears in his published correspondence (vol. 11, letter 3881). Borah was known for raising religious freedom issues regarding the USSR.
Tags: library, senator borah, schneersohn library, soviet union, lobbying, rayatz

Title: Maharayatz urges Eliezerov to focus on youth and children of Kollel Chabad
Summary: On 6 Menachem Av 5692 Maharayatz wrote to R. Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov urging deeper engagement with the youth, girls and children of Kollel Chabad families.
Story: Beyond his focus on the elders and avreichim, the Rebbe wanted a dedicated vaad to periodically examine children studying in cheders and yeshivos, give prizes for good behavior and excellence in learning, and gently discipline those who needed it. For the older youth he proposed structured study sessions or printed materials to keep them connected to the kollel. The same theme is taken up in his 12 Cheshvan letter to the kollel's nesius committee.

Title: Rebbe sends R. Refael Stein to Vilna region
Summary: On 8 Menachem Av 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz praised R. Refael Stein for his work on the mikveh in Poretz.
Story: Sent on a mission to strengthen Torah and Yiddishkeit in the Vilna region, Stein traveled first to Poretz to address the mikveh there. The Rebbe wrote to him on 8 Menachem Av 5692 (Igros Kodesh vol. 11, letter 3882) expressing great delight at the success of the mikveh effort in Poretz.
Tags: stein, poretz, mikveh, vilna-region

Title: Founding of Kupat Bachurim student welfare fund in Warsaw
Summary: The Kupat Bachurim fund supporting Tomchei Temimim students was established on 15 Av 5692.
Story: On 15 Av 5692, a dedicated fund called Kupat Bachurim was founded to support the bachurim of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw. Its honorary chairman was R. Menachem Mendel Schneerson (the Rebbe's son-in-law), with R. Yechezkel Feigin as chairman.
Tags: warsaw, kupat bachurim, tomchei temimim, poland

Title: Rayatz travels to Ludmir via Brisk and Kovel
Summary: Leaving Druskenig on 23 Av, the Rayatz traveled to Ludmir, stopping along the way in Brisk and Kovel.
Story: Each stop on the journey allowed local communities to receive the Rebbe. The route through Brisk and Kovel passed through major centers of Polish Jewish life.
Tags: ludmir, brisk, kovel, poland

Title: Rebbe directs further travels for R. Refael Stein
Summary: On 22 Menachem Av 5692 the Rebbe wrote to Stein again, noting the Poretz mikveh's expected completion and instructing him on his next trips.
Story: Following up on the Poretz mikveh project, the Rebbe wrote on 22 Menachem Av 5692 (Igros Kodesh vol. 11, letter 3883) that he expected the mikveh to be made fit soon. He decided that Stein should now travel further, with instructions to be communicated by R. Moshe Leib Rothstein. The Rebbe also addressed a letter to all anash in the Vilna region (letter 3884) introducing Stein as his emissary.
Tags: stein, poretz, rothstein, vilna-region

Title: Rebbe Rayatz visits Lodmir in Volhynia
Summary: From 23 Av 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz visited Lodmir for several days, meeting Anash from across the Volhynia region.
Story: Traveling from Druskininkai through Brisk and Kovel, the Rebbe arrived in Lodmir to be greeted by massive crowds requiring police escort. He delivered the maamar 'Re'eh Anochi Notein' before Shabbat at the great synagogue holding two thousand people, addressed an audience of hundreds in Yiddish on the nature of Chassidus, visited the gravesite of Rabbi Shlomo of Karlin, and discussed strengthening the mikveh and establishing a yeshiva with community leaders.
Tags: lodmir, volhynia, wolyn, poland, kovel, lokatch

Title: Rebbe Rayatz makes brief stop in Warsaw en route from Ludomir
Summary: On 28 Menachem Av 5692, the Rebbe Rayatz stopped in Warsaw on his way home from Ludomir to Riga.
Story: On Tuesday 28 Menachem Av 5692 (August 31, 1932), the Rebbe Rayatz made a brief stop in Warsaw while traveling from Ludomir back to his home in Riga. It was one of two short visits to Warsaw in the years immediately preceding his 5693 relocation there.
Tags: warsaw, ludomir, riga, rayatz, fourth visit

Title: Rebbe Rayatz stops in Vilna returning from Lodmir
Summary: On his way back from Lodmir to Riga in early Elul 5692, the Rebbe stopped in Vilna for several days.
Story: Accompanied by his son-in-law Rashag, the Rebbe stayed at the Briston Hotel and prayed at the Apatov Chabad synagogue. He held a third Shabbat meal with senior Chabad rabbis including those of Kornitz, Postov, Doksitz, Dolhinov and Radoshkovitz, received many for yechidus, and visited Rabbi Chaim Ozer Grodzinski and the wealthy chassid Shneur Zalman Zeligson.
Tags: vilna, lithuania, chaim ozer, rashag

Title: Maamar Ani LeDodi delivered in Vilna
Summary: On 6 Elul 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz delivered the maamar 'Ani LeDodi' in Vilna during his stop returning from Lodmir.
Story: During his several-day stop in Vilna on the way back from Lodmir to Riga, the Rebbe Rayatz delivered the maamar 'Ani LeDodi' on Wednesday 6 Elul. The maamar is recorded in the index of the Rebbe's discourses for that period.
Tags: vilna, maamar, elul

Title: Rayatz returns to Riga via Warsaw and Vienna
Summary: The Rayatz arrived back in Riga on 9 Elul after delivering maamarim in Warsaw and Vienna.
Story: The Rayatz used travel stops to deliver chasidic discourses, strengthening the connection of remote communities. The trip closed a summer of extensive movement through Poland, Lithuania, and Austria.
Tags: riga, warsaw, vienna, maamar

Title: Shabbat Teshuvah 5693 spent stranded at Rioni train station
Summary: Sent to Baku by R. Zalman Levitin, the author and Shlomo Matusov returned late and were forced to spend Shabbat Teshuvah 5693 at the Rioni station.
Story: Rumors of an imminent crackdown caused the mashpia to send the author and Shlomo Matusov to Baku, but they could not stay there. Returning on a delayed train they arrived at the Rioni junction just before sunset on erev Shabbat Teshuvah and could not travel the last quarter-hour leg to Kutaisi. They guarded their belongings, davened, and made kiddush on borrowed bread at the station until motzaei Shabbat.
Tags: rioni, georgia, shabbat teshuvah, travel

Title: Simchat Torah 5693 farbrengen at the Liebov home in Kutaisi
Summary: The Kutaisi underground community held the Simchat Torah 5693 farbrengen at the Liebov home and prayed all Shabbatot at Bas-Sheva Lipsker's home.
Story: On Simchat Torah 5693 a farbrengen was held in the Liebov family home, and the weekly Shabbat minyan and learning were hosted by Rebbetzin Bas-Sheva Lipsker, mother of the Lipsker family. The hidden community continued to function despite the rising danger and persistent fears of arrest.
Tags: kutaisi, simchat torah, liebov, georgia

Title: Rebbe Rayatz proposes dismissing R. David Teiblum to cut costs
Summary: On 26 Tishrei 5693 the Rebbe suggested converting R. David Teiblum's class into a mechina under R. Shneur Zalman Gurary to save salary costs.
Story: Facing the financial crunch, the Rebbe Rayatz proposed to the Warsaw administration that R. David Teiblum be released and his class be turned into a mechina taught by R. Shneur Zalman Gurary. The administration ultimately decided it was impossible to dismiss him mid-term and kept the arrangement unchanged.
Tags: warsaw, david teiblum, shneur zalman gurary, finance, poland

Title: R' Schneur Zalman Gourary appointed maggid shiur of upper Mechina class
Summary: At the start of 5693 R' Schneur Zalman Gourary became maggid shiur for the upper Mechina class in Warsaw.
Story: R' Yehuda Eber reported to the Rebbe Rayatz on 7 Marcheshvan 5693 that R' Schneur Zalman Gourary would teach the upper Mechina class while R' Moshe Meirowitz continued the lower class. The two Mechina classes at the Agudas Chabad shul on Dzika 8 had grown to about 50 students.
Tags: warsaw, schneur zalman gourary, tomchei tmimim, mechina, dzika

Title: R. Shmuel Zalmanov resigns from yeshiva administration in Warsaw
Summary: R. Shmuel Zalmanov stepped down as administrator of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw at the start of Kislev 5693 to focus on his private business.
Story: Having taken on private business obligations, R. Shmuel Zalmanov informed the Rebbe at the start of Marcheshvan 5693 that he could no longer manage yeshiva administration. From Rosh Chodesh Kislev he ceased most involvement, and the burden fell on R. Yehuda Eber until a new manager could be appointed.
Tags: warsaw, shmuel zalmanov, tomchei temimim, finance, poland

Title: Yeshiva Warsaw faces severe financial crisis at start of 5693
Summary: R. Shmuel Zalmanov reported to the Rebbe on 5 Marcheshvan 5693 that the yeshiva treasury was empty and the administration was considering downsizing.
Story: Facing crushing debts and humiliating creditor pressure, the yeshiva leadership concluded on Sunday before 5 Marcheshvan 5693 that they would have to reduce the institution's size. Not a single coin remained in the treasury, and they could not even begin to cover daily expenses.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei temimim, finance, crisis, poland

Title: Riga yeshivah opens then closes within months
Summary: The Riga Tomchei Temimim yeshivah, opened by Latvian Chasidim in 1932 to keep the Rebbe nearby, closed by 10 Marcheshvan 5693.
Story: Following the success of the Warsaw visit, Riga Chasidim mobilized to establish their own yeshivah hoping it would anchor the Rebbe in Latvia. Students came from chasidic backgrounds via Lithuanian yeshivas, but the effort was short-lived. The Evening Post reported its closure in November, and Feigin later wrote that students were unable to secure military service deferments.

Title: Three students dispatched from Kutaisi to Kulashi for 19 Kislev 5693
Summary: Fearing arrests in Kutaisi, R. Zalman Levitin sent the author, Yitzchak Hakohen Shtetin, and Avraham Kievman to Kulashi around 19 Kislev 5693.
Story: As the GPU crackdown intensified, the Haditcher dispersed students to lower-profile locations. The three were warmly received in Kulashi and learned in a tiny shul lit by a single kerosene lamp. Avraham Kievman was an extreme masmid who balanced his oil lamp by the clock so he could rise at 5 a.m. and continue until past midnight.

Title: R' Chaim Shpreyreg, Vilna yeshiva committee member, passes away
Summary: R' Chaim ben Yehuda Shpreyreg, a member of the Vilna yeshiva committee, passed away on 25 Kislev 5693.
Story: R' Chaim Shpreyreg served on the founding executive committee of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim and was remembered with blessing for his contributions to the institution until his passing on 25 Kislev 5693.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, yahrzeit

Title: Anash families begin leaving Russia for Eretz Yisrael
Summary: Between 5693 and 5698, many Anash families succeeded in leaving Russia for the Land of Israel, settling mainly in Tel Aviv.
Story: During the years 5693–5698 (1933–1938), many Lubavitcher families managed to leave the Soviet Union and immigrate to the Land of Israel. They settled mainly in Tel Aviv, where they founded a cheder and a Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch yeshiva.

Title: Chassidim in Russia begin sending photos to Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: In summer 5693 Chassidim in Russia began the practice of sending personal photos to the Rebbe Rayatz.
Story: In the summer of 5693 (1933), several years after the Rebbe Rayatz was forced to leave Russia and settled in Riga, a custom arose among anash in Russia of sending personal photographs to the Rebbe. Persecution of Chabad in Russia was intensifying, and the Rebbe encouraged the practice in a general letter (Igros Kodesh II, no. 633), writing that seeing the families' faces brought him great joy.

Title: Expansion of Chassidus study program for yeshiva students in Brooklyn
Summary: The author expanded a Chassidus study program for yeshiva students into multiple weekly sessions of Tanya and maamarim.
Story: Beginning with a Motzaei Shabbat Tanya class accompanied by stories of Lubavitch, the program grew to weekday classes on maamarim received from Europe and on Likutei Dibburim. The author also traveled twice weekly to the Division Ave Shtibel in Williamsburg to teach students. Participants included Avraham M.M. Barnetzki, Meir Greenberg, Menachem Mendel Feldman, and Yitzchak Kaladny.

Title: Holodomor famine grips Ukraine while Kiev yeshiva learns 5693
Summary: A devastating Stalin-imposed famine struck Ukraine in 5693 even as the harvest was strong, forcing yeshiva students to scheme to get bread.
Story: Although 5693 was a year of abundant harvest, Stalin's decrees caused mass starvation in Ukraine. Yeshiva students stood in bread lines for days, taking multiple places in the queue to feed the chevra. The young Jewish father-and-son bakers serving bread quietly risked their own safety by repeatedly handing out loaves to the bearded bochurim.

Title: New Colel Chabad charter formalized
Summary: The governance and financial reforms the Rebbe Rayatz had requested were codified in a new Colel Chabad charter.
Story: Among the changes: procedures to ensure monies received from overseas were properly recorded, and financial statements submitted to the board. Rabbi Shlomo Leib Eliazrov, appointed as chairman during the Rebbe's 1929 Jerusalem visit, oversaw the new structure.

Title: R' Avraham Naftali Goldberg publishes Maaseh Zayit
Summary: In 5693 R' Avraham Naftali Hirtzka Goldberg published Maaseh Zayit, chiddushim and derashot on the midrashim of the weekly parshiot with halachic notes.
Story: Goldberg, then teaching the lower class at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw, also prepared a companion volume Yad LeKiddushin on Tractate Kiddushin, which did not appear in his lifetime and was finally published in Tel Aviv in 5746.

Title: R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie heads Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw mechina
Summary: At the start of 5693 R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie was appointed to head the preparatory division (mechina) of the Warsaw yeshiva.
Story: At the start of 5693 (autumn 1932) R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie was appointed head of the mechina — the preparatory division of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw, then located at Maranow 9 with two classes. The appointment marked his transition from senior student to leadership within the yeshiva system. He would soon take on broader organizational roles.

Title: R' Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz turns against Chabad influence at Torah Vodaas
Summary: Torah Vodaas head R' Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz, alarmed at growing Chabad influence on his students, attached a group of them to R' Chaim Avraham Dov Levin (the Malach).
Story: After introducing Kuzari, Chovos Halevavos, Noam Elimelech and Tanya into Torah Vodaas, Mendlowitz objected to the author 'turning students into Lubavitcher chassidim.' He led a group of students, joined by several baalei batim, to R' Chaim Avraham Dov Levin — the Malach — who served as rav in the Nusach Ha'ari shul in the Bronx. R' Moshe David Rivkin was later sent to ask the author to stop teaching Chassidus to the students.

Title: R' Yechezkel Himelstein perishes in Holocaust
Summary: In 5693 R' Yechezkel Himelstein emigrated from Russia to Riga and headed a Tomchei Tmimim branch in Dankra, Latvia, where he later perished in the Holocaust.
Story: R' Yechezkel Himelstein, who had served as general manager and mashgiach over the shiurim and chadarim in Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch from 5671, continued in this role through Kremenchug and managed branches in Polotsk, Homel and Cherson. In 5693 (1933) he emigrated from Russia to Riga and headed the Tomchei Tmimim branch in Dankra, Latvia, where he perished in the Shoah.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, himelstein, latvia, holocaust, dankra

Title: R' Yitzchak Hamasmid Horowitz arrives in USA as Rebbe's shadar
Summary: The renowned chassid R' Yitzchak Horowitz (Hamasmid) arrived in America as a shadar of the Rebbe Rayatz before Rosh Hashana 5694.
Story: Coming on a mission related to Maamad (financial support for the Rebbe), he lodged at the author's home during his stay. After his visit he returned to Riga and corresponded with the author. His presence helped consolidate Chabad activity in New York.
Tags: yitzchak hamasmid, horowitz, shadar, maamad, riga, fundraising

Title: R. Elchanan Yakubovitz emigrates to the Land of Israel
Summary: In 5693 R. Elchanan Yakubovitz emigrated to Eretz Yisrael and settled in Jerusalem.
Story: In 5693 (1933) R. Elchanan Yakubovitz left Latvia for Eretz Yisrael, settling in Jerusalem. There he published the second volume of Even Shimon and remained until his death. He represents one of the few Lubavitch-era rabbinical figures whose career spanned both the late Russian period and the British Mandate yishuv.

Title: Ramash and Chaya Mushka leave Berlin for Paris
Summary: As the Nazi threat began to grow, the Ramash and Chaya Mushka left Berlin and after a brief interlude in Riga resettled in Paris.
Story: In Paris, the Ramash pursued a degree in engineering. He continued attending classes at European universities and remained involved in the Rebbe's affairs from a distance, exchanging hundreds of letters with his father-in-law about Chabad theology, history, and practical matters.

Title: Rayatz settles in Warsaw after emigrating from Riga
Summary: At the end of 5693, the Rebbe Rayatz moved his residence from Riga to Warsaw.
Story: After several years of leading Chabad from Riga, where he had settled following his release from Soviet imprisonment, the Rebbe Rayatz relocated to Warsaw in late summer 1933. The transition marked a new phase of his European leadership, though he continued to visit Riga and maintain close ties with the chassidim there.
Tags: rayatz, warsaw, riga, latvia, poland, emigration

Title: Reb Itche der Masmid arrives in New York as Rebbe's emissary
Summary: Rabbi Yitzchak Horowitz, the first of the Rebbe's American emissaries, arrived in New York a few weeks before the High Holidays of 1933.
Story: Celebrated for his diligence and piety, Reb Itche spent two years in the US teaching Chasidism and raising funds for the Rebbe's European work. The New York Chabad community borrowed money to gather $5,000 for his mission. He visited Boston and other cities, deeply impressing all who met him; the Rebbe later wanted to send him again but could not secure a visa.
Tags: america, new-york, shadar, fundraising, horowitz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz moves from Riga to Warsaw
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz relocated from Riga to Warsaw in 5693, again moving the library with him.
Story: In 5693 (1933), the Rebbe Rayatz left Riga for Warsaw, Poland. The cherished books and manuscripts of the Chabad Rebbeim accompanied him on this next stage of his wanderings, an exile that would continue as conditions in Europe deteriorated.
Tags: riga, warsaw, poland, library, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz relocates from Riga to Warsaw
Summary: In the late summer of 5693 the Rebbe Rayatz moved from Riga to Warsaw to live in proximity to the central yeshiva.
Story: After years of leading the movement from Riga, the Rebbe Rayatz moved to Warsaw in late summer 5693 to be near Tomchei Temimim. This ended the need for the lengthy written correspondence between the Rebbe and the yeshiva administration that had marked the previous years.
Tags: warsaw, riga, rayatz, poland, latvia

Title: Rebbe relocates from Latvia to Poland
Summary: Six years after arriving in Riga, the Rebbe moves his residence to Poland.
Story: Riga had served as a base for years of travel and recovery, but Poland — home to a vast Jewish population and the growing Warsaw yeshivah — became the next station. The yeshivah was eventually based in the suburb of Otwock.
Tags: poland, otwock, latvia, rayatz

Title: Rebbe relocates from Riga to Poland
Summary: After six years in Latvia, the Rebbe relocates his court to Poland.
Story: Throughout his Riga years the Rebbe's stationery read 'Riga, temporary.' Permanence remained elusive: 'The Rebbe resided in Riga for six years and during that extended time, no decision was made on his permanent place of residence,' wrote chasidic historian Rabbi Sholom Ber Levin. Poland too would only provide a home for a few years.
Tags: riga, poland, warsaw, otwock, relocation

Title: Rebbe travels to Berlin for medical treatment
Summary: In the winter of 5693, after his condition worsened and his voice weakened, the Rebbe traveled to Berlin to consult the leading specialists, including Professor Loewy.
Story: The Berlin doctors concluded they could not identify the underlying illness and that the Rebbe required ongoing expert supervision. From Berlin the Rebbe continued to Paris for further consultations before returning to Riga in late Adar.
Tags: berlin, germany, health, loewy

Title: United States extends diplomatic recognition to Soviet Union
Summary: US diplomatic recognition of the Soviet Union, which had been withheld since the Bolshevik revolution, finally came in 1933.
Story: The absence of US recognition was a key part of Soviet diplomatic isolation in 1927, alongside the British rupture. That isolation made the Latvia trade deal — and Mordechai Dubin's leverage — crucial to securing the Rebbe's exit visa.
Tags: america, soviet union, diplomacy

Title: US recognizes Soviet Union; Rebbe's religious-freedom campaign fails
Summary: The Rebbe launched a global campaign pressuring the US to condition Soviet recognition on religious freedom, but the Roosevelt administration declined.
Story: Russian Foreign Minister Maxim Litvinov traveled to Washington to negotiate diplomatic recognition. The Rebbe drafted seven demands and mobilized leaders including Chaim Ozer Grodzinski, Nahum Sokolow, Rabbi Eliezer Silver, and US Senators Borah and King. The US declined to make recognition contingent on Jewish religious freedom, securing only a concession for visiting American citizens.
Tags: soviet-union, russia, religious-freedom, litvinov, roosevelt, jdc

Title: Warsaw Haggadah 'Tiferet Ish' by Alter Yisrael Shimon Perlov of Novominsk
Summary: The 'Tiferet Ish' Haggadah by Alter Yisrael Shimon Perlov of Novominsk was published in Warsaw with an appendix on Chad Gadya by Mordechai of Chernobyl.
Story: In 5693 (1933), the Haggadah 'Tiferet Ish' by Rebbe Alter Yisrael Shimon ben Yaakov Perlov of Novominsk was published in Warsaw by the Feder Brothers. The 96-plus-24-page octavo edition included a brief manuscript work by the author on Shir HaShirim and concluded with a commentary on Chad Gadya by his ancestor Rebbe Mordechai of Chernobyl. It represented the Novominsk Chassidic dynasty's interpretive tradition.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, novominsk, warsaw, perlov, chernobyl

Title: Yehuda Eber transferred from Vilna to Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw
Summary: In 5693 R' Yehuda Eber was appointed spiritual director of the central Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Warsaw, ending his tenure in Vilna.
Story: Eber had run the Vilna branch since his appointment in 5691. His move to Warsaw placed him at the head of Tomchei Tmimim's flagship institution in interwar Poland. The Vilna branch continued under Eliyahu Weitz and the local committee.
Tags: yehuda eber, tomchei tmimim, warsaw, vilna

Title: Kuperstock installed in Globoke after two-year delay
Summary: After the Globoke opposition forced a two-year postponement, R. Kuperstock was finally installed as rabbi of the Chabad community in the winter of 5693.
Story: Following the violent rejection of his appointment, the decision was made to keep Kuperstock in Fastov for two more years. In the winter of 5693 (1933) he was at last accepted as the rabbi of the chassidic community in Globoke, where he then served for two years.
Tags: kuperstock, globoke, appointment

Title: Rebbe Rayatz enters Berlin clinic for medical treatment
Summary: In January 1933 the Rebbe spent two months in a Berlin clinic seeking diagnosis for his deteriorating speech and weakness.
Story: After his return from America the Rebbe's speech had slowly changed. Riga doctors urged him to Berlin's superior medical resources. The renowned Professor Leve and other experts could not identify the illness but recommended ongoing medical supervision. His son-in-law Menachem Mendel visited daily.
Tags: berlin, germany, health, professor-leve

Title: Rebbe Rayatz stays in Berlin for medical treatment
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz began a two-month stay in Berlin for medical care, during which the Ramash was at his side as informal secretary.
Story: Throughout the 1930s, as the Rebbe sought medical care in Berlin, Vienna, Paris, and Marienbad, the Ramash accompanied him. These extended periods together provided extensive opportunities for mentorship, conversation, and assistance with correspondence and other affairs.
Tags: berlin, germany, medical, mentorship

Title: Rayatz travels to Berlin for medical care
Summary: The Rayatz traveled from Riga to Berlin on 12 Tevet for approximately two months of medical care.
Story: His arrival in Berlin came just as Adolf Hitler's rise to power approached its peak; the Nazis would take control of Germany weeks later. The Rayatz nonetheless spent two months there receiving treatment before continuing his European travels.
Tags: berlin, germany, health

Title: Kulashi students arrested by drunk Communist officials at night
Summary: A drunk Georgian Communist council head, a GPU agent, and other officials spotted lamplight in the Kulashi shul and arrested the three sleeping bochurim.
Story: Walking home after a drinking party in Shevat 5693, the local officials noticed the elevated lamp glowing in the closed shul and burst in to arrest the students. They were held overnight in freezing police cells where local women came in the morning to weep at seeing them through the cracks, then transferred to the district prison in Samtredia where the warden slapped the tall author across the face on arrival.
Tags: kulashi, georgia, gpu, arrest, samtredia

Title: Author's father Ephraim Shmuel passes away on 15 Shevat 5693
Summary: While back in Kutaisi after his escape from Samtredia prison, the author received a telegram that his father Ephraim Shmuel had died on 15 Shevat 5693.
Story: After being put on a transport to Ukraine, the author escaped at Sharafan station by hiding inside an iron staircase and Georgian Jews smuggled him back to Sachkhere. Back in Kutaisi a telegram arrived informing him that his father Ephraim Shmuel had passed away on 15 Shevat, and he sat shiva in the Kutaisi shul.
Tags: family, death, kutaisi

Title: Death of Ephraim Shmuel Levin in Lipovets
Summary: Ephraim Shmuel ben Yosef, the author's father, died on 15 Shevat 5693 in Lipovets, leaving his widow Leah Beila to support four orphans.
Story: Ephraim Shmuel had taught Torah in Lipovets with great devotion, refusing to allow his daughters to attend Soviet schools even under threat of fines. His widow Leah Beila was sickly with heart disease and struggled to support the younger children Sarah, Rivka, and Freide. The eldest son Yosef was then nearing twenty-five and Yisrael Yehuda was about twenty-one.
Tags: lipovets, yahrzeit, ephraim shmuel levin

Title: Passing of R. Ephraim Shmuel Levin
Summary: R. Ephraim Shmuel Levin, father of the chassid Yisrael Yehuda Levin, passed away on 15 Shevat 5693.
Story: On 15 Shevat 5693 R. Ephraim Shmuel Levin passed away, leaving his wife Leah Beila a widow with three daughters and two sons. The author's brother Yosef and sister Sara Yehudit were studying in Kharkov to become a doctor and nurse, while the family pressed the author to abandon yeshiva study and find work. This bereavement and family pressure would later push the author to write to the Rebbe Rayatz for guidance and support.
Tags: levin family, russia, ephraim shmuel levin, tu bishvat

Title: Rayatz visits Riga from Warsaw, 12-20 Adar
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz returned from Warsaw to visit Riga, staying from 12-20 Adar 5693.
Story: Shortly after relocating to Warsaw, the Rebbe traveled back to Riga for a nine-day visit covering Purim. He recited the maamar 'Zachor Es Asher Asah Lecha Amalek' on the night of his arrival, delivered a talk to the women later published in Likkutei Dibburim vol. 3, and farbrenged at length with the temimim and anash on Shabbos.
Tags: rayatz, riga, latvia, purim, visit

Title: Rayatz returns to Riga from Paris
Summary: After traveling from Berlin to Paris in March 1933, the Rayatz returned to Riga on 23 Adar.
Story: This trip wove together stops in Berlin, Paris, and Riga, reflecting both medical needs and communal obligations. Paris would later host a sanitorium that the Rayatz visited repeatedly.
Tags: riga, paris, france

Title: Rebbe details cataloging priorities for the library
Summary: On 23 Adar 5693 the Frierdiker Rebbe described the library's cataloging order: Yiddish, sacred works, secular Hebrew, broadsides, then catalogues.
Story: Writing from Riga, the Rebbe acknowledged that comprehensive cataloging remained far off. Only a partial typed inventory existed, prepared by R. Chaim Liberman, used principally to know which holy books still needed acquiring. The Rebbe sketched the planned cataloging sequence by category, reflecting his ongoing struggle to bring scholarly order to the collection.
Tags: riga, library, rayatz, cataloging, yiddish, hebrew-secular

Title: Rebbe returns to Riga from Paris
Summary: On 23 Adar 5693 the Rebbe returned to Riga after his medical consultations in Berlin and Paris.
Story: Despite treatments through the spring and summer, his health did not noticeably improve. The doctors insisted he travel to a spa, and that summer he went to Marienbad for therapy.
Tags: paris, riga, health

Title: Faigin reports on Rebbe's Riga visit to Jacobson
Summary: Secretary Yechezkel Faigin wrote to R. Yisrael Jacobson on 26 Adar 5693 describing the Rebbe's recent visit to Riga.
Story: Faigin reported that the chassidic community in Riga had grown with newly arrived refugees from Russia, including R. Shlomo Tumarkin, Michael Dvorkin, and R. Rafael Cohen. They had established a shul named for the Rebbe with daily Gemara and Chassidus shiurim, plus chadarim for children and adults.
Tags: faigin, jacobson, riga, shul, russian-refugees

Title: Rayatz writes to son-in-law on Erev Rosh Chodesh Nissan
Summary: On 29 Adar 5693 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his son-in-law (later Rebbe) describing the Riga visit.
Story: The letter (vol. 15, no. 5533) recounts the warm reception by the young temimim, the recital of maamarim including 'V'Hayah Kaasher Yarim Moshe', the Purim seudah lasting past midnight, and the Shabbos meals among anash that ran far longer than usual.
Tags: rayatz, rebbe-menachem-mendel, riga, letter, purim

Title: Author smuggles shemurah flour by train from Georgia to Kiev
Summary: Fleeing the Pesach 5693 arrests, the author traveled by rail to Kiev carrying shemurah flour from harvest-time despite repeated NKVD inspections.
Story: He boarded the train carrying flour that was shemurah from the time of cutting, a stricter standard than what was available in Kiev. The flour bundle was searched multiple times during the multi-day journey but he reached Kiev safely. The matzot baked from his flour were divided among all ten bochurim of the Kiev yeshiva for the sedarim.
Tags: kiev, ukraine, georgia, shemurah, matzah, escape

Title: Mass arrest of Anash and yeshiva students on Erev Pesach 5693 in Kutaisi
Summary: On Erev Pesach 5693 many Kutaisi Anash and yeshiva students were arrested, including the mashpia R. Zalman 'Haditcher' Levitin.
Story: The Soviet authorities swept through Kutaisi just before Pesach 5693, seizing many chassidim and bochurim along with the yeshiva's mashpia, director, and mentor R. Zalman Levitin. The older bochurim were already imprisoned by the NKVD in Batumi. Any students who remained free had no choice but to flee.
Tags: kutaisi, georgia, gpu, arrest, zalman levitin, pesach

Title: Rebbe writes Persitz soliciting books for library
Summary: On 3 Iyar 5693 the Rebbe wrote to publisher Shoshana Persitz asking that every publisher honor the Lubavitch library with copies of their books.
Story: The Rebbe explained that he was a collector of everything printed in Hebrew letters regardless of subject, and considered it fitting for publishers to gift the Lubavitch book-collection with their imprints. The note was one of many sent over years in which the Rebbe personally enlisted authors and publishers to enlarge the library at minimal cost.
Tags: library, rayatz, shoshana-persitz, book-collecting, publishers

Title: Rebbe asks R. Stein to push Freidin's election in Fastov
Summary: On 6 Iyar 5693 the Rebbe wrote to R. Refael Stein, asking him to travel to Fastov and urge the chassidim to elect R. Yehuda Leib Freidin as Kuperstock's successor.
Story: With Kuperstock to be relocated, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote on 6 Iyar 5693 (Igros Kodesh vol. 11, letter 3888) asking R. Refael Stein to travel to Fastov and remind the chassidim of their duty to choose a chassidic rabbi from anash. He specifically endorsed R. Yehuda Leib Freidin for the role.
Tags: fastov, freidin, stein, rabbinic-selection

Title: R. Yehuda Eber appointed director of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw
Summary: On 11 Iyar 5693 the Rebbe Rayatz formally appointed R. Yehuda Eber as overall director of the Warsaw yeshiva, in addition to his role as rosh yeshiva.
Story: After R. Yehuda Eber visited the Rebbe in Riga during Nisan 5693, the Rebbe gave him authority over the yeshiva's entire operation, including budget and personnel. The formal appointment letter was issued on 11 Iyar 5693, empowering him to manage all aspects of the institution and to correspond with donors.
Tags: warsaw, yehuda eber, tomchei temimim, poland

Title: Library acknowledges Iyar 5693 book donations
Summary: On 29 Iyar 5693 the Frierdiker Rebbe confirmed receipt of donated books for the library on its newly printed institutional stationery.
Story: Using letterhead headed 'Aseifas Sefarim u'Kisvei Yad Lubavitch — temporarily in Riga, Latvia,' the Rebbe acknowledged a recent shipment with thanks. The stationery, envelopes and postcards bearing this header were one of several mechanisms — alongside newspaper advertisements — used to formalize the library as an institution rather than a private collection.
Tags: riga, library, rayatz, book-donations

Title: Shavuos farbrengen with yeshiva students sparks public scandal
Summary: A Shavuos farbrengen at the author's home where bochurim tasted mashke for the first time provoked a public outcry in Brownsville.
Story: At the gathering R' Yochanan Gordon and his brother R' Yitzchak Yaakov Gordon participated; the boys, seated on the floor, were given mashke two or three times. News quickly spread that 'R' Yisroel Jacobson had gotten the boys drunk,' causing an uproar throughout Brownsville and the Williamsburg yeshiva. Parents from non-Chabad backgrounds began visiting the author's home to understand his influence on their sons.
Tags: shavuos, farbrengen, torah vodaas, brownsville, mashke, yochanan gordon

Title: R. Yehuda Leib Freidin elected rabbi of Fastov
Summary: By mid-Sivan 5693, R. Yehuda Leib Freidin had been elected rabbi of Fastov, as reported by R. Yehuda Eber and noted in 'Shaarei Tziyon'.
Story: R. Yehuda Eber, head of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw, wrote to the Rebbe on 12 Sivan 5693 reporting that Freidin had been elected rabbi in Fastov. The journal 'Shaarei Tziyon' (vol. 13, no. 6-12) also announced his appointment. The general kehilla's rabbi, R. Shmuel Dovid Walkin, initially opposed it and even summoned Freidin to a din torah in Vilna, but tensions eventually subsided.
Tags: fastov, freidin, rabbinic-election, shaarei-tziyon

Title: R. Yisrael Eber proposes new Otwock branch on 12 Sivan 5693
Summary: On 12 Sivan 5693, Rosh Yeshiva R. Yisrael Eber reported a possible new Tomchei Tmimim branch in Otwock built on a local yeshiva ketana of 35 students.
Story: Eber wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe describing a local Otwock yeshiva of about 35 students, previously funded by the late gvir R. Shlomo Goldberg, whose heirs would only give 400 zlotys monthly per his will. The local teachers proposed merging with Tomchei Tmimim provided the name retained a reference to Goldberg, but the plan ultimately did not materialize.
Tags: poland, otwock, yisrael eber, shlomo goldberg, yeshiva ketana

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes about move to Poland for sake of yeshiva
Summary: On 26 Sivan 5693, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his son-in-law (later the Rebbe) expressing his hope to relocate to Poland to be near the yeshiva.
Story: After years of failed plans to bring Tomchei Temimim closer to him (Riga in 1931, Otwock in 1931), the Rebbe Rayatz finally decided to move from Riga to Warsaw. In this letter he wrote of his 'innermost yearning' to dwell amid the tent and surroundings of Torah, identifying proximity to the yeshiva as the central motivation for the move.
Tags: warsaw, poland, tomchei-temimim, rayatz, letter

Title: Rebbe receives Latvian citizenship clearing way for Polish move
Summary: On 26 Sivan 5693 the Rebbe wrote that the Latvian citizenship he had been waiting for had finally been granted, enabling him to proceed with the relocation to Poland.
Story: The Rebbe explained to his daughter that he had nearly decided in favor of the move the previous summer in Druskininkai, but had waited several months for citizenship to simplify his future Polish residency. With citizenship now in hand, he expected to carry out the move successfully.
Tags: latvia, citizenship, poland, letter

Title: Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5693 farbrengen at R. Zalman Moshe in Ilyinka
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5693 the author traveled from Moscow to Ilyinka with R. Dovber Gurevitch to farbreng at R. Zalman Moshe Yitzchaki's home.
Story: Having arrived in Moscow at the end of Sivan to raise funds for the Kiev yeshiva, the author joined R. Dovber Gurevitch on Rosh Chodesh Tammuz for a major farbrengen in Ilyinka. R. Yaakov Gurkov of Kharkov attended as well. R. Zalman Moshe explained that the simcha of preparation for 12 Tammuz must begin already on Rosh Chodesh.
Tags: ilyinka, moscow, zalman moshe yitzchaki, tammuz, 12 tammuz

Title: Rayatz leaves Riga permanently
Summary: The Rayatz departed Riga on July 4, 1933, leaving Latvia permanently though the move was not publicly announced.
Story: After years based in Riga, the Rayatz quietly relocated his residence to Warsaw. He stopped first at the Warsaw yeshiva to lead a farbrengen, then continued to Marienbad before formally settling in Warsaw later that summer.
Tags: riga, latvia, warsaw, poland, relocation

Title: Rebbe departs Riga for Marienbad via Warsaw
Summary: On 10 Tammuz 5693 the Rebbe left Riga, visiting the Warsaw yeshiva on 12 Tammuz and arriving in Marienbad on 13 Tammuz for spa treatment.
Story: Doctors had warned of severe consequences if the Rebbe did not travel to a spa. He had nonetheless delivered Chassidus on Shavuos against medical advice, with no apparent ill effects. During the stop in Warsaw he gave the Warsaw vaad their first private notice of his decision to settle in the city.
Tags: marienbad, warsaw, riga, health

Title: Rebbe travels to Warsaw and on to Marienbad
Summary: On 10 Tammuz 5693 the Frierdiker Rebbe departed Riga, stopping at the Warsaw yeshiva on 12 Tammuz and arriving in Marienbad on 13 Tammuz for medical treatment.
Story: Doctors insisted the ailing Rebbe travel to the Marienbad spa. With great difficulty Lubavitch chassidim raised the funds for the trip. R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote that the Rebbe left Riga on 10 Tammuz, visited the yeshiva in Warsaw on 12 Tammuz, and arrived in Marienbad on 13 Tammuz to begin medical care during the deepest months of the economic depression.
Tags: warsaw, marienbad, rayatz, illness, yeshiva

Title: Rayatz leads farbrengen at Warsaw yeshiva en route to Marienbad
Summary: Passing through Warsaw on his way to Marienbad, the Rayatz led a farbrengen at the yeshiva.
Story: The Warsaw yeshiva, a flagship of Tomchei Temimim outside the USSR, would soon become the Rayatz's home base. His farbrengen on the way to Marienbad already signaled the deepening relationship.
Tags: warsaw, poland, yeshiva, farbrengen, tomchei temimim

Title: 12 Tammuz 5693 farbrengen in Malachovka with new maamar from Rayatz
Summary: Anash gathered in Malachovka for 12 Tammuz 5693 received the maamar 'Nasata Lirei'echa Nes Lehisnoses' from the Frierdiker Rebbe.
Story: An exceptional farbrengen brought together R. Zalman Moshe Yitzchaki, R. Shmuel Levitin, R. Shmuel Aba Dolitzky, and many younger Anash. The newly arrived maamar 'Nasata Lirei'echa Nes Lehisnoses' from the Frierdiker Rebbe was studied at length and Anash drank substantial mashke in celebration.
Tags: malachovka, moscow, 12 tammuz, rayatz, frierdiker rebbe, maamar

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe plans to relocate from Riga to Warsaw, 12 Tammuz 5693
Summary: A letter from R. Yehuda Eber read at the Malachovka 12 Tammuz 5693 farbrengen announced the Frierdiker Rebbe's intent to move from Riga to Warsaw.
Story: R. Shmuel Levitin read aloud a letter from R. Yehuda Eber reporting that the Frierdiker Rebbe planned to relocate his residence from Riga to Warsaw and required $1,500 for the move. The Rebbe requested that the relocation expenses be covered by the Moscow-area Anash, which they apparently quietly fulfilled.
Tags: riga, warsaw, rayatz, frierdiker rebbe, latvia, poland, yehuda eber

Title: Rebbe Rayatz stops in Warsaw en route to Marienbad
Summary: On 12 Tamuz 5693, the Rebbe Rayatz stopped in Warsaw for two days while traveling from Riga to Marienbad.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz left Riga on 10 Tamuz 5693 and arrived in Warsaw on 12 Tamuz (July 6, 1933) for a two-day stop that included a visit to the yeshiva. He continued onward to Marienbad on 13 Tamuz. This was the last of his short visits before relocating to Warsaw permanently later that year.
Tags: warsaw, marienbad, riga, rayatz, fifth visit

Title: Rayatz arrives in Marienbad for extended stay
Summary: The Rayatz arrived in Marienbad on 13 Tamuz for a six-week health-focused stay.
Story: His Marienbad stays were a fixed feature of his European years. He remained there until 29 Av before officially moving to Warsaw.
Tags: marienbad, czechoslovakia, health

Title: Rebbe begins apartment search for Warsaw move
Summary: On 22 Tammuz 5693, writing from Marienbad to R. Y. Y. Gourary, the Rebbe directed the start of organized preparations for moving his household to Warsaw.
Story: The Rebbe instructed that the practical apartment search should be deferred until mid-Av while financial and organizational arrangements were settled first. From Marienbad over the next several weeks the Rebbe coordinated by detailed correspondence all the logistics of the relocation.
Tags: warsaw, marienbad, letter, gourary

Title: Rebbe pushes Faigin on Agudas Nashim expansion
Summary: On 26 Tammuz 5693 the Rebbe wrote to Faigin urging serious action on establishing Agudas Nashim chapters everywhere possible.
Story: The Rebbe expressed frustration: 'I already spoke with R. Mordechai Leib about this in Druzgenik - that they needed to establish Agudas Nshei Yisrael in every possible place... But to my regret all proposals for work and action remain only on paper as good intentions. Going forward, with G-d's help, this general matter must be rectified.'
Tags: rayatz, faigin, agudas-nashim, expansion

Title: Rebbe Rayatz instructs Rosh Yeshiva to organize Warsaw move
Summary: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Menachem Av 5693 the Rebbe wrote to Rosh Yeshiva R. Yehuda Eber urging diligent preparations to relocate the yeshiva.
Story: With the move to Warsaw finalized, the Rebbe instructed R. Yehuda Eber to seek a suitable courtyard with multiple apartments for the yeshiva and its officials. He emphasized that the relocation was specifically to spread Torah 'in the spirit of Tomchei Temimim of Lubavitch' — not a yeshiva that merely bore the name.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-temimim, yehuda-eber, rayatz, letter

Title: Rebbe directs library packing for Warsaw move
Summary: From Marienbad on 3 Menachem-Av 5693 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote his two Riga secretaries with detailed instructions for crating and shipping the library to Warsaw.
Story: In separate letters to R. Chaim Liberman and R. Moshe Leib Rothstein, the Rebbe specified wooden-box packing, censorship approvals, freight-company arrangements and even the labeling — directing that crates be numbered rather than marked 'Bibliotheca Lubavitch.' A subsequent letter on 22 Av to the Rebbetzin added detailed instructions about manuscript shipment and the yellow case of his father's writings.
Tags: riga, warsaw, library, rayatz, relocation

Title: Rebbe relocates from Riga to Warsaw
Summary: In August 1933 the Sixth Rebbe relocated from Riga to Warsaw to be near the yeshivah and strengthen chasidic life in Poland.
Story: The move placed him at the center of Polish chasidic life for the rest of the decade. He moved again to Otwock in 1934 for health reasons, where he remained until German bombs forced him back into Warsaw at the outbreak of World War II.
Tags: riga, warsaw, poland, yeshivas tomchei temimim

Title: R' Mordechai Mentlik dispatched to Krakow for outreach work
Summary: In late summer 5693 the Rebbe selected R' Mordechai Mentlik to spend weeks teaching the Chassidus circle of avreichim in Krakow.
Story: On 14 Menachem Av 5693 the Rebbe wrote to Rosh Yeshiva R' Yehuda Eber proposing such a mission, offering to fund up to 100 zloty, and noting that the local circle led by R' Michael Zeligson studied Chassidus twice weekly. By 23 Av the Rebbe had settled on Mentlik and authorized an expanded budget of 125 zloty. The students later recalled this mission in a 18 Elul 5701 letter from Shanghai, when one of the avreichim from that Krakow circle resurfaced as a refugee in the Far East.
Tags: poland, krakow, tomchei temimim, mordechai mentlik, yehuda eber, michael zeligson, rayatz

Title: Rayatz officially relocates to Warsaw
Summary: Leaving Marienbad on 29 Av, the Rayatz settled in Warsaw as his new permanent residence.
Story: Warsaw replaced Riga as the seat of the sixth Rebbe. The move strengthened his ties to Polish Chasidim and centered Chabad operations in the heart of European Jewry.
Tags: warsaw, poland, relocation

Title: Rebbe arrives in Warsaw to settle permanently
Summary: On 1 Elul 5693 the Rebbe arrived directly from Marienbad in Warsaw, beginning his residence in Poland.
Story: He had written on Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul that he was leaving for Warsaw that day. Upon arrival he reported that the trip went well and that several apartment options were under discussion. The struggle to find a suitable apartment would dominate the next month.
Tags: warsaw, marienbad, poland, emigration

Title: Warsaw apartment search proves difficult
Summary: On 9 Elul 5693 the Rebbe wrote that he had been alternating between Warsaw and Otwock searching for an apartment, with rental terms heavy and no final agreement reached.
Story: He had been staying at the Wiederszal pension in Otwock during the search. By 20 Elul a suitable apartment in Warsaw had been arranged and renovations begun. The Rebbe's family arrived in Warsaw on 21 Elul, but the renovations were not yet complete.
Tags: warsaw, otwock, apartment, letter

Title: HaPardes advertisement solicits donations for Lubavitch library
Summary: In Elul 5693 the journal HaPardes carried an advertisement thanking authors and publishers for sending their works to the Lubavitch library and requesting future donations.
Story: Dictated by the Rebbe himself and signed in the library's institutional name rather than his own, the notice appeared in the American journal HaPardes and listed the Riga address Pulko, Briero 10/5. It instructed rabbis, authors, publishers, and printers to send every imprint — books, broadsides, posters and notices alike — to the library, formalizing its public-institution character.
Tags: library, rayatz, hapardes, advertisement, publishers, usa

Title: Rebbe Rayatz moves to Warsaw
Summary: In September 1933, after securing Latvian citizenship, the Rebbe completed his relocation from Riga to Warsaw.
Story: The Rebbe had delayed the move until obtaining a Latvian passport, which would later prove lifesaving during the Nazi invasion. He spent the summer at Marienbad, holidays at Otwock, and then settled in Warsaw to be near the flagship Tomchei Temimim yeshivah. Feigin wrote that the Rebbe "returned to his old self," delivering long maamarim again.
Tags: warsaw, poland, tomchei-temimim, latvian-citizenship

Title: Separate Yamim Noraim minyan organized for Chabad students in Brooklyn
Summary: A dedicated High Holidays minyan was established for select chassidim and the author's students at the Bikur Cholim hall on Osborne Street.
Story: R' Yochanan Gordon served as the baal tefillah and baal tokea. Separate hakafos were held on Simchas Torah after those at the author's main shul. The success of this arrangement led to the idea of a year-round dedicated minyan for the students.
Tags: yamim noraim, rosh hashana, yochanan gordon, bikur cholim, brownsville, minyan

Title: Ludmir Anash write joyful letter on Rebbe's settling in Warsaw
Summary: On 12 Elul 5693, leaders of the Anash community in Ludmir, Volhynia, sent a letter expressing their joy at the Rebbe's relocation to Warsaw.
Story: The signatories described how the spark of Chabad chassidus had burned only privately and in limited measure since the war years, and they now hoped that the Rebbe's nearness would rekindle it into a great fire. The letter was signed by twenty community members and concluded with New Year blessings.
Tags: ludmir, volhynia, warsaw, letter, anash

Title: Passing of Rabbi Meir Shlomo Yanovsky, Rabbi of Nikolayev
Summary: Rabbi M.S. Yanovsky, grandfather of the Rebbe and Rabbi of Nikolayev for 43 years, passed away on 23 Elul 5693.
Story: On 23 Elul 5693 (Sept. 14, 1933), Rabbi Meir Shlomo Yanovsky, the Rebbe's maternal grandfather and longtime Rabbi of Nikolayev, passed away. He had served the community since 5650, succeeding his grandfather Rabbi Avraham David Lavut. After his passing, his son-in-law Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn (uncle of the Rebbe) succeeded him in the rabbinate.
Tags: yanovsky, nikolayev, yahrzeit, schneersohn

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Warsaw and begins Tiku 5694 maamarim
Summary: Beginning Rosh Hashana 5694, immediately upon arriving in Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz delivered the Hemshech maamarim 'Tiku 5694'.
Story: On Rosh Hashana 5694 the Rebbe Rayatz began delivering the long Hemshech 'Tiku' which concluded on Shabbos Parshas Toldos. Talmidim repeated the maamarim, and select students entered the Rebbe's room to chazer them before him. The Rebbe also wrote down the maamarim, which were then copied and studied by the talmidim.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-temimim, maamarim, tiku, rosh-hashana

Title: Rebbe enters new Warsaw apartment
Summary: On 8 Tishrei 5694 the Rebbe and his family moved into their new apartment in Warsaw.
Story: Writing the next day on Erev Yom Kippur, the Rebbe noted with symbolic emphasis that the move had taken place in 'the seventh month, sated with joys, on the eighth day, oily with every good.' The household had spent Rosh Hashanah at the yeshiva while renovations were finished.
Tags: warsaw, apartment, tishrei

Title: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn writes from Nikolaev on erev Yom Kippur
Summary: On erev Yom Kippur 5694 Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn of Nikolaev wrote to Rachel Schneersohn mentioning the recent passing of his father-in-law.
Story: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn, rabbi of Nikolaev and uncle of Zelda, wrote on erev Yom Kippur 5694 to his relative Rachel. He shared that his father-in-law had passed away one week before Rosh Hashanah of that year and offered New Year blessings for her and her daughter Zelda.
Tags: nikolaev, schneersohn family, yom kippur, condolence

Title: Kiev yeshiva students arrested by NKVD agents after Simchat Torah 5694
Summary: After Simchat Torah and Shabbat Bereishit 5694, two disguised NKVD agents entered the Kiev yeshiva's ezras nashim and arrested the bochurim.
Story: Two clean-shaven, fashionably dressed agents quietly entered the upstairs ezras nashim where the yeshiva learned, tested the two youngest bochurim on their gemara, then announced they were under arrest with police already at the door. The author escaped through the women's gallery windows while others were taken to NKVD headquarters; a sympathetic Jewish interrogator later returned most papers but denied them Kiev passports and warned them to flee.
Tags: kiev, ukraine, nkvd, arrest, pasportization

Title: R. Mordechai Leizer Lapatovsky visits Kiev yeshiva for Sukkot 5694
Summary: During Tishrei 5694, especially Sukkot, R. Mordechai Leizer Lapatovsky came from nearby Zhitomir to farbreng with the Kiev yeshiva students.
Story: R. Mordechai Leizer Lapatovsky, brother-in-law of R. Yona Cohen and R. Eli Chaim Roitblat, traveled from Zhitomir to Kiev to spend Sukkot with the underground yeshiva. He farbrenged with the bochurim in a spirit of mesirus nefesh and shared eyewitness stories of avodah from Lubavitch.
Tags: kiev, zhitomir, sukkot, lapatovsky, lubavitch stories

Title: Rafael Cohen leaves Soviet Russia for Riga
Summary: In Tishrei 5694, R. Rafael Cohen succeeded in leaving Russia and settled in Riga.
Story: Cohen had served as rabbi in Osvet, Shchedrin, and Nevel before being forced to flee Nevel after the 5689 arrests. He served as ram in the Tomchei Temimim yeshivos in Vitebsk and Moscow before his emigration. The Rebbe wrote to welcome him to Riga, noting that 'here it is a land where the government does not interfere with the observance of Torah and mitzvos.'
Tags: rafael-cohen, russia, riga, emigration, refugee

Title: Maciów yeshiva proposal revived by R' Yitzchak Aryeh Mandelbaum
Summary: On the 3rd day of Chol Hamoed Sukkot 5694, Mandelbaum again wrote to the Rebbe urging the founding of a yeshiva in Maciów to serve graduates of local cheders.
Story: Mandelbaum warned that the largest cheder class in Maciów and surrounding towns was only beginning Gemara, and that students leaving without further Torah education risked drifting from religious life entirely. He committed to personally establishing a small yeshiva on his return home, teaching the local boys Gemara and Chassidus daily. The plan, however, did not materialize.

Title: Secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin reports Rebbe's recovery in Warsaw
Summary: On 27 Tishrei 5694 the secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote that the Rebbe had returned to himself spiritually now that the yeshiva was near him.
Story: Feigin reported that during the Yamim Noraim and Sukkos the Rebbe delivered deep Hemshech maamarim of nearly two hours, though it was beyond his strength. Students repeated the maamarim and selected ones entered the Rebbe to chazer them, evoking the atmosphere of Lubavitch twenty years earlier.

Title: Librarian writes David Sassoon requesting Ohel David
Summary: From Warsaw on 7 Cheshvan 5694, librarian Chaim Liberman wrote collector David Solomon Sassoon asking him to gift his catalogue Ohel David to the Lubavitch library.
Story: The letter, signed only as 'director of the Lubavitch book and manuscript collection' without mentioning the Rebbe by name, reflected the library's new institutional identity. Liberman cited the precedent of many authors and publishers who had sent their works as gifts and thanked Sassoon in advance for joining them — one of dozens of such solicitation letters dispatched in this period.

Title: Passing of R' M.M. Lukshin, head of Agudas Chassidei Chabad
Summary: R' M.M. Lukshin, head of Agudas Chassidei Chabad in America, passed away in Cheshvan 5694.
Story: His death left a leadership gap in the American Chabad organization at a pivotal moment when student activities in Brooklyn were expanding. The author was simultaneously organizing a dedicated High Holidays minyan for his students.

Title: Feigin reports weekly maamarim and chazara in Warsaw
Summary: On 5 Kislev 5694 Feigin wrote that the Rebbe was saying deep maamarim almost every Shabbos and the students were chazering them with him.
Story: The secretary described how, with the Rebbe and yeshiva united in Warsaw, the atmosphere of pre-revolution Lubavitch was being restored. Students repeated the maamarim together and entered for chazara before the Rebbe, sometimes feeling as though the past twenty years had not intervened.

Title: Third Mechina class added; classes split between Twarda and Zamenhof
Summary: By 7 Tevet 5694 the Mechina had grown to three classes spread between Twarda and Zamenhof Street locations.
Story: Class A learned at Twarda (Proste 10) and Classes B–C at Zamenhof 8. R' Yehuda Eber reported tighter admissions standards had slightly lowered numbers but expected the Twarda branch to grow. Around the same time R' Mordechai Mentlik joined the staff as maggid shiur for the youngest class.

Title: Extraordinary 19 Kislev farbrengen in Malachovka
Summary: A remarkable Chag HaGeulah farbrengen was held in Malachovka outside Moscow, attended by many senior Chassidim hiding from Soviet authorities.
Story: On 19 Kislev 5694 (December 7, 1933), an extraordinary farbrengen took place in the Malachovka shul. Many anash and elder Chassidim gathered there because the area was quiet in winter — Moscow officials had returned to the city and vacated their dachas. The farbrengen lasted several nights; at one point Rabbi Shmuel Levitin stood on the table with his long peyot loose over his face and sang 'Az der Rebbe iz do, iz doch hoderes vehaemunah uday do' — a moment that pierced the author's heart given his personal and the broader circumstances.

Title: US Acting Secretary of State Phillips declines formal book intervention
Summary: On December 19, 1933, US Acting Secretary William Phillips replies that the government cannot formally pressure the Soviets to return the books to a non-citizen.
Story: Following efforts by R. Avraham Eliyahu Axelrod to mobilize American officials around Litvinov's Washington visit (negotiating US recognition of the Soviet Union), Acting Secretary Phillips writes that 'in view of the fact that Rabbi Schneerson is not a citizen of the United States, this Government is not in a position to take any formal steps to induce the Soviet Government to return to him the books and documents in question.'

Title: Rosh Yeshiva Eber introduces new written-exam method
Summary: On 7 Tevet 5694 R. Yehuda Eber reported to the Rebbe on a new method of examining students with written questions.
Story: Eber gave the talmidim five questions with about two weeks to answer them; more than ten students responded with mostly accurate answers. The youngest, such as 14-year-old Eliezer Feldberg and Yaakov Falkenfeld, produced especially well-ordered and clear replies. The Rosh Yeshiva planned to pause briefly to avoid pulling students from their regular shiurim.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-temimim, yehuda-eber, exams, feldberg, falkenfeld

Title: 'Igud Talmidei HaTemimim' association founded
Summary: In 5694 the 'Igud Talmidei HaTemimim' association was founded under R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie's leadership.
Story: In 5694 (1933/34) the Igud Talmidei HaTemimim — Union of Tomchei Tmimim Students — was established, with R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie at its head. The association coordinated alumni and student activities and would, the following year, launch the Chabad periodical HaTamim. It also took responsibility for printing the Rebbe Rayatz's discourses and addresses.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-tmimim, igud-talmidei-hatemimim, shneur-zalman-gurarie

Title: First Haggadah printed in South America (Buenos Aires)
Summary: The first Haggadah ever printed in South America was issued in Buenos Aires in 5694 by Yekutiel Weiss.
Story: In 5694 (1934), Yekutiel Weiss issued the first Haggadah printed in South America, in Buenos Aires. Titled Bonah Zeret, it featured his commentary Yeku L'Or alongside the laws of Passover from the Derech HaChaim.
Tags: haggadah, buenos-aires, argentina, south-america

Title: Hatamim journal published in Warsaw
Summary: From 5695 to 5699 (1934-1939) the Hatamim journal was published in Warsaw by the alumni of Tomchei Temimim.
Story: The Hatamim collection devoted to Chabad Chasidism appeared in Warsaw during the years 5695-5699. It included a regular section on biographies of prominent Chasidim of past generations, for which the Rayatz commissioned several memorial articles. Publication ceased with the outbreak of World War II.
Tags: hatamim, warsaw, tomchei temimim, poland

Title: Hodakov appointed chief inspector of Jewish schools in Latvia
Summary: Rabbi Chaim Mordechai Aizek Hodakov is named chief inspector of Latvia's Jewish schools, beginning reforms toward traditional Judaism.
Story: Orchestrated by Dubin, the appointment let Hodakov replace secular curricula with Torah lessons. Yiddishist teachers staged a strike but failed. Hodakov instituted required prayer and yarmulkes, transforming the historically secular schools.
Tags: hodakov, latvia, dubin, derech-eretz, yiddishism

Title: Igud Talmidei HaTmimim alumni organization founded
Summary: The Igud Talmidei HaTmimim alumni organization was founded in 5694 to unite graduates of Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: In 5694 (1934), three years after the Rebbe Rayatz had directed R' Zalmanov to compile a list of all Tomchei Tmimim alumni, the Igud Talmidei HaTmimim was founded. Its purpose was to unite the graduates of the yeshiva for joint efforts in spreading Torah, yiras shamayim, and the study of chassidus.
Tags: alumni, tomchei tmimim, igud talmidei hatmimim

Title: Malach's students leave Torah Vodaas to found Yeshivas Nesivos Olam
Summary: Students of the Malach broke away from Torah Vodaas to establish a separate yeshiva called Nesivos Olam.
Story: Adopting distinctive external practices — long coats, large tzitzis, no ties, unfolded hat brims, and learning only from Slavita and Zhitomir Talmud editions — the Malach's students openly clashed with Torah Vodaas. They eventually left and founded Nesivos Olam, drawing major support from R' Ben Tzion Weberman (formerly a pillar of Torah Vodaas) and the wealthy R' Avraham Yaakov Katz.
Tags: nesivos olam, the malach, torah vodaas, slavita, zhitomir, ben tzion weberman, chaim katz

Title: Permanent students' minyan established at Toras Mitzion in Brownsville
Summary: With help of R' Aba Rivkin, a permanent Shabbos minyan for the author's students was established at the Toras Mitzion building.
Story: Initial Shabbatos sometimes lacked a full minyan and R' Yochanan Gordon complained about the difficulty. Over time the minyan grew and moved to the Anshe Ozaritz shul at 885 Hopkinson Ave. Eventually the minyan flourished with multiple minyanim attending Shabbos services and influence spread further into the yeshiva world.
Tags: minyan, toras mitzion, aba rivkin, brownsville, anshe ozaritz, hopkinson ave

Title: R' Eliyahu Weitz proposes opening Tomchei Temimim branch in Braslau
Summary: In winter 5694, R' Eliyahu Weitz, director of the Vilna yeshiva, wrote to the Rebbe proposing a new yeshiva ketana branch in Lithuanian Braslau.
Story: Weitz suggested sending a particular individual to serve as rosh mesivta in Braslau. The proposal reached the Rebbe during the winter months and set off several months of consultation about whether the branch should be established and who should be appointed to lead it.
Tags: lithuania, braslau, tomchei temimim, eliyahu weitz, vilna

Title: R' Shimon Zelichover leaves Lublin for Krakow
Summary: In 5694, following the death of R' Meir Shapiro, R' Shimon Zelichover left Lublin and settled in Krakow.
Story: In Krakow he continued to teach select students. He remained there until 5703, when he was deported by the Nazis.
Tags: krakow, lublin, shimon engel zelichover, meir shapiro

Title: R' Yaakov Landa makes aliyah to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: R' Yaakov Landa left Latvia for Eretz Yisrael in 5694 (1934), initially serving as rabbi of Ramatayim.
Story: In 5694 (1934), R' Yaakov Landa immigrated to Eretz Yisrael, leaving his Libau rabbinate. He first took up the rabbinate of Ramatayim (today part of Hod Hasharon) before being chosen the following year as rabbi of Bnei Brak.
Tags: landa, aliyah, ramatayim, hod-hasharon

Title: R' Yisrael Jacobson founds students' minyan in New York
Summary: In 5694 R' Yisrael Jacobson founded a minyan for his students, with R' Yochanan Gordon teaching Chassidus before davening and serving as baal korei.
Story: R' Yisrael Jacobson established a minyan in New York in 5694 for the young men he was teaching. R' Yochanan Gordon played a central role: he learned Chassidus with the students before davening and served as the Torah reader. This represented one of the early efforts to transplant Lubavitcher chinuch and chassidic practice to American soil.
Tags: new york, yisrael jacobson, yochanan gordon, minyan, chassidus

Title: R. Menachem Mendel Rozenmutter appointed head of Łódź yeshiva
Summary: In 5694 R. Menachem Mendel Rozenmutter was appointed rosh yeshiva of Tomchei Tmimim Łódź.
Story: In 5694 (1934), R. Menachem Mendel Rozenmutter, son-in-law of R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin of Warsaw, was appointed rosh yeshiva of the Łódź branch. He refused to accept a salary, supporting himself from his candle factory; when the Rebbe heard this he was displeased, quoting 'a free doctor is worth nothing.' Rozenmutter was murdered in the Holocaust.

Title: R. Teitz leaves Livenhof yeshiva for America
Summary: After roughly one year leading the Livenhof yeshiva, Pinchas Mordechai Teitz left for the US in 5694 as Telz emissary.
Story: Pinchas Mordechai Teitz ran the original Livenhof yeshiva for only about a year. In 5694 he traveled to the United States as a shaliach for the Telz yeshiva, married there, and was appointed rabbi of Elizabeth, New Jersey, leaving Livenhof without its founding director.

Title: Rayatz moves to Warsaw, Poland
Summary: The Rayatz settled in Warsaw, Poland, as recorded in the canonical timeline of his life.
Story: Although he had relocated in mid-1933, official chronologies record 1934 (5694) as the year of his Warsaw residency. From here he led the Chabad movement until his move to Otwock in 1936.
Tags: warsaw, poland

Title: Rebbe Rayatz sends Torgsin dollars to Levin family in USSR
Summary: In summer 5694 Rebbe Rayatz sent seven dollars in Torgsin coupons to support Yisrael Yehuda Levin and his widowed mother.
Story: Hiding in a corner of the Marina Roshcha shul yard, the author wrote a desperate letter to the Rebbe Rayatz describing his hunger, persecution, and his family's pressure to abandon yeshiva study. To his surprise he received a reply enclosing three dollars for himself and four for his mother, with a blessing that Hashem strengthen his siblings' resolve. The dollars arrived as Torgsin coupons—redeemable in the Soviet hard-currency stores—allowing him to buy rice, oranges and other unobtainable goods to send home.

Title: Rebbe relocates from Warsaw to Otwock
Summary: Health concerns prompted the Sixth Rebbe to move from Warsaw to the suburban resort town of Otwock in 1934.
Story: Otwock served as the seat of his leadership and the home of Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim until German bombing on September 1, 1939 destroyed any possibility of staying. Otwock is where Jacobson met him on the eve of the war and where he resolved to move to America.
Tags: warsaw, otwock, poland, health

Title: Ulmanis coup d'état in Latvia; political parties disbanded
Summary: Prime Minister Kārlis Ulmanis dissolves the elected parliament and bans political parties, including Jewish ones.
Story: Only Agudath Israel was allowed to function because of Mordechai Dubin's personal bond with Ulmanis. Multi-party elections did not return until 1990. Dubin used his expanded influence to engineer Hodakov's appointment as inspector of Jewish schools.
Tags: latvia, ulmanis, coup, politics

Title: Ulmanis coup; Rabbi Hodakov appointed chief inspector of Jewish schools
Summary: After the Ulmanis coup, Rabbi Mordechai Dubin orchestrates Rabbi Hodakov's appointment as chief inspector of Latvia's Jewish schools.
Story: Prime Minister Kārlis Ulmanis disbanded political parties and parliament, but Dubin's personal bond with Ulmanis kept Agudath Israel functioning. Dubin arranged for Rabbi Chaim Mordechai Aizek Hodakov, the eighteen-year-old founding dean of Derech Eretz, to take over school inspection. Hodakov shifted historically secular Yiddishist schools toward Torah-based curriculum, replacing Sholem Aleichem with religious study and instituting prayer and yarmulkes.
Tags: latvia, ulmanis, coup, hodakov, dubin, agudath israel

Title: Underground Malakhovka farbrengen reorganizes bochurim's nigleh learning
Summary: A summer 5694 farbrengen in Malakhovka assigned R. Refael Cohen of Nevel to teach nigleh to the bochurim.
Story: In the summer of 5694 (1934) a chassidic farbrengen was held in the Malakhovka shul where it was decided that R. Refael Cohen of Nevel would begin teaching the bochurim nigleh. R. Pinchas Schreiber (Pinye Rakshiker) regularly taught them Hemshech 5666, while R. Elchonon Morozov occasionally taught a maamar. The group included future Lubavitcher figures like R. Shlomo Matusof, R. Meir Zarchi, R. Michoel Teitelbaum and R. Mendel Morozov, who later joined from Malakhovka.

Title: Vienna Haggadah 'Maadanei Melech' by Asher Horowitz of Dzikov
Summary: The Haggadah 'Maadanei Melech' by Rebbe Asher Horowitz of Dzikov, residing in Vienna, was published there.
Story: In 5694 (1934), the Haggadah 'Maadanei Melech' by the Admor Asher ben Meir Horowitz of Dzikov, who was then residing in Vienna, was published by the Appel Brothers in Vienna. The 80-page octavo edition served the Dzikov-Ropshitz Chassidic community and disciples of the Horowitz dynasty. It became one of the notable Hungarian-Galician Chassidic Haggadot of the interwar period.

Title: Rebbe Rayatz reports success of move to Poland
Summary: On 3 Adar 5694 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Yitzchak Horowitz that the move to Poland was bearing good fruit in Torah and avoda.
Story: The Rebbe summarized the results of relocating his residence to Poland, expressing satisfaction that students of the yeshivos were diligent in their studies. He saw it as fulfillment of the mission set by his father, the Rebbe Rashab.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-temimim, rayatz, letter, horowitz

Title: Rayatz visits Riga for nine days
Summary: The Rayatz visited Riga from 12-20 Adar 5694, delivering maamarim and speaking to the women of the community.
Story: Returning to the Latvian community he had lived among for years, the Rayatz used the visit to reconnect with his former host city. His talks to the women of the community were a notable feature of the visit.
Tags: riga, latvia, maamar, women

Title: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn visits his mother's grave in Kiev
Summary: Around Parshat HaChodesh 5694 Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn wrote from Nikolaev describing a recent pilgrimage to his mother's grave in Kiev.
Story: In a letter dated erev Shabbat Parshat HaChodesh 5694, Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn told Rachel that he had recently visited and prayed at his mother's grave in Kiev. He noted that his mother's yahrzeit had just passed and asked her merit to protect the family.
Tags: kiev, nikolaev, schneersohn family, yahrzeit

Title: Purim farbrengen at Reb Elchanan Morozov in Leningrad
Summary: Chassidim farbrenged at Reb Elchanan Morozov's home in Leningrad on Purim 5694, then continued at Reb Shmuel Nemotin's home.
Story: On Purim 5694 (around March 1, 1934), Chassidim farbrenged at the home of Rabbi Elchanan Morozov in Leningrad. They later continued at the home of Rabbi Shmuel Nemotin, where a large farbrengen was held with long tables — Rabbi Chaikel Chaikin had just become engaged to his daughter. Rabbi Peretz Mochkin spoke, with prominent participants including Rabbi Baruch Shifrin, Rabbi Menashe Althaus, and Rabbi Michael Dvorkin (who was preparing to emigrate to Riga).
Tags: leningrad, purim, elchanan-morozov, shmuel-nemotin, peretz-mochkin, baruch-shifrin, menashe-althaus, michael-dvorkin, farbrengen

Title: 13 Nissan farbrengen at Reb Zalman Moshe's home in Moscow
Summary: On the yahrtzeit of the Tzemach Tzedek, a small farbrengen took place late at night at Reb Zalman Moshe's home in Moscow.
Story: On the night of 13 Nissan 5694 (March 29, 1934), the yahrtzeit of the Tzemach Tzedek, the author overcame his exhaustion and went late at night to Reb Zalman Moshe's home. Soon afterwards, Rabbi Berel (Garfinkel) Kornitzer — the pride of the Rostov tmimim — arrived on a mission from Rabbi Zalman Schneersohn regarding communal finances, followed by Reb Yaakov Maskalik (Yaakov Zhuravitzer) who had come specifically to farbreng. The three sat down to farbreng and the author listened from the side.

Title: R. Shimon Levi Belastotzky reports from Disna
Summary: On 13 Nissan 5694, R. Shimon Levi Belastotzky, rabbi of Disna, reported to the Rebbe on his chavura learning chassidus and attempts at a Tiferes Bachurim group.
Story: Writing to the Rebbe on 13 Nissan 5694, R. Shimon Levi b'R. Shneur Zalman Belastotzky of Disna reported that the chavura studying chassidus was growing and gaining strength. However, his repeated attempts to establish a 'Tiferes Bachurim' group had not yet succeeded in taking firm hold.
Tags: belastotzky, disna, tiferes-bachurim, chassidus, shiurim

Title: Rebbe encourages founding a Tomchei Temimim branch in Braslau
Summary: On 13 Nissan 5694 the Rebbe wrote both to R' Eliyahu Weitz and to R' Shneur Aron of Braslau, urging immediate steps to establish a yeshiva ketana there.
Story: To Weitz the Rebbe suggested that a Tomchei Temimim student would be a more suitable rosh mesivta than the candidate Weitz had proposed, and that the cost would be lower. To R' Shneur Aron the Rebbe described Braslau as urgently needing a yeshiva in the spirit of Tomchei Temimim and asked him to rally local Anash to bring the plan to fruition without delay, coordinating logistics through Weitz in Vilna.
Tags: lithuania, braslau, tomchei temimim, shneur aron, eliyahu weitz, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz refuses R' Eliyahu Weitz's resignation in Vilna
Summary: On 13 Nisan 5694, the Rebbe Rayatz refused to accept R' Eliyahu Weitz's resignation from leading the Vilna yeshiva, fearing the institution would collapse.
Story: R' Eliyahu Weitz, who bore the main burden of the Vilna yeshiva's leadership, wrote that he could no longer continue alone. The Rebbe Rayatz refused to accept his resignation, knowing it would mean the institution's destruction, and the same day wrote to Anash of Vilna chastising their cold attitude and pleading they actively support R' Weitz and the yeshiva.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, rebbe rayatz, rabbi eliyahu weitz, fundraising

Title: Yisrael Yehuda Levin returned from Leningrad to Moscow for Pesach
Summary: Yisrael Yehuda Levin returned from Leningrad to Moscow on Erev Pesach 5694 after about a month with Chassidim in Leningrad.
Story: On Erev Pesach 5694 (March 30, 1934), the author returned from Leningrad to Moscow and back to Malachovka. He had spent roughly a month in Leningrad, lodging with Rabbi Yitzchok Raskin and attending farbrengens and Shabbos seudos at the home of Rabbi Elchanan Morozov. Hosting unregistered Chassidim in Leningrad was literal mesirat nefesh given Soviet surveillance.
