Title: Rebbe offers R' Yitzchak Dov Ber Ushpal the Braslau yeshiva leadership
Summary: On 26 Nissan 5694 the Rebbe wrote to R' Yitzchak Dov Ber Ushpal of Korniec offering him the post of rosh yeshiva and educator at the planned Braslau branch.
Story: After R' Shneur Aron of Braslau responded affirmatively, the Rebbe informed him that the candidate would be named the following week. The same day he wrote to Ushpal asking whether he could accept the appointment as rosh yeshiva and mechanech at the new Tomchei Temimim branch in Braslau. The Braslau branch never materialized; some months later Ushpal was instead sent to head the Vilna yeshiva.
Tags: lithuania, braslau, korniec, tomchei temimim, yitzchak dov ber ushpal, shneur aron, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz proposes R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal for Braslav branch
Summary: On 27 Nisan 5694, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal inquiring whether he would accept a position as Rosh Yeshiva of a proposed Tomchei Tmimim branch in Braslav.
Story: Discussions arose in spring 5694 about opening a new Tomchei Tmimim branch in Braslav. R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal was among the candidates proposed to lead it. Though the Braslav branch ultimately never opened, this exchange set the stage for his appointment as Rosh Yeshiva in Vilna the following year.
Tags: braslav, vilna, tomchei tmimim, rebbe rayatz, rabbi yitzchak dov oshpal

Title: Yisrael Yehuda Levin wrote to Rebbe Rayatz requesting blessing for exit visa
Summary: Yisrael Yehuda Levin wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe in Riga requesting a blessing as he applied for an exit permit from Soviet Russia.
Story: On Erev Shabbat Parshat Shemini, 28 Nissan 5694 (April 13, 1934), Yisrael Yehuda ben Ephraim Shmuel Levin wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz from Moscow. He asked for arousal of mercy from on high so that the Soviet officials granting exit permits would look favorably on his case and issue him travel documents. The letter was preserved in the archive of the Rebbe Rayatz's correspondence at the library of Agudas Chasidei Chabad.
Tags: moscow, rayatz, exit-visa, soviet-russia, yisrael-yehuda-levin, agudas-chassidei-chabad-archive

Title: Feigin describes Shabbos maamarim and Polish attendees
Summary: On 9 Iyar 5694 R. Yechezkel Feigin described weekly Shabbos maamarim attended by anash, talmidim and many Polish Jews who had drawn close.
Story: Feigin wrote that every Shabbos the Rebbe delivered maamarim during Kabbalas Shabbos as in Lubavitch days, students gathered in the morning for chazara, and after mincha talmidim and anash assembled in the Rebbe's beis hamedrash. Many local Polish Jews drew close in order to hear Chassidus.
Tags: warsaw, feigin, maamarim, polish-chassidim, letter

Title: Levin writes to Rebbe Rayatz from Lipovets
Summary: In Iyyar 5694 Yisrael Yehuda Levin wrote to Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn describing his late father's mesirus nefesh in raising the children as Torah-observant.
Story: The letter recounted that Ephraim Shmuel had insisted his daughters not attend the Soviet school despite repeated official demands and threats of fines. Levin listed his mother and three younger sisters by name and age, noting his mother's heart disease prevented her from earning a living. The letter was preserved in the Rebbe's archive.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, lipovets, correspondence, yisrael yehuda levin

Title: Rebbe writes reflection on the meaning of his 1927 imprisonment
Summary: In a letter dated 17 Iyar 5694, the Rebbe wrote that suffering for an ideal develops a person's abilities and transforms weakness into strength.
Story: Years after the ordeal, the Rebbe reflected that his eighteen days, eleven hours, and fifteen minutes in Shpalerka should be marked down to the minute. Every moment of suffering for the strengthening of religion, he wrote, brings tremendous reward and infinite fortitude of mind.
Tags: letter, imprisonment, reflection, 17 iyar

Title: Rebbe Rayatz blesses founding of Agudas Talmidei HaTmimim
Summary: On 28 Iyar 5694 the Rebbe Rayatz approved an alumni association of Tomchei Tmimim graduates.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz blessed the proposal from former students to form a network for Tomchei Tmimim alumni. Headed by R' Schneur Zalman Gourary, the Agudah set up offices at Moranowski 7/9 in Warsaw — the same address as the Rebbe's beit midrash. Its aims included disseminating Chassidus and helping members secure rabbinic, shochet, and commercial positions.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei tmimim, agudas talmidei hatmimim, alumni, schneur zalman gourary

Title: Rebbe summarizes library's growth 5688–5694
Summary: On 10 Sivan 5694 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote his son-in-law summarizing that the library had nearly doubled and gained some 700 holy books since the move from Russia.
Story: Reviewing six years of acquisitions, the Rebbe reported that according to Liberman the collection had grown nearly twofold, with paper and binding alone now worth more than what had been spent, and roughly seven hundred new sefarim added, many donated by authors and publishers. He noted that if Heaven helped him retrieve the Moscow library as well, the combined holdings would constitute an enormous treasure.
Tags: library, rayatz, ramash, warsaw, growth

Title: Rebbe visits Glubok and witnesses miraculous healing of Ida Haberman
Summary: In June 1934 the Rebbe returned to Glubok in Lithuania and was welcomed by thousands; he blessed ten-year-old Ida Haberman who regained her sight.
Story: The local Yiddish paper Gluboker Lebn claimed the reception surpassed those given to the presidents of Czechoslovakia and Austria. Ida's father, not a Chasid, brought her to the train station fearing she was going blind. She regained her sight; later hidden during the Holocaust, she immigrated to the US. During the visit the Rebbe also navigated a local conflict over a rabbinic appointment.
Tags: glubok, lithuania, blessing, haberman, gluboker-lebn

Title: Rayatz visits Glubok and Vilna
Summary: The Rayatz left Warsaw on June 3 for a visit to Glubok in Lithuania, stopping in Vilna along the way.
Story: He remained in Glubok through 6 Tamuz, an inspiring visit for the Chasidim of the region. The trip continued his pattern of bringing himself to communities that could not easily come to him.
Tags: glubok, vilna, lithuania

Title: Rebbe Rayatz visits Glubokoe for two weeks
Summary: From 20 Sivan to 6 Tammuz 5694 the Rebbe Rayatz visited Glubokoe, his final visit to the Vilna region.
Story: Traveling from Warsaw via a brief stop in Vilna, the Rebbe was received at the Glubokoe station by Rabbi Menachem Mendel Kupershtok and a large crowd. Over the two-week visit he delivered the maamar 'Az Yibaka' at the Lubavitch shul, received Anash for yechidus throughout each day, and prayed at the Starashele and Lubavitch synagogues. On 5 Tammuz community leaders informed him of their decision to open a branch of Tomchei Tmimim in the town.
Tags: glubokoe, vilna region, poland, tomchei tmimim, kupershtok

Title: Leah Beila Levin writes memoir-letter to Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5694 Leah Beila Levin sent the Rebbe Rayatz a detailed account of her family history and her late husband's piety from Lipovets.
Story: The letter described her descent from Reb Avraham Yehuda of Linets and the Kosover-Berditchev rabbinic line, her childhood in Dashov, and her marriage to Ephraim Shmuel of Zhivotov. It detailed how their small shop and his teaching supported the family, and how she herself sometimes taught the children of his cheder. The letter is preserved in the Lubavitch library archive.

Title: Decision to open Tomchei Tmimim branch in Glubokoe
Summary: On 5 Tammuz 5694 Glubokoe community leaders announced to the Rebbe their decision to open a branch of Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva.
Story: On Monday 5 Tammuz during the Rebbe Rayatz's visit to Glubokoe, he met at the home of Rabbi Kupershtok with gabbaim of the local batei midrash and town notables. There they informed him of their decision to open a branch of Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva in the town.
Tags: glubokoe, tomchei tmimim, yeshiva, vilna region

Title: 12 Tammuz farbrengen in Malakhovka marks year since author's arrival
Summary: On 12 Tammuz 5694 the author returned from Moscow to Malakhovka for a farbrengen marking a year since first arriving there.
Story: On 12 Tammuz 5694 (June 25, 1934)—the anniversary of the Rebbe Rayatz's liberation from Soviet imprisonment—the author returned from Moscow to Malakhovka, completing a full year since first arriving in summer 5693. A farbrengen was held in the Malakhovka shul. He resumed sleeping and learning there, joined by a growing number of Anash families and bochurim fleeing intensifying decrees throughout the country.
Tags: malakhovka, 12 tammuz, soviet union, farbrengen, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz thanks R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch for reports
Summary: On 15 Tammuz 5694 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote that reports of public Chassidus study by anash and tmimim were 'a true medicine' sustaining his health.
Story: In Igros Kodesh vol. 17, no. 6369, the Rebbe Rayatz thanked R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch of Kovno for reports about anash holding public shiurim in Chassidus. The Rebbe wrote that such news literally sustained his physical strength, and blessed all who concerned themselves with this work.
Tags: kovno, lithuania, yehoshua-isaac-baruch, tammuz, shiurim

Title: Rayatz travels to Marienbad
Summary: On 22 Tamuz the Rayatz departed Warsaw for another stay in Marienbad.
Story: His annual summer trips to Marienbad for health treatment were a fixture of his Warsaw years. The 1934 trip was followed by a visit to Prague on the way home.
Tags: marienbad, czechoslovakia

Title: Rayatz visits Prague
Summary: Returning from Marienbad, the Rayatz visited Prague on 15 Av before continuing to Warsaw.
Story: Prague hosted a small but historic Jewish community. The Rayatz's visit allowed him to engage with local Jews before completing his journey back to Warsaw.
Tags: prague, czechoslovakia

Title: Rosh Yeshiva examines all students in Warsaw
Summary: On 15 Menachem Av 5694 R. Yehuda Eber reported he had examined all the preparatory and main yeshiva students with generally good results.
Story: Eber reported that the spiritual state was good: he had tested the preparatory students and all the classes of the yeshiva. Most students of the yeshiva, particularly the third class, possessed relatively strong knowledge.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-temimim, yehuda-eber, exams

Title: Womens committee establishes yeshiva kitchen support
Summary: On 16 Menachem Av 5694 R. Yehuda Eber reported on the Frauen Komitet, founded by Rebbetzin Shterna Sarah, supporting the yeshiva kitchen.
Story: The womens committee, headed by the Rebbe Rayatzs mother Rebbetzin Shterna Sarah, hired a cook for 40 zloty a month to assist the existing helper. The Rebbetzin personally inspected the kitchen daily, and despite tight conditions almost all needy students were now eating proper meals.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-temimim, rebbetzin-shterna-sarah, womens-committee, kitchen

Title: Anash expand prayer arrangements in Malakhovka for Tishrei 5695
Summary: For Tishrei 5695 the Malakhovka Anash community rented a separate prayer hall to handle the growing crowd of chassidim and bochurim.
Story: By Tishrei 5695 (Fall 1934) the influx of Anash families and yeshiva bochurim to Malakhovka had grown so large that a separate prayer hall had to be rented for the High Holidays. The main shul served the general religious public while the new venue hosted only Anash and yeshiva bochurim, recreating the prayer atmosphere of pre-revolution Lubavitch. Sukkos and Simchas Torah were celebrated with extraordinary farbrengens.
Tags: malakhovka, high holidays, tishrei, anash, soviet underground, rosh hashana, yom kippur

Title: Founding convention of Agudas Talmidei HaTmimim in Warsaw
Summary: About 100 alumni gathered at the Rebbe Rayatz's Warsaw beit midrash on 3 Tishrei 5695 to formally inaugurate Agudas Talmidei HaTmimim.
Story: The convention drew Tmimim from Poland and abroad to the beit midrash at Moranowski 7/9. The assembly elected R' Shmaryahu Gourary as chairman and R' Schneur Zalman Gourary as director, with R' Moshe P. Katz as secretary. The agenda included Chassidic outreach, member assistance with placements, and a charter for the Agudah.
Tags: warsaw, agudas talmidei hatmimim, tomchei tmimim, shmaryahu gourary, alumni

Title: Drabitscher writes Rayatz from Moscow with possible book recovery channel
Summary: On 7 Tishrei 5695, R. Baruch Drabitscher, rav of Mezhibuzh, writes Rayatz from Moscow about a potential channel through Mezhdunarodnaya Kniga officials.
Story: Drabitscher reports that R. A. A. Axelrod of Baltimore asked him to use a senior contact at Mezhdunarodnaya Kniga to obtain the Schneersohn libraries, originally taken from the Kokorev warehouses and now in the Lenin Museum. After meeting them, Drabitscher was told they would consider it only if a foreign catalog were submitted and a substantial foreign currency payment offered.
Tags: library, moscow, soviet, drabitscher, lenin-library, mezhdunarodnaya-kniga

Title: Mashpi'im assigned Chassidus shiurim with Malakhovka bochurim after Simchas Torah
Summary: After Simchas Torah 5695 the Malakhovka Anash organized that each mashpia would teach Chassidus to several bochurim.
Story: Following the Simchas Torah 5695 farbrengens (October 1934), a planning meeting of Anash activists assigned each mashpia to learn Chassidus with a small group of bochurim. The author and R. Shlomo Matusof were assigned to study with R. Nissan Nemenov, who traveled almost daily from Ilinka to teach them Hemshech 5664. Bochurim were also boarded with Anash families—the author lodged with R. Zalman Alpert (Zalman Kornitzer).
Tags: malakhovka, nissan nemenov, chassidus, underground yeshiva, shlomo matusof, hemshech 5664

Title: Russian rabbi writes to Rebbe about library in Leninsky Museum
Summary: A rabbi in Russia wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe describing ongoing efforts to retrieve the library still held at the Leninsky Museum.
Story: In October 1934, one of the rabbis of Russia wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe about the continuing effort to recover the Schneersohn library, which was still housed in the Leninsky Museum. The letter is documented in the Rebbe Rayatz's published correspondence (p. 182).
Tags: library, leninsky museum, soviet union, schneersohn library, russia, rayatz

Title: Rebbe diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in Vienna
Summary: In November 1934 doctors in Vienna identified the Rebbe's mysterious illness as multiple sclerosis after nearly two years of uncertainty.
Story: The Ramash accompanied the Rebbe to Vienna where experts finally diagnosed the autoimmune disease, though they had no cure. Conflicting advice created confusion until they met Dr. Max Gerson, a German-Jewish refugee whose holistic dietary approach appealed to the Rebbe. The Rebbe moved into Gerson's Westend Sanatorium in Purkersdorf in December 1934.
Tags: vienna, austria, health, multiple-sclerosis, ramash, gerson

Title: Rebbe Rayatz stays at Vienna sanitorium
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz began a six-month stay at the West End Sanitorium in Perchtoldsdorf on the outskirts of Vienna.
Story: The Ramash spent these months at the Rebbe's side, providing extended opportunities for mentorship and conversation. The Rebbe entrusted his son-in-law with many private affairs during these stays, and the Ramash functioned at times as the Rebbe's secretary.
Tags: vienna, austria, perchtoldsdorf, medical, mentorship

Title: Yeshiva reaches nearly 200 students in winter 5695
Summary: On 29 Marcheshvan 5695 R. Yehuda Eber reported nearly 200 students enrolled across the yeshivas departments.
Story: The Rosh Yeshiva detailed enrollment: about 60 in the kibbutz, 30 in the great class, 29 with R. Dovid Teiblum, 23 with R. Zalman Gurary, and nearly 60 at the Zamenhof branch. He noted improvement in chazaras hamaamarim, with nearly all kibbutz students participating.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-temimim, yehuda-eber, enrollment, zamenhof

Title: Globoke chassidim ask Rebbe for new rabbi
Summary: On 4 Kislev 5695, sixteen Globoke chassidim wrote to the Rebbe in Yiddish lamenting Kuperstock's imminent departure for Eretz Yisrael.
Story: Sixteen members of the Globoke chassidic community signed a heartfelt Yiddish letter on 4 Kislev 5695, telling the Rebbe Rayatz how Kuperstock had elevated the chassidic spirit not only locally but throughout the wider Vilna region. They mourned his impending departure to Eretz Yisrael and asked for a successor.
Tags: globoke, kuperstock, mandelbaum, yiddish-letter, vilna-region

Title: Rayatz travels to Perchtoldsdorf sanitorium near Vienna
Summary: On 6 Kislev 5695 the Rayatz traveled to the West End Sanitorium in Perchtoldsdorf for treatment by Dr. Max Gerson.
Story: Dr. Max Gerson was a famous physician known for innovative dietary therapies. The Rayatz spent nearly half a year under his care, returning to Warsaw only in mid-April 1935.
Tags: perchtoldsdorf, vienna, austria, health, max gerson, sanitorium

Title: Rayatz farbrengs in Vienna at Reb Klonimus Kalman Poppenheim's home
Summary: During his Perchtoldsdorf stay, the Rayatz led a farbrengen at the home of Reb Klonimus Kalman Poppenheim in Vienna.
Story: Poppenheim's home was a hub for Chabad life in Vienna. The farbrengen on 4 Tevet drew together local Chasidim, an important communal moment during the Rayatz's lengthy Austrian convalescence.
Tags: vienna, austria, farbrengen, poppenheim

Title: Chabad periodical 'HaTamim' begins publication
Summary: In 5695 the 'Igud Talmidei HaTemimim' began publishing the journal 'HaTamim,' edited under R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie's responsibility.
Story: In 5695 (1934/35) the Igud Talmidei HaTemimim began issuing the periodical HaTamim, with R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie responsible for its publication. The journal collected discourses, articles and historical material from the world of Chabad and Tomchei Tmimim. It became a major outlet for the movement's printed output in pre-war Europe.
Tags: warsaw, hatamim, tomchei-tmimim, shneur-zalman-gurarie, igud-talmidei-hatemimim

Title: First Haggadah printed in Morocco
Summary: Ya'ish Krispin's Rakik Echad — the first Haggadah printed in Morocco — appeared in Casablanca in 5695.
Story: In 5695 (1935), the first Haggadah ever printed in Morocco was issued in Casablanca by the press of Y. Razon. The volume, titled Rakik Echad, was written by Ya'ish Krispin and was bound together with his commentary Anaf Shoshan on Pirkei Avot.
Tags: haggadah, casablanca, morocco, north-africa

Title: Founding of Mesivta R' Chaim Berlin after Chabad-led plan is blocked
Summary: An attempt to establish a Chabad-led mesivta at the Stone Ave Talmud Torah was preempted by local rabbanim who founded Mesivta R' Chaim Berlin instead.
Story: Parents from R' Chaim Berlin's yeshiva had approached the author to start a high school division combining limudei kodesh with secular studies, and R' Yitzchak Shmidman of Yeshivas Toras Chaim had pledged support. Brownsville and East New York rabbanim, fearing Lubavitch influence, secretly approached the young R' Yitzchak Hutner and the Stone Ave Talmud Torah baalei batim. They opened what became known as Mesivta R' Chaim Berlin with Hutner as Rosh Mesivta.
Tags: mesivta chaim berlin, yitzchak hutner, brownsville, east new york, stone ave talmud torah

Title: Gerrer Rebbe attempts to visit Me'arat Hamakhpelah
Summary: Rabbi Avraham Mordechai Alter, the Gerrer Rebbe, attempted to visit the Tomb of the Patriarchs but was blocked.
Story: Crowds of Muslims blocked his access, continuing the centuries-old ban broken only briefly by the Rebbe Rayatz in 1929. The Gerrer Rebbe's attempted visit underscored how exceptional that earlier admission had been.
Tags: hebron, meorat-hamachpelah, gerrer-rebbe, alter

Title: Gertrude Zuckerkandel paints portraits of the Rebbe Rashab
Summary: Artist Gertrude Zuckerkandel signed and dated four paintings of the Rebbe Rashab in 1935.
Story: Four previously unpublished portraits of the Rebbe Rashab were found in a wall-cabinet of the Rayatz's yechidus room. Three are signed by Gertrude Zuckerkandel and dated 1935 (5695) — fifteen years after the Rashab's passing — leading to scholarly discussion as to whether they depict the Rashab from memory or are partly based on his son the Rayatz.
Tags: rashab, portrait, zuckerkandel

Title: Hatomim magazine founded
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz founded the Hatomim periodical as a platform to promulgate Chabad teachings and reinforce the Tomchei Temimim yeshivah in Poland.
Story: The magazine featured chasidic teachings, history, and scholarly essays. The Rebbe asked the Ramash, then in Paris, to review articles for the magazine, though few knew the Ramash was assisting with editing. It promoted Tomchei Temimim, then located in Poland, as a premier center of Jewish learning.
Tags: hatomim, poland, tomchei-temimim, magazine

Title: JTA reports Latvia's secular Jewish school union disbanded
Summary: New York's JTA reports the secular Jewish Parents Union in Latvia disbanded, with all educational programs transferred to Agudath Israel.
Story: The shift marked a major victory in the culture war between traditional Jewish education and the secular Yiddish identity movement in Latvia.
Tags: latvia, yiddishism, press, agudath-israel

Title: Mandelbaum appointed rabbi of Globoke
Summary: In 5695, after Kuperstock left for Eretz Yisrael, the Rebbe sent R. Yitzchak HaLevi Mandelbaum to fill the rabbinate of the Globoke chassidic community.
Story: Following Kuperstock's aliyah and the appeal of the Globoke chassidim on 4 Kislev 5695, the Rebbe Rayatz sent Mandelbaum - a Tomchei Tmimim alumnus and head of the Lodz branch - to take over the Globoke rabbinate. He led weekly chassidus farbrengens, Tanya lessons, and oral discourses for the community.
Tags: mandelbaum, globoke, kuperstock-successor

Title: Publication of HaTamim journal first issue
Summary: The first issue of HaTamim was published in Warsaw in 5695, including a letter of the Baal Shem Tov.
Story: The first issue of the HaTamim journal was published in Warsaw in 5695 (1935). It contained the first printing of a handwritten letter of the Baal Shem Tov addressed to his disciple Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polnoye, alongside notes on its provenance in the handwriting of the Rebbe Rayatz.
Tags: warsaw, hatamim, baal shem tov, rayatz

Title: R' Yaakov Landa elected rabbi of Bnei Brak
Summary: R' Yaakov Landa was elected rabbi of Bnei Brak in 5695 (1935), a position he held for fifty years.
Story: In 5695 (1935), R' Yaakov Landa was selected as rabbi of Bnei Brak. He would serve the city for half a century — a full jubilee — until his death in 5746, becoming one of the most influential Chabad rabbis in the Holy Land.
Tags: bnei-brak, landa, rabbinate, eretz-yisrael

Title: R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal appointed Rosh Yeshiva in Vilna
Summary: After the Yamim Noraim of 5696, R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal was appointed Rosh Yeshiva and director of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim by directive of the Rebbe Rayatz.
Story: Following the Days of Awe in 5695, R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal received instructions from the Rebbe Rayatz's secretariat to travel immediately to Vilna to take up the position of Rosh Yeshiva and director. Despite his youth, his scholarship was already renowned. He found roughly sixty students and worked to restore the discipline that had loosened since R' Spitz had departed. The third (top) class was led by Rabbi Israel Gustman.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, rabbi yitzchak dov oshpal, rabbi israel gustman, rebbe rayatz

Title: R' Yitzchak Mandelbaum appointed rabbi of Chabad community in Glubokoye
Summary: In 5695 the Rebbe dispatched R' Yitzchak Mandelbaum to serve as rabbi of the Chabad community in Glubokoye.
Story: After the Maciów initiative failed to advance, the Rebbe Rayatz reassigned Mandelbaum in 1935, sending him to lead the Chabad kehillah in Glubokoye. This appointment redirected Mandelbaum's communal work from the abandoned Volhynian yeshiva project to congregational leadership.
Tags: poland, glubokoye, chabad community, yitzchak mandelbaum

Title: R' Yosef Blumenfeld immigrates to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: In winter 5695, R' Yosef Blumenfeld immigrated to Eretz Yisrael and served on the beis din in Tel Aviv.
Story: After serving as rabbi in Krolewska Huta, R' Yosef Blumenfeld immigrated to Eretz Yisrael in the winter of 5695. There he served on the rabbinical court (beis din) in Tel Aviv and authored a commentary on the Kaftor VaFerach by Eshtori HaParchi.
Tags: yosef blumenfeld, eretz yisrael, tel aviv, beis din, aliyah

Title: Rayatz begins publication of Hatomim journal
Summary: The Rayatz launched Hatomim, a chasidic journal published from his base in Warsaw.
Story: Hatomim became an influential publication for the Chabad world, featuring chasidic teachings, history, and contemporary content. It documented the movement's life in interwar Poland and amplified the Rayatz's voice.
Tags: hatomim, journal, warsaw, poland, tomchei temimim

Title: Rebbe and Tomchei Tmimim relocate from Warsaw to Otwock
Summary: In the summer of 5695 it was decided that the Rebbe Rayatz and the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva would move together from Warsaw to Otwock.
Story: Otwock's clean air suited the Rebbe's health, and the resort town also proved a better setting for the yeshiva than Warsaw. The move fulfilled a plan the Rebbe had already harbored in 5691 but which had been deferred. Otwock would remain the seat of the court and the yeshiva until the outbreak of World War II.
Tags: otwock, warsaw, tomchei-tmimim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz considers second Eretz Yisrael visit
Summary: The Rebbe considered returning to Eretz Yisrael to pray at the graves of the righteous, but the plan did not come to fruition.
Story: He would remain the only Lubavitcher Rebbe to actually visit Eretz Yisrael. The second trip he contemplated would have continued his tradition of seeking divine blessing at the kivrei tzaddikim, especially in preparation for the High Holidays.
Tags: rayatz, eretz-yisrael, kivrei-tzaddikim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz moves from Warsaw to Otwock
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz left Warsaw for Otwock in 5695, where Tomchei Temimim's central yeshiva would be based.
Story: In 5695 (1935), the Rebbe Rayatz moved from Warsaw to the resort town of Otwock, Poland. There the central yeshiva of Tomchei Temimim continued under his leadership, and his library remained with him until the outbreak of war forced its dramatic rescue from occupied Poland.
Tags: warsaw, otwock, poland, tomchei temimim, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz relocates from Warsaw to Otwock
Summary: Two years after moving to Warsaw the Rebbe relocated to nearby Otwock, a resort town better suited to his health.
Story: Otwock's pine-scented air and quieter atmosphere benefited the ailing Rebbe, and the town boasted many tzaddikim and a chasidic ambiance. The Tomchei Temimim yeshivah soon followed the Rebbe there, and Otwock became one of Europe's great centers of Jewish learning until the Nazi invasion in 1939.
Tags: otwock, poland, tomchei-temimim, health

Title: Refugee Chabad families from Russia resettle in Tel Aviv
Summary: Between 5695 and 5697 dozens of Chabad families escaped from Soviet Russia and settled in Tel Aviv, founding a new center of Chabad life.
Story: Between 5695 and 5697, dozens of Chabad families escaped the Soviet Union and arrived in the Land of Israel, most settling in Tel Aviv. They organized themselves and even established a yeshiva. The Rebbe Rayatz founded Agudas Chabad B'Eretz HaKodesh, headquartered in Tel Aviv, alongside the older Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem.
Tags: tel aviv, russia, refugees, agudas chabad

Title: Sholem Aleichem School (Yiddish day school) founded in Melbourne
Summary: Originally called I.L. Peretz Sunday School, the Melbourne institution is founded; today it is the world's only full-time Yiddish day school.
Story: The school promotes Yiddish language and literature alongside 'veltkhe yiddishkayt' — a secular approach to Jewish history and ethics. It survives as the last vestige of a movement that flourished in interwar Europe and faded elsewhere.
Tags: melbourne, australia, yiddish, peretz, secular

Title: Tanya manuscript catalogued in Friedland collection
Summary: The Tanya manuscript previously in Wiener's collection was catalogued as item 177 in the Friedland collection.
Story: In 1935, the handwritten Tanya manuscript that had passed through Wiener's hands was catalogued as item 177 in the Friedland collection at the Asiatic Institute in Leningrad. This inscription was still visible when Chabad emissaries examined the manuscript on their 1991 mission to locate Chabad manuscripts in Soviet collections.
Tags: tanya, manuscript, friedland, leningrad, asiatic institute, catalog

Title: Tomchei Tmimim branches founded in Globoke and Raciaz
Summary: Two new Tomchei Tmimim branches opened in Globoke and Raciaz in 5695 (1935).
Story: The Globoke and Raciaz branches were added to the network as part of ongoing efforts to seed Chabad education across provincial Polish towns. Both appeared on the official 5695 list of branches published in HaTamim Vol. 1 that summer.
Tags: poland, globoke, raciaz, tomchei tmimim, branch

Title: Kuperstock decides to make aliyah
Summary: In the winter of 5695 R. Kuperstock resolved to leave Globoke and settle in Eretz Yisrael.
Story: After two years of serving as rabbi of the Chabad community in Globoke, R. Menachem Mendel Kuperstock decided in the winter of 5695 (1935) to make aliyah. He eventually settled in Haifa and founded a Chabad community there.
Tags: kuperstock, globoke, haifa, aliyah

Title: Mrs. Rashka Rivlin, granddaughter of Hebron's Chabad rav, dies at 92
Summary: Mrs. Rashka Rivlin, granddaughter of R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin of Hebron, died in Jerusalem in Tevet 5695 at age 92.
Story: Rashka Rivlin, wife of R' David Tzvi Rivlin, was according to the introduction of 'Ohalei Yosef' on the Talmud (Jerusalem 1956) and a letter from M.S. Slonim, the granddaughter—not daughter—of Hebron's chief rabbi R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin. Born in 5603, she lived to 92 and died in Tevet 5695 in Jerusalem.
Tags: jerusalem, hebron, rivlin family, shimon menashe chaikin

Title: Yeshiva enrollment reaches 197 students
Summary: On 26 Tevet 5695 the Rosh Yeshiva reported total enrollment of 197 students, up from roughly 155-160 the previous summer.
Story: R. Yehuda Eber sent updated student lists for the hall, classes and branches, noting significant growth in the kibbutz and other departments. He prayed for the financial means to maintain them and thereby improve quality alongside quantity.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei-temimim, enrollment

Title: Rebbe directs book purchases from Purkersdorf sanitorium
Summary: From the Purkersdorf sanitorium in winter 5695 the Frierdiker Rebbe sent funds and detailed purchasing instructions to librarian Chaim Liberman in Warsaw.
Story: During the Rebbe's winter convalescence in Austria, he and his librarian conducted an active correspondence about acquisitions. Liberman's responses — including 7 Shevat 5695 — describe specific purchases of book lots for 25 to 200 zlotys, queries about exchanges of duplicates, and consultation on individual titles, evidence of the Rebbe's hands-on involvement in every significant decision.
Tags: purkersdorf, warsaw, library, rayatz, chaim-liberman, book-collecting

Title: Yeshaya Chanoch Berchen becomes rabbi of Gostini
Summary: Yeshaya Chanoch Berchen, born in Livani in 5644, took up his post as rabbi of Gostini on 11 January 1935.
Story: According to the volume 'Latvia: Synagogues and Rabbis' (Riga 2005), Yeshaya Chanoch Berchen was installed as rabbi of Gostini on 11 January 1935 (26 Tevet 5695). The town had two Chassidic shuls and two for the misnagdim. He would soon lead the Chabad yeshiva there and serve as a key node in the Latvia branch network.
Tags: gostini, dankra, latvia, yeshaya-chanoch-berchen

Title: Rebbe writes long Yiddish history of early Chasidism
Summary: From the Purkersdorf sanatorium the Rebbe wrote a 100+ page Yiddish letter to his daughter Chaya Mushka on the early history of Chasidism.
Story: Known as Der Longa Brief, the letter offered a graphic portrait of shtetl spiritual life and the figures who spread chasidic teachings. It was composed while the Rebbe was under Dr. Gerson's care and is filled with rich prose about the genesis of the chasidic movement.
Tags: chasidism, history, yiddish, der-longa-brief, purkersdorf

Title: Leah Beila Levin writes Rebbe Rayatz after being injured in food line
Summary: On Tuesday of Parshas Yisro 5695 the author's mother Leah Beila wrote the Rebbe Rayatz describing her injury when a non-Jew pushed her in a food queue.
Story: On Tuesday of Parshas Yisro 5695 (around January 22, 1935), Leah Beila Levin—widow of R. Ephraim Shmuel and mother of the author—wrote a letter to the Rebbe Rayatz, now preserved in the archives. She described being shoved by a non-Jew while waiting on a sidewalk in a Soviet food queue, falling and gashing her head open and requiring stitches. She wrote of her hope for redemption and ascribed her survival to the merit of her orphaned children.
Tags: leah beila levin, rayatz, soviet union, injury, famine, yisro, levin family

Title: R. Yechezkel Feigin summarizes branch finances on 18 Shevat 5695
Summary: On 18 Shevat 5695, secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to R. Yisrael Jacobson detailing how the central yeshiva and branches were funded.
Story: Feigin explained that the Warsaw kibbutz and top two classes ran on their own income, while four lower Warsaw classes plus the Vilna, Lodz and Patzanow branches were funded by the Rebbe's accounts. In times of severe shortage, R. Yehuda Eber would appeal directly to the Rebbe to prevent closures.
Tags: yechezkel feigin, yisrael jacobson, tomchei tmimim, yehuda eber, finance

Title: Photograph of Rayatz with the Rebbe at Pirkersdorf
Summary: On 25 Adar I 5695 the Rayatz was photographed with the Rebbe standing among the trees at the Pirkersdorf convalescent resort.
Story: On 25 Adar I 5695 (28 February 1935), at the Pirkersdorf convalescent resort where the Rayatz had gone for medical treatment, the Rayatz was photographed standing among the trees together with the Rebbe. Two further photographs from the same session show the Rayatz alone among the trees.
Tags: rayatz, rebbe, pirkersdorf, austria, convalescence, photograph

Title: Rafael Cohen elected rabbi of Riga chassidic community
Summary: In Adar Sheni 5695, R. Rafael Cohen was elected to serve as rabbi of the chassidic community in Riga.
Story: On Motzaei Shabbos Parshas Pekudei, R. Faigin had written to the Rashag (Chadakov) conveying the Rebbe's instruction that anash should work and campaign for Cohen's appointment. He was confirmed in the position in Adar Sheni 5695, with Chief Rabbi R. Menachem Mendel Zak requesting his official authorization to perform marriages.
Tags: rafael-cohen, riga, rabbinate, chassidic-community

Title: Yisrael Yehuda Levin arrested at R. Zalman Kornitzer's Malakhovka home
Summary: The author and Avraham Kievman were arrested at R. Zalman Kornitzer's Malakhovka home for residing within 100 km of Moscow without registration.
Story: Soon after Purim 5695, Soviet detectives raided R. Zalman Kornitzer's Malakhovka home in the night and arrested the author and Avraham Kievman, who were sleeping there unregistered within the forbidden 100-kilometer Moscow zone. They were jailed in Lyubertsy in a cell with thieves and murderers; the criminals plucked hairs from Kievman's red beard, breaking his spirit. After several days they were released on signing a pledge that a second offense would mean two years of exile.
Tags: malakhovka, nkvd, arrest, soviet persecution, lyubertsy prison, avraham kievman, zalman kornitzer

Title: Purim 5695 farbrengen at R. Zalman Kornitzer's Malakhovka home
Summary: On Purim 5695 R. Elchonon Morozov led a farbrengen at R. Zalman Kornitzer's Malakhovka home with R. Yonah Cohen.
Story: The Purim 5695 farbrengen at R. Zalman Kornitzer's home was led by R. Elchonon Morozov and joined by R. Yonah Cohen, a fervent singer who drank heavily and led niggunim while R. Elchonon spoke. R. Elchonon expounded that the Rebbe Rayatz is 'Avinu Malkenu'—just as the Alter Rebbe was Atzmus, so too the present Rebbe—and that, unlike the Alter Rebbe's chassidim, the Rayatz's chassidim include those who never saw him yet bind themselves to him with mesirus nefesh. The drasha left a deep impression on the bochurim present.
Tags: malakhovka, purim, elchonon morozov, zalman kornitzer, yonah cohen, farbrengen, rayatz

Title: Second arrest at Malakhovka shul with Shimshon Charitonov
Summary: After Pesach 5695, NKVD detectives raided the Malakhovka shul at night and arrested the author together with Shimshon Charitonov.
Story: After Pesach 5695 the author resumed sleeping in the Malakhovka shul together with Shimshon Charitonov. In a midnight raid, detectives shone flashlights and burst through the door, taking both bochurim to the Lyubertsy police. At dawn the author quickly donned tefillin and prayed, then persuaded the police chief—through humor and a misfiled prior pledge—to release them. R. Yaakov Maskalik later comforted him by recounting the Tzemach Tzedek's blessing of 'mice' that ate incriminating court papers.
Tags: malakhovka, nkvd, arrest, soviet persecution, shimshon charitonov, tefillin, yaakov maskalik, tzemach tzedek

Title: Researcher Zalman Reisen visits Warsaw library
Summary: On 27 Adar Sheni 5695 the Yiddish scholar Reisen spent an hour and a half studying Yiddish books and manuscripts in the Lubavitch library in Warsaw.
Story: Librarian Liberman reported to the Rebbe that Reisen was especially interested in the Yiddish and Ivri-Taytsh divisions and was shown manuscripts and broadsides. Reisen requested permission to publish some items in YIVO's anthologies, asked to borrow others, and inquired whether the library had a room where scholars could work — leaving the visit deeply impressed by holdings he had not expected to find.
Tags: warsaw, library, yivo, zalman-reisen, yiddish, research

Title: Rayatz returns to Warsaw before Passover
Summary: The Rayatz arrived back in Warsaw on 12 Nisan, just in time for Passover.
Story: His half-year stay in Austria had ended after a few additional days of communal meetings in Vienna. He returned home for the holiday with his family.
Tags: warsaw, passover, perchtoldsdorf

Title: Yisrael Yehuda Levin mails photograph to Rebbe Rayatz from Moscow
Summary: On Erev Shabbos Emor 7 Iyar 5695, the author photographed himself in Moscow and mailed his picture to the Rebbe Rayatz with a request for blessing.
Story: Hearing while in prison that the Rebbe Rayatz had asked chassidim to send him their photographs, the author resolved to comply once freed. On Friday 7 Iyar 5695 (May 10, 1935) he entered a Moscow photo studio, urging them to finish before Shabbos, and just before sunset received the prints and mailed them at the post office. His accompanying letter asked the Rebbe to arouse mercy for 'Yisrael Yehuda ben Leah Beila' that he merit to see the Rebbe face to face, and listed R. Chaim Ezra Bronstein as his return address.
Tags: rayatz, photograph, soviet union, moscow, chaim ezra bronstein, samizdat

Title: Rayatz letter mentioning Mohar'mtz Landau
Summary: On 3 Sivan 5695 Rayatz wrote a letter addressed to a relative identified as Mohar'mtz Landau, descended from the Tzemach Tzedek's son Baruch Shalom.
Story: In a letter of 3 Sivan 5695 (June 1935), Rayatz addressed an elder relative as 'sh'ber bsari' (my flesh-relation), with the surname Landau noted at the top. Chabad historian Rabbi Levin conjectures this is Moshe Tzvi Landau, son of Dan Landau (a son-in-law of Rabbi Baruch Shalom), illustrating how scattered branches of the Tzemach Tzedek's descendants were tracked through Rayatz's correspondence.
Tags: rayatz, landau, letters, family

Title: Rebbe decides to spend summer in Warsaw suburbs
Summary: On 3 Sivan 5695 the Rebbe wrote that for several important reasons he could not travel abroad that summer and would rent a residence in the resort area around Warsaw.
Story: This decision laid the groundwork for the Rebbe's extended summer stay in Otwock that year, which evolved into a permanent move of his household and the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim to Otwock by year's end.
Tags: warsaw, otwock, letter

Title: Rebbe Rayatz replies to Yisrael Yehuda Levin's photograph
Summary: On 16 Sivan 5695 Rebbe Rayatz replied to the author's photo letter, blessing him and sending regards to his friends and relatives.
Story: On 16 Sivan 5695 (around June 18, 1935), the Rebbe Rayatz replied to the photograph and letter the author had sent the previous month. The Rebbe wrote that he had enjoyed seeing the photograph, asked the author to convey greetings to his friends and relatives, and blessed him with Hashem's help. In the darkness of those Soviet years, the letter and blessing gave the author considerable joy and encouragement.
Tags: rayatz, photograph, soviet union, letter, blessing

Title: HaTamim reports Tomchei Temimim activity in Chelm
Summary: The journal HaTamim reports on a group of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw students active in spreading Torah and Chassidus among the youth of Chelm.
Story: Issue 1 of HaTamim (Tammuz 5695) describes a cluster of Tomchei Temimim alumni in Chelm running Torah classes and a Chassidus shiur for members of Tzeirei Agudas Yisrael. The chief organizer is identified as Yaakov Yitzchak Rosenbaum, a Warsaw Tomchei Temimim student. This reporting laid the groundwork for the formal Chelm branch founded the next year.
Tags: chelm, poland, ha-tamim, tomchei-temimim, yaakov-yitzchak-rosenbaum

Title: HaTamim Vol. 1 publishes 5695 branch list
Summary: In Tammuz 5695 (June/July 1935), HaTamim Vol. 1 summarized the Tomchei Tmimim branches operating across Poland.
Story: The summary listed branches in Vilna, Globoke, Lodz, Chmielnik, Patzanow and others. This published account served as the first widely circulated public record of the network's reach during the interwar period.
Tags: hatamim, poland, tomchei tmimim, branches

Title: Rebbe moves from Warsaw to Otwock
Summary: After nearly two years in Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz relocated to nearby Otwock in early Tammuz 5695.
Story: The sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, had lived in Warsaw from Elul 5693 (1933). In early Tammuz 5695 (July 1935) he moved with his household and library to the smaller town of Otwock outside Warsaw, where he would remain for about four years until the end of 5699 (1939). The library was relocated under his oral direction since he was personally present in Warsaw at the time.
Tags: poland, warsaw, otwock, rayatz, library

Title: Rebbe Rayatz and Tomchei Temimim relocate to Otwock
Summary: In summer 5695 the Rebbe Rayatz moved from Warsaw to Otwock, and the central Tomchei Temimim yeshiva relocated with him.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz moved his residence to the nearby town of Otwock, and the yeshiva followed into a three-story building at Slowackiego 1. Initially considered temporary (as letterhead reflected), the move soon became permanent, opening the 'golden era' of Tomchei Temimim in Otwock that lasted four years until the war.
Tags: otwock, warsaw, tomchei-temimim, rayatz, relocation

Title: Twelfth of Tammuz celebrated at Rebbe's residence in Otwock
Summary: On 12 Tammuz 5695, the Rebbe's chag ha'geulah was celebrated with great honor in Otwock, where the Rebbe was then staying.
Story: Many chassidim and Tmimim came from Warsaw and the surrounding towns. The Rebbe delivered numerous sichos and inyanim. By late summer it had been decided that both the Rebbe and the yeshiva would relocate permanently to Otwock.
Tags: otwock, yud-beis-tammuz, geulah

Title: Elul 5695 NKVD sweep of Malakhovka thwarted by R. Zalman Kornitzer
Summary: In early Elul 5695 the NKVD came to round up Anash in Malakhovka; R. Zalman Kornitzer warned the targeted families and many escaped.
Story: At the start of Elul 5695 (late August 1935), NKVD investigators came to R. Zalman Kornitzer (Alpert) demanding 'Zalman Kornitzer'—which he denied, giving his legal name Alpert. While held at the village council he overheard officers reading a list of Anash to arrest: Shmuel Leib Paritzer (R. Shmuel Levitin), Shlomo Chaim Palatzker (Kesselman), Avraham Mayarer (Dreizin) and others. After being released he raced to warn each family on the list, saving many from arrest; investigators had tricked two captured boys into naming Anash, mistaking nicknames for surnames. R. Yonah Cohen then took it upon himself with mesirus nefesh to care for the bochurim and Anash children, receiving the Rebbe's blessing to be strong in this work.
Tags: malakhovka, nkvd, soviet persecution, zalman kornitzer, shmuel levitin, shlomo chaim kesselman, avraham dreizin, yonah cohen

Title: First issue of HaTamim journal printed in Warsaw
Summary: The first issue of HaTamim, the Chabad journal of Agudas Talmidei HaTmimim, was completed at the end of Menachem Av 5695.
Story: On 20 Menachem Av 5695 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote that HaTamim was ready for press. Its formal editors were R' Yechezkel Feigin and R' Yehuda Eber, with R' Shmuel Zalmanov as general editor, but in practice the Rebbe Rayatz's son-in-law (later the Rebbe) in Paris substantially edited and annotated the material. R' Schneur Zalman Gourary oversaw publication on behalf of the Agudah.
Tags: warsaw, hatamim, agudas talmidei hatmimim, rayatz, rebbe rashab successor, paris

Title: Tel Aviv cheder has closed; Havlin seeks to rent the building
Summary: On 20 Menachem Av 5695 Havlin asked the Beit Din for permission to rent out the closed cheder's building on Rav Kook Street to support Torat Emet.
Story: Citing the dire financial state of Torat Emet in Jerusalem, Havlin requested rabbinic approval to rent out the building at 16 Rav Kook Street in Tel Aviv, which had been donated by Mr. Friedman and registered in Havlin's name to circumvent registration restrictions. The rental did not actually take place, and the building was soon dedicated as a Chabad synagogue.
Tags: tel aviv, rav kook street, torat emet, shlomo zalman havlin, friedman, beit din

Title: Main yeshiva moves from Warsaw to Otwock; Mechina remains in Warsaw
Summary: At the start of 5696 the senior division of Tomchei Tmimim relocated to Otwock while the three Mechina classes stayed in Warsaw.
Story: The Olam and two upper classes moved to Otwock, leaving roughly 60 Mechina talmidim in Warsaw under R' Schneur Zalman Gourary and R' Moshe Pinchas Katz. The Mechina initially stayed at the Agudas Chabad shul at Zamenhof 8, then later relocated to the Shmotkin family compound at Moranowska 32 when a third class was added.
Tags: warsaw, otwock, tomchei tmimim, mechina, poland, moshe pinchas katz

Title: Shmuel Tzvi Fuchs enters Otwock yeshiva after bar mitzva
Summary: At the end of Elul 5695, immediately after his bar mitzva, Shmuel Tzvi Fuchs arrived to study at Tomchei Temimim in Otwock.
Story: Fuchs entered the first preparatory class, where nigleh was studied by day and Tanya at night. He would learn there until the outbreak of WWII at the end of 5699, and counted his Tishrei 5696 with the Rebbe as a central experience of his life.
Tags: otwock, tomchei-temimim, fuchs, talmidim

Title: Rayatz relocates permanently to Otwock
Summary: On 21 Elul, the Rayatz moved permanently to Otwock, and the central Tomchei Temimim yeshiva was transferred there from Warsaw.
Story: Otwock's clean air and quiet streets suited the Rayatz's health needs while keeping him close to Warsaw. The yeshiva's transfer made the town a major center of Chabad life in interwar Poland.
Tags: otwock, warsaw, poland, tomchei temimim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz recalls Rosenbaum's gift of the Tzemach Tzedek's tallis
Summary: On 12 Tishrei 5696 the Rebbe Rayatz writes that R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum had sent his father, the Rebbe Rashab, the tallis in which the Tzemach Tzedek had prayed.
Story: In a letter dated 12 Tishrei 5696 (1935), published in Igros Kodesh vol. 3, the Rebbe Rayatz tells R. Dovid Shifrin that 'many years ago' R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum had presented his father, the Rebbe Rashab, with the Tzemach Tzedek's tallis gadol. Rosenbaum had purchased the tallis with a generous sum from the meshulach R. Madil, recognized it physically as the one in which the Rebbe had prayed, and eventually sent it to Lubavitch rather than wear it himself.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, rebbe rashab, rebbe rayatz, tallis, letters, lubavitch

Title: Tishrei 5696 holiday minyanim in Moscow under Soviet surveillance
Summary: During Tishrei 5696, Anash held clandestine High Holiday and Sukkot minyanim in Moscow, including a Shmini Atzeret farbrengen held adjacent to Butyrka prison where many Chassidim were jailed.
Story: On Hoshana Rabbah and Simchat Torah, Israel Yehuda traveled to the Marina Roshcha synagogue, where the sharp-minded R' Mendel Leib Yaakobson unexpectedly joined the hakafot. Fearing arrest, on Shmini Atzeret the group gathered at the home of a friendly Lithuanian Jew situated directly next to the Butyrka prison, holding a heartfelt farbrengen with R' Melech Kaplan while their imprisoned brethren sat just meters away.
Tags: moscow, marina roshcha, butyrka prison, simchat torah, shmini atzeret, melech kaplan, mendel leib yaakobson

Title: Yeshiva relocates from Warsaw to Otwock
Summary: In Tishrei 5696 Tomchei Tmimim left its Warsaw building of nearly a decade and moved to Otwock at Slovatzkenya 1.
Story: In Tishrei 5696 (autumn 1935) the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim — having outgrown the building at Mlawska 7 / Sapuzinski 17 where it had operated for nearly ten years — relocated to the nearby town of Otwock, taking up new quarters at Slovatzkenya Street 1. The move responded to overcrowding that had developed even before the expansion noted in earlier internal reports.
Tags: warsaw, otwock, poland, tomchei-tmimim, yeshiva

Title: Israel Yehuda's military exemption via glasses ruse on 11 Tishrei
Summary: Israel Yehuda received a full Red Army exemption at his Yegoryevsk induction by feigning poor eyesight on the advice of the Rebbe Rayatz.
Story: Facing conscription that endangered observant Jews, Israel Yehuda wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz and consulted senior Tmimim including R' Nissan Nemanov and R' Yaakov Maskalik. After receiving the Rebbe's directive to wear glasses, he obtained reading glasses at the Semashko clinic and on 11 Tishrei 5696 deliberately misread the eye chart, securing a complete exemption rather than the conditional one given to two other Anash bochurim that day.
Tags: soviet union, russia, yegoryevsk, military draft, rebbe rayatz, nissan nemanov, yaakov maskalik

Title: Levin reports for army induction in Moscow
Summary: On 11 Tishrei 5696 Yisrael Yehuda Levin was required to appear for army induction in Moscow, weeks after the senior Lubavitchers there had been arrested and exiled.
Story: Levin had no proper identity papers and a record of arrests, and his classmates warned that the secret police were inquiring about a young man matching his description. The Rebbe Rayatz instructed him to put on eyeglasses, and miraculously he received a total exemption from military service. He immediately fled Moscow for Voronezh.
Tags: red army, moscow, draft, soviet union, kgb

Title: Rebbe Rayatz recalls Rosenbaum's Tzemach Tzedek gift in 5696 letter
Summary: On 12 Tishrei 5696 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' David Schifrin recalling how Rosenbaum had years earlier sent the Rebbe Rashab a handwritten power-of-attorney of the Tzemach Tzedek, a gift the Rebbe had cherished greatly.
Story: In a letter dated 12 Tishrei 5696 (Igrot Kodesh vol. 3 #803), the Rebbe Rayatz reminded R' David Schifrin that many years earlier the chassid Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum had presented the Rebbe Rashab with a handwritten power-of-attorney signed by the Tzemach Tzedek. The Rebbe Rashab had treasured the gift, and the memory was preserved in the Rebbe Rayatz's correspondence decades later.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, tzemach tzedek, manuscripts, schifrin

Title: Israel Yehuda relocates to Voronezh to study under R' Betzalel Wilshansky
Summary: After Tishrei 5696, Israel Yehuda traveled to Voronezh at R' Yonah Cohen's direction to learn under the influence of R' Betzalel Wilshansky alongside other older bochurim.
Story: R' Yonah Cohen sent the older bochurim approaching marriage age to receive guidance from R' Betzalel Wilshansky in Voronezh. Israel Yehuda joined Michoel Teitelbaum, Shaul Prafoisker (Steinbach), and Shalom Wilenkin there to learn, while also tutoring R' Betzalel's twelve-year-old son Folka (later R' Refoel Wilshansky).
Tags: voronezh, betzalel wilshansky, yonah cohen, underground yeshiva, michoel teitelbaum

Title: Latvian police raid four Chasidim running Russia aid operation
Summary: In November 1935 Latvian police simultaneously raided the homes of four Russian Chasidim running the Rebbe's covert aid operation to Soviet Jews.
Story: Moshe and Shmaryahu Gurary, Dovber Chaskind, and Yosef Rosenblum had been working full-time from Riga shipping food packages and transferring funds to Jews in Russia. All four were jailed and released on bail. Forced to choose between prison or expulsion, the Rebbe advised emigration to British Mandate Palestine, where they continued the operation from Tel Aviv.
Tags: riga, latvia, russia, food-packages, gurary, chaskind, rosenblum

Title: Rayatz letter to Rabbi Eliyahu Chaim Althoyz on recording chasidic history
Summary: On 17 Marcheshvan 5696 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote letter no. 810 to R' Eliyahu Chaim Althoyz urging him to record his memories of Lubavitch and Kremenchug.
Story: On 17 Marcheshvan 5696 (November 1935), Rayatz pressed the chasid R' Eliyahu Chaim Althoyz to set aside time to write down what he had heard from his father and uncle about their time in Lubavitch and what he remembered from Kremenchug, particularly about the elder chasidim known as 'the bears.' The letter is part of Rayatz's larger campaign to recruit chasidim to preserve oral chasidic history.
Tags: rayatz, althoyz, letters, kremenchug, historiography

Title: Rebbe directs Rabbi Cheifetz to teach his daughter chasidic philosophy
Summary: Asked whether women may study chasidic philosophy, the Rebbe answers emphatically yes and tells Rabbi Cheifetz to study maamarim with his daughter.
Story: The Rebbe quoted his grandfather Rabbi Shmuel: 'amongst Chasidim there is no difference between a boy or a girl.' He lamented that this had been said fifty-five years earlier 'when the light of Chasidism was burning brightly,' adding that 'now this is an even greater imperative.' The directive catalyzed the formation of Achot Hatemimim, bringing teens and young women into serious study of chasidic texts.
Tags: women, cheifetz, chasidut, maamar, achot hatemimim

Title: Rebbe writes Rabbi Cheifetz endorsing women's chasidic study
Summary: The Rebbe instructs Rabbi Mordechai Cheifetz to teach maamarim to his daughter, citing his grandfather's teaching.
Story: Quoting Rabbi Shmuel that 'amongst Chasidim there is no difference between a boy or a girl,' the Rebbe lamented neglect of girls' chasidic education. This catalyzed the formation of Achot Hatemimim and serious women's chasidic study.
Tags: women, chasidic-philosophy, cheifetz, letter

Title: Achos Tmimim founded in Riga
Summary: The Achos Tmimim organization for daughters of Chabad chassidim was established in Riga during winter 5697.
Story: Beginning the previous winter, daughters of Riga chassidim had organized informal gatherings. By Yud-Tes Kislev 5697 they were structured enough to send a collective letter to the Rebbe describing their celebration. Over the course of 5697 the framework crystallized into the named organization Achos Tmimim, with three appointed 'shepherds': R. Avraham Eliyahu Asherov, R. Mordechai Chefetz, and R. Eliyahu Chaim Altheuse.
Tags: achos-tmimim, riga, women, chassidus-study, girls

Title: Arab Revolt against the British Mandate
Summary: Jerusalem's mufti Mohammed Amin al-Husseini led a major Arab revolt against the British Mandate.
Story: The revolt was one in a sequence of violent campaigns al-Husseini orchestrated, including the 1920 Balfour-protest riots and the 1929 Hebron massacre. He would later travel to Berlin during World War II to encourage the Holocaust.
Tags: palestine, arab-revolt, mufti, husseini, british-mandate

Title: Author becomes director of Yeshivas Toras Emes in Boro Park
Summary: After Chabad chassidim were invited into the leadership of Yeshivas Toras Emes in Boro Park, the author entered as director at the start of 5697.
Story: He brought in R' Yosef Dov Castel as Rosh Mesivta of the upper division, R' Yissachar Frankel for the Gemara class, and R' Nachman Mandel as a teacher. The yeshiva's spiritual standard rose substantially and Brownsville parents sent their sons there. However, Anash failed to engage with the yeshiva's leadership, the finances deteriorated under fundraiser R' Baruch Karf, and the author eventually withdrew when salaries went unpaid.
Tags: toras emes, boro park, yosef dov castel, yissachar frankel, nachman mandel

Title: Central yeshiva moves to Otwock
Summary: The central Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva relocated from Warsaw to Otwock in 5696.
Story: In 5696 (1935-1936), the central Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva (with the older students) moved from Warsaw to Otwock, a resort town and known recuperative location near the Polish capital. Three lower classes remained in Warsaw, while the central yeshiva occupied several buildings in a healthful pine forest setting in Otwock.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, otwock, warsaw, poland

Title: Chelm yeshiva opens with 40 students
Summary: In summer 5696 the new Achei Temimim branch in Chelm began operating with roughly forty students in two classes.
Story: The yeshiva opened with about forty students, mostly local Chelm boys with some from surrounding towns. Avraham Goldman taught the lower class and Pesachya Meller the upper class. Local balebatim provided room and board for out-of-town students, while the Otwock central yeshiva sent a monthly subsidy for staff salaries.
Tags: chelm, poland, achei-temimim, avraham-goldman, pesachya-meller

Title: Death of Rabbi Yosef Leib Beriya
Summary: Rabbi Yosef Leib Beriya, the scholar who maintained Lubavitch's last synagogue, passed away in 1936.
Story: In 1936, Rabbi Yosef Leib Beriya, a scholar respected by both Jews and non-Jews alike, passed away in Lubavitch. His death directly preceded the Soviet authorities' closure of the town's last synagogue, which he had maintained until his passing. His death marked the practical end of Lubavitch's organized Jewish life.
Tags: lubavitch, soviet union, yosef leib beriya, synagogue closure, scholar

Title: Death of RashZ Hablin
Summary: RashZ Hablin, the director of Yeshivat Torat Emet in Jerusalem, passed away in 5696.
Story: SiLA later recounted to RashZ Hablin's sons the early days of the yeshiva's reestablishment, describing how on the day of his arrival in Jerusalem he had been given a note from the Rebbe Rayatz indicating that Hablin alone should direct the institution. SiLA helped him in good faith with all that was needed for the yeshiva.
Tags: jerusalem, rashaz hablin, yeshiva torat emet

Title: JDC begins winding down Agro-Joint
Summary: With the farming communities believed to have gained economic stability, the JDC began closing the Agro-Joint program.
Story: Leaders did not anticipate the wave of Stalinist terror that would follow. Within a year, secret police would arrest close to two hundred Agro-Joint workers as members of a 'foreign organization,' bringing a tragic end to the JDC-Soviet partnership.
Tags: jdc, agro-joint, soviet-union, wind-down

Title: Lentschna branch founded by Pesachya Meller
Summary: After 5696 Pesachya Meller founded the Achei Temimim Lubavitch branch in Lentschna, where he also served as maggid shiur.
Story: After leaving his post in Chelm in 5696, Pesachya Meller founded a new Achei Temimim Lubavitch yeshiva in Lentschna and served as its maggid shiur. It was listed in the 5699 yeshiva calendar and reported in HaPardes as having 75 students.
Tags: lentschna, poland, achei-temimim, pesachya-meller, tomchei-temimim

Title: Lubavitch's last synagogue closed by Soviets
Summary: The last synagogue in Lubavitch was shuttered by Communist authorities in 1936.
Story: In 1936, Communist authorities shuttered the last operating synagogue in the town of Lubavitch, ending centuries of organized Jewish religious life there. The closure followed the passing of Rabbi Yosef Leib Beriya, a scholar respected by Jews and non-Jews alike, who had maintained the synagogue. This marked the end of Lubavitch as a functioning Jewish community under Soviet rule.
Tags: lubavitch, soviet union, communism, synagogue closure

Title: Mechina relocates to Murnowska 32
Summary: In 5696, the Mechina moved into the Chabad shul built by R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin at Murnowska 32 in Warsaw.
Story: Over the years, R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin had acquired a courtyard and building at Murnowska 32 in Warsaw, dedicating part of it as a Chabad shul. In 5696 (1936) the Mechina relocated there from Dzika 8. The same address would later host the Rebbe Rayatz himself during the first days of WWII.
Tags: warsaw, murnowska 32, mechina, shneur zalman shmotkin

Title: Polish government enacts currency restrictions
Summary: Poland withdrew from the 'gold block' and instituted currency restrictions, making it problematic to transfer funds in and out of the country.
Story: The restrictions hampered the Rebbe's ability to manage finances from Poland. In response, the Rebbe entrusted the Ramash in Paris with much of his financial affairs, having him open accounts and maintain records. The Rebbe instructed donors globally to send contributions directly to the Ramash in Paris.
Tags: poland, currency, finance, gold-block

Title: R' Yosef Rosen ends second Dvinsk tenure
Summary: The Rogatchover Gaon's second tenure as rabbi of Dvinsk's Planover Minyan ended in 1936.
Story: After returning to Dvinsk in 1926, R' Yosef Rosen, the Rogatchover Gaon, served at the Planover Minyan until 1936 (5696). His departure marked the close of one of the most renowned Chabad rabbinates in interwar Latvia.
Tags: dvinsk, rogatchover, rabbinate

Title: R. Dovber Garfinkel (Kornitzer) appointed mashgiach in Otwock
Summary: In 5696 R. Dovber Kornitzer (Garfinkel) fled Russia and was immediately appointed by the Rebbe as general mashgiach and examiner.
Story: Renowned for knowing Shas by heart and for unusual clarity of explanation, Kornitzer transformed the yeshiva atmosphere from the moment he arrived. He instituted Erev Shabbos chazara of maamarim in the forest surrounding the yeshiva, where chaburos of students sat at fixed tables among tall trees to repeat Chassidus before Kabbalas Shabbos.
Tags: otwock, tomchei-temimim, garfinkel, kornitzer, russia, mashgiach

Title: R. Moshe Eliyahu Gerlitzky sent to teach in Łódź
Summary: In 5697 the Rebbe instructed R. Moshe Eliyahu Gerlitzky to leave Otwock and return to Łódź to teach.
Story: Having studied in Otwock until 5697, R. Moshe Eliyahu Gerlitzky was instructed by the Rebbe to return to Łódź — this time as a teacher. He found a group of devoted chassidish bochurim and taught them nigleh and chassidus through 5699, ultimately managing the division during the final two years of the yeshiva's existence.
Tags: poland, lodz, moshe-eliyahu-gerlitzky, otwock, tomchei-tmimim, appointment

Title: Rabbi Yechezkel Abramsky visits Tomchei Temimim
Summary: During 5696 Rabbi Yechezkel Abramsky (Chazon Yechezkel) visited Tomchei Temimim while passing through Poland.
Story: Abramsky, dayan of the London Beis Din, deliberately detoured to visit the yeshiva and found there about 200 fine bochurim diligently learning Torah and yiras Hashem, all sustained by the yeshivas treasury. A year later, on Lag BaOmer 5697, he publicized this visit in a letter of support urging Jews everywhere to become regular supporters of the yeshiva.
Tags: otwock, tomchei-temimim, abramsky, london, visitors

Title: Rayatz moves Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim and his residence to Otwock
Summary: The Rayatz's official chronology records 1936 as the year his residence and the central yeshiva moved to Otwock.
Story: Although the actual relocation occurred in 1935, the canonical timeline assigns it to 5696. Otwock became the Rayatz's home until his escape from Nazi-occupied Poland.
Tags: otwock, poland, tomchei temimim

Title: Rebbe convenes senior students on Polish yeshivah challenges
Summary: In 1936 the Rebbe gathered senior Tomchei Temimim students privately, urging them to deepen their classmates' connection to chasidic teachings.
Story: Some students wanted to expand Talmud study and minimize chasidic philosophy, concerning the Rebbe who wished the Polish yeshivah to mirror the original Lubavitch model. He asked seniors to win over peers to the integration of nigleh and nistar. He confided his personal anguish: "In Russia I experienced self-sacrifice. Now I am experiencing it again with the move from Riga to Poland."
Tags: otwock, tomchei-temimim, chasidic-philosophy, self-sacrifice

Title: Stopnica branch of Tomchei Temimim active
Summary: A Tomchei Temimim branch in Stopnica operated from 5696 through 5699, listed in official yeshiva calendars and US fundraising correspondence.
Story: The Stopnica branch existed from 5696 until 5699 and is referenced in the yeshiva calendar for 5697, in a 16 Elul 5698 letter from the US Vaad LeHachzakas Tomchei Temimim listing active yeshivos, and in the 5699 yeshiva calendar. Beyond these mentions no further details are known.
Tags: stopnica, poland, tomchei-temimim

Title: Tomchei Tmimim branch founded in Chelm
Summary: A Tomchei Tmimim branch was founded in Chelm in 5696 (1936).
Story: Per the 5697 yeshiva calendar, the Chelm branch was organized in the summer of 5696. It would grow to about 100 students by the eve of WWII and was specifically named by the Frierdiker Rebbe in 5700 as a community whose students needed to be hurried to Vilna.
Tags: poland, chelm, tomchei tmimim, branch

Title: Tomchei Tmimim class photographs taken at Otwock
Summary: At the beginning of 5697, class photographs were taken of all Tomchei Tmimim students and staff in Otwock and Warsaw.
Story: At the beginning of 5697 (autumn 1936), class photographs were taken of every student of the yeshiva — both those in the main study hall and classes at Otwock and those in the preparatory program in Warsaw — along with every member of the yeshiva staff. The photo also included images of the yeshiva buildings in Otwock, which the yeshiva had entered at the beginning of 5696.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, otwock, photographs, class photo

Title: Toras Emes destroyed in 1936 Arab violence
Summary: During the 5696 disturbances the Toras Emes building was destroyed and burned by Arab attackers.
Story: Despite earlier discussions about relocating, the yeshiva had remained at its post-1929 location until the 5696 violence forced its hand. From there the yeshiva moved permanently to the Bukharian quarter, where it remained for the rest of Havlin's life.
Tags: jerusalem, toras emes, 1936 riots, destruction, bukharian quarter

Title: Warsaw rabbis sign support letter for yeshiva
Summary: In autumn 5697, members of the Warsaw rabbinical council signed a letter of support for Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: On the Sunday of parshat Haazinu 5697 (autumn 1936), a portion of the rabbis of the Warsaw rabbinical council signed a letter of support for the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva. A similar letter would be issued by the full council in Kislev 5698.
Tags: warsaw rabbinical council, tomchei tmimim, support letter, poland

Title: Yeshivas Zichron Yosef founded in Dankra
Summary: In 5696, after the Rogatchover Gaon's passing, a Chabad yeshiva named Zichron Yosef was opened in Dankra (Gostini), Latvia.
Story: Following the death of the Rogatchover Gaon Yosef Rosen in 5696, the town of Dankra (also called Gostini) in Latvia established a Chabad yeshiva named Zichron Yosef in his memory. The yeshiva was run by the town rabbi, Yeshaya Chanoch Berchen, son-in-law of Refael Hakohen of Riga.
Tags: dankra, gostini, latvia, zichron-yosef, rogatchover, yeshaya-chanoch-berchen

Title: Rayatz writes Zislin about discreet inquiry on the Kokorev crates
Summary: In Teves 5696, Rayatz writes chassid R. Zalman Idel Zislin asking him to discreetly locate where the crates from R. Zalka Persitz's storage are now held.
Story: The letter (4745) instructs Zislin to obtain information about the location of the boxes taken from the bailee R. Zalka Persitz — but without revealing who sent him on the errand. This represents one of the last surviving traces of the active 1930s effort to track the library, before contact was largely lost for fifty years.
Tags: library, soviet, moscow, kokorev-warehouses, zislin, persitz

Title: Rayatz returns to Perchtoldsdorf sanitorium
Summary: The Rayatz returned to the Perchtoldsdorf sanitorium on 17 Tevet for additional medical treatment.
Story: His ongoing health issues required regular treatment by Dr. Max Gerson. The Rayatz stayed in Austria until late February, returning home for his grandson's bar mitzvah.
Tags: perchtoldsdorf, vienna, austria, health

Title: Eber reports Otwock relocation and financial strain
Summary: On 18 Tevet 5696 R. Yehuda Eber wrote to R. Yehuda Leib Horowitz in Boston about the move of much of the yeshiva to Otwock.
Story: Eber described the new building amid a great forest in the best part of Otwock, housing the kibbutz and the two large classes (the two smaller remained in Warsaw as a branch). Hundreds of students were diligent, but the move and renovations had increased expenses while income shrank, exhausting the leaderships endurance.
Tags: otwock, tomchei-temimim, yehuda-eber, finances, horowitz, boston

Title: Group photo of students in Otwock
Summary: On 18 Tevet 5696 a group photograph was taken of Tomchei Temimim students in Otwock, including R. Moshe Beitch and R. Avraham Yitzchak Garfinkel.
Story: The photograph documents talmidim of Tomchei Temimim at Otwock during the yeshivas Otwock period, including R. Netta Denderowitz of Rika, R. Avraham Yitzchak Garfinkel of Warsaw, R. Moshe Beitch of Swierze and R. Moshe Rudnier of Krasne.
Tags: otwock, tomchei-temimim, talmidim, photo, beitch, garfinkel

Title: Bar mitzvah of Shalom Ber (Berke) Gurary
Summary: The Rayatz's grandson, Shalom Ber (Berke) Gurary, celebrated his bar mitzvah on 25-26 Shevat.
Story: The Rayatz returned from Perchtoldsdorf specifically to attend the bar mitzvah. Berke was the son of the Rayatz's eldest daughter Chana and her husband Rabbi Shmaryahu Gurary.
Tags: bar mitzvah, berke gurary, shalom ber gurary, warsaw

Title: Bar mitzvah of Shalom Dovber Gourary, grandson of the Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz farbrenged with Tomchei Tmimim talmidim in Otwock on 25 Shevat 5696 to mark the bar mitzvah of his grandson.
Story: The celebration was held in the yeshiva hall at Otwock, drawing guests from Poland, Riga, Vienna and elsewhere. Sichos delivered at the farbrengen were later printed in Likkutei Dibburim vol. 2. A surviving photograph shows the Rebbe Rayatz at the head table with the bar mitzvah boy, his father R' Shmaryahu Gourary, and the Rebbe's secretary R' Yechezkel Feigin.
Tags: otwock, shalom dovber gourary, shmaryahu gourary, rayatz, bar mitzvah, farbrengen

Title: Passing of the Rogatchover Gaon
Summary: The Rogatchover Gaon (Rabbi Joseph Rosen) passed away in Dvinsk on 11 Adar 5696.
Story: Rabbi Joseph Rosen, the renowned Rogatchover Gaon of Dvinsk, passed away on 11 Adar 5696 (March 5, 1936). Immediately after the shiva, his widow Rebbetzin Rivka organized a committee to print his manuscripts. His death set in motion decades of efforts to publish his extensive Torah writings.
Tags: rogatchover, dvinsk, latvia, rabbi joseph rosen

Title: Rogatchover Gaon passes away in Dvinsk
Summary: The Rogatchover Gaon (R. Yosef Rosen) passed away on 11 Adar 5696.
Story: The death of one of the great halachic luminaries of the era prompted commemorations across the Jewish world. R. Rafael Cohen, rabbi of the Riga chassidic community, delivered a eulogy at Erev Rosh Chodesh Nissan in the beis medrash named for the Rogatchover, later published as the booklet 'Emunah V'Zechirah'.
Tags: rogatchover, yosef-rosen, dvinsk, petira, halacha

Title: Dvinsk committee letter to Rabbi Goldfein on printing Rogatchover writings
Summary: The Dvinsk committee wrote to Rabbi Abba David Goldfein, the Rogatchover's son-in-law, asking him to come edit the manuscripts.
Story: On 19 Adar 5696, immediately after the shiva, a member of the committee organized by Rebbetzin Rivka wrote on her behalf to her son-in-law Rabbi Abba David Goldfein in his name, asking him to come to Dvinsk for several months to edit and prepare the Rogatchover's manuscripts for publication.
Tags: rogatchover, dvinsk, latvia, goldfein, manuscripts

Title: Rafael Cohen eulogizes the Rogatchover in Riga
Summary: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Nissan 5696, R. Rafael Cohen delivered a hesped for the Rogatchover Gaon.
Story: The eulogy was delivered in the beis medrash bearing the Rogatchover's name. In 5699 it was printed as the kuntres 'Emunah V'Zechirah' with the Rebbe Rayatz's haskama affirming that 'the entire content is true and proper and worthy of publication.'
Tags: rafael-cohen, rogatchover, riga, hesped, emunah-vzechirah

Title: Second Dvinsk letter to Rabbi Goldfein
Summary: A second letter was sent to Rabbi Goldfein urging a reply about coming to Dvinsk.
Story: Two weeks after the first letter, on 7 Nissan 5696, the Dvinsk committee wrote again to Rabbi Abba David Goldfein. Rebbetzin Rivka was anxiously awaiting his reply about coming to organize the publication of her late husband's manuscripts.
Tags: rogatchover, dvinsk, latvia, goldfein

Title: Decision to found Achei Temimim yeshiva branch in Chelm
Summary: At a post-Pesach gathering at Moshe Berland's home in Chelm, students returning from Tomchei Temimim Otwock resolved to open a local branch yeshiva.
Story: After Passover 5696, students who had been home for the holiday from Tomchei Temimim Lubavitch in Otwock convened a farbrengen at the home of Moshe Berland. They decided to establish a yeshiva in Chelm as a branch of the Otwock yeshiva, to be named Yeshivas Achei Temimim Lubavitch. Yaakov Yitzchak Rosenbaum was elected chairman and Avraham Yitzchak Kornblit secretary.
Tags: chelm, poland, achei-temimim, tomchei-temimim, otwock, moshe-berland

Title: Yeshiva refuses new students for summer 5696
Summary: On 18 Iyar 5696 R. Yehuda Eber wrote that for the first time the yeshiva had publicly announced it would accept no new students due to capacity.
Story: The Rosh Yeshiva reported it was the first time since Tomchei Temimims founding that they advertised in the press that no new talmidim would be accepted. Dozens of students from across Poland and abroad still came begging entry. The Rebbe Rayatz suffered greatly at having to refuse so many promising bochurim while other major yeshivos shrank to mere dozens of students.
Tags: otwock, tomchei-temimim, yehuda-eber, enrollment, rayatz

Title: Passing of Rabbi Abba David Goldfein
Summary: Rabbi Abba David Goldfein, the Rogatchover's son-in-law, passed away on 19 Iyar 5696.
Story: At the time the Dvinsk committee was writing him about editing the Rogatchover's manuscripts, Rabbi Abba David Goldfein was lying ill with severe heart disease. He passed away on 19 Iyar 5696, and the planned editorial project never came to fruition under him.
Tags: rogatchover, goldfein

Title: R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal reports 33 Vilna yeshiva students
Summary: On 24 Sivan 5696, director R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal reported to the Vilna Vaad HaYeshivot that the yeshiva had 33 students across three classes.
Story: R' Oshpal submitted a formal report stating the yeshiva contained three classes: 15 in class A, 7 in class B, and 11 in class C. Of the 33 students, 7 were residents of Vilna while 26 came from other towns. A full roster of students with their ages was attached the following day.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, rabbi yitzchak dov oshpal, vaad hayeshivot

Title: Rayatz travels to Paris for medical treatment
Summary: The Rayatz traveled to Paris on June 28 for treatment at the sanitorium in Ville-d'Avray.
Story: Ville-d'Avray, a suburb of Paris, hosted a major sanitorium the Rayatz used over multiple summers. He remained in France until the end of August, also engaging with the local chasidic community.
Tags: paris, ville d avray, france, health, sanitorium

Title: R' Shneur Zalman Slonim dies in Yafo
Summary: R' Shneur Zalman Slonim died on 11 Tammuz 5696 after serving as rabbi in Yafo-Tel Aviv for 37 years.
Story: He had built the Chabad community in Yafo from the ground up: founding the women's mikveh, organizing shechita, building a Chabad shul in Neve Shalom, delivering weekly chassidus, and serving on the Tel Aviv Chief Rabbinate until his death. His 37-year tenure shaped Chabad presence in the city.
Tags: yafo, tel aviv, shneur zalman slonim, rabbinate

Title: R. Yehuda Eber writes about student Moshe Pinchas Katz
Summary: On 29 Tammuz 5696, Rosh Yeshiva R. Yehuda Eber wrote to R. Avraham Ziskind about efforts to arrange entry papers for R. Moshe Pinchas Katz to the US.
Story: On 29 Tammuz 5696 (July 19, 1936), Rosh Yeshiva R. Yehuda Eber wrote to R. Avraham Ziskind regarding their student Moshe Pinchas Katz, noting they were doing everything possible — and more than was within their means — to help him. The letter was part of efforts to arrange a shidduch with one of R. David Stockhamer's daughters and secure US entry papers.
Tags: yehuda eber, moshe pinchas katz, avraham ziskind, matchmaking, emigration

Title: Rabbi David Meir Rabinowitz visits yeshiva in Otwock
Summary: On 29 Tammuz 5696 R. Yehuda Eber described the recent visit of Rabbi David Meir Rabinowitz of Boston to the yeshiva.
Story: Rabinowitz, en route to Eretz Yisrael, stopped at Otwock with his son Peretz and other American travelers. Upon entering the hall where about 70 senior students were learning, he was so overcome with emotion that he sat speechless against the wall for some time. At his farewell gathering he cried out that he had never imagined Tomchei Temimim could be so elevated.
Tags: otwock, tomchei-temimim, rabinowitz, boston, visitors

Title: Future Rebbe writes to R. Eliyahu Simpson about acquiring books
Summary: On 21 Menachem Av 5696 the Rebbe's son-in-law (later the Rebbe) asked R. Eliyahu Simpson to help collect books in America for the Rayatz's library.
Story: Writing on 21 Menachem Av 5696 (August 9, 1936), Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson asked R. Eliyahu Simpson, a senior Tomim in America, to organize anash there to send books to the Rebbe Rayatz's library. He specifically requested old siddurim, chumashim, haggadot, machzorim, and any early Hebrew imprints from America.
Tags: library, ramash, eliyahu-simpson, usa, manuscripts

Title: Lamm letter to Rayatz on portrait sale
Summary: On 19 August 1936 (Rosh Chodesh Elul 5696) Louis Lamm wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz detailing the provenance of oil portraits and 31 additional prints he sold him.
Story: In a German letter dated 19 August 1936, Amsterdam dealer Louis Lamm wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz about the sale of two oil portraits — R. Yosef Hatzaddik of Posen (obtained from Dr. Calvary of Posen in a barter for 60 Reichsmark in books) and R.
