Akiva Eiger (acquired from the Eiger family in 1913 for 25 Reichsmark) — along with 31 additional prints. Decades later this letter, found by R. Yitzchak Wilhelm during the archiving of the Rayatz's papers, finally identified the provenance of the portraits and many old calendars in the library.
Tags: louis lamm, amsterdam, portrait, rabbi akiva eiger, rayatz, correspondence

Title: Rayatz says maamar in the Paris chasidic community
Summary: Before leaving Paris, the Rayatz delivered a maamar in the chasidic community on 8 Elul.
Story: The maamar marked the conclusion of his summer stay and strengthened the Paris Chabad community ahead of the High Holidays. He then traveled via Vienna and Perchtoldsdorf back to Otwock.
Tags: paris, france, maamar

Title: Mikhail Nachmanson arrested by Soviet authorities
Summary: One of the two officers who arrested the Rebbe was himself arrested on his birthday and sentenced to a labor camp in Kolyma.
Story: Nachmanson, a Nevel-born Chabad-family Chasid turned Bolshevik who had risen to head regional NKVD departments, was transferred to Lubyanka Prison and given an extrajudicial five-year sentence. He was released in 1941, re-arrested in 1950, freed in 1953 after Stalin's death, and amnestied in 1956 — yet remained a committed Communist until the Soviet Union's collapse.
Tags: nachmanson, nkvd, leningrad, lubyanka, kolyma, purges

Title: Mikhail Nachmanson arrested for counterrevolutionary activity
Summary: GPU/NKVD officer Mikhail Nachmanson, who had arrested the Rebbe, was himself arrested on his birthday and sent to Lubyanka prison and later the Kolyma labor camp.
Story: On September 9, 1936, his birthday, former GPU/NKVD officer Mikhail Nachmanson was arrested for counterrevolutionary activity and transferred to Lubyanka Prison in Leningrad. Without trial, he received an extrajudicial five-year sentence in Kolyma. He was released in 1941, rearrested in 1950, freed after Stalin's death in 1953, and given amnesty in 1956, yet remained a committed Communist until the end of his life.
Tags: russia, nkvd, gpu, kolyma, lubyanka, purge

Title: Rayatz returns to Otwock after Paris and Austria
Summary: Returning from Paris via Vienna and Perchtoldsdorf, the Rayatz arrived back in Otwock on 22 Elul.
Story: The complex itinerary reflected the layered concerns of health, communal engagement, and family. He was home in time to lead the chasidim through the Tishrei holidays.
Tags: otwock, poland, vienna, perchtoldsdorf

Title: Secretary Feigin writes R. Yehuda Shmotkin about library acquisitions
Summary: On 3 Chol Hamoed Sukkos 5697 the Rebbe's secretary asked R. Yehuda Shmotkin to solicit book donations for the Otwock library.
Story: On the third day of Chol Hamoed Sukkos 5697 (October 1936), Rabbi Yechezkel Feigin wrote to R. Yehuda Shmotkin in Eretz Yisrael at the Rebbe Rayatz's request. Shmotkin was asked to approach authors and book-buyers to donate copies to the Rebbe's library at his Otwock address (Pruse 6), continuing the established custom of presenting books as gifts to the Lubavitch Bibliothek.
Tags: library, yechezkel-feigin, yehuda-shmotkin, eretz-yisrael, otwock

Title: 19 Kislev celebrations across Lithuania reported
Summary: Around Zos Chanukah 5697, R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch reported to the Rebbe Rayatz on widespread 19 Kislev celebrations among anash throughout Lithuania.
Story: R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch detailed gatherings in Kovno (with over 200 attendees including students of the local yeshiva), Kelm, Telz, Ponevezh (both shtiblach), Vilkomir, Anikst, and other towns. R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevitch had come from Kopishok to spend the chag in Kovno; the Rebbe's klali letter for 19 Kislev was relayed by mail to each community.
Tags: 19-kislev, kovno, kelm, telz, ponevezh, vilkomir, anikst, lithuania, chanukah, yisrael-noach-chatzkevitch

Title: Vilna chassidim describe 19 Kislev farbrengens to Frierdiker Rebbe
Summary: In Kislev 5697 chassidim of Vilna wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe about their 19 Kislev farbrengens at the Apatov synagogue and the Shnipishok minyan.
Story: The letter was signed by Yitzchak Weiman, Anshil Aronovich, Menachem Mendel Levin and Chaim Yehoshua Baruch Kapelovich. It documents the active chassidic life in multiple Vilna minyanim on the eve of the Holocaust, including Apatov, Kirzner, Shnipishok and Novogrod.
Tags: vilna, 5697, kislev, 19 kislev, farbrengen, anshil aronovich

Title: 19 Kislev farbrengen at Chelm yeshiva
Summary: Chelm's Achei Temimim yeshiva held a 19 Kislev seudah where the Rebbe Rayatz's general letter and a 1928 maamar were studied.
Story: On 19 Kislev 5697 the Chelm branch hosted a celebration of the Chag HaGeulah starting at 7 PM, including students, hanhalah members and visiting avreichim. They read the Frierdiker Rebbe's klali letter and the parsha of the Chag HaGeulah, then learned the maamar 'Asarah Sheyoshvim' from 12 Tammuz 5688 during the seudah.
Tags: chelm, poland, yud-tes-kislev, achei-temimim, farbrengen

Title: 19-20 Kislev farbrengens across Riga's Chabad minyanim
Summary: Yud-Tes Kislev 5697 was celebrated in over ten minyanim across Riga, including the Rebbe's main minyan and the Beis Medrash Chabad.
Story: R. Eliyahu Chaim Altheuse reported the festivities in detail: a newly received account of the arrest and liberation in colloquial language was read aloud in each minyan, the Shas was divided for the year, and chazaras maamarim and divrei hisorerus extended deep into the night. The Rebbe's minyan at Kurmanava 20/01 functioned as the central chassidic hub.
Tags: yud-tes-kislev, riga, farbrengen, altheuse, blinner

Title: Dvinsk anash commit to weekly chassidus study
Summary: On 19 Kislev 5697 the Dvinsk community held a farbrengen and committed to weekly chassidus study.
Story: On 19 Kislev 5697 (December 3, 1936) a farbrengen was held in a Dvinsk hall, and the participants accepted upon themselves to learn chassidus together once a week. They signed a letter that day informing the Rebbe Rayatz, who responded with blessing on 29 Kislev. Organizer R' Baruch Eliyahu Peletz reported on 24 Tevet that 40-50 men, including older anash, were attending.
Tags: dvinsk, latvia, yud-tes-kislev, chassidus-study, peletz

Title: Chelm hanhalah confirms receipt of Rebbe's monthly stipend
Summary: Rosenbaum and Kornblit wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe acknowledging his Kislev stipend, which alone covered two weeks of staff wages.
Story: On 22 Kislev 5697 the Chelm yeshiva managers Yitzchak Yaakov Rosenbaum and Avraham Yitzchak Kornblit wrote the Frierdiker Rebbe thanking him for the monthly support, noting that they had no other source to pay the maggidei shiurim for the last two weeks. They also reported on the 19 Kislev farbrengen and asked the Rebbe to confirm Tanya study with the second class.
Tags: chelm, poland, achei-temimim, kornblit, rosenbaum, tomchei-temimim

Title: Altheuse reports on Yud-Tes Kislev to Faigin
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Tevet 5697, R. Eliyahu Chaim Altheuse wrote a detailed report to secretary Faigin about the Yud-Tes Kislev farbrengens.
Story: Altheuse described the Lubavitcher Rebbe's minyan as 'der Lubavitcher Rebbe's minyan' - the central chassidic gathering place where shiurim in Chassidus were learned daily, where one could obtain a kuntres, kosher tefillin straps, or Lubavitcher tzitzis, and where the name 'Lubavitch' was constantly on every mispallel's lips.
Tags: altheuse, faigin, riga, yud-tes-kislev, minyan

Title: Mandelbaum reports on 19 Kislev gatherings in Globoke
Summary: On 2 Tevet 5697 Mandelbaum wrote to the Rebbe describing the 19 Kislev farbrengens and the new Torah-study programs he had launched in Globoke.
Story: Mandelbaum reported that during the Yud-Tes Kislev celebrations he had pushed for strengthened Ein Yaakov shiurim in every minyan, Mishnayos and Shulchan Aruch classes, his own daily gemara shiur in the Starasele minyan, and a resolution to learn Tanya on Friday nights.
Tags: mandelbaum, globoke, yud-tes-kislev, ein-yaakov, tanya

Title: Girls' letter to the Rebbe on Yud-Tes Kislev gathering
Summary: A group of daughters of Chabad chassidim in Riga wrote to the Rebbe on 5 Tevet 5697 describing their Yud-Tes Kislev gathering.
Story: The letter, photographed in Di Yiddishe Heim no. 88 (Tammuz 5742), opens 'We the daughters of Chabad chassidim celebrated this year as well the Chag HaGeulah Yud-Tes Kislev, as in the past year.' It shows that organized women's farbrengens preceded the formal naming of Achos Tmimim.
Tags: achos-tmimim, riga, girls, yud-tes-kislev, letter

Title: R. Morgel reports on Połaniec yeshiva to the Rebbe
Summary: On 7 Tevet 5697 R. Moshe Aharon Morgel reported to the Rebbe on the expanded Połaniec yeshiva.
Story: In his report of 7 Tevet 5697, R. Moshe Aharon Morgel informed the Rebbe Rayatz that the yeshiva had grown to approximately forty students divided into three divisions studying Bava Metzia, Bava Kamma, Yevamos and Shevuos with Rashi, Tosafos and select commentaries. After Maariv R. Yitzchok Pinchas, son of the tzaddik of Kinsk, taught a public Tanya chapter for laymen, youth and students of the third division.
Tags: poland, potshanov, polaniec, moshe-aharon-morgel, tomchei-tmimim, rebbe-correspondence

Title: Rayatz departs Otwock for Vienna
Summary: On December 27, the Rayatz left Otwock for Vienna and a week of treatment in Perchtoldsdorf.
Story: This trip kicked off a multi-month journey that took him to Paris through February. Health remained the consistent driver of these long winter absences from Otwock.
Tags: otwock, vienna, perchtoldsdorf, austria

Title: Israel Yehuda dispatched to teach underground yeshiva in Krivoy Rog
Summary: R' Yonah Cohen sent Israel Yehuda to Krivoy Rog to instruct a group of young Anash boys in an underground yeshiva housed at R' Yoel Itkin's home.
Story: Following a clandestine meeting at R' Zalman Pruss's home in Moscow, R' Yonah Cohen organized the dispatching of older bochurim to teach groups of four boys per location, reportedly on the Rebbe's instruction. Israel Yehuda took over from Michoel Teitelbaum in Krivoy Rog, teaching Perek Shnayim Ochzin to boys including Leibke Mochkin, Yoel Duchman, Mendel Raskin, and Yehoshua Katzenelenbogen-Raskin at R' Yoel Itkin's home, which served the cause with extraordinary mesirat nefesh.
Tags: krivoy rog, yonah cohen, underground yeshiva, yoel itkin, leibke mochkin, yoel duchman, mendel raskin

Title: Israel Yehuda visits R' Levi Yitzchak Schneerson in Dnepropetrovsk
Summary: While fundraising for the Krivoy Rog yeshiva, Israel Yehuda visited Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson in nearby Dnepropetrovsk.
Story: Traveling to Dnepropetrovsk to raise funds for the underground yeshiva, Israel Yehuda came to the home of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, the future Lubavitcher Rebbe's father. The Rebbetzin Chana directed him to the synagogue, where he found Rabbi Levi Yitzchak sitting and praying.
Tags: dnepropetrovsk, levi yitzchak schneerson, chana schneerson, fundraising

Title: Moshe Feinstein immigrates from Lyuban to United States
Summary: After serving as rabbi of Lyuban, Belorussia, Rabbi Moshe Feinstein received an exit visa secured by US-based relatives.
Story: He had remained in the Soviet Union trying to preserve a core of observant Jews under relentless anti-religious propaganda. He would later become dean of Mesivta Tifereth Jerusalem in the United States and one of the leading halachic authorities of the twentieth century.
Tags: feinstein, lyuban, belorussia, emigration

Title: Opportunity to purchase yeshiva building arises
Summary: At the beginning of Tishrei 5698, an opportunity arose to purchase the entire yeshiva building in Otwock.
Story: At the beginning of Tishrei 5698 (autumn 1937), an opportunity arose to purchase the entire building housing the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Otwock. The building cost more than the Rebbe Rayatz's available means, and he decided to organize a special fundraising campaign among Chabad chassidim in the United States and the Land of Israel.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, otwock, real estate, fundraising

Title: Piskei HaSiddur by Rabbi Avraham Chaim Naeh published in Jerusalem
Summary: First edition of Piskei HaSiddur by Rabbi Avraham Chaim Naeh was printed in Jerusalem in 5697.
Story: Rabbi Avraham Chaim Naeh, author of Ketzos HaShulchan, published his Piskei HaSiddur in Jerusalem in 5697 (1937). It is displayed at the Lubavitch Library's exhibition of works by the great chassidim of Chabad.
Tags: jerusalem, naeh, halacha, siddur

Title: Rabbi Moshe Feinstein immigrates to United States
Summary: The rabbi of Lyuban, Belorussia, received an exit visa through American relatives' lobbying.
Story: Like dozens of other rabbis, Reb Moshe had stayed in Russia trying to preserve a core of observant Jews despite Yevsektzia oppression. He later became dean of Mesivta Tifereth Jerusalem and one of the greatest Jewish legal scholars of the twentieth century. He recalled discovering a family connection to Chabad — his great-grandmother Rochel had been a classmate of the Tzemach Tzedek in the Alter Rebbe's cheder.
Tags: moshe feinstein, lyuban, united states, emigration

Title: Rebbe Rayatz proposes 40th anniversary HaTamim issue
Summary: In early summer 5697, the future Rebbe (Ramash) proposed to his father-in-law that HaTamim's 12 Tammuz issue commemorate Tomchei Tmimim's 40th anniversary.
Story: At the beginning of summer 5697 (1937), the future Rebbe (Ramash, the Rebbe Rayatz's son-in-law) wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz proposing that since summer marked the 40-year anniversary of Tomchei Tmimim's founding, the upcoming 12 Tammuz issue of HaTamim should be dedicated to the yeshiva's history with special material. He also urged that a list of all yeshiva students throughout the years be published in time for the jubilee.
Tags: hatamim, rebbe rayatz, ramash, 40th anniversary, tomchei tmimim

Title: Sara Katzenelenbogen's husband Michoel assassinated
Summary: In 1937 Russian authorities assassinated Michoel Katzenelenbogen, leaving his wife Sara to take over financing the clandestine Chabad educational network.
Story: After her husband's murder Sara Katzenelenbogen became a primary organizer of underground Chabad education and later of the Great Escape. Eventually captured in Uzbekistan after being placed on the most-wanted list, she died of a heart attack in prison in 1952.
Tags: sara katzenelenbogen, michoel katzenelenbogen, russia, kgb, stalin

Title: Stalin's purges target JDC Agro-Joint workers
Summary: Soviet secret police arrested close to two hundred JDC Agro-Joint workers as 'foreign agents.'
Story: Many were shot, others died in prison or remained jailed for long periods. Among those targeted were forty-one German physicians who had come to serve the settlements — seventeen were shot or died in Soviet camps. JDC director Rosen protested unsuccessfully. The JDC remained publicly silent about the catastrophe, continuing instead to paint a positive picture of Soviet life.
Tags: stalin, jdc, agro-joint, great-terror, soviet-union

Title: Stanislav Messing executed in Soviet purges
Summary: Stanislav Messing, the Jewish Communist head of the Leningrad GPU who had opposed the Rebbe's release, was shot.
Story: Messing had threatened to countermand any order from Moscow freeing the Rebbe and to arrest him again if he returned to Leningrad. A decade later he himself was swept up in Stalin's purges. Some accounts say he came from a chasidic family.
Tags: messing, gpu, leningrad, purges

Title: Tomchei Tmimim branch founded in Dankera, Latvia
Summary: A Tomchei Tmimim branch was founded in Dankera, Latvia, in 5697 (1937).
Story: Dankera was one of two Latvian branches in the Tomchei Tmimim network. By Tishrei 5701 it had merged with the Livenhof (Livani) branch and relocated to Riga as the Polish branches collapsed under the German invasion.
Tags: latvia, dankera, tomchei tmimim, branch

Title: Trotsky sentenced to death in absentia in Moscow trial
Summary: Leon Trotsky was sentenced to death in absentia in a Moscow show trial.
Story: By this point Trotsky was living in Mexico after years of exile. The sentence would be executed three years later when a Stalinist agent assassinated him in his Mexico City home, fulfilling the Rashab's prediction made in 1920 that Trotsky would be executed.
Tags: trotsky, moscow, stalin, soviet union

Title: Yezhovshchina terror disrupts underground yeshiva networks
Summary: The Yezhovshchina purges of 5697 brought mass street arrests and Siberian exile, forcing Israel Yehuda to flee Voronezh temporarily.
Story: During the height of Stalin's Great Terror in 5697, the NKVD arrested people directly off the streets and deported them to Siberia, creating a 'terrible fear' Israel Yehuda could no longer endure. He fled to Moscow before Purim to consult R' Yonah Cohen, returning to Voronezh only for Passover, where the group baked matzot with utmost stringency under R' Betzalel Wilshansky's supervision.
Tags: soviet union, stalin, great purge, yezhovshchina, nkvd, siberia

Title: Levitin leaves the Soviet Union
Summary: In Shevat 5697 R. Shmuel Levitin finally escaped the Soviet Union and was reaccepted as rabbi of Rakishok.
Story: After years of struggle, in Shevat 5697 (January 1937) Levitin succeeded in leaving Russia. He returned to Lithuania and was once again accepted as rabbi of the Rakishok community.
Tags: levitin, soviet-union, rakishok, emigration

Title: Rayatz arrives in Paris for extended stay
Summary: After a week in Perchtoldsdorf, the Rayatz arrived in Paris on 21 Tevet for a stay lasting until 7 Adar.
Story: The extended stay combined treatment and engagement with Parisian Chabad. He would head back to Perchtoldsdorf before returning to Otwock in late March.
Tags: paris, france, ville d avray

Title: Rayatz returns to Otwock from Paris and Austria
Summary: After his Paris-Perchtoldsdorf circuit, the Rayatz arrived back in Otwock on 11 Nisan, just before Passover.
Story: The return home gave him a few weeks with family before the holiday. He would head out again to Perchtoldsdorf in mid-June for the summer.
Tags: otwock, poland, perchtoldsdorf

Title: R' Yehoshua Heshel Reizman appointed maggid shiur in Warsaw Mechina
Summary: Around Pesach 5697 R' Yehoshua Heshel Reizman, then about 18, was appointed maggid shiur in the Warsaw Mechina.
Story: After three years in the Olam, R' Heshel Reizman was called in spring 5697 to teach the junior Mechina class alongside R' Schneur Zalman Gourary, who led the upper class. When Gourary later left the yeshiva, Reizman took over the upper class and R' Yitzchak Hendel filled the junior position. Reizman remained in his hometown of Suchedniow when WWII broke out and survived the war.
Tags: warsaw, heshel reizman, tomchei tmimim, mechina, yitzchak hendel

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe lists branches on 28 Nisan 5697
Summary: In a letter dated 28 Nisan 5697, the Frierdiker Rebbe enumerated the cities hosting Tomchei Tmimim branches.
Story: The letter (Igros Vol. 17, no. 6420) listed Warsaw, Otwock, Lodz, Vilna, Globoke, Chelm, Chmielnik and Patzanow as homes of Tomchei Tmimim branches. This contemporaneous list anchors the historical picture of the network at its peak.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, tomchei tmimim, branches, letter

Title: Abramsky publishes letter of support for Tomchei Temimim
Summary: On Lag BaOmer 5697 Rabbi Yechezkel Abramsky wrote a public letter calling on all Jews to support Tomchei Temimim regularly.
Story: Drawing on his personal visit to the yeshiva the previous year, Abramsky testified that seeing is not the same as hearing, and that he found 200 bochurim shokdim on Torah and yiras Hashem. He signed as 'dayan of the Beis Din of London and the country' and promised Hashems blessing in all good for those who became fixed supporters.
Tags: otwock, tomchei-temimim, abramsky, london, fundraising

Title: Abraham Kvash writes to Ezras Torah about flight from Russia
Summary: On Isru Chag Shavuos 5697 R. Abraham Kvash wrote to Ezras Torah recounting his five-year-old flight from Soviet Russia and his father's subsequent five-year Siberian exile.
Story: Kvash described leaving Russia for Warsaw because he could find no place of Torah there, and that his father R. Aharon Kvasha had been arrested by the GPU on suspicion of complicity in his escape and for Jewish religious activity. R. Aharon was sentenced to five years in Siberia.
Tags: abraham kvash, ezras torah, warsaw, ussr, siberia, border crossing

Title: Rebbe formally addresses Achos Tmimim in letter
Summary: On 23 Sivan 5697 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Mordechai Chefetz about the work of Achos Tmimim.
Story: This is the earliest extant letter explicitly naming the organization. The Rebbe asked Chefetz to write in detail about the learning sessions and whether any practical results were visible, emphasizing how much he wanted to know about the conduct of every child of the chassidim.
Tags: rayatz, achos-tmimim, chefetz, girls-education

Title: Rayatz travels to Perchtoldsdorf for summer
Summary: The Rayatz left Otwock on 6 Tamuz for a summer-long stay at the Perchtoldsdorf sanitorium.
Story: He remained in Austria until late August. This was his last summer of regular Austrian treatment; Nazi annexation of Austria in March 1938 would cut off this route.
Tags: perchtoldsdorf, austria, health

Title: HaTamim issue 7 published for 40th anniversary
Summary: The 7th issue of HaTamim was dedicated to the 40th anniversary of Tomchei Tmimim's founding.
Story: On 12 Tammuz 5697 (June 21, 1937), the 7th issue of HaTamim was published, dedicated to the 40-year jubilee of the founding of Tomchei Tmimim in 5657. The issue began a series of articles on the founding, purpose, development, and growth of the yeshiva, with promises of more letters and essays in future issues.
Tags: hatamim, tomchei tmimim, 40th anniversary, 12 tammuz

Title: HaTamim Vol. 7 publishes overview of Tomchei Tmimim
Summary: In Tammuz 5697, HaTamim Vol. 7 published a general overview of Tomchei Tmimim's development with the branch count for that year.
Story: The piece reported that seven additional departments operated under the central yeshiva in Otwock-Warsaw, with hundreds of students across the network. It described the talmidim as G-d-fearing, talented and ready to be recognized as 'seed blessed by Hashem.'
Tags: hatamim, tomchei tmimim, otwock, warsaw

Title: Survey of Tomchei Tmimim history published in HaTamim
Summary: In Tammuz 5697 the seventh issue of HaTamim journal published a general survey of the development of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva.
Story: The survey recorded the 1921 transfer of the yeshiva to Poland on the yahrzeit of the Rebbe Rashab. HaTamim was the central scholarly journal of the Lubavitch yeshiva network during the interwar period.
Tags: hatamim, tomchei-tmimim, journal

Title: Author departs USA on Queen Mary to visit Rebbe Rayatz in Europe
Summary: On 28 Tammuz 5697 the author sailed from the USA on the Queen Mary to visit the Rebbe Rayatz at Perchtoldsdorf near Vienna.
Story: Almost all his students gathered at the dock to see him off. He carried a list of 213 students learning Chassidus and brought pidyonos from each one. He also planned to visit the yeshiva at Otwock during the trip.
Tags: queen mary, europe, rayatz, perchtoldsdorf, vienna, austria, tammuz

Title: Rebbe sends emissary to arrange Levitin's Rakishok role
Summary: On 29 Tammuz 5697 the Rebbe informed Levitin he would send R. Mordechai the shochet of Riga as a special emissary to formalize matters in Rakishok.
Story: Writing to Levitin on 29 Tammuz 5697 (Igros Kodesh vol. 4, letter 920), the Rebbe Rayatz said it was worthwhile to dispatch R. Mordechai, the shochet from Riga, as a special emissary with a letter to the chassidim in Rakishok, in order that Levitin's reinstallation be carried out properly and respectfully.
Tags: levitin, rakishok, riga, mordechai-shochet

Title: Author meets Rebbe Rayatz at Perchtoldsdorf near Vienna
Summary: The author met the Rebbe Rayatz at his Austrian retreat to report on the 213 students learning Chassidus in America.
Story: The Rebbe took deep interest in the students; when asked which maamarim to teach them, he answered 'whatever you learn with them — the main thing is the embroidery (ushibatzta).' The Rebbe also remarked on R' D.M. Rabinowitz's unsanctioned trip to Eretz Yisrael saying 'Grandfather would command, Father would say, and I say as it comes out — but one must obey.' Before parting, the Rebbe instructed the author to write down everything he saw and heard on the journey.
Tags: rayatz, perchtoldsdorf, vienna, austria, yechidus, pidyonos

Title: Author visits Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Otwock
Summary: During his European trip the author visited the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva at Otwock, Poland.
Story: The visit gave the author a direct view of the yeshiva's mashpi'im and study atmosphere. This experience later shaped his decisions about sending American students to study there.
Tags: otwock, poland, tomchei tmimim, yeshiva

Title: Yakovshvili arrested in Moscow
Summary: Armed men burst into Simon Yakovshvili's home, accusing him of counterrevolutionary activity.
Story: Yakovshvili was offered freedom in exchange for confirming the counterrevolutionary status of one hundred named Jews; he refused. He was flogged repeatedly and ultimately given a death sentence. Minutes before execution, an edict from fellow Georgian Lavrentiy Beria — head of Stalin's secret police — spared his life, though he served nearly a decade in the gulag.
Tags: yakovshvili, jacobson, moscow, gulag, beria

Title: Author departs Vienna at end of European visit
Summary: The author left Vienna on 2 Elul 5697 after his visit with the Rebbe Rayatz.
Story: He proceeded to Paris en route home, arriving there the following day. His journey would later resonate with the Rebbe's letter to R' D.M. Rabinowitz about the spiritual significance of arriving in America.
Tags: vienna, austria, elul, rayatz

Title: Author arrives in Paris en route home from Rebbe
Summary: On 3 Elul 5697 the author reached Paris and visited R' Shneur Zalman Schneerson.
Story: R' Schneerson informed him that R' D.M. Rabinowitz had been in Paris hoping to meet him and convey regards from the Rebbe Rayatz, but had been forced to leave for Marseille to catch his ship to America. The author's own ship would depart Le Havre the following day.
Tags: paris, france, shneur zalman schneerson, elul

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Simpson about three donated manuscripts
Summary: On 8 Elul 5697 the Rebbe Rayatz acknowledged three manuscripts sent by R. Eliyahu Simpson, including a Siddur of the Arizal and a Venice machzor.
Story: Replying to R. Eliyahu Simpson on 8 Elul 5697 (August 15, 1937), the Rebbe Rayatz identified the three manuscripts received as a portion of Sefer HaKavanot, a Siddur of the Arizal, and a handwritten machzor of the type used by Venetian notables on festivals. The Siddur HaArizal is cataloged in the Lubavitch manuscript collection as no. 1991 and the Venice machzor as no. 1996.
Tags: manuscripts, library, eliyahu-simpson, kavanot, siddur-arizal

Title: Rebbe urges importing Lithuanian students to Dankra
Summary: On 8 Elul 5697 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to Refael Hakohen of Riga that Dankra must bring students from Lithuania to ignite local Latvian youth.
Story: In a letter of 8 Elul 5697 (Igrot vol. 4, no. 940) the Frierdiker Rebbe told Refael Hakohen, head of the Chabad community in Riga, that the Dankra yeshiva was obligated to import students from Lithuania to inspire 'feelings of love for Torah' among Latvian youth. This was part of his strategy of seeding new branches with veteran Tomchei Temimim talmidim.
Tags: dankra, latvia, lithuania, tomchei-temimim, refael-hakohen

Title: Rebbe writes about Dankra yeshiva branch
Summary: On 8 Elul 5697 the Rebbe wrote to R. Rafael Cohen about establishing a Tomchei Temimim branch in Dankra under the leadership of his son-in-law R. Yeshaya Chanoch Berkhan.
Story: R. Berkhan had been appointed rabbi of Dankra in 5695 and founded the yeshiva there in 5696. The Rebbe's letter (vol. 4, no. 949) addressed practical aspects of operating the branch as part of the Tomchei Temimim network.
Tags: rayatz, dankra, tomchei-tmimim, berkhan, yeshiva

Title: Author returns to New York from European trip
Summary: The author arrived in New York on 10 or 11 Elul 5697 after his visit with the Rebbe Rayatz in Vienna.
Story: On returning he immediately arranged through Agudas Chassidei Chabad secretary Asher Hershman to monitor newspapers for the arrival of R' D.M. Rabinowitz's Dollar Line ship. Upon his return, the regular Chassidus study sessions and farbrengens strengthened and more students joined.
Tags: new york, queen mary, elul, rayatz

Title: R' D.M. Rabinowitz arrives in USA on Chai Elul
Summary: R' Dovid Meir Rabinowitz arrived in New York from Eretz Yisrael on Chai Elul 5697 (the Baal Shem Tov's birthday).
Story: Delayed a week by a maritime workers' strike, he understood the Rebbe Rayatz's earlier letter — which had said his date of arrival would be propitious — as a hint to the spiritual significance of Chai Elul. He convened a farbrengen with Anash that day at the Broadway Central Hotel to fulfill the Rebbe's allusion. The letter cited tradition that on Chai Elul the Baal Shem Tov spoke Torah publicly before his students.
Tags: chai elul, david meir rabinowitz, eretz yisrael, rayatz, besht

Title: Rayatz returns to Otwock for holidays
Summary: On 19 Elul, the Rayatz returned to Otwock from Perchtoldsdorf in time for the holidays.
Story: Returning before Rosh Hashanah ensured he could lead the Tishrei observances with his chasidim. He would not return to Austria for treatment until just before the Anschluss.
Tags: otwock, perchtoldsdorf, high holidays

Title: Rosh Hashanah and Sukkot 5698 minyan in Krivoy Rog
Summary: For Tishrei 5698, R' Mikhoel Rapoport joined the Krivoy Rog group to establish a clandestine High Holiday minyan at R' Yoel Itkin's home.
Story: Fearing exposure at the main synagogue where a chazzan from Kremenchug officiated, the group organized their own minyan at R' Yoel Itkin's home. On Simchat Torah they secretly observed the synagogue hakafot and saw the visiting young chazzan from Dnepropetrovsk dancing to Chabad niggunim, later learning he was among Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson's students at the local technicum.
Tags: krivoy rog, mikhoel rapoport, yoel itkin, underground minyan, dnepropetrovsk, levi yitzchak schneerson

Title: R' Aharon Eliezer Tzeitlin arrested on first night of Sukkos 5698
Summary: R' Aharon Eliezer Tzeitlin, shochet in Mozhaysk and the author's brother-in-law, was arrested on the first night of Sukkos 5698 and exiled to Siberia.
Story: Serving as shochet in Mozhaysk and operating a clandestine synagogue from his home, R' Aharon Eliezer Tzeitlin was seized by Soviet authorities on the first night of Sukkos 5698. He was deported to Siberia, where, weak in health, he died in his place of exile. The author had earlier exhausted himself attempting to bring Tzeitlin and his family to America; in 1929 the Rebbe Rayatz had told the author that only supernatural intervention could bring them out.
Tags: soviet union, mozhaysk, arrest, shochet, siberia, kgb

Title: R. Feigin writes Tel Aviv Chabad about building purchase
Summary: On 28 Tishrei 5698, secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to the heads of the Chabad community in Tel Aviv about the urgent need to purchase the yeshiva building.
Story: On 28 Tishrei 5698 (October 3, 1937), secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to the heads of the Chabad community in Tel Aviv urging quick action on the building purchase. He explained that the Rebbe Rayatz had departed from his usual practice and personally assigned set sums to each chassid and student as founding members of the campaign.
Tags: yechezkel feigin, tel aviv, chabad, fundraising, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Cramer about building purchase
Summary: On 12 Cheshvan 5698, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Chaim Shneur Zalman Cramer, chairman of Agudas Chassidei Chabad in the US, about purchasing the yeshiva building.
Story: On 12 Cheshvan 5698 (October 17, 1937), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Chaim Shneur Zalman Cramer, chairman of Agudas Chassidei Chabad in the United States. He explained that for over a month he had decided that it was essential to purchase a building and courtyard for the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva, and that thank G-d a suitable opportunity had arisen.
Tags: chaim shneur zalman cramer, aguch, united states, fundraising, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rebbe writes to Hatamim about Achos Tmimim Riga
Summary: On 28 Cheshvan 5698 the Rebbe instructed the Hatamim editorial board to cover the new Achos Tmimim organization in Riga.
Story: The Rebbe named the three appointed shepherds - R. Avraham Eliyahu Asherov, R. Mordechai Chefetz, and R. Eliyahu Chaim Altheuse - and asked Hatamim to solicit each of their perspectives on the new women's organization, with Altheuse particularly asked to describe the matter at length.
Tags: rayatz, hatamim, achos-tmimim, asherov, chefetz, altheuse

Title: Warsaw Rabbinical Committee letter of 10 Kislev 5698
Summary: On 10 Kislev 5698, the Warsaw Vaad HaRabbanim wrote a letter of support emphasizing the seven branches and roughly 700 students.
Story: The endorsement letter noted that seven branches operated under the Tomchei Tmimim banner with close to seven hundred students between the center and branches. Such rabbinical endorsements were essential to fundraising efforts during the difficult late-1930s economic climate.
Tags: warsaw, rabbinical committee, tomchei tmimim, fundraising

Title: Warsaw rabbis issue support letter for Tomchei Tmimim
Summary: On 10 Kislev 5698, the Council of Rabbis of Warsaw issued a letter of support for the yeshiva.
Story: On 10 Kislev 5698 (November 14, 1937), members of the Council of Rabbis of Warsaw issued a letter of support praising Tomchei Tmimim as one of the most exalted Torah institutions in the world. They noted that they had personally tested many of the students, were amazed by their sharpness and erudition, and had granted them rabbinical ordination. The letter stated that seven branches of the yeshiva operated in Poland with nearly 700 students in total.
Tags: warsaw rabbinical council, tomchei tmimim, support letter, poland, semicha

Title: Rebbe urges founding similar Achos Tmimim chapters elsewhere
Summary: On 14 Kislev 5698 the Rebbe called on anash and temimim worldwide to establish chapters modeled on the Riga Achos Tmimim.
Story: The Rebbe wrote that 'recently the daughters of the chassidim in Riga have organized to learn maamarim and hold farbrengens' and that 'it is correct and necessary' for chassidim in other locales to take this as an example, founding similar groups to 'revive the hearts of their daughters with the dew of life of the pleasant ways of Chassidus.'
Tags: rayatz, achos-tmimim, expansion, women, girls-education

Title: Arrest of R. Moshe Rubinson and his students in Berditchev
Summary: On 19 Kislev 5698 R. Moshe Rubinson and his students were arrested in Berditchev and interrogated about contact with the Rebbe Rayatz.
Story: Under interrogation Rubinson disclosed that his correspondence with the Rebbe Rayatz was conducted through a longtime acquaintance named Kvash who lived in Poland. The Kvash connection between the underground Soviet talmidim and the Rebbe also surfaced in the 1935 interrogation file of R. Shammai Vigon in Rostov.
Tags: moshe rubinson, berditchev, ussr, nkvd, tomchei tmimim, interrogation

Title: Rayatz returns to Perchtoldsdorf
Summary: The Rayatz traveled to Perchtoldsdorf on 24 Tevet for what would be his final visit before Austria fell to the Nazis.
Story: He stayed until 6 Adar Alef before relocating to Paris. The timing proved providential, as the German annexation of Austria came just three days after his departure.
Tags: perchtoldsdorf, austria, health

Title: American students Berel Levy and Hecht enroll in Otwock yeshivah
Summary: In 1938 Berel Levy, Avraham Barnetsky, and newly married Shlomo Zalman Hecht enrolled at the Otwock yeshivah, the first Americans there.
Story: The Rebbe worried Americans accustomed to comfort would struggle with Otwock's austere conditions, but Levy wrote home that they felt little strangeness. Levy described hundreds of students from across Europe and hundreds of Chasidim arriving for yechidut. The Rebbe took personal interest, advising Levy on his English reading habits and suggesting he read New York Times briefs.
Tags: otwock, america, tomchei-temimim, levy, barnetsky, hecht

Title: Arrest of R' Avraham Sverdlov in Leningrad
Summary: In 5698 (1938) the chassidic scholar R' Avraham Sverdlov, a co-leader of the Chabad yeshiva in Odessa, was arrested in Leningrad and never heard from again.
Story: Sverdlov had been one of the directors of the underground Tomchei Tmimim branch in Odessa, an unusually broad talent — a master of nigleh and chassidus, a brilliant darshan, a first-rate ba'al koreh. He was arrested in Leningrad in 1938; no trace of him was found thereafter, Hashem yikom damo.
Tags: leningrad, soviet union, nkvd, arrests, sverdlov

Title: Berdichev underground yeshiva raided, 12 students and Rosh Yeshiva arrested
Summary: The NKVD arrested 12 students of the Berdichev underground yeshiva along with their Rosh Yeshiva R' Moshe Korolevitzer (Rubinson).
Story: Following the Berdichev arrests, the remaining students in Krivoy Rog fled to Kutaisi in Georgia. Around the same time the Kursk yeshiva was also shut down and its students dispersed; several young learners including R' Zalman Levin and R' Dovber Kiubman made their way to Kharkov, where Israel Yehuda and Michoel Teitelbaum sheltered and taught them.
Tags: berdichev, nkvd, underground yeshiva, moshe korolevitzer, moshe rubinson, siberia

Title: Chaim Liberman publishes list of 32 unknown Haggadot
Summary: Chaim Liberman, librarian of the Lubavitch library, published a bibliographical list of 32 previously unknown Haggadot in 5698.
Story: In 5698 (1938), Chaim Liberman — then director of the Rebbe's library in Warsaw — published in Kiryat Sefer (vol. 15, p. 258) a list of 32 editions of the Haggadah unknown from any other source. The Haggadot had been acquired by the Rebbe Rayatz between 5660 and 5698.
Tags: bibliography, haggadah, liberman, warsaw, rayatz-library

Title: Elchonon Morozov and son Shmuel killed by Soviet secret police
Summary: After eight years hiding under the alias Berke Pesner, Morozov and his son Shmuel were arrested; both were killed.
Story: Investigators tortured Shmuel to confirm his father's identity. Shmuel refused; Morozov, hearing him, cried out to identify himself and was told he was being put to death as the Rebbe's representative. He was killed by firing squad; Shmuel had already died under torture.
Tags: morozov, leningrad, secret-police, firing-squad

Title: First wall calendar of Chabad customs by R. A.C. Naeh
Summary: The earliest extant Chabad wall calendar edited by R. Avraham Chaim Naeh and issued by Kollel Chabad is from 5699.
Story: R. Avraham Chaim Naeh authored a calendar of synagogue laws and Chabad customs, initially as a booklet and later as a wall calendar. The oldest wall-calendar copy preserved in the library is from 5699 (1938-1939), published by Kollel Chabad — beginning an annual tradition that continued under his son R. Baruch Naeh and beyond.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, minhagim, avraham chaim naeh

Title: Founding of Achos Hatmimim in Brooklyn
Summary: Achos Hatmimim, a Chabad study group for girls, was founded in Brooklyn in 5698 with Kazarnovsky as one of three appointed mashpi'im.
Story: In 5698, the Achos Hatmimim study group for Chabad girls was established in Brooklyn. Rayatz appointed R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky as one of three mashpi'im to serve as 'shepherds' of this group of young women.
Tags: achos-hatmimim, brooklyn, girls-education, kazarnovsky, rayatz

Title: Founding of Achos Tmimim in New York
Summary: The Achos Tmimim women's organization was founded in New York in 5698, with a three-man va'ad overseeing it.
Story: In 5698 the Chabad women's organization Achos Tmimim was founded in New York. R' Yochanan Gordon learned Chassidus with the members and led farbrengens for them. The Rebbe Rayatz appointed a va'ad of three to oversee the group: Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson, Rabbi Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky, and R' Yochanan Gordon.
Tags: new york, achos tmimim, women, yochanan gordon, kazarnovsky

Title: Kaloszyn branch of Tomchei Temimim founded
Summary: A Tomchei Temimim branch was founded in Kaloszyn in 5698, eventually growing to about 60 students under Leib Kremer.
Story: The Kaloszyn branch yeshiva was established in 5698 (1938) under the leadership of Rabbi Leib Kremer, later director of Tomchei Temimim Montreal. According to a report in HaPardes it eventually enrolled around 60 students.
Tags: kaloszyn, poland, tomchei-temimim, leib-kremer

Title: Letter on Chabad Chassidus translated and published in Yiddish
Summary: In 5698 Achos Tmimim Riga published a Yiddish translation of the Rebbe's letter on the moral and educational meaning of Chabad Chassidus.
Story: Members B. Gadin and Ch. Mikhailover of Achos Tmimim translated the Hebrew letter (vol. 3, no. 837) into Yiddish and printed it as a standalone kuntres in Riga. It was titled 'Di Moralishe un Dertzierishe Badaytung fun Chassidus Chabad' and presented as an answer to an inquiry from Germany.
Tags: achos-tmimim, riga, yiddish, chassidus, samizdat-style

Title: Levin marries in Kharkov
Summary: Yisrael Yehuda Levin married in Kharkov in late winter 5698, ending a decade of wandering between underground yeshivos.
Story: After running an underground yeshiva branch in Krivoy Rog for over a year, Levin married and settled in Kharkov. His army exemption obtained through the eyeglasses miracle remained valid until World War II, when the Soviets stopped honoring such exemptions and drafted virtually every young man with hands and legs. Many of his friends were taken to the front and never returned.
Tags: kharkov, marriage, ukraine

Title: Mass arrests of Lubavitcher activists in Leningrad
Summary: On the same winter 5698 (early 1938) night that arrests occurred in Zlobin, R' Elchanan Dov Morozov, R' Yitzchak Raskin, and R' Shmuel Nimaytin were arrested in Leningrad.
Story: On the Thursday night that seven 'shul-Jews' were arrested in Zlobin, the NKVD in Leningrad simultaneously arrested R' Elchanan Dov Morozov, R' Yitzchak Raskin, R' Shmuel Nimaytin, and others. When the memoirist himself fled to Leningrad days later, he learned of the parallel arrests.
Tags: leningrad, soviet union, nkvd, morozov, raskin, nimaytin, arrests

Title: Memoirist and father flee Zlobin to Zhitomir
Summary: On a Friday night in Shvat or Adar 5698 (early 1938), warned by a contact in the NKVD that more arrests were imminent, the memoirist and his father fled Zlobin for Zhitomir.
Story: A woman who worked at the bread shop and was friendly with the NKVD secretary tipped the memoirist off that another round of arrests was planned that very night. Knowing his father and himself were on the list, the memoirist made hurried arrangements and that Friday night the two boarded a train for Zhitomir. From there the memoirist continued to Gomel, then to his brother Zev in Leningrad, until the danger passed.
Tags: zlobin, zhitomir, gomel, leningrad, nkvd, flight

Title: Morozov killed by firing squad
Summary: The Rebbe's longtime secretary was executed after refusing to deny his true identity to interrogators.
Story: Having hidden since 1930 under the false identity Berke Pesner, Morozov was finally caught in 1938 along with his son Shmuel. Police tortured Shmuel to confirm his father's identity; Morozov cried out, 'Shmuel, tell them that I am your father!' Police told Morozov his crime was being 'a representative of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, who is G-d's representative in Russia.'
Tags: morozov, leningrad, execution, underground, berke pesner

Title: Munkacs Haggadah with 'Sha'ar Yissachar' commentary by Chaim Elazar Shapira
Summary: A Haggadah commentary based on Chaim Elazar Shapira of Munkacs's 'Sha'ar Yissachar' manuscript was published in Munkacs.
Story: In 5698 (1938), a Haggadah with a commentary on the Pesach Aggadah drawn from the manuscript of Rebbe Chaim Elazar Shapira of Munkacs's work 'Sha'ar Yissachar' was published in Munkacs by Grafia Press. The 54-leaf octavo edition preserved the teachings of the famed Munkacher Rebbe on the Passover Seder. It appeared just before the Holocaust devastated the Munkacs Chassidic community.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, munkacs, chaim elazar shapira, sha'ar yissachar

Title: Rabbi Mordechai Cheifetz dispatched to US as Rebbe's emissary
Summary: In 1938 the Rebbe sent Rabbi Mordechai Cheifetz to the US, where his farbrengens drew yeshivah students including Avraham Hecht.
Story: Cheifetz led chasidic gatherings lasting almost till dawn at New York yeshivas such as Torah Vodaath. Avraham Hecht recalled, "He could melt a stone. He melted me." Cheifetz inspired Hecht and five friends to travel to Otwock to study. Returning to Poland, Cheifetz spent ten days with the ailing Rebbe at Shavuot, reporting on each US Chasid by name.
Tags: america, new-york, shadar, torah-vodaath, hecht

Title: Rashag named president of Tomchei Tmimim executive board
Summary: Beginning in 5699, Rabbi Shmaryahu Gurary (the Rashag), son-in-law of the Rebbe Rayatz, served as president of the Yeshiva's executive committee.
Story: After a brief earlier involvement in 5691, the Rashag returned to active leadership of Tomchei Tmimim in 5699. Letters from this year, written on the Yeshiva's stationery, identify him as president of the executive board. By Adar 5699 he was taking part in all of the Yeshiva's operations, with all expenditures passing through him.
Tags: rashag, shmaryahu gurary, tomchei tmimim, otwock

Title: Rayatz founds Achei Tmimim yeshiva in Tel Aviv
Summary: In 5698 the Rayatz established the Achei Tmimim yeshiva in Tel Aviv as a Chabad institution independent of Kollel Chabad.
Story: Continuing the pattern set by his predecessor, the Rayatz founded Achei Tmimim in Tel Aviv and later added a Tomchei Tmimim division. Both operated separately from Kollel Chabad's Jerusalem-based framework, shifting Chabad's institutional center of gravity in the Holy Land away from the older kollel structure.
Tags: rayatz, achei tmimim, tel aviv, tomchei tmimim, yeshiva

Title: Rebbe Rayatz sends Rabbi Shmuel Levitin to the United States
Summary: The Rebbe dispatched the prominent scholar and devoted Chasid Rabbi Shmuel Levitin to inspire the American community.
Story: Levitin was unable to return to Europe due to the outbreak of war and remained in the US, where he played a key leadership role in the US Chabad community until his passing in 1974. He was part of a wider mission of Rebbe-sent emissaries who acted as a living bridge between the Rebbe in Europe and his followers in America.
Tags: levitin, rayatz, united-states, shliach

Title: Severe financial deterioration at Tomchei Temimim Warsaw in summer 1938
Summary: On erev Shabbat Parshat Shelach 5698, R. Yehuda Eber reported a dire financial situation and a collapsing administrative office.
Story: By summer 5698, the yeshiva's secretariat was barely functioning. The chief secretary R. Yosef Avraham Kagan was preparing to leave for London, and his colleague R. Moshe Pinchas Katz had married and was no longer working. R. Yehuda Eber lamented to the Rebbe that income had collapsed and no suitable replacements were available.
Tags: warsaw, tomchei temimim, finance, crisis, poland

Title: Tomchei Tmimim branches founded in Kaluszyn, Lenchna, Stopnica
Summary: Three new Tomchei Tmimim branches opened in Kaluszyn, Lenchna and Stopnica in 5698 (1938).
Story: The 5698 expansion marked one of the last major growth waves before the war. Lenchna grew rapidly, reaching 75 students by the eve of war, while Kaluszyn would later be specifically mentioned by the Frierdiker Rebbe among the branches whose talmidim he rescued to Lithuania.
Tags: poland, kaluszyn, lenchna, stopnica, tomchei tmimim, branch

Title: Yezhov takes over NKVD and Great Terror peaks
Summary: In 5698 (1938), Yezhov became NKVD chief and the wave of nighttime arrests in the Soviet Union reached its peak — the Hebrew letters of the year forming the word 'tirtzach' (murder).
Story: The Soviet situation deteriorated steadily, and in 5698 it became so murderous that the Hebrew letters of the year spelled 'murder.' Plain-clothed 'visitors' came in the dead of night to drag people from their homes on no charge, and Jews would ask each other every morning whom the GPU had taken the night before.
Tags: soviet union, nkvd, yezhov, great terror, arrests

Title: Israel Yehuda's engagement to Itta Devorah Gurkov of Kharkov
Summary: In Shvat 5698, Israel Yehuda entered into tnaim with Itta Devorah, daughter of R' Meir Gurkov of Kharkov.
Story: Despite warning his kallah that he could be arrested at any moment, Itta Devorah was undeterred since she too was prepared for arrest because of her commitment to Yiddishkeit and Chabad. The match represented a partnership ready to bear the cost of religious life under Soviet persecution.
Tags: kharkov, meir gurkov, itta devorah gurkov, tnaim

Title: Reports on 24 Tevet (Alter Rebbe yahrzeit) observances
Summary: In a letter near Parshas Bo 5698, R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch reported sending 22 letters to anash ahead of the Alter Rebbe's 24 Tevet yahrzeit, with farbrengens held across Lithuania.
Story: R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz that he had dispatched 26 letters to 24 communities urging hisva'adus and limud Chassidus on 24 Tevet, including double letters to Ponevezh (for both shtiblach) and Skopishok. He cited responses describing observances in Anikst, Traskun, Salok, Yanove, Mazheik, Vizun, and other towns.
Tags: 24-tevet, alter-rebbe, hilula, lithuania, kovno, anikst, salok, yosef-genkin, tevet

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes about house and library near yeshiva
Summary: On 3 Shevat 5698, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Israel Jacobson about the urgent need to purchase a residence and space for the library adjacent to the yeshiva.
Story: On 3 Shevat 5698 (January 5, 1938), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Israel Jacobson explaining the urgency of purchasing a residence for himself and the library, both for health reasons and for the inner workings of his activities. He stressed it must be adjacent to the yeshiva — courtyard next to courtyard — since he had moved from Riga to Poland only for the yeshiva's sake.
Tags: israel jacobson, otwock, tomchei tmimim, library, real estate

Title: R. Feigin summarizes Rebbe Rayatz's chassidus discourses
Summary: On 15 Shevat 5698, secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to R. Sholom Posner summarizing the Rebbe Rayatz's recent activities.
Story: On 15 Shevat 5698 (January 17, 1938), secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to his brother-in-law R. Sholom Posner reporting that until 19 Kislev the Rebbe Rayatz had delivered chassidus on every Shabbat as usual, but only before a small group of about 20-30 yeshiva students who rotated each Shabbat. Feigin also noted that the Rebbe had spoken at the beginning of Kislev about the need to travel to a sanatorium to renew medical treatment.
Tags: yechezkel feigin, sholom posner, chassidus, 19 kislev, health, otwock

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Ramash about transferring funds
Summary: On 23 Shevat 5698, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his son-in-law in Paris about transferring 10,000 zloty for the yeshiva building.
Story: On 23 Shevat 5698 (January 25, 1938), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his son-in-law (the future Rebbe, Ramash, in Paris) inquiring about the most economical way to transfer 10,000 zloty to his Warsaw account — whether by purchasing a bank check or direct transfer. Due to Polish currency restrictions, all support funds were routed to the Rebbe Rayatz through his son-in-law in Paris.
Tags: ramash, paris, poland, banking, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rayatz follow-up letter to Althoyz pressing for chasidic memoirs
Summary: On 3 Shevat 5698 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote letter no. 975 again urging R' Eliyahu Chaim Althoyz to record short notes on the elder chasidim he had known.
Story: Roughly two years after his first request, Rayatz wrote to Althoyz on 3 Shevat 5698 (February 1938) reiterating that he should write at least short notes — names, nicknames, appearances, and occupations — of the elder chasidim he had seen in childhood, youth, and adulthood, asking especially about 'the bears' (di berelech).
Tags: rayatz, althoyz, letters, lubavitch, historiography

Title: Rebbe thanks Dubin and Westerman for Dankra donation
Summary: On 3 Shevat 5698 the Frierdiker Rebbe acknowledged a gift from Westerman, arranged through Mordechai Dubin, for the Dankra mechina.
Story: Six months after pushing for Lithuanian recruits, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to Eliyahu Chaim Althoiz of Riga on 3 Shevat 5698 thanking him for news of a donation from the philanthropist Westerman for the Tomchei Temimim mechina in Dankra. The gift had been secured through the efforts of the Latvian parliamentarian Mordechai Dubin.
Tags: dankra, latvia, mordechai-dubin, westerman, althoiz, tomchei-temimim

Title: Kollel Chabad sends summary of Tzemach Tzedek yeshiva to Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: Kollel Chabad's leadership submitted a protocol and roster of 22 Tzemach Tzedek students to the Rebbe Rayatz.
Story: The 19 Adar I 5698 protocol included a short overview of the yeshiva and a list of its students with their stipends. The report described the institution as fulfilling the Rebbe Rashab's wish to bind kollel scholars to Chassidus study and to memorialize donors through Mishnah study. The 22 students were avreichim from various Jerusalem kollelim spending two hours daily at Beit Menachem.
Tags: jerusalem, kollel chabad, yeshiva tzemach tzedek, rebbe rayatz, protocol

Title: Shadar R' Mordechai Chefetz arrives in America
Summary: R' Mordechai Chefetz, sent by the Rebbe Rayatz, arrived in the USA in early Adar 5698 to warm up Anash.
Story: Stationed at the author's home at 494 Stone Ave for about twelve weeks, his farbrengens drew students and bochurim from major New York yeshivos and sometimes lasted until just before dawn. R' Yisroel Jacobson Feigin's letter of 21 Shevat 5698 conveyed the Rebbe's praise of Chefetz as a 'penimi who remembers the past with fine inner sensitivity.' His visit substantially elevated the reputation of Lubavitch among yeshiva students.
Tags: mordechai chefetz, shadar, adar, riga, rayatz, farbrengen

Title: Rayatz departs Austria for Paris before the Anschluss
Summary: The Rayatz left Austria for Paris on March 9, just three days before Germany annexed Austria.
Story: The Anschluss on March 12, 1938 closed Austria as a safe destination for the Rayatz. Had he stayed longer, he could have fallen into Nazi hands. He continued his medical treatment in Ville-d'Avray, France.
Tags: austria, paris, anschluss, nazi germany, escape

Title: Engagement of Chaya Sarah Jacobson to R' Shlomo Zalman Hecht
Summary: The engagement (kishurei tnaim) of the author's eldest daughter Chaya Sarah to R' Shlomo Zalman Hecht took place on 3 Nissan 5698.
Story: Immediately after the tnaim, Hecht stopped removing his beard, an act that made a strong impression on the students. That summer R' Yitzchak Kaladny also stopped shaving his beard. The simcha was infused with a Chassidic atmosphere.
Tags: hecht, kishurei tnaim, nissan, chaya sarah, jacobson

Title: Wedding of Israel Yehuda and Itta Devorah Gurkov on 5 Nissan
Summary: Israel Yehuda married Itta Devorah Gurkov on 5 Nissan 5698 in Kharkov.
Story: The wedding took place under the shadow of constant NKVD danger. Around the same time, R' Yonah HaKohen of Poltava sent flour for shemurah matzah for the entire Passover holiday from Hadiach, and a particularly fine talit gadol made by the righteous converts of Voronezh as a wedding gift, which Israel Yehuda treasured and used for decades.
Tags: kharkov, meir gurkov, itta devorah gurkov

Title: Rayatz returns to Otwock from Paris for Passover
Summary: After his Paris sanitorium stay, the Rayatz returned to Otwock on 12 Nisan in time for Passover.
Story: Following his last extended treatment abroad, the Rayatz returned to Otwock for the holiday. Nazi Germany's tightening grip on Europe would soon end his ability to travel for health care.
Tags: otwock, paris, passover

Title: Rebbe Rayatz describes Pesach with talmidim in Otwock
Summary: On 25 Nisan 5698 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his son-in-law (later the Rebbe) about Pesach spent with the talmidim and their teachers.
Story: Though he had not said Chassidus on the first days, the Rebbe wrote that the Sedarim and Yom Tov meals passed pleasantly and unhurriedly, with talmidim of Tomchei Temimim and their teachers joining. They spent long hours delighting in the goodness of Hashem and in memories of earlier days.
Tags: otwock, rayatz, pesach, letter, maamarim

Title: R. Geleshrtein writes about new student Preger
Summary: On 4 Iyar 5698, R. A.M. Gelershtein from Brisk wrote about a new candidate, Preger, seeking to study at Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock.
Story: On 4 Iyar 5698 (May 5, 1938), R. Avraham Mordechai Gelershtein of Brisk wrote to yeshiva secretary R. Yosef Avraham Kagan urging acceptance of the student Menachem Nachum Preger of Brisk, describing him as an outstanding talmid with fine character and talent. Preger was accepted, studied in Otwock until the war's outbreak, later escaped to Vilna and then Japan and Shanghai, and ultimately reached New York.
Tags: avraham mordechai gelershtein, menachem nachum preger, brisk, yehuda eber, yosef avraham kagan, otwock

Title: R. Mordechai Mentlik marries Gittel Stockhamer
Summary: R. Mordechai Mentlik married Gittel Stockhamer on Isru Chag Shavuos 5698.
Story: On Isru Chag Shavuos 5698 (7 Sivan, June 6, 1938), R. Mordechai Mentlik married Gittel Stockhamer, one of the daughters of R. David Stockhamer of Newark. The Rosh Yeshiva and the Rebbe Rayatz's secretaries — R. Yechezkel Feigin, R. Moshe Leib Rotshtein, and board member R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov — participated in the wedding and the sheva brachos.
Tags: mordechai mentlik, gittel stockhamer, wedding, otwock, sheva brachos

Title: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz marries Mindel Stockhamer
Summary: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz married Mindel Stockhamer on 15 Sivan 5698 at the Rebbe's residence in Otwock.
Story: On 15 Sivan 5698 (June 14, 1938), R. Moshe Pinchas Katz married Mindel Stockhamer at the building where the Rebbe Rayatz resided in Otwock — Prusa Street 6, as specified on the invitation. The Rosh Yeshiva, secretaries, and close friends of the groom participated in both the wedding and the sheva brachos.
Tags: moshe pinchas katz, mindel stockhamer, wedding, otwock, sheva brachos

Title: Rebbe blesses founding of Society of the Sisters of the Temimim in US
Summary: The Rebbe writes in English blessing the founding of an Achot Hatemimim women's group in America.
Story: He wrote, 'In reply to your letter advising me of your excellent resolution to interest yourselves in the study of Chasidism… I was greatly gratified with your good decision.' He appointed a committee of three prominent American rabbis — Yisrael Jacobson, Yisrael Kazarnovsky, and Yochanan Gordon — to teach the group and advise on format and curriculum, instructing them to set up weekly classes.
Tags: united states, women, achot hatemimim, jacobson, kazarnovsky, gordon

Title: Women's Achot Hatemimim group founded in United States
Summary: The Rebbe writes in English to a new women's group in America, appointing three prominent rabbis to teach them chasidic philosophy.
Story: The Rebbe expressed gratification with their decision to study Chasidism and selected Rabbis Yisrael Jacobson, Yisrael Kazarnovsky, and Yochanan Gordon as their mentors. The model expanded the women's chasidic study initiative pioneered in Riga.
Tags: women, achot-hatemimim, america, letter

Title: Feigin urges Jacobson to expedite Agudath Chabad statute for Otwock purchase
Summary: On 9 Tammuz 5698 secretary Feigin pressed R. Yisrael Jacobson to finalize Agudath Chabad's statute so a building in Otwock could be purchased in its name.
Story: On 9 Tammuz 5698 (July 8, 1938), Rabbi Yechezkel Feigin wrote to Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson, head of Agudath Chassidei Chabad in America, urgently requesting completion of the organization's official statute. The Rebbe Rayatz had decided that a building in Otwock — to house his residence, library, and the yeshiva — must be purchased in the American organization's name, since the security of Jews and their property in Poland was no longer assured. The lawyer required the statute to explicitly authorize the Aguda to acquire real estate abroad.
Tags: agudath-chassidei-chabad, otwock, yeshiva, tomchei-temimim, real-estate, yechezkel-feigin

Title: R. Feigin writes Jacobson about renewed building plans
Summary: On 9 Tammuz 5698, secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote R. Israel Jacobson that talks had resumed about purchasing the yeshiva building.
Story: On 9 Tammuz 5698 (July 8, 1938), secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to R. Israel Jacobson, director of Aguch in America, that after a long silence concerning the purchase of the yeshiva property — for various reasons the discussion had been suspended — by the Rebbe Rayatz's will, talks had been renewed to bring the purchase closer to fruition.
Tags: yechezkel feigin, israel jacobson, tomchei tmimim, otwock, fundraising

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe writes about branch management on 18 Tammuz 5698
Summary: In a letter of 18 Tammuz 5698, the Frierdiker Rebbe described the great effort required to run the yeshivos in Lodz, Vilna and the provincial yeshivos ketanos.
Story: The letter (Vol. 4, no. 1042) testified to the personal toll of managing the network. It positioned the provincial yeshivos ketanos as central to the Rebbe's ongoing chinuch mission rather than peripheral satellites.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, lodz, vilna, yeshivos ketanos, letter

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Boston rabbi about cramped library conditions
Summary: On 18 Tammuz 5698 the Rebbe described his 13,000-volume library as crammed into boxes in his Otwock home.
Story: Writing to Rabbi David Meir Rabinowitz of Boston on 18 Tammuz 5698 (July 17, 1938), the Rebbe Rayatz lamented that he and his books were 'in an exile of pressure and constraint' without adequate space. He reported owning approximately 13,000 printed volumes of holy books plus several thousand history and related works, only some of which stood on shelves while the rest had been locked in crates for years.
Tags: library, otwock, david-meir-rabinowitz, boston

Title: Rebbe Rayatz directs registration of Otwock property under American Aguda
Summary: On 19 Tammuz 5698 the Rebbe instructed Jacobson to secure US and Polish-consular approval of Agudath Chabad's statute so the Otwock building could be acquired.
Story: Writing on 19 Tammuz 5698 (July 18, 1938), the Rebbe Rayatz personally pressed Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson to obtain governmental and Polish-consular ratification of Agudath Chabad's statute. He asked that the approved document arrive by the end of Menachem Av so the courtyard and building for Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim in Otwock could be purchased in time. The added clauses designated the Rebbe as Honorary President and recorded all real estate as Aguda property.
Tags: agudath-chassidei-chabad, otwock, yisrael-jacobson, tomchei-temimim, real-estate

Title: Rebbe Rayatz on building purchase obstacle
Summary: On 19 Tammuz 5698, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Israel Jacobson about the obstacle to the building purchase.
Story: On 19 Tammuz 5698 (July 18, 1938), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Israel Jacobson that the obstacle to advancing the yeshiva building purchase was the lack of approved bylaws for Agudas Chabad from the US government and the Polish consul in New York. Only once these were approved could the building be purchased in Aguch's name.
Tags: israel jacobson, aguch, tomchei tmimim, real estate, united states

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe writes on 25 Tammuz 5698 about Polish yeshivos ketanos
Summary: On 25 Tammuz 5698, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote that modest funding could establish many yeshivos ketanos in Poland.
Story: He emphasized that no Polish city had organized Jewish chinuch outside of secular Tarbut schools and that small sums could fund roshei yeshiva for many new yeshivos ketanos. He cited the demonstrated success of existing Tomchei Tmimim preparatory branches as proof of concept.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, poland, yeshivos ketanos, chinuch, letter

Title: Rebbe Rayatz requests detailed roster of Tzemach Tzedek students
Summary: On 3 Menachem Av 5698 the Rebbe Rayatz asked Kollel Chabad for detailed information on each Tzemach Tzedek student.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz wrote requesting names, ages, family situation, intellectual capacities, duration of study in revealed Torah and Chassidus, and how long each student had been at Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek. The letter reflects his close attention to the Jerusalem institution and ongoing concern for the spiritual development of its students.
Tags: jerusalem, yeshiva tzemach tzedek, rebbe rayatz, correspondence

Title: Rebbe contrasts Chabad and Polish chasidism in letter on identity
Summary: The Rebbe defines Chabad's identity in contrast to Polish chasidic groups, emphasizing personal avodah over the Rebbe-bond.
Story: He wrote, 'One of the fundamental principles of Chabad is that it teaches its followers to be deeply engaged in the avodah of Chasidism. In contrast, for the Polish Chasidim, the main point is the connection to the Rebbe.' The letter framed Chabad's focus on internalizing Torah ideals through one's own effort, contrasting the Polish emphasis on the bond with the tzaddik.
Tags: poland, chabad, polish chasidim, avodah, identity

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Jacobson about sons-in-law visas
Summary: On 18 Av 5698, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote R. Israel Jacobson urging help to obtain US visas for the new sons-in-law of R. David Stockhamer.
Story: On 18 Av 5698 (August 15, 1938), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Israel Jacobson, director of Aguch in America, urging him out of inner love to help obtain US entry visas for both of R. David Stockhamer's new sons-in-law — R. Mordechai Mentlik and R. Moshe Pinchas Katz — so they could settle near him in Newark, 'a good place for a ben Torah.'
Tags: israel jacobson, david stockhamer, visas, newark, emigration, tomchei tmimim

Title: Wedding of Chaya Sarah Jacobson and R' Shlomo Zalman Hecht
Summary: The wedding of the author's daughter Chaya Sarah to R' Shlomo Zalman Hecht took place on 3 Elul 5698 with the Rebbe Rayatz's blessing.
Story: The Rebbe had agreed that after the seven days of feasting the couple would travel to study at Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock. Their departure together with other American students became a milestone in Chabad outreach. The wedding was thus a turning point in the American student movement.
Tags: hecht, wedding, elul, chaya sarah, jacobson, rayatz

Title: Wedding of Shlomo Zalman Hecht, son-in-law of Rabbi Jacobson
Summary: On 3 Elul 5698, Rabbi Shlomo Zalman Hecht married the daughter of Rabbi Israel Jacobson in New York before traveling to study at the Otwock yeshiva.
Story: Rabbi Israel Jacobson, head of Achei Tmimim in America, arranged that immediately after his daughter's wedding on 3 Elul 5698, the young couple would travel to Poland so the groom could study in Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock. This had been approved in advance by the Rebbe Rayatz, and the trip was made with great fanfare.
Tags: shlomo zalman hecht, israel jacobson, achei tmimim, new york

Title: Author moves to Moscow to learn the retouching trade
Summary: In Elul 5698 the author left his hometown Zlobin and settled in Moscow to learn photo-retouching and to be able to daven with a minyan for the approaching High Holidays.
Story: In Zlobin it was impossible to daven with a minyan on the Yamim Noraim, so the author moved to Moscow, found temporary lodging in the Marina-Roshcha neighborhood near the shul, and began studying retouching. R' Zusya Paz, the chassidic shamash of the Marina-Roshcha synagogue who had known him from Surazh years earlier, welcomed him warmly. Hearing that a shidduch had been proposed for him, R' Zusya immediately said, 'Don't even think about a shidduch — I have one for you,' meaning his niece in Shumyachi.
Tags: moscow, marina-roshcha, zlobin, soviet-era, zusya-paz

Title: Levitin sent as shadar to America
Summary: In Elul 5698 the Rebbe sent Levitin to the United States as a special emissary on his behalf.
Story: In Elul 5698 (1938), R. Shmuel Levitin was sent by the Rebbe Rayatz to America as a shadar. When his primary mission concluded in the spring of 5699, he asked whether to return home to Rakishok, but the Rebbe instructed him to remain in America - which ultimately spared him from the Holocaust.
Tags: levitin, usa, shadar, emissary

Title: Feigin confirms plan for Hecht couple to travel to Otwock
Summary: On 6 Elul 5698, the Rebbe's secretary Rabbi Yechezkel Feigin wrote to Rabbi Jacobson promising to help arrange his son-in-law's arrival in Otwock.
Story: Following the Hecht wedding, secretary Feigin wrote that he would do everything possible to assist the young couple's transition to Poland and would press the Yeshiva administration to give special attention to the new student arriving from America.
Tags: yechezkel feigin, shlomo zalman hecht, otwock, israel jacobson

Title: US Vaad publishes Tomchei Tmimim branch list on 16 Elul 5698
Summary: On 16 Elul 5698, the US-based Vaad LeHachzakas Yeshivos Tomchei Tmimim issued a letter listing the network's branches.
Story: The American Vaad listed branches in Warsaw, Otwock, Vilna, Lodz, Chmielnik, Patzanow, Raciaz, Globoke, Stopnica and Chelm. The letter was part of fundraising efforts to support a network the founders rightly sensed was facing existential threats from the deteriorating European political situation.
Tags: united states, vaad, tomchei tmimim, warsaw, vilna, lodz, fundraising

Title: Yeshivas Tomchei Tmimim report lists over 700 students across branches
Summary: On 7 Tishrei 5699, the Yeshiva administration issued a report stating that over 700 students were enrolled across the central Yeshiva in Otwock, the preparatory school in Warsaw, and branches in various towns.
Story: The letter from the Yeshiva leadership in early Tishrei 5699 (October 2, 1938) summarized the scope of Tomchei Tmimim under the previous Rebbe (Rayatz). It reported that the institution had become world-renowned, producing thousands of Torah scholars, and that more than 700 students were currently being educated and supported through the central yeshiva and its many branches.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, otwock, warsaw, poland, branches

Title: Shlomo Zalman Hecht and wife arrive in Otwock
Summary: By 12 Tishrei 5699, Rabbi Shlomo Zalman Hecht and his wife had arrived in Otwock to begin his studies at Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: Rabbi Feigin reported to Rabbi Jacobson on 12 Tishrei 5699 that his daughter and son-in-law had arrived safely. Because they came right before Yom Tov, they initially stayed at a pension, but the Rebbe Rayatz advised them to find their own apartment for both material and spiritual reasons.
Tags: shlomo zalman hecht, otwock, achei tmimim

Title: Hecht couple rents apartment near Rebbe's secretary in Otwock
Summary: By 26 Tishrei 5699, the Hechts had rented an apartment in the same courtyard where Rabbi Feigin and the Rebbetzin lived in Otwock.
Story: Following the Rebbe Rayatz's advice, the young couple moved out of the pension and rented an apartment in the courtyard where the Rebbe's secretary and the Rebbetzin also lived. The arrangement was deemed beneficial both for the wife, who would not be alone while her husband studied, and for the young couple's domestic guidance.
Tags: shlomo zalman hecht, otwock, yechezkel feigin

Title: American bochurim travel to Tomchei Tmimim Otwock to study
Summary: Right after Sukkos, around Parshas Lech Lecha 5699, the author's son-in-law, daughter, and bochurim Avraham M.M. Barnetzki and Dovber Levy sailed on the Queen Mary to study at Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock.
Story: R' Dovber Levy, an American-born great-nephew of the Malach, had transferred to the author's circle and wanted to study in Europe; the author personally covered the shortfall in his fare. R' Aryeh Leib Gellman of Mizrachi, who sailed with them, later returned praising the bochurim's stringent yiras shomayim aboard ship, including their refusal to daven in a shul without a mechitza. The departure boosted morale among the remaining students in New York.
Tags: otwock, poland, tomchei tmimim, hecht, barnetzki, dovber levy, queen mary, lech lecha

Title: Jacobson writes Rebbe about two students preparing to travel to Otwock
Summary: On 7 Cheshvan 5699, Rabbi Jacobson informed the Rebbe Rayatz that two students, Abraham Menachem Mendel Barnetzky and Dovber Levy, would soon travel to study at Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: Jacobson described both students positively: Barnetzky as a deep, hard-working chossid, and the 17-year-old Levy as exceptionally gifted, a nephew of the chassid 'Reb Avraham Dov the Malach.' Levy had only joined Achei Tmimim months earlier but Jacobson believed he could become 'a beautiful vessel.'
Tags: israel jacobson, achei tmimim, abraham barnetzky, dovber levy, otwock

Title: Barnetzky and Levy arrive at Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock
Summary: On 17 Cheshvan 5699, the two American students Abraham Barnetzky and Dovber Levy arrived unexpectedly at Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock.
Story: The two students sailed on the Queen Mary shortly after Sukkos 5699 and arrived in Otwock without prior notice. Rabbi Feigin wrote to Jacobson that the administration had been unprepared and noted that American students could not be sustained on the same austere terms as the local talmidim, requiring special attention both materially and spiritually.
Tags: abraham barnetzky, dovber levy, otwock, achei tmimim, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz instructs Jacobson to send Achei Tmimim students to Otwock
Summary: On 12 Kislev 5699, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote Rabbi Jacobson instructing him to send Achei Tmimim students to Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock as the foundation for a future American yeshiva.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz directed Jacobson 'to make efforts to send students from Achei Tmimim to the Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva in Otwock,' adding that with God's help this would become the seed for establishing a yeshiva in their own country in the spirit of Tomchei Tmimim. This shaped subsequent travel plans for additional groups.
Tags: israel jacobson, achei tmimim, tomchei tmimim, otwock, iggros kodesh

Title: 5699 yeshiva calendar lists 9 Tomchei Tmimim branches
Summary: The yeshiva's 5699 calendar listed nine branch departments across Poland and Latvia.
Story: The published list named Vilna, Lodz, Chmielnik, Patzanow, Stopnica, Globoke, Chelm, Lenchna, Kaluszyn and Dankera (Latvia). This represented the network's largest documented extent just before its near-total destruction in WWII.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, calendar, branches, poland, latvia

Title: Achei Tmimim students escape Otwock through Vilna to America
Summary: Some students of the Achei Tmimim yeshiva in Otwock fled to Vilna and were rescued via Russia, Japan, and China to America.
Story: With the Rebbe Rayatz's rescue from Warsaw, part of the Otwock yeshiva's students escaped to Vilna. From there they were saved through Russia, Japan, and China, eventually reaching the United States and Canada. The dispersal made it impossible to send support to the Tel Aviv yeshiva from abroad.
Tags: otwock, vilna, wwii, yeshiva tomchei tmimim, escape route

Title: Author's second trip to Rebbe Rayatz in Otwock with six students
Summary: In late summer of 5699, the author traveled to Otwock, Poland with six chosen Achei Tmimim students to study at Tomchei Tmimim and have yechidus with the Frierdiker Rebbe.
Story: On the eve of World War II, the author led a group of six of his best students from Achei Tmimim to Europe, where the Frierdiker Rebbe then resided in Otwock, Poland and the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was located. The trip required complex arrangements, especially convincing parents who saw the plan as extreme and dangerous. During their first yechidus, prepared for over a long spiritual period, the Rebbe told the author that if he came to America it would be solely to function as Nasi of Chabad and spread the Alter Rebbe's teachings.
Tags: otwock, poland, tomchei tmimim, achei tmimim, yechidus, pre-war

Title: Booklet 'Kiyum Nefesh M'Yisrael' printed in Riga
Summary: In 5699 Achos Tmimim Riga received permission to print the Rebbe's letter on saving a Jewish soul as a standalone kuntres.
Story: The Rebbe noted to his son-in-law on 7 Tevet 5699 that 'the Achos Tmimim institution in Riga requested permission to print the letter that begins 'all who sustain one Jewish soul' - I have surely sent him a copy - and I granted them permission.' The original letter had been addressed to Mr. Elchanan Cohen of New York.
Tags: achos-tmimim, riga, elchanan-cohen, publication

Title: Chelm community grants land for new yeshiva building
Summary: In 5699 the Chelm kehilla allotted land and Keren HaTorah pledged major funds to build a new yeshiva campus, plans aborted by the war.
Story: By 5699 student numbers in the Chelm branch had outgrown its premises. Kornblit obtained a building site from the kehilla and a substantial pledge from Dr. Shmuel Deutschlander of Agudas Yisrael's Keren HaTorah. The outbreak of WWII cancelled all construction plans, and most Chelm Jews were later murdered.
Tags: chelm, poland, achei-temimim, keren-torah, deutschlander

Title: Germans close Chmielnik yeshiva
Summary: On Rosh Hashanah 5700 the Germans entered Chmielnik and outlawed study at the Toras Emes yeshiva.
Story: With the German invasion on Rosh Hashanah 5700, study at the Chmielnik yeshiva was officially banned. Despite the prohibition, many students continued learning clandestinely in the women's section above the shul, and lessons persisted until the end of winter 5701. The clandestine yeshiva represents one of the documented cases of continued Torah study under Nazi occupation in occupied Poland.
Tags: poland, chmielnik, holocaust, wwii, nazi-occupation, toras-emes, underground

Title: Hyman writes JDC assessment for American Jewish Yearbook
Summary: JDC director Joseph Hyman published a glowing assessment of Agro-Joint's accomplishments without disclosing the Stalinist purges.
Story: 'In less than a decade and a half,' Hyman wrote, 'the work of the Agro-Joint helped transform Russian Jewry from a downtrodden, almost helpless ghetto population into self-reliant and productive workers.' The piece did not reveal that close to two hundred staff had been killed, imprisoned, or deported and that all JDC assets in Russia had been seized.
Tags: hyman, jdc, agro-joint, american-jewish-yearbook, soviet-union

Title: Levi Yitzchak Schneerson arrested in Dnepropetrovsk
Summary: The Rebbe's father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, was arrested in Dnepropetrovsk in 1939.
Story: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson—chief rabbi of Dnepropetrovsk and father of the seventh Lubavitcher Rebbe—was arrested by Soviet authorities in 1939. The Seventh Rebbe later denied that his father's writings had been confiscated at the time of arrest, but still directed the 1988 mission to inquire about related papers held in Dnepropetrovsk.
