Tags: levi-yitzchak-schneerson, dnepropetrovsk, soviet, arrest, nkvd

Title: Likutim Yekarim printed in Riga
Summary: In 5699 R. Shimon Noach Nimoitin printed the sefer Likutim Yekarim in Riga.
Story: R. Shimon Noach Nimoitin, mashpia of Vilna and its surrounding communities, produced the volume Likutim Yekarim through a Riga press in 5699, on the very eve of the Second World War.
Tags: riga, latvia, shimon-noach-nimoitin, likutim-yekarim, chassidus

Title: R. Mordechai Mentlik arrives in United States
Summary: R. Mordechai Mentlik arrived in the United States in Tishrei 5700.
Story: R. Mordechai Mentlik arrived in the United States in Tishrei 5700 (September-October 1939), having received his US visa at the beginning of Elul 5699 just before the outbreak of war. He later served as the senior rosh yeshiva of Tomchei Tmimim in New York and was a member of the Aguch executive.
Tags: mordechai mentlik, united states, newark, tishrei, emigration

Title: R. Yosef Avraham Kagan emigrates from Poland to England
Summary: At the start of 5699 R. Yosef Avraham Kagan left Warsaw for England, where he would settle permanently in London.
Story: After years serving as chief secretary at Tomchei Temimim Warsaw, R. Yosef Avraham Kagan departed for England at the start of 5699. He had become engaged to a young woman from England, and a farewell gathering was held before his journey.
Tags: poland, london, england, yosef avraham kagan, emigration

Title: Rabbi Aryeh Leib Kaplan arrested and exiled to Uzbekistan
Summary: Rabbi Kaplan, who had heeded the Rebbe's advice to remain in Russia, was arrested and deported to Uzbekistan.
Story: On the train into exile he met Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, father of the seventh Rebbe, who was also being banished. They were placed in villages thirty miles apart and stayed in contact. Kaplan was killed by anti-Semitic thugs on Yom Kippur 1943; Rabbi Levi Yitzchak died in 1944 and is buried in Alma Ata.
Tags: kaplan, uzbekistan, exile, levi-yitzchak-schneerson

Title: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson arrested by Soviet authorities
Summary: The Rebbe's father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson of Yekaterinoslav, was arrested in 5699 for his work spreading Judaism.
Story: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, kabbalist and rabbi of Yekaterinoslav and father of the seventh Rebbe, was arrested by the Soviet regime in 5699 (1939) as punishment for promoting Jewish observance. A photograph of him taken on the day of his arrest is preserved in the Lubavitch Library.
Tags: russia, levi yitzchak schneerson, soviet, kgb, yekaterinoslav

Title: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson begins exile glosses
Summary: From 5699 onward, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson wrote glosses on the Zohar during Soviet exile.
Story: After being exiled by the Soviet government as punishment for spreading religion, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson—Yekaterinoslav rabbi and father of the Rebbe—wrote Kabbalistic glosses on the few books he had with him from 1939 to 1944. He also sent his son letters and kuntreisim on Chassidut and Kabbalah from exile.
Tags: levi yitzchak schneerson, soviet exile, kazakhstan, zohar

Title: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson exiled to Kazakhstan
Summary: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, father of the future seventh Rebbe, was jailed by Soviet authorities and exiled in 1939 to a remote village near the Chinese border.
Story: His wife Rebbetzin Chana followed him into exile in Kazakhstan and was at his bedside when he passed away in Alma Ata in 1945. She later escaped Russia through the Great Escape, made it to Paris, and was reunited with her son the Ramash in 1947 after twenty years of separation.
Tags: levi yitzchak schneerson, kazakhstan, russia, kgb, exile

Title: Rabbi Shmuel Levitin arrives in US as Rebbe's emissary
Summary: In 1939 Rabbi Shmuel Levitin arrived in the US just before the High Holidays as the Rebbe's emissary; the war prevented his return.
Story: Levitin, born in 1883, had been imprisoned by the Soviets for religious activities in Georgia before escaping Russia in 1937. He visited communities across America until war broke out. His wife was trapped in Europe and killed by the Nazis. Levitin emerged as a chasidic elder playing a major role in Chabad's American development.
Tags: america, shadar, soviet-georgia, holocaust

Title: Rabbi Zelig Slonim sent to Australia as Rebbe's emissary
Summary: In 1939 the Rebbe dispatched Rabbi Zelig Slonim on his final long mission, traveling Australia and New Zealand.
Story: Slonim had previously served as the Rebbe's emissary in England, Scandinavia, and South Africa. The Sydney Jewish News announced his arrival as a distinguished scholar endorsed by the chief rabbis of Palestine, the UK, and South Africa. He worked on projects including building a mikveh in Brisbane before departing Perth in March 1940 on a dangerous journey back to Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: australia, new-zealand, shadar, mikveh

Title: Rashag begins teaching Chassidus to Tomchei Tmimim students
Summary: In the early months of 5699, the Rashag began regularly speaking with the Yeshiva students about Chassidic teachings.
Story: Rabbi Yisrael Yaakov Yeber, the rosh yeshiva, reported at the start of the year that the Rashag had recently begun speaking with the talmidim in Chassidus. The Rashag came to regard one of the senior students, Mendel Tenenboim, as outstanding among the talmidim.
Tags: rashag, chassidus, otwock, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz besieged in Warsaw during German invasion
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz spent most of the winter of 5700 trapped in besieged Warsaw before being rescued to Riga and then America.
Story: As WWII engulfed Europe, funding from abroad to Yeshivat Achei Tmimim in Tel Aviv nearly ceased. The Rebbe Rayatz himself spent much of the winter caught in the siege of Warsaw until divine assistance enabled his escape from the persecutors to Riga and onward to America. The crisis severely disrupted communication and support for Chabad institutions in Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: warsaw, wwii, rebbe rayatz, poland

Title: Rebbe Rayatz requests US immigration papers
Summary: In the winter of 5699, the Rebbe Rayatz asked aides to prepare US immigration papers as a precaution.
Story: Though not yet planning to emigrate, the Rebbe Rayatz instructed his secretariat to begin preparing immigration documents for the United States. Secretary Yechezkel Feigin explained in correspondence that the move was contingent on conditions; if Europe stabilized, no emigration would occur.
Tags: rayatz, otwock, poland, usa, immigration, pre-war

Title: Rotstein flees Warsaw with wife before Rosh Hashana
Summary: R. Moshe Leib Rotstein and his wife fled Warsaw on foot the week before Rosh Hashana 5700, eventually reaching Vilna safely.
Story: As war broke out, R. Moshe Leib Rotstein and his wife fled Warsaw on foot the week before Rosh Hashana 5700, intending to reach Globoke. Their fate was initially unknown, but it later emerged that they had arrived safely in Vilna, where many Polish yeshiva students had relocated.
Tags: warsaw, war, wwii, escape, moshe leib rotstein, vilna

Title: Rotstein meets Rebbe in Riga to report on Vilna yeshiva
Summary: When the Frierdiker Rebbe arrived in Riga at the beginning of Tevet 5700, Rotstein and R. Shmuel Zalmanov came to report on the yeshiva's reorganization in Vilna.
Story: At the start of Tevet 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe arrived in Riga. R. Moshe Leib Rotstein traveled there together with R. Shmuel Zalmanov to brief the Rebbe on how the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva had been reconstituted in Vilna after fleeing Poland.
Tags: riga, vilna, tomchei temimim, moshe leib rotstein, shmuel zalmanov, frierdiker rebbe

Title: Shimon Goldman studies in Kaloszyn yeshiva
Summary: At his bar mitzvah Shimon Goldman entered the Lubavitch yeshiva in Kaloszyn, where students were learning Masechet Pesachim.
Story: In summer 5699 the 13-year-old Shimon Goldman from Siedlce began learning at the Lubavitch branch yeshiva in Kaloszyn, recalling Leib Kremer as menahel and the dayan's son as maggid shiur. The boys studied Masechet Pesachim and ate 'days' arrangements with local families. He later recorded his memories in Kfar Chabad magazine.
Tags: kaloszyn, poland, shimon-goldman, masechet-pesachim, eating-days

Title: Stalin deports tens of thousands of Polish Jews to Siberia
Summary: After the Soviet army occupied eastern Poland in 1939, Stalin seized thousands of Polish Jews and deported them to forced-labour camps in Siberia.
Story: Many of the deportees perished from hunger, illness and cold. Two years later, when Hitler turned on the USSR, Stalin made peace with the Polish government-in-exile and released the surviving Polish citizens — who poured southward into the warm Central Asian republics, including Samarkand, where they would later collide with Lubavitcher refugees at clandestine Yom Kippur minyanim.
Tags: poland, siberia, soviet-deportations, wwii, stalin, polish-jews

Title: Tomchei Temimim branch reopens in Livenhof
Summary: Around 5699 the Frierdiker Rebbe established a Tomchei Temimim branch in Livenhof, run together with the Dankra yeshiva by R. Berchen.
Story: Approximately in 5699 the Frierdiker Rebbe founded a Tomchei Temimim branch in Livenhof, separate from R. Teitz's earlier yeshiva. Yeshaya Chanoch Berchen of Gostini directed both Latvian branches simultaneously, corresponding with the Rebbe about each.
Tags: livenhof, livani, latvia, tomchei-temimim, yeshaya-chanoch-berchen

Title: Tomchei Temimim relocates to Otwock; network reaches 1,440 students
Summary: On the eve of the war the flagship Tomchei Temimim yeshivah relocated from Warsaw to Otwock with a network of ten branches and 1,440 students.
Story: From a single Warsaw branch with modest enrollment in 1930, the yeshivah grew into an educational empire spanning Poland and Lithuania. Otwock held 450 students, Warsaw 250, and Lodz 150, with the rest distributed among other branches. Many branches also spawned Chabad chadarim. The relocation forced by the war later led to new branches in Japan, China, and elsewhere.
Tags: otwock, warsaw, poland, lithuania, tomchei-temimim, lodz

Title: Tomchei Tmimim branch founded in Livenhof (Livani), Latvia
Summary: A Tomchei Tmimim branch was founded in Livenhof (Livani), Latvia, in 5699 (1939).
Story: The final pre-war branch opened in Livenhof shortly before the outbreak of WWII. By the start of 5701 (autumn 1940), Livenhof and Dankera merged and relocated to Riga as Polish branches collapsed and Latvia fell under Soviet control.
Tags: latvia, livenhof, livani, tomchei tmimim, branch

Title: Winter devoted to rescuing Rebbe Rayatz from Nazi-occupied Warsaw
Summary: The entire winter of 5700 was devoted to rescuing the Frierdiker Rebbe, his family, and entourage from Nazi-occupied Warsaw.
Story: After the German invasion of Poland, the winter of 5700 (1939–1940) was consumed by coordinated efforts to extract Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, his family, and his entourage from occupied Warsaw. A dedicated book documenting the events and testimony of those days is being prepared for publication. The rescue effort drew on diplomatic, logistical, and financial mobilization across the Chabad network.
Tags: warsaw, nazis, world war ii, rescue, poland

Title: Rayatz travels to Riga for health reasons
Summary: The Rayatz visited Riga from 4 Shevat to 11 Nisan 5699 for health reasons.
Story: With Austria closed and tensions rising across Europe, Riga remained accessible. The Rayatz spent over two months in Latvia before returning to Otwock for Passover, his last calm period before war.
Tags: riga, latvia, health

Title: Arrest of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson
Summary: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, father of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, was arrested in March 1939.
Story: In March 1939, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson was arrested by Soviet authorities. From the moment of his imprisonment, his physical strength deteriorated rapidly day by day, though his spirit remained strong. His suffering was intensified by the absence of Jewish spiritual life in his place of exile.
Tags: soviet union, kgb, exile, levi yitzchak schneerson

Title: Jacobson outlines plan for new group of students to travel to Otwock
Summary: On 9 Adar 5699, Rabbi Jacobson wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz detailing plans to send another group of American students to study at Otwock.
Story: Jacobson's letter outlined which talmidim from Achei Tmimim were prepared to travel to Poland. The Rebbe Rayatz responded on 28 Adar that he was too busy to reply at length and would answer in due time, beginning a months-long planning process for the trip.
Tags: israel jacobson, achei tmimim, tomchei tmimim, otwock

Title: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz writes about visa difficulties
Summary: On 11 Adar 5699, R. Moshe Pinchas Katz wrote about his ongoing difficulties obtaining a US visa.
Story: On 11 Adar 5699 (March 2, 1939), R. Moshe Pinchas Katz wrote to R. Yosef Avraham Kagan about the difficulty of obtaining a US visa. He had visited the consulate the previous week with an American yeshiva student, hoping that the citizen sponsor might receive favorable consideration, and the consul had promised a quick response, but the waiting was agonizing.
Tags: moshe pinchas katz, yosef avraham kagan, visas, consulate, emigration, otwock

Title: R' Yosef Morgenstern, Rebbe of Kotzk-Pilov, passes away
Summary: On 14 Adar 5699 the Rebbe of Kotzk-Pilov, R' Yosef Morgenstern, passed away leaving no descendants.
Story: On 14 Adar 5699 (5 March 1939) the Admur of Kotzk-Pilov, R' Yosef Morgenstern, passed away. He left no descendants, and his chassidim sought a successor among his close circle. Their choice fell on R' David Teiblum, then a maggid shiur at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw.
Tags: kotzk, pilov, rebbe-of-kotzk, morgenstern, poland

Title: NKVD arrests R' Meir Gurkov in Kharkov on Shushan Purim
Summary: On Shushan Purim 5699 the NKVD searched R' Meir Gurkov's home and arrested him along with three other Anash, following the arrival of informer David Itze in Kharkov.
Story: After the informer David Itze appeared in Kharkov and lodged with R' Meir Gurkov, the family realized danger and Gurkov briefly hid at his son-in-law Israel Yehuda's apartment on the city's outskirts. On Shushan Purim 5699 the NKVD raided Gurkov's home, arresting him and three other Anash members under harsh conditions and interrogating their sons; the fear was so severe that family members could not look one another in the eye.
Tags: kharkov, nkvd, meir gurkov, informer, david itze

Title: Passing of R' Alter Simchowitz, mashpia of Toras Emes in Jerusalem
Summary: R' Alter Simchowitz, longtime mashpia of Toras Emes in Jerusalem, passed away on 7 Nissan 5699.
Story: After his brief 5689 stint in Warsaw, R' Alter continued serving as mashpia of the Toras Emes yeshiva in Jerusalem for the next decade. He held that post until his passing on 7 Nissan 5699.
Tags: jerusalem, toras-emes, alter-simchowitz, death, yahrzeit

Title: R' Alter Simchowitz passes away in Jerusalem
Summary: On 7 Nissan 5699 R' Alter Simchowitz passed away in Jerusalem after years of service as mashpia at Yeshivat Toras Emet and for Anash in the city.
Story: Simchowitz had been appointed by the Rebbe Rayatz to those roles after his final return from Warsaw. His career, traced in detail in Toldot Chabad b'Eretz HaKodesh, spanned founding roles in Hebron, Shchedrin, Kremenchug, Rostov, Warsaw and Jerusalem.
Tags: jerusalem, eretz yisrael, alter simchowitz, toras emet, passing

Title: R' David Teiblum crowned as Admur by Kotzk-Pilov chassidim
Summary: In Nisan 5699 R' David Teiblum, a longtime Tomchei Tmimim maggid shiur, was crowned Admur by the Pilov chassidim.
Story: In Nisan 5699 (April 1939) R' David Teiblum — known as R' David Riker after his hometown Reika — was crowned Admur by the chassidim of Kotzk-Pilov following the death of R' Yosef Morgenstern. He had served as maggid shiur of the lowest class at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw since 5686. Before accepting, he sought and received the affirmation of the Rebbe Rayatz; he was later murdered in the Holocaust.
Tags: david-teiblum, kotzk, pilov, tomchei-tmimim, warsaw

Title: Feigin writes Jacobson about US immigration preparations
Summary: Secretary Yechezkel Feigin wrote to Israel Jacobson explaining the Rebbe Rayatz's instructions to prepare US immigration papers.
Story: On 28 Nissan 5699, Feigin conveyed the Rebbe's directive to Jacobson, director of Agudas Chabad in the US. The letter clarified that preparing papers was precautionary against worsening conditions, not yet a firm decision to emigrate.
Tags: feigin, jacobson, agudas-chabad, immigration, correspondence

Title: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz departs for United States
Summary: On 7 Iyar 5699, secretary Nissan Mindel reported that R. Moshe Pinchas Katz was departing for London en route to the US.
Story: On 7 Iyar 5699 (April 26, 1939), secretary Nissan Mindel wrote to R. Yosef Avraham Kagan in London that R. Moshe Pinchas Katz was departing that day for London on his way to America. R. Mentlik later confirmed on 23 Iyar (May 12) that he had received a telegram on Tuesday that his brother-in-law had arrived safely.
Tags: moshe pinchas katz, nissan mindel, london, united states, emigration

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes Ramash about renting Gelbfish building
Summary: On 15 Iyar 5699, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote his son-in-law about renting the Gelbfish building for the yeshiva.
Story: On 15 Iyar 5699 (May 4, 1939), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his son-in-law (Ramash) about a strong possibility of renting a spacious residence in the courtyard adjacent to his own home — the Gelbfish pension with about forty rooms and large halls. The plan required a two-year-plus lease at 8,000 zloty per year paid in advance, totaling nearly 18,000 zloty, to be financed from funds collected by R. M.D. — but a few months later the war erupted and all plans came to a halt.

Title: Rayatz writes to R. Michael Vilensky to commemorate his father
Summary: On 3 Tammuz 5699 the Rayatz wrote to R. Michael Vilensky asking him to compose a biography of his father for the Hatamim journal.
Story: The Rayatz wrote to R. Michael Vilensky requesting that he prepare a memorial article about his father, the Chasid R. Chaim Dover of Kremenchug, for the ninth volume of Hatamim then being edited. World War broke out shortly afterward, the issue never appeared, and Vilensky's reply never reached its destination.

Title: Feigin updates Jacobson on planning for second American student group
Summary: On 4 Tammuz 5699, Rabbi Feigin conveyed the Rebbe's response that doubled the proposed group size and set the stay at two years.
Story: Feigin wrote that the Rebbe Rayatz, comparing Jacobson's proposed five talmidim with what the Rebbe's own secretariat had suggested, was prepared for double that number, to study in Otwock for two years. Jacobson then began final arrangements to escort the group personally to Poland.

Title: Wedding of R. Yosef Avraham Kagan in London
Summary: R. Yosef Avraham Kagan's wedding was held in London on 8 Tammuz 5699, after which he settled there permanently.
Story: On 8 Tammuz 5699, R. Yosef Avraham Kagan, formerly chief secretary of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw, married in London. He lived in London for the rest of his life.

Title: Feigin reports on Hecht's studies and difficulties of distance in Otwock
Summary: On 17 Tammuz 5699, Rabbi Feigin updated Jacobson about his son-in-law's studies in Otwock, noting both progress and challenges.
Story: Feigin wrote that although Hecht's learning was now well arranged, the physical distance between home and yeshiva remained difficult. Hecht traveled early each morning to the yeshiva, where he learned Chassidus and prayed before turning to nigleh.

Title: Jacobson sets August departure date for next group to Otwock
Summary: On 2 Menachem Av 5699, Rabbi Jacobson wrote to Rabbi Yehuda Leib Horowitz of Boston announcing his departure to the Rebbe Rayatz with a group of students.
Story: Jacobson informed Horowitz that he would sail on Erev Shabbos Parshas Eikev, 19 Menachem Av (August 4, 1939), to travel to the Rebbe in Otwock with some of his talmidim. The original date was ultimately postponed.
Tags: israel jacobson, achei tmimim, boston, yehuda leib horowitz, tomchei tmimim

Title: Birth of Ephraim Shmuel son of Israel Yehuda on Tisha B'Av
Summary: Israel Yehuda's son Ephraim Shmuel was born on 9 Av 5699 in Kharkov and was given a brit milah with a minyan of ten men.
Story: The boy was named for Israel Yehuda's father. Despite the danger of gathering openly, a minyan was assembled for the brit. R' Betzalel Wilshansky later fled Voronezh and joined the family in Kharkov around this period.
Tags: kharkov, ephraim shmuel, brit milah

Title: Final photograph of students learning at Otwock
Summary: On 10 Av 5699, a photograph was taken of students learning at the Gelbfish pension, likely the last picture of Tomchei Tmimim students at Otwock.
Story: On 10 Av 5699 (July 26, 1939), approximately one month before the outbreak of World War II, a photograph was taken at the Gelbfish pension showing yeshiva students learning sugyot together in the courtyard. R. Yosef Rodal sat at the center. The photograph was sent to R. Moshe Pinchas Katz, who had recently emigrated to America, and is likely the last image of Tomchei Tmimim students learning in Otwock.
Tags: otwock, tomchei tmimim, gelbfish, photograph, moshe pinchas katz, yosef rodal

Title: Author's second visit to the Frierdiker Rebbe in Elul 5699
Summary: In Elul 5699 the author visited the Rebbe for a second time and discussed the question of the Rebbe's settling in America.
Story: The author delivered 213 pidyonot and regards from individuals and communal matters. The Rebbe explained that although people had approached him about moving to the United States, he had not held by the idea because the mode of his earlier American visit had been that of a public askan rather than reflecting his true purpose with chassidim and chassidus.
Tags: rayatz, elul, 1939, yechidus, settlement, pidyonot, poland

Title: Final pre-war letter from Rebbe to Chadakov in Riga
Summary: The Rebbe's last pre-war letter to R. Chaim Mordechai Aizik Chadakov in Riga was written 17 Menachem Av 5699, one month before World War II broke out.
Story: The Riga correspondence covered farbrengens of anash, rabbinical appointments, taharas hamishpacha, mikvaos, tefillin campaigns, kosher food for Jewish soldiers, summer camps, education, refugee aid for Ashkenaz refugees in Riga, separation of boys' and girls' schools in Lvov, and plans for an Achos Tmimim monthly journal. War cut short the journal and many other plans.
Tags: rayatz, chadakov, riga, pre-war, achos-tmimim

Title: Jacobson sails for Poland with six Achei Tmimim students on Île de France
Summary: On 23 Menachem Av 5699 (August 8, 1939), Rabbi Jacobson set sail on the Île de France with six Achei Tmimim students bound for Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock.
Story: The group included Mordechai Dov Altein, Meir Greenberg, Avraham Dovber Hecht, Yitzchak Kalodny, Zerach Gordon, and Mordechai Fisher, intending to study in Poland for two years. They traveled by train through France, Belgium, and Germany after disembarking, reaching Otwock at the start of Elul.
Tags: israel jacobson, achei tmimim, tomchei tmimim, otwock, ile de france, altein, greenberg, hecht, kalodny, gordon, fisher

Title: Six American students depart for Otwock yeshivah with Rabbi Jacobson
Summary: Rabbi Jacobson personally escorted six American boys aboard the Isle de France from the US to study at the Otwock yeshivah.
Story: On 24 Av 5699, Jacobson left New York with six American students bound for Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim in Otwock. They arrived just seventeen days before the outbreak of World War II. The Rebbe had assured the parents 'you have nothing to fear,' and the boys' presence later became central evidence that a Chabad yeshivah could succeed in America.
Tags: united states, poland, otwock, yeshivas tomchei temimim, yisrael jacobson, isle de france

Title: R. Mentlik to receive visa
Summary: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5699, secretary R. Moshe Leib Rotshtein wrote that R. Mordechai Mentlik would receive his visa the next day.
Story: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5699 (August 15, 1939), secretary R. Moshe Leib Rotshtein wrote to R. Yosef Avraham Kagan that R. Mordechai Mentlik would receive his visa in practice the next day. With the war breaking out only weeks later, this was among the final pieces of correspondence from Otwock's yeshiva administration.
Tags: mordechai mentlik, moshe leib rotshtein, visa, united states, emigration

Title: Six American students arrive at Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Elul 5699, Rabbi Jacobson and the six American talmidim arrived in Otwock to begin their studies.
Story: Met in Paris by the Rebbe's son-in-law (the future Rebbe), the group continued by train through Europe, arriving at the Yeshiva on Rosh Chodesh Elul. Rabbi Shmuel Dovid Reitchik was the first to engage them in learning, and they were tested in both nigleh and Chassidus by Rabbi Berel Kornitzer.
Tags: achei tmimim, tomchei tmimim, otwock, meir greenberg, israel jacobson

Title: American students hear Maamar Shoftim and have first yechidus with Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: On 3 Elul 5699, the Rebbe Rayatz delivered Maamar Shoftim and admitted the newly-arrived American talmidim to their first yechidus.
Story: Two days after their arrival, on Friday 3 Elul (Parshas Shoftim), the Rebbe Rayatz delivered the maamar 'Shoftim v'shotrim titen lecha b'chol she'arecha,' which was then repeated by the chozer Rabbi Mordechai Mentlik before his own departure to America. That night a farbrengen was held in Shlomo Zalman Hecht's home led by Rabbi Yechezkel Feigin.
Tags: otwock, achei tmimim, maamar, mentlik, shoftim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes son-in-law about Jacobson's arrival with students
Summary: On 3 Elul 5699, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote his son-in-law (the future Rebbe) that Rabbi Jacobson had arrived in Otwock with six new students.
Story: The Rebbe wrote that he had been busy since Jacobson's arrival answering hundreds of letters the latter had brought from America. He also directed that two hundred copies of Rabbi Simpson's sefer be given to Jacobson to take back.
Tags: iggros kodesh, israel jacobson, achei tmimim, tomchei tmimim, otwock

Title: Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson meets with the Rebbe in Otwock about US relocation
Summary: On Saturday night, Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson met the Rebbe in Otwock, where the Rebbe resolved to relocate to the United States within about six months.
Story: Five days before the German invasion of Poland, Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson met privately with the Sixth Rebbe in Otwock. The Rebbe announced his firm decision to move to the United States, citing the success of American students at the Polish yeshivah and Rabbi Shmuel Levitin's assessment that a Lubavitcher yeshivah could thrive in America. He told Jacobson, 'Arrange everything systematically. In about half a year, with G-d's assistance, we will come to America,' and signaled a turn inward toward teaching Chasidism and caring for Chasidim.
Tags: otwock, poland, united states, yisrael jacobson, rayatz, yeshivas tomchei temimim, pre-war

Title: Jacobson holds farewell yechidus before returning to America
Summary: On 14 Elul 5699, Rabbi Jacobson had yechidus with the Rebbe Rayatz before departing back to the United States from Poland.
Story: During this final yechidus Jacobson asked what answer to give the parents of the talmidim he had escorted from America. The Rebbe replied that whatever would happen to all the talmidim would also happen to them, but added that as American citizens they could always escape to Riga.
Tags: israel jacobson, otwock, achei tmimim, yechidus

Title: Farbrengen at Otwock yeshivah marking its 32nd founding anniversary
Summary: Students of the Lubavitch yeshivah in Otwock held an all-night farbrengen on 16 Elul commemorating the founding of Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim 32 years earlier.
Story: On the eve of Germany's invasion, students gathered through the night singing melodies and hearing chasidic stories to mark the yeshivah's founding. Avraham Garfinkel recalled the celebration ending at sunrise — none of them imagined that within hours their world would be shattered by war.
Tags: otwock, poland, yeshivas tomchei temimim, farbrengen, pre-war

Title: American talmidim study in Riga under Rabbi Itche Masmid
Summary: Following their flight from Otwock, the American students remained in Riga to continue their studies through mid-Tishrei 5700.
Story: During Chol HaMoed Sukkos the group decided to remain in Riga as long as possible to fulfill their original purpose of intensive study. Rabbi Yitzchak the Masmid taught them Likkutei Torah, another chossid taught them Tanya in the evenings, and Rabbi Mordechai Dubin paid for their lodging.
Tags: riga, achei tmimim, isaac matmid, mordechai dubin, world war ii

Title: Father buys an apartment in Cherbinov ahead of the wedding
Summary: In Tishrei 5700 the author's father came to Moscow and bought him a 20-square-meter apartment in the Cherbinov settlement, about an hour by tram from the Marina-Roshcha synagogue.
Story: Moscow's housing shortage was so severe that many bochurim could not marry. The father's finances had improved, so he came in Tishrei 5700, purchased the small apartment, and bought the essential furniture. The author would later travel into Moscow only rarely, working from home on retouching jobs.
Tags: moscow, cherbinov, housing, marriage-preparation, tram

Title: Jacobson's yechidus with Rebbe Rayatz in Otwock
Summary: During mid-Elul 5699, Israel Jacobson met with the Rebbe Rayatz in Otwock, who told him to prepare for the family's arrival in America within six months.
Story: Jacobson arrived in Otwock with a group of students from New York. In yechidus, the Rebbe Rayatz instructed him to arrange matters in America 'on solid foundations,' saying that within about half a year they would arrive there. By summer's end, the decision to emigrate was final.
Tags: jacobson, otwock, yechidus, immigration, usa

Title: Kaloszyn yeshiva dispersed at outbreak of WWII
Summary: After the German invasion of Poland, Rabbi Kremer dissolved the Kaloszyn yeshiva and sent out-of-town students home.
Story: During the first week of the war the Kaloszyn yeshiva kept its learning schedule, but as the Wehrmacht's rapid advance became clear, Leib Kremer and the hanhalah declared an emergency. Unable to take responsibility for boys from other towns, they dispersed the yeshiva and sent students such as Shimon Goldman back to families like his in Siedlce.
Tags: kaloszyn, poland, wwii, tomchei-temimim, leib-kremer

Title: Publication of HaTamim journal halted by outbreak of WWII
Summary: Publication of HaTamim ceased at the end of 5699 when WWII broke out, after eight issues had appeared.
Story: From the first issue in late summer 5695 through the eighth issue in winter 5699, the Rebbe Rayatz's son-in-law in Paris had continued to substantively edit HaTamim under cover of named Warsaw editors. The outbreak of war in autumn 5699 ended the journal's run; Agudas Talmidei HaTmimim had also been publishing Likkutei Dibburim, the Megillas Yud-Tes Kislev, and a Tehillim compilation under R' Schneur Zalman Gourary's direction.
Tags: warsaw, hatamim, wwii, poland, war, agudas talmidei hatmimim

Title: Rebbe and family relocate from Otwock to Warsaw under Latvian diplomatic cover
Summary: In early September the Latvian Embassy sent a car with diplomatic plates to ferry the Rebbe and his family from bombed Otwock to Warsaw.
Story: With trains halted and roads under bombardment, the Latvian Embassy dispatched its diplomatic vehicle twice. Chaim Lieberman left with part of the family on Monday, and the Rebbe followed the next day, taking valuable historic manuscripts but leaving the bulk of his library behind in Otwock. A tearful crowd bade him farewell as he blessed them, saying 'A king guards his subjects.'
Tags: otwock, warsaw, poland, latvia, luftwaffe, escape, rashag, chaim lieberman

Title: Rebbe Rayatz flees Otwock for Warsaw as WWII begins
Summary: In late Elul 5699, as the war began, the Rebbe Rayatz left Otwock for Warsaw, taking refuge in the Shmotkin home at Murnowska 32.
Story: At the outbreak of World War II in late Elul 5699 (early September 1939), the Rebbe Rayatz left his home in Otwock and traveled to Warsaw, where he stayed in R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin's house at Murnowska 32. During the German bombing of Warsaw, the building was hit and burned, destroying the Rebbe's clothing and belongings, and he relocated to the home of R. Yechiel Tzvi Gurary.
Tags: warsaw, otwock, world war 2, rayatz, german invasion, murnowska 32

Title: WWII breaks out and Vilna Tomchei Tmimim temporarily closes
Summary: With the outbreak of World War II in Elul 5699, the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva closed and its students were sent home.
Story: When World War II broke out in Elul 5699, the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim shut down and dispersed its students to their homes. R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal returned to his family in Koretz. Shortly afterward, the yeshiva reopened as a refuge for displaced Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim students, with R' Oshpal returning to head it.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, war, wwii, rabbi yitzchak dov oshpal, koretz

Title: American students bid farewell to the Rebbe and flee Otwock for Latvia
Summary: On the first day of the war, the six American students visited the Rebbe in Otwock, who blessed them and sent them to Mordechai Cheifetz's care in Riga.
Story: After the American Consul urged them to leave, the boys stopped at the Rebbe's home before departing. The Rebbe, already in silk Shabbat garments, told them to head to neutral Latvia and asked Meir Greenberg to tell Mordechai Dubin to have the Latvian government request a permit for the Rebbe and family. When asked about possibly desecrating Shabbat, the Rebbe replied that the merit of the Baal Shem Tov and Rabbi Schneur Zalman — both born on 18 Elul — would suffice that they would not need to transgress.
Tags: otwock, warsaw, riga, latvia, united states, american students, chai elul, escape

Title: American Tomchei Tmimim students instructed to flee Poland
Summary: On 17 Elul the Rebbe Rayatz directed American students in the Otwock yeshiva to escape via Warsaw, Riga, and Stockholm back to the United States.
Story: Once war began, the Rebbe Rayatz told the American bochurim at Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock to seek passage out of Poland alongside foreign diplomats and citizens. The mashpia R. Yisroel Eber distributed travel money. They escaped via Warsaw, Riga, and Stockholm, eventually returning to the United States.
Tags: poland, usa, tomchei-tmimim, rayatz, wwii, rescue

Title: Germany invades Poland; bombs fall on Otwock and the yeshivah
Summary: Germany launched its invasion of Poland at dawn, and within hours Luftwaffe bombers struck Otwock, including the new Lubavitch yeshivah building.
Story: At 4:45 a.m. a German battleship shelled Gdańsk, and panzer columns crossed into Poland. By 8:00 a.m., as students prepared for morning prayers in Otwock, German planes were bombing the town. Ten children in the Jewish orphanage were killed, and the new yeshivah building was struck though no students died. The Rebbe later admitted to the American students, 'I did not foresee it.'
Tags: world war ii, otwock, poland, luftwaffe, yeshivas tomchei temimim, nazi germany

Title: World War II begins; Rebbe Rayatz directs American talmidim to Warsaw and Riga
Summary: On 17 Elul 5699 (1 September 1939), with the outbreak of World War II, the Rebbe Rayatz instructed the American talmidim to leave Otwock for Warsaw and continue on to Riga before Shabbos.
Story: On Friday morning the students heard the roar of aircraft and bombings begin. The Rebbe Rayatz called them in to yechidus, told them to travel calmly to Warsaw and then on to Riga 'to my Chassidim,' where Rabbi Mordechai Chefetz would arrange their studies in nigleh and Chassidus until the storm passed. Meir Greenberg was given a private mission to communicate with Mordechai Dubin in Riga regarding a Latvian visa for the Rebbe.
Tags: world war ii, otwock, warsaw, riga, achei tmimim, mordechai chefetz

Title: World War II breaks out; Germany invades Poland
Summary: On 17 Elul 5699, World War II began with the German invasion of Poland, trapping the Rebbe Rayatz and his family in Otwock.
Story: The outbreak of war drastically changed the situation for the Rebbe Rayatz, who had been staying in Otwock. Within days he and his family would be forced to flee, beginning a four-month ordeal under Nazi occupation in Warsaw.
Tags: wwii, poland, nazi-invasion, otwock

Title: WWII breaks out; German bombs fall on Otwock during yeshiva founding-day gathering
Summary: On the eve of 17 Elul, after an all-night yeshiva-founding-day farbrengen, German bombs began falling on Otwock as the students returned from the mikveh.
Story: Rabbi Dov had led the Tomchei Tmimim bochurim in a yeshiva-anniversary farbrengen through the night of 17 Elul. At dawn, walking back from the mikveh half an hour away, the students heard explosions they first mistook for Polish drills. By morning it was clear that Germany had invaded Poland, bombs had hit Jewish neighborhoods, and the Second World War had begun.
Tags: poland, otwock, wwii, tomchei-tmimim, rayatz, war

Title: American talmidim arrive in Riga and cable Agudas Chabad
Summary: On 20 Elul 5699, the group of American students arrived safely in Riga from war-torn Poland and cabled Agudas Chabad in New York.
Story: After spending Shabbos in Warsaw with help from the Joint and the American consulate, the talmidim continued to Riga, where they sent a cable to Agudas Chabad in New York reading: 'Arrived safely Riga out of danger. Rabbi well Otwock.' The signatories were the three Hechts, Barnetzky, Levy, Kalodny, Gordon, Greenberg, Fisher, and Altein.
Tags: world war ii, riga, agudas chabad, achei tmimim, warsaw

Title: Rebbe Rayatz flees Otwock for Warsaw as war breaks out
Summary: On 20–21 Elul 5699 the Rebbe Rayatz left Otwock for Warsaw with his family and secretaries as German forces advanced.
Story: With the outbreak of World War II in Poland, on 20 or 21 Elul 5699 (around September 4, 1939) the Rebbe Rayatz evacuated Otwock together with his household and secretariat, traveling to Warsaw with the intent of continuing to Riga. Only manuscripts were taken; the entire library of roughly 120 crates and many household effects had to be left behind in Otwock. The party became trapped in the Warsaw siege for four months.
Tags: wwii, poland, otwock, warsaw, library, evacuation

Title: Rayatz leaves Otwock for Warsaw after the start of WWII
Summary: Four days after the German invasion of Poland, the Rayatz left Otwock for Warsaw.
Story: On 21 Elul, with German forces racing into Poland, the Rayatz relocated from Otwock to Warsaw. The move began the harrowing months of his rescue from Nazi-occupied Warsaw, eventually engineered through US diplomatic channels.
Tags: warsaw, otwock, poland, world war ii

Title: Rebbe Rayatz leaves Otwock as war engulfs Poland
Summary: On Tuesday 21 Elul 5699 at 3pm, the Rebbe Rayatz left Otwock weeping, blessing the crowd that gathered to bid farewell.
Story: As bombings intensified, the Rebbe departed Otwock for Warsaw with deep bitterness on his face. He blessed those gathered, telling them to accept the yoke of Heaven, and that God would protect them and the Rebbe wherever each would be. The original plan to reach Riga proved impossible; the family ended up at the Schmotkin apartment, Muranowska 32, Warsaw.
Tags: rayatz, otwock, warsaw, poland, wwii, flight

Title: Rebbe Rayatz travels from Otwock to Warsaw with family
Summary: On the Tuesday after war broke out, the Rebbe Rayatz moved from Otwock to Warsaw with his family and inner circle.
Story: After the German invasion, many bochurim had already fled toward Warsaw, hoping the capital would be safer from German bombardment. On Tuesday, 21 Elul, the Rebbe Rayatz himself followed with his family and close attendants, where they would remain under aerial bombardment for the next four months.
Tags: poland, warsaw, otwock, rayatz, wwii

Title: Rebbe Rayatz flees Schmotkin apartment as bombs fall
Summary: On Erev Rosh Hashanah 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz and family fled the Schmotkin apartment as German bombs set the building ablaze.
Story: Just before candle-lighting, a bomb struck the Schmotkin home and the building caught fire. Neighbors screamed and ran toward the gate, while chassidim surrounded the Rebbe to shield him. He sat on a chair murmuring with his lips while a chassid reviewed Mishnayos by heart, with the Rebbe correcting his errors. The family fled to another neighborhood for the High Holy Days.
Tags: warsaw, wwii, luftwaffe, schmotkin, fire

Title: Rosh HaShanah under German bombing in Warsaw
Summary: On the eve of Rosh HaShanah, German bombs destroyed Shmotkin's building where the Rebbe was staying, forcing the family to flee mid-day to a medical clinic.
Story: At 5 p.m. on 29 Elul, bombs struck the Muranowska Street building. Thrown across the courtyard by a blast, the Rebbe's family briefly feared a gas attack. With sunset approaching, a Jewish wagon driver risked arrest to transport them to 8 Gegrnitche Street. The Rebbe prayed Maariv without a minyan in barely a half hour, exhausted and unable to stand, yet reassuring everyone around him.
Tags: warsaw, poland, rosh hashanah, luftwaffe, shmotkin, rashag, high holidays

Title: Rabbi Jacobson arrives back in New York to launch the rescue campaign
Summary: After a harrowing roundabout journey via Hungary, Yugoslavia, Italy and France, Rabbi Jacobson reached New York and immediately began organizing efforts to save the Rebbe.
Story: Jacobson had missed his original passage on the Queen Mary and crossed the Atlantic in a converted swimming-pool locker aboard an overcrowded ship, leading Rosh HaShanah services on deck. Back in New York he enlisted attorney Samuel Kramer and called Asher Rabinowitz late at night, dispatching him to Washington to find a way to contact the Rebbe — refusing to let Shabbat or Yom Kippur deter the mission.
Tags: new york, united states, yisrael jacobson, sam kramer, rescue, agudas chassidei chabad

Title: Chaim Liberman flees Warsaw to Riga
Summary: The Rebbe's secretary R. Chaim Liberman fled from Warsaw to Riga on 8 Tishrei to organize rescue efforts.
Story: With the outbreak of WWII, the Frierdiker Rebbe's secretary R. Chaim Liberman escaped Warsaw and reached Riga on 8 Tishrei 5700. From Riga he conducted rescue advocacy for the Rebbe and his family, remaining there until they too were rescued. He later traveled with the Rebbe and his household to the United States.
Tags: warsaw, riga, war, wwii, escape, chaim liberman, secretary

Title: Librarian Chaim Lieberman escapes Warsaw to Riga
Summary: On 8 Tishrei 5700 the librarian Chaim Lieberman fled Warsaw for Riga, leaving behind his belongings and Rebbe's effects in his care.
Story: On 8 Tishrei 5700 (September 21, 1939), librarian R. Chaim Lieberman left Warsaw for Riga with only a summer coat. He later recounted that all his possessions remained behind, including manuscripts of the Rebbe Maharash he had hoped to organize and effects of the Rebbe Rayatz entrusted to him. A suitcase he tried to forward via Zalmanov demanded an exorbitant ransom and was abandoned.
Tags: chaim-lieberman, warsaw, riga, wwii, library, manuscripts

Title: Rabbi Chaim Lieberman flees Warsaw
Summary: Rabbi Chaim Lieberman (Rachal) left Warsaw on 8 Tishrei 5700, the same day the Frierdiker Rebbe's household began their escape from Nazi-occupied Poland.
Story: On 8 Tishrei 5700 (Sept 21, 1939), Rabbi Chaim Lieberman left Warsaw separately, having only about twenty minutes to prepare. The Frierdiker Rebbe's son-in-law Rashag had planned to join him but stayed behind because his wife and son refused to leave the Rebbe. Lieberman departed alone with nothing, while the rest of the family would remain in Warsaw until early Teves before traveling together to Riga.
Tags: warsaw, poland, wwii, escape, chaim lieberman, rayatz

Title: Rebbe returns to Shmotkin's apartment two days before Yom Kippur
Summary: On 8 Tishrei the Rebbe moved back to Shmotkin's apartment in Warsaw, where he led a small Yom Kippur service punctuated by thunderous explosions.
Story: As bombs continued falling, the Rebbe recited maftir Yonah with overflowing emotion. The closing service was hastened and the shofar sounded before nightfall to let worshippers leave before further bombing. After breaking the fast on soup, the Rebbe led the family in singing a chasidic melody while Warsaw was bombarded around them.
Tags: warsaw, poland, yom kippur, shmotkin, high holidays, luftwaffe

Title: Secretary Chaim Lieberman escapes Warsaw to Riga
Summary: On 8 Tishrei 5700, secretary Chaim Lieberman managed to escape Warsaw to Riga with only twenty minutes to prepare.
Story: Leaving 'naked and destitute,' Lieberman had no time to gather belongings. From Riga he began the intensive three-month effort to obtain exit permits and US entry visas for the Rebbe Rayatz and his family. The same day, the Rebbe and his family returned to their original Muranowska 32 apartment.
Tags: lieberman, warsaw, riga, wwii, rescue

Title: Senator Wagner appeals to Secretary of State Hull regarding the Rebbe's fate
Summary: New York Senator Robert Wagner wrote to Secretary of State Cordell Hull asking the State Department to locate Rabbi Joseph Isaac Schneersohn in Poland.
Story: On the eve of Yom Kippur, Wagner relayed appeals from leading New York Jews seeking the Rebbe's whereabouts. Days later, House Foreign Affairs chairman Sol Bloom replied that communication with Poland had been disrupted but the department would advise when contact was reestablished. The exchange marked the entry of US government channels into the rescue effort.
Tags: united states, washington, robert wagner, cordell hull, sol bloom, rescue, state department

Title: Heavy Luftwaffe bombing strikes Warsaw on 12 Tishrei
Summary: On 12 Tishrei 5700, intense aerial bombardment forced the Rebbe Rayatz and his family to take shelter in a basement.
Story: Telephone lines were cut and water mains broken across the city. The Rebbe descended with his family to a cellar, and on exiting fled from gate to gate. At one point a gate nearly collapsed on Rabbi Dovber Schneerson, who managed to brace it. Massive bombings continued on the eve of Sukkot.
Tags: warsaw, wwii, luftwaffe, bombing

Title: Polish army in Warsaw surrenders hours before Sukkot
Summary: On 14 Tishrei the Polish army in Warsaw surrendered to Germany just hours before the holiday of Sukkot began.
Story: Even as skirmishes continued around the city, the Rebbe insisted that a sukkah be built. The bewildered building manager complied, and late that night the Rebbe recited the traditional blessings in the sukkah, saying, 'Never once have I missed sitting in the sukkah, and I won't this year.'
Tags: warsaw, poland, sukkot, nazi germany, surrender, rashag

Title: Benjamin Cohen and Robert Pell strategize the Rebbe's rescue
Summary: Senior White House aide Benjamin Cohen pressed State Department European-affairs head Robert Pell to seek the Rebbe through German contacts.
Story: Cohen impressed on Pell the Rebbe's standing as 'one of the leading Jewish scholars of the world' and suggested approaching Helmuth Wohlthat, a German diplomat Pell had befriended at the 1938 Evian Conference. The same day Pell telegrammed US consul Raymond Geist in Berlin, asking him to discreetly enlist Wohlthat in arranging safe passage for the Rebbe to Riga.
Tags: washington, united states, benjamin cohen, robert pell, helmuth wohlthat, state department, raymond geist, rescue

Title: Zerach Gordon and Hecht couple arrive in Stockholm en route to New York
Summary: On 19 Tishrei 5700, Zerach Gordon and Rabbi Shlomo Zalman Hecht and his wife arrived in Stockholm after a 36-hour sea voyage from Riga.
Story: After a difficult ship journey, the small group reached Stockholm on the second day of Chol HaMoed Sukkos. From there they planned to continue to New York, separate from the remaining seven talmidim who left Riga later. In Stockholm they were assisted by Rabbi Yisrael Zuber, who arranged food, lodging, and a place to learn in the synagogue.
Tags: zerach gordon, shlomo zalman hecht, stockholm, riga, achei tmimim

Title: Pell briefs US ambassador in Berlin on rescue priority
Summary: State Department representative Robert Pell informed the US ambassador in Berlin of the importance of rescuing the Rebbe Rayatz.
Story: On October 3, 1939 (20 Tishrei), Pell formally communicated the priority of the rescue mission to the US embassy in Berlin. This initiated months of US-German diplomatic coordination that would ultimately enable the Rebbe's extraction from Warsaw.
Tags: state-department, pell, berlin, rescue, diplomacy, usa

Title: Hitler enters occupied Warsaw
Summary: Just over a month after invading Poland, Hitler arrived in Warsaw and was welcomed by a massive Nazi military parade down the capital's main avenues.
Story: Thousands of German soldiers strutted through Warsaw as Hitler reviewed his conquest of Poland. The display dramatized the new occupation order under which the Rebbe was hiding, while Polish Jews — initially comparing it to Germany's relatively benevolent World War I occupation — soon discovered the true face of Nazi anti-Semitism.
Tags: warsaw, poland, nazi germany, adolf hitler, occupation

Title: Future Rebbe submits family birth records for US visas
Summary: On 28 Tishrei 5700, the future Rebbe wrote from Paris to Israel Jacobson with family birth dates and places to facilitate American visa applications.
Story: Writing in French to Rabbi Israel Jacobson in New York, the future Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson provided personal details to assist with US visa procurement: Chaya Mushka Schneersohn (b. Aug 13, 1901, Smolensk) and Menachem Mendel Schneersohn (b. Mar 1, 1895, Nikolaev, to Levik and Chana). The application was meant to bring the future Rebbe and Rebbetzin together with the Frierdiker Rebbe's family to America.
Tags: paris, visas, usa, israel jacobson, ramash, chaya mushka

Title: Benjamin Cohen advises Pell on locating the Rebbe
Summary: On October 26, 1939, advisor Benjamin Cohen informed Robert Pell, on attorney Asher Rabinowitz's behalf, how to locate the hidden Rebbe.
Story: Because callers seeking the Rebbe Rayatz at Rabbi Tzvi Gurary's home had been turned away by frightened residents, US officials needed help finding him. Cohen's guidance to Pell helped advance the search and eventual rescue effort.
Tags: cohen, pell, rabinowitz, state-department, rescue

Title: Lieberman appeals to American Aguda to rescue the Otwock library
Summary: From Riga between Yom Kippur and Sukkot 5700, Lieberman wrote to Jacobson detailing the library's abandonment in Otwock and urging American intervention.
Story: Immediately upon reaching Riga, librarian Chaim Lieberman wrote to Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson of Agudath Chassidei Chabad in America. He reported that when they fled Otwock for Warsaw only the manuscripts were taken; the entire library — valued at perhaps thirty thousand zloty — and many household effects remained in Otwock. He warned that with Otwock falling under foreign control all could be lost, urging strong efforts to obtain export permission though prioritizing rescue of lives.
Tags: chaim-lieberman, yisrael-jacobson, library, otwock, wwii, rescue

Title: American talmidim return to New York from Stockholm
Summary: On 22 Cheshvan 5700, the remaining seven American talmidim arrived back in New York after some weeks in Stockholm.
Story: Following Zerach Gordon and the Hechts, the rest of the group sailed from Stockholm to America. They reached New York on 22 Cheshvan 5700, ending their abbreviated study mission in Europe.
Tags: new york, stockholm, achei tmimim, world war ii

Title: Haaretz reports the Rebbe has perished
Summary: The Israeli newspaper Haaretz, relaying a dispatch from London, reported that the Rebbe had died in war-torn Warsaw.
Story: With the Rebbe's whereabouts unknown to Chasidim worldwide, false reports of his death circulated in the press. Two days later Haaretz relayed a Vilna dispatch saying he was alive, and on November 16 reported that Tel Aviv Chasidim had received a telegram from Rabbi Chaim Ozer Grodzinski confirming the Rebbe was alive in Warsaw.
Tags: haaretz, tel aviv, london, press, false report, rescue

Title: Lieberman reports Rebbe's hiding address to Jacobson
Summary: On 4 Kislev 5700, Lieberman informed Jacobson that the Rebbe was hiding at Bonifratrska 29 — the home of Yechiel Tzvi Gurary.
Story: By November 16, the rescue effort needed a precise address to proceed. Lieberman confirmed the Rebbe's hiding place so the diplomatic and military extraction plan could be set in motion.
Tags: lieberman, jacobson, warsaw, gurary, rescue

Title: Lieberman cables the Rebbe's Warsaw address from Riga
Summary: Rabbi Chaim Lieberman cabled Jacobson from Riga with the message 'Rabbi healthy, situation gross, awfully dangerous,' supplying the address Bonifraterska 29.
Story: Lieberman, having escaped Warsaw to Riga, transmitted the Rebbe's location and pleaded for accelerated immigration. Asher Rabinowitz wired Justice Brandeis with the address, who passed it to Cohen in the White House, then to Geist in Berlin, and finally to Lt. Col. Ernst Bloch leading the search in Warsaw.
Tags: riga, latvia, warsaw, chaim lieberman, yisrael jacobson, louis brandeis, rescue, bonifraterska

Title: About 20 Otwock students reach Vilna on foot
Summary: By 10 Kislev, secretary R. Chaim Lieberman reported from Riga that some twenty Otwock bochurim had walked to Vilna.
Story: After the Ribbentrop-Molotov partition of Poland, Tomchei Tmimim students began making their way north on foot across two borders to reach Vilna, which had just been transferred from Soviet to Lithuanian control. Writing from Riga to R. Yisroel Jacobson on 10 Kislev 5700, R. Chaim Lieberman reported that some twenty bochurim had already arrived in Vilna.
Tags: vilna, lithuania, otwock, tomchei-tmimim, wwii, border-crossing, rescue

Title: German military unit locates the Rebbe and delivers exit visas
Summary: Lt. Col. Ernst Bloch and his Abwehr unit forced their way into the Gurary apartment where the Rebbe was hiding and announced they had come to save him.
Story: After weeks of searching ruined Warsaw, Bloch's soldiers — several of Jewish background — entered the apartment as the Rebbe's grandson Berke and others braced for execution. Instead, the soldiers handed out exit visas and travel papers. The mission had been authorized at the highest levels of the Abwehr under Admiral Wilhelm Canaris, working through Helmuth Wohlthat in Goering's office.
Tags: warsaw, poland, ernst bloch, abwehr, wilhelm canaris, rescue, nazi germany, berke gurary

Title: Kirk informs Pell that rescue is feasible
Summary: On November 25, 1939, US embassy official Alexander Kirk in Berlin notified Pell that the Rebbe had been located and could be extracted around December 1.
Story: Kirk reported that the German army would assign an officer to travel with the Rebbe and his entourage and ensure the journey. Although the December 1 date slipped, this set the framework for the extraction.
Tags: kirk, pell, berlin, wehrmacht, rescue, diplomacy

Title: Rebbe transfers yeshiva sections from Poland to Lithuania
Summary: The Frierdiker Rebbe wrote on 14 Kislev 5700 that he had succeeded, with great effort, in moving part of the yeshiva's Polish branches to Lithuania.
Story: In a letter dated 14 Kislev 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe reported that with great toil and expense he had transferred to Lithuania part of the Tomchei Temimim sections from Warsaw, Lodz, Kaloszyn, Chelm and elsewhere. This move was part of the Chabad effort to preserve the yeshiva network as the Nazi occupation of Poland tightened.
Tags: wwii, lithuania, warsaw, lodz, kaloszyn, chelm, tomchei-temimim, relocation

Title: Pell confirms to Rhoade that the Rebbe has been found alive
Summary: Robert Pell informed attorney Max Rhoade that German soldiers had located the Rebbe alive in Warsaw and placed him under the protection of a staff officer.
Story: A cable from the US Embassy in Berlin confirmed: 'He has been ill and is recovering' and that a German officer 'has been assigned to look after him.' Rhoade relayed the news to Sam Kramer and the American Chasidim, who rejoiced — though the road to safety remained long, dangerous, and dependent on still-elusive US visas.
Tags: washington, united states, robert pell, max rhoade, sam kramer, state department, rescue

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes coded letter from besieged Warsaw
Summary: By 15 Kislev 5700 Lieberman had received the Rebbe's first letter from Warsaw, written in German to evade censors and signaling the Aguda to reclaim its library.
Story: In a letter dated 15 Kislev 5700 (around November 27, 1939), Chaim Lieberman quoted the Rebbe Rayatz's first dispatch from besieged Warsaw. Because of heavy censorship the Rebbe wrote in German and in hints, stating he had no apartment and was crowded with his family at a friend's place with no room for the books Agudath Chabad had lent him for study — and would gladly see Agudath Chabad take them back, signaling the American organization to formally petition for the library's return.
Tags: warsaw, wwii, library, agudath-chassidei-chabad, censorship, rescue

Title: Rebbe Rayatz instructs Warsaw students to escape to Vilna
Summary: In early Kislev the Rebbe Rayatz directed Tomchei Tmimim students in Warsaw to smuggle across two borders to Vilna and re-establish the yeshiva there.
Story: After the Soviets handed Vilna over to independent Lithuania, the Rebbe Rayatz saw an opening to save his yeshiva. In mid-Kislev he received bochurim including R. Avraham Yitzchak Garfinkel for yechidus, blessed their escape, and pledged the funds needed to cross the German-Soviet and Soviet-Lithuanian borders. R. Shmaryahu Gourary handed each escapee 100-150 zlotys for travel and bribes.
Tags: poland, warsaw, vilna, tomchei-tmimim, rayatz, wwii, rescue, border-crossing

Title: Reitchik departs Warsaw after parting blessing from the Rebbe
Summary: On the night of 18 Kislev R. Shmuel Dovid Reitchik received the Rebbe's parting blessing and set out from Warsaw for Vilna.
Story: R. Shmuel Dovid Reitchik later wrote a detailed report of his escape route. After parting blessings from the Rebbe Rayatz on the night of 18 Kislev, his group farbrenged on 19 Kislev in Praga, then traveled to Siedlce. After many obstacles they crossed the German-Soviet border on the night of 26 Kislev and reached Slonim by 29 Kislev.
Tags: warsaw, vilna, reitchik, tomchei-tmimim, border-crossing, wwii

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe's family arrives in Riga
Summary: In early Teves 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe's remaining family departed Warsaw together and reached Riga, Latvia, en route to the United States.
Story: After remaining in Warsaw through the early months of the German occupation, the Frierdiker Rebbe, his family, and son-in-law Rashag traveled together to Riga at the start of Teves 5700 (December 1939). From Riga they would continue to the United States, while the future Rebbe and Rebbetzin remained behind in Paris awaiting their own visas.
Tags: warsaw, riga, latvia, wwii, escape, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz rescued from Warsaw to Riga
Summary: On 2 Tevet 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz was rescued from Nazi-occupied Warsaw and arrived in Riga.
Story: Having been trapped in Warsaw at the outbreak of World War II, the Rebbe Rayatz was extracted to Riga on 2 Tevet 5700. Once safe in Latvia he immediately turned to organizing the rescue of his Tomchei Tmimim students from Vilna to the United States, opening the long campaign that occupies this chapter.
Tags: riga, warsaw, world war ii, rescue, latvia, poland

Title: Max Rhoade updates Kramer on Berlin rescue plan
Summary: Attorney Max Rhoade informed attorney Sam Kramer that Berlin had prepared a rescue plan, redirecting from Sweden to Riga.
Story: Rhoade told Kramer the German authorities had a plan to evacuate the Rebbe to Sweden but preferred Latvia (Riga). He expected this to occur within two to three days — which is precisely what happened.
Tags: rhoade, kramer, berlin, rescue, latvia

Title: Rayatz departs Warsaw after rescue from the Nazi army
Summary: The Rayatz was rescued from Nazi-occupied Warsaw on 21 Kislev, departing for Riga.
Story: An extraordinary multinational rescue effort, including high-level US diplomatic intervention, extracted the Rayatz from Warsaw. He left the besieged city on December 14, en route to Latvia and ultimately America.
Tags: warsaw, poland, rescue, world war ii, nazi germany

Title: Rebbe and family depart Warsaw for Berlin on the last day of Chanukah
Summary: Escorted by Lt. Col. Bloch and Abwehr soldiers, the Rebbe and his entourage left occupied Warsaw by truck and wagon for a peripheral train station to Berlin.
Story: The central station had been bombed, so Bloch arranged transport to the city's outskirts. German soldiers along the route challenged the obvious group of religious Jews, and at one checkpoint rifles were aimed at the Rebbe; Bloch invoked the authority of Admiral Canaris and threatened arrest if they interfered. After a full-day journey, the group reached Berlin, staying at the Jewish Community Center and then a hotel for Shabbat.
Tags: warsaw, berlin, chanukah, ernst bloch, abwehr, nazi germany, escape, rescue

Title: Rebbe Rayatz extracted from Warsaw to Berlin
Summary: On Thursday 2 Tevet 5700, German Abwehr officers extracted the Rebbe Rayatz and his family from Warsaw to Berlin by train.
Story: Following coordination by German military intelligence chief Wilhelm Canaris, half-Jewish officer Ernst Bloch and Klaus Schenk escorted the family from the Gurary home in Warsaw to the train station. Despite hostile German soldiers en route, the escort ensured safe passage. They arrived in Berlin that evening and lodged at the Jewish community building.
Tags: rescue, warsaw, berlin, canaris, abwehr, bloch, schenk, wwii

Title: Open letter 'To Our Brethren of Israel' appeals for Polish Jewry via the Joint
Summary: On the day of his arrival in Riga, the Rebbe published a general letter (Igros V:1132*) calling for a worldwide collection for starving Polish Jewry, with funds to be channeled through the Joint in Warsaw.
Story: The Rebbe described soup kitchens, hospitals, old-age homes and orphanages running on Joint funding inside Warsaw, and asked Jews of every party affiliation to contribute. A parallel circular addressed to anash and Tomchei Tmimim students worldwide called the health and economic situation 'terrifying' and demanded rapid practical help.
Tags: joint distribution committee, poland, warsaw, relief, fundraising, world war ii

Title: Rebbe arrives safely in Riga after escape from Nazi Europe
Summary: On 5 Tevet the Rebbe reached Riga from Berlin via Lithuania, greeted by ecstatic crowds; that night a telegram 'The Rebbe is free' reached New York.
Story: The Rebbe was met by chasidic crowds at Vilnius and Kovno stations, where Eliyahu Vad of Dos Vort interviewed him about the state of the Jewish nation. At the Latvian border Bloch's escort departed. In New York Rabbi Jacobson did handsprings on the sidewalk in joy and hosted a farbrengen, then placed a transatlantic call to thank the Rebbe the next day.
Tags: riga, latvia, kovno, vilnius, dos vort, yisrael jacobson, rescue, new york

Title: Rebbe issues twin encyclicals on Polish Jewry's plight from Riga
Summary: Within hours of arriving in Riga the Rebbe composed two letters — one to world Jewry and one to Chabad Chasidim — describing the devastation in Warsaw and demanding relief.
Story: Writing on 5 Tevet, the Rebbe described Jews 'burned alive' and homes turned to graves, urged worldwide fundraising channeled through the JDC 'irrespective of political party or personal philosophy,' and called on Chabad communities globally to treat aid to Polish Chasidim as 'saving lives and redeeming captives.'
Tags: riga, poland, joint distribution committee, fundraising, letter, relief, chabad worldwide

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Riga after escaping Warsaw
Summary: On 5 Tevet 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Riga after escaping Nazi-occupied Warsaw.
Story: Following his dramatic rescue from Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz reached Riga on 5 Tevet 5700. From there he immediately began encouraging the Tomchei Tmimim students who had also fled to Vilna, urging them to maintain their studies. His arrival in Riga marked the start of a transitional period before his eventual emigration to the United States.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, riga, warsaw, wwii, escape

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Riga from Berlin
Summary: On Sunday 5 Tevet 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz and his family reached Riga after a Shabbat stopover in Berlin.
Story: After spending Shabbat at a Berlin hotel arranged through the Latvian consulate, the family traveled onward and arrived in Riga on Sunday evening. The Rebbe immediately wrote a general letter to chassidim announcing his safe arrival, and would remain in Riga for nearly three months.
Tags: riga, latvia, berlin, rescue, wwii

Title: Rebbe Rayatz reaches Riga from besieged Warsaw
Summary: After four months under siege, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Riga on 5 Teves 5700 following a major American rescue operation.
Story: Trapped in besieged Warsaw for four months, the Rebbe Rayatz, his family, and his secretaries were finally permitted to leave following an enormous rescue effort mounted by Agudath Chassidei Chabad in America. On 5 Teves 5700 (December 17, 1939) they reached Riga, where they would remain about two and a half months while preparations were made for the journey to the United States.
Tags: riga, latvia, warsaw, wwii, rescue, agudath-chassidei-chabad

Title: Rebbe Rayatz rescued from Warsaw to Riga
Summary: On 5 Tevet the Rebbe Rayatz escaped war-torn Warsaw and reached Riga, after four months under German aerial bombardment.
Story: After four months in Warsaw under relentless German bombing, an elaborate international rescue effort brought the Rebbe Rayatz, his family, and close attendants safely to Riga on 5 Tevet 5700. From Riga he immediately turned to mobilizing American Chabad and the Joint Distribution Committee to fund the evacuation of his remaining students.
Tags: warsaw, riga, latvia, rayatz, wwii, rescue

Title: Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak arrives in Riga after escaping Warsaw siege
Summary: On 5 Tevet 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe reached Riga immediately after the Nazi siege of Warsaw and at once began organizing aid for the chassidim left behind in occupied Poland.
Story: Having been smuggled out of war-torn Warsaw, the Rebbe arrived in Riga on Sunday, 5 Tevet, and made relief for Polish Jewry his very first order of business. That same day he issued public appeals — one to general Jewry and one to anash worldwide — describing the catastrophic conditions and urging immediate fundraising through the Joint Distribution Committee. The arrival marked the start of a half-year base in Riga from which he would coordinate aid before sailing to America.
Tags: riga, warsaw, rescue, world war ii, latvia, poland, yosef yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Rayatz arrives in Riga after escape from Warsaw
Summary: Following his escape from Warsaw, the Rayatz arrived in Riga on Sunday, December 18 (25 Kislev).
Story: Latvia provided a way station while plans were finalized for the next leg of his journey. He would remain in Riga for several months before continuing to Sweden and onward to America.
Tags: riga, latvia, warsaw, rescue

Title: R. Yitzchak Dov Oshpal smuggled across border into Vilna
Summary: At 4 a.m. on 7 Tevet, the head of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim branch crossed from Soviet-held Kornitz into Lithuania.
Story: R. Yitzchak Dov Oshpal, head of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim branch, had fled to his home in Kornitz when war erupted. In Tevet 5700, his student Yosef Kaminetsky came as a special emissary from Vilna with funds and a US visa held for him by R. Chaim Ozer Grodzenski. At 4 a.m. on 7 Tevet, after enormous danger, Oshpal crossed the border into Lithuania, noting the event in his Mishnayos.
Tags: vilna, lithuania, kornitz, oshpal, tomchei-tmimim, border-crossing, rescue

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes son-in-law of survival of manuscripts and library
Summary: On 8 Teves 5700 the Rebbe wrote his son-in-law in France that the manuscripts and library were intact, and inquired about photographic copies.
Story: On 8 Teves 5700 (December 20, 1939), shortly after reaching Riga, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his son-in-law (the future Rebbe), then in France, reporting that thank God the manuscripts had been preserved and so had the library. Uncertain whether they could yet be extracted from Otwock, he asked for a detailed list of which kisvei kodesh his son-in-law had photographed in prior years, including the small notebooks, letters, and the maamar 'Toldot HaChozrim' he feared had been burned.
Tags: library, manuscripts, ramash, riga, photographs, wwii

Title: Letter to Israel Jacobson urging rescue of 50 students
Summary: On 14 Tevet 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Israel Jacobson, head of Agudas Chabad in America, urging immediate effort to bring fifty Tomchei Tmimim students to the United States.
Story: The Rebbe stressed that the matter touched the inner foundation of the yeshiva's future in America and asked that everything possible be done with speed. The letter (Igros vol. 5, no. 1133) opened a sustained correspondence with American Chabad activists about routes, visas and funding for the trapped Vilna students.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, vilna, usa, israel jacobson, agudas chabad, rescue

Title: R. Reitchik visits Globoke amid 1939 flight
Summary: Reporting on the eve of 14 Teves 5700, R. Shmuel Dovid Reitchik described how Mandelbaum wanted to flee Globoke for Vilna but felt bound to his community.
Story: In Motzaei Shabbos Parshas Ki Sisa 5700, while Tomchei Tmimim students were fleeing Poland for Vilna, R. Shmuel Dovid Reitchik wrote to the Rebbe that he had traveled to Globoke on the eve of 14 Teves. He found Mandelbaum torn: he too wished to escape to Vilna but felt unable to abandon the town as its appointed rabbi.
Tags: reitchik, mandelbaum, globoke, vilna, tomchei-tmimim-flight, wwii

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe transfers branches to Lithuania on 14 Tevet 5700
Summary: In a letter of 14 Tevet 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe described relocating parts of the yeshiva from Otwock and Polish branches to Lithuania.
Story: The letter (Vol. 5, no. 1136) recounted great effort and expense to evacuate portions of the central yeshiva in Otwock and the branches in Warsaw, Lodz, Kaluszyn and Chelm to Lithuania. A large portion of students nonetheless remained trapped in Poland after the German invasion.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, wwii, lithuania, vilna, warsaw, lodz, kaluszyn, chelm, rescue

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes returned talmidim from Riga after escaping besieged Warsaw
Summary: On 14 Teves 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the American talmidim from Riga after his escape from the siege of Warsaw.
Story: The Rebbe described how during the siege he had worried about them, repeatedly asking the American consul in Warsaw for news. Only on reaching Riga did he learn that they had returned safely home, and he thanked God 'for His kindness endures forever.'
Tags: riga, warsaw, iggros kodesh, world war ii, achei tmimim

Title: Rebbe writes from Riga seeking funds for student evacuation
Summary: On 14 Tevet the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Yisroel Jacobson and to Dr. Leo Jung requesting urgent funds to evacuate remaining students from Poland to Lithuania.
Story: Once safe in Riga, the Rebbe Rayatz immediately mobilized international Chabad and the Joint. In letters of 14 Tevet he reported having moved part of the central yeshiva from Otwock and branches from Warsaw, Lodz, Kaluszyn and Chelm to Lithuania, and pleaded for $4,000 from the Joint to rescue the remainder still in mortal danger in Poland.
Tags: riga, joint-distribution-committee, rescue, tomchei-tmimim, rayatz, fundraising

Title: Anonymous donor begins funding Achei Tmimim children's class
Summary: An anonymous monthly donor was secured for Yeshivat Achei Tmimim in Tel Aviv at the start of 5701.
Story: The funds enabled hiring R. Refael Nachman HaKohen to teach the small children ages 6-9; the yeshiva then had about 25 students. The anonymous donor, revealed later, was Baruch Eliyahu Schneersohn, son of the holy R. Mendel of Babruysk, a truly God-fearing man and great philanthropist. He insisted his identity remain unpublicized.
Tags: tel aviv, yeshiva achei tmimim, baruch eliyahu schneersohn, donor

Title: Chabad purchases 770 Eastern Parkway as movement headquarters
Summary: At the end of summer 5700, Chabad purchased the building at 770 Eastern Parkway as its central headquarters.
Story: At the end of summer 5700, the Chabad movement purchased the building at 770 Eastern Parkway in Brooklyn. From that point on, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky was responsible for managing the building. He later led the expansion construction of the enlarged main synagogue in 5719-5720, built on what had previously been the courtyard.
Tags: 770, eastern-parkway, brooklyn, rayatz, kazarnovsky

Title: Eber reports cold rejection on travel
Summary: In Tevet 5701, R. Yehuda Eber wrote to the Rebbe that the Soviet official had coldly told him no decision was yet made.
Story: In Tevet 5701, R. Yehuda Eber wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe that nothing had changed regarding their travel. He had visited the relevant official, who responded coldly that no decision had been made and they would be notified when one was, telling him not to come asking.
Tags: riga, soviet union, rescue, yehuda eber

Title: Eber's family receives bureaucratic setbacks in Cheshvan
Summary: In Marcheshvan 5701, R. Yehuda Eber wrote that the prior arrangements were nullified and they had to file fresh autobiographies with the Soviets.
Story: In Marcheshvan 5701, R. Yehuda Eber wrote that the early Russian envoy's communication had been mistaken; the Russian connection was now entirely voided. They had to file fresh passport applications with detailed autobiographies covering themselves, siblings, and parents from birth. Acceptance of applications had only just begun the previous week.
Tags: riga, soviet union, passports, yehuda eber, rescue

Title: Feigin and Eber appeal for Petsamo route via Rashag
Summary: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5700, Feigin and Eber wrote to the Rashag asking him to pressure Finland to permit the Petsamo route.
Story: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5700, with the Italian route closed, R. Yechezkel Feigin and R. Yehuda Eber wrote a joint letter to the Rashag describing their plight. They had been ready to travel five times already, all foiled. The only remaining option was via Petsamo in Finland, but Finland had refused entry permits; they urged the Rashag to leverage US senators or the Finnish consul to intercede.
Tags: riga, finland, petsamo, rescue, yechezkel feigin, yehuda eber, rashag

Title: Feigin briefs Rebbe on stalled rescue while at sea
Summary: On 1 Adar Sheni 5700, R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to the Rebbe — then at sea — explaining HIAS funding confusion delaying his departure.
Story: On Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni 5700, with the Rebbe aboard ship bound for America, R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote detailing the obstacles to his family's travel. HIAS New York would not raise the $1,200 ceiling, and confusion arose over whether the Joint had given monetary aid or only endorsement, delaying the matter further.
Tags: riga, rescue, hias, joint, yechezkel feigin

Title: Feigin reports HIAS will cover only 50%
Summary: On Ta'anit Esther 5700, Feigin wrote that HIAS had agreed to cover only about fifty percent of his travel costs.
Story: On Ta'anit Esther 5700, R. Yechezkel Feigin reported that Rosenbaum had received a telegram indicating HIAS would participate only at about 50% of the travel costs. With time running short, he was still uncertain how matters would resolve, and Rosenbaum was pushing him toward the April 13 Swedish ship despite the Pesach problem.
Tags: riga, rescue, hias, yechezkel feigin, ta'anit esther

Title: Feigin reports rescue logistics struggles in Riga
Summary: On 12 Adar Rishon 5700, R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote that his travel from Riga was still uncertain pending HIAS funding.
Story: On 12 Adar Rishon 5700, the secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to his brother-in-law R. Shalom Posner that his travel arrangements were stalled while he sought funding sources. He was in discussion with HIAS and hoped a solution would soon emerge, noting the Rebbe was planning to depart Riga around March 4.
Tags: riga, rescue, hias, yechezkel feigin, secretary

Title: Feigin submits Soviet exit application
Summary: On 9 Marcheshvan 5701, R. Mordechai Chefetz reported that R. Y. Eber had submitted his application and would await an answer in about two months.
Story: On 9 Marcheshvan 5701, R. Mordechai Chefetz wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe that R. Yehuda Eber had already submitted his application and was told to expect a response in about two months. R. Yechezkel Feigin had not yet submitted his.
Tags: riga, soviet union, passports, yechezkel feigin, yehuda eber, rescue

Title: Feigin weighs Norwegian vs Swedish ship options
Summary: On 3 Adar Sheni 5700, Feigin wrote that he was pursuing Norwegian and Swedish transit visas for an April 5 sailing from Bergen.
Story: On 3 Adar Sheni 5700, Feigin wrote again about logistics. A Norwegian ship would sail from Bergen April 5–8, while a Swedish ship would depart Gothenburg April 13. The Swedish option would mean spending the start of Pesach aboard ship, which he hoped to avoid, especially given his wife's frail health.
Tags: riga, bergen, norway, sweden, passover, rescue, yechezkel feigin

Title: Feigin writes of voided permits and new passport requirement
Summary: In Tishrei 5701, Feigin wrote that they had been told to reapply for Soviet passports, with a two-month wait for Moscow's reply.
Story: In Tishrei 5701, R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe that they had been instructed to submit fresh applications for Soviet passports, with a two-month wait for a Moscow decision. The American consul meanwhile would not renew expired visas without new authorizations from the US, including a new affidavit for their son Shmuel Leib.
Tags: riga, soviet union, passports, visas, yechezkel feigin, rescue

Title: Founding of 'Achei Temimim' youth division in New York
Summary: In the winter of 5701 the Rebbe Rayatz founded the Achei Temimim youth division of Tomchei Tmimim in New York, appointing R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie to head it.
Story: In the winter of 5701 (1940–41) the Rebbe Rayatz established Achei Temimim, the youth division of Tomchei Tmimim, in New York. He appointed R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie — newly settled in New York through his marriage into the Kopytznitz family — to head the new division. The story is recounted in Toldot Chabad in the United States, p. 180 onward.
Tags: new-york, united-states, achei-temimim, tomchei-tmimim, shneur-zalman-gurarie, rebbe-rayatz

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe departs Riga for America
Summary: On 24 Adar Rishon 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe left Riga on his journey to America.
