Story: On 24 Adar Rishon 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe departed Riga on his journey to the United States. R. Yechezkel Feigin and his family remained behind in Riga, with HIAS funding for their tickets still unresolved.
Tags: riga, usa, rescue, frierdiker rebbe, travel

Title: Funds wired for rabbis' Pacific crossing
Summary: On 21 Elul 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe acknowledged a $500 check from R. Yaakov Katz of Chicago used to fund rabbis' travel.
Story: On 21 Elul 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to R. Yaakov Katz of Chicago confirming receipt of his $500 check and that arrangements for the two rabbis' travel had been made. A telegram had already confirmed they had set out on their journey.
Tags: chicago, rescue, finance, yaakov katz, shliach

Title: Italian route blocked for Riga refugees
Summary: On 18 Iyar 5700, Chefetz reported the Italian sea route had been cut off, stranding the rescuees in Riga.
Story: On 18 Iyar 5700, R. Mordechai Chefetz wrote that those preparing to travel were ready to leave, but the Italian route had now been suspended with no ship departing. R. Feigin and R. Eber and their families therefore remained stranded in Riga.
Tags: riga, italy, rescue, yehuda eber, yechezkel feigin

Title: Last pre-war European Haggadah printed in Munkacs
Summary: The Tov Devarcha Haggadah by Rabbi Shaul Brach was among the last Haggadot printed in Europe before WWII, in Munkacs in 5700.
Story: In 5700 (1940), Rabbi Shaul Brach's son Shmuel published his father's Haggadah Tov Devarcha at the Grafia press in Munkacs. With the war engulfing Europe, it became one of the last Haggadot printed there before printing in Europe ground to a halt.
Tags: haggadah, munkacs, hungary, world-war-ii

Title: Levitin becomes chief mashpia of Tomchei Tmimim NY
Summary: From 5700 onward, R. Shmuel Levitin served as the head mashpia at Tomchei Tmimim in New York.
Story: Once the Rebbe Rayatz secured Levitin's right to remain in America, he was installed as the chief mashpia at the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in New York, a role he held for decades until his passing.
Tags: levitin, tomchei-tmimim, new-york, mashpia

Title: Livenhof and Dankera merge and relocate to Riga in 5701
Summary: At the start of 5701, the Tomchei Tmimim branches in Livenhof and Dankera merged and moved to Riga.
Story: As the war engulfed Eastern Europe and Latvia fell under Soviet control, the two Latvian branches consolidated in Riga. This merger marked the end of the dispersed pre-war Tomchei Tmimim network in the Baltic region.
Tags: latvia, livenhof, dankera, riga, wwii, tomchei tmimim

Title: Maamar written in the Rebbe Rayatz's handwriting in 5700
Summary: A chassidic discourse written in the Rebbe Rayatz's own handwriting dates to the year 5700 (1940).
Story: Among the exhibition holdings is a maamar in the Rebbe Rayatz's hand from 5700, the year of his escape from Nazi-occupied Europe and arrival in the United States.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, maamar, manuscript

Title: Marriage of R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie in New York
Summary: In the winter of 5700 R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie married the daughter of the Admur of Kopytznitz, R' Avraham Yehoshua Heschel, in New York.
Story: In the winter of 5700 (1939–40) R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie was married in New York to the daughter of the Admur of Kopytznitz, R' Avraham Yehoshua Heschel. The wedding took place against the backdrop of the European war, with much of the Chabad world already in flight. His position in New York would soon allow him to assist the Rebbe Rayatz in establishing new institutions in America.
Tags: new-york, shneur-zalman-gurarie, kopytznitz, morgenstern, wedding

Title: Publication of first volume of Tzofnat Paneach responsa
Summary: The first volume of the Rogatchover's responsa 'Tzofnat Paneach' was published in 5700.
Story: After Rebbetzin Rachel Tzitran, the Rogatchover's daughter, came from the Land of Israel to Dvinsk, she began handling the publication of her father's writings. In 5700 (1940) the first volume, Responsa Tzofnat Paneach, was finally issued.
Tags: rogatchover, tzofnat paneach, tzitran

Title: R. Sholom Noach Berzovsky appointed RaM at Achei Tmimim Tel Aviv
Summary: Rabbi Sholom Noach Berzovsky—later the Slonimer Rebbe—was appointed RaM for the older class at Achei Tmimim in Tel Aviv during 5700.
Story: When external funding nearly collapsed and the yeshiva nonetheless flourished with growing enrollment, the administration restructured staff. R. Shaul Bruk was named mashpia in addition to his roles as RaM and supervisor, while R. Berzovsky was newly appointed for the senior class. R. Nissan Eber remained with the younger class, allowing the yeshiva to continue functioning that year.
Tags: tel aviv, yeshiva achei tmimim, sholom noach berzovsky, slonim

Title: R. Yehuda Eber arrives in Riga from Warsaw
Summary: On Friday before Purim Sheni 5700, Rosh Yeshiva R. Yehuda Eber arrived safely in Riga from Warsaw.
Story: Rosh Yeshiva R. Yehuda Eber had failed to depart with the Rebbe in early Tevet. On 12 Adar Sheni 5700, R. Mordechai Chefetz reported he would arrive that Tuesday from Warsaw. On 21 Adar Sheni, Feigin confirmed Eber's safe arrival in Riga the previous Erev Shabbat.
Tags: riga, warsaw, rescue, yehuda eber, rosh yeshiva

Title: Rashag appeals for rescue funds from Chicago
Summary: On 27 Elul 5700, the Rashag wrote to R. Shalom Posner in Chicago seeking $1,000 in pidyon shvuyim funds to bring two families to America.
Story: On 27 Elul 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe's son-in-law the Rashag wrote to R. Shalom Posner, the shliach in Chicago. He reported that R. Yitzchak Dov Ushpal had already departed Japan for the US on June 26, while the Zalmanov and Rotstein families had reached Vladivostok needing funds and ship tickets for the next leg.
Tags: chicago, rescue, finance, vladivostok, japan, shliach, rashag

Title: Rebbe announces Eber's arrival in Riga to Chicago
Summary: On 3 Nissan 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe informed Agudas Chabad in Chicago that Rosh Yeshiva R. Yehuda Eber had reached Riga.
Story: On 3 Nissan 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to Agudas Chabad in Chicago that a telegram had arrived from the chief Rosh Yeshiva R. Yehuda Eber confirming his safe arrival in Riga. This was part of efforts to coordinate continued rescue funding from America.
Tags: chicago, agudas chabad, yehuda eber, rosh yeshiva, riga

Title: Rebbe escapes German-occupied Poland to New York via Riga
Summary: The outbreak of World War II compels the Rebbe to escape to New York, ending his European wanderings.
Story: After escaping German-occupied Poland, the Rebbe made few public appearances during a short second stay in Riga before departing to the US. One of these was a rare public talk to Achot Hatemimim. The wandering ended in New York, where the Rebbe established Chabad's permanent base at 770 Eastern Parkway.
Tags: holocaust, world war ii, new york, 770, poland, riga

Title: Rebbe escapes Nazi-occupied Poland and arrives in New York
Summary: After a brief second stay in Riga, the Rebbe escapes Europe and establishes Chabad's permanent base in America.
Story: The wandering that began with the 1927 exile from Russia ended at 770 Eastern Parkway in Brooklyn, the iconic Gothic-style building where the Rebbe spent the last decade of his life. He addressed Achot Hatemimim in Riga during the second interlude.
Tags: america, new-york, wwii, rayatz, escape

Title: Rebbe inquires about Feigin's contacts with Soviet relative
Summary: On 27 Marcheshvan 5701, the Rebbe inquired whether Feigin was in contact with 'R. Nissan,' a coded reference in rescue correspondence.
Story: On 27 Marcheshvan 5701, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to R. Yechezkel Feigin asking if he was in contact with 'sh'b R. Nissan' and what replies he had received. The cryptic references reflected the wartime need to mask the actual nature of Soviet rescue communications.
Tags: riga, soviet union, rescue, yechezkel feigin, code

Title: Rebbe instructs delivery of 25 books to Rotstein
Summary: On 14 Iyar 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe instructed that 25 copies of the Rayatz's sefer be given to R. Moshe Leib Rotstein.
Story: On 14 Iyar 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to R. Mordechai Chefetz instructing that 25 copies of his sefer be given to R. Moshe Leib Rotstein. The directive was part of ongoing arrangements connected to Rotstein's anticipated departure for the United States.
Tags: moshe leib rotstein, books, frierdiker rebbe

Title: Rebbe instructs loans for rescue travel expenses
Summary: On 25 Adar Sheni 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe wired instructions to extend interest-free loans to fund travel for Eber, Rotstein, and Zalmanov.
Story: On 25 Adar Sheni 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to R. Mordechai Chefetz in Riga instructing that gemach loans be given: 2,500 to R. Yehuda Eber, 1,500 to R. Moshe Leib Rotstein, and up to 500 lats to R. Shmuel Zalmanov, all on the Rebbe's account.
Tags: riga, rescue, finance, yehuda eber, moshe leib rotstein, shmuel zalmanov

Title: Rebbe obtains 127 US visas for European talmidim
Summary: At the start of 5701 the Frierdiker Rebbe secured 127 US visas for top Tomchei Temimim talmidim across occupied Europe, including Latvia.
Story: Early in 5701 the Frierdiker Rebbe arranged 127 visas to the United States for select Tomchei Temimim students across Nazi-occupied Europe, with a portion allocated to Latvia. Almost none were permitted to leave; most of the intended recipients perished in the Holocaust.
Tags: usa, visas, wwii, tomchei-temimim, latvia, europe, holocaust

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in America and opens Tomchei Tmimim in New York
Summary: In late winter 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in America and opened the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in New York, where R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal was appointed Rosh Mesivta.
Story: Upon the Rebbe Rayatz's arrival in America at the end of winter 5700, he established the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in New York. R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal, who had escaped to America during the war, was appointed Rosh Mesivta and educator, a position he held the rest of his life.
Tags: new york, america, tomchei tmimim, rebbe rayatz, rabbi yitzchak dov oshpal

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in New York and founds Agudas Chasidei Chabad
Summary: In 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in New York and established Agudas Chasidei Chabad, with R' Yochanan Gordon appointed as one of the founding members of its hanhalah.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz reached New York in 5700 after his escape from Nazi-occupied Europe, and shortly thereafter founded Agudas Chasidei Chabad to organize the chassidic community in America. R' Yochanan Gordon was appointed as one of the members of its founding management. This event marked the formal beginning of organized Chabad institutional life in the United States.
Tags: new york, rebbe rayatz, agudas chasidei chabad, world war 2, yochanan gordon

Title: Rebbe Rayatz escapes Nazi-occupied Warsaw
Summary: In late winter 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz was rescued from Nazi-occupied Warsaw along with members of his household and secretaries.
Story: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn had been in Warsaw when Nazi Germany invaded Poland at the start of 5700. After several months under occupation, a coordinated rescue effort succeeded in extracting him along with family members and secretaries in late winter 5700 (early 1940). They first traveled to Riga and from there continued onward to New York.
Tags: rayatz, warsaw, nazi, wwii, escape, riga, rescue

Title: Rebbe Rayatz escapes Nazi-occupied Warsaw and reaches the United States
Summary: In the winter of 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz was miraculously rescued from Nazi-occupied Warsaw and arrived in the United States.
Story: During the winter of 5700 (1940), the Rebbe Rayatz was miraculously saved from Nazi-occupied Warsaw and reached the United States. He spent the final ten years of his life — from 5700 to 5710 — in America, where he established institutions across the country.
Tags: rayatz, warsaw, united-states, world-war-ii, nazis, rescue

Title: Rebbe Rayatz launches Pidyon Shvuyim rescue fund
Summary: Upon arrival in the United States in 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz immediately launched a Pidyon Shvuyim fund to rescue Tmimim and Anash from Nazi-occupied Europe.
Story: Immediately upon his arrival in the U.S. in 5700 (1940), the Rebbe Rayatz established a dedicated fund called Pidyon Shvuyim aimed at rescuing Tmimim and Anash trapped in Nazi-occupied Europe. A group of more than thirty students was eventually routed through Russia, Japan, and Shanghai to safety.
Tags: rayatz, rescue, world-war-ii, pidyon-shvuyim, tmimim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz relocates to the United States
Summary: The Rebbe permanently moved to America, settling in Crown Heights, Brooklyn.
Story: His 1929 visit had set the stage for the relocation. He chose Crown Heights, which had hosted him a decade earlier, as his new center. The relocation would shape the future trajectory of Chabad and global Jewish life.
Tags: rayatz, united-states, crown-heights, world-war-ii

Title: Rebbe writes Feigin about Soviet rescue caution
Summary: On 15 Kislev 5701, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to Feigin about the difficulty of pressuring Soviet contacts without backfiring.
Story: On 15 Kislev 5701, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to R. Yechezkel Feigin describing the painful constraints in maneuvering for Soviet exit permits. 'Everyone knows how hard it is to move people whose word is empty,' he wrote, expressing fear that any pressure on the contact might prove counterproductive.
Tags: riga, soviet union, rescue, yechezkel feigin, diplomacy

Title: Rebbe writes letters of thanks for US entry permits
Summary: After reaching Riga, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote thank-you letters acknowledging US entry permits for himself, his family, and his secretaries.
Story: Upon arriving in Riga in early 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote several letters of gratitude for US entry permits obtained for himself, his family, and his secretaries Feigin, Liberman, Rotstein, and Rosh Yeshiva Eber. Ultimately only Liberman, Chadakov, and Mindel would accompany the Rebbe and his family to America.
Tags: riga, usa, visas, rescue, frierdiker rebbe, secretaries

Title: Reburial of the Rebbe Rashab in Rostov
Summary: When Rostov planned to destroy the old Jewish cemetery, Chasidim secretly transferred the Rashab's grave to a new Jewish cemetery.
Story: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson gave detailed instructions to a group of ten Chasidim, who fasted and performed the transfer late at night despite the danger of police discovery. Twenty years after the Rashab's passing, his body was found whole and intact, shocking the participants. Shmuel Gurary was also reinterred next to him.
Tags: rashab, rostov, reburial, levi-yitzchak-schneerson

Title: Riga rescue hopes rise then fall in late summer 5700
Summary: On 28 Menachem Av 5700, R. Mordechai Chefetz reported hopes that Feigin and Eber would soon receive travel permits.
Story: On 28 Menachem Av 5700, R. Mordechai Chefetz wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe expressing hope that R. Yechezkel Feigin would soon receive his travel permit and that R. Yehuda Eber had already obtained his. By 4 Tishrei tash'a, however, both were still waiting in vain for salvation.
Tags: riga, rescue, yechezkel feigin, yehuda eber

Title: Rotstein and Zalmanov depart Riga for America
Summary: On 19 Elul 5700, R. Moshe Leib Rotstein and R. Shmuel Zalmanov departed Riga for America at 7 PM.
Story: On 19 Elul 5700, R. Mordechai Chefetz wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe that he was going to escort R. Moshe Leib Rotstein and R. Shmuel Zalmanov, who were leaving Riga that day at 7 PM en route to America. The journey would take them through Russia and Japan.
Tags: riga, usa, rescue, moshe leib rotstein, shmuel zalmanov, travel

Title: Rotstein and Zalmanov travel from Vladivostok to Japan
Summary: On 4 Tishrei 5701, the Frierdiker Rebbe reported receiving a telegram that Rotstein and Zalmanov had arrived safely in Vladivostok and were traveling to Japan.
Story: On 4 Tishrei 5701, the Frierdiker Rebbe relayed in a letter that he had received a telegram that day from R. Moshe Leib Rotstein and R. Shmuel Zalmanov, reporting their safe arrival in Vladivostok and their continuing travel to Japan en route to America.
Tags: vladivostok, japan, moshe leib rotstein, shmuel zalmanov, rescue, travel

Title: Rotstein appointed to head Agudas Chabad in Chicago
Summary: Upon arriving in America in late 5701, R. Moshe Leib Rotstein was sent to lead Agudas Chabad in Chicago.
Story: After arriving in the United States in late Tishrei 5701, R. Moshe Leib Rotstein was dispatched to direct Agudas Chabad in Chicago. He served there before later returning to the Rebbe's secretariat.
Tags: chicago, agudas chabad, moshe leib rotstein, usa

Title: Rotstein, Zalmanov, and Ushpal arrive in San Francisco
Summary: In late Tishrei 5701, R. Moshe Leib Rotstein, R. Shmuel Zalmanov, and R. Yitzchak Dov Ushpal arrived in San Francisco from Japan.
Story: At the end of Tishrei 5701, the three Lubavitch rabbis arrived in San Francisco after their long journey through Russia, Siberia, and Japan. On 29 Tishrei, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to R. Yaakov Katz in Chicago that the three rabbis had safely arrived in America and were traveling on to New York.
Tags: san francisco, usa, rescue, moshe leib rotstein, shmuel zalmanov, yitzchak dov ushpal

Title: Skobla reports Rotstein's visa secured
Summary: On 11 Adar Sheni, R. Chaim Yitzchak Skobla wrote from Riga to the Rashag that R. M.L. Rotstein had received his visa.
Story: On 11 Adar Sheni 5700, R. Chaim Yitzchak Skobla wrote from Riga to the Rashag — who had just arrived in America with the Rebbe — informing him that R. Moshe Leib Rotstein's visa had been received and that he would soon travel.
Tags: riga, usa, visa, moshe leib rotstein, rescue

Title: Soviet conquest of Latvia voids exit documents
Summary: During summer 5700, Latvia was conquered by the Soviets, voiding the refugees' Latvian passports and complicating exit.
Story: In Sivan 5700, the Soviets conquered Latvia. R. Feigin and R. Eber were Russian citizens whose Latvian-era documents now lost validity. They were forced to re-apply for new Soviet passports — a process taking many months requiring Moscow approval — during which their American visas expired.
Tags: riga, latvia, soviet union, russia, passports, visas, rescue

Title: Soviet Union takes over Latvia
Summary: Russian forces took over Latvia, seizing much of the Rebbe Rayatz's correspondence in Riga.
Story: The Rebbe's letters to his wife from his 1929–30 voyage, primarily in Yiddish, were among the materials captured. The papers were eventually transferred to the Russian National Library.
Tags: soviet-union, latvia, world-war-ii, rayatz-archives

Title: Three Lubavitch rabbis arrive in New York
Summary: On Friday Parshat Noach 1 Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan 5701, three Lubavitch rabbis arrived in New York and HaKeriah VeHakedusha reported on their rescue.
Story: On Friday Parshat Noach, 1 Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan 5701, R. Moshe Leib Rotstein, R. Shmuel Zalmanov, and R. Yitzchak Dov Ushpal arrived in New York with their families. The Lubavitch periodical HaKeriah VeHakedusha (issue 2) reported on their rescue from the 'European inferno' through the Pidyon Shvuyim Fund established by the Lubavitcher Rebbe.
Tags: new york, usa, rescue, hakeriah vehakedusha, moshe leib rotstein, shmuel zalmanov, yitzchak dov ushpal

Title: Trotsky assassinated by Stalinist agent in Mexico City
Summary: Trotsky was assassinated by a Stalinist agent at his home in Mexico City.
Story: His assassination completed the fulfillment of the Rashab's 1920 prediction that 'Trotsky will be exiled, and they will execute him.' The Rayatz had recorded his father's prophetic warnings in his diary years earlier, noting how remarkably they were coming to pass.
Tags: trotsky, mexico city, stalin, assassination

Title: Trotsky assassinated in Mexico City
Summary: A Stalinist agent assassinated Leon Trotsky at his home in Mexico City.
Story: In 1940, three years after a Moscow trial sentenced him to death in absentia, Leon Trotsky was assassinated by a Stalinist agent at his home in Mexico City. The killing completed the arc of Stalin's elimination of his exiled rival, fulfilling the Rashab's twenty-year-old prediction.
Tags: trotsky, mexico city, stalin, assassination

Title: Underground Tomchei Temimim yeshiva founded in Radom ghetto
Summary: At the start of 5701, Meir Hendel and Yosef Goldstein founded a clandestine branch of Tomchei Temimim in the Radom ghetto, ultimately gathering close to two hundred students.
Story: Funding for the yeshiva came largely from the father of bochur Motl Bumelgrin, a wealthy and respected community member who took on its principal expenses. The roshei yeshiva and mashpi'im R' Berl Kornitzer and R' Baruch Friedman were brought in from Otwock, leaving their families behind to teach and inspire the students. Despite the dangers of underground life under Nazi occupation, the yeshiva continued operating until the end of summer 5702.
Tags: poland, radom, ghetto, tomchei temimim, holocaust, meir hendel, yosef goldstein, berl kornitzer, baruch friedman

Title: Visa #42 issued for R. Betzalel Katz
Summary: In the summer of 5700, visa #42 to the United States was arranged by the Rebbe Rayatz for R. Betzalel HaKohen Katz, the senior rabbi of Rakishok.
Story: R. Betzalel HaKohen Katz, called the elder of Lithuania's rabbis, had served the Rakishok community alongside R. Shmuel Levitin. In the summer of 5700 (1940), as part of the rescue effort, the Rebbe Rayatz arranged visa #42 of the first list of recipients for him to travel to the United States.
Tags: katz, rakishok, visas, usa-rescue, shoah-rescue

Title: Rebbe Rayatz and family stay in Riga
Summary: During Tevet through Adar Rishon 5700, the Rebbe and his family - including his mother Rebbetzin Shterna Sarah - resided in Riga.
Story: The extended stay came in the early months of World War II, before the Rebbe's departure to America. Photographs preserved from this period show classes of Achos Tmimim posing with Rebbetzin Shterna Sarah and with two of their mashpiim. Soviet Latvia would be invaded the following summer.
Tags: rayatz, riga, rebbetzin-shterna-sarah, wartime

Title: Letter to Chief Rabbi Herzog about Palestine certificates
Summary: On 21 Tevet 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz clarified to Chief Rabbi Isaac Herzog that the five Palestine certificates were meant not for his own family but for endangered yeshiva students.
Story: Rabbi Herzog had assumed the Rebbe's request for British Mandate certificates was for his own household and granted five. The Rebbe responded that he had requested them to distribute among those in real danger in Europe, and pressed for a larger allotment because of the dire situation he had personally observed in Poland.
Tags: isaac herzog, palestine, certificates, rescue, yeshiva students

Title: Rayatz writes Vilna students after Warsaw and Polish branches flee to Vilna
Summary: On 20 Tevet 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Tomchei Tmimim students newly arrived in Vilna from Warsaw and other Polish branches, urging them to recognize their situation as one of transition.
Story: After the German invasion of Poland, students of the Warsaw yeshiva and other Polish branches fled to Vilna, joining the existing branch there. In his letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. 5, letter 1141), the Rayatz acknowledged a report relayed by R' Shmuel Zalmanov and R' M. L. Rodshtein on the temporary arrangements. He told the talmidim to internalize that the yeshiva was in a state of relocation, not stable settlement.
Tags: rayatz, tomchei tmimim, vilna, warsaw, war, refugees, wwii

Title: Rebbe writes to Vilna students about the yeshiva's transitional state
Summary: On 20 Tevet 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the Vilna yeshiva students through R. Shmuel Zalmanov and R. Moshe Leib Rodstein.
Story: Writing from Riga on 20 Tevet 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz acknowledged the temporary arrangements established for Tomchei Tmimim in Vilna and asked every student to understand that the yeshiva was in a state of transition and preparation. The letter was carried by R. Shmuel Zalmanov and R. Moshe Leib Rodstein, who were helping run the yeshiva-in-exile.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, vilna, tomchei tmimim, wwii

Title: Rebbe writes JDC head Morris Troper urging mass emigration of Polish Jewry
Summary: From Riga, the Rebbe wrote JDC European chairman Morris Troper urging a vast relief campaign and the inclusion of emigration in the JDC's mandate.
Story: Calling it his 'sacred duty to give firsthand information,' the Rebbe lauded the JDC as the only Jewish institution still working in Warsaw. He pressed Troper to extend relief into emigration assistance — first for the most urgent cases and ultimately for 'the wholesale immigration of Polish Jewry to a quiet place under the sun, where they can live a normal Jewish life.'
Tags: riga, poland, joint distribution committee, morris troper, emigration, palestine, relief

Title: State Department investigators meet Chabad leaders in New York
Summary: Two senior State Department visa officials met Chabad leadership in New York to evaluate the claim that Chabad qualified as a religious hierarchy.
Story: After Max Rhoade's relentless lobbying, the visa division finally accepted the principle that the Rebbe's entourage might be admitted as the leadership of a religious hierarchy rather than each requiring an individual congregational sponsor. The officials received a detailed briefing on Chabad's history, structure, finances, and US synagogue network — a precondition for issuing the long-delayed visas.
Tags: new york, united states, visa, state department, agudas chassidei chabad, religious hierarchy, immigration

Title: Three Tomchei Tmimim bochurim reach Vilna after border crossing
Summary: On the night of 29 Tevet, R. Shmuel Dovid Reitchik, R. Yosef Menachem Mendel Tannenbaum, and R. Menachem Zev Greenglas arrived in Vilna.
Story: After zig-zagging through Slonim, Lida, Oshmany, Globoka, Postov and Sventzian, dodging border guards and changing currency twice, the group of bochurim crossed the second border on the night of 28 Tevet and reached Vilna the next night. They found Tomchei Tmimim already operating in the Apatow Kloiz with dozens of bochurim from Otwock.
Tags: vilna, lithuania, reitchik, tannenbaum, greenglas, tomchei-tmimim, border-crossing, wwii

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe reports US visas approved in Riga
Summary: On 7 Shevat 5700 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote from Riga that US visas had been received for the entire family, including the future Rebbe in Paris.
Story: The Frierdiker Rebbe informed his son-in-law in Paris that, thank G-d, all were alive and well, and that American visas had been arranged for the entire family. He proposed planning a joint journey to the United States. In practice, the Paris visas had only been promised, not issued, and the actual struggle to obtain them would continue for over a year.
Tags: riga, usa, visas, ramash, rayatz

Title: US visas confirmed for Rebbe Rayatz and family
Summary: On 7 Shevat 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote that visas for the United States had been received for the entire family.
Story: Writing to his son-in-law (the future Rebbe), the Rebbe Rayatz reported that visas had been issued for everyone, including the son-in-law's family. They now needed to coordinate the journey so all could travel together to America.
Tags: visa, usa, riga, immigration

Title: Rebbe welcomes new Vilna arrivals and urges them to summon others
Summary: On 8 Shevat the Rebbe Rayatz wrote from Riga blessing Greenglas, Tannenbaum and Reitchik on their arrival in Vilna and pressing them to urgently summon remaining students.
Story: Receiving Greenglas's report that the three bochurim had reached Vilna, the Rebbe replied on 8 Shevat 5700 with effusive blessing and a pressing instruction: write at once to every remaining talmid scattered across Poland to come to Vilna without delay. He demanded a list of names contacted, warning that 'the time is exceedingly precious.'
Tags: riga, vilna, tomchei-tmimim, rayatz, rescue, correspondence

Title: GPU officer Grigory Lulov executed
Summary: Grigory Lulov, one of the two GPU agents who arrested the Rebbe in 1927, was executed by verdict of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR.
Story: On January 21, 1940, GPU officer Grigory Nikolaevich Lulov was executed following his arrest at the end of 1938. Born in Riga in 1899, Lulov had joined the Communist Party in 1916 and the Cheka in 1919, becoming an 'Honorary Worker of the Cheka-GPU' decorated with the Order of Lenin in 1937 before falling victim to the purges himself.
Tags: russia, gpu, cheka, purge, supreme soviet

Title: Grigory Lulov executed by Supreme Soviet verdict
Summary: Grigory Lulov, the second GPU officer who arrested the Rebbe, was shot by order of the Supreme Soviet.
Story: Born in Riga in 1899, Lulov had joined the Communist party in 1916 and the Cheka in 1919. He received the Order of Lenin and an 'Honorary Worker of the Cheka-GPU' badge in 1937. Arrested at the end of 1938, he was executed on January 21, 1940, during Stalin's purges of the security organs.
Tags: lulov, gpu, execution, purges

Title: Achos Tmimim Riga designated central body for Latvia
Summary: On 16 Shevat 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz officially designated the Riga Achos Tmimim as 'Achos Tmimim HaMerkazi d'Medinas Latvia'.
Story: The Rebbe's letter to the leadership directed them to receive the central name, establish a board of directors with appropriate committees - first among them a publicity committee and a teachers' committee - and to draft appropriate regulations for the organization's central operation across Latvia.
Tags: rayatz, achos-tmimim, riga, latvia, structure

Title: Rebbe breaks his hand in Riga
Summary: On 6 Shevat the Rebbe fell and broke his hand, wearing a cast for three weeks and a bandage in the fourth.
Story: The injury kept the Rebbe from writing until just days before his departure for the US. During the same period his mother Rebbetzin Shterna Sara underwent a twelve-hour stomach operation, and the Rebbe delayed his travel until she recovered.
Tags: riga, latvia, health, injury, shterna sara

Title: Rebbe Rayatz breaks his right hand on Shabbos Yisro
Summary: On Shabbos Parshas Yisro 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz fell and broke a bone in his right hand while walking to make Kiddush.
Story: The injury required a cast for three weeks and a bandage afterward. Combined with an emergency hernia operation needed by his mother Rebbetzin Shterna Sarah, this delayed the family's planned departure from Riga to the United States.
Tags: injury, riga, shabbos, kiddush

Title: List of 43 students at Tomchei Tmimim in Vilna compiled
Summary: An archival roster dated 31 January 1940 (21 Shevat 5700) lists 43 bochurim studying at the re-established Tomchei Tmimim in Vilna.
Story: Secretary R. Moshe Leib Rothstein compiled a detailed register of the bochurim who had reached Vilna, recording their origins, ages, and arrival dates, plus those still stuck at the border. A photograph of the 31 January 1940 list of 43 students survives in the archive. Most of those listed were later saved via Russia-Japan-China, though not all.
Tags: vilna, lithuania, tomchei-tmimim, wwii, rescue, archive

Title: Rebbe urges Vilna students to greater diligence
Summary: On 25 Shvat 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to three Vilna students urging them to greater diligence in study and avodah.
Story: The Rebbe addressed Yosef Hakohen Bornstein (Portowicz), Menachem Zev Greenglass and Avraham Yitzchak Garfinkel, noting that while the yeshiva was reorganizing well, the spiritual impact expected of the students was not yet evident. He pressed them to strengthen both their study and their avodah shebalev.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, vilna, tomchei tmimim, yosef bornstein, menachem zev greenglass, avraham yitzchak garfinkel

Title: Rebbe Rayatz cables New York demanding Joint funding for student rescue
Summary: On 26 Shevat the Rebbe cabled Jacobson and Lavut, demanding pressure on the Joint to fund Pesach relief, evacuation of 200 students, and rescue of six rabbis' families.
Story: After Tropper of the European Joint deferred his earlier appeal, the Rebbe Rayatz wired R. Yisroel Jacobson and R. Shmuel Levitin in New York on 26 Shevat 5700, itemizing $5,000 for Pesach aid, $4,000 to rescue 200 yeshiva students, and $5,143 to bring six rabbis and their families to the US. He instructed them to meet Rosen urgently and recruit Kramer and Dr. Jung to lobby the Joint.
Tags: riga, new-york, joint-distribution-committee, tropper, rescue, fundraising, rayatz

Title: Abraham Kvash begins service as rabbinic intern in Riga
Summary: On 28 Shevat 5700 / 7 February 1940 R. Abraham Kvash began service as a 'rabbinic intern' in the Riga rabbinate.
Story: Per the Rebbe's instructions to prepare paperwork and meanwhile take employment, Kvash took a junior rabbinic position in Riga. He served there until the Nazi conquest of Latvia.
Tags: abraham kvash, riga, latvia, rabbinate

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe urges talmidim to relocate to Vilna on 3 Adar I 5700
Summary: On 3 Adar I 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe urged talmidim from Chelm, Lodz and other branches to relocate to Tomchei Tmimim in Vilna.
Story: The letter (Vol. 5, no. 1153) instructed the recipients to hurry along talmidim who had learned in the smaller branches in Chelm, Lodz and elsewhere to make their way to Vilna. From there, a group of 38 talmidim was ultimately rescued and brought to safety.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, wwii, vilna, chelm, lodz, rescue

Title: Rebbe Rayatz urges students to flee Poland for the Vilna yeshiva
Summary: On 3 Adar I 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote from Riga urging students to hurry to the Vilna yeshiva and to mobilize one another to escape Poland.
Story: Still based in Riga before his journey to New York, the Rebbe Rayatz sent a letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. 5, no. 1153) to one of the Tomchei Temimim students. He instructed each student to write to his peers in Poland — including those at the Chelm branch and other smaller yeshivot — to rouse them to come, to seek out missing students, and to push past every obstacle to reach the yeshiva.
Tags: poland, vilna, lithuania, tomchei temimim, war, rescue, yosef yitzchak schneersohn, wwii

Title: Attorney Kremer petitions for future Rebbe's US visa
Summary: On 4 Adar I 5700, attorney Sam Kremer wrote to attorney Henry Butler in Washington urging that a US visa be secured for Rabbi Mendel Schneerson in Paris.
Story: Kremer, a member of the Agudas Chabad executive, formally requested Butler's assistance in securing a US visa for Rabbi Mendel Schneerson 'as a member of the leadership of the movement.' This began over a year of intensive correspondence between Chabad's New York lawyers and the State Department to extract the future Rebbe and Rebbetzin from Nazi-controlled Europe.
Tags: washington, visas, paris, sam kremer, henry butler, agudas chabad

Title: Kramer confirms all Riga visas received
Summary: On February 13, 1940, attorney Sam Kramer informed Henry Butler that all US visas for the rabbis in Riga had been received.
Story: Kramer relayed news from a cable sent by the Rebbe Rayatz that the visa process was complete. With travel preparations and convalescence still underway, departure was scheduled for early March.
Tags: kramer, butler, visa, usa, riga

Title: US visas issued to the Rebbe and entourage in Riga
Summary: The US Consulate in Riga issued immigration visas to the Rebbe and the rabbis of his entourage, clearing the final bureaucratic hurdle to America.
Story: After months of pressure from Rhoade, Cohen, and a coalition of congressmen and senators, the visas were granted. Sam Kramer informed Henry Butler the same day. The Rebbe's daughters Sheina and Chaya Mushka and their husbands were not included; the Schneersons later escaped via France and Spain, while the Horensteins were killed in Treblinka.
Tags: riga, united states, visa, state department, max rhoade, sam kramer, immigration, horenstein

Title: Rebbe asks U.S. government to keep Levitin in America
Summary: On 9 Adar I 5700 the Rebbe wrote to the Agudas Chabad leadership in New York requesting that Levitin remain in America to assist his work after the move from Warsaw to Riga.
Story: After escaping Warsaw to Riga, the Rebbe wrote on 9 Adar I 5700 (Igros Kodesh vol. 14, letter 5261) to the Agudas Chabad leadership in New York. He asked them to lobby the Washington government to allow Levitin to remain in America and to bring his family to join him, since he was essential to the work of disseminating chassidus and organizing Chabad chassidim worldwide.
Tags: levitin, agudas-chabad, usa, warsaw-riga-rescue, visas

Title: Rebbe endorses the Hassidic-lineage students' union
Summary: On 11 Adar I 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz endorsed the new union of Hassidic-lineage yeshiva students.
Story: Responding to a letter dated 4 Adar I, the Rebbe approved the founding of an union of students of Hassidic lineage who were studying in the Lithuanian yeshivot of Kamenitz, Kletzk, Pinsk, Bialystok, Lomza, Ostrow-Brisk, Chachmei Lublin, Tomchei Tmimim and Slonim. He praised the new bylaws, the spiritual committee and the executive board, and emphasized that success would depend on the spiritual committee's commitment.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, igud hatalmidim, kamenitz, kletzk, pinsk, bialystok, lomza, lublin

Title: Reitchik sends detailed escape report and rescue updates to the Rebbe
Summary: On Motzaei Shabbat Ki Tisa, 15 Adar I, R. Shmuel Dovid Reitchik wrote the Rebbe a full account of his escape and the names of students still trapped at borders.
Story: From Vilna, Reitchik catalogued his entire route to the Rebbe and reported on bochurim still stuck near borders in Oshmany, Lida and Sventzian, plus those rescued via Mendel Tenenbaum. He proposed sending an emissary back across the border to bring the remaining students and the chossid Chaim Meir Lis, and noted that the Vilna yeshiva had already drawn other bochurim attracted to Chassidus.
Tags: vilna, riga, reitchik, tomchei-tmimim, border-crossing, rescue, correspondence

Title: Achos Tmimim chapter opened in Dvinsk
Summary: On 17 Adar Rishon 5700 the first session of Achos Tmimim Dvinsk took place at the Pinkovich home with six girls present.
Story: R. Baruch Eliyahu Peletz reported to the Rebbe that the chapter had begun in Dvinsk (renamed Daugavpils). Six girls attended; some committed to come weekly and others said they needed to consult their parents. Mrs. Esther Pinkovich corresponded with the Riga central office for guidance on curriculum and method.
Tags: achos-tmimim, dvinsk, daugavpils, pinkovich, peletz

Title: Group photo of Tomchei Tmimim students taken in Vilna
Summary: On 17 Adar I 5700 (Feb 26, 1940), the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim students and faculty were photographed.
Story: A series of group photographs of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim students, mashgiach R. Eliyahu Moshe Lis, and administrators including R. Moshe Leib Rodstein, R. Shmuel Zalmanov and R. Yitzchak Dov Ber Ushpal were taken on 17 Adar I 5700. These photos are among the few surviving images of the yeshiva-in-exile in Vilna.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, photograph, 17 adar

Title: Founding members of Dvinsk Achos Tmimim documented
Summary: On 18 Adar Rishon 5700, R. Shraga Yitzchak Pinkovich listed the six founding girls of Achos Tmimim Dvinsk in a letter to the Rebbe.
Story: The girls were Abigail Golda, Sara Sheskin, Mina Schneersohn, Roza Kagan, Zelda Westerman, and Chaya Zayer - all from chassidic families, several with fathers who had learned in Lubavitch or Rostov. R. Peletz spoke to them about the Baal Shem Tov and explained that the Rebbe wished such a society be founded in their city.
Tags: achos-tmimim, dvinsk, pinkovich, founding-members

Title: JDC meets Chabad delegation on aid to refugees and the Vilnius yeshivah
Summary: JDC officials met Agudas Chassidei Chabad representatives, offering limited discretionary funds for the Rebbe but refusing to subsidize US immigration or the Vilnius yeshivah.
Story: Citing US law forbidding organizations from financing immigration, the JDC declined the larger requests but agreed to a discretionary grant 'in view of Rabbi Schneersohn's leadership' and approved funding for Passover matzah for rabbis in Russia. The Rebbe would have to rely on his own resources to sustain the Vilnius yeshivah and rescue Chasidim still in Poland.
Tags: new york, joint distribution committee, vilnius, passover, matzah, russia, yeshivah

Title: Greenglas reports widening rescue correspondence to the Rebbe
Summary: On 19 Adar I, R. Menachem Zev Greenglas reported writing to scattered students across Poland urging them to reach Vilna at once.
Story: Following the Rebbe's directive, Greenglas wrote from Vilna to bochurim in Sidlowice, Suchedniow, Chmielnik, Pociejow, and Lodz, naming specific talmidim to bring along. He also reported on shtot rabbanim who had hosted and fed Tomchei Tmimim students in Otwock during the war's opening months, including Rabbi Yechiel Yeshaya Weinberg of Yendrzejov.
Tags: vilna, greenglas, tomchei-tmimim, rescue, correspondence, poland

Title: 'Pidyon Shvuyim' rescue fund established in New York
Summary: Shortly after arriving in America in Adar Sheni 5700, the Rebbe founded the Pidyon Shvuyim fund to rescue anash and yeshiva students from Nazi-occupied Europe and support their families.
Story: From his quarters at the Greystone Hotel, the Rebbe entrusted Rabbi Eliyahu Simpson with the work of registering European families in urgent need. The first list, written on hotel stationery, recorded nearly one hundred families totaling roughly 500 souls across nineteen Lithuanian towns, with parallel lists soon prepared for occupied Poland.
Tags: pidyon shvuyim, rescue, fundraising, new york, europe, world war ii, eliyahu simpson

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe arrives in the United States
Summary: Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn arrived in America in the winter of 5700, opening a new chapter of Chabad activity in the United States.
Story: After being rescued from Nazi-occupied Warsaw, the Frierdiker Rebbe reached the United States in the winter of 5700. His arrival mobilized the author, who immediately took on intensive new responsibilities: mashpia at central Tomchei Tmimim, chairman and director of Beis Rivkah and its New York branches, general gabbai of the Chevra Kadisha, rav of the Lubavitch community in New York, organizer of the Tomchei Tmimim branch in Newark, and founder and mashpia of the Hadar HaTorah yeshiva for newly observant students.
Tags: usa, new york, frierdiker rebbe, immigration, world war ii

Title: Letter from Shainin in Dokshitz during wartime
Summary: On 2 Rosh Chodesh Adar II 5700, Rabbi Aryeh Leib Shainin of Dokshitz wrote a coded letter to R' Yochanan Gordon describing wartime suffering and asking for support.
Story: From within Nazi-shadowed Dokshitz at the height of winter 5700, Rabbi Aryeh Leib Shainin sent a disguised letter to his former townsman R' Yochanan Gordon in New York. Writing as 'Uncle Yaakov Leib Glaz,' Shainin reported that he and his wife were severely ill and begged for material support. Shainin, who had been sent to serve as rabbi of Dokshitz by the Rebbe Rayatz in 5683, would later perish in the Holocaust.
Tags: world war 2, dokshitz, leib shainin, yochanan gordon, holocaust

Title: Rayatz arrives in the United States after escaping Europe
Summary: At the end of winter 5700 the Rayatz was rescued from Nazi-occupied Europe and arrived in the United States.
Story: After the outbreak of war disrupted Chabad publishing in Warsaw, the Rayatz was rescued from Europe and reached the United States in late winter 5700 (March 1940). From New York he soon resumed correspondence about projects interrupted by the war, including the commemorations of past Chabad Chasidim.
Tags: rayatz, usa, wartime escape, warsaw, new york

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in New York
Summary: In the late winter of 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz reached New York after escaping war-torn Europe.
Story: In the late winter of 5700 (early 1940) the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in New York, having been rescued from Nazi-occupied Warsaw. From New York he began the rebuilding of Chabad institutions on American soil. Within months he would found new branches of Tomchei Tmimim and youth divisions to anchor the movement in the New World.
Tags: rebbe-rayatz, new-york, united-states, wwii, escape-from-europe

Title: Rebbe Rayatz cables Jacobson to extract library from Warsaw
Summary: In early Adar Sheni 5700 the Rebbe cabled Jacobson from Riga to do everything possible to extract his library and effects from Warsaw.
Story: In early Adar Sheni 5700 (early March 1940), still in Riga, the Rebbe Rayatz sent a telegram to Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson urgently instructing him to do whatever possible to extract his library and personal effects from Warsaw. He asked Jacobson to also enlist the assistance of Kremer and Kleinfeld in the rescue effort.
Tags: library, warsaw, wwii, yisrael-jacobson, kremer, kleinfeld, rescue

Title: Rebbe Rayatz heads to New York
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz traveled to New York, while the Ramash hesitated to leave Paris to join him.
Story: Feigin wrote to Jacobson asking him to encourage the Ramash to come to the US, noting his great ability to draw the younger generation closer to Jewish observance. The Ramash resisted, seemingly fearing it would detract from his studies, but Feigin argued he had completed his secular studies and could now dedicate himself totally to Torah.
Tags: new-york, usa, feigin, jacobson

Title: Sheinin's final letter from Dokshytsy
Summary: On the eve of Rosh Chodesh Adar II 5700, Sheinin sent a Yiddish letter from Dokshytsy describing his weak health.
Story: Sheinin's last surviving letter from Dokshytsy, addressed to R. Yochanan Gordon and dated Erev Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheini 5700, said simply that he was alive but his aunt was very weak and he himself was ill and had no strength to move about.
Tags: sheinin, dokshytsy, gordon, wwii, yiddish-letter

Title: Rebbe Rayatz departs Riga for Stockholm en route to America
Summary: At the end of Adar I 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz left Riga for Stockholm, continuing on to the United States.
Story: After two months in Riga coordinating the rescue of his yeshiva students from Poland and Soviet-held territory, the Rebbe Rayatz left for Stockholm at the end of Adar I 5700. From Stockholm he continued onward to the United States, where he would arrive that spring and re-establish the center of Chabad.
Tags: riga, stockholm, sweden, rayatz, rescue, wwii

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe departs Riga for America
Summary: On 24 Adar I 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe left Riga with his family on the final leg of his escape to the United States.
Story: With Latvia threatened by the war, the Frierdiker Rebbe departed Riga for Stockholm, where he would board a ship to New York. His daughter Chaya Mushka and her husband, the future Rebbe, remained behind in Paris, unable to obtain visas in time. The separation marked the start of more than a year of intense rescue efforts on the family's behalf.
Tags: riga, stockholm, usa, wwii, escape, rayatz

Title: Rayatz departs Riga for Stockholm
Summary: On 24 Adar Alef, the Rayatz left Riga for Stockholm, Sweden.
Story: The Stockholm transit allowed the Rayatz to board a transatlantic ship from neutral Sweden, the safest available route to the United States as the war engulfed Europe.
Tags: riga, stockholm, sweden, latvia

Title: Rebbe departs Riga for Stockholm before crossing the Atlantic
Summary: Thousands of Chasidim gathered in Riga to bid farewell to the Rebbe, who refused to leave seven empty plane seats and held up the flight until they were filled.
Story: Shraga Feivel Zisman organized a human chain to allow the Rebbe's mother to be carried on a stretcher to the ambulance. The Rebbe asked Rabbi Mordechai Cheifetz to tell the crowd, 'The great ocean is not a barrier but a connector.' Discovering empty seats on the plane, he refused to depart until others were brought aboard, declaring, 'I cannot leave, I need to save others.'
Tags: riga, latvia, stockholm, sweden, mordechai cheifetz, leibel zisman, departure, escape

Title: Rebbe Rayatz departs Riga for the United States
Summary: On 24 Adar I 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz left Riga to make his way to America.
Story: After roughly two and a half months in Riga, the Rebbe Rayatz set out for the United States on 24 Adar I 5700 (March 4, 1940). The relocation marked the transfer of the headquarters of the Chabad movement from war-torn Europe to America, consistent with planning begun in winter 5699.
Tags: riga, usa, emigration, wwii, agudath-chassidei-chabad

Title: Rebbe Rayatz flies from Riga to Stockholm
Summary: On Monday 24 Adar I 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz departed Riga by airplane to Stockholm, with thousands gathered at the airport.
Story: Jews of Riga, chassidim and non-chassidim alike, packed the aerodrome to bid farewell. Chief of Riga's community Mordechai Dubin accompanied the family. The elder Rebbetzin was carried aboard on a stretcher. The Rebbe blessed the Latvian government, its president, and the Jewish community, urging all to join Agudas Yisroel.
Tags: riga, stockholm, sweden, departure, flight, latvia

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe writes from Stockholm before sailing
Summary: On 25 Adar I 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote a disguised letter in Russian from Stockholm to the future Rebbe in Paris, fearing censorship.
Story: Awaiting his transatlantic crossing, the Rebbe Rayatz used Russian to evade wartime censors. He confirmed that $1,000 had been allocated for travel preparations and asked whether Mushka and Mendel could purchase tickets themselves or required them to be forwarded by Jacobson. Coded references and intermediaries became central to the rescue correspondence.
Tags: stockholm, censorship, russian, ramash, chaya mushka

Title: Rebbe Rayatz replies with welcome blessing to Reitchik in Vilna
Summary: On 25 Adar I the Rebbe Rayatz responded to Reitchik's report with a Bruchim Habaim blessing and exhortation to succeed in learning.
Story: Replying from Riga on 25 Adar I 5700 (Igros Kodesh vol. 14, letter 5261), the Rebbe Rayatz acknowledged Reitchik's safe arrival in Tomchei Tmimim, blessed him, and reminded him to follow the directives in the Rebbe's general letter to the students - to succeed in learning and become a G-d-fearing chossid and lamdan.
Tags: riga, vilna, reitchik, tomchei-tmimim, rayatz, correspondence

Title: Rebbe Rayatz boards ship at Gothenburg for America
Summary: After a brief stay in Stockholm, the Rebbe Rayatz boarded a transatlantic ship from Gothenburg en route to America.
Story: From Stockholm the party traveled overnight by train to the port city of Gothenburg, where they were taken directly to the ship as a special exception. The vessel finally departed Thursday morning. During the Stockholm stay, Stockholm Chief Rabbi Yisrael Yaakov Zuber and his family visited the Rebbe.
Tags: stockholm, gothenburg, sweden, voyage, usa

Title: Rebbe Rayatz departs Riga en route to the United States
Summary: At the end of Adar I 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz set out from Riga to the United States.
Story: Together with his family and secretaries R. Chaim Liberman, R. Chaim Mordechai Aizik Hodakov and R. Nissan Mindel, the Rebbe began his journey to America. On 27 Adar I 5700 he wrote en route to the Vilna students, asking the senior students in particular to take responsibility for every aspect of the yeshiva and to conduct it in the spirit of Tomchei Tmimim as it had been in Otwock.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, emigration, usa, riga, wwii

Title: Rayatz boards transatlantic ship in Gothenburg
Summary: The Rayatz boarded a ship in Gothenburg, Sweden, on 27 Adar Alef for his transatlantic journey.
Story: Gothenburg was a major port for transatlantic crossings during the war. The voyage from Sweden to the US took nearly two weeks, taking him through dangerous wartime waters.
Tags: gothenburg, sweden, transatlantic, rescue

Title: Rebbe boards the SS Drottningholm in Gothenburg bound for America
Summary: Three days after leaving Riga, the Rebbe and his eleven-person entourage boarded the SS Drottningholm at the Swedish port of Gothenburg for the voyage to the United States.
Story: The Drottningholm was the only ocean liner still operating between neutral Sweden and the US. Mechanical problems detained it overnight at Bergen, Norway, with German submarines patrolling below in preparation for the invasion of Denmark a month later. German U-boats stopped the ship twice and British warships three times during the crossing, but each time the refugees were allowed to continue.
Tags: gothenburg, sweden, ss drottningholm, atlantic, united states, escape, u-boats

Title: Drottningholm arrives in New York Harbor with the Sixth Rebbe aboard
Summary: The Swedish liner Drottningholm pulled into New York Harbor at 4:00 p.m. carrying the Sixth Rebbe and his family after a perilous voyage from Gothenburg.
Story: After a harrowing twelve-day crossing during which the ship was stopped by British warships and German submarines, the Drottningholm reached New York. Port regulations required passengers to wait aboard overnight. A delegation of US Chabad leaders boarded the ship to greet the Rebbe in his stateroom.
Tags: sweden, usa, yosef yitzchak, wwii, rescue, drottningholm

Title: Announcement of Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim Lubavitch in America
Summary: On his first day in America the Sixth Rebbe declared that Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim Lubavitch would open the next day at the Oneg Shabbat Synagogue in Brooklyn.
Story: Speaking at the Greystone Hotel, the Rebbe announced his vision to fortify Jewish education in the US and told the crowd the new yeshivah would launch at once. He pressed Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson that he would not sleep until Jacobson promised to open it. Jacobson began enlisting students the next morning.
Tags: tomchei temimim, brooklyn, oneg shabbat synagogue, jacobson

Title: Rayatz arrives in New York from Europe
Summary: Rayatz arrived safely in New York on 9 Adar Sheni 5700, after being rescued from Nazi-occupied Europe.
Story: On 9 Adar Sheni 5700, Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn (Rayatz) arrived safely in New York after being rescued from Nazi-occupied Europe. R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky immediately began searching for a building to serve as the Chabad headquarters and the Rebbe's residence. On 13 Nissan, Rayatz wrote thanking him for these efforts.
Tags: rayatz, new-york, rescue, wwii, kazarnovsky

Title: Rayatz arrives in the United States
Summary: The Rayatz arrived in the United States on March 19, 1940 (9 Adar Bet), settling in Brooklyn and establishing Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim there.
Story: His arrival in America launched a new chapter for Chabad. From Brooklyn's Crown Heights, the Rayatz reestablished Tomchei Temimim and began transforming American Jewry, founding institutions that his son-in-law would later expand into a global movement.
Tags: united states, new york, brooklyn, tomchei temimim, immigration

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in New York
Summary: On 9 Adar II 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz reached New York with his family and secretaries, transferring Chabad's center to America.
Story: On 9 Adar II 5700 (March 19, 1940), the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in New York with his household and secretariat, completing the rescue from Europe. His arrival formalized the long-planned transfer of Chabad's worldwide headquarters from Eastern Europe to the United States, where Agudath Chassidei Chabad had already been organized since 5684 (1924).
Tags: new-york, usa, agudath-chassidei-chabad, wwii, 770

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in New York harbor
Summary: On Tuesday 9 Adar II 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived at the New York harbor, greeted by thousands.
Story: Delegations from Agudas HaAdmorim, Agudas HaRabbonim, major yeshivos, communal askanim, and charitable institutions welcomed him. In the harbor's largest hall, he conveyed greetings from European Jewry and urged American Jews to redouble efforts to aid those still trapped overseas. He stayed at the Greystone Hotel for nearly a month.
Tags: new-york, usa, arrival, agudas-chabad, immigration

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in the United States for the second time
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz arrived in America for the second time on 9 Adar Sheni 5700, this time to remain.
Story: Having been extricated from Nazi-occupied Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz landed in America on 9 Adar Sheni 5700, beginning the era in which Lubavitch's center moved permanently to the United States. A small remaining stock of the 1928 Likkutei Torah reprint was still available on his arrival. Unlike his 1929 visit, this arrival marked permanent settlement and the relocation of the movement's leadership.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, united states, immigration, world war ii, warsaw

Title: Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak arrives in New York; addresses thousands at the port
Summary: On 9 Adar Sheni 5700 the Rebbe landed in New York and immediately addressed a crowd of several thousand in the port hall, conveying greetings from European Jewry and calling for material and spiritual aid.
Story: Stepping into the largest hall of the harbor, the Rebbe relayed regards from the Jews of Europe and called on American and Canadian Jewry to redouble their relief work and help refugees relocate. The very same day he issued a general letter (Igros V:1165) and within days established the 'Pidyon Shvuyim' fund to rescue chassidim and yeshiva students from occupied Europe.
Tags: new york, united states, arrival, world war ii, yosef yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Sixth Rebbe disembarks at Pier 97 in Manhattan
Summary: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn disembarked at Pier 97 on West 57th Street, declaring that America would become a center of Torah.
Story: Thousands welcomed the Rebbe as he came down the gangway in a wheelchair, bedecked in a shtreimel. When a reporter expressed skepticism, the Rebbe insisted 'America iz nisht aderesh — America is no different. It will become a center of Torah.' Later that day he addressed crowds at the Greystone Hotel, calling for rescue of Polish Jewry and the founding of a yeshivah.
Tags: usa, new york, yosef yitzchak, 9 adar ii, america iz nisht aderesh

Title: Greenglass reports to Rebbe on students trapped in Poland
Summary: On 10 Adar II 5700, the student Menachem Zev Greenglass wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz about fellow Temimim facing severe obstacles trying to reach Vilna.
Story: Greenglass relayed letters from Yechezkel Shpiorvach of Kombin and Yitzchak Stulman of Bichawe, both of whom asked the Rebbe to arouse heavenly mercy on their behalf as they struggled to cross the closed Polish-Lithuanian border. His report was part of the steady stream of intelligence the Rebbe was receiving about scattered Tomchei Temimim students.
Tags: poland, vilna, tomchei temimim, war, rescue, menachem zev greenglass

Title: Sixth Rebbe appeals to Leo Jung to complete a Manhattan mikveh
Summary: Less than a week after arriving, the Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Dr. Leo Jung urging him to help finish a stalled new mikveh in Manhattan.
Story: Rabbi Joseph Lookstein had told the Rebbe the project was stuck. On Purim, the Rebbe pressed Jung — a champion of aesthetically pleasing mikvehs — to push it to completion, signaling his intent to support broader Orthodox infrastructure beyond his own circle.
Tags: mikveh, manhattan, leo jung, lookstein, purim

Title: Studies begin at Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim in Brooklyn
Summary: A week after the Rebbe's arrival, the new American Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim opened its doors in the basement of Congregation Oneg Shabbat in East Flatbush.
Story: Rabbi Mordechai Mentlik was appointed dean. The first cohort was barely a minyan, drawn mostly from American students who had been studying chasidic philosophy with Rabbi Jacobson, plus a few alumni of the Otwock yeshivah. Benches and a makeshift kitchen were assembled in the cellar.
Tags: tomchei temimim, brooklyn, east flatbush, oneg shabbat

Title: Rayatz writes that some Polish talmidim remain stranded in Poland
Summary: On 17 Adar Sheni 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote that part of the Polish Tomchei Tmimim talmidim were already in Vilna but others remained in Poland and would still need to be brought across.
Story: The letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. 12, letter 4362) describes an operation still very much in progress — moving students from German-occupied territory into Vilna. It reflects the patchwork rescue of yeshiva students in the months following the invasion. The Rayatz's concern was both logistical and pastoral.
Tags: rayatz, tomchei tmimim, vilna, poland, wwii, refugees

Title: Rebbe Rayatz in New York describes plight of European yeshivot
Summary: On 17 Adar II 5700, shortly after arriving in New York, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to supporters that the situation of his European yeshivot was dire and some students still needed to be smuggled out of Poland.
Story: Writing in Yiddish (Igrot Kodesh vol. 12, no. 4362), the Rebbe described how part of his students were already in Vilna while others remained in Poland and had to be brought across the border. The letter served as a discreet appeal for help in continuing the rescue effort from the safety of America.
Tags: new york, vilna, poland, tomchei temimim, war, rescue, yosef yitzchak schneersohn

Title: Rebbe writes Achos Tmimim regulations and program
Summary: On 17 Adar Sheni 5700 the Rebbe wrote to Achos Tmimim Riga regarding regulations and the order of their work and lectures.
Story: Following his earlier instruction to formalize Riga as the central body for Latvia, the Rebbe sent detailed guidance on operating procedures. He also inquired in this letter whether Riga had received his earlier letter about Dvinsk and what had been done there.
Tags: rayatz, achos-tmimim, regulations, riga

Title: Gerer Rebbe escapes Poland to Trieste
Summary: Around Erev Pesach 5700 the Gerer Rebbe (Imrei Emes) escaped Nazi-occupied Poland with 14 followers and reached Trieste, Italy.
Story: In a letter to attorney Butler on Erev Pesach 5700, Rashag noted that the Gerer Rebbe and 14 of his people had obtained German exit permits and reached Trieste roughly ten days earlier. He urged that the same channel be investigated for his brother-in-law Mordechai Menachem Mendel Horenstein, who was trapped with his wife Sheina in Otwock.
Tags: poland, trieste, italy, wwii, escape, imrei emes, gerer

Title: Rebbe Rayatz issues general letter pledging not to rest until students saved
Summary: In a Nisan 5700 general letter, the Rebbe Rayatz publicly pledged to not rest until he had rescued every Tomchei Tmimim talmid still trapped in Poland.
Story: Writing his klali letter in Nisan 5700 (Igros Kodesh vol. 5, letter 1181), the Rebbe Rayatz described in Yiddish the terror of being trapped under bombs in Warsaw with hundreds of his Tomchei Tmimim students. He declared his life-mission upon being rescued: to do everything in his power to save every dear talmid chacham still left behind in Poland.
Tags: rayatz, tomchei-tmimim, rescue, wwii, klali, yiddish

Title: Sixth Rebbe spends Passover in Lakewood, New Jersey
Summary: The Rebbe took a Passover interlude in Lakewood, New Jersey, before returning to the Greystone Hotel in Manhattan.
Story: While searching for a permanent residence, the Rebbe used the Greystone Hotel as his base. Some Chasidim later proposed Lakewood as a quieter location for his headquarters, but the Rebbe rejected suburban isolation in favor of a visible presence in urban Brooklyn.
Tags: lakewood, passover, greystone hotel

Title: Civil registration of the marriage in Moscow
Summary: On 1 April 1940 the author and his fianceé entered a Soviet registry office and registered her as his wife so she could gain residency rights in Moscow.
Story: Without a Moscow residence permit, the bride-to-be had to drift among relatives, and anyone caught without papers was deported from the city within 24 hours. Because the author held a permit for his apartment in Cherbinov, the couple went to the registry office on 1 April 1940 and registered her legally as his wife. Only later did the idea of an actual wedding crystallise in her mind.
Tags: moscow, soviet-bureaucracy, residence-permit, marriage

Title: Rayatz renews request to R. Michael Vilensky from New York
Summary: On 23 Adar Sheni 5700 the Rayatz wrote again from America asking R. Michael Vilensky to record his father's biography for Hatamim.
Story: Having received Vilensky's address through the Kiryat Sefer editorial board, the Rayatz wrote once more from New York asking for biographical material about R. Chaim Dover Vilensky for the Hatamim journal. He hoped to revive publication of the journal in America, but the plan never materialized.
Tags: rayatz, hatamim, michael vilensky, new york

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes thanks to Justice Louis Brandeis
Summary: On 23 Adar II 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a letter of thanks to Justice Louis Brandeis for his rescue intervention.
Story: The Rebbe credited Brandeis with going beyond promises and immediately undertaking decisive action when no one else could have accomplished what he did. Attorney Asher Rabinowitz, son of Rabbi David Meir Rabinowitz, had worked through Brandeis to secure the rescue.
Tags: brandeis, rabinowitz, rescue, usa, supreme-court

Title: Rebbe wires Riga to spend up to 3,000 lats on Pesach matzah and food for Warsaw
Summary: On 25 Adar Sheni 5700 the Rebbe telegraphed R' Mordechai Chefetz in Riga authorizing shipment of matzah and food packages worth up to 3,000 lats for Pesach relief to anash in Poland.
Story: Chefetz had reported obtaining a Soviet permit to ship 1,600 kilos of matzah and 1,600 kilos of other foodstuffs to Poland, and was already sending roughly 500 lats' worth to brethren in Russia. The Rebbe authorized expanding the operation, ultimately covering $3,000 personally plus $2,000 via Mizrach, with additional small Pesach shipments bringing the total to 6,000 lats.
Tags: pesach, matzah, warsaw, riga, mordechai chefetz, food aid, world war ii

Title: First $2,000 wartime aid transfer via the Mizrach channel from Riga
Summary: On 29 Adar Sheni 5700 the wealthy Yehoshua ben Kalman Mizrach handed the Rebbe $2,000 in Riga so that an equivalent sum could later be released in America for rescue work in Poland and Russia.
Story: Because direct money transfers from the US to occupied Europe were illegal, the Rebbe ran a hidden parallel-payment scheme: Mizrach gave dollars in Riga to R' Mordechai Chefetz, and the Rebbe matched the sum from New York to a beneficiary Mizrach designated. The arrangement was concealed in coded correspondence using terms like 'books,' 'Ben Kalman,' and 'RIVK,' and ultimately moved $5,500 through this single channel.
Tags: mizrach, yehoshua ben kalman, riga, mordechai chefetz, covert finance, world war ii, pidyon shvuyim

Title: New York Released Time statute signed into law
Summary: Governor Herbert Lehman signed the statute approving Released Time for religious instruction during the public school week in New York.
Story: The law allowed public-school children to leave school one hour weekly for religious instruction at nearby venues. The Sixth Rebbe would seize on this in coming years, directing Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch to mobilize a citywide Jewish Released Time program against significant liberal-Jewish opposition.
Tags: released time, governor lehman, public schools, new york

Title: Tena'im in the author's Cherbinov apartment
Summary: On the night of 4 Nisan 5700, ten chassidim gathered in the author's Cherbinov apartment for the formal tena'im, with his father representing the chosson and the bride's uncles R' Zusya and R' Chaim Chanye Paz representing the kallah.
Story: The seasoned businessman father insisted the matter not be left hanging in mid-air, saying, 'Let the child have a name.' R' Zusya brought ten men from the shul — among them R' Sa'adia Liberov and his brother R' Chaim Chanye Paz of Klimovichi — to Cherbinov, and the tena'im were signed on the night before 4 Nisan 5700. The father then returned to Zlobin together with the author's sister Esther.
Tags: moscow, cherbinov, tenaim, engagement, fradkin, paz

Title: R' Mordechai Chefetz reports library shipment from Otwock unexpectedly delayed
Summary: From Riga, R' Mordechai Chefetz writes that the library and manuscripts which had been ready for shipment were suddenly held up, with no explanation given.
Story: Before the Rebbe Rayatz left Warsaw he had arranged with attorney Aharon Blum to handle export of his library and manuscripts. Under the original plan the books were to leave Otwock through Italy in Adar II 5700. In a letter of 6 Nissan, R' Mordechai Chefetz of Riga — who served as the conduit for correspondence with the Hornstein family in Otwock — reported that shipment had inexplicably stalled.
Tags: library, otwock, warsaw, schneersohn-library, mordechai-chefetz, riga, wwii

Title: Rebbe Rayatz travels to Lakewood for a month
Summary: On 8 Nissan 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz moved to Lakewood, New Jersey, where he stayed in a private home for about a month.
Story: After spending nearly a month at the Greystone Hotel in New York, the Rebbe relocated to Lakewood where a residence was placed at his disposal. He would remain there until returning to New York on 7 Iyar.
Tags: lakewood, new-jersey, usa

Title: Rebbe requests reports on the Hassidic yeshiva students' union
Summary: On 9 Nissan 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz asked the union's leaders to send him details of their gatherings.
Story: The Rebbe expressed pleasure at hearing of the students' gatherings and asked to be informed of the topics of the talks. He requested copies of meeting records, the names of students at each yeshiva, and the founding regulations along with any additions.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, igud hatalmidim

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe sends final letters to Anshil Aronovich in Vilna
Summary: On 13 Nissan 5700 the Frierdiker Rebbe sent R. Anshil Aronovich six letters for distribution to chassidim and the yeshiva then operating in Vilna.
Story: This letter, recorded as Iggeret 4382 in volume twelve, is the last known correspondence between the Rebbe and Aronovich, his long-time representative in Vilna. Aronovich was later murdered in the Holocaust.
Tags: vilna, anshil aronovich, 13 nissan, 5700, frierdiker rebbe, yeshiva

Title: Polish authorities revoke library export permit; threat to confiscate Jewish books
Summary: R' Chefetz writes that the export permit for the library was withdrawn and a new decree threatened confiscation of all Hebrew books in occupied Poland.
Story: On 13 Nissan, R' Mordechai Chefetz received word — and a confirming visit from the wife and son of R' Shmuel Zalmanov — that the German occupation authorities had revoked the library's export license and issued a general order that all sefarim in Poland would be confiscated. The disclosure put the entire Schneersohn library at imminent risk.
Tags: library, warsaw, poland, nazis, schneersohn-library, mordechai-chefetz, zalmanov

Title: Rebbe encourages Avraham Tzvi Segal to join Tomchei Tmimim
Summary: On 13 Nissan 5700 the Rebbe encouraged Pinsk student Avraham Tzvi Segal in his desire to study at Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: Responding to the Pinsk student's longing for a chassidic yeshiva, the Rebbe told him to thank Hashem for awakening such a desire and assured him that Hashem had arranged the opportunity to realize it at Tomchei Tmimim. Segal eventually became a student at the Vilna yeshiva and its union secretary.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, avraham tzvi segal, pinsk, tomchei tmimim

Title: Letter to R. Chaim Ozer requesting 100 Palestine certificates
Summary: On Isru Chag Pesach 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz asked R. Chaim Ozer Grodzinski to allocate at least one hundred Palestine certificates for Lubavitch students and their teachers.
Story: Hearing that R. Chaim Ozer was about to receive a batch of British certificates through Rabbi Herzog's intervention, the Rebbe wrote requesting that the committee under R. Chaim Ozer's leadership reserve at least one hundred for Tomchei Tmimim talmidim and their rashei yeshiva. This was part of a parallel track to the American visa effort.
Tags: chaim ozer grodzinski, palestine, certificates, tomchei tmimim, lubavitch

Title: Eber plans departure via Italy on May 28
Summary: On 5 Iyar 5700, R. Mordechai Chefetz wrote that R. Yehuda Eber had a permit to travel via Italy and planned to sail May 28.
Story: On 5 Iyar 5700, R. Mordechai Chefetz reported to the Frierdiker Rebbe that R. Yehuda Eber had received a transit permit through Italy and intended to depart on a ship leaving from there May 28. Two weeks later, however, the route was cut off when no ship was available.
Tags: riga, italy, rescue, yehuda eber

Title: Letter to Rabbi Herzog on Palestine certificates for Polish yeshiva students
Summary: On 1 Iyar 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz again wrote to Chief Rabbi Herzog asking that a portion of the new certificates be placed at his disposal for Lubavitch students still in Poland.
Story: With the British certificates being prepared for Polish yeshiva students, the Rebbe pressed Rabbi Herzog to reserve a known number for him personally to allocate to Tomchei Tmimim talmidim, some still in Poland and some already rescued. He also wrote the same day to R. Chanoch Hendel Havlin in Eretz Yisrael coordinating the request through R. Chaim Ozer.
Tags: isaac herzog, palestine, certificates, tomchei tmimim, poland

Title: Rebbe allocates $1200 between Dankra and Livenhof
Summary: Now in the US, the Rebbe wrote on Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5700 instructing how to split $1200 sent via Mordechai Chefetz between the two Latvian branches.
Story: After arriving in America, the Frierdiker Rebbe managed to send $1200 to Mordechai Chefetz in Riga. On 1 Iyar 5700 he wrote (Igrot vol. 12, no. 4391) directing that R. Berchen receive 100 lats per month for the Dankra yeshiva and 50 lats per month, from Nissan onward, for the Livenhof branch.
Tags: dankra, livenhof, latvia, mordechai-chefetz, usa, wwii, tomchei-temimim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz returns from Lakewood to New York
Summary: On 7 Iyar 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz returned from Lakewood to New York, where he again stayed in a hotel.
Story: He remained in a New York hotel through the summer months while plans for a permanent residence and headquarters were finalized.
Tags: lakewood, new-york, usa

Title: First Achos Tmimim Dvinsk farbrengen with Riga delegation
Summary: On 6 Iyar 5700 the first formal farbrengen of Achos Tmimim Dvinsk was held, attended by three delegates from the Riga central office.
Story: Mrs. Basya Chefetz, Mrs. Mina Skobla, and Mrs. Rivka Kramnikov traveled from Riga to attend. About fourteen girls came from Dvinsk. R. Peletz opened the gathering on the purpose of Chassidus, and three girls - Mrs. Kayder, Mrs. Zelikman, and Mrs. Kaufman - addressed the group. The Rebbe responded with a 200-lat gift to seed a gemach for Achos Tmimim Dvinsk.
Tags: achos-tmimim, dvinsk, riga, farbrengen, pinkovich

Title: Lag BaOmer farbrengen held at Tomchei Tmimim Vilna
Summary: On Lag BaOmer 5700, R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch led a farbrengen at the Vilna yeshiva attended by local anash.
Story: Mashpia R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch arranged that the Kerzner minyan announce the farbrengen, and over a minyan from each of the Kerzner and Apatow chassidim joined. At the gathering he repeated the maamar 'Ein HaKadosh Baruch Hu Ba B'Trunya' of the Rebbe Rashab.
Tags: lag baomer, vilna, farbrengen, yehoshua isaac baruch

Title: Rayatz blesses Hillel Horwitz engagement
Summary: On 20 Iyar 5700 the Rebbe wrote to R. Yitzchak Matmid Horwitz blessing the engagement of his son Hillel to the daughter of R. Rafael Cohen.
Story: In the same letter the Rebbe addressed efforts to secure Hillel a rabbinical position in Livenhof. The Rebbe also wrote on the same date to Achos Tmimim Dvinsk acknowledging their first farbrengen and to R. Mordechai Chefetz about their Pesach gatherings.
Tags: rayatz, hillel-horwitz, yitzchak-matmid, engagement

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe writes Pidyon Nefesh for daughter trapped in Paris
Summary: On 21 Iyar 5700, while crossing to America, the Frierdiker Rebbe entered a special Pidyon Nefesh in his diary for his daughter and son-in-law in Paris.
Story: The prayer asked Heaven to protect Chaya Mushka and Menachem Mendel — the latter not a French citizen and registered for national defense service — and to soften the heart of the American consul to grant their visa. The text was written in the days surrounding the German advance on France, capturing the family's acute fear for the couple stranded in Paris.
Tags: paris, wwii, france, ramash, chaya mushka, prayer

Title: Joint telegram requesting American ship berths
Summary: On 22 Iyar 5700, Feigin and Eber jointly telegraphed the Rebbe requesting help booking berths on an American ship.
Story: On 30 May 1940 / 22 Iyar 5700, R. Yechezkel Feigin and R. Yehuda Eber jointly cabled the Frierdiker Rebbe requesting his help to book berths on an American vessel. They asked the shipping company to wire Cook's Riga office authorization to sell them tickets, and sought guidance on whether to try the Italian sailing if it materialized.
Tags: riga, rescue, telegram, yechezkel feigin, yehuda eber

Title: R. Chaim Liberman writes to Mendel Rosenbaum for father's biography
Summary: On 22 Iyar 5700 the secretary R. Chaim Liberman wrote in Yiddish to Mendel Rosenbaum requesting a biography of his father, the Chasid R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum.
Story: Acting on behalf of the Rayatz, secretary Chaim Liberman wrote to Mendel Rosenbaum, recently arrived in America, asking him to compose a full biography of his father R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum. The letter explained that former Lubavitch yeshiva students were producing collections devoted entirely to Chabad Chasidism and Chasidim of past generations.
Tags: chaim liberman, mendel rosenbaum, avraham chaim rosenbaum, hatamim, yiddish

Title: R. Shmuel Tzvi Lisson reports Lag B'Omer farbrengen in Ponevezh
Summary: On 23 Iyar 5700 the Ponevezh mashpia R. Shmuel Tzvi Lisson reported a Lag B'Omer farbrengen at which a maamar was repeated and chassidim drank lechaim.
Story: Lisson, who had studied at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch from 5660 to 5669 and served as Ponevezh mashpia since 5669, wrote that the gathering was held at both Chabad minyanim in the city. The chassidim prayed for the speedy revelation of the wellsprings of Baal Shem Tov's teachings.
Tags: ponevezh, lithuania, lag b'omer, 5700, farbrengen, shmuel tzvi lisson

Title: Rabbi Baruch reports to the Rebbe on Vilna yeshiva life
Summary: On 23 Iyar 5700 R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch sent a detailed report to the Rebbe about Vilna yeshiva activities.
Story: Baruch described a kiddusha rabba for new arriving students that ran until evening, the Lag BaOmer and Pesach Sheni farbrengens, and the system he had instituted for monitoring both nigleh and chassidus learning. At the time there were 26 students in the senior group.
Tags: yehoshua isaac baruch, vilna, tomchei tmimim, rebbe rayatz

Title: Reports on 2 and 13 Nissan hilula observances
Summary: On 23 Iyar 5700, after the outbreak of WWII, R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch reported on Nissan hilula observances across Lithuania.
Story: Even after the war had broken out in Europe but before the German conquest of Lithuania, R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch continued his correspondence. He reported to the Rebbe Rayatz on hisva'aduyos held for the 2 Nissan (Rebbe Rashab) and 13 Nissan (Tzemach Tzedek) yahrzeits in Panidel, Kelm, Anishishok, Ponevezh, and Taurage, including the daily Tanya shiur of R.
