Yehoshua Asher Rotfeld's chaburah.
Tags: nissan, iyar, rebbe-rashab, tzemach-tzedek, panidel, kelm, anishishok, ponevezh, taurage, lithuania, war

Title: Breckinridge Long memo instructs State Department to obstruct Jewish immigration
Summary: Assistant Secretary of State Breckinridge Long circulated a memo urging consular officials worldwide to 'delay and effectively stop' Jewish immigration to the US.
Story: Long instructed US representatives to 'put every obstacle in the way' of refugees and to 'postpone and postpone and postpone the granting of the visas.' The memo crystallized the bureaucratic anti-Semitism that had nearly prevented the Rebbe's own rescue and would doom countless others seeking refuge from the Nazis.
Tags: washington, united states, breckinridge long, state department, immigration, refugees, anti-semitism

Title: Shavuot celebrated joyfully at Ponevezh Chabad minyan
Summary: On both days of Shavuot 5700 the Chabad minyan in Ponevezh studied Chassidus, read the Baal Shem Tov's letter on his ascent of soul, and held a celebratory meal of the Chevra Tehillim.
Story: R. Shmuel Tzvi Lisson reported to the Frierdiker Rebbe that the chassidim learned the maamar 'Va'ehyeh Etzlo Amun' from Likutei Torah on the first day and held a festive meal with dancing on the second. The Soviet occupation had not yet extinguished chassidic joy.
Tags: ponevezh, shavuot, 5700, chevra tehillim, shmuel tzvi lisson

Title: New opportunity emerges to ship Schneersohn library to USA
Summary: After months of impasse, attorney Aharon Blum in Warsaw signals via R' Y.L. Blum of Vilna that shipment of the library to America is again possible.
Story: On 3 Sivan, R' Chefetz reported to the Rebbe Rayatz that R' Yisroel Yaakov Ever had received word from Vilna that Aharon Blum needed an additional 500 sefarim of Rashi (i.e., dollars) to renew the shipment. The Rebbe authorized payment, and R' Ever wrote urgently to Blum to dispatch the library at once.
Tags: library, warsaw, schneersohn-library, aharon-blum, yisroel-yaakov-ever, mordechai-chefetz

Title: Future Rebbe and Rebbetzin flee Paris to Vichy
Summary: As the Germans entered Paris, the future Rebbe and Rebbetzin escaped by train to Vichy, arriving Erev Shavuot 5700 toward evening.
Story: With the Paris train station overwhelmed by Jews fleeing the Wehrmacht, the future Rebbe's enlistment in the French army eased his passage out of the city. The couple reached Vichy on Erev Shavuot and would remain there about two and a half months before continuing south. The Rebbetzin later related these events to the chronicler.
Tags: paris, vichy, france, wwii, escape, ramash, chaya mushka

Title: R. Berchen reports founding Livani branch
Summary: On Erev Shavuos 5700 Yeshaya Chanoch Berchen wrote the Rebbe that, after great effort, the Livani branch had been established with students from Riga and the region.
Story: In an Erev Shavuos 5700 letter R. Berchen described how, after toil and travail, they finally succeeded in founding the small yeshiva in Livani, staffed by Tzvi Cohen and Shalom Ber Asherov who had relocated there. A planned Preili branch failed for lack of a teacher willing to relocate, and the Riga vaad had functionally collapsed. He confirmed receipt of $50 toward Livani.
Tags: livani, livenhof, latvia, tzvi-cohen, shalom-ber-asherov, tomchei-temimim

Title: The Rebbe and Rebbetzin flee Paris on erev Shavuot
Summary: On erev Shavuot 5700 the Rebbe and Rebbetzin fled Paris for Vichy as the Nazis advanced into France.
Story: With Nazi forces overrunning France, the Rebbe and Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka escaped from Paris on erev Shavuot 5700. They traveled to Vichy where they remained for several months attempting to secure American immigration papers. The flight began a year of wandering across France that would not end until their arrival in New York in Sivan 5701.
Tags: paris, vichy, france, war, wwii, escape

Title: Soviet army enters Vilna on Shavuot eve
Summary: On Shavuot eve 5700, Soviet tanks rolled past the Vilna yeshiva's beis hamidrash as students recited Tikkun Leil Shavuot.
Story: During the recitation of Tikkun Leil Shavuot, students heard the heavy chains of Soviet tanks moving on the main street opposite the yeshiva. The Red Army was occupying Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia. A heavy dread fell over the Jewish community, especially Torah students, but the Soviets initially refrained from closing the yeshivot and allowed the Joint to continue supporting Jewish refugees.
Tags: soviet union, lithuania, vilna, wwii, shavuot, occupation

Title: Soviet Union occupies Lithuania during Shavuot
Summary: On Shavuot 5700 the Soviets occupied Lithuania, fusing Vilna into the same Soviet bloc as Russian-held Poland and making border smuggling vastly harder.
Story: With both eastern Poland and Lithuania now under Soviet rule, the smugglers who had been bringing Tomchei Temimim students into Vilna lost their motivation: any 'merchandise' they delivered would simply remain under the same Soviet authorities. The shift dramatically tightened the noose around the students still stranded in Poland.
Tags: lithuania, soviet union, russia, vilna, wwii, war, borders

Title: Soviet Union invades Latvia
Summary: Soviet forces invaded Latvia, fulfilling the fears that had driven the urgency to extract the Rebbe from Riga only months earlier.
Story: The Chasidim's warnings to US officials that the Rebbe and his entourage faced execution under a Soviet regime proved well founded. Latvia remained under Soviet control until regaining independence in 1991, validating the rescue coalition's insistence that Riga could only be a temporary haven and that America was the sole durable refuge.
Tags: latvia, soviet union, russia, occupation, riga

Title: Rayatz responds to Yehoshua Isaac Baruch on Vilna talmidim and Lithuanian anash
Summary: On 14 Sivan 5700, the Rayatz wrote R' Yehoshua Isaac Baruch acknowledging his detailed report on the Tomchei Tmimim talmidim studying in Vilna and on anash in Lithuania.
Story: The mashpia R' Yehoshua Isaac Baruch was on the ground with the talmidim and corresponded directly with the Rayatz about their condition. The Rebbe's reply (Igrot Kodesh vol. 12, letter 4408) expresses satisfaction at the fullness of the information. Over the following year the Rayatz wrote frequently about the talmidim's situation and their eventual rescue.
Tags: rayatz, yehoshua isaac baruch, tomchei tmimim, vilna, lithuania, wwii

Title: Rebbe replies to Rabbi Baruch's Vilna yeshiva report
Summary: On 14 Sivan 5700 the Rebbe responded with satisfaction to R. Baruch's detailed report on the Vilna yeshiva.
Story: The Rebbe wrote that he greatly enjoyed the detailed account of the students and anash of Lithuania and asked to be kept informed of subsequent reports from anash. He blessed the students and confirmed that the arrangements Baruch had set in place at the yeshiva were excellent.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, yehoshua isaac baruch, vilna

Title: Rashag appeals to Latvian envoy in Washington
Summary: On 17 Sivan 5700 / June 23, 1940, the Rashag wrote to Latvian envoy Alfred Bilmanis seeking Finnish diplomatic help for the refugees.
Story: On June 23, 1940 / 17 Sivan 5700, the Rashag wrote to Alfred Bilmanis at the Latvian embassy in Washington following a phone conversation. He listed the Hornstein, Eber, and Feigin families with their dates of birth, noted they held US visas, and asked Bilmanis to request Finland's envoy to instruct his Riga embassy to facilitate transit through Petsamo.
Tags: washington, latvia, finland, rescue, rashag, diplomacy

Title: Rebbe asks union manager to send regular updates
Summary: On 19 Sivan 5700 the Rebbe asked Avraham Tzvi Segal to write him regularly about the union's progress.
Story: Writing to Segal, the Rebbe asked him to keep him informed regarding fellow students in and outside the union. He blessed all the students with success in study and yiras shamayim, that they should widen the borders of bnei Torah and illuminate the darkness of the world.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, igud hatalmidim, avraham tzvi segal

Title: Rebbe writes Dr. Yang that yeshivot continue under Soviet rule
Summary: On Erev Shabbat Shelach 5700 the Rebbe wrote to Dr. Yang that despite Soviet occupation, the Lithuanian and Latvian yeshivot remained intact.
Story: The Rebbe reported receiving telegrams from Vilna and Riga indicating that, despite the entry of Soviet forces into Lithuania and Latvia, the situation of the yeshivot was unchanged and their continued operation had not been impaired. He confirmed the wellbeing of the yeshivot and 'our dear students.'
Tags: rebbe rayatz, dr yang, soviet union, vilna, yeshivos, wwii

Title: Letter to Rabbi Meir Ashkenazi of Shanghai on transit visas
Summary: On 27 Sivan 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Rabbi Meir Ashkenazi, rabbi of Shanghai, exploring rescue of the Vilna students via transit visas through China.
Story: With the Atlantic route closed, the Rebbe asked Rabbi Ashkenazi to obtain transit visas for the students so they could travel through Russia and on to Shanghai en route to America. This Far East route would soon prove the only viable corridor and would shape the entire rescue plan that followed.
Tags: meir ashkenazi, shanghai, china, transit visa, rescue, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rebbe responds to Berchen on Latvian yeshivot
Summary: On 5 Tammuz 5700 the Frierdiker Rebbe replied to Berchen with blessings for students, teachers and supporters of the Dankra and Livani branches.
Story: Replying on 5 Tammuz 5700 (Igrot vol. 12, no. 4426), the Frierdiker Rebbe expressed great satisfaction at hearing news of the talmidim at Dankra and Livani. He asked Berchen to convey his brachos to the students for health and success in Torah, and to their teachers and supporters.
Tags: dankra, livani, latvia, yeshaya-chanoch-berchen, tomchei-temimim

Title: Wedding of the author at the Marina-Roshcha synagogue, Moscow
Summary: On 9 Tammuz 5700 the author married Henya Chasha Fradkin of Shumyachi, with kabbalas panim and chuppah held at the Marina-Roshcha synagogue and the meal in a neighbour's house next door.
Story: The principal mechutanim from the bride's side were her mother Feigl, her brother Gershon, and her uncle R' Zusya the shamash with his daughter. R' Yakov 'Yana' Goray of Romen and R' Shmarya Sasonkin (Batumer), who had fled Leningrad, were among the chassidim who attended. Because of the Soviet climate of fear, no invitations were sent and no photographs were taken.
Tags: moscow, marina-roshcha, marriage, fradkin, no-photos, kgb-fear

Title: 12 Tammuz farbrengen held quietly in wartime Ponevezh
Summary: On 12 Tammuz 5700, with Soviet occupation underway, more than ten chassidim gathered at R. Shmuel Tzvi Lisson's minyan in Ponevezh, drank mashke and repeated a maamar.
Story: Lisson wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe that 'the time caused it' that the celebration could not be public as in previous years. Despite the dangers of the new Soviet regime in Lithuania, the chassidim marked the Frierdiker Rebbe's redemption day in private.
Tags: ponevezh, lithuania, 12 tammuz, 5700, war, farbrengen, shmuel tzvi lisson

Title: Underground Yud-Beis Tammuz farbrengen during the author's sheva brachos
Summary: Because Yud-Beis Tammuz 5700 fell within the author's sheva brachos, his home in Cherbinov became the disguised venue for a clandestine Chag HaGeulah farbrengen led by R' Nissan Nemenov and attended by R' B-Z Shemtov, R' Dovid Bravman and many others.
Story: With public farbrengens impossible, R' Zusya the shamash quietly redirected anyone asking where to celebrate Yud-Beis Tammuz to the author's home, since the sheva brachos provided a cover for the NKVD. Chassidim arrived from the tram carrying a suitcase of mashke and farbeisen; the house and courtyard filled, and they danced 'Veharikosi lochem brocho' so vigorously that the floor began to creak. R' Yona Cohen broke up the gathering at dawn so that participants could leave individually — a neighbour across the lane worked for the NKVD.
Tags: moscow, yud-beis-tammuz, frierdiker-rebbe, farbrengen, nissan-nemenov, shemtov, nkvd-fear

Title: Report on Shabbos Mevarchim Tammuz farbrengens
Summary: In a letter of 18 Tammuz 5700, R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch described Shabbos Mevarchim Tammuz observances of tehillim, Chassidus and farbrengens in Kovno and Vizun.
Story: R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch reported the full Shabbos Mevarchim Tammuz seder in Kovno: tehillim said by the community, a Chassidus shiur, davening, and a farbrengen lasting until mincha. R. Yosef Genkin in Vizun wrote separately that they had also observed Shabbos Mevarchim with tehillim and a farbrengen, and intended to mark 12 Tammuz similarly.
Tags: tammuz, shabbos-mevarchim, kovno, vizun, yosef-genkin, lithuania

Title: Vilna Temimim send coded letter to Rebbe about arrested students
Summary: On 19 Tammuz 5700, students in Vilna sent the Rebbe a heavily coded letter reporting Soviet arrests of Tomchei Temimim and renewed efforts to smuggle them out.
Story: Disguising names and events as a commercial correspondence about 'merchants' and 'merchandise,' the students reported that Shmuel Arbis, Avraham Rayevski, and Shraga of Lodz had been imprisoned, while Yisrael Ratzer was in hiding. They feared the prisoners would be deported to Siberia and described how R. Yehuda Eber, then in Riga, had authorized resuming costly smuggling attempts despite tighter Soviet border controls.
Tags: vilna, poland, soviet union, nkvd, tomchei temimim, arrest, siberia, rescue, samizdat

Title: Vilna yeshiva students begin learning trades
Summary: On 18 Tammuz 5700 senior Vilna students began learning trades including shechita, sofrus and milah.
Story: R. Baruch reported that Yosef Weinberg, Gershon Chanovitz and Moshe Eliyahu Gerlitzky began learning poultry shechita (about six weeks of training, two hours daily). Menachem Zev Greenglass and Chaim Leib Praffs took up stam writing for four weeks, three hours daily, while Tzvi Fuchs began learning milah. Baruch approved these vocational studies given wartime conditions.
Tags: vilna, shechita, stam, milah, vocational, wwii

Title: Library rerouted via Stettin-Stockholm to evade Soviet-occupied Latvia
Summary: R' Chefetz telegrams from Riga that the 100 crates en route to him should instead be sent via Stettin to Stockholm rather than reaching Soviet-controlled Latvia.
Story: By late July the Soviets had annexed Latvia and installed a Communist regime. R' Chefetz — citing his poor health and unable to receive the books in Riga — instructed Schenker shipping to redirect the cargo through Stettin and on to Stockholm, to wait there for transit to New York. The reroute spared the library from Soviet confiscation.
Tags: library, stettin, stockholm, riga, latvia, soviet-union, schenker, schneersohn-library, mordechai-chefetz

Title: Reports on 12-13 Tammuz Geulah celebrations
Summary: On 24 Tammuz 5700 R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch reported to the Rebbe Rayatz on 12-13 Tammuz farbrengens across Lithuania.
Story: R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch transmitted reports from R. Leib Kamraz of Ushpol, R. Zev Razinkevitch of Birz (joined by bochurim from the Novardok yeshiva), R. Yosef Genkin of Vizun (who said the maamar 'Baruch HaGomel l'Chayavim Tovos'), and R. Itche Bangs of Taurage on the Chag HaGeulah farbrengens.
Tags: 12-13-tammuz, chag-hageulah, ushpol, birz, vizun, taurage, lithuania, novardok

Title: Future Rebbe and Rebbetzin reach Nice under Italian zone
Summary: In Av 5700 the future Rebbe and Rebbetzin left Vichy southward for Nice, then under Italian control and a refuge for many Jews.
Story: After roughly two and a half months in Vichy, it became clear that the German-subordinate Vichy regime was equally dangerous for Jews. The couple moved to Nice, where they would spend 8–9 months while the Frierdiker Rebbe coordinated intensive efforts from New York to secure their visas, travel papers, and basic provisions including matzah and an esrog for Sukkos.
Tags: vichy, nice, france, italy, wwii, ramash, chaya mushka

Title: Soviet annexation of Lithuania closes Kovno consulates
Summary: In summer 5700 Lithuania ceased to exist as an independent state and became part of the Soviet Union, forcing the Japanese consulate in Kovno to close.
Story: Sugihara told the refugees he was being recalled because Lithuania was no longer independent and a Japanese consul existed in Moscow. Before leaving he reportedly entrusted his stamp to a yeshiva student so that hundreds more passports could still be stamped with transit visas after the consulate officially closed.
Tags: lithuania, ussr, soviet union, kovno, annexation, world war ii

Title: Sugihara issues Japanese transit visas to Mir and Tomchei Tmimim students
Summary: In summer 5700 Japanese consul Chiune Sugihara in Kovno issued transit visas to yeshiva students, including Tomchei Tmimim talmidim, on the advice of the Amshinover Rebbe.
Story: Mir students from Holland first obtained Dutch visas to Curacao and then Japanese transit visas through Sugihara in Kovno. The Amshinover Rebbe, R. Shimon Shalom Kalish, urged the rest of the refugees to follow suit. After telegraphing the Rebbe Rayatz, the Tomchei Tmimim students did the same and obtained Japanese transit visas before the consulate closed when Lithuania was absorbed into the Soviet Union.
Tags: chiune sugihara, japan, kovno, lithuania, transit visa, amshinov rebbe, mir yeshiva, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz approves new shipping route in three telegrams
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz cables attorney Blum and the Schenker shipping offices in Warsaw and Berlin authorizing the Stettin-Stockholm route.
Story: On 26 Tammuz / 1 August 1940, the Rebbe Rayatz dispatched three telegrams instructing that the library be redirected to Eydtkuhnen and on through Stettin to Stockholm, where it would be held until shipment to New York became feasible. R' Chefetz confirmed three days later that the cargo had been halted and rerouted as instructed.
Tags: library, schenker, stettin, stockholm, warsaw, berlin, schneersohn-library

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe cables son-in-law about manuscripts
Summary: On 6 Av 5700 the Frierdiker Rebbe cabled the future Rebbe in Vichy asking about his health and whether he had taken the family's books and manuscripts.
Story: The cable referred to the trunks of seforim and ksav-yad in the future Rebbe's possession, including his wedding gift books, photographic volumes of the Rebbe Rashab's maamarim, and his own Reshimos. Many of these manuscripts, preserved through the wartime ordeal, are today housed in the Chabad library.
Tags: vichy, france, manuscripts, reshimos, rashab, ramash

Title: Report on Shabbos Mevarchim Av and tamim Zelig Glass tour
Summary: On the eve of 8 Av 5700, R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch reported on the visiting tamim Zelig Glass who delivered Chassidus across Lithuanian shtetlach.
Story: R. Yosef Genkin wrote that the tamim Zelig Glass had spent Shabbos Mevarchim Av in Vizun, delivering the maamar 'Ma Tovu' before three minyanim. The tamim Glass also spent four Shabbosos in Autian and visited the Amshinover Rebbe's shtibel in Kovno. R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch's brother-in-law R. Moshe Yosef Gottlieb meanwhile delivered Chassidus in Kovno every Shabbos.
Tags: av, shabbos-chazon, vizun, kovno, autian, zelig-glass, amshinov, lithuania

Title: 770 Eastern Parkway purchased by Agudas Chassidei Chabad
Summary: Chabad purchased a three-story brownstone at 770 Eastern Parkway in Crown Heights to serve as the Rebbe's permanent residence and headquarters.
Story: Rejecting Brownsville and suburban options, the Rebbe selected prestigious Crown Heights despite there being only three Chabad families in the neighborhood. The building, originally built as a doctor's home and clinic by architect Edwin Kline, had an elevator essential to the Rebbe's mobility. It would become the iconic '770,' replicated worldwide.
Tags: 770, crown heights, eastern parkway, 12 av, agudas chassidei chabad

Title: 770 Eastern Parkway purchased for the Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: On 12 Menachem Av 5700, the building at 770 Eastern Parkway in Brooklyn was purchased as the Rebbe Rayatz's residence and headquarters.
Story: The acquisition of 770 Eastern Parkway marked the establishment of what would become the permanent center of Chabad-Lubavitch worldwide. The purchase was completed during the Rebbe's stay at a New York hotel.
Tags: 770, eastern-parkway, brooklyn, headquarters, real-estate

Title: First railcar with 100 crates of Schneersohn library leaves Stettin for Stockholm
Summary: Attorney Aharon Blum reports by postcard that a railcar with 100 cases of sefarim has been dispatched from Stettin toward Stockholm.
Story: On 16 Menachem Av, Blum confirmed that the first transport — 100 cases — was on its way from Stettin to Stockholm. A second railcar with 17 additional cases remained in Warsaw pending further payment. Blum sent repeated reminders through autumn 1940, but the second shipment never left Poland.
Tags: library, stettin, stockholm, warsaw, schneersohn-library, aharon-blum

Title: Rebbe approves vocational training for Vilna students
Summary: On 17 Av 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz approved the Vilna students learning shechita, sofrus and crafts.
Story: Writing to R. Baruch, the Rebbe endorsed Yosef Weinberg and Gershon Chanovitz's shechita studies and Menachem Zev Greenglass and Chaim Leib's stam studies. He suggested that if other students were similarly inspired, an 'artel' of craftsmen should be organized among the students, given the conditions of the time.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, vilna, vocational, shechita, stam

Title: First visa application list for 47 anash families submitted to US government
Summary: On 22 August 1940 (18 Menachem Av 5700) Agudas Chabad submitted to the US government a first list of 47 visa applications — covering over 100 souls — together with a seven-paragraph petition signed by the Rebbe.
Story: The petition asked for temporary visas to shelter anash in America until the war ended. It accompanied a separate list of 127 yeshiva-student visas already in process. A second batch of 62 visas covering roughly 200 more souls would follow in November, after which attorney Arthur Rabinowitz filed a consolidated brief through Rashag.
Tags: visas, united states, agudas chabad, immigration, rescue, world war ii, state department

Title: Rebbe directs Kollel Chabad funds to support Vilna yeshiva
Summary: On 25 Av 5700 the Rebbe instructed that Kollel Chabad funds collected in Lithuania be redirected to the Vilna yeshiva.
Story: Through coded language about a 'Ramban commentary,' the Rebbe arranged for monies collected in Lithuania for Kollel Chabad (Kupat Rabbi Meir Baal Hanes) to be given to R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch to support the Vilna yeshiva. The Rebbe undertook to remit equivalent funds to Kollel Chabad in Eretz Yisroel.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, vilna, kollel chabad, yeshiva funding

Title: Tomchei Tmimim bochurim arrested in Kursk
Summary: In late Av or early Elul 5700 the NKVD arrested all the bochurim of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Kursk, including the author's brother-in-law Gershon Fradkin.
Story: Coming to daven at the Marina-Roshcha shul, the author was told by R' Zusya that the entire Kursk yeshiva had been seized. During the search of Gershon's lodgings the NKVD had found a postcard addressed to the author's Cherbinov apartment and taken it with them. The author's mother-in-law rushed to Kursk to plead for Gershon, his wife went to Shumyachi to nurse her ailing father, and the author himself fled to his parents in Zlobin to wait out the Yamim Noraim.
Tags: kursk, tomchei-tmimim, nkvd, arrest, fradkin, postcard

Title: Menachem Zev Greenglass travels to Telz yeshiva
Summary: On 15 Elul 5700 Menachem Zev Greenglass was sent to the Telz yeshiva on a mission for Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: Sent by mashpia R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch, Greenglass traveled to Telz primarily to enroll a talented young orphan in the yeshiva there. While there he also studied with and held farbrengens with the local Hassidic-lineage students.
Tags: telz, greenglass, shliach, yehoshua isaac baruch

Title: 52 US visas secured for Tomchei Tmimim students
Summary: On 16 Elul 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz reported that 52 student visas and 47 rabbinic visas had been obtained for entry to the United States.
Story: Writing to R. Yaakov Katz, the Rebbe announced the breakthrough that 52 entry permits for students and 47 for rabbis, their families and rashei yeshiva had been secured. The first list contained mostly senior Tomchei Tmimim talmidim from the Otwock branch and became the basis of the first rescue convoy through Russia and Japan.
Tags: usa, visas, tomchei tmimim, vilna, rescue, yaakov katz

Title: Hillel Horwitz marries Rivka Cohen
Summary: On 17 Elul 5700, R. Hillel Horwitz - son of R. Yitzchak Matmid - married Rivka, daughter of R. Rafael Cohen.
Story: The Rebbe had blessed the engagement on 20 Iyar 5700 and worked to secure a rabbinical position for Hillel in the town of Livenhof (Livani), writing to R. Mordechai Dubin on 29 Nissan to advocate for the appointment. R. Yitzchak Matmid sent the Rebbe a wedding invitation with a pidyon nefesh attached.
Tags: hillel-horwitz, rivka-cohen, rafael-cohen, yitzchak-matmid, wedding

Title: Chai Elul farbrengen at Telz led by Greenglass
Summary: On Chai Elul 5700, Menachem Zev Greenglass led a Hassidic farbrengen in Telz attended by close to 30 students.
Story: After mincha at the home of R. Tzvi Merkin, close to three minyanim of students gathered, including the son-in-law of Reb Elchanan Wasserman. Greenglass spoke about the chiddush of the Baal Shem Tov, sang Chabad niggunim including the niggun of the Alter Rebbe, and recited the maamar of Yom Tov Shel Rosh Hashana 5666.
Tags: chai elul, telz, baal shem tov, farbrengen, greenglass

Title: Rebbe Rayatz moves into 770 Eastern Parkway
Summary: On 19 Elul 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz moved into his private residence at 770 Eastern Parkway in Brooklyn.
Story: The move into 770 marked the formal establishment of the building as the residence of the Rebbe and headquarters of Chabad-Lubavitch. From this address the movement's American rebirth and global expansion would unfold over the coming decades.
Tags: 770, eastern-parkway, brooklyn, headquarters, chabad-center

Title: Sixth Rebbe moves into 770 Eastern Parkway
Summary: Just after Chai Elul, the birthday of the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe, the Sixth Rebbe took up residence in his newly acquired Crown Heights home.
Story: Chasidim described overflowing joy at finally seeing the Rebbe in a permanent base. Avraham Pariz wrote of indescribable happiness on every face, though Avraham Hecht noted that the celebration was tinged with anxiety as European Jewry was being consumed by war even as American Chabad took root.
Tags: 770, crown heights, chai elul

Title: HaKriah VeHaKedushah monthly magazine launched
Summary: The Sixth Rebbe launched HaKriah VeHaKedushah, a monthly Yiddish magazine calling for spiritual renewal and immediate teshuvah as a response to the war.
Story: Published from late 1940 through the war's end, the magazine carried the Rebbe's call of 'L'alter leteshuvah, l'alter legeulah' — immediate repentance prompts redemption. A small English section was added in April 1941. Its message was that prayer and repentance would catalyze divine deliverance.
Tags: hakriah vehakedushah, yiddish, teshuvah, wwii, kehot

Title: Latvian branches consolidate in Riga
Summary: At the start of Tishrei 5701 the three Latvian branches (Riga, Dankra, Livenhof) merged in Riga as Dankra became untenable.
Story: By Tishrei 5701 conditions in Dankra had become unbearable and the yeshiva relocated to Riga, where it joined the Livenhof branch and the Riga branch reopened in 5699. R. Berchen wrote the Rebbe on 6 Tishrei 5701 in coded language about his sons (the students) having left him for Riga to continue their studies, hinting at the move under Soviet censorship.
Tags: riga, dankra, livenhof, latvia, wwii, soviet-occupation, tomchei-temimim

Title: Greenglass reports to Rebbe on Telz mission
Summary: On 7 Tishrei 5701 Greenglass reported to the Rebbe in detail on his recent Telz mission.
Story: Greenglass described placing the young orphan at the Telz yeshiva with the help of R. Tzvi Merkin and Yehuda Leib Mintz, the Chai Elul farbrengen he had led, and his shiur in Tanya chapter 29 with local Hassidic-lineage students. He also reported on a new student, Yehuda Leib Mintz, with whom he had begun studying maamarim.
Tags: telz, greenglass, rebbe rayatz, vilna

Title: R. Eliyahu Moshe Lis writes Rebbe about wife's plan to flee Poland
Summary: On 7 Tishrei 5701, R. Eliyahu Moshe Lis informed the Rebbe that his wife Golda had registered to leave Biala for Vilna, fearing she might share his brother's fate of Siberian exile.
Story: Lis, who served as mashgiach in the Vilna yeshiva, had left his wife Golda and daughters Rachel Miriam and Bluma behind in Biala. He worried that registering to cross into Soviet-held Lithuania could mean deportation to Siberia, as had happened to his older brother Chaim Meir. His family ultimately remained in Poland and perished in the Holocaust while he escaped via Shanghai to America.
Tags: poland, vilna, lithuania, soviet union, siberia, biala, eliyahu moshe lis, rescue, family

Title: US Interior Department forwards visa list to Moscow and Tokyo embassies
Summary: On 31 October 1940 the US Interior Department notified the Rebbe Rayatz that the approved visa name list had been sent to the US embassies in Moscow and Tokyo.
Story: Because of wartime conditions the visas could not be issued at the US embassy in Lithuania. Washington forwarded copies of the approved names to Moscow, where students could collect them in transit, and also to Tokyo as a fallback for any who failed to obtain them in Moscow.
Tags: usa, visas, moscow, tokyo, japan, ussr, state department

Title: Gershon Fradkin released from solitary confinement in Kursk
Summary: In Cheshvan 5701 Gershon Fradkin returned to Moscow after being released from solitary confinement in Kursk, where he had spent all of Tishrei.
Story: Gershon had been the last bochur to arrive in Kursk before the mass arrest and had 'not yet had time to sin much,' so the NKVD released him alone. He spent all of Tishrei — Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Simchas Torah — in the 'Kamera Adinochka' solitary cell, and told the author he had even worked out without pencil or paper on what date Yom Kippur would fall the following year. The imprisonment damaged his lungs and he travelled back to Shumyachi to recuperate.
Tags: kursk, fradkin, nkvd, solitary-confinement, kamera-adinochka

Title: Rebbe responds to Feigin on visa rescue limits
Summary: On 2 Marcheshvan 5701, the Frierdiker Rebbe replied that everything possible had been done and care had to be taken not to worsen matters.
Story: On 2 Marcheshvan 5701, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to R. Yechezkel Feigin acknowledging that everything possible had been done. Only one further option remained — asking the local representative to press his superiors — but they feared that pushing too hard might backfire and harm matters.
Tags: new york, riga, rescue, visas, yechezkel feigin, frierdiker rebbe

Title: Letter to R. David Meir Rabinowitz on Moscow visa pickup
Summary: On 4 Marcheshvan 5701 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. David Meir Rabinowitz of Boston that the Vilna students had been summoned to the US consulate in Moscow to receive their visas.
Story: The Rebbe described receiving a cable from his students in Vilna reporting that each had been told to come to Moscow to collect his American visa, and pleaded for immediate fundraising to pay for steamship tickets and travel costs. The pidyon shvuyim campaign would dominate his correspondence for the next several weeks.
Tags: usa, visas, moscow, boston, david meir rabinowitz, pidyon shvuyim

Title: Altheuse writes to Rebbe about returning to Russia
Summary: On 6 Cheshvan 5701, after the Soviet conquest of Latvia, R. Eliyahu Chaim Altheuse wrote to the Rebbe about his plan to return to his family in Leningrad.
Story: Altheuse - who had been the matchmaker for the Rebbe and Rebbetzin, accompanied the Rebbe into Kostroma exile in 5687, and remained the lifeblood of Riga anash after the Rebbe's departure - now considered returning to Russia to be with his son and household in Leningrad, despite worsening Soviet decrees. The plan never materialized.
Tags: altheuse, rayatz, leningrad, soviet-latvia, wartime

Title: Letter to R. David Meir Rabinowitz on Rebbe's failing health
Summary: On 16 Marcheshvan 5701 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Rabinowitz noting weeks of poor health while pressing the urgent need for student travel funds.
Story: The Rebbe described laboring under physical weakness and emotional strain while writing to every direction asking for help. He noted that he had been compelled, against his will, to ask friends to assist financially with the rescue, which had drained him further.
Tags: usa, boston, david meir rabinowitz, pidyon shvuyim, health

Title: Second visa list of 62 anash families submitted to US government
Summary: On 19 November 1940 (18 Cheshvan 5701) Agudas Chabad filed a second list of 62 visa applications covering some 200 anash, accompanied by a brief prepared by Rashag for attorney Arthur Rabinowitz.
Story: Together with the two student lists and the earlier 47-family list, this submission brought the total to over 100 family-visa applications. The State Department later confirmed it would issue immigration visas for the 75 students and 62 anash on this batch, conditional on affidavits being filed for each applicant.
Tags: visas, united states, rashag, shmaryahu gourary, immigration, rescue, arthur rabinowitz, world war ii

Title: Abraham Kvash writes to Rebbe about visa interview
Summary: On Motzaei Shabbat Chayei Sarah, 22 Marcheshvan 5701, R. Abraham Kvash wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz asking guidance on whether to attend his US visa interview.
Story: In coded language Kvash explained that the consul required a full account of his life including his illegal flight from Russia to Poland, and asked whether it was worth pursuing the visa at all given that he could not travel through Russia. He also marked his approaching 26th birthday on 1 Kislev.
Tags: abraham kvash, visas, usa, rescue, border crossing

Title: Letter to Abraham Kvash with rescue advice
Summary: On 12 Kislev 5701 the Rebbe Rayatz replied to R. Abraham Kvash advising him to prepare his papers and meanwhile take work, since he could not yet travel via Russia.
Story: Kvash, who had fled Soviet Russia to Poland and could not legally travel back through Russia to Japan, had asked whether to even attempt the US visa interview. The Rebbe answered that he should do everything possible to be ready so that when an opportunity arose his visa would be in hand, and meantime arrange employment.
Tags: abraham kvash, riga, latvia, rescue, russia, visas

Title: Rebbe orders weekly contact with European talmidim
Summary: On 15 Kislev 5701 the Frierdiker Rebbe instructed Moshe Pinchas Katz to correspond weekly with Tomchei Temimim students in Vilna, Riga and Poland.
Story: From New York, on 15 Kislev 5701, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to Moshe Pinchas Katz (Igrot vol. 5, no. 1310) instructing him to maintain weekly correspondence with Tomchei Temimim students still in Vilna, Riga and Poland, keeping them informed and gathering reports on their material and spiritual situations.
Tags: vilna, riga, poland, tomchei-temimim, moshe-pinchas-katz, wwii

Title: Rebbe Rayatz directs weekly correspondence with scattered Temimim
Summary: On 15 Kislev 5701, the Rebbe Rayatz instructed R. Moshe Pinchas Katz to maintain a weekly written link with Tomchei Temimim students in Vilna, Riga, and Poland.
Story: In Igrot Kodesh vol. 5, no. 1310, the Rebbe urged that the students report regularly on their physical and spiritual state and receive news in return, so a meaningful bond could be sustained across the war zone. The directive came just as mail between Europe and the United States was beginning to break down entirely.
Tags: new york, vilna, riga, poland, tomchei temimim, moshe pinchas katz, communications

Title: Meir Hendel calls for Tomchei Temimim gathering in Radom
Summary: On 19 Kislev 5701, Meir Hendel sent a postcard inviting senior Tomchei Temimim students near Radom to gather and establish a yeshiva branch in the city.
Story: Hendel, a student of Tomchei Temimim Otwock who had failed to cross the border into Vilna, returned to his home city of Radom. He called for senior students such as Yaakov Falkenfeld to gather on Yud-Tes Kislev to found a Radom branch of the yeshiva, but heavy snow and cold prevented anyone from reaching him at that time. The plan would later materialize as a clandestine yeshiva in the Radom ghetto.
Tags: poland, radom, tomchei temimim, meir hendel, holocaust, yud-tes kislev

Title: Cable from Vilna students on Polish passports and visa fees
Summary: On 30 Kislev 5701 the Vilna students cabled the Rebbe Rayatz that they had submitted Polish passports for visas and expected approval on 6 Tevet.
Story: The students reported that under the latest decree all costs had to be paid in US dollars, $118 per train ticket plus another $50 in mandatory expenses, deposited at the Soviet state bank. They asked for detailed instructions, intensifying the funding crisis at the New York office.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, passports, rescue, ussr, tickets

Title: Cable from Vilna students on four-day visa validity
Summary: On 2 Tevet 5701 the Vilna students cabled that the exit permit had been received, valid only four days, and that funds must be deposited at the Soviet state bank immediately.
Story: Signed 'Rachamim Tmimim,' the urgent cable warned 'if not now, then never,' and requested that the New York office pay for everyone still missing funds. This precipitated emergency borrowing in New York to pay the Soviet bank within the narrow window.
Tags: vilna, rescue, ussr, visas, deadlines

Title: Beis Rivkah schools established by Achot Hatemimim in New York
Summary: Members of Achot Hatemimim of Greater New York establish Beis Rivkah, the future flagship Chabad girls' school network.
Story: The founding crowned years of women's chasidic study development that began with the Rebbe's Riga initiatives. Beis Rivkah grew into the Chabad system that today integrates chasidic philosophy into the standard women's curriculum.
Tags: beis-rivkah, women, new-york, achot-hatemimim

Title: Beis Rivkah schools established in New York by Achot Hatemimim
Summary: In the fall of 1941 the members of Achot Hatemimim of Greater New York establish the Beis Rivkah schools.
Story: The schools grew directly out of the women's empowerment work the Rebbe had begun in Riga and continued in the US. With Beis Rivkah, the initiative to translate maamarim and form women's farbrengens evolved into a permanent institution for chasidic girls' education.
Tags: beis rivkah, new york, women, achot hatemimim, united states

Title: Chabad library arrives in America via Stockholm
Summary: The majority of the Rebbe's library arrived in the United States in 1941 via Stockholm after his escape from Nazi-occupied Poland.
Story: When the Rebbe fled to America at the war's onset, he worked to transfer the library. Most reached him via Stockholm in 1941. A portion was lost during the war and ended up in the Polish National Library, where it was discovered in 1983 and ultimately repatriated to Chabad's Brooklyn library in 1988.
Tags: america, stockholm, library, war, poland

Title: Chabad library rescued from occupied Poland to New York
Summary: In 5701 the library of Rebbe Rayatz was rescued from Nazi-occupied Poland and brought to New York.
Story: After the German invasion of Poland and the Rayatz's own escape, his library and manuscript collection were extracted from occupied territory in 5701 (1940-1941) and shipped to New York. From that point forward the books rested in the Rebbe's quarters at 770 Eastern Parkway, where they have remained the heart of the Chabad library.
Tags: poland, new york, library, world war ii, rayatz, rescue

Title: Eber's pidyon nefesh from Riga
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Adar 5701, R. Yehuda Eber sent a pidyon nefesh to the Rebbe asking for mercy on his family's rescue.
Story: On Rosh Chodesh Adar 5701, R. Yehuda Eber sent the Frierdiker Rebbe a pidyon nefesh — the final extant correspondence from him. He asked the Rebbe to arouse mercy for his family, naming each by their mother's name, that the officials should mercifully grant the documents needed to reach America.
Tags: riga, pidyon nefesh, yehuda eber, rescue

Title: First Chabad yeshivah students arrive in Kobe, Japan
Summary: The first group of Tomchei Temimim students reached Kobe, Japan in early 1941 after traversing the Soviet Union by trans-Siberian railway.
Story: After Russian official Schlossberg — whose father had been a Chabad Chasid — arranged exit visas, the students traveled via Moscow and Vladivostok. The small Jewish community in Kobe, established 1912, opened its doors to them while they awaited US visas that would ultimately be revoked.
Tags: kobe, japan, tomchei temimim, rescue, siberia, trans-siberian

Title: Germans capture the town of Lubavitch
Summary: In the summer of 5701 the German army captured the town of Lubavitch.
Story: In the summer of 5701 (1941), as part of the German invasion of the Soviet Union, German forces conquered the town of Lubavitch. The occupation set the stage for the destruction of the town's remaining Jewish community a few months later.
Tags: holocaust, lubavitch, germans, war, world war ii

Title: Jews of Latvia executed by Nazis; Abraham Kvash killed
Summary: In Kislev 5702 the Jews of Latvia, including R. Abraham Kvash, were executed by the Nazis.
Story: After Latvia was overrun by the Nazis, the Jewish community was murdered in Kislev 5702. Kvash, whom the Rebbe Rayatz had tried unsuccessfully to extract via the Vilna-Russia-Japan route because of his Soviet origin, was among those killed.
Tags: latvia, nazis, holocaust, abraham kvash, riga

Title: Kehot Publication Society founded
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz established Kehot Publication Society, a publishing house for the works of Chasidism and Judaism, appointing the Ramash as its chairman.
Story: Kehot became the central publishing organ for Chabad-Lubavitch literature. Its founding marked the beginning of the Ramash's expanded public role in the movement, paving the way for him to eventually assume leadership as the seventh Rebbe.
Tags: kehot, new-york, publishing, ramash

Title: Machne Israel founded
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz founded Machne Israel, Chabad's social service agency, with the Ramash as executive director.
Story: Machne Israel was one of three corporations founded by the Rebbe in 1941, all with the Ramash in leadership positions. The trio of new organizations expanded the Ramash's involvement with American Chabad institutions and laid the foundation for the global Chabad outreach network.
Tags: machne-israel, new-york, social-service, ramash

Title: Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch founded
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz founded Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch, Chabad's central education branch, with the Ramash as executive director.
Story: Merkos took the lead in establishing the first national network of Jewish day schools and eventually began overseeing the global network of Chabad shluchim and institutions. It became one of the most consequential Chabad organizations, transforming American Jewish education.
Tags: merkos, new-york, education, shluchim, day-schools

Title: Mimeographed Haggadah produced in occupied Nice
Summary: In 5701, a hand-written, mimeographed Haggadah following the Rambam's text was produced in Nazi-occupied Nice by Agudat HaRabbanim of Paris.
Story: During the wartime spring of 5701 (1941), with France under Nazi occupation and printing impossible, the rabbinic association of Paris (then exiled in Nice) produced a Haggadah by hand and duplicated it on a mimeograph. The Lubavitcher Rebbe and Rebbetzin were among the Jews who had taken refuge in Nice that Passover.
Tags: haggadah, nice, france, world-war-ii, rebbe, rambam

Title: Murder of Riga's Jews by Nazis
Summary: In Kislev 5702, the Jews of Riga were murdered by the Nazis, including R. Yechezkel Feigin, R. Yehuda Eber, and their families.
Story: In Kislev 5702, the Nazis murdered the Jews of Riga, including the families of R. Yechezkel Feigin and R. Yehuda Eber, who had spent two years trying to escape to America. According to estimates from survivors of the killing, R. Eber and his family were among the thousands killed al kiddush Hashem.
Tags: riga, nazis, holocaust, wwii, yechezkel feigin, yehuda eber

Title: Nazi conquest of Latvia and establishment of ghetto
Summary: In the summer of 5701 the Nazis conquered Latvia and established a ghetto for its Jews.
Story: Following Operation Barbarossa, Nazi Germany overran Latvia in the summer of 1941. A ghetto was set up to confine the Jewish population, ending centuries of Jewish communal life and the Chabad presence centered in Riga.
Tags: latvia, riga, nazis, holocaust, ghetto, world-war-ii

Title: Nazi conquest of Latvia; Riga Jews murdered
Summary: In summer 5701 the Nazis conquered Latvia and murdered its Jewish community.
Story: Among those killed were R. Rafael Cohen, who ran into the burning shul to save the Sefer Torah and was locked inside; R. Eliyahu Chaim Altheuse, the leading figure of Riga anash; and R. Hillel Horwitz and his family. The decades of Chabad institutional growth in Riga came to an abrupt and devastating end.
Tags: holocaust, latvia, riga, nazis, rafael-cohen, altheuse, hillel-horwitz

Title: Nazi conquest of Riga
Summary: In the summer of 5701, Riga was conquered by the Nazis, sealing the fate of its Jewish refugees.
Story: In the summer of 5701, Riga fell to the Nazis. The Jews there, including R. Yechezkel Feigin, R. Yehuda Eber, and their families — all of whom had spent months trying in vain to escape to America — were unable to flee further. They would be murdered in the months that followed.
Tags: riga, nazis, war, wwii, holocaust

Title: Nazi massacre of Lubavitch Jews
Summary: The Nazis murdered 630 Jews of Lubavitch in a mass grave during World War II.
Story: After the Nazis conquered Lubavitch during World War II, around 5701 (1941), they found 630 Jews remaining—men, women, and children. They dug a mass grave and in a single day shot them all to death. By 5700 (1940), only about 120 Jewish families had remained in the town, as many had left when the courtyard and yeshiva closed.
Tags: holocaust, nazis, lubavitch, massacre, wwii

Title: Previous Rebbe declares 'Immediate Teshuvah, Immediate Redemption'
Summary: In 5701, the Frierdiker Rebbe (Rayatz) declared the campaign of 'L'alter L'teshuvah, L'alter L'geulah.'
Story: In 5701 (1940–41), Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, declared the famous slogan 'L'alter L'teshuvah, L'alter L'geulah' (immediate repentance, immediate redemption) shortly after arriving in the United States. This call set the tone for ongoing Chabad efforts to hasten the redemption.
Tags: redemption, messiah, teshuvah, usa

Title: R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich perishes in the Holocaust
Summary: In late 5701 R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich was murdered in the Holocaust.
Story: R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich, rabbi of Kupishok and longtime emissary of the Rebbe across Lithuania and Latvia, perished at the end of 5701 (1941), Hashem yikom damo.
Tags: chatzkevich, kupishok, holocaust, shoah

Title: Rabbi Shila Eliezerov notifies Rabbi Zevin of Moshiach Torah scroll
Summary: Rabbi Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov informed Rabbi Shlomo Yosef Zevin by letter of the Rebbe Rayatz's telegram about the Moshiach Torah scroll.
Story: Shortly after Simchat Torah 5702, Rabbi Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov (Shila), the Rebbe's representative in the Land of Israel, wrote to Rabbi Shlomo Yosef Zevin notifying him of a telegram received from the Frierdiker Rebbe announcing his decision to write a Torah scroll to greet Moshiach. Anash in Eretz Yisrael immediately began purchasing letters in the scroll, and the Kollel secretary recorded 156 buyers in a special ledger. Among the registrants were Rabbi A.C. Naeh, Rabbi Yaakov Landau of Bnei Brak, Rabbi Yaakov Yisrael Kanievsky, and Rabbi Zevin himself.
Tags: shila eliezerov, shlomo yosef zevin, kollel chabad, jerusalem, moshiach torah, 5702

Title: Rabbi Yosef Dov Soloveitchik appointed rosh yeshivah of Yeshivah University
Summary: After his father Rabbi Moshe Soloveichik passed away, Rabbi Yosef Dov Soloveitchik was appointed rosh yeshivah of Yeshivah University with crucial backing from the Sixth Rebbe.
Story: The YU board was divided, but the Sixth Rebbe wrote a letter calling Soloveitchik a 'gaon' whose appointment would 'restore the school's former glory.' He also personally lobbied board member Abraham Mazer. Soloveitchik's son Haym later said the Rebbe was 'the deciding factor' in the appointment.
Tags: soloveitchik, yeshivah university, the rav, moshe soloveichik, mazer

Title: Rayatz founds Agudat Chabad of Eretz Yisrael in Tel Aviv
Summary: In the summer of 5701 the Rayatz established Agudat Chabad of Eretz Yisrael in Tel Aviv as a new umbrella organization for Chabad institutions.
Story: Under the Rayatz's direct supervision, Agudat Chabad expanded into a new umbrella organization rivaling the older Kollel Chabad structure based in Jerusalem. This created tension over whether oversight of chassidus study programs in Jerusalem belonged to the Tel Aviv-based Agudat Chabad or to Kollel Chabad.
Tags: rayatz, agudat chabad, tel aviv, kollel chabad, jerusalem

Title: Rayatz founds HaKriah VeHaKedushah and Machne Israel
Summary: The Rayatz began publication of the journal HaKriah VeHaKedushah and founded Machne Israel, a Chabad outreach organization.
Story: HaKriah VeHaKedushah gave the Rayatz a public voice in wartime America, addressing both refugees and American Jews. Machne Israel became one of Chabad's central organizational arms, dedicated to strengthening Jewish observance and identity.
Tags: hakriah vehakedushah, machne israel, brooklyn, united states, journal

Title: Rebbe instructs Chaim Gutnick to remain in Australia
Summary: In early 1941 the sixth Rebbe directed Chaim Gutnick to stay in Australia and prepare the ground for postwar Jewish refugees.
Story: Gutnick, the only Chabad follower among the Telz refugees, wrote to the Rebbe in Brooklyn asking him to arrange US admission. Instead the Rebbe charged him with a mission: 'Prepare the ground for the arrival of Jewish refugees so that it will be a place of Torah.' At a time when Allied victory was uncertain, Gutnick later called this 'the vision of a true Jewish leader.'
Tags: australia, chaim gutnick, shlichus, tomchei temimim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz library collection arrives in New York
Summary: After eighteen months of clandestine transit through occupied Europe, the Rebbe Rayatz's library reached New York in late 5701.
Story: When the Rebbe Rayatz was rescued from Warsaw in early 1940 his book collection remained behind in Nazi-occupied Poland. For a year and a half emissaries worked to move the collection through occupied Europe in stages. In late 5701 (1941) it finally arrived in New York and was housed on the ground floor of the newly acquired Chabad center at 770 Eastern Parkway.
Tags: library, manuscripts, warsaw, new york, 770, rescue, wwii

Title: Rebbe summarizes Feigin and Eber's situation
Summary: On 17 Tevet 5701, the Rebbe's secretariat informed R. Yerachmiel Binyaminson that Feigin and Eber remained in Riga unable to obtain exit permits.
Story: On 17 Tevet 5701, the Rebbe's secretariat wrote to the Gaon HaChasid R. Yerachmiel Binyaminson summarizing the situation: R. Yechezkel Feigin and Rosh Yeshiva R. Yehuda Eber remained in Riga, still unable to obtain exit permits. They prayed for divine mercy on all of them.
Tags: riga, rescue, yechezkel feigin, yehuda eber, tomchei temimim, otwock

Title: Rebbe writes about Eber's role at Otwock yeshiva
Summary: On 21 Shvat 5701, the Rebbe wrote that R. Yehuda Eber had been Rosh Yeshiva at Tomchei Temimim in Otwock and was awaiting travel in Riga.
Story: On 21 Shvat 5701, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote that R. Yehuda Eber had served as Rosh Yeshiva at Tomchei Temimim in Otwock. He had sent visas for Eber and his family, who were now waiting along the way in Riga.
Tags: otwock, tomchei temimim, yehuda eber, rosh yeshiva, visa

Title: Rebbe writes Eber hoping for travel papers
Summary: On 7 Shvat 5701, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote praying R. Yehuda Eber would soon receive the necessary papers and travel safely.
Story: On 7 Shvat 5701, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to R. Yehuda Eber expressing the prayer that he would soon receive the needed travel documents and that his journey would prove safe and successful in material and spiritual matters.
Tags: riga, rescue, yehuda eber, frierdiker rebbe

Title: Telz students flee east with British passports
Summary: Students from Poland's Telz Yeshiva, including 20-year-old Chaim Gutnick, fled east via Russia and Japan to Brisbane, Australia.
Story: Holding British passports and Japanese transit visas from Chiune Sugihara, the Telz group made a long and hazardous journey by train and ship to Australia. Local Jewish leaders, anxious that idealistic students would disrupt the religious status quo, paid for their onward tickets to the United States, where Telz had reopened in Cleveland.
Tags: telz, poland, russia, japan, australia, chaim gutnick, chiune sugihara

Title: The Rebbe arrives in New York
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson, the future seventh Rebbe, arrived in New York in summer 5701.
Story: After fleeing wartime Europe, the future seventh Lubavitcher Rebbe arrived in New York in the summer of 5701 (1941). His father-in-law, the Rebbe Rayatz, immediately appointed him to head Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch, the educational arm of the movement. He soon began assembling a working library to support its activities.
Tags: rebbe, new york, 770, machne israel, wwii

Title: Tomchei Tmimim Vilna closes; talmidim scattered or rescued via Japan
Summary: The Vilna branch of Tomchei Tmimim ceased to exist in 5701 as some talmidim were rescued via Russia, Japan and Shanghai while others were murdered or sent to Nazi labor camps.
Story: Across 5700–5701 the Rebbe Rayatz worked to obtain visas and travel papers for the Vilna talmidim, routing many through the Soviet Union to Japan, on to Shanghai, and ultimately to the United States and Canada. Some talmidim perished in the Shoah and others were swept into Nazi labor camps, surviving only by the end of the war. The branch that had taken root in the Apatov shul thirty-two years earlier closed with the broader destruction of Lithuanian Jewry.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, vilna, wwii, holocaust, shanghai, japan, rescue

Title: Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva established in Montreal
Summary: In early 5702, students rescued via Russia, Japan, and Shanghai founded the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Montreal.
Story: In early 5702 (late 1941), some of the more than thirty students rescued from Nazi-occupied Europe via Russia, Japan, and Shanghai arrived in Montreal. They immediately founded the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva there, with the rescued students themselves later becoming its leaders.
Tags: montreal, canada, tomchei-tmimim, yeshiva, rescue, shanghai

Title: Letter to R. Yaakov Schechter on dire pidyon shvuyim cash crunch
Summary: On 14 Tevet 5701 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Yaakov Schechter in Pittsburgh that with only four days to wire funds the rescue would fail unless emergency loans were secured.
Story: He related that the previous week he had been forced to send 5,040 dollars beyond earlier remittances, and that a fresh cable required two more ship tickets at 400 dollars. The pidyon shvuyim fund was empty, and the rescue depended on free-loan funding sourced from the Ladies Auxiliary and other supporters.
Tags: pidyon shvuyim, rescue, yaakov schechter, pittsburgh, fundraising

Title: First three students depart Vilna for Russia
Summary: By 16 Tevet 5701 the first three Tomchei Tmimim students had departed Vilna and were on their way to Vladivostok and Japan.
Story: Writing to the mashpia R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch, the Rebbe Rayatz expressed both relief at the first departures and frustration that the rest had not yet left. The journey crossed Russia to Vladivostok and continued by ship to Japan, financed by funds wired from New York.
Tags: vilna, tomchei tmimim, russia, japan, rescue, trans-siberian

Title: Feigin informs Binyaminson of American visas for Vilna students
Summary: On 17 Tevet 5701 secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to R. Yerachmiel Binyaminson that American visas had been obtained for Tomchei Tmimim students in Vilna with thirty expected soon.
Story: Feigin reported that some students had already set out via Russia and the rest were prepared to depart shortly. The letter formalized internal communication about a rescue already underway after weeks of cables and emergency wires.
Tags: yechezkel feigin, yerachmiel binyaminson, tomchei tmimim, vilna, visas

Title: Rebbe describes acute fundraising difficulty in letter to R' Yehoshua Isaac Baruch
Summary: On 16 Tevet 5701 the Rebbe wrote to R' Yehoshua Isaac Baruch in Lithuania explaining that every dollar of rescue money was being raised as a personal loan and asking that expenses be minimized accordingly.
Story: The letter (Igros V:1337) noted that he had no fixed source of funds and that the travel costs already sent had required enormous effort to scrape together as gemach loans. He requested that Kovno and Riga representatives keep package costs as low as possible and send detailed accountings of past disbursements.
Tags: fundraising, loans, lithuania, yehoshua isaac baruch, kovno, world war ii, pidyon shvuyim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz replies to Lithuania reports
Summary: On 16 Tevet 5701 the Rebbe Rayatz responded to R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch expressing pleasure at news of how anash had passed the recent festivals.
Story: Despite the deteriorating wartime situation, the Rebbe Rayatz continued to receive and respond to detailed reports from R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch. In Igros Kodesh vol. 5, no. 1337, he wrote of the great pleasure the letter brought him and expressed hope to soon receive similar updates from later dates.
Tags: tevet, yehoshua-isaac-baruch, lithuania, wartime, correspondence

Title: Gershon Chanowitz and five students depart Vilna
Summary: On 22 Tevet 5701 R. Shmaryahu Gourary reported that Gershon Chanowitz had left Vilna together with five other students.
Story: Writing to R. Moshe Leib Rotshtein in Chicago, Rashag also noted that Shmuel and Fruma Chanowitz cabled that they were leaving Vilna that week and needed $14 each for the leg from Vladivostok to Tokyo. The remaining students were expected to depart by the end of the month.
Tags: gershon chanowitz, vilna, rescue, tomchei tmimim, russia

Title: Rebbe Rayatz responds about Achei Tmimim Tel Aviv leadership
Summary: On 23 Tevet 5701 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote seven letters about the reorganization of Yeshivat Achei Tmimim Tel Aviv.
Story: The Rebbe expressed great pleasure at the appointment of two committees—financial and spiritual—to assist director R. Eliezer Karasik. He acknowledged the institution's difficult material situation and committed to borrowing funds to send support, despite uncertainty about repayment. He sent personal greetings to each RaM, mashpia, teacher, and committee member by name.
Tags: tel aviv, yeshiva achei tmimim, rebbe rayatz, correspondence

Title: Rebbe reports thirty students en route and pays for thirty-eight more
Summary: On 24 Tevet 5701 the Rebbe Rayatz reported that thirty students were already on the road and a further thirty-eight had just been booked for travel from Vilna to New York.
Story: Beyond the first thirty for whom all costs had been paid, Rashag committed an additional $10,000 in loans to cover thirty more students and eight rabbis and rashei yeshiva so that no eligible person would be left behind under Soviet rule. The pace of departures and the accumulating debt drove ongoing cables to Chicago and Pittsburgh.
Tags: pidyon shvuyim, tomchei tmimim, rescue, vilna, trans-siberian

Title: First party of 30 students reaches USA stage of journey
Summary: On 28 January 1941 the first party of thirty Tomchei Tmimim students was confirmed to be on its way to the United States via Japan.
Story: The annotation appended to the second mimeographed list of seventy-five names recorded that thirty students had already left for America and the remainder were expected to follow shortly. This was the moment the rescue tipped from preparation to active migration.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, usa, japan, rescue, vilna

Title: Gershon Chanowitz arrives in Vladivostok
Summary: On 2 Shevat 5701 Gershon Chanowitz reached Vladivostok along with other Tomchei Tmimim students, with departure for Japan set for the following day.
Story: Rashag wired Rotshtein that the group was scheduled to sail from Vladivostok to Japan on 31 January 1941. The Trans-Siberian crossing had taken roughly two weeks, after which the convoy waited a few days in port before boarding the ship to Japan.
Tags: gershon chanowitz, vladivostok, japan, rescue, tomchei tmimim

Title: Tomchei Tmimim students sail from Vladivostok to Japan
Summary: On 31 January 1941 the first group of Tomchei Tmimim rescuees sailed from Vladivostok across to Japan, eventually reaching Kobe.
Story: The two-day sea voyage from Vladivostok brought the students to a Japanese port where they were met by members of the small Japanese Jewish community and taken to Kobe. From Kobe most would continue onward to the United States, although a number would remain stranded in Asia for many months.
Tags: vladivostok, japan, kobe, rescue, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rayatz sends telegram to Barcelona about Schneersohn rescue file
Summary: In late Shevat 5701 the Rayatz cabled Barcelona from Brooklyn asking what more could be done to expedite the Schneersohn rescue file.
Story: As efforts to extract his son-in-law the Rebbe from France dragged on, the Rayatz sent a telegram from Brooklyn to Barcelona in late Shevat 5701. He requested detailed information about what additional steps were needed to advance the Schneersohn file. A parallel telegram was sent to Marseille at the same time.
Tags: barcelona, brooklyn, rescue, rayatz, wwii, telegram

Title: Rashag summarizes visa-rescue effort for secretary Roitstein
Summary: On 7 Shevat 5701 Rashag forwarded to secretary Moshe Leib Roitstein the complete roster of students and anash for whom American visas had been obtained from Lithuania, Latvia and Soviet-occupied Poland.
Story: He noted that further lists from Warsaw–Otwock and additional applicants were forthcoming, and that the State Department had agreed to convert the second batch from temporary to immigration visas, provided affidavits be supplied. The summary remains the clearest contemporary inventory of the Chabad visa operation just before American consular practice tightened.
Tags: rashag, shmaryahu gourary, moshe leib roitstein, visas, rescue, lithuania, latvia, soviet poland

Title: Rashag asks R' Yisroel Chasdan in Stockholm to expedite shipment to New York
Summary: The Rebbe's son-in-law Rashag writes Chasdan in Stockholm to push Schenker to ship the library and the Jacobson/Hecht manuscripts to the USA without further delay.
Story: On 26 Shevat the Rashag wrote in English to R' Yisroel Chasdan, asking him to press the Schenker firm to release the Stockholm cargo and to arrange transit via Lisbon for the three crates of manuscripts being held under American Embassy custody in Berlin in the names of Rabbis Jacobson and Hecht.
Tags: library, stockholm, berlin, lisbon, schenker, schneersohn-library, jacobson, hecht, rashag, yisroel-chasdan

Title: R' Yisroel Chasdan secures place for library on freighter from Stockholm
Summary: Chasdan reports he persuaded the Schenker director in Stockholm to load 12 tons of the Rebbe's library onto a ship sailing the following week.
Story: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Adar, R' Chasdan replied to the Rashag describing his joy at securing the shipment. He had explained to the Schenker director the long history of the books — through 'Edom' and beyond — and obtained agreement to load 12 tons of sefarim onto a freighter departing Stockholm the next week.
Tags: stockholm, schenker, library, schneersohn-library, yisroel-chasdan

Title: R. Zalman Butman sends coded report from Riga to Rebbe Rayatz on arrests
Summary: R. Zalman Butman smuggled a coded report through Riga to the Rebbe Rayatz listing Chabad chassidim arrested or executed by the Soviets.
Story: On 1 Adar Aleph 5701 (27 February 1941), R. Yehuda Eber forwarded from newly Soviet-occupied Riga a letter that R. Shneur Zalman Butman had smuggled out of the USSR to the Rebbe Rayatz in America. The body of the letter, encoded in 'ksav stam' lettering and other cryptic devices to evade NKVD censorship, named anash arrested and executed by the Soviets in recent years, those who had been released, conditions of shechita and food in Moscow and Leningrad, and the impossibility of writing openly abroad. Eber, who had escaped Warsaw to Riga but was unable to obtain US visas, would be murdered together with the rest of Riga's Jews after the German conquest later that year.
Tags: soviet-union, riga, latvia, nkvd, arrests, samizdat, rebbe-rayatz, zalman-butman, yehuda-eber, ksav-stam-code

Title: Ramash and Chaya Mushka arrive in the United States
Summary: After a harrowing escape from Paris via Vichy France and Portugal, the Ramash and his wife arrived in the United States.
Story: The escape followed the German invasion of France a few months earlier. Upon arrival in the US, the Ramash's involvement in the Rebbe's affairs expanded greatly, and he soon took on multiple leadership roles in newly established Chabad institutions.
Tags: new-york, usa, paris, vichy, portugal, escape, nazi

Title: Rayatz sends follow-up telegram to Barcelona on Schneersohn file
Summary: In early Adar 5701 the Rayatz sent a second telegram from Brooklyn to Barcelona requesting an update on the status of the Schneersohn file.
Story: Continuing his frantic efforts to free the Rebbe from Nazi-occupied Europe, the Rayatz sent another telegram from Brooklyn to Barcelona in early Adar 5701. The cable simply requested the current status of the Schneersohn rescue file. These telegrams reflect the extraordinary length of the bureaucratic process that ultimately led to the Rebbe's escape.
Tags: barcelona, brooklyn, rescue, rayatz, wwii, telegram

Title: Yosef Goldstein flees from Chmielnik to Radom
Summary: On Purim 5701, Yosef Goldstein fled his home in Chmielnik after learning the Germans were searching for him, eventually reaching Radom.
Story: Once in the Radom ghetto, Goldstein was struck by the poverty and the sight of Jewish children and bochurim wandering without teachers or supervision. He concluded that a yeshiva was urgently needed, and together with Meir Hendel resolved to establish one. His arrival was a key catalyst for the underground Tomchei Temimim yeshiva in the Radom ghetto.
Tags: poland, radom, chmielnik, yosef goldstein, holocaust, purim

Title: Goldstein flees Chmielnik after Nazi search
Summary: On Purim 5701, Nazi agents searched Yosef Goldstein's home in Chmielnik; he escaped with only his tefillin and a letter from the Rebbe.
Story: On Purim 5701 (March 13, 1941), German agents came to seize Yosef Goldstein at his home in Chmielnik but did not find him, as he was praying in the beis midrash below. Realizing he had been informed upon — either over the yeshiva or his continued shechita work — he returned briefly, took only his tefillin (in which he had kept a 1933 letter from the Rebbe Rayatz), and fled the city. He credited that letter with miraculously saving him in the labor camps, escaping every Nazi search that followed.
Tags: poland, chmielnik, holocaust, wwii, yosef-goldstein, nazi-occupation, purim, rebbe-letter

Title: Rashag-led delegation meets First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt at the White House
Summary: A Chabad delegation led by the Rashag met Eleanor Roosevelt to plead for emigration of the Bobover Rebbe and Chabad Chasidim trapped under Soviet rule.
Story: Arranged by the Quaker-led American Friends Service Committee after Clarence Pickett's appeal to Mrs. Roosevelt, the delegation requested intervention with the Russian government. The effort failed: the Bobover Rebbe, who fled to Lvov, was beaten to death by German soldiers months later, and the Riga Chasidim were killed after the German invasion of Latvia.
Tags: eleanor roosevelt, rashag, quakers, afsc, bobover rebbe, rescue

Title: US Embassy in Marseille confirms passage from Lisbon to New York
Summary: On 21 Adar 5701 the American Embassy in Marseille confirmed it had arranged travel for Menachem Mendel and Chaya Mushka Schneersohn from Lisbon to New York.
Story: After months of effort, the American Embassy in Marseille notified the Schneersohns on March 20, 1941 (21 Adar 5701) that its Lisbon office had arranged their passage from Lisbon to New York no later than July 15, 1941. An advance payment of 840 US dollars was required and the cable was transmitted from Lisbon four days later on March 24.
Tags: marseille, lisbon, new york, rescue, wwii, us embassy

Title: Rebbe announces Tomchei Tmimim students have received visas in Japan
Summary: On 4 Nisan 5701, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote that his students in Japan had received their visas and were awaiting transit arrangements.
Story: In a letter dated 4 Nisan 5701 (April 1, 1941), the Frierdiker Rebbe announced that his students who had escaped to Japan already held their visas and were only waiting for travel arrangements. He prayed that they would arrive safely and continue their Torah studies with fear of Heaven. This was part of the broader rescue effort to move Tomchei Tmimim students from Nazi-occupied Europe through Japan to America.
Tags: japan, kobe, tomchei tmimim, visas, wwii, refugees, rayatz

Title: Rebbe asks Rabbi Ashkenazi in Shanghai to obtain visas for Vilna students
Summary: On 4 Nisan 5701, the Rebbe asked Rabbi Meir Ashkenazi of Shanghai to secure visas for students stranded in Vilna and Riga.
Story: Writing to Rabbi Meir Ashkenazi in Shanghai, the Frierdiker Rebbe explained that he could not bring all his students to America and therefore needed Ashkenazi's help to obtain Shanghai transit visas for talmidim in Vilna, in newly Soviet-occupied territories, and from Riga, where the large yeshiva in Dvinsk had operated. He pleaded that the effort be undertaken with maximum urgency.
Tags: shanghai, vilna, riga, meir ashkenazi, visas, tomchei tmimim, refugees

Title: US visas granted to future Rebbe and Rebbetzin in Marseille
Summary: On 20 Nissan 5701, after more than a year of effort, the future Rebbe and Rebbetzin received their US visas at the American consulate in Marseille.
Story: The State Department had cabled the Marseille consulate in mid-March that the Schneersohns qualified for visas under the quota. The Rebbetzin wrote her father on 26 Adar II that the consul had promised the documents. The visas were finally issued on April 17, 1941, paving the way for travel through Lisbon to New York.
Tags: marseille, france, visas, usa, ramash, chaya mushka

Title: About forty Tomchei Tmimim students gathered in Japan awaiting US travel
Summary: On 4 Iyar 5701, the Rebbe reported that about forty students were in Japan awaiting travel to the United States.
Story: In a letter dated 4 Iyar 5701 (May 1, 1941), the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote that roughly forty of his students were now in Japan, anticipating their journey to America. He noted that countless pleas were arriving from Lithuania and Latvia to be rescued in time, and his office maintained constant correspondence with those communities.
Tags: japan, kobe, tomchei tmimim, refugees, wwii, lithuania, latvia, rayatz

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes to Tzemach Tzedek yeshiva students
Summary: On 11 Iyar 5701 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the students of Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek urging them to spread Torah study.
Story: The Rebbe asked about their fixed Chassidus learning schedule on weekdays and Shabbat and instructed them to study his recently delivered maamarim. He emphasized that each student of Tzemach Tzedek must create an atmosphere of Torah study around himself. He blessed them and their families with health, livelihood, and protection from trouble.
Tags: jerusalem, yeshiva tzemach tzedek, rebbe rayatz, correspondence

Title: Rabbi Yechiel Yaakov Weinberg requests visas for Warsaw rabbis and activists
Summary: On 25 May 1941 Rabbi Yechiel Yaakov Weinberg, author of Seridei Eish and former director of the Berlin Rabbiner-Seminar, sent the Rebbe's secretariat a list of Warsaw rabbis and communal activists for whom he asked help obtaining American visas.
Story: Weinberg, then in Warsaw, forwarded names of admorim, rabbis and askanim — but by this date the US government had stopped issuing new visas to European Jews and had revoked many already approved. The list survives in the secretariat archive as documentation of an effort that could no longer succeed.
Tags: yechiel yaakov weinberg, seridei eish, warsaw, visas, rabbiner-seminar berlin, rescue, world war ii

Title: Telegram reports US consul has obtained nothing from Washington for refugees
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5701, a telegram from Japan reported that the American consul had received no new instructions from Washington regarding the students' visas.
Story: On 27 May 1941 (Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5701), students wired Rashag that the American consul in Yokohama had visited but had received nothing new from Washington and that the situation remained as before. Student Goldman had denied his Polish relatives on the application form and would receive his visa, while the Canadian visas had not yet arrived.
Tags: japan, yokohama, us state department, visas, tomchei tmimim, refugees, kgb

Title: Yehonatan Gershon Balter forced to leave Kobe yeshiva for Eretz Yisroel
Summary: On 3 Sivan 5701, student Yehonatan Gershon Balter was forced to leave the Kobe yeshiva and depart by ship for Eretz Yisroel.
Story: On 3 Sivan 5701 (May 29, 1941), Yehonatan Gershon Balter was compelled to depart Kobe by sea. The yeshiva students escorted him to the ship with brotherly farewells, and he later reported reviewing Chassidus aloud aboard the vessel. He eventually reached Tel Aviv where he joined Yeshivas Achei Tmimim.
Tags: japan, kobe, eretz yisroel, tel aviv, achei tmimim, tomchei tmimim, refugees

Title: Germany invades the USSR; the bride's family flees Shumyachi
Summary: When Germany attacked the Soviet Union in the summer of 5701, the author's wife's family — her parents R' Zusman and Feigl and her brothers Gershon and Nechemia — abandoned Shumyachi and fled eastwards, only to be overtaken by the Wehrmacht and murdered.
Story: Gershon, the same brother who had been freed from Kursk, ultimately perished with the rest of his family, while the Tomchei Tmimim bochurim who had remained in NKVD captivity — including R' Yehoshua Raskin of London — survived their sentences and went on to rebuild families in Israel. The author writes that 'the ways of Hashem are hidden from us.' His wife Henya was the sole survivor of the entire Fradkin–Paz family.
Tags: wwii, operation-barbarossa, shumyachi, evacuation, fradkin

Title: Portion of the Rebbe's library reaches the United States
Summary: A portion of the Rebbe's library, left behind in Otwock and entrusted to the US Embassy in Warsaw, arrived in the United States.
Story: Yechezkel Feigin had urged Rabbi Jacobson to intervene with US officials to save the 127 cases of books and three cases of manuscripts the Rebbe had been forced to leave behind. Jacobson's efforts were partially successful — some of the collection reached the US embassy in Warsaw and was eventually transferred to America in June 1941.
Tags: otwock, warsaw, united states, library, manuscripts, yechezkel feigin, yisrael jacobson

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in the United States
Summary: At the end of Sivan 5701 Rebbe Rayatz arrived in America and began using the second-floor 770 room as his yechidus room.
Story: From his arrival at the end of Sivan 5701 until his histalkus in the winter of 5710, Rebbe Rayatz used the second-floor room at 770 as his yechidus chamber, where he also delivered maamarim. After his passing the same room became the Rebbe's and Machneh Israel's office until the office layout was reorganized.
Tags: rayatz, 770, america, wwii

Title: 100 crates of the Rebbe Rayatz's library arrive in New York
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz announces that part of his library has reached New York, with formal receipt scheduled for the following Monday.
Story: On 11 Sivan 5701, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote that the first transport of the library had arrived in New York. Secretary R' Chaim Lieberman confirmed on 20 Sivan that about 100 crates of sefarim had been received that week, with roughly 50 more crates plus the manuscripts still in Warsaw.
Tags: library, new-york, stockholm, schneersohn-library

Title: Future Rebbe records 'Reshima' in Lisbon
Summary: On 16 Sivan 5701 the future Rebbe wrote a Reshima in Lisbon while awaiting transatlantic passage.
Story: The note, published in Reshimos issue 11, is headed 'Lisbon, 16 Sivan 5701' — documenting that the couple had reached Portugal after the long struggle for Portuguese transit visas and ship tickets. The following day they would board the Serpa Pinta bound for New York.
Tags: lisbon, portugal, reshimos, ramash

Title: Future Rebbe boards Serpa Pinta in Lisbon
Summary: On 17 Sivan 5701, the future Rebbe and Rebbetzin boarded the Portuguese ship Serpa Pinta in Lisbon, bound for New York.
Story: The passenger manifest lists Mendel Schneersohn (46, rabbi, Russian refugee, born Nikolaev) and Chaya Mussia Schneersohn (40, Russian refugee, born Smolensk), both with visas issued in Marseille on April 17, 1941, and tickets paid by her father, the Rebbe Rayatz, with destination 770 Eastern Parkway, Brooklyn.
Tags: lisbon, portugal, serpa pinta, ship, ramash, chaya mushka

Title: Ramash and Chaya Mushka Schneerson board ship in Lisbon for America
Summary: Menachem Mendel Schneerson and his wife Chaya Mushka boarded a ship in Lisbon bound for the United States after fleeing Nazi-occupied France.
Story: After Paris fell, the couple fled to Vichy France. The US consulate in Nice was hostile to Jews, but they obtained visas in Marseille. Acquiring Spanish and Portuguese transit visas was difficult, but at the last minute permission came through and they sailed for America.
Tags: ramash, chaya mushka, lisbon, paris, marseille, rescue

Title: Rashag writes Tomchei Tmimim students about affidavits sent for US visas
Summary: On 17 Sivan 5701, Rashag wrote to the students in Kobe explaining the affidavits Agudas Chassidei Chabad had dispatched on their behalf.
Story: Rashag (Rabbi Shmaryahu Gourary) wrote on 17 Sivan 5701 (June 12, 1941) instructing the Kobe students to tell the consul that Agudas Chassidei Chabad guaranteed responsibility for them and that the affidavits were secondary. He listed by name the affidavits already sent for individual students and elder refugees, including telegraphed affidavits for Bornstein and Feder.
Tags: affidavits, us visas, tomchei tmimim, agudas chassidei chabad, rashag, refugees
