Title: German invasion of the Soviet Union begins Operation Barbarossa
Summary: On 22 June 1941 Germany invaded the USSR, prompting Israel Yehuda and Michoel Teitelbaum to seek papers to flee Kharkov, though others delayed evacuation.
Story: When the war began, Israel Yehuda and Michoel Teitelbaum urged immediate efforts to obtain documents and leave Kharkov, but they were not heeded. As the front approached and German bombardments intensified, the families ultimately chose to wait through the High Holidays and Shabbat Bereishit before departing.
Tags: world war ii, operation barbarossa, germany, soviet union, kharkov

Title: Molotov radio broadcast announces Nazi invasion of USSR
Summary: Soviet Foreign Minister Molotov announced over the radio that Hitler had launched a surprise invasion of the USSR.
Story: On Sunday at noon, while the author was sitting at home in Moscow doing portrait retouching work, Foreign Minister Vyacheslav Molotov broadcast news that Hitler had begun invading the Soviet Union and had already captured many cities. The announcement upended life for Soviet Jewry instantly — portrait commissions evaporated and within days the Luftwaffe began nightly raids over Moscow, forcing residents into trench shelters dug in their courtyards. Refugees soon poured eastward in masses, and the author would shortly join them.
Tags: moscow, ussr, ww2, molotov, nazi-invasion, soviet-union, operation-barbarossa

Title: Future Lubavitcher Rebbe arrives in America and begins communal work
Summary: On 28 Sivan 5701 the future Lubavitcher Rebbe arrived in America and was appointed to lead Machne Israel, Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch, and Kehot.
Story: 28 Sivan 5701 (June 23, 1941) marks the Rebbe's arrival in the United States after fleeing Nazi-occupied Europe. Upon arrival he was appointed by his father-in-law, the Previous Rebbe, to lead three of Chabad's central institutions: Machne Israel (the social services arm), Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch (the educational arm), and the Kehot Publication Society. The anniversary was marked fifty years later, in 1991, by the Chabad delegation in Moscow with a yeshiva farbrengen.
Tags: rebbe, america, new york, immigration, world war ii, machne israel, merkos l'inyonei chinuch, kehot

Title: Future Rebbe and Rebbetzin arrive in New York
Summary: On 28 Sivan 5701 the future Rebbe and Rebbetzin arrived in New York, ending nearly two years of separation from her father.
Story: The Frierdiker Rebbe immediately dispatched letters and a cable to Chicago, Baltimore, and elsewhere announcing that 'my daughter and son-in-law have arrived safely.' The day later became one of the most significant in Chabad's modern calendar, marking the future seventh Rebbe's entry to America and the eventual revival of Chabad Lubavitch from 770 Eastern Parkway.
Tags: new york, 770, arrival, ramash, chaya mushka, wwii

Title: Ramash and Chaya Mushka arrive in the United States
Summary: The future Seventh Rebbe and his wife reached the United States after an eleven-day Atlantic crossing from Lisbon.
Story: The Sixth Rebbe greeted his son-in-law warmly and tasked him with chairing three new pillars of Chabad: Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch, Kehot Publication Society, and Machne Israel. Yitzchok Groner recalled the Ramash personally greeting each of the forty yeshivah students who waited at the dock.
Tags: ramash, chaya mushka, new york, merkos, kehot, machne israel

Title: The Rebbe and Rebbetzin arrive in New York
Summary: On 28 Sivan 5701 the Rebbe and Rebbetzin reached New York after their year-long flight from Nazi-occupied Europe.
Story: After fleeing Paris in June 1940, spending months in Vichy, Nice and Marseille obtaining papers, and crossing through Lisbon, the Rebbe and Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka arrived safely in New York on 28 Sivan 5701. Their arrival concluded a perilous year-long escape from Europe coordinated by the Rayatz through American diplomats and rescue networks. The date is commemorated annually in Chabad as a day of gratitude.
Tags: new york, lisbon, rescue, wwii, arrival, brooklyn

Title: R. Avraham Lisson flees Ponevezh as Germany invades
Summary: On 24 June 1941 (29 Sivan 5701) R. Avraham Lisson fled Ponevezh as the German invasion overran Lithuania; his father R. Shmuel Tzvi and the rest of the family remained and were murdered in the Holocaust.
Story: The Frierdiker Rebbe had obtained American visas for R. Shmuel Tzvi Lisson at the end of 5700, but they did not reach him in time. When the Germans invaded the Soviet Union, the son escaped while his father and household perished in the Shoah, may Hashem avenge their blood.
Tags: ponevezh, lithuania, holocaust, 5701, 29 sivan, german invasion, avraham lisson

Title: Balter arrives safely in Cape Town en route to Eretz Yisroel
Summary: On 4 Tammuz 5701, Yehonatan Gershon Balter reached Cape Town, where he met local Anash and visited the Chabad shul.
Story: On 4 Tammuz 5701 (June 29, 1941), Balter arrived safely in Cape Town. He spent only a few days there but met members of Anash and visited the small Chabad shul. He had planned to review Chassidus on Shabbos there, but a ship for Eretz Yisroel departed before Shabbos, requiring him to continue his journey.
Tags: cape town, south africa, tomchei tmimim, refugees, chabad

Title: Bobover Rebbe Benzion Halberstam killed by German soldiers in Lvov
Summary: Rabbi Benzion Halberstam, the Bobover Rebbe, was beaten to death by German soldiers shortly after the Nazi invasion of Russian-controlled Lvov.
Story: Months earlier, the Rashag-led Chabad delegation to Eleanor Roosevelt had specifically pleaded for his emigration from the Soviet zone, but the intervention failed. His death came just after the German invasion in July 1941.
Tags: bobover rebbe, halberstam, lvov, holocaust, lwow

Title: German conquest of Riga and murder of R. Yehuda Eber and family
Summary: After the German conquest of Riga in summer 1941, R. Yehuda Eber — a Warsaw refugee who had been seeking US visas — was murdered together with his family.
Story: The Chassidic scholar R. Yehuda Eber had fled Nazi-occupied Warsaw to Riga, where in early 1941 he served as the conduit for R. Zalman Butman's coded reports to the Rebbe Rayatz in New York. Eber and his household were unable to obtain travel permits from Riga to the United States before the German army overran the city later in 1941. He and his family perished along with the rest of Riga's Jews in the subsequent Nazi massacres.
Tags: latvia, riga, holocaust, yehuda-eber, warsaw-refugees

Title: Germany invades Latvia
Summary: The German invasion ends Latvian independence and devastates the country's Jewish population.
Story: Latvian independence, which had begun in 1918, lasted until the German invasion. Riga's chief rabbi Mendel Zak and his family were among those killed in the Holocaust. In 1945 Soviet troops would seize Latvia, making it part of the Soviet Union until 1991.
Tags: latvia, germany, world war ii, holocaust, invasion

Title: Rebbe Rayatz founds Agudat Chasidei Chabad in Eretz Yisrael
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz issued the founding letter establishing Agudat Chasidei Chabad in Eretz Yisrael.
Story: On 19 Tammuz 5701 (July 1941), during WWII, Rebbe Rayatz issued the founding letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. V, 1482) establishing Agudat Chasidei Chabad in Eretz Yisrael. He called for branches in every city to host public chassidus classes and gatherings, and appointed R. Shaul Dov Zislin, R. Moshe Gurary and R. Chaim Yosef Rosenblum as the founding committee.
Tags: rayatz, agudat chasidei chabad, eretz yisrael, wwii

Title: Kobe students summary letter on US visa cancellations dated 8 Tammuz
Summary: On 8 Tammuz 5701, the Kobe students summarized in writing that the Yokohama consul was issuing visas only to those who denied having relatives in occupied Europe.
Story: A document preserved in the secretariat archive, dated 8 Tammuz 5701 (July 3, 1941), summarized the students' situation: the consul in Yokohama would grant visas to those who denied their relatives, but a July 2 telegram from the State Department appeared to nullify this. The document also discussed students changing their surnames (e.g., Rodal to Bodal) and securing new affidavits under those names.
Tags: japan, kobe, us state department, visas, yokohama, tomchei tmimim, refugees

Title: Riga's Choral Synagogue burned with Jews locked inside
Summary: Riga's Choral Synagogue was set ablaze by Nazi forces with many Jews locked inside, killing senior Chasidim including Yechezkel Feigin and Reb Itche der Masmid.
Story: Among those murdered were some of the Sixth Rebbe's closest Chasidim and his secretary Rabbi Yechezkel Feigin. When the Rebbe received the report years later it triggered his heart attack of November 1944. A government memorial is held annually at the site of the ruined synagogue.
Tags: riga, latvia, holocaust, choral synagogue, feigin, cheifetz, itche der masmid

Title: Yud-Beis Tammuz farbrengen organized by Kobe Tomchei Tmimim students
Summary: On 12-13 Tammuz 5701, the Tomchei Tmimim students in Kobe celebrated the Chag HaGeulah with a major farbrengen attended by leading refugee rabbanim.
Story: For Yud-Beis and Yud-Gimmel Tammuz 5701 (July 7-8, 1941), the Kobe students organized a public farbrengen in addition to their internal seudah. They invited the refugee Vaad of leading rabbanim, who filled three rooms of the yeshiva to capacity. Talmidim explained the meaning of the day and reviewed Chassidus, and the Amshinover Rebbe participated and spoke several times.
Tags: japan, kobe, yud beis tammuz, farbrengen, amshinov, tomchei tmimim, refugees

Title: Last news from anash in Warsaw reaches the Rebbe's secretariat
Summary: A 15 Tammuz 5701 secretariat briefing relayed the final updates received from anash in Warsaw, including from R' Shmuel Shmotkin, R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin, and R' Leib Raskin, confirming receipt of food packages and visa questions.
Story: Shmuel Shmotkin had received his visa but did not know what to do for his daughters over eighteen or his sons-in-law; Shneur Zalman Shmotkin reported that the packages were a literal lebens-frage and that R' Moshe Schneersohn had been moved from Lublin to Izbica; Leib Raskin thanked the Rebbe for parcels keeping his family alive. After this date contact with Warsaw effectively ceased.
Tags: warsaw, shmotkin, leib raskin, food packages, lisbon, world war ii, izbica

Title: Nazi seizure of Lubavitch
Summary: German forces seized the town of Lubavitch and established a ghetto that September.
Story: On July 21, 1941, Nazi forces seized the town of Lubavitch during their invasion of the Soviet Union. By September of that year, they had established a Jewish ghetto in the historic town. The Nazis targeted Lubavitch's residents with particular brutality because of its history as the center of Chabad Chasidism.
Tags: lubavitch, nazi germany, holocaust, world war ii, ghetto

Title: Japanese government relocates yeshivah students from Kobe to Shanghai
Summary: Japanese authorities transferred all yeshivah students from Kobe to the international city of Shanghai, including some forty Chabad students and around 200 from the Mir Yeshivah.
Story: Rabbi Meir Ashkenazi, Shanghai's Ashkenazi chief rabbi and a Chabad Chasid, arranged for the Mir to use the Beth Aharon Synagogue. The Chabad students rented a separate location and continued their Polish-style integrated study of Talmud and Chasidut, isolated from teachers and from the Rebbe in New York.
Tags: shanghai, kobe, japan, mir yeshivah, tomchei temimim, beth aharon

Title: Jews of Dankra (Gostini) murdered by Nazis
Summary: On Erev Tisha B'Av 5701 the Jewish community of Dankra (Gostini), including the yeshiva network families, was murdered by the Nazis.
Story: According to 'Hashmadat Yehudim B'Latvia' p. 198, on Erev Tisha B'Av 5701 the Jews of Dankra/Gostini were killed by the Nazis. The Frierdiker Rebbe, lacking firsthand information, later asked in coded language on 23 Adar II 5703 about Himmelstein of Dankra and R. Berchen ('Refael's son-in-law'), seeking news of their fate.
Tags: dankra, gostini, latvia, holocaust, wwii, nazis

Title: Birth of daughter Leah outside Moscow during wartime
Summary: The author's eldest daughter Leah was born on the night of 12 Menachem Av 5701 in the town of Yegoryevsk, where his wife had relocated to escape Moscow's air raids.
Story: With Luftwaffe air raids forcing Muscovites into makeshift shelters and many residents fleeing the city, the author's pregnant wife went to stay with her cousin Sterke in Yegoryevsk (116 km from Moscow), beyond the range of the bombers. There their first daughter Leah was born on the night of 12 Av 5701. The author later traveled to retrieve mother and 'new face' back to their home in Cherinya.
Tags: moscow, yegoryevsk, family, ww2, soviet-union

Title: Rashag reports efforts to secure US and Canadian visas for Kobe students
Summary: On 12 Av 5701, Rashag wrote to Rabbi Mordechai Leib Rotstein that they were pursuing both US and Canadian visas for the Kobe students.
Story: Rashag wrote on 12 Menachem Av 5701 (August 5, 1941) to Rabbi Rotstein, reporting that they were not sitting idly by but were working actively to secure American entry permits as well as Canadian visas for the students. He acknowledged the harsh new immigration restrictions and the worsening situation, awaiting new State Department forms.
Tags: us visas, canada, rashag, rotstein, tomchei tmimim, refugees

Title: Rashag begins seeking Paraguay visas for the Kobe students
Summary: On 22 Av 5701, Rashag reported they were rushing to obtain Paraguayan visas for the students forced to leave Kobe.
Story: On 22 Menachem Av 5701 (August 15, 1941), Rashag reported the urgent push to secure Paraguayan visas for the talmidim being expelled from Kobe. He noted that each Paraguay visa cost $60.
Tags: paraguay, visas, kobe, rashag, tomchei tmimim, refugees

Title: Rebbe cables Kobe committee to delay students' departure to Shanghai
Summary: On 23 Av 5701, the Rebbe cabled the Jewish committee in Kobe to delay the students' departure to Shanghai pending visas to Paraguay and Canada.
Story: On 23 Menachem Av 5701 (August 16, 1941), the Frierdiker Rebbe sent a telegram to the Jewish committee in Kobe asking them to delay the transfer of his Tomchei Tmimim students to Shanghai, as he had obtained Paraguayan and Canadian visas for them that were expected within days. The following day he cabled the Polish ambassador in Japan asking for Canadian visas for 38 students.
Tags: japan, kobe, shanghai, paraguay, canada, visas, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rebbe cables Rabbi Abramsky and Dr. Schwarzbart in London for Canadian visas
Summary: On 6 Elul 5701, the Rebbe telegraphed Rabbi Abramsky and Dr. Schwarzbart in London asking them to use their connections to obtain Canadian visas.
Story: On 6 Elul 5701 (August 29, 1941), the Rebbe sent telegrams to Rabbi Abramsky and to Dr. Schwarzbart in London. He explained that 39 of his finest Tomchei Tmimim students were trapped in Kobe under the Jewish committee's supervision, all Polish citizens, and asked them to leverage their contacts to obtain Canadian visas — at least ten.
Tags: london, canada, visas, abramsky, schwarzbart, polish government in exile, tomchei tmimim

Title: First refugee group including Tomchei Tmimim arrives in Shanghai from Kobe
Summary: On 7 Elul 5701, 350 Polish-Jewish refugees including the Lubavitcher students arrived in Shanghai from Kobe.
Story: Erev Shabbos Parshas Shoftim, 7 Elul 5701 (August 30, 1941), 350 Polish-Jewish refugees arrived in Shanghai from Kobe. Among them were the Mir Yeshiva headed by mashgiach Rabbi Yechezkel Levenstein and Rosh Yeshiva Rabbi Chaim Shmuelevitz, students of Chachmei Lublin, the Lubavitcher Yeshiva, and talmidim from Telz, Kamenitz, Kletzk, and Radin. A special reception committee met them at the port and transported them to prepared lodgings in shuls and batei medrash.
Tags: shanghai, kobe, meir ashkenazi, tomchei tmimim, mir yeshiva, refugees, expulsion

Title: Author and family evacuate from Moscow to Samarkand
Summary: Facing conscription and the approaching German front, the author closed his Moscow apartment and fled by passenger train through Tashkent to Samarkand.
Story: Acting on his uncle R' Zusya's counsel to head for a 'Jewish city' rather than join his parents in Mozdok, the author dried bread into rusks, sold his cookware in Yegoryevsk, and on a Thursday in mid-Elul boarded a passenger train for the week-long journey to Tashkent with his wife, infant Leah, and sister Esther. The family spent Shabbat stranded in the Tashkent station park alongside refugees from Latvia, Lithuania, and Poland, then continued the twelve-hour ride to Samarkand. The author records that only in Tashkent did he begin to feel himself a refugee like the rest.
Tags: moscow, samarkand, tashkent, uzbekistan, ww2, evacuation, refugee, soviet-union

Title: Author arrives in Samarkand and joins an underground minyan
Summary: On the last Shabbos of Elul 5701 the author reached the old city of Samarkand, joined the Lubavitcher refugees who had already escaped Leningrad, and attended the secret Torah reading hosted by R' Aizik Karasik.
Story: R' Yeshaya Hofin helped him rent an upstairs room in a tupik near the Mahalla market and warned that Lubavitcher chassidim feared to daven in the Bukharan synagogue. The author was let into the underground minyan in time for the last Shabbos of Elul. Because his landlady also possessed a sefer Torah, he and R' Aizik agreed to alternate Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur services between their homes, with the strict condition that only ten men attend.
Tags: samarkand, evacuation, wwii, underground-minyan, bukharan-jews, aizik-karasik

Title: Canada allocates visas for 80 Polish refugee yeshivah students
Summary: After Rabbi Oscar Fasman's lobbying, the Canadian Jewish Congress agreed to a small allotment of visas for Polish Jewish scholars in neutral countries, including nine Chabad students.
Story: The Rebbe dispatched Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson to Canada to push for inclusion of the Chabad students. Only twenty-nine of the eighty visa holders ultimately departed Shanghai; the rest waited and were trapped in Asia for the war's duration, with some interned in the Philippines.
Tags: canada, shanghai, fasman, rescue, visas

Title: Passing of R. Elchanan Yakubovitz in Jerusalem
Summary: R. Elchanan Yakubovitz, formerly second rabbi of Lubavitch, passed away in Jerusalem on 24 Elul 5701.
Story: R. Elchanan Yakubovitz, the last man to bear the title 'rabbi of Lubavitch' before the dissolution of the community, died in Jerusalem on 24 Elul 5701 (September 1941). With his death the direct rabbinical line of the historic Chabad town came to an end. His biographical notes were preserved by his son R. Aharon Yakubovitz.
Tags: elchanan yakubovitz, jerusalem, lubavitch

Title: Rebbe Rayatz responds to R. Nissan Horowitz on Tzemach Tzedek learning
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz replied on 17 Elul 5701 expressing satisfaction with the Chassidus learning at Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: Responding to a detailed letter from mashpia R. Nissan Horowitz dated 22 Sivan, the Rebbe expressed great pleasure at the description of Chassidus study at the yeshiva. He blessed the students that their learning should bear fruit in heartfelt service through prayer. The exchange shows the close ongoing supervision the Rebbe Rayatz maintained over the Jerusalem yeshiva.
Tags: jerusalem, yeshiva tzemach tzedek, nissan horowitz, rebbe rayatz, mashpia

Title: Tomchei Tmimim talmidim send detailed report to Rebbe from Shanghai
Summary: On 18 Elul 5701, the student leaders in Shanghai sent a detailed report to the Rebbe describing their reception by Rabbi Ashkenazi.
Story: On Chai Elul 5701 (September 10, 1941), the student-leaders Yitzchok HaKohen Hendel, Yosef Weinberg, Yosef Menachem Mendel Tenenbaum, and Yosef Rodal wrote to the Rebbe. They described how Rabbi Meir Ashkenazi welcomed them warmly upon arrival before Shabbos Tetzei, hosted them for a farbrengen, and planned another for Chai Elul itself.
Tags: shanghai, meir ashkenazi, chai elul, tomchei tmimim, farbrengen

Title: Nine Tomchei Tmimim students sail from Shanghai toward Canada
Summary: On Erev Yom Kippur 5702, nine Tomchei Tmimim students sailed from Shanghai en route to Montreal via San Francisco.
Story: On Erev Yom Kippur 5702 (September 30, 1941), nine of the senior Tomchei Tmimim students who had received Canadian visas sailed from Shanghai. The ship traveled to San Francisco rather than directly to Canada; from there the students would travel by train across the United States to Montreal under special supervision to prevent them from disembarking on US soil.
Tags: shanghai, canada, montreal, san francisco, tomchei tmimim, refugees

Title: Israel Yehuda's family flees Kharkov amid German bombing after Shabbat Bereishit
Summary: After Shabbat Bereishit 5702 Israel Yehuda fled Kharkov by freight train with his family, Michoel Teitelbaum, and the elder R' Avraham Katzenelson as the Germans bombed the city.
Story: The night before departure a massive German bombardment partially destroyed their building; the families wrote a pidyon nefesh to the Rebbe during the raid. With the main Kharkov station destroyed and only the freight terminal operating, Israel Yehuda was nearly stranded with his belongings until two passing gentile laborers agreed to carry his bundles down the hill for thirty rubles. The train was bombed en route, but the group survived by remaining inside rather than running into the open.
Tags: kharkov, world war ii, evacuation, michoel teitelbaum, avraham katzenelson, freight train

Title: Polish refugees crash the Yom Kippur minyan in Samarkand
Summary: On Erev Yom Kippur 5702 Polish-Jewish refugees newly released from Siberia overheard 'Kol Nidrei' from R' Aizik Karasik's courtyard in Samarkand and forced their way in, far overflowing the planned ten-man minyan.
Story: After Stalin made peace with the Polish government-in-exile in 1941 he released his Polish-citizen prisoners from Siberia, and thousands drifted south into the warm Central Asian republics, including Samarkand. Wandering from courtyard to courtyard in search of a Kol Nidrei, they began pounding on R' Aizik's gate until it opened and the house filled. Frightened by the exposure, R' Aizik refused to host the following day, and the worshippers returned to the author's apartment to complete Yom Kippur.
Tags: samarkand, polish-refugees, yom-kippur, kol-nidrei, wwii, aizik-karasik

Title: Rebbe Rayatz announces Torah scroll to greet Moshiach
Summary: At the Simchat Torah 5702 farbrengen, the Rebbe Rayatz declared his decision to begin writing a Torah scroll with which to greet Moshiach.
Story: On Simchat Torah 5702 (October 1941), the Frierdiker Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, announced his decision to commission the writing of a Sefer Torah 'to greet Moshiach with.' After the holiday he publicized the initiative to chassidim across the world so that anyone who wished could take part in purchasing letters. This was launched amid the devastation of World War II as a call to spiritual mobilization and faith in the imminent redemption.
Tags: rayatz, moshiach, simchat torah, torah scroll, 5702

Title: Telz Yeshiva reopens in Cleveland, Ohio
Summary: Rabbis Mordechai Katz and Eliyahu Meir Bloch reopened the Telz Yeshiva in Cleveland in October 1941 with a nucleus of ten students who had come via Australia.
Story: Telz roshei yeshivah Katz and Bloch had traveled to the US in 1940 to explore relocation options, settling on Cleveland. The ten students who escaped Poland eastward and crossed to America through Australia became the founding cohort of the American Telz Yeshiva, which became a major center of American Orthodoxy.
Tags: telz, cleveland, ohio, mordechai katz, eliyahu meir bloch

Title: Rashag confirms students arrived in San Francisco and depart for Canada
Summary: On 29 Tishrei 5702, Rashag wrote that the students had reached San Francisco safely and would travel that evening through Chicago to Canada.
Story: On 29 Tishrei 5702 (October 20, 1941), Rashag informed Rabbi Rotstein in Chicago that the students had arrived safely in San Francisco and would depart that evening for Canada via Chicago. He urged Rotstein to arrange to meet them on the train, since they would not be permitted to disembark in the city.
Tags: san francisco, chicago, canada, montreal, rashag, rotstein, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz describes financial difficulty supporting Achei Tmimim
Summary: On 29 Tishrei 5702 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote that he had no source from which to take funds for the yeshiva.
Story: The Rebbe explained that even prior sums sent to Achei Tmimim had been borrowed and remained unpaid. He nonetheless committed to sending 200 shekels soon to ease their debt burden but stated he could not undertake regular monthly support. The letter reflects the severe financial straits during wartime.
Tags: tel aviv, yeshiva achei tmimim, rebbe rayatz, financial crisis

Title: Nine Tomchei Tmimim students arrive in Montreal to establish yeshiva
Summary: On 2 Cheshvan 5702, nine Tomchei Tmimim students arrived in Montreal, where they were tasked with founding a branch of the yeshiva.
Story: On 2 Marcheshvan 5702 (October 23, 1941), the nine students reached Montreal. Rabbi Yisroel Jacobson came immediately, and a week later Rabbi Shmuel Levitin arrived from New York. The students wrote that the Rebbe had instructed them to establish Yeshivas Tomchei Tmimim in Montreal in the spirit of the original yeshiva in Lubavitch and Otwock, marking the founding of Lubavitch institutions in Canada.
Tags: montreal, canada, tomchei tmimim, jacobson, levitin, yeshiva founding

Title: Polish refugee yeshivah students reach Montreal train station
Summary: After sailing from Shanghai via San Francisco and traveling overland by train, the refugee yeshivah students arrived in Montreal on a Friday and were welcomed by the community.
Story: Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson met them at the station with instructions from the Rebbe: they were to establish a yeshivah in Montreal. Their arrival had been hastened by the Rebbe's insistence that they take the very first ship despite the dateline-Yom Kippur dilemma.
Tags: montreal, shanghai, jacobson, rescue, kotlarsky

Title: Remaining Kobe students write farewell letter to Montreal-bound talmidim
Summary: On 3 Cheshvan 5702, the talmidim remaining in Shanghai wrote to their fellow students traveling to Montreal expressing regret over their abrupt parting.
Story: On 3 Marcheshvan 5702 (October 24, 1941), the students who remained behind wrote to those headed for Montreal. They lamented that the rapid departure had not allowed time for proper farewells or to discuss yeshiva matters, but trusted it was hashgachah pratis that they had not parted for long, and reported that Erev Yom Kippur and Yom Kippur passed with their accustomed order.
Tags: kobe, shanghai, montreal, tomchei tmimim, yom kippur

Title: Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim opens in Montreal
Summary: At a community reception on Saturday night, Rabbi Jacobson surprised Montreal Jewry by announcing that Yeshivas Tomchei Temimim would open the next day.
Story: Local leaders had wanted a single combined yeshivah, but Jacobson's unilateral move resulted in two institutions opening — Tomchei Temimim and Mercaz HaTorah. The Chabad yeshivah became the foundation for Montreal's growing network of Chabad schools, synagogues, and campus centers.
Tags: montreal, tomchei temimim, jacobson, mercaz hatorah

Title: Rebbe responds with joy to news of his students' arrival in Montreal
Summary: On 7 Cheshvan 5702, the Rebbe wrote that Rotstein's report about the students brought him more relief than all the world's medicines.
Story: On 7 Marcheshvan 5702 (October 28, 1941), the Frierdiker Rebbe replied to Rabbi Rotstein. He wrote that the news had revived him physically and was better for his weakened health than any medicine. He prayed that Hashem would help the students settle and succeed in their learning and avodah shebalev, and use the opportunity Providence had granted them to enliven Anash.
Tags: montreal, canada, tomchei tmimim, rotstein

Title: Yosef Weinberg reports on the Radom yeshiva to the Rebbe
Summary: On 7 Cheshvan 5702, just after arriving in Montreal with rescued students, Yosef Weinberg wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe describing the Radom yeshiva.
Story: Weinberg reported receiving a postcard from Meir Hendel announcing that he had founded a yeshiva in Radom with roughly 150 students, with Hendel as rosh mesivta and Yaakov Yehuda Goldberg delivering a shiur to one class. The letter conveyed news of the underground yeshiva functioning in Nazi-occupied Poland to the Rebbe in North America.
Tags: poland, radom, tomchei temimim, yosef weinberg, montreal, holocaust

Title: 30 crates of sefarim still held by Schenker in Warsaw, Rebbe seeks transit route
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz reports to R' Chasdan that 100 crates were received but about 30 more crates of his library remain at Schenker's Warsaw office.
Story: On 9 Cheshvan 5702 the Rebbe wrote that the New York shipment was being unpacked. He noted that among the 100 boxes received were seven of household items of little value, and that some 30 more crates of sefarim remained in Warsaw; he asked Chasdan to find any forwarding firm with a Warsaw connection to retrieve them.
Tags: library, warsaw, schenker, schneersohn-library, yisroel-chasdan

Title: Rabbi Yehoshua Isaac Baruch perishes in the Kovno Shoah
Summary: On 9 Cheshvan 5702 R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch, mashpia of Tomchei Tmimim Vilna, was murdered in Kovno.
Story: Before the Rebbe Rayatz left for America in winter 5700, R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch had traveled from Vilna to Riga to take leave of him. The Rebbe's parting blessing — 'May Hashem help that we merit to meet again with Moshiach' — deeply troubled Baruch, who took it as a prophecy that they would not meet again before the redemption. He was murdered in the Kovno Holocaust on 9 Cheshvan 5702.
Tags: holocaust, kovno, yehoshua isaac baruch, shoah, wwii

Title: Founding Vaad of Agudat Chasidei Chabad reports first progress
Summary: The Founding Vaad of Agudat Chasidei Chabad sent Rebbe Rayatz its first detailed progress report.
Story: On 8 Kislev 5702 (Nov 1941), the Founding Vaad wrote to Rebbe Rayatz reporting that branches of Agudat Chasidei Chabad had been established in Tel Aviv and Jerusalem (as central branches), as well as in Haifa, Petach Tikvah, Bnei Brak, Ramat Gan, Rishon LeTzion, Chadera, Kfar Yechezkel and Migdal.
Tags: agudat chasidei chabad, rayatz, eretz yisrael

Title: Great Aktion against Latvian Jewry
Summary: At the beginning of Cheshvan 5702 the Nazis carried out the great Aktion in which the Jews of Latvia were murdered.
Story: Only months after sealing the Latvian ghetto, the Nazis conducted the major Aktion at the start of Cheshvan 5702 (late October/November 1941), murdering the bulk of Latvian Jewry. The Chabad chassidim of Riga and the surrounding region were largely annihilated in this killing.
Tags: latvia, riga, holocaust, aktion, cheshvan, nazis, rumbula

Title: Israel Yehuda Leib Levin's family arrives in Samarkand
Summary: Israel Yehuda Leib Levin and his family arrived in Samarkand in Kislev 5702 amid wartime overcrowding, disease, and famine.
Story: After fleeing wartime Russia, the Levin family reached Samarkand in Kislev 5702 (late 1941). They found the city packed with newly released Polish deportees, swept by disease and starvation, with people collapsing dead in the streets daily. There was no place to settle and medicines were nearly impossible to obtain.
Tags: samarkand, uzbekistan, wwii, refugees, kislev, famine, epidemic

Title: Israel Yehuda's family arrives in Kzyl-Orda en route to Samarkand
Summary: On Shabbat Mevarchim Kislev 5702, Israel Yehuda's family reached Kzyl-Orda in Kazakhstan during the wartime evacuation toward Samarkand.
Story: The journey took the family first to Saratov, where they sheltered with the distinguished R' Yaakov Yitzchak Karasik, who advised them that the evacuation already amounted to leaving the country since everyone was heading to Samarkand. Boarding another train, they reached Kzyl-Orda for Shabbat Mevarchim Kislev, finding bitter cold nights, hot days, and severe hunger.
Tags: kzyl-orda, kazakhstan, samarkand, world war ii, evacuation, saratov, yaakov yitzchak karasik

Title: Rabbi Itche der Masmid Gurewicz burned alive in Kherson
Summary: The renowned Chabad emissary and scholar Rabbi Itche Gurewicz was murdered by the Nazis in the synagogue of Kherson, Ukraine.
Story: Gurewicz had served as an emissary of both the Rebbe Rashab and the Rebbe Rayatz, and was renowned for his commitment to learning and scholarship. His martyrdom in November 1941 stands among the many tragedies of the Holocaust that claimed devoted Chasidim.
Tags: gurewicz, kherson, ukraine, holocaust, nazis

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe writes back about the Radom yeshiva
Summary: On 14 Cheshvan 5702 the Frierdiker Rebbe replied with delight at the news of Meir Hendel's yeshiva in Radom and asked for assistance to be sent.
Story: In Iggeret 1603, the Rebbe expressed his pleasure at the report and asked that blessings be conveyed to Hendel and his students. He instructed contacts in Japan, Shanghai, Warsaw and elsewhere to investigate sending parcels to Hendel, with the cost to be reimbursed.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, iggeret, radom, meir hendel, japan, shanghai, warsaw

Title: Massacre of Lubavitch's Jews
Summary: 483 Jews of Lubavitch were murdered and the ghetto destroyed on November 4, 1941.
Story: On November 4, 1941, Nazi forces murdered 483 Jews and destroyed the ghetto in Lubavitch, effectively ending the Jewish presence in the historic town. Only one Jewish resident remained in Lubavitch until the early 1960s. The Hebrew Standard of Australia later reported that the brutality of the extermination in Lubavitch 'supersedes anything the Red Army committee investigating Nazi atrocities have thus far come across.'
Tags: lubavitch, nazi germany, holocaust, world war ii, massacre, ghetto

Title: Massacre of the 483 Jews of Lubavitch
Summary: On November 4, 1941 (Cheshvan 5702), the Germans murdered all 483 Jews of Lubavitch.
Story: On November 4, 1941, corresponding to Cheshvan 5702, German forces murdered all 483 Jews remaining in the town of Lubavitch, Hashem yikom damam. The massacre effectively ended Jewish presence in the town that had given Chabad its name. Russian-language documents preserve the historical record.
Tags: holocaust, lubavitch, germans, massacre, world war ii

Title: R. Lis writes from Shanghai pleading for news of wife and children
Summary: On 14 Cheshvan 5702, R. Eliyahu Moshe Lis wrote to the Rebbe from Shanghai begging for any word from his wife and children in Poland, after ten months of silence.
Story: Having reached Shanghai with the rest of the Tomchei Temimim refugees, Lis appealed to the Rebbe to help locate his family and send whatever aid was possible, since he himself could do nothing from East Asia. The Rebbe responded (Igrot Kodesh vol. 6, no. 1604) with consolation and a prayer for good news, but Golda and the daughters never escaped — they perished in the Holocaust while Lis survived alone and continued on to America.
Tags: shanghai, poland, biala, eliyahu moshe lis, rescue, family, wwii, holocaust

Title: Montreal students thank Rotstein and Chicago Lubavitchers for reception
Summary: On 16 Cheshvan 5702, the newly arrived Montreal students thanked Rabbi Rotstein for the warm reception during their stopover in Chicago.
Story: On 16 Marcheshvan 5702 (November 6, 1941), the students wrote from Montreal to Rabbi Rotstein in Chicago thanking him for the warm reception, the $25 stipend they had received via Rabbi Rubinstein, and the provisions prepared for the remainder of their journey. They confirmed they had settled and were beginning to establish Yeshivas Tomchei Tmimim in Montreal per the Rebbe's special directive.
Tags: montreal, chicago, rotstein, rubinstein, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rebbe Rayatz sends 150 shekels to Achei Tmimim by telegraphic transfer
Summary: On 21 Cheshvan 5702 the Rebbe Rayatz sent 150 shekels via R. Moshe Gurary to Yeshivat Achei Tmimim.
Story: The Rebbe described the transfer as coming not from any cash reserve but from his 'trust fund' confident that God would help him repay. The letter highlights the personal sacrifice involved in sustaining the Tel Aviv yeshiva during WWII when normal channels of support had collapsed.
Tags: tel aviv, yeshiva achei tmimim, rebbe rayatz, moshe gurary

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe writes about Tomchei Temimim students in Poland
Summary: On 7 Kislev 5702 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote of the mesirat nefesh of Tomchei Temimim students still in Poland, including one who had assembled around 150 students.
Story: In Iggeret 1640 the Rebbe described how his students who remained in Poland were giving themselves over literally to Torah study and teaching others. He noted that they were keeping the Torah not merely amid poverty but amid hunger and cold, and that in one place a single student had gathered roughly 150 talmidim — a clear reference to Hendel's yeshiva in Radom.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, iggeret, poland, tomchei temimim, holocaust, mesirat nefesh

Title: Death of Levin's son Ephraim Shmuel in Samarkand hospital
Summary: Ephraim Shmuel, two-and-a-quarter-year-old son of Israel Yehuda Leib Levin, died in a Samarkand hospital on erev Shabbat 9 Kislev 5702.
Story: On erev Shabbat 9 Kislev 5702, Levin's wife brought their two-and-a-quarter-year-old son Ephraim Shmuel to a Samarkand hospital, where he died — almost no one who entered the hospital in those days came out alive. The couple themselves carried his body several kilometers to the cemetery after Shabbat. Crushed, Levin prayed only that he not lose his faith and his bond with the Rebbe.
Tags: samarkand, wwii, epidemic, family, kislev, child mortality

Title: Burning of R. Yechezkel Feigin in synagogue
Summary: On 10 Kislev 5702, the Nazis burned R. Yechezkel Feigin in a synagogue together with chasidim R. Yitzchak Horowitz and R. Eliyahu Chaim Althaus.
Story: On 10 Kislev 5702, the Nazis burned R. Yechezkel Feigin alive in a synagogue together with the chasidim R. Yitzchak Horowitz (Hamasmid) and R. Eliyahu Chaim Althaus. They were among the many Lubavitch chassidim murdered al kiddush Hashem in occupied Riga.
Tags: riga, nazis, holocaust, wwii, yechezkel feigin, yitzchak horowitz, eliyahu chaim althaus

Title: Rebbe instructs Levitin to pursue 300 visas for students stranded in Shanghai
Summary: On 10 Kislev 5702, the Rebbe wrote Rabbi Shmuel Levitin urging maximum effort to obtain visas for talmidim still stranded in Shanghai.
Story: On 10 Kislev 5702 (November 30, 1941), the Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Shmuel Levitin, who had been sent to greet the students in Montreal. He noted that Rashag had forwarded the list of remaining Shanghai students to Levitin and Rabbi Yosef Albert, urging that no effort be spared to fill all 300 visas being sought. These additional visas were never granted, and the talmidim remained in Shanghai until the war's end.
Tags: shanghai, canada, visas, levitin, albert, tomchei tmimim

Title: Rabbi Yechezkel Feigin killed by Nazis in Warsaw
Summary: Unable to obtain a passport to join the Rebbe in the United States, Feigin was burned alive in a Warsaw synagogue by the Nazis.
Story: The Nazis brought most of the city's Jews into a synagogue and set it on fire, forcing other Jews to watch. By some accounts, Rabbi Yitzchak Gurevitz removed a Torah scroll from the ark and danced with Feigin as they burned. When the Rebbe received word of these deaths in 1945, he fainted from grief.
Tags: feigin, warsaw, holocaust, nazis

Title: Rabbi Yechezkel Feigin killed in Warsaw synagogue fire
Summary: The Rebbe's longtime secretary perished when Nazis burned a Warsaw synagogue with Jews trapped inside.
Story: Passport issues had prevented Feigin from leaving Riga with the Rebbe in 1939 for the United States. In December 1941, Nazis brought most of the city's Jews into a synagogue and set it ablaze, forcing other Jews to watch. According to some reports, Rabbi Yitzchak Gurevitz removed the Torah scroll from the ark and danced with Feigin as they burned alive; when news reached the Rebbe in 1945, he fainted from grief.
Tags: feigin, warsaw, holocaust, nazis, martyrdom

Title: Riga's Chabad community murdered by the Nazis
Summary: During Kislev 5702 the anash of Riga — including the families of Feigin, Chefetz, Asheroff, Althaus, Horowitz, Volshanik and others — were murdered by the Nazis.
Story: Months earlier the Soviet conquest of Latvia had already cut off the package-shipment lifeline from Riga to Poland. With the German occupation that followed Operation Barbarossa, the Chabad community of Riga that had hosted the Rebbe in early 1940 was annihilated; the specific fates would only be confirmed gradually through later correspondence.
Tags: riga, latvia, holocaust, shoah, nazis, elya chaim althaus, world war ii

Title: Rotstein replies to Rodal with joy over Montreal arrival photographs
Summary: On 13 Kislev 5702, Rabbi Mordechai Leib Rotstein wrote to student Yosef Rodal expressing joy at receiving photographs from the Montreal reception.
Story: On 13 Kislev 5702 (December 3, 1941), Rabbi Rotstein replied to talmid Yosef Rodal. He wrote that receiving the letter and two photographs had brought him great joy at seeing the students together with the gedolim, and hoped Rodal had also sent the photos to the Rebbe, anticipating the nachas this would cause the leader of the generation.
Tags: montreal, chicago, rotstein, rodal, tomchei tmimim

Title: Mottel Altein sent to Pittsburgh's Nusach Ari Congregation
Summary: On the morning of the Pearl Harbor attack, twenty-two-year-old Mottel Altein boarded a train to Pittsburgh on the Rebbe's instructions to take over a struggling Orthodox synagogue.
Story: The night before, the Rebbe had summoned Altein and refused to delay the trip. Altein heard news of the Japanese attack en route. He arrived to find his telegram unopened at the synagogue and the president debating whether to relocate the shul and join the Conservative movement. The Rebbe's intervention kept it Orthodox.
Tags: pittsburgh, altein, nusach ari, pearl harbor

Title: R' Mordechai Dubin released from Soviet prison
Summary: On 23 Kislev 5702 R' Mordechai Dubin, head of the Riga Chabad community and former Latvian Saeima deputy, was freed from Soviet imprisonment and resettled in Saratov.
Story: Dubin had been arrested during the Soviet annexation of Latvia and deported into Russia proper. His release left him stranded in Saratov rather than Riga — which in any case had by then been destroyed under Nazi occupation — and he resumed correspondence with the Rebbe in America under heavy censorship.
Tags: mordechai dubin, saratov, soviet union, latvia, kgb, rescue, world war ii

Title: Achei Tmimim yeshiva founded in Newark
Summary: R. Mentlik and R. Katz founded the Achei Tmimim yeshiva in Newark in 5702.
Story: In 5702 (1941-1942), R. Mordechai Mentlik and R. Moshe Pinchas Katz — both living in Newark and commuting daily to their yeshiva work in New York — founded the Achei Tmimik yeshiva in Newark, New Jersey. They continued to reside in Newark until 5706, when they moved to New York.
Tags: achei tmimim, newark, new jersey, mordechai mentlik, moshe pinchas katz

Title: Chabad purchases Montefiore cemetery section
Summary: In 5702 R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky arranged the purchase of the Chabad section at Montefiore Cemetery in Queens.
Story: In 5702, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky arranged the purchase of the Chabad section at Montefiore Cemetery. This is the cemetery that would later house the Ohel of Rayatz and the Rebbe.
Tags: montefiore, cemetery, queens, kazarnovsky

Title: Death of Levins' only son in Samarkand
Summary: The Levins' two-and-a-half year old son, their only child, died upon their arrival in Samarkand after a three-week train journey fleeing the war.
Story: When the Eastern Front reached Kharkov, the Levins fled with thousands of other Jews to Central Asia. The grueling three-week journey in a freight car proved fatal for their young son, who died soon after they reached Samarkand. The couple would not have more children until after leaving the Soviet Union.
Tags: samarkand, world war ii, evacuation, kharkov

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe begins writing Torah scroll to greet Moshiach
Summary: In 5702, the Frierdiker Rebbe began writing a special Torah scroll to greet Moshiach.
Story: In 5702 (1941–42), the Previous Rebbe initiated the writing of a special Sefer Torah intended to welcome Moshiach. He began the writing but did not complete it in his lifetime; the completion would only be announced decades later by his son-in-law and successor.
Tags: sefer torah, moshiach, redemption

Title: Hebrew Parochial School opens in Chicago
Summary: A new Jewish day school opened on Chicago's West Side that would evolve into the Arie Crown Hebrew Day School.
Story: The Sixth Rebbe sent Rabbi Chaim Hodakov to help organize the school and urged Chicago Chasidim to support it. Chabad rabbis including Zalman Posner taught there. The school faced a financial crisis in 1946, which the Rebbe quietly resolved by activating his network of donors.
Tags: chicago, arie crown, hodakov, hebrew parochial school

Title: Luach HaYom Yom published by Kehot
Summary: Luach HaYom Yom was issued by Kehot in 5703.
Story: The Rebbe compiled and edited Luach HaYom Yom, a calendar with daily teachings of the Chabad Rebbes, published by Kehot in 1942/43.
Tags: the rebbe, hayom yom, kehot

Title: Lubavitch yeshivah opens in Samarkand
Summary: A Lubavitch yeshivah opened in Samarkand during World War II, signaling a relaxation of Soviet religious persecution.
Story: In 1942, twenty-two years after the Rashab's prediction to the Rayatz, the Soviet government's active religious persecution eased during World War II. A Lubavitch yeshivah opened in Samarkand, and the Russian Orthodox Church was again permitted to operate publicly.
Tags: samarkand, uzbekistan, wwii, chabad, yeshivah

Title: R' Berl Kornitzer captured by the Germans in Radom
Summary: In mid-summer 5702, the Germans seized R' Berl Kornitzer as he left the Radom synagogue wrapped in tallit and crowned with tefillin, and he was never seen again.
Story: All efforts to free him failed, and his fate remained unknown. The yeshiva feared retribution because Kornitzer had been entrusted with gold coins received from the wealthy patron for the yeshiva's support, but news arrived that he had hidden the coins in his shoes and they were apparently not discovered. The incident shook the entire underground community in Radom.
Tags: holocaust, radom, berl kornitzer, nazis, tallit, tefillin

Title: Radom underground yeshiva ceases to exist
Summary: By the end of summer 5702 the Radom yeshiva ceased to function, its students and faculty murdered along with the rest of the kehilla.
Story: Yosef Goldstein later summarized that the yeshiva had operated from the beginning of 5701 until the end of 5702, after which all were destroyed and led as sheep to the slaughter together with the holy communities of Poland. R' Berl Kornitzer and R' Baruch Friedman were among those killed, along with most of the close to two hundred bochurim.
Tags: holocaust, radom, tomchei temimim, ghetto

Title: Rayatz expands American institutions and establishes Kehot Publication Society
Summary: The Rayatz established Tomchei Temimim yeshivas in Montreal, Newark, Worcester, and Pittsburgh, and founded Kehot Publication Society.
Story: Within two years of arriving in America, the Rayatz built a network of yeshivas across North America. Kehot Publication Society became the official publishing arm of the Chabad movement, producing thousands of works of Torah and chasidic teachings over subsequent decades.
Tags: montreal, newark, worcester, pittsburgh, tomchei temimim, kehot

Title: Rebbe Rayatz sends letter of encouragement to Shomrei Shabbos gemach
Summary: In 5702 the Rebbe Rayatz sent a letter of encouragement together with a check to the Shomrei Shabbos free-loan society, asking to participate in their good works.
Story: The earliest documented contact between the Rebbe Rayatz and the Chabad Shomrei Shabbos gemach is a 5702 letter in which the Rebbe sent encouragement together with a check, asking 'to participate with them in their good actions.' This was during the Rebbe Rayatz's early American years and the height of World War II.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, shomrei shabbos, gemach, new york

Title: Rebbe's first publication: Luach 5703 in English
Summary: The Rebbe's first publication, an English Luach for 5703, appeared in the United States.
Story: After settling in New York, the Rebbe was appointed by his father-in-law to head Machne Israel, Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch, and Kehot. His first published work, in 1942/43, was an English-language Luach for 5703 with laws, customs and information for young students.
Tags: the rebbe, english, machne israel, kehot, education

Title: Yosef Rodal — first Shanghai student to marry — weds in Montreal
Summary: Yosef Rodal, the oldest of the Shanghai refugee students, became the first of the group to marry, with the Rebbe personally providing funds for a diamond ring.
Story: Rodal had lost most of his family in the Holocaust. The Rebbe, knowing the bride was a Canadian who expected a diamond, gave Rodal money to buy one. A delegation of New York rabbis attended the wedding. Most of the Shanghai cohort would settle in Montreal, marry, and become teachers, rabbis, and dayanim.
Tags: rodal, montreal, shanghai students, diamond ring

Title: Passing of Rebbetzin Sterna Sarah, 13 Shevat 5702, in the United States
Summary: Rebbetzin Sterna Sarah passed away in the United States on 13 Shevat 5702 in the same manner as Rebbetzin Rivka.
Story: Rebbetzin Sterna Sarah, wife of the Rebbe Rashab and mother of the Rayatz, passed away on Shabbos morning 13 Shevat 5702 in the United States. As her mother-in-law Rebbetzin Rivka had decades earlier, she asked her attendant for a siddur, davened, and handed it back; when the attendant turned to put it away she had already passed. The Rayatz was in Chicago on klal matters at the time, mirroring the Rebbe Rashab's absence at the petira of his own mother.
Tags: rebbetzin sterna sarah, rebbe rashab, rayatz, united states, chicago, 13 shevat, rebbetzin rivka

Title: Rayatz responds to Agudat Chasidei Chabad first report
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz acknowledged the first report from the Founding Vaad but urged greater effort.
Story: On 6 Adar 5702 (Feb 1942), Rebbe Rayatz wrote letter 1719 acknowledging receipt of the Vaad's 8 Kislev report, the first since the founding letter of 19 Tammuz tashah. While crediting them for what was accomplished, he urged that more must be done to spread chassidus and strengthen Torah learning.
Tags: rayatz, agudat chasidei chabad

Title: Tu BiShvat farbrengen launches Samarkand Tomchei Tmimim
Summary: At a Tu BiShvat 5702 farbrengen at R' Yehoshua Karf's home, Michael Teitelbaum proposed founding a Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Samarkand.
Story: On Tu BiShvat 5702 the chassidim gathered at R' Yehoshua Karf's home, where Michael Teitelbaum urged arousing mercy for Anash and called for starting a Tomchei Tmimim in Samarkand. They began with three boys — Sholom Levertov, Zelig Katzman, and Heishke Dobrawski — each chassid pledging to feed and teach them on assigned days. The yeshiva soon expanded greatly once R' Mendel Futerfas and R' Abba Pliskin arrived to hire teachers and run it.
Tags: samarkand, tomchei tmimim, yeshiva, michael teitelbaum, yehoshua karf, tu bishvat, orphans

Title: Yarn-trade livelihood begins after Purim 5702
Summary: After Purim 5702, Levin began trading yarn with Bukharian Jews in Samarkand, suddenly earning 1,400 rubles and easing the family's hunger.
Story: After Purim 5702 a stranger left yarn at Levin's home; that same day a Bukharian Jew offered to buy it at double the price. Reciting Tanya by heart to calm his fear of walking the streets without papers, Levin delivered seven kilos and earned 1,400 rubles in one transaction. From then on his livelihood eased, and he partnered with R' Pinchas Levitin in buying a wooden weaving machine.
Tags: samarkand, parnassah, underground economy, weaving, purim, bukharian jews

Title: Author's wife hospitalized with typhus on Purim in Samarkand
Summary: On Purim 5702 the author's wife fell ill with typhus and was hospitalized; she recovered only just before Passover.
Story: The first winter in Samarkand brought famine, unusual cold, and a typhus epidemic that filled the city's hospitals to capacity. Returning home from the Purim farbrengen, the author found his wife unwell; the next morning she was taken to hospital with typhus. Fearing the Soviet army press-gangs ('oblavy') that grabbed men off the streets and shipped them to the front, he could not even visit her — his sister Esther served as her contact until she returned home shortly before Passover.
Tags: samarkand, purim, typhus, disease, ww2, uzbekistan, soviet-union

Title: Father-in-law Zussman ben Gershon murdered in the Shoah
Summary: The author's father-in-law R. Zussman ben Gershon was murdered by the Nazis on 28 Adar 5702.
Story: R. Zussman ben Gershon, the father of the author's wife, was murdered by the Nazis on 28 Adar 5702 (March 17, 1942). His granddaughter Zissel, born in 5714, was named after him.
Tags: holocaust, shoah, nazis, death

Title: Nazi murder of the Jewish women of Shumyachi and surrounding shtetlach
Summary: On 28 Adar 5702 the Nazis murdered the Jewish women gathered from Shumyachi, Klimovichi, Potsep and surrounding shtetlach, including the author's mother-in-law Feigl bas R' Moshe Leib Paz.
Story: After the war the author learned that the Germans had concentrated the Jews of the surrounding shtetlach in a single killing site, murdering the women on 28 Adar 5702. The author's wife Henya was the sole survivor of the entire Fradkin–Paz family; the children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren they raised are credited to the merit of these kedoshim.
Tags: shoah, shumyachi, klimovichi, potsep, paz, fradkin

Title: Nazi murder of the Jewish men of Shumyachi and surrounding shtetlach
Summary: On 29 Adar 5702 the Nazis murdered the Jewish men of the Shumyachi region, including the author's father-in-law R' Zusman b'r Gershon Fradkin and his sons Gershon and Nechemia.
Story: A day after killing the women, the Germans murdered the men of the gathered community. R' Zusman, the Shumyachi shochet and bodek who had also served as acting rav after R' Tzvi Edelstein left for Eretz Yisrael, had refused earlier suggestions to move to Moscow, saying that without him the townspeople would be forced to eat treif. He, his two young sons and the rest of the men were murdered on 29 Adar 5702.
Tags: shoah, shumyachi, fradkin, shochet, rav

Title: Children's Passover parade in Crown Heights
Summary: Yitzchok Groner and Moshe Kazarnovsky led roughly three hundred children carrying placards down Eastern Parkway in a public parade urging Jewish observance.
Story: Organized at Rabbi Hodakov's direction, the parade passed beneath the Rebbe's second-floor window. The Ramash later reported the Rebbe's enthusiasm. The event marked a shift toward public Jewish celebration and became a precursor to the Lag BaOmer parades the Seventh Rebbe inaugurated in 1953.
Tags: passover, groner, kazarnovsky, crown heights, lag baomer

Title: R. Aryeh Leib Sheinin perishes in the Holocaust
Summary: R. Aryeh Leib Sheinin was murdered during Chol HaMoed Pesach 5702.
Story: After more than two decades as rabbi of Dokshytsy and a tireless emissary of the Rebbe through the Vilna and Minsk regions, R. Aryeh Leib Sheinin perished in the Holocaust on Chol HaMoed Pesach 5702 (April 1942), Hashem yikom damo.
Tags: sheinin, dokshytsy, holocaust, shoah

Title: Annual Tomchei Temimim celebration in New York
Summary: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5702, the annual celebration of Merkos HaYeshivos Tomchei Temimim featured the Rayatz speaking while the Rebbe supported him with both hands.
Story: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5702 (14 June 1942), the central yeshiva organization Tomchei Temimim held its annual celebration in New York. A photograph captures the Rayatz speaking while standing, with the Rebbe physically supporting him with both hands. Also present in the images are Dr. Leo Jung, the Rashag, R. Joseph B. Soloveitchik, R. Dovber Chaskind and others.
Tags: tomchei temimim, new york, 770, rayatz, rebbe, soloveitchik

Title: Aussiedlung of Radom ghetto and murder of R' Baruch Friedman
Summary: In mid-Elul 5702 the Germans gathered the Jews of Radom in a large square for selection, sending R' Baruch Friedman and most of the ghetto to the gas chambers of Treblinka.
Story: Yosef Goldstein, who survived because of his work permit, walked beside R' Baruch Friedman to the selection and described how the mashpia stood with eyes raised heavenward, hands clasped, completely detached from his surroundings. Friedman had refused to seek a work permit, certain that he would not be taken to labor; he had once said at a Simchat Torah farbrengen in Warsaw that the Rebbe had blessed him that he would not die without teshuvah. He was deported to Treblinka along with most of the ghetto's inhabitants.
Tags: holocaust, radom, ghetto, aussiedlung, treblinka, baruch friedman, nazis

Title: Wedding of R' Moshe Ashkenazi and Devora Krasik
Summary: The chassid R' Moshe Ashkenazi married Devora Krasik, daughter of R' Chaim Eliezer Krasik and Leah née Gurary, on 5 Elul תש"ב in Tel Aviv.
Story: On 5 Elul תש"ב the chassid R' Moshe Ashkenazi married Devora Krasik in Tel Aviv. As a wedding gift, R' Nachum Yehoshua Ershler, shochet u-bodek of Königsberg, presented the couple with his rare copy of the third edition of the Siddur with Da"Ch — the small Königsberg-printed batch with the openly-acknowledged title page — inscribed with blessings for them to celebrate their golden jubilee.
Tags: wedding, tel aviv, ashkenazi, krasik, gurary

Title: Farbrengen in Radom ghetto on Rosh Chodesh Elul
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Elul 5702, Anash and the temimim of Radom held a farbrengen at which R' Baruch Friedman rebuked a participant for suggesting their suffering was God's will.
Story: When one of the participants groaned that nothing could be done if it was the Holy One's will that Jews suffer, R' Baruch Friedman rose and emotionally protested that it was forbidden to say such a thing. The gathering took place under intensifying persecution, with the yeshiva continuing its learning despite the deteriorating conditions in the ghetto.
Tags: holocaust, radom, ghetto, farbrengen, baruch friedman, elul

Title: Rebbetzin Chana Horenstein murdered at Treblinka
Summary: On 14 Elul 5702, Rebbetzin Chana Mushka Horenstein, mother of Rabbi Mordechai Menachem Mendel Horenstein, was taken to the gas chambers at Treblinka.
Story: According to the testimony of survivor Mordechai Unrad, who shared a barrack with Rabbi Horenstein at Treblinka, a Kapo brought a note from Sheina informing her husband that his mother had been led to the crematoria on 14 Elul 5702. The Horensteins had been trapped in Otwock since 1939 despite the Frierdiker Rebbe's prolonged efforts to extract them.
Tags: treblinka, holocaust, poland, horenstein, chana mushka

Title: R. Moshe Leib Rotstein reports on Tomchei Tmimim on 18 Elul 5702
Summary: On 18 Elul 5702, secretary R. Moshe Leib Rotstein issued a report on Tomchei Tmimim listing the pre-war Polish branches.
Story: The booklet 'Yeshivas Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch' described the network as having operated in Lodz, Vilna, Chelm, Patzanow, Chmielnik, Globoke, Kaluszyn and other cities. By the time of publication most of these communities and their yeshivos had been destroyed.
Tags: moshe leib rotstein, tomchei tmimim, lodz, vilna, chelm, patzanow, wwii

Title: Sheina Schneersohn-Horenstein killed in Treblinka
Summary: Sheina, the Sixth Rebbe's younger daughter, was killed at Treblinka on the second day of Rosh HaShanah.
Story: Sheina and her husband Menachem Mendel Horenstein had been unable to leave Poland because the Horensteins were Polish citizens denied entry to Latvia. Their fate remained unknown until after the war. The Ramash withheld the confirmed dates from the ailing Rebbe; the Seventh Rebbe later recited Kaddish annually on the second day of Rosh HaShanah for Sheina.
Tags: sheina horenstein, treblinka, holocaust, rosh hashanah

Title: Rebbetzin Sheina Horenstein murdered at Treblinka
Summary: On the second day of Rosh Hashanah 5703, Rebbetzin Sheina, youngest daughter of the Frierdiker Rebbe, was taken to the gas chambers at Treblinka.
Story: A Kapo informed the survivor Mordechai Unrad on 3 Tishrei 5703 that Sheina had been led to the crematoria on the second day of Rosh Hashanah. The Frierdiker Rebbe, not yet knowing the details, continued to refer to his youngest daughter and her husband as still being in Otwock in correspondence into Adar II 5703.
Tags: treblinka, holocaust, poland, horenstein, sheina, rayatz

Title: Sheina Horenstein killed at Treblinka
Summary: Sheina Horenstein, the Rebbe Rayatz's youngest daughter, was killed at Treblinka on the second day of Rosh HaShanah 5703.
Story: With the outbreak of war, Sheina and her husband Rabbi Mendel Horenstein had traveled with their adopted son to Otwock to care for Rabbi Mendel's aging parents. Eventually they were all captured by the Nazis. Their fate was unknown for years until a Treblinka survivor described the details in 1950.
Tags: treblinka, holocaust, nazi, horenstein, rosh-hashanah, otwock

Title: R. Yechiel Meir Blumenfeld murdered in Warsaw Ghetto
Summary: R. Yechiel Meir Blumenfeld, a founding figure of the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim and Tachkemoni rav, was murdered in the Warsaw Ghetto on Yom Kippur 5703.
Story: Born in 1893, Blumenfeld had returned to Warsaw after wartime exile in Russia and helped establish Tomchei Tmimim there, while serving as a Mizrachi rav at Tachkemoni and publishing his sefer Kol HaMitzvah. His death on Yom Kippur 1942 was part of the Nazi destruction of the Warsaw Jewish community.
Tags: warsaw-ghetto, holocaust, blumenfeld, yom-kippur

Title: Tomchei Temimim branch opened in Samarkand
Summary: During World War II, a branch of the underground yeshivah was established in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, followed shortly after by one in Tashkent.
Story: Between 1922 and 1940, the yeshivah had opened and closed in twenty-seven cities, often operating in multiple places at once, including remote Soviet Georgia. The Uzbekistan branches sustained Jewish life through and after the war.
Tags: samarkand, tashkent, uzbekistan, ww2, tomchei-temimim

Title: Yeshivah branch established in Samarkand
Summary: During wartime evacuation, a branch of Tomchei Temimim opened in remote Uzbekistan.
Story: As Chabad Chasidim fled the German invasion to Central Asia, a branch of the yeshivah was established in Samarkand. Within a short period another branch opened in Tashkent. These wartime outposts later became the nucleus that sustained Jewish life in the region for decades.
Tags: samarkand, uzbekistan, tashkent, tomchei temimim, wwii

Title: Menachem Mendel Horenstein killed in Treblinka
Summary: The Sixth Rebbe's son-in-law Mendel Horenstein was killed at Treblinka on 25 Cheshvan, seven weeks after his wife Sheina.
Story: Mordechai Unrad, who had been in Mendel's barracks at Treblinka, confirmed the dates of death to the Ramash in August 1949. The couple had adopted their nephew Yaakov Yosef Lis, who also perished. The information was withheld from the Sixth Rebbe in his lifetime.
Tags: mendel horenstein, treblinka, holocaust, 25 cheshvan

Title: Rabbi Mendel Horenstein killed at Treblinka
Summary: Rabbi Mendel Horenstein, son-in-law of the Rebbe Rayatz, was killed at Treblinka on 25 Marcheshvan, almost two months after his wife Sheina.
Story: His adopted nephew Yaakov Yosef Liss was also killed by the Nazis in 1942. The couple had adopted Yaakov Yosef when his mother (Mendel's sister Sara) died a few days after giving birth to her second child. In 1950 the seventh Rebbe received details of their fate from a Treblinka survivor.
Tags: treblinka, holocaust, nazi, horenstein, marcheshvan

Title: Rabbi Mordechai Menachem Mendel Horenstein murdered at Treblinka
Summary: On 25 Cheshvan 5703, Rabbi Mordechai Menachem Mendel Horenstein, son-in-law of the Frierdiker Rebbe, was taken from work at Treblinka to the gas chambers.
Story: Survivor Mordechai Unrad, returning from his work assignment, found that Rabbi Horenstein had been removed from his barrack along with a group of other Jews and led to the crematoria. The Frierdiker Rebbe's nearly four-year rescue effort — visas, exit permits, intermediaries in Italy, Germany, Sweden, and the State Department — had been thwarted at every turn by the Germans' refusal to grant exit permits.
Tags: treblinka, holocaust, poland, horenstein, rayatz

Title: Vaad Hatzalah cuts off funding to Chabad students in Shanghai
Summary: Beginning in December 1942, the Vaad Hatzalah rescue committee ceased life-saving disbursements to the Chabad yeshivah students stranded in Shanghai.
Story: While the Mir Yeshivah and other yeshivos received generous stipends for food and clothing, the Chabad students were left to fend for themselves. Rabbi Chaim Shmuelevitz quietly tried to assist them. After the war, the policy became a lasting wound; in 1962 the Seventh Rebbe told Rabbi Gutnick that it had caused his father-in-law to weep.
Tags: vaad hatzalah, shanghai, mir yeshivah, ashkenazi, agudas harabonim

Title: First edition of Hayom Yom published by Kehot
Summary: The first edition of Hayom Yom, a daily Chabad almanac compiled by the future Rebbe, was published by Kehot in 5703 (1943).
Story: Hayom Yom was compiled by Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson at the request of his father-in-law the Rebbe Rayatz, with each calendar day pairing a teaching, custom, or anecdote. Kehot's 1943 first edition made it a daily companion across Chabad households.
Tags: rebbe, kehot, hayom yom, first edition

Title: First Mesibos Shabbos children's parade
Summary: A children's parade through the city streets was held in 5703 to publicly affirm Torah and mitzvos.
Story: While the Rebbe headed the Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch before his nesius, he ran the Mesibos Shabbos campaign for children. In 5703 (1943) a public parade was organized through main streets, with children carrying signs about Torah and mitzvos after hearing the Rebbe speak. A special booklet with photos was published. The parade later became an annual Lag BaOmer event.
Tags: united states, mesibos shabbos, merkos, parade, children

Title: Hayom Yom first edition published
Summary: The first edition of Hayom Yom, compiled by the Rebbe, was published in New York in 5703.
Story: In 5703 (1942–43), the first edition of Hayom Yom was published in New York. Compiled by Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson, the future Rebbe, the daily-calendar book gathers Chassidic teachings, customs and stories. The Lubavitch Library preserves a copy of this first edition.
Tags: hayom yom, rebbe, brooklyn

Title: Japanese authorities establish Jewish ghetto in Shanghai's Hongkou district
Summary: Japanese occupation authorities confined Jewish refugees in Shanghai to a designated ghetto in the Hongkou district, administered by Sgt. Kano Ghoya.
Story: Food became scarce and the Chabad yeshivah students, already cut off from Vaad Hatzalah funds, were barely surviving on a bit of rice per day. Aryeh Leib Brailovsky, prompted by an enigmatic dream of the Rebbe pleading for his hungry children, raised funds locally to sustain them.
Tags: shanghai, hongkou, ghetto, kano ghoya, wwii

Title: Levin hides from Red Army search in wall cavity
Summary: In summer 5703, Levin hid inside a wall cavity while Red Army search parties broke into his home looking for draft evaders.
Story: During a summer 5703 sweep for army draft evaders, Levin hid in a wall cavity behind a curtain, reciting the maamar D"H Dirshu 5690 to himself. Soldiers broke the lock, searched the room, and one peered straight through the curtain crack but did not see him. A second search party was told 'we already checked here' and left — Levin and his wife celebrated their open miracle.
Tags: samarkand, wwii, red army, draft evasion, miracle, dirshu 5690

Title: Levin obtains false Polish-refugee papers as Naftali Batt
Summary: After abandoning a military medical exam in summer 5703, Levin received forged Polish-refugee papers — eventually under the name Naftali Batt.
Story: Summoned to a military medical exam, Levin slipped out before being seen and fled home without his papers. R' Waldman, a Polish Jew, supplied him with documents from a Polish refugee who had died in Siberia; when those wore out, Waldman brought new papers in the name Naftali Batt. Under that identity Levin lived hidden in Samarkand for several years, unable even to speak the Polish his papers claimed as his mother tongue.
Tags: samarkand, wwii, false papers, naftali batt, waldman, polish refugees, siberia

Title: Levin's sister Freida traced through Soviet bureau
Summary: In summer 5703, Levin's wife traced his sister Freida to a camp near Stalingrad through a new Soviet missing-persons bureau.
Story: Hearing in summer 5703 that a Soviet office had opened to trace people lost since the war began, Levin's wife inquired about his family and learned that his sister Freida was in a camp near Stalingrad. Sharing the surname Levin, she presented herself as Freida's sister-in-law and obtained her travel papers. Freida joined them in Samarkand and helped run the household weaving operation.
Tags: samarkand, wwii, family reunion, stalingrad, soviet bureaucracy

Title: Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch founded by Rayatz
Summary: The Rayatz established Chabad's central educational organization, the first network of Jewish day schools in the U.S.
Story: While other postwar Orthodox leaders focused on yeshivas as citadels of scholarship for a small nucleus, the Rebbe campaigned for fundamental change in general Jewish life worldwide. Merkos became the engine for that mission, predating other national Jewish educational organizations such as Torah Umesorah. The work would later expand into the global shluchim network.
Tags: merkos, united states, day schools, rayatz

Title: Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch founded in the United States
Summary: The Rayatz established Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch, Chabad's central educational organization, in the United States.
Story: Merkos seeded the first network of Jewish day schools in the United States, preceding similar national organizations such as Torah Umesorah. It would also lay groundwork for the postwar global shluchim movement.
Tags: merkos, united-states, day-schools, education

Title: R' Shimon Zelichover deported from Krakow to the death camps
Summary: In 5703 R' Shimon Zelichover was deported from Krakow to the Nazi extermination camps, where he was murdered.
Story: After years of teaching in Tzanz, Krzanov, Stolin, Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw, Yeshivat Chochmei Lublin and finally Krakow, Engel's life ended in the Shoah. His Torah was later collected in the volume Naharei Eish, printed in New York in 5753.
Tags: krakow, shoah, shimon engel zelichover, death camps, war

Title: Rabbi Aryeh Leib Kaplan killed on Yom Kippur
Summary: The Slabodka-trained rabbi who heeded the Rayatz's advice to remain in Russia was murdered by anti-Semitic thugs.
Story: Kaplan had been planning to immigrate to Palestine in 1922 when the Rayatz advised him to stay and help Russian Jews: 'If you protect the children of G-d, G-d will watch over your children.' He served as a rabbi near Kiev until his 1939 arrest and exile to Uzbekistan, where on the train he met Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson. His children all later escaped to Israel and the United States.
Tags: kaplan, uzbekistan, yom kippur, antisemitism, exile

Title: Ramash describes parental-love teaching to Edelman and Fogelman
Summary: At 770 Eastern Parkway, the Ramash recounted to yeshivah students Dovid Edelman and Hershel Fogelman a teaching from the Rebbe about loving every Jew completely.
Story: The Ramash had been chastised by elder Chasidim for warmly welcoming non-observant Jews rather than criticizing them. He asked the Rebbe if he was acting correctly. The Rebbe replied that just as a parent feels deeper love for a child missing a limb, G-d loves every Jew completely, but loves those who are missing observance even more. This philosophy clearly infused the Ramash's later leadership as the seventh Rebbe.
Tags: 770, new-york, edelman, fogelman, ahavat-yisrael, outreach

Title: Rebbe begins sending yeshivah students as US emissaries
Summary: In 1943, after relocating to America, the Rebbe began sending yeshivah students to American Jewish communities to teach chasidic philosophy.
Story: The idea had originated in a 1938 letter from Otwock to Rabbi Dovid Rabinowitz, proposing that outstanding yeshivah students spend extended time in US communities on purely spiritual missions. The project did not materialize before the war but was realized in 1943 in America. The program continues today as a global Merkos Shlichus initiative.
Tags: america, merkos-shlichus, yeshivah-students

Title: Rebbe Rayatz summarizes: 90 crates of sefarim rescued, 30 still in occupied Poland
Summary: In a letter of 11 Adar 5703 the Rebbe writes that ninety crates of sefarim have been saved from his former home and roughly thirty crates remain there.
Story: By early 1943 the Rebbe Rayatz could put a tally to the rescue effort: ninety crates of his library had reached safety, while approximately thirty more crates were still in Poland under Nazi occupation, with no realistic way to extract them while the war raged.
Tags: library, warsaw, wwii, schneersohn-library

Title: Children of Tehran arrive in Palestine
Summary: Some 1,228 Polish Jewish refugee children, most from religious families, arrived in Palestine after a long trek via Russia and Iran.
Story: The quasi-governmental Jewish Agency, controlled by Mapai, placed the children on secular kibbutzim without religious teachers, kosher food, or Shabbat observance. Their forced secular indoctrination would prompt international Orthodox protest led by Chief Rabbi Herzog and the Sixth Rebbe.
Tags: tehran children, palestine, jewish agency, mapai, herzog, stalin-sikorski

Title: Rebbe writes coded inquiry to Dubin about fate of Riga anash
Summary: On 23 Adar Rishon 5703 the Rebbe wrote to Dubin in Saratov, asking in disguised Yiddish about the welfare of named relatives and chassidim in Riga (Igros XIV:5306).
Story: Phrased to evade Soviet censors, the letter inquired after Chatche Feigin, Mottel the shochet Chefetz, Avraham Eli Asheroff, Elya Chaim Althaus, Mendel Zak, Avigdor Volshanik and others — all of whom, unknown to the Rebbe at that point, had already perished in the Riga massacres.
Tags: mordechai dubin, riga, saratov, yiddish, censorship, holocaust, shoah, world war ii

Title: Rayatz at Tomchei Tmimim annual celebration holding London cane
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz appears holding his metal-handled London cane at the annual Tomchei Tmimim celebration on 7 Adar II 5703.
Story: A photograph from the annual fundraising celebration for the Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch yeshivos, held on 7 Adar II 5703, shows Rebbe Rayatz holding the cane catalogued as library item 5188, whose metal handle is engraved 'LONDON SOLID S K.' Several other canes from his estate, including one purported to belong to R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, are preserved in the library archive.
Tags: tomchei tmimim, rayatz, cane, fundraising

Title: Talmid Shmuel Avraham Chanovitz dies in exile in Shanghai
Summary: On 9 Adar II 5703, Tomchei Tmimim student Shmuel Avraham Chanovitz passed away in exile in Shanghai.
Story: Of the 38 students who reached Japan and then Shanghai, talmid Shmuel Avraham Chanovitz did not survive the exile. He passed away in Shanghai on 9 Adar Sheini 5703 (March 16, 1943). A memorial matzeivah was erected in his honor; the remaining 27 students reached the United States only in the summer of 1946.
Tags: shanghai, yahrzeit, tomchei tmimim, refugees, wwii

Title: Sixth Rebbe writes anguished letter to Jacob Klatzkin on Jewish leadership
Summary: The Rebbe sent a long, bitter letter to philosopher Jacob Klatzkin lamenting media silence, government apathy, and Jewish leaders' failure during the Holocaust.
Story: Responding to Klatzkin's call for public demonstrations with Torah scrolls, the Rebbe wrote that media 'sit behind a shade,' political leaders' ears are 'closed to our cries,' and that the time had come to call all Jews — irrespective of party — to fasting, prayer, and teshuvah. He compared the Jewish silence unfavorably to that of other faith communities.
Tags: klatzkin, holocaust, stephen wise, war refugee board, rebbe letters

Title: Sixth Rebbe publishes letter protesting Jewish Agency treatment of Tehran Children
Summary: Two weeks before Passover, the Rebbe issued a public letter in Jewish newspapers protesting the Jewish Agency's placement of refugee children in irreligious settings.
Story: Responding to a request from the Gerrer Rebbe, he urged Orthodox groups to demand the children's transfer to a proper educational environment. He later organized over four hundred American rabbis in support of Chief Rabbi Herzog and proposed an international donations boycott of the Jewish Agency until it acceded.
Tags: tehran children, jewish agency, mapai, herzog, agudas harabonim

Title: Death of R' Yosef Garfinkel in wartime exile
Summary: R' Yosef Shmuel Garfinkel passed away on 28 Nissan 5703 in Ferghana while in WWII exile.
Story: On 28 Nissan 5703, during the World War II evacuation of Chabad families from Russia, R' Yosef Shmuel Garfinkel passed away in exile in Ferghana, Uzbekistan. His widow Chaya Mushka, along with their son Nechemia Sholom Rephael and daughter Rivka, later left Russia during the 5706-7 mass emigration of Chabad chassidim.
Tags: garfinkel, ferghana, wwii, uzbekistan, exile

Title: Levin and Teitelbaum smuggle a letter to the Rebbe
Summary: On Sunday of Parshat Bamidbar 5703, Israel Yehuda Levin and Michael Teitelbaum sent a joint Yiddish letter to the Rebbe via R' Leib Cohen.
Story: After years cut off from the Rebbe, an opening to write through Eretz Yisrael appeared in 5703. On the first day of the week of Bamidbar, Levin and Michael Teitelbaum jointly wrote a Yiddish letter — Teitelbaum opening, Levin closing — and gave it to R' Leib Cohen for transmission. Cohen, who did not know the writers, forwarded it with a note that it had come from Samarkand via Mrs. A. Dvoskin (Teitelbaum's wife).
Tags: samarkand, correspondence, michael teitelbaum, leib cohen, eretz yisrael, esther dvoskin

Title: Rabbi Chaim Kavash passes away in Samarkand
Summary: Rabbi Chaim Kavash, rabbi of Yochavitch who fled the Nazi advance to Samarkand, died there on 24 Iyar 5703.
Story: Born in Vyetka in 5649, Chaim Kavash studied at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch and in 5686 became rabbi of Yochavitch in the Polotsk district. As Soviet persecution of rabbis intensified he fled to Nevel; when the Germans invaded he escaped further east to Samarkand among Anash, dying there on 24 Iyar 5703. His estate included several heirloom vessels, including a spoon attributed to the Baal Shem Tov and a cup of R' Mordechai of Lechovitch.
