Tags: chaim kavash, samarkand, rabbi, wwii refugee, yochavitch, nevel, russia

Title: R. Yitzchak Mandelbaum perishes in Globoke
Summary: R. Yitzchak HaLevi Mandelbaum was murdered in Globoke on 19 Menachem Av 5703, as recorded in 'Churban Globak'.
Story: According to the memorial volume 'Churban Globak' (p. 28), Mandelbaum perished in the Holocaust in Globoke on 19 Menachem Av 5703 (August 20, 1943), Hashem yikom damo.
Tags: mandelbaum, globoke, holocaust, shoah

Title: Rabbis' March on Washington
Summary: More than 400 Orthodox rabbis marched from the Capitol to the White House three days before Yom Kippur, demanding US government action to rescue European Jewry.
Story: Organized by Peter Bergson with Vaad Hatzalah and Agudas Harabonim, the march was the only Jewish demonstration at the Capitol during the war. The Sixth Rebbe, unable to travel, sent a delegation of four — Mindel, Quint, Gurary, and Binyamin Levitin. President Roosevelt left the White House by a back exit on the advice of Wise and Roseman.
Tags: rabbis march, washington, fdr, bergson, silver, stephen wise, vaad hatzalah

Title: Tomchei Temimim Montreal dedicates former orphanage as new home
Summary: After Sam Bronfman and other donors helped acquire a former orphanage, the Montreal yeshivah dedicated its new permanent facility.
Story: Chief Rabbi Yehoshua Hirshorn called for the day to be marked as a Yom Tov for Montreal Jewry. By this point Bronfman, who had earlier tried to push the yeshivah to Toronto, had come to see its value. The yeshivah continued to expand, with the Rebbe corresponding regularly on curriculum and staffing.
Tags: montreal, tomchei temimim, bronfman, hirshorn

Title: R' Meir Gurkov released and arrives in Samarkand
Summary: In summer 5704, Levin's father-in-law R' Meir Gurkov was released and arrived in Samarkand with his wife Feiga Rivka.
Story: Levin's father-in-law R' Meir Gurkov was released from Soviet detention in summer 5704 and made his way to Samarkand with his wife Feiga Rivka. The couple rented an apartment in the city, rejoining the family circle there.
Tags: samarkand, soviet prison, meir gurkov, feiga rivka, family

Title: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson released from Soviet exile
Summary: After five years of Soviet exile, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson was released in 5704.
Story: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson was released from Soviet exile in 5704 (1944). A photograph taken after his release so changed his appearance that the Rebbe, on first seeing it, wrote in disbelief 'AAZ"L?' — 'is this truly my late father?' During his exile his wife Rebbetzin Chana joined him and produced ink from local plants so he could write his Torah glosses.
Tags: russia, levi yitzchak schneerson, soviet, exile

Title: Rebbe Rayatz founds Bikur Cholim department of Machne Israel
Summary: In the summer of 5704 the Rebbe Rayatz founded the Bikur Cholim department of Machne Israel and appointed R' Yochanan Gordon as its chairman.
Story: In summer 5704 the Rebbe Rayatz established a Bikur Cholim (visiting the sick) division within his Machne Israel organization. He appointed R' Yochanan Gordon as its chairman, leveraging Gordon's communal credibility and pastoral disposition. This was one of several institutional building blocks the Rebbe Rayatz put in place during his early American years.
Tags: new york, rebbe rayatz, bikur cholim, machne israel, yochanan gordon

Title: Torah Umesorah founded by Rabbi Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz
Summary: Rabbi Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz of Torah Vodaath was instrumental in establishing Torah Umesorah, the National Society for Hebrew Day Schools.
Story: Torah Umesorah took the first tentative steps to open Orthodox day schools beyond New York. The Sixth Rebbe — already running a network of yeshivos in over a dozen cities — welcomed the new initiative rather than treating it as competition.
Tags: torah umesorah, mendlowitz, day schools

Title: Roosevelt creates the War Refugee Board
Summary: President Roosevelt signed an executive order establishing the War Refugee Board three months after the Rabbis' March on Washington.
Story: Created over the opposition of Secretary of State Breckinridge Long and pushed by Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau, the Board ultimately helped save many Jews — particularly in Hungary. But it came too late for the more than five million Jews already murdered.
Tags: fdr, war refugee board, morgenthau, bergson, rabbis march

Title: Final accounting: 100 of 117 crates of library reached USA
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz writes that of approximately 117 crates of sefarim only 100 reached America; the remaining 17 were lost in Poland.
Story: In an igeres dated 7 Shevat 5704, the Rebbe noted that not all of his sefarim were saved from Poland: of some 117 crates only 100 had arrived in the USA. R' Chaim Lieberman later told the author that the Germans inspected the first transport and found nothing objectionable, but by the second transport America was already at war; the storehouse holding the remaining books was eventually bombed.
Tags: library, schneersohn-library, warsaw, new-york

Title: Rebbe's response letter to Levin written in Brooklyn
Summary: On 24 Nissan 5704 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote a response from Brooklyn blessing Levin with healthy offspring and good livelihood.
Story: On 24 Nissan 5704, the Rebbe — through R' Moshe Gurary — answered Levin's smuggled letter from Brooklyn, blessing him with 'zera chaya vekayama' and good parnassah in both material and spiritual matters. The letter never reached Levin in Russia; only forty years later did he discover in the archive that the Rebbe had blessed him before his children were born. He saw in this the hidden providence behind his eventual escape from Russia.
Tags: brooklyn, frierdiker rebbe, correspondence, moshe gurary, blessing for children, archive

Title: Chabad Old City synagogue faces wartime closure
Summary: On 10 Iyar 5704, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Agudat Chasidei Chabad in Eretz Yisrael urgently appealing to save the Chabad Old City synagogue from closure during WWII.
Story: With WWII straining the Jewish yishuv, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote on 10 Iyar 5704 that maintaining the Chabad synagogue in Jerusalem's Old City required 4–5 pounds per month to hire men for the minyan. He instructed Agudat Chasidei Chabad to take responsibility, allocating one pound monthly and securing matching contributions from Kolel Chabad, the Gemach, and Toras Emes. The Rebbe wrote separately to each institution.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, jerusalem, old city, world war ii, kolel chabad

Title: Levin matches his sister Freida with R' Asher Sasonkin
Summary: In Tammuz 5704, Levin arranged the marriage of his sister Freida to R' Asher Sasonkin, who began running a bread-distribution kiosk.
Story: In Tammuz 5704 Levin matched his sister Freida with R' Asher Sasonkin in Samarkand. He rented them an apartment, and Sasonkin took a job distributing bread at a kiosk, giving the new household a steady livelihood.
Tags: samarkand, shidduch, asher sasonkin, family

Title: 1,000 European Jewish refugees arrive at Oswego, New York camp
Summary: Roughly 1,000 European Jewish refugees, many concentration-camp survivors, were admitted to the United States and placed in a camp at Oswego in upstate New York.
Story: The camp was the only one in the US for European refugees during the war, operated by the War Relocation Authority. The refugees were not given US immigration status. The Rebbe sprang into action to provide religious services and educational programming for them.
Tags: oswego, fort ontario, refugees, war relocation authority

Title: Rayatz orders Kollel Chabad to follow Agudat Chabad directives
Summary: On 19 Menachem Av 5704 the Rayatz wrote to Kollel Chabad's leadership directing them and Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek to obey Agudat Chassidei Chabad of Eretz Yisrael.
Story: Disputes between Kollel Chabad and Agudat Chabad over jurisdiction—particularly over chassidus shiurim in Jerusalem—had been escalating between the two organizations. The Rayatz resolved the conflict by formally subordinating Kollel Chabad and Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek's administrators to Agudat Chabad's directives. The ruling consolidated authority over Chabad activity in the Holy Land under the newer Tel Aviv-based body.
Tags: rayatz, kollel chabad, agudat chabad, tzemach tzedek yeshiva, jerusalem, tel aviv

Title: Passing of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson in Alma-Ata
Summary: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson passed away in exile in Alma-Ata on 20 Av 5704.
Story: The Rebbe's father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, passed away on 20 Menachem Av 5704 (August 1944) in Alma-Ata, capital of Kazakhstan. He had been allowed, after great efforts of devoted friends working at risk to their lives, to move from the village of Chili to Alma-Ata, where conditions were better both materially and spiritually because a Jewish community existed there.
Tags: alma-ata, kazakhstan, soviet union, exile, levi yitzchak schneerson

Title: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson passes away in exile
Summary: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson passed away on 20 Av 5704 in Alma-Ata.
Story: After Soviet exile in Chiili (Kazakhstan), Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson was eventually permitted to move to Alma-Ata, where he passed away on 20 Av 5704 (Aug 9, 1944). His wife Rabbanit Chana had sent him the Tehillim he recited tearfully in his final years; she later brought it out of Russia.
Tags: levi yitzchak schneerson, soviet exile, kazakhstan, alma ata, yahrzeit

Title: Sixth Rebbe's delegation visits Oswego refugee camp
Summary: Eleven days after the refugees' arrival, the Rebbe sent Rabbis Hodakov and Kazarnovsky and Dr. Mindel to Oswego to assess their needs.
Story: Over the following months Chabad supplied religious provisions, educational programs, and general assistance. When the refugees were released in 1945–46, a group of the children enrolled in the Chabad yeshivah in Brooklyn.
Tags: oswego, hodakov, kazarnovsky, mindel, refugees

Title: Midrash Shmuel yeshiva opens in Old City Jerusalem
Summary: On 15 Elul 5704 the Chabad yeshiva Midrash Shmuel, named for the Rebbe Maharash, began classes in the Old City of Jerusalem.
Story: The yeshiva was led by Rabbi Yitzchak Avigdor Ornstein as the Rayatz's representative, with Rabbis Alexander Yudasin and Yitzchak Naeh on the standing administration. Its stated mission was to anchor a Chabad center in the Old City for serious learners, teaching Shas, poskim and Chassidus in the path of Chabad's rebbeim.
Tags: jerusalem, old city, midrash shmuel, ornstein, yudasin, naeh, kollel chabad, maharash

Title: Rebbe Rayatz falls ill with heart disease
Summary: Beginning in late Tishrei 5705, the Rebbe Rayatz began suffering fatigue and pains around the heart, marking the onset of a serious heart illness.
Story: Already at the end of Tishrei 5705 (October 1944), Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn began to feel fatigue, agitation and pains around the heart. Dr. Wilder visited him almost daily, several times together with the cardiologist Dr. Dressler. They prescribed medication and ordered him to rest, though the Rebbe continued his writing, correspondence, and reception of visitors as much as possible.
Tags: illness, heart disease, rayatz, brooklyn, dr. wilder, dr. dressler

Title: Founding meeting for Yeshivat Achei Tmimim Lubavitch Chicago
Summary: On 28 Tishrei 5705 a meeting with Chicago donors raised $25,000 in two-year loans toward purchasing a building for Yeshivat Achei Tmimim Lubavitch in Chicago.
Story: On 28 Tishrei 5705 (15 October 1944) Mr. Pinchas Rismann, Mr. and Mrs. Yechezkel Liesner, Mr. Palmer, Rabbi Rodstein, Rabbi Predmesky and the Rebbe's son-in-law Rashag met with the Rebbe Rayatz about establishing Yeshivat Achei Tmimim in Chicago. The Liesners pledged a $15,000 two-year loan, with Rismann and C. S. Palmer each adding $5,000, all earmarked to purchase a building for the new yeshivah.
Tags: chicago, achei tmimim, yeshiva, liesner, rismann, palmer, fundraising

Title: Assembly on reviving Chassidic communities in America
Summary: On 29 Tishrei 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz convened an assembly of Anash on reviving Chassidic communities, organized around shul congregants, scattered Anash, and Chassidic lineage families.
Story: On the evening of 29 Tishrei 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz convened an assembly of Anash that he had summoned regarding the revival of Chassidic communities in the present generation. The discussion was framed around three categories: regular congregants of Anash shuls, individual Anash who pray in other shuls, and descendants of Chassidic families — with a coordinating committee to be selected.
Tags: anash, america, shuls, community

Title: Suitable building identified in Chicago for Yeshivat Achei Tmimim
Summary: On 5 Marcheshvan 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz was told that a large, suitable building had been identified in Chicago to house the new Achei Tmimim Lubavitch yeshivah, with purchase planned the next day.
Story: On the evening of 5 Marcheshvan 5705, the Rebbe Rayatz's son-in-law Rashag informed him that contacts in Chicago had reported finding a large, suitable building for Yeshivat Achei Tmimim Lubavitch and intended to purchase it the next day. The development came less than two weeks after the founding fundraising meeting on 28 Tishrei.
Tags: chicago, achei tmimim, yeshiva building

Title: Mindel project to compile English booklet on Chabad communal work
Summary: On Motzaei Shabbat Lech Lecha 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz began dictating, to son-in-law Ramash and R. Nissan Mindel, material on the communal and economic activity of the Chabad Rebbes for an English-language booklet.
Story: From Motzaei Shabbat Lech Lecha, 11 Marcheshvan 5705, the Rebbe Rayatz began quietly relating to his son-in-law Ramash (the future Rebbe) and to Nissan Mindel an account of the communal activity — especially economic — of the Mitteler Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek, the Maharash, and the Rashab through 5661. Ramash relayed the words to Mindel, who took notes; their stated aim was to compile and print a Chabad-leadership communal-activity booklet in English.
Tags: nissan mindel, ramash, english, chabad rebbes, biography

Title: Rebbe Rayatz directs Anash that he can no longer receive visitors
Summary: On 21 Marcheshvan 5705, the Rebbe Rayatz issued a general directive to Anash that, per his doctors, he must rest from receiving people and could communicate only in writing.
Story: On 21 Marcheshvan 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a general directive (printed in Igrot Kodesh vol. 8, letter 2,535) informing Chassidim that his doctors had ordered him to cease in-person audiences. He explained that he was suffering chest pain requiring full rest, yet noted that the demands of spreading Torah, fear of Heaven, and proper chinuch required tenfold more strength than before.
Tags: illness, rayatz, anash, yechidus, correspondence

Title: Roosevelt elected to a fourth term as US President
Summary: Diary entry of 22 Marcheshvan 5705 records that Franklin D. Roosevelt had been elected US President for a fourth term.
Story: Writing on 22 Marcheshvan 5705 (8 November 1944), the Rebbe Rayatz recorded that it had become known that Mr. F. D. Roosevelt had been elected President of the United States for the fourth time. The previous day's diary entry — written on US election day, 21 Marcheshvan / 7 November 1944 — had noted the day's significance.
Tags: usa, roosevelt, election, wwii

Title: Rayatz sends congratulatory letter to President Roosevelt
Summary: On 23 Marcheshvan 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz drafted a letter of blessing to President Roosevelt on his re-election and asked R. Nissan Mindel to translate it into English.
Story: On 23 Marcheshvan 5705 (9 November 1944), although feeling unwell, the Rebbe Rayatz composed a letter of blessing to the newly re-elected President Roosevelt. He gave the draft to Nissan Mindel to translate into English so that it could be sent in the language of the country.
Tags: usa, roosevelt, letter, mindel

Title: Rebbe Rayatz suffers heart attack
Summary: On 26 Marcheshvan 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz suffered a heart attack and remained bedridden for approximately three weeks.
Story: On 26 Marcheshvan 5705 (12 November 1944) the Rebbe Rayatz suffered a heart attack. He lay bedridden in serious condition for roughly three weeks, during which time he did not write in his diary at all. Drs. Wilder and Dressler attended him throughout the recovery.
Tags: illness, heart attack, rayatz, brooklyn

Title: Sixth Rebbe suffers heart attack
Summary: The Rebbe suffered a heart attack on 26 Cheshvan, triggered by a letter detailing the Nazi murder of his closest Chasidim in Riga.
Story: Already weakened after the High Holidays and ordered to rest by his cardiologist, the Rebbe received the report describing how Reb Itche der Masmid, Rabbi Mordechai Cheifetz, Rabbi Yechezkel Feigin and others had been burned to death in a Riga synagogue. He slowly recovered over the following weeks but his health remained fragile.
Tags: heart attack, 26 cheshvan, riga, holocaust, illness

Title: First 19 Kislev farbrengen in Samarkand and birth of Miriam Reizel
Summary: Anash held their first large 19 Kislev farbrengen in Samarkand, and that same evening the author's daughter Miriam Reizel was born at home.
Story: For the first time since arriving in wartime exile, the Chabad chassidim of Samarkand secured a large room and organized a major 19 Kislev farbrengen for 5705. The author hauled his big number-30 kerosene retouching lamp to the venue to illuminate it. Returning home, he ran to fetch a nurse for his wife's labor, but by the time he came back she had given birth on her own to their daughter Miriam Reizel — 'a chassidishe daughter' — at the very hour of the farbrengen.
Tags: samarkand, 19-kislev, farbrengen, chassidim, family, uzbekistan, ww2

Title: Rebbe Rayatz publishes thanksgiving letter for recovery
Summary: On 24 Kislev 5705, beginning to recover, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a general letter thanking God and Anash for prayers during his illness.
Story: On 24 Kislev 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz, beginning to regain strength, composed a public letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. 8, letter 2,548) thanking God for His great kindness and Anash for their prayers and blessings, which he credited with raising him from three weeks of severe suffering. Even then, he was confined to bed by day and forbidden from returning to the yechidus room.
Tags: illness, rayatz, anash, letter

Title: Rebbe Rayatz returns to study after six-week heart illness
Summary: On 7 Tevet 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz returned to his yechidus room for the first time after roughly six weeks of illness.
Story: On 7 Tevet 5705 (23 December 1944), after about six weeks of heart illness, the Rebbe Rayatz returned to his study for the first time, reading books although still feeling weak. He prayed for strength to resume spreading Torah with fear of Heaven, strengthening institutions, kosher education, guiding Anash, and editing his memoir manuscripts.
Tags: illness, rayatz, yechidus

Title: Maamar Mai Chanukah written for Kriah V'Kedushah Kislev issue
Summary: On 15 Tevet 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote the maamar 'Mai Chanukah' for the delayed Kislev issue of the Yiddish journal Kriah V'Kedushah.
Story: Because of the Rebbe Rayatz's illness, the monthly Yiddish journal Kriah V'Kedushah had not appeared during Kislev. On Sunday 15 Tevet 5705 he wrote the maamar 'Mai Chanukah' for the Kislev issue and sent it to Mr. L. The Tevet issue maamar, 'Ki Ner Mitzvah V'Torah Or,' followed the next day, 16 Tevet.
Tags: kriah vkedushah, chanukah, maamar, yiddish

Title: End of World War II in Europe
Summary: The Second World War ended in the summer of 5705 (1945), prompting the Chabad refugee community in Samarkand to begin planning their departure.
Story: Even before the war ended, the material and spiritual situation among the Lubavitcher refugees in Samarkand had improved — life became more cheerful and bachelors began marrying. But everyone understood they would not remain in Samarkand once the war ended, which it did in the summer of 1945.
Tags: world war ii, samarkand, soviet union

Title: First edition of Tehillas Hashem siddur published in New York
Summary: The first edition of the Tehillas Hashem siddur was published in New York in 5705 (1945) by the Central Organization for Jewish Education.
Story: Largely a photographic reissue of the 1911 Vilna Seder HaAvodah with corrections, the 1945 New York Tehillas Hashem became the most widely used Chabad siddur of the modern era, eventually printed in close to one hundred subsequent editions.
Tags: new york, siddur, tehillas hashem, kehot, first edition

Title: First Haggadah printed in the Far East (Shanghai)
Summary: A Haggadah containing 238 commentaries was printed in Shanghai in 5705, the first ever in the Far East.
Story: In 5705 (1945), a remarkable Haggadah was printed in Shanghai, containing 238 commentaries and supplementary materials. It was the first Haggadah ever printed in the Far East, produced amid the displaced Jewish community there during World War II.
Tags: haggadah, shanghai, china, far-east, world-war-ii

Title: First post-war Haggadah printed in Föhrenwald DP camp
Summary: A photo-offset Haggadah was printed in the Föhrenwald DP camp in liberated Germany in 5705 for survivors.
Story: In 5705/5706 (1945–1946), the first Haggadah in liberated Europe was printed in Föhrenwald as a photo-offset reproduction of a Warsaw edition. Produced by the YPA publishing house, it was intended for the She'erit HaPleita displaced-person camps in Germany and was supplemented with illustrations taken from other Haggadot.
Tags: haggadah, föhrenwald, displaced-persons, germany, world-war-ii

Title: Itta Devorah Levin survives typhus at home in Samarkand
Summary: In winter 5705 Itta Devorah Levin contracted brushnoi typhus and recovered at home rather than risk hospitalization.
Story: In winter 5705 Itta Devorah Levin fell ill with brushnoi typhus; with Soviet hospitals nearly a death sentence, she was nursed at home and slowly recovered. Left weakened, she moved to her parents' home to convalesce, and the family changed apartments. The couple poured out prayers for healthy children, fulfilling 'horidi kanachal dimah.'
Tags: samarkand, typhus, illness, family, soviet hospitals

Title: Lubavitcher Rebbe publishes Haggadah for children with English translation
Summary: The Lubavitcher Rebbe issued a Haggadah following the Alter Rebbe's nusach with English Seder laws for children in New York.
Story: In 5705 (1945), a Haggadah following the Chabad Alter Rebbe's nusach was published in New York with laws and Seder signs in English at its end. The 32-page octavo edition was designed for children. It launched the Lubavitcher Rebbe's project of producing Haggadot specifically suited for educating Jewish youth.
Tags: chabad, rebbe, new york, english, haggadah, children

Title: Publication of Maamarei Maharash on Likutei Torah in New York
Summary: The Chabad Maharash Rebbe Shmuel's discourses 'Torat Shmuel - Likutei Torah - Matzah Zu - 5640' were published in New York.
Story: In 5705 (1945), 'Torat Shmuel - Likutei Torah - Matzah Zu - 5640' was published in New York, containing the Chassidic discourses of the Maharash Rebbe Shmuel Schneersohn of Lubavitch. The 94-page edition focused on the Pesach-related discourse 'Matzah Zu' delivered in 5640 (1880). It served the Chabad community's tradition of studying the Rebbes' annual maamarim.
Tags: chabad, maharash, new york, torat shmuel, matzah zu

Title: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson passes away in Alma Ata
Summary: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson died in Alma Ata, Kazakhstan in 1945 with his wife Rebbetzin Chana at his bedside, after years of Soviet exile.
Story: Exiled in 1939 from his rabbinical post for religious activism, Levi Yitzchak endured years in a remote Kazakh village. After his death his wife eventually escaped Russia through the Great Escape, reaching a German DP camp and ultimately Paris.
Tags: levi yitzchak schneerson, alma ata, kazakhstan, rebbetzin chana

Title: Rayatz launches refugee relief, public school program, and Jewish farmer outreach
Summary: The Rayatz opened a relief office for refugees with a Paris branch, established Shaloh for public-school Jewish education, and launched outreach to Jewish farmers.
Story: In 1945, as the Holocaust ended, the Rayatz expanded Chabad's footprint into three new spheres: postwar refugee aid, religious instruction for Jewish children in American public schools, and connecting with isolated Jewish farmers. Each initiative reflected his vision of reaching every Jew, wherever they were.
Tags: refugees, paris, shaloh, public schools, jewish farmers, outreach

Title: Soviet Union annexes Latvia at end of WWII
Summary: Soviet troops seize Latvia, incorporating it into the USSR until 1991.
Story: Latvia's first independence ended; the surviving Jewish community came under Soviet rule. Religious life persisted underground, sustained by the legacy of the Rebbe's six-year stay decades earlier.
Tags: latvia, soviet, wwii

Title: Soviet Union seizes Latvia
Summary: Soviet troops seize Latvia, ending German occupation and making the country part of the USSR.
Story: Latvia remained part of the Soviet Union until it regained independence in 1991. The vibrant Riga Jewish community the Rebbe had served in the late 1920s and early 1930s lived on in fragments under Soviet rule, as Rabbi Rakeffet would discover during his 1985 Mossad mission.
Tags: latvia, soviet, world war ii

Title: WWII ends in summer 5705
Summary: World War II ended in summer 5705 with the Allied victory over Germany and Japan.
Story: In the summer of 5705 (1945), World War II ended with the victory of the United States and its allies over Germany and Japan. In Shanghai, the Japanese forces who had controlled the city for several years and confined Jews to a ghetto-like area were replaced by American troops. Among the American soldiers were many Yiddish-speaking Jews from New York's East Side and Manhattan, whose presence cheered the Chabad yeshiva students stranded there.
Tags: war, wwii, shanghai, japan, united states, allied victory

Title: Passing of R' Tzvi Hirsh Padnes, treasurer of Shomrei Shabbos
Summary: R' Tzvi Hirsh Padnes, treasurer of the Shomrei Shabbos free-loan society, passed away on 11 Shevat 5705 and was buried the following day.
Story: R' Tzvi Hirsh Padnes, who served as treasurer (gizbor) of the Chabad Shomrei Shabbos gemach in New York, passed away on 11 Shevat 5705 and was buried on 12 Shevat. R' Yochanan Gordon wrote a touching biographical letter about him to the Rebbe Rayatz, describing how Padnes had been orphaned young in Russia, served four years in the Russian army at Libau, fled the Russo-Japanese War to America, and spent his evenings emptying Rabbi Meir Baal HaNess pushkas for Chabad and visiting the sick. The Rebbe Rayatz responded with letters of consolation (Igros Kodesh vol. 8, nos. 2630-2631).
Tags: new york, tzvi hirsh padnes, shomrei shabbos, gemach, obituary

Title: Editing of Likkutei Dibburim from 5700 begun
Summary: On 17 Tevet 5705, at his son-in-law Ramash's prompting, the Rebbe Rayatz began reviewing his 5700 sichot starting from his arrival in America, in preparation for printing.
Story: On 17 Tevet 5705 (2 January 1945) the Rebbe Rayatz began going through transcripts of sichot from 5700, starting from the day of his arrival in the United States, in order to prepare them for publication. The project — eventually published as part of Likkutei Dibburim — was undertaken at the urging of his son-in-law Ramash (the future Rebbe).
Tags: likkutei dibburim, sichot, 5700, ramash

Title: Pledge of $8,000 to print Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: On 19 Tevet 5705 Mr. Elchanan Glazer pledged $8,000 in his ailing father's name toward the printing of the Tzemach Tzedek's writings.
Story: On 19 Tevet 5705 (4 January 1945) the Rebbe Rayatz received Mr. Elchanan Glazer, whose father Mr. Yisrael Glazer was ill. He promised to give $8,000 — the estimated cost of printing the Tzemach Tzedek's works — toward that project. The Rebbe prayed that the pledge would quickly come to fruition.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, fundraising, glazer, printing

Title: Chevrei Adei-Ad organization launched
Summary: On 22 Tevet 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz drafted founding letters for the Chevrei Adei-Ad institution and invited rabbis Silver, Dushavitz and Telushkin to join its Torah council.
Story: On 22 Tevet 5705 (7 January 1945) the Rebbe Rayatz prepared the founding letters for the new institution Chevrei Adei-Ad: a general circular announcing its establishment, a supplementary letter to Rabbi Mordechai Mentlik regarding the administrative board, and individual letters to Rabbis Silver, Dushavitz and Telushkin inviting them to serve on its Torah council.
Tags: chevrei adei-ad, mentlik, torah council, silver, telushkin

Title: Reception of Rabbi Aryeh Leib Kramer of Montreal Tomchei Tmimim
Summary: On 22 Tevet 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz received Rabbi Aryeh Leib Kramer, principal of Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim in Montreal, who reported on the state of the yeshivah and its branches.
Story: On the evening of 22 Tevet 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz received Rabbi Aryeh Leib Kramer, principal of Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch in Montreal and its branch ketanot yeshivot. Kramer reported in detail on the yeshivah's physical and spiritual state, and the Rebbe urged him to establish Beit Rivka, a school for girls aged 15–18 to be trained as teachers, alongside Beit Sarah for younger girls.
Tags: montreal, tomchei tmimim, kramer, beit rivka, beit sarah

Title: Rayatz receives Massechet Chagigah at Machaneh Israel Siyum HaShas
Summary: At the Siyum HaShas of Machaneh Israel held the night of 23 Tevet 5705, the Rebbe Rayatz took Tractate Chagigah as his portion in the chalukat haShas.
Story: On Tuesday 24 Tevet 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz recorded that, at the previous night's chalukat haShas of Machaneh Israel, he had taken Massechet Chagigah as his portion. He prayed that God enlighten his eyes and heart in Torah and bless his work in all Torah and charitable institutions, despite the cold and head pains he was then suffering.
Tags: machaneh israel, siyum hashas, chagigah, talmud

Title: Cold passes; Rebbe Rayatz resumes yechidus on 26 Tevet
Summary: On 26 Tevet 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz, his cold and fever having passed, received people in yechidus, including the principal of Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim Montreal.
Story: On 26 Tevet 5705 the cold, nasal congestion and fever the Rebbe had been suffering finally passed. That evening he received Rabbi R. Sh. L. about the administration of Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch in Montreal, and also Rabbi Kramer, the principal of that yeshivah.
Tags: illness, rayatz, yechidus, montreal

Title: Lt. Col. Ernst Bloch killed at the front in the final days of the war
Summary: Ernst Bloch, the half-Jewish Abwehr officer who escorted the Rebbe out of Warsaw, was killed near Berlin only days before the war's end.
Story: After leading the Rebbe's rescue, Bloch was promoted to colonel and later appointed a battalion commander in Russia in 1943. In February 1945 the SS forced his dismissal from the army due to his Jewish background. When the Red Army reached Berlin in April 1945, he returned to the front and was killed days before the German surrender.
Tags: nazi germany, ernst bloch, berlin, abwehr, world war ii, death

Title: Admiral Wilhelm Canaris executed by the Nazis
Summary: Admiral Wilhelm Canaris, head of the Abwehr who had authorized the Rebbe's rescue, was hanged just weeks before the end of World War II.
Story: Canaris had grown disillusioned with Hitler after witnessing atrocities in Warsaw, attempted a 1943 ceasefire with the Allies through intelligence chiefs in Spain, and was eventually implicated in a plot to kill Hitler. His execution on April 9, 1945, came only weeks before Germany's surrender.
Tags: nazi germany, wilhelm canaris, abwehr, resistance, execution, world war ii

Title: Tomchei Tmimim children's parade from 770 courtyard
Summary: A parade for the Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch chadarim children set out from the 770 courtyard on 9 Iyar 5705.
Story: Rebbe Rayatz's network of Tomchei Tmimim chadarim in America held a children's gathering in the 770 courtyard, where the synagogue was later built. On 9 Iyar 5705 a parade was organized for them, departing from the courtyard. Surviving photographs from that period show R' Yitzchak Dovber Ushpal, R' Shneur Zalman Gourary, and R' Shmuel Isaac Popack with the children at the Eastern Parkway entrance.
Tags: 770, tomchei tmimim, brooklyn, children, chadarim

Title: Rayatz formally christens Midrash Shmuel and pledges Pesach support
Summary: On 17 Iyar 5705 the Rayatz wrote to Rabbi Yudasin confirming Midrash Shmuel's founding, its name in honor of his grandfather the Maharash, and his 50-shekel Pesach donation.
Story: The Rayatz had earlier written on Rosh Chodesh Adar 5705 asking Rabbi Ornstein for a full roster of students with ages, conduct, and family details. The Iyar letter expressed his blessing on Yudasin for the merit of helping establish the institution.
Tags: jerusalem, midrash shmuel, ornstein, yudasin, rayatz, maharash

Title: Rebbe weeps over Chasidim murdered in the Holocaust
Summary: In May 1945, as news of the Holocaust reached America, the Rebbe wept uncontrollably over photographs of his murdered Chasidim.
Story: With the war in Europe ended and the scope of the Nazi genocide becoming clear, the sixth Rebbe sat in his office gazing at pictures of devoted followers like Rabbis Yechezkel 'Chatche' Feigin and Yitzchak 'Itche der Masmid' Horowitz. The fate of his daughter Sheina remained unknown. Rabbi Shmuel Levitin could not console him, and only the upbeat Rabbi Moshe Chaim Yehoshua Schneersohn-Twerski was finally able to lift his mood.
Tags: holocaust, world war ii, yechezkel feigin, itche der masmid, shmuel levitin, moshe chaim yehoshua schneersohn-twerski

Title: End of WWII celebrated by Samarkand chassidim
Summary: On 5 Sivan 5705 (May 17, 1945) Levin and Michael Teitelbaum farbrenged in Samarkand to mark the end of the war.
Story: When news arrived on 5 Sivan 5705 that the war was over, Levin and Michael Teitelbaum sat together drinking l'chaim in great joy. Others mocked their celebration — they had profited from valid wartime travel papers — but Levin gave thanks that the bloodshed of Jews had ended and that he might now leave the house openly and resume contact with the Rebbe.
Tags: samarkand, wwii, victory, michael teitelbaum

Title: Stalin elevated to supreme military rank of generalissimo
Summary: The Supreme Soviet elevated Stalin to the highest military rank of generalissimo.
Story: Though Stalin rejected the new generalissimo uniform and continued referring to himself as a marshal, his military attire fulfilled the Rashab's 1920 prediction that 'Stalin will follow the spirit of the time as needed, and he will be adorned with epaulets.' At Yalta and Potsdam, Stalin had appeared in his marshal uniform.
Tags: stalin, soviet union, world war ii

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes to Aryeh Leib Kremer about visas
Summary: On 24 Tammuz 5705, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Aryeh Leib Kremer urging stronger measures to secure American visas for the students stranded in Shanghai.
Story: On 24 Tammuz 5705 (Igrot Kodesh vol. 8, letter 2736), the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to R. Aryeh Leib Kremer in response to his letter about visas for the Tomchei Tmimim students stranded in Shanghai. The Rebbe instructed him to take stronger and more reliable measures, to immediately send the list of students to R. Yerachmiel Binyaminson, and announced that he himself would write to Binyaminson asking him to intervene with those who had influence in such matters.
Tags: visas, united states, shanghai, tomchei tmimim, kremer, binyaminson

Title: Shanghai students send petition to Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: On Chai Elul 5705, the Tomchei Tmimim students in Shanghai sent a heartfelt letter to the Rebbe Rayatz begging to be rescued from Shanghai's harsh climate.
Story: On 18 (Chai) Elul 5705, the students wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe pleading from the depths of their hearts to be saved quickly from Shanghai — described as a city of an abyss with harsh, oppressive air that drained their strength and caused various illnesses. They emphasized that the city was unsuitable for yeshiva students and bnei Torah, and begged to be brought close to the Rebbe and his chassidim to resume orderly study and inner avodah.
Tags: shanghai, tomchei tmimim, letter, petition, health

Title: Dr. Nissan Mindel sent on mission to England
Summary: In September 1945 the Rebbe sent his secretary Dr. Nissan Mindel to England to survey postwar European Jewry and explore Chabad expansion.
Story: Mindel's mandate was to 'collect detailed information on the economic and spiritual status of our fellow Jews in liberated Europe' and to scope options for Chabad's educational programs in the United Kingdom. The Rebbe wrote ahead to Jewish leaders and the British Chabad community asking them to assist him.
Tags: nissan mindel, england, united kingdom, postwar survey, shlichus

Title: HaKriah VeHaKedushah ceases publication
Summary: The Sixth Rebbe's wartime monthly HaKriah VeHaKedushah ceased publication the month the war ended.
Story: Founded in October 1940 to call American Jewry to teshuvah and spiritual mobilization during the war, the magazine ended its run after five years. Its closing the month of victory suggests its mission was deliberately tied to providing a spiritual response to the conflict.
Tags: hakriah vehakedushah, wwii, yiddish magazine

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes 6 Tishrei letter on student visas
Summary: On 6 Tishrei 5706, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to the Shanghai students confirming his telegram about visa applications and his efforts on their behalf.
Story: In a letter dated 6 Tishrei 5706 (Igrot Kodesh vol. 9, letter 2766), sent alongside the telegram via R. Yaakov Yisrael Zuber of Stockholm, the Frierdiker Rebbe informed the students that a telegram had been sent to his contact about what they needed to do to obtain entry permits to the United States. He assured them that he was working on their behalf and prayed that G-d would fulfill their hearts' requests for good in both material and spiritual matters.
Tags: visas, united states, shanghai, zuber, telegram

Title: Students send letter on 7 Tishrei that is returned
Summary: On 7 Tishrei 5706 the students sent another letter to the Rebbe Rayatz, but it was returned and resent on Hoshana Rabbah.
Story: On 7 Tishrei 5706, the Shanghai students sent another letter to the Frierdiker Rebbe, but to their great sorrow it was returned. They then resent it on Hoshana Rabbah via the postal service, which had just begun accepting direct mail to America again after years of wartime disruption.
Tags: shanghai, letter, mail, postal, yom kippur

Title: Students receive first telegram from Rebbe Rayatz erev Yom Kippur
Summary: On erev Yom Kippur 5706, the Shanghai students received their first telegram from the Frierdiker Rebbe via R. Yaakov Yisrael Zuber, instructing them to apply for visas to America.
Story: On erev Yom Kippur 5706, the students in Shanghai received the first telegram from the Frierdiker Rebbe via R. Yaakov Yisrael Zuber of Stockholm, instructing them to file visa applications and reporting his wish to bring them to the United States. After more than three years of no contact, this brought tremendous joy — a triple celebration — and the news was marked with farbrengens, niggunim, and dancing on motzaei Yom Kippur.
Tags: shanghai, telegram, yom kippur, zuber, visas, united states

Title: Students cable Rebbe on Chol HaMoed Sukkot
Summary: On the fourth day of Chol HaMoed Sukkot 5706, the Shanghai students cabled the Rebbe Rayatz via R. Yaakov Yisrael Zuber explaining that visa applications were not yet possible.
Story: On the fourth day of Chol HaMoed Sukkot 5706, the students sent a telegram in reply to the Frierdiker Rebbe via R. Y. Zuber, explaining that the American consul in Shanghai was not yet handling visa matters. They asked whether all formalities could be prepared in advance before applications could be filed locally, hedging against further delays.
Tags: shanghai, telegram, sukkot, visas, zuber

Title: Shanghai yeshivah students send report to Rashag exposing Vaad Hatzalah policy
Summary: After the Japanese surrender restored communications, the Chabad students in Shanghai sent a detailed letter to the Rashag documenting Vaad Hatzalah's discriminatory funding policy.
Story: The letter described how funds were cut off in December 1942 and only small humiliating amounts dispensed thereafter. It also noted that Vaad Hatzalah had initially refused funding to the Amshinover Rebbe. The revelations prompted New York rabbis to seek intervention from Chabad leaders in Israel.
Tags: shanghai, rashag, vaad hatzalah, 26 tishrei, amshinover rebbe

Title: Students send detailed letter on 23 Marcheshvan
Summary: On 23 Marcheshvan 5706, parashat Chayei Sarah, the Shanghai students wrote a detailed report to the Frierdiker Rebbe describing their joy at receiving his telegram.
Story: On the third day of parashat Chayei Sarah, 23 Marcheshvan 5706, the students wrote a fuller report to the Frierdiker Rebbe describing the telegram received via R. Y. Zuber on erev Yom Kippur instructing them to file visa applications. They expressed threefold joy: that this was the first news of his welfare in over three years, that it was the first telegram from him since their arrival in Shanghai, and most of all that he wished to bring them close to him in America.
Tags: shanghai, letter, tomchei tmimim, united states, visas

Title: Students write Rebbe on 25 Marcheshvan
Summary: On 25 Marcheshvan 5706, the Shanghai students wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz, sending the letter via an American soldier.
Story: On 25 Marcheshvan 5706, the students again wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe, sending the letter through an American serviceman because they were unsure whether their earlier postal letters had arrived. They reported that they still could not file visa applications in Shanghai but expected this might become possible within a week.
Tags: shanghai, letter, visas, soldier, mail

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes to Elchanan Glaser about Polish quota
Summary: On 26 Tishrei 5706 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to R. Elchanan Glaser urging him to seek Congressman Dickstein's help in bringing the Shanghai students under Poland's immigration quota.
Story: On 26 Tishrei 5706 (Igrot Kodesh vol. 9, letter 2772), the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote in Yiddish to R. Elchanan Glaser explaining that his best students from the Warsaw and Vilna Tomchei Tmimim yeshivos were now stranded in Shanghai after missing the last ship due to visa formalities. He noted that with strong advocacy in Washington it might be possible to bring them under the Polish quota, or quotas of other countries that were nearly unused, and asked if Congressman Dickstein could be enlisted to take a serious interest in the matter.
Tags: shanghai, visas, united states, poland, tomchei tmimim, warsaw, vilna, dickstein, washington

Title: Students cable Rashag on first night of Chanukah
Summary: On the first night of Chanukah 5706, Rabbi Meir Ashkenazi and the Tmimim cabled the Rashag from Shanghai about visa appointment dates with the American consul.
Story: On the first night of Chanukah 5706, Rabbi Meir Ashkenazi and the Tmimim cabled the Rashag (R. Shmaryahu Gourary) in English, reporting that the visa department had scheduled their appointments with the consul between 20 and 31 December. They warned that all necessary papers had to arrive in Shanghai by the 20th, or the matter would be delayed by months.
Tags: shanghai, visas, consul, chanukah, ashkenazi, telegram

Title: Shabbos Chanukah 5706 farbrengen on emigration plans
Summary: On Shabbos Chanukah 5706, senior chassidim gathered at Levin's home and argued against his plan to leave Russia.
Story: On Shabbos Chanukah 5706, Rabbis Nachum Sasonkin, Dov Chen, and other senior chassidim gathered at Levin's home for a farbrengen and challenged Levin and Michael Teitelbaum's plan to apply for exit papers. Teitelbaum, well into the mashke, retorted that those whose lives were comfortable in Russia could stay where they were — he and Levin, whose lives were bitter both materially and spiritually, would do everything in their power and trust in Hashem to help them.
Tags: samarkand, chanukah, nachum sasonkin, dov chen, michael teitelbaum, emigration, farbrengen

Title: Rebbe tells Russian Chasidim to wait before fleeing
Summary: On 8 Tevet 5706 the Rebbe responded in code to Russian Chasidim asking whether to attempt escape, telling them the situation was unclear and they should wait.
Story: Rabbi Shmuel Levitin in New York relayed a coded message from his son-in-law Binyamin Gorodetsky in Uzbekistan. The Rebbe's actual words being too dangerous to wire, Levitin sent a telegram saying simply, 'Grandfather says it's better to stay put,' urging caution until the window for safe Polish-passport border crossings became clearer.
Tags: russia, uzbekistan, shmuel levitin, binyamin gorodetsky, samizdat, kgb

Title: About 1,000 Chabad chassidim emigrate from Soviet Russia
Summary: In the years 5706–5707 around one thousand Chabad chassidim leave the Soviet Union.
Story: Over 5706–5707 (1946–1947) approximately a thousand Anash escaped Soviet Russia. After two years in displaced-persons camps in Germany and Austria and an extended stay in Paris, they began to settle permanently in various countries. A portion made aliyah to the Land of Israel on the instruction of the Frierdiker Rebbe.
Tags: russia, soviet union, refugees, anash, displaced persons, paris

Title: Arrest of Yeshiva Rosh R' Yitzchak Kopelman
Summary: After Polish Jews left Samarkand in summer 5706, Soviet authorities openly arrested Rosh Yeshiva R' Yitzchak Kopelman and interrogated other Chabad rabbinic figures.
Story: Once Polish-Jewish refugees emptied out of Samarkand in summer 1946, the atmosphere grew colder for those who remained. The famed Rosh Yeshiva R' Yitzchak Kopelman was arrested in broad daylight, and the memoirist's uncle R' Chaim Leib Zaks, rabbi of Uzda, was called for interrogation. R' Chaim Stein of Telshe, who had married into the Zaks family, fled by truck to Tashkent in the dead of night after being inquired about.
Tags: samarkand, soviet union, yeshiva, kgb, arrests

Title: Chabad network smuggles 1,000 Chasidim across Polish border
Summary: The underground Chabad network orchestrated the audacious escape of one thousand Chasidim from the Soviet Union into Poland using false passports.
Story: Drawing on the clandestine infrastructure that had survived the arrests, imprisonments, and executions of the previous two decades, the network exploited a brief postwar window to extract Chasidim and their families. Those who escaped, along with their children, provided the leadership that fueled a global Jewish renaissance after the war.
Tags: escape, poland, russia, false passports, lvov

Title: Chabad network smuggles 1,000 Chasidim out of the USSR on false passports
Summary: The clandestine Chabad network orchestrated the audacious escape of about one thousand Chasidim across the Soviet border into Poland using forged Polish passports.
Story: In 1946, the underground Chabad network — which had endured through decades of Soviet persecution — orchestrated the escape of roughly a thousand Chasidim across the border to Poland on false passports. They and their children went on to provide leadership for the global Jewish renaissance and to inspire a new generation of postwar Chasidim.
Tags: russia, poland, escape, false passports, underground

Title: First edition of the Chabad Haggadah with Likkutei Taamim u'Minhagim
Summary: Kehot published the first edition of the Chabad Haggadah with Likkutei Taamim u'Minhagim in 5706 (1946).
Story: The Haggadah's commentary, gathering sources and customs, was the future Rebbe's compilation. Its 1946 first edition became the standard Chabad Haggadah used at seder tables for generations.
Tags: rebbe, kehot, haggadah, first edition, passover

Title: First Haggadah printed in Central America (Mexico)
Summary: The first Haggadah printed in Central America, with a Spanish translation by Z. Shipmanovich, was issued in Mexico in 5706.
Story: In 5706 (1946), the first Haggadah ever printed in Central America was issued in Mexico City. Sponsored by Yitzchak Krochmalnik and his wife Sarah, it featured a Spanish translation by Z. Shipmanovich and was illustrated.
Tags: haggadah, mexico, central-america, spanish-translation

Title: Haggadah with Likutei Minhagim u'Taamim published
Summary: The Rebbe's annotated Haggadah was issued by Kehot in 5706.
Story: Kehot issued the Rebbe's Haggadah with Likutei Minhagim u'Taamim in 1946. It collected Chabad customs and reasons for the seder, including the note that 'in the Rebbe's house the matzot are arranged on a cloth, not a plate—except the Rebbe himself, who arranges them on a silver tray.'
Tags: the rebbe, haggadah, kehot, minhagim

Title: Hebrew Parochial School Chicago financial rescue
Summary: Facing mortgage default and closure, Chicago's Hebrew Parochial School was rescued overnight after board member Yankel Katz phoned the Sixth Rebbe.
Story: When the board met to discuss closing, Katz left to find a payphone. The Rebbe told him to reconvene the meeting the next night. By the next evening a group of affluent donors the Rebbe had personally contacted were waiting at the gate, and within minutes the pledges to save the school were in place.
Tags: chicago, arie crown, yankel katz, mortgage, rescue

Title: Kielce pogrom kills 42 Jews returning to Poland
Summary: A year after the war's end, Polish residents murdered 42 Jews in a vicious pogrom in Kielce, signaling that survivors were unwelcome.
Story: When Holocaust survivors returned to Poland to reclaim homes and businesses seized by neighbors, they met violent resistance. The Kielce pogrom drove home the reality that prewar Jewish life in Poland could not be revived, accelerating refugee flows to the United States, Canada, South America, Australia, and Mandatory Palestine.
Tags: poland, kielce, pogrom, antisemitism, postwar

Title: Levin escapes Soviet Union as Polish refugee 'Naftali Bat'
Summary: In summer 1946 Levin used forged Polish refugee documents in the name Naftali Bat to leave the Soviet Union among the first wave of Anash to escape.
Story: Unable to renew his army exemption in Samarkand, Levin had gone underground using papers identifying him as a Polish refugee not yet drafted. He could not work openly under this name without Polish-language skills, so he worked under his wife's name. The same Polish papers eventually allowed both of them to leave Russia, with his wife re-registered as having remarried a Pole named Naftali Bat.
Tags: samarkand, lvov, escape, polish papers, samizdat, naftali bat, soviet union

Title: Levins submit OVIR exit applications via Polish identity
Summary: In mid-winter 5706 the Levins submitted exit applications to OVIR, doctoring Itta Devorah's passport to match Naftali Batt's Polish identity.
Story: Hearing that Polish refugees could repatriate and possibly continue on to American-occupied Germany, Levin and Michael Teitelbaum applied to OVIR in mid-winter 5706. To register his wife under the Polish name Naftali Batt, Levin tore numbered pages from her passport that recorded her maiden name Gurkov; the clerk did not notice and stamped her marriage to 'Batt.' A subsequent midnight visit from NKVD-linked questioners about the application terrified them but did not stop them.
Tags: samarkand, ovir, polish refugees, emigration, false papers, nkvd

Title: Lubavitcher refugee yeshivot founded in DP camps
Summary: Refugee Anash settled in DP camps in Pocking and Steyr in 5706–5707, immediately establishing yeshivot for surviving students.
Story: Following the mass escape from the Soviet Union in 5706–5707 (1946–1947), several hundred refugee families settled in displaced-persons camps in Pocking, Germany and Steyr, Austria. Upon arrival they founded yeshivot for the surviving students.
Tags: displaced-persons, pocking, steyr, germany, austria, world-war-ii, yeshiva

Title: Mailufim volume of Tzemach Tzedek edited by the Rebbe
Summary: In 5706 the Rebbe (then Ramash) edited, at the direction of his father-in-law the Rayatz, a Milu'im volume of Tzemach Tzedek responsa including the previously censored Choshen Mishpat material.
Story: Eighty years after the Tzemach Tzedek's passing, the previously blocked Choshen Mishpat responsa finally appeared in print. The Milu'im volume edited by the future Rebbe included Choshen Mishpat teshuvos, supplements across all four chelkei Shulchan Aruch, additions to the chiddushim on Shas, and further omissions discovered during typesetting.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, rebbe, rayatz, choshen mishpat, milu'im

Title: Mass escape of Anash from the Soviet Union
Summary: Around 1,000 Anash succeeded in escaping the Soviet Union across the border into liberated Europe in 5706–5707.
Story: With the end of World War II in 5706–5707 (1946–1947), a large group of about one thousand Lubavitcher chassidim managed to smuggle themselves across the Soviet border into liberated Europe. The Rebbe then asked these refugee chassidim to send him their photographs as a record of their rescue.
Tags: soviet-union, russia, escape, world-war-ii, anash-emigration, displaced-persons

Title: Moshe Binyamin Kaplan flees Russia in Great Escape
Summary: Moshe Binyamin Kaplan, a former underground yeshivah student, fled Russia in the 1946 Great Escape and reached a German DP camp.
Story: From the DP camp Kaplan wrote to the Rebbe in Brooklyn wondering what bond he could have, having never met him. The Rebbe replied that he remembered him very well and that the bond was through learning each other's Torah. Years later Rabbi Shalom Ber Levin found among the Rebbe's possessions a 1935 photo of Kaplan, taken when he was eighteen and sent secretly from Russia to Poland.
Tags: russia, great-escape, dp-camp, germany, kaplan, underground-yeshivah

Title: Polish repatriation office opens in Samarkand
Summary: In the winter of 5706 (early 1946), the Polish government's representation in Samarkand opened a repatriation office issuing Polish passports to former Polish nationals.
Story: After the war, Poland's representation in Samarkand announced that Poles wishing to return to their homeland could register. By winter 5706 an office opened where anyone presenting some 'paperel' showing Polish birth could obtain (after a few months) a Polish passport allowing emigration to Poland — and from Poland onward, to the free world. Many Lubavitchers obtained such passports despite confusion over what the Frierdiker Rebbe wanted them to do.
Tags: samarkand, poland, repatriation, passports, post-war

Title: R' Dovber Lebertov warns memoirist to leave Moscow immediately
Summary: Stopping in Moscow en route to Lemberg, the memoirist was told by R' Dovber Kobeliaker (Lebertov) to flee the city at once rather than spend Shabbos there.
Story: Arriving in Moscow on a Thursday, the memoirist intended to spend Shabbos with relatives. When he told R' Dovber Kobeliaker of his plan, R' Dovber sharply commanded him to leave immediately, knowing how dangerous the city had become. The memoirist left the next day; R' Dovber was later repeatedly summoned by the GPU, ultimately arrested and exiled, dying in the wilds.
Tags: moscow, kgb, r dovber lebertov, kobeliaker, emigration

Title: R' Yonah Cohen visits Tashkent fertility doctors with Levin's wife
Summary: In winter 5706 R' Yonah Cohen brought Levin and Teitelbaum's wives from Samarkand to Tashkent specialists, hosting them for a month.
Story: Childless after years of marriage, Levin and Michael Teitelbaum confided in their friend R' Yonah Cohen of Tashkent. Himself childless, R' Yonah declared he would do everything in his power for them: he hosted both wives at his Tashkent home for a month in winter 5706 and personally escorted them to leading specialists.

Title: Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson dispatched to Paris and Prague
Summary: In summer 1946 the Rebbe sent Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson to Paris and Prague to coordinate the escape of Russian Chasidim from Poland to the American zone.
Story: Working with the Brichah underground, Jacobson organized clandestine border crossings from Poland into Czechoslovakia and secured papers permitting refugees to move into Germany's American zone. He was followed by other emissaries including the Rebbe's son-in-law, the Rashag.
Tags: yisrael jacobson, paris, prague, brichah, germany, refugees

Title: Rebbe Rayatz instructs Anash to record Soviet-era memoirs
Summary: After Chassidim began leaving the Soviet Union in 1946-1947, the Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn directed them to write down their memories of clandestine activity and the names of those involved.
Story: The Rebbe specifically asked that participants record everything they could remember about underground religious work, the names of fellow Chassidim and students, and the places and times of their activities. Reb Bentzion Shemtov was charged with coordinating the collection. The instruction launched a tradition of Chabad memoir writing that produced major historical sources including Reb Meir Gurkov's Sefer HaZichronot.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, memoirs, soviet union, tomchei tmimim, anash

Title: Rebbe's first edition of Haggadah 'Likutei Minhagim u'Ta'amim' in New York
Summary: The Lubavitcher Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson published his Haggadah 'Likutei Minhagim u'Ta'amim' in New York for the first time.
Story: In 5706 (1946), the Lubavitcher Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson published for the first time his Haggadah 'Likutei Minhagim u'Ta'amim' (Anthology of Customs and Reasons) in New York. The 47-page octavo edition presented a systematic anthology of Chabad customs and explanations for the Seder. It established the foundational Lubavitch Haggadah for subsequent decades and was reprinted dozens of times with additions over the following half-century.
Tags: chabad, rebbe, new york, haggadah, likutei minhagim

Title: Rebbe's Haggadah with Likkutei Minhagim first edition
Summary: The Rebbe's Haggadah with Likkutei Minhagim u'Ta'amim was first published in New York in 5706.
Story: In 5706 (1946), the Rebbe's Haggadah of Passover with Likkutei Minhagim u'Ta'amim was first published in New York. The work compiles Chabad customs and reasons accompanying the Pesach Haggadah. The Lubavitch Library preserves a copy of this first edition.
Tags: haggadah, rebbe, brooklyn

Title: Rotstein returns to serve as Rebbe's secretary
Summary: In 5706, R. Moshe Leib Rotstein returned to work as secretary to the Frierdiker Rebbe.
Story: In the year 5706 (1946), R. Moshe Leib Rotstein returned from his post in Chicago to once again serve as secretary to the Frierdiker Rebbe in New York. He would continue this role until the Rebbe's passing.
Tags: new york, usa, moshe leib rotstein, secretary, frierdiker rebbe

Title: Shanghai refugee yeshiva students arrive in the United States
Summary: After years of wartime exile in Shanghai, the refugee students of Tomchei Temimim finally received visas and arrived on American shores.
Story: Having fled Poland to Lithuania at the war's onset, the students were forcibly relocated through Russia and Japan to Shanghai, where they endured isolation and starvation. At the war's end they learned that almost all of their relatives had perished in the Holocaust. After a year waiting for American visas, they arrived in 1946 and became a key cadre for the sixth Rebbe's postwar vision.
Tags: shanghai, tomchei temimim, refugees, russia, japan, poland

Title: Wedding of Golda Schusterman and Nechemia Nodel in Samarkand
Summary: The memoirist's sister Golda married Nechemia Nodel, son of a chassidic shochet from the Kherson colonies, in Samarkand around 5706.
Story: R' Tzemach HaLevi Horowitz proposed the match between Golda and Nechemia Nodel, a young man recently returned wounded from the front. He was described as 'a very refined bachelor,' and the wedding took place in good fortune. The match later kept the memoirist's parents from emigrating with him, since Nechemia's elderly parents were staying behind.
Tags: samarkand, schusterman family, nechemia nodel, shidduch

Title: Rashag writes to U.S. Embassy in Shanghai
Summary: On 4 Shevat 5706, the Rashag wrote in English to the American Embassy in Shanghai, enclosing affidavits and a list of the students.
Story: On 4 Shevat 5706, the Rashag wrote to the American Embassy in Shanghai per the advice of Mr. Eliot B. Coulter of the State Department, enclosing the required affidavits and a list of the names of the Tomchei Tmimim students stranded in Shanghai, China. He expressed hope that these documents would facilitate issuance of American visas so the immigration could take place as soon as possible.
Tags: shanghai, visas, united states, affidavits, state department, coulter

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes to students on 7 Shevat
Summary: On 7 Shevat 5706 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote a letter of profound joy and blessing to his Shanghai students upon news of imminent rescue.
Story: On 7 Shevat 5706 (Igrot Kodesh vol. 9, letter 2839), the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to his beloved students, thanking G-d for the great kindness shown to them in the merit of his holy forebears — especially his father, the Rebbe Rashab, who gave his soul for the building of Tomchei Tmimim. He expressed inexpressible joy at the news of their rescue and strong hope that they would soon arrive in America to spread Torah and yiras Shamayim from a settled material and spiritual situation.
Tags: shanghai, tomchei tmimim, rashab, blessing, united states

Title: Shanghai students receive visa application forms
Summary: On 7 Shevat 5706, the Shanghai students received the visa application forms but could not yet return them without the affidavits.
Story: On the same 7 Shevat 5706, the students wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe that they had received the visa application blanks, but since they had not yet received the affidavits, they could not return them to the consulate — the applications required the names and addresses of those sending the affidavits, which they did not yet know. They asked for the Rebbe's blessing that they obtain the visas quickly and easily.
Tags: shanghai, visas, united states, affidavits

Title: Bochur Shlomo Zilberberg reports library found in Otwock
Summary: Holocaust survivor and former bochur Shlomo Zilberberg writes that the library he had packed in Otwock in 1939 has been found.
Story: On Rosh Hashanah La'ilanot (Tu BiShvat) 5706, Shlomo Zilberberg — who as a young man had packed the library in Otwock in 1939 — wrote that the books had been located, promising precise details to follow. It was the first postwar word that any of the lost crates might be recoverable.
Tags: library, otwock, poland, holocaust-survivors, schneersohn-library, shlomo-zilberberg

Title: Shlomo Zilberberg writes to the Rebbe after surviving the war
Summary: On 15 Shevat 5706, surviving talmid Shlomo Zilberberg wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe from Poland reporting that he and several other talmidim had survived.
Story: Zilberberg informed the Rebbe in Yiddish that he and a few other students remained alive after the cruel hands of the Nazis, and that they were currently in Poland. He pleaded with the Rebbe to have mercy upon them and acknowledge their survival.
Tags: holocaust, survivors, poland, shlomo zilberberg, tu bishvat

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe replies to Shlomo Zilberberg
Summary: On 4 Adar I 5706 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to Shlomo Zilberberg expressing joy at his survival and asking for details of him and his brother.
Story: The Rebbe wrote that he was very pleased to hear that Hashem had saved Zilberberg and his brother through His great kindness, and requested a detailed account of what had happened to them and to the other surviving Anash. He blessed them to settle into a good family life with parnassah and fixed times for Torah study in nigleh and chassidut.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, survivors, shlomo zilberberg, holocaust

Title: R. Menachem Mendel Kuperstock passes away in Haifa
Summary: R. Menachem Mendel Kuperstock, founder of the Chabad community in Haifa, passed away on 7 Adar I 5706.
Story: After making aliyah from Globoke, R. Kuperstock settled in Haifa where he founded the local Chabad community. He passed away on 7 Adar I 5706 (February 8, 1946).
Tags: kuperstock, haifa, passing

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe writes to Yehoshua Heshel Reizman
Summary: On 13 Adar I 5706 the Frierdiker Rebbe replied to surviving talmid Yehoshua Heshel Reizman, encouraging him to strengthen Torah, Jewish education, and good middot.
Story: Replying to a letter from 8 Kislev, the Rebbe expressed joy that Reizman had been saved from the Nazis and pleasure at his efforts together with his fellow temimim to strengthen Torah, kosher chinuch, good middot and ahavat Yisrael. He urged them to persist despite all obstacles and obstructions in their country.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, survivors, yehoshua heshel reizman, tomchei temimim, poland, holocaust

Title: Pinchas Klein details Schneersohn library remnant found in Warsaw
Summary: Bochur Pinchas Klein writes from Lodz that a small portion of the Rebbe's library, including manuscripts, has been located at the Jewish Central Committee in Warsaw.
Story: On 19 Adar I, Pinchas Klein wrote his friend R' A.L. Kramer that, having been in Lodz at the end of the week, he had learned that a small fraction of the Rebbe's library — including many manuscripts and printed sefarim — had been found in Warsaw and was being held by the Historical Department of the Yiddish Central Committee.
Tags: library, warsaw, lodz, manuscripts, schneersohn-library, pinchas-klein, jewish-central-committee, holocaust-survivors

Title: Pinchas Klein sends list of surviving Tomchei Temimim talmidim
Summary: On 19 Adar I 5706, Pinchas Klein wrote to Arye Leib Kremer in Montreal listing the Tomchei Temimim students still alive in Poland.
Story: Klein asked that his name and that of his wife be brought before the Rebbe for blessings. He listed surviving talmidim including Yosef Goldstein, a shochet in Lodz; Heshel Reizman in Częstochowa; Feivel Griner; Yehoshua Wolf Abramtchak from Koszwin; the Zilberberg brothers; Fishel Gitelis from Kowel; Yaakov Katz from Chelm; and Motl Bumelgrin from Zwolen.

Title: Montreal students form Ezras Achim relief group
Summary: As the Shanghai students' departure approached, the rescued Tmimim in Montreal organized 'Ezras Achim' to raise relief funds for them.
Story: As the Shanghai students' travel approached, the previously rescued Tomchei Tmimim students in Montreal organized 'Ezras Achim' to collect tzedakah for the needs of the students still in Shanghai waiting to come to America. The Frierdiker Rebbe replied on 24 Adar Rishon 5706 (Igrot Kodesh vol. 13, letter 4897) thanking them for arranging help for their brother-students of Tomchei Tmimim and blessing them to soon be reunited in a life of Torah.
Tags: montreal, ezras achim, shanghai, tomchei tmimim, relief

Title: Rebbe Rayatz appeals to NY librarians for State Department intervention
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz writes Alexander Marx and Joshua Bloch asking them to certify to the State Department the historical value of the seized Chabad manuscripts and books.
Story: On 24 Adar I 5706, after the war's end, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Alexander Marx of the JTS library and Joshua Bloch of the NY Public Library. He explained that three crates of ancient manuscripts — spanning 150 years of Chabad nesius — together with thousands of rare sefarim from the Shmuel Wiener collection, had been seized by the Nazis from his library in Otwock. The crates had been registered under Rabbis Jacobson and Hecht (US citizens) and were the property of Agudas Chasidei Chabad; he asked the librarians to write the State Department vouching for their scholarly and national-Jewish importance.

Title: Students cable visa news on erev Shabbat Pekudei
Summary: On erev Shabbat Pekudei, 5 Adar Sheni 5706, the students cabled the Rebbe Rayatz that UNRRA reported good prospects for visas soon.
Story: On erev Shabbat Parashat Pekudei, 5 Adar Sheni 5706, the Shanghai students cabled the Frierdiker Rebbe in Yiddish that UNRRA was reporting good prospects of obtaining the visas soon, but expressing doubt whether all 29 of them would be able to travel together. The number reflected the 27 students plus the wives of the two who were married.

Title: Rebbe Rayatz blesses students on 8 Adar Sheni
Summary: On 8 Adar Sheni 5706, the Frierdiker Rebbe replied with blessings that the students obtain their visas easily and find means to travel to America.
Story: On 8 Adar Sheni 5706 (Igrot Kodesh vol. 13, letter 4901), the Frierdiker Rebbe replied to the Shanghai students' telegram that they were expected to receive the U.S. visas. He blessed them to receive them with ease and success in material and spiritual matters, that G-d would arrange a means of travel, and that they would arrive and become settled in a complete order of Torah study and avodah she-balev, and engage in spreading Torah and yiras Shamayim.

Title: Rebbe Rayatz asks U.S. government to allow plane travel
Summary: On 3 Nissan 5706 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to R. Yosef Fleischer of Chicago that he had asked the U.S. government to allow the Shanghai students to fly home.
Story: On 3 Nissan 5706 (Igrot Kodesh vol. 9, letter 2883), the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to R. Yosef Fleischer, a Chabad askan in Chicago, that he had written to the U.S. government as president of Chabad chassidim, requesting the Secretaries of the Interior and War to grant the students permission to travel on a government airplane, since they were needed for teaching and ruling for the Chabad organization. He noted that the matter had to remain confidential.

Title: R' David Levanon, head of Kollel Chabad, passes away
Summary: On 4 Nissan 5706 R' David Levanon, longtime co-administrator of Kollel Chabad, passed away and was succeeded by R' Yitzchak Avigdor Ornstein.
Story: Levanon had served as co-signer on Kollel Chabad correspondence from 5688 through 5706, paired first with R' Yisrael Asher Liba and later with R' Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezrov. After his death on 4 Nissan, his administrative role was filled by R' Yitzchak Avigdor Ornstein, continuing the kollel's leadership structure.

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe writes to Yerucham Fishel Gitelis
Summary: On 22 Iyar 5706 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to survivor Yerucham Fishel Gitelis in Iggeret 6643, expressing pleasure at his rescue.
Story: The Rebbe noted his delight that Hashem in His great kindness had saved Gitelis from the Nazis, and blessed him with healing, strengthened health, and assistance in all his material and spiritual needs.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, iggeret, survivors, yerucham fishel gitelis, holocaust

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe writes letter endorsing Rabbi Eliezer Silver
Summary: On 27 Iyar 5706 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote a letter (Igros Kodesh vol. 9 p. 128) instructing the refugees in Łódź to honor the visiting Rabbi Eliezer Silver.
Story: The letter reached the Anash refugees in Łódź a day or two before Rabbi Silver's visit and resolved their hesitation about how to receive a non-chassidic American rav. The Rebbe praised Silver's self-sacrifice in saving Jews and ranked him above factional politics. Receiving the letter after years of severed contact was experienced as the first overt miracle the refugees saw from the Rebbe after leaving Russia.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, eliezer silver, agrot kodesh, lodz, refugees

Title: R' Yonah Cohen's farewell blessing to Levin
Summary: Shortly before Levin's 5706 departure, the martyred R' Yonah Cohen came to bless him and asked to be remembered.
Story: Before Levin left Samarkand, R' Yonah Cohen — later martyred — came to his home, kissed him, and said: 'Hashem should help you with what you need; remember me. You will succeed.' Levin recalled the visit as 'cold water on a weary, thirsty soul.'
Tags: samarkand, yonah cohen, emigration, blessing

Title: Chabad refugees board freight train out of Samarkand (Eshelon No. 3)
Summary: On 4 Sivan 5706, Chabad refugees loaded their belongings and boarded Eshelon No. 3, a windowless freight train, departing Samarkand toward Poland.
Story: After waiting on the tracks most of the day, the refugees were finally permitted to board the freight train in the late afternoon. For the narrator it was the first time leaving Samarkand, where fear of the Soviet authorities had kept him indoors for years. The departure marked the start of the post-war 'Eshelonim' escape from the USSR using forged Polish papers.
Tags: samarkand, soviet union, uzbekistan, escape, refugees, freight train, eshelon 3, post-war

Title: Levin family departs Samarkand on echelon no. 3
Summary: On 4 Sivan 5706 (June 3, 1946) the Levins left Samarkand on echelon no. 3, repatriating to Poland under Polish-refugee papers.
Story: After receiving their OVIR exit permits, the Levins were assigned to echelon no. 3, departing Samarkand on Monday 4 Sivan 5706 / June 3, 1946. They traveled with many Polish-refugee families rather than risk solo train travel, gambling on a chance — however slim — to escape Russia and reach the Rebbe.
Tags: samarkand, echelon, ovir, emigration, polish repatriation, naso

Title: Refugees immerse in roadside puddle on Erev Shavuot mid-journey
Summary: On 5 Sivan 5706, Erev Shavuot, the narrator and R. Michoel Teitelbaum jumped from the halted train into a muddy roadside puddle to immerse themselves in honor of the festival.
Story: The freight train suddenly stopped beside a field with a muddy puddle nearby. Seizing the opportunity, the two chassidim climbed down and immersed quickly before the train moved on. It was exactly one year since they had celebrated the end of the war together in Samarkand.
Tags: shavuot, mikveh, samarkand-to-poland, refugees

Title: Eshelon train halted near Tambov, refugees fear deportation to Siberia
Summary: On 15 Sivan 5706 the train stopped for hours near Tambov on a route that could lead either to Poland or to Siberia, triggering deep anxiety among the passengers.
Story: Rumors spread that earlier eshelonim were still circling within Russia and that the passengers might be diverted to Siberia. After a long wait the train suddenly resumed moving, and by the next day they could see it was headed via Kursk toward Ukraine and Poland. A later remark attributed by the narrator to an American general framed Stalin's decision to release the Jews as a miracle.
Tags: tambov, siberia, soviet union, refugees, eshelon 3, fear

Title: Eshelon No. 3 crosses Dnieper at Darnitsa, route to Poland confirmed
Summary: On 17 Sivan 5706 the train crossed the long Dnieper bridge by Darnitsa near Kiev, definitively confirming that the refugees were being routed to Poland.
Story: After a long halt near Darnitsa the train began moving across the Dnieper, and the passengers realized for certain they were on the road to Poland rather than Siberia. The narrator silently thanked God for being granted to see the journey 'from narrowness to expanse.' Further west they were shown mounds where Germans and Ukrainians had buried murdered Jews alive.
Tags: dnieper, darnitsa, kiev, ukraine, samarkand-to-poland, refugees

Title: Refugees reach the old Russian-Polish border
Summary: Around 18 Sivan 5706 the eshelon reached the pre-war Russian-Polish border, a moment the narrator had awaited for twelve years since the Frierdiker Rebbe's 1934 reply.
Story: The narrator had been refused exit permits in 5694 (1934) despite the Rebbe's instructions to apply, and again the same summer. Now, after twelve years, the train passed the red-and-white striped border posts of the old border at about 11 a.m. He privately thanked God but hid his joy until they were beyond Russian territory.
Tags: russia-poland border, soviet union, refugees, eshelon 3

Title: Banderite raiders attempt to attack Eshelon No. 3 in western Ukraine
Summary: During a night halt by a forest in western Ukraine, Banderite raiders tried to break into the refugees' freight car before being driven off until morning.
Story: Rumors said the train drivers cooperated with Banderite bandits, halting at forests so that the cars could be looted; Eshelon No. 2 had already been robbed in this way. R. Michoel Teitelbaum bolted the door from inside and beat off the attackers' fingers with empty bottles until dawn broke and the train moved on. The car had no windows because it was a freight and livestock wagon.
Tags: banderites, western ukraine, antisemitism, refugees, eshelon 3

Title: Eshelon No. 3 crosses into Poland at Przemyśl
Summary: On about 20 Sivan 5706 the refugees crossed the new Russian-Polish border into Przemyśl after exchanging rubles for złoty at the Soviet bank.
Story: Soviet officials forced an unfavorable ruble-to-złoty rate at the border but the narrator and R. Michoel refused to risk delay and exchanged everything they had. Border guards merely called out names from a list without searching the cars, allowing undocumented young women hidden in the wheat fields to slip aboard. Once in Przemyśl Polish merchants paid three złoty per ruble, and the refugees realized they were finally out of Russia.
Tags: przemysl, poland, soviet union, refugees, currency exchange, eshelon 3

Title: Lubavitcher refugees arrive in Łódź
Summary: On Thursday, 21 Sivan 5706, the eshelon reached Wrocław and the Anash refugees continued by hired rail car to Łódź, settling at 42 Zachodnia Street.
Story: At Wrocław German and Polish locals warned that many Jews had survived, and the refugees grasped that danger still lay ahead. Bribed Polish officials let them disembark, and Anash who had arrived earlier hired a truck to bring them to 42 Zachodnia Street, where the Lubavitch refugees from Russia lodged together. A va'ad of Anash in Łódź coordinated relief, likely with Joint Distribution Committee aid, and began arranging onward travel out of Poland.
Tags: lodz, poland, refugees, anash, joint, wroclaw

Title: Rabbi Eliezer Silver reception in Łódź; Frierdiker Rebbe's letter read aloud
Summary: On Friday, 29 Sivan 5706 (Erev Shabbos Korach), American Chief Rabbi Eliezer Silver was received by the religious parties in Łódź, and R. Benyamin Gorodetzky read the Frierdiker Rebbe's letter publicly.
Story: Held in the Agudath Israel secretariat at 66 Zachodnia Street, the reception included delegates from Agudah, Poalei Agudah, Mizrachi and Hapoel Hamizrachi. When R. Benyamin Gorodetzky rose with the Rebbe's letter, Rabbi Silver also stood out of respect, forcing the entire assembly to rise — a public win for the small Lubavitch contingent. At Mincha afterward Silver crossed the synagogue to greet Gorodetzky beside the Aron Kodesh, demonstratively honoring Chabad before the other delegates.
Tags: eliezer silver, lodz, agudath israel, mizrachi, benyamin gorodetzky, refugees, post-war

Title: Rabbi Eliezer Silver's drasha in Łódź on Rosh Chodesh Tammuz
Summary: On Shabbos Parshas Korach, 1 Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5706, Rabbi Eliezer Silver addressed a large crowd in Łódź, praising the Frierdiker Rebbe as the hidden source of the refugees' mesirus nefesh.
Story: Silver compared the chassidim's spiritual endurance under Soviet persecution to a flourishing tree in the desert whose water comes from a distant hidden spring — the Rebbe.
