He added that the Rebbe was likewise working with mesirus nefesh in the United States, and that he himself was strengthened by him. He then held a separate private meeting with the small Anash group in honor of the Rebbe, and afterward began advocating for Polish passports to Prague for them.
Tags: eliezer silver, lodz, drasha, shabbat korach, frierdiker rebbe, refugees

Title: Rebbe Rayatz thanks Rashaz Gurevitch for visit to Dr. Kahane on book list
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz writes R' Shneur Zalman Gurevitch thanking him for visiting Rabbi Dr. Kahane and asking him to expedite the catalog and shipment of the recovered books.
Story: On 1 Tammuz 5706, the Rebbe acknowledged Rashag's report on Rashaz Gurevitch's visit to Rabbi Dr. David Kahane regarding the books found at the Warsaw Jewish community archive. The Rebbe urged Gurevitch to hurry the cataloging and shipment of the recovered volumes.
Tags: library, warsaw, schneersohn-library, rashaz-gurevitch, david-kahane

Title: Departure from Samarkand to Lemberg via Moscow
Summary: In late Tammuz 5706 (July 1946), the memoirist left Samarkand with his wife and two daughters for Lemberg, traveling via Moscow alongside the Kalmanson family.
Story: After packing the household belongings, the memoirist boarded the train at Samarkand with the Kalmanson family. Parting from his elderly parents at the platform, he sensed he would never see them again. The Polish passport, held by his father, was swapped to him only at the moment of boarding the train.
Tags: samarkand, moscow, lemberg, lvov, emigration, polish passports, schneersohn refugees

Title: Reception receptions in Seattle, San Francisco, Los Angeles
Summary: Upon arrival in America, the 29 Shanghai students were divided among three West Coast cities for receptions arranged by Tomchei Tmimim.
Story: Tomchei Tmimim representatives sent from New York by the Rashag — among them R. Yosef Weinberg and R. Moshe Hecht — met the students upon disembarkation. The group of about thirty was divided three ways: ten traveled to Seattle, Washington (welcomed at the train station by Rabbi Shapira and others), ten remained in San Francisco, and ten went to Los Angeles, where R. Moshe Hecht hosted a large reception in a packed Moshav Zekenim hall, the first such welcome for yeshiva war refugees in America.
Tags: seattle, san francisco, los angeles, reception, tomchei tmimim, weinberg, hecht, shapira

Title: Shanghai students reach San Francisco
Summary: In Tammuz 5706 the group of Shanghai Tmimim arrived in San Francisco aboard an American military ship.
Story: The students sailed from Shanghai on an American military ship — the only available option, as airfare was prohibitively expensive — and the voyage was uncomfortable, with military two-tier bunks and many travelers feeling unwell. They were joined by a large group of refugees including other yeshiva students, and the ship landed in San Francisco on the West Coast of the United States.
Tags: united states, shanghai, san francisco, ship, military, arrival

Title: Rebbe Rayatz arranges welcome receptions on 2 Tammuz
Summary: On 2 Tammuz 5706 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to Chabad askanim in America directing them to arrange splendid receptions for the Shanghai students.
Story: On 2 Tammuz 5706 (Igrot Kodesh vol. 9, letter 2923), as soon as the Shanghai students set out from China, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to several Chabad askanim asking them to arrange a fine reception for the Tomchei Tmimim students along their travel route, with special emissaries to organize welcome events in as many towns as possible.
Tags: united states, reception, tomchei tmimim, shanghai, rashag

Title: Three Shanghai students arrive by plane
Summary: In Tammuz 5706 three Shanghai Tmimim — Avraham Yitzchak Garfinkel, Nachum Preger, and Mordechai Meir Brziski — arrived in America by plane.
Story: As reported in HaPardes (Tammuz 5706), three students arrived by plane from Shanghai a few weeks earlier: Avraham Yitzchak Garfinkel, Nachum Preger, and Mordechai Meir Brziski of Chmielnik. The Frierdiker Rebbe's efforts to bring all the students by airplane had not succeeded; only two or three made the trip by air while the rest traveled by U.S. military ship.
Tags: shanghai, united states, airplane, tomchei tmimim, garfinkel, preger, brziski

Title: Rebbe writes Achei Tmimim heads on 3 Tammuz
Summary: On 3 Tammuz 5706 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to heads of Achei Tmimim yeshivas in various American cities, instructing them to travel to arrange receptions for the arriving students.
Story: On 3 Tammuz 5706 (Igrot Kodesh vol. 9, letter 2924), the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to the heads of Achei Tmimim yeshivas in several American cities asking them to travel to the towns the Rashag would suggest and arrange welcome celebrations for the Tomchei Tmimim students arriving from Shanghai.
Tags: united states, achei tmimim, shanghai, reception, rashag

Title: Rebbe writes Chicago Anash on 15 Tammuz
Summary: On 15 Tammuz 5706 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to Chicago Anash announcing the Shanghai students' arrival that week and asking them to arrange a splendid reception.
Story: On 15 Tammuz 5706 (Igrot Kodesh vol. 9, letter 2928), the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to Anash in Chicago that, thank G-d, his beloved Tmimim from Tomchei Tmimim in Shanghai were arriving safely in America at the end of that week. He asked them to organize a splendid reception in their city, conducted in proper order.
Tags: chicago, united states, reception, shanghai, tomchei tmimim

Title: Bricha crossing from Poland into Czechoslovakia by night, late Av 5706
Summary: After motzaei Shabbat Mevorchim Elul 5706, the narrator, his wife, and daughters Miriam and Leah climbed mountains by night with a Bricha guide and reached a DP camp on Czech soil by dawn.
Story: The Bricha was an underground operation run by young Eretz Yisrael emissaries in coordination with the Joint and the American Vaad Hatzalah, smuggling Soviet refugees on foot across borders into Czechoslovakia, Austria, and Germany. The narrator carried two suitcases while his wife held the 1½-year-old Miriam and led five-year-old Leah by the hand. From the Czech DP camp they were transferred to Vienna and housed in the former Rothschild Hospital.
Tags: bricha, joint, vaad hatzalah, czechoslovakia, refugees, displaced persons, kgb era

Title: Train ride from Vienna toward Steyr stalled in Soviet zone, Erev Shabbat Elul 5706
Summary: Traveling by freight train from Vienna to the Austrian town of Steyr in late Av 5706, the refugees were stalled for many hours when Soviet zone authorities refused passage; the train finally moved overnight and arrived in Steyr on Shabbat morning.
Story: Post-war Austria and Germany were divided into American, British, French, and Soviet occupation zones, and the Soviet zone authorities held the freight cars indefinitely. The travelers sat in darkness without food in cattle wagons, and the narrator gave R. Avraham Eliyahu Plotkin a piece of bread for kiddush. They were instructed to identify themselves as Greek nationals if questioned. The train finally rolled overnight and reached Steyr by Shabbat dawn, where the Joint and Vaad Hatzalah received them.
Tags: austria, soviet zone, steyr, vienna, refugees, freight train, avraham eliyahu plotkin

Title: Secretariat writes to Sweden on behalf of Heshel Reizman and wife
Summary: On 5 Menachem Av 5706 the Frierdiker Rebbe's secretariat wrote to Anash in Sweden requesting an additional affidavit for Heshel Reizman's wife.
Story: Reizman had married Sheindel and was living in Czechy near Liptovský Mikuláš, with a Swedish visa already in hand and a passport expected soon. Since his wife had no visa of her own, the Rebbe's office — likely writing to Yaakov Yisrael Zuber — asked that an additional affidavit be sent on her behalf so the couple could travel together.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, survivors, yehoshua heshel reizman, sweden, yaakov yisrael zuber, immigration

Title: R. Levin's group leaves Lodz for Katowice on Bricha escape route
Summary: R. Yisrael Yehuda Levin and his Chabad group depart Lodz for Katowice on 10 Menachem Av as part of the Bricha escape effort.
Story: After finally receiving passports, Levin and a Chabad group left Lodz for Katowice on 10 Menachem Av 5706. Upon arrival they were asked not to appear on the streets with long beards. Mikhael Teitelbaum departed separately via Stettin, while Levin remained with the main group to travel by train toward Prague.
Tags: bricha, poland, lodz, katowice, escape, refugees

Title: Author crosses the Russian border, leaving the Soviet Union
Summary: On 15 Av 5706 the author and his family crossed the border out of Russia — 'the homeland and cradle of Chabad' — beginning a year-and-a-half journey westward that would end in America.
Story: After the war an organised effort smuggled Lubavitcher chassidim out of the Soviet Union via Poland. The author crossed the border on 15 Av 5706 and reached America on 18 Adar Sheni 5708. He contrasts the eighteen-month exodus with the twelve-hour Moscow-to-New-York flights available to Soviet Jews leaving in 5752.
Tags: soviet-exit, post-war, border-crossing, russia

Title: Family crosses Soviet border from Lemberg to Poland on 15 Av 5706
Summary: On 15 Menachem Av 5706 the narrator and Reb Yisrael Shimon, with their families, boarded a train from Lemberg and crossed the Soviet-Polish border using a passport whose photograph the narrator had affixed and stamped himself by candlelight.
Story: Because Yisrael Shimon's purchased passport lacked a photograph and Polish border crossing required one, the narrator forged a Samarkand police seal onto an affixed photo using ink-pencil tools acquired in Lemberg. Anash including R. Yehuda Leib Matzkin and R. Yaakov Yosef Raskin examined and approved the forgery. The train passed through the border station Medyka, and a Soviet officer accepted the doctored passport, allowing the families to reach Przemyśl on the Polish side.
Tags: lemberg, lviv, poland, bricha, refugees, border crossing, forged passport, post-war escape, soviet union

Title: Rebbe's letter to Shanghai students charges them with mission
Summary: On 15 Av 5706 the Rebbe wrote to his Shanghai students, telling them divine providence had brought them to warm up 'tepid America' with chasidic passion.
Story: Upon their arrival from Shanghai, the sixth Rebbe sent a poignant letter laying out a new vision for his refugee students. He framed their long odyssey from Poland through China to America as a divine mission to bolster Jewish life, instructing them not to be sidetracked by American bounty but to look for the positive in others and the deficiencies in themselves.
Tags: igrot kodesh, shanghai, poland, tomchei temimim, america

Title: Levin's group reaches Prague; Rebbe sends R. Yisroel Jacobson
Summary: On 17 Menachem Av the group reaches Prague where R. Yisroel Jacobson, sent specially by the Frierdiker Rebbe, awaits them.
Story: After a polite border check by Czech police, the Warsaw–Prague express reached Prague on Wednesday, 17 Av 5706. R. Yehuda Chitrik told Levin the verse 'I bore you on eagles' wings' was being fulfilled. The Frierdiker Rebbe had dispatched R. Yisroel Jacobson from America specifically to receive them and arrange their onward journey.
Tags: prague, bricha, refugees, yisroel-jacobson, shliach, yehuda-chitrik

Title: Levin prays at the Maharal's grave in Prague
Summary: On 18 Av the refugees daven in the Maharal's synagogue and Levin visits his grave to plead for children.
Story: On Thursday Parshat Ekev, 18 Menachem Av 5706, the Chabad refugees went into Prague to daven at the Altneuschul. Afterward Levin and his wife Itta Devorah visited the adjacent graves of the Maharal of Prague and his righteous wife to beg for healthy offspring.
Tags: prague, maharal, graves, children, altneuschul

Title: Friday-night farbrengen with R. Yisroel Jacobson in Prague camp
Summary: On 19 Av 5706 the Rebbe's emissary leads a Friday-night farbrengen in the Prague refugee camp.
Story: On Erev Shabbat Ekev, 19 Av 5706, bottles of mashke were brought to the camp from the city. At the Friday-night meal R. Yisroel Jacobson farbrenged with the group — Levin's first time experiencing a personal emissary of the Rebbe at a tisch. Jacobson, who otherwise ate only food brought from America, accepted chicken that Itta Devorah had koshered in Katowice once told her father was R. Meir Gorkov, and blessed her with offspring.
Tags: prague, farbrengen, yisroel-jacobson, refugee-camp, meir-gorkov

Title: Rabbi Herzog addresses refugees at Maharal's Prague synagogue
Summary: On 21 Av Chief Rabbi Herzog speaks in Prague urging refugees to make aliyah to Eretz Yisrael.
Story: On Sunday Parshat Re'eh, 21 Menachem Av 5706, the Chabad group returned to the Altneuschul. Rabbi Yitzchak Halevi Herzog, Chief Rabbi of Eretz Yisrael, spoke on Parshat Re'eh and called on all to immigrate to Eretz Yisrael. Litvish yeshiva talmidim Levin knew from Samarkand and other Polish refugees were also present.
Tags: prague, rabbi-herzog, aliyah, refugees, litvish-yeshivos, samarkand

Title: Shabbat Mevorchim Elul 5706 spent near Polish-Czech border before Bricha crossing
Summary: On the last Shabbat of Menachem Av 5706, near the Polish-Czech border in a town the narrator recalls as Kliatzk, Anash held a farbrengen where R. Nissan Nemenov declared that they were leaving a 'true world' under Soviet persecution for a 'false world' where Torah brought honor and money.
Story: The Anash group waited at this settlement near the Polish-Czech border for the Bricha to move them onward. At the Shabbat Mevorchim Elul farbrengen, one of the participants — likely R. Nissan Nemenov — observed that in Russia Yiddishkeit had been authentic precisely because Torah-learning and Shabbat brought five-year prison sentences, while in the West religious life would be cheapened by ease. On motzaei Shabbat they were told to prepare to cross the border that night.
Tags: bricha, poland, czechoslovakia, kliatzk, farbrengen, refugees, nissan nemenov

Title: First attempted Czech–German border crossing repulsed by U.S. MPs
Summary: On 28 Av the group is driven from Asch to the border but turned back at gunpoint by American MPs.
Story: After Shabbat in Asch the Chabad group was driven by Bricha guides to the U.S.-zone border on Sunday Parshat Shoftim, 28 Av 5706. The original guards had been replaced and U.S. Military Police forced them — including pregnant women such as R. Pinchas Schreiber's daughter — back onto the truck. They returned to Asch and soon moved to a former Wehrmacht camp closer to the frontier to wait for another attempt.
Tags: bricha, germany, asch, border, us-military, refugees, pinchas-schreiber

Title: Ketubah d'irkesa written in Vienna on 1 Elul 5706
Summary: Having left their original ketubah in Moscow, the narrator arranged a replacement ketubah d'irkesa dated Wednesday, 1 Rosh Chodesh Elul 5706, while housed in Vienna's former Rothschild Hospital.
Story: Because halacha forbids living without a ketubah even for an hour, once the family reached the relative safety of Vienna the narrator commissioned a replacement ketubah arranged by R. Avraham Eliyahu Plotkin. The witnesses were R. Moshe Binyamin Kaplan and R. Menachem Mendel Raskin. The document confirms the family was already in Austria by Rosh Chodesh Elul 5706.
Tags: vienna, austria, rothschild hospital, ketubah, moshe binyamin kaplan, menachem mendel raskin, refugees

Title: Night march through forest into U.S.-occupied Germany
Summary: On 6 Elul Bricha guides lead the group at night through a forest toward the U.S. zone under MP gunfire.
Story: On Monday Parshat Ki Seitzei, 6 Elul 5706, Bricha activists trucked the group to a stable beside a forest. After dark a guide led them into the woods; jeeps of U.S. Military Police fired into the trees on hearing rustling, forcing them to lie still. The guide briefly led them toward the Soviet zone before correcting course; they walked nearly all night.
Tags: bricha, germany, forest, us-military, border, refugees

Title: Levin's group reaches UNRRA camp at Rehau
Summary: On 7 Elul 5706 the group slips into the UNRRA gate at Rehau, escaping pursuing U.S. MP jeeps.
Story: At dawn the guide ordered them onto the road; Itta Devorah ran ahead and reached the UNRRA gate first on 7 Elul 5706 (Parshat Ki Seitzei). Once inside they were protected from being returned to Czechoslovakia by UNRRA jurisdiction. An MP jeep — driven by the same officers from the earlier turn-back — passed moments later but could not enter UNRRA territory. The next day a Jewish woman ran in reporting that 150 refugees just behind them had been seized by MPs.
Tags: unrra, rehau, germany, dp-camp, bricha, refugees

Title: R. Chaikel Chaikin escorts Levin's group to Hof DP camp
Summary: On 9 Elul R. Chaikel Chaikin arrives by truck and brings the group from Rehau to the larger Hof DP camp.
Story: On Thursday Parshat Ki Seitzei, 9 Elul 5706, R. Chaikel Chaikin — already settled at Hof — drove out to fetch them. Hof was further from the border and considered safer. The group spent Shabbat Parshat Ki Seitzei (11 Elul) there before moving on.
Tags: hof, germany, dp-camp, chaikel-chaikin, refugees

Title: Chabad refugees settle at Waldstadt Pocking DP camp
Summary: After Shabbos the Chabad refugees move to Waldstadt 'Pocking', a forested DP camp of 7,000 Jews near Munich.
Story: Following Shabbat at Hof the group moved to Waldstadt Pocking, a sprawling DP camp of about 7,000 Jews not far from Munich. Two blocks were assigned temporarily, with a permanent Lubavitcher corner — one room per family — promised within days. Pocking would become the main Chabad refugee hub in occupied Germany.
Tags: pocking, waldstadt, germany, dp-camp, munich

Title: R. Nissan Nemanov organizes Anash vaad at Pocking
Summary: On 15 Elul 5706 R. Nissan Nemanov convenes an assembly and appoints a Chabad vaad including Mikhael Teitelbaum.
Story: On Wednesday Parshat Ki Tavo, 15 Elul 5706, R. Nissan Nemanov gathered the Lubavitchers in Pocking and, with general consensus, established a vaad to run their communal affairs. Mikhael Teitelbaum, reunited with Levin at Pocking, was included among the appointees. The community was filled with joy at having reconstituted itself in safety.
Tags: pocking, nissan-nemanov, vaad, mikhael-teitelbaum

Title: R. Nissan Nemanov leads Chai Elul farbrengen in Pocking
Summary: On Shabbos Chai Elul 5706 R. Nissan Nemanov farbrengs in the Agudah shul at Pocking with singing and dancing.
Story: On Shabbat 18 Elul 5706 R. Nissan Nemanov held a joyous farbrengen in the Agudah synagogue at Pocking. The broken refugees in the camp could not understand the Lubavitchers' jubilation at having escaped Russia; one was overheard calling them 'a meshugene Agudah.' R. Nemanov soon arranged daily shiurim and rebuilt a yeshiva structure with melamdim.
Tags: chai-elul, pocking, nissan-nemanov, farbrengen

Title: Shabbat Slichot 5706: refugees arrive at Pocking DP camp
Summary: By Shabbat Slichot 5706, the last Shabbat of the year, the Anash refugee group had reached the Pocking DP camp in Germany, completing roughly two months of travel from Samarkand.
Story: Pocking, a former wartime airbase converted into a vast refugee camp, housed many factions — Hungarian, Polish, right-wing, left-wing, Betar, Hashomer Hatzair — each in separate barracks. Anash received five or six barracks, with one set aside as a Tomchei Temimim yeshiva and another as a beit knesset. R. Nissan Nemenov organized a full daily seder of Tehillim, tefillah, and learning from dawn through ma'ariv, and arranged a group to study sh'chita; the narrator received his sh'chita certification later in Paris.
Tags: pocking, germany, displaced persons camp, tomchei temimim, nissan nemenov, shechita, joint, unrra

Title: Group yechidus with Rebbe Rayatz on 27 Elul
Summary: On Monday, 27 Elul 5706, the Shanghai students finally entered for a brief group yechidus with the ailing Frierdiker Rebbe in New York.
Story: Upon arriving in New York, the students found the Frierdiker Rebbe in weakened health, and their yechidus was repeatedly postponed. As R. Shmuel Dovid Reitchik wrote, each day they were told they could enter 'tomorrow or the day after,' until finally on Monday before Rosh Hashanah — 27 Elul 5706 — the entire group entered together for a few minutes, during which the Rebbe spoke to them briefly.
Tags: new york, yechidus, tomchei tmimim, shanghai, rosh hashanah, health

Title: Group of 232 Chasidim cross Soviet border on December 2, 1946
Summary: Fifty families totaling 232 Chasidim, including Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, crossed from Russia into Poland during a tense two-hour border inspection.
Story: Russian guards removed all passengers and inspected papers; Rabbi Berel Gurewicz was arrested while the rest were allowed to reboard. The Ramash (later the seventh Rebbe) later told Chasidim in Paris that during those exact two hours, the sixth Rebbe in Brooklyn sat reciting the Az Yashir prayer and finally exclaimed, 'They got through, they got through,' moments before a telegram arrived from Przemysl.
Tags: great escape, lvov, russia, poland, rebbetzin chana schneerson, berel gurewicz, kgb

Title: Rebbe appoints Binyamin Gorodetsky as European representative
Summary: On 15 Kislev 5707 the Rebbe named Rabbi Binyamin Gorodetsky his European representative and instructed him to open an office in Paris.
Story: Gorodetsky was tasked with assisting the refugees in France and other countries and facilitating their permanent resettlement. The Rebbe asked him to compile a detailed questionnaire on each refugee with photographs and ages. The bureau, known as 'the lishkah,' continues to operate from Paris to the present day.
Tags: paris, france, lishkah, binyamin gorodetsky, refugees

Title: Rebbe sends celebratory letter to escapees from Russia
Summary: On 15 Kislev 5707 the Rebbe wrote a letter overflowing with joy to anash and the students of Tomchei Temimim who had escaped from Russia.
Story: Six days after the December 2 crossing, the Rebbe wrote, 'Blessed is the Lord, our G-d... who saved you and your family members.' He assured the refugees that 'all of our brothers and sisters will help you with love and affection' to find livelihoods and Jewish education for their children.
Tags: igrot kodesh, great escape, tomchei temimim, anash

Title: Chabad mass escape from Soviet Union on Polish passports
Summary: Roughly one thousand Chabad Chasidim fled the USSR using forged Polish documents in a clandestine operation.
Story: Among those who escaped were Bentzion Shemtov, the Yakovshvili family (who changed their name to the more Polish-sounding Jacobson), and many activists from the underground network. After surviving the war in Tashkent and elsewhere, they masquerade as Polish refugees. Most were later resettled by the Rebbe to communities around the world.
Tags: lvov escape, polish passports, emigration, shemtov, jacobson

Title: Ireland offers thousands of tons of kosher meat to the Yishuv
Summary: The Irish government offered the Jewish settlement in the Holy Land thousands of tons of meat to be made kosher, prompting a major shechita operation organized from Paris.
Story: After the war, the Irish government proposed gifting thousands of tons of meat — kashered on site and canned — to the Jewish settlement in the Holy Land, an undertaking requiring shochtim, menakrim, supervising rabbis, and laborers. The Union of Refugee Rabbis in Paris, headed by the author's uncle R' Chaim Leib, judged the project beyond its capacity and referred it to R' Benyamin Gorodetzky's bureau, which obtained the Rebbe Rayatz's approval to take it on. Gorodetzky drew up a roster of avreichim who had studied shechita in Pocking, the author among them, though by then his U.S. visa was already in hand.
Tags: ireland, paris, kosher-meat, shechita, post-war, refugee-rabbis-union, benyamin-gorodetzky, yishuv, pocking

Title: Kehot publishes introduction analyzing the Mitteler Rebbe's petition
Summary: Kehot published in 5707 an edition containing the Rebbe's introduction examining the authorship of the Mitteler Rebbe's petition to Khovansky.
Story: In 5707 (1946-1947), Kehot Publication Society issued an edition featuring an introduction by the Rebbe examining the petition written to Vitebsk's General-Governor Khovansky. The introduction argued against attributing the petition to the Alter Rebbe, demonstrating from internal evidence and historical circumstances that it was authored by the Mitteler Rebbe during his Vitebsk arrest. The analysis became foundational to subsequent Chabad scholarship on the imprisonment and acquittal.
Tags: kehot, lubavitch, historiography

Title: Kehot publishes Sefer HaToldot Admur Maharash
Summary: In 5707 Kehot published Sefer HaToldot Admur Maharash, including a photograph of one page of the megillah he wrote.
Story: The biography described how the Maharash, on doctors' orders for physical activity, produced craftworks including a man-height menorah, mosaic tables, sifrei Torah, megillos, and mezuzos. While the household vessels were lost in transit out of Russia, the megillah and one of the tables survived; Kehot's 5707 edition reproduced one of its pages, and a clearer reproduction appeared in Igros Kodesh Admur Maharash in 5753.
Tags: kehot, maharash, biography, toldos

Title: New York Haggadah 'Eshei Yisrael' on Modzitz teachings by Taub family
Summary: An 'Eshei Yisrael' Haggadah featuring Modzitz dynasty teachings by Yisrael Taub and his son Shaul Yedidya Eliezer Taub was published in New York.
Story: In 5707 (1947), the Haggadah 'Eshei Yisrael' was published in New York, featuring two commentaries: 'Divrei Yisrael' by Rebbe Yisrael Taub of Modzitz and 'Yisa Berachah' by his son Rebbe Shaul Yedidya Eliezer Taub of Modzitz. Material from Rebbe Yechezkel of Kazmir and Rebbe Shmuel Eliyahu of Zvolin was also included. The 119-page octavo edition preserved the musical-Chassidic legacy of the Modzitz dynasty in postwar America.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, modzitz, kazmir, zvolin, new york, taub

Title: Publication of Sefer HaToldot Admur Maharash with maamar registry
Summary: In 5707 (1947) the Rebbe Rayatz published Sefer HaToldot Admur Maharash, which included his chronological registry of the Maharash's discourses.
Story: The Rebbe Rayatz expanded the registry methodology he had developed earlier for his father's maamarim, applying it to the maamarim of his grandfather, the Rebbe Maharash. The work was printed as a booklet in 1947 as part of Sefer HaToldot Admur Maharash. It would later be supplemented in 1981 with more than two hundred additional maamarim discovered in manuscript.
Tags: maharash, rayatz, maamarim, registry

Title: R' Shmuel Grossman appointed director of Tomchei Tmimim in Wegscheid DP camp
Summary: After leaving Russia in 5707, R' Shmuel Grossman served as director of the newly founded Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in the Wegscheid DP camp in Austria.
Story: Following his emigration from Russia in 5707, R' Shmuel Grossman served for a period as director of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva that was established at the Wegscheid displaced persons camp in Austria. He later moved to Paris before eventually settling in London.
Tags: wegscheid, austria, displaced-persons, grossman, tomchei-tmimim, wwii

Title: R' Yitzchok Goldin in Poland searches Warsaw cellars for lost manuscripts
Summary: In the summer of 1947 the Rebbe Rayatz asks his son-in-law (the Ramash) to instruct R' Yitzchok Goldin to search Warsaw cellars for the missing Chabad manuscripts.
Story: While R' Yitzchok Goldin was in Poland in summer 5707, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote secretary R' Moshe Leib Rodstein asking that his son-in-law the Ramash write Goldin about searching specific Warsaw cellars and other sites where many manuscripts had been gathered. The search produced no results at that time.
Tags: manuscripts, warsaw, schneersohn-library, yitzchok-goldin, ramash

Title: The Rebbe travels to Paris to bring his mother Rebbetzin Chana
Summary: In 5707 the Rebbe traveled to Paris to bring his mother Rebbetzin Chana, who had been rescued from Russia, to America.
Story: While in Paris in 5707 the Rebbe also received from Mrs. Chana Uzerman — the granddaughter of R' Menachem Mendel of Paris, son of the Maharash — a mosaic-style table built by the Maharash himself. The collapsible table had passed from the Maharash to his youngest son and then to Uzerman after R' Menachem Mendel's death during WWII. The Rebbe reassembled it in his 770 yechidus room, where it has remained ever since.
Tags: paris, rebbetzin chana, rebbe, maharash table, uzerman

Title: Thinner-format Tehillas Hashem siddur issued in New York
Summary: A second, thinner-format edition of Tehillas Hashem was published in New York in 1947, photographed from the 1918 Rostover Siddur.
Story: The 5707 (1947) New York edition reproduced the Rostov 1918 siddur, itself based on the Tefillas Kol Peh corrected under the Rebbe Rashab. Issued alongside the thicker 1945 edition, it gave Chabad davveners two parallel formats.
Tags: new york, siddur, tehillas hashem, rostov

Title: Yakovshvili family escapes Russia as 'Polish' refugees
Summary: After nine years in the gulag, Simon Yakovshvili and his family fled Russia using false Polish passports, changing their name to Jacobson.
Story: Yakovshvili was part of the audacious escape of about one thousand Chasidim organized by the Chabad underground in late 1946 and early 1947. The Shemtov family escaped on the same route. In 1952 the Jacobsons settled in Toronto, where Simon served briefly as rabbi of the local Chabad congregation before his death in June 1953.
Tags: jacobson, yakovshvili, escape, polish-passports, uzbekistan

Title: Rabbi Mendel Futerfas arrested ending the Great Escape
Summary: Soviet secret agents arrested Rabbi Mendel Futerfas and other Chasidim aboard a passenger train, ending the organized exodus from Russia.
Story: When remaining Chasidim attempted to cross on a regular passenger train, agents circulated onboard and arrested Futerfas at the border. The arrests began a roundup that ensnared other organizers including Sara Katzenelenbogen, forcing the Lvov network to scatter deep into Russia to evade the secret police. Futerfas would be sentenced to nine years in prison.
Tags: lvov, mendel futerfas, kgb, great escape, russia

Title: R. Levin receives first letter from Frierdiker Rebbe at Pocking
Summary: On 23 Shevat 5707 Levin receives a welcome and blessing letter from the Frierdiker Rebbe via the Paris lishka.
Story: After Levin and others demanded the camp leadership find a way to reestablish direct contact with the Rebbe, the Paris lishka began conveying letters. The Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to Levin on 23 Shevat 5707 with a 'baruchim haba'im' blessing for him and his wife and wishes for success in material and spiritual matters. Levin had waited for such a letter throughout the entire flight from Russia.
Tags: pocking, frierdiker-rebbe, correspondence, paris-lishka, hiskashrus

Title: Rashag and R. Benyamin Gorodetzky visit Pocking before Pesach
Summary: Before Pesach 5707 the Rashag and R. Benyamin Gorodetzky visit Pocking with letters and maamarim from the Rebbe.
Story: Before Pesach 5707 R. Benyamin Gorodetzky and the Rashag came from the Rebbe to Pocking. The Rashag held a Shabbat farbrengen with anash; afterward R. Shlomo Matusof delivered a letter from the Rebbe rebuking Levin's preoccupations and urging him to immerse in study. They also brought freshly copied maamarim of the Rebbe from that year.
Tags: pocking, rashag, benyamin-gorodetzky, shlomo-matusof, maamarim

Title: R. Levin receives Rebbe's letter dated 27 Nissan 5707
Summary: Letter dated 27 Nissan 5707 from the Frierdiker Rebbe to Levin blessing his health and that of his family.
Story: Through the Paris office Levin received a letter from the Frierdiker Rebbe dated 27 Nissan 5707, blessing his health and that of his household along with success in their material and spiritual needs. This was part of a series of letters now flowing between Pocking and the Rebbe via the Paris lishka.
Tags: pocking, frierdiker-rebbe, correspondence

Title: Rebbe instructs Chasidim to stay in Poland to free prisoners
Summary: On 8 Iyar 5707 the Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Shalom Mendel Kalmenson directing Zalman Serebryanski and Yitzchak Goldin to remain in Poland to help free three jailed Chasidim.
Story: Berel Gurewicz, Berke Chein, and Tzipa Kozliner had been detained by local police in Lvov unaware of the larger escape network. The Rebbe coordinated a $7,000 bribe routed through a contact in Vilnius, written about in code as 'medicine' for those ill. The bribe led to improved conditions and reduced sentences for all three.
Tags: poland, berel gurewicz, berke chein, tzipa kozliner, bribery, vilnius

Title: Author and family arrive in Paris under the Joint and the Lubavitch Refugee Bureau
Summary: Just before Shavuos 5707 the author and his family arrived in Paris, where the Joint and the Frierdiker Rebbe's Refugee Bureau (headed by R' B. Gorodetzky with R' Rafael Wilshansky as secretary) took charge of their care.
Story: After temporary housing at the Hotel La Chapelle, the family was moved to a sub-divided room in a former noble château in Sèvres, where more than ten refugee families lived together. During his stay in Paris the author received hagahah and kabbalah for shechting poultry, having begun sharpening knives back in Pocking, and shechted in the Pletzl market alongside R' Betzalel Wilshansky.
Tags: paris, joint, refugee-bureau, gorodetzky, wilshansky, sevres, shechita

Title: Family departs Pocking DP camp on forged Prague passports, end of Iyar 5707
Summary: At the end of Iyar 5707, after eight months in Pocking, the narrator's family left Germany on passports arranged by the Rebbe Rayatz's Paris lishka, ostensibly traveling from Prague to Paris via Germany.
Story: The Paris lishka headed by R. Benyamin Gorodetzky supplied Pocking refugees with passports lacking the required Czech-German border stamps because the bearers had never actually been in Prague. Boarding the train at Munich, the family was discovered by a strict American military conductor who put them off at Karlsruhe, the last station before the French border. After hours of uncertainty, a station official ruled the documents valid and they continued on the next train to Paris, ending the Pocking-Germany chapter that had spanned late Elul 5706 through late Iyar 5707.
Tags: pocking, germany, munich, karlsruhe, paris, france, passport, displaced persons, lishka, ben gurodetzky

Title: Rebbe's interrogation-day response to Futerfas
Summary: On 17 Iyar 5707, the day Mendel Futerfas was brought into Soviet interrogation, the Rebbe sent his wife a letter answering an imagined telegram from her husband.
Story: Futerfas later recounted that at his moment of crisis, he envisioned writing to the Rebbe and conjured the image of Simchat Torah 1927, the last time he saw him. On that same day his wife in England received a letter beginning 'Your telegram has been received,' dated 17 Iyar 5707. Only when reunited in 1963 did the couple piece together what had occurred.
Tags: mendel futerfas, russia, kgb, prison, telepathic letter

Title: R. Chaim Asher brings Rebbe's letters to Pocking on Lag B'Omer
Summary: On Lag B'Omer 5707 R. Chaim Asher arrives from Paris with replies from the Frierdiker Rebbe.
Story: On Lag B'Omer 5707 R. Chaim Asher came from Paris bearing further letters from the Rebbe in response to those sent after the first 'baruchim haba'im' batch. Levin then wrote again pleading for mercy on his sister Frayde Meni Sosonkin, her husband Asher (son of R. Shmaryahu Sosonkin of Batum) and their daughter Chava, who remained stranded in Lvov.
Tags: pocking, paris-lishka, lag-baomer, chaim-asher, correspondence, sosonkin-family

Title: Ramash leads Lag BaOmer farbrengen in Paris
Summary: On Lag BaOmer 1947, while in Paris arranging his mother's emigration, the Ramash led a farbrengen recounting the Rebbe's mystical role in the December border crossing.
Story: The future seventh Rebbe traveled to France in 1947 to reunite with his mother Rebbetzin Chana after twenty years of separation. At the Lag BaOmer gathering he told the story of how, on December 2, 1946, the sixth Rebbe had recited Az Yashir and proclaimed 'They got through' at the exact hour the refugees were detained at the border.
Tags: paris, france, lag baomer, ramash, rebbetzin chana

Title: Rayatz instructs Atkin to send the Kavash vessels via the Rebbe
Summary: On 29 Iyar 5707 Rebbe Rayatz wrote R' Meir Atkin to hand the holy vessels from R' Chaim Kavash's estate to R' Benjamin Gorodetsky.
Story: Having fled the Soviet Union, R' Meir Atkin offered Rebbe Rayatz the heirloom vessels he had purchased from the estate of R' Chaim Kavash — including a spoon attributed to the Baal Shem Tov and a cup of R' Mordechai of Lechovitch. Rayatz replied on 29 Iyar 5707 directing him to entrust them to R' Benjamin Gorodetsky for safekeeping. Atkin, however, ultimately handed them to the Ramash (the future Rebbe) in Paris on 25 Sivan, before the Rebbe's return to New York.
Tags: atkin, kavash, baal shem tov, paris, gourary, gorodetsky

Title: Pocking Shavuos memorial morphs into Lubavitch chinuch drive
Summary: On Shavuos 5707 Levin and Mikhael Teitelbaum convert a yizkor assembly into a Lubavitch education drive.
Story: Acting on a rebuke from the Ramash that Pocking's Lubavitchers were sitting idle while DP children went untaught, Levin and Mikhael Teitelbaum independently summoned all 7,000 refugees on Shavuos 5707 to a 'memorial' at the Chabad shul. R. Avraham Eliyahu Plotkin and R. Yisrael of Nevel delivered fiery drashos linking Dovid HaMelech to the chinuch of children. After a stormy split between Mizrachi and Cherut factions, an agreement emerged: Lubavitcher melamdim would supplement the camp's secular schools with Torah hours, planting decades of warmth toward Yiddishkeit in Pocking-raised children.
Tags: pocking, shavuos, chinuch, memorial, mikhael-teitelbaum, ramash, plotkin, schools

Title: Rebbe's letter dated 29 Sivan 5707 reaches R. Levin
Summary: On 29 Sivan 5707 the Frierdiker Rebbe answers Levin's plea for the Sosonkin family stranded in Lvov.
Story: Replying via the Paris office, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote on 29 Sivan 5707 invoking blessings on the family members in Levin's earlier letter — his sister Frayde, her husband Asher Sosonkin, and their daughter Chava — who remained in the Soviet Union. The Rebbe blessed them with refuah, deliverance from hardship, and reunion with anash in the Rebbe's presence.
Tags: pocking, frierdiker-rebbe, correspondence, sosonkin-family, ussr

Title: Israel Aryeh Leib Schneersohn writes to his mother after her arrival in the US
Summary: On 4 Tammuz 5707 the Rebbe's brother Israel Aryeh Leib wrote to his mother Chana after she escaped the Soviet Union and reached the United States.
Story: Following the dramatic rescue of Rebbetzin Chana Schneersohn from the Soviet Union and her arrival in the United States in summer 5707, her younger son Israel Aryeh Leib wrote her a warm letter on 4 Tammuz 5707. He expressed relief that her ordeal of waiting and travel had ended and asked after her health and her injured leg. He sent photographs of his daughter Dalia and looked forward to a reunion with his mother and brother.
Tags: rebbetzin chana, israel aryeh leib, schneersohn family, letter

Title: Yisrael Azriel Feldman aids Anash refugees in Steyer DP camp
Summary: On 20 Menachem Av 5707, Yisrael Azriel Feldman wrote to the Rebbe from Steyer, Austria, reporting on his aid to Anash arriving from the Soviet Union.
Story: Feldman, a former Tomchei Temimim Warsaw student who had fled to Russia and then to the Steyer DP camp, was serving as the camp's rav and av beit din. He built a mikvah and arranged an oven for baking matzot at the highest standard, helping Anash including R' Moshe Zalman Kaminetzky, R' Elimelech Perman, R' Zalman Teibel and R' Menachem Mendel Seitz. He noted that he and Pinchas Klein were the only Tomchei Temimim talmidim in the camp.
Tags: yisrael azriel feldman, steyer, austria, displaced persons, mikvah, matzah, anash

Title: Rebbe Rayatz gives 50th anniversary gift to Rebbetzin Nechama Dina
Summary: On their 50th anniversary, Rebbe Rayatz gifted Rebbetzin Nechama Dina a new coat with $500 from their joint fund, and the future Rebbe gifted her a printed copy of Sefer HaZichronot.
Story: On 13 Elul 5707, marking fifty years since their wedding, Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak wrote a brief Yiddish note to his wife wishing many long, healthy, content years, nachas from their children, and all good both materially and spiritually. He gifted her a new coat funded by $500 from 'our joint fund,' to be worn in health and with a joyful heart. The future Rebbe (then Ramash) gifted Rebbetzin Nechama Dina a printed copy of Rebbe Rayatz's Sefer HaZichronot, which he had brought to press that same year.
Tags: rayatz, nechama-dina, anniversary, sefer-hazichronot, yiddish

Title: Birth of Sterna Sarah Levin in Pocking DP camp
Summary: On 24 Elul 5707 Itta Devorah Levin gives birth to a daughter, Sterna Sarah, at Pocking.
Story: On 24 Elul 5707 Itta Devorah Levin gave birth to a daughter — Sterna Sarah — while still in Pocking awaiting visas. The yeshiva's cooks prepared a large and lengthy kiddush, with much mashke and a farbrengen lasting until evening. R. Avraham Mayor was so joyful he rolled along the benches.
Tags: pocking, birth, sterna-sarah, levin-family, avraham-mayor

Title: JDC sends 27 Chabad shochtim to Ireland for kosher meat production
Summary: The JDC sponsored twenty-seven Chabad-affiliated kosher slaughterers to staff a Dublin meat plant supplying kosher meat to European Jewish refugees.
Story: Working in partnership with the Sixth Rebbe in the postwar refugee period, the JDC arranged this large-scale shechita operation to feed survivors in displaced-persons camps in Italy and elsewhere. Rabbi Benjamin Gorodetsky helped coordinate.
Tags: jdc, shochtim, ireland, dublin, refugees, kosher meat

Title: Bentzion Shemtov sent to establish Chabad in London
Summary: In October 1947 the Rebbe sent Bentzion Shemtov, one of the nine Chasidim of the 1924 oath, to establish Chabad in London.
Story: Shemtov was among the trusted veterans of Chabad activism whom the Rebbe deployed in the postwar years to build infrastructure in Western communities. His mission in London laid groundwork for Chabad's enduring presence in the United Kingdom.
Tags: bentzion shemtov, london, england, shlichus

Title: Rebbe writes about Levin's ailing daughter
Summary: On 5 Kislev 5708 a letter in the Rebbe's name responds to news of the infant Sterna Sarah's illness.
Story: In early winter 5708 Levin's infant daughter took ill and he wrote to the Rebbe. The reply, dated 5 Kislev 5708 and sent in the Rebbe's name, conveyed mazal tov on her birth and a blessing to raise her to Torah, chuppah and good deeds amid material and spiritual ease.
Tags: pocking, frierdiker-rebbe, correspondence, children-health

Title: Birth of son Gershon in Paris during postwar refugee interlude
Summary: The author's son Gershon was born in Paris on the eve of Shabbat Vayishlach, 15 Kislev 5708, while the family awaited departure for the United States.
Story: Holding a U.S. visa but pregnant near term, the author's wife had consulted the Rebbe Rayatz on whether to sail before or after the birth, since trans-Atlantic travel was then by ship. The Rebbe approved their plan to emigrate. On the night entering Friday — erev Shabbat Vayishlach, 15 Kislev 5708 — their son Gershon was born in Paris among the postwar Chabad refugee community.
Tags: paris, france, family, post-war, 15-kislev, vayishlach, refugee

Title: R. Michael Vilensky sends completed questionnaire on his father
Summary: On 15 Kislev 5708 R. Michael Vilensky finally sent in his written answers to the questionnaire about his father's life.
Story: After nearly a decade of repeated requests, R. Michael Vilensky completed and dispatched his replies to a special questionnaire that the Rebbe's secretariat had prepared to help him record his father's biography. He apologized that the answers were heavy on quantity but light on quality, and that he had no written notes from which to work.
Tags: michael vilensky, chaim dover vilensky, kremenchug, biography

Title: Berel Gurewicz freed in Poland before Passover
Summary: Just before Passover 1948, Berel Gurewicz was freed in Poland as part of a prisoner exchange after maintaining his cover as a Polish citizen.
Story: Bribed Soviet officials included Gurewicz in a Russia-Poland prisoner exchange. He then secretly crossed into Czechoslovakia, and with Vaad Hatzalah's help, he traveled to Paris to reunite with the family that had fled Russia without him.
Tags: berel gurewicz, poland, czechoslovakia, paris, vaad hatzalah

Title: First printing of Kitzurim v'Hearos al Tanya at Gertz Brothers press
Summary: The memoirist typeset and printed the first edition of Kitzurim v'Hearos al Tanya (by the Tzemach Tzedek) at the Gertz Brothers press in 5708/1948.
Story: The Rebbe (then Ramash) handed the memoirist successive manuscript fascicles of the Tzemach Tzedek's Kitzurim v'Hearos al Tanya to typeset, until a small kuntres grew into a full book. When the Gertz print shop's vacation ended before the book was finished, the brothers gave him a key so he could work alone until midnight to complete it. The first edition's colophon reads 'Printed at the Gertz Brothers Press.'
Tags: tanya, tzemach tzedek, brooklyn, gertz brothers press, memoirist as typesetter

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe directs memoirist to buy a Linotype machine
Summary: In a yechidus with the Frierdiker Rebbe, the memoirist was told to purchase a Linotype machine to print the chag-and-mo'ed kuntreisim — replacing the cumbersome Shulsinger workflow.
Story: The Frierdiker Rebbe knew the memoirist had begun printing the kuntresim and was paying others for typesetting. In yechidus he instructed him to purchase a Linotype machine. When the memoirist objected that the $3,000 price (an enormous sum at the time) was beyond him, the Rebbe answered, 'You don't need to pay it all — a bit on the mountain and a bit on the worry!'
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, linotype, yechidus, kuntresim, shulsinger

Title: Kfar Chabad established
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz established Kfar Chabad, the Chabad village in Israel, instructing that its focus should be to reach beyond religious Jews to all Israelis.
Story: Kfar Chabad became a hub for Chabad activity in the newly founded State of Israel. The Rebbe's directive that it reach all Israelis foreshadowed the broader outreach philosophy that the Ramash would later expand globally as the seventh Rebbe.
Tags: kfar-chabad, israel, village, outreach

Title: Lubavitchers regroup in Paris and found Brunoy yeshiva and Beis Rivka
Summary: In 5708, most refugee Anash regrouped in Paris and founded the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Brunoy and the Beis Rivka school in Yerres.
Story: In 5708 (1948), the bulk of the Lubavitcher refugees from the DP camps gathered in Paris and then dispersed across France. They immediately founded the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Brunoy and the Beis Rivka girls' school in Yerres, both of which have continued to grow until today.
Tags: paris, brunoy, yerres, france, tomchei-tmimim, beis-rivka, displaced-persons

Title: Memoirist begins typesetting at Modern Linotype on Eastern Parkway
Summary: After completing Kitzurim v'Hearos al Tanya, the memoirist arranged to use Yechiel Shapira's 'Modern Linotype' shop on Eastern Parkway and St. Johns each evening to typeset further works for the Rebbe.
Story: With no equipment of his own, the memoirist arranged through the Gertz brothers to work at R' Yechiel Shapira's Modern Linotype shop each evening from dusk until 10 p.m., paying Shapira for use of the machine. The Rebbe gave him manuscripts to typeset, including Ohr HaTorah on Shemos, Mafteach Ma'amarei Admur Maharashab, and the kuntresim for each chag and mo'ed.
Tags: brooklyn, eastern parkway, linotype, yechiel shapira, kehot

Title: Midrash Shmuel closes with fall of Old City Jerusalem
Summary: The Midrash Shmuel yeshiva ended when the Old City of Jerusalem fell during the War of Independence in 5708.
Story: The yeshiva had run for roughly four years in the Chabad synagogue inside the Old City. The last documented references in the Rayatz's correspondence date to 16 Cheshvan 5708, only months before the Jewish Quarter was overrun and its institutions ceased to function.
Tags: jerusalem, old city, midrash shmuel, 1948 war

Title: Publication of Rayatz's Kuntres Chag HaPesach 5708 in New York
Summary: The Chabad Rayatz Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak's 'Kuntres Chag HaPesach 5708' was published in New York.
Story: In 5708 (1948), Kuntres Chag HaPesach of the Chabad Rayatz Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was published in New York. The 29-page octavo edition contained the sixth Chabad Rebbe's discourses for the festival. It was issued during the Rebbe Rayatz's American years following his arrival in 1940.
Tags: chabad, rayatz, new york, pesach, kuntres

Title: R. Bentzion Shemtov dispatched to lead Chabad institutions in England
Summary: In 5708, Rabbi Bentzion Shemtov was sent to direct Chabad educational institutions in England.
Story: In 5708 (1948), Rabbi Bentzion Shemtov was dispatched to manage Chabad's educational institutions in England. About ten years later, his son-in-law Rabbi Nachman Sudak joined him to help with the leadership of the British Chabad institutions.
Tags: england, london, shemtov, chabad-uk, shluchim

Title: Rabbi Aloy told to return to South Africa after election scare
Summary: Following the 1948 victory of the Nationalist Afrikaner Party, Rabbi Yirmiyahu Aloy met the Rebbe in New York and was simply told, 'Fuhr aheim — go back home.'
Story: Many Jews feared the Nationalist victory presaged another Holocaust. Aloy, who had emigrated from Lithuania to South Africa before the war, asked the Rebbe in private whether to leave. The Rebbe laughed and dismissed the concern; Aloy returned and emerged as one of South Africa's most prominent rabbis on the rabbinical court.
Tags: yirmiyahu aloy, south africa, afrikaner nationalists, apartheid

Title: Rabbi Meir Ashkenazi relocates from Shanghai to New York
Summary: Shanghai's former Ashkenazi chief rabbi Meir Ashkenazi settled in Brooklyn after over two decades in China.
Story: Once in New York, members of Vaad Hatzalah initiated a din Torah accusing him of having diverted Mir Yeshivah funds to Chabad students in Shanghai. Ashkenazi argued that taking a small percentage was justified given the mortal risk of collecting funds at a neutral embassy under Japanese occupation. The rabbinical court ruled in his favor.
Tags: ashkenazi, shanghai, vaad hatzalah, din torah, mir yeshivah

Title: Rayatz establishes Kfar Chabad in Israel for Russian refugees
Summary: The Rayatz founded Kfar Chabad, a Chabad village in Israel, primarily as a settlement for refugees arriving from the Soviet Union.
Story: Founded in the year of Israeli statehood, Kfar Chabad gave the chasidic refugees from the USSR a community of their own in the Holy Land. The village became and remains a major Chabad center in Israel.
Tags: kfar chabad, israel, russian refugees, settlement

Title: Setting type for Hachaltzu 5659 in late summer 1948
Summary: In late summer 5708 (1948), the memoirist typeset the Hachaltzu 5659 ma'amar, though the kitzurim had not yet been provided.
Story: Late in the summer of 1948, the Rebbe gave the memoirist the Hachaltzu 5659 ma'amar to typeset. The kitzurim accompanying the ma'amar were only delivered after Sukkos, allowing publication of the full version with corrections.
Tags: hachaltzu, rashab, kuntres, typesetting

Title: Shemtovs sent to build Chabad in England
Summary: Following their escape from Russia, the Rebbe dispatched Bentzion Shemtov and family to develop the Chabad community in England.
Story: Having survived three years in Siberia and decades of underground activism, Shemtov was sent on a new mission to the United Kingdom. He worked to build the Chabad community there before later moving to Israel, where he founded Machon Levi Yitzchak to publish the seventh Rebbe's talks in Hebrew. He passed away in 1975 at age seventy-two.
Tags: shemtov, england, shliach, united kingdom

Title: Shemtovs sent to England by the Rebbe
Summary: After leaving Russia, Bentzion Shemtov was dispatched to England to help build the Chabad community there.
Story: Shemtov later moved to Israel, where he founded Machon Levi Yitzchak to publish the seventh Rebbe's talks in Hebrew. He died in Israel in 1975.
Tags: shemtov, england, shliach

Title: State of Israel formally declared
Summary: The land formerly known as British Mandate Palestine became the State of Israel upon its declaration of independence.
Story: The seventh Rebbe later asserted that the historical name Eretz Yisrael would be more appropriate. The Jordanian occupation of the Old City of Jerusalem began the same year and would last until 1967.
Tags: israel, independence, british-mandate, eretz-yisrael

Title: Tzemach Gurewicz brings family to Cuba
Summary: In summer 1948 Tzemach Gurewicz, unable to obtain a US visa, took his family to Cuba hoping to find an onward route to New York.
Story: Having endured five years in a Russian prison and the Great Escape, Gurewicz longed to reach his relatives in America. The Rebbe redirected his focus, telling him to build educational programs in Cuba first; only after he had done so would the Rebbe finally signal that the time had come for him to come.
Tags: tzemach gurewicz, cuba, refugees, visa

Title: Recovered Warsaw sefarim shipped via Paris to New York
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz thanks Rashaz Gurevitch via R' Shmuel Zalmanov for shipping the recovered books — including many marked from the Natan of Kremenchug collection — through Paris to New York.
Story: In winter 5708, R' Shmuel Zalmanov reported that his relative R' Shneur Zalman Gurevitch had finally shipped, together with his own possessions, all the recovered Chabad books obtained from Dr. Kahane at the Warsaw kehilla. On 17 Shevat the Rebbe Rayatz wrote Gurevitch directly to thank him. Whether any of these were among the missing 17 crates remained unverified.
Tags: library, warsaw, paris, new-york, schneersohn-library, rashaz-gurevitch, natan-of-kremenchug

Title: Author arrives in the United States aboard the SS Sobieski
Summary: On 18 Adar Sheni 5708 the author's family disembarked from the Polish liner SS Sobieski in New York, completing a year-and-a-half journey from the Soviet Union.
Story: Knowing he would be at sea for Purim, the author bought a kosher Megillas Esther in Paris and read it aboard the ship. The American visa that brought him over came not from Tomchei Tmimim but from Telz Yeshiva of Cleveland — one of the six 'professor' visas allotted to Telz was redirected to the 'Lubavitcher,' thanks to the intervention of Freidel Stein (née Sacks), niece of his wife and wife of Telz mashgiach R' Chaim Stein.
Tags: new-york, ss-sobieski, immigration, telz-yeshiva, purim-at-sea

Title: Author's first Shabbos at 770 Eastern Parkway
Summary: On his first Shabbos in New York the author walked over an hour from East New York to 770 Eastern Parkway, where he was admitted to the Frierdiker Rebbe's upstairs cabinet for kri'as haTorah.
Story: The sefer Torah was carried up from the ground-floor shul to the Rebbe's second-floor study, where the leining took place on his writing desk before a tiny minyan. As a newly-arrived refugee the author was let in, wearing a heavy hand-spun woollen tallis from Russia that looked like a winter blanket. The gabbai R' Yochanan Gordon later told him the Rebbe could not stop looking at the tallis throughout the reading; the author kept it as a memento of 'what anash wore in the land of Egypt.'
Tags: 770, frierdiker-rebbe, yochanan-gordon, tallis, kriah, east-new-york

Title: Levin family receives French visa and moves toward Paris
Summary: After Pesach 5708 Levin receives a visa to Paris arranged by his in-laws R. Meir and Fayge Rivka Gorkov.
Story: After Pesach 5708 the long-delayed visa to France finally came through. Levin's in-laws R. Meir Gorkov and Fayge Rivka Gorkov, already in Paris, had pushed the paperwork while Mikhael Teitelbaum waited on a U.S. visa. The Levins relocated from Pocking to Bezancourt outside Paris.
Tags: paris, visa, france, besancon, pocking, meir-gorkov

Title: Rebbe rebukes Paris refugees for relying on JDC support
Summary: In a letter to the Paris community the Rebbe wrote that it was 'inappropriate' and 'not the way of Chasidism' to sit idle while depending on JDC charity.
Story: Many Chasidim transferred from DP camps to France, where the JDC generously supported them. The Rebbe pressed them toward self-sufficiency: 'Each one of you must make an effort to earn a livelihood... Exert yourselves and move quickly, be it in an institution of Torah, business, or employment.'
Tags: paris, jdc, self-sufficiency, tomchei temimim, anash

Title: Feldman founds Tomchei Temimim in Steyer DP camp
Summary: On 16 Sivan 5708, Feldman wrote to the Rebbe announcing he had founded a Talmud Torah and yeshiva called Tomchei Temimim in the Steyer DP camp.
Story: Under his supervision the new institution comprised two classes of students. The founding extended the Tomchei Temimim network into postwar Austria, serving Jewish refugees in the displaced persons camp.
Tags: yisrael azriel feldman, steyer, austria, tomchei temimim, displaced persons, talmud torah

Title: Rebbe's welcome letter to R. Levin on arrival in Paris
Summary: On 21 Sivan 5708 the Rebbe writes 'baruchim haba'im' to R. Levin on his arrival in Paris.
Story: On Levin's arrival in Paris the Frierdiker Rebbe sent a personally signed welcome letter dated 21 Sivan 5708. The Rebbe blessed him and his family with health, a comfortable livelihood and immersion in Torah and avodah in their new home.
Tags: paris, frierdiker-rebbe, correspondence, besancon

Title: Rebbe asks Levin to consult elder chassidim about employment
Summary: On 29 Sivan 5708 the Rebbe directs Levin to consult senior chassidim about his employment.
Story: Idle in Bezancourt with no parnasa, Levin asked the Rebbe what work to pursue. The reply, dated 29 Sivan 5708, instructed him to consult senior anash and report back their advice. R. Yisrael Noach and other elders subsequently advised him to take up melamdus.
Tags: paris, frierdiker-rebbe, correspondence, career, yisrael-noach

Title: R' Shmuel Grossman becomes shochet in London
Summary: R' Shmuel Grossman moved from Paris to London to serve as shochet in 5708, with blessings from both Rayatz and the future Rebbe.
Story: In 5708, R' Shmuel Grossman moved from Paris to London after receiving a visa through his brother-in-law R' Asher Abramson. On 10 Nissan 5708 he wrote Rayatz seeking approval, which Rayatz granted. On 3 Av 5708, the future Rebbe wrote to him expressing satisfaction at hearing he had not only settled successfully but was also engaging in outreach work to strengthen Chassidus and Torah observance.
Tags: london, grossman, shechita, ramash, rayatz

Title: Rebbe endorses melamdus as Levin's path in Paris
Summary: On 21 Av 5708 the Rebbe endorses Levin's plan to support himself teaching the children of Parisian Jews.
Story: Replying to Levin's report on the elders' counsel, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote on 21 Av 5708 strongly endorsing his becoming a melamed. He blessed him with the gift of teaching, influence over students in conduct and chassidic ways, and ample parnasa. Levin then began traveling from Bezancourt into Paris, using addresses given by R. Zalman Serebryanski, to teach Sephardi 'patrons' who had never before encountered a Torah tutor.
Tags: paris, frierdiker-rebbe, melamdut, career, outreach, zalman-serebryanski

Title: Rabbi Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz passes away
Summary: Rabbi Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz, longtime principal of Torah Vodaath and architect of Torah Umesorah, passed away on 3 Elul.
Story: Shortly before his death he told a group of close friends gathered at his bedside about how the Sixth Rebbe had quietly saved Torah Vodaath from foreclosure during the war years — a secret he refused to take to the grave.
Tags: mendlowitz, torah vodaath, torah umesorah, 3 elul

Title: Levin reports on Paris kiruv work to the Rebbe
Summary: On 11 Elul 5708 Levin reports to the Rebbe on tutoring eight Parisian children, including putting on tefillin.
Story: Levin wrote on 11 Elul 5708 that he was traveling daily from Bezancourt into Paris to teach the children of French Jewish 'patrons' who spoke only French. He had grown his roster from one student to eight, teaching kamatz alef and laying tefillin. He described coaxing reluctant students to don a hat and tefillin and distributing French-language Merkos pamphlets in the homes.
Tags: paris, outreach, tefillin, french-jews, kiruv, merkos

Title: Birth of R. Shalom DovBer Levin in Paris
Summary: On 27 Elul 5708 Itta Devorah Levin gives birth in Paris to a son, the future Chabad librarian R. Shalom DovBer Levin.
Story: On 27 Elul 5708 in Paris Itta Devorah Levin gave birth to a son. He was named Shalom DovBer — the future longtime director of the Chabad Library at 770.
Tags: paris, birth, shalom-dovber-levin, levin-family

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe's Rosh Hashanah blessing letter to Levin
Summary: On Erev Rosh Hashanah 5709 the Frierdiker Rebbe sends Levin a kesiva v'chasima tova blessing.
Story: On Erev Rosh Hashanah 5709 the Frierdiker Rebbe sent Levin a personally signed blessing. The letter wished him and his family a kesiva v'chasima tova and a sweet new year in both material and spiritual realms.
Tags: paris, frierdiker-rebbe, rosh-hashanah, correspondence

Title: Thirty copies of Hachaltzu printed overnight for 50th anniversary
Summary: On the night of Hoshana Rabbah 5709 (24 October 1948), the memoirist and R' Tzvi Gansburg worked through the night to print 30 copies of Hachaltzu 5659 for its 50th anniversary on Simchas Torah.
Story: On Chol HaMoed Sukkos close to Hoshana Rabbah, the Rebbe told the memoirist that the Frierdiker Rebbe wished a small printing of Hachaltzu to mark its 50th anniversary on Simchas Torah. With time short, the memoirist and Bochur Tzvi Gansburg worked through Hoshana Rabbah night — in place of Tikkun — typesetting and producing thirty stapled copies, which were handed to the Rebbe the next morning.
Tags: hachaltzu, rashab, hoshana rabbah, simchat torah, jubilee, kuntres

Title: Rebbe's bris mazal-tov letter for Shalom DovBer Levin
Summary: On 25 Tishrei 5709 the Rebbe writes congratulating Levin on the bris of his son Shalom DovBer.
Story: Following the bris of his newborn son, Levin received a letter dated 25 Tishrei 5709. In it the Frierdiker Rebbe wished him mazal tov on entering his son into the covenant of Avraham Avinu and blessed him to raise the child to Torah, chuppah and good deeds amid expansiveness in body and spirit.
Tags: paris, frierdiker-rebbe, correspondence, bris, shalom-dovber-levin

Title: Rebbe inquires about ohel restoration in Lubavitch
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz wrote from 770 inquiring about the state of the ohel in Lubavitch.
Story: On 5 Marcheshvan 5709 (November 7, 1948), while living in 770 in New York, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Yonah Eidelkop inquiring about the ohel in Lubavitch. He asked about arrangements for repairs and indicated that he would cover all related expenses. He requested information on what repairs were needed.
Tags: lubavitch, ohel, restoration, 770

Title: Rebbe writes Rodshtein questioning Gurewicz's rush to America
Summary: On 7 Marcheshvan 5709 the Rebbe wrote Rabbi Moshe Leib Rodshtein questioning why Tzemach Gurewicz was rushing to leave Cuba for the US.
Story: Rodshtein had been working to secure visas for his nephew's family. The Rebbe responded, 'I do not understand why he is rushing to come here. So much can be done there in the sphere of spreading Torah and boosting Jewish education,' redirecting Gurewicz to communal labor in Havana.
Tags: tzemach gurewicz, moshe leib rodshtein, cuba, outreach

Title: Wedding of Chava, daughter of Rabbi Y. Jacobson
Summary: The wedding of Chava (daughter of Rabbi Y. Jacobson) took place on 5 Kislev 5709 with a classic chassidic celebration.
Story: On 5 Kislev 5709, the daughter of Rabbi Yaakov Yehuda Jacobson was married. The Rebbe Rayatz's daughter Chana attended and described it as a genuine first-class chassidic simcha, with men and women dancing in two separate halls and the Tomchei Tmimim students enlivening the celebration with love and friendship.
Tags: jacobson, 770, simcha, tmimim

Title: Levin opens cheder for Anash children in Bezancourt
Summary: On 18 Kislev 5709 Levin reports to the Rebbe that he has begun teaching the young children of Anash in Bezancourt.
Story: On 18 Kislev 5709 Levin wrote to the Rebbe that he had now established himself fully as a melamed. In addition to his outreach work with Parisian families, he was teaching the small children of Anash families living in Bezancourt — laying the seeds of an Anash cheder for the postwar French community.
Tags: paris, besancon, anash, melamdut, cheder

Title: Rebbe approves Gurewicz move from Cuba to New York
Summary: On 19 Kislev 5709 the Rebbe told Rodshtein it was finally time for Tzemach to come to America, having praised his educational work in Cuba.
Story: After Gurewicz set up educational programs in Cuba as the Rebbe had directed, the Rebbe relayed approval for him to move on. He would not arrive in New York until June 1950, after the sixth Rebbe's passing.
Tags: tzemach gurewicz, moshe leib rodshtein, cuba, new york

Title: Chabad refugees settle in Lod and in newly named Kfar Chabad
Summary: In 5709 two groups of Chabad refugees from Russia settle in the Land of Israel — one near Lod's train station, the other in the renamed Kfar Chabad.
Story: Mainly in the year 5709 (1949), Chabad refugees arriving in the Land of Israel settled in two groups. One took over abandoned houses near the Lod train station; the other moved into the abandoned village of Safriya, renamed Kfar Chabad. Agudat Chabad of the Holy Land also received a dedicated building in the Lod compound to house a new Chabad yeshiva.
Tags: lod, kfar chabad, refugees, anash, agudat chabad

Title: First Lubavitch families settle in Australia
Summary: In 5709, the first Lubavitcher families from the Soviet Union exodus settled in Australia and were instructed to open educational institutions immediately.
Story: In 5709 (1949), several Lubavitcher families from among those who had escaped the Soviet Union in 5706–5707 settled in Australia. The Rebbe instructed them to immediately establish educational institutions, and over time he dispatched additional shluchim from New York to strengthen the work.
Tags: australia, melbourne, refugees, anash-emigration

Title: Golda Meir attends Rosh HaShanah at Moscow's Choral Synagogue
Summary: Israel's first ambassador to Russia was greeted by thousands of Jews on the second day of Rosh HaShanah outside the Moscow synagogue.
Story: Meir had been disappointed by the small attendance on the first day, but the second day's enormous crowd — which she later told Italian reporter Oriana Fallaci had been orchestrated by Chabad — moved her deeply. She said it was 'the one time in my life that I considered becoming religious,' and recounted the moment to soldiers during the 1973 Yom Kippur War.
Tags: meir, israel, moscow, choral synagogue, rosh hashanah, diplomacy

Title: Golda Meir witnesses Chabad-organized Rosh Hashanah crowds in Moscow
Summary: Israel's first ambassador to Russia, Golda Meir, was greeted at Moscow's Choral Synagogue by thousands of Jews on the second day of Rosh Hashanah, an event she later credited to Chabad.
Story: In 1949, newly appointed Ambassador Golda Meir attended High Holiday services at Moscow's Choral Synagogue. On the first day of Rosh HaShanah she found only a small group of elderly Jews, but on the second day thousands filled the streets to welcome her. Decades later she told Italian reporter Oriana Fallaci that 'it was Chabad that orchestrated the welcome of thousands.'
Tags: russia, moscow, israel, choral synagogue, golda meir, rosh hashanah

Title: Illustrated Haggadah with hand-written text printed in New York
Summary: An illustrated Haggadah with text hand-written by the artist was published in New York.
Story: Around 5709 (1949), a 58-page Haggadah was printed in New York featuring colorful illustrations and the text itself hand-lettered by the artist. The quarto edition exemplified the mid-20th-century trend of artist-designed liturgical works. It served the American Jewish community of the post-war period.
Tags: haggadah, new york, united states, illustrated

Title: Kfar Chabad founded with 70 families
Summary: Kfar Chabad was founded in 5709 by 70 families of Lubavitch refugees from the Soviet Union, settling in abandoned Arab houses.
Story: In 5709 (1949), the majority of the Lubavitch refugees arriving in the Land of Israel settled in the newly established village of Kfar Chabad. Beginning with 70 families occupying abandoned Arab homes, the village grew over time to become the central hub of Chabad activity in Israel.
Tags: kfar-chabad, eretz-yisrael, refugees, settlement

Title: Levin family arrives in Eretz Yisrael
Summary: After three years of wandering since leaving the Soviet Union, the Levins reached Eretz Yisrael in early summer 5709 and settled in Kfar Chabad.
Story: Their post-Soviet journey had taken them through Lodz, the Föhrenwald-area DP camps including Pocking, and Paris. Settlement in the newly established Chabad village proved difficult; the family lived in hardship until the new permanent homes were built in 1957.
Tags: kfar chabad, eretz yisrael, aliyah, immigration

Title: Major Aliyah of Lubavitch refugees to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: In 5709, the bulk of Lubavitcher refugees who had escaped the Soviet Union finally reached the Land of Israel.
Story: In 5709 (1949), a major portion of the chassidim who had fled the Soviet Union in 5706–5707 finally arrived in the Land of Israel after extensive wanderings in Europe. The yeshiva students from Tel Aviv moved to Lod, where several Anash families had settled, and reopened the yeshiva.
Tags: eretz-yisrael, aliyah, lod, kfar-chabad, tel-aviv, refugees

Title: Rayatz inquires from 770 about Lubavitch and the Ohel
Summary: In 5709, while living at 770 in New York, the Rayatz inquired into the state of Lubavitch and the feasibility of repairing the Ohel.
Story: In 5709 (1949), in his final years from his residence at 770 Eastern Parkway in New York, the Rayatz sought information on the condition of the town of Lubavitch and the Ohel of his predecessors and explored whether any repair work could be undertaken. The political conditions of the time made it impossible for Jews to travel to Lubavitch for such purposes.
Tags: rayatz, lubavitch, ohel, 770, new york

Title: Rebbe sends first students to Brandeis University
Summary: In 1949 the Rebbe dispatched two students, Shlomo Carlebach and Zalman Schachter, to Brandeis University in Chabad's first formal college campus outreach.
Story: Telling them 'the time has come for us to reach out to college students,' the Rebbe inaugurated what would become a defining feature of Chabad activity. The seventh Rebbe would later expand this into a global Chabad House network beginning at UCLA in 1969; Carlebach and Schachter each eventually broke away from Chabad.
Tags: brandeis, campus outreach, shlomo carlebach, zalman schachter, college

Title: Rebbe writes about R. Shmuel Abba Sneg
Summary: In 5709 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Chief Rabbi Herzog of Eretz Yisrael describing R. Shmuel Abba Sneg, a former Lithuanian army chaplain then serving in postwar Germany.
Story: In 5709 (1948/49), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote about R. Shmuel Abba Sneg to Israel's Chief Rabbi Herzog (Igros Kodesh vol. 10, letter 3499). The Rebbe noted Sneg's earlier role as chaplain in the Lithuanian army and his postwar role as av beis din for the Orthodox kehillos in the American zone of Germany, in connection with an offer he had received to serve as rabbi of Jaffa.
Tags: sneg, kovno, germany, herzog, jaffa

Title: Aaron Dingol of The Day reports on Chabad refugee work in Paris
Summary: Mr. Dingol, editor of The Day newspaper, reported to Rebbe Rayatz on his tour of European refugee centers, noting Chabad's prominent role.
Story: On 9 Tevet 5709, Mr. Aaron Dingol, editor of the Yiddish daily Der Tog, visited Rebbe Rayatz and reported on his tour of post-war refugee camps. He described how most rabbis, shochtim and teachers there were affiliated with Lubavitch, and detailed the orderly Chabad institutions in Paris including Bais Rivka and Bais Sara schools serving Lubavitch refugees.
Tags: paris, refugees, displaced persons, morgen journal, the day, bais rivka, bais sara, dingol

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes to Shemtov about memoir collection
Summary: On 18 Tevet 5709 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Reb Bentzion Shemtov about coordinating the collection of memoirs from Anash and the temimim in Eretz Yisrael.
Story: The letter, published as Iggros Kodesh vol. 10, no. 3365, directed Shemtov to correspond with Anash and Tomchei Tmimim alumni in Eretz Yisrael and elsewhere, gather their memoirs, and forward everything to the Rebbe. The Rebbe assigned a specific editor to organize the incoming material. This launched the project that produced multiple memoir volumes.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, bentzion shemtov, correspondence, memoirs, iggros kodesh

Title: Rebbe Rayatz writes about Lubavitch ohel state
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Moshe Yitzchak Zuskewitz asking about the state of the ohelim in Lubavitch.
Story: On 4 Shevat 5709 (February 3, 1949), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Moshe Yitzchak Zuskewitz requesting detailed information about the ohelim of the Tzemach Tzedek and the Rebbe Maharash in Lubavitch. He asked whether they needed repairs, how much such repairs would cost, and through whom such work could be arranged. He requested that this be handled discreetly without mentioning his name.
Tags: lubavitch, ohel, restoration, graves

Title: Klausenberger Rebbe asks Rayatz how to relate to Israel's declaration
Summary: The Klausenberger Rebbe inquired in the name of Agudas HaAdmorim how to respond to the proclamation of the State of Israel.
Story: On 17 Shevat 5709, the Klausenberger Rebbe approached Rebbe Rayatz on behalf of Agudas HaAdmorim with the question of how the Rebbes should relate to the recent declaration of the State of Israel. Rayatz replied that the matter was very serious and would have to be resolved by the senior Rebbes, and that he would give his opinion only after receiving their written, signed question.
Tags: klausenberg, agudas haadmorim, state of israel, zionism, rebbes

Title: Mr. Palmer reports on visit to Paris and Eretz Yisrael refugee camps
Summary: Mr. Palmer delivered a detailed multi-hour report on his fact-finding mission to Chabad communities and refugee camps.
Story: On 17–18 Shevat 5709, Mr. Palmer (R.Ch.S.) presented Rebbe Rayatz with a lengthy report (six to nine hours over two days) on his visit to Chabad communities in Paris and refugee camps in Eretz Yisrael. He expressed amazement at the state of hiskashrus among anash, and Mr. Broida marveled at the closeness shown to children and at the diligent learning of the Tomchei Tmimim students.
Tags: paris, eretz yisrael, refugees, palmer, broida, tmimim

Title: Rayatz instructs R' Yisrael Yehuda Levin to travel to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: On 19 Shevat 5709 the Rayatz wrote to Yisrael Yehuda Levin advising him to travel to Eretz Yisrael and to consult the Vaad HaMesader of Anash in Tel Aviv.
Story: Levin had written asking the Rebbe Rayatz where to go after leaving Europe. The Rebbe's secretariat replied on 19 Shevat 5709 directing him to Eretz Yisrael, where he should contact Rabbi R. S. D. Zislin and R. M. Gurary of the Vaad HaMesader of Anash and Tmimim in Tel Aviv. The letter set the direction for Levin's emigration after the war.
Tags: rayatz, letter, yisrael yehuda levin, aliyah, eretz yisrael, vaad hamesader, zislin, gurary

Title: Eight Tmimim approved to train as shochtim under R. Gordon
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz approved a list of eight Tmimim to study shechita knife-setting under shochet Rabbi Gordon.
Story: On 23 Shevat 5709, Rebbe Rayatz recorded the names of eight Tomchei Tmimim students approved to study the craft of setting the shechita knife under shochet Rabbi Gordon at a cost of $25 per student, meeting daily at 4pm. The Rebbe arranged loans through his sons-in-law for the purchase of knives and sharpening stones, blessing the students that they should become skilled and disseminate proper chinuch in their future posts.
Tags: shechita, tmimim, gordon, tt

Title: Rabbi Raichik dispatched as shliach to central locations
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz gave Rabbi Raichik and his wife a blessing for their shlichus, with arrangements made by Rabbi M.M. Schneerson.
Story: On 23 Shevat 5709, Rebbe Rayatz blessed Rabbi Raichik and his wife for their journey on shlichus. The terms of his work were arranged by the Rebbe's son-in-law Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson (the future Rebbe), who organized his deployment to central locations.
Tags: shlichus, raichik, ramash

Title: Rebbe Rayatz follow-up letter on memoir project
Summary: On 24 Shevat 5709 the Rebbe Rayatz thanked Reb Bentzion Shemtov for taking up the task of organizing alumni of the underground yeshiva to record their experiences.
Story: Published as Iggros Kodesh vol. 10, no. 3398, the letter expressed deep satisfaction with Shemtov's decision to enlist the temimim and Anash in writing memoirs of their clandestine Torah work in their homeland. The Rebbe blessed the participants with material and spiritual success.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, bentzion shemtov, correspondence, memoirs, iggros kodesh

Title: Rayatz sends blessing letter to Shanghai refugees bound for Israel
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Adar, Rebbe Rayatz sent a blessing letter to Chabad refugees traveling from Shanghai to Eretz Yisrael via the US.
Story: On Rosh Chodesh Adar 5709, Rebbe Rayatz dispatched a letter of blessing to Chabad refugees traveling from Shanghai to Eretz Yisrael via America. The letter was drafted on the suggestion of his son-in-law Rabbi M.M. Schneerson and delivered through Rabbi Ashkenazi and Rabbi Chadakov. Rabbi Chadakov later reported that the emissaries and letter generated great emotional impact and brought hearts closer.
Tags: shanghai, eretz yisrael, refugees, ashkenazi, chadakov, ramash

Title: Rebbe Rayatz becomes a citizen of the United States
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz was sworn in as a US citizen at his home in Brooklyn before Judges Reifel and Kleinfeld.
Story: On Thursday 16 Adar 5709 (parashas Ki Sisa), Rebbe Rayatz became a citizen of the United States. The ceremony took place at his home with Judges Reifel and Kleinfeld officiating, witnessed by Rabbi Kazarnovsky, attorney Yekusiel Kramer, and Rabbi Chadakov; the proceedings were organized by his son-in-law the future Rebbe. The Rebbe expressed hope that the citizenship would bring health and success to him, his family, and his work in spreading Chassidus and strengthening Judaism.
Tags: citizenship, united states, 770, brooklyn, ramash, chadakov, kazarnovsky

Title: Rebbe Rayatz receives US citizenship wearing shtreimel
