Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz received US citizenship, an occasion on which he wore his grandfather's shtreimel.
Story: The Rebbe had begun wearing the shtreimel publicly at his daughter Chaya Mushka's 1928 wedding, after a fourteen-year hiatus since the Rashab fled Lubavitch. He continued wearing it on Shabbat, holidays, and other special occasions, including this citizenship ceremony.
Tags: citizenship, usa, shtreimel, new-york

Title: Frierdiker Rebbe advises on Lod yeshiva and refugee student placement
Summary: On 19 Adar 5709 the Frierdiker Rebbe writes R' Zushe Vilimovsky directing that newly arrived students go to the Tel Aviv yeshiva for now.
Story: On 19 Adar 5709 (March 20, 1949), the Frierdiker Rebbe replied to R' Zushe Vilimovsky, the manager designated for the Lod yeshiva, that arriving Anash students should be placed in Tomchei Tmimim in Tel Aviv. He suggested that the Lod building be reserved so it could later serve as the site of the new Tomchei Tmimim branch when conditions were right.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, lod, vilimovsky, tomchei tmimim, tel aviv

Title: Narrator reads Torah for Rebbe Rayatz on Shabbat HaChodesh 5709 at 770
Summary: On Shabbat Mevorchim Nisan 5709 (Parshat HaChodesh), the narrator was unexpectedly called to read the Torah upstairs at 770 in the presence of the Rebbe Rayatz, who took the maftir aliyah from his wheelchair.
Story: R. Yitzchak Dzikobson brought the narrator to 770 hoping merely to observe the Rebbe's maftir aliyah on this last Shabbat before Beis Nisan, the Rashab's yahrtzeit. Because the regular ba'al korei R. Yochanan Gordon was occupied downstairs at the aufruf of his future son-in-law Shimon Goldman, Dzikobson sent the narrator upstairs to lein for the Rebbe. The Rebbe Rayatz, seated in his wheelchair, signaled with his head the moment the reader accidentally voiced a stray 'beit' from 'bnei Yisrael' that does not appear in the verse — a final demonstration of his exacting attention to leining. This was the Rebbe's last Beis Nisan in this world.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, 770, shabbat hachodesh, parshat hachodesh, yochanan gordon, yitzchak dubov dzikobson, leining, wheelchair

Title: Author becomes shamash at Yeshivat R. Meir Simcha HaKohen shul in Brooklyn
Summary: In Nissan 5709 the author began serving as shamash at the Yeshivat R. Meir Simcha HaKohen shul in East Flatbush alongside Rabbi J.J. Hecht.
Story: In Nissan 5709 (April 1949), the author began a four-year tenure as shamash at the Yeshivat R. Meir Simcha HaKohen shul in East Flatbush. He worked alongside Rabbi J.J. Hecht, the shul's rav, in friendship and harmony. The shul's contract had to be renewed annually around Pesach.
Tags: brooklyn, shamash, east flatbush, rabbi jj hecht

Title: Rebbe Rayatz provides $500 'shlissel-geld' through Ramash for narrator's apartment, Nisan 5709
Summary: In Nisan 5709 the Rebbe Rayatz, through his son-in-law the Ramash, advanced the narrator $500 in 'shlissel-geld' to secure a scarce apartment near his East Flatbush shul.
Story: Apartments in East Flatbush were so scarce that an under-the-table $500 key-fee was required. When the narrator asked the Ramash to consult the Rebbe Rayatz, the Rebbe answered that he must take the apartment but asked where such a sum would come from. The Ramash replied that he himself would supply the money, and the next day at 770 he counted out $500 for the narrator. The narrator repaid the full sum once his financial situation improved.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, ramash, 770, east flatbush, apartment, shlissel geld, post-war new york

Title: Asterisk footnote convention introduced in Kuntres 2 Nissan 5709
Summary: Just before printing the Kuntres of 2 Nissan 5709 (1 April 1949), the Frierdiker Rebbe required asterisks be added in the body of the ma'amar to mark Ramash's footnotes — a convention used in all subsequent kuntreisim.
Story: After the lead pages of the 2 Nissan 5709 kuntres had already gone to the Manhattan press, R' Chadakov telephoned: the Frierdiker Rebbe had asked why no marker in the body of the ma'amar indicated the Ramash's marginal notes. The memoirist set new lines with asterisks, rushed them to the press at dawn, and replaced the old slugs. From that kuntres onward, asterisks marked the Ramash's marginal notes throughout the chassidus kuntreisim.
Tags: frierdiker rebbe, footnotes, ramash, typography, kuntres

Title: Rayatz writes Henry Morgenthau requesting aid for Chabad aliyah colonies
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Henry Morgenthau seeking £100,000 to settle 100 Chabad refugee families in Eretz Yisrael.
Story: On 6 Nissan 5709, Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Mr. Henry Morgenthau requesting that £100,000 (Eretz Yisrael pounds) be allocated to establish colonies for 100 Chabad refugee families, with £2,000 needed per family. Half would come from local Israeli institutions on the guarantee of Zalman Shazar (Rubashov), and half from Agudas Chassidei Chabad. The letter was composed in Hebrew by the future Rebbe and translated to English by Mr. Mindel.
Tags: morgenthau, eretz yisrael, aliyah, kfar chabad, shazar, fundraising

Title: Rayatz blesses Levin's aliyah plans for Nissan 5709
Summary: On 11 Nissan 5709 the Rayatz wrote Levin to proceed with his journey to Eretz Yisrael with his family and to settle in agriculture or poultry-raising.
Story: As a large group of Chassidim prepared to sail from Europe, Levin informed the Rebbe of his plans. The Rayatz responded on 11 Nissan 5709 with blessings for safe travel and a successful settlement, suggesting agricultural work or chicken farming as a livelihood.
Tags: rayatz, letter, yisrael yehuda levin, aliyah, agriculture, parnasah

Title: Daughter Feigel born to narrator on last day of Pesach 5709
Summary: On the last day of Pesach 5709 — 22 Nisan — a daughter was born to the narrator and named Feigel after his wife's mother, who had perished in the Shoah.
Story: The narrator had begun serving as shamash at his East Flatbush shul at the start of Pesach and walked home on the final yom tov evening to discover the news. Feigel was the first child they named after his murdered mother-in-law, once they had confirmed she did not survive. Their son Gershon was similarly named after the wife's brother Gershon, hy'd.
Tags: family, birth, holocaust memorial naming, east flatbush

Title: Farbrengen near Marseille on the eve of departure
Summary: On Motzaei Shabbat Parshat Emor 5709, R' Peretz Mochkin came to the group of Chassidim waiting by the sea near Marseille and held a farbrengen.
Story: Levin and a group of Chassidim, including R' Shlomo Chaim, gathered by the sea near Marseille to board a ship to Eretz Yisrael. On Motzaei Shabbat Parshat Emor R' Peretz Mochkin joined them and led a farbrengen the night before they sailed.
Tags: france, marseille, peretz mochkin, shlomo chaim, aliyah, farbrengen

Title: Levin's group sails from Marseille to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: On Sunday of Parshat Behar 5709, Levin and his family set sail from near Marseille to Eretz Yisrael.
Story: After the Motzaei Shabbat farbrengen, the group boarded their ship on Sunday of Parshat Behar 5709 and began the voyage to Eretz Yisrael, marking the start of a new chapter for the post-war emigrants.
Tags: france, marseille, aliyah, ship, eretz yisrael

Title: Yisrael Azriel Feldman arrives in the United States
Summary: On Erev Shabbat 21 Iyar 5709, Yisrael Azriel Feldman arrived in the United States from the Steyer DP camp in Austria.
Story: Feldman wrote to the Rebbe describing his background as a native of Różan, Poland and son of a shochet from the chassidim of Uman, his studies in Tomchei Temimim Warsaw in 5694-95, and his sojourn in Russia before reaching the Steyer camp. After his arrival in America he was accepted as rabbi of Beth Knesses Agudath Achim in Milwaukee.
Tags: yisrael azriel feldman, immigration, milwaukee, agudath achim, steyer, austria

Title: Rebbe writes Gurewicz before voyage to Australia
Summary: On 23 Iyar 5709 the Rebbe wrote Nachum Zalman Gurewicz urging him to influence fellow passengers en route to Australia.
Story: Before Gurewicz's departure from Europe, the Rebbe wished him mazel tov on his son's bar mitzvah, to be celebrated aboard ship docked at Port Said. The Rebbe instructed him to use the long voyage to influence others, particularly the young, to study Torah.
Tags: nachum zalman gurewicz, australia, melbourne, outreach, bar mitzvah

Title: Rebbe rebukes Wilshanski to pursue outreach to Australian youth
Summary: On 26 Iyar 5709 the Rebbe urged Reb Betzalel Wilshanski, age 52, to reach out to Australian youth even those uninterested in study.
Story: Known for his scholarship from his Lubavitch yeshivah years, Wilshanski was learning to adapt as a public activist. The Rebbe exhorted him: 'Even those who apparently don't want to study, you should draw them closer by giving them reading material in their language. Don't get disillusioned in your efforts.'
Tags: betzalel wilshanski, australia, outreach, youth

Title: Morgen Zhurnal article on R. Gorodetzky's Paris refugee work
Summary: The Morgen Zhurnal newspaper published an article on Rabbi Benjamin Gorodetzky's refugee work outside Paris.
Story: On 27 Sivan 5709, the Morgen Zhurnal carried an article about the work of Rabbi Benjamin Gorodetzky in Paris arranging temporary housing for refugees in special homes around Paris and organizing their emigration to Eretz Yisrael and other countries. His operation included partnership with the Joint Distribution Committee for refugee resettlement.
Tags: gorodetzky, paris, refugees, morgen zhurnal, joint, aliyah

Title: Rashag returns to New York from Eretz Yisrael via Paris
Summary: Rebbe Rayatz's son-in-law Rashag flew in from Paris after visiting Eretz Yisrael, praising the spiritual state of anash.
Story: On 7 Tammuz 5709 at 5pm, Rebbe Rayatz's son-in-law Rabbi Shmaryahu Gurary (Rashag) arrived by airplane from Paris on his return from Eretz Yisrael. He extolled the spiritual state of anash in general and the refugees in particular, expressing astonishment at their devotion to Chassidus and to avodas hatefillah.
Tags: rashag, shmaryahu gurary, eretz yisrael, paris, refugees

Title: Rebbe encourages Meir Chaikin to stay in Stockholm
Summary: On 13 Tamuz 5709 the Rebbe rejected Rabbi Meir Chaikin's idea of leaving disappointing Stockholm, framing his post as an honor of divine providence.
Story: Disillusioned with Stockholm's lackluster religious community, Chaikin sought to relocate. The Rebbe wrote, 'You should consider your arrival in Stockholm a great honor that divine providence has chosen you to illuminate with the light of Torah in an unplanted field.'
Tags: meir chaikin, stockholm, sweden, shlichus

Title: Yud-Beis Tammuz farbrengen marking entry into Rayatz's 70th year
Summary: A Yud-Beis Tammuz Chag HaGeulah farbrengen took place marking the start of Rebbe Rayatz's 70th year.
Story: On 14 Tammuz 5709 at 6pm, a farbrengen was held in honor of the Chag HaGeulah and Rebbe Rayatz's entry into his 70th year. The Rebbe delivered an extended sicha — over an hour long — on avodah, the ways of Chassidus, and avodas hatefillah, and recorded that he would later arrange it in writing.
Tags: yud beis tammuz, geulah, farbrengen, chassidus, avodah

Title: Rayatz welcomes Levin's arrival in Eretz Yisrael
Summary: On 27 Menachem Av 5709 the Rayatz responded to Levin's report of safe arrival in Eretz Yisrael and his settlement in Kfar Sefaria.
Story: Levin wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz on 16 Av 5709 reporting that he had reached Eretz Yisrael and settled in Kfar Sefaria, where he worked irrigating orchards. The Rebbe's reply, dated 27 Menachem Av, blessed the family with material and spiritual sustenance. The signature notably emphasized the letter yud, a usage Rayatz adopted from Shevat 5709 onward.
Tags: rayatz, letter, kfar sefaria, eretz yisrael, yud emphasized

Title: Rebbe presses Gurewicz to lead change in Melbourne
Summary: On 17 Elul 5709 the Rebbe responded to Gurewicz's lament about Melbourne's anemic Jewish life by declaring this was the very reason providence had brought him there.
Story: Gurewicz had reported discouragingly on the state of Melbourne Jewry. The Rebbe wrote back emphatically: 'The time has come that he, along with his fellow Chasidim, should work with zealousness and joy to improve the situation. This is a mission that the divine providence has brought you there to fulfill.'
Tags: nachum zalman gurewicz, melbourne, australia, outreach

Title: Rayatz sends New Year blessing letter for 5710
Summary: On Erev Rosh Hashana 5710 the Rayatz wrote Levin a New Year blessing letter for a good and sweet year.
Story: Approaching Rosh Hashana 5710, Levin received a personal greeting from the Rebbe Rayatz blessing him and his family within the broader community of Israel and Anash. The letter again featured the emphasized yud in the signature that had become Rayatz's custom.
Tags: rayatz, letter, rosh hashana, ktiva vechatima tova

Title: Yom Kippur Mincha 5710: narrator leins for Ramash while Rebbe Rayatz takes maftir Yonah
Summary: At Mincha of Yom Kippur 5710 the narrator, having come to 770 from his East Flatbush post, leined the Torah for the Ramash in the upstairs minyan as the Rebbe Rayatz, seated in the adjacent room, took maftir Yonah.
Story: On yom tov a second minyan was held upstairs in 'the Alte Rebbetzin's room,' where the chazan stood and the leining took place, with the door to the Rebbe Rayatz's office open so he could hear the davening. Arriving from his East Flatbush shamash duties for Mincha, the narrator was asked by the Ramash to lein; a Torah scroll was placed on a small table in the corridor near the dining room. The Ramash himself received maftir Yonah at this minyan.

Title: Six Tel Aviv yeshiva students granted permission to study in New York

Title: 19 Kislev 5710 farbrengen with Rebbe Rayatz upstairs at 770

Title: Rabbi Zevin urges Ramash to become Rebbe

Title: Shulsinger Brothers Haggadah with English translation by Abraham Regelson

Title: Sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn passes away
Summary: The sixth Rebbe passes away in Brooklyn after a decade leading Chabad from 770 Eastern Parkway.

Summary: On 7 Shevat 5710 the Rebbe wrote Rabbi Yosef Wineberg summarizing his goal: a Tomchei Temimim student in every community and country.

Summary: The Rayatz passed away on 10 Shevat 5710 and was interred in Montefiore Cemetery, New York.

Title: Passing of Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn (Rayatz)
Summary: The sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, passed away on 10 Shevat 5710 in New York.

Title: Rebbe Rayatz passes away on 10 Shevat 5710
Summary: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the Rebbe Rayatz, passed away on 10 Shevat 5710.
Story: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, passed away on 10 Shevat 5710 (January 28, 1950). Title: Levin learns of Rayatz's passing en route to Bnei Brak
Summary: On Sunday 11 Shevat 5710 Levin saw a newspaper report at the Tel Aviv central bus station announcing the histalkus of the Rebbe Rayatz.

Title: R. Yerachmiel Binyaminson leads minyan to Rebbe Rayatz's tziyun on 15 Elul 5710 to plead for Ramash to accept nesius

Yisrael Shimon Kalmenson and laid a written pidyon at the kever asking Heaven to move the Ramash to accept the nesius. Title: Levin recovers from illness in Sarafand

Summary: In summer 5711 the Rebbe founded Tzeirei Agudas Chabad in Eretz Yisrael to spread Judaism among youth.

Summary: After Pesach 5711 the main division of the Tel Aviv yeshiva moved to the Lod campus by the railway station.

Title: Memorial kuntres for Rebbe Rayatz published with dedication to Eliyahu Shusterman

Title: Chanukat habayit of the Lod yeshiva in the pardes

Title: Rebbe uses the third amud at 770 by Tishrei 5712

Title: Alter Rebbe portrait printed by Kehot
Summary: Kehot published a print of the Alter Rebbe's portrait in 5712.

Summary: When many sefarim arrive in Eretz Yisrael from Europe, R' Shlomo Yosef Zevin asks the Rebbe (Ramash) how to identify volumes from the Rebbe Rayatz's library.

Title: Rebbe edits Kollel Chabad calendar for 5713

Title: Sara Katzenelenbogen dies in Soviet prison

Title: Tel Aviv Haggadah illustrated by Y. Zimberknopf (Zim)
Summary: Y. Zimberknopf (Zim) illustrated and decorated a Haggadah printed in Tel Aviv.
Story: In 5712 (1952), an illustrated and decorated Haggadah by Y. Zimberknopf, known as Zim, was published in Tel Aviv. Title: Tzvi Gansburg marries in Montreal and leaves printing partnership

Title: Passing of Rabbi Avraham Eliyahu Axelrod in Baltimore
Summary: Rabbi Avraham Eliyahu Axelrod, prominent chassid and Tomchei Temimim alumnus, passed away in Baltimore on 4 Adar 5712.
Story: On 4 Adar 5712 the famed chassid Rabbi Avraham Eliyahu Axelrod passed away in Baltimore. Title: Israel Aryeh Leib Schneersohn passes away

Title: First yahrzeit kuntres dedication for Eliyahu Shusterman
Summary: The kuntres appearing for 18 Elul 5712, the first yahrzeit of Eliyahu Shusterman, again carried a dedication to his memory.
Story: On the first yahrzeit of his father, 18 Elul 5712 (September 8, 1952), the author again included a memorial dedication in the kuntres that appeared at that time. He also completed learning the entire Shisha Sidrei Mishnah during the year of mourning.

Title: Sukkot tension at shul exposes author's split focus

Story: On Sukkot 5713 (October 1952), at a kiddush in the shul sukkah in East Flatbush, the author told the balebatim that he had not come to the shul to 'make a living' but to accomplish something in Yiddishkeit. Tags: sukkot, east flatbush, shul, shamash, print shop

Title: Daughter Nechama Shusterman born
Summary: On 4 Kislev 5713 the author's daughter Nechama was born, named after his wife's brother Nechemia who perished in the Shoah.
Story: On 4 Kislev 5713 (November 22, 1952), the author and his wife had a daughter, Nechama. She was named for his wife's brother Nechemia, who was murdered in the Shoah.
Tags: birth, shusterman family, holocaust memorial

Title: First Lag BaOmer parade held on Eastern Parkway
Summary: The Seventh Rebbe inaugurated the first Lag BaOmer children's parade on Eastern Parkway, building on the precedent of the 1942 Passover parade in Crown Heights.
Story: The annual parades would become a hallmark of Chabad communities worldwide, expressing Jewish public pride in the streets. The format echoed the children's procession that Yitzchok Groner and Moshe Kazarnovsky had led past 770 a decade earlier.
Tags: lag baomer, parade, eastern parkway, seventh rebbe, crown heights

Title: Israel establishes Lishkat Hakesher to support Soviet Jewry
Summary: Israel's prime ministerial office set up Lishkat Hakesher, the secret liaison bureau directed at strengthening Jewish life in the USSR.
Story: Headed first by Shaul Avigur from 1953 to 1970, Lishkat Hakesher worked closely with Chabad's clandestine network in Russia. Its open activities ended after the Six-Day War when the Soviets cut ties with Israel, but it later became the global coordinator of the Soviet Jewry movement.
Tags: israel, lishkat hakesher, soviet jewry, avigur, mossad

Title: Kehot reissues the Tzemach Tzedek portrait
Summary: In 5713 Kehot reprinted the Tzemach Tzedek's portrait, deliberately flipping the plate so the coat overlap and the held book read right-to-left.
Story: In 5713 (1953), Kehot Publication Society reissued the Tzemach Tzedek's portrait. The plate was intentionally reversed so the right side of the coat would lie over the left (as Jewish custom dictates) and so that the book held in his hand would open from the right like a Hebrew text — corrections to the original gentile artist's depiction discussed in Chabad tradition.
Tags: kehot, tzemach tzedek, portrait, 770

Title: Merkos becomes one-third partner in Empire Press (Ezra) by directive of the Rebbe
Summary: By directive of the Rebbe, Merkos L'inyonei Chinuch was made a one-third profit-sharing partner of the narrator's Ezra print shop, registered with the authorities as a tax-exempt department of Merkos.
Story: The Rebbe pressed the narrator's partner R. Tzvi on why Merkos was not yet a partner in the press; when the partners and R. Chadakov disagreed about whether Merkos should join — Chadakov insisting Merkos should not be in partnership at all — the Rebbe overruled all of them, ruling that the partners would draw a worker's salary and that Merkos would receive one-third of the profits when there were any. The print shop opened a 'Ezra–Merkos L'inyonei Chinuch' bank account signed by Chadakov or Shusterman. The narrator did not insist on a formal contract — a decision he later regretted on the advice of the Merkos bookkeeper Mr. Telushkin, son of R. Nissan Telushkin.
Tags: merkos linyonei chinuch, ezra press, empire press, rebbe ramash, tzvi, chadakov, shusterman, telushkin, kehot publishing

Title: Tzemach Tzedek and Rayatz portraits printed by Kehot
Summary: Kehot issued portrait prints of the Tzemach Tzedek and the Rayatz in 5713.
Story: In 5713 (1953), Kehot Publication Society printed portraits of both the Tzemach Tzedek and the Rayatz writing chassidus. A colored version of the Rayatz print was also produced. The prints are displayed in the Lubavitch Library.
Tags: kehot, tzemach tzedek, rayatz, portrait

Title: Tzemach Tzedek portrait reprinted by Kehot
Summary: Kehot printed a mirrored version of the Tzemach Tzedek's portrait in 5713.
Story: In 1953 Kehot reissued the Tzemach Tzedek portrait, reversing the engraving plate so the right side of the garment lapped over the left and the book in his hands would open to the right.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, kehot, portrait, brooklyn

Title: R. Sh.D.B. joins author's printing house as partner
Summary: In Shevat 5713 R. Sh.D.B. became a partner in the author's printing house after about eighteen months of the author working alone.
Story: In Shevat 5713 (January 1953), after roughly eighteen months working without a partner, the author brought R. Sh.D.B. into the printing house. The author had invested $14,000; the new partner had promised $5,000 but produced only $1,500 in cash, which the author accepted because he wanted a working partner more than capital. The funds were transferred to R. Tzvi Gansburg for his share.
Tags: print shop, partnership, ezra, balshan

Title: Death of Joseph Stalin
Summary: Soviet dictator Joseph Stalin died five days after Purim.
Story: On March 5, 1953, Joseph Stalin died of a stroke, five days after Purim. At the Purim farbrengen that year, the seventh Rebbe had alluded to the death of the czar; when news of Stalin's collapse emerged, Chasidim saw a connection to those remarks.
Tags: stalin, soviet union, purim

Title: Author's contract as shamash not renewed
Summary: In Nissan 5713 the East Flatbush shul declined to renew the author's contract; Rabbi Avigdor Miller protested and the chevra mishnayos honored him with five hundred dollars and silver candlesticks.
Story: In Nissan 5713 (April 1953), the East Flatbush shul did not renew the author's contract as shamash, ending his four-year tenure. Rabbi Avigdor Miller, mashgiach of Yeshivat Rabbi Chaim Berlin, banged the table in protest, ceased davening there, and gathered neighborhood signatures protesting to the absent president in Florida. When the balabatim later invited the author back for lesser duties, the Rebbe responded 'avekgegangen iz avekgegangen' — once gone, gone. The chevra mishnayos he had led gave him their entire $500 treasury and presented silver candlesticks his wife still uses.
Tags: brooklyn, shamash, shul, avigdor miller, chevra mishnayos

Title: Rabbi Alexander Yudasin and Tel Aviv shul gabbaim petition the Rebbe
Summary: On erev Shabbat 9 Iyar 5713 Rabbi Alexander Yudasin and the gabbaim of several Tel Aviv synagogues signed a letter inviting the Rebbe to visit Israel.
Story: Rabbi Alexander Yudasin, former head of the Krivoy Rog beis din, joined with gabbaim of the Chabad shul, Beis Hamedrash Perushim in Neve Tzedek, the Shas chevra, Kahal Chassidim in Neve Shalom and other Tel Aviv synagogues in signing a petition to the Rebbe on 9 Iyar 5713. They pleaded for him to visit the Holy Land to illuminate the present era, invoking the Talmudic blessing 'blessed is your coming in peace.'
Tags: tel aviv, petition, synagogues, yudasin, visit request

Title: Anash of Jerusalem petition the Rebbe to visit Israel
Summary: In Iyar 5713 Chabad chassidim in Jerusalem signed a formal petition pleading with the Rebbe to visit the Holy Land.
Story: In Iyar 5713 the community of Anash in Jerusalem composed and signed a heartfelt petition imploring the Rebbe to make a visit to the Land of Israel. Citing the historic bond between Rebbe and chassid and noting that only a select few could afford to travel to Brooklyn, they begged him to come strengthen the community and its institutions in Jerusalem, Tel Aviv, Lod, Safed and elsewhere. Roughly three hundred signatures from across Israel and France were collected in total.
Tags: jerusalem, israel, petition, chabad community, visit request

Title: Simon Jacobson dies in Toronto
Summary: The Georgian-born underground rabbi died at age 53, broken by years of torture in the Soviet gulag.
Story: After immigrating to Toronto in 1952 with his family, Jacobson was appointed rabbi of the local Chabad congregation. His grandson Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Jacobson recalled, 'he was worn out from years of suffering.' He passed away in June 1953, followed by his wife two years later, leaving three orphaned sons.
Tags: jacobson, yakovshvili, toronto, georgia, canada

Title: Yakovshvili (Simon Jacobson) dies in Toronto
Summary: Simon Yakovshvili, by then known as Jacobson, died in Toronto at age fifty-three from the effects of years of Soviet imprisonment.
Story: He had served as rabbi of the local Chabad congregation after immigrating to Toronto in 1952. His wife followed him in death two years later, leaving three orphaned sons aged six, twelve, and fourteen.
Tags: jacobson, toronto, gulag-aftermath

Title: Anash of France petition the Rebbe to visit
Summary: Chabad chassidim in France submitted a petition asking the Rebbe to visit, received by the Rebbe on 12 Tammuz 5713.
Story: Anash in France, many of them refugees who had escaped the Iron Curtain, submitted a petition begging the Rebbe to travel abroad to visit them. They wrote that most chassidim of the past several decades knew the Rebbe only through hearsay and pleaded for a face-to-face encounter. The Rebbe noted in his own handwriting that the petition was received on 12 Tammuz 5713.
Tags: france, petition, tomchei temimim, iron curtain, visit request

Title: First Chabad girls' summer camp founded
Summary: The Rebbe founded the first Chabad girls' summer camp, Machaneh Emunah, in summer 5713.
Story: In summer 5713 (1953) the Rebbe founded a dedicated summer camp for girls, later named Machaneh Emunah. The Rebbe explained that the influence achievable in summer camp far exceeds that of the school year. The camp model rapidly spread to Chabad centers worldwide.
Tags: machaneh emunah, camp, girls, summer

Title: Rebbe responds to invitations to visit Israel and France
Summary: On 13 Elul 5713 the Rebbe wrote a formal response to the invitations from Anash, citing concealments preventing the visit.
Story: Responding to the petitions of Anash in Israel and France, the Rebbe wrote on 13 Elul 5713 acknowledging their invitation to visit. He explained that material and spiritual concealments and obstacles prevented him from fulfilling the desired visit, and prayed that God would remove them so they could meet in abundance of joy. He enclosed the newly published Kuntres for Chai Elul and offered blessings for the new year. The response was published in Igrot Kodesh vol. 7.
Tags: letter, elul, visit declined, igrot kodesh, kuntres chai elul

Title: R. Yekutiel Zusman 'Zushya' Paz dies in Moscow
Summary: R. Yekutiel Zusman ben Moshe Leib 'Zushya' Paz, longtime shamash of the Marina-Roshcha shul in Moscow, died on 2 Cheshvan 5714 and was buried in Malachovka.
Story: R. Yekutiel Zusman Paz, the legendary shamash of the Marina-Roshcha shul in Moscow, died on 2 Cheshvan 5714 (October 11, 1953) and was buried in Malachovka. Every night after maariv he would pretend to evict homeless mispalelim so the Gentile watchman Simon would lock up and leave, then quietly readmit them through a side door. During the war he reached Samarkand, where he served as shamash on Khodzhum Street and ran an unpaid cheder.
Tags: moscow, marina-roshcha, samarkand, shamash, death, soviet union

Title: Passing of Rabbi Avraham Zev Sharfstein
Summary: Rabbi Avraham Zev Sharfstein, who had served on the Shomrei Shabbos gemach management since 5707, passed away on 21 Kislev 5714.
Story: Rabbi Avraham Zev Sharfstein, who had joined the management of the Shomrei Shabbos free-loan society in 5707 to fill R' Tzvi Hirsh Padnes's place, passed away on 21 Kislev 5714. After his death, R' Yochanan Gordon ran the gemach kupah by himself until his own final day on Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5729.
Tags: new york, avraham zev sharfstein, shomrei shabbos, obituary

Title: Seventh Rebbe's 25th wedding anniversary farbrengen
Summary: On Shabbat 14 Kislev, the seventh Rebbe held a farbrengen marking his twenty-fifth wedding anniversary, with uncharacteristically personal reflections.
Story: He noted that 'generally speaking, even regarding a private person, his wedding constitutes an all-encompassing event. For me, however, my wedding day brought me into more general and communal affairs.' He told those gathered that the wedding 'connected me to you, and you to me,' framing his marriage as a bond with the Chasidim.
Tags: wedding-anniversary, farbrengen, kislev, new-york, chasidim

Title: Mother Rachel Shusterman dies in Tashkent
Summary: On 4 Tevet 5714 Rachel bat Aharon Tzvi Shusterman died in Tashkent; news was withheld from the author in New York for a year and a half.
Story: On 4 Tevet 5714 (December 10, 1953), the author's mother Rachel bat Aharon Tzvi died in Tashkent. Because of the climate of fear in the Soviet Union, the family did not inform the author for a year and a half; he therefore sat no shiva and recited no kaddish. His brother Yosef said kaddish in Tashkent and arranged a minyan there with great mesirat nefesh.
Tags: tashkent, shusterman family, death, soviet union

Title: Daughter Zissel Shusterman born
Summary: On 14 Tevet 5714 the author's daughter Zissel was born, named for his father-in-law Zussman ben Gershon who was killed by the Nazis on 28 Adar 5702.
Story: On 14 Tevet 5714 (December 20, 1953), the author and his wife had a daughter, Zissel. She was named for the author's father-in-law, R. Zussman ben Gershon, who was murdered by the Nazis on 28 Adar 5702 (March 17, 1942).
Tags: birth, shusterman family, holocaust memorial

Title: Arba Minim campaign launched
Summary: The Rebbe founded the Arba Minim campaign in 5714 to bring the four species to Jews on Sukkos.
Story: In 5714 (1954) the Rebbe established the campaign of bringing the four species to fellow Jews on Sukkos. Letters in Igros Kodesh vol. 12 describe inviting passersby to make the blessing and visiting hospitals and convalescent homes, which the Rebbe noted was particularly successful in 5716.
Tags: sukkos, arba minim, mivtzaim, lulav

Title: Kehot edition of Tanya with full correction list
Summary: In 5714 (1954), Kehot published a new edition of Tanya into which the Lubavitcher Rebbe incorporated R' Asher Grossman's correction sheets.
Story: The Rebbe stated in his preface that the new edition included corrections that R' Asher had recorded on his personal copy of Tanya after the Vilna printing — material that had reached the Kazarnovsky family through R' Asher's son-in-law. The Rebbe noted that the Rayatz had endorsed using this correction sheet.
Tags: tanya, kehot, lubavitcher rebbe, asher grossman, corrections

Title: Rebbe launches Shmurah Matzah campaign on Shabbos Parshas HaChodesh
Summary: At a Shabbos Parshas HaChodesh 5714 farbrengen the Rebbe called for distributing shmurah matzah broadly.
Story: At the Shabbos Parshas HaChodesh farbrengen of 5714 (1954), the Rebbe declared a request — 'lu yeyasher cheili' even a mitzvah — that all who can influence others should ensure they receive shmurah matzah for Pesach. The campaign grew over the years into a worldwide distribution reaching hundreds of thousands of Jews.
Tags: matzah, pesach, mivtzaim

Title: Rebbe receives Slavita Sefer Torah
Summary: Late in 5714 the Rebbe received the Slavita Sefer Torah, written by the imprisoned Slavita brothers, and kept it close ever after.
Story: In late 5714 (1954) the Rebbe received the small Sefer Torah of the Slavita brothers — the holy printers arrested by the Tzarist government, who read from this scroll during their many years of imprisonment. From then on the Rebbe used it for his aliyos on Shabbos and Monday/Thursday, and held it during Hakafos. A wall-mounted Aron Kodesh was built to house it and later transferred to the Library.
Tags: slavita, sefer torah, tzarist russia, arrest

Title: Seventh Rebbe issues new Tanya edition with index and printing list
Summary: In 5714 (1954) the Rebbe sent a new edition of Tanya to press, adding a topical index, list of corrections, and printing history.
Story: From this 1954 edition forward, every printing of the Tanya included the Rebbe's added apparatus—index, errata, and a record of prior editions. Over the next two decades the Tanya would be reprinted more than thirty further times in this enhanced format.
Tags: rebbe, tanya, index, kehot

Title: Author begins regular Torah reading at 770
Summary: Around mid-5715 the author became the regular baal korei at 770 after Reb Yochanan Gordon told him to come up on his own.
Story: After a year of being called up each Shabbat by Reb Yochanan Gordon, the elderly gabbai told the author, 'How long must I call you each week? Go up on your own!' From mid-5715 (1955) onward the author served as the regular baal korei at 770.
Tags: 770, torah reading, baal korei, yochanan gordon, memoir

Title: R' Shmuel Schneiderman passes away in Philadelphia
Summary: R' Shmuel Schneiderman, who had arrived in America in the late 5680s and settled in Philadelphia, passed away there in 5715.
Story: R' Schneiderman was among the small group of Tmimim who reached the United States during 5686–5688. He made his home in Philadelphia and remained there for the rest of his life, until his passing in 5715. His arrival had been part of the early wave that gradually rebuilt a Lubavitcher Tmimim presence in America during the years following the First World War.
Tags: philadelphia, tmimim, schneiderman, petira

Title: Tzeirei Agudas Chabad founded in the United States
Summary: In 5715 the Rebbe founded Tzeirei Agudas Chabad in the United States.
Story: In 5715 (1955), the Rebbe founded Tzeirei Agudas Chabad in the United States. In a special letter (Igros Kodesh vol. 11 letter 3429), he laid out a detailed program of activity for spreading Judaism and chassidus among broad circles of Jewish youth.
Tags: united states, tzeirei agudas chabad, youth

Title: Rebbe's letter to Rabbi Mordechai Savitsky on the Rogatchover
Summary: The Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Mordechai Savitsky praising his frequent citations of the Rogatchover Gaon.
Story: On 17 Tevet 5715, the Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Mordechai Savitsky acknowledging receipt of his books Beit Mordechai vol. 2 and Mayim Adirim vol. 1. The Rebbe noted a special thread he saw in the books — Savitsky's frequent citation of the Rogatchover Gaon — and remarked on the wonder that scholars overlooked the wealth of insights in the Rogatchover's writings.
Tags: rogatchover, savitsky, letters

Title: R. Yerachmiel Binyaminson niftar on Rosh Chodesh Shevat 5715
Summary: R. Yerachmiel ben Avraham Yehuda Leib Binyaminson, the elder Lubavitcher rabbinic figure of Montreal, passed away on Rosh Chodesh Shevat 5715 and was buried close to the Rebbe Rayatz's tziyun.
Story: Binyaminson, a venerable Chabad rabbi who had previously brought a minyan to plead at the Rebbe Rayatz's kever for the Ramash to accept the nesius, came regularly from Montreal to New York and lodged with the narrator or with his sister. His passing on Rosh Chodesh Shevat 5715 was honored with burial adjacent to the Frierdiker Rebbe at the Old Montefiore section that would later become known as the Ohel.
Tags: yerachmiel binyaminson, montreal, burial near rebbe rayatz, ohel

Title: Shusterman family moves into Crown Heights home at 1717 President Street
Summary: On Erev Purim 5715 the Shusterman family moved into 1717 President Street in Crown Heights with the Rebbe's blessing to buy rather than rent.
Story: On Erev Purim 5715 (March 7, 1955), the author's family moved into their newly purchased Crown Heights home at 1717 President Street, beside the shul of Rabbi B.Z. Frankel with its mikveh. Earlier the author had asked the Rebbe about renting a Crown Heights apartment; the Rebbe replied that smaller people than him had managed to buy. The doubled 'tov' in the number 1717 was taken as a good sign.
Tags: crown heights, brooklyn, home, president street

Title: Author moves to Crown Heights and becomes regular at 770
Summary: The author moved to Crown Heights before Pesach 5715 and became a regular Shabbat worshipper at 770.
Story: Before Pesach 5715 (April 1955) the author relocated from East Flatbush to Crown Heights, becoming a fixed Shabbat mispallel at 770. The gabbai Reb Yochanan Gordon, who had been the regular baal korei for the Rebbe Rayatz, began calling him up each week to read from the Torah.
Tags: crown heights, 770, east flatbush, memoir, yochanan gordon

Title: Ezra & Balshan press buys 480 Sutter Avenue building
Summary: In 1956 the Ezra & Balshan printing house bought a building at 480 Sutter Avenue in Brownsville to accommodate its expansion.
Story: The Ezra & Balshan print shop had outgrown its original premises at 238 Belmont Avenue. In 1956 the partners purchased a building at 480 Sutter Avenue in the Brownsville section of Brooklyn, moved all the machinery there, and added new equipment.
Tags: ezra ubalshan, printing, brownsville, brooklyn, press

Title: Founding of Kfar Chabad vocational school
Summary: The Rebbe founded the Beis Sefer Lemelacha vocational school in Kfar Chabad in 5716, appointing Kazarnovsky as his emissary for the dedication.
Story: In 5716, the Rebbe founded the Beis Sefer Lemelacha (vocational school) in Kfar Chabad, Israel. He appointed R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky as his personal emissary for the dedication ceremony, and Kazarnovsky subsequently served as director of the fund supporting the institution.
Tags: kfar-chabad, israel, vocational-school, ramash, kazarnovsky

Title: Jerusalem Haggadah 'Aryeh D'Bei Ilai' of Shinava-Stropkov Chassidut
Summary: An 'Aryeh D'Bei Ilai' Haggadah pamphlet from the Shinava-Stropkov community, drawing on 'Divrei Yechezkel Shraga', was published in Jerusalem.
Story: In 5716 (1956), a pamphlet entitled 'Aryeh D'Bei Ilai' was published in Jerusalem by the Shinava-Stropkov Chassidic council, containing essential matters drawn from the 'Divrei Yechezkel Shraga' Haggadah commentary, along with responsa and letters from holy Geonim. The surviving copy contains only 32 pages of the original. It served the Shinava-Stropkov community after the Holocaust.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, shinava, stropkov, jerusalem, divrei yechezkel shraga

Title: Mariasha Putrefas writes Pleshchenitsy memoir
Summary: Mariasha Badana Putrefas, a native of Pleshchenitsy, wrote a memoir of the Kugel family and Chassidic life there in 5716.
Story: In 5716 (1956), Mariasha Badana Putrefas, a native of Pleshchenitsy, wrote a Yiddish memoir recounting the beginnings of Chassidut in the town. Her account—covering R' Shlomo Kugel of Kiskoriene, his sons Hendel, Yosef and Gershon, and the arrival of Chassidut in the mitnagdic town—was later translated into Hebrew by R' Y. Mondshine and published in Kfar Chabad issue 883.
Tags: pleshchenitsy, kugel family, memoir, yiddish

Title: R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal becomes rabbi of Anshei Lubavitch of Boro Park
Summary: From 5716, R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal served as rabbi of the Anshei Lubavitch synagogue in Boro Park, New York.
Story: Beginning in 5716, R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal served as rabbi of the Anshei Lubavitch of Boro Park synagogue. He also directed the Chevra Kadisha of Agudas Chabad, authoring the work 'Darchei Chesed' in that capacity.
Tags: new york, boro park, anshei lubavitch, rabbi yitzchak dov oshpal, chevra kadisha

Title: Rabbi Menachem Kasher receives Rogatchover microfilms
Summary: In 5716, Rabbi Menachem Kasher received the Rogatchover's manuscripts and began preparing them for publication.
Story: Rebbetzin Rachel Tzitran had photographed much of her father's writings on microfilm and sent them to family in America for safekeeping. In 5716 (1956), Rabbi Menachem Kasher received these manuscripts and began the work of editing them for the Tzofnat Paneach series on Talmud and Torah.
Tags: rogatchover, tzofnat paneach, kasher, manuscripts

Title: Second stender built for the Rebbe
Summary: A taller stender with a hinged top was built for the Rebbe around 5716.
Story: Around 1956 a more comfortable stender was constructed for the Rebbe with a hinged top that opened to hold his siddur during prayer. He used it from then on for daily prayer.
Tags: the rebbe, stender, 770, brooklyn

Title: First Chabad boys' summer camp Gan Yisroel founded
Summary: The Rebbe founded the first Chabad boys' summer camp, Gan Yisroel, in summer 5716.
Story: In summer 5716 (1956) the Rebbe founded the first boys' summer camp and named it Gan Yisroel. The Rebbe personally visited the camps from 5716 through 5720 (1956-1960), and at a Shavuos 5716 talk explained the unique educational influence camps exert on children.
Tags: gan yisroel, camp, boys, summer

Title: Government-sanctioned yeshivah opens at Moscow's Choral Synagogue
Summary: During a brief period of Soviet tolerance, a small state-approved yeshivah opened in Moscow's Choral Synagogue.
Story: The program was tiny and tightly constrained; by 1962 it had just six students. The Lubavitch underground network remained the primary engine sustaining Jewish learning under Communism.
Tags: moscow, choral-synagogue, yeshivah

Title: Kfar Chabad residents move into newly built homes
Summary: In 5717 the Levin family and other Kfar Chabad residents moved from abandoned Arab homes into newly built dwellings constructed for them in the village.
Story: For eight years after their arrival in 5709, the Levins lived in the abandoned Arab homes that had been allocated to settlers of Kfar Chabad. In 5717 new houses built specifically for the residents were finally ready, and the families moved into the new dwellings.
Tags: kfar chabad, housing, eretz yisrael, abandoned arab homes

Title: New homes constructed in Kfar Chabad
Summary: In 5717 new permanent homes were built in Kfar Chabad, finally allowing families like the Levins who had immigrated from the Soviet Union to settle properly.
Story: The years preceding the new construction had been very hard for the Russian Anash who had arrived in 1948-1949. The new housing project marked a turning point that enabled families to stabilize and resume normal communal life. Yisrael Yehuda Levin began preparing for his first trip to the Rebbe in New York soon after.
Tags: kfar chabad, eretz yisrael, housing

Title: Walking stick of Berditchev and Slavita sent to the Rebbe
Summary: In 5717, R. Shmuel Aba Shapira sent the Rebbe a family walking stick tied to Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev.
Story: In 1957 R. Shmuel Aba Shapira sent the Rebbe a walking stick that had belonged to the family—linked through marriage to Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev and the Slavita brothers (R. Pinchas and R. Shmuel Aba). The stick had survived seizures by the Bolsheviks and Hitler; it broke en route to a Moscow prison and was repaired by a Polish prince who fashioned the current handle.
Tags: the rebbe, berditchev, slavita brothers, soviet union, shapira family

Title: The Rebbe acknowledges Slavita brothers' cane from R' Shmuel Aba Shapira
Summary: On 16 Iyar 5717 the Rebbe wrote R' Shmuel Aba Shapira thanking him for the cane of the holy Slavita brothers.
Story: The Rebbe's letter, printed in Igros Kodesh vol. 15 (#5452), thanked R' Shmuel Aba Shapira for sending 'a cane from a holy place.' The accompanying note explained the cane had belonged to R' Pinchas of Slavita, passed via his only son R' Heshel and his daughter-in-law Treina, who had carried it to the brothers' Moscow prison and broken it in the mud. A Polish prince repaired it with a new handle; the cane is catalogued in the library archive as item 5186.
Tags: slavita, cane, shapira, igros kodesh, heirloom

Title: Yechidus with the Rebbe and instruction to write memoirs
Summary: On 2 Marcheshvan 5718, R. Yisrael Jacobson had a yechidus in which the Rebbe instructed him to write his memoirs of Lubavitch.
Story: On 2 Marcheshvan 5718 (October 1957), R. Yisrael Jacobson entered the Rebbe's chamber for a yechidus, marking the 50th anniversary of his first entry to the Rashab's chamber. During that audience, the Rebbe instructed him to record his memoirs of his time in Lubavitch. He continued writing these memoirs through 5718-5719 and later published selections in the quarterly Di Yiddishe Heim from 5724 until his passing on 17 Sivan 5735.
Tags: yechidus, memoirs, jacobson

Title: Beis Lubavitch established in London
Summary: A central Chabad building was purchased in London in 5718 and named 'Beis Lubavitch' by the Rebbe.
Story: In 5718 (1958), a building was purchased in London to serve as a regional Chabad headquarters. The Rebbe instructed it be named 'Beis Lubavitch' (Igros Kodesh vols. 17-18). When construction was completed, the building's key was sent to the Rebbe, who responded with a special letter expressing great satisfaction at the milestone.
Tags: london, england, beis chabad, beis lubavitch

Title: Rebbe declares 'U'fartzta' expansion on 12 Tammuz
Summary: At a 12 Tammuz 5718 sicha the Rebbe declared the 'U'fartzta' campaign of unrestricted outreach.
Story: In a sicha on 12 Tammuz 5718 (summer 1958), the Rebbe announced the campaign of 'U'fartzta' — bursting through all barriers in spreading chassidus and Judaism. This call, repeated throughout 5718-5719, marked the beginning of a major expansion in the shlichus enterprise (Igros Kodesh vol. 18 letter 6541).
Tags: ufartzta, mivtzaim, 12 tammuz, shlichus

Title: Publication of Tzofnat Paneach on Tractate Makkot
Summary: The first volume issued by Rabbi Kasher, Tzofnat Paneach on Tractate Makkot, appeared in 5719.
Story: In 5719 (1959), Rabbi Menachem Kasher published the first volume of his edition of the Rogatchover's writings, Tzofnat Paneach on Tractate Makkot. As soon as it appeared, Kasher sent a copy to the Rebbe.
Tags: rogatchover, tzofnat paneach, kasher, talmud

Title: Rebbe's letter with notes on Tzofnat Paneach Makkot
Summary: The Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Kasher with comments on the newly issued Tzofnat Paneach Makkot.
Story: On 23 Sivan 5719, immediately after receiving the new volume of Tzofnat Paneach on Tractate Makkot, the Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Kasher with notes and observations on its content. This letter appears in Igrot Kodesh vol. 18, letter 6903.
Tags: rogatchover, tzofnat paneach, kasher, letters

Title: Rebbe's second letter to Kasher on Tzofnat Paneach
Summary: The Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Kasher again on the substance of his notes on the Rogatchover.
Story: After Rabbi Kasher replied to the Rebbe's notes on Tzofnat Paneach Makkot, the Rebbe wrote back on 15 Tammuz 5719 further engaging with the substance of the discussion. This second letter appears as Igrot Kodesh letter 6936.
Tags: rogatchover, tzofnat paneach, kasher, letters

Title: The Rebbe writes R' Yosef Chaim Rosenfeld accepting the Bezpaloff cane
Summary: On 13 Kislev 5720 the Rebbe acknowledged receipt of the second Bezpaloff cane sent by R' Yosef Chaim Rosenfeld.
Story: R' Shneur Zalman Bezpaloff had originally brought two silver-handled canes to Rebbe Rayatz, who kept one; Bezpaloff later moved to San Francisco. When the shliach R' Yosef Chaim Hakohen Rosenfeld visited him there, Bezpaloff gifted him the second cane, which Rosenfeld then forwarded to the Rebbe. The Rebbe's reply (Igros Kodesh vol. 18 #6612) noted his habitual avoidance of gifts and enclosed a check in exchange.
