Title: Yaari's comprehensive Haggadah bibliography published in Jerusalem
Summary: Avraham Yaari's comprehensive Haggadah bibliography listing 2,717 editions was published in Jerusalem in 5721.
Story: In 5721 (1960/61), Avraham Yaari published in Jerusalem his Bibliografia Shel Haggadot Pesach, listing 2,717 editions of the Haggadah from the dawn of printing through 5720. The bibliography drew in part on the descriptions of Haggadot in the Lubavitch library that had been sent to him by librarian Chaim Liberman.
Tags: bibliography, haggadah, yaari, jerusalem, library

Title: Berke Chein immigrates to Israel after Soviet imprisonment
Summary: Berke Chein, whose death sentence had been commuted following a bribe arranged by the Rebbe, immigrated to Israel in 1961 after his Soviet imprisonment.
Story: Chein had been arrested in Lvov for attempting to escape during the Great Escape and held by local police. The $7,000 bribe arranged by the sixth Rebbe through a Vilnius contact reduced his sentence; he was freed after three years and ultimately settled in Israel.
Tags: berke chein, russia, israel, great escape, prison

Title: Chabad Haggadah for Kfar Chabad youth published
Summary: Tzeirei Agudat Chabad in the Holy Land published a Haggadah following the Alter Rebbe's nusach for Kfar Chabad youth.
Story: In 5721 (1961), Tzeirei Agudat Chabad in the Holy Land published a Haggadah for youth visiting Kfar Chabad. The 32-page sixteenmo edition was based on the Chabad Alter Rebbe's nusach. A second printing followed in 5732 (1972) for the next generation of Israeli Chabad youth.
Tags: chabad, kfar chabad, israel, haggadah, youth, tzeirei agudat chabad

Title: Facsimile of the first printed Haggadah from Guadalajara published in Jerusalem
Summary: A facsimile of the first printed Haggadah (Guadalajara, c. 1482) was published in Jerusalem from the National Library's unique copy.
Story: In 5721 (1961), a facsimile edition of the earliest printed Haggadah, originally produced around 1482 in Guadalajara (Wadi al-Hagara), was published in Jerusalem. The 12-leaf folio reproduction was made from the unique copy preserved in the National Library of Israel's Jewish National and University Library. It appeared as an appendix to the 'Bibliography of Passover Haggadot'.
Tags: haggadah, facsimile, jerusalem, guadalajara, bibliography, national library

Title: New York Haggadah with 'Divrei Binah' and 'Toldot Adam' Biala commentaries
Summary: A Haggadah with the 'Divrei Binah' (Yitzchak Yaakov of Biala) and 'Toldot Adam' (Yehoshua of Ostrova) commentaries was published in New York.
Story: Around 5721 (1961), a Haggadah was issued in New York featuring the 'Divrei Binah' commentary by Rabbi Yitzchak Yaakov of Biala and the 'Toldot Adam' commentary by Rabbi Yehoshua of Ostrova. The 91-page octavo edition included a preface by the Admor of Biala. It represented the publishing efforts of the Biala Chassidic dynasty in postwar America.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, biala, new york, yitzchak yaakov biala, ostrova

Title: Publication of Tzofnat Paneach on Exodus
Summary: Tzofnat Paneach on the Book of Exodus appeared in the summer of 5721.
Story: In the summer of 5721 (1961), Rabbi Menachem Kasher's volume of Tzofnat Paneach on the Book of Exodus was published. As soon as the Rebbe received it, he reviewed it, wrote comments, and sent them back to Kasher.
Tags: rogatchover, tzofnat paneach, kasher

Title: Purim children's campaign letter sent by Rebbe's secretariat
Summary: In early Adar 5721 the Rebbe's secretariat sent a general letter urging organized Purim observance by children.
Story: At the beginning of Adar 5721 (1961), the Rebbe directed his secretariat to send a general letter to institutions, rabbis, yeshiva heads, teachers, and parents, urging organized efforts to ensure every child observes the mitzvos of Purim — especially mishloach manos and matanos l'evyonim — themselves (Igros Kodesh vol. 20 letter 7598).
Tags: purim, children, mivtzaim

Title: Wedding of Leah to Yerachmiel Binyamin Klein
Summary: On 21 Adar 5721 the author's daughter Leah married Yerachmiel Binyamin Halevi Klein at the Melrose-Chateau hall in Brownsville.
Story: The wedding was celebrated on 21 Adar 5721 (March 9, 1961) at Melrose-Chateau in Brownsville. Since Kollel Avreichim did not yet exist, the Rebbe instructed the chatan to specialize in the laws of mikvaot, which he learned with the Rav of Norolsk. A few months later the couple was sent on shlichus by Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch to Australia.
Tags: wedding, klein, melrose-chateau, brownsville, shlichus, australia

Title: Manuscript volume sent to Chabad library for review
Summary: On 27 Nisan 5721 (1961), librarian R. Chaim Lieberman responded to R. Shmuel Ber Leikin describing the contents of a buch he had sent in for review.
Story: R. Shmuel Ber Leikin sent a manuscript volume to the Chabad library asking what it contained. On 27 Nisan 5721 Lieberman replied that the volume held copies of chassidic discourses plus three original pages: two by the Tzemach Tzedek and one by the Rebbe Maharash — a letter to R. Chaim Yaakov Widrewitz. The original three pages later disappeared from the volume, and locating them became a decades-long search.
Tags: shmuel ber leikin, chaim lieberman, chabad library, manuscripts, rebbe maharash, chaim yaakov widrewitz

Title: Kasher's Pesach Sheni letter on Tzofnat Paneach on Exodus
Summary: Rabbi Kasher updated the Rebbe on the imminent appearance of Tzofnat Paneach on Exodus.
Story: On Pesach Sheni 5721, Rabbi Menachem Kasher wrote to the Rebbe that Tzofnat Paneach on Exodus was nearly finished and would be completed within a month. He also mentioned having submitted volumes on Leviticus and on Tractates Horayot, Eduyot and the minor tractates for printing in Israel.
Tags: rogatchover, tzofnat paneach, kasher, letters

Title: Kasher's letter thanking the Rebbe for Joint Distribution Committee support
Summary: Rabbi Kasher thanked the Rebbe for unsolicited intervention with the JDC to support the Tzofnat Paneach project.
Story: On 24 Sivan 5721, Rabbi Kasher wrote to the Rebbe with heartfelt thanks. JDC representatives had told Kasher that during their yechidut with the Rebbe, in the middle of discussing their own support for Chabad activities, the Rebbe had taken the opportunity to praise the Tzofnat Paneach project and urge them to support it.
Tags: rogatchover, tzofnat paneach, kasher, joint distribution committee

Title: Sheina Paz dies in Moscow
Summary: Sheina bat Mordechai, wife of R. Zushya Paz, died on 28 Tammuz 5721 and was buried beside him in Malachovka.
Story: Sheina bat Mordechai, the wife of the Marina-Roshcha shamash R. Yekutiel Zusman 'Zushya' Paz, died on 28 Tammuz 5721 (July 12, 1961). She was buried beside her husband in Malachovka outside Moscow. Their daughter, who lived in a village near Moscow, had supplied chalav yisrael to the shul daily from her cow.
Tags: moscow, marina-roshcha, death, soviet union

Title: Rebbe's letter urging publication of Rogatchover on Talmud
Summary: The Rebbe urged Rabbi Kasher to prioritize publishing a Tzofnat Paneach volume on a yeshiva tractate.
Story: On 1 Menachem Av 5721, the Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Kasher acknowledging Tzofnat Paneach on Exodus and urging that, if possible, he should publish a volume on a Talmudic tractate studied in yeshivot in time for the upcoming zman. The Rebbe noted that volumes on Talmud make a different first impression than volumes on Chumash.
Tags: rogatchover, tzofnat paneach, kasher, yeshivot, letters

Title: Fourth amud for the Rebbe built at Kfar Chabad trade school
Summary: In 5722 a fourth amud for the Rebbe was constructed at the Kfar Chabad trade school for shipment to 770.
Story: The fourth amud was built in 5722 at the Beis Hasefer Le'Mlacha trade school in Kfar Chabad, modeled on the wide and elegant third amud already in use at 770, with two small doors and a fold-out shelf. The new amud differed in having a thin dividing column between the two doors — a detail that mattered for Yom Kippur, when the Rebbe used to place his hat inside the amud during the Minchah-Maariv break.
Tags: kfar chabad, amud, trade school, 770

Title: Haggadah 'Kol Yehuda' on the teachings of Belz Rebbes printed in London
Summary: A Haggadah 'Kol Yehuda' built on Belz teachings by Chaim Yehuda Segal Deutsch was printed in London with material from Rebbe Aharon of Belz.
Story: In 5722 (1962), the Haggadah 'Kol Yehuda', interwoven with teachings from the Belz Rebbes by Rabbi Chaim Yehuda Segal Deutsch, was published in London. The 212-page octavo edition included notes by the author's son and added Passover discourses from Rebbe Aharon Rokeach of Belz. It contributed to the Belz Chassidic community's postwar publishing renaissance.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, belz, london, aharon rokeach, chaim yehuda deutsch

Title: Kiryat Gat mayor sends Rebbe key of the city — first such gift
Summary: In Elul 5722, the mayor of Kiryat Gat became the first mayor to honor the Rebbe by sending him the key to the city.
Story: In Elul 5722 (August–September 1962), the mayor of Kiryat Gat in Israel became the first municipal head to express appreciation for Chabad by sending the Rebbe the key of the city. He entrusted the key to Rabbi Yaakov Peles, who later delivered it. This precedent led many other mayors to follow suit through their local shluchim.
Tags: israel, kiryat gat, yaakov peles, key of the city, elul

Title: Stender built in Kfar Chabad for the Rebbe
Summary: In 5722 students at the Kfar Chabad trade school built a stender for the Rebbe.
Story: In 1962 the trade school in Kfar Chabad, Israel, constructed a stender for the Rebbe. It was carried by air with the group of Chassidim who chartered a flight to spend Tishrei 5723 with the Rebbe in New York.
Tags: the rebbe, stender, kfar chabad, israel

Title: Yechidus on Alter Rebbe's 150th yahrzeit and bochurim's roles
Summary: At his Erev R"Ch Elul 5722 yechidus the Rebbe asked the author to publish unpublished manuscripts for the Alter Rebbe's 150th yahrzeit year and to revive bochurim's leining and davening at the amud.
Story: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5722 (August 30, 1962) the author entered yechidus for his birthday. The Rebbe noted that this was the 150th year since the Alter Rebbe's passing and asked for a list of unpublished manuscripts at the print shop to release that year. He also pressed the author to resume the Torah-reading dikduk shiur for bochurim and to have bochurim daven before the amud on weekday Mincha.
Tags: alter rebbe, yechidus, kehot, manuscripts, menteliek, torah reading, amud

Title: First Chabad charter flight from Eretz Yisrael to the Rebbe
Summary: In Elul 5722 the first charter flight of chassidim from Eretz Yisrael came to the Rebbe, carrying a wooden amud as a gift.
Story: In Elul 5722 (August/September 1962), the first chartered flight of chassidim traveled from Eretz Yisrael to be with the Rebbe. They brought an amud (prayer-leader's stand) crafted at the trade school in Kfar Chabad. The amud was presented at a special farbrengen the Rebbe held in honor of the guests on the eve of Rosh Hashana 5723.
Tags: eretz yisrael, charter flight, kfar chabad, amud

Title: Kfar Chabad delegation brings new amud to the Rebbe on Erev Rosh Hashanah
Summary: On Or L'Erev Rosh Hashanah 5723 a delegation from Eretz Yisrael presented the Kfar Chabad-built amud to the Rebbe.
Story: A chartered flight brought a group from Eretz Yisrael for the Tishrei holidays of 5723, and R' Chaim Schneur Zalman Lipsker carried the new amud with them. He and R' Dovber Teichman presented it at the special farbrengen held Or L'Erev Rosh Hashanah 5723, after which the Rebbe delivered a sicha explaining the inner meaning of the 'shtender' and recounted the Mitteler Rebbe's exchange with the Alter Rebbe about davening 'with the shtender.'
Tags: kfar chabad, amud, lipsker, teichman, rosh hashanah, 770

Title: Levin's first trip to the Rebbe for Tishrei 5723
Summary: In late Elul 5722 Yisrael Yehuda Levin traveled from Kfar Chabad to New York for his first visit to the Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson.
Story: Levin had hoped for this meeting through years of underground religious work in the Soviet Union. He spent the entire month of Tishrei 5723 with the Rebbe, attending farbrengens, yechidus, and the Sukkos and Simchas Torah celebrations at 770. The memoir ends with the description of this Tishrei month.
Tags: rebbe, new york, kfar chabad, rosh hashanah, first visit

Title: Special farbrengen for charter-flight guests on eve of Rosh Hashana 5723
Summary: On the eve of Rosh Hashana 5723 the Rebbe held a special farbrengen for visiting chassidim and explained the meaning of the amud.
Story: At the special farbrengen held on the eve of Rosh Hashana 5723 (September 1962) for the chassidim who had come on the charter flight, the Rebbe spoke about the maaleh of the amud they had presented. He related the famous story in which the Mitteler Rebbe asked his father the Alter Rebbe what he had prayed with on Rosh Hashana, and was answered 'with the shtender' — for all is G-dliness and 'He alone is, and there is none besides Him.'
Tags: rosh hashana, amud, alter rebbe, mitteler rebbe, farbrengen

Title: Rebbe receives Kiryat Gat's key at Erev Rosh Hashana farbrengen
Summary: On Erev Rosh Hashana 5723, Rabbi Yaakov Peles handed Kiryat Gat's city key to the Rebbe at the welcome farbrengen for guests.
Story: On the night of Erev Rosh Hashana 5723 (September 18, 1962), Rabbi Yaakov Peles delivered Kiryat Gat's city key to the Rebbe during the welcome farbrengen for visiting guests in 770. The Rebbe responded with a sicha explaining the symbolism of a city key — that it opens and closes the city gates to protect it from outside threats (Toras Menachem Hisvaaduyos vol. 34, p. 324).
Tags: israel, kiryat gat, yaakov peles, key of the city, rosh hashana

Title: Levin's first flight to the Rebbe via charter from Lod
Summary: On Tuesday 26 Elul 5722 Levin flew from Lod via Paris to New York on a charter flight to spend Tishrei with the Rebbe for the first time.
Story: After years of yearning, Levin joined a charter flight at the end of Elul 5722 for his first trip to the Rebbe. The plane departed Lod at noon, stopped two hours in Paris where Chassidim could see them only through a thick glass partition (only R' Raphael Wilshansky was allowed in), then continued to New York. The Rebbe was waiting at 770 and emerged from his room to daven Maariv when the group arrived.
Tags: 770, charter flight, first visit, lod, paris, raphael wilshansky, tishrei guests

Title: Erev Rosh Hashana 5723 farbrengen on Tzemach Tzedek's birthday
Summary: On the night of 29 Elul 5722, the birthday of the Tzemach Tzedek, the Rebbe led a farbrengen with women in the ezrat nashim and spoke on hachnasat orchim.
Story: On Thursday night, the eve of 29 Elul 5722 — the birthday of the Tzemach Tzedek — the Rebbe held a farbrengen at 770 with a microphone since it was the night before Rosh Hashana. The ezrat nashim was filled with women and the Rebbe addressed a sicha to them. He spoke about the mitzvah of hachnasat orchim being greater than receiving the Divine Presence, embracing the assembled guests.
Tags: 770, tzemach tzedek, birthday, farbrengen, hachnasat orchim, ezrat nashim, microphone

Title: Rebbe receives pidyonot on Erev Rosh Hashana 5723
Summary: On Erev Rosh Hashana 5723 the Rebbe led Selichot, performed hatarat nedarim, received pidyonot, and the Vaad HaMesader presented a collective pan.
Story: Early Friday morning of Erev Rosh Hashana 5723, the Rebbe led Selichot and Shacharit before a large crowd of Tishrei guests. He performed hatarat nedarim before a minyan of elder Chassidim, then received personal pidyonot at his hand. The Vaad HaMesader and elder Anash then brought a collective pan, with each signer giving a dollar. The Rebbe then traveled to the Ohel to read and tear the pidyonot.
Tags: 770, selichot, hatarat nedarim, pidyon nefesh, vaad hamesader, ohel

Title: Stender presented to the Rebbe at erev Rosh Hashana farbrengen
Summary: On the eve of Rosh Hashana 5723 the Kfar Chabad stender was presented to the Rebbe at a special farbrengen.
Story: On the night of erev Rosh Hashana 5723 (1962), the Rebbe held a farbrengen for the Israeli Chassidim who came for the month of Tishrei. The new stender was presented, and the Rebbe spoke about its significance, recounting the Mitteler Rebbe's question to his father, the Alter Rebbe, on what he had prayed with on Rosh Hashana—answered with 'with the stender,' since 'all is G-dliness, He alone exists.'
Tags: the rebbe, stender, kfar chabad, rosh hashana, 770

Title: Rebbe called for maftir on first day of Rosh Hashana 5723
Summary: On Shabbat, first day of Rosh Hashana 5723, the Rebbe was called to the Torah for maftir and read the haftarah of Chana with great emotion.
Story: Because the first day of Rosh Hashana 5723 fell on Shabbat there was no shofar blowing. Levin pushed his way onto the bima next to baal koreh R' Mordechai Shusterman to hear the maftir from the Rebbe. The Rebbe read the haftarah of Chana with such inner weeping and sweetness that Levin had to cover his face with his tallit to muffle his sobs.
Tags: rosh hashana, 770, maftir, haftarah of chana, mordechai shusterman, shabbat

Title: Rebbe blows shofar on second day of Rosh Hashana 5723
Summary: On the second day of Rosh Hashana 5723 the Rebbe blew shofar, led Tashlich, and delivered the maamar 'Yivchar Lanu Et Nachalateinu.'
Story: Levin again ascended the bima and unexpectedly received the honor of gelilah. The Rebbe covered the bundled pidyonot with his tallit, wept, and blew only the first tekiah. After Mincha the Rebbe led the entire crowd to Tashlich along Eastern Parkway in remarkable order, with even non-Jewish onlookers watching with reverence. The maamar 'Yivchar Lanu Et Nachalateinu' was delivered at the farbrengen that followed.
Tags: rosh hashana, 770, shofar, tashlich, yivchar lanu, maamar, gelilah, eastern parkway

Title: Kfar Chabad delegation presents Rebbe with the village's etrog
Summary: On the night of 4 Tishrei 5723, representatives of Kfar Chabad delivered the village's etrog to the Rebbe, who blessed them in return.
Story: Members of Anash from Kfar Chabad presented the Rebbe with the etrog grown in the village. The Rebbe blessed them that just as the etrog has both taste and fragrance — symbolizing all qualities — so should all Israel, Anash, and Kfar Chabad in particular be granted matters of taam and reach throughout the entire year.
Tags: 770, kfar chabad, etrog, tishrei, blessing, taam vareach

Title: Levin's first yechidus with the Rebbe
Summary: On the night of 6 Tishrei 5723, just before 3am, Levin entered yechidus with the Rebbe for the first time and recited Shehecheyanu.
Story: After a lifetime of hoping for this moment, Levin entered the Rebbe's room for his first yechidus in the early hours of 6 Tishrei 5723. He recited Shehecheyanu and presented a long written tzettel of questions. The Rebbe answered each one in depth, and when Levin failed to grasp a detail, the Rebbe patiently repeated his words verbatim.
Tags: yechidus, 770, shehecheyanu, tzettel, tishrei, first yechidus

Title: Levin davens before the amud on Shabbat Shuva 5723
Summary: On 8 Tishrei 5723 (Shabbat Shuva and his mother's yahrzeit), Levin led prayers at the Rebbe's beit midrash and was called up for shevii.
Story: On 8 Tishrei 5723, the yahrzeit of his mother (Hashem yikom damah), Levin davened all the Shabbat tefillot before the amud in the Rebbe's beit midrash, with the gabbai R' Yochanan Gordon pushing him toward the amud for Musaf. He stood beside the Rebbe for maftir. Before the Shabbat, an Anash printer had given him a galley of the Tzemach Tzedek's maamar 'V'chol Adam' brought from Russia, which the Rebbe delivered at the farbrengen that day.
Tags: shabbat shuva, 770, yochanan gordon, yahrzeit, yom hashana, tzemach tzedek maamar, v'chol adam

Title: Lekach distribution before Yom Kippur 5723
Summary: On Erev Yom Kippur 5723 Levin received lekach from the Rebbe and also obtained lekach from Rebbetzin Chana.
Story: Levin waited in line to receive lekach from the Rebbe, who gave him a piece for his daughter as well. He also visited Rebbetzin Chana with his host's family — R' Berl Yunik's family — and received lekach and a blessing from her. She remembered Levin from Pocking, where he had stayed with Michoel Teitelbaum.
Tags: erev yom kippur, lekach, rebbetzin chana, 770, berl yunik

Title: Levin blesses on the Rebbe's etrog on Sukkot 5723
Summary: On the second day of Sukkot 5723 Levin entered the Rebbe's sukkah and blessed on the Rebbe's arba minim.
Story: After the first day of Sukkot fell on Shabbat, Levin waited in line on the second day to enter the Rebbe's sukkah and bless on his arba minim. The Rebbe stood in a corner holding a sefer and watched Levin throughout, who silently prayed not to fumble the brachah from the intensity of the moment.
Tags: sukkot, etrog, 770, rebbe sukkah, arba minim

Title: Hoshana Rabbah 5723 hakafot mission and 770 farbrengen
Summary: On Erev Shabbat Hoshana Rabbah 5723, Chassidim were dispatched to distant shuls to lead hakafot, then converged at 770 for the Rebbe's farbrengen.
Story: On Erev Shabbat Hoshana Rabbah 5723, Levin and others were sent according to a list to far-away shuls to gladden Jews with hakafot. They later gathered at Rabbi Yaakov Hecht's shul for kiddush and walked together with song and dance back to 770. At the farbrengen the Rebbe asked all those who had gone to gladden others to say l'chaim and recite Atah Hareita and the hakafot — a peak of joy as the Rebbe danced with the Rashag during the first and seventh hakafot.
Tags: hoshana rabbah, 770, hakafot, yaakov hecht, shliach, atah hareita

Title: Simchat Torah 5723 hakafot and 'Stav Ya Pitu' niggun
Summary: On Simchat Torah night 5723 the Rebbe taught the Russian niggun 'Stav Ya Pitu' for the first time at 770.
Story: After the late-night hakafot of Simchat Torah 5723, Chassidim waited as the Rebbe was set to distribute mashke. The Rebbe recounted the story behind the niggun 'Stav Ya Pitu' and began to sing it. Standing right beside the Rebbe, Levin watched as the Rebbe repeated the Russian-lyric melody many times until R' Yoel Kahn finally picked it up — since the wave of bochurim from Russia had not yet arrived.
Tags: simchat torah, 770, stav ya pitu, niggun, kalman brickman, yoel kahn, russian

Title: Rebbe calls Israeli army veterans up at Motzaei Simchat Torah farbrengen
Summary: At the Motzaei Simchat Torah 5723 farbrengen the Rebbe asked all Israeli army or reserve veterans to ascend the table and say l'chaim, hinting at the Cuban missile crisis.
Story: Toward the end of the Motzaei Simchat Torah farbrengen the Rebbe unexpectedly invited all those from Eretz Yisrael who had served in the army or miluim to come up on the table and say l'chaim, then led the singing of 'V'haya Machanecha Kadosh' and 'Shalom Al Yisrael.' He said cryptically 'one should fulfill it with the fear,' which Chassidim later interpreted in light of Soviet missiles approaching Cuba. Levin received kos shel bracha and was called back to receive a bottle of wine to distribute in Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: motzaei simchat torah, 770, idf, miluim, v'haya machanecha kadosh, cuban missile crisis, kos shel bracha, wine

Title: Levin's second yechidus on Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan 5723
Summary: On the night of Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan 5723 Levin had a second yechidus, during which the Rebbe instructed him to establish a yahrzeit for the martyred R' Yona Cohen.
Story: On his second yechidus, just before 10pm on the night of Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan 5723, Levin handed in a lengthy tzettel and mentioned the kadosh R' Yona Cohen. The Rebbe asked for his mother's name and his date of death and instructed Levin to fix a yahrzeit, say kaddish, and learn mishnayot. Levin later confirmed with R' Elya Chaim Roitblat (R' Yona's brother-in-law) that the date was 22 Shevat and the mother's name was Frade, and conveyed the information to R' Chadakov.
Tags: yechidus, rosh chodesh cheshvan, yona cohen, samarkand, yahrzeit, kaddish, chodakov, elya chaim roitblat

Title: Rebbe permanently positions the new amud in the upstairs beis medrash
Summary: During Pesach 5723 the Rebbe instructed R' Chadakov to permanently place the new amud upstairs in the small beis medrash.
Story: After the new amud spent more than half a year in the Rebbe's room, the downstairs courtyard shul at 770 was already serving for Kabbalas Shabbos, Shacharis, and Mussaf, while Minchah on Erev Shabbos and Shabbos remained upstairs — requiring staff to carry the third amud up and down. On Pesach 5723 the Rebbe told R' Chadakov to leave the older amud downstairs permanently and bring the new amud up to the small beis medrash as its fixed amud.
Tags: 770, amud, pesach, chadakov

Title: Rebbe describes how Rebbetzin Chana made ink in exile
Summary: At the farbrengen of 20 Menachem-Av 5723, the Rebbe recounted how his mother improvised colored inks from grasses so his father could write glosses on a Zohar in Soviet exile.
Story: On 20 Menachem-Av 5723 (10 August 1963), the yahrzeit of his father R. Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, the Rebbe told that when his father was in Soviet exile, he eventually received some books — including a Zohar — but no paper, so he wrote his Kabbalistic glosses in the margins. He also lacked ink, so Rebbetzin Chana learned to manufacture ink from grasses; lacking expertise, her batches came out red, green or black, accounting for the varied colors visible in the manuscript glosses later published as Likutei Levi Yitzchak.
Tags: levi yitzchak schneerson, exile, soviet union, zohar, rebbetzin chana, yahrzeit

Title: Wedding of Miriam Reizel to Moshe Nemenov
Summary: On 23 Kislev 5724 the author's daughter Miriam Reizel married Moshe Nemenov at Grand-Paradise Hall in Williamsburg.
Story: The wedding took place on 23 Kislev 5724 (December 9, 1963) at the Grand-Paradise Hall in Williamsburg, joining the families of two Zlobin natives. On the Rebbe's instruction, sheva brachos were held in Cleveland — first at the shul of Reb Zalman Kaizen and then at the home of Reb Chaim Stein, mashgiach of Telshe Yeshiva, where the Telshe roshei yeshiva attended.
Tags: wedding, nemenov, williamsburg, zlobin, telshe, cleveland, sheva brachos

Title: Jerusalem Spinka Haggadah with Imrei Yosef and Chakal Yitzchak commentaries
Summary: A Spinka-rite Haggadah with the 'Imrei Yosef' and 'Chakal Yitzchak' commentaries from the Weiss dynasty was published in Jerusalem.
Story: In 5724 (1964), a Haggadah following the Spinka rite was published in Jerusalem featuring the 'Imrei Yosef' commentary by Rebbe Yosef Meir Weiss of Spinka and the 'Chakal Yitzchak' commentary by Rebbe Yitzchak Aizik Weiss of Spinka. The 239-page octavo edition served the Spinka Chassidic community. It transmitted the teachings of the Carpathian dynasty to the Israeli Spinka community.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, spinka, jerusalem, yosef meir weiss, yitzchak isaac weiss

Title: Shulsinger Brothers facsimile of Gershom Cohen's Prague Haggadah
Summary: The Shulsinger Brothers reissued in New York a facsimile of Gershom Cohen's 1527 Prague Haggadah.
Story: In 5724 (1964), the Shulsinger Brothers issued in New York a facsimile reproduction of the Haggadah printed at the press of Gershom Cohen in Prague in 1527. The 42-leaf folio edition revived one of the most influential early printed Haggadot for modern audiences. It was a key contribution to mid-20th-century Hebrew bibliophilic publishing.
Tags: haggadah, facsimile, new york, prague, gershom cohen, shulsinger

Title: Tel Aviv Haggadah illustrated by Gad Ullman from Massada Press
Summary: Gad Ullman wrote and illustrated a Haggadah published by Massada Press in Tel Aviv.
Story: In 5724 (1964), Massada Press in Tel Aviv issued a Haggadah whose calligraphy and illustration were both executed by Gad Ullman. The 20-leaf landscape edition (12x34 cm) showcased Ullman's artistic approach to the Haggadah text. It reflected the developing Israeli book arts tradition of the mid-1960s.
Tags: haggadah, tel aviv, israel, gad ullman, massada

Title: Passing of Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson
Summary: Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, the Rebbe's mother, passed away in New York on 6 Tishrei 5725.
Story: Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, mother of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, kept the Tehillim that had belonged to her husband Rabbi Levi Yitzchak in his Kazakhstan exile. She recited Tehillim from it until her passing in New York on 6 Tishrei 5725 (September 1964), having brought it with her when she left Russia.
Tags: new york, chana schneerson, exile

Title: Rabbanit Chana passes away on 6 Tishrei
Summary: The Rebbe's mother, Rabbanit Chana, passed away on 6 Tishrei 5725.
Story: After leaving Russia, Rabbanit Chana continued reciting her husband's Tehillim daily until her passing in New York on 6 Tishrei 5725 (Sept 12, 1964). She had recorded on its flyleaf the story of how the Tehillim had been brought to her late husband in Soviet exile.
Tags: rabbanit chana, the rebbe, yahrzeit, new york

Title: Rebbetzin Chana Schneersohn passes away
Summary: Rebbetzin Chana Schneersohn, mother of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, passed away on 6 Tishrei 5725.
Story: Rebbetzin Chana Schneersohn, mother of the Lubavitcher Rebbe and widow of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, passed away on 6 Tishrei 5725. With her death ended the twelve-year concealment of her younger son Israel Aryeh Leib's earlier passing, which had been hidden from her to protect her health.
Tags: rebbetzin chana, schneersohn family, passing, brooklyn

Title: New edition of Hilchos Talmud Torah with sources and notes
Summary: Rabbi Nissan Mangel produced a new edition of the Alter Rebbe's Hilchos Talmud Torah in 1965, complete with source references and footnotes.
Story: The 5725 (1965) Mangel edition added marginal notes and sources to the Alter Rebbe's halachot of Torah study. It became the standard, photo-reproduced in countless later printings and embedded into subsequent Shulchan Aruch editions.
Tags: alter rebbe, talmud torah, nissan mangel

Title: Rabbi Shlomo Cunin sent as shliach to California
Summary: Rabbi Shlomo Cunin was sent by the seventh Rebbe to California, an early and then-controversial example of Chabad shlichut.
Story: Cunin recalls Chasidim in New York telling him he would not last long on the West Coast and insinuating he was only going because he could not get a job close to home. The concept of shlichut to communities lacking basic religious infrastructure was revolutionary in the 1950s and 1960s, even within Chabad.
Tags: california, cunin, shluchim, outreach, west-coast

Title: Theodore Wiener publishes supplements to Yaari's Haggadah bibliography
Summary: Theodore Wiener published supplements to Yaari's bibliography in Studies in Bibliography and Booklore in 5725.
Story: In 5725 (1965), Theodore Wiener published bibliographical supplements to Avraham Yaari's Haggadah bibliography in Studies in Bibliography and Booklore, vol. VII (Cincinnati, 1965, p. 90). The supplements further refined the bibliographic record of printed Haggadot.
Tags: bibliography, haggadah, wiener, cincinnati, supplements

Title: Rebbe writes to Zelda about her mother's tombstone inscription
Summary: On 9 Shevat 5725 the Rebbe wrote to the poet Zelda regarding the inscription for her mother Rachel's tombstone.
Story: Following the passing of Rebbetzin Rachel Schneersohn in 5725, the Rebbe wrote on 9 Shevat 5725 to her daughter, the poet Zelda Mishkovsky, regarding the wording of the matzeva. The letter was later published in Igrot Kodesh vol. 23, letter 8934.
Tags: zelda, tombstone, matzeva, schneersohn family, letter

Title: Hemshech 5666 typesetting begins by Rebbe's instruction
Summary: On 2 Nisan 5725, after returning from the Ohel, the Rebbe directed Kehot to begin typesetting Hemshech Yom Tov shel Rosh Hashanah 5666 that same evening.
Story: On the night of 2 Nisan 5725 (April 4, 1965) Rabbi Chadakov phoned to relay that the Rebbe, on returning from the Ohel, ordered typesetting of the Hemshech Yom Tov shel Rosh Hashanah Tarsa"v to begin immediately and that the most corrected manuscript be sought. Reb Baruch Sholom Shvei went to the press that very night and began setting the type. On the following motzaei Acharon Shel Pesach the Rebbe gave the author a bottle of wine 'for the Samach-Vov.'
Tags: hemshech 5666, rashab, kehot, chadakov, typesetting, rosh hashanah

Title: Rebbe announces 100-year hilula initiatives
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Elul 5725 (August 1965) the Rebbe announced fundraising and learning programs for the Tzemach Tzedek centennial.
Story: At the farbrengen of Rosh Chodesh Elul 5725, the Rebbe announced that, in connection with the centennial of the Tzemach Tzedek's hilula, every chassid should contribute 100 coins toward printing his works. He reiterated the call at the Shabbat Nitzavim (28 Elul) farbrengen and added a directive to study the first three chapters of Tanya on Erev Rosh Hashanah, the Tzemach Tzedek's birthday.
Tags: rebbe, tzemach tzedek, 100 year hilula, kerren hameah, elul 5725

Title: Alter Rebbe's tefillin brought from Russia to the Rebbe
Summary: Tefillin attributed to the Alter Rebbe were brought from Russia in 5726 (1966) and placed for viewing on the bima at 770.
Story: On their 1966 arrival the Rebbe directed that the tefillin be set on the synagogue bima so that those who had immersed in the mikveh could file by to see them. They remain part of the library's object collection (#6104).
Tags: alter rebbe, tefillin, russia, 770

Title: First post-war visit of Anash to Lubavitch; gravestones restored
Summary: In 5726, Rabbi Dovid Gurevitz traveled from Samarkand to Lubavitch and re-erected the destroyed gravestones of the Tzemach Tzedek and Rebbe Maharash.
Story: In 5726 (1966), for the first time since the war, members of Anash found an opportunity to come to Lubavitch. Rabbi Dovid Gurevitz traveled from distant Samarkand all the way to Lubavitch, where he re-erected the destroyed gravestones of the Tzemach Tzedek and the Rebbe Maharash. This visit marked the beginning of efforts to restore the holy site.
Tags: lubavitch, ohel, tzemach tzedek, maharash, samarkand, soviet, dovid gurevitz

Title: Mass Soviet Jewish exodus begins
Summary: Beginning in 5726, the great exodus of Jews from the Soviet Union began, restoring contact between Russian Anash and the outside world.
Story: Following the post-WWII period during which Russian Anash had been nearly completely cut off from those outside the Soviet Union, the great Jewish exodus from Russia began in 5726 (1966). Before this point, Chabad activity in Russia had been entirely underground, conducted via the Rebbe's secret shluchim, with photographs and printed announcements forbidden.
Tags: soviet-union, russia, anash-emigration, iron-curtain

Title: R' David Gurevitch restores Lubavitch tombstones
Summary: R' David Gurevitch traveled from Samarkand to Lubavitch to restore the destroyed tombstones.
Story: In 5726 (1966), the first opportunity arose for chassidim to visit Lubavitch. R' David Gurevitch traveled from distant Samarkand to Lubavitch and re-erected the destroyed tombstones of the Tzemach Tzedek and the Rebbe Maharash. Many of the cemetery's tombstones had previously been stolen by locals for use as building foundations.
Tags: lubavitch, ohel, graves, tombstones, restoration

Title: Seventh Rebbe dispatches elite students to Australia
Summary: The seventh Rebbe dispatched a group of elite students to Australia, beginning a global expansion model.
Story: Following the model pioneered by the Rashab and Rayatz of sending selected students from flagship yeshivos to establish new centers, the seventh Rebbe set up new yeshivos around the globe. Today some fifty Chabad yeshivos exist worldwide, with senior students sent for one or two years to maintain scholarship standards in branches.
Tags: seventh rebbe, australia, chabad expansion, shluchim

Title: Seventh Rebbe sends students to Australia
Summary: The seventh Rebbe dispatched a group of elite students to Australia to establish a new center of Chabad learning.
Story: In 1966, the seventh Rebbe began applying the model pioneered by the Rashab and Rayatz, dispatching senior students from the central yeshivas to seed new institutions abroad. The Australia dispatch became the template for the global network of some fifty Chabad yeshivas today.
Tags: australia, seventh rebbe, shluchim, yeshivah, global expansion

Title: Rebbe issues centennial klalli letter
Summary: On 8 Nisan 5726 (March 29, 1966) the Rebbe's office issued a klalli letter to Chabad institutions worldwide for the Tzemach Tzedek's 100-year hilula.
Story: The Rebbe's secretariat sent a klalli letter on 8 Nisan 5726 to 'Chabad organizations and institutions in every locality,' authorizing them as the Rebbe's shluchim to receive special hilula-day donations to a 'Keren HaMeah' for the printing of the Tzemach Tzedek's writings. The letter is published in Igrot Kodesh vol. 24, p. 113.
Tags: rebbe, tzemach tzedek, klalli letter, kerren hameah, 8 nisan 5726

Title: Rebbe leads 100-year hilula farbrengen
Summary: On the eve of 13 Nisan 5726 (April 3, 1966) the Rebbe held a special farbrengen marking the Tzemach Tzedek's 100-year hilula.
Story: On the eve of 13 Nisan 5726, the Rebbe held a dedicated farbrengen elucidating teachings of the Tzemach Tzedek and again repeating his maamar 'HaChodesh HaZeh Lachem,' said by the Tzemach Tzedek shortly before his own passing. At the close he again urged participation in Keren HaMeah, with joy.
Tags: rebbe, tzemach tzedek, 13 nisan, farbrengen, hahodesh hazeh lachem

Title: Library building adjacent to 770 purchased
Summary: In 5727 the building adjacent to 770 Eastern Parkway was purchased to house the Rebbe's growing library collection.
Story: By 5727 (1967) the Rebbe's working library, built up since 1941 through emissaries around the world, had outgrown its space. The building next to 770 Eastern Parkway was purchased to house it. From then until 1985 two parallel libraries existed at the Chabad headquarters — the Rayatz's collection in 770 and the Rebbe's collection next door.
Tags: library, 770, brooklyn, expansion

Title: Seventh Rebbe inaugurates worldwide tefillin campaign on eve of Six-Day War
Summary: As Israel faced existential threat in 1967, the Seventh Rebbe launched a global tefillin campaign as a spiritual response to the danger.
Story: The campaign echoed the Sixth Rebbe's wartime call for repentance as a means to invoke divine deliverance, and reflected Chabad's view — rooted in Kabbalah and Chasidism — that spiritual transformation precipitates physical salvation. It became one of the Seventh Rebbe's signature 'mivtzoim' (campaigns).
Tags: tefillin, six-day war, israel, seventh rebbe, mivtza

Title: Seventh Rebbe launches tefillin campaign before Six-Day War
Summary: In the weeks before the Six-Day War, the seventh Rebbe initiates the first of Chabad's public mitzvah campaigns.
Story: The campaign entailed Jews donning tefillin in public venues, drawing directly from the Simchat Torah 1930 directive in Riga to 'stand on the street corners and pull Jews into a synagogue.' What had begun as a Western European innovation became the symbol of postwar Chabad outreach worldwide.
Tags: tefillin, six day war, mitzvah campaigns, outreach, seventh rebbe

Title: Six-Day War and liberation of Jerusalem's Old City
Summary: Israel liberated Jerusalem's Old City, ending the Jordanian occupation.
Story: After the war, the area in front of the Western Wall was cleared, creating the broad plaza of today. The first Jew to return to live within the walls of the Old City was Moshe Zvi Segal, who took up residence in the heavily damaged Tzemach Tzedek Shul that had survived the Jordanian occupation.
Tags: six-day-war, jerusalem, old-city, western-wall, israel

Title: Six-Day War triggers Russian Jewish identity awakening
Summary: Israel's victory inspired young Soviet Jews to explore their heritage, fueling a religious awakening nurtured by the Chabad underground.
Story: Many young Russian Jews, including future Knesset Speaker Yuli Edelstein, became students of Chabad rabbis who had continued teaching despite decades of harassment. The same year, the Soviets broke diplomatic relations with Israel, ending Lishkat Hakesher's open activities in Russia and pushing them underground in cooperation with Chabad.
Tags: six-day war, israel, soviet jewry, renaissance

Title: Tefillin campaign launched before Six-Day War
Summary: The seventh Rebbe initiates the first mitzvah campaign, urging Jews to don tefillin even in public venues.
Story: Launched in the weeks before the Six-Day War, the campaign was the first of the Rebbe's public mitzvah initiatives. It traced directly back to the 1930 Simchat Torah talk in Riga, where the sixth Rebbe called for outreach on street corners — with the future seventh Rebbe present.
Tags: tefillin, six-day-war, mitzvah-campaigns, seventh-rebbe

Title: R. Avraham Ziskind passes away
Summary: R. Avraham Zushe Ziskind passed away in New York on Rosh Chodesh Nisan 5727.
Story: R. Avraham Zushe Ziskind passed away in New York on Rosh Chodesh Nisan 5727 (April 11, 1967). After his marriage he had served as a shochet in New York, engaging extensively in halacha and chassidus, and in his final years headed the avreichim kollel attached to the Rebbe's secretariat.
Tags: avraham ziskind, new york, kollel, yarzheit

Title: Rebbe launches Mivtza Tefillin during Six-Day War
Summary: In Iyar 5727 the Lubavitcher Rebbe announced the worldwide Mivtza Tefillin campaign in connection with the Six-Day War and the ensuing victory.
Story: In Iyar 5727 (May 1967), in the lead-up to and aftermath of the Six-Day War, the Rebbe declared Mivtza Tefillin — a global initiative urging volunteers to help Jewish men, including many entirely unaffiliated, don tefillin. The campaign quickly became one of the Rebbe's signature mivtzaim, but also drew halachic and ideological questions from various rabbinic circles over the summer of 5727.
Tags: mivtza tefillin, six-day war, israel, tefillin, outreach

Title: Tefillin campaign launched during the Six-Day War
Summary: In summer 5727 during the Six-Day War the Rebbe launched the first formal mitzvah campaign — Mivtza Tefillin.
Story: During the Six-Day War in summer 5727 (1967), the Rebbe launched Mivtza Tefillin, the first of his formal mitzvah campaigns, citing the verse that the nations will see G-d's name on Israel — interpreted as the tefillin of the head — and thereby fear them, bringing victory over their enemies.
Tags: tefillin, six day war, mivtzaim, eretz yisrael

Title: Rebbe defends Mivtza Tefillin at Shabbat Bereishit 5728 farbrengen
Summary: At the Shabbat Bereishit 5728 farbrengen the Rebbe systematically answered the questions and objections raised against Mivtza Tefillin.
Story: After receiving numerous queries and challenges to Mivtza Tefillin during the summer, the Rebbe devoted his Shabbat Bereishit 5728 farbrengen (Oct 28, 1967) to addressing them publicly. The edited sicha was printed as its own kuntres opening 'בהיות שהגיעו אלי כמה שאלות וטענות בנוגע לההתעוררות דמבצע תפלין' and was later reprinted in Likkutei Sichot vol. 6 p. 271ff.
Tags: mivtza tefillin, farbrengen, kuntres, likkutei sichot, tefillin

Title: Death of R. Moshe Leib Rotstein
Summary: R. Moshe Leib Rotstein passed away on 9 Marcheshvan 5728.
Story: R. Moshe Leib Rotstein, longtime secretary to the Frierdiker Rebbe and the Rebbe, passed away on 9 Marcheshvan 5728. He had served the Lubavitch movement faithfully from his time in Warsaw through his decades in America.
Tags: moshe leib rotstein, secretary, death

Title: Rebbe responds to Agudat Yisrael attack on Lubavitch
Summary: At his Shabbat Toldot 5728 farbrengen the Rebbe responded to a speaker at the Agudat Yisrael annual convention who attacked him and Lubavitch.
Story: Around the time of the annual Agudat Yisrael leadership convention, one of the speakers publicly attacked the Rebbe and the Lubavitch movement, drawing a comparison to Yitzchak Avinu who loved Esav 'because there was trapping in his mouth.' The Rebbe responded at the Shabbat Toldot 5728 farbrengen (Dec 2, 1967) and at subsequent gatherings, as later published in Sichot Kodesh p. 179ff.
Tags: agudat yisrael, lubavitch, mivtza tefillin, convention

Title: Rabbi Yitzchak Hutner writes Rebbe questioning Mivtza Tefillin halacha
Summary: Rabbi Yitzchak Hutner wrote the Rebbe arguing that Mivtza Tefillin volunteers must tell recipients that parshiyot lie inside the batim, else it is mit'asek.
Story: After reading the Rebbe's Shabbat Bereishit kuntres, Rabbi Yitzchak Hutner — Rosh Yeshiva of Chaim Berlin and author of Pachad Yitzchak — sent his first letter to the Rebbe on Or L'Yom Bet of Parshat Vayeshev 5728. Citing the Ra'ah on one who eats matzah without knowing it is matzah, he argued that many 'tinokot shenishbu' approached by mivtza volunteers had no idea anything was inside the batim, and that without such knowledge the act constituted mit'asek rather than fulfillment of the mitzvah.
Tags: yitzchak hutner, mivtza tefillin, halacha, mit'asek, tinokot shenishbu, chaim berlin, pachad yitzchak

Title: Rebbe publishes index of Rayatz's maamarim and sichos
Summary: In 5728 (1968) the Rebbe edited and published a chronological index of the maamarim and discourses of his father-in-law the Rayatz.
Story: Titled 'Maftech Sifrei Maamarei v'Drushei Admur Mohorayatz,' the booklet built on the registry tradition of organizing maamarim by year of delivery. The Rebbe personally edited the material and gave it to print. The work serves as an essential research tool for tracing the Rayatz's Chassidic discourses across his nesi'us.
Tags: rebbe, rayatz, maamarim, index

Title: Rabbi Hutner sends apology letter after Agudat Yisrael convention reports
Summary: Hearing of the Agudat Yisrael convention attack on the Rebbe, Rabbi Hutner wrote to clarify he had not attended and to apologize if his earlier letter caused pain.
Story: On Yom Rishon of Parshat Vayechi 5728 (Jan 7, 1968), Rabbi Hutner wrote a second letter to the Rebbe after hearing from Rabbi Zalman Gurary about the recent Agudat Yisrael convention and its attacks on the Rebbe. He stressed that he had never attended any such convention, that his earlier halachic letter was strictly private and personal, and asked forgiveness if it had caused any pain — while noting that the Torah content itself was not subject to retraction.
Tags: yitzchak hutner, agudat yisrael, mivtza tefillin, zalman gurary

Title: Rabbi Hutner asks Rebbe to clarify objection to his first letter
Summary: Concerned by the Rebbe's silence, Rabbi Hutner sent a brief note on 16 Tevet 5728 asking him to identify the precise nature of any objection.
Story: On 16 Tevet 5728 (Jan 17, 1968), Rabbi Hutner sent a very short third letter to the Rebbe, asking that he do him the kindness of pointing out the nekudat ha-hakpadah — the precise point of objection — to his original Mivtza Tefillin letter. This brief note appears to have prompted the Rebbe's lengthy detailed reply two days later.
Tags: yitzchak hutner, mivtza tefillin

Title: Rebbe sends detailed halachic reply to Rabbi Hutner on tefillin
Summary: On Erev Shabbat 18 Tevet 5728 the Rebbe wrote a lengthy halachic reply to Rabbi Hutner rejecting the mit'asek concern.
Story: On Erev Shabbat 18 Tevet 5728 (Jan 19, 1968), the Rebbe wrote his major reply in the exchange, drafting it by hand directly on Rabbi Hutner's letter. He marshaled counter-proofs from tefilah (the Rambam's 'as if standing before the Shechinah'), korbanot, etrog and matzah, arguing that 'ein la-davar sof' if one demands knowledge of every halachic detail, and that general awareness of tefillin as a special mitzvah-object suffices. The handwritten draft was typed by the mazkirut and re-edited again in the Rebbe's own hand.
Tags: yitzchak hutner, mivtza tefillin, halacha, mit'asek, tinokot shenishbu, igrot kodesh

Title: Rabbi Hutner replies restating his halachic position to Rebbe
Summary: On Thursday of Parshat Va'era 5728 Rabbi Hutner thanked the Rebbe but insisted that absent knowledge of the parshiyot, Mivtza Tefillin recipients are mit'asek.
Story: On Yom Hamishi of Parshat Va'era 5728 (Jan 25, 1968), Rabbi Hutner wrote back, opening with thanks for the Rebbe's reply but maintaining his original position. He insisted his argument was ikar ha-din and not a mere chashash, brought further proofs from Responsa Rabbi Akiva Eiger §8, the Chavat Daat, and Tosafot Shabbat 11, and concluded that without awareness of the parshiyot the brachah would be in vain.
Tags: yitzchak hutner, mivtza tefillin, halacha, mit'asek, rabbi akiva eiger

Title: Rebbe sends second halachic reply to Rabbi Hutner on tefillin
Summary: On 8 Shevat 5728 the Rebbe wrote his second reply to Rabbi Hutner, distinguishing mistaken knowledge from absence of knowledge.
Story: On 8 Shevat 5728 (Feb 7, 1968), the Rebbe responded a second time, opening by noting that Rabbi Hutner had not addressed his core proofs from tefilah and korban. He drew a sharp distinction between mistaken knowledge ('kasavur she'hu basar') as in the Shulchan Aruch HaRav on matzah, versus mere absence of knowledge, and added new chiddushim from the Alter Rebbe's pesakim on tefillin.
Tags: yitzchak hutner, mivtza tefillin, halacha, mit'asek, shulchan aruch harav, alter rebbe

Title: Rabbi Hutner sends third letter defending his position to Rebbe
Summary: On 13 Shevat 5728 Rabbi Hutner sent his third and final letter, restating his arguments and adding a story about tinokot shenishbu extending both hands.
Story: On 13 Shevat 5728 (Feb 12, 1968), Rabbi Hutner sent his third reply, opening with thanks for 'a second utterance' from the Rebbe while reiterating his prior reservations. He elaborated his mit'asek argument with proofs from Rabbi Akiva Eiger §8, the Chavat Daat, the Alter Rebbe's Kuntres Acharon on safek p'sik reisha, and Tosafot Shabbat 11. In a postscript he relayed Rabbi Zalmanov's recent report of seeing tinokot shenishbu offering both hands for tefillin — illustrating, in his view, how complete their unfamiliarity could be.
Tags: yitzchak hutner, mivtza tefillin, halacha, mit'asek, zalmanov

Title: First Beis Chabad opens in Los Angeles
Summary: The first Beis Chabad opened in Los Angeles in 5729; its golden key was sent to the Rebbe.
Story: In 5729 (1969) the first 'Beis Chabad' opened in Los Angeles, and its golden key was delivered to the Rebbe. The Rebbe replied to those presenting the key that a chain of Chabad Houses would now spread across the length and breadth of the country, and wrote a special letter marking the occasion.
Tags: los angeles, beis chabad, california, united states

Title: Passing of R' Yochanan Gordon
Summary: R' Yochanan Gordon, longtime gabbai of 770 and director of the Shomrei Shabbos gemach, passed away on Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5729.
Story: R' Yochanan Gordon, the longtime gabbai of 770 Eastern Parkway and a fixture of Chabad communal institutions in New York, passed away on Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5729. After his death, leadership of the Shomrei Shabbos gemach he had directed alone since 5714 passed to his son-in-law R' Shimon Goldman, who continued its work for many years thereafter.
Tags: new york, yochanan gordon, 770, obituary, shomrei shabbos

Title: Rebbe references searching Rayatz's general index in Riga
Summary: On 25 Tishrei 5730, during nichum aveilim for Rashag, the Rebbe recalls searching the general index of his father-in-law in Riga.
Story: In Sichos Kodesh 5730 p. 719, recorded during the consolation visit for Rashag (Rabbi Shemaryahu Gurary), the Rebbe says 'I looked for this when I was in Riga, in the index of my father-in-law.' The reference confirms the general index was already a working scholarly tool while Rayatz lived in Latvia.
Tags: rebbe, rayatz, riga, manuscripts, rashag, shiva

Title: Wedding of Feigel to Menachem Mendel Wolf
Summary: On 15 Kislev 5730 the author's daughter Feigel married Menachem Mendel (Mani) Wolf at the Menorah hall in Boro Park.
Story: The match was arranged by son-in-law Binyamin Klein, who proposed Feigel to the Wolfs while they were waiting for yechidus; in the yechidus the Rebbe himself raised the same suggestion. The wedding was on 15 Kislev 5730 (November 24, 1969) at the Menorah hall in Boro Park, and the couple later settled in Nachalat Har Chabad in Eretz Yisrael.
Tags: wedding, wolf, boro park, shidduch, shadchanus, nachalat har chabad

Title: Hemshech 5666 published bound
Summary: At the beginning of 5731 the bound volumes of Hemshech 5666 were finally received from the binder.
Story: At the start of 5731 (fall 1970) Kehot received the bound copies of the long-delayed Hemshech 5666. The author distributed the bottle of wine the Rebbe had given him in 5725 to all the workers involved and gave each a bound copy. The Rebbe responded via Rabbi Chadakov, 'Their merit is very great; may it stand for them in this world and the next, I will mention them at the Tziyun.'
Tags: hemshech 5666, kehot, rashab, chadakov

Title: Likkutei Levi Yitzchak printed by Kehot
Summary: Kehot published Likkutei Levi Yitzchak on Zohar and on Tanya in 5730 from Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson's exile-era glosses.
Story: The marginal notes that Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson wrote on his few books during his Soviet exile of 5699-5704 (1939-1944) miraculously reached his son the Rebbe, who from 5730-5743 (1970-1983) prepared them for print. The first volumes — Likkutei Levi Yitzchak on Zohar and on Tanya — were published by Kehot in 5730 (1970).
Tags: levi yitzchak schneerson, kehot, zohar, tanya

Title: R' Yisrael Poizner brings Baal Shem Tov kettle to the Rebbe
Summary: Around 5730 R' Yisrael Poizner of Klimovitch brought to the Rebbe a small kettle attributed to the Baal Shem Tov.
Story: R' Yisrael Poizner had purchased the small kettle in Samarkand in 5726 from a member of Anash, who said it was among the vessels left by R' Chaim Kavash and was used by the Baal Shem Tov. In 5729 the kettle was smuggled across the Soviet border to Eretz Yisrael via R' Avraham Leib Godin of Riga, and around 5730 Poizner presented it to the Rebbe with an accompanying letter of provenance.
Tags: baal shem tov, kettle, poizner, samarkand, klimovitch, smuggling

Title: Rebbe announces completion of Moshiach Torah scroll

Summary: Tuvia Pereshel published a facsimile of a 1772 manuscript Haggadah by the scribe Netanel ben Aharon Segal in New York.

Title: Rebbe's 70th birthday: Vaad 71 Mosdos established

Summary: On 24 Elul 5734 the Rebbe issued a special call for every woman and girl to light Shabbos candles.

Summary: Tuvia Pereshel published a facsimile of an illustrated 1782 Kitse-community manuscript Haggadah in New York.

Title: Family Purity campaign launched on 15 Tammuz

Story: In a special sicha on 15 Tammuz 5735 (1975), the Rebbe directed the launching of a broad education and outreach campaign to strengthen family purity observance (Likkutei Sichos vol. 13 pp. 259-260). This established family purity as one of the ongoing mivtzaim of Chabad.

Summary: In 5736 the Rebbe sent his first group of shluchim to Eretz Yisrael, including the Greismans, to found the Chabad neighborhood in Tzfat.

Story: Gurkov was the father-in-law of Yisrael Yehuda Levin and one of the first Anash to comply with the Rebbe Rayatz's 1946-1949 directive to record memoirs of Soviet-era religious work. His volume became a foundational primary source for the history of Chabad in the Soviet Union.

Summary: On the eve of Shabbat Mevarchim Menachem Av 5736, the Rebbe called for study of the laws of the Beit HaMikdash during the Three Weeks.
Story: In a special sichah delivered on Thursday night, the eve of Shabbat Mevarchim Menachem Av 5736 (1976), the Rebbe urged the study of topics related to the Beit HaBechirah during the days of Bein HaMetzarim. Title: Death of Chaya Mushka Garfinkel in New York
Summary: Chaya Mushka Garfinkel, daughter of R' Asher Grossman of Nikolayev, passed away in New York on Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5736.

Tags: garfinkel, new-york, passing, grossman-family

Title: Yagdil Torah institute founded on 20 Av
Summary: At a 20 Av 5736 farbrengen the Rebbe announced founding centers in Jerusalem and New York to collect the Rebbeim's chiddushei Torah.
Story: At the 20 Menachem Av 5736 (1976) farbrengen, the Rebbe announced the founding of a special institute — with centers in both Jerusalem and New York — to collect novellae of the Lubavitcher Rebbeim and publish them in a special compilation. The publication was later named 'Yagdil Torah.'

Story: Published in the supplements to Hemshech BeSha'a SheHikdimu 5672 vol. 3 (1993 edition, p. 12), the sicha describes how, when his father-in-law had to leave his home, Rayatz sought someone he could trust to keep the manuscripts and return them intact — and apparently had no choice but to entrust them to him. Title: Chabad manuscript collection returned from Warsaw to New York
Summary: In early 5738 the manuscript collection of the Chabad Rebbes, lost in occupied Warsaw since 1939, was returned to the central Chabad library in New York.
Story: When the Nazis occupied Warsaw at the start of 5700, the precious manuscript collection of the Chabad Rebbes was lost for thirty-eight years. It was eventually located in a library in Warsaw. At the beginning of 5738 (late 1977) the collection was returned to the central Chabad library at 770 in Brooklyn, rejoining the corpus from which scholars continue to edit and publish the Chasidic teachings of the Rebbes.

Title: Death of R. Yosef Avraham Kagan
Summary: R. Yosef Avraham Kagan, longtime chief secretary of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw, passed away in 5737.
Story: R. Yosef Avraham Kagan, who had served as chief secretary of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw before emigrating to London in 1939, died in 5737 (1977). He had lived out his life in London after his marriage there.

Title: Kfar Chabad Haggadah with additions on matzah campaign
Summary: A Kfar Chabad Haggadah added material on chametz, matzah, the Mivtza Matzah campaign, and the 12 Pesukim was published.
Story: In 5737 (1977), Kfar Chabad published a Haggadah following the Alter Rebbe's nusach with added sections on chametz and matzah, the Mivtza Matzah campaign, and the 12 Pesukim (twelve verses). The 69-page duodecimo edition served the Israeli Chabad community. It exemplified the Rebbe's worldwide matzah campaign.

Title: Lost manuscripts found and returned to Lubavitch
Summary: The three crates of manuscripts seized by the Nazis from Otwock and considered lost for decades are located and returned in the summer of 5737.
Story: The three crates of ancient Chabad manuscripts — Torah and correspondence of the Alter Rebbe and the five Chabad Rebbes who followed him — had been held by the American Embassy in Berlin before the US entered the war, then seized when the Germans confiscated embassy property. They were considered lost for decades, until summer 5737, when they were located and returned, as recorded in the 'Sifriyas Lubavitch' chapter 11.

Title: Poland returns Chabad manuscripts to the movement
Summary: The Polish government returned Chabad manuscripts to the movement in 1977, an act later cited as precedent by the Moscow delegation when lobbying other governments to pressure the USSR.
Story: Veronika and the delegation cited the 1977 Polish return of Chabad writings as proof that Eastern European governments could and did restore confiscated Jewish religious texts. The precedent was used to argue that Poland, Britain, Israel and the United States should pressure Gorbachev to do the same with the Schneersohn library. The Polish return was invoked repeatedly in 1991 as the delegation built its diplomatic case.

Title: Shalom Dovber Levine appointed director of the Chabad Library
Summary: Rabbi Shalom Dovber Levine was appointed to direct the Chabad Library in 5737.

From that year onward he began publishing serialized articles drawn from the library's collections — first in Yagdil Torah and later in Kfar Chabad, Heoros U'Biurim, Heichal HaBesht and other journals. These articles later formed the basis of his book MiBeit HaGenazim.

Title: R. Meir Blizinski recounts Otwock founding in letter of 13 Shevat 5737
Summary: On 13 Shevat 5737, R. Meir Blizinski wrote to his grandson R. S. Heber describing how he founded the Otwock branch in 5686.

Shlomo Tziley, and the eventual collapse of the branch in spring 5687. The letter became the primary first-person source for understanding the Otwock branch's brief existence.

Title: NYC Mayor Beame presents Rebbe city medallion shaped as a cup
Summary: On 11 Nissan 5737, NYC Mayor Abraham Beame presented the Rebbe a city medallion shaped like a cup.
Story: On 11 Nissan 5737 (March 30, 1977), New York City Mayor Abraham Beame presented the Rebbe with a medallion of the city, fashioned in the shape of a cup. Title: Pereshel facsimile of Aharon Schreiber Erlangen's 1751 Vienna Haggadah
Summary: Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of the 1751 Vienna manuscript Haggadah by Aharon Schreiber Erlangen.
Story: In 5738 (1978), Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of a Haggadah manuscript written in Vienna in 5511 (1751) by Aharon Schreiber Erlangen. Title: Shaar HaMilu'im IV of Tzemach Tzedek printed
Summary: In 5738 the fourth Shaar HaMilu'im volume was printed, gathering responsa, chiddushim, and piskei dinim that had been discovered in the years since the previous milu'im publication.
Story: By 5738 a further wave of newly surfaced material had accumulated, warranting another supplementary volume. Title: Institute for preparing Rebbeim's maamarim founded on Shavuos 5738
Summary: On Shavuos 5738 the Rebbe announced founding an institute to prepare the Rebbeim's chassidic discourses for print.
Story: In a special sicha on Shavuos 5738 (1978), the Rebbe announced the opening of an institute dedicated to preparing the chassidic discourses of the previous Rebbeim for publication. The institute produced the series of Maamarei Admur HaZaken, Maamarei Admur HaEmtzaei, Ohr HaTorah of the Tzemach Tzedek, Toras Shmuel of the Rebbe Maharash, and Sefer HaMaamarim of the Rashab and Rayatz — about two hundred new volumes prepared from manuscript.

Title: Rebbe launches Maamarei Admur HaZaken editing project on Shavuos 5738
Summary: At a Shavuos 5738 (June 1978) farbrengen the Rebbe announced the founding of a system to edit and publish the rebbes' discourses from manuscript.
Story: The Rebbe's Shavuos announcement gave rise to a long-running editorial enterprise whose first major output was the multi-volume series Maamarei Admur HaZaken. Over the following years more than twenty volumes appeared, mostly arranged by the year each maamar was originally said.

Title: Rebbe issues call to print Tanya in every Jewish locale, Eikev 5738
Summary: In a special talk on Motzei Shabbos Parshas Eikev 5738 (August 1978) the Rebbe directed that the Tanya be printed in every locality where Jews live.
Story: The Rebbe's directive launched what became a global mivtza of Tanya printing. By the time of writing, the Tanya had been printed more than five thousand times—often by mobile presses brought to distant cities—each printing carrying the imprimatur of the local Jewish community.

Title: Toras Levi Yitzchak Yalkut Shimoni supplement published
Summary: Kehot published a Toras Levi Yitzchak supplement on Yalkut Shimoni and tractate Gittin in 5739.
Story: In 5739 (1979), Kehot published a supplementary volume of Toras Levi Yitzchak — comprising glosses on Yalkut Shimoni and on tractate Gittin from Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson's exile-era writings.

Title: Marina Rosche becomes nucleus for underground Moscow yeshivah
Summary: In the late 1980s, as Communism weakened, students studied more openly at Moscow's Marina Rosche Chabad synagogue.
Story: Students educated during those late-Communist years formed the nucleus sustaining Jewish life in Moscow until and after the Soviet collapse.
Tags: marina-rosche, moscow, underground

Title: Pereshel-Weintraub facsimile of the Hamburg 1728 Abarbanel Haggadah
Summary: Tuvia Pereshel and Munish Weintraub issued in New York a facsimile of the Hamburg 1728 Abarbanel Haggadah by Yaakov Sofer of Berlin.
Story: In 5740 (1980), Tuvia Pereshel and Munish Weintraub published in New York a facsimile of an illustrated manuscript Haggadah by Yaakov Sofer of Berlin, who had copied it from the 1695 Amsterdam edition. Title: Rebbe begins efforts to recover Chabad library from Moscow
Summary: From 5741 onward the Rebbe directed emissaries to work for the return of the Chabad library held in Moscow since World War I.
Story: When the Rebbe Rashab fled Lubavitch in World War I, he placed the family library in storage in Moscow with the intention of retrieving it after the war. After the Soviet takeover, the books were nationalized and moved into the Russian State Library, where they remain. Beginning in 5741 (1980), the seventh Rebbe sent dedicated emissaries to Russia and pursued every avenue to secure their return, an effort that continues today.

Title: Sh. D. Levin begins editing Igrot Kodesh series
Summary: In 5740, the Lubavitcher Rebbe assigned R' Shalom DovBer Levin the editing of Igrot Kodesh of the Chabad Rebbes.
Story: Starting in 5740 (1980), at the Lubavitcher Rebbe's directive, R' Shalom DovBer Levin began assembling and editing the Igrot Kodesh series of the Chabad Rebbes' letters. The historical research generated by this editorial work became the seed material for the Toldot Chabad volumes — including this one on Tsarist Russia.

Title: Shaglov publishes index of the Rebbe's maamarim, sichos and letters
Summary: In 5740 (1980) R. Yosef Yitzchak Shaglov prepared and printed an index of the Rebbe's maamarim, sichos and letters.
Story: The volume, titled 'Maftech Maamarim Sichos uMichtavim,' continued the line of chronological registries begun by the Rayatz for earlier Rebbeim. By the early 1980s registries had been compiled for all the Rebbeim except the Tzemach Tzedek, whose maamarim posed special chronological difficulties because most were preserved undated in volumes organized by Tanach and Chazal rather than by year.

Title: Aseres HaDibros children's campaign announced

Story: In a special sicha on Erev Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5740 (1980), the Rebbe announced a special Shavuos campaign — that all children, even toddlers, be brought to synagogue to hear the reading of the Aseres HaDibros (Likkutei Sichos vol. 23 p. 50).

Title: Rebbe issues call against family planning on Shabbos Naso
Summary: On Shabbos Parshas Naso 5740 the Rebbe issued a special call against family planning.

Title: Maamarei Admur HaZaken HaKtzarim editing project begins
Summary: In 5741 (1981), work began on compiling Maamarei Admur HaZaken HaKtzarim, the Liozna-period short maamarim of the Alter Rebbe.
Story: The Rebbe directed the editor to arrange the discourses by the order of Torah verses, then by Sages' sayings. Summary: Tuvia Pereshel and Munish Weintraub issued in New York a facsimile of the 1662 Amsterdam Haggadah.

Summary: R. Menachem Nachum Preger of Brisk passed away in 5741.
Story: R. Menachem Nachum Preger passed away in 5741 (1980-1981). Originally from Brisk, he had been accepted to Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock in 5698, fled to Vilna at the war's outbreak, and was saved with the group of students who traveled to Japan, Shanghai, and eventually New York.

Story: In 5741 (1981) the Rebbe founded Tzivos Hashem, the children's organization, building on the verse 'Hakhel… the children' so that even young boys and girls would influence their friends to walk in the ways of Torah and chassidus.

Summary: In Nissan 5741 the Rebbe directed beginning a special Sefer Torah in Jerusalem uniting Jewish children before bar mitzvah.

Title: Publication of Rashimat Maamarei DACh of Maharash and Rashab
Summary: In Iyar 5741 (May 1981) the Rashimat Maamarei DACh of the Maharash and Rashab was published, incorporating over two hundred newly identified maamarim.
Story: R. Naftali Greenberg compiled supplements to the existing registries based on manuscripts in the Rebbe's library, identifying more than two hundred Maharash maamarim missing from the 1947 list. Title: Tomchei Tmimim and Beis Rivkah Sifrei Torah announced
Summary: On the eve of Rosh Hashana 5742 the Rebbe directed beginning a Sefer Torah for Tomchei Tmimim students and one for Beis Rivkah girls.
Story: In a special sicha on the eve of Rosh Hashana 5742 (1981), the Rebbe directed the writing of a special Sefer Torah by Yeshivas Tomchei Tmimim for its students, and a separate Sefer Torah by Beis Rivkah for its female students.

Summary: Tuvia Pereshel and Munish Weintraub published in New York a facsimile of the Frankfurt 1710 'Mateh Aharon' Haggadah.

Title: Wedding of Rachel Klein and Mendel Gordon
Summary: On 3 Shevat 5742, the author's granddaughter Rachel Klein married Mendel Gordon, who would serve as a ram in the Lubavitch yeshiva of London.

Title: Death of R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky
Summary: R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky passed away on 7 Marcheshvan 5743 after decades of service to Chabad institutions.
Story: On 7 Marcheshvan 5743, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky passed away. His tombstone records his energetic work for Chabad institutions in Eretz Yisrael, his role as one of the planters of the Chabad orchard in America, his closeness to the Rebbeim, his decades of rabbinical service, and his outreach work, particularly with youth, up until his final day.

Summary: On Parshat Miketz 5743 the Rebbe explained the differences between Sefardic and Ashkenazi customs regarding naming children after living relatives.
Story: In a sicha delivered on Parshat Miketz 5743 (December 1982), printed in Hisvaaduyos vol. 43, the Rebbe Menachem Mendel addressed the differing customs between Sefardim and Ashkenazim regarding naming a child after a living grandparent. Summary: Tuvia Pereshel issued in New York a facsimile of the 1722 Offenbach 'Avodat HaGefen' Haggadah by Yehuda Leib and his son Ze'ev Wolf.
Story: In 5743 (1983), Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of the 1722 Offenbach Haggadah with the 'Avodat HaGefen' commentary by Yehuda Leib ben Eliyahu and his son Ze'ev Wolf. Title: Polish National Library collection identified as Rebbe's books
Summary: In 1983 microfilm copies of the Polish National Library's collection of the Rebbe's books were discovered in Canada, sparking an investigation.
Story: Two years later a Canadian student visiting the Warsaw library was given an actual manuscript of the Rebbe's that eventually reached Toronto rabbis. Title: Publication of Maamarei Admor HaZaken (collected discourses of the Alter Rebbe) in New York
Summary: A collection of the Alter Rebbe's Chassidic discourses on the Torah portions and festivals was published in New York.
Story: In 5743 (1983), 'Maamarei Admor HaZaken' was published in New York, containing the Chabad Alter Rebbe Schneur Zalman of Liadi's Chassidic discourses on the Torah portions and festivals. Title: Shmuel Horowitz's Yiddish children's Haggadah 'V'Higadta L'Vincha' in New York
Summary: Shmuel Horowitz published 'V'Higadta L'Vincha' in Yiddish, a children's Mah Nishtanah and Seder guide with illustrations, in New York.
Story: In 5743 (1983), Shmuel Horowitz published in New York 'V'Higadta L'Vincha', a Yiddish-language children's guide containing Mah Nishtanah, Seder laws and customs for cheder-aged children, with explanations and illustrations. Title: Toras Levi Yitzchak Tehillim and Purim supplement published
Summary: Kehot published a Toras Levi Yitzchak supplement on Tehillim and Purim in 5743.
Story: In 5743 (1983), Kehot published the final supplement of Toras Levi Yitzchak, comprising notes on Tehillim and on Purim from Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson's writings. This concluded the publishing of his Soviet-exile glosses that the Rebbe had been preparing since 5730.

Title: Wedding of Feigel Klein and Levi Yitzchak Sudak

Title: R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal passes away in New York
Summary: R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal, longtime Rosh Mesivta of Tomchei Tmimim and former Rosh Yeshiva in Vilna, passed away in New York on 12 Adar 5743.
Story: R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal, born in Svintzian in 5671, was among the earliest students of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim, later its Rosh Yeshiva, and eventually a longtime Rosh Mesivta at Tomchei Tmimim in New York. Title: Certificate of honor for the Rebbe from US president and Congress, 11 Nisan 5743
Summary: For the Rebbe's 11 Nisan 5743 birthday in 1983, the US president, senators, and members of Congress signed a certificate of honor naming the day a national Day of Education.
Story: Coordinated annually in Washington by shliach Rabbi Avraham Shemtov, the 1983 certificate paired with Congressional Record speeches and a presidential greeting letter, anchoring the recurring 11 Nisan Day of Education in the United States.

Title: R. Z. Veliszher reminiscence published in Kfar Chabad magazine
Summary: On 27 MarCheshvan 5744 (Nov 1983), Kfar Chabad magazine issue 118 published R. M. Z. Gringlas's note recording R. Zalman Veliszher's recollection of the Rashab's 1903 talk.
Story: Gringlas's account preserves R. Zalman's recollection that as the Rashab uttered 'lo shamati,' he turned his head and confirmed: 'It is not written lo yadati but lo shamati.' The note resolves the textual puzzle that the Rashab had raised about R. Levi Yitzchok's letter.

Story: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Kasher, who edited and published the Rogatchover's Tzofnat Paneach series including the Klalei HaTorah V'HaMitzvot volumes, passed away on 27 Marcheshvan 5744 (November 3, 1983). The continuation of his publication project passed to others.

Title: Rebbe reaffirms mivtza Tanya on 3 Shvat 5744
Summary: On Shabbos Parshas Bo, 3 Shvat 5744 (January 7, 1984), the Rebbe again called for the worldwide printing of the Tanya in a special talk.
Story: The 3 Shvat 5744 sicha reignited mivtza Tanya several years after its 1978 launch and brought renewed momentum to local Tanya printings in cities around the globe.

Title: Daily Rambam study program instituted on Acharon shel Pesach
Summary: On Acharon shel Pesach 5744 the Rebbe instituted daily Rambam study in three tracks.
Story: In a special sicha on Acharon shel Pesach 5744 (1984), the Rebbe instituted the daily study of Rambam's Mishneh Torah in three tracks — three chapters per day, one chapter per day, and Sefer HaMitzvos (Likkutei Sichos vol. 27 p. 229).

Title: The poet Zelda Mishkovsky-Schneersohn passes away
Summary: Zelda Schneersohn Mishkovsky, the celebrated Hebrew poet and cousin of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, passed away on 27 Nissan 5744.
Story: Zelda Schneersohn Mishkovsky, the renowned Hebrew poet and only child of Rabbi Shalom Shlomo Schneersohn and Rachel Chen, passed away on 27 Nissan 5744. Summary: On Shabbos Bereishis 5745 the Rebbe announced the 'shliach oseh shliach' program to appoint additional shluchim.

Title: Didan Notzach library trial begins in U.S. federal court
Summary: In 5745 a U.S. federal lawsuit was filed by a grandson of the Rebbe Rayatz claiming personal ownership of part of the Chabad library.
Story: In 5745 (1985) a grandson of the Rebbe Rayatz initiated proceedings claiming that a portion of the central Chabad library belonged to him personally. Title: Italian facsimile of the 15th-century Yoel ben Shimon Haggadah from the British Library
Summary: A facsimile of a 15th-century Haggadah manuscript by Yoel ben Shimon Feibush from the British Library was published in Italy.

Title: Paris Haggadah of the Rebbe with French translation

Title: Pereshel facsimile of the Sulzbach 1755 Abarbanel Haggadah
Summary: Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of the 1755 Sulzbach Abarbanel Haggadah.

Title: Publication of Maamarei Admur HaEmtza'i (Mittler Rebbe) discourses in New York
Summary: Two volumes of the Mittler Rebbe Dovber's discourses on Vayikra were published in New York.
Story: In 5745-5746 (1985-1986), 'Maamarei Admur HaEmtza'i' (the Mittler Rebbe Dovber Schneuri) on Sefer Vayikra was published in New York in two octavo volumes. Title: Rabbi Aaron Rakeffet visits Riga on covert Mossad mission
Summary: Rabbi Dr. Aaron Rakeffet is dispatched to the Soviet Union as a covert Mossad agent and discovers a vibrant Riga community.
Story: Rakeffet was surprised to find at the Riga synagogue a group of older Jews who had held on through Communism. After the service, he was told to wait until the government agents left, then 'they broke out vodka and cake, and we sat and had a farbrengen.' The Rebbe's six-year stay in Riga half a century earlier was still 'what kept them going all those years.'

Story: During a summer 5746 (1986) visit to Jerusalem, R' Sh. D. Levin consulted the genealogist R' Shmuel Gur on the disputed question of whether R' Shmuel ben Bezalel (grandson of the Maharal) had any sons. Gur pointed him to a Prague tombstone inscription that resolved the question and validated the Rebbe Rayatz's family tradition.

Title: Chabad Persian-translation Haggadah by Yehoshua Netaneli

Title: Kfar Chabad Haggadah with 'V'Higadta L'Vincha' practical guide by Yekutiel Green

Title: Polish non-Jew brings Shu't Maharik with Alter Rebbe's glosses to America
Summary: A Polish non-Jew arrived in America carrying a copy of Shu't Maharik bearing handwritten glosses by the Alter Rebbe.
Story: In the summer of 5746 (1986), a Polish non-Jew arrived in the United States carrying a copy of Shu't Maharik (Lvov 5558) with handwritten glosses by the Alter Rebbe in its margins. The book was acquired by a Chabad chassid and returned to the Chabad library — joining the small group of surviving books bearing the Alter Rebbe's own hand to escape the Lyadi fires.

Title: Publication of Klalei HaTorah V'HaMitzvot volume 3

Title: Tel Aviv facsimile of the Copenhagen Haggadah by Uri Feivush ben Yitzchak
Summary: A facsimile of the 1739 Copenhagen Haggadah by Uri Feivush ben Yitzchak Segal was published in Tel Aviv by Nahar and Steimatzky.

Title: Yossi Rosenstein illustrated Haggadah with English translation published in Jerusalem
Summary: Yossi Rosenstein illustrated a Haggadah with English translation that was printed in Jerusalem.
Story: In 5746 (1986), an illustrated Haggadah by Yossi Rosenstein was printed in Jerusalem with an English translation. Title: R' Yaakov Landa, rabbi of Bnei Brak, passes away
Summary: R' Yaakov Landa passed away on 26 Shevat 5746 after fifty years as rabbi of Bnei Brak.
Story: After serving Bnei Brak as its rabbi for a full jubilee — fifty years — R' Yaakov Landa passed away on 26 Shevat 5746 (February 5, 1986). Title: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz passes away
Summary: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz passed away in New York on Erev Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni 5746.
Story: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz passed away in New York on Erev Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni 5746 (March 11, 1986). He had served as a gabbai of the 770 synagogue and a member of the executive of Agudas Chassidei Chabad, Vaad HaMesader, Vaad LeHafatzas Chassidus, Vaad HaMaamad, and Vaad Kupas Bachurim.

Title: Wedding of Sterna Sarah Klein and Levi Yitzchak Krinsky
Summary: On 17 Sivan 5746, Sterna Sarah Klein married Levi Yitzchak Krinsky, future director of the Chabad House in Manchester, New Hampshire.
Story: Sterna Sarah, daughter of Leah and Yerachmiel Binyamin HaLevi Klein, married Levi Yitzchak Krinsky on 17 Sivan 5746. Levi Yitzchak Krinsky serves as director of the Chabad House in Manchester, New Hampshire.
