Title: Children's home declared a Beis Chabad on Shabbos Vayigash
Summary: On Shabbos Vayigash 5747 the Rebbe directed Tzivos Hashem children to designate a room in their home as a Beis Chabad.
Story: On Shabbos Parshas Vayigash 5747 (December 1986), the Rebbe directed children of Tzivos Hashem to fix a special sign in their home declaring that the room — or the home — is a 'Beis Chabad' (Hisva'aduyos 5747 pp. 208-212).

Title: Didan Notzach — Chabad Library trial concludes in favor of Agudas Chassidei Chabad
Summary: In 5747 the U.S. court ruled that the entire library belongs to Agudas Chassidei Chabad and not to any individual heir.
Story: In 5747 (1987) the court issued its ruling: the Rebbeim had not held the library as personal property and the entire collection belonged to Agudas Chassidei Chabad. Following the verdict, the Rebbe launched a massive book-donation campaign and ordered the two parallel libraries — the Rayatz's and his own — to be merged into a single central library of Agudas Chassidei Chabad. The day of the verdict, 5 Tevet, entered the Chabad calendar as 'Didan Notzach.'

Title: Haggadat Am published by Adamah with English translation by Mordechai HaCohen
Summary: Adamah Press published 'Haggadat Am' with English translation by Mordechai HaCohen and illustrations by Chaim Ron.
Story: In 5747 (1987), Adamah Press in the Holy Land issued 'Haggadat Am', translated and commented in English by Mordechai HaCohen and illustrated by Chaim Ron. Title: Hebrew-English Haggadah for children illustrated by Nachum Waldman and Boruch Gorkin
Summary: A children's Haggadah following the Alter Rebbe's nusach was published in New York with English translation by Yaakov Emanuel Schochet and illustrations by Nachum Waldman and Boruch Gorkin.
Story: Around 5747 (1987), a Haggadah following the Chabad Alter Rebbe's nusach was published in New York with English translation by Yaakov Emanuel Schochet and illustrations by Nachum Waldman and Boruch Gorkin. Summary: Menachem Mendel Brod edited a Kfar Chabad Haggadah with a 'Pesach BiTzva'im' (Pesach in Color) photographic children's booklet.
Story: In 5747 (1987), Menachem Mendel Brod edited a 40-page Haggadah printed in blue letters in Kfar Chabad, accompanied by a 22-leaf 'Pesach BiTzva'im' (Pesach in Color) booklet with photographs and illustrations for the Seder night. Title: Leeds Chabad children's Haggadah with English translation
Summary: A children's Chabad Haggadah translated into English and illustrated for children was published by Tzeirei Agudat Chabad of Leeds.
Story: In 5747 (1987), Tzeirei Agudat Chabad of Leeds published a Haggadah for children translated into English and illustrated. The 67-page octavo edition served the British Chabad children's community. It demonstrated Chabad's commitment to producing locally adapted children's Haggadot worldwide.

Title: Library books trial: artifact collection transferred to library archive
Summary: Following the 5746–47 books trial, the artifact collection from Rayatz's wall cabinet was transferred to the Chabad library archive.
Story: Rebbe Rayatz's yechidus room had contained a wall cabinet holding inherited holy objects, several without provenance markings. After the conclusion of the books-trial saga in 5746–47, this collection — including a much-used black silk sleeve attributed to the Tzemach Tzedek and a silver atarah likely traced to the Chernobyl–Cherkas families — was moved into the library's artifact archive for cataloguing and preservation.

Title: Pereshel facsimile of the Babad Amsterdam 1769 manuscript Haggadah
Summary: Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of the 1769 Amsterdam 'Babad Haggadah' manuscript.
Story: In 5747 (1987), Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of an illustrated manuscript Haggadah written in Amsterdam in 5529 (1769) by Yehoshua ben Mordechai Babad of Volochisk. Title: Tel Aviv facsimile of the Altona 1738 manuscript Haggadah by Yosef ben David of Leipnik
Summary: A facsimile of the 1738 Altona manuscript Haggadah by Yosef ben David of Leipnik was published in Tel Aviv with Abarbanel's commentary.
Story: In 5747 (1987), a facsimile edition of a manuscript Haggadah from the Rosenthaliana Library, written in Altona in 5498 (1738) by Yosef ben David of Leipnik, was published in Tel Aviv. Title: Death of Chaya Frieda Kazarnovsky

Story: R. Mordechai Mentlik passed away in New York on 25 Tishrei 5748 (October 18, 1987). He was the author of the work Amrei Mordechai and served as a member of the executive of Agudas Chassidei Chabad. Beginning when the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in New York and opened Tomchei Tmimim there, R. Mentlik served as the senior rosh yeshiva.

Story: Rabbi Yehuda Krinsky, the Rebbe's secretary, told Rabbi Shalom DovBer Levin that within several weeks a delegation would travel to Moscow. It was to include Rabbi Baruch Shlomo Kunin (head shliach in California), Rabbi Nissan Mindel (the Rebbe's English-language secretary), and Rabbi Levin himself.

Title: Reprint of Hachaltzu for 127th birthday of the Rebbe Rashab
Summary: On 20 Cheshvan 5748 (12 November 1987), Hachaltzu was reissued in a special edition marking 127 years since the birth of the Rebbe Rashab.
Story: For the 127th birthday of the Rebbe Rashab, the Hachaltzu kuntres was reprinted in a special edition. Story: Levin asked whether manuscripts brought from Leningrad by Prof. A.I. Katz indicated more items still lay there, whether to chase materials seized in 1927, and whether to extend the search to Rostov and Dnepropetrovsk. Title: Avraham Meir Pinchas Rodes founds evening kollel for working avreichim
Summary: In 5748 (1988), Avraham Meir Pinchas Rodes founded an evening kollel for working avreichim who learn Torah Monday through Thursday evenings at the Frenkel shul.
Story: Starting in 5748, Avraham Meir Pinchas Rodes established an evening kollel for avreichim whose Torah study is not their primary occupation. Title: Fenton Haggadah illustrated and designed by Zvi Fenton in London
Summary: Zvi Fenton's illustrated and designed 'Fenton Haggadah' was published in London with a supplementary English translation booklet.
Story: In 5748 (1988), 'The Fenton Haggadah' was published in London, designed and illustrated by Zvi Fenton. The 64-page quarto edition was accompanied by a separate 26-page booklet containing an English translation. It served the English-speaking Jewish community of Britain.

Title: Mondshine searches Touro library for missing Maharash letter
Summary: In 5748 (1988), R. Yehoshua Mondshine traveled to Touro College in New York seeking the missing Maharash letter among Leikin's books.
Story: Researcher R. Yehoshua Mondshine traced Leikin's library to Touro College in New York and visited there in 5748 looking for the lost manuscript pages, including the Maharash letter to R. Chaim Yaakov Widrewitz. After being passed between librarians, clerks, and managers, he left empty-handed. The search continued unresolved for over a decade more.

Title: Pereshel facsimile of Meshulam Zimel's 1719 Vienna manuscript Haggadah
Summary: Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of Meshulam Zimel ben Moshe's 1719 Vienna manuscript Haggadah created for Natan Oppenheim.
Story: In 5748 (1988), Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of an illustrated manuscript Haggadah written by Meshulam Zimel ben Moshe in Vienna in 5479 (1719) for Natan Oppenheim. Title: Rebbe affirms all hidden manuscripts were returned after Rayatz's release
Summary: During the 5748 special mission to Russia, the Rebbe is asked whether some 5687 manuscripts may have been left behind, and answers definitively that all were returned immediately.
Story: On the special shlichus to Russia in 5748 — documented in 'Yoman HaShlichus HaMeyuchedes' — the question was put to the Rebbe whether perhaps not all the manuscripts hidden during the 5687 arrest had been recovered, and whether it might be worth searching for them. The Rebbe replied: 'They were returned immediately!!' — closing the question on the manuscript dispersal during the 12 Tammuz episode.

Title: Tel Aviv Haggadah illustrated by Bilha Krieger Barzel
Summary: An illustrated Haggadah by Bilha Krieger Barzel was printed in Tel Aviv.
Story: In 5748 (1988), an illustrated Haggadah by Bilha Krieger Barzel was published in Tel Aviv. The 56-page octavo edition exemplified contemporary Israeli Haggadah artistry. It contributed to the rich late 20th-century tradition of Israeli illustrated Passover texts.
Tags: haggadah, tel aviv, israel, bilha krieger barzel, illustrated

Title: Tomchei Temimim Moscow students seek Rebbe's approval for Lubavitch house
Summary: Students from Tomchei Temimim Moscow sought the Rebbe's approval to purchase a house in Lubavitch.
Story: At the start of 5749 (late 1988), yeshiva students from Tomchei Temimim in Moscow contacted the Rebbe's secretariat requesting approval to purchase a house in the town of Lubavitch. Within a few days, they received the Rebbe's response along with several hundred dollars as his participation in the purchase. The Rebbe wanted to be personally involved in establishing a Chabad presence in Lubavitch.
Tags: lubavitch, moscow, tomchei temimim, beis chabad, 770

Title: Search begins for the Mitteler Rebbe's arrest file in Soviet archives
Summary: During R. Shalom DovBer Levin's mission to Moscow, the Rebbe directs that Russian archives also be searched for the Mitteler Rebbe's arrest file.
Story: In winter 5748 (early 1988), Rabbi Shalom DovBer Levin was dispatched to Moscow to search for the seforim collection of the Rebbeim. Before the trip he wrote to the Rebbe suggesting that R. Nissan Mindel also check the Tsarist government archives for documents related to the Mitteler Rebbe's arrest. The Rebbe replied that the search should extend to documents concerning the Alter Rebbe and the Tzemach Tzedek as well. On Erev Rosh Chodesh Shevat the team visited Hendel Deutsch in Petersburg, who suggested the Khovansky archive might be in Minsk.
Tags: levin, deutsch, soviet union, leningrad, petersburg, archives, mitteler rebbe

Title: Rebbe's Shemot farbrengen frames mission as pidyon shevuyim
Summary: On Shabbat Parshat Shemot 5748 the Rebbe publicly framed the upcoming mission as 'pidyon shevuyim'—redeeming captives—applied to a tzaddik's books.
Story: Without naming the delegation, the Rebbe told his Shabbat farbrengen that one must redeem the books, manuscripts and possessions of righteous leaders from captivity with self-sacrifice. He invoked the Tzemach Tzedek's principle that an emissary is empowered to make on-the-spot decisions, and afterward instructed the three delegation members to say l'chaim on a full cup.
Tags: library, pidyon-shevuyim, shemot, 770, farbrengen, tzemach-tzedek

Title: Yechidus and departure of Chabad library delegation
Summary: On 20 Tevet 5748—Maimonides' yahrzeit—the Rebbe held yechidus with the three delegates before their departure for Moscow.
Story: Speaking in Yiddish, the Rebbe described the trip as 'one unified shlichus' that should function 'like a single body,' gave them three multiples of chai dollars for charity in Russia, and told them to treat every doubt leniently. He concluded: 'I am not thanking you—the greatest thanks will come from the books themselves.'
Tags: library, moscow, yechidus, kunin, mindel, levin, rambam-yahrzeit

Title: Chabad delegation arrives in Moscow
Summary: The delegation landed in Moscow on Monday evening, 21 Tevet 5748, and walked to the Lenin Library to scout its buildings.
Story: The plane arrived at 4:30 PM and the team reached the Hotel Intourist by 7. Realizing the library housing the Schneersohn collection was only a few blocks away, they walked over to inspect its three buildings—the Rumyantsev wing, the Muzei Knigi where the first books had been located, and the high-rise stacks—so they would recognize them in negotiations to come.
Tags: moscow, library, intourist, lenin-library, mission

Title: First negotiating day at the Lenin Library
Summary: On 22 Tevet 5748 the delegation met Lenin Library PR director Olga Diakonova, who refused to admit outside experts to the stacks.
Story: Through Armand Hammer's Moscow office head Nina Vlasova and Deputy Culture Minister Litvinov, the delegation gained a 90-minute meeting at the library. Diakonova rejected their request to search alongside library staff, insisting outsiders had never been permitted into the holdings, and asked them to hand over their lists for internal review. The delegation supplied 12 representative titles and pressed for a reversal.
Tags: moscow, lenin-library, diakonova, litvinov, hammer, vlasova

Title: Library director appeals to Soviet Culture Minister to block search
Summary: On 23 Tevet 5748 the library director wrote to the Soviet Culture Minister opposing Chabad's search request; the delegation visited the Marina Roscha shul.
Story: Diakonova's written objection prompted Nina Vlasova to suggest Hammer escalate directly to Culture Minister Vasily Zakharov. While waiting, the delegation drafted a formal memorandum with Mindel and Hammer's chief aide Jacobs, visited the Marina Roscha synagogue (where they immersed in the mikveh for the Alter Rebbe's yahrzeit), and reported the impasse back to the Rebbe's office in New York.
Tags: moscow, lenin-library, diakonova, marina-roscha, 770, zakharov

Title: Hammer and Kunin meet Soviet Culture Minister Zakharov
Summary: On the Alter Rebbe's yahrzeit, R' Kunin accompanied Armand Hammer to meet Soviet Culture Minister Vasily Zakharov.
Story: On 24 Tevet 5748—the yahrzeit of the founder of Chabad—the delegation finalized a supplemental memorandum laying out the documentary case that the Schneersohn collection had grown to roughly 7,000 titles by 1915. R' Kunin then joined Hammer for the high-level meeting with the Culture Minister, the escalation toward which the impasse had been pointing.
Tags: moscow, hammer, zakharov, library, kunin, alter-rebbe-yahrzeit

Title: Beis Chabad house purchased in Lubavitch
Summary: A house was purchased in Lubavitch on 21 Marcheshvan 5749 to serve as a Beis Chabad.
Story: On 20 Marcheshvan 5749 (November 1988), the yeshiva students traveled to Lubavitch to find a house for sale. After a day of searching, they found the only house available for purchase, and on 21 Marcheshvan it was purchased in the name of student Nachum Tamarin. They added the inscription '770 - Beis Chabad' on the gate. The Rebbe subsequently called it 'Beis Schneersohn.'
Tags: lubavitch, beis chabad, 770, nachum tamarin

Title: Beit Chabad established in Lubavitch
Summary: In 5749, a courtyard and house were purchased in Lubavitch and turned into a Beit Chabad to host visitors to the Ohel.
Story: In 5749 (1989), a courtyard with a house was acquired in Lubavitch and converted into a Beit Chabad. The house serves as a gathering point for travelers visiting the Ohel: there they write their pidyon notes before walking to the holy gravesite.
Tags: lubavitch, beit chabad, soviet collapse

Title: Haggadah 'BiMesila' anthology of Zidichov dynasty teachings published in New York
Summary: Moshe Aharon Moshkovitz compiled and published in New York the 'BiMesila' Haggadah anthology of teachings from the Zidichov, Komarno, Sambor, and Rozdol dynasties.
Story: In 5749 (1989), Moshe Aharon Moshkovitz published in New York the Haggadah 'BiMesila', a collection of Torah novellae from the Chassidic dynasties of Zidichov, Komarno, Sambor, and Rozdol, drawn from the writings of the Rebbes and their descendants. The 232-page octavo work gathered material from printed books and manuscripts. It served as a comprehensive anthology of these closely related Galician Chassidic courts.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, zidichov, komarno, new york, moshkovitz

Title: Jerusalem Haggadah 'Hallel Nirtzeh' and 'Chasdei David' by Greenwald brothers
Summary: A Haggadah featuring the 'Hallel Nirtzeh' commentary by Moshe Greenwald and 'Chasdei David' by Eliezer David Greenwald was issued in Jerusalem.
Story: In 5749 (1989), a Haggadah featuring two commentaries by the brothers Moshe Greenwald ('Hallel Nirtzeh') and Eliezer David Greenwald ('Chasdei David') was published in Jerusalem by Kollel Arugat HaBosem. The 177-page edition included drashot for Shabbat HaGadol and explanations of Sefirat HaOmer and Ketzirat HaOmer alongside laws of bedikat and biur chametz. It was published in honor of the wedding of Eliezer Tzvi and Leah Toiba Safrin.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, greenwald, jerusalem, arugat habosem

Title: Ohel of the Rebbes in Lubavitch rebuilt
Summary: In 5749, Rabbis Dovid Nachshon and Avi Taub rebuilt the Ohel of the Rebbes in Lubavitch.
Story: In 5749 (1989), Rabbi Dovid Nachshon and Rabbi Avi Taub rebuilt the Ohel of the Rebbes in Lubavitch over the graves of the Tzemach Tzedek and Maharash. From that point onward, Anash began traveling regularly to Lubavitch to visit the courtyard of the Rebbes and pray at the Ohel. The restoration coincided with the opening of the Soviet Union.
Tags: lubavitch, ohel, soviet collapse, dovid nachshon, avi taub

Title: Ohel rebuilt in Lubavitch
Summary: The ohel in Lubavitch was rebuilt by R' David Nachshon and R' Avi Taub.
Story: In 5749 (1989), the ohel in Lubavitch was rebuilt anew by R' David Nachshon and R' Avi Taub. From that time onward, more chassidim began traveling to Lubavitch to visit the Rebbes' courtyard and pray at their gravesites.
Tags: lubavitch, ohel, graves, restoration

Title: Pereshel facsimile of Yosef of Leipnik's 1733 manuscript Haggadah
Summary: Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of Yosef ben David of Leipnik's 1733 illustrated manuscript Haggadah.
Story: In 5749 (1989), Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of an illustrated manuscript Haggadah by Yosef ben David of Leipnik from 5493 (1733). The 48-page octavo edition included a bilingual Hebrew-English introduction by Pereshel. The work continued his annual series of facsimiles of rare Haggadot.
Tags: haggadah, facsimile, new york, leipnik, manuscript, tuvia pereshel

Title: Publication of Toldot Chabad in Soviet Russia
Summary: Rabbi Shalom Dovber Levin's Toldot Chabad B'Russia HaSovietit was published by Kehot in 5749, drawing in part on his father's then-unpublished memoirs.
Story: Shalom Dovber Levin, son of Yisrael Yehuda Levin and longtime librarian of the Central Lubavitch Library, used excerpts from his father's accumulating memoir notes in this historical work. The full memoir Zichronotai was prepared for publication separately and signed by the author in Elul 5755.
Tags: kehot, soviet union, shalom dovber levin, history

Title: Rebbe directs reprinting Chabad works in square script
Summary: At a Shabbos Kedoshim / Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5749 farbrengen, the Rebbe directed that all older Chabad publications previously typeset in Rashi script be reprinted in newly set square (meruba) letters for easier study.
Story: Older Chabad works had long been reproduced via photo-offset of original printings in small Rashi script, hindering study. At the Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5749 farbrengen the Rebbe instructed that these works be reset in square letters. This launched the project to prepare a new edition of the entire Tzemach Tzedek series, integrating all the supplements, omissions, and milu'im accumulated over the previous century.
Tags: rebbe, rosh chodesh iyar, chabad seforim, square script

Title: Rebbe orders expansion of central Chabad Library building
Summary: In 5749 the Rebbe directed the renovation and expansion of the library building physically connected to 770.
Story: Following the consolidation of the library after the 1987 verdict, the Rebbe in 5749 (1989) instructed that work begin on enlarging and renovating the building that housed the library and connected it to 770 Eastern Parkway. The work was intended to make the unified collection accessible to scholars and researchers.
Tags: library, 770, expansion, construction

Title: Sefer HaTmimim first edition published
Summary: The first edition of Sefer HaTmimim, listing alumni of Tomchei Tmimim, was published at the beginning of 5750.
Story: At the beginning of 5750 (late 1989), the first edition of Sefer HaTmimim was published, recording students of the Lubavitch yeshiva Tomchei Tmimim. Shortly afterward additional names were uncovered from a 5670 Vaad Agudas HaTmimim membership roster, leading to a second expanded edition published in 5751 that included the previously missing names.
Tags: sefer hatmimim, kehot, tomchei tmimim, alumni

Title: Soviet committee clears name of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson
Summary: A special Soviet commission reviewed the 1939 arrest file of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson and formally exonerated him of the charges.
Story: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, father of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, had been arrested in 1939 by Soviet authorities in Yekaterinoslav (Dnepropetrovsk). Fifty years later, on June 28, 1989, a special commission reviewed the more than one thousand documents in his case file and cleared his name. The exoneration opened the legal path for the archive to be transferred to the family of the accused.
Tags: soviet union, levi yitzchak schneerson, rehabilitation, kgb archive, dnepropetrovsk, yekaterinoslav

Title: Reprint of Kitzurim v'Hearos al Tanya for Tzemach Tzedek bicentennial
Summary: In late Elul 5749 (September 1989), Kitzurim v'Hearos al Tanya was reissued in an enlarged edition to mark 200 years since the birth of the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: For the bicentennial of the Tzemach Tzedek's birth, the work was reprinted in an enlarged edition, though without the 'Gertz Press' attribution of the original. When the memoirist passed by during the Rebbe's distribution of the volume, he told the Rebbe that this was the first book he had ever printed, and the Rebbe responded with a smiling face.
Tags: tanya, tzemach tzedek, bicentennial, elul

Title: Aguda Tmimim membership flyer arrives at the Library
Summary: A 5670 flyer listing the members of Vaad Aguda Tmimim was acquired by the Lubavitch Library on Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5750.
Story: On Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5750, a flyer was brought to the Lubavitch Library showing that already in 5670 a printed list of Tmimim had been prepared. The list contained only members of the Vaad Aguda Tmimim — alumni of Tomchei Tmimim from 5657 to 5670 who had married before 14 Teves 5670 — and notably included the Rebbe's father Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson and his two brothers, prompting the Rebbe's later acknowledgment 'I have seen and thank you.'
Tags: aguda tmimim, tomchei tmimim, library, alumni, mundshein

Title: Wedding of Sterna Sarah Nemenov and Yosef Yitzchak Paltiel
Summary: On 6 Kislev 5750, Sterna Sarah Nemenov married Yosef Yitzchak Paltiel, who serves as a ram at Tomchei Temimim in Brooklyn.
Story: Sterna Sarah, daughter of Miriam Reizel and Moshe Nemenov, married Yosef Yitzchak Paltiel on 6 Kislev 5750. Yosef Yitzchak Paltiel serves as a ram in the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva in Brooklyn.
Tags: wedding, nemenov family, paltiel family, brooklyn, tomchei temimim

Title: Chabad Russian-translation Haggadah by Dovber Chatzkelevich
Summary: Dovber Chatzkelevich translated a Chabad Haggadah into Russian, published in New York.
Story: In 5750 (1990), an 80-page octavo Haggadah with Russian translation by Dovber Chatzkelevich was published in New York. It served the rapidly expanding Russian-speaking Jewish community as the Iron Curtain began to fall. It joined the Chabad effort to provide Jewish liturgical texts in Russian for newly accessible Soviet Jews.
Tags: chabad, russian, new york, soviet jewry, chatzkelevich

Title: Collapse of the Soviet Union
Summary: The Soviet Union disintegrated after 70 years of Communist rule.
Story: Its eventual collapse fulfilled the Rashab's 1920 prediction to the Rayatz that 'a country that persecutes Judaism will eventually fall.' This may have inspired the Rayatz to confront the Communists knowing their regime would end and Jewish life would be restored. Following the fall, Chabad returned to Rostov and reclaimed the building owned by the Rashab.
Tags: soviet union, russia, collapse

Title: Facsimile of the Kaufmann Haggadah published in Budapest
Summary: A facsimile of the 14th-century Kaufmann Haggadah, held by the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, was published in Budapest.
Story: Around 5750 (1990), the Hungarian Academy of Sciences Library's Oriental Collection sponsored the publication of a facsimile of the 14th-century illuminated 'Kaufmann Haggadah' in Budapest. Limited to 1,000 copies, the 60-page facsimile was accompanied by a separate English introductory booklet by Gabriel Sed-Rajna. The featured copy was number 21 of the print run.
Tags: haggadah, facsimile, budapest, hungary, kaufmann, 14th century

Title: First public menorah lighting in Moscow's Red Square
Summary: Chabad held the first public menorah lighting in Moscow's Red Square as the underground network emerged into the open.
Story: With the Soviet system collapsing, the seventh Rebbe in New York began dispatching young rabbis and rebbetzins to rekindle Jewish life in Russia. They linked up with the clandestine activists who had operated for decades. Chabad rabbis went on to reclaim historic synagogues, open schools, and rebuild Jewish life across the former Soviet Union.
Tags: moscow, red square, menorah, chanukah, soviet union

Title: Haggadah 'Kedushat Levi' compilation from the Berditchever's works issued in Bnei Brak
Summary: Machon Nachalat Tzvi issued a Haggadah 'Kedushat Levi' compiled from the writings of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev and his disciples in Bnei Brak.
Story: In 5750 (1990), Machon Nachalat Tzvi, edited by Shimon Hirshler, published in Bnei Brak the Haggadah 'Kedushat Levi', an anthology of Pardes-style commentaries on the Haggadah, Shir HaShirim, and the holiday, drawn from the writings of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev and his disciples and sons. The 252-page octavo edition also incorporated material from Yesod V'Shoresh HaAvodah. It made the Berditchever's teachings on Passover available in consolidated form.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, berditchev, levi yitzchak, bnei brak, machon nachalat tzvi

Title: Multi-party elections return to Latvia after 56-year hiatus
Summary: Latvia holds its first multi-party elections since the 1934 Ulmanis coup.
Story: After more than five decades without competitive elections, the move marked the beginning of political pluralism's return and preceded Latvia's full independence in 1991.
Tags: latvia, elections, politics

Title: Seventh Rebbe dispatches shluchim to rebuild Jewish life in Russia
Summary: From New York, the seventh Lubavitcher Rebbe began sending young rabbis and rebbetzins to reestablish Chabad institutions in the former Soviet Union.
Story: The new shluchim joined with veterans of the clandestine network who had operated under the Soviets. Together they opened schools, restored historic synagogues, and established cultural and social-service centers. Today Chabad is the premier force in Jewish life in the former Soviet Union.
Tags: shluchim, russia, soviet union, schools

Title: Polyakov-Schneersohn collection survey at Moscow Lenin Library
Summary: The Chabad delegation cross-referenced 87 cards in the Polyakov collection against the Lubavitch library list at the Lenin Library in Moscow.
Story: On Sunday, 5 Shevat 5750 (January 31, 1990), Rabbi Shlomo Cunin and his colleagues spent two and a half hours in the rare books reading room of the Moscow library identifying books from the Polyakov collection that matched the Lubavitch inventory. The Polyakov collection contained over 8,000 books numbered up to 8,577, while the Lubavitch list compiled around 1906 recorded 5,642 books. The discrepancy reflected both multi-volume works counted separately and post-1906 acquisitions never catalogued in the original Lubavitch list.
Tags: russia, moscow, library, schneerson library, soviet union, manuscripts

Title: Official meeting with Lenin Library archivists on Schneerson manuscripts
Summary: The delegation met Medvedev and archive directors at the Lenin Library, clarifying that the manuscript holdings included roughly 30 volumes of Chabad Chassidus.
Story: On Tuesday, 7 Shevat 5750 (February 2, 1990), Rabbi Nissan Mindel, Rabbi Shlomo Cunin and Rabbi Berel Levine met with Medvedev, department head Dyragin and his deputy Midovich at the Lenin Library. Through pointed questioning they established that only part of the manuscript holdings came from the Ginzburg collection and that some 30 volumes of Chabad Chassidus were among the manuscripts. The meeting marked progress after a frustrating day of bureaucratic obstacles in arranging onward travel to Ukraine.
Tags: russia, moscow, library, schneerson library, manuscripts, ginzburg collection, soviet union

Title: Delegation flies from Moscow to Kiev to search for the lost library
Summary: Accompanied by Soviet escort Andrei Kasianenko, the Chabad delegation flew from Moscow to Kiev to begin searching Ukrainian libraries for the lost Yiddish Cultural Institute collection.
Story: On Thursday, 9 Shevat 5750 (February 4, 1990), the eve of the Frierdiker Rebbe's yahrzeit, Rabbi Shlomo Cunin and Rabbi Berel Levine flew from Moscow to Kiev together with their assigned Soviet librarian-escort Andrei Kasianenko. Their visas, hotel bookings and tickets had been obtained only after days of bureaucratic struggle, including a night spent crowded into Rabbi Mindel's single hotel room. They arrived in Kiev around 12:40 PM and immediately began arranging meetings with library officials to locate the confiscated Yiddish Cultural Institute library.
Tags: russia, ukraine, kiev, moscow, soviet union, library, travel

Title: Meeting with Ukrainian Academy of Sciences library in Kiev
Summary: The delegation met Kiev Academy of Sciences scholarly secretary Ivanchenko Vasilyevna and located two Hebrew incunabula traced to the lost Yiddish Cultural Institute library.
Story: On 9 Shevat 5750 (February 4, 1990), Rabbi Berel Levine and Rabbi Shlomo Cunin met with the scholarly secretary of the Kiev Academy of Sciences library. Levine explained how the books of the Institute for Jewish Culture had been seized by the Yevsektsiya from synagogues, confiscated by the Soviet government in 1949, and stored in two cellars. They located two Hebrew incunabula (Abudraham, Lisbon 1491, and a Shorashim from Naples 1491) bearing the stamp of the Institute, suggesting that the rest of the lost collection might also have ended up at the Academy.
Tags: ukraine, kiev, library, yiddish cultural institute, incunabula, yevsektsiya, manuscripts

Title: Pechersk Lavra library search reveals 1960 manuscript fire
Summary: Inquiries at Kiev's Pechersk Lavra revealed that confiscated Hebrew books had been stored in the bell tower until a 1960 fire at the Vodavitsky monastery destroyed part of the collection.
Story: On Friday, 10 Shevat 5750 (February 5, 1990), the yahrzeit of the Frierdiker Rebbe, Rabbi Berel Levine's delegation visited three libraries at Kiev's Pechersk Lavra complex. A veteran librarian named Tsedenko revealed by telephone that book treasures had been stored in the Lavra's bell tower since 1951, transferred to the Vodavitsky monastery building around 1960, and that a fire that same year had destroyed part of the collection. Surviving books had reportedly been returned to the Academy of Sciences library, suggesting the lost Institute collection might still lie in unsorted storage there.
Tags: ukraine, kiev, pechersk lavra, library, fire, yiddish cultural institute, soviet union

Title: Night train from Kiev to Dnepropetrovsk to continue library search
Summary: After Shabbos, the Chabad delegation took an overnight train from Kiev to Dnepropetrovsk to continue searching for the lost Schneerson and Jewish library holdings.
Story: On Motzaei Shabbos Beshalach, 11 Shevat 5750 (February 10, 1990), having exhausted leads in Kiev, Rabbi Shlomo Cunin's delegation boarded an overnight sleeper train to Dnepropetrovsk. Their Soviet escort Kasianenko had secured the tickets after multiple ticket offices initially refused. They arrived the next morning at 9:45 AM and immediately surveyed three Dnepropetrovsk libraries — the university library, the public library, and the historical museum — though most were closed for the day.
Tags: ukraine, kiev, dnepropetrovsk, travel, library, soviet union

Title: Fiftieth wedding anniversary celebration
Summary: On 9 Tammuz 5750 the author marked fifty years since his marriage in Moscow with an intimate family gathering hosted by his daughter Leah.
Story: On 9 Tammuz 5750 (July 2, 1990) the family marked fifty years since the author's 5700 wedding in Moscow with a small jubilee gathering at his daughter Leah's home. The author repeated themes from the maamar 'Kol Hamaarich Be'echad' that the Frierdiker Rebbe had said on 12 Tammuz 5700 in New York during the week of his sheva berachos, and made a siyum on Maseches Nedarim.
Tags: anniversary, moscow, frierdiker rebbe, maamar, siyum nedarim

Title: Wedding of Esther Klein and Pinchas Tziment
Summary: On 8 Elul 5750, Esther Klein married Pinchas Tziment, future director of the Chabad House in Little Rock, Arkansas.
Story: Esther, daughter of Leah and Yerachmiel Binyamin HaLevi Klein, married Pinchas Tziment on 8 Elul 5750. Pinchas Tziment serves as director of the Chabad House in Little Rock, Arkansas.
Tags: wedding, klein family, tziment family, little rock, arkansas, chabad house

Title: Chabad delegation buys Moscow office near Kremlin
Summary: The Chabad delegation paid a $300 deposit on a small room in a historic building near Gorky Street and the Kremlin to serve as Agudas Chassidei Chabad's Moscow office.
Story: During the special mission to Moscow the delegation acquired a 15-by-15-foot room in a historic building near Gorky Street and the Kremlin, paying a $300 down payment. They placed a set of Rambam in the office and started a library with the three volumes of Toldos Chabad, holding a siyum and hatchalah on the Rambam study. The Rebbe approved hanging a Beis Agudas Chassidei Chabad sign in Hebrew and Russian on the door and affixing a mezuzah.
Tags: russia, moscow, agudas chassidei chabad, didan notzach, gorky street

Title: James Baker asks Shevardnadze to return Chabad library
Summary: U.S. Secretary of State James Baker formally requested that Soviet Foreign Minister Shevardnadze approve the return of the Schneersohn library to Chabad.
Story: During Chanukah 5751, through Baruch Hecht and producer Jerry Weintraub, U.S. Secretary of State James Baker submitted a request to Soviet Foreign Minister Eduard Shevardnadze that Chabad's request for the rebbes' library be granted. The intervention was part of broader pressure from American officials, senators, and press as the delegation pushed through the Soviet Foreign and Culture ministries.
Tags: united states, russia, james baker, shevardnadze, jerry weintraub, schneersohn library, didan notzach

Title: Large public Chanukah menorah lighting in central Moscow
Summary: Chabad in Moscow organized its first major public Chanukah menorah lighting near the Hammer Center, with extensive Soviet TV coverage.
Story: During Chanukah 5751 Rabbi Moshe Chaim Levin and Veronika arranged a large public menorah on a Moscow square. After protests over a Manezh Square site near monasteries, the menorah was relocated near the Hammer Center on the riverfront. Busloads of children from the Chabad school, the Chernobyl children's camp, and the Sunday school attended with dancing, a play, and the twelve pesukim, and Soviet television gave the event wide coverage.
Tags: russia, moscow, chanukah, hammer center, marina roshcha, chernobyl children, sunday school

Title: Rebbe announces Soviet recognition of Agudas Chassidei Chabad
Summary: At a Shabbat Vayishlach farbrengen the Rebbe announced that the Soviet authorities had recognized Agudas Chassidei Chabad and agreed to return the rebbes' library.
Story: On Shabbat Vayishlach 5751 the Lubavitcher Rebbe declared at a farbrengen that the Soviet government had officially recognized Agudas Chassidei Chabad as a separate entity, provided it with a building, and committed to return the seforim, manuscripts, and correspondence of the Chabad rebbes. He compared the return to retrieving a pledge and urged that pikuach nefesh of pidyon shvuyim justified non-Jewish officials working on the matter even on Shabbat. The announcement framed the Moscow mission's pursuit of the Schneersohn collection.
Tags: russia, soviet union, schneersohn library, agudas chassidei chabad, didan notzach, moscow

Title: Culture Minister Gubenko refuses to sign book-return order
Summary: Soviet Culture Minister Gubenko refused to sign the document returning the Schneersohn library to Chabad, deferring it to the Supreme Soviet.
Story: On 16 Kislev 5751 the Chabad delegation, with Veronika as their advocate, brought a prepared memo to Culture Minister Nikolai Gubenko for signature. Gubenko refused to sign, claiming the matter required the Supreme Soviet, and at first refused even to meet them. After pressure he met the delegation with deputies Zolotov and Babushkin and ultimately agreed to instruct the Lenin Library director to draft a fresh memo distinguishing duplicates so a final approval could be issued.
Tags: russia, soviet union, moscow, schneersohn library, didan notzach, gubenko, ministry of culture

Title: Veronika summoned by KGB at Gorbachev's office
Summary: Veronika, the delegation's advocate, was summoned by the KGB office of Gorbachev's staff and questioned about the Chabad delegation's activities.
Story: On 17 Kislev 5751 Veronika was called in by the KGB section attached to Gorbachev's office and questioned about the Chabad mission and its members. She left the encounter satisfied and rejoined the delegation at the Lenin Library, where they were meeting with director Grigorov and manuscripts librarian Medvedev about the Schneersohn collection.
Tags: russia, soviet union, kgb, gorbachev, schneersohn library, didan notzach, moscow

Title: Yeltsin signs order to return Schneersohn collection
Summary: Russian Federation President Boris Yeltsin signed a directive to transfer the Schneersohn collection to Chabad.
Story: On 18 Kislev 5751 the Chabad delegation worked with Yeltsin's staff on memos and received an initial promise, then word, that the Russian Federation president had signed an order to give them the Schneersohn library. Yeltsin's office asked Chabad to organize broad press coverage and senatorial thank-you letters for a ceremonial transfer the next day on Yud-Tes Kislev.
Tags: russia, yeltsin, russian federation, schneersohn library, didan notzach, moscow

Title: Foreign Ministry meeting with Deputy Minister Petrovsky
Summary: Chabad met for hours with Soviet Deputy Foreign Minister Vladimir Petrovsky, who promised to escalate the book issue to Foreign Minister Shevardnadze.
Story: On 19 Kislev 5751 at 4:30 PM the delegation met with Deputy Foreign Minister Petrovsky and three aides. Petrovsky promised to speak with Gubenko and to seek 'other means' if no positive decision came. By night the case was being routed via Foreign Minister Shevardnadze, who was asked to deliver a Chabad file to Gorbachev.
Tags: russia, soviet union, foreign ministry, petrovsky, shevardnadze, schneersohn library, didan notzach

Title: Yeltsin reneges, defers Schneersohn books to Gorbachev
Summary: On Yud-Tes Kislev Yeltsin canceled the planned ceremonial book transfer and told Chabad the matter depended only on Gorbachev.
Story: On 19 Kislev 5751, after Chabad arrived for the promised ceremonial handover, Yeltsin had press coverage canceled and told the delegation that returning the books was up to Gorbachev, not him. The reversal coincided with a long Yeltsin-Gorbachev meeting that day in which Deputy Prime Minister Ryzhkov was sidelined and Yeltsin and Gorbachev publicly closed ranks. Veronika assessed that Yeltsin had originally planned a publicity move against Gorbachev but switched to a unity stance once the leaders aligned.
Tags: russia, yeltsin, gorbachev, ryzhkov, schneersohn library, didan notzach, moscow, yud-tes kislev

Title: Russian Federation approves Poliakov Synagogue for Chabad
Summary: The Russian Federation Council of Ministers approved transferring the historic two-story Poliakov Synagogue in central Moscow to Chabad.
Story: On 20 Kislev 5751 the Council of Ministers of the Russian Federation approved giving Chabad the Poliakov Synagogue, a handsome two-story building in central Moscow. The delegation toured the building and was deeply impressed, although it remained temporarily occupied by another office. Local leaders planned to relocate the yeshiva and Tzeirei Agudas Chabad activities there from the Marina Roshcha synagogue.
Tags: russia, moscow, poliakov synagogue, russian federation, agudas chassidei chabad

Title: Chabad delegation visits Lubavitch town graves
Summary: The Moscow delegation drove overnight to the town of Lubavitch to pray at the graves of the Chabad rebbes and visit the original courtyard site.
Story: Late on 21 Kislev 5751 the delegation left Moscow by car with Veronika's driver, arriving in Lubavitch at 8 AM on 22 Kislev. They prayed at the ohel for the success of their mission, visited the Chabad house and the site of the courtyard, and observed that only a well — and perhaps the surrounding trees — remained as physical markers of the rebbes' era. They departed at 10 AM and returned to Moscow that night.
Tags: russia, lubavitch, smolensk, ohel, didan notzach

Title: Gubenko letter formally refuses Schneersohn library return
Summary: Soviet Culture Minister Gubenko's office sent a formal letter to Dr. Armand Hammer refusing to return the Schneersohn collection, citing its 1921 nationalization.
Story: On 23 Kislev 5751 a reply from Culture Minister Gubenko to Dr. Armand Hammer's appeal arrived at Hammer's office, announcing the decision not to return the Schneersohn-Agudas Chassidei Chabad collection because it had been nationalized in 1921. Veronika dismissed it as a personal opinion lacking response to Hammer's letter to Gorbachev and continued working through the Foreign Ministry. Copies of the letter were taken in Russian and English and delivered to the Foreign Ministry the same afternoon.
Tags: russia, soviet union, armand hammer, gubenko, schneersohn library, didan notzach

Title: Gorbachev declines to meet Chabad delegation
Summary: After Gubenko warned Gorbachev against returning the books, the Soviet president's office informed Chabad that no meeting or decision was possible.
Story: On the first day of Chanukah 5751 (25 Kislev) the delegation was told that Culture Minister Gubenko had personally warned Gorbachev against returning the Chabad library. Gorbachev's office informed Chabad that the inter-ministerial disagreement left him unable to decide and a planned meeting — at which Chabad had hoped to present a special menorah — would not take place. Veronika immediately began preparing a legal brief and worked through the night with a partner attorney to build a court-ready dossier.
Tags: russia, soviet union, gorbachev, gubenko, chanukah menorah, schneersohn library, didan notzach

Title: Russian White House backs Chabad property requests
Summary: Yeltsin's office at the Russian White House issued letters supporting Chabad's plans in Lubavitch, the Poliakov Synagogue, and a Maimoni center in Moscow.
Story: On Shabbat Miketz 5751 (4th Chanukah) the delegation met with four of Yeltsin's officials at the Russian government's White House. The officials agreed to write supportive letters on three Chabad initiatives — construction in Lubavitch town, the Poliakov Synagogue, and a Maimoni Center — addressed to the Smolensk city council and the Moscow city council under Deputy Mayor Muzykantsky. Copies were dispatched to each jurisdiction and to the delegation as confirmation.
Tags: russia, yeltsin, moscow, lubavitch, smolensk, poliakov synagogue, maimoni center, russian federation

Title: Gubenko delivers formal rejection of Chabad library petition
Summary: Soviet Culture Minister Nikolai Gubenko issued a written letter rejecting the Chabad delegation's petition, claiming the Schneersohn library was ownerless when nationalized and had become state property.
Story: On Zos Chanukah (2 Tevet 5751) the Chabad delegation in Moscow received Gubenko's formal rejection of their request to repatriate the Lubavitcher Rebbes' library held by the Lenin Library. The letter argued the books had become national property when nationalized in 1918–1919 and offered at most to provide copies after further consultation with jurists and scholars. The delegation immediately escalated through American senators, an Inyurkollegia legal opinion contradicting Gubenko, and outreach to Russian Federation officials, while continuing their hunger strike.
Tags: chabad library, moscow, soviet union, gubenko, ministry of culture, schneersohn collection, perestroika

Title: Chabad delegation meets new Soviet Justice Minister Lushchenkov
Summary: After the Soviet Justice Minister was replaced, the new minister Lushchenkov received Veronika and instructed his deputies to study the Chabad library case in depth.
Story: On 3 Tevet 5751 Veronika met briefly with the newly appointed Soviet Justice Minister Lushchenkov, who directed her to brief his deputies in detail and scheduled a full delegation meeting before Shabbat. Lushchenkov later told the delegation that Gubenko's refusal did not accord with Soviet law and pledged to back their effort, though formal action would await the conclusion of the Congress of People's Deputies. The change of minister was viewed as providential after weeks of stalemate at the Ministry of Culture.
Tags: chabad library, moscow, soviet union, lushchenkov, ministry of justice, schneersohn collection

Title: Chabad delegation expelled from Moscow hotel, shelters at Chernobyl camp
Summary: After OVIR attempted to invalidate the delegation's visas, the Chabad emissaries left their hotel and spent Shabbat Vayigash at a recuperation camp for Chernobyl children outside Moscow.
Story: On Friday 4 Tevet 5751, hotel staff abruptly demanded the delegation's passports for visa stamping while OVIR moved to nullify their recently extended visas. A parallel five-week visa had been issued by the Russian Federation Foreign Ministry, sidestepping the central Soviet authorities. Veronika urged the group to leave the hotel for safety, and they spent Shabbat with roughly seventy children at a Chernobyl recovery camp, davening, learning, and discovering descendants of the chossid R. Shmuel Dobruskin among the staff.
Tags: chabad library, moscow, soviet union, chernobyl children, visa, ovir, kgb

Title: Chabad delegation meets Soviet political adviser Yuli Gelman
Summary: Returning from the Chernobyl camp, the Chabad delegation met with Soviet adviser Gelman, who urged them to focus their lobbying on cultural-collections expert Dmitry Likhachov.
Story: On the evening of 6 Tevet 5751 the delegation moved into Hotel Ukraina and traveled to Yuli Gelman, who advised that the decisive figure was now Dmitry Likhachov, the Russian Federation's chief authority on rare collections. Gelman, then in Moscow for the Congress of People's Deputies, said Likhachov was open to meeting before returning to Leningrad. He also pledged to lobby Jewish deputies at the Congress and to seek a meeting with Gorbachev after the Congress closed.
Tags: chabad library, moscow, soviet union, gelman, likhachov, schneersohn collection

Title: Soviet police arrest R. Yitzchak Kogan en route to Chernobyl camp
Summary: Soviet police halted a car carrying R. Yitzchak Kogan five kilometers from the Chernobyl children's camp and detained him as collateral while ordering the rest of the group back to Moscow.
Story: In the early hours of Sunday 6 Tevet 5751 a car carrying R. Yitzchak Kogan, R. Yisroel Aronov, Kogan's eldest daughter, and Veronika's driver was stopped by Soviet police outside the children's camp. After a prolonged exchange the police held R. Kogan as a pledge and forced the others to return to the capital, ostensibly because the delegation's visas were restricted to Moscow. The incident was understood as retaliation by Gubenko's faction, and prompted Veronika to escalate the matter to the Russian Federation Foreign Ministry.
Tags: chabad library, moscow, soviet union, yitzchak kogan, arrest, kgb, chernobyl children

Title: OVIR apologizes to Chabad delegation for visa incident
Summary: Soviet migration office OVIR apologized to the Chabad delegation, claiming it had been unaware of the mission's status, while the Mossoviet signaled it intended to return the Polyakov Synagogue.
Story: On 7 Tevet 5751 Veronika met with OVIR officials who apologized for the Friday hotel incident, blaming their ignorance of the delegation's diplomatic status. The same day R. Kogan met with Mossoviet officials about the Polyakov Synagogue and Chabad's building needs, hearing that a positive decision was pending final approval. The delegation also began coordinating to send the rescued books out through the upcoming Chernobyl children's charter flight to Israel.
Tags: chabad library, moscow, soviet union, ovir, visa, polyakov synagogue

Title: Breakthrough meeting with Dmitry Likhachov on Schneersohn library
Summary: The delegation persuaded Dmitry Likhachov, the Soviet government's chief expert on rare collections, that the Schneersohn library must be returned, and he committed to writing Gorbachev in support.
Story: On 8 Tevet 5751 the delegation met Dmitry Likhachov, the renowned Leningrad scholar overseeing the Russian Federation's rare cultural collections. Initially favoring a general principle of state custodianship, Likhachov was won over by Rabbi Shlomo Cunin and R. Kogan's exposition of the library's history and meaning. He attempted to call Gubenko on the spot and then drafted letters to Gorbachev and Justice Minister Lushchenkov recommending the books be returned. The night before, the delegation had also consulted journalist Viktor Louis, who counseled sustained pressure backed by the threat of litigation.
Tags: chabad library, moscow, soviet union, likhachov, schneersohn collection, viktor louis, leningrad

Title: Likhachov dispatches letter to Gorbachev backing Schneersohn return
Summary: Word reached the Chabad delegation that Likhachov had already forwarded his recommendation to Gorbachev and the Justice Minister, while a Moscow district leader offered land for a Chabad-affiliated Maimoni medical-educational center.
Story: By 9 Tevet 5751 the delegation learned that Likhachov had sent his letter to Gorbachev and Lushchenkov backing the return of the Schneersohn library, with plans to follow up with Gubenko the next day. The same evening they met with the head of a Moscow suburban district who offered land for a Maimoni Center — a Veronika-led medical and educational complex including schools. Authorities had renewed their inquiries about the delegation's status, and two letters arrived from the Russian Federation government supporting their visas.
Tags: chabad library, moscow, soviet union, likhachov, gorbachev, lushchenkov, maimoni center

Title: Asara b'Tevet diplomacy day for Chabad mission in Moscow
Summary: On the fast of 10 Tevet the Chabad delegation packed in meetings on the Schneersohn library, the Polyakov Synagogue, the Chernobyl airlift, and US diplomatic support.
Story: On 10 Tevet 5751 the delegation met Moscow deputy mayor Muzykantsky regarding restitution of the Polyakov Synagogue (still partly occupied by a choir); the US ambassador Maxwell at his residence; American philanthropist Tom Ferris on medical aid; and Israeli consular officials to finalize the next-morning Chernobyl children's airlift. News came that Likhachov had spoken with Gorbachev and Supreme Soviet chairman Lukyanov to recommend return of the books and that Lushchenkov was preparing to issue a binding decision.
Tags: chabad library, moscow, soviet union, polyakov synagogue, us ambassador, asara btevet, muzykantsky

Title: Chernobyl children airlift departs Moscow for Israel
Summary: A Chabad-organized charter flight carrying Chernobyl-affected children and their families departed Moscow for Israel, with the delegation seeing them off at the airport.
Story: On Friday 11 Tevet 5751 the delegation accompanied Chernobyl children and their families to the Moscow airport for the Chabad-coordinated airlift to Eretz Yisrael, which lifted off before Shabbos and landed in Israel on schedule. The same day Veronika met with the Justice Minister, who confirmed that a special government commission under Lukyanov had been convened to decide the library question. The successful airlift removed a parallel concern that the library campaign might endanger the children's evacuation.
Tags: chabad, moscow, soviet union, chernobyl children, aliyah, israel

Title: Gorbachev and Lukyanov approve return of Schneersohn library
Summary: On Motzei Shabbos Vayechi the Chabad delegation received word that Mikhail Gorbachev and Supreme Soviet chairman Anatoly Lukyanov had signed approval for the Schneersohn library to be returned.
Story: Motzei Shabbos Vayechi 12 Tevet 5751 brought the long-sought message: Gorbachev and Lukyanov had signed off on returning the books, and the file had been forwarded to Culture Minister Gubenko for implementation. Lukyanov's commission concluded the books should be returned without a public government ceremony. Likhachov warned obstacles from Gubenko's office were still likely, gave Veronika his private Leningrad number, and instructed her to call immediately if problems arose.
Tags: chabad library, moscow, soviet union, gorbachev, lukyanov, schneersohn collection, vayechi

Title: Gubenko televised speech prompts new Chabad appeal
Summary: After Culture Minister Gubenko called the Ministry of Culture 'a ministry of kindness' on Soviet television, the Chabad delegation drafted a new appeal quoting his words and delivered it at his office before 9am.
Story: On the evening preceding 13 Tevet 5751 Gubenko appeared on Soviet television describing the Ministry of Culture as 'a ministry of kindness' whose central mission was 'to open the soul'. Veronika proposed turning his own words against him; R. Kogan drafted the letter overnight at Armand Hammer's Moscow office and presented it to the Ministry of Culture before 9am on 13 Tevet. The maneuver came as Gorbachev and Lukyanov's decision was being slowly implemented over Gubenko's continued resistance.
Tags: chabad library, moscow, soviet union, gubenko, schneersohn collection, television

Title: Kogan meets Russian State Library deputies on Schneersohn collection
Summary: R' Yosef Kogan met with deputies and staff at the Russian State Library, who claimed the Schneersohn books would be returned.
Story: On 13 Tevet 5751 Director Gubinko was unavailable, but his deputies and the adviser Yefimovich told R' Yosef Kogan the books would be returned and asked him to leave his letter with them. Yefimovich said a committee had been convened and a response was promised on Wednesday, November 2. Later Lichachev told Veronika that Gubinko had promised return but suggested waiting until after the Russian holiday.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneersohn library, gubinko, yosef kogan, soviet union, lichachev

Title: Chabad ships Ezras Achim food packages to eight Russian cities
Summary: The mission packed and dispatched food packages by rail from Moscow to eight Russian Jewish communities.
Story: On 14 Tevet R' Yosef Kogan and R' Shlomo Cunin packed Ezras Achim food parcels at Marina Roshcha for distribution to eight Russian towns. The delegation held an internal meeting with R' Moshe Chaim Levin and R' Dovber Lazar on Chabad work in Moscow and Aguch oversight. After Maariv the parcels were sent by train.
Tags: russia, moscow, ezras achim, marina roshcha, yosef kogan, shlomo cunin, berel lazar, food aid

Title: Approval to publish Jacobson's memoirs
Summary: At the start of 5752, the Rebbe gave approval and praise for editing and publishing R. Yisrael Jacobson's memoirs.
Story: In late 1991 / early 5752, family members proposed editing and publishing R. Yisrael Jacobson's memoirs. They sought the Rebbe's approval, and he responded with not only consent but with strong encouragement, noting that many would learn from the reading, especially regarding authentic Chabad communal activism. Work began first on a separate volume covering events of the winter of 5700 (1939-40) and the rescue of the Rebbe Rayatz from Nazi-occupied Warsaw.
Tags: memoirs, jacobson, rebbe approval

Title: Bnei Brak Haggadah 'Birkat Moshe' of Lelov Chassidut
Summary: Simcha Krakowski compiled and published the 'Birkat Moshe' Haggadah of Lelov Chassidic teachings in Bnei Brak.
Story: In 5751 (1991), Simcha Krakowski compiled and published in Bnei Brak the Haggadah 'Birkat Moshe' according to the customs and teachings of the Lelov Rebbes, with material from Rabbi Moshe Mordechai Biderman of Lelov and Rabbi Shimon Natan Nata Biderman. The 148-page octavo edition combined teachings, Pesach customs, and conduct guides. It served the Lelov community and admirers of their distinct Chassidic path.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, lelov, bnei brak, biderman, birkat moshe

Title: Bnei Brak Haggadah 'Siach Avot' from Lechovitch-Koidanov dynasties
Summary: Yaakov Tzvi Meir Erlich compiled the 'Siach Avot' Haggadah of Lechovitch-Koidanov teachings, published in Bnei Brak.
Story: In 5751 (1991), Yaakov Tzvi Meir Erlich compiled and the Siach Avot Institute published in Bnei Brak the 'Siach Avot' Haggadah, a collection of holy teachings from the Lechovitch and Koidanov Rebbes. The 236-page octavo edition added Seder laws and customs, Exodus material, and Passover and Sefirat HaOmer letters. It served the Belarussian Chassidic dynasty's contemporary followers.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, lechovitch, koidanov, bnei brak, siach avot

Title: Chabad Russian-translation Haggadah issued by FREE in New York
Summary: FREE published its 15th-edition Russian translation Haggadah in New York to serve Russian-speaking Jewish immigrants.
Story: In 5751 (1991), the FREE organization (Friends of Refugees of Eastern Europe) published in New York the 15th edition of a Russian-translation Haggadah. The 36-page quarto edition served the wave of Russian-speaking Jewish immigrants arriving from the collapsing Soviet Union. It exemplified the Chabad-FREE initiative to make Jewish observance accessible to Soviet Jewry.
Tags: chabad, russian, new york, free, soviet jewry

Title: Hendel Deutsch emigrates and is sent by ChaMa to search Russian archives
Summary: After emigrating to the United States, R. Hendel Deutsch is dispatched by ChaMa to search Russian archives for Chabad historical documents.
Story: In 5751 (1991), R. Hendel Deutsch emigrated from the Soviet Union to the United States. That year the ChaMa organization sent him back to continue searching Russian archives for documents related to Chabad history. He returned with many documents but, despite further guidance from R. Shalom DovBer Levin, did not locate the Mitteler Rebbe's arrest file.
Tags: hendel deutsch, chama, archives, russia, lubavitch, historical research

Title: Latvia regains independence from Soviet Union
Summary: Latvia regains its independence after almost half a century under Soviet rule.
Story: The end of Soviet rule reopened Latvia to wider Jewish religious activity. Multi-party elections, which had not been held since the 1934 Latvian coup d'état, had only resumed in 1990, the year before formal independence.
Tags: latvia, soviet, independence

Title: Lubavitcher Rebbe sends delegation to Russia for redemption of books
Summary: In 5751 the Lubavitcher Rebbe sent a four-member delegation to Russia regarding the redemption of the Chabad books and manuscripts seized in 5676.
Story: The Rebbe appointed the four delegates to lead the newly formed Agudas Chabad in Russia and later in the Commonwealth of Independent States. The delegation met with the Russian government to discuss the books still held in the Moscow public library. The government subsequently sent a recommendation to the leadership of the Smolensk region, which includes Lubavitch, to assist with related plans including the future museum project.
Tags: didan-natzach, books, russia, manuscripts, library

Title: Mordechai Perl delivers Ruzhin family letters to the Lubavitcher Rebbe
Summary: In 5751, Mordechai Perl brings the Lubavitcher Rebbe a cache of letters from the Ruzhiner and his descendants, carried from Moscow.
Story: In 5751 (1991), Mordechai Perl carried from Moscow to the Lubavitcher Rebbe a letter of Rabbi Yisrael of Ruzhin together with letters from his sons and grandsons — the rebbes of Chortkov, Sadigura, Husiatyn, and Mezhibuzh. Perl had inherited the letters from his father Yitzchak Dov Muterperel and grandfather Rabbi Asher Zelig Muterperel, rabbi of Michelfaliye.
Tags: ruzhin, lubavitcher-rebbe, moscow, archives, muterperel, soviet-union

Title: Rebbe dispatches Russia delegation for redemption of seforim
Summary: In 5751 the Rebbe sent a special delegation to Russia regarding the redemption of the Schneersohn library and appointed its members to lead Agudat Chabad in Russia.
Story: In 5751 (1991), the Rebbe sent a special delegation to Russia to address the redemption of the Schneersohn family seforim, and appointed its four members as the leadership of Agudat Chabad in Russia (and later in the CIS). The delegation met with the Russian government, which then sent a recommendation to the Smolensk regional authorities to assist with Chabad's plans for the town of Lubavitch. Following the meeting, the chairman of the Council of Ministers wrote to Agudat Chabad proposing that a Chabad representative work directly with the Smolensk leadership on the project.
Tags: didan notzach, russia, books, library, agudat chabad, smolensk

Title: Rebbe declines proposal to name Aguch representative in Russia
Summary: After the mission proposed an Aguch representative in Russia to coordinate Chabad institutions, the Rebbe told them not to intervene.
Story: On 15 Tevet the delegation faxed R' Yehuda Leib Groner a proposal that Aguch appoint a representative in Russia to coordinate all Chabad institutions there. Groner replied that he had already raised the idea with R' Cunin and that the Rebbe had instructed not to intervene in such matters. The same day Veronika reported that Lichachev and Shenazara, a Gorbachev adviser, had pressed Gubinko to release the library.
Tags: russia, moscow, agudas chassidei chabad, leib groner, shlomo cunin, schneersohn library

Title: Chabad winter camp opens for Moscow children during school break
Summary: A two-week Chabad winter camp ran in a vacant state school building for about 60 children of the Moscow Chabad school.
Story: On 17 Tevet R' Shalom Dovber Levin visited a Chabad winter camp where roughly 60 pupils from the Moscow Chabad school spent two weeks of school break living in a Jewish environment. The camp ran in a state school building empty for the holiday and was run by R' Moshe Chaim Levin and R' Zalman Korbsky. The visit also covered the new Aguch office obtained from the Mossoviet.
Tags: russia, moscow, winter camp, marina roshcha, moshe chaim levin, zalman korbsky, chabad school

Title: Soviet law signed returning religious books and objects to faith bodies
Summary: R' Refael relayed that a Soviet law had been signed Friday evening returning to religious institutions the books and objects nationalized in Soviet times.
Story: On 20 Tevet morning the delegation learned from the local press that a law had been signed Friday evening to return to religious institutions books and objects nationalized under Soviet rule. R' Levin assessed that the law did not cover the Schneersohn case, since Chabad sought the books for its headquarters abroad rather than for a Russian institution. The delegation continued pressing for an exception, as Lichachev had previously conceded the Chabad case warranted unique treatment.
Tags: russia, soviet union, religious restitution, schneersohn library, refael

Title: Chabad delegation rents Moscow apartment near Marina Roshcha
Summary: The mission rented a year-long apartment near Marina Roshcha at $150 a month and began moving out of the hotel.
Story: On 21 Tevet R' Cunin signed a one-year lease at $150 a month, replacing the hotel's $340 a day rate. The team prepared the apartment overnight and packed to move. The day was quiet because Russian Orthodox Christmas (25 December Julian) closed Soviet offices.
Tags: russia, moscow, marina roshcha, shlomo cunin, russian christmas

Title: Mayor Popov writes Rebbe; Gorbachev orders Schneersohn books returned
Summary: Moscow Mayor Gavriil Popov sent a letter to the Rebbe, and that evening Gorbachev's office reported he had ordered Gubinko to return the books.
Story: On 22 Tevet R' Kogan brought back Mayor Popov's letter to the Rebbe, thanking him for help with Chernobyl children and Jewish education in Moscow and signaling the return of the Polyakov synagogue to Chabad. That evening Veronika called to report that Gorbachev's office had dispatched a government message to Gubinko ordering the Schneersohn library returned. The delegation broke into dance and l'chaim while R' Yehuda Leib Groner was still on the second telephone line.
Tags: russia, moscow, gavriil popov, gorbachev, gubinko, schneersohn library, chernobyl children, polyakov synagogue, veronika

Title: Alter Rebbe yahrzeit farbrengens held in Moscow amid Gubinko backlash
Summary: On 24 Tevet, the Alter Rebbe's yahrzeit, Gubinko went to Gorbachev to challenge the order to return the books while Chabad farbrengens were held in Moscow.
Story: On 24 Tevet 5751 Gubinko told Gorbachev that Arthur Schneier, Adolph Shayevitch and Edgar Bronfman opposed returning the library, prompting the delegation to spend the night chasing rebuttals via Bronfman's deputy Israel Singer at the Savoy hotel. Rosh Yeshiva R' Uri Kamishov hosted a farbrengen at Marina Roshcha that R' Levin then continued at the Aguch office until 11:30 pm, reviewing the Alter Rebbe's biography on his yahrzeit. The delegation returned to the apartment around 2 am.
Tags: russia, moscow, alter rebbe, shneur zalman of liadi, marina roshcha, uri kamishov, schneersohn library, yahrzeit, arthur schneier, edgar bronfman

Title: Pidrubsky meeting and Israeli consulate inauguration in Moscow
Summary: The delegation met Rabbi Pidrubsky of the Choral Synagogue and attended the inauguration of the Israeli consulate in Moscow.
Story: On 25 Tevet R' Kogan, R' Cunin and R' Levin met Pidrubsky at the Arkhipova Choral Synagogue, who wrote a letter to Gubinko stating that anything tied to the Rebbe must be returned immediately. They then attended the inauguration of the Israeli consulate building, meeting U.S. deputy ambassador Collins, Moscow Mayor Popov and Israeli ambassador Arye Levin. The day closed with a farbrengen for Marina Roshcha talmidim at the Aguch office, filmed for video.
Tags: russia, moscow, israeli consulate, pidrubsky, arkhipova synagogue, gavriil popov, arye levin, schneersohn library

Title: Russian actor Stas warns Chabad library return has been blocked
Summary: Actor Stas told the delegation that Russian decision-makers had agreed to block return and proposed a Russian press campaign.
Story: On 27 Tevet R' Cunin and R' Levin spent hours with Stas, a prominent young Russian actor, who said his contacts confirmed a group around Gubinko had decided to block the library to avoid setting a restitution precedent. He proposed a Russian press campaign in Ogoniok and Literaturnaya Gazeta, including a piece by Lichachev, to shape opinion before approaching President Bush. He offered to introduce the delegation to the Gorby Club, where the real decision sat.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneersohn library, stas, shlomo cunin, ogoniok, literaturnaya gazeta, media strategy, george h w bush

Title: Gorby Club director offers paid US loan of Schneersohn collection
Summary: Ilya Osadchuk of the Gorby Club told the delegation the library would only move via paid arrangement or a US exhibition loan.
Story: On 28 Tevet the delegation, brought by Stas, met Ilya Osadchuk, director of the Gorby Club at the Mossoviet. Osadchuk said no one in power intended to return the books and proposed instead a US fund to develop the Moscow library in exchange for an exhibition loan of the collection. The delegation declined to respond on the spot and decided to wait for Veronika's return before deciding.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneersohn library, gorby club, ilya osadchuk, mossoviet

Title: Alexander Bessmertnykh appointed Soviet Foreign Minister
Summary: Alexander Bessmertnykh, the former Soviet ambassador in Washington, was named Foreign Minister of the USSR.
Story: Bessmertnykh had previously served as Soviet ambassador to the United States, where he had once written a letter recommending that the Schneerson library be returned to Chabad. His appointment to head the Soviet foreign ministry was welcome news to the Chabad delegation in Moscow, who immediately received a fax copy of his earlier supportive letter. The delegation began maneuvering through American and Soviet diplomatic channels to secure a meeting with him about the library.
Tags: russia, soviet union, bessmertnykh, diplomacy, schneerson library, moscow

Title: Diarist records somber assessment of Schneersohn library mission
Summary: On Rosh Chodesh Shevat R' Levin wrote that the mission seemed blocked and weighed whether to send headquarters a bleak assessment.
Story: On Rosh Chodesh Shevat 5751 R' Shalom Dovber Levin wrote that the statements from Stas and Osadchuk made the situation appear hopeless and that the delegation's efforts felt like water wearing away stone. His colleagues disagreed with his dark mood and urged continued effort, but he felt duty-bound to report an accurate situation to Lubavitch headquarters. He resolved to keep the diary going regardless of his unsettled state.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneersohn library, shalom dovber levin, veronika

Title: Rebbe's 'Song in every interpretation' response on the library mission
Summary: The Rebbe responded to Rabbi Berel Kunin's request for a blessing by linking the library mission to Parashat Beshalach and 'song in every interpretation.'
Story: After Rabbi Kunin wrote to the Lubavitcher Rebbe describing the delegation's frustrations in Moscow and asking for a blessing, the answer came in the morning: 'We stand in immediate proximity to Parashat Beshalach — song in every interpretation. I will mention it at the gravesite.' The cryptic, encouraging response reframed the mission's hardships as a prelude to triumph and song. It was received as the Gulf War was breaking out and the delegation faced repeated rebuffs from Soviet officials over the Schneerson collection.
Tags: lubavitcher rebbe, schneerson library, parashat beshalach, moscow delegation, blessing

Title: Iraqi Scud missiles first strike Israel during Gulf War
Summary: Iraq launched its first Scud ballistic missiles at Israel, with eight missiles fired and two houses destroyed in the opening barrage.
Story: Soon after the U.S.-led coalition began its air campaign against Iraq, Saddam Hussein retaliated by firing Scud missiles at Israeli cities. Word reached the Chabad delegation in Moscow from Kfar Chabad that there were no fatalities, only a few wounded, with two homes destroyed. The unfolding war became an obstacle to their library efforts, as Soviet officials cited the Gulf crisis as a reason to delay decisions on the Schneerson collection.
Tags: israel, iraq, gulf war, scud missiles, kfar chabad, war

Title: Rebbe's cable calling for 'visible and revealed joy' during the war
Summary: The Rebbe sent a cable about the situation in the Land of Israel, instructing that there should be 'visible and revealed joy.'
Story: As Iraqi Scud missiles struck Israel during the Gulf War, the Lubavitcher Rebbe dispatched a telegram declaring that joy must be made visible and revealed. The cable was read aloud by Rabbi Moshe Chaim Levin in the Marina Roscha synagogue in Moscow on Shabbat Parashat Bo, before the Torah reading. The community responded with extensive dancing and a heightened spirit during the prayers and farbrengen that followed.
Tags: lubavitcher rebbe, gulf war, israel, moscow, marina roscha

Title: All-Soviet Jewish Vaad convention opens in Moscow
Summary: A newly organized 'Vaad' convention opened in Moscow, claiming to represent all Jewish organizations in the USSR.
Story: The Vaad, an umbrella body recently formed to speak for Soviet Jewry, convened in Moscow with roughly a thousand delegates from across Russia. Chabad leadership viewed its agenda warily, since Reform Jewish representatives were included and the body claimed to speak for Chabad organizations as well. After deliberation, the Chabad delegation decided neither to participate formally nor to issue public protests, but to respond that they were still studying the Vaad's platform.
Tags: russia, soviet jewry, vaad, moscow, jewish organizations, reform judaism

Title: Pavlov currency reform cancels Soviet 50- and 100-ruble notes
Summary: A Soviet law issued at night invalidated all banknotes of 50 rubles and above, allowing only limited exchange at banks.
Story: The Soviet government decreed that all banknotes of 50 rubles and higher were no longer legal tender, with citizens permitted to exchange up to 500 rubles at the bank and lose anything beyond that. The reform — equivalent to roughly two dollars per note at black-market rates — became the dominant topic of conversation across Moscow. The Chabad delegation noted it as part of the chaotic political and economic backdrop to their library campaign.
Tags: soviet union, russia, currency reform, pavlov, ruble, economy

Title: Rebbe's response: 'Together they went, together they will return'
Summary: The Rebbe answered the author's request to return early to 770, telling him not to separate from his colleagues on the mission.
Story: Feeling sidelined from the library negotiations and immersed instead in teaching at the Moscow yeshiva, the author asked the Rebbe via Rabbi Leibel Groner whether he should return to 770. The Rebbe's reply came that night: 'Let him not separate from his fellows on this mission — together they went, together they will return when the time comes. I will mention it at the gravesite.' The answer confirmed the delegation as an indivisible unit and effectively defined the author's role as combining the library mission with sustained Torah teaching in Moscow.
Tags: lubavitcher rebbe, schneerson library, moscow delegation, shlichus, yeshiva

Title: Vaad convention votes to demand return of Schneerson library
Summary: Rabbi Berel Kunin addressed the Vaad convention on the library, and the assembly voted unanimously to demand the books' return.
Story: After Soviet officials kept insisting that Russian Jews wanted the Schneerson collection to remain in the USSR, the Chabad delegation went to the Vaad convention to refute that claim. Rabbi Kunin spoke before roughly a thousand Jewish delegates from across Russia, who responded with enthusiasm and voted overwhelmingly that the books must be returned to Chabad. A strongly worded letter from the Vaad demanding the return was drafted on the spot.
Tags: russia, soviet jewry, vaad, schneerson library, moscow, petition

Title: 10 Shevat 5751 farbrengen marks 41st yahrzeit of Rebbe Rayatz in Moscow
Summary: A Yud Shevat farbrengen was held in Moscow commemorating the 41st yahrzeit of the Previous Rebbe and the Rebbe's acceptance of leadership.
Story: On the eve of 10 Shevat, a gathering opened at 7 p.m. in honor of the yahrzeit of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn and the Rebbe's assumption of leadership in 5711 (1951). The author addressed the talmidim about the 1950–1951 period and the acceptance of the nesius, with Rabbi Moshe Nudelman translating into Russian. Rabbi Dovid Berel Lazar and Rabbi Moshe Chaim Levin also spoke, and the assembly listened to a recording of the Rebbe's original Yud Shevat 5711 farbrengen.
Tags: yud shevat, rebbe rayatz, moscow, marina roscha, farbrengen, yeshiva

Title: Rabbi Zalman Tuvia Abelsky installed as Rabbi of Kishinev
Summary: Rabbi Zalman Tuvia Abelsky was installed as Rabbi of Kishinev.
Story: On 15 Shevat, the formal installation of Rabbi Zalman Tuvia Abelsky as Rabbi of Kishinev took place in Moldova. The author had planned to travel with Rabbi Dovid Berel Lazar to attend the event, but Veronika Monosonik, who was to arrange their visas, refused to do so, so they remained in Moscow. The installation was part of a wider rebuilding of Chabad rabbinic infrastructure across the former Soviet Union during this period.
Tags: kishinev, moldova, chabad shluchim, rabbinate, soviet union

Title: Cold Shabbat keeps delegation indoors in Moscow
Summary: The Chabad delegation in Moscow stayed in their apartment over Shabbat due to -30°C cold.
Story: On Shabbat 19 Shevat 5751, while in Moscow pursuing the return of the Chabad library, the delegation remained indoors because of extreme cold of -30°C and inadequate winter clothing for the over-hour walk to synagogue. The Shabbat was used to plan the next moves, including sending Rabbis Koegan and Cunin to Leningrad to obtain a fresh letter from Ligachev.
Tags: moscow, russia, soviet union, chabad library, weather, delegation

Title: Delegation prepares memorandum sets for Soviet officials
Summary: The Chabad delegation produced twelve sets of about fifty pages of key documents and faxed them to Yona Pruss in London for translation.
Story: On 20 Shevat 5751, Rabbi Aharonov and the diarist traveled to the Armand Hammer office in Moscow to prepare twelve sets of all the main documents in their possession, totaling some fifty pages. They faxed a copy to Yona Pruss in London to arrange Russian-to-English translation and recruit someone to compose a general historical and documentary overview, work that continued through the night.
Tags: moscow, armand hammer office, chabad library, documents, yona pruss, london

Title: Koegan and Cunin travel to Leningrad to meet Ligachev
Summary: Rabbis Koegan and Cunin took an overnight train to Leningrad and obtained a strong new letter from Ligachev supporting return of the seforim.
Story: Because Gubenko claimed Ligachev had retracted his support for returning the Chabad library, the delegation decided over Shabbat to send Rabbis Koegan and Cunin by overnight train to Leningrad. They met Ligachev at his vacation site about ninety minutes from Leningrad, received a strong new letter of support, and prepared to return that night on the train.
Tags: leningrad, ligachev, chabad library, soviet union, delegation, yosef yitzchak koegan, boruch shlomo cunin

Title: Delegation sends document sets to Gorbachev and Gubenko aides
Summary: Document packets were delivered to Gorbachev's aide Chernyaev and Gubenko's aide Babushkin to push the seforim case forward.
Story: On 21 Shevat 5751 the delegation finalized memoranda received from Yona Pruss in London and from Singer regarding Bronfman's conversations with Yakovlev, and made copies at the Armand Hammer office. Rabbi Koegan delivered four sets to Veronika and then a set each to Chernyaev, Gorbachev's aide, and Babushkin, Gubenko's aide, while Rabbi Aharonov and the diarist brought four sets to Rabbi Cunin at the U.S. Consulate.
Tags: moscow, gorbachev, gubenko, chabad library, chernyaev, babushkin, delegation
