Title: Russian government discusses return of Chabad library
Summary: A roughly half-hour cabinet-level discussion was held in the Russian Federation government regarding the return of the Chabad library.
Story: Rabbi Koegan received word that on 22 Shevat 5751 the government of the Russian Federation held a roughly thirty-minute discussion concerning the return of the Chabad library. The information arrived as the delegation was setting up a video monitor in their Moscow office for upcoming gatherings and screenings.
Tags: russian federation, chabad library, moscow, government, soviet union

Title: Around 25 yeshiva students arrive in Moscow as shluchim to Russia
Summary: About twenty-five young shluchim arrived in Moscow to fan out in groups to towns across Russia for three months.
Story: On 22 Shevat 5751, approximately twenty-five bochurim shluchim arrived in Moscow to travel in groups to various Russian cities for three-month assignments. A welcome reception was held at Marina Roscha at 2:00 p.m. and the groups departed that evening for their destinations; among those assigned to the Moscow yeshiva were Yaakov Goldschmid and Shlomo Wilhelm.
Tags: shluchim, russia, moscow, marina roscha, yeshiva, tomim, yaakov goldschmid, shlomo wilhelm

Title: Chabad delegation buys 22,000 Shabbat candles for distribution in Russia
Summary: The delegation decided to purchase 22,000 Shabbat candles for distribution throughout Russia in honor of the Rebbetzin's yahrzeit.
Story: On 22 Shevat 5751, the yahrzeit of Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, the delegation in Moscow resolved to buy twenty-two thousand Shabbat candles to distribute as part of Mivtza Neshek across Russia. They began the purchase and distribution that day and wrote to the Rebbe asking permission to appoint a local person to manage the project; the Rebbe replied with a blessing to continue spreading good tidings.
Tags: mivtza neshek, moscow, russia, rebbetzin chana, shabbat candles, rebbetzin

Title: Khasbulatov letter refers Chabad library claim to arbitrage court
Summary: Ruslan Khasbulatov, head of the Russian Supreme Soviet, wrote to the Moscow arbitrage court asking it to consider Chabad's claim for the Schneersohn library because the matter was needed for foreign relations.
Story: Disclosed by Judge Gribenikov at the press conference defending the court's later ruling, Khasbulatov's February 6 1991 letter was the mechanism that put the case before the arbitrage court. Gribenikov stressed it was a routine policy referral rather than political pressure, and that the court took seven months of independent study before reaching its unanimous decision.
Tags: russia, khasbulatov, schneersohn-library, soviet-union, foreign-relations

Title: Chabad delegation submits joint letter to Gorbachev on library return
Summary: The delegation signed and delivered three copies of a joint letter to Gorbachev demanding clear action on returning the seforim.
Story: On 23 Shevat 5751, after meeting U.S. Consulate officials about U.S. visas and meeting with Stas and Ilya, the four delegation members signed a letter drafted at Stas's office to Gorbachev. They prepared three copies — one delivered by Rabbi Koegan to Gorbachev's office, one taken by Stas for Primakov, and one taken by Ilya for Raisa Gorbachev — while they awaited a positive reply.
Tags: gorbachev, chabad library, moscow, primakov, raisa gorbachev, delegation

Title: Address to women in Moscow on Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka
Summary: The diarist delivered a 45-minute Hebrew address to a women's gathering in Moscow about his personal acquaintance with the Rebbetzin.
Story: On Sunday 25 Shevat 5751, while other delegation members met with Veronika and prepared to host her party that evening, the diarist traveled to a women's gathering in Moscow marking 22 Shevat. He spoke for about three-quarters of an hour in Hebrew about his personal acquaintance with Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, with Rabbi Z. Korobsky translating into Russian.
Tags: moscow, rebbetzin, 22 shevat, women's gathering, korobsky

Title: Melaveh Malkah hosted for Stas and family in Moscow
Summary: The delegation hosted a four-hour Melaveh Malkah for Stas, his mother (Mikoyan's daughter-in-law), wife, and aides.
Story: On Motzaei Shabbat 25 Shevat 5751 the delegation organized a Melaveh Malkah at their Moscow apartment for Stas and his entourage, including his mother — daughter-in-law of former USSR President Mikoyan — and the Levin sisters. From 9:00 p.m. to 12:30 a.m. they screened Chabad videos including on Chernobyl, sang Chabad songs in Russian, and the matriarch confided that she had spoken with Gorbachev at a cemetery visit, who said he intended to return the books but had been hindered by Gubenko.
Tags: moscow, stas namin, mikoyan, melaveh malkah, chabad library

Title: Soviet Foreign Ministry calls Veronika with decision to return Chabad library
Summary: Around 1:00 a.m. Veronika received a call from Deputy Foreign Minister Ivanov announcing the decision to return the Chabad seforim.
Story: In the early hours of 28 Shevat 5751, Veronika (Devorah Rochel) phoned the delegation to relay that Deputy Foreign Minister Ivanov had just informed her of the decision to return the Chabad library, with details to follow at 10 a.m. Shortly afterward Rabbi Leibel Groner relayed from New York that Secretary of State Baker had received a positive reply on the matter and that Mr. Shishlin reported a Friday government meeting that had decided in favor of return.
Tags: chabad library, moscow, ivanov, veronika, soviet foreign ministry, delegation

Title: Cunin and Koegan present menorah request at Gorbachev's office
Summary: Rabbis Cunin and Koegan waited two hours at Gorbachev's office and met chief secretary Malokoyedov to request an audience to thank Gorbachev for ordering the books returned.
Story: On 30 Shevat 5751 / Rosh Chodesh Adar, Rabbis Cunin and Koegan went to Gorbachev's office to seek a thank-you audience in connection with the menorah they had presented earlier and the order to return the seforim. The secretary who had received the menorah recognized them, and after a two-hour wait — during which Rabbi Cunin recited Tehillim and davened Minchah in the waiting room — they were ushered in to chief secretary Malokoyedov, who took down their details and promised a reply within a day or two.
Tags: gorbachev, menorah, chabad library, moscow, malokoyedov, delegation

Title: Gorbachev's office declines audience with Chabad delegation
Summary: Malokoyedov's office phoned to thank for the menorah and confirm approval to return the books but said Gorbachev was too busy to receive the delegation.
Story: Later on Rosh Chodesh Adar 5751, Malokoyedov's office called the Chabad delegation in Moscow with three points: thanks for the menorah, confirmation that authorization had been issued to the Ministry of Culture to return the books, and a refusal of the requested audience with Gorbachev citing his schedule. Rabbi Cunin was then summoned to the U.S. Consulate, where Mr. Collins relayed similar news from the Foreign Ministry and was about to meet with Tolstikov of the Ministry of Culture.
Tags: gorbachev, chabad library, moscow, malokoyedov, ministry of culture

Title: Threat to Stas and Ilya over Chabad library assistance
Summary: Ilya received a 1 a.m. phone threat that he and Stas would pay with their lives if they continued helping the delegation.
Story: On the night of Rosh Chodesh Adar 5751, Stas told the Chabad delegation in Moscow that Ilya had received a call around 1:00 a.m. warning that he and Stas would pay with their lives if they kept helping with the seforim. Stas linked the threat to a similar warning conveyed earlier by an Academy of Sciences contact to Rabbi Koegan, suggesting both calls came from the same source.
Tags: moscow, chabad library, threats, stas namin, ilya, academy of sciences

Title: Ministry of Culture issues restrictive letter on Chabad library
Summary: The Soviet Ministry of Culture handed the delegation a six-week-old letter permitting only photocopies and duplicate exchanges, not return of the seforim.
Story: On Erev Shabbos Adar I 5751, the diarist retrieved from the Ministry of Culture a letter dated six weeks earlier stating that the delegation would only be allowed to photograph the books and discuss exchanges of duplicates — not receive them. He asked that the letter be dated the day of receipt to demonstrate that the Ministry had ignored Gorbachev's instructions to return the library.
Tags: chabad library, ministry of culture, moscow, gubenko, gorbachev

Title: Gorbachev's office transfers Chabad library file back to Gubenko
Summary: Gorbachev's office told the delegation it transferred the seforim file to Gubenko and would issue nothing in writing.
Story: On 4 Adar 5751, Rabbis Cunin and Koegan made the rounds in Moscow. Gorbachev's office said it gives nothing in writing and clarified that, contrary to what was said before Shabbos, the office had merely transferred the file to Gubenko rather than issued an instruction to return the books; Tolstikov said he was no longer involved and only Yefimovich at the Ministry of Culture was now handling the matter.
Tags: chabad library, gorbachev, gubenko, moscow, ministry of culture

Title: Meeting at Stas's mother's home with Time photographer
Summary: The delegation met at Stas's mother's Moscow home with a journalist and a Time magazine photographer to brief them on the campaign.
Story: On the night of 4 Adar 5751 the delegation met at the home of Stas's mother together with a reporter and the Time magazine photographer they had met previously at Stas's office. They walked the journalists through every step of the campaign and showed them the support letters; Rabbi Cunin compared Stas's mother to Queen Esther bringing about a Purim-style miracle through her closeness to power, and she committed herself to the cause.
Tags: chabad library, moscow, stas namin, time magazine, media, purim

Title: Inyurkollegia issues second legal opinion on library ownership
Summary: R. Y. Kogan met with Vladimir Mozheisky of the Inyurkollegia to request an updated legal assessment of Chabad's rights to the library.
Story: After all the steps taken since the initial legal opinion, the delegation sought a fresh evaluation. Mozheisky heard the details and said he would consult with the chairman, asking them to call back the next morning at 11. The resulting strong letter affirmed Agudas Chasidei Chabad's ownership and challenged Gubenko's silence on the issue.
Tags: moscow, schneerson library, inyurkollegia, legal, agudas chasidei chabad

Title: Meeting with Israeli Consul Aryeh Levin about Schneerson Library
Summary: The Chabad delegation met with Israeli Consul Aryeh Levin in Moscow to seek help transmitting President Herzog's letter to Gorbachev about returning the Schneerson library.
Story: On Tuesday, 5 Adar 5751, Rabbi B.S. Kunin, R. Y.Y. Aharonov, and the diarist visited Israeli Consul Aryeh Levin to discuss the library's return. They informed him of the Ministry of Culture's falsehoods, Gorbachev's instruction to return the books, and Gubenko's refusal to cooperate. Levin promised to assist with President Herzog's letter and inquire about the best route to deliver it to Gorbachev.
Tags: moscow, israel, schneerson library, aryeh levin, consulate, gorbachev, herzog

Title: Yeltsin publicly demands Gorbachev's resignation on Russian television
Summary: Russian Federation President Yeltsin demanded Gorbachev's resignation during a televised interview in preparation for the referendum on power between the federations and the USSR.
Story: On Tuesday, in a major escalation of tensions between the USSR and Russian Federation governments, Yeltsin publicly called for Gorbachev to step down. The demand came in an all-Russian television interview ahead of a referendum on the balance of powers between the union and federation governments. The political turbulence created uncertainty for delegations working with Soviet officials.
Tags: russia, yeltsin, gorbachev, referendum, ussr, russian federation

Title: Meeting with Russian Federation Foreign Ministry on Schneerson books
Summary: The delegation met officials at the Russian Federation Foreign Ministry; the planned meeting with Minister Kozyrev was postponed when he was called to an urgent USSR government session.
Story: On Wednesday 6 Adar at 10am, the delegation arrived to meet Foreign Minister Kozyrev, who maintains good relations with Gorbachev and intended to discuss the library matter with him. Sergei Reznikov received them and recounted how Gubenko had earlier called demanding their expulsion from Russia, a request the ministry refused. The visit took place amid sharp tensions between the USSR and Russian Federation governments, with Yeltsin publicly demanding Gorbachev's resignation.
Tags: moscow, russian federation, foreign ministry, schneerson library, gorbachev, yeltsin

Title: Sergei Shishlin sends Schneerson library memorandum to Gorbachev
Summary: Shishlin informed the delegation that he had submitted a memorandum about returning the Schneerson library to Gorbachev and hoped for a reply by Friday.
Story: From the Hammer offices, the diarist phoned Shishlin, who reported sending a memorandum on the library matter to Gorbachev. He declined to provide a copy but expected an answer by Friday. The delegation took this as a meaningful step in the high-level Kremlin track of their advocacy.
Tags: moscow, schneerson library, shishlin, gorbachev, kremlin

Title: Stas Vatulin visits the Rebbe in New York
Summary: Stas, a Russian official assisting the library effort, traveled to New York, visited the Lubavitch library, and met the Lubavitcher Rebbe, who gave him dollars for success in the books matter.
Story: Y. Wilhelm picked Stas up around noon, showed him manuscripts and books from the Rebbe Rashab, the broadcasting room, and the synagogue, then brought him to the Rebbe. The Rebbe, told that Stas was working on the books issue, urged that the return happen 'as quickly as possible' and gave him an additional dollar for his mother who was also helping. Stas later prepared a five-page Russian memorandum for the Rebbe summarizing the situation.
Tags: stas, library, schneerson collection, 770, yitzchak wilhelm, lubavitch library

Title: Meeting with Canadian Ambassador on Schneerson library
Summary: Rabbi Kunin and R. Y.Y. Aharonov (a Canadian citizen) met the Canadian ambassador in Moscow to brief him and request his appeal to Gorbachev about returning the books.
Story: Following a strategy of broadening diplomatic pressure suggested by Mr. Collins, the delegation sought support from additional embassies. The Canadian ambassador received them warmly and sat with them for nearly an hour to hear the full library story. That evening they also contacted Chabad activists in Canada to lobby from there.
Tags: moscow, canada, ambassador, schneerson library, gorbachev, aharonov

Title: Gulf War ends with US-led coalition victory
Summary: The Gulf War ended in victory for the United States and the coalition, with Iraqi forces expelled from Kuwait and large parts of Iraq occupied.
Story: On Purim morning the delegation heard the news that the war in Iraq had ended in victory for the US-led coalition. Iraqi forces were entirely driven out of Kuwait, significant portions of Iraq were taken, and Saddam Hussein was given 48 hours to comply with UN resolutions or face continued advance. The diary frames this as a redemption parallel to the ongoing struggle to free the Schneerson library.
Tags: iraq, kuwait, gulf war, united states, coalition, saddam hussein

Title: Meeting with former Soviet Foreign Minister Shevardnadze
Summary: The delegation finally met Eduard Shevardnadze, who now headed a new oversight office, to enlist his help on the Schneerson library issue.
Story: After several failed attempts, the delegation reached Shevardnadze in his new ministerial-oversight role. He recounted that two months earlier he had passed their matter to President Gorbachev, who had referred it to Culture Minister Gubenko. He accepted their memoranda and documents and promised to study what he could do, while advising them to also approach the ministers of culture and justice again.
Tags: moscow, shevardnadze, schneerson library, gorbachev, soviet government

Title: Polyakov Synagogue officially designated for return to Chabad
Summary: On Taanit Esther, Moscow city official Natalia formally informed occupants of the Polyakov Synagogue (seized from Jews in 1937) that it would be returned to Chabad.
Story: The delegation, joined by R. M.M. Levin and R. Z. Koravsky, visited the synagogue building with Natalia from the Mossoviet. She told the current occupants on behalf of the municipality that the building, taken from the Jewish community in 1937, had been designated for return and they would need to vacate. The building required extensive repairs after a recent failure of its water and heating systems.
Tags: moscow, polyakov synagogue, mossoviet, natalia, agudas chasidei chabad, 1937

Title: Purim mass Megillah reading at Ezras Achim hall in Moscow
Summary: On Purim evening, the diarist read the Megillah before approximately one thousand people at a large Purim gathering organized by Ezras Achim in Moscow.
Story: After Mincha and the half-shekel offering at the Marina Roscha synagogue, the diarist traveled to a major Purim event in a large hall organized by Ezras Achim. He read the Megillah for around a thousand attendees and stayed about an additional hour. The program included separate adult and children's activities in adjoining halls.
Tags: moscow, purim, megillah, ezras achim, marina roscha

Title: Domostroy newspaper publishes article attacking Chabad library claim
Summary: The Soviet newspaper Domostroy published a defamatory article against the Chabad delegation and its demand for the return of the Schneerson library.
Story: Shortly before Passover 5751, the newspaper Domostroy printed an article attacking the Chabad mission and its claim to the Schneerson library held in Moscow. The piece's contents made clear it had been commissioned by the Ministry of Culture, raising the question of whether it had been ordered before or after recent talks with Gubenko. The mission concluded that the time had come to begin its own press campaign and prepared a written response.
Tags: soviet union, moscow, domostroy, schneerson library, ministry of culture, propaganda, special mission

Title: Delegation delivers mishloach manot to Soviet Foreign Ministry
Summary: On Purim day the delegation stopped at the Soviet Foreign Ministry to deliver mishloach manot to Foreign Minister Bessmertnykh and thank him for his help on the library issue.
Story: After receiving permission to enter the building, they were told Bessmertnykh was not present; a staff member recorded their names and purpose. Veronika later reported that Deputy Minister Ivanov had quietly come down to identify the delegation in person and afterward arranged a fresh inquiry into the library status. However, the Supreme Council was in session appointing new ministers (with Gubenko expected to be replaced), delaying any new information.
Tags: moscow, purim, bessmertnykh, foreign ministry, schneerson library, mishloach manot

Title: Bris milah for 16-year-old Zev from Zhitomir in Moscow
Summary: A 16-year-old yeshiva student named Zev, who had run away from his home in Zhitomir a month earlier to study in yeshiva, had his bris milah in Moscow after his parents agreed.
Story: Zev had fled his Zhitomir home about a month before the bris in order to learn in the Chabad yeshiva. His parents eventually consented to both his Torah study and his circumcision. The diarist served as sandek at the ceremony, held at the Moscow synagogue on 18 Adar 5751.
Tags: zhitomir, moscow, yeshiva, baal teshuva, ussr

Title: Rebbe's encouraging response on Adar arrives in Moscow delegation
Summary: The Lubavitcher Rebbe sent a written response emphasizing the word 'Adar' in the date and expressing hope that the ongoing efforts in Adar would succeed in redeeming the captive books held more than seventy years.
Story: On 18 Adar 5751, R. Yisroel Wilhelm relayed the Rebbe's reply to Stas's general report. The Rebbe pointedly highlighted 'Adar' in the date line and wrote that the continuing efforts should succeed in freeing the books. The delegation in Moscow took this as a major morale boost and intensified their lobbying with renewed vigor.
Tags: seforim, moscow, ussr, schneersohn library, stas wilhelm

Title: Chabad delegation meets Israeli consul Levin on Schneersohn books
Summary: The Chabad delegation in Moscow met with Israeli consul Mr. Levin, who clarified that Soviet talk of supplying photocopies instead of originals applied only to the Ginzburg collection, while the Schneersohn books should be returned in full.
Story: Veronika had warned the delegation that Consul Levin spoke of providing only photocopies. In the 19 Adar meeting, Levin explained the photocopy proposal concerned the separate Ginzburg collection sought by the Israeli national library. He confirmed that everyone he spoke to assumed the Chabad books would be returned outright, urging the delegation to keep pressing firmly.
Tags: israel, schneersohn library, ginzburg collection, diplomacy, ussr

Title: Declaration signed that Poliakov synagogue belongs to Agudas Chabad
Summary: R. Zev Korabelsky and R. M.M. Levin signed a declaration that any contract they would sign with the Moscow city authorities concerning the Poliakov synagogue was being signed only as representatives of Agudas Chabad.
Story: The Mossoviet had summoned Korabelsky to sign a renovation and office-transfer agreement for the Poliakov shul. Because the formal status of the synagogue between Agudas Chabad and the local community had never been settled, the diarist met both rabbis and required them to sign a declaration affirming that Agudas Chabad alone would determine how the synagogue was run.
Tags: moscow, poliakov synagogue, agudas chabad, korabelsky, lazar

Title: PM John Major sends detailed letter to Gorbachev on Chabad books
Summary: British Prime Minister John Major sent Mikhail Gorbachev a detailed written letter about the Schneersohn books, following up on his earlier oral mention of the issue during their meeting.
Story: Lord Young informed R. P. Vogel by fax that Major had raised the books in conversation with Gorbachev and promised to write in detail. On Thursday 21 Adar Major's full letter was sent. Lord Young also advised contacting British ambassador Braithwaite, leading to a meeting set for the following Monday.
Tags: united kingdom, john major, gorbachev, schneersohn library, diplomacy, lord young

Title: Three-hour meeting at Soviet Foreign Ministry on Schneersohn books
Summary: The Chabad delegation held a three-hour meeting at the Soviet Foreign Ministry with deputy American-desk chief Igor Lebedev, presenting a dossier of 40 documents and demanding the return of the Schneersohn library.
Story: On 21 Adar 5751, Rabbis Kunin, Aharonov, Kogan and the diarist met Lebedev, Kruchkolov and Shmatov starting at 10am. Kunin handed over a numbered packet ranging from accreditation papers and letters from Senator Kennedy and Armand Hammer to letters from Soviet rabbis and Chabad leaders. Lebedev promised to study the material and try to give an answer the following Tuesday.
Tags: moscow, soviet foreign ministry, lebedev, kruchkolov, schneersohn library, diplomacy

Title: London-printed booklet on Schneersohn library arrives in Moscow
Summary: Fifty copies of an explanatory booklet about the Chabad library mission, edited by R. Yossi Pross in London based on the delegation's diary, arrived in Moscow for distribution.
Story: Pross had spent weeks editing the booklet based on long phone conversations with R. Y.Y. Aharonov and the diarist's running journal. After final corrections were faxed in, the booklet was printed in London on 21 Adar. Fifty copies reached Moscow the next evening, ready to be handed to officials, journalists and public figures as a propaganda counterweight to Soviet stonewalling.
Tags: london, moscow, schneersohn library, yossi pross, media campaign

Title: Meeting at Gelman's home with theater director Smilansky
Summary: The Chabad delegation met at Vladimir Gelman's Moscow home with theater director Anatoly Smilansky, who knew Culture Minister Gubenko personally and promised to lobby him and Shevardnadze's aide Stepanov on behalf of the books.
Story: Smilansky was surprised by Gubenko's hostile behavior, having known him as liberal and sympathetic before he became Culture Minister. He pledged to speak with everyone connected to the case in private and with force, and to approach Stepanov in Shevardnadze's office. Gelman added that Yakovlev had told him he was considering writing to Gorbachev about the books and raising the matter directly with Gubenko.
Tags: moscow, gelman, smilansky, gubenko, shevardnadze, schneersohn library

Title: Chabad delegation meets Chief Rabbi Eliyahu at Hotel Rossiya in Moscow
Summary: The special Chabad delegation met with Sephardic Chief Rabbi Mordechai Eliyahu at Hotel Rossiya in Moscow to brief him on the Schneersohn library campaign.
Story: On the night of 25 Adar 5751, Rabbis Aharonov, Cunin, Kogan, and Levin met with newly arrived Chief Rabbi Mordechai Eliyahu at his Moscow hotel. They presented a decade of effort to recover the Schneersohn library from Soviet custody and discussed strategy for the days ahead. Rabbi Eliyahu pledged to raise the matter with senior Soviet religious-affairs officials and with the head of the Russian Orthodox Church.
Tags: russia, moscow, soviet union, schneersohn library, mordechai eliyahu, shlichus, yitzchak aharonov, shlomo cunin

Title: Rebbe approves distribution of Chabad library booklet
Summary: The Lubavitcher Rebbe gave his approval to begin distributing the London-prepared booklet about the captive Chabad library, advising the delegation to proceed in good time and as the askanim see fit.
Story: On motzaei Shabbos 24 Adar the booklet was brought before the Rebbe, who replied 'May it be in a good and auspicious time, and the moment and the matter — as the askanim advise.' The delegation decided to begin distributing it privately to individuals; if Secretary of State Baker's visit later that week failed to produce results, they would launch a full press campaign. R. Sholom Ber Kunin also wrote to the Rebbe about sending his sons to Washington to lobby senators.
Tags: schneersohn library, media campaign, james baker, washington

Title: VAAD conference convenes; rabbis press Soviet officials on Schneersohn library
Summary: At the inaugural VAAD conference of Soviet Jewish communities, the visiting chief rabbis pressed Soviet religious-affairs chairman Kristopanov over the Schneersohn library.
Story: On 26 Adar 5751, the Chabad delegation joined Chief Rabbi Eliyahu and other rabbinic guests at the VAAD conference luncheon, seated beside religious-affairs chairman Kristopanov and his deputy Moldaviewicz. The rabbis raised the urgent question of returning the Schneersohn library while Rabbi Kogan continued the case in Russian. Soviet librarian Kozlova later told the delegation she had still received no instruction to show them the collection at Khimki.
Tags: russia, moscow, soviet union, schneersohn library, vaad, kristopanov, moldaviewicz, shlichus

Title: Chief Rabbis visit Marina Roshcha shul and Chabad yeshiva in Moscow
Summary: Chief Rabbis Mordechai Eliyahu and Shaar Yashuv Cohen visited Marina Roshcha synagogue and the Chabad yeshiva, examined students, and ruled the Schneersohn books must be returned.
Story: On the morning of 28 Adar 5751, after a brit milah arranged by Rabbi Avraham Genin, the chief rabbis toured Marina Roshcha synagogue with Rabbi Berel Lazar. They examined students Baruch Gorin and Eliyahu Kazatzkov on tractate Gittin and marveled at their progress after less than a year of returning to Jewish learning. The rabbis then ruled, per Halacha, that the Schneersohn library must be returned to Chabad immediately, and recited Psalms 140 and 144 at the Lenin Library to hasten the redemption of the books.
Tags: russia, moscow, marina roshcha, yeshiva, berel lazar, mordechai eliyahu, shaar yashuv cohen, brit milah

Title: Veronica Irina confronts Soviet Culture Minister Gubenko over Schneersohn library
Summary: Attorney Veronica Irina met Soviet Culture Minister Nikolai Gubenko, who acknowledged the library could be returned but blamed delays on procedure and internal Jewish opposition.
Story: On 28 Adar 5751, Veronica Irina met privately with Culture Minister Gubenko after refusing to negotiate in front of his recording device and aides. Gubenko admitted the Schneersohn collection had never been nationalized and conceded he was open to returning it, while saying preparations could take until May 1. He revealed that Rabbis Shayevich and Schneier had personally urged him not to rush the return, citing internal Jewish disagreement, and said only his own signed order would release the books for Gorbachev to authorize.
Tags: russia, moscow, soviet union, schneersohn library, nikolai gubenko, ministry of culture, veronica irina, yefimovich

Title: Baker raises Chabad library return with Gorbachev in Moscow
Summary: US Secretary of State James Baker raised the Chabad library issue with Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev during his Moscow visit, pressing for the books' return.
Story: During Baker's March 1991 Moscow visit, the Chabad delegation worked through Dennis Ross and Ambassador Matlock to ensure the library question reached Gorbachev directly. Baker first pressed Bessmertnykh, then raised the matter with Gorbachev himself, telling them the US considered the books American property. A Chabad delegation including Rabbi Shlomo Cunin intercepted Baker at his hotel late Friday night to thank him for his intervention.
Tags: russia, ussr, chabad library, didan notzach, james baker, gorbachev, diplomacy, state department

Title: Chabad delegation briefs Dennis Ross before Baker-Gorbachev summit in Moscow
Summary: On the eve of James Baker's meeting with Gorbachev, the Chabad delegation briefed US Deputy Dennis Ross on the Schneersohn library campaign.
Story: On 29 Adar 5751, at the Hammer Center in Moscow, the delegation met for thirty minutes with Dennis Ross, deputy to US Secretary of State James Baker, joined by Ambassador Collins and aide Downey. Rabbi Cunin recounted the long campaign to recover the Schneersohn library and presented nearly forty letters of support from US senators gathered in Washington. Ross conveyed that Baker had already raised the matter with Soviet Foreign Minister Bessmertnykh, whose hands were tied by Gubenko's refusal — setting the stage for Baker to press Gorbachev directly later that day.
Tags: russia, moscow, soviet union, schneersohn library, james baker, dennis ross, gorbachev, us state department, us senators

Title: Chabad delegation debates founding Igud Kehilot Chabad in Russia
Summary: On 3 Nissan 5751 a meeting at the Hammer office in Moscow weighed whether to register a union of Chabad communities in Russia immediately to avoid being absorbed into a state-recognized umbrella body.
Story: Five activists including Rabbi Berel Lazar, Rabbi M. Ch. Levin and Rabbi Z. Korobkin pressed the visiting delegation to formally register an Igud Kehilot Chabad before Pidrovsky's 'Vetzirna' body received exclusive recognition as the representative of Judaism in the USSR. The delegation declined to decide on the spot and asked for written pros and cons. The Rebbe later replied that the matter should be decided by experienced Chabad askanim.
Tags: russia, ussr, igud kehilot chabad, vesirah, vetzirna, religious registration, communities

Title: Shluchim convention of the Soviet Union opens in Moscow
Summary: On 5 Nissan 5751 the Kinus HaShluchim of the Soviet Union opened in Moscow, gathering Chabad emissaries from across the USSR for the first such conference.
Story: The convention's main sessions were held at the Molodyozhna Hotel, with Rabbis Krasik, Moskowitz, Levin, Avelsky, Slonim, Lazar, Korobkin and Brook on the dais. Talmidim shluchim came in from Rostov and other cities, and the special delegation from Eretz Yisrael addressed the gathering, including a talk on synagogue libraries throughout Russia. A public banquet that evening drew a wide audience.
Tags: russia, ussr, kinus hashluchim, shluchim, marina roshcha, molodyozhna hotel, chabad russia

Title: Rabbi Cunin instructed by the Rebbe to return to Los Angeles for Pesach
Summary: On 9 Nissan 5751 the Rebbe sent a note instructing Rabbi Shlomo Cunin to leave Moscow and celebrate Pesach with his family in Los Angeles.
Story: After Jerry Weintraub wrote to the Rebbe that there was no point in Cunin remaining in Moscow over Pesach, the Rebbe replied that Weintraub had great merit for his efforts on the books and that the main thing was that the books arrive soon. The Rebbe then handed Cunin a separate note: 'In my opinion it is fitting that he celebrate the festival of Pesach with his family in Los Angeles.' Rabbi Leibel Groner relayed that no parallel directive had been given to the rest of the delegation.
Tags: russia, ussr, shlomo cunin, jerry weintraub, pesach, didan notzach, los angeles

Title: Gubenko writes birthday letter to the Lubavitcher Rebbe
Summary: For the Rebbe's 89th birthday on 11 Nissan 5751, Soviet Culture Minister Nikolai Gubenko sent a letter to the Lubavitcher Rebbe praising Chabad but deferring the library decision to a committee.
Story: Meeting Cunin and Kogan in Madrid, Gubenko drafted a letter for Yud-Aleph Nissan describing the greatness of the Rebbe and the dedication of Chabad chassidim. Regarding the library he wrote that the books were important to the Jewish people and to Russia, that a committee was now working on the question, and expressed confidence that its decision by May 1 would satisfy everyone. The Chabad emissaries faxed copies to Moscow and to the Rebbe in New York.
Tags: russia, ussr, gubenko, chabad library, didan notzach, soviet culture ministry, yud-aleph nissan

Title: Rabbis Cunin and Kogan fly to Madrid to confront Gubenko
Summary: On 11 Nissan 5751 Rabbis Shlomo Cunin and Yitzchak Kogan flew from Moscow to Spain to meet Mr. Lubimov and Soviet Culture Minister Gubenko in person about releasing the Chabad library.
Story: After Veronika Irina-Kogan reached Gubenko by phone in his Madrid hotel and Yitzchak Kogan continued the conversation with Lubimov, the delegation decided that Cunin and Kogan should fly out immediately to meet them face to face. They wrote to the Rebbe describing the plan as 'l'chatchila aribber' and received the reply 'Azkir al hatziyun.' In Madrid they laid tefillin with Lubimov, who tried to persuade Gubenko to authorize the warehouse to begin packing the books in honor of Yud-Aleph Nissan.
Tags: spain, madrid, didan notzach, chabad library, gubenko, lubimov, shlomo cunin, yitzchak kogan

Title: Soviet secret police file on Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson surfaces
Summary: Around 11–12 Nissan 5751 a Chabad shliach in Dnepropetrovsk reported access via a local contact to NKVD archive files on Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, the Rebbe's father.
Story: Talmid shliach Manes Barash phoned Moscow to report that a man with access to secret police archives had shown him a photograph of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak and the interrogation file from his arrest, claiming there were many more manuscripts to be retrieved. The Moscow delegation told him to fly in immediately with the contact and whatever documents he could obtain. The discovery opened a new front for recovering Soviet-era Chabad materials alongside the library campaign.
Tags: russia, ussr, dnepropetrovsk, levi yitzchak schneerson, nkvd archives, secret police, manuscripts

Title: Lania Odnopozov delivers Rabbi Levi Yitzchak's prison photo to mission
Summary: On the Tzemach Tzedek's yahrtzeit, Lania Odnopozov brought the mission a 1939 prison photo of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak and a summary of his KGB archive file.
Story: On 13 Nisan 5751, the yahrtzeit of the Tzemach Tzedek, Mr. Lania Odnopozov of Yekaterinoslav arrived in Moscow with a photograph of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson taken at his 1939 arrest, together with a written survey of the archive's more than one thousand documents. The materials confirmed many known details of his self-sacrifice under interrogation and added new ones. The mission's emissary, Rabbi Shalom Dovber Levin, wrote to the Rebbe asking whether to pursue the archive; the Rebbe's reply emphatically encouraged him to begin.
Tags: soviet union, moscow, levi yitzchak schneerson, kgb archive, dnepropetrovsk, special mission

Title: Rebbe's 13 Nisan sicha alludes to Kremlin library mission
Summary: On the Tzemach Tzedek's yahrtzeit, the Lubavitcher Rebbe spoke of the Tzemach Tzedek sitting in Lubavitch and arranging matters in Petersburg, hinting at the ongoing mission in Moscow.
Story: In his 13 Nisan 5751 sicha at 770, the Lubavitcher Rebbe discussed the Tzemach Tzedek, the day's baal hilula, noting how he had remained in Lubavitch while arranging affairs in the capital, Petersburg. Hasidim understood this as an allusion to the Rebbe himself, sitting in New York while directing the mission to recover the Schneerson library from the Kremlin. The sicha was delivered while the special delegation was actively pressing the Soviet government on the books.
Tags: new york, 770, tzemach tzedek, schneerson library, special mission, petersburg

Title: Chabad delegation travels to Leningrad to lead public seders
Summary: Rabbi Yitzchak Kogan and Rabbi Shalom Dovber Levin traveled by overnight train from Moscow to Leningrad to help conduct large public Passover seders.
Story: On the eve of Pesach 5751, two members of the special mission to recover the Schneerson library left Moscow by night train for Leningrad to lead public seders in the city's Great Synagogue. Three separate seders were held there, organized respectively by Shamir, the Jewish Agency, and the local Anash community, each drawing close to a hundred participants. Rabbi Levin led the seders while Rabbi Kogan translated and spoke; they also led prayers, Torah reading, and communal discussions before returning to Moscow.
Tags: leningrad, soviet union, passover, public seder, shamir, jewish agency, special mission

Title: Veronika delivers press response on Chabad library to Tomarkin
Summary: Veronika finalized a long article on the library mission and a response to the Domostroy attack, sending them via Tomarkin to be placed in the Soviet press.
Story: Through the second day of Chol HaMoed Pesach 5751, Veronika worked on a lengthy philosophical article on the return of the Schneerson books, with a section introducing the Chabad mission, plus a sharper rebuttal to the Domostroy attack. Tomarkin, an aide to Gorbachev, sent a driver to collect the material and undertook to place it in the press. The Rebbe had directed the delegation to take its cues from Veronika on whether and how to respond publicly.
Tags: soviet union, moscow, schneerson library, press campaign, veronika irina-kogan, tomarkin, gorbachev, special mission

Title: Soviet justice minister tells Chabad mission he cannot help on library
Summary: Soviet Justice Minister Lushchikov told Rabbi Yitzchak Kogan that although Chabad's claim to the library was just, the matter was now controlled by senior politicians.
Story: On 3 Chol HaMoed Pesach 5751, the Chabad mission tried again to obtain a written statement from Justice Minister Lushchikov, who had privately supported the legality of returning the library. Reached by phone, the minister told Rabbi Kogan that he recognized the justice of Chabad's claim but that the issue had been taken over by senior political figures and was beyond his ability to influence. The delegation pivoted toward a press campaign instead.
Tags: soviet union, moscow, schneerson library, ministry of justice, lushchikov, special mission

Title: Komsomolskaya Pravda editor agrees to publicize Chabad library case
Summary: Komsomolskaya Pravda editor Filinov agreed to publish material on the Schneerson library and to help draw other Soviet papers into the campaign.
Story: On the seventh day of Pesach 5751, Rabbi Yitzchak Kogan met with Mr. Filinov, editor of Komsomolskaya Pravda, delivered the mission's documents and brochures, and explained Chabad's case for the library. Filinov entered into the issue enthusiastically, promising not only to publish a series in his own paper but to draft a press release and circulate it to other Soviet outlets. The meeting marked the start of Chabad's coordinated press push in the Soviet Union.
Tags: soviet union, moscow, schneerson library, komsomolskaya pravda, press campaign, filinov, special mission

Title: Author first views original Tzemach Tzedek portrait in Moscow
Summary: On Issru Chag Pesach 5751 the author visited Yehuda Leib Ginzburg in Moscow and saw the original Tzemach Tzedek oil painting on his wall.
Story: On Issru Chag Pesach 5751 (7 April 1991), the librarian visited the Moscow home of Yehuda Leib Ginzburg — a great-grandson of R. Shlomo Zalman of Kapust (the Magen Avot), himself a grandson of the Tzemach Tzedek — and saw on the wall a vivid colored portrait of the Tzemach Tzedek. Years of attempts to obtain the painting or a photo for the Chabad library followed; eventually R. Baruch Gorin succeeded in securing a copy of this rare and beautiful image.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, portrait, moscow, ginzburg, magen avot, kapust

Title: Mission views original Tzemach Tzedek portrait at Ginzburg home
Summary: Rabbi Shalom Dovber Levin visited Yehuda Leib Ginzburg, a Schneerson descendant in Moscow, and viewed an apparently original 19th-century portrait of the Tzemach Tzedek.
Story: On Isru Chag of Pesach 5751, Rabbi Levin visited the Moscow home of Yehuda Leib Ginzburg, a descendant of the Admor Maharshaz of Kopust and thus of the Tzemach Tzedek. On the wall hung a vivid color portrait of the Tzemach Tzedek that appeared at least a century old and clearly predated the standard image. Nearby stood a cabinet of bichlach manuscripts recognizable by their bindings as matching items in the Chabad library, and Levin proposed that the portrait too belonged in the Chabad library museum.
Tags: soviet union, moscow, tzemach tzedek, schneerson family, kopust, portrait, chabad library museum

Title: Rabbi Bentzion Kunin returns to Moscow with Rebbe's dollars
Summary: Rabbi Bentzion Kunin flew back to Moscow on 24 Nisan carrying dollars the Rebbe had given for each member of the mission and one specifically dedicated to Lenin.
Story: On 24 Nisan 5751, Rabbi Bentzion Kunin returned to Moscow to rejoin the library mission. The day before, at the regular Sunday dollar distribution, the Rebbe had given him two dollars apiece for each of the three colleagues in Moscow and added a separate dollar 'for Lenin,' remarking that Lenin was said to be of Jewish descent. Kunin brought with him a tehillim soaked, he told the Rebbe, with tears shed in Moscow, wrapped in an image of the library where the books were being held captive.
Tags: soviet union, moscow, bentzion kunin, rebbe's dollars, schneerson library, lenin, special mission

Title: Komsomolskaya Pravda issues press release on Schneerson library
Summary: Komsomolskaya Pravda issued a press release demanding the return of the Schneerson library, broadcast on Soviet radio and circulated to other outlets.
Story: On 26 Nisan 5751, the editor of Komsomolskaya Pravda issued a press release on the Schneerson library, with the text read on Soviet radio at 10:40 that morning. The statement declared that the Chabad library, which had belonged to the Rebbe Rayatz, had been located after decades, that academics agreed it should be returned, and that despite the Chabad delegation's four-month presence in Moscow, Minister Gubenko refused to meet them while the books deteriorated uncatalogued. A copy was faxed to the Rebbe in New York.
Tags: soviet union, moscow, schneerson library, komsomolskaya pravda, press campaign, gubenko, ministry of culture, special mission

Title: Rabbi Kunin burns Rebbe's 'Lenin dollar' near Lenin's tomb
Summary: Unable to enter Lenin's mausoleum, Rabbi Bentzion Kunin burned the dollar the Rebbe had given 'for Lenin' on Red Square near the tomb.
Story: On 26 Nisan 5751, after meetings with the U.S. embassy and Soviet officials, the Chabad delegation walked to Red Square to fulfill the Rebbe's instruction concerning the dollar he had given 'for Lenin.' The mausoleum was closed to visitors until the following week, so Rabbi Bentzion Kunin burned the dollar adjacent to Lenin's tomb. The Rebbe had told him to use it to elevate the side of 'sitra achra' and bring good news.
Tags: soviet union, moscow, red square, lenin's tomb, bentzion kunin, rebbe's dollars, special mission

Title: Chabad enters Polyakov Synagogue in Moscow to reclaim it
Summary: The Chabad mission, joined by yeshiva students and a Torah scroll from Leningrad, occupied the Polyakov Synagogue in Moscow to forestall its transfer to the Reform movement.
Story: Hearing that the Mossoviet had decided to return Moscow's Polyakov Synagogue to Chabad but was hesitating to issue the decision in writing under Reform pressure, the delegation moved to take physical possession. On the morning of 28 Nisan 5751 they brought a Sefer Torah down from Leningrad, gathered with yeshiva students, prayed and studied in the building, and refused to leave when the resident company cut the electricity and called the police. Veronika negotiated through the day with the company, police, and Mossoviet officials, securing a meeting with deputy mayor Sevastianov for the following day to resolve the matter.
Tags: soviet union, moscow, polyakov synagogue, reform judaism, mossoviet, yeshiva, veronika irina-kogan, police, special mission

Title: Rebbe declares duty to bring Moshiach in famed 27 Nissan sichah
Summary: On 27 Nissan 5751, the Rebbe declared that every individual must do all in their power to bring Moshiach and publicize the redemption.
Story: In a famous sichah delivered on 27 Nissan 5751 (April 11, 1991), the Rebbe declared that the obligation rests on every Jew to do everything possible to bring about the coming of Moshiach and to publicize the message of redemption on the broadest scale. The sichah marked a turning point in Chabad's intensified Moshiach campaign in its final years.
Tags: moshiach, redemption, tnash"a, sichah

Title: Rebbe's 'I have done all I can' sicha on bringing Moshiach
Summary: On the night of 27 Nissan 5751, the Rebbe declared he had done all in his power to bring Moshiach and called on chassidim to act.
Story: On the night leading to Thursday, 27 Nissan 5751, the Rebbe delivered a sicha stating that he had done everything in his ability to bring Moshiach and it had not helped, and now one, two, or three people should determine what to do to bring him. The Rebbe pointed to the special days around Tiferes shebeTiferes. The sicha sparked worldwide awakening: at the Shabbos farbrengen and dollar distribution chassidim called for the Rebbe to reveal himself and lead them to Eretz Yisrael, but the Rebbe responded that they should not give him advice, indicating instead that the practical response was to add in Torah and mitzvos with hiddur.
Tags: moshiach, 27 nissan, 770, tiferes shebetiferes, sicha

Title: Moscow officials decide to return Polyakov synagogue to Chabad
Summary: After a five-month campaign, Moscow Soviet officials decided on erev Shabbos 28 Nissan 5751 to return the Polyakov synagogue to Chabad rather than to the Reform community.
Story: After friendly meetings with Mr. Svastianov of the Moscow Soviet and behind-the-scenes work by Natalia and Veronika, the Moscow city authorities resolved to return the Polyakov synagogue to Chabad. Rabbi Shloime Kunin reported on erev Shabbos 28 Nissan that the decision had been signed. The decision came despite intense competing pressure from the Reform community, who had brought press and television hoping to take possession of the building, and despite a subsequent court challenge by the tenant organization claiming it was not obligated to vacate.
Tags: polyakov synagogue, moscow, moscow soviet, reform, soviet union, shloime kunin, svastianov

Title: Visit to the Malachovka synagogue outside Moscow
Summary: On Sunday 30 Nissan 5751, the special emissary visited the Malachovka synagogue near Moscow, where his father had studied as a youth.
Story: On Sunday 30 Nissan 5751 (April 14, 1991), with all government offices closed, the writer drove about an hour from central Moscow to visit the Malachovka synagogue, accompanied by shluchim Yaakov Goldschmidt and Shlomo Wilhelm and bochur Yitzchak Reitman in a car provided by R' A. Shentsis of Marina Roscha. The synagogue had been renovated since his father studied there sixty years earlier. They then visited the nearby cemetery with thousands of graves, recognizing only one — that of Rabbi M.L. Ginzburg, son-in-law of the Rebbe Maharash.
Tags: malachovka, moscow, russia, soviet union, cemetery, ramyl ginzburg

Title: Chabad mass pilgrimage to Lubavitch on Maharash's birthday
Summary: On 2 Iyar 5751, two busloads of Moscow yeshiva students plus anash from Leningrad and Cherson made the largest Chabad gathering in Lubavitch since the yeshiva fled in 1918.
Story: On 2 Iyar 5751 (April 16, 1991), the birthday of the Rebbe Maharash, two busloads of Moscow yeshiva students, the girls of Beis Chaya Mushka, anash and tmimim from Leningrad, and two shluchim from Cherson converged on Lubavitch — likely the largest gathering of anash there since the yeshiva left in the summer of 5678/1918. The trip, led by Rosh Yeshiva R' Uri Kamishov and shluchim Yaakov Goldschmidt and Shlomo Wilhelm, included visiting the Ohel of the Maharash and the Tzemach Tzedek, writing a klali pidyon nefesh for the Rebbe's success and the coming of Moshiach, and touring the burnt-out courtyard of the Rebbeim where a Soviet post office was being built. The travelers returned to Moscow at 2:30 a.m.
Tags: lubavitch, maharash, tzemach tzedek, ohel, yeshiva, moscow, leningrad, cherson, beis chaya mushka, russia

Title: Favorable Schneersohn-library article in Nyezavisimaya Gazeta
Summary: On 2 Iyar 5751 the Independent newspaper (Nyezavisimaya Gazeta) printed a favorable article on the campaign to return the Schneersohn library.
Story: An article prepared by Filinov, former editor of Komsomolskaya Pravda and then head of an information agency, appeared on 2 Iyar 5751 (April 16, 1991) in Nyezavisimaya Gazeta, supporting the campaign to return the Schneersohn library to Chabad. Filinov had picked up the story through his agency rather than his former paper. He subsequently said he had no time to follow up and transferred the topic to a colleague, Detshkov, who set up a follow-up interview with the Chabad delegation.
Tags: schneersohn library, russian press, nyezavisimaya gazeta, komsomolskaya pravda, filinov, moscow

Title: New York Times article on Chabad and the Schneersohn library
Summary: A New York Times article by Francis Kleins on Rabbi Berel Lazar, Chabad in Russia, and the Schneersohn books was published on 6 Iyar 5751.
Story: An article on Rabbi Berel Lazar, Chabad activity in Russia, and the disputed Schneersohn library, written by Francis Kleins, was published in the New York Times on 6 Iyar 5751 (April 20, 1991). The article was arranged after 'Stas' connected the team with the photographer Avakian. It notably omitted any mention of the official Chabad delegation in Moscow and portrayed Rabbi Lazar as the one handling the books issue.
Tags: new york times, berel lazar, schneersohn library, francis kleins, moscow, russia, press

Title: Delegation meets Geleman and Rizov on Schneersohn library
Summary: On 8 Iyar 5751, the Chabad delegation met with Soviet figures Geleman and Rizov to discuss returning the Schneersohn library.
Story: On the morning of 8 Iyar 5751 (April 22, 1991), the delegation, together with Mr. Geleman, met with Rizov in Moscow. Rizov related that two months earlier Yegorov had told him, in Gorbachev's name, that Gorbachev could not take responsibility for returning the books and wanted Gubinko and one other to decide. Rizov had proposed a special commission with two representatives each from Jewish communities, the Academy (including Likhachev), and the Ministry of Culture. He suggested approaching Gubinko directly during the parliamentary break that day.
Tags: schneersohn library, rizov, geleman, yegorov, gorbachev, gubinko, likhachev, moscow

Title: Rick Jacobs meets Chabad delegation in Moscow on Schneerson library effort
Summary: Rabbis Shlomo Cunin and Yosef Yitzchak Aharonov met PR consultant Rick Jacobs in Moscow to enlist his contacts in pressing the Soviets to return the Schneerson library.
Story: Jacobs, who had previously arranged a Hammer–Gorbachev meeting, agreed to approach academician Yevgeny Velikhov on behalf of the delegation. The meeting was part of a wider effort to enlist American media and figures to pressure Moscow into returning the Lubavitch book collection held at the Lenin Library.
Tags: moscow, russia, didan natzach, schneerson library, rick jacobs, yevgeny velikhov, public relations

Title: Two-hour meeting with Tolstikov on Schneersohn library access
Summary: On 10 Iyar 5751, the delegation met Tolstikov for about two hours and learned the library issue was being held at the level of President Gorbachev himself.
Story: On 10 Iyar 5751 (April 24, 1991), the delegation met Mr. Tolstikov for some two hours. He stated the Schneersohn library issue was an ideological-political position held at the very top of the government — not by the deputy or minister of culture, nor by Prime Minister Pavlov, but by President Gorbachev himself. He compared it to Gorbachev's recent trip to Japan, where despite Russia needing 22 billion dollars and not needing the two small Kuril islands, no agreement was reached. Tolstikov stepped out to consult Babushkin and returned admitting he had been mistaken: the bar on the Chabad team helping librarians identify the Schneersohn collection had come from above, pending the commission's final ruling. He accepted a letter from the four-member delegation and promised to forward their requests to the Minister of Culture.
Tags: schneersohn library, tolstikov, babushkin, gorbachev, pavlov, japan, kuril islands, moscow, soviet ministry of culture

Title: Baker raises Schneerson books with Bessmertnykh at Kislovodsk talks
Summary: U.S. Secretary of State James Baker pressed Soviet Foreign Minister Bessmertnykh on the Lubavitch books during their Kislovodsk meeting; Bessmertnykh later raised the matter with Gorbachev.
Story: The delegation in Moscow received conflicting State Department reports about whether the topic had been raised. It was ultimately confirmed that Baker did bring up the seforim and that Bessmertnykh then took it to Gorbachev, who deferred a response pending the work of a special commission.
Tags: russia, soviet union, schneerson library, didan natzach, james baker, bessmertnykh, gorbachev, kislovodsk, diplomacy

Title: Israeli ambassador Aryeh Levin briefs Chabad delegation on Soviet stance
Summary: At the Israeli embassy in Moscow, Ambassador Aryeh Levin told the delegation that Culture Minister Gubenko was firm in refusing to return the Lubavitch books.
Story: Levin reported the Soviet political climate was hostile to such an initiative and shared news that Gorbachev had offered to resign but his resignation was refused. He also disclosed a leaked report that Foreign Minister Bessmertnykh might soon visit Israel.
Tags: moscow, israel, aryeh levin, schneerson library, didan natzach, gubenko, soviet union

Title: LA Times photographs Chabad delegation outside Lenin Library in Moscow
Summary: Los Angeles Times photographers shot the delegation outside Moscow's Lenin Library after officials refused to allow photography inside.
Story: Library staff barred the photographers from entering, saying they did not want the scandal publicized. Soviet official Tolstikov then telephoned the LA Times to ask the paper not to write about the dispute, claiming the special commission's work would yield positive results.
Tags: moscow, russia, los angeles times, lenin library, schneerson library, didan natzach, media coverage

Title: Soviet authorities pressure Moscow Chabad community over Polyakov synagogue
Summary: Building authorities summoned Zev Korbsky and demanded that the new Chabad community in Moscow be disbanded as punishment for entering the Polyakov synagogue without permission to pray and learn.
Story: Korbsky explained the community's position, and the officials ultimately apologized. The community continued to await formal approval transferring the historic Polyakov synagogue to Chabad's use, expected within days.
Tags: moscow, russia, polyakov synagogue, soviet union, zev korbsky, religious freedom

Title: Chabad delegation pursues Polyakov synagogue transfer at Mossoviet
Summary: The delegation went to the Mossoviet to receive a signed authorization transferring the Polyakov synagogue in Moscow to Chabad, but found the document still missing required signatures.
Story: Official Moskovsky received them and showed papers partially signed; deputy Natalya promised to obtain the remaining signature that day. The transfer of the historic synagogue had been promised repeatedly and was still awaiting final bureaucratic approval.
Tags: moscow, russia, polyakov synagogue, mossoviet, moskovsky, religious freedom

Title: CNN films Chabad delegation challenging Soviets over Schneerson library
Summary: CNN's Moscow crew filmed the Chabad delegation pressing Soviet official Tolstikov on why they were barred from meeting the special commission or seeing the books.
Story: Culture Minister Gubenko refused to be interviewed, so CNN settled for Tolstikov. On camera in Russian, Rabbi Shalom Ber Levin asked why the delegation could not meet the commission, view the books, or help identify the Lubavitch collection; Tolstikov claimed he did not know the reasons.
Tags: moscow, russia, cnn, schneerson library, didan natzach, tolstikov, gubenko, media coverage

Title: Soviet OVIR refuses to extend Chabad delegation's visas
Summary: OVIR refused to renew the Chabad delegation's expired Soviet visas and held their passports until a fine was paid for overstaying.
Story: Their attorney Lada and patron Veronika (Deborah Rachel) consulted with Soviet officials Yegorov, Ivanov, Babushkin, and Tolstikov, but found no solution. The delegation decided to pay the fine, retrieve their passports, and seek extensions piecemeal — a setback that came as the visa office itself faced impending closure.
Tags: moscow, russia, soviet union, ovir, visa, didan natzach

Title: Devorah Rachel Kogan writes Rebbe about opening Chabad library in Moscow
Summary: In early Sivan 5751, attorney Devorah Rachel Kogan wrote to the Rebbe about establishing a Chabad library in Moscow, separate from the Schneerson collection question.
Story: The Rebbe responded that opening a new Chabad library in Russia could provoke opponents to argue the Schneerson books should stay in Russia rather than leave it. He framed the argument as so distorted yet predictable that Chabad should avoid raising any such ideas. This ruling guided Levin's opposition to subsequent wing proposals for years afterward.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, devorah-rachel-kogan, menachem-mendel-schneerson

Title: Chabad holds Lag BaOmer boat parade for 600 children in Moscow
Summary: About 600 Jewish children in Moscow took part in a Lag BaOmer rally and outing, traveling on three cruise boats up the Moscow River to an island for games and a program.
Story: It was an unprecedented public Lag BaOmer event for Jewish children in the post-Soviet capital. Three Moscow River cruise boats carried participants to a rented island site for several hours of games framed by an opening and closing program of Twelve Pesukim, a short speech, and a raffle.
Tags: moscow, russia, lag baomer, children, soviet jewry, parade

Title: Soviet OVIR visa office dissolved; jurisdiction shifts to the Republics
Summary: Veronika informed the Chabad delegation that the central Soviet OVIR visa office had been abolished and that visa control was being transferred to the constituent Republics.
Story: The shift reflected the rising power of Yeltsin's Russian Federation government over the crumbling Soviet center. The delegation, whose existing visas were already expired, hoped relations with the Russian Republic's friendlier Foreign Ministry would help, though OVIR retained nominal control for another two weeks.
Tags: moscow, russia, soviet union, ovir, visa, russian federation

Title: Israeli Deputy Health Minister Eliezer Mizrachi visits Moscow Chabad
Summary: Deputy Minister Eliezer Mizrachi made a private visit to Moscow, touring the Marina Roshcha synagogue, yeshiva, mikvah, the Kremlin, the Lenin Library and the Polyakov synagogue.
Story: Mizrachi addressed the Moscow yeshiva students with words of encouragement and met with Ambassador Aryeh Levin, where the upcoming visit of Foreign Minister Bessmertnykh to Israel was discussed. Plans were made for Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy to raise the seforim issue directly with Bessmertnykh.
Tags: moscow, russia, marina roshcha, eliezer mizrachi, israel, kremlin, lenin library

Title: Soviet commission again defers decision on Schneerson library
Summary: The Soviet special commission on the Lubavitch books met with Culture Minister Gubenko and voted to extend its deliberations by another month rather than rule.
Story: Both delegation members and Veronika were refused permission to attend; even sympathetic Soviet figures Rizhov and Gelman were not invited. The further delay was seen as a deliberate stalling tactic meant to ease international pressure from heads of state, senators, scientists, and the press.
Tags: moscow, russia, soviet union, schneerson library, didan natzach, gubenko, commission

Title: Chabad delegation ordered out of USSR by May 15
Summary: Veronika (Deborah Rachel) informed the Chabad delegation that Soviet authorities required them to leave the USSR by 15 May, with no further extensions possible.
Story: Officials warned that defying the order would harm the seforim cause and Veronika's own access. After hours of consultations and a written appeal to the Rebbe, the Rebbe instructed them to follow her counsel and depart, prompting the delegation to plan an immediate return to the United States.
Tags: moscow, russia, soviet union, didan natzach, visa, expulsion

Title: Chabad delegation flies from Moscow to New York via Belfast and Gander
Summary: Forced out of the USSR, the Chabad delegation boarded an Aeroflot flight at dawn from Moscow with stopovers in Belfast and Gander, Canada, arriving in New York that afternoon.
Story: Veronika (Deborah Rachel) and her husband Andrei traveled with them to apply pressure in Washington and seek new visas. The delegation planned only a short stay in New York before returning to Moscow to continue lobbying for the return of the Schneerson library.
Tags: moscow, new york, didan natzach, aeroflot, belfast, gander, soviet union

Title: Rebbe blesses Chabad delegation at dollar distribution before returning to USSR
Summary: At a Sunday dollar distribution, the Rebbe addressed the Chabad delegation and their Russian partner Veronika (Deborah Rachel) and her newly converted husband Israel, blessing them for the return trip to Moscow.
Story: The Rebbe (in Russian) told Veronika that what had been achieved was 'only a beginning' and praised Rabbi Shalom Ber Levin's deep familiarity with the books, saying she should now learn from him. He gave them additional dollars for tzedakah to be given in Russia and wished them 'good news, great success.'
Tags: 770, dollar distribution, didan natzach, veronika irina antonova, deborah rachel, schneerson library

Title: Chabad delegation returns to Moscow to resume library mission
Summary: After two weeks back in New York, the Chabad delegation arrived in Moscow to resume their lobbying for the return of the Schneerson library and continue communal work.
Story: The trip resumed the diary of the special mission, which had been paused during the New York interlude. The delegation expected renewed efforts in Moscow and Washington — including a planned Baker–Bessmertnykh meeting the following Sunday and a Bessmertnykh visit to Israel — to keep pressure on the Soviet government over the Lubavitch books.
Tags: moscow, russia, soviet union, didan natzach, schneerson library

Title: First Agudas Chabad meeting in Soviet Union convenes in Moscow
Summary: The first Agudas Chabad meeting in the USSR convened in Moscow after the Chabad delegation returned from New York.
Story: On 16 Sivan 5751 (May 29, 1991), the inaugural meeting of Agudas Chabad in the Soviet Union took place in Moscow. R' Yitzchak Kogan opened with words of Torah on Parshat Beha'aloscha, and R' Shlomo Cunin read a response from the Lubavitcher Rebbe. The agenda covered the Schneersohn library campaign, the Polyakov synagogue, future organizational structure, and the Chernobyl children rescue.
Tags: agudas chabad, moscow, soviet union, russia, soviet jewry

Title: Chabad delegation adopts organizational structure for work in Russia
Summary: Agudas Chabad in Moscow adopted six formal decisions establishing Chabad's organizational structure in Russia.
Story: On Friday 18 Sivan 5751 (May 31, 1991), Agudas Chabad members in Moscow finalized resolutions to hire a Chabad manager working from a dedicated office, contract with Veronika for synagogue restoration and visa work, appoint a food distribution administrator, establish a Chabad beis din in Moscow recognized by Israel's chief rabbinate, recruit donors to fund operations, and designate R' Yosef Yitzchak Aharonov as coordinator reporting to the Agudas Chabad committee. The resolutions were sent to the Rebbe before Shabbat with a request for blessing.
Tags: agudas chabad, russia, moscow, beis din, soviet jewry, veronika, yosef yitzchak aharonov

Title: Chernyaev signals Gorbachev plans to release Schneersohn library to Chabad
Summary: Gorbachev aide Anatoly Chernyaev signaled to the Chabad delegation that the Schneersohn library matter would be resolved positively within days.
Story: On Monday 21 Sivan 5751 (June 3, 1991) in Moscow, Veronika reported to the Chabad delegation that Anatoly Chernyaev had said Gorbachev would come to Moscow on June 6 to settle the library question, with books to begin transfer from the Lenin Library on June 8. Chernyaev added that this time the books would be returned even without the consent of Lenin Library director Gubinko. The delegation also negotiated a three-month trial contract with Veronika to coordinate visas, synagogue recovery, and related advocacy.
Tags: schneersohn library, gorbachev, chernyaev, russia, books, lenin library, moscow

Title: Russian FM tells delegation Gorbachev will resolve Schneersohn books matter
Summary: The Russian Federation foreign minister told Veronika that Gorbachev informed the US embassy he had decided to resolve the Schneersohn books matter positively.
Story: On Tuesday 22 Sivan 5751 (June 4, 1991), the foreign minister of the Russian Federation told Veronika by phone that Gorbachev had replied to the US embassy in Washington that he had decided to conclude the Schneersohn books matter positively. The delegation continued parallel work on recovering the Polyakov synagogue in Moscow and preparing the Chernobyl children's camp for the planned airlift to Israel. David Kogan arrived from Leningrad to help run the camp.
Tags: schneersohn library, gorbachev, us embassy, books, russia, diplomacy, washington

Title: Wedding of Levi Yitzchak HaLevi Klein and Rivka
Summary: On 23 Sivan 5751, Levi Yitzchak HaLevi Klein married Rivka; he would serve as director of the Chabad House in Memphis, Tennessee.
Story: Levi Yitzchak HaLevi Klein, son of Leah and Yerachmiel Binyamin HaLevi Klein, married Rivka on 23 Sivan 5751. He serves as director of the Chabad House in Memphis, Tennessee.
Tags: wedding, klein family, memphis, tennessee, chabad house

Title: Chabad emissaries spend Shabbat with rescued Chernobyl children at camp
Summary: Three Chabad emissaries spent Shabbat at the Chernobyl children's preparation camp outside Moscow, leading the children's first communal Shabbat.
Story: On Shabbat 26 Sivan 5751 (June 8, 1991), R' Yosef Yitzchak Aharonov, R' Shlomo Cunin, and R' M.M. Shemtov stayed at the preparation camp for roughly 140 Chernobyl rescue children awaiting evacuation to Israel. For most of the children it was their first experience of communal prayer, Kiddush, Shabbat meals, and Havdalah. Several girls received Jewish names during the Torah reading, and many boys said they would receive Hebrew names at brit milah upon arriving in Israel.
Tags: chernobyl children, shabbat, summer camp, rescue, moscow, kfar chabad

Title: Russian Ministry of Culture rules Schneersohn library should stay in Russia
Summary: A Russian Ministry of Culture meeting concluded the Schneersohn library was confiscated property needed for Russian Jewry and should remain in Russia.
Story: On Monday 28 Sivan 5751 (June 10, 1991), a multi-hour meeting at the Russian Ministry of Culture with Lenin Library director Gubinko and three lawyers produced a 16-page memorandum concluding the Schneersohn library collection should remain in Russia. Near the end of the meeting Gubinko fell ill; an ambulance was called but he refused hospitalization. Chernyaev later told Veronika by phone that the memo did not concern him and he still intended to conclude the matter favorably within days.
Tags: schneersohn library, gubinko, ministry of culture, russia, books, lenin library, moscow

Title: Chabad airlifts ~130 Chernobyl rescue children from Moscow to Israel
Summary: Chabad airlifted roughly 130 Chernobyl rescue children from Moscow to Israel after overcoming visa, capacity, and mid-flight emergency problems.
Story: On 1 Tammuz 5751 (June 13, 1991), the first flight of Chernobyl children rescued by Chabad reached Israel despite severe complications. Visas were granted only at the last minute and Aeroflot initially refused to board children without them. After takeoff a mechanical fault forced an emergency return to Moscow; the children boarded a replacement aircraft and arrived in Israel that evening, greeted by Chabad with Shehecheyanu, singing, and dancing.
Tags: chernobyl children, israel, aeroflot, evacuation, rescue, aliyah, moscow, kfar chabad

Title: Failed attempt to print Sichas Hashavua in Moscow
Summary: Chabad emissaries in Moscow tried but failed to find an affordable printer for the Russian-language Sichas Hashavua, with Alagraphics quoting $2,500 for one issue.
Story: On 6 Tammuz 5751, R. Y.Y. Aharonov and the special-mission delegation in Moscow tried to arrange printing of the Russian Sichas Hashavua. After visiting Alagraphics, a dollar-only printer, and receiving an exorbitant $2,500 quote, Aharonov decided to print the sheets in Eretz Yisrael and ship them ready. The episode illustrates the extreme practical difficulties Chabad faced operating in post-Soviet Moscow.
Tags: moscow, russia, sichas hashavua, aharonov, alagraphics, printing

Title: Gorbachev decides to return the Chabad seforim
Summary: Veronika reported that Gorbachev had finally resolved on 19 June 1991 to return the Chabad library, intending to do so before the G7 summit.
Story: On 8 Tammuz 5751 the delegation learned that Gorbachev, at 1 p.m. the previous day, had made a definitive decision to return the seforim of the Rebbeim. He aimed to complete the transfer before July 10 (28 Tammuz), ahead of the G7 meeting opening July 14. Veronika and Chernyaev's office were preparing the formal paperwork.
Tags: seforim, library, russia, gorbachev, chernyaev, g7, veronika

Title: Rebbe inquires about the seforim case
Summary: The Rebbe asked R. Leibel Groner for an update on the seforim, the same night word came that Gorbachev had decided to return the Chabad library.
Story: On the evening of 7 Tammuz 5751, R. Leibel Groner reported that the Rebbe had asked him about developments in the seforim case. That same night Veronika informed the Moscow delegation that Gorbachev had finally decided at 1 p.m. to return the Chabad library, hoping to do so before July 10 and the G7 summit. The delegation was instructed to keep the news confidential among themselves.
Tags: seforim, library, russia, gorbachev, chernyaev, veronika

Title: Shabbos Chukas at the Kremlin memorial ceremony
Summary: On Shabbos Chukas, members of the delegation attended a memorial ceremony at the Kremlin and met Moscow mayor Popov and Rabbi Pinchas Goldschmidt.
Story: On Shabbos Chukas (10 Tammuz 5751), the delegation traveled to Marina Roshcha to be close to the Kremlin for a morning memorial ceremony. About 50 attended, including Mayor Popov, representatives of the Great Synagogue and the delegation, and clergy. The author had a long, emotional conversation with Rabbi Pinchas Goldschmidt about Chabad activity and the Chernobyl children's operation.
Tags: moscow, kremlin, marina roshcha, popov, goldschmidt, chernobyl

Title: Meeting with Robert Maxwell about the Chabad seforim
Summary: The Moscow delegation met for over an hour with Robert Maxwell, Max Fisher and Jacobs to plan an approach to Gorbachev for return of the Chabad seforim.
Story: On Motzaei Shabbos, 10 Tammuz 5751, Maxwell, Fisher and Jacobs hosted the delegation at Moscow's Hotel Oktyabrskaya. Fisher had spoken the day before with Zolotov, the Deputy Culture Minister, who confirmed only Gorbachev could now decide. Maxwell agreed Fisher would prepare the legal angle and Maxwell would press Primakov, Yakovlev and ultimately Gorbachev himself for the seforim's return.
Tags: maxwell, fisher, jacobs, moscow, seforim, library, gorbachev, yakovlev, primakov

Title: CNN segment on the Chabad library
Summary: CNN broadcast a 3.5-minute report on the campaign to return the Chabad library, just before 6 p.m. Moscow time.
Story: On 14 Tammuz 5751 (June 26, 1991), CNN aired its prepared piece on the seforim case, lasting about 3.5 minutes. The diary describes the coverage as objective and middle-of-the-road. Earlier that day the delegation was photographed in front of the library for a parallel article being prepared by Maxwell's reporter for a European newspaper.
Tags: cnn, media, moscow, seforim, library

Title: Delegation pursues ownership order for Polyakov shul
Summary: R. Z. Korovsky and R. M.C. Levin went to Moscow's privatization office to obtain the ownership order transferring the Polyakov synagogue to Agudas Chassidei Chabad.
Story: On 14 Tammuz 5751 Korovsky and M.C. Levin traveled to the privatization office of the Mossoviet to receive the order assigning the Polyakov synagogue to Agudas Chassidei Chabad. They were given paperwork to fill out at home, then redirected to obtain entrance approval from the building manager. When she denied knowing of any decision, the author faxed the formal decision document, but the manager continued to stonewall.
Tags: moscow, polyakov, synagogue, privatization, agudas chassidei chabad

Title: Lazaniya brings Rayatz arrest file from Dnepropetrovsk
Summary: Lazaniya was scheduled to arrive in Moscow from Dnepropetrovsk with his KGB contact, bringing the complete arrest file of R. Levi Yitzchak Schneerson.
Story: On 14 Tammuz 5751, Lazaniya was expected in Moscow from Dnepropetrovsk together with his liaison and a KGB official, carrying the full file on the arrest of R. Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, the Rebbe's father. He had confirmed by phone on multiple recent days that he would deliver the materials. The diary lists this as one of four major expected events of the day.
Tags: dnepropetrovsk, levi yitzchak schneerson, kgb, rayatz, archives

Title: Maxwell raises seforim with Gorbachev
Summary: At a 40-minute meeting with Gorbachev, Maxwell requested the Chabad seforim; Gorbachev affirmed they belonged to the Chassidim and would be returned.
Story: On 14 Tammuz 5751, Maxwell pressed Gorbachev for the seforim at the end of a productive 40-minute meeting. Gorbachev replied that the books belong to the Chassidim and his aides were already preparing the paperwork to return them through the emissaries in Moscow. He pointedly added that Russia must not sell sacred objects, even in exchange for Maxwell's many favors. Chernyaev then urgently summoned Tumarkin to prepare return documents.
Tags: maxwell, gorbachev, moscow, seforim, library, tumarkin, chernyaev

Title: Author's family arrives in Moscow for summer camp
Summary: The author's family flew in from the U.S. along with 28 counselors for Ezras Achim summer camps across Russia.
Story: On Thursday evening 13 Tammuz 5751, the author's wife and children arrived from the U.S. together with 28 young men and women coming to staff the Ezras Achim summer camps throughout Russia. They also brought roughly 150 packages of food and supplies for the camps. With no help available, the delegation unloaded everything from the truck themselves at the Molodyozhnaya Hotel.
Tags: moscow, ezras achim, camp, family, tinok, sheliach

Title: Shabbos at the Ezras Achim children's camp
Summary: The author and his family spent Shabbos at the Ezras Achim children's camp outside Moscow, walking the final stretch as Shabbos arrived.
Story: On erev Shabbos 15 Tammuz 5751, the delegation traveled to the camp but, with sunset approaching while still several kilometers away, they left their belongings on the bus and walked. Arriving in the middle of the seudah, they sang with the campers and the author related the journey. Through Shabbos they spoke with the children, davened slowly together word-by-word, and the head counselor Shlomo Varovich explained tefillah and Torah reading.
Tags: camp, ezras achim, russia, chinuch, tefilla, family

Title: Fixed delegation work pattern for Moscow and camp
Summary: The author's wife took on kashrus supervision at the Ezras Achim camp kitchen while he commuted between Moscow and the camp on Shabbos.
Story: On Motzaei Shabbos 16 Tammuz 5751, the family settled into a routine: the rebbetzin would oversee the camp kitchen during the day from a nearby inn, while the author would spend Shabbos at camp and weekdays in Moscow with the delegation. The diary notes the camp lacked proper kashrus oversight in the kitchen before her arrival. The author's sons began integrating with the campers despite the language barrier.
Tags: moscow, camp, kashrus, ezras achim, family

Title: Shiur at the Moscow yeshiva on eruvin
Summary: The author delivered a shiur on hilchos eruvin (tavshilin, chatzeiros, techumin) at the Moscow yeshiva on 19 Tammuz 5751.
Story: On Monday 19 Tammuz 5751, with delegation activity slow, the author traveled to the Moscow yeshiva and taught a class in the halachos of eruvin — covering eruvei tavshilin, chatzeiros and techumin. Afterwards he went to the delegation office, where R. Yitzchak Kogan and Ziva Mikieva of the Joint Venture magazine were preparing a feature article on the Polyakov synagogue.
Tags: moscow, yeshiva, halacha, eruvin, tomchei tmimim

Title: Fatal car accident kills yeshiva secretary
Summary: A nighttime car crash in Moscow killed the yeshiva's secretary and seriously injured the man named Shenetsis, leaving him hospitalized with broken bones.
