Story: On the night of 20-21 Tammuz 5751, a car struck the vehicle carrying Shenetsis and the secretary of the Moscow yeshiva. The secretary was killed and Shenetsis lay in hospital with multiple broken bones. The author learned of the tragedy the next morning, 21 Tammuz, when he came to Marina Roshcha en route to camp.
Tags: moscow, yeshiva, accident, tragedy

Title: Meeting on Lubavitch rabbinic presence in Leningrad
Summary: R. Netta Berchen and the author concluded that the highest Chabad priority for Leningrad was placing a Chabad rav there, with R. Yerachmiel Bleinov proposed.
Story: On 21 Tammuz 5751, the author met R. Netta Berchen, in Moscow on behalf of Shamir to supervise activity in Leningrad. After a lengthy conversation at the home of his relative, they agreed the single most important step for Leningrad was bringing a Chabad rav, and discussed R. Yerachmiel Bleinov as the candidate.
Tags: leningrad, shamir, rabbinic, bleinov, chinuch

Title: Push to enlist G7 leaders on Chabad seforim
Summary: The delegation moved to enlist G7 heads of government, including Andreotti and John Major, to pressure Gorbachev directly on releasing the Chabad library.
Story: On the evening of 27 Tammuz 5751, Veronika urged that the leaders of the seven major nations ask Gorbachev directly when the seforim would be returned. She drafted a letter from the delegation to be co-signed by their seven ambassadors. R. Y.Y. Aharonov phoned R. Garlick (who had earlier moved Andreotti to act) and R. Pinchas Wagle (for British PM John Major), requesting renewed letters and meetings.
Tags: g7, gorbachev, andreotti, major, garlick, wagle, veronika, seforim

Title: Veronika returns; Gorbachev delays seforim decision
Summary: Veronika returned to Moscow via Cyprus but found Gorbachev still had not issued the order to release the Chabad seforim.
Story: On 26 Tammuz 5751, Veronika returned from Eretz Yisrael through Cyprus expecting to meet Chernyaev with news on returning the seforim. Instead she only reached Tumarkin, who admitted the matter was unresolved and that Gorbachev had told Chernyaev, 'when we return to Moscow we'll talk.' Alarmed, she directed the delegation to escalate pressure from abroad.
Tags: veronika, chernyaev, gorbachev, seforim, library, tumarkin, cyprus

Title: Delegation departs for G7 summit in London
Summary: The delegation flew to London to intensify pressure on Gorbachev during the G7 summit after he again deferred the seforim decision.
Story: On 3 Menachem Av 5751, Veronika reported that Chernyaev had told her Gorbachev had pushed the seforim file back to Govinko and would not engage with it before the G7 summit. She insisted on traveling that night to London with R. Y.Y. Aharonov and R. Y. Kogan to escalate pressure during the summit. The Rebbe, informed by R. Groner, instructed: 'do everything as she says.'
Tags: g7, london, seforim, library, gorbachev, kovinko, veronika, aharonov, kogan

Title: Visits to Chabad summer camps in beis hamikdash halachos
Summary: The author taught hilchos beis hamikdash at the boys' and girls' Chabad camps and at the Moscow yeshiva during the Three Weeks.
Story: On Monday morning 5 Menachem Av 5751, the author traveled with his wife to the boys' camp and stayed through Tuesday afternoon, teaching the upper grades in hilchos beis hamikdash and continuing the nightly group. On Tuesday afternoon he visited the girls' camp, spoke during dinner on beis hamikdash, and reviewed the next day's shiur with a counselor. On Wednesday 7 Menachem Av he taught the fourth-year class in the Moscow yeshiva on the same topic.
Tags: camp, beis hamikdash, halacha, russia, chinuch

Title: Bush raises seforim with Gorbachev at G7
Summary: At the London G7 summit, President George Bush handed Gorbachev a letter prepared by Sandy raising three issues, including the Chabad library, to which Gorbachev promised prompt action.
Story: On 9 Av 5751 (the nidcheh), R. Y.Y. Aharonov reported by phone the delegation's London activity. Bush handed Gorbachev a letter prepared by Sandy on three subjects including the seforim, and Gorbachev replied that he knew of the matter and would arrange it shortly. The delegation also met Peter Hartman, an aide to Chancellor Kohl, after the Rebbe approved approaching the German delegation. Aharonov told Hartman that the whole saga began when the Frierdiker Rebbe fled Lubavitch as the Germans approached the region in 1915.
Tags: g7, london, bush, gorbachev, seforim, sandy, andreotti, chernyaev, hartman, kohl

Title: Government commission votes to return Chabad seforim
Summary: A 100-member Soviet government commission unanimously recommended returning the Chabad library, sending the decision to Gorbachev for signature.
Story: On the afternoon of 13 Menachem Av 5751, Veronika told the delegation that a government commission had sat that day on several pending matters, with return of the seforim as the second item on the agenda. Eight representatives presented the case and all 100 members voted in favor. The resulting resolution, citing legal and political grounds for the return, was to be presented for Gorbachev's signature that Friday; Gorbachev himself had missed the session for another meeting.
Tags: seforim, library, gorbachev, veronika, moscow, commission

Title: Meeting with Italian ambassador in Moscow
Summary: The author and Italian shluchim met Italy's ambassador to Russia, who knew of the seforim case but had no readout of Andreotti's recent talks with Gorbachev.
Story: On Wednesday 13 Menachem Av 5751, the Italian shluchim arrived for the kinus and went to meet Italy's ambassador in Moscow, asking the author to join. They first met his deputy, fully briefed on the seforim, then the ambassador himself, who likewise knew the file but lacked any record of Andreotti–Gorbachev exchanges from London. The ambassador requested community paperwork, but Veronika preferred to wait, expecting good news that evening.
Tags: italy, ambassador, moscow, seforim, shluchim, andreotti

Title: European shluchim kinus opens with trip to Lubavitch
Summary: More than 100 European shluchim opened their kinus in Moscow with a bus convoy to Lubavitch, davening at the Ohel and touring the historic Chabad courtyard.
Story: On Friday 15 Av 5751, four buses of more than 100 shluchim plus a busload of Minsk yeshiva students drove to Lubavitch, arriving around 4 p.m. R. Moshe Kotlarsky opened the program at the Ohel, the author spoke about the seforim, and the general pan was read by R. N. Sudak; Tehillim by R. S. Matusof; siyum by R. Y.Y. Matusof; dvar malchus by R. M. Garlick. They then davened Mincha in the courtyard, the author surveyed the history of the chatzer and its buildings, and they returned to Moscow at 4 a.m.
Tags: shluchim, kinus, lubavitch, ohel, minsk, kotlarsky, garlick, lazar

Title: Gorbachev defers seforim decision again
Summary: Late on 15 Av 5751, Chernyaev told the delegation Gorbachev would not decide the seforim case that day — perhaps Monday, perhaps when Bush visited Moscow.
Story: Returning at dawn on Friday 15 Av 5751 from the Lubavitch trip, the author spoke with R. Y.Y. Aharonov, who reported Chernyaev's latest update: no decision today, possibly Monday, possibly only when Bush arrived in Moscow. Veronika was deeply disappointed. The repeated postponements, despite the commission vote and high-level pressure, left the delegation again in suspense.
Tags: gorbachev, chernyaev, seforim, library, bush, veronika, aharonov

Title: Shluchim visit Gan Yisrael summer camp in Moscow
Summary: International Chabad shluchim visited the Gan Yisrael summer camp in Moscow on Erev Shabbat, where children and shluchim spoke and a video greeting from the Rebbe was shown.
Story: Shluchim including R' Gurevich, R' Friedman, and R' Gerlik addressed the camp in Russian, while R' Moshe Kotlarsky spoke in English. R' Y. Meshulvin conveyed regards from the Rebbe and brought a video of the children's rally to show the campers. The child Moshe Pesach Finkel concluded by publicly thanking the Rebbe in fluent English for sending the shluchim.
Tags: russia, moscow, shluchim, summer camp, moshe pesach finkel, kotlarsky, gan yisrael

Title: Shabbat farbrengen at Polyakov Synagogue with shluchim kinus
Summary: Shabbat farbrengen at Moscow's Polyakov Synagogue with the European shluchim kinus, where R' Shmuel Motusov recounted his arrest for learning Torah in that very shul.
Story: After Friday-night seudah at Molodyozhnaya Hall, the kinus participants marched in procession to the Polyakov Synagogue under a militia honor guard. Following the Torah reading, R' Berel Lazar and R' B. Cunin spoke and led dancing into the courtyard. The featured speaker at the multi-hour farbrengen was R' Shmuel Motusov, who described being arrested decades earlier for learning Torah in this same synagogue.
Tags: russia, moscow, polyakov synagogue, shluchim, farbrengen, shmuel motusov, molodyozhnaya

Title: Shluchim banquet at Hotel Kosmos in Moscow
Summary: The Third European Shluchim Kinus held its banquet at Hotel Kosmos in Moscow with dignitaries and press in attendance.
Story: The banquet opened with Tehillim chapter 90 read by R' B. Cunin. Speakers included Kogan on behalf of Agudat Chabad, Shmuel Levin, Yaakov Weisselbach of Kishinev, Shaievich, and Pidrovsky, with R' Kotlarsky as MC and R' M. Levin speaking in Russian. Important Soviet figures and journalists attended this milestone marking Chabad's public emergence in Russia.
Tags: russia, moscow, shluchim, banquet, hotel kosmos, media, kishinev

Title: Tour of Moscow landmarks with European shluchim delegation
Summary: The shluchim toured central Moscow sites including the Schneersohn library at the Lenin Library, the Kremlin, Red Square, and the Polyakov Synagogue.
Story: The diarist served as guide, beginning at the library steps for a group photograph, then continuing through the Kremlin and Red Square. The route pointedly passed the Mossoviet, the Chabad office building, and the Polyakov Synagogue, after which buses brought the delegation to the Timiryazevskaya lecture hall. Word arrived that the Rebbe had spoken on Shabbat about the kinus shluchim visiting Lubavitch, Alma-Ata, and now the Soviet capital, instructing them to daven Mincha as well in Alma-Ata.
Tags: russia, moscow, shluchim, kremlin, red square, schneersohn library, lenin library

Title: Chabad shluchim wave to President Bush outside Moscow embassy
Summary: Chabad shluchim gathered outside the US Embassy in Moscow waving to President Bush as he departed for talks with Gorbachev about returning the Chabad library.
Story: Following R' Yosef Aronov's proposal at the kinus, shluchim halted their bus convoy en route to the airport for Alma-Ata and positioned themselves at the embassy corner. After more than an hour of waiting, Bush slowed his motorcade and waved at length as he passed. Bush carried a letter to Gorbachev about the Schneersohn library and raised the issue at their meeting, though no answer had yet come back.
Tags: russia, moscow, george h.w. bush, gorbachev, schneersohn library, us embassy, summit

Title: Shluchim fly from Moscow to Alma-Ata for kinus closing
Summary: After the embassy stop, the shluchim flew four hours to Alma-Ata for the kinus closing in honor of the yahrzeit of R' Levi Yitzchak Schneersohn.
Story: Upon arrival a celebration was held drawing about 200 local Jews, with speeches by R' Berel Lazar, R' Kotlarsky, R' Raskin, R' Yaffe and two local community leaders. R' A. Niselevich led the singing, the 'Lamplighters' video was shown with R' Y. Gisser explaining in Russian, and Yaakov Weisselbach of Kishinev translated the Yiddish speeches. The Rebbe had instructed during the prior Shabbat farbrengen that the shluchim daven both Shacharit and Mincha in Alma-Ata.
Tags: alma-ata, kazakhstan, shluchim, kinus, levi yitzchak schneersohn, lamplighters

Title: Yahrzeit visit to grave of R' Levi Yitzchak Schneersohn in Alma-Ata
Summary: On 20 Menachem Av, the yahrzeit of the Rebbe's father, the European shluchim visited the grave of R' Levi Yitzchak Schneersohn in Alma-Ata.
Story: After mikveh and Shacharit at a local shul, the delegation went to the gravesite. R' Kotlarsky and the diarist spoke (the latter about the arrest file then being negotiated for return) and R' Kamenetzky spoke in Russian, after which R' Y.L. Raskin read the general Pan. Strong winds and a technical airport shutdown delayed the return flight to Moscow several hours, during which they davened Mincha as the Rebbe had directed and R' Kotlarsky formally closed the Third European Shluchim Kinus.
Tags: alma-ata, kazakhstan, levi yitzchak schneersohn, yahrzeit, 20 av, raskin, kotlarsky

Title: Mass bris milah for ten boys in Moscow
Summary: Ten boys were brought by bus from the Chabad summer camp to Moscow for circumcisions on 24 Menachem Av.
Story: Returning to Moscow that morning with the bus carrying the boys, the diarist served as sandek for Yosef (Sergey), one of his regular students. The mass bris was part of the Chabad shluchim's push to bring Russian Jewish children into the covenant during the brief window of religious openness before the political situation shifted.
Tags: russia, moscow, bris milah, soviet jewry, yosef sergei

Title: KGB returns arrest file of R' Levi Yitzchak Schneersohn in Kiev
Summary: The Ukrainian KGB formally returned the roughly 65-page arrest and interrogation file of R' Levi Yitzchak Schneersohn, the Rebbe's father, at a ceremony in Kiev.
Story: Following months of negotiation through Lanya Odnopozov, the diarist and R' Yosef Kogan took a night train to Kiev and met with the KGB deputy chairman for all of Ukraine, who delivered a Russian-language speech blaming the original arrests on 'our elders' and presenting the file as a gesture of esteem for Chabad. The file included the original interrogation documents, the sentence of exile without trial, R' Levi Yitzchak's unanswered appeal to KGB chief Beria, and a recent rehabilitation ruling clearing him of all charges. Officials also offered to search for files of four Chabad rabbis arrested the same day in Kharkov — Pevzner, Gorkov, Pinson and Gurewitz — and to help retrieve the file of the Rayatz.
Tags: ussr, kgb, kiev, ukraine, levi yitzchak schneersohn, rehabilitation, soviet archives, yekaterinoslav

Title: Polyakov Synagogue returned to Chabad possession in Moscow
Summary: Chabad took physical possession of the historic Polyakov Synagogue in Moscow on 27 Menachem Av, three months after the official decision to return it.
Story: Despite the current tenants' refusal to vacate on the grounds that the city had not yet provided alternate premises, large groups of Chabad children and adults pushed through the doors after davening at camp, broke into the sanctuary, turned on the electricity and began davening. Police observed and left while officials negotiated at the Mossoviet; Veronika intervened forcefully and returned with a decision that the building would transfer to Chabad that very night, with militia stationed to protect it.
Tags: russia, moscow, polyakov synagogue, agudat chabad, veronika, marina roscha

Title: Aron Kodesh installed at Lubavitch Synagogue Agudat Chabad in Moscow
Summary: An aron kodesh was brought from Marina Roscha and installed at the Polyakov shul, now named Beit Knesset Lubavitch Agudat Chabad, on Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul.
Story: After the building was secured, a mezuzah was affixed, a large Russian-language sign reading 'Beit Knesset Lubavitch Agudat Chabad' was hung, and Meir Stambler distributed flyers announcing the synagogue's return and the upcoming Shabbat tefillot. The diarist worked on setting up the aron until 4:30 PM before travelling back to camp for Shabbat, leaving the new shul ready for its first public Shabbat.
Tags: russia, moscow, polyakov synagogue, agudat chabad, marina roscha, aron kodesh, meir stambler

Title: Rebbe gives dollar with blessing for long life on Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul
Summary: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5751, during the dollar distribution, the Rebbe gave the writer a birthday blessing and an additional dollar for success.
Story: The author marks his birthday on Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5751 by receiving dollars from the Rebbe, who blessed him with long and good years. The Rebbe then handed an additional dollar and added a blessing for success 'like the king who read the Torah before all the people,' with good timing and health.
Tags: dollars, blessing, birthday, 770

Title: Agudat Chabad committee meeting on aid, arrest file, and library
Summary: The Agudat Chabad committee met in Moscow on 1 Elul to coordinate food shipments, publicity around the returned arrest file, and the still-pending library return.
Story: Decisions included moving food aid shipments from the Monosonik depot to the new synagogue, publicizing in Kfar Chabad magazine that the file documents proved R' Levi Yitzchak's arrest had been deliberately framed, and dispatching photographs of the documents for the article. Veronika reported that the synagogue building handover would be finalized the next day; on the library, however, she urged patience and waiting for the right opportunity rather than further public pressure.
Tags: russia, moscow, agudat chabad, schneersohn library, kfar chabad, veronika

Title: Rabbis Aronov and Cunin fly to New York with R' Levi Yitzchak file
Summary: R' Yosef Aronov and R' Shlomo Cunin flew from Moscow to deliver the returned arrest file of R' Levi Yitzchak to the Rebbe and to advance the library campaign.
Story: Veronika asked them to also carry a letter requesting the Rebbe's blessing for the library after Gorbachev had told Chernyaev he wished to defer signing the prepared release papers. In a brief late-night yechidus the Rebbe accepted the file with words about the merit of pidyon shevuyim and 'every moment one hastens,' and when R' Cunin reported that only the Rebbe's blessing remained for the library the Rebbe replied 'do you suspect me?' He added that the book matter could yet be finished before R' Cunin's son's wedding on 18 Elul, and that bringing 'one more file' would mean Moshiach has come.
Tags: new york, 770, yechidus, levi yitzchak schneersohn, pidyon shevuyim, schneersohn library, chernyaev

Title: Rebbe directs diarist to remain on Schneersohn library work
Summary: Asked whether to accept a permanent rabbinic post in Leningrad or a Russia-wide yeshiva supervisor role, the Rebbe answered that involvement with the library obligated him to continue.
Story: The diarist had submitted a written question on 4 Elul presenting offers to serve as av beit din of Leningrad and as general supervisor of Tomchei Temimim branches across Russia under Ezrat Achim. The Rebbe's reply read 'one engaged with the library here and connected to it — this requires continuation, etc. I will mention at the tziyun,' effectively keeping him in Moscow until the library matter was resolved.
Tags: russia, moscow, leningrad, schneersohn library, ezrat achim, shlichus, tomchei temimim

Title: Distribution of clothes at Moscow Chabad boys' summer camp
Summary: Chabad emissaries distributed donated clothing to children at a Moscow boys' summer camp.
Story: Clothing shipments meant for the camp were stuck in Soviet customs for a month and only cleared the previous Wednesday. On Friday the author drove four large crates to the boys' camp, addressed the children on the laws of erev Shabbos, and distributed the garments together with his wife. The talk framed the gift as a reason to thank the Rebbe and his shluchim by committing to Shabbos, kashrus and Torah observance.
Tags: moscow, soviet union, summer camp, shluchim, levi heber, chinuch

Title: Final agreement signed for Polyakov synagogue handover in Moscow
Summary: A meeting at the Polyakov shul on 6 Elul produced final terms for transferring rooms, telephone service and utilities to Agudat Chabad.
Story: Veronika, Natalya from the Mossoviet, the building's former director Galina, R' Y. Kogan and the diarist agreed that two women's section rooms and three ground floor rooms would transfer immediately, a phone line at 202-7696 would be installed at once, and electricity billing would shift to Chabad after paperwork. The question of whether Chabad would have to finance the new building for the displaced tenants was deferred, with Chabad arguing that other religious communities had not been required to pay.
Tags: russia, moscow, polyakov synagogue, agudat chabad, mossoviet, veronika

Title: Distribution of clothes at Moscow Chabad girls' summer camp
Summary: Seven crates of clothing were brought to the Chabad girls' summer camp outside Moscow and distributed to the campers.
Story: Following the boys' camp distribution two days earlier, the author and his wife drove with seven crates to the girls' camp. He spoke about Chabad's broader work in Russia — bringing in kosher food, opening schools, and now leaving each girl Shabbos clothes as a keepsake of what they had learned about Shabbos and mitzvos. His wife organized the garments and helped the girls choose.
Tags: moscow, soviet union, summer camp, shluchim, girls, chinuch

Title: Double wedding held in Moscow Chabad shul during the August 1991 coup
Summary: A double wedding for two young Chabad couples was held in the Moscow AGUH shul on the opening day of the Soviet coup attempt.
Story: With tanks in central Moscow and Shaievich unable to appear, the community moved the chuppah into the AGUH synagogue and added a second couple — Igor and Asya Gerkovsky of Moscow and Yura and Palina Kreimer of Kishinev. About forty guests and visiting bochurim attended. Before the chuppah, word arrived from the Rebbe that no one should change their travel or wedding plans, lifting morale; Rabbi B.S. Kunin arrived from the airport at the last minute and was honored with mesader kiddushin.
Tags: moscow, soviet union, soviet coup, wedding, marina roshcha, agudas chasidei chabad, kunin, gerkovsky, kreimer, kishinev

Title: Soviet August Coup against Gorbachev begins in Moscow
Summary: From his Moscow office on 9 Elul the diarist recorded the start of the coup deposing Gorbachev, with KGB, army and police seizing control and Vice President Yanayev installed.
Story: Walking out into the streets the diarist found people debating on every corner along Tverskaya, a demonstration of one to two thousand at Manezhnaya Square, and Red Square sealed off by guards. A friendly policeman assured Chabad's new shul was being protected and that all was calm, but reports were coming in that tanks were on the main thoroughfares and rumors circulated that Gorbachev had been killed. The diarist sat writing calmly in the Lubavitch Synagogue office as the August Coup unfolded around him.
Tags: ussr, moscow, gorbachev, yanayev, august coup, kgb, tanks, manezhnaya square, tverskaya

Title: Chabad delegation petitions Lubyanka KGB for return of Schneersohn library
Summary: On the second night of the August coup, the Chabad delegation went to KGB headquarters to request a meeting about the Schneersohn library.
Story: While tanks were rolling through Moscow during the attempted hardline coup, Rabbis Aharonov, Kunin and Kogan walked into Lubyanka to request a meeting with the KGB chairman about the seized Schneersohn library. They were redirected to an adjacent building where two women received them, said they were aware of the books issue, and ultimately told them only to submit a formal written request — the KGB chairman was in fact one of the coup organizers.
Tags: moscow, soviet union, kgb, lubyanka, schneersohn library, seforim, soviet coup, kunin, aharonov, kogan

Title: Chabad delegation tries to reach Yeltsin at the White House during coup
Summary: On the third day of the coup the delegation pushed through the crowds at Yeltsin's besieged White House to request a meeting about the books.
Story: With rumors that Yeltsin was gaining strength, the delegation made its way through thousands of demonstrators and police surrounding the Russian White House to one of Yeltsin's aides — the same official who had hosted them on 20 Kislev when Yeltsin promised to return the books at the first opportunity. The aide took the details to Yeltsin's office, but Yeltsin had just gone into an emergency session as the coup collapsed and could not receive the delegation.
Tags: moscow, soviet union, yeltsin, white house, schneersohn library, soviet coup, sukhanov

Title: Chabad summer camp ends, campers return to Moscow
Summary: The second session of the Moscow Chabad summer camp closed and campers and staff returned to the city.
Story: The camp's closing program had included a writing exercise where every child sent a letter to the Rebbe, and an evening celebration combining brisos, pidyonei haben and bar mitzvos for children who had passed those milestones during the session. The staff had planned to fly by helicopter directly to Lubavitch after the buses left, but rainy weather grounded the helicopter and they returned to Moscow instead.
Tags: moscow, soviet union, summer camp, shluchim, lubavitch town

Title: Chabad delegation visits Yeltsin's White House on day of coup's collapse
Summary: As the coup collapsed, the delegation entered the Russian White House, was filmed by television, and pressed officials again about the Schneersohn library.
Story: The delegation walked past the barricades of metal drums, stones and planks that had stopped the tanks and entered the main hall where Yeltsin was seated; Yeltsin noticed them and watched them at length. They met Ryzhkov, who said the new political moment brought the books closer. Elie Wiesel, also present, promised to raise the books with Gorbachev. The delegation later spoke at length in aide Sukhanov's office, who said he would try to arrange a Yeltsin meeting.
Tags: moscow, soviet union, yeltsin, white house, elie wiesel, schneersohn library, soviet coup, ryzhkov, sukhanov

Title: Wedding of Yaakov Weisblach of Kishinev at Moscow AGUH shul
Summary: Yaakov Weisblach, head of the Kishinev Jewish community, married a Machon Chaya Mushka graduate at the Moscow AGUH shul.
Story: The groom led Chabad activity in Kishinev; the bride came from Machon Chaya Mushka. Reception and chuppah were held at the AGUH synagogue and the seudah at Hotel Kosmos, with visiting bochurim and seminary girls (the summer-camp counselors) leading the dancing. The author and his wife served as shushvinim and the chosson declared in his speech that it was the most beautiful wedding he had ever seen.
Tags: moscow, kishinev, weisblach, agudas chasidei chabad, wedding, machon chaya mushka, hotel kosmos

Title: First day of Chabad yeshiva learning in Moscow (5752)
Summary: The Chabad yeshiva in Moscow opened its 5752 zman with a general shiur introducing Maseches Bava Basra.
Story: Learning began at the Marina Roshcha shul while preparations were finalized at the AGUH building. The author delivered a general introductory shiur on Bava Basra to the two upper classes. Earlier discussions with Rabbi Berel Lazar and Uri Kamishov resulted in opening the yeshiva to thirteen- and fourteen-year-olds, who would learn secular studies in the morning at the Archipov shul school and join the yeshiva afterwards.
Tags: moscow, marina roshcha, yeshiva, bava basra, lazar, kamishov

Title: Chabad press conference on the Schneersohn library at Hotel Orlonok
Summary: R. Yitzchok Kogan held a press conference at Hotel Orlonok in Moscow on the seized Schneersohn library.
Story: Attendance was small. R. Kogan recounted the full history of the library struggle for about half an hour and then took questions; the author answered questions on the history of the collection in Yiddish, with Kogan translating. Earlier the same day Kogan and Aharonov had met with the wife of Yeltsin's deputy Rutskoi, herself politically active, to press the books issue.
Tags: moscow, schneersohn library, press conference, hotel orlonok, seforim, kogan

Title: Chabad yeshiva holds first day of learning at Moscow AGUH shul
Summary: The Moscow Chabad yeshiva transitioned its learning from Marina Roshcha to the AGUH shul.
Story: After a day delay caused by a missing bus on the planned transfer date, the yeshiva held its first day of seder at the AGUH shul. The author delivered a general introductory shiur to the upper class. The arrangement followed an internal division of responsibilities in which R. Kogan took over running the AGUH shul, the author took on building Agudas Chasidei Chabad activity and public relations, and R. Aharonov took the connection with Veronika Irina, food and clothing imports, and Russian-language publishing.
Tags: moscow, agudas chasidei chabad, yeshiva

Title: Chai Elul farbrengen at Moscow AGUH shul
Summary: About a hundred people gathered at the AGUH shul for a Chai Elul farbrengen.
Story: Following his regular Shulchan Aruch shiur in the yeshiva, the author drove to the AGUH shul for the farbrengen. He spoke on the ahavas Yisrael of the Baal Shem Tov and of the Rebbe, who sends shluchim to care for every Jew in Russia, with Korbsky translating. Speakers also included R. Kogan, the shochet R. Mottel Lifshitz, and Rappoport.
Tags: moscow, agudas chasidei chabad, chai elul, baal shem tov, farbrengen, korbsky

Title: Seminary girls leave Moscow by bus for Lubavitch
Summary: The visiting seminary girls who had served as camp counselors departed Moscow by bus for the town of Lubavitch.
Story: Before they left, the author met the group at Hotel Molodyozhnaya to brief them on how to find the historic Chabad sites in Lubavitch. The author's wife and children traveled with them.
Tags: moscow, lubavitch town, seminary girls, shluchos

Title: Opening ceremony of Chabad school at Moscow's Archipov Great Synagogue
Summary: A formal opening ceremony marked the new school year at the Chabad school in Moscow's Archipov Great Synagogue.
Story: After morning selichos the family attended the ceremony, where speakers included Korbsky, the author, R. Kogan, R. Lazar, Cherbinsky and Varovich. Yeshiva learning was meant to start the same morning at the AGUH shul, but the bus did not arrive and the students learned at Marina Roshcha instead.
Tags: moscow, archipov synagogue, school, korbsky, lazar, kogan, chinuch

Title: First day of classes at new Chabad school in Moscow
Summary: Classes began at the new Chabad school inside Moscow's Archipov Great Synagogue.
Story: The author's wife taught two classes of limudei kodesh; his three sons each taught a class or an individual child for the first ninety minutes before davening. The author supervised the school day on site and then taught Gemara, Halachah and trop in the yeshiva at the AGUH shul.
Tags: moscow, archipov synagogue, school, limudei kodesh, chinuch

Title: Chabad shlichus family relocates from hotel to Tikhvinskaya apartment
Summary: On erev Rosh Hashana the author moved his family from Hotel Molodyozhnaya to an apartment on Tikhvinskaya Street between Moscow's two Chabad shuls.
Story: Hotel Molodyozhnaya was over an hour and a half on foot from the AGUH shul, making it impractical for the Yamim Noraim. The new apartment sat about half an hour from the AGUH shul and a similar distance from Marina Roshcha. The author planned to spend Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur at the AGUH shul.
Tags: moscow, tikhvinskaya, erev rosh hashana, shluchim

Title: Yakovlev drafts letter for Gorbachev to return Chabad library
Summary: Soviet minister Aleksandr Yakovlev prepared a letter for Gorbachev urging him to sign an immediate order returning the Schneersohn library to Chabad.
Story: On the eve of Rosh Hashana 5752, a Chabad delegation met Yakovlev in his Kremlin office. He told them he had repeatedly pushed for a positive ruling on the books and was now going directly to Gorbachev. Veronika drafted the letter, Yakovlev revised it in pen, and his secretary typed the corrected version before he carried it to Gorbachev.
Tags: russia, moscow, soviet-union, yakovlev, gorbachev, chabad-library, schneersohn-collection, veronika

Title: Yakovlev meeting with Chabad delegation on the Schneersohn library
Summary: Erev Rosh Hashana the delegation met Minister Alexander Yakovlev about the Schneersohn library, with the author left to supervise students at the Lenin Library.
Story: A writer named Lanya from Dnepropetrovsk had spent days arranging a meeting with Yakovlev. That morning his office called urgently for R. Kogan, and Veronika, R. Aharonov, R. Kogan and Lanya went to Yakovlev's office at 12:30. The author remained at the Lenin Library with the yeshiva and school children to await results. Lenin Library director Volik then unexpectedly invited him upstairs for the first time, but he declined to come alone without the rest of the delegation.
Tags: moscow, yakovlev, schneersohn library, seforim, veronika irina, kogan, aharonov, dnepropetrovsk

Title: Yeshiva and school students brought to Lenin Library awaiting Schneersohn books
Summary: Erev Rosh Hashana, yeshiva and school students were rushed to the Lenin Library in anticipation of the Schneersohn books' return.
Story: Word came that the Russian Federation foreign ministry had prepared papers for the USSR Culture Ministry to sign for releasing the library, and the boys were to be on hand before noon. Two busloads arrived at the library. Veronika gathered them into the waiting hall, where the author told them the story of the books and led them in saying L'Dovid Hashem Ori. The Culture Ministry then replied that they could not sign without a full council decision.
Tags: moscow, lenin library, schneersohn library, seforim, russian foreign ministry, yeshiva, school

Title: Chabad delegation stages Shabbat sit-in at Lenin Library
Summary: Chabad emissaries and yeshiva students refused to leave the Lenin Library before Shabbat 5752, waiting for Gorbachev's decision on returning the seforim.
Story: On the Shabbat before Rosh Hashana 5752 the delegation chose to remain inside the library when no answer came. The director offered them the conference room beside his office; police escorted students over 18 upstairs while younger boys walked to the Agudas Chassidei Chabad synagogue. They davened Kabbalas Shabbos, ate the Shabbos meal together, and slept on chairs and carpets as messages continued from Gubenko late into the night.
Tags: russia, moscow, lenin-library, schneersohn-collection, yeshiva-students, vigil, shabbat

Title: TASS reports Chabad sit-in, drawing international press
Summary: After the library director phoned TASS about the Chabad delegation, Soviet TV broadcast the story and waves of local and international reporters descended on the library.
Story: In the middle of the night the director told the TASS news agency about the Jewish guests inside the library. Soviet television aired the news immediately, and throughout Shabbos reporters and photographers from local, American and other international outlets crowded the building. The delegation kept Shabbos strictly, declining to speak on camera and answering questions only after havdalah.
Tags: russia, moscow, tass, media, schneersohn-collection, television, american-press

Title: The Rebbe endorses the library vigil
Summary: When informed of the Chabad team's sit-in, the Rebbe responded 'a glaiche zach' and said they should stay until the books are returned.
Story: Rabbi Leibel Groner told the Rebbe about the delegation's continued presence inside the library director's office. The Rebbe answered 'a glaiche zach' (a fitting thing), adding that ultimately the world — including this place — must be conquered. When told about the ongoing vigil outside the library, he encouraged it and said they evidently understood they should stay there until the books were returned.
Tags: russia, moscow, rebbe, groner, schneersohn-collection, vigil

Title: Gorbachev refers Chabad books case to the Gos-Soviet
Summary: On the first day of Rosh Hashana 5752, Gorbachev summoned Culture Minister Gubenko and agreed to hand the Chabad library question to the new Gos-Soviet super-commission.
Story: On the first day of Rosh Hashana Gorbachev called Gubenko to discuss the seforim. Gubenko proposed transferring the matter to the Gos-Soviet — the new umbrella body including Gorbachev, Yeltsin and the heads of the federations — and Gorbachev consented. Yeltsin reportedly took part in the session, and Veronika brought word to the Chabad delegation immediately.
Tags: russia, soviet-union, gorbachev, yeltsin, gubenko, gos-soviet, schneersohn-collection

Title: Gubenko vows on radio no Chabad book will be returned
Summary: USSR Culture Minister Nikolai Gubenko declared on radio that not a single book of the Schneersohn collection would be returned as long as one Jew remained in Russia.
Story: Following the Gos-Soviet referral, Gubenko gave a radio interview asserting the collection was needed by Jews in Russia and accusing the Chabad delegation of intimidation. Kol Yisrael reached Rabbi Aharonov for a live response, who explained that Gubenko was alone in the government in opposing the return. Pravda printed against the delegation while Nezavisimaya printed in favor, and Soviet TV ran several positive segments.
Tags: russia, moscow, gubenko, radio, schneersohn-collection, media

Title: Petrovsky deflects Chabad team at Moscow human rights conference
Summary: On 4 Tishrei 5752 the Chabad team tried to reach Deputy Foreign Minister Petrovsky at the Moscow CSCE human rights meeting but could only wave at him from the gallery.
Story: Petrovsky, who nine months earlier had told the delegation they should have come to the foreign ministry from the start, was now chairing the human rights conference. From the gallery the Chabad team could only speak with a deputy; when Secretary of State Baker rose to speak they waved and he nodded back. A staffer named Babilkov later told them the books issue could not be raised at the conference without consent of the 35 participating states.
Tags: russia, moscow, human-rights-conference, petrovsky, baker, schneersohn-collection, csce

Title: Diragin threatens self-immolation with Chabad manuscripts
Summary: On Erev Yom Kippur 5752 the head of the Lenin Library's manuscript department, Diragin, threatened to burn himself together with the Chabad manuscripts if they were returned.
Story: Press reports on the afternoon of Erev Yom Kippur carried Diragin's threat to set himself and the manuscripts on fire rather than let them go back to Chabad. Police were sent to the library, though the follow-up was not known to the delegation. The threat was rebroadcast on Soviet television, and Rabbi Yitzchak Kogan publicly answered the library staff in a televised reply.
Tags: russia, moscow, lenin-library, diragin, manuscripts, schneersohn-collection, threat

Title: Russian arbitrage court orders Chabad collection sealed
Summary: Erev Shabbos of Chol Hamoed Sukkot the arbitration court issued a formal order to seal the Chabad books and manuscripts and transfer them to safekeeping.
Story: After Ruslan Khasbulatov sent the books matter to four Supreme Soviet committees, Veronika reached the arbitrage judge Grebenikov and obtained a court order to seal the Schneersohn collection. With the order in hand she went to the militia and into the library accompanied by police. A commission was set up to handle the transfer including Veronika, Rabbi Levin, Yakirson and Professor Chelnov.
Tags: russia, moscow, arbitrage-court, khasbulatov, schneersohn-collection, lenin-library, yakirson

Title: Chabad of Moscow hosts mass Sukkot children's gathering
Summary: Some 1,000 children with their parents joined a Sukkot celebration at the Marina Roscha synagogue, where the launch of a new Chabad Sunday school was announced.
Story: During Chol Hamoed Sukkot a huge children's party filled the Agudas Chassidei Chabad synagogue in Marina Roscha. Korbsky spoke about the holiday, Rabbi Bentzion Shem Tov Kunin offered a blessing, Rabbi Kogan spoke about Simchas Torah, and the speaker announced that following the Rebbe's directive to open new yeshivos and schools especially in Russia, a Sunday school would now open at the synagogue. Raffles, food in the sukkah and singing left families eager to register.
Tags: russia, moscow, sukkot, children, marina-roshcha, kunin, kogan, korbsky, school

Title: Library worker reveals discarded Shut Maharik in trash
Summary: On Hoshana Rabbah eve, Soviet TV filmed a Lenin Library librarian who testified anonymously that three years earlier he had found discarded Jewish books, including Shut Maharik, in the Khimki warehouses.
Story: About fifty Chabadniks visited the library for dancing and singing while a TV crew interviewed Rabbi Kogan and library director Valik. Kogan displayed a copy of Shut Maharik that had been found discarded; Valik bristled but Kogan refused to say who provided it. The librarian who had found the volume three years earlier in the Khimki storage rooms then gave testimony — filmed so his face and voice could not be identified — and the segment aired before Yom Tov.
Tags: russia, moscow, lenin-library, shut-maharik, khimki, media, schneersohn-collection

Title: Moscow arbitration court hears Chabad library case
Summary: On 25 Tishrei 5752 a three-judge panel of the Moscow arbitrage court heard arguments on returning the Schneersohn library to Chabad.
Story: Veronika argued for Chabad while a Jewish attorney represented the library; the diary records that her arguments were clearly persuading the judges while the library lawyer grew flustered. Closing, she described the false imprisonment of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, asked the courtroom to rise in his memory, and argued that after the Previous Rebbe's exile and passing the moral duty was to return the books to his son. The judges announced a ruling would be given the following Tuesday.
Tags: russia, moscow, arbitrage-court, schneersohn-collection, veronika, rayatz, previous-rebbe

Title: Soviet arbitrage court rules to return Schneersohn library to Chabad
Summary: The Moscow arbitrage court chaired by Judge Gribenikov delivered a signed two-page ruling ordering the Lenin Library to return the Schneersohn collection of books and manuscripts to Chabad within thirty days.
Story: On Monday afternoon the three judges summoned the Chabad delegation, a US embassy representative, and CNN, and at 5:30 PM handed over the signed ruling. The court found that claims of nationalization or ownerless property were baseless, that the collection belonged to the Chabad movement as a whole rather than personally to the Rebbe, and that it must be returned to Chabad within one month. The delegation faxed the ruling to the Rebbe through Rabbi Groner, to the Kfar Chabad newspaper and Algemeiner, to Rabbi Krinsky for the general press, and arranged English translations sent to governments in the UK, Italy, and Germany.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneersohn-library, court-ruling, gribenikov, soviet-union, library, rebbe

Title: Arbitrage court rules to return seforim to Moscow Chabad community
Summary: The Moscow arbitration court announced it would issue a verdict on Tuesday after Shabbos Bereshis ordering the Schneersohn library returned to the Chabad community of Moscow.
Story: Following the Thursday hearing, the judges informed the parties that the formal verdict on the next Tuesday would be to return the books to the Moscow Chabad community. On the intervening Friday the court also received a letter from Moscow City Hall signed by Sevastyanov recommending the return, along with a legal opinion by attorney Kabalkin commissioned by the court itself.
Tags: russia, moscow, arbitrage-court, schneersohn-collection, ruling, sevastyanov, kabalkin

Title: Sunday school for Jewish children opens at Moscow Agudat Chabad synagogue
Summary: About forty children attended the first session of a new Sunday school for Jewish education at the Agudat Chabad synagogue in Moscow.
Story: Rabbi D.B. Lazar opened the day with a brief address, after which the children prayed together with explanations given in Russian. Rabbi Kogan also addressed the children before they were divided into classes and learned for several hours in the synagogue hall, while the yeshiva students moved to the dining room and some helped teach. The opening took place while the formal struggle to recover the Schneersohn library was at its peak.
Tags: moscow, russia, sunday-school, lazar, kogan, jewish-education, soviet-jewry

Title: Judges hold press conference defending Schneersohn library ruling
Summary: Chief Judge Gribenikov and his fellow judges held a 90-minute press conference at the court to defend their ruling and expose Culture Minister Gubenko's attempts to pressure them.
Story: Russian and foreign press attended with simultaneous English translation, and the chief judge detailed how Gubenko had written letters to multiple officials and phoned him repeatedly trying to alter or block the ruling. Gribenikov said any informal appeal would not delay execution, that if the library refused to comply within thirty days an enforcement officer would be appointed, and that police could be used to compel cooperation. He distinguished sharply between Khasbulatov's policy referral and Gubenko's improper political pressure.
Tags: russia, moscow, gribenikov, press, schneersohn-library, gubenko, cnn

Title: Chabad delegation meets US Ambassador Strauss in Moscow over library
Summary: The Chabad delegation met US Ambassador Robert Strauss and Deputy Chief Collins at the American embassy in Moscow to coordinate continued diplomatic pressure for the library's return.
Story: Strauss recounted that the library had been raised in every meeting Secretary of State Baker held with Soviet officials, and that he himself had pressed the Soviet Foreign Minister at a Shabbat luncheon by telling him the matter stood at the top of President Bush's priorities. The Foreign Minister promised to study the issue within 24 hours, and inquiries were already coming in to the court from the Soviet Foreign Ministry. Rabbi Kunin urged Strauss to push Gorbachev and Yeltsin for a definitive presidential order to return the books immediately.
Tags: us-embassy, strauss, schneersohn-library, moscow, diplomacy, baker, bush

Title: Judges' letter to Lenin Library director orders immediate compliance
Summary: After the library refused to cooperate, the arbitrage court judges issued a special letter to the Lenin Library director instructing him to execute the ruling himself without waiting for enforcement.
Story: Rabbi Kogan had visited the judges to report that the library was not cooperating, that the enforcement office would not act without a separate court order, and that the library was distributing leaflets attacking the ruling. The judges wrote a formal letter to director Vyalik declaring he had a personal duty to carry out the ruling immediately, independent of any enforcement proceedings. Rabbi Kogan hand-delivered the letter to the director's secretary and obtained her signed acknowledgment of receipt.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneersohn-library, lenin-library, court-ruling, vyalik

Title: Yeltsin refuses Gubenko's request to halt Schneersohn library return
Summary: Russian Culture Minister Gubenko approached Boris Yeltsin asking him to stop the return of the Chabad library, but Yeltsin replied that the matter was in court and refused to intervene.
Story: Reported on Leningrad television and seen by congregants in the Moscow synagogue, Gubenko reportedly left the meeting in anger declaring that Yeltsin was prepared to destroy Russia. The episode was part of a broader pattern of interference by Gubenko, including political maneuvering with Gorbachev's office, pressure on the library director, and later a decision to dismiss the director for cooperating with the court.
Tags: russia, yeltsin, gubenko, schneersohn-library, politics, leningrad-tv

Title: Rebbe gives extra dollar for tzedakah before family's trip to Israel
Summary: On 12 Marcheshvan 5752, before the family's three-week trip to Eretz Yisrael, the Rebbe gave an additional dollar to be donated as tzedakah in the Holy Land.
Story: Before traveling to Israel on Sunday, 12 Marcheshvan 5752, the family received dollars from the Rebbe, who added an extra dollar for tzedakah in Eretz Yisrael. With a smile he remarked that surely they had arranged who would read from the Torah, to which the writer's wife replied 'certainly!' — and the Rebbe blessed them with great success.
Tags: dollars, israel, tzedakah, 770

Title: Soviet TV channel TCH airs false report of judge retracting library ruling
Summary: At midnight on Saturday, Channel TCH broadcast that Chief Judge Gribenikov had reversed the library ruling based on supposed new information, prompting an immediate protest from the judge.
Story: When the broadcast reached Gribenikov he issued a strong protest, which TCH and the Vesti network agreed to air in correction. Around the same time, Culture Minister Gubenko reportedly decided to dismiss library director Vyalik for cooperating with the court's order to return the books to Chabad, raising the stakes of the unfolding struggle.
Tags: russia, media, schneersohn-library, gribenikov, tch, vesti, gubenko

Title: Library appeals ruling; arbitrage court orders rehearing of Chabad case
Summary: After formal appeals by the Soviet prosecutor and the Lenin Library director, the Moscow arbitrage court decided to hold a full rehearing of the Chabad library case the following week.
Story: An initial appeal under Culture Minister Gubenko's signature was rejected as improperly drafted, but new appeals of three and thirteen pages from the prosecutor general and from director Vyalik forced the court to respond. The chief judge and panel chose to convene a rehearing rather than answer by letter, and asked Chabad to supply evidence under Torah law that the collection belonged to the movement as a whole rather than personally to the Rebbe. When informed of the request, the Rebbe reportedly responded with displeasure: 'They need proofs again? This still isn't clear?'
Tags: russia, moscow, schneersohn-library, appeal, gribenikov, vyalik, rebbe

Title: Robert Maxwell's last phone call with Rabbi Aharonov on Chabad library
Summary: Rabbi Y.Y. Aharonov spoke by phone with Robert Maxwell in the middle of the night about pressuring Yeltsin to return the Chabad books, in what proved to be Maxwell's last conversation before he fell from his yacht and drowned.
Story: Maxwell, the British publisher, was working with Chabad activists to push Yeltsin and his circle to release the Schneerson library from the Russian State Library. Hours after the call he fell overboard near the Canary Islands and died. In that final conversation, conducted from the deck of his yacht, he had reaffirmed his desire to see the book-restoration effort completed.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, robert-maxwell, rabbi-aharonov, lawsuit

Title: Rabbi Aharonov flies to Israel for Maxwell's funeral on Rebbe's instruction
Summary: On the Rebbe's instruction, Rabbi Aharonov set out in the middle of the night together with Rabbi P. Vogel and Rabbi Y. Pruss to attend Robert Maxwell's funeral in Israel.
Story: With no direct Friday-morning flight available, the delegation flew via Europe hoping to reach the Holy Land before Shabbat or to continue from London after Shabbat. The three men had been among Maxwell's closest rabbinic contacts and the last to speak with him before he died, and were expected to take part in the Sunday funeral and possibly to deliver remarks.
Tags: robert-maxwell, rabbi-aharonov, israel, schneerson-library, rabbi-vogel, rabbi-pruss

Title: Russian Supreme Court appeal hearing on the Schneerson library
Summary: The appellate retrial in the Chabad library lawsuit was held in Moscow before Chief Justice Grebennikov and seven other judges over roughly three hours, with the Chabad side's arguments well received.
Story: State Library staff packed the courtroom while about ten counter-protesters with anti-Chasidic placards demonstrated outside, a few hurling Nazi-style epithets at arriving Chabad supporters. Attorney Veronika spoke for Chabad along with the bibliographic expert Yakirson, while the library directors struggled to produce documentation of any nationalization. The chief justice announced the ruling would come the next day.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, lenin-library, lawsuit, judge-grebennikov, veronika, yakirson

Title: Synagogue land dispute with neighboring bank in Moscow
Summary: Rabbi Kogan led yeshiva students out to physically halt a neighboring bank's unauthorized paving of synagogue land, after a month of fruitless complaints and police calls.
Story: For a month the bank next to the Marina Roscha synagogue had been encroaching on synagogue property to build extended parking, ignoring police, letters and protests. When workers arrived on Thursday with asphalt the yeshiva crowd dismantled the construction; police, summoned again, sided with Chabad and the bank was forced to restore the area and pay damages. The same day a slanderous newspaper article attacked the synagogue, apparently from tenants still occupying its upper floor.
Tags: russia, moscow, marina-roscha-synagogue, rabbi-kogan, property-dispute, press-attack

Title: Russian court rules Schneerson collection belongs to Chabad
Summary: Chief Justice Grebennikov issued a three-and-a-half page ruling declaring the Schneerson library belongs to the Chabad Rebbe and ordering its immediate transfer to a new Jewish library being opened by Agudas Chasidei Chabad.
Story: The verdict rejected the State Library's claims, finding no evidence the collection had ever been nationalized or left without an owner. The court declined to adjudicate internal Chabad-community ownership questions but ordered the books moved to the new general Jewish library being established under Agudas Chasidei Chabad. Disputes over which volumes belonged to the collection would be settled jointly between library and Chabad representatives, with court-appointed experts as backstop.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, lawsuit, judge-grebennikov, agudas-chasidei-chabad

Title: Chabad demonstration at Russian State Library over book transfer
Summary: Chabad delegates and about ten yeshiva students spent the day at the State Library with crates demanding immediate handover of the books per the court order, before being told to leave at 11pm.
Story: Despite a fresh court order compelling the library to release the books, the directors refused to comply, and the lobby filled with prayers, communal singing, lectures on bibliography by the diarist, and arguments with opponents. Press, television and a US embassy representative were present. The library leadership lobbied Yeltsin's government and new-old foreign minister Shevardnadze, while Chabad activists pushed Yeltsin's deputy Primokin and the justice minister to force compliance.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, lenin-library, protest, us-embassy, media, rabbi-kunin

Title: Russian government order on Chabad academy, yeshiva and library
Summary: Attorney Veronika spent more than twelve hours at Russian government offices preparing a directive — to be signed by Yeltsin's deputy Burbulis — approving a Chabad academy, university-yeshiva and library inside the Marina Roscha synagogue.
Story: The directive redirected the destination of the Schneerson books from a free-standing Jewish library to one housed inside the Chabad synagogue complex, alongside a new academy and yeshiva-university. The Rebbe, asked through Rabbi Groner whether to accept this arrangement, expressed sharp concern that under such a structure it would be unclear how the books could ever be brought to 770 if ownership formally passed to a Russian-Jewish library.
Tags: russia, moscow, marina-roscha-synagogue, yeltsin, burbulis, schneerson-library, veronika

Title: Belovezha Accords dissolve the Soviet Union
Summary: The presidents of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus met and founded the Commonwealth of Independent States, effectively dissolving the Soviet Union.
Story: The historic meeting produced a treaty establishing the CIS and was widely seen as the end of the USSR. Diary entries from Moscow record local and international anxiety about the implications, including for the unresolved Chabad library case. The Rebbe, asked about the new situation, replied that nothing needed to change — one must trust in G-d and increase the spread of Yiddishkeit.
Tags: russia, ukraine, belarus, soviet-union, yeltsin, cis, geopolitics

Title: Hei Tevet celebrations at Moscow yeshiva and Machon Chaya Mushka
Summary: Rabbi Berel Lazar and his wife and the diarist convened farbrengens at the yeshiva and at Machon Chaya Mushka to mark Hei Tevet 5752 with hope for the imminent return of the Chabad books.
Story: Hei Tevet commemorates the 1987 US court ruling that the Chabad library belongs to the movement, and the night before the diarist's celebrations the Rebbe delivered a special sicha tying that victory to the books still awaiting redemption. The diarist spent the afternoon recounting the library saga to the bochurim and the evening doing the same in Russian and in Hebrew for the local and Israeli students at the women's institute.
Tags: russia, moscow, marina-roscha-synagogue, hei-tevet, didan-natzach, schneerson-library, rabbi-lazar, rabbi-kunin, machon-chaya-mushka

Title: Rebbe speaks again about Chabad books at Shabbat Vayechi farbrengen
Summary: At the Shabbat farbrengen on 7 Tevet 5752 the Rebbe again addressed the still-unrealized return of the Chabad books, linking it to current Russian events and ending with a prayer that they reach '770', the gematria of 'pirtzta'.
Story: The Rebbe noted that even after the nations had ruled and promised the books' return, they had not yet been moved. He hinted at a gentile and several Jews actively blocking the transfer — 'woe to them' — and tied the delay to the geopolitical upheaval and the relocation of capitals across the former USSR.
Tags: 770, schneerson-library, moshiach, beis-rabeinu-shebebavel

Title: Decision to convene Chabad Shluchim and Rabbinical Conference in Moscow
Summary: Rabbi Berel Lazar, Rabbi Aharonov and the diarist finalized plans to hold the first conference of Chabad shluchim and rabbis serving in the former USSR during the week of 22 Shevat.
Story: The schedule placed the women's gathering on the night of 22 Shevat, the shluchim and shluchos conferences on Monday, and the rabbinical conference on Tuesday, with rabbis traveling in from outside the FSU. The Rebbe later replied that 'the time itself contributes to great success,' and added a blessing for 'great and abundant' success.
Tags: russia, moscow, shluchim, rabbis, kinus, rabbi-lazar, rabbi-aharonov

Title: Chabad delegation confronts Yeltsin and Kozyrev in Rome over books
Summary: On the margins of Yeltsin's Rome visit, Rabbi Aharonov, Rabbi Garelik and Rabbi Chazan handed Yeltsin a written demand to return the Chabad books and pressed Foreign Minister Kozyrev and adviser Petrov, but received only deflections.
Story: Italian Prime Minister Andreotti had already raised the books with Yeltsin to an unsatisfactory reply. At the businessmen's meeting Yeltsin took the Chabad letter without responding. In a recorded exchange Kozyrev told Aharonov he personally favored returning the books but the moment was too turbulent, while Petrov claimed the library deserved compensation for years of storage and falsely asserted the ruling required the collection to stay in Russia.
Tags: russia, italy, yeltsin, kozyrev, petrov, andreotti, schneerson-library, diplomacy, rabbi-aharonov, rabbi-garelik

Title: Chabad Portuguese-translation Haggadah by Shmuel Asher Bigon
Summary: Shmuel Asher Bigon translated a Chabad Haggadah into Portuguese, illustrated by Zalman Kleiman, published in New York.
Story: In 5752 (1992), Shmuel Asher Bigon's Portuguese translation of the Chabad Haggadah, with Zalman Kleiman's illustrations, was published in New York. The 84-page quarto edition served Brazilian and Portuguese-speaking Jewish communities. It continued the Chabad project of issuing the Haggadah in major world languages.
Tags: chabad, portuguese, new york, brazil, shmuel asher bigon

Title: Chabad Spanish-translation Haggadah by Natan Greenblatt
Summary: Natan Greenblatt translated a Chabad Haggadah into Spanish, with Zalman Kleiman's illustrations, published in New York.
Story: In 5752 (1992), a Chabad Haggadah with Spanish translation by Natan Greenblatt and illustrations by Zalman Kleiman was published in New York. The landscape-format 17-page-plus-50-leaf edition served the growing Spanish-speaking Chabad communities in Latin America and the United States. It expanded the Chabad Haggadah project into the Spanish-speaking Jewish world.
Tags: chabad, spanish, new york, natan greenblatt, zalman kleiman

Title: Hebrew-English Chabad Haggadah illustrated by Zalman Kleiman
Summary: A Chabad Haggadah following the Alter Rebbe's nusach with English translation by Yaakov Emanuel Schochet and illustrations by Zalman Kleiman was published in New York.
Story: In 5752 (1992), a Haggadah following the Chabad Alter Rebbe's nusach was published in New York with English translation by Yaakov Emanuel Schochet and illustrations by Zalman Kleiman. The 81-page quarto edition also appeared in a miniature format. Kleiman's distinctive illustrations became iconic in Chabad children's Haggadah publishing.
Tags: chabad, new york, english, haggadah, children, zalman kleiman

Title: Keller completes registry of Alter Rebbe's maamarim
Summary: In 5752 (1992) R. Yosef Yitzchak Keller completed the chronological registry of the Alter Rebbe's discourses, published in Kerem Chabad.
Story: Building on a 1981 preliminary list appended to Maamarei Admur HaZaken — HaKetzarim, R. Yosef Yitzchak Keller completed a comprehensive registry of the Alter Rebbe's maamarim, organized by year of delivery up through the Liadi period. The completed registry was published in the journal Kerem Chabad. The success of this project led directly into preparing a parallel registry for the Tzemach Tzedek.
Tags: alter rebbe, maamarim, registry, keller, kerem chabad

Title: Library staff identify 3,000 books from Schneersohn collection
Summary: Russian State Library staff identified 3,000 volumes as belonging to the Schneersohn (Lubavitch) collection within the larger Polyakov holdings.
Story: In 5752 (1992), librarians at the Russian State Library sorted through the Polyakov collection and identified clear markings on 3,000 volumes as belonging to the Schneersohn library — 700 in the main building and 2,300 in the Khimki warehouse. These were consolidated on the 11th floor of the main building. The Chabad emissary was not permitted to participate, leaving the identification incomplete.
Tags: moscow, russia, khimki, polyakov-collection, schneersohn-library, russian-state-library, books

Title: Painting of Rebbe receiving pidyonos
Summary: Artist A.K. Tiefenbrun painted the Rebbe receiving pidyonos in 5752.
Story: In 5752 (1992) the artist A.K. Tiefenbrun painted a depiction of the Rebbe receiving pidyonos. The work is displayed in the Lubavitch Library's exhibition of portraits of the Rebbeim.
Tags: portrait, pidyonos, tiefenbrun

Title: Pereshel facsimile of the Livorno 1825 Ladino Haggadah
Summary: Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of the 1825 Livorno Ladino Haggadah.
Story: In 5752 (1992), Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of the 1825 Livorno Haggadah with Ladino translation. The 34-leaf octavo edition (including cover) came with an introduction by Pereshel. It marked his ongoing commitment to resurrecting rare printed Haggadot for new generations.
Tags: haggadah, facsimile, new york, livorno, ladino, tuvia pereshel

Title: Settlement check sent to Merkos over old partnership
Summary: In 5752 the author sent a $500 check to Merkos via Rabbi Krinsky as a halachic settlement of any unintended discrepancies in the long-running printing partnership.
Story: Citing Rambam's halachot of partners — that when partners separate each must swear about possible inadvertent overcharges — the author in 5752 (1992) wrote out a $500 check to Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch. He delivered it to Rabbi Yehuda Krinsky, his liaison to Rabbi Chadakov, asking him to verbally mochel on behalf of Merkos any sums that may have remained with the partners contrary to din.
Tags: merkos, pevzner, krinsky, chadakov, partnership, halacha

Title: Updated chronological list of Alter Rebbe's maamarim
Summary: In 5752 (1992), R' Yosef Yitzchak Keller completed an updated chronological list of the Alter Rebbe's maamarim, published in Kerem Chabad issue 4.
Story: The list reflected research drawn from the additional volumes of maamarim issued during the intervening decade, incorporating newly identified headings with dates for both Liozna and Liadi discourses. It expanded considerably on the original 1981 list.
Tags: alter rebbe, maamarim, yosef yitzchak keller, kerem chabad

Title: Rebbe's blessing for the international Chabad Shluchim Conference
Summary: Rabbi Berel Lazar received the Rebbe's reply to the conference plan: 'And the time itself contributes to great success.'
Story: The brief reply confirmed both the date and the structure that Lazar, Aharonov and the diarist had been drafting through Tevet — a women's evening on the night of 22 Shevat, then back-to-back shluchim, shluchos and rabbinical conferences. With the Rebbe's go-ahead, organizers moved into invitations and logistics.
Tags: shluchim, kinus, moscow, rabbi-lazar

Title: Worldwide Shabbat Mevarchim sermons on Moshiach in Moscow
Summary: On a Shabbat designated worldwide for speaking about Moshiach, the diarist addressed the Marina Roscha shul on Friday night and the women's institute at lunch, and organized a motzaei-Shabbat gathering at the shul with Rabbis Kunin and Ashkenazi.
Story: About eighty women and girls attended the motzaei-Shabbat gathering at the shul, with Rabbi Kogan translating for the visiting rabbis. The diarist himself spent motzaei-Shabbat teaching Gemara and Mishnayos classes to the yeshiva students, content to delegate the women's program while ensuring the worldwide Moshiach focus reached every group in Moscow.
Tags: moshiach, moscow, marina-roscha-synagogue, rabbi-kunin, rabbi-ashkenazi, rabbi-kogan

Title: Meeting with prospective State Library director Filipov
Summary: The Chabad delegation held a four-and-a-half hour meeting with the incoming Russian State Library director Filipov in the office of Burbulis' deputy Zhitinov, but Filipov stalled on transferring the books.
Story: Filipov asked for a month's delay before any meeting with the librarians, demanded that Chabad first prepare secure stacks before transfer, and floated 'compromises' such as having Chabad finance photocopies of the entire collection — moves the diarist read as new excuses. The diarist returned convinced the road to recovering the books in Moscow was hopeless and that the effort should pivot to bringing the collection to the Chabad library in New York.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, filipov, veronika, burbulis, zhitinov

Title: Diarist travels to New York for Yud Shevat 5752
Summary: After the Rebbe blessed his request, the diarist flew Delta from Moscow via Frankfurt to New York to attend Yud Shevat with the Rebbe and raise funds to cover the deficit of the Russia shlichus.
Story: Seven months of phone and letter appeals had barely dented the shlichus expenses despite tight economizing. The Rebbe's reply, 'agreement and blessing — I will mention at the Ohel,' authorized the trip. The diarist traveled with Rabbi S. Heber and hoped to land in time to daven Maariv with the Rebbe, who was leading the amud that evening.
Tags: new-york, 770, yud-shevat, fundraising, schneerson-library, rabbi-heber

Title: Rebbe distributes Kuntres Maamarim 5682 on Yud Shevat
Summary: After leading Maariv on Yud Shevat 5752, the Rebbe distributed Kuntres Maamarim 5682 and handed the diarist a second copy 'far di sforim' — for the books.
Story: The diarist had arrived from Moscow hours earlier. When he passed in the distribution line the Rebbe added an extra booklet with the words 'far di sforim,' explicitly linking the publication to the still-unresolved Chabad library campaign in Russia. The same week the Rebbe gave him a second dollar 'for the books' at the Friday dollars distribution.
Tags: 770, yud-shevat, maamarim, schneerson-library, rayatz

Title: Rebbe's response to concerns over Moscow Jewish library plan
Summary: The Rebbe replied to a letter from the diarist warning that the Moscow Jewish-library structure might block the books' eventual transfer: 'As advised by the askanim and rabbis of Anash who understand this. I will mention at the Ohel.'
Story: The diarist had written that the delegation had never received explicit instructions to consent to the Moscow academy/university/library plan, had refused to sign any document that could be read as such consent, and feared the books could become locked into a Russian Jewish library. The Rebbe's reply pushed the decision back onto senior askanim while withholding personal endorsement of either course.
Tags: schneerson-library, moscow, rabbi-groner, agudas-chasidei-chabad

Title: Chabad delegation greets US Secretary Baker at Russian Foreign Ministry
Summary: About forty Chabad emissaries gathered outside the Russian Foreign Ministry to greet US Secretary of State James Baker during his visit to Foreign Minister Kozyrev.
Story: During the Shluchim conference, the delegates drove to the Foreign Ministry and sang as Baker's motorcade entered. Rabbis Y. Kogan and Sh.B. Cunin then went to the Penta Hotel to meet Baker on his return and urged him to press for the return of the Schneerson books. Baker said he would raise it with Yeltsin once the Russian president was back in town.
Tags: moscow, james baker, schneerson library, us-russia, kozyrev, kunin, kogan

Title: Moscow Chabad Shluchim and Shluchot conferences open
Summary: The annual Chabad Shluchim and Shluchot conferences opened in Moscow with delegates from across the former Soviet Union.
Story: On 22 Shevat 5752, Chabad emissaries gathered in Moscow for parallel Shluchim and Shluchot conferences. The author opened the Shluchim session and then crossed to address the Shluchot. The gatherings ran alongside ongoing negotiations to recover the Schneerson library from the Russian State Library.
Tags: moscow, russia, shluchim, post-soviet, kunin, kogan

Title: Rabbinical Association of CIS founded in Moscow
Summary: Chabad rabbis serving the former Soviet Union founded a regional Rabbinical Association covering Russia, Ukraine, Moldova and Kazakhstan.
Story: Meeting on 23 Shevat as part of the Moscow Rabbis Conference, the assembled rabbis established a joint Rabbinical Association with Rabbi Berel Lazar of Moscow as chairman and Av Beis Din. Rabbi Azriel Chaikin of Brussels was appointed adviser on marital law and Rabbi Dan Yoel Levi of the US adviser on kashrus, with an executive board drawn from Moldova, Kazakhstan, Dnipropetrovsk, Kharkov, Ukraine, Zhitomir and Samarkand. The body also resolved to publish a Torah journal addressing rabbinic questions across the region.
Tags: moscow, russia, ukraine, moldova, kazakhstan, rabbis, berel lazar, chaikin, levi

Title: Founding of Rabbinical Association at Moscow Shluchim Conference
Summary: The Chabad rabbinical conference on 24 Shevat 5752 in Moscow founded the Association of Chabad Rabbis of the former USSR, capping a week of shluchim, shluchos and rabbinical gatherings.
Story: The week of 22–24 Shevat brought the first major gathering of Chabad shluchim, shluchos and rabbis serving in the former Soviet Union. A founding photograph of the rabbinical association captures Rabbis Gurevitch, Mushkovitz, Kaminetzky, Geisser, Levi, Levin, Chaikin, Avelsky, Berkahn and Krasik. The conference was organized in Moscow despite the parallel pressure of the unresolved library case.
Tags: russia, moscow, shluchim, kinus, rabbis, agudas-harabbonim, fsu

Title: Moscow Yeshiva Tmimim Conference held with 80+ students
Summary: More than eighty yeshiva students from Moscow and surrounding cities gathered for a Tmimim conference and were tested in Gemara, Halacha and Chassidus.
Story: On 24 Shevat, visiting rabbis Eisenbach, Yaroslavsky and Levi examined the assembled students across all classes and reported strong results. The afternoon featured addresses on the virtues of yeshiva study chaired by Grossman. A multi-day seminar for the visiting students followed.
Tags: moscow, yeshiva, tmimim, russia, eisenbach, yaroslavsky, levi

Title: Yeltsin aide Shakhin orders Lenin Library to release Schneerson books
Summary: Russian deputy premier Shakhin, acting on instructions from Yeltsin's office, ordered the new Lenin Library director Philipov to begin transferring the Schneerson collection to Chabad's Moscow building.
Story: On 24 Shevat, lawyer Veronika reported that Philipov had received an unambiguous order to return the books, with deputy PM Burbulis warning Shakhin that the dispute could derail Yeltsin's upcoming US trip. Officers were posted at the manuscripts department, which was sealed pending return of the Schneersohn manuscripts. The arrangement, however, kept the books at Chabad's Moscow shul rather than allowing transfer to the Rebbe in New York.
Tags: moscow, schneerson library, books, lenin library, yeltsin, shakhin, burbulis, philipov

Title: Lenin Library workers stage protest against Schneerson book return
Summary: Dozens of Lenin Library employees rallied with a red flag and loudspeaker to block Rabbi Yitzchak Kogan-Lewinson from entering, while a government commission was set up to identify the Schneerson books.
Story: On 25 Shevat, the author arrived at the library to find a protest led by director Dyragin and his deputies chanting 'Down with Levinson.' Police restricted him to the waiting hall and helped push him out. He returned that evening with a KGB escort and a government delegation, was shown about 700 already-segregated Schneerson books and another 1,500 awaiting verification, but was told nothing would be released until a 'commission' completed its review.
Tags: moscow, schneerson library, books, lenin library, protest, levinson, dyragin, kgb, philipov

Title: Baker meets Kozyrev to discuss the library books
Summary: U.S. Secretary of State Baker was scheduled to arrive in Moscow to meet Foreign Minister Kozyrev and discuss return of the Rebbe's books.
Story: The shluchim anticipated that Baker's upcoming visit and meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Kozyrev would include the library books issue. They believed the Friday events around the library had been staged in preparation for this diplomatic meeting. Hopes were high that the books matter would be resolved favorably at or before the meeting.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneersohn library, james baker, kozyrev, diplomacy, usa

Title: Library book transfer halted by Shakhin's intervention
Summary: Shakhin called Zhitinov and Veronika to delay removing the Rebbe's books from the library, citing political risk before Yeltsin and Burbulis returned from Minsk.
Story: When the plan was set to transfer the Schneersohn library books to Veronika's academy, Shakhin abruptly intervened, telling Zhitinov to halt because he was about to fly to Petersburg and Yeltsin and Burbulis would return the next day. At the subsequent meeting Zhitinov hid Shakhin's decision and sought pretexts to delay. Under attack, Veronika canceled the academy transfer plan, leaving Zhitinov to argue the books must be returned to the Rebbe.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneersohn library, shakhin, zhitinov, veronika, yeltsin, burbulis

Title: Rebbe's instruction confirmed to Rabbi Cunin
Summary: Through Leibel Gruner the Rebbe confirmed to Rabbi Cunin that they should obey Veronika's directive to focus only on Torah and prayer for a week.
Story: After Veronika instructed the shluchim to occupy themselves only with Torah and prayer for a week while she met with government offices, Rabbi Cunin reported the meeting back. Leibel Gruner relayed that Cunin had said nothing was being done according to her instruction. The Rebbe responded in Yiddish: 'So it should be — that is what was agreed.'
Tags: russia, moscow, schneersohn library, cunin, gruner, veronika

Title: Shluchim move to new Moscow apartment near synagogue
Summary: On Thursday the author moved his family from the hotel to a new apartment in Moscow, hosting Shabbat guests including the Tolochinsky chassan and kallah.
Story: After staying at a hotel, the family moved Thursday afternoon into a new apartment close to the synagogue, rented for two months. The first Shabbat there featured the whole family eating together and hosting guests: the chassan and kallah Chaim and Talia Tolochinsky at night and school children for shul on Shabbat morning. The author expressed gratitude for finding the apartment so easily.
Tags: russia, moscow, apartment, tolochinsky wedding, shabbat

Title: Helicopter trip to Lubavitch with Jerry Levin film crew
Summary: American producer Jerry Levin and his crew flew by helicopter to the town of Lubavitch to film footage for a documentary marking the Rebbe's ninetieth birthday.
Story: On 28 Shevat the author accompanied Levin's crew as guide, while a busload of visiting yeshiva students travelled in parallel with Rabbis Eisenbach and Yaroslavsky. Aerial shots of the historic courtyard of the Rebbeim were captured for the 11 Nissan film. The party returned to Moscow that evening so the author could resume Schneerson-library negotiations the next morning.
Tags: lubavitch, jerry levin, documentary, russia, rebbe 90th birthday, yud aleph nissan

Title: Confrontation with Lenin Library commission over Polyakov collection
Summary: The Lenin Library's special commission refused to let the author demonstrate that the Polyakov collection was in fact part of the Schneerson library.
Story: On 3 Adar I the commission tried instead to enlist him in cataloguing damaged pages of an early Bologna print. Director Philipov backed commission chair Livachkin against the author, denying he had ever been invited to prove ownership. Later that day the Rebbe reiterated through R. Leibel Groner that the delegation must follow lawyer Veronika's lead.
Tags: moscow, schneerson library, books, lenin library, philipov, polyakov, muzey knigi, livachkin

Title: Chabad meets US Ambassador Strauss in Moscow over Schneerson books
Summary: Rabbi Shlomo Cunin met with US Ambassador Robert Strauss in Moscow, who reported that President Bush had personally raised the Schneerson books with Yeltsin at Camp David.
Story: On 8 Adar I the author and others travelled with R. Cunin to the embassy but Strauss received only Cunin. The ambassador described sustained US pressure, including approaches by visiting senators, and promised to use the latest developments in further talks with the Russian government.
Tags: moscow, schneerson library, robert strauss, us-russia, shlomo cunin, george bush

Title: Rabbi Zev Wagner arrested at Lenin Library protest
Summary: Russian police arrested Rabbi Zev Wagner near the Lenin Library, accusing him of a scuffle with protesters opposing the return of the Schneerson collection.
Story: On the evening of 8 Adar I, Wagner's wife alerted the author, who appealed unsuccessfully to the Israeli and US embassies; the US declined because Wagner was an Israeli citizen. Rabbis Lazar, Lipsker, Aharonov and the author visited the police station and learned that charges would be filed the next day.
