Veronika urged a public outcry, viewing the arrest as pressure tied to the book negotiations.
Tags: moscow, schneerson library, lenin library, zev wagner, arrest, protest, berel lazar

Title: Russian raid to seize Schneerson books from Lenin Library blocked by protest
Summary: A secret Russian government plan to send a special police unit into the Lenin Library and seize the Schneerson collection collapsed when about a hundred protesters massed outside the building.
Story: On Friday 10 Adar I, deputy PM Shakhin and Zaitinov convened a closed meeting with Veronika, Moscow Soviet representative Natalia, library leadership and police to organize an immediate extraction of the books to government offices on the Old Square. Director Philipov managed to delay the unit at shift change, and twenty minutes later news arrived that a hundred-strong protest had formed outside the library, halting the operation.
Tags: moscow, schneerson library, books, lenin library, protest, shakhin, zaitinov, philipov

Title: Yeshiva students protest at Lenin Library
Summary: About 30 yeshiva students and shluchim demonstrated outside the Moscow library demanding return of the Rebbe's books, ending in a melee with militia officers.
Story: Veronika requested that yeshiva students organize a demonstration at the library Monday morning. At 10:30 about 30 people gathered there, expecting a quiet protest. Almost immediately tensions with militia officers escalated into a mass scuffle in which a policeman was injured and bled. The shluchim then drove to government offices in the old square briefly before returning to the yeshiva to continue regular learning.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneersohn library, protest, yeshiva, police, veronika

Title: Baker-Yeltsin meeting on Schneersohn books
Summary: Secretary Baker met Yeltsin in Moscow with Ambassador Strauss, Dennis Ross, and Foreign Minister Kozyrev; Yeltsin promised the books would soon be returned via the Academy.
Story: Mr. Collins descended at the embassy to report that Baker had met Yeltsin to discuss the books. Yeltsin assured Baker the matter was already arranged and the books would soon be transferred to the Academy of Sciences for delivery to the Rebbe, adding that the requested photocopies had been made. Collins asked the Chabad delegation to wait patiently and avoid making noise while the process proceeded.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneersohn library, james baker, yeltsin, strauss, dennis ross, kozyrev, diplomacy

Title: Russian parliament votes against returning the books
Summary: After Yeltsin's promise, the Russian parliament held a long debate and resolved not to return the Schneersohn books, with some demanding Yeltsin resign.
Story: Just a day after Yeltsin assured Baker the books would come back, the Russian parliament held a prolonged session and the majority voted against return; some legislators called for Yeltsin's resignation over his stance. Only about 150 of 500 deputies were in the plenum. Simultaneously the new court panel reversed the original ruling, holding that the books need not be returned. On TV that evening Yeltsin promised he would find a way to implement his plans.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneersohn library, duma, yeltsin, court

Title: Chernobyl children's camp opens in Kiev
Summary: A Chabad camp opened in Kiev for about 80 Chernobyl children preparing to make aliyah to Eretz Yisrael at Kfar Chabad.
Story: Rabbi Yitzchak Kogan ran the camp with the author and his family, who traveled overnight by train from Moscow. The first day went well with 45 girls and 35 boys settled in two adjacent camps. Most lacked any traditional background but wanted to study at the religious school in Kfar Chabad. Rabbi Dov Ber Krasik in Kiev had organized the children and prepared the camp.
Tags: ukraine, kiev, chernobyl, tzeirei agudat chabad, aliyah, krasik

Title: Press conference on Schneersohn books with Shakhrai aide
Summary: Yitzchak Kogan and Tanya Pirtsova attended a press conference by Shakhrai, head of Russia's justice department, raising the unreturned books.
Story: At a press conference held by Shakhrai, an aide to Yeltsin and head of the State Legal Office, Kogan and Pirtsova asked publicly about the justice of not returning the books despite a clear court ruling. Shakhrai said he knew of the matter though not closely, invited them to approach him after the press conference, and requested that they bring related documents the next day for review and possible help. Rabbi Cunin was meanwhile preparing a memorandum on the matter.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneersohn library, shakhrai, press conference, kogan, pirtsova

Title: Wedding officiated in Kharkov 54 years after parents' clandestine wedding
Summary: The author traveled to Kharkov by overnight train to officiate a wedding in the same city where his parents had wed secretly under Stalin 54 years earlier.
Story: With Rabbi Moshe Moshkovitz away in America, the author was asked to come to Kharkov to perform a Jewish wedding ceremony. Fifty-four years earlier in the winter of 5698, his own parents had married in Kharkov under entirely different conditions during the terrifying Stalin-Yezhov era—in secret, then renting a modest flat outside the city to avoid attention. Now their son openly performed a wedding ceremony in that same city with publicity and joy.
Tags: ukraine, kharkov, wedding, moshkovitz, stalin era

Title: Rebbe suffers stroke at the Ohel
Summary: The Rebbe was found lying at the Ohel by Rabbi Krinsky and brought back to 770 where doctors tended to him; speech and hand movement gradually returned.
Story: While visiting the Ohel the Rebbe collapsed; Rabbi Krinsky entered, found him, and immediately called an ambulance and doctors. The Rebbe instructed that he be taken specifically to 770, where doctors treated him continuously. When his speech became unclear, doctors tried showing him siddur letters, but the Rebbe pushed the siddur away and worked to speak; speech returned slowly along with hand strength, suggesting the episode was mild and passing.
Tags: brooklyn, 770, ohel, krinsky, stroke, illness

Title: Rebbe declares 'a healing soon with song and praise'
Summary: The Rebbe told Rabbi Leibel Gruner in Yiddish: 'There will be a healing soon with abundant song and music.'
Story: After two grave days when the Rebbe was at times unconscious, on Thursday evening he already stood for Maariv prayers with assistance, saying he would soon be able to do so alone. Rabbi Dov Ber Lazar reported that the Rebbe told Leibel Gruner: 'S'vet zayn a refuah b'karov b'rov shira u'b'zimra.' At the general gathering downstairs in the shul, the news brought joy and consolation to all assembled.
Tags: brooklyn, 770, gruner, lazar, illness, yiddish

Title: Flight transports 75 Chernobyl children to Eretz Yisrael
Summary: On 5 Adar Sheni, 75 children flew from Kiev to Israel to study at Kfar Chabad while a return load of 6-8 tons of Passover food came back to Kiev.
Story: Seventy of the children were from Kiev region and five from Moscow, accompanied by the author and his son Meir. After landing at Lod the plane was loaded with food supplies organized by Tzeirei Agudat Chabad in Eretz Yisrael for return to Kiev. About ten children from previous groups who needed to return came back on the same flight. The author left his son Meir to spend Passover with grandparents and the Hertzel family at Kfar Chabad.
Tags: ukraine, kiev, chernobyl, aliyah, kfar chabad, tzeirei agudat chabad, passover supplies

Title: Yeltsin's adviser proposes raising books at the Congress
Summary: A Yeltsin aide told Tanya Pirtsova the only path to approval was raising the books at the Russian Congress in April, ideally through Ambassador Strauss.
Story: Senator Gore reported that the new Russian ambassador to Washington had called him saying Yeltsin would return the books after the April 6 Congress and asked Chabad not to make noise. Gore was skeptical that promises tied to upcoming summits would be honored. Meanwhile Shakhrai's aide told Pirtsova the only way to push the issue through was via the April Congress, preferably through Ambassador Strauss raising it with Shakhrai.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneersohn library, shakhrai, yeltsin, senator gore, strauss, diplomacy

Title: Synagogue arson attempt in Moscow
Summary: Unknown attackers broke into the Marina Roscha synagogue overnight, poured gasoline and set fire to Rabbi Kogan's bedroom, but it was extinguished quickly.
Story: Intruders entered the Chabad synagogue at night, doused Rabbi Yitzchak Kogan's bedroom with gasoline and set it ablaze. People heard the commotion and rushed in to put out the fire. Rabbi Kogan was in Petersburg at the time. The shluchim believed it was intimidation by opponents of their work over the books campaign; Veronika tried to link it to her recent efforts to recover the synagogue's upper floor.
Tags: russia, moscow, marina roscha, arson, schneersohn library, kogan

Title: Sample Passover seder taught to yeshiva students
Summary: The author conducted a demonstration seder for yeshiva students preparing to lead public seders in remote Russian towns.
Story: Many of the 20 yeshiva students had only become observant within the past year and had never seen a seder. About 15 students attended a three-hour demonstration seder so they could learn to lead public seders. Together they were preparing seders in about 25 towns across Russia, relying mainly on Chabad shluchim in the towns and the yeshiva students themselves, with no help from American bochurim that year.
Tags: russia, moscow, passover, yeshiva, seder training, outreach

Title: Author moves to Petersburg for Passover
Summary: The author arrived in Petersburg at 6:30 AM to prepare for Passover, inspect the matzah bakery, give shiurim and arrange the seder at the Great Synagogue.
Story: Yaakov Krovliak and Mendel Balkin met him at the train station. He inspected the Great Synagogue's matzah bakery — far from satisfactory — and Chief Rabbi Lewitas asked him to supervise the baking of 5 tons of shemurah flour. The author insisted Krovliak would supervise but he would not certify the matzot as fully proper. He gave a shiur on Passover halacha to the elders, visited a children's garden in the city, and discussed the rabbinic position offered to him by Lewitas.
Tags: russia, petersburg, passover, matzah bakery, lewitas, krovliak, balkin

Title: Pesach shiurim across Petersburg shuls and yeshiva
Summary: On 10 Nisan 5752, the author taught Pesach halachos across Petersburg's synagogues, yeshiva, and parent groups during his special shlichus mission to Russia.
Story: Based in Petersburg ahead of Pesach 5752, the author records giving shiurim before Kabbalat Shabbat in the small shul, before Musaf in the great shul, and again in the small shul; speaking at a post-tefillah farbrengen about yetzias mitzrayim in our times; teaching a parents' group of day-school children on Sunday afternoons; and learning with yeshiva students from 5 to 8 pm. Alongside the classes he handled chametz sales using forms specially printed by Kuritz and fielded live halacha questions throughout the day, noting deep satisfaction with the output of the learning.
Tags: petersburg, russia, pesach, shlichus, halacha, soviet jewry

Title: US Congress awards the Rebbe a Congressional Gold Medal
Summary: The US Congress presented the Rebbe with a gold medal of honor on the occasion of his 90th birthday, 11 Nisan 5752 (April 1992).
Story: The 1992 award marked the Rebbe's ninetieth birthday and stood out among the many official tributes from American officials over the years.
Tags: rebbe, us congress, gold medal, 11 nisan

Title: Pesach visit to Peter and Paul Fortress, site of Alter Rebbe's imprisonment
Summary: On 1st day Chol HaMoed Pesach 5752, the author visited Petersburg's Peter and Paul Fortress and the wooded grove marking where the prison that held the Alter Rebbe once stood.
Story: During Chol HaMoed Pesach 5752 the author crossed into the Peter and Paul Fortress on Petersburg's Neva island and toured its prison cells. Guides explained that the current prison post-dates the Alter Rebbe — they pointed to a sparse grove not far from the present building where the older prison had stood before being demolished when the current one was built. Afterwards he toured the nearby palace housing the Asian Institute, where Shimon Yakerson showed him rare books and incunabula from the institute's collection and heard updates on the campaign to recover the Schneersohn library.
Tags: alter rebbe, petersburg, russia, imprisonment, yakerson, asian institute

Title: Major diplomatic push for return of Schneersohn library
Summary: On 15 Iyar 5752 several parallel meetings on the Schneersohn library converged: Aharonov and Cunin met Vorontsov in NY; Yeltsin summoned culture minister Sidorov; Strauss met Yeltsin; and Veronika met PM Gaidar.
Story: After a long lull the books issue exploded into activity. Rabbi Yosef Yitzchok Aharonov flew to New York and, through Mr. Fishman, arranged a meeting between himself, Rabbi Shlomo Cunin, and Vorontsov — Yeltsin's deputy, in NY for the UN. Yeltsin called culture minister Sidorov for a report; Robert Strauss was to meet Yeltsin on the library that day; Aubrey at the US embassy summoned Mr. Weissman for a briefing; and Veronika was scheduled to meet Prime Minister Gaidar. Veronika also received a copy of a letter from Mr. Philipov to the Rebbe stating that beyond the 2,000 books previously identified, the library had now found Schneersohn-collection markings on another 700 volumes, with months of identification work still ahead.
Tags: schneerson library, yeltsin, russia, vorontsov, gaidar, strauss, philipov, books campaign, fishman

Title: Rebbe's first post-stroke visit to the upstairs shul at 770
Summary: On Monday 15 Iyar 5752 the Rebbe visited the upstairs shul at 770 for the first time since his stroke, marking another step in his gradual recovery.
Story: In the weeks following his stroke on Purim 5752 the Rebbe gradually resumed public activities. The diary notes that on the Monday before Lag BaOmer the Rebbe was brought upstairs to visit the shul at 770 for the first time. The next day he would tour the library; both visits were framed as part of a slow return that those close to him hoped would lead to full recovery.
Tags: 770, stroke recovery, wheelchair

Title: Rebbe tours all floors of Schneersohn library at 770
Summary: On Tuesday 16 Iyar 5752 the Rebbe was brought through every floor and department of the Schneersohn library at 770, then sat on the roof terrace, answering written questions by nodding.
Story: Doctors had encouraged the Rebbe to go up to the roof terrace to enjoy the warm weather. Before reaching the terrace the Rebbe toured every floor and department of the library — pushed in his wheelchair by his three secretaries Yitzchok Wilhelm, Moshe Klein, and Yengi Bistritzky. On the terrace he sat for tea while Rabbi Leibel Groner read aloud the contents of submitted questions; the Rebbe responded with nods of his head. The library visit lasted roughly half an hour, and the terrace visit another half hour.
Tags: 770, library, stroke recovery, wheelchair, leibel groner, yitzchok wilhelm, moshe klein, bistritzky

Title: Lag BaOmer parade through Moscow with cruise to river island
Summary: On Lag BaOmer 5752, hundreds of children and adults paraded with a band and signs from Moscow's great shul to the river, then boarded two cruise boats to an island.
Story: Lag BaOmer 5752 in Moscow opened with a parade from the great synagogue to the riverbank, drawing several hundred children and adults marching with a band and placards. Participants then boarded two cruise ships out to an island on the river. The author returned to Marina Roshcha to daven, then drove with Rabbi Ariel Chaikin — back from inspecting the mikveh under construction in Kharkov — to catch the last leg of the boat trip to the island. They addressed the gathered children briefly before returning.
Tags: moscow, russia, lag baomer, children, parade, marina roshcha, rabbi chaikin

Title: Wedding of Chaim Tolochinsky at Moscow Aguch shul
Summary: On Lag BaOmer night 5752, Chaim Tolochinsky — the first top student of the Moscow yeshiva and institute to marry through the shlichus mission — was wed at the Aguch shul.
Story: The wedding was prepared by Rabbi Yitzchok Kogan, Rabbi Berel Lazar, and Rabbi Daniel Edri, with Rabbi Ariel Chaikin serving as mesader kiddushin. The author escorted the chossen to the Aguch shul and managed proceedings throughout the evening, returning home at 1 am. He records that this was the first time one of the top talmidim of the Moscow yeshiva and institute had married under the mission's auspices, calling the chuppah very beautiful and joyous.
Tags: moscow, russia, wedding, yeshiva, aguch, rabbi chaikin, rabbi kogan, rabbi lazar, rabbi edri

Title: Shloshim for traveling shliach R. Avraham Yitzchok Glick in Stamford Hill
Summary: On the evening of 2 Sivan 5752, a large London crowd gathered at the Stamford Hill shul for the shloshim of the traveling shliach R. Avraham Yitzchok Glick.
Story: Stopping in London en route from Moscow to New York, the author found a packed shul at Stamford Hill assembled for the shloshim of R. Avraham Yitzchok Glick, a longtime traveling shliach. The elder Rabbi Padwa, Rabbi Ashkenazi, and other senior figures spoke in his memory. Spotting the author as he entered, the organizers seated him at the head table and asked him to say a few words. The evening concluded with maariv.
Tags: london, stamford hill, shloshim, traveling shliach, rabbi padwa, rabbi ashkenazi

Title: Baker to deliver 100-senator letter demanding return of Schneersohn library
Summary: Around 7 Sivan 5752, Secretary Baker was to hand Foreign Minister Kozyrev a letter from 100 US senators demanding Yeltsin honor his promise to return the Schneersohn library.
Story: Rabbi Shlomo Cunin assembled signatures from 100 US senators demanding that Yeltsin honor his commitment to Baker to return the Schneersohn library. Baker was to deliver the letter and signatures to Foreign Minister Kozyrev, who had come to Washington to prepare the Bush–Yeltsin summit. The author judged Yeltsin unlikely to ignore it, since he was hoping for major US aid and could not afford bitterness from senators and the administration. The pressure was compounded by separate leverage over the Smolensk archive — three million documents whose return to Russia President Bush had paused pending release of the Schneersohn collection.
Tags: james baker, kozyrev, schneerson library, senators, books campaign, us state department, smolensk archive, george h.w. bush

Title: Rebbe appears publicly in wheelchair after Shavuot tahalucha
Summary: On motzaei Shavuot 5752, after the tahalucha, the Rebbe was brought to the entrance of 770 in a wheelchair to see the assembled crowd for about four minutes.
Story: On the evening following the Shavuot tahalucha of 5752 the Rebbe was brought to the 770 entrance in his wheelchair to see the assembled crowd. He stayed outside for roughly four minutes; when asked if he wished to go back inside he nodded yes. The author, standing in the corridor as the Rebbe emerged from his room, noted that the Rebbe's face appeared almost as usual but that he looked only straight ahead at the crowd. Some reported the Rebbe slightly inclined his head toward Rabbi Yoel Kahan.
Tags: 770, shavuot, tahalucha, stroke recovery, wheelchair, yoel kahan

Title: Bush–Yeltsin summit: Bush raises Schneersohn library; Yeltsin silent
Summary: At the Washington summit in mid-June 1992 Bush raised the Schneersohn library with Yeltsin and received no answer, reportedly because Yeltsin lacked authority to commit.
Story: Around 1 Tammuz 5752 the author noted that for the two weeks since the Bush–Yeltsin summit there had been no news from Washington on the library. Reports filtered back that Bush had raised the books issue with Yeltsin during the summit but Yeltsin had not responded — apparently because he wanted to release the collection but had not been authorized internally, and rather than admit that publicly chose to stay silent. Soon after, a fax from Devorah Rochel reported fresh movement on the library issue and urged immediate return to Moscow.
Tags: bush yeltsin summit, washington, schneerson library, books campaign

Title: Completion of first edit of Igrot Kodesh volume 20
Summary: On 29 Sivan 5752 the author completed the first editing pass of Igrot Kodesh volume 20.
Story: Back in New York between trips to Russia, the author spent two weeks editing Igrot Kodesh volume 20, finishing the first pass on Tuesday afternoon 29 Sivan 5752. He noted the absence of news from Washington in the wake of the recent Bush–Yeltsin summit. The next morning a fax arrived from Devorah Rochel in Moscow reporting renewed movement on the library and urging the delegation's immediate return.
Tags: igrot kodesh, frierdiker rebbe, kehot, editing, library

Title: Chabad delegation hands Yeltsin appeal for Schneersohn library at Munich G7
Summary: On 6 Tammuz 5752 the Chabad delegation greeted Yeltsin on his arrival at Munich's Marriott during the G7 summit with 'Davai knigi Schneersohn!' — and Yeltsin replied 'Skoro' (soon).
Story: Having transferred from the Arabella to the Marriott — where Yeltsin and his government were staying — the delegation was on hand when Yeltsin arrived in the evening. Rabbis Cunin and Aharonov shook his hand and said 'Davai knigi Schneersohn!' (Give us the Schneersohn books!). Caught off guard, Yeltsin had no real answer; pressed by Aharonov 'Kogda?' (When?), he replied 'Skoro' (Soon). The next morning the delegation approached him again, and Rabbi Yitzchok Kogan gave him a Chitas as a segulah for success. The shliach Rabbi Diskin took members of the delegation to meet US official Spakoyne, who promised to push Helmut Kohl to raise the library with Yeltsin.
Tags: yeltsin, munich, g7 summit, schneerson library, rabbi cunin, rabbi aharonov, books campaign, marriott, rabbi kogan

Title: R. Shalom DovBer Levin briefs Prof. Yirmiyahu Branover on the missing arrest file
Summary: Prof. Yirmiyahu Branover visits New York, where Levin lays out a detailed search plan for the Mitteler Rebbe's arrest file via Shamir's archive access.
Story: At the beginning of Tishrei 5753 (October 1992), Prof. Yirmiyahu Branover visited New York. R. Shalom DovBer Levin met with him and laid out his theory that the Khovansky-era arrest file of the Mitteler Rebbe could finally be located through the Shamir organization's newly authorized archive access in Russia. Levin then wrote a detailed memorandum identifying which provincial archives — particularly Minsk — should be searched.
Tags: branover, shamir, levin, archives, russia, mitteler rebbe, historical research

Title: Levin writes letter expressing crisis about abandoning book restitution mission
Summary: Rabbi Shalom Dovber Levin wrote to Yosef Yitzchak Aharonov, agonizing over whether he could ethically abandon the mission to recover the Schneerson library books from Moscow.
Story: After a discouraging phone call, Levin fell into depression questioning his role in Moscow. Concluding he was too personally invested to judge alone, he consulted three uninvolved advisors per the Rebbes' guidance. Most agreed he must continue the effort and travel at least briefly to publicly demonstrate the demand for the books' return.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, shalom-dovber-levin, yosef-yitzchak-aharonov

Title: Haggadah 'Yismach Yisrael' of Alexander Chassidut reprinted in Bnei Brak
Summary: The 'Yismach Yisrael' Haggadah commentary by Yerachmiel Yisrael Yitzchak of Alexander was reprinted with extensive additions in Bnei Brak.
Story: In 5753 (1993), the Haggadah with the 'Yismach Yisrael' commentary by Rabbi Yerachmiel Yisrael Yitzchak of Alexander was reissued in Bnei Brak with many added materials. The 176-page octavo edition served the Alexander Chassidic community and admirers of their teachings. It demonstrated the continued vitality of classical Polish Chassidic Haggadah commentary.
Tags: haggadah, chassidic, alexander, yerachmiel yisrael yitzchak, bnei brak

Title: Igros Kodesh Admur Maharash published
Summary: In 5753 the Igros Kodesh of Rebbe Maharash was published, including clearer reproductions of the megillah he wrote.
Story: The 5753 volume of Rebbe Maharash's letters included higher-quality photographs of several pages of the megillah he wrote in his own hand, which had been mentioned in earlier sources as having been distributed among his sons. The original megillah is preserved in the Chabad library archive.
Tags: maharash, igros kodesh, kehot, megillah

Title: Publication of Rashab Maamarim Likut Vol. 2 in New York
Summary: Volume 2 of 'Sefer HaMaamarim - Likut' of the Rashab Rebbe was published in New York.
Story: In 5753 (1993), 'Sefer HaMaamarim - Likut' Volume 2 of the Chabad Rashab Rebbe Shalom Dovber Schneersohn was published in New York. The 328-page octavo edition added to the publication of the fifth Chabad Rebbe's prolific Chassidic output. It maintained the Chabad publishing effort to release the discourses of the Rebbe Rashab in systematic order.
Tags: chabad, rashab, new york, maamarim, rebbe rashab

Title: Levin meets Igor and Boruch Gorin in Moscow's Marina Roshcha
Summary: In Moscow, Levin instructs Shamir's archive researcher Igor to focus the search on Minsk for the Mitteler Rebbe's file.
Story: On 2 Shevat 5753 (24 January 1993), R. Shalom DovBer Levin met in Marina Roshcha, Moscow, with Igor, who was working for Shamir to locate Chabad-related documents, together with Boruch Gorin. Levin explained why the search should now concentrate on Minsk and handed over a written summary. A few months later Wagner joined the project.
Tags: shamir, moscow, marina roshcha, minsk, archives, mitteler rebbe, historical research

Title: Librarian confirms forgery markings then receives orders to stop showing books
Summary: Ashkenazi confirmed nearly every catalogue card showed a 'P' mark overwritten with 'S', and the very next day Russian inspectors were told the operation was over.
Story: Ashkenazi reported that without exception the old cards revealed a 'P' (Polyakov) had been overwritten by an 'S' (Schneerson). When confronted, Goldenberg deflected, saying what mattered was that they had the books. The next day access was cut off, having lasted only one day.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, polyakov-collection, forgery, shmuel-goldenberg

Title: Russian Ministry of Culture grants permission to inspect Schneerson books
Summary: Shortly before Purim 5753, the Russian Ministry of Culture notified the Chabad delegation that they would be permitted to view and inspect the disputed library books.
Story: After prolonged negotiations, the Russian authorities granted limited access to inspect the Schneerson collection. Levin, then in New York, viewed this skeptically as a distraction tactic from the real goal of returning the books. He wrote to Aharonov questioning the purpose of merely viewing the books rather than receiving them.

Title: Levin protests inspection-only access as distraction from book return
Summary: Levin wrote in distress to Aharonov, arguing that the offer to merely inspect the books was a Russian tactic to deflect pressure for actual restitution.
Story: Levin questioned what value there was in just viewing books in the library. He pointed out a pattern: whenever the Russians felt pressure to return the books, they introduced a distraction to silence the demand. The only proper response, he insisted, was to declare this is not what was requested.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, shalom-dovber-levin

Title: Levin suspects librarians of forging collection markings on the books
Summary: Examining inspection notes faxed by Chaim Eliezer Ashkenazi, Levin concluded the librarians were actively forging markings to obscure that Polyakov-collection books were really Schneerson books.
Story: Levin noted that on several books the 'P' mark for Polyakov coexisted suspiciously with an 'S' for Schneerson freshly written on the card. He suspected the librarians were systematically erasing 'P' marks and adding 'S' marks to hide the books' true provenance. He urged Ashkenazi to keep checking discreetly since the Russians would block Levin himself.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, polyakov-collection, forgery, chaim-eliezer-ashkenazi

Title: Levin writes to Moscow librarian Goldenberg requesting Polyakov book list
Summary: Levin sent a diplomatic letter to librarian Shmuel Goldenberg asking him to provide the list of Polyakov collection books in the Muzey Knigi to verify Schneerson provenance.
Story: Thanking Goldenberg for helping his colleagues view books, Levin asked for the list of over 100 Polyakov books in the rare-books museum so he could compare them to the Schneerson catalogue. He framed this as a small first step before tackling the larger collections of 2,000 books in Moscow and 10,000 in the Khimki depot.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, polyakov-collection, shmuel-goldenberg

Title: Rebbe's 91st birthday celebrated with kos shel berachah
Summary: On 11 Nissan 5753, Rabbi Yitzchak Kaduri sent a kos shel refuah blessing for the Rebbe's 91st birthday.
Story: On 11 Nissan 5753 (April 2, 1993), Rabbi Yitzchak Kaduri sent a 'cup of healing' inscribed with a blessing for the Lubavitcher Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson on his 91st birthday. The cup carried the inscription invoking blessings for the Rebbe, son of Chana, and is preserved among the personal items associated with the Rebbe.
Tags: menachem mendel schneerson, 770, yitzchak kaduri, birthday

Title: Rabbi Hodakov passes away after decades as Chabad chief of staff
Summary: Rabbi Hodakov passes away after serving as the seventh Rebbe's chief of staff and secretary.
Story: He had overseen Chabad's global growth, accompanied the Rebbe to America in 1940, and helped establish the first national Jewish school system in the US. His career spanned from chief inspector in 1930s Latvia to the postwar Chabad headquarters.
Tags: hodakov, passing, 770, seventh-rebbe

Title: Tziyun HaMetzuyenes published
Summary: In Iyar 5753, R. Yosef Menachem Weiss published Tziyun HaMetzuyenes, documenting the graves of the Nodah BiYhudah and his family in Prague.
Story: In Iyar 5753 (May 1993), R. Yosef Menachem Weiss published the book Tziyun HaMetzuyenes about the graves of the Nodah BiYhudah and his family in the Prague cemetery, with documents, photographs and biographies — including an entry on the Nodah BiYhudah's distinguished son-in-law R. Yosef Hatzaddik of Posen.

Title: Wedding of Batya Nemenov and Shneur Zalman Marcus
Summary: On 5 Tammuz 5753, Batya Nemenov married Shneur Zalman Marcus, a member of the kollel in New York.
Story: Batya, daughter of Miriam Reizel and Moshe Nemenov, married Shneur Zalman Marcus on 5 Tammuz 5753. Shneur Zalman Marcus is a member of the kollel in New York.

Title: Levin and Wagner plan a Shamir trip to Minsk archives
Summary: Meeting in Moscow, Levin and Wagner finalize a plan to search Minsk archives for the Mitteler Rebbe's arrest file.
Story: On Erev Shabbat 20 Tammuz 5753 (9 July 1993), R. Shalom DovBer Levin met with Igor Wagner in Moscow to discuss the methodology of the document search. They agreed that immediately after Shabbat the team would travel to Minsk to look specifically for the file relating to the arrest and liberation of the Mitteler Rebbe.

Title: Wedding of Eli Wolf and Nechama Dina
Summary: On 13 Elul 5753, Eli Wolf married Nechama Dina; the couple is associated with the Gutnick Center in Jerusalem.
Story: Eli, son of the author's daughter Feigel and Mendel Wolf, married Nechama Dina on 13 Elul 5753. The couple is associated with the Gutnick Center in Jerusalem.

Title: Author's first pilgrimage to parents' graves in Samarkand and Tashkent
Summary: In Elul 5753 the author traveled for the first time to Samarkand and Tashkent to visit his parents' graves and arrange for repairs and a new matzevah.
Story: In Elul 5753 (August/September 1993), the author traveled for the first time to Samarkand to visit his father Eliyahu's grave and to Tashkent to visit his mother Rachel's grave. He left funds in Samarkand for restoration of the matzevah and arranged for a new matzevah in Tashkent. For decades earlier he had relied on shluchim traveling to the Soviet Union to bring back photographs of the gravestones.

Title: Russians propose exchanging Schneerson collection for substitute books
Summary: Rabbi Yisroel Kogan phoned Levin reporting that Russian officials offered to return the Schneerson collection if Chabad provided substitute books of equivalent value.
Story: Kogan also reported receiving the full archive file on the books, including over ten previously unseen documents. Levin rejected the exchange concept outright, predicting it would lead to endless demands for matching books, hidden payments, and ultimately government-funded receptions before any real return. He insisted the books must be returned unconditionally.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, yisroel-kogan

Title: Seven additional Schneerson books transferred to US government as temporary loan
Summary: Beyond the gifted Tanya, Russia transferred seven more books from the Schneerson collection to the US government as a temporary loan, which Cunin brought directly to the Rebbe.
Story: These seven books were framed as a borrowed loan to the American administration rather than a return. Rabbi Cunin carried them straight to the Rebbe's room and placed them on his table. They became the focal point of the IFLA complaint that followed when they were not returned.
Tags: russia, usa, schneerson-library, diplomacy, boruch-shlomo-cunin

Title: Russian Culture Minister presents first returned Tanya to Vice President Gore
Summary: On Zos Chanukah 5754, Russian Culture Minister Yevgeny Sidorov hosted Vice President Al Gore at the Moscow public library and handed him a 1900 Tanya from the Schneerson collection.
Story: Sidorov showed Gore twelve books from the Schneerson collection and gave him one: a Tanya printed in 5660 by the Rebbe Rashab through Tomchei Tmimim. A special leather-bound copy inscribed as a gift 'to the head of Tomchei Tmimim, the Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak' was the actual volume transferred. Vice President Gore handed it to Rabbi Boruch Shlomo Cunin to deliver to the Lubavitcher Rebbe.
Tags: russia, usa, moscow, tanya, al-gore, yevgeny-sidorov, diplomacy

Title: Special delegation brings the first returned Tanya to the Lubavitcher Rebbe
Summary: On Erev Shabbos Vayigash, the special delegation including Cunin, Aharonov, Kogan, and Levin presented the recovered 1900 Tanya to the Rebbe at 770.
Story: At 3:20 PM the entire delegation, with attorney Devorah Rachel Kogan and supporter Albi Rozhouse, approached the Rebbe at the entrance to his room. Cunin placed the Tanya on the table; the Rebbe raised his eyes and gazed at each person passing before him. The delegation then sang and danced in the Gan Eden HaTachton for about an hour.
Tags: usa, 770, tanya, menachem-mendel-schneerson, boruch-shlomo-cunin, schneerson-library

Title: Chabad Library begins annual themed exhibitions
Summary: Starting in 5754, the Chabad Library at 770 began mounting a new themed exhibition every one to two years.
Story: In 5754 (1993–1994), the Agudas Chasidei Chabad – Ohel Yosef Yitzchak – Lubavitch Library at 770 Eastern Parkway began its tradition of mounting themed exhibitions of rare items from its archives. Over the years more than ten exhibitions have been organized, each dedicated to a different theme such as rare manuscripts, Chabad Rebbeim, Haggadot, or the bicentennial of the Alter Rebbe's liberation.
Tags: 770, chabad library, exhibitions, brooklyn

Title: Chabad Library exhibition hall opens to the public
Summary: In 5754 the exhibition hall of the Chabad Library was opened to the general public.
Story: In 5754 (1994) a dedicated exhibition hall within the Chabad Library was opened to the public. It displays rotating selections of rare books, manuscripts, photographs, objects, and artwork drawn from the library's collections, with a new thematic exhibit chosen roughly every year or two by the library's administration.

Title: Complete new edition of Tzemach Tzedek published
Summary: In 5754 a complete and reset edition of the Tzemach Tzedek series was published, integrating all supplements, omissions, and milu'im in newly typeset square letters.
Story: Five years after the Rebbe's 5749 directive, the new comprehensive edition of the Tzemach Tzedek appeared. It consolidated 110 years of supplements, omissions, additions, and milu'im (including Choshen Mishpat) into a unified typeset series, finally resolving the longstanding difficulty of locating a given responsum scattered across multiple appendices.

Title: Discovery of the Reshimot
Summary: The seventh Rebbe's private diary, the Reshimot, was discovered in his desk shortly after his passing.
Story: The diary, begun in 1928 and containing a wealth of chasidic lore, history, and customs, was later published as Torat Menachem: Reshimat HaYoman by Kehot Publication Society in 2006. It opened a window into the seventh Rebbe's decade-long spiritual dialogue with the Rebbe Rayatz.
Tags: reshimot, diary, kehot, torat-menachem

Title: Gold medal "L'taken Olam" issued in honor of the Rebbe
Summary: A specially minted gold medal bearing the Rebbe's likeness, the image of 770, and the inscription "L'taken Olam" was issued in 5754 (1994).
Story: The 1994 medal carried the Rebbe's portrait on one side and the iconic facade of 770 Eastern Parkway on the other, along with the Hebrew motto "L'taken Olam" and the English values Benevolence, Ethics, Leadership, and Scholarship.
Tags: rebbe, gold medal, ltaken olam, 770

Title: Hendel Deutsch publishes Russian booklet documenting Lubavitch history
Summary: In 5754 (1994) Mr. Hendel Deutsch compiled and published a small Russian-language booklet titled 'Lubavitch — Center of Chabad Chassidus, Documentary Sketches.'
Story: Deutsch gathered surviving documents and general information about the town across the centuries. His booklet was published in Russian in 1994, providing a documentary basis for later historical accounts of Lubavitch's pre-Chabad and early-Chabad history.

Title: Hendel Deutsch publishes Russian documentary booklet on Lubavitch
Summary: In 5754 Hendel Deutsch published a small Russian-language booklet titled Lubavitch - Center of Chabad Chassidus: A Documentary Description.
Story: Deutsch collected documents and general information about the town across its centuries of history. The booklet included material such as a 5544 list of approximately fifty Jewish families living in Lubavitch. It served as a key reference work for the contemporary effort to recover and document the town's Chabad history.

Title: Publication of Rashimat Maamarei DACh of the Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: In 5754 (1994) the Rashimat Maamarei DACh of the Tzemach Tzedek was published, organizing his maamarim chronologically for the first time.
Story: The work was based on a card catalog compiled beginning in 5741 (1981) by R. Avraham Boruch Yunik, drawing on dated discourse headings in Or HaTorah, R. Hillel of Paritch's hanachos, the Maharash's hanachos, and the Tzemach Tzedek's own manuscript volumes. R. Yosef Yitzchak Keller completed and prepared the work after finishing the Alter Rebbe registry. It overcame the unique difficulty that the Tzemach Tzedek's maamarim were preserved by topic rather than by year.

Title: Seven Lubavitch books loaned to Rabbi Cunin via US government
Summary: Seven books from the Schneersohn collection were given to Rabbi B.S. Cunin as a two-month loan arranged through US government channels and never returned.
Story: In 5754 (1994), Rabbi B.S. Cunin signed for seven books from the Schneersohn collection as a two-month loan, the transaction mediated through the US government. He was told his signature was a mere formality and the books would not need to be returned; they were given to the Rebbe and placed sealed in his study. The Moscow Library subsequently filed a claim at the International Court of Justice in The Hague.

Title: Yitzchak Shamir addresses Tel Aviv memorial for seventh Rebbe
Summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Yitzchak Shamir recounted discovering Chabad's clandestine Soviet network as a young Mossad operative.
Story: Speaking at a Tel Aviv memorial for the seventh Lubavitcher Rebbe, Shamir said that on his early-1950s mission to Russia, 'we were surprised to discover that in every city across Russia, there was an existing clandestine Jewish network being directed by the Rebbe in New York.' The discovery led to a long partnership between the Mossad and Chabad's underground.

Title: Wedding of Rivka Klein and Mordechai Grossbaum
Summary: On 19 Adar II 5754, Rivka Klein married Mordechai Grossbaum, a member of the kollel in New York.

Title: Mitteler Rebbe's arrest file located in Minsk
Summary: After years of searching, the file from the Mitteler Rebbe's arrest is found and photographed in Minsk.
Story: On 2 Nissan 5754 (14 March 1994), R. Boruch Schiff received notification from Minsk that the long-sought file had been located and photographed — some 120 pages of documents from the Khovansky chancellery covering the entire 1825-1828 affair. The find ended a search that had begun in 1976 with the Rebbe's instructions to Hendel Deutsch and intensified in winter 1988. The translated dossier became the basis for the published volume of the case.

Title: Russian official Shvydkoy visits Levin to pitch loan-language compromise
Summary: Russian deputy culture minister Mikhail Shvydkoy and two colleagues brought Levin a letter from Filipov proposing Chabad officially request the books as a loan.
Story: Levin refused firmly but gently to sign anything framed as conceding the books did not belong to Chabad. Shvydkoy described plans to allocate buildings at Chekhova 18 or Mokhovaya 6 for a special center housing the collection. Levin objected that participating in such a center would imply Chabad accepted the books were not theirs.

Title: Russia files IFLA complaint demanding return of seven loaned books
Summary: When the April 19 return deadline arrived for the seven loaned books, Moscow library immediately filed a formal complaint to the IFLA international library association.
Story: The original loan deadline had been described as a mere formality, but the Russians used it as a trap. Upon the deadline passing, the Moscow library filed an official grievance with IFLA over the unreturned books. Chabad received the complaint letter in early winter 5755 and after deliberation decided not to respond.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, ifla, diplomacy

Title: Passing of the seventh Lubavitcher Rebbe in Brooklyn
Summary: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson, the seventh Lubavitcher Rebbe, passed away in Brooklyn at age 92 and was interred alongside his father-in-law.
Story: After 42 years of leadership during which he transformed Chabad into the largest Jewish movement in the world, the seventh Rebbe passed away on 3 Tamuz 5754. He was buried in Montefiore Cemetery, New York, next to the Rayatz. The Ohel has since become a pilgrimage site visited by close to a million Jews and non-Jews seeking prayer and inspiration.
Tags: menachem mendel schneerson, brooklyn, montefiore cemetery, ohel

Title: Hatamim archive found after Rebbe's passing on 3 Tammuz 5754
Summary: After 3 Tammuz 5754, when the Rebbe's writings were reviewed, the long-lost Vilensky and Rosenbaum biographical files were discovered.
Story: More than sixty years after the Rayatz first requested it, the file containing R. Michael Vilensky's answers about his father, together with the dossier on R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum, was found among the Rebbe's papers. The material was reviewed after the Rebbe's passing on 3 Tammuz 5754 and later published in Pardes Chabad and Toldos Avraham Chaim.
Tags: rebbe, histalkus, archives, hatamim, chaim dover vilensky, avraham chaim rosenbaum

Title: Former librarian Goldenberg visits Levin in Brooklyn after leaving Russia
Summary: Shmuel Goldenberg, the former Moscow librarian who had moved to Brighton Beach, visited Levin and disclosed details about Schneerson book quantities and markings.
Story: Goldenberg revealed he had been ordered to separate marked books at the Khimki depot, selecting 3,500 of 8,000 books and transferring them to the Moscow library's restricted basement. He claimed most of the remaining 4,500 in Khimki also bore identifying marks but he was instructed not to be thorough. He confirmed 750 of the 2,000 books at the main library bore Schneerson marks, plus nearly 100 at the Muzey Knigi.

Title: Lubavitch Library exhibition hall opens
Summary: The exhibition hall of the Library of Agudas Chassidei Chabad opened to the public on Chai Elul 5754.
Story: On Chai Elul 5754 (August 1994) the Lubavitch Library inaugurated its exhibition hall in Brooklyn, opening selected treasures from the archive to the broader public. The library had previously been intended only for researchers, rabbis and authors, but the Rebbe had earlier approved opening an exhibition once a suitable space became available. The first exhibit, which ran until Erev Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5755, featured items connected to each of the Chabad Rebbes and to every area of Chabad activity.

Title: Lubavitch Library exhibition hall opens on 18 Elul
Summary: The Lubavitch Library exhibition hall opened on 18 Elul 5754.
Story: The exhibition hall of the Library of Agudas Chasidei Chabad - Ohel Yosef Yitzchak - Lubavitch opened on 18 Elul 5754 (September 1994). Over the following years it hosted a sequence of major exhibitions on Chabad history, manuscripts, sacred objects, and the work of the seventh Rebbe.

Title: First Library exhibition closes
Summary: The inaugural Lubavitch Library exhibition closed on Erev Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5755.
Story: The first exhibition of the Lubavitch Library, which opened on Chai Elul 5754, closed on Erev Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5755 (early November 1994). Title: English-language 'V'Higadta L'Vincha' Chabad Haggadah translated by Moshe Miller
Summary: Moshe Miller translated Yekutiel Green's 'V'Higadta L'Vincha' Chabad Haggadah into English.
Story: In 5755 (1995), Moshe Miller's English translation of Yekutiel Green's Chabad practical guide Haggadah 'V'Higadta L'Vincha' was published. The 334-page octavo edition expanded access to Chabad Pesach teaching for English-speaking Jews worldwide. It served as a definitive English Chabad Pesach resource.

Title: Exhibition on Chabad in the World and Torah Giants
Summary: The Library's second exhibition, on Chabad worldwide and Torah and Chassidic leaders, ran from Rosh Chodesh Sivan through after 3 Tammuz 5755.
Story: Opening on Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5755 and continuing past the yahrzeit of the Rebbe on 3 Tammuz, this exhibition focused on the Rebbe, the Chabad Rebbes, and gedolei Yisrael, alongside the spread of Chabad activity around the world. It emphasized the leadership era of the Rebbe Rayatz and the early years of the Rebbe's nesius, when Chabad activity expanded globally. Items included photographs, letters, signs and artifacts from Chabad centers in Russia, Eretz Yisrael, Europe, America and beyond.

Title: Publication of 'At Our Rebbe's Seder Table' in English by Eliyahu Touger
Summary: Eliyahu Touger published 'At Our Rebbe's Seder Table' in English in New York, an anthology of the Lubavitcher Rebbe's talks on the Haggadah.
Story: In 5755 (1995), Eliyahu Touger published 'At Our Rebbe's Seder Table' in English in New York. The 119-page octavo edition collected the Lubavitcher Rebbe's talks on the Haggadah translated into English. It made the Rebbe's Pesach teachings accessible to English-speaking Chabad followers worldwide.

Title: Yisrael Yehuda Levin completes memoir introduction
Summary: On 18 Elul 5755 in Kfar Chabad, Yisrael Yehuda Levin signed the introduction to his memoir Zichronotai, completing 35 years of writing.
Story: Levin had begun writing his memories around 1960 and added to them periodically through the 1990s. His son Shalom Dovber and grandson Yosef Yitzchak Keller edited the manuscript for publication. The memoir covers his life from the 1919-1920 pogroms in Zhivotov through his first month with the Rebbe in Tishrei 5723.
Tags: kfar chabad, zichronotai, yisrael yehuda levin, memoirs

Title: Albany Haggadah 'Kuntres Marbeh L'Saper' on personalities in the Haggadah
Summary: Yisrael Rubin, Chabad shaliach in Albany, published 'Kuntres Marbeh L'Saper' with notes on the personalities mentioned in the Haggadah.
Story: In 5756 (1996), Yisrael Rubin, the Chabad shaliach in Albany, New York, published 'Kuntres Marbeh L'Saper' (The Albany Haggadah), containing notes and studies on the personalities mentioned in the Haggadah. The 110-plus-10-page octavo edition exemplified the personalized scholarly Haggadah pamphlets produced by Chabad emissaries. It served the Albany Chabad community.
Tags: chabad, new york, albany, haggadah, yisrael rubin

Title: Eli Segal purchases first portion of the Lubavitch courtyard
Summary: In 5756 the philanthropist Eli Segal bought the first portion of the courtyard of the Rebbes in Lubavitch for the planned museum.
Story: In 5756 (1996), the philanthropist Mr. Eli Segal joined the long-running effort to build a museum on the site of the courtyard of the Rebbes in Lubavitch, purchasing the first portion of the courtyard. The initiative built on years of negotiation by Rabbi Natan Gurary with the Russian government following the opening of the Iron Curtain, in response to repeated encouragement from the Rebbe.

Title: Eliyahu Segal purchases first portion of Lubavitch courtyard
Summary: In 5756 the philanthropist Eliyahu Segal purchased the first portion of the original Lubavitch courtyard for the museum project being led by Rabbi Nosson Gourary.
Story: The purchase was the first step in reassembling the historic courtyard for use as a Chabad museum. Rabbi Nosson Gourary, the Rebbe's emissary to Buffalo, had been negotiating with the Russian government on the project since the opening of the Iron Curtain. The Rebbe had repeatedly urged him to bring the plan to fruition.

Title: Exhibition of Haggadot in the Library
Summary: The Library mounted an exhibition of Passover Haggadot in spring 5756.
Story: In the spring of 5756 (1996), the Lubavitch Library presented an exhibition devoted to the collection of Passover Haggadot held in its archive. Title: Exhibition of Rabbeinu Nesieinu (1996)
Summary: An exhibition devoted to the Chabad Rebbes was held at the Library in late 5756.
Story: Toward the end of the year 5756 (1996), the Lubavitch Library held an exhibition focused on the Chabad Rebbes. It was the fourth in the series of themed exhibitions launched after the hall opened in 5754. The display drew on manuscripts, photographs and personal items connected to each successive Rebbe.
Tags: library, exhibition, chabad rebbes

Title: First portion of Lubavitch courtyard purchased for museum
Summary: R' Natan Gurary purchased part of the Rebbes' courtyard in Lubavitch to build a museum.
Story: In 5756 (1996), R' Natan Gurary purchased part of the Rebbes' courtyard in Lubavitch in order to build a museum on the site. He would later purchase additional portions in 5758 (1998), and the final third portion in 5760 (2000).
Tags: lubavitch, museum, courtyard, gurary

Title: R. Yisrael Grossman writes to cousin documenting MaHaRIL descent
Summary: In 5756 (1996) R. Yisrael Grossman, rosh yeshiva of Tomchei Temimim in Kfar Chabad-Lod, wrote a letter detailing the family's descent from MaHaRIL, brother of the Alter Rebbe.
Story: The letter identifies three brothers — R. Schneur Zalman, R. Yisrael, and another — buried on the Mount of Olives, and traces the line back to MaHaRIL. It is a primary source for the family tree linking the Brimat/Saulson/Singer/Grossman families to the brother of the Baal HaTanya.
