Title: Publication of edited Jacobson memoirs
Summary: Shalom DovBer Levin completed the editing introduction to Zichron LiBnei Yisrael on 15 Shevat 5756.
Story: On 15 Shevat 5756 (February 1996), Rabbi Shalom DovBer Levin in Brooklyn, NY, signed off on the foreword to Zichron LiBnei Yisrael, the edited volume of R. Yisrael Jacobson's memoirs. The volume covered Jacobson's years 5667-5699 in Lubavitch, Shchedrin, Kremenchug, Kherson, Homel, and New York. Levin organized the fragmentary original writings into chapters with annotations, photographs, and indexes.
Tags: memoirs, jacobson, levin

Title: Rabboseinu exhibition opens on 18 Elul
Summary: The Rabboseinu exhibition of the Lubavitch Library opened on 18 Elul 5756.
Story: The fourth exhibition of the Library — Taarukhas Rabboseinu — opened on 18 Elul 5756 (1996), the joint birthday of the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe. It displayed first editions of the Rebbeim's works, manuscripts, sacred objects, and portraits, with dedicated cases for the Baal Shem Tov, Maggid of Mezeritch, and each of the Chabad Rebbeim.
Tags: library, exhibition, 18 elul, besht, alter rebbe, portraits

Title: Exhibition on Chabad, Shlichus and the Mivtzaim
Summary: The Library's summer 5757 exhibition focused on Chabad activity, shlichus and the mitzvah campaigns.
Story: In the summer of 5757 (1997), the Lubavitch Library presented an exhibition on Chabad's worldwide activity, the work of shluchim, and the Rebbe's mivtzaim—campaigns to spread observance of mitzvos such as tefillin, mezuzah, Shabbos candles, kashrus and the four species. The exhibit displayed candle-lighting sets, tzedakah boxes, menorahs, mivtza tanks' keys and other items sent to the Rebbe from Chabad centers around the world.
Tags: library, exhibition, shlichus, mivtzaim, mitzvah campaigns

Title: Publication of 'Toldos Avraham Chaim' book
Summary: The biographical work 'Toldos Avraham Chaim' was published at the start of 5758, including the detailed will of R' Avraham Chaim.
Story: At the start of 5758, the book 'Toldos Avraham Chaim' was published, including on pages 62-64 the detailed will of R' Avraham Chaim. The will requested burial in Achuzas Olam cemetery in New York. Following publication, various searches were undertaken to locate the original Chabad cemetery plot in New York.
Tags: avraham-chaim, publication, biography

Title: Levin travels to Moscow for Agudas Chabad conference around Yud Shevat
Summary: Levin flew from New York to Moscow for an Agudas Chabad conference organized by Rabbi Yisroel Kogan around Yud Shevat 5757.
Story: Levin arrived Monday afternoon for the conference at Agudas Chabad's Moscow center. Aharonov also flew in Thursday afternoon. Conference attendees were invited to visit the library to view 16 Schneerson books prepared in a new wing, but Levin refused to formally request fuller access and left publicly to avoid legitimizing the new wing concept.
Tags: russia, moscow, agudas-chabad, yud-shevat, yisroel-kogan

Title: Chabad activities exhibition opens on Lag BaOmer 5757
Summary: The fifth Library exhibition on Chabad activities, shlichus and mivtzaim opened on Lag BaOmer 5757.
Story: On Lag BaOmer 5757 (1997) the fifth major Library exhibition opened — Taarukhas Chabad: HaPe'ilus, HaShlichus UMivtza'ei HaMitzvos. It presented the worldwide network of more than two thousand institutions run by the Rebbe's shluchim and the mivtzaim he founded over the half-century of his nesius, organized into thirteen themed display cases.
Tags: library, exhibition, lag baomer, shlichus, mivtzaim

Title: Levin issues open letter rejecting Moscow Schneerson wing proposal
Summary: On 7 Av 5757, Levin published an open letter to Anash explaining why reports of a planned Schneerson wing at the Moscow library were misleading and contrary to the Rebbe's wishes.
Story: Levin cited the Rebbe's 5751 ruling that opening a Chabad library in Russia would only fuel arguments against the books' return. He argued the 12,000-book collection was not particularly rare, with a market value under a quarter-million dollars, and held only sentimental value. He warned that sensational press coverage misled the Russians into thinking they had something marketable, undermining return efforts.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, shalom-dovber-levin, menachem-mendel-schneerson

Title: Rashab's Rostov home redeemed by Chabad
Summary: In Marcheshvan 5758, several apartments on the upper floor of the Rashab's former Rostov residence were purchased.
Story: After more than seven decades in foreign hands, in Marcheshvan 5758 the upper floor of the Rebbe's Rostov home was reclaimed through the purchase of several small apartments. The acquired rooms included most of the Rashab's living quarters: the 'zal' where he delivered chassidic discourses on Shabbos and yom tov and held yechidus, the dining room where he farbrenged, and the porch where the sukkah had stood.
Tags: rostov, bratsky pereulok, restoration, heritage

Title: Chassidut exhibit marking 300 years since the Baal Shem Tov's birth
Summary: In 5758 the Chabad library mounted an exhibit of early chassidic books marking 300 years since the Baal Shem Tov's birth.
Story: The Chabad library curated an exhibit of foundational chassidic works printed during the first jubilee following the Baal Shem Tov's passing (5520–5570). The exhibit opened toward Shavuot — the Baal Shem Tov's yahrzeit — and ran until 18 Elul 5758, marking 300 years since his birth on 18 Elul 5458 (1698).
Tags: baal shem tov, exhibit, library, chassidut

Title: Eli Segal purchases second portion of the Lubavitch courtyard
Summary: In 5758 Eli Segal acquired an additional portion of the courtyard of the Rebbes in Lubavitch for the museum project.
Story: In 5758 (1998), Mr. Eli Segal acquired a further portion of the courtyard of the Rebbes in Lubavitch. This was the second of three stages by which he was assembling the historic site for the construction of a Chabad museum at its center.
Tags: lubavitch, museum, eli segal, courtyard

Title: Exhibition of Chassidus
Summary: The Library held an exhibition devoted to Chassidus in summer 5758.
Story: The summer 5758 (1998) exhibition at the Lubavitch Library was dedicated to the broader Chassidic movement. It was the sixth in the rotation of themed exhibitions begun in 5754. The display drew on the library's holdings of early Chassidic books, manuscripts and related artifacts.
Tags: library, exhibition, chassidus

Title: Second portion of Lubavitch courtyard acquired
Summary: In 5758 Eliyahu Segal purchased an additional portion of the original Lubavitch courtyard for the museum project.
Story: The acquisition continued the multi-year effort to reassemble the courtyard plot under the museum's ownership. The work was coordinated by Agudas Chasidei Chabad of the CIS together with Rabbi Nosson Gourary. Each phase brought the project closer to enabling construction of the museum at the original site.
Tags: museum, segal, purchase, lubavitch-courtyard

Title: Tolodos Avraham Chaim biography published
Summary: Otzar Hachassidim publishes 'Tolodos Avraham Chaim,' the biography and writings of R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum of Plescenice, edited by R. Shalom Dovber Levin.
Story: Issued in Brooklyn on 24 Teves 5758 (1998), the volume compiles the life story of the chossid R. Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum of Plescenice along with his correspondence with the Rebbe Rashab, R. Shmuel Dovber of Borisov, the mashpia R. Hendel Kugel and other senior chassidim. It also publishes his writings in halacha, Kabbalah, Chassidus, language and avodas Hashem, drawn from his archive in the Agudas Chassidei Chabad–Lubavitch library.
Tags: biography, rosenbaum, otzar hachassidim, shalom dovber levin, plescenice

Title: Hidden Rostov mikvah uncovered intact on Lag B'Omer
Summary: On Lag B'Omer 5758, excavators found the Rashab's sealed mikvah preserved beneath the basement floor.
Story: Guided by the testimony of elder chassidim who had studied in Rostov decades earlier, workers on Lag B'Omer 5758 began excavating the suspected location of the Rashab's hidden mikvah. Beneath the basement floor they found the mikvah whole, and continuing to dig they exposed the lower reservoir — still holding the rainwater the Rebbeim had used to fill it, sealed there since 1924.
Tags: rostov, mikvah, lag bomer, restoration

Title: Dr. Nissan Mindel passes away
Summary: Dr. Nissan Mindel, longtime Chabad secretary and English translator of the Tanya, passes away.
Story: He served on the boards of Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch and Agudas Chassidei Chabad and wrote major works on chasidic history and philosophy in addition to his Tanya translation.
Tags: mindel, passing, tanya, translation

Title: Exhibit marking 200 years since Alter Rebbe's liberation
Summary: In 5759 the Chabad library held an exhibit marking 200 years since the Alter Rebbe's liberation on 19 Kislev 5559.
Story: On Tuesday, 19 Kislev 5759 (1998), 200 years had passed since the liberation of Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi from his first imprisonment. The Chabad library mounted an exhibit running through 11 Nissan 5759 (1999), displaying first editions of the Alter Rebbe's works, original handwritten manuscripts, ancient copies, sacred artifacts, and portraits.
Tags: alter rebbe, yud tes kislev, exhibit, library, 200 years

Title: Exhibition on the Alter Rebbe's 200th liberation anniversary
Summary: The Library mounted an exhibition marking 200 years since the Alter Rebbe's liberation, in winter 5759.
Story: In the winter of 5759 (1998–99), the Lubavitch Library presented an exhibition marking the 200th anniversary of the liberation of the Alter Rebbe, Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, from Czarist imprisonment on Yud Tes Kislev. Exhibits included items associated with the Alter Rebbe, such as a first edition of his Shulchan Aruch (Kapust 5574) and the first edition of Tanya (Slavita 5557), as well as a handwritten letter.
Tags: library, exhibition, alter rebbe, yud tes kislev

Title: Likkutei Torah expanded chronology of maamarim
Summary: A more complete chronological list of Likkutei Torah maamarim was printed in the Kehot 5759 (1999) edition supplement.
Story: This was the most refined dating effort to date for the maamarim included in Likkutei Torah, building on the prior work of R' Yosef Yitzchak Keller and the editorial team behind subsequent volumes of Maamarei Admur HaZaken.
Tags: likkutei torah, alter rebbe, kehot, maamarim

Title: R' Avraham Chaim's grave located at Mount Zion cemetery
Summary: After 5760 Tishrei, R' Yisrael Mordechai Kozaminsky located R' Avraham Chaim's grave at Mount Zion cemetery in Brooklyn.
Story: After Tishrei 5760, R' Yisrael Mordechai HaLevi Kozaminsky discovered through a Brooklyn Charedi newspaper that R' Avraham Chaim's gravestone was at Mount Zion cemetery in Brooklyn rather than the Achuzas Olam plot in Staten Island where searchers had been looking. Upon visiting with R' Meir Simcha Abramovich, he confirmed the gravestone and corrected the recorded death year from 5674 to 5675.
Tags: mount-zion, brooklyn, avraham-chaim, cemetery, research

Title: Lost Maharash letter rediscovered as photo in geniza
Summary: On 27 Elul 5759 (1999), a photocopy of the missing Rebbe Maharash letter to R. Chaim Yaakov Widrewitz surfaced in a municipal library geniza.
Story: After nearly forty years of unsuccessful searches, R. Shaul Vilhelm called from Detroit on 27 Elul 5759 to report that Yosef Levin had found a photocopy of the lost buch in a public library's geniza. The photocopy contained the long-sought Maharash letter to R. Chaim Yaakov Widrewitz, in which the Rebbe acknowledged receiving Widrewitz's kuntress and promised to set aside time to study it despite poor health and many demands.
Tags: maharash, shmuel of lubavitch, chaim yaakov widrewitz, yosef levin, shaul vilhelm, detroit, manuscripts

Title: Levin replies to Aharonov on commission letter, eve of Rosh Hashanah 5760
Summary: On erev Rosh Hashanah 5760, Levin wrote to Aharonov rejecting Russian library proposals for an international commission funded by Agudas Chabad.
Story: Library Eastern department head Mira Trifonenko proposed an international commission to identify Polyakov collection ownership, with Chabad covering all expenses. Levin suspected this would lead to hundreds of thousands of dollars in costs for hostile commission members while never actually allowing real inspection. Still, he offered to travel personally if needed, but only with a precise agenda.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, mira-trifonenko, shalom-dovber-levin

Title: Mira Trifonenko confirms Levin's solo inspection visit to Moscow library
Summary: On 2 Kislev 5760, Levin received Trifonenko's reply approving his plan to come for a week of book inspection without waiting for the commission's formation.
Story: Mira welcomed the proposal that Levin alone visit on Agudas Chabad funding, rather than convening the full commission. She asked him to indicate his preferred dates. Levin offered November 21–26 or December 12–17 and outlined a three-list inspection plan: marked Schneerson books, books in the 1914 Lubavitch catalogue, and unmarked unlisted books.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, mira-trifonenko

Title: Levin sends detailed Moscow library inspection plan by fax
Summary: On 14 Kislev 5760, Levin faxed Trifonenko a detailed work plan covering each library department he would inspect with a day-by-day schedule.
Story: Mira quickly confirmed his visa was arranged for pickup at the embassy on December 3 and accepted his agenda and department list. Levin finalized his departure for motzei Shabbos Zos Chanukah and planned to start work the morning of 4 Tevet. He remained undecided whether to stay one or two weeks, depending on his access.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, shalom-dovber-levin, mira-trifonenko

Title: Levin records detailed diary entry about renewed Moscow library negotiations
Summary: After years of silence in his diary, Levin resumed writing on 17 Kislev 5760 after receiving a formal invitation from the Moscow library to inspect the books.
Story: Levin noted nothing had moved on the books for years. The new invitation asked him to join a special commission to discuss the books. He accepted and prepared to fly to Moscow in two weeks, motzei Shabbos Zos Chanukah, viewing it as a rare opportunity to actually check the books one by one.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, shalom-dovber-levin

Title: Levin arrives in Moscow at Hotel Minsk to begin library inspection
Summary: Levin arrived in Moscow the morning of 4 Tevet 5760, stopping at the Agudas Chabad center on Bolshaya Bronnaya before settling at Hotel Minsk.
Story: His original plan had been to start work the same day, but Mira had warned by fax that a Russian national holiday closed the library. He spent the day at the Agudas Chabad center conversing with Rabbi Yisroel Kogan and Boruch Gorin, then returned to his hotel to rest and pray. He scheduled the first inspection day for the morning of 5 Tevet, 'didan natzach' day.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, hotel-minsk, yisroel-kogan, boruch-gorin

Title: Didan Notzach farbrengen at Moscow's Agudas Chabad synagogue
Summary: About fifty Chabad community members in Moscow gathered on 5 Tevet to mark Didan Notzach, the anniversary of the Lubavitch library court victory.
Story: On the night of 5 Tevet 5760, the diarist joined a Didan Notzach gathering at the Agudas Chabad synagogue in Moscow with roughly fifty Anash members and yeshiva students. He spoke in Hebrew while Rabbi M. Hochberg translated to Russian. He also joined a live broadcast to a parallel farbrengen at Beis Rivka in New York to report progress in identifying Schneersohn books that day.
Tags: moscow, russia, didan-notzach, agudas-chabad, schneersohn-library, farbrengen, celebration

Title: First day Levin permitted to fully inspect Schneerson collection
Summary: On 5 Tevet 5760, the Didan Natzach anniversary, Levin was granted unprecedented access to inspect the Schneerson collection book by book at the Moscow library.
Story: Mira Trifonenko, head of the Eastern books department, told Levin all 110 rare-museum books were confirmed Schneerson. The Polyakov collection was split into four parts: 110 rare museum books, 2,300 old books, 8,350 books from 17th–18th centuries at the Khimki depot, and 280 manuscripts known as the Schneerson archive. Levin began his planned categorization of marked, catalogued, and unmarked unlisted books.
Tags: russia, moscow, schneerson-library, polyakov-collection, mira-trifonenko, didan-natzach

Title: First inspection of Schneersohn books at Khimki warehouse
Summary: The Chabad emissary was first permitted to examine the 6,000 Polyakov-collection volumes stored in Khimki, identifying about 70 of 250 sampled as Lubavitch books.
Story: On 6 Tevet 5760, the emissary traveled with librarian Oleg to the Russian State Library's Khimki branch. After being required to obtain a special permit on site, he was allowed onto the 10th floor for the first time, where 6,000 unsorted Polyakov-collection volumes were kept. He recorded about 250 volumes and identified roughly 70 as bearing clear Lubavitch markings.
Tags: moscow, khimki, russia, schneersohn-library, polyakov-collection, oleg-librarian, books

Title: Meeting with US embassy representative Mary Dietrich on the books
Summary: A 2.5-hour meeting between the emissary, US embassy representative Mary Dietrich, and library department head Mara Trifonenko outlined a Russian proposal for returning the Lubavitch library.
Story: On 7 Tevet 5760, the emissary met with US embassy representative Mary Dietrich and Russian State Library Oriental Books department head Mara Trifonenko for over two hours. Trifonenko detailed a four-stage plan involving a committee, duplicate-checks, and a new building before any books could be returned. The emissary argued the plan was unrealistic and would take decades, but provided a list of 100 books for the librarians to verify.
Tags: moscow, russia, us-embassy, mary-dietrich, mara-trifonenko, schneersohn-library, diplomacy

Title: Exhibition on the Rebbe Rayatz
Summary: The Library's summer 5760 exhibition was devoted to the Rebbe Rayatz.
Story: In the summer of 5760 (2000), the Lubavitch Library held an exhibition dedicated to the sixth Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn (Rayatz). Exhibits drew on his manuscripts, the spodik he wore, his writing implements and items from his secretariat. It was the eighth in the library's series of themed exhibits.
Tags: library, exhibition, rebbe rayatz, yosef yitzchak

Title: Final portion of Lubavitch courtyard acquired
Summary: In 5760 the third and final portion of the original Lubavitch courtyard was purchased by Eliyahu Segal, completing the site assembly for the museum.
Story: With the full courtyard now under museum ownership, construction of the museum building could proceed at the center of the historic site. The acquisitions had taken four years across three transactions. The completed assembly enabled immediate construction work to begin.
Tags: museum, segal, purchase, lubavitch-courtyard

Title: Final portion of the Lubavitch courtyard purchased; museum built
Summary: In 5760 Eli Segal purchased the third and final portion of the courtyard of the Rebbes, completing the site for the Chabad museum which was then built and opened.
Story: In 5760 (2000), Mr. Eli Segal purchased the third and final portion of the courtyard of the Rebbes in Lubavitch. Construction of the museum building began immediately at the center of the courtyard, and by the beginning of Nissan the museum was completed and opened to the public.
Tags: lubavitch, museum, eli segal, courtyard

Title: Library opens Rebbe Rayatz exhibition on 12 Tammuz 5760
Summary: The Chabad library opened a major exhibition of the Rebbe Rayatz's possessions, manuscripts, and books around 12 Tammuz 5760 (July 2000).
Story: Marking the 120th anniversary of the Rebbe Rayatz's birth and 73 years since his Soviet liberation, the exhibition displayed his shtreimel, kittel, walking staff, passport, diaries, and chassidic manuscripts. It ran through the jubilee 50th yahrzeit period ending 10 Shvat 5761.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, library, exhibition, yud beis tammuz

Title: 'Lubavitch Collection' labeling of Polyakov books begins in Khimki
Summary: On a second Moscow visit, the emissary began affixing 'Lubavitch Collection' stickers — prepared himself in New York — onto Polyakov-collection books identified as Schneersohn library volumes.
Story: On 8 Tammuz 5760, the emissary arrived in Moscow with 3,000 self-printed 'Lubavitch Collection' stickers, having distrusted the library's offer of blank labels. Working with librarians Oleg and Lena on the 10th floor in Khimki, he passed over about 2,500 books and identified 263 as bearing clear Lubavitch markings, which they immediately labeled.
Tags: moscow, khimki, russia, schneersohn-library, polyakov-collection, labels, oleg-librarian, books

Title: Meeting at US embassy in Moscow with deputy ambassador John Ordway
Summary: A two-hour meeting at the US embassy with deputy ambassador John Ordway and aide Howard Solomon to discuss returning the Lubavitch library.
Story: On 9 Tammuz 5760, after a morning session with Mara Trifonenko, the emissary went to the US embassy for a two-hour meeting with deputy ambassador John Ordway and his aide Howard Solomon. He argued the Russian side had no real intention of returning books, using duplicate-checks and a committee to stall indefinitely. He proposed starting returns with the 500+ books the librarians had already verified, but was refused.
Tags: moscow, russia, us-embassy, john-ordway, howard-solomon, mara-trifonenko, schneersohn-library, diplomacy

Title: Identification of 845 new Lubavitch books in Moscow library
Summary: The emissary finished examining the 1,500 unidentified books on the 12th floor of the main library, bringing his total newly identified Lubavitch volumes to about 845.
Story: On 16 Tammuz 5760, the emissary completed sorting through the 1,500 unidentified volumes in the main building, identifying an additional 74 Lubavitch books and bringing his two-visit total to about 845. The team also began affixing 'Lubavitch Collection' stickers to the 3,000 books originally identified by library staff in 5752, completing 825 of them that day.
Tags: moscow, russia, schneersohn-library, polyakov-collection, russian-state-library, books

Title: Final labeling of 4,354 books as 'Lubavitch Collection' in Moscow
Summary: The emissary completed labeling 4,354 identified Schneersohn-collection volumes in the Russian State Library with 'Lubavitch Collection' stickers, finishing his identification mission.
Story: On 17 Tammuz 5760, the labeling project was completed: 4,354 books in the public library bore 'Lubavitch Collection' stickers — 770 in the Khimki branch and the rest in the main building. The emissary estimated roughly 2,500 additional Lubavitch volumes remained mixed in the Polyakov collection without identifying marks, alongside 110 rare books in the museum and 280 manuscripts outside Trifonenko's jurisdiction.
Tags: moscow, khimki, russia, schneersohn-library, polyakov-collection, labels, russian-state-library, books

Title: Lubavitch museum building completed
Summary: The museum building in the center of the Lubavitch courtyard was completed and opened to the public.
Story: At the start of Nissan 5761 (2001), the construction of the museum building in the center of the Rebbes' courtyard in Lubavitch was completed. The museum was then opened to the public, marking the restoration of an active Jewish presence in the historic town.
Tags: lubavitch, museum, courtyard

Title: Rebbe Rayatz exhibition closes on jubilee yahrzeit, 10 Shvat 5761
Summary: The Rebbe Rayatz exhibition concluded on 10 Shvat 5761, marking the fiftieth-year jubilee of his passing and of the Rebbe's assumption of Chabad leadership.
Story: The 10 Shvat 5761 close date matched the half-century since the Rebbe Rayatz's 1950 passing and the seventh Rebbe's acceptance of the Chabad nesius. The yom hilula remains the central Chabad date for the seventh Rebbe's leadership.
Tags: rebbe rayatz, yahrzeit, yud shvat, jubilee

Title: Lubavitch Museum opens in original Chabad courtyard
Summary: The Lubavitch Museum, operated by Agudas Chasidei Chabad of the CIS, opened to the public on 3 Nisan 5761 at the historic courtyard.
Story: The opening commemorated 80 years since the 5681 fire that destroyed the courtyard and 81 years since the passing of the Rashab in Rostov. The museum building had been constructed at the center of the courtyard reassembled through purchases in 5756, 5758, and 5760. It is administered by Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Aharonov, Rabbi Shalom Dovber Levin, and Rabbi Nosson Gourary.
Tags: museum, lubavitch, agudas-chasidei-chabad, cis

Title: Exhibition of the Rebbeim's books
Summary: The Lubavitch Library held an exhibition of books authored by the Chabad Rebbes in 5762.
Story: During the year 5762 (2001–02), the library displayed first editions and other significant printings of works authored by the Chabad Rebbes. The exhibit included items such as the first edition of Maggid Devarav LeYaakov (Koretz 5541), Imrei Binah (Kapust 5581) and Tzemach Tzedek (Vilna 5631). It was the ninth themed exhibit since the hall opened in 5754.
Tags: library, exhibition, rare books, first editions

Title: Passing of R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie in New York
Summary: R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie passed away in New York on the first day of Rosh Hashana 5764.
Story: On the first day of Rosh Hashana 5764 (27 September 2003), Shabbat, R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie passed away in New York. He had served as a senior leader within the Chabad movement for decades — heading the Warsaw mechina in his youth, leading Achei Temimim in New York, and later serving on the Vaad HaMesader and the Vaad Hanhalat Agudat Chabad. His life spanned the destruction of pre-war European Chabad and its rebuilding in America.
Tags: new-york, shneur-zalman-gurarie, rosh-hashana, death

Title: Exhibition of certificates of honor to the Rebbe
Summary: The Library mounted an exhibition of honorary certificates given to the Rebbe in spring 5765.
Story: In the spring of 5765 (2005), the Lubavitch Library held an exhibition focused on the honorary certificates, keys, medals and scrolls of honor presented to the Rebbe by heads of state, mayors, military commanders and institutional leaders. It was the tenth themed exhibit since the hall opened in 5754.
Tags: library, exhibition, keys, medals, honorary scrolls

Title: Library opens exhibition of certificates of honor to the Rebbe
Summary: On 11 Nisan 5765 (April 20, 2005) the library opened an exhibition of medals, keys, and certificates given to the Rebbe by heads of state and city governments.
Story: Exhibition Yud featured items presented to the Rebbe by world leaders and municipal authorities, alongside keys to Chabad houses and mitzvah tanks from his shluchim around the globe.
Tags: rebbe, library, exhibition, 11 nisan, certificates

Title: Passing of R' Moshe Ashkenazi
Summary: The chassid R' Moshe Ashkenazi passed away on 23 Tevet תשס"ח; his rare wedding-gift Siddur with Da"Ch later passed via his son-in-law R' Nachman Yosef Tversky to the library.
Story: R' Moshe Ashkenazi, who had received the unusual Königsberg-imprint Siddur with Da"Ch at his 1942 wedding, passed away on 23 Tevet תשס"ח. The siddur — one of only a handful of copies printed openly for Königsberg's own Jewish residents rather than smuggled into Russia — was given by his son-in-law R' Nachman Yosef Tversky to the Lubavitch library, where it provided definitive evidence that the disputed third edition had in fact been printed in Königsberg in תרי"ב.
Tags: ashkenazi, passing, chassid

Title: Shaar HaMilu'im V from Moscow archives printed
Summary: In 5769 photographs of seven additional bichlach arrived from the Moscow archives, and Shaar HaMilu'im volume V was compiled from them and printed.
Story: Decades after the original supplements series began, photocopies of seven more manuscript volumes from Russian state archives reached the Chabad library. The material was edited into Shaar HaMilu'im V and published in 5769. A list of seven additional volumes still held in Russian archives was printed at the back of this volume.
Tags: tzemach tzedek, moscow archives, shaar hamilu'im, manuscripts

Title: R' Yehoshua Heshel Reizman passes away
Summary: R' Yehoshua Heshel Reizman, former maggid shiur of the Warsaw Mechina, died on 10 Tevet 5769.
Story: Born on 1 Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5678 in Wodzislaw and raised in Suchedniow, R' Heshel Reizman studied at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw from 5692, taught in its Mechina from spring 5697, and survived WWII. He passed away on 10 Tevet 5769. A short biography appears at the start of his sefer Iyunim B'Ta'aniyos.
Tags: heshel reizman, tomchei tmimim, mechina, yahrzeit, suchedniow

Title: MiBeis HaGenazim exhibition and album
Summary: The Library held the 'MiBeis HaGenazim' exhibition in winter 5770 and printed an accompanying album of 154 archive items.
Story: In the winter of 5770 (2009–10), the Lubavitch Library presented its eleventh exhibition, titled 'MiBeis HaGenazim,' surveying treasures held in the archive. A printed album of the same name accompanied the exhibit, documenting 154 special items preserved in the library's collection. The volume later served as a model for a successor work compiled in 5778.
Tags: library, exhibition, archive, mibeis hagenazim

Title: Publication of Toldot Chabad B'Russia HaTza'arit
Summary: Sh. D. Levin signs the preface to Toldot Chabad B'Russia HaTza'arit in Brooklyn on 12 Tammuz 5770.
Story: The fourth volume of the Toldot Chabad series, covering Tsarist Russia in selected chapters across the first five generations of Chabad leadership, was completed in Brooklyn on 12 Tammuz 5770 (June 24, 2010) and published by Otzar HaChassidim at 770 Eastern Parkway. The preface acknowledges R' Yitzchak Wilhelm and R' Dovid Moshe Olidort for their editorial review.
Tags: kehot, lubavitch, tsarist russia, brooklyn

Title: Exhibition of keys and certificates of honor
Summary: The Lubavitch Library held an exhibition of keys and certificates of honor in summer 5773.
Story: In the summer of 5773 (2013), the Lubavitch Library presented an exhibition focused on keys and honorary certificates given to the Rebbe. It was the twelfth themed exhibition in the hall since 5754. Items displayed included tokens sent by municipalities, governments and institutions around the world.
Tags: library, exhibition, keys, honorary scrolls

Title: Library opens "Keys and Certificates of Honor" exhibition in Elul 5773
Summary: A library exhibition of keys and honor certificates given to the Rebbe opened in Elul 5773 (August/September 2013).
Story: Exhibition Yud-Beis displayed medallions, mitzvah-tank keys, and Chabad-house keys gathered by the Rebbe over the decades, illustrating his global network of shluchim and official ties with heads of state and municipal authorities.
Tags: rebbe, library, exhibition, elul, shluchim

Title: Exhibition of book treasures
Summary: The Library mounted a 'Treasures of Books' exhibition in summer 5774.
Story: In the summer of 5774 (2014), the Lubavitch Library held an exhibition of rare books and bibliographic treasures from its collection. It was the thirteenth themed exhibit since the hall opened in 5754. The library's holdings include some 200,000 books, many of them incunabula and first editions.
Tags: library, exhibition, rare books, manuscripts

Title: Roza Melamed, last witness to Sixth Rebbe's Kostroma exile, dies in Beer Sheva
Summary: Roza Melamed, who was twelve when her family hosted the Rebbe in Kostroma in 1927, died at the age of 99.
Story: The daughter of the Kostroma shochet Yerachmiel Kugel, Melamed recalled the Rebbe constantly studying Torah and asking the children daily how they were doing. He blessed her with long life and prayed she never know the suffering he had endured. She lived to fulfill the blessing, dying in Beer Sheva.
Tags: kostroma, melamed, beer sheva, witness

Title: Library opens 13th exhibition of rare incunabula on 20th yahrzeit
Summary: On 3 Tammuz 5774, the library opened its 13th exhibition, displaying rare books printed in the first century of Hebrew printing.
Story: On 3 Tammuz 5774 (July 1, 2014), marking the 20th yahrzeit of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, the Chabad Library opened its 13th exhibition — Ta'aruchat Ginzei Sefarim. The exhibition displays incunabula and rare books printed in the first 100 years of Hebrew printing (1475–1574), along with rare manuscripts, broadsides and posters. A guide booklet was prepared by Rabbi Shalom DovBer Levin and R. Moshe Heller.
Tags: 770, chabad library, exhibition, incunabula, gimmel tammuz, yahrzeit

Title: Exhibition on the Tzemach Tzedek
Summary: The Library held an exhibition on the Tzemach Tzedek in winter 5776.
Story: In the winter of 5776 (2015–16), the Lubavitch Library presented its fourteenth themed exhibit, devoted to the third Chabad Rebbe, Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneersohn, the Tzemach Tzedek. The display drew on his manuscripts, his Tanach (used for reading the Haftarah), his siddur and the first edition of his responsa work, Tzemach Tzedek (Vilna 5631).
Tags: library, exhibition, tzemach tzedek

Title: Yuli Edelstein addresses International Conference of Chabad Shluchim
Summary: Israeli Knesset Speaker Yuli Edelstein paid tribute to the Chabad underground in Moscow that had inspired his return to observance.
Story: A former Soviet refusenik who was sentenced on false charges to a Siberian prison camp for three years, Edelstein credited Rabbi Getche Vilensky and Rabbi Mottel Lipshitz of the Moscow Chabad underground as his inspiration on his journey to Jewish observance.

Title: Exhibition of Rabbeinu Nesieinu (2017)
Summary: The Library's spring 5777 exhibition was devoted to the Chabad Rebbes.
Story: In the spring of 5777 (2017), the Lubavitch Library held its fifteenth themed exhibit, again focused on the Chabad Rebbes. The display included manuscripts in the handwriting of each successive Rebbe, personal items such as the Mitteler Rebbe's tefillin pouch and the Rebbe Rashab's passport, and selected first editions of their works.

Title: Sequel to 'MiBeis HaGenazim' published
Summary: A sequel volume to 'MiBeis HaGenazim' was completed by Rabbi Shalom Dovber Levin in Brooklyn on 5 Teves 5778.
Story: On 5 Teves 5778 (December 2017), Rabbi Shalom Dovber Levin, director of the Lubavitch Library, signed the preface to a new book continuing the work of the earlier album 'MiBeis HaGenazim,' which had accompanied the winter 5770 exhibition. The new volume collected the guide booklets the library had printed for each exhibition since 5754, together with summaries of those exhibits for which no booklet had been printed. Together the book documented 15 exhibitions across more than two decades.

Title: Agudath Israel siyum HaShas at MetLife Stadium
Summary: Some ninety thousand attend the global celebration marking the completion of the daf yomi cycle of Talmud study.
Story: Organized by Agudath Israel in New Jersey, the event reflected the movement's continuing global Orthodox influence more than a century after its founding.

Title: Siyum HaShas held at MetLife Stadium
Summary: Agudath Israel organizes the Siyum HaShas at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey with some ninety thousand in attendance.
Story: The celebration marked the completion of the daf-yomi cycle of Talmud study. Today Agudath Israel — founded in 1912 — is a major religious party with seats in the Israeli Knesset and a significant presence in the US and European countries. The MetLife event reflected the global scope of Talmud study in the postwar era.
